reviews.comment: She was the best. She is approachable outside of class. That being said make sure you go to class and take good notes and you will be just fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Tara is a great professor. She is well-versed in the course material and cares deeply about the success of her students. The course is a good amount of reading but still manageable. Tests and quizzes are open note. If you attend class, engage in discussion, and take good notes you will do well.
Professor Ali is amazing! She is very knowledgeable and is always super enthusiastic to teach. The course does usually a decent amount of reading but overall its not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ali is great. She allowed outlines for tests and quizzes which was extremely helpful. She is very nice and gives interesting lectures. Highly recommend
Professor Ali is amazing!! The tests are open note which is so nice. As long as you do the readings (heads up there are a lot), you will do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such a wonderful professor. I loved Tara. She broke material down extremely well in her lectures. I took her SPEA-V 536 (law in public affairs course). She is very accessible outside of class. Her application assessments seemed hard at first, but as long as you pay attention in lectures, you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor emphasized "in-class demonstrations" over textbook/notes content for exams, and teaches at a fast pace using family members or past experiences as examples. And assigned seating was a personal discomfort/distraction. To succeed in this course, focus on in-class demonstrations and get ready for a fast-paced teaching style.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice professor. She actually makes an effort to learn individual students' names and connect with them. A lot of pre-class reading, with questions about the reading in class, so get ready to read a lot. All tests are open note, which is nice. As long as you pay attention in class and take good notes, you'll be fine.

One of the best professors i have ever had. She does have havy lectures but everything said in class is on the tests and exams. Her quizes and exams are open note and she gives you a study guide. She genuinely wants us all to succeed. She is amazing I will always look back on her has a mentor as well.
Professor Ali was amazing! By far my favorite professor. Would highly recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Such a sweet instructor who is always willing to meet and help. Although the course is very lecture heavy, and the exams are long, make sure you attend class and you should be good.

This class was the bane of my existence. Ali goes on tons of tangents about her career and it isn't helpful. Tests are extremely hard and she's confusing. Readings are long. This class doesn't have anything to do with business, really. She'll cold call on you if no one's participating, hard to reach, and rude.

A professor who is a kind person, but research is calling, not teaching. She had a hard time communicating what she knew to a class of beginners. I often did not understand her lectures as they were a bit all over the place. In terms of positive things, you did get a cheat sheet on every exam and the TA study sessions were the reason I passed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HER! The lectures made no sense. We had to have our AI beg for some type of quiz even though it was in the syllabus. Anna then said that she didn't have time to make a 10 question weekly quiz? She interrupted our other professor often during his lectures. Very awkward. Do not take her, take class another semester I beg you!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had in the history of my education.  The class was not super hard, but Dr. Kalinovsky would talk in circles throughout the duration of the class.  I never paid attention and was only there for attendance.  She completely overshadowed the other professor and tbh ruined my day when we had class.

Genuinely the worst prof I have had at IU. Her and the other prof would bicker in class. No assignments, and even though quizzes were on the syllabus, she claimed she was "too busy" to write them... we had to ask for them before our midterm. Every single class was full of wasted time. I learned almost nothing from her. A waste of time and sanity.

While she is very passionate about neurology, she is hard to understand. She has a bit of an accent, which is easily understood, but she talks so fast, that you can hardly catch what she's saying/means. She expects high comprehension, so this is difficult. Does not stick to original syllabus as well :(

there were only three tests in the entire course and eight homework assignments. basically your entire grade comes from the three exams and normally the exams only have around 30 questions, so if you miss more than 5 questions you're screwed. and she offers 0 extra credit and also does not curve any of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. K does a fantastic job teaching the course and you can truly see her passion for neuroscience. This class contains 3 exams which are hevily based on the lectures. ATTENDANCE matters and those who fail to show up do not do well in the class. She even allows a one-page of notes that can be used for the exams. Overall, I recommend the class.

The class I took with Dr. Kalinovsky was by far one of my hardest courses, but if you put the time into the class, you'll do good. She's available if you need any help at all, and you can have one notebook paper per test to have notes on. The class is only graded on a few homework assignments and the tests(85%!). I loved working with her.

The class average score for the first exam was 64%. Nobody had a very clear idea what her exams would be like and we got murdered on them. The lectures are extremely long and boring, I fell asleep more than once. There were 7 homework assignments but the largest chunk of your grade came from the exams. Exams were about half MC and half essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Insanely easy class. Show up to class and get attendance but that's the most work you have to do for lecture. Class is built on a project grade, a final project/paper, online quizzes over articles (that you don't have to read), and attendance. Pretty boring lectures if you don't know about music theory. Very easy grader.

Prof. Kalinovsky was a decent professor. She taught straight from lecture slides so lectures are very boring, but important because attendance is taken frequently. Very little homework. You don't need to read any of the book chapters and the exams are pretty easy mostly multiple choice. Just study the lecture slides and you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Anna is a great professor for P346. She has a Russian accent but it's not impossible to understand her at all. She is extremely intelligent and knowledgeable about neuroscience and her lectures go into a lot of detail which is great. Tests don't go into as much detail as the lectures do but it's a fascinating class.

Highly recommend taking either P346 or P337 (if possible, both!) with Dr. Kalinovsky. While the material can be fairly difficult to comprehend at times, her tests are straightforward and her knowledge of neuroscience is extensive. She is very passionate about her research and the lecture topics.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good Professor, tough class. Unfortunately the exam criteria isn't clearly stated,I went to the first review session directed by her and she had about 10 slides of review that we want over for 1 1/2 hours, and absolutely NONE of it was remotely on the exam. Not even helpful details that might benefit other questions. it was useless.

She is very smart and knows the material. She is a little awkward and difficult to follow at times. The learning objectives and things you need to know for the tests aren't clearly stated. I would recommend having a foundation in other chem and bio courses before taking this class.

Anna is extremely knowledgable about neuroscience. She is a very intelligent woman and can answer any question you throw at her. She has a very thick accent and is difficult to understand--especially if you are not familiar with the material. There are only three exams which means there is a lot of material cover a LOT and the grades really count!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Emailed her for clarification a lot about info on slides & she replied with "This is very clear in the slides." Half the test is verbatim the study guide and review questions. Most of the answers are in the readings/powerpoints but requires details from the lecture that you'll miss because she has a heavy accent and speaks somewhat quietly.

She has a Russian accent that is sometimes a little hard to understand. If you read the book you will know what to look for so it isn't much of a problem. My favorite thing about Prof Kalinovsky was her love of the material and her willingness to discuss any questions. It was a tough class, but I really enjoyed it.

This class is pretty intense. It is very molecular and detail oriented. She will explain mechanisms unlike any Professor you have had at IU, but she can get a bit lost in the details sometimes. I suggest this class for someone interested in the finer points of neurobiology. Also a good course for premed students.

I found her to be quite clear and even funny in lectures, especially for being Russian (heads up- she has an accent but its not bad). Lectures were interesting but not too difficult to wrap your head around and her practice tests are the same format as the real ones. Slides are online but class has extra info. Good prof and likeable person.

Lectures are tough to follow and seem to make the material more difficult than what it really is or needs to be. The review sessions and practice exams are not good preparation for the exams. I would suggest taking this course with someone else.
Don't take classes with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I was originally worried about taking this class because of the RMP reviews, but DrA was AMAZING. She values in class participation, so she might call on you without you wanting to talk, which is the worst part. She assigns long essays, but you have plenty of time to do them. Definitely recommend this course to good writers willing to participate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
PROS: You will learn about her whole life story, including all the troubles and how she gets vengeance on her students. Scary (Not someone you want as a role model) 
CONS: She wont teach you anything that has to do with any class. She also has a vendetta against people that make fun of her so keep all the comments to yourself. LIT.

Sadly, shes more focus on proving why she got the job than to teach anything. She will tell you how she has belittled students in the past, will make threats if you dare point out shes colombian (which clearly bothers her, wdk y ) and give you a bad grade. AND LITERALLY leave class if she has other plans. No type of profesonalist.
dismal class with Prof. Avellanada: belittles, will tell you she fails you if you dont agree with her, insecure, no dialogue. Uninspiring environment, stifling growth. Cautionary warning!

I really like Professor A, when you meet her she is quite intimidating, but she grows on you. The class is lecture-heavy, but the content is not crazy hard or anything, there are a lot of little assignments but tests and papers are the largest part of the grade. That being said she is amazing, very knowledgeable and dynamic and is very helpful.

Dr. A was not respectful nor understanding while talking to students. The curriculum is solely framed around extensive outside academic articles each week in which we discuss in class. I did not learn much relevant information, and the only value system was paper writing. I would not recommend taking this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr A was not a good teacher. She was super unreasonable and spoke very poorly to me when I went to her privately. She gives unnecessary reading and class time is spent going over the readings rather than learning or being taught new material. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor A is a badass. She was a lieutenant in the columbian army which is dope... but it also means she's a stickler for attendance and showing up on time. Lots of group work. She's passionate which makes the class fun and interesting, but beware her heavy accent. Classes are discussion-based and easy. Tests are tough-ish, lots of writing.

She gives tests that are all short answers, but she tells you what the questions will be in advance so it's all just memorization and easy if you study a little bit. There are a few easy assignments early in the class but the further along you get the less work there is. Attendance is taken not sure how it factors in yet. No textbook all on canvas.

She doesn't believe in multiple choice, so the test are just multiple essays. She has no problem failing many people, over a third of my class failed the midterm. Her lectures manage to be both extremely complex and extremely boring at the same time. I got nothing from the class. I recommend taking it with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Respected. Lecture Heavy. Accessible outside class.

Really interesting lectures if you're looking to go into a policy field--each lecture is part of a larger chart on the policy process that you discover at the end. She doesn't take attendance but the class is so small she calls you out if you skip without letting her know. Pay attention in the lectures and skim the readings or you'll be lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very good professor. take advantage of her feedback. Will help you always. Went in to office hours and she told me what to fix on my paper. Then got a 100 on that paper.
Deserves the hate he gets. It is his own doing.
Teaching? Kind of Bad. Behaviour? Worse Very unhelpful office hours. AIs were more helpful than him. Also been years since I took him. Not sure how much he has improved himself now.

Amr responded the average for the midterm was 77 and the final 84 something. It is because he handed out of 60 A's in a class of 120 student. Man if you teach well and do not criticize others. You do not have do such desperate attempt at image cleaning. 60 As are unusual as per his track record and other faculty teaching same class.
He tries to make everything about himself and constantly tries to one-up and compete with his own students. Just stop teaching and become a self-promoter then.
Prides himself in hurting students and colleagues. He is supposedly carrying PL.
Amr Sabry or Anna Sparkle??

Amr Sabry is an aggressive and combative individual who creates a stressful classroom environment by demeaning and unnecessarily criticizing students. Instead of inspiring students like other teachers he is leaving a behind a trail where students resist asking for help because he criticizes and demeans students. Just take an another proffessor.
Human Brick Wall.

took this class with Amr just a little while ago and had worst experience. He is not interested in addressing student grievances. Just gives feedback instead of correcting his own teaching methods. He also thinks it is cool to make students fail. More interested in revolting. So why is even teaching then? He is wasting students time and tuition.

He cannot teach to save his life. Unpleasant to interact with. He keeps deleting ratings. Him Deleting actual ratings is not going to make a better professor. He also tells irrelevant stories in his class and goes on a mini rant so many times. We are not interested in learning about your research trips dude.

I have graduated but still unsure if he is a bad teacher or the class material is bad. I took this class a while ago, and this is the only CS/INFO class that I got a D in. Now that I have graduated my entire cumulative gpa is 3.76. The second time I took this class I got a A-. Kinda leaves me wondering perhaps it wasn't just the material.

Grades Harshly. Makes class unnecessarily difficult. Good Material though. Class is not weeder. He is weeder. TAs are whatever. Sabry teaching is you watching copilot generating code. Yet I will never encourage anyone to take this class with him. He acts like he is doing a favor by delivering lectures with help of autopilot + TAs.

Avoid at all costs!!! Even after bad reviews I decided to give him a shot and it Is probably my worst mistake in my undergrad career. Material is Worse but he teaching and testing makes it 100x worse. He also doesn't accept late work unless you're dying in literal sense.
Late responses to emails. Cocky attitude cause of tenure

Extra Credit and Curve given to make up for his incompetence in teaching. Yaps on random stuff a lot. His 5 star ratings are inflated by him and his TAs. Simply avoid him or take course from other Iu institutions if other section by Dr. Jeremy Siek is full. His research doesn't help you in class.

Not as bad as ppl say. So much extra credit and the lectures are enough to do well if you pay attention. Hw has little to do with what's tested though. I also wish a reference textbook was provided for help. Just practice the algorithms a lot and you'll do fine. Final also wasn't cumulative
If there is one professor that you must avoid at IU. It is HIM. You probably can't find someone who is worse in terms of teaching, grading, office hours. This ain't cap.

The grading is messed up! The way he teaches is not really fun. So much is much expected but only little is taught in class. Expect to learnt a lot on your own, and fill in the gaps by watching youtube. If you get a good grade, it is coz of outside effort not coz how he teaches or how his office hours helped. Discord is just there to be there.
Would not reccomend this lecturer. I took him because other section was full.
One word for amr and my experience with him in this class: problematic

Worst. Proffessor. Ever.Can't grade exams!! He brought  by entire grade down. Never met a single person in class who liked him. Also how has he gotten these 5 stars reviews. Did he write them himself??!
Wannabe  Daniel Friedman.
If ya care for your grade avoid him and his section like the plague. If you want misery for 4 months then go ahead and take the class with him.

Assignments are the way it is. There is one project. Lectures are either too slow or too fast cause of autopilot generating all the code. There is no in-between. If you want a good grade, you have to know all the material before even before taking the class. I self-studied all the time. Got B because of Amr's harsh grading in final instead of A.

Grandiose Narcissist who pretends to be caring to students. -100000/10. Worst professor EVER in IU and BEYOND. Will do anything to protect his ego even if he is wrong. someone should tell he is no longer department chair.

Lectures are a snoozefest, but they aren't the worst when it comes to understanding the material. He loses track of his thinking when explaining, and it's obvious that he's way smarter than his students are. Get ready to learn a lot on your own.

Awful Professor. No connection between the previous lecture and next. Sometimes he taught, the other times his TA! Lectures & HWs were so bad that I ended up dropping the class. One word for Amr and this class: Problematic

The assignments were overwhelming, and the course was disorganized. Lack of clear instructions made coding for assignments worse. Lectures were often vague or went too fast.  Course was hard because expectations weren't aligned with lectures.  Frustrating experience. If you can find, please find worse professor at IU in Computer Science
Only 10-15 people would show up to his lectures out of 100+ s
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The time required for this class is off the charts. If you are ever taking C343, take it with Amr, and obviously build a bond with him. He is the absolute best. Great guy, helps you out with everything. Do not skip the chance to take classes with him. Highly reccomended proffesor for an undegrad student. He usually teaches C343 in fall. Solid 1/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took data structures SP24 and retook it FA24. I did better with Sabry, but that could just be because I had a bit of prior knowledge. The HW in spring was awful for me because you had to guess and debug errors that you couldn't see. I will say that the spring lectures are definitely better in quality, but beg for extra credit & you might survive
Easily the hardest proffesors to work with during my time at IU.

Gives so called "feedback" sessions in Office hours. After designing a horrible test. Someone said tests are "rigged". Didn't know it would be terrible. Other proffessors are not offered in fall. Got stuck with Amr.

If you need anything you need to know about him and his class. Just check the grade distribution for his sections. It will answer all your questions that you did not know you had. If you can just avoid.

The midterm was not hard if you took the time to understand the homework and it was even graded out of 25 instead of 30 (he also gave points back if you talked to him). He offered extra credit throughout the semester and the homework could easily be completed if you started early. Take time to learn the theory of data structures and you'll be fine

He is one of the smartest professors I have ever come across. Known for his research, but the problem with such a learned and educated proffessor is that they suffer from the curse of knowledge. They basically expect you to understand their complex assignments, and lectures. The concepts are difficult, so it will take time to be familiar with them

The class is extremely difficult, in order to suceed in this class, you need great amounts of self discipline. Make sure to attend Amr's office hours, and be in his good books. Ask him questions that demonstrate high order thinking. Talk to Amr about quantum and philosophy and demonstrate interest, and that you would like to get into research.

He loves students who consistently show up to class, but attendance isn't mandatory.  Reasonable guy with good humour. Would highly reccomend attending his lectures, and paying attention, and taking concrete notes.
Make sure to do the practice exams for midterm, and final if you want a good grade. DSA is difficult to say the least.

He's a good professor overall. Can be a little quiet when speaking so if you have issues with that, sit in the front of class. He also expected us to remember everything from C212 which caught many off guard. But he's very approachable, very transparent with grading, and if you put in the effort in class, he'll do what he can to help you succeed

there is a huge curve in the class but Amr is a very biased professor. he doesn't admit that he has favorites but he clearly does because they feed his ego. want to pass his class? flatter him go to his office hours and do the homework and tests well.  ask him doubts. basically become his favourite. if he likes you he will go to lengths for you

Amr is an AMAZING prof. While attending lecture isn't required, you should attend lecture + go to office hours if you want a good grade. The HWs are long, weekly assignments that are dense conceptually, but Amr is really easy to contact + meet with outside of class. So long as you put effort into his class, he'll do what he can to help you succeed.

Sabry is a nice man, and he's certainly not a fool. On those axes, he's an excellent professor.

However, this course was still something of a dumpster fire.

I don't have the space to list all my complaints, but I will say this: the tests were particularly bad. Both had extremely weighty points, ambiguous writing, and shoddy grading.

Prof. Sabry is probably the best professor I have had at my time in Bloomington. If you have the opportunity to take a course taught by him, do it. He explains things very well and you can tell he actually cares about his students. 10/10.

Best CS professor I have ever had. Star lecturer,he explains concepts very clearly, AND will take the time to go over them again and again,tweaking his explanations until students get it. Very accessible,manages his UIs so students get the most opportunities to learn. Class is tough,but he makes it worth the effort. Would take any class he teaches.

One of the best lecutures I have seen even though the course had to be online due to COVID. His lectures are all about understanding and applying the theory behind certain data structures and algorithms used in the course. He was always available, super understanding, and was able to explain complex concepts so well as to make it seem easy.

Fantastic professor for one of the hardest classes a computer scientist will have to take. Cares a lot about his students and is almost always available to answer questions and give feedback on homework. Handled the COVID pandemic perfectly and was one of my favorite professors in CS.
Definitely one of my favorite professors at IU so far.

When I realized I wasn't doing well, he told me I could redo my assignments & do the bonus assignments & I would pass. Got a tutor. Did the work. Failed me anyways. If you're failing, don't bother going to him, drop & take it again next semester. Go to class, his office hours, the AI's office hours and DO THE WORK ON TIME. Don't be cocky, get help.
He is insanely smart and expects students to be able to understand his lectures verbatim.

He gives great lectures and but expects a lot in homework and tests so be ready to learn a lot by yourself. As with any computer science course, there will be a lot of homework. If you need help, Amr is very accessible and helpful
not willing to answer questions or helping students out with any issue they may have.He will do anything to make the students fail.

He's solid in what he teaches, knows the pitfalls, subtle details, and most importantly understands students' questions. Very friendly. The course content is hard if you don't put enough effort, but in the end it's well worth it!

An instructor who knows the course content and more.  He is willing to answer questions and help students out with any issues they may have.  He is also very reasonable when it comes to attendance and grades.  By no means is it an easy course, but he will do everything in his power to help students succeed.
Very helpful and extremely good one-on-one. Willing to make time for students.

Dalton is by far my favorite professor I've had at IU. His passion for teaching and connecting with students made class very fun, and he made me look at science fiction in a light I never had before. As long as you read the books and take notes, the tests are easy!
Best class I took all semester, it made me switch to an English major. Funny professor and super interesting topic. Would definitely recommend.

ngl - this was a tough class. Theory is not for me and the readings were hard but dalton's lectures helped a ton and he gives good feedback. It's more of a lecture class than most english courses, but he's funny and pretty chill. Don't think I'd take this one again, but I'd take another one with dalton.

Dalton was one of my favorite professors. I was a little nervous going into CP - but am so glad I took it with him. He basically lectures the whole time but in a way that feels like a discussion and makes the ideas clear and he's funny. 9.5/10
He was the one to convince me to be an English major and helped outside of class to get the sources for me to do so, was very understanding of deadlines, and is a good lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: had him for paradise in literature: SUCH A KIND AND OUTGOING PROF! You can really tell that he cares about your success and the content that he is teaching. He's not a tough grader, but there is a lot of reading. Make sure you participate! it makes class so much more engaging!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dalton is the GOAT. Every single time I got into the classroom, it felt like there was a tube of straight knowledge going into my brain. Dalton knows so much about the subject, and it really shows. He is always willing to take questions and elaborate on things you are confused by. Great sense of humor and loves to teach. Use his office hours!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this one for A&H but completely loved it. Dalton made the class fun and with only 2 papers and 3 tests it wasn't too much work.

Dalton is the like the golden retriever of IU English profs. He's pretty high energy and bounces around a bit, but really fun and keeps things interesting. I had low expectations going into this class, but ended up really glad I took it.

Dalton really wants his students to understand and thrive in the extremely difficult course. He always stresses how we are people outside of his class and don't need to attend if we can't and gives amazing feedback. His lectures are always entertaining and I've learned more in a few weeks of his class than most other classes in total.

Cost accounting is not supposed to be easy. This is a hard class with hard exams. Exams cover a ton of different topics and take a ton of studying to understand and score well on the exams. She is the best prof offered for this class due to her clarity in explanations and free homework points. Take A325 with her, but don't expect it to be easy.

Hard class with very hard exams. To do well on the exams you really have to master the material, it takes more than just a few hours of studying. Other points are free 100%'s so as long as you aren't failing the exams you will be fine. She is prob the best A325 prof but the class is challenging. She is very nice and gives extra credit aswell.

Really great professor, by far the best for A325. Cost accounting is a hard topic but she uses class time for examples and going through the material which makes it easier to digest. Also she breaks down the group project into multiple parts making it much easier and grades that very easily so it's a nice grade boost. Overall great professor.

Worst professor I've had at IU so far. I loved and excelled at A306, but everyone in my class now doesn't like her. Her inverted teaching style could work if her videos were updated since COVID and actually included all of the information that was on the exams, but they aren't and don't. Hardly any practice and she doesn't care about your success.
The worst.

I think I could have done better in this class but I really enjoyed it overall. I loved having flipped classroom format and videos to look back on. She has some of the best clarity in her explanations out of most professors I've had!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Required video lectures before class. In class, she mostly goes through example questions. Content is fairly challenging, but she teaches it well - it just depends on if you like the inverted lecture style. She splits the project up to make it a really light load.

Ashley is a great teacher. The format of the class this year was super helpful. Watch a couple short videos outside of class, then spend the entire class time doing examples. She is very thorough and provides plenty of information to help study for exams. The material is difficult, but she makes it very manageable.

She cares about her students but makes the tests ridiculously hard. This is the hardest class I have taken at Kelley (coming from someone who found Finite, K201, A304, and A306 easy). I would study my butt off and still not be able to finish her tests. Wouldn't wish this on anyone.

Professor Saiciuc is a great teacher. You learn content outside of class and she does all practice problems in class, super easy to talk to and understanding. Cares about her students. 3 exams, clear what content will be and no final, instead a very straight forward group project. The project is a bit of work but it is super clear what she expects

Tests were hard and weighed very heavy. 12 questions for 200 points and 2 questions are free response. Cost is challenging in general and it was nice to have videos to look back on. She's nice but monotone. Class was useful for going over practice problems step by step. Group project was kinda difficult and have to give presentation on it.

Do not take this class. Every exam feels like going to war. There is no standardization of questions, confusing wording, and little in-class oversight as to what content will be on the test. Practice exams are always entirely different from real exams in content and question variety. Sauciuc just makes a difficult subject even more stressful.

reviews.comment: This professor does not care about the students in her class. She grades exams very slowly, unfairly, and subjectively, which leads to very low grade distributions. The module quizzes can be tricky and make up a decent portion of the final grade. I regret taking this course; take an A325 professor who actually wants to help students succeed.
The class is tough but she's pretty awesome. Definitely cares a lot and takes the time to make sure students understand concepts.

This class is challenging, but Professor Sausiuc does her best to help her students. She is always available to answer our questions after class.

The exam questions are much more complicated than the ones she goes through in her lectures. My recommendation is to do the extra practice problems she assigns.

The class is tough, the concepts are sometimes difficult to understand, but Professor Sauciuc is a very nice person and does her best to provide many examples to help students. Be prepared to study a lot if you want to do well

I knew this class would be difficult but Professor Sauciuc somehow makes it worse.The questions on exams are different from those done in class and it is VERY hard to finish on time. Before this class I have never not completed an exam on time. It's also a flipped classroom with lectures for homework and class time is practice questions.

I really wanted to like this class. However lectures were disorganized, feedback on assignments was limited and inconsistent, and assignments were graded months after submission. He would often share personal anecdotes that had little if anything to do with the subject matter, like how he once abandoned his wife at a protest.

I appreciate a discussion-based course but it was honestly a little too much at times for me, I can def see why others like it though. I wish there was a bit more structure to the class - prof is a great guy though! Super knowledgable and clearly knows what he's talking about

I liked this course, but I was not prepared for how little we would use the material on the syllabus. Instead, we mostly had lengthy discussions about a few lecture materials, with a couple papers in between. I enjoyed Professor Ashutosh's lecture style, but be ready to speak up - it matters! He has a lot of great insights and a lot to learn from.

Everyone should take this class! Current events and some "underground" ideas were integrated into the course which was awesome. There are no exams in this course which is a plus. Also, there are a few papers but if you attend/pay attention in class you should be fine.

While I enjoyed learning about the various topics in G314, I would say that the professor is what made me dislike the course. The prof. would be rude to students if they were uncomfortable participating in class or if he didn't feel like they were paying enough attention. Some of the lectures also felt unnecessary and were very discussion heavy.

Professor Ashutosh was an amazing professor. Very accommodating, thought-provoking lectures, and clearly knew what he was talking about but was always interested in students' input. Would definitely take him again and recommend this course to anyone.

Place and Politics is the best class Ive taken. There is never a dull moment and I learn something interesting every day. Absolutely fantastic man, clearly loves what he does and cares about what we have to say. 10/10 absolutely recommend

Enjoyable class and professor! Ashutosh is a pretty funny and relatable guy and you can tell he's passionate about urban geography. Concepts can be tough to follow sometimes but the subject matter is usually really interesting. I can definitely say I left this class with a new, different perspective on cities. I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS COURSE!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Very caring professor who really wants to see students succeed. He can definitely tell when students stop doing the readings/slack off and gets annoyed, but is still understanding. Some of the lectures felt purposeless but others were super super enlightening it's a weird split. I wish the textbook was used a little more

Professor Ashutosh is the best professor at IU. His classes challenge you to think deeply and critically about what you are reading. He allows you to shape the class around the interests of the students. He leaves you think long after you leave the class and inspires you to be a revolutionary. I will always recommend taking his classes to anyone!

I took this class because I thought it looked somewhat interesting and I needed the credit. It might be my favorite class I have taken at IU (I am currently a senior). Without fail, every time I go to this class I'm hit with heavy, philosophical questions that leave me confused and challenged for hours after I leave the class. What more can I want?

Professor Ashutosh is one of the best professors I have had at IU. His urban geography course was engaging and challenging. He gave great feedback on papers and held us accountable for the work we did through the semester. I would highly recommend him for anyone who is looking to learn a lot and challenge themselves.

Great Professor, I didn't even think I would care about the class (I needed credits). He is funny, smart, and made me think about life. His lectures are often based on our feedback and our questions. He's also a sharp dresser.

Professor Ashutosh is excellent. He is constantly challenging your perspectives of society and geography as a field. His courses in Urban Geography and Advanced Urban Geography are discussion-heavy. Read the many materials and come ready with your own perspective.

I am a pre-med student who has taken some very difficult 300 and 400-level classes here at IU, and I would take ANY of them again over this class. Amena doesn't know what she wants. By taking an online speech class I thought it would be easier, I was totally wrong. Her grading policy is very strict and all over the place, and her assignments and directions are not clear. For a 155 level class, it is extremely difficult.

When she calls on you to ask your opinion or an example, she shuts you down and just gives her idea instead. If you take this class, do it with anyone but her.

One of the worst experiences I have had with any professor. She was unbelievably strict with her grading and acted like the students should be professionals when it comes to giving a speech. Inconsiderate to students effort and time. Constantly contradicting herself. Does not understand the material she is teaching. Managed to complicate concepts that I had a clear understanding of when watching the lecture individually.

reviews.comment: I just graduated, and looking back he was probably the most enjoyable professor I had at IU! If you like history, this is the class for you! Easy class, but study guides are lowk pointless (i.e. "have to know xyz..." it's just EVERYTHING we went over, like duh). Lectures and, discussions esp., are also pointless...he's super passionate abt. F101, but holy ramble---disorganized too. Final proj. is a TON of points, but he gives us ample time to complete. Not a bad class, just boringgg.

There are two really easy tests. Participation matters. You do have to go to the classes and discussions. There are readings for each of the discussions but you don't really have to do them each week but catch up for the test. There's no study guide provided. There's some extra credit. The professor gets really pressed about technology in class.

He is super passionate about Folklore and wants all students to be the same. 2 tests which are easy and there are study guides and a project at the end which is alot of points but rly easy. Attendence is mandatory and he does monitory technoogy use in class which can get annoying, but its only 50 minutes so its not that bad. Super approachable+nice

I actually enjoyed this class. He truly cares about the teaching and the material. Show up to class and study the study guides for the tests. The course does take some outside time of studying and doing an interview(s). Overall, good though.

Very funny professor. Tests are easy as long as you do the study guides. Prof. Barker is really passionate about folklore so lectures are engaging and fascinating. Lots of reading but nothing to complain about. My discussion section TA was the BEST. Easy A class, would recommend.

Dr. Barker genuinely cares about all of his students so much, the course content can be difficult but he explains it all clearly and ensures that the content is accesible. You do have to read a lot but its a 300 level folklore class so that's expected. All grading is fair, and Dr. Barker provides helpful individual and feedback on assignments.

Great professor. He's very enthusiastic and made the class genuinely interesting to learn. There are discussions you meet up with every week, but they're easy and the TA's are nice and helpful. Only thing is he monitors electronics heavy, but it's literally a 50 minute class so it's not hard to stay off your phone.

Dr. Barker is really passionate about his subject, but he doesn't realize that most students are just taking this class for an A&H credit. He is worried about monitoring technology and stops each lecture multiple times to call students out to pay attention. Class is so easy and all you need to do to pass is study the study guide, but he's annoying.
Lecture was good but discussion is kinda useless

Dr. Barker is VERY passionate about folklore and he's very silly. He's genuinely a very nice guy and wants people to succeed. As long as you do the study guides for the tests you'll do well on them. Go to the last two discussion sections for 20 extra points on your final project. He is very crazy about attendance tho lol

very passionate about folklore. the things he covers in class are what he will put on the exams so as long as you review the material before the exams you will be fine. Final project sounds like a fun project that won't be too diffucult as long as you put some time into it. I highly recommend Dr.Barker he is by far one of my favorite professors.

Great professor, so passionate that it makes you interested in what he's talking about. Tests were harder than we thought, they grade the write out questions kinda strict. Still easy.

Professor Barker is extremely knowledgeable and well-spoken about Folklore and the best part of this class was his lectures as they were so interesting to listen to.
