Professor Barker was a super fun lecturer, I looked forward to going to lectures all the time. The coursework was interesting and fun, the tests were never too hard. There were some pop quizzes, but you could guess when they would happen. However, pick a GOOD TA to do your discussion with. Loved the lectures, not so much the discussions.

I took F368 in Spring 2020 and it was one of my favorite classes so far. I thought Dr. Barker was great. There was a lot of reading, but its manageable. Weekly quizzes were always on Wednesday, covering Wednesdays readings, so occasionally you could get away with skipping Monday. I was the only freshman in the class and I got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You could tell how much passion he had when giving lectures. He was also super helpful in producing in class discussion. I was worried that I wouldn't be interested in most of the stuff in this class but he made me see the importance of certain parts of Southern culture and I found myself every interested!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor and super knowledgeable in his field, incorporates a lot of his own research and personal interests into his lectures like the children's folklore and folk in southern Louisiana which was super interesting. Definitely not an easy A like I heard, but not impossible either- make sure to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although Prof. Barker was very nice, funny, and created interesting courses I do want to warn future students about this course. It is very reading intensive for a 100 level course, and attendance is mandatory. The method of taking attendance is to turn up 15 min early for lecture and physically sign into a 250 person class. Ridiculous.

Professor Barker is a funny and intriguing dude, the lecture usually goes by pretty quickly. The class is alright, a lot of reading but that mainly it beside one project which involved interviewing people. As long as you keep up with the semi-long reading on a weekly basis, you will do fine on the pop quizzes, tests and get in A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Barker is an awesome teacher, very funny and personable. The class on the other hand is very challenging for a 100 level class. I loved Barker but did not like my AI, gives hard quizzes and is not the friendliest. A lot of reading every week, but if you read thoroughly you should do somewhat well on the quizzes every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: At first, I really liked professor Barker but as the class went on I liked him less and less. His lectures become boring and most of the material is useless. The quizzes are difficult and the readings are dry. Also, he is not very good at answering emails and when you go to his office hours he will be rude to you. Would not recommend him or F-101.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Anyone that doesn't think this class is an easy A is just flat out lazy. Professor Barker has very entertaining lectures and overall is just a really great guide. All you have to is attend lecture and keep up with reading, which is pretty interesting and easy to comprehend. Do those two simple things and you will pass this class with flying colors
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Barker is a nice guy, and his lectures are interesting. However, F101 was wildly challenging for a 100 level gen ed. Quizzes every discussion over 50 pages of reading and the questions are crazy specific. Very difficult to get an A. Lectures aren't bad, AI's and quizzes/reading ruined folklore for me forever lol
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Barker was a really good lecturer but the quizzes in the discussion sessions were very difficult. If you just need to take a gen ed credit then I would not recommend this course because it can be challenging, but if you're interested definitely take it. Not the easy A that everyone says it is. May depended on discussion AI though.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Barker made this class a lot of fun and he was very engaging. One fieldwork paper was pretty easy and exams were a bit extensive, but other than that highly recommend!

Dr. Barker was a great lecturer and made all the topics relatable and interesting. He was able to create a comfortable environment even in a 200 person class. If you do the reading. the weekly quizzes in discussion are pretty easy. The midterm and final are straight from the study guide he makes, so overall it's a pretty easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The quizzes are difficult but the Dr. Barker is a fantastic lecturer and has an awesome vocabulary. AI discussion section is boring. Tests are not difficult and you get a great deal of points for showing up. Overall, great lectures with less than stellar discussions and assignments
I had a terrible AI so the class was not enjoyable. A lot of work and difficult pop quizzes with no direction on what to study for them. Avoid this class.

Dr. Barker is a sweet guy. He is very passionate about folklore and takes his class to heart. That said he wasted a lot of time in class talking about things off topic, and the mid-term project felt rushed and unexplained. He only gave us a few vague guidelines and graded easy but left a lot of stress. Would recommend for your critical app class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Barker made the lectures interesting because he clearly cares about folklore. There are quizzes in discussion every week, but as long as you do the reading from the textbook you're good. There is mandatory attendance that isn't very strict. (you should go to class anyway) Two "pop" quizzes in lecture, but he tells you when you'll have them. Easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Everyone says this is an easy class, but it requires a lot more work than what an easy 100 level class should consist of. The midterm and final exam both consisted of almost all writing portions with very few multiple choice. He will tell you that the test is half and half but it is certainly not. Would not recommend this class for an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great class and great Professor, there are some quizzes but as long as you read the title and some of the paper you can get a good grade. Also he tells you when you have the quiz.
The class is really easy and you learn about a lot of interesting things. Barker is a cool dude too.

F101 is a easy class that requires a small amount of reading. You can definitely tell that Barker cares about what he teaches and is very enthusiastic. Do the extra credit and small amount of weekly reading and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I really liked his lectures. Honestly, if you go to class and do the review sheet before the exams you should be able to pull out an A.

Dr. Barker is very passionate about the topics that he teaches. The class is fairly easy. There is a quiz over the reading almost every week, but he is a fairly easy grader and the questions are not all that hard. There is a final presentation for the class though.

His classes are interesting and he is a very nice guy. The course load really isn't that difficult.. All you have to do is read a chapter every week and study a little to get an A on the quizzes. Always pay attention during lectures because he does give an occasional pop quiz.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Okay so let me start by saying this really isn't as easy of a class as I thought it would be. Folklore 101 how hard could it be? Actually kind of hard. Attendance is mandatory for both discussion and lecture (if you miss more than what you're allowed 15 points is automatically deducted from your grade which is a killer). Also, he gives pop quizzes

Textbook needed to passing quizzes. Pop quizzes in lecture. Sometimes contradicts the book so you don't know what to answer on the quizzes/tests. Difficult to meet with if your classes conflict with his office hours. Lectures really boring.

Dr. Barker really knows how to make his class interesting. He has random pop quizzes so its in your best interest to go to class, usually about 20-30 pages of reading a week which you get quizzed over in discussion. I recommend Dom as your AI if possible, funny and makes material easy to understand.

Barker's class is interesting. We have no tests. Lots of projects, but they're pretty darn easy and not super time consuming. Quizzes over readings, but they're easy, and he warns you in advance. Plus he's super hot. Like woah. (You won't have a problem with attendance, because you don't want to miss an opportunity to look at him.)

Barker is an excellent professor. He lectures over interesting material and is very straight forward. I had no clue what Folklore consisted of prior to taking this class and I found it pretty interesting.

Interesting class and Barker's is a good lecturer. Very clear and straightforward about expectations. However, he always takes attendance at lectures and there are weekly quizzes in sections. And he's oddly strict about phones/laptops. He's also ridiculously good looking with a cute accent.
Very interesting class with a great teacher.  Easy A
Professor Barker is a very straight forward professor. Lectures are actually kind of interesting and the course is extremely easy. Recommend Myc as your AI.

Avoid this professor. For a business class, her lack of professionalism is concerning. She struggles to maintain her emotions when speaking with students and is extremely preachy, often centering the lecture on herself rather than student examples. Communication is poor, and the workload is not justified. Look for a more balanced instructor.
Most chill professor at IU, always keeps it 100% honest. Just do the work in class, show up, and do ur homework and you're getting a B+ or higher guaranteed. Anyone saying otherwise is trippin
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Beranova is a very passionate and amazing person. Would highly recommend taking her for compass.

Such a cool professor, very smart and in to what she teaches. She wants you to do well and is knowledgable, she also makes the class interesting. Grading can be tougher sometimes with smaller details, but overall an easy class.

I took this class with her because of her good ratings. She's a good person and inspirational but SO boring. I don't think a single person in class was actually listening to her. Picture it as a study hall from high school basically. Extremally light class but dreaded going bc so boring.
Go to class and participate; you will get an A.
Although the class had a lot of busy work, she is so sweet and caring. Feedback was very direct and clear and her instructions were super clear and easy to follow.
I mean, compass is never going to be a very hard class, and she dosen't make it hard, so that's all you need.

Compass is a pretty easy class regardless of your teacher. She had some long lectures but the information she instructed was helpful. Very resourceful if you speak to her outside of class regarding professional stuff (interviews, applications, etc.)

she is nice and cares enough in the class makes it very clear to not contact outside though, just show that you care in class make sure you get feedback for assignments and make sure you get full scores on the quizzes and you will get an A
Great professor, and very knowledgeable. I would 100% retake the class.
very very artificial; do not take her! lots of other professors that are better than her that teach Compass! grades harshly for no reason.
Probably the best compass professor. Doesn't give too much work, assignments are chill, and she cares about teaching students in class.
She is a very good professor and cares about her students. Compass isn't a challenging class to begin with, but she makes it easier.
Great Professor! The class is very easy just do your homework and you'll have an A.
Just show up to class & do your assignemnts and you''ll get an A.
such an easy class and she actually cares
Pretty easy class.

Really nice professor, she always makes conversation during class. Professor Beranova seems to truly care about her students. The only downside I would say is that she does make you write an excessive amount for some assignments. The class is pretty easy, but towards the end, she adds a couple of assignments that are definitely writing-heavy.

This is the most inspirational professor I've ever had. She is extremely approachable as a person, and the class is an easy A as long as you follow the rubric and attend class. She also has had a very accomplished career before her time at IU Kelley, which all started with an education at Wharton.

Professor Beranova was a fine lecturer and had strong experience. She seemed very qualified to teach the class and made it as engaging as it could be. She was very personable and could connect with you if you participated frequently. It was a dull and easy class for me. She canceled class a few times. Compass is Compass.

She is super nice and caring, sometimes her lectures are boring but its only once a week and she cancelled class a couple of times. I think you will learn a lot from this class, I would definitely recommend her, she really cares about her students and wants them all to succeed!

All Professor Beranova wants is for you to succeed. Her assignments genuinely help you build your conversation skills and spends a lot reflecting on yourself. I heard other compass teachers are easier, but her assignments are useful! Great class and simple work if you complete it according to the instructions.

Great professor! She is a super nice professor and is really to approach. Only wants you to succeed and all you need to do is complete the assignments properly. Directions are pretty clear, and give extra credit if you go above and beyond. I heard there is a little more work than other compass teachers, but it's not that bad at all.
Great professor and easy A if you show up to class and dont miss assignments.
Professor Beranova was very kind, and the Kelley Compass was quite easy. However, I found her lectures to be airy, roundabout, and boring.

She is a kind teacher, I just personally don't like her a lot. She assigns more work than other Compass sections, but it is not a difficult. She has 3 major assignments, which she grade harder than others. Taking the class with her is not a bad decision, it might just feel like a waste of an hour.

Professor Beranova is unwilling to work with students. She also provides very little feedback, leaving students to figure everything out on their own. Other professors that teach Kelley Compass assign much less work, and are much more flexible/pleasant.

She is a very kind person. However, she is sometimes strict about small details of assignments, and can be a harder grader than other professors I have heard about. Pay very close attention to the rubric and you will be fine.

Professor Beranova was awesome, she switches back and forth from being all business to cracking jokes with the class. She is fantastic at her job and is really kind. Her class is very calm and shes always there to help

Professor Beranova is a very accomplished professor who knows what she is talking about. The assignments are very straightforward and towards the end of the course you take the quizzes in classes. The LinkedIn assignment can take forever for some people so start early. Also, she is not lenient on late work.

The class is easy as long as you turn in everything on time and pay attention to the rubric. If you respond with a thorough answer on quizzes/assignments, she often gives extra credit. She also gives good feedback if you ask why you missed points.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: As long as you go to class and turn in everything in on time it's an easy A. She is a very interactive and helpful professor.

Very clear that Prof Beranova is very passionate about business and extremely intelligent. She cares about her students and wants to see them succeed in the business world. Gave very clear rubrics for even the easiest assignments. Gives extra credit if you do what she asks.

I think that she is the best compass professor. If you show up to class and do the work on time, you will do fine. She doesn't give any extra credit though, which can be annoying. She is a tough grader at some points, so make sure to have her check your projects before you turn them in, and she will give u critiques that will get you an A.

Professor Beranova was fine. The class she taught was perhaps the easiest one at Kelley, and she was clearly trying to make it a bit more interesting. Graded pretty easily, so long as you put in any effort. That said, she spoke in this really high-minded way, and tried to make the lessons about herself. Again, it was fine, but I wouldn't say great.

Professor Baranova is by far one of my favorite professors that I have had at IU. You can tell that she cares deeply about what she talks about and gives good tips based on her past business experiences.

I had Beranova for Compass 1, and she was an amazing professor. She helps you understand what your person brand is and helps you learn how to talk to people in the business world. She uses real life examples from her life experiences in business, and is inspiring. It is a fairly easy class, just make sure to write long paragraphs when she asks.

While the class is ridiculously easy and all test answers can be googled or CTRL + F'd, she is so obnoxious as a person and I hate being in her classroom. She wants us to write 1 thing we learn in class each day, which is fine, except for that she needs us to write it in a very specific "blue book" that can only be bought from one place. So dumb.
He is one of the nicest professors. Tests are hard, but class is great other wise. Take him!

Class is not hard if you actually do the readings and take good notes. Exams are a bit harder than I expected but nothing to stress over. Getting good team members is essential to the group project unless you want to do the entire thing on your own. Dawson will not be much help with bad team members
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof Dawson is great! He's very accessible by email, knows his material, and cares about his students doing well. Definitely take notes in class and remember material from activities.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Dawson is the nicest guy I've ever taken at IU. The class isn't bad at all, tests are exactly what he covers in lectures, literally no suprises. I think he is a pretty fair grader, nothing is really up to opinion it is all based on the textbook. It isn't very assignment heavy either. Take him if you can ദ്ദി˙ ᴗ ˙ )
Best B252 professor. He is insanely straightforward with exams and hw. Just go to class (its for credit) and pay attention and you will be completely fine. I recommend!!!!

Great Professor considering the class is pretty boring. He is a very caring and understandable guy who wants to help students. Although the lectures are boring and hard to pay attention to, he did a good job making the exams straightforward and good reflections of the content. Overall, I would recommend for B252.

JB is a nice professor, but his class and lectures are super boring. I would suggest going to the CL Sessions, which are extra credit, for additional insight/practice questions. For the final, I would suggest studying the two past exams, as that makes up the bulk of the exam. Overall, his class isn't that much work, but very boring.
Barnette's exams pretty straightforward. Attendance required (tophat). a little easier than the other B252 profs, but Econ is a pretty easy class anyhow

Overall, one of my favorite professors to date, which is impressive considering he taught in a 250 person lecture hall. He teaches an overall boring course, but does a good job of keeping students engaged. Homework is free points and exams are easily sudyable given the slides and homework quizzes.

I think Barnette is really nice and does a good job of giving quiz materials and slides. I did bad because of issues that were my fault. I also thought his exams were not that hard. My grades were bad but again not his fault. Considering they are lecture hall classes he is very available for help.

Teaches a required class that no one is passionate about and will never let you forget that he teaches 700 students a semester. Overall, class is not bad but he overly weights exams that are realistically pretty hard to do well on. One of very few non-Kelley taught classes that should be.
Hes a good professor just very boring. Content is not difficult, go to CL sessions which will boost your GPA a lot

Professor Bernatt teaches exceptionally well. He skillfully uses concrete examples to explain the rationale behind complex formulas in the course, enabling students to deeply absorb knowledge and facilitating understanding. Additionally, he covers many extra useful topics in class, helping us broaden our understanding of macroeconomics.

This class's content was easier for me than 251. I took both AP Micro/Macro in high school, so about 40% of the class was review. Professor Barnette got through a lot of content in a small amount of time. He provides current examples in his lectures, which adds some spice. The lectures are boring, but he does provide nuance and a lot of examples.

Pretty straightforward class. Barnette likes what he teaches and explains it pretty well but its boring and every class is just a long lecture with tophats throughout. Don't worry about the textbook. Quizzes and past tests are the best things to study

He is so boring, I swear I've fallen alseep sm times in class. This is also a peak self-study course, I did not learn anything from lecture. The CL sessions are a must though. Try to take a better prof!

JB gets unnecessary hate in some of these reviews. He's a good no-nonsense teacher. His lectures are boring, but it's Macro, no lectures would be entertaining. The material is self-explanatory, if you do the practice questions and go to CL you will do well. He explains concepts well, posts slides, and this class wont take up too much of your time.

JB is a great macro professor. Exam 1 and the final are basically copied from the quizzes. Exam 2 is the most difficult, make sure to understand the graphs for this exam. Go to the CL sessions cause it's free points. JB provides a ton of practice problems, and if you can do those, you'll be just fine for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This guy is the gold standard of college professors. He loves his profession, and its clear he tries to share that magic with his students. Tests are very manageable if you read the textbook, and overall a really great guy. Really brings energy into the room.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: The other reviews about this teacher rambling during lectures are correct; he means well, but only half the lecture time is actually spent going over new material—the other half is spent talking about administrative items pertaining to class, or going off on a lengthy tangent about a subject vaguely related to the daily material.
Do not take this professor
Professor Barnette does not care about the wellbeing of his students
Professor Barnette is an average Economics professor. However, if you need accommodations don't expect them to be met without grade penalties.

He is great in teaching, making concepts clear, values students and always help them to be successful in the course. The hack to ace the class is to keep showing up and make notes. Exams are relatively easy if you have gone to the class.

Is NOT Accessible outside of class I once had to send him 7+ emails for a question. and still got no response. Test is very different than practice questions, much harder. I always got a 100 on the quizzes but B's on the tests. Also gives no extra practice problem help outside of CL sessions and quizzes, and lectures are SOOO boring!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Barnette is a good professor, and explains things pretty well. Econ is a hard class, and that was reflected in exams. He lets you use a notecard on each one though which is really nice. Sometimes rambles but is pretty funny

Prof Barnette does a great job of explaining everything, he's super passionate about topics in economy. I was able to ask him questions through email which was helpful - very responsive. 

Tips to do well: go to class, take notes, go to CL sessions, study with a group of friends, stay on top of all the assignments

Very boring Professor who goes on and on about  the GDP, unemployment and Federal Reserve. CL sessions are good as they are run by PhD students who explain things better. Very little application during the class. The exams are confusing.

Barnette is 100% the best Econ professor I've had between this class, B251, and high school econ. He's super nice and does his best to make the content engaging. The 2nd exam is much tougher than the 1st, so study hard for that, and in general, for a better grade, be on top of Packbacks, Quizzes, and GO TO CL SESSIONS - it's literally free points!!

Very good professor. The lecture can be a bit boring at times, but if you go to his office hours, he's very helpful. 1st & 3rd exam average is about 86%, but 2nd exam average is 73%, so make sure you study harder for the second exam. Packback assignments are very annoying and this is honestly the only thing I disliked about this class.

Justin is so sweet!  He genuinely cares about his class and students -- the second test is hardest, but you HAVE to go to class during middle of the semester (I missed a week and it took me double to catch up before the exam).  At the end of semester, he gives a big curve if you fill out the OCQ, heads up

Great professor who makes this class easier than all the difficult sophomore year classes you are required to take. Exams are copy & paste from the quizzes and you are allowed a notecard for them. If you get 100% on the quizzes and packbacks, attend all CL sessions and write a good notecard for each exam, you should get an A or B in his class.
All love for JB! He brings such passion and love for economics. It is truly inspirational and motivates me to attend his lectures. Highly recommend.

As a senior taking B252 I've seen a lot of awful profs. Prof Barnette wasn't one of them. He's passionate abt the topic and keeps lectures moderately engaging. So what he takes attendance before and after class? Go to class lol ur in college. You might learn a bit about our economy. Easy A if you pay attention, take notes & cram before exams

Very nice and funny guy who tries to make class as engaging as possible. Provides a lot of extra credit through CL sessions and extra tophat points + allows a notecard for tests. Exam 2 is supposed to be difficult but Exam 1 and the final are easier so don't be discouraged. Just show up to class, do the practice quizzes, & attend CL's

Justin Barnette is kind and has jokes during lectures. His class (not himself) is awful. I have never fallen asleep in class until this class. Every day GDP this GDP that, the exams are hard even though you get a notecard for it. I left exams 1 and 2 thinking I did well only to realize it would be a miracle to get a B in the course.

This dude absolutely blows. Sets up his classes with a bunch of top hats that drain a ton of points. He takes attendance twice a f-ing day, assigns a bunch of bs quizzes, and I lost at least 3 years off my life listening to his lectures. Take this class with someone else. I think he tries his best but he is my least favorite teacher I have atm.

Absolutely loved B252 with Professor Barnette! Lot of people complain about his lectures but I loved them. Thought he did a great job explaining concepts and he's funny! Super sweet guy & a very fair professor. Go to class and CL sessions, take quizzes together and you'll be fine. If you took AP macro in high school, it's similar.

Professor Barnette is one of my favorites that I have had at IU. His course is more difficult than B251 but with the same workload. In order to keep that A, I recommend taking notes weekly, collaborating on Canvas quizzes, and attending CL sessions. The rest can be saved by a notecard on each exam. Overall, an enthusiastic yet caring Econ lecturer
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Barnette is super caring, allows a note card on the exams, gave us plenty of extra credit on top of CL. His lecture is kind of boring. Most people say the second exam is hard is because the were many graph problems. But if you draw them out and read over the textbook you will be just fine. Take him!

professor Barnette is the best choice for B252. His lectures are boring, and the second test is absolutely brutal. However, if you go to the CL sessions and study the homework then you will be fine in his course. The exams are copy and paste from the homework. Overall, he is a good teacher and would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy but struggles explaining some of the material to large classes. About 3/4 of the grade is the 3 exams. First one: majority exact quiz questions. Second: pretty bad. Third/Final: Easy. The quizzes are much harder than B251 ones. I got a 70 on the 2nd exam so that's why I have an A-. About 15 EC from CL possible. Rarely curves.

One of the best choices for B252 from what I've seen. Lectures are very comprehensive and cover content very well. Exam 2's easily the most difficult of the 3. Canvas Quizzes are also tough but a lot of those questions appear on exams as well so study those. Allows note cards on exams too which is really helpful.

Professor Barnette is one of the best lecture professors I have had. He is very passionate and takes the time to explain things. Office hours are helpful. The only reason I did not get an a is because I was not prepared for the second of three exams which is difficult. Participation matters and the weekly quizzes add up in your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While the content in this class is not easy, Professor Barnette makes it the easiest to learn out of all the other 252 professors. He has great energy and is a very smart professor. If you pay attention in class, you'll do just fine. Quizzes are not the easiest, but almost identical to the tests, so study them up.

The lectures were boring, hard to follow, and included very little information actually tested. Quizzes were given once a week and were also on information not taught. In order to do okay on the quizzes, you need to read the textbook and to do well on the exams you need to do well on the quizzes.
Good teacher would take again.

Intelligent guy who loves what he teaches. His lectures may come across as boring at first, but give him a chance and you'll find he's quite funny. Weekly canvas quizzes are difficult, as they don't always match what is explicitly covered in class, but exams are almost identical. Generous extra credit. A good choice, ignore those who say otherwise.

Dr. Justin clearly knows his stuff, and has a passion for it. Unfortunately, that doesn't translate to his teaching. He doesn't know how to give a lecture, he'll spend 20 minutes on a topic that could be covered in a sentence, and for every informative statement, there are three sentences of gibberish. He's a good guy, but not a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His weekly canvas quizzes get a little more difficult after exam 1 but he gives plenty of opportunities for you to ask him about the questions and retake the quiz once. The exams are exactly like canvas quizzes and extremely straightforward. Somewhat complex material in the middle half but otherwise he gives extra credit. Just don't fall behind.

Very nice guy and very funny/ entertaining during lecture, but exams and quizzes are EXTREMELY DIFFICULT even with notes, slides from class, and the textbook. He acknowledges that we are all doing poorly and then blames us instead of reevaluating his questions. He does not teach the basics and then asks very complicated questions.

This is his first year so maybe it will get better, but this semester has been a wreck. Class is very poorly structured with assignments on 3 different platforms. Quizzes are nearly impossible due to the fact many questions can not be answered with the book, his notes, or within class. Very very bad class.
Boring lectures with a rigid attendance policy. Lecture provides little help on any class assignments. Exams are poorly constructed and difficult.

Professor Barnette is my favorite teacher at Indiana. He explains concepts clearly and passionately in a subject that is tough to grasp. His astounding humor goes unrecognized by students who fail to give him the attention he deserves. Come to class and take good notes. You'll do fine.

Professor Barnette is an awesome guy and very charismatic. He is always available to help his students and gives everyone the correct resources to succeed in his class. He gives weekly quizzes that are tough but other than that he prepares you very well for every single exam.

Had very high hopes for this teacher as he was new and had good reviews from his last college, but these fell through. His quiz questions are extremely hard as no examples are done in class or can be found in the book. Do not recommend.

Amazing professor! I do not like econ but he made it bearable. Lectures make sense and tests are straightforward if you complete the weekly canvas quizzes. He actually cares about his students understanding the concepts and wants them to succeed in his class.
Great professor, always willing to help and is very understanding.
I took his compass class. Not hard. Boring. Good dude overall I would take.

Grading criteria gets muddy & class is sometimes a little boring, overall good guy & ok professor.

Professor Brothers was a great teacher. Always talked to me after class if I had questions and even gave me advice on how to succeed in other courses. His lectures are kind of boring, but if you look like you're paying attention, you'll get the easy participation grade. Very easy grader and gives room for mistakes. Overall, I would take him again
i took him for business presentations - his lectures are confusing and the rubrics are even more confusing, but overall you can tell he cares about his students. good person, ok professor.
One of the best professors I've ever had the pleasure of learning from. Class can be challenging but the information and experiences you will have after make it worth it!

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable and extremely intelligent- being fluent in both Hungarian and English is no easy feat. Always willing to take questions and has some interesting stories. Be prepared for class and have questions over the reading materials. Readings were provided over Canvas.

Extremely knowledgeable on the course subject matter and is able to have very in-depth conversations with you. A great guy, however, lectures almost the entire time every single class and is a pretty tough grader so you can't treat this as a blow off class.
Professor Borhi is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is incredibly knowledgable on the material and encourages participation of his students. Great teacher, but not easy.

This class is extremely difficult so make sure you allocate time in your schedule to study a lot. Betty's exams are what gives her a low rating because they're very difficult, but she wants everyone to succeed and makes time to see students who need help. She is always willing to go through your exam and fix your study habits to help!
Betty has a great attitude and lights up the room. Her class is difficult, but she explains the lessons in simple, easy-to-understand terms.

A311 is a weed-out class, so it will be hard regardless of Prof. Although it is mostly a self-study, going to class is very useful and she explains things very methodically, which I enjoyed. Plus, you get to drop one exam out of 4. Her humor is also dry, and shes super sweet!

This course is super hard, put in the work you will do fine. She heavily curved and there is no assignments except the in-class top hats, one project, and the three exams. She gives you optional final to replace an exam. Focus on the in-class problems, textbook hw problems, and the slides to study. Easy extra credit opportunities too!!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: tough class/step up from A304; exam problems - TB problems, practice exams and TopHats so know those cold. The first unit is easy but don't that let that fool you with the exam. Get used to how she writes the exam for the 1st one; then you'll know what to expect. Overall class is work heavy; be ready to spend 8-10 hours outside class per week.
Practice exams are pretty similar to the exams. Overall grade is curved by a lot.

This is class is known to be hard, but she does a good job of explaining things. She will only present off the slides because that is the information she will put on the exam, and she always prepares practice problems at the end of each presentation to ensure we are learning the concept. Just pay attention in class and attend office hours when lost

This is a notoriously challenging class, but I felt like Betty did a good job of breaking down and explaining the content, along with providing sample problems and practice problems. A-311 is a tough class, but Professor Liu does a good job explaining concepts in class during lectures. If you go to each class, take notes, do the homework review, ask professor for clarification and study hard, you'll be ok.

reviews.comment: Such a gem!  The class is hard (just in general, no matter who you take) -- she knows her stuff through and through (her dry humor always got me lol), generous curves on exams (which are 20 MC questions, there are 3 total).  Tophat attendance with several drops; she has the best distributions out of any A311 teacher!
ggez freelo

her dry humor cracks me up, gave out extra credit if you made an accounting meme. just be prepared to use a lot of slides to study for exams. otherwise, the class isn't hard, just lots of information to digest.

New professor at IU, young and relatable, funny memes on slides and she talks about video games.

While I agree with the other reviewers that the lecture slides are dense and there are a lot of them, I think they are full of useful information and everything on exams can be found on slides. 

She's very available outside of class for feedback.

- Go to class and you'll be fine
- Group project is super easy

Do not recommend prof Liu. Worst prof at Kelley. The lectures were so boring and unhelpful to learning. Test averages were all Ds and she refused to curve. Take any other professor. She gives the hardest exams.

Unfortunately all professors for F303 do not seem the best so best of luck

She is the least engaging professor I've had in my time in Kelley. Her lectures make zero sense, and the whole course is unorganized. I would highly recommend taking any other professor, or taking this class a different semester.

Cyndi was genuinely the worst professor I have ever had. Seriously, if you take her, you are going to spend the whole semester teaching this pretty difficult content to yourself.
By far the worst teacher I have had during my entire education at this school.

The simplest way to put it is, if you can wait another semester to take F303, do it. If you have to take this class this semester, just don't go to class and do the practice tests. I have never felt less motivated to put effort into a course than this class. Practice tests are the same as the tests, pretty much, though.

Worst professor at IU, doesn't know how to keep students engaged at all. Half the time, she's mumbling on about something that no one understands. Slides are a mess. Extremely vague for everything. Doesn't release course grades, and frankly, you're graded on 4-5 things, and 3 of them are exams. No idea how she is still employed. Avoid at all costs.

Overall, as others have mentioned, she's not good at explaining the material. You will need to teach yourself. That said, I disagree that her practice exams aren't helpful. I've compared them with other classes and hers are far more robust than most other F303 professors. If you really study the practice exam inside and out, you will do ok.
Worst professor I have ever taken. She should get her teaching license revoked.

I have also never reviewed a professor but avoid her at all costs. She is a smart woman but she does not know how to teach properly. The practice problems are nothing like the exam and she does not teach you anything in class. It is better to just not go to class.
Never wrote a review for a professor on this site until right now. Potentially the worst teacher/lecturer I've had through 4 years in kelley. Extremely confusing, nonsensical, unclear etc.
Most disorganized professor. No one in class understands a thing she is trying to say. She refuses to answer a single question clearly. NEVER TAKE!
Straight up awful.

She is a smart woman and she knows her stuff. She may have the credentials on paper and past work experiences, but that doesnt mean she can teach. The entire semester I had to teach myself the material. Slides=disorganized, lectures=confusing.Ive never had a teacher who consistently answers students Qs by asking them the same Q which confused them

Do not take this class with Hou. Lectures do not help you. You have to go through every set of slides yourself and teach yourself everything before the exams to maybe get an 80%. Class itself is tough but Hou made it harder than it needed to be.

reviews.comment:
F303 is hard, but Prof Hou makes it easy to understand. She does not grade attendance, but you must go to class if you want to do well on the exams. Group project is hard, but you have all semester to do it with a group. Basically a free 20%. 

Slides are well organized and she posts lots of practice problems.

Prof Hou is great. Out of all the F303 professors, I would highly recommend her. She uses real world examples to help explain the theory and math. Lots of practice problems that are very similar to the exams. Attendance is not required, but F303 is really hard, so go to class or you will fail.

Do not take her class. If you ask a question about something you don't understand, she makes you even more confused. The final project is unnecessary and makes no sense. Class sucks overall but with her its even worse.

Does not prepare students for the tests. Lectures are decent, but she does not provide enough practice problems to prepare students for the tests. The final project is also decently difficult and vaguely guided.

reviews.comment: 100% the worst professor Ive ever had at IU. Very easy to get lost in her poor lectures, and asking for an explanation provides almost no clarity.  Variables are used for the multiple meanings making it is so hard to follow. Wouldn't tell my worst enemy to take her. While the class is undeniably hard on its own, she will only make it harder on you.

This teacher is the most biased person I have ever learned from. She has a whole section lecturing about learning where the author and their biases are from, but is the most liberal teacher ever and the book is so far-left it is unbelievable. I am not saying I am not open to left-sided views but she is very condescending towards different views.
This woman cannot be objective if her life depended on it. Everything is her bias and inability to convey facts over opinions. 0/10 would never take again.

Lectures can be dry, but the class content is interesting. Professor Barbour has an unconventional teaching style that may not work for everyone. Use unstuck AI and the textbook to supplement the material - that combo really helped me do well.

I think the other reviews are misleading when they say her bias is *left leaning. She is a partisan Democrat, and frames class discussion with her perspective as the only reasonable framework. Her perspective seems stuck in the politics of the '90s, so she pushes back, and is even condescending, to pro-Trump or pro-Bernie arguments.

Her lectures are long and heavy. Tends to get off topic very easily and is hard to follow along since she gets all over the place. She claims to be "non-biased", however the majority of the readings or articles she assigns are extremly left-leaning. She means well, but if your looking for a non-biased teacher she is definitely not it. Iritating!

This rating is for POLS-Y300, the class for students in DC. Loves the sound of her voice. Nobody wants to be there. Has yet to learn how Canvas works. Her husband came to guest lecture, and she treats him quite badly. Chastises students when they follow her instructions. The program itself, you should do. The class, don't waste your energy.

This class had overall good information. However recorded lectures were dense and did not provide much information about the subject. Textbook had many tangents. Key words were all that helped. 

Textbook is also re-written often and new version *must* be purchased.

(i took for dual credit, so not entirely accurate to taking her class at iub) Wasn't too bad. Prof Barbour is extremely opinionated, and is very *very* left leaning. If you figure out what exactly she wants on tests, (and her personal values), just regurgitate it. Lectures are long and rambly. Practice tests are your best friend. IDs are confusing.

reviews.comment: She is amazing. I took her class as dual credit with my high school, so we watched her lecture videos. Her lectures were amazing and I watched them several times over just because they were so good. The biggest plus, she's non-biased with politics, and won't sway left or right with things.
Not my favorite.

reviews.comment: She tended to ramble on a lot which made lectures really hard to pay attention to. Go to lectures to see which current events you will be tested over and read the book to learn about the other content. Definitely take the practice multiple choice she gives you for each test!
She rumbles through political anecdotes from an extremely liberal point of view, no substantive discussion of the subject or political issues. I feel like I learned nothing by attending this class.

5 tests, over vocab and MC questions that are all found in quizzes she posts to canvas that dont affect your grade. Take the quizzes, learn the vocab and its political significance and you will easily get a B in this class. You can literally not attend a single class all semester other than the tests and do well.

reviews.comment: Definitely don't take this professor if you get the chance. She's a very rude professor and if you don't agree with her, she degrades you. You're only graded by tests and she makes the whole class stay on exam day until the class is over. Tests are pretty easy they're just over vocab and quizzes exactly from canvas. attendance isn't mandatory.

It took me a Couple weeks to understand her style but once I did I realized the class wasnt just about history and current events but it was to help you learn how to think. Professor Barbour definityexpresses her opinions but I felt like she made then understandable even if I didnt always agree. I Felt like a learned a lot actually.
Worst class at iu. SUPER bias!!!! Goes on rampages all class. Will NEVER take her class again

Barbour is great - pay attention to definitions and you will go far! Realistic comments on current political events that some conservative students have a hard time with, but definitely worth the class in spite of the general student body from IN!
Great teacher.
Barbour is an amazing professor. She is very liberal, but the tests are very easy and her lectures are amazing.
Most opinion based class I have taken at IU. Not only does she force her extreme bias on you, she lectures and references a Politics textbook that she wrote herself...
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Barbour was without a doubt the worst professor I have had in college. Constantly unorganized, forgetful about showing up to class, and a shrewd attitude almost every day upon showing up for class. Especially for younger students, I would recommend taking another professor for this course. You will learn more and do better in their class.

She's not too bad but makes this 100 level class a bit more than it should be. It's based on nothing but exams which she grades you hard on (the vocab questions- will make or break grade on exam). I got all questions right except some of ID's (Vocab & their significance) and received a D on the exam. The ID's are worth too many pts in my opinion..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Barbour is by far the worst professor. reviews.comment: Don't take this class. Professor Barbour is extremely rude to her students. She clearly states that she hates it when students email her. The tests are over at least 100 different definitions. She spends most of the class bashing the current republican party, and involving her personal views with class lectures.

She is the rudest and meanest professor I have ever had. She belittles her students when they answer wrong and calls out individual people in her class for talking in a lecture hall of 500 people. The lectures are irrelevant, don't bother going to class. Take the online quizzes, memorize vocab, and you'll get an A. All in all, she's just plain rude
I loved having Professor Barbour and she was very easy and fun to talk to outside of class.

Barbour is one of the worst teachers I've had in college. she is very entitled to her opinion (very liberal) and regardless of what questions you ask she will just refer you to the book that she wrote. i had to study a lot for her tests due to her hard grading and the amount of terms on each test. do yourself a favor and find another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Probably one of the meanest teachers I have. Teaches from her own opinion by the book that she wrote herself. Goes off on tangents that are not at all relevant to the class. Can be very rude to students and unkind if you disagree with her own opinion. Would not take with her again.

She has ridiculous rules for our class. Despite our usage of an online textbook, online quizzes, and online notes, we are not allowed to use laptops in class. She also forces every student to stay in the room after finishing our tests, which is insanely boring. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I personally liked her but she would go off on tangents that put the class behind schedule. To make up for this she would shorten lectures or skip whole chapters. This wasnt so bad though because the class is basically AP Gov in college. She also has movies that you can watch and answer easy questions for EC on every test. These can be very helpful

reviews.comment: Tests are mostly multiple choice and vocabulary in which you have to give political significance. Lectures are very boring and she often goes off on tangents. Reading the book is highly recommended although it mostly contains filler information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is the author of the textbook and LOVES to use it. She gives you quizzes that have the answers to her multiple choice sections of the test. Class is based on 5 tests, with EC from an optional lecture. Her grading is very specific on exams. She is very biased and will let you know her views. Class attendance not required, but it helps
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Barbour is a Political Scientist. She is so knowledgable not only on Poly Sci, but U.S. history. Her lectures are very fluid and she will make this topic very interesting, if only you mentally and emotionally buy into the lectures. 100% do the readings. Get involved. Broaden your horizons.

If you take this class and you want to pass just make sure you go to the extra credit classes the regular classes aren't nearly as important. Also if anyone asks about a term from the book during the extra credit class write down what she says in your notes because that will most likely be on the test. That's mostly all I did and I got an A.

I never went to class because her lectures are pointless.  Go to her extra credit classes (brought my grade up from a B plus to an A minus) and study the terms!! If you read over the chapters and memorize the terms, the tests are easy.  Go to office hours too, I got points back on my test for arguing my point to my TA.
Very mean. Tests are meant to be hard. Study the vocabulary. Don't ever dare to email her, or she will be very rude in her response. Worst professor of my semester. 0/10 recommend taking her class.

This class is 2.5 hours long, and it is only so because the professor loves to hear herself talk. It's not necessary. Hard to pay attention if politics are not for you. Get the book if you expect to pass.
This class is easy if you study the terms in the book. That's about all you have to do along with listening in class.

Professor Barbour is very passionate about what she teaches... almost too passionate. She wrote the textbook and holds it very dear, however, it is lengthy and not very  enjoyable to read.   If you are used to professors who give relevant lectures and post slides with useful information, look for another professor.

She preaches no "gotcha questions" on exams and that they are pretty straight forward. This is a lie. Very subjective grading. If you don't think like her you won't pass.  Often rambles during lectures. The AI I had for the class was more helpful than her.  Much of the material she will not cover, but it will still be on the exam.
She offers many opportunities to discuss terms and provide help. She is eloquent and a great lecturer.
Worst professor that I have ever had. Drop this professor.

In order to do well on her tests you have to read her book. Also, there are so many terms to study! I about went crazy trying to look at them before tests. She offers extra credit movies, however, that can really change your grade.
I really like Prof Barbour. She really knows what she is talking about! I thought the class was very relevent to what is currently happening in American Politics. It was an interesting class.

Class is pointless and this comes from someone who takes good notes, because tests are mainly vocab. In order to get full points I had to state the definition exactly as stated in the book. This proves to be difficult when there are 100 vocab words. Tests were extremely subjective. One test was an A- and another a D, studied the same both times

Horrible teacher. Spends most of the lecture ranting about useless information that will not be covered on the exam. Oh yeah and she wrote the book so good luck asking her any specifics about the exams because she will just refer you to it. Test are subjectively grade, since half of the exam relies on what she believes "the" political significance

I was actually surprised to see Barbour had such a low rating online. She is extremely passionate about what she teaches and makes you interested as well. She is very liberal though. Attendance is not required except for discussions and overall a pretty easy class. Only one complaint- the written identification on the exams is pretty subjective.

Great professor! really gained my interest in politics. because of this class i have changed my major and gained a much better interest in this field. she is super clear and tests fairly on the material you read in the book which is also pretty entertaining. offers extra credit and study sessions.

This woman way over complicates standard material.  Her test are, which are 80% of the grade, are half multiple choice about minute info from the textbook (that she wrote) and the other half is "ID" which are the 60+ vocab words that you have to give a definition more in depth than given in the book, and the political significance based on her bias

The class was fairly easy if you know anything about American politics in general. Class attendance isn't recorded and isn't necessary for most. She knows her viewpoint very well, but also makes some pretty partisan statements in class and the book she co-authored is quite liberal leaning.

This is an introductory course. Some students struggled because they weren't used to doing a lot of work, but the lectures were interesting and if you studied the textbook and made flashcards for the Identifications and Significance of them it was very manageable. Make sure you watch the EC movies. Helps a lot.
She is fantastic!

Really loves talking about politics, which are rather boring for me. Her lectures were well done/clear, but you really need to read the book closely to stay on top in this class. The tests were multiple choice and identification of key terms, and contained questions of "which is MORE right".  Overall, not the worst professor but not the best
It's a fairly easy class if you just do the reading.  I thought she was a decent professor.  Just your typical liberal professor.  The book was pretty interesting, but she just struck me as average.

She is a great teacher and the textbook for the class, which she co-wrote, is one of the best textbooks I have ever read. It is informative and actually interesting. She doesn't get to cover all of the material in lecture though, so keeping up with reading is important, and sometimes it ends up being a chapter or two a week, so don't fall behind!
Great professor, interesting class, easy if you read and study, helpful teacher, engaging, intriguing and very helpful! Love her1

Textbook is used frequently because she herself wrote the book. Book is somewhat repetitive, but informative. Excellent lecturer, and an excellent interpreter of current events. Tests are reasonable, sometimes her current events questions are extremely obscure or specific though.
All you have to do is literally memorize the book and you will get an A. The problem is that you have to literally memorize the book.
Tends to get off topic and tangents when talking about current events. Yet still teaches well, and is good at explaining things.
Most pointless class of my life. Sometimes, the discussions weren't even about food. I don't understand how the projects evaluated how we knew anything.

I agree with some of the other people who said the people who gave bad reviews had to have been incredibly lazy. The tests were based on the books and the lectures. If you don't go to class and don't do the readings, then don't expect to do well in her class.
Pretty cool class not that hard. She is very concise. But she takes attendance, normally the class isn't very hard.

Found her to be a very lazy teacher.  We relied heavily on the books assigned, but if you'd already read any of them, the course was virtually point less.  We mostly watched youtube videos and discussed, which I found rather annoying.  Easy class to get an A in, but not worth the money or your time.

In order to do well in the class, you must read every chapter. There are a ton of questions from the books as well as current events and classes. If you study, read, and pay attention, you will do well. She has a very liberal view on politics which can be annoying. But she is very well informed.

It's not a class for non-majors, but it's not difficult if you have a basis of information on the topic before you go in. She wrote the textbook, so you have to read, but it's written at the level of a high school government book, so it's not difficult. I pulled a 98 percent. Definitely not impossible.

Everyone rating her are clearly lazy asses who don't know how to read a textbook. If you even showed up to half the lectures or less, yet still read the book, you could easily get a C or higher on the tests. reviews.comment: Dr. Choksy is one of the best professors I've had at IU. His lectures are super detailed, but he includes pictures of archaeological artifacts as a nice addition. Really a great professor and person overall. The class was not hard but I learned a lot from it. You can tell he is extremely knowledgable and cares about what he is teaching. He was always willing to give great feedback and never hesitated to help out when asked. I wish I could've taken more classes from him.
You will be challenged to be your best student-self.

You can tell from the lectures that not only does Professor Choksy have limitless knowledge about Iran, but has a passion for the history and culture. This made the lectures, which easily could have been dry, much more fun. He was very helpful when I needed input on my papers. Great professor, would take another class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Choksy is wonderful! Very smart and knows his field very well. The pictures from his field were a good addition. He is so interested in students and genuinely wants you to do well. I am glad that he is on my PhD advisory committee.
Great teacher. He made the subject really interesting. He is clearly brilliant and loves his work. Professor Choksy really focuses on student learning. Plus he is super hot too!!!
Vigorous, intellectually demanding, gifted, helpful instructor who knows everything about the Persian language, literature and culture.
Outstanding, brilliant professor.

I enjoyed this class, but it covered so much history I don't remember many specifics. It gave me a good background to learn more about specific topics through the papers. You will write a lot - at least 20 pages even if not taken as IW. Prof. Choksy was nice and approachable and very helpful with recommending and lending books for papers.
Awesome class and professor
No Comments
I took this class for a topics course and it was so awful I dropped it after not even two days. He had us buy a $50 book from his dept that can't be returned or resold.
No Comments

This class is about analyzing earnings reports, but lectures stayed at a surface level, making little of what we learned applicable in practice. The practice exams were the only real study material, yet they covered concepts never taught and didn't reflect the actual exams. Grading by percentile also hurt strong students in more competitive classes

There's in-class assignments everyday which are really annoying and kinda stressful. The exams are pretty similar to the practice exams, but still difficult. There's no final, just a group project that wasn't bad. Overall he's a nice guy and tries to make jokes and real world connections in class because A310 is just boring in general.

Not as bad as others make him out to be. Exams are relatively similar to practice exams and he does a decent job of making the lectures interactive. That said, the group project turn around was a bit quick and annoying with all the other group projects after Thanksgiving, and he made a lot of mistakes in his questions. Not awful but could be better

1 group project, attendance quizzes, and 2 exams but the content is definitely dry like others mentioned. He's humor doesn't land but he tries his best and the exams really aren't that bad. He gives a practice exam, which most of the questions come from. People are overly harsh here when if you do the practice test you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This dude is legit the worst teacher I have ever had in any class dating back to my time in elementary school. He makes lectures ungodly boring with his uncomfortable sense of humor and total lack of understanding of his students. He makes class absolutely impossible to attend and worth absolutely nothing could not recommend this Prof less.

Let me start by saying that accounting is a dry course. However, Professor Volant makes the course very bearable. This course takes what you learn in A-304 and adds many more nuances. If you did well in A-304, you will do well in this class. The Professor uses great real-world examples to bring the class to life. I would highly recommend.

Let me put it this way. If I had the option of being awake while someone sawed off three of my limbs, I would do that as opposed to take this course again. Four however, I would take the course again. If you want to suffer more than you should for a 300 level accounting course this is it.

extremely low exam average seems focused on stressing students out rather than helping them learn. 
Would not take it again.
No
Insanely boring lectures but if you actually listen he is extremely intelligent and educated. If you're on his good side you will be fine grade wise.

He is very knowledgeable, but his lectures are not focused, and he talks a lot and goes on a lot of tangents. The books we read were interesting, but he does not post grades, assignments, or feedback on Canvas whatsoever. You will be confused about due dates and criteria. Participation is very important to him, so it's easy to get on his good side.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dov-Ber was a very kind professor and clearly passionate about what he was teaching, but it's true that he just rambles for 2 hours about mostly nonsense. Learning goals were confusing and lectures were tedious, didn't learn much from them and sat there for 2 hours. Very late grader, don't expect any grades until the class is about over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a truly among the worst professors of Indiana University. He sits in front of you for two and a half hours mumbles incoherent nonsense with nothing to do with the curriculum in an attempt to pad the class time. He is not open questions and refuses to provide feedback. He refused to give info over the final paper until 3 days before due. 0/10.

I took the online version of PSY 155 and thought it was okay. Very helpful to attend the optional lectures and his study guide can be important. This class tests how effective your studying is, sometimes hard to know what to study though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I like Dr. Kennedy, very fair grader, but he tends to drone on and on making concepts seem larger than they are. The hybrid concept was a challenging learning curve, it is very fast paced and tests on small details in reading and lectures. If planning to take this course, be prepared for lots of time spent! optional lectures were unhelpful
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This course is very dependent on reading, but as a Biology major taking this course, this is definitely one of the best teachers I have had. His grading is VERY fair. I did not pay much attention to the course the first few exams and was still able to maintain a good understanding and grade. He teaches hybrid, and does it well.

P155 is online and in person, but I never go in person for the lectures because he is a boring lecturer.   This class is veeeery homework heavy so if you're not willing to put in a lot of effort don't take this class. This class isn't for lazy people because it is very fast-paced.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had to drop this class because it was hybrid. The tests actually had nothing from the lecture videos.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Students come in expecting psychology and leave questioning their own life choices. You start out thinking you're in a course; two weeks later, you're reconsidering your major, your future, and maybe your sanity. It's like the class exists not to teach, but to test how long you can endure rambling disguised as wisdom.

Class was mainly made up of assignments that were no where related to the course modules.
He adds random questions in the tests which are no where related to anything in the syllabus.
DONT take this class thinking its online and for credit, has more assignments and tests than an in person class.

The class was asynchronous and I did not interact with the professor. Lectures were recorded and dragged on longer than needed. Definitely read the book and take notes from the book. A lot of lecture material skipped over a lot of book details. Exams are quite rigorous but doable if you put in extra work for each module.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: It seemed as if the exams had almost nothing to do with the readings or lectures. He got off topic with the lectures sometimes which added more time to the videos. This made me question my major and I would not take again.

Professor Kennedy's communication with the class was always informative, yet very kind and supportive. Your overall grade is determined mainly by 4 difficult exams. If you're willing to study hard or you consider yourself to be a good test-taker, this class may be for you. Taking notes over the material is a necessity!

Dan was friendly, and his lectures were okay. Unfortunately, grades are calculated as 90% from exams and 10% from homework. He stressed his generosity with extra credit, but you can only get a measly 3% bump at most. Exams were sometimes frustrating, and very few received A's. Dan rushed through some lecture topics that were on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not many students did well in this class. This class literally depended on lectures, but Dan often became distracted and couldn't even finish the lectures. However, still tested on the material. Questions didn't align with what we were taught. Went into office hours and the man genuinely gave me a pop quiz while I was in there!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A lot of people had troubles getting a good grade in the class, including myself

If you pay attention to lectures and read the material, you'll do well. The tests are always over exactly what you should know and study guides aren't provided. I suggest either taking notes when you read or making note cards. The final ended up not being cumulative, but keep notes just in case.

Only grades in the class are 3 tests.  There are 4 tests throughout the semester including the final.  He drops your lowest grade.  Tests are mainly based on lectures but also on the book.  Not hard to pass if you can memorize vocab definitions and what they mean.  He doesn't round grades, so don't ask, and he only cancelled class once.
Test are really book and class heavy

Mike is an incredible lecturer given the very bland material that I-Core Leadership covers. He is always energetic and fun, but when it comes to the tests many questions are often a toss-up. All the tests are standardized for I-Core, so it is not necessarily his fault. Very good speaker and makes the class as interesting as it can be.
Leadership is a pretty boring class, but DeShano made it as entertaining as he could and genuinely cared about how well everyone in the class did.

DeShano is a great prof. Talked with enthusiasm and class was engaging. Tests were harder than I thought as there were a lot of concepts but you have a notecard which helps a lot. Review class before exams are very helpful. Definitely recommend his class!

Professor DeShano is an awesome guy! He is constantly making me and other students feel welcome in his class. He does a great job of keeping the class engaging with stories from his family and his past experiences. As long as you stay focused and go to class, you will do great. Would highly reccomend taking any class with him.

He cares about the topics he teaches as well as his students, and is consistently looking for feedback to help the current cohort as well as future ones in terms of what students prefer for assignment formats and lecture topics.

Prof Deshano is a nice guy who clearly cares about the material - and because of that he gives a LOT of work on it. We had nearly 7 group projects, alongside 2 exams and another solo project. For the course content, this is wholly unnecessary. If you want to breeze through this class, I'd take it with another Professor.

Liked DeShano but J375 was a lot of work and took lots of time. Be prepared for lots of group project work along with exams and an individual project. The class is hybrid which is nice but in-class components and examples are used as exam questions. DeShano's a nice guy but the class wasn't my favorite.

DeShano does a great job of making the leadership lectures entertaining, which is a difficult task to achieve. You honestly don't need to go to class to pass the course but you should because he's got lots of real-world experience that he is always sharing and does a good job reviewing what will be on the tests.

Very very nice guy who is always looking for feedback and doing his best to enact it. He went out of his way to inform us on need-to-knows for recruiting season, intern life, etc., as he used to be a recruiter for big companies once. If you get the chance to enroll with him, I highly recommend it. You will learn a lot from him and he's very upbeat.

One of the best Profs I have had at IU. He showed up everyday and tried to make class engaging and enjoyable, even when the material wasn't very interesting. As long as you show up to most lectures, the HW, projects, and exams are all pretty easy. Would strongly recommend taking him for J-375, and any other class he teaches.

Really enjoyed his class. A very solid guy with good experience that takes time to make class as enjoyable and useful as possible. Usually not a big fan of strategy classes because they can be a bit formulaic, but Mike made me want to come to class and participate. My advice is be there consistently and you will do fine.

I think Dr. Patton was great! She was always available outside of class and would always explain everything, as well as keeping us routinely updated about what needed to get done and what was upcoming. I found the class to be rather difficult (though I am not the greatest student) but I do think it was quite rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take any class with this professor.  The only way you can act "right" with her is if you do everything completely aligned with what she wants, not being flexible or understanding at all. She thinks she is very skilled in this area, but all she does is ramble on; it is very hard to stay attentive. Worst professor I've had here at IU.
Great professor. Moderate workload. Curves exams and with possible extra credit.

The hybrid version of class typically has homework due M/W/F with in-person exams every other week.  The material is digestible and easy to understand. Has other assignments like experiment credit and Inscribe that can sneak up on you. Just actually pay attention to the work and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Don't take, crazy workload, no lectures, poor communication.

She's very nice, only reason I don't rate her amazing is because the amount of modules assigned each week are very time consuming. MC on exams I also found very hard at times. No attendance but go to class to learn the math for the exams! A lot of points given in this course that can help grade, lectures can be boring, overall meh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Tendency to ramble during lectures, pretty boring but very nice and understanding. Structure of class is very annoying, test heavy. More tedious than difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While the workload was considered a lot week by week, she taught us very well and made sure to make the classroom as interactive as possible to engage your mind. She was also very caring, and she made sure that we felt heard and understood when it came to our struggles. Exams were curved and there was extra credit. Overall amazing professor.

I had her for K300 and she was a great prof. Attendance was never taken by students greatly benefited from going to class. We did online canvas modules twice a week for homework and had 4 exams. I would definitely recommend if you need a stats course. She curved all of our exams.

Awful late-work policy, assigns entire modules of 8 assignments but only allows you to make up 3 of the *individual* assignments if you forget.  So much busywork and it does not even matter if you get the math right if your wording is not 100% as she wants it to be.  Take a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took this class 100% online asynchronous, so it is a bit different; however, her class setup is extraordinary and very much streamlined. She and her TAs answer very quickly and are very helpful if you ever need anything. Grading criteria is absolutely clear and she is very communicative / reminds you when important dates are.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really solid intro class, I appreciate how it was organized. When I did need help I got the answered I needed, so can't complain. I do recommend writing nice detailed and organized notes because the tests are all open book and there are a few tricky questions that can pop up, but overall I wouldn't worry about grades as long as you take good notes
Find a different professor. The tests are impossible.

Her lectures did not go over conceptual stuff that was needed for the exams and she assigned quizzes during the week that were honestly more helpful than her lectures but they weren't easy to pass.
