You have to put effort into understanding the material on your own or you won't pass. I recommend taking this class with another professor.

So much unnecessary busy work. If you take this class study guides and homework problems will be most helpful, but it's so tedious. Her lectures are so pointless, teaches the wrong material and has to backtrack, I was just more confused anytime I went to her lectures. You're better off just taking the course with a different professor if you can.

Dr. Patton shows zero compassion for her students, and assumes the worst in us, even when we reach out for help. She constantly makes mistakes during lectures, overcomplicates everything, and doesn't explain why we got things wrong on tests and assignments. Definitely find another K300 professor if possible.
She is a good professor, just not my vibe. She gives lots of busy work and focuses on things that aren't necessarily on the exams :/
So much unimportant busy work.

Canvas page was organized and everything was easy to find. Lecture quizzes were easy, material was interesting, quizzes weren't too bad. Just do the work and you'll be fine. She is always available to answer questions. Easy, interesting, and enjoyable class. Felt like busywork but was useful for the assignments.
This class was a lot of work, but the work was relatively simple. Be prepared for a lot of assignments in the asynchronous version of P101.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took this as the online psy-p 101. Although I liked not going to class, she made this class the most time consuming and annoying class I took this semester. There is typically about 7 hours of work a week, and you have 3 modules due in that week, which contained lots of reading and notetaking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this as a fun class and it is so hard. Do not expect this to be an easy class you will have so much work and she grades so hard. The tests are impossible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: I would not take this class with this professor again. I feel like I spent too long studying for a 100-level course. Questions are worded weirdly in tests, wouldn't really cover much in class, and random facts were also tested on the tests/quizzes, making it hard to know what to study for + a lot of studying necessary to be comfortable.

Dr. Patton's lectures are pretty boring and there are multiple assignments due typically 3 times a week. I actually liked the structure of the online modules, they taught me more than going to lectures did and there were really nice to use for exam review. I recommend for a basic psych class!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: There is a level of professional trust you should have between a student and teacher. I received an A on an assignment and she went back to lower my grade after she graded it. I made the changes (which were incredibly small) and she refused to raise my grade back up. The W was worth it to not have to put up with her.

For such a great class like the Psychology of Women, I was very disappointed in how this class was taught. I wish the class was more discussion based considering that mostly only women took the course and we all can relate to the material. Exams were "fair game" but usually never related to the study guide or what was taught in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Syllabus way too content heavy for how short the exams are, discussion not welcome. I feel like I taught myself the entire semester with the use of the textbook and homework assignments. My class times were on Tuesdays & Thursdays and she'd make homework due Mon & Wed. Kind of silly and lack of consideration.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I feel like this professor has gone above and beyond for me in terms of helping me understand the class. She's strict and a tough grader, true, but if you put your all into it, she helps you understand and get better. She might not be for everyone, but for those who try their hardest and really want to learn, she really shines.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Patton creates this class to be way harder than it needs to be. The weekly assignments are extremely long and time consuming. Exams are only 30 questions, which doesn't allow for much mistake. She does not except late/early work and never provides extra credit. Not very nice in general. Do not recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I've been at IU for 4 years and she is by far the worst prof I've ever had. She is super unorganized and never posts modules until Monday or Tuesday. Syllabus took like 3 weeks to be posted. Super rude and will ask questions to the class and tell everyone they're wrong. She also said misogynistic things while talking about misogyny...

Patton's transition onto online coursework (COVID) was the worst I have ever seen. Cynthia promised assignments would be posted early on Mondays and due on Fridays - however assignments were usually posted Tuesday afternoon or Wednesday night, and still due on Friday. The way she handled this class was unprofessional and she treated students unfair
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Sweetest lady ever. Although there is a LOT of work and time required for this class, as long as you complete the assignments, you will get an A in this class. I failed just about every exam, but still ended with an A because of all the assignments. The class was horrible (just like any stats)and lots of work, but worth it for the grade in the end.

one of the nicest professors I have ever had. attendance is mandatory or you wont pass the class. she was very understanding of outside circumstances when it came to assignments. she did her best to be politically correct and was very kind and considerate to all of her students. Would take any class with her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Patton is really understanding of student experiences and needs. Her "cushioning" is built into her syllabus, such as dropping the lowest 2 quiz scores and offering 3 late "tokens" to avoid a late-grade. As such, don't ask for further accommodations and make sure you understand the syllabus. Attendance is both mandatory and enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: The way she words her questions is so confusing. I had a few of my friends who had already taken stats look at the quizzes she was giving and we were all stumped at what she was asking in the questions. She doesn't tolerate students not understanding what she is asking. I reached out for help and she basically told me 'too bad'.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Patton's class was one of the most boring classes I have ever taken in my college career. Attendance in her excruciatingly slow lectures is unfortunately graded, so be sure to bring a coffee. Further, she assigns about 30 minutes of busywork homework for each lecture. Try to take with a different prof if possible, if only to keep your sanity.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I did not really like the class and I think she was one of the reasons for it.

She talked down to students often and was not helpful when you had questions. There were online quizzes every week, often twice a week. Her exams also contain "choose one OR MULTIPLE" answers.. Not super available outside of class time

Sweet lady but lectures are boring. Just reads off slides that she posts after, attendance is mandatory but there are ways to get around that (tophat from home). The textbook is online and there are quizzes that go along with it, time-consuming but not difficult. Just study and read and the exams are a breeze. Most quizzes are online (quizlet).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She explains statistics very well. Probably wouldnt have passed with a good grade under another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Unavailable to students & inconsiderate to situations that may be happening outside her class. Tests are the hardest psychology tests I've ever taken; with some being check all that apply & only 1 of them being the correct answer. Loves the sound of her own voice but makes no sense. Multiple chapters to read every night along with quizzes. 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: ALL OVER THE PLACE! This woman tries so hard to be organized but is incredibly far from it. Lectures are two weeks behind readings. TopHat/in class quiz questions do not have nearly enough time. To top it off, canvas assignments are very difficult to do well on. You will get a B in this class and you will like it. Wears very questionable shirts too
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If it weren't for the daily participation grades, there would be absolutely no reason to go to lecture. If you do the readings, you'll be fine. Lectures consist of her reading off of the slides (that are posted after class) and telling stories from her experience. Nice lady, interesting, good for a funny joke/story every so often.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Yikes. Avoid her at all costs for P199, although I think this may be the only instructor available for this course. Way too much work for a Pass/Fail, one credit course and lecture was extremely boring, I loathed going to it. Only plus side is she splits the class in half and you only have to go to class once every two weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her makeup assignments for my class were: Interview a professional and write 500 words about it, or a few different types of research papers w/ 1,000 words and 3 sources. This is by far one of the worst classes at IU. I forgot the first deadline and magically turned 3 teeny quizzes into 3 teeny quizzes and 3,000 words worth of essay with 9 sources.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Patton was awesome. She is such a sweet lady, gives great examples, and really knowledgable in her field. I will say, however, if you expect to take a first year psych class where you can barely show up or fail everything and still get an A, take Irene's class. Dr Patton's test are difficult, and there is a daily participation grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I PROMISE THIS CLASS IS NOT AS BAD AS SOME PEOPLE ON HERE SAY IT IS! Dr. Patton is amazing and I loved her. She made me want to minor in psych. Great teacher; she does a fantastic job at making sure we understand the material. You will get your moneys-worth for this class because she uses your TopHat code and the textbook frequently. Great lady.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Would take again

reviews.comment: Assignments are much too difficult and extensive for a pass/fail class. Her idea of makeup work is whole different assignments on top of the original, and sometimes deadlines do not matter because she can tell you it was not to her liking and make you redo it. Consists of a ton of busy work and her telling you things you likely already know.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I really like this professor, she explains things very well and takes her time teaching us. There is a lot of reading, but do it because it is very helpful!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I'm a senior and she is the worst professor I have ever had. She talks to you like you are stupid. If you take this class as anything other than a freshmen she makes you feel stupid and just wastes time. This is a required class that requires a new teacher. Hard grader for a 1 credit with so many long assignments that do not help. SHE NEEDS TO GO.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Absolutely way too much work for such an insignificant, 1 credit hour class. Class is mandatory, but the information she gives is such common sense. She provides some helpful links and websites in the first couple classes, but after that, the classes are pointless to attend. Assignments too detailed, the deadlines aren't clearly communicated

Did not say a single important thing the entire semester I took her class. Attendance was mandatory, so I showed up every single time, and every single time she wasted my time by talking extensively about ideas that are common sense. Ex: Transferable skills are important, having a degree in psychology doesn't mean you need a job in psych, etc.

This class was extremely unorganized and was difficult to follow at most times. Students were expected to know deadlines and understand what she wanted without her actually relaying the information to them. I often felt like I was being talked down to, and I never felt as though I could ask a question. If taking this as an elective, don't.

Says "Right??" after everything she says, is very rude and unhelpful when responding to emails, class is redundant and pointless unless you know literally nothing about the workforce, criteria for assignments are super ambiguous, unable to miss even one class/assignment, literally hated this class and would avoid the professor at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very unhelpful and rude when it comes to asking questions, even when were entirely her fault (i.e., she forgot to post the link to a video). The assignments are unnecessarily long and tedious, and feel like pointless busy work. Class is a waste of time, as she plays music and the programs she uses crash just about every single class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Overly complicated for a pass/fail class that is merely to help students development their future career skills. The professor was helpful overall but the amount of homework and bizarre rules regarding their submission made this class rather unbearable.

Dr. Patton was super nice but you get what you'd expect from a 1 credit hour required course, so it was boring. It was INCREDIBLY time consuming for a class graded pass/fail, and if you miss an assignment, you have to do that assignment plus another to pass for the one assignment. More time consuming than any 3 cr. hour class I took this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had so far in college. She almost failed me because of one assignment and then wouldn't tell me what I did wrong or how to fix it so I could pass. Pretentious about grammar, rarely checks emails, not at all helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Prof is great but her structure for this class is ridiculous. If you do an assignment wrong/turn it in late you have to redo it PLUS do another assignment usually a 2 page paper. She's knowledgeable and great, but the class is time consuming. Makes you buy a $70 clicker just for a few chat questions in class that she barely even looks at.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: For P199, since it's a pass/fail class, you have to receive all assignment credits and all attendance credits. Class is only ONCE EVERY OTHER WEEK. If you miss class or don't turn in an assignment, you can attend an event through the career center and just have someone sign a paper, and there are alternative assignments. The assignments are long.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This class was a huge eye-opener. I highly recommend taking it in your sophomore year, or freshman if you have a good idea of what you want to do with your professional life. Cynthia clearly knows her stuff and is a very good professor to have a rapport with, especially for references on grad school apps or RA apps. Don't be daunted by paper length

Professor Patton is excellent for PY155 if you're really looking to learn all of the basic concepts of psychology in a single semester. I thoroughly enjoyed her lectures. She wants you to pass! The course is easy to pass as long as you attend lectures and read/take notes over the textbook. As a neuroscience major, I highly recommend this class.

Instead of helping me through anxiety, she asked me to consider how the stress of the class was effecting the rest of my life. I made the mistake of getting flustered and dropping the class. I could have done it with a little support.
She sounds like she's crying when she talks. Wouldn't take a class with her again. For P199, need to attend 8 classes and complete 6 assignments. Super simple class. Pass/Fail grading.
Great professor, loved the class. She's very knowledgable.

This class has a lot of homework, but it's homework that helps you understand the material. Lectures are straight forward. There's no textbook, just a work book to take notes in. The quizzes are easy and the tests are exactly like the assignments. If you go to class and do the homework, you'll do well. One of the easiest stats classes at IU.

This class isn't very helpful if you already know what you want to do with your life but if you don't it should be helpful. A lot of busy work and many papers but none of them are hard, just very time consuming. I sat in class and watched Netflix and participated in clicker questions when needed. All work is pretty much done outside of class.

Professor Hoffman was great. You don't buy a textbook, you buy a ringed notebook from Mr. Copy that is basically a textbook with blanks and examples for you to fill in. She goes through it page by page. She signs A LOT of homework, but it honestly helps so much. She's a great professor and it's an easy A if you pay attention and try on homework.

Great stats teacher. She assigns a lot of homework and projects, but they all help with tests. Moves quickly and goes really in depth during class, but really works with you outside of class time if you need it. Challenging class, but teaches you a ton about stats in psych!! All helpful applicable concepts!

Makes you do a TON of work for a 1-credit class and you need a certain number of attendance credits to pass. Had to force myself to go to class because it was so annoying. She's a big fan of making you talk to your neighbors and calls you out if you don't. Sit in the back.

While the work load was pretty lengthy, she was very helpful. The class certainly gives you perspective on where you are or where you need to be. She is one of the nicest professors I have encountered.

The most annoying teacher I've ever had. Cannot stand her lectures but had to suffer through 10 of them. Had to write over 9000 words, or over 30 pages, just to pass this worthless 1 credit class. This took time away from my other five classes that count toward my GPA and actually MATTER. Don't buy textbook it is also worthless and you don't use it

The assignments are fairly long for a one credit class, just a warning.  However, some of the later papers are really helpful in getting research done in your field of interest, and aren't as bad as they seem at first.  Her lectures are quite boring, but you only need to attend 10 classes to pass.  I wouldn't bother buying the textbook.

work load is a lot for a one credit class but not hard to BS papers (honestly most people tried too hard on them and overreact; if you work hard on them fine, if you don't, you'll still pass). she is extremely good at what she does though and knows what she's talking about when it comes to preparation.

Awful!  Absolutely no flexibility.  Most annoying teacher I've ever had.  Work load is crazy and if you miss an assignment you have to do that assignment and an additional assignment to pass.  Absolutely ridiculous and unhelpful if you already have a plan for your future.  A proactive student would never need this class, especially with her.

It is very clear that she is well educated, and is passionate about teaching the topic. She keeps the class interesting, and uses an appropriate amount of student interaction for discussions. Being a psychology professor however, she was not at all helpful and compassionate when it came to my brief hospitalization, and did not help me one bit.
Fantastic! Made course easy to understand and applicable to degree program. Very helpful too!

Her lecture and book are informative, but she expects way too much from students. The last month of class has more work than essentially the rest of the semester. She's like that in every class I've taken with her. Exams are ambiguous and VERY difficult. Weekly packets & quizzes, a report, and 3 projects. I'd recommend taking a different professor.

I learned what I needed to know to prepare for my career just in time. Dr. Hoffman does make the class a lot of work, but if you have a pretty good idea what you want to do, the assignments are genuinely helpful in figuring out the specifics and how to prepare. If it had been easier, I wouldn't have learned as much.
Very intelligent and engaging teacher, but very difficult tests.

HORRIBLE! Take P199 from anyone else! This 1 credit pass/fail class had more writing than my English and Chemistry (lab reports) combined. I thought this class would be helpful in discovering my interests to decide on a career, but she wants you to know the career you will pursue by week 3.

Absolutely the worse professor to take this class with if you have any idea of what you want to do with your life.  She has a LOT of things to say, all of which could be summarized to about 2 classes.  Teaches as if she is teaching an elementary school class, but gives and UNBELIEVABLY large amount of work.

Found the class needlessly difficult for an intro course.  I never mind working hard in a class within my major but the tedious study guides, random assignments, and exams that consisted of word for word definitions made it seemed designed to be a weed-out class.That being said she knows her stuff and is a great lecturer, but be warned, tough class

Professor Hoffman is extremely knowledgeable about psychology and provides interesting lectures. She expects alot concerning reading and taking your own notes, and requires exact definitions on essay portions of exams, but she is completely willing to help you earn a top grade.

I'm sure it's a great class if you put a lot of effort into the assignments, but if you aren't willing to you would probably do better to take 199 from someone else.  You'll get the same stuff out of it and have to do a lot less work. Wrote more for this class than my 4-credit intensive writing course.

Really clear, loves what she teaches about, not the easiest class but you will learn a lot if you read and go to class and pay attention! Quizzes are kind of annoying because so low in points but you must put in a lot of effort.

She is an excellent teacher.Her lectures are clear and engaging, with time to ask ?s and repeat material. She has a passion for what she does, and she really cares about students doing well. About those who have given bad reviews- I'd be curious to see how often they study and visit office hours. Those who try in the class have no need to complain.
She is extremely boring. Her voice is soooo annoying. And she is inflexible. She is not the worst but certainly not the best one.

I thought she was great teacher. She's really passionate about what she's teaching. Go to class and read and it's fine. The only thing I hated was how many definitions we had to know word for word on tests. Overall a great class though.

First--she makes you purchase a packet for her class that she put together which is very hard to follow in class. She isn't clear when explaining material. This class should be very easy and she made it harder than it should be.

Helpful to my future career; annoying class but it did help. Must attend 8 classes throughout the semester and complete 6 (I think) assignments in order to pass, but as long as you do that its okay. Straightforward, and easy to complete but worthless since it doesn't actually count towards GPA.

At first she seems like a witch, but then you realize she just has a burning desire for her course and wanting you to learn it. If you read the assigned chapters and really study the reader, then you will pass. Class is nothing but memorization. Doesn't give extra credit. No hw. Fun and sorta easy but hafta keep up on reading and memorizing.
Great professor, the class can seem boring at times while other parts are exciting. It just matters what you're interested in. Exams are very difficult, so prepare a ton!

Her lecturing style is difficult to keep up with. You take notes using a packet she made up with blanks/ problems that you're supposed to fill in lecture, but she speeds through them and flips back and forth between pgs mid-problem. Homework is WAY too time consuming! Exam m.c. questions can be really ambiguous. Makes material harder than necessary

very helpful class and teacher. She really helps you plan out your future with all the guest speakers. I definitely learned a lot, but I admit this class is annoying. not because of anything she does wrong, but because the assignments can take a little while, but they are helpful.

Very nice and always willing to help/clarify.  The book she provides is great because you take your notes right in it.  Very helpful!  She makes you memorize definitions, but if you're willing to sit down the night before and just memorize them, you'll do fine.  It's worth it to have a prof who likes teaching and uses interesting examples, etc.

I've had her for 101, and 199.  Great professor.  Pay attention and she won't have to do that thing where she stands there not talking until everyone else does.  :)  I've heard she's really good at teaching stats too, which a requirement for me, so I'll be returning a third time I think!

Maybe if I wanted to spend an extraordinary amount of time learning statistics, this would of been a great class. But when all you want to do is fulfill a Statistics requirement- do not take this class. You will spend more time than you ever wanted to.

Dr. Hoffman is a good teacher. I tried to take Stats with Guth, but did not understand his teaching and was not learning anything. I actually learned a lot from Dr. Hoffman. She's hard - there's a lot of homework and you have to stay caught up for every class - but you'll actually learn statistics. I'm glad I took it with her.

Very good at teaching the material so that you learn and understand it.  Tests are pretty fair and not really any homework which makes tests very important.  Only knock on her is that she treats students like they are 12 yrs old.  Otherwise a solid class.

I love her!!! I had her for P155 and she was great in that too. She knows exactly what she's doing, and she makes sure that you're actually LEARNING the material. She cares about her students, and though she brings her political views into the classroom at times, it's interesting. I highly recommend her!

I had her for Psychology 101. She was a decent teacher, class wasn't hard at all. However, she sometimes brought her personal political views into the classroom at irrelevant times. She's a member of the PFC. Beware!
Extremely passionate teacher.  Makes this introductory class engaging and interesting.

This professor is amazing. She challenges you at just the right rate and level. She is very helpful, clear, and well organized. I hated statistics before her class. By the end of the semester, I was getting an A felt confident, and wanted to learn more.
She was an excellent professor. Very interesting lectures and always a lot of fun to talk to out of class. I would recommend her to anyone!
Does a great job of teaching and while making the subject suitably challenging.
Dr. Hoffman is an excellent professor I ever met. She can always use her unique methods to make hard knowledge easier to study. I really appreciate her!

I thought that she was easily one of my favorite professors from my freshmen year. She really made the effort to make the material as comprehensible as possible. Easy tests if you put in the effort to study all the material

Read the book and take the notes and you'll be fine. She's not out to make you fail, she actually wants you to succeed in her class. Her lectures are well organized and she keeps them fairly entertaining.
Easy A if you do the work.
tricky questions. boring lectures. but easy, very easy.

I love Dr. Hoffman! I had her for Stats which I never would have gotten the hang of if I had had another prof. It's a lot of work and she is much harder than other professors, but again, you really come out of the class knowing the information!!

Pretty good teacher, usually enthusiastic. For her quizes, just showing up to class and paying attention is enough. For tests, make sure you read the chapter! Overall, if you do that, tests are cookie-cutter - easy A.
Very caring and understanding. Overall tough, but fair.
I learned so much in this class. She prepared me SO well for upper level psychology classes.

She was an amazing professor. She did everything possible to teach the material as clear and concise as possible and she really was interested in helping students. She's also a really easy person to talk to. The work load and the level of difficulty is extremely fair.

Take her for stats! She teaches the class like high school, with homework due once a week, but it really helps learn stats. You need to keep practicing to get it. Her tests are straightforward and she explains everything very well.
No Comments
No Comments
He just yaps about random stuff and the tests are just worded terribly. He seems so genuine and excited to teach though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Davis is the better D270 prof, he rambles a lot though and his lectures can be boring but when he's actually teaching its important. Take notes during the lecture and study the cases from the textbook. Some test questions are on quizlet which helps. All other assignments besides tests are easy
Attend lectures and pay attention in class and you won't need to do readings. The assignments are very easy. The exams are not bad, find the Quizlets to help study.
Professor is pretty awful. Both exams are loaded directly onto quizlet if you know where to look. Don't even have to study or read the book as long as you attend the lecture you'll be fine.

the worst professor I've had at IU. He makes the exams so that you have to study literally everything. you have to: write down every word he says in class, read all 200 pages of the book, and watch every video he provides. 99% of the information you absorb won't be on the exam but you'll have to learn it anyways! his lectures are also very boring!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Davis was probably the worst prof I have ever had. He yaps for 75 min straight and then gives test questions that are so specific to things in the textbook. Would highly recommend staying away unless you are ready to buckle down and grind for 8 weeks. Only people that do well are if you read the entire 200 page textbook and grind this for hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Injects his democratic party ideals into class in a subtle enough way that he knows he would probably get away with it if any formal complaint were ever to be filed. Tests are HORRIBLE, take notes on everything he says beyond the slides because I promise, some random thing he said one time will absolutely be on an exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Does an ok job explaining topics, but tests are extremely difficult and oftentimes certain questions are borderline unfair. Homework is not crazy. Also makes it a point to subtly but clearly inject political viewpoints into every class.

Prof. Davis was a great lecturer but his lectures are so boring. Its hard to pay attention or even go to class for that matter. That being said, 80% of your grade is made up by 2 tests so if you fail one you are kinda screwed. The tests ask super specific questions from things he talks about in class and are kinda unfair tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Davis is interested in what he is teaching, that being said, his lectures can be fast-paced and dense. I often took 4-5 pages of notes per class. Although attendance isn't mandatory, If you don't go to class you won't do well on the tests. Use the quizlets online and read the textbook cases to study. Take him over the other profs for D270.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was alr, not the best but better than the other profs.

D-270 is going to be tough no matter who you have, lots of reading in an 8 week course, but Davis is by far the best of them. Extremely knowledgeable, great background, knows his stuff, and an all around kind and caring person. Attend lectures, both because LOTS of what is said in class is on the test, and because they are interesting.Overall 10/10
He's a nice guy and is passionate about the subject. The class in general is tough no matter who you take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are very interesting and engaging, and he is knowledgeable of the course material. The bulk of the grade in his class comes from a midterm and final exam, but if you read the textbook thoroughly and utilize Quizlet, it shouldn't be too bad at all. You will learn a lot in this class, and I recommend this professor for D270.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed his class. Davis's lectures are interesting, and he makes it worth coming to lecture. Make sure you thoroughly read the textbook to get an A. I recommend taking heavy notes/outlines by hand while reading to memorize everything. The majority of your grade is based on 2 exams, and the HW is a bit tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Davis is an "alright" professor. You can tell he's passionate about the stuff, but the lectures are rather lacking. Make sure to read, and re-read, the textbook. Will not lie, this class should be an easy A if you put in work and show up to class (I didn't, it was a 7:45AM). The two tests are 40% of your grade and questions and be ambiguous.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: TAKE D270 WITH DAVIS!! It is your best chance of getting an A. As long as you read the textbook, listen in class, and study a regular amount for tests you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class over the summer and Professor Davis is very energized during lectures and always gives the class a good vibe. Midterm and Final are 80% of your grade, so make sure you do all the reading assignments, study, and do well on them. The midterm was harder than the final IMO but every semester it's different. Pretty easy class overall
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Davis is a solid choice for D270 (there are no amazing options). He knows what he's talking about and it's clear he likes this stuff. D270 is reading-intense and there is no way to do well without reading & taking notes. Tests are open note but are timed at 1min per question, so you don't have time to look everything up from the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Davis is great. He's the easy choice for D270. Very clear expectations and requirements but make sure to study for the tests. Don't let open book/open note fool you.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Davis because he was very invested in what he was teaching. However, this class was a lot of reading and you need to pay attention to every detail in the lectures because he will ask questions about certain videos watched in class on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: With the COVID-19 situation causing the class to become online, Davis decided to make his tests 40 questions with a 40 minute time limit. Absolutely ridiculous. Some of the questions were a paragraph long with 6-7 answer choices. Test questions were also absurdly difficult and there was no practice available for them. Avoid him at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: D270 was one of the hardest classes I've taken at IU, but Davis is a pretty interesting guy. He has some great stories to tell, and the videos he shows in class are super helpful and really reinforce many important concepts. Definitely a lot of work, but an A isn't impossible to achieve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall, I do think Davis is a better option than other D270 professors. I actually found his lectures to be pretty interesting, as he bring a lot of real world international business experience. Despite this, exam questions were always far more difficult than his lectures theme of respect different cultures as you do business across the world

Professor Davis boasts quite the resume as far as international business is concerned. The one hour and fifteen minute classes are brutally boring and dry. He just displays text dense slides and literally reads them off the board. I found every lecture to be some sort of "you must know the culture before you move your business to a country."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Davis has a lot of industry experience and enjoys what he teaches. However, the class itself can be boring sometimes and his tests are weird. Just make sure you read before everyclass, pay attention to what he talked about, and do the extra credit because it can save your grade from one letter off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a decent professor. I'm really interested in Int'l Bus and I found myself getting excited for the lectures only to be mostly let down by the boring, common-sense material. One time he said that Norway was in the EU which kinda pissed me off, but everyone makes mistakes. There were a few other instances that needed to be fact-checked but o well

Attendance not mandatory, but lots of test questions come from lecture. He is a very passionate prof who knows a lot about the material he teaches. His tests are easier than Garcia's. The course is still moderately time intensive despite this. Probably a good idea to read the book and attend class even though you can succeed w/o it.

Davis has a ton of industry experience and really knows what he's talking about. As far as the global business classes go, his is by far the easiest. I didn't do any of the readings and just listened to the class and still managed to get high B's on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: He's really passionate about the material he teaches and he uses real examples to help explain stuff. There's just a lot of reading, but it is an 8-week course. Overall, pretty good professor. It was his first-semester teaching D270 tho and he messed up when making the exams. The midterm exam average was 90% and the final exam average was 70%.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Donaldson is straightforward in teaching style and assigning coursework, and I appreciate that assignments/readings tied directly into the professional world, which I've found helpful post-graduation. Readings and homework are regular but manageable. In-class group projects are common, so come to class ready to engage.
Hello! I highly advise not taking classes with Dr. Donaldson. His lectures are long, his assignments have little to do with course materials, and he is impossible to contact outside of class.

Two tips for getting the most out of Dr. Donaldson's courses: be prepared to engage and take him up on his willingness to help. He will help you to increase your level of professionalism and to develop new digital skills. Ask a lot of questions. Attend his office hours. He will help you to advance your career. I highly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Donaldson is an excellent professor and helps prepare students for an actual career in the field. While at first I found his syllabus daunting (especially the amount of reading per week), it is a) useful for me now as a professional, looking back at what to read, and b) essential for learning how to read a lot of content quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Devan really understands the subjects he teaches. Readings that are assigned in his classes, I feel, give you a good understanding about the kinds of discussions that you would have once you start working after graduation. He is also always available to answer questions inside and outside of class as well. I had a great time working with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took 3 of Devan's classes and would definitely recommend them! At first his lectures seem like a lot but he puts everything he talks about on slides that are available outside of class. He also provides all the readings for class so you don't need to buy anything, either. As long as you pay attention and do the work you should be good!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took ILS-Z604 Advanced Archives with Dr. Donaldson and found it both engaging and highly practical. Donaldson was passionate about teaching us what it means to be responsible archivists and I received many real-world skills I now use daily as a working archivist, such as digital preservation methods, CAS, advocacy, budgeting, and networking.

Devan was not the most helpful professor I've ever had. Classes were him reading the slides to the class, then assigning exercises that required little or no thought to complete. In contrast, the group project was difficult because of his high expectations and lack of preparation for us.

A sweet guy, but a bad grading system. Did not grade anything until end of semester, so I did not know how I was doing in the class until after finals. Would test over anecdotes about his career that did not teach me about the actual material. He is incredibly nice and knowledgeable, but I found it near impossible to get a good grade in his class.
Great dude
Really great lectures, enjoyable class. The tests were definitely difficult, but manageable.

He's very old so he goes off on tangents and gets disorganized a lot but he is very knowledgable and caring. I found his experience and stories very informative and interesting. You need to take notes on what he is saying (not just the slides) and mark "test questions waiting to happen" to get a good test grade.
He is super knowledgeable and hilarious however he is slightly disorganized and tends to go on random tangents during class.

I have him for PSY-P 303 health psych--pls do not take classes with him, as he is really disorganised and definitely getting too old to manage a class. He is obviously very knowledgable and he is entertaining, but he pretty much rambles the whole class, leaving exams to be really hard to study for and subjective.
Long lectures, lot of tangents, he's very experienced and passionate. Slides are helpful. Reading the textbook is imperitive
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he is very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. quiz/exam matter is heavily specific and covers both textbook and in class materials

I dont have much positive to say. He seems to care about the class and the students, but his lectures are rambles of random things not tested on. The lecture slides are not helpful and theres literally nothing but 4 exams that make up your entire grade. I ended up ok but most people  were not. There were no extra worksheets or lecture practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams are entirely based on lectures so if your not good at going through lecture slides to understand material you should go to class. He expects you to know the material like really know it which I think is fair. Great guy in fairness in dealing with tech problems and such. Knows the material well and cares about it.

Do not take this class. Has the worst micro grade distribution. Only graded based on exams. I ended with a C only because he had to switch the final. If this was your only class it wouldn't be bad but insanely lecture heavy. AND BORING He is a good guy who cares about what he is teaching. Just no grade buffer at all. STUDY for exams!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DBK is a great guy, funny, knows what he's talking about. However, he's very lecture-heavy, and they can be boring/extensive if micro isnt what you're interested in. No homework or attendance. 4 exams + 1 final (drops 1), so if you're a bad test taker, grade may reflect this. I never go to class, I just do optional worksheets & study before exams.

Would NOT take this professor. 4 exams drop 1 with a cumulative final. His AI grades INSANELY hard so no room for error. Reads off slides, exams are the tiniest details. Not engaging at all. Luckily attendance wasn't mandatory. Lowest grade distribution of all micro professors. Lowest grade I've ever received and never reflected the effort put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weekly homework is over main topics during lecture and exams are not too difficult
Grade is based on 4 tests, easy weekly worksheet, and final. He posts his lecture powerpoints on Canvas that cover everything so I only went to class for the 4 exams. Very straightforward class.

Genuinely a good guy. He usually moves too fast through slides to get everything written down but posts them after class with audio so not really a big deal. Cares about what he's teaching and has a great sense of humor. Loves to be asked questions. Tests make up your grade, but if you study will be just fine!

Graded on 4 exams, so make sure to study. He obviously loves microbiology and is always helpful if you go to office hours. Not super great lectures, but reading the book can help with that. Overall pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class only graded on 4 exams... thats it, nothing else.

Very boring class. Kearns moves too quickly through lecture slides and does not post them before class so you cannot even take notes during class. Going to class is a waste of time; just review the powerpoints later. He often cannot answer simple questions. Does not know a lot about biochem, even when it is simple things I have already learned.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. His course has influenced my path as a now prospective graduate student in microbiology. The lectures were fascinating and kept my attention--definitely go to class! It's worth it!

Dr. Kearns is an awesome professor, appears to have a very positive rapport around the school, and is quite easily one of my top 5 professors. He breaks tough concepts down into bite-sized metaphors and pictures.  He is very willing to help and answers every question I ask if it is within his ability.

Great professor. Very organized, entertaining, and engaging. He makes the topic extremely interesting and relatable to other fields. His exams are extremely fair and well written. I very highly rate this professor.

Amazing professor. His lectures are very clear and straightforward - if it's not on the slides, it's not on the exam. Easy trick to know what's important - if he bothered to put it in color, it's more important. Very helpful outside of class as well, and also actively seeks out students who might fit well in his lab as undergrad researchers.

A friend of mine told me he looks like an older Atticus Shaffer from "The Middle!" Lectures are not boring, although once he got into metabolics I lost most of my interest (not because of him, the material was boring). Tests are very straightforward, and don't be alarmed when I say his tests are part short answer! They're very simple, no tricks.

I had the privilege to have him in my PhD Committee. He is a super nice person, extremely knowledgeable, down to earth and very helpful to students. He is very sincere and dedicated to science and is a true mentor. I had the privilege to work with him in his lab. I have learnt a lot from him. He is my inspiration.

Absolutely phenomenal. I loved having him as a professor: He was clear when speaking, engaging, had both informative and interesting slides, and to top it off, the exams were easy. To go along with the lecture material, he gives examples of organisms that are special in regards to what we are learning about, which is quite helpful.

Dr. Kearns is awesome. He definitely is there to teach you instead of tricking you and is really reasonable with his grading.  I still remember most of the material and it really helps with other Microbiology classes.  He is extremely knowledgeable and if he doesn't have an answer to a question he will find out for you.

Hands down one of the best, if not the best, and most helpful professors I've ever had. If you don't go for the subject matter, you'll get a good lecture or laugh no matter what. He's extremely passionate about his job which makes it a contagious learning environment. DO NOT TAKE ANYONE ELSE BUT KEARNS!!
Great lecturer, takes time to answer questions, extremely knowledgeable. The class is fairly easy but interesting nonetheless.
My new favorite bio professor, fun to listen to and he always brings the topics back into perspective with the big picture... loved the class

Absolutely the best lecturer ever.  You will learn an unbelievable amount of information from his fantastic lecture slides (which are available on Oncourse, so attendance is optional).  The highest quality instructor and course I've taken in 2 years at IU.  Recommended for both an easy A and learning lots of useful microbiology.

Such a wonderful professor! Lots of reading and some tedious homework, but gives great feedback and has lots of real experience. She is very kind and will do her very best to help you succeed and tests are not too challenging if you study what she tells you to. Overall, a great class and great instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. S is the best professor on planet earth. She is so caring and very knowledgable about clinical science. She explains things so well and is very accessible outside of class. I took PY318 and PY483 with her, and absolutely loved both. Her classes are the kind where you get out of it what you put into it. I have learned SO MUCH from her!!
Dr. Schiestl is very knowledgeable about clinical psychology. She cares a lot about each of her students. I highly recommend her class.

Dr. Schiestl is one of the kindest professors out there. She cares about all of her students enough to learn their names on an individual basis, and is so flexible about meeting up to discuss anything. She always makes lectures interesting and is very clear about what you need to know for the exams. I seriously could not recommend her enough!
One of my favorite professors ever. She is willing to help with all subjects, not just clinical science. She is so kind and I definitely recommend taking her classes!!

Holzman was great. Very personable but knowledgeable at the same time. A311 is not the hardest class but it is not the easiest class either. His attendance policy is a little odd but as long as you study you should be fine. Do not be afraid to ask him for help as he is very accommodating as well. Great guy and great professor.

100% recommended. Wonderful slides and teaching style. As long as you review the slides and do the homework, it is quite easy to get an A for the course, His practice exam materials are super helpful.

Holzman is a great lecturer and his exams are very fair and similar to practice problems. There is suggested homework but it is not required. He does cold call for answers to the in class worksheets and uses that to determine your participation grade; however, he will not make fun of you or fault you for not knowing the answer. Very nice guy!

Eric is the best professor I have ever met at Kelley so far. His lectures are very detailed and interesting. His teaching mode is very organized, with timely uploading of required materials. His practical exam is very effective, with a high similarity to real exams, and the group projects are also simple with high ratings. Just choose him!

I think Prof. Holzman was fantastic. You have to be there since he cold calls for participation points (you don't even have to get question right, just attempt it). If you aren't there when he calls you, you'll miss 10 points from your grade. His practice exams & quizzes are very on par with actual exams, so study enough and you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really nice guy. Lectures were boring sometimes but does cold call for participation so you have to attend class. Tests are very similar to practice exams/in class problems so easy to study for. Grades pretty easily and weighs best test grade more. Group project is also very easy and simple to do. will help you understand the content if confused.

She's a good professor, mostly nice, and she explains things clearly. Quite a bit of homework and exams account for most of your grade, but you can retake each one once. The content wasn't too difficult but required practice and effort. Overall, the class was fine.
Great professor, works with you, has clear guidelines, a great teaching style, funny, nice, and overall great.  Pretty hw heavy, tests can be retaken once, huge lecture hall. Very manageable class

Annie is nice though her personality comes off passive agresssive. If you're good at math the class will be fine but if your not, like me, its not gonna be easy. The tests are weighted 26% each, there are three of them, they are multiple choice. Homework barley raises grades so you have to do good on the exams which she gives two attempts for each.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a great professor. She responds to emails quickly and gives you external resources to use. I do not like Finite and found it extremly difficult- tests are worth pretty much your entire grade (which is common for college math courses). Overall good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall rude, she likes her students and wants them to suceed but she is very passive-aggressive.
Edwards was amazing for finite- her lectures even if you didn't attend them were easy to follow and if you put in the effort you can do well in the class.

wonderful professor, always passionate about helping students figure out their problems and care much about students' progress and achievement !!! I often asked her about some homework questions through e-mail and she was always there and answered the questions in detail, just trying to do her best to make me totally understand them.

Even though finite can be a very difficult class, she did everything possible to make it a good experience. Her lectures consist of guided note taking and example problems, and she did an amazing job explaining difficult concepts. Additionally, all of her notes are posted online.

Professor Edwards was great. I had heard that Finite was going to be difficult but she made it one of the easier classes I took. Lectures can be a bit long but she goes right to the point and gets the information across. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For finite, Mrs Edwards is who you want to have. Finite is not an easy subject, but she makes it bearable by her teaching style - she essentially take notes with you, allowing the student to copy down notes that are essential to understanding the subject. The in-class notes are posted online, so you don't have to make it to every class.

Very good lecturer with good problem selections in class that made it easy to learn the material. The tests she makes are also pretty easy if you study for them and are very inline with what she teaches in class.

Edwards is the teacher you want to take for Finite. She taught Finite as a high school teacher, so she makes everything really easy to understand. I took the 1 hour and 15 minute class and she is so entertaining it went by very quickly. This class is hard but she really wants you to succeed and make it so much easier to succeed.

Gareth obviously knows his stuff, and is nice in class. Grading is sort of vibes based, there are rubrics for papers but he still just assigned a grade at the end of things so it was hard to know how I stood, and getting one or two Bs on things sets you back in terms of getting an A. Still a good class and positive experience.

Subject matter was interesting. Dr. Evans is knowledgable and open to wherever the dicussion goes in class. Attendance "required' but he doesn't take it, so long as you usually show up you're fine. Only 4-5 grades but there are so many essay topics to choose from. Dr. Evans is quite moody and a tough grader. This class did get off topic a lot too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Knowledgeable about the topics taught in the course and covered in the novels assigned. If you enjoy reading, take the class. If you do not enjoy reading, do not take the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The subject matter for this class was so interesting. So long as you planned, the reading was manageable. I appreciated his letting the discussion flow as we brought in outside subject matter connections. He made me think. I'm pursuing a minor in Medical Humanities because of his class and how it changed my perspective on psychology and psychiatry.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Read the books, go to class, participate in discussions, pay attention to the feedback he gives you when you write, and go to office hours if you're struggling. If you do those things, I can basically guarantee you'll pass with an A or B. There is a LOT of reading, but all fiction, and mostly pretty enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Evans is pretty friendly and can definitely make class discussion more interesting. However, most of how discussion periods go depend on your class, so be sure to participate. He lets you read sample essays to get a feel for his grading and gave a good amount of feedback on my essays, even when I did well on them.

I was excited to take this class, but Professor Evans made it extremely boring. All we did was discuss readings (and get extremely off-topic) for an hour and 15 minutes twice a week. There are only five grades for the whole semester and they're all writing assignments, so if you don't like writing -- good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
If you give him your paper to look over, he will scrutinize every word and put vague suggestions on sections like, "be clearer" without truly explaining what he didn't understand. 
He loves discussing how he dislikes Trump and Boris Johnson. The novels he chooses are anti-American and it felt like an indoctrination of anti-American propaganda.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I honestly did not enjoy his class; everything is a discussion about some mediocre books for 1.25 hours. The only grades are 2 essays, so if you bomb them, you'll bomb the class. I thought this class would be an easy grade booster, but it honestly wasn't. I went to get help from him and he still did not give me a fair grade on my final essay. GL.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a pretty tough, but fair grader. He's very consistent with his grades and leaves very insightful feedback. You will get the grade you deserve, so if you read and participate and discussion expect an A. I highly recommend going to his office hours before you turn in your essays. Will vastly improve your writing. Great prof and great guy
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Evans is really knowledgable on his subject matter, so he has good insight into the literature he teaches. However, he's sometimes kind of dull, and his class requires a TON of reading (about 150 pages before each class). If you love to read, the class is great for you, but if reading Jane Austen isn't your thing it's tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Two essays make up most of the grade and participation pretty important. Very available to provide extra help and willing to connect with you personally
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: You have to take time and put effort into writing your essays but he gives back great feedback. Very interesting subject matter and grading description is followed exactly. You will get an A on any non-essay work you do as long as it is completed. I enjoyed his class.

I enjoyed the class a lot and learned a lot from the readings.  Prof. Evans is a cool guy who challenges his students to think in new ways. I recommend that you go to his office hours and talk to him about your essays; I found this helpful. A particularly good class for underclassmen, though I enjoyed it a lot as a junior.

Important warnings about this class: 1) it's a lot of reading 2) it WILL eat up your print quota 3) you will have to push yourself to get good grades on the essays.  Gareth is a tough but fair grader. I had to REALLY work for decent grades. He's a quiet, quirky guy with a dry sense of humour. I enjoyed getting to know him.

There aren''t any tests just some extended essays due throughout the year. There is a lot of reading and a lot of printing so if you''re worried about printer quota make sure to learn to print double sided.
Awesome Prof
Gareth is not very good at leading discussions, and his novel selections are incredibly odd and frustrating. I do not recommend his class.
He's a funny dude and grades kind of easy...love him. Such a bro
Gareth is an odd fellow with a dry sense of humor. Overall, I wasn't a huge fan of the class, but he's a pretty cool guy.
Loved this class and Prof Evans.

Really great professor. He chooses the readings carefully and does listen and consider student input. Don't listen to the people who criticized him -- likely they deserved the grades they received. If you're willing to do the readings, carefully consider and discuss them, and put a bit of effort into your writing you'll do just fine!

I liked Prof Evans a lot! He was very picky about what he wanted in a paper, but that's what you should expect in an honors intensive writing course. His tough grading made me push myself to become a better writer.
would not recommend this prof evans at all
Don't believe many of these comments.  Professor Evans expects a lot but he is fair and the class is interesting when people participate.

Prof Evans criticized the class for lack of participation but it was because he lacked any sort of structure for discussion.  His negative/pessimistic attitude made class time very tense and uncomfortable. The papers were fairly difficult; class average was generally a B- and he provided little constructive criticism. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!

This class required a lot of work, not to mention using up my print quota. I received poor grades on my essays, as well as on participation although I spoke daily. I went to a couple office hours and my essays still did not improve enough to receive better than a C. Favoritism of some students is apparent. I don't recommend taking this class.

Gareth brought up interesting questions in class and kept us talking. He even cracked jokes sometimes. His paper assignments were fair and clear, and he answered any questions we had about them. Contrary to popular belief, he is not impossible to get As from.

He is one of the most unfair teachers I have ever had. He is totally pretentious - I think he fakes his accent sometimes. He makes the class unnecessarily hard, and is unpredictable about his grades so it's hard to do well no matter how much time you put in. He prides himself on not giving out As. And he is weird and boring. Don't take his classes.

A very disorganzed professor with a very disorganized class. It is near impossible to execute the assignments up to Gareth's standards, even if you visit him during office hours. Hope your love of literature is enough to keep you in this class.

One of the best profs I've had. Cares about his students but only if he sees an equal effort in his class. Always willing to meet after class and review course work. Material isn't something you can gloss over though. Wish I could have him again.
The only comment I have is a quote from professor Haghverdi, "The best teacher is the worst teacher." By that standard, he was the "best" I've ever had.

Had him for info math, was what I expected. Hard. Material is hard enough on its own, but you MUST attend lectures.  The dicussions are where all the quizzes are.  He is difficult to understand during lecture, but not attending or falling asleep will ruin your grade. Lastly, the tests are VERY HARD. I had a solid B before the final, dropped to a C-

Esfandiar Haghverdi is one of the worst professors that I have had since coming to IU. He doesn't care about his students grades and isn't willing to try to meet with them outside of class. If there is any way around taking one of his courses I would highly advise that you do so!

I think he explains the material very clearly! His English is perfect, and if you're good at math, attend class, and put in a little effort outside of class to understand the material, then I201 is not hard. He answers students' questions and is very helpful. I've learned a lot in his class. If you work reasonably hard, it's easy to get an A or B.
Not very clear when teaching. It's a tough class and his teaching methods don't help. The AI's are much more helpful.

Prof. Haghverdi does have an accent but has great English so is easily understood.  Class can be tough at times, but he will always go back and explain a section if you don't get it.  Very nice professor.
Very nice professor
Professor is a little hard to understand and the material is difficult, be he wants all students to succeed and does curve the course!
Second half of the semester is soooo much harder. He explains everything clearly but if you miss a class it can get confusing. HW due every week and theres a quick EVERY lab
Tough material...he's a good professor and is fair.  Do the homework and study for the tests and the curve will save you.

Nice guy and is clearly passionate and very knowledgeable about the subject. However, his exams are very difficult and doesn't give much preparation for them (study the audios!). Lots of HW assignments, but they're not (typically) too hard. Some random ones take very long to complete though. Interesting topic, just a hard class to keep up with.

Spanish phonetics is a challenging subject, and so naturally the class wont be a breeze. However, having a professor who is clearly so fascinated by, experienced + invested in the subject himself has made it one of the most interesting courses I've taken yet, and has made all of the concepts completely graspable. He cares about you & your learning!

This was my least favorite Spanish class I've ever taken. He was unorganized and I didn't learn anything before teaching myself for the exams. The vibe of the class: the second exam most of the class failed; he didn't let us see the grade or the exam just made us retake the almost exact same exam a week later (without re-teaching any information).
Take this class if you're trying to tank your GPA.

hate this class ngl... nice and funny professor but he makes the exams so hard and expects you to figure everything out because it's an "honors" class. even when majority of the students are clearly struggling.

Loved this class so much! Lots of HW but most of it is completion. All he asks is for you to try your best, and if you do you are guaranteed a good grade. Pay attention, attend lecture, and participate! He is so fun and passionate about what he teaches. You can tell he appreciates people's effort because he cares so much about the class. Loved it!

Great professor. He's clearly very passionate about his work. He uses activities and memorable metaphors to teach concepts, and it is very effective. There is a lot of homework, and a lot of the homework involves listening to recordings of your own voice. I strongly recommend taking as many of his classes as you can.

He's a pretty excellent professor--very enthusiastic about his subject matter, clearly cares about student progress, and encourages students to make connections outside of the classroom. Make sure you memorize the charts at the beginning of the class because they will be used throughout the semester.

Erik is an expert on this topic, but is aware that we are not and therefore structures this course around our personal development and introducing us into what he has devoted his life to. He was very understanding with me the whole semester when I kept making mistakes I'm sure he found basic. Some of the hw takes a long time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Profe Willis is great! Very passionate about phonetics and his students--and that's why there's lots of homework! You need to show up and do the assignments to pass, but you get so much out of it! At times the course can seem a little unorganized, but it all makes sense towards the midterm. You just really need to engage with the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: At first he comes out as super passive aggressive, very direct but overall he is one of the best IU Spanish Professors ! If you have any questions he's always willing to meet up. Hes very caring and so passionate with the Spanish language. He may be scary at first but he truly wants his students to succeed. Get prepared to do a lot of homework.

By far, one of the most knowledgeable, but accessible Spanish professors I've ever had! At first I was a little wary, but he genuinely wants you to succeed. The exams are hard, but they help you learn. If something isn't clear, use the textbook and go to his office hours. Studying in groups helps too! Outside of class stuff, his humor grows on you!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Willis is easily one of the most passionate professors I have ever had at IU. His passion and dedication to the Spanish language and teaching itself make learning from him so much more enjoyable than any other course. He explained concepts in relatable ways. He incorporated useful activities that effectively helped us understand concepts.
I really enjoyed taking S326 with Profe Willis! One of my favorite professors at IU by far!
Super nice guy, who genuinely cares for his students and has a passion for what he teaches. Quite a lot of small homework assignments - not difficult but at least one assignment due each class.
He is a very solid professor. There are times when his instructions and expectations were unclear to the entire class, but his passion for the subject makes up for that.

I had Prof. Willis for an honors linguistics class and I was wary of him at first, because from time to time he is unorganized and confusing with assignments, but I came to love him by the end of the course. He is truly passionate about linguistics and is excited to share this knowledge with students. Best Spanish prof I've had at IU so far.

I really liked him for the study abroad I did. He is very funny and usually nice. Occasionally he acts offended, and like you're an idiot for asking questions, but overall he was a good guy. He also changed the class so the tests won't be as bad any more.

Profe is very good at what he does-he is passionate about linguistics, and his enthusiasm shows in class when he lectures. Class is very inclusive of all students, workload is very manageable until the last week when there was a final paper, research project, and exam all due at nearly the same time. Exams are MUCH tougher than anticipated

He is a good prof. His Spanish is very easy to understand and he speaks slowly. Class seems easy, but exams (online) are very challenging. The assignments are all online, but are not difficult and should pad your grade. He has a unique and very dry personality but is tolerable. Would recommend.
Best teacher, makes class interesting and pretty easy honestly. Wants you to be curious over anything else. Tests are online and can be pretty in-depth, but pay attention and you should be fine.
Great class, interesting topic. Online tests are tough.

He gives so much explanation with his examples that you're left with very few actual examples to study with. It's necessary to go to every office hour for a good grade. Tips: don't major in CS & don't major @ Luddy unless you're Cyber GP

Alright professor for a horribly designed class. His lectures are detailed with examples but can be overwhelming. The lectures and the discussions have very different content. There is a quiz every week and you WILL fail a few because they are so poorly written. TAKE Info201 instead if youre allowed or take this class with a therapist on speed dial
C241 was really intense but Wennstrom might be my favorite CS professor at Luddy

I hated this class! The professor was constantly stuck in analysis paralysis. it was difficult to follow his lectures at the best of times, nearly impossible at the worst. used terminology without explaining what it was, and the class was incredibly fast paced. overall just not super clear to understand. 0/10 would recommend.

Homeworks were graded ruthlessly and the tests were brutal. Lectures were quite boring but probably just the topics were boring. Upper level class so in my opinion there was too much emphasis on rigorously finishing proofs (instead of just doing proof sketches). We can do that ourselves. Clear explanations though and overall, you will learn well.

Not a bad prof. Compared to the vast majority of CS profs he's golden. But everyone has flaws. I think grading was WAY too tough, took long, and oftentimes quizzes/exams were too difficult/short. He's lenient with grades at times (resubmissions, extra credit, etc.), but even those moments of grace feel outweighed by the course's shortcomings.

Absolutely horrible Professor. The class is so difficult but he makes it so much harder. Lots of Assignments and difficult questions. Pages upon pages of tests and homework. He only gives 4 days for such lengthy homework and that's including Saturdays and Sundays. Absolutely stressful Would never take him again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Tests are quite challenging even for the best of students. Basically nobody, out of multiple hundred students, aces it precurve. Weekly quizzes over stuff students don't understand yet. Some homework problems are way harder than even the teacher intends.

This class was done so badly this semester that he had to send an apology letter. While I believe Dr. Wennstrom is a great person, the course changes he made this semester practically ruined what could have been a great class. There was no textbook, as he was constantly changing things. I hope this class is improved for future CS students.

Great professor teaching likely the hardest course I've ever taken since this semester was extraordinarily difficult due to curriculum changes. That came with typos, unintentionally difficult exams, and lots of confusion. There are some holes in the course format, including weekly quizzes (worth 20%) on material they KNOW you don't understand yet.

This is the best designed, most fairly taught course I have ever taken. Wennstrom is a fantastic lecturer, knows what he's talking about, and is willing to entertain pushback as long as you're willing to hear his side. He can come off as condescending at first, but really, he's just precise. Could not recommend taking this class with him enough.

Dudes the goat, I showed up to every single lecture and only paid about 10% attention, but his resources and knowledge is strong and his pacing, curriculum, and explanations are great.

Assume G,

Easily one of the best professors I've had. Yes there is a lot of homework, and the material can be difficult. His lectures make the most complicated topics clear. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him, do it. He is understanding with assignments, and offers a bank of late points and HW resubmissions. You'll learn a lot from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework
