reviews.comment: His discrete structures class is a relatively difficult class for being a 200-level one, but his lectures are amazing. If you skip them, then you will not understand nearly as much as if you did go.
Such a good lecturer! Makes a class that feels inapproachable and difficult feel reasonable and fun. If you don't take 241 with him, you are actually setting yourself up for failure!
good teacher

c200 goes very fast for a student who might know the basics of programming. make sure to be on his good side, and go to his office hours. try your best to build a connection If not, he will give you a very tough time. Also, do the work on time, and ask doubts in his class. Mandatory to go to his class, if you want to pass, and not have him hate you

Erik has written 200+ page pdf of the content that he is going to teach, almost like his own textbook, apart from that we don't use any textbook. However, reading it alone will not help, there are a lot of crucial examples that are taught only in his classes. Class is designed for you to go to office hours, and seek help. Don't skip office hours.

Wennstorm teaches a stupidly hard class, and if you pay attention to his lectures he'll fool you into believing it's easy. Then you'll start doing the assignments and getting A's on everything, and you'll think that the class is really easy, so you stop showing up to lecture and all of a sudden you aren't getting A's anymore. His lectures are godly

Class: CSCIB401 (not 200 lol)

Most entertaining & informative prof I've had in CS. Class structure is great w/ a great late policy & homework corrections.

I don't think he's a bad teacher but I think he's not the best for c200, the homework is hard and lengthy, but doable. don't take this course if you've never programmed before, they move kind of fast and teach it like you already know the basics of coding, you'll be self learning a lot. make sure you really pay attention at the beginning as well

in my opinion, this course was too difficult to be an intro course for computer science. the assignments, which are due every week and are 70% of your grade, are veryyyyyy hard. i heard there's a big curve at the end but idk. wennstrom was okay at lecturing... i just think the assignments are overly difficult (which isn't his fault)

Tough material for some, but there is a generous late homework point refund and Erik is a great lecturer. If you show up for the lectures, you should have no problem passing. There's also a PDF written by Wennstrom that provides notes for virtually everything in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: understanding and accommodating
Class is low stress, nice late policy. Also assignments are very clear about how to answer
The material is incredibly difficult, but he is a good teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Homework rubrics and the late penalty refund are designed to encourage correct answers rather than half-assed ones. Erik has an all inclusive pdf with detailed notes, which is without a doubt the best resource for success in the class. Lots of opportunities for extra credit and lots of office hours.

First of all, I couldn't deny that he is a very kind person. However, his lectures are not helpful at all. By taking his lectures along, it's impossible to finish his assignments. And you have to take extra time to study yourself. Then, those TAs are terrible. I went to multiple lab session and none of them read the HWs. TAs are irresponsible.

Really great professor. attendance isn't mandatory but he provides new information in every lecture so i highly recommend going to all the classes, and also taking strong notes. i didn't find his office hours too helpful but i went to the AIs' office hours and that helped a ton. he replaces lowest exam grade with final exam grade if it's better.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Taking C241 right now and he teaches with enthusiasm. It's the UIs and AIs you should watch out for as they are the ones who grade your homework. Some of the UIs and AIs don't know what they're talking about. Go to his office hour, his lecture and do your hw in lab and you'll most likely get an A.

This was by far one of the hardest classes I've taken at IU. It may have been because I didn't have as strong of a math background as some of the other students, but it was hard. I really enjoyed the class overall though. Erik does care about his students and met with me countless times outside of normal office hours to explain things.

The Best teacher in my university experience, quiz, and tests are much easier than homework, unless you have to do all of the homework. His lecture is super clear and easier to understand. And he seems like a kid who likes to play those questions with his students. best teacher

Prof Wennstrom is an excellent lecturer and is very approachable in person.  However, due to the size of the class, he relies on his TA/GAs for labs and grading.  Because of this, grading and feedback can be inconsistent.  He can also be slow to respond to emails.

Prof. Wennstrom is one of the best professors I had in Computer Science. Not only can he explain the subject well, but he is super helpful in lecture and in office hours. True baller.  Expect a lot of homework, quizzes outside of lecture, (reasonably) hard tests, and being called on to participate if you don't voluntarily participate often.

He is one of the most helpful professors I've had at IU. Yes, the class is difficult, but if you do the work and ask for help when you need it, you will do great! He has been more than willing to meet with me outside of his scheduled office hours, and often answers questions I ask via email. Great teacher, I highly recommend him!
Just look at his grade distribution online. He's one of the worst instructors for this course.

Erik is one of the best teachers I've ever had at IU.  He is always willing to help and makes sure you understand something before you leave to do homework.  Yes, his class is hard.  But this is computer science, not basket weaving.

He's a very smart guy who encourages his students to try their best, but this class was WAY too challenging and homework-heavy for an intro course for non-computer science majors. Sure, it's 4 credit hours, but I spent more time studying for this course than all my other classes combined and it was STILL my lowest grade. Do not take this class.
Worse experience of my life. If you don't want to hate your life for a semester DO NOT take. Please fire her immediately.Took years off my life I can never get back

Doesn't know her own syllabus. Takes points off for breathing the wrong way. Probably the worst teacher in Kelley. Not a bad person but a bad teacher and tries to make an easy Kelley pre req some hard, meaningful class

A lot of people complain about her and say she is mean or a tough grader or makes the projects. If you want a teacher who coddles you and only gives A's she isn't for you, but if you want a professor who makes you learn and prepares you for the real business world that's what she'll do.

Nearly cost my my admission to kelley. Just very demeaning in the sense that she rarely acknowledges the day-to-day of a student. Doesn't make much time for for students. Disappointing experience that reflects badly on the school
Every day on my walk to this class I hoped a car would hit me so I would not have to attend. Even then, she would take points off for attendance.

Very negative experience. Expectations constantly changed and instructions were unclear. Meeting outside of class was nearly impossible. Missing even one presentation or makeup day meant no chance to make it up, despite being told otherwise. Professionalism was also questionable. Would not recommend.
Really bad, please don't loose any points outside presentations. Show up to class do the readings random extra credit in the class. Avoid if you can.
Kelley needs to fire her already.
Her class was difficult, but it honestly did push me out of my comfort zone a lot. I did have immense levels of anxiety before every single class period. Communication was unclear most times.

Nivia ran her BUS-C 104 class in a way genuinely make me want to puke. I felt sick every time I walked in her classroom. Every time she criticized me or my peers, I was ready to puke all over her. College classes in general shouldn't feel this sickening to even attend. Take someone else for a more peaceful experience and drop her if pre-enrolled.

Ummm so if you want to stay sane, please do not take this class. I only got a good grade, because I met with her multiple times a week on my presentations, and I still will never get full credit. Even just simply peer reviews are obscenely graded hard, with my peers getting multiple 6/10s dropping their grades significantly. There better professors

She will fool you for the first couple of weeks, but by the end of the semester, she will be failing the class and barely responding to anyone. DO NOT TAKE HER. She's a tough grader, so she can cope with the fact that she teaches a gimme class and wants to make it way more complicated than it is. She also embarrasses nervous kids during Q and A.

I had a medical appointment (from a month ago) that required immediate x-ray and care from my orthopedic surgeon, so I requested for our group's presentation to be on the 2nd available day instead. However, she was adamant on doing randomized presentation order rather than a sign-up sheet which she did for all of our previous presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Just don't take her please please please listen to this

If I regret anything about my freshman year, it's taking this class. The professor was the most unprofessional instructor I've had. She grades harshly w/ little explanation, makes students feel embarrassed for asking questions, and is incredibly difficult to communicate with. Unless you're a perfect student by her standards, don't expect anything.

Nivia isn't the best professor, but she's also not as bad as people are saying. One thing I will say: if you take her class, you will make a huge jump as a presenter, almost guaranteed. She gives tough, but fair criticisms and genuinely wants to see you continue to grow as the semester goes on. Be ready though, this class with her is a TON of work.
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS PLEASE FOR YOUR OWN SANITY. unless you like doing the most unbearable horrible terrible things, that will make you grow as a person (a little).
Do not take her at all costs.
terrible do not take her

She would shame me in front of the whole class, her directions for assignments were very vague which stressed everyone out, and her grading criteria is strict. I don't recommend at all and whenever I tried emailing her for questions, she would straight up tell me to open my ears up more in class and to ask classmates. I'm at word limit but don't.
She is so unclear about what she expects and is very strict. All other C-104 teachers are very easy, but she just makes people's lives difficult for no reason

I liked her as a person, and when I talked to her outside of class she was always nice to me. However, she is very tough in class. Mostly you will feel like going to class is a waste of time because you can never work with your group in class. If you have her, memorize all assignments, due dates, and points! It determines when you present.

Nivia is a good person, but has certain aspects to her teaching style that make her a bad teacher. She oftentimes doesn't explain the grading criteria very clearly, and she is a very tough grader when it comes to presentations. If you step up, go above and beyond, do your work, and present like an adult, you'll be fine and respected in her class.

Is flat out mean to students, and not like the "giving feedback" normal comments. Takes forever to grade. Takes forever to reply to an email. Nothing is ever clear in this class; most presentations are unnecessarily overcomplicated. Group projects, make sure you pick a good group at the beginning of the class as that's your group until the end

Dr. Escobar is a very tough grader in presentations, however she does it because she wants each individual in her class to become a stronger presenter. If you make it clear that you are trying to become better and putting your best foot forward, you will not have an issue in her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Escobar's class was difficult to say the least. She is motivational and wants her students to work hard, but she does not provide clear guidelines. This makes it very difficult to get a good grade because there are many things she expects that are abstract. She is nice, but only if you truly try and do your best.

Nivia Escobar is an exceptional teacher who makes learning engaging and accessible. Her passion, clarity, and real-world connections inspire students to excel. She's supportive, approachable, and always ready to help, leaving a lasting impact on everyone she teaches. P.S. I'm Cap
Just don't man, just don't do it.

She is brutal. Tells you to email her, but then emails you back with an email that simply just won't answer your question. Extremely tough grader, and makes you go out of your way to get the smallest bit of knowledge for the class. makes this class 100x harder than it should be. Take any other teacher than her.

Absolutely brutal. Dr. Salazar inflicted upon an environment of stress and anxiety for a presentation class that was meant to be straightforward and simple. She expects perfection from students yet doesn't give out clear directions for assignments and is a brutal grader. Save yourself and take this class with quite literally any other professor.

The fact Nivia thinks its ok to chew out and insult individual students WHO PAID TO BE THERE in front of the entire class should say a lot about her. Take this class if you're ok with extremely unclear guidelines, your grade being dependent entirely on her mood, and the expectation of having the syllabus and every announcement she sends memorized

Barely taught the class - usually just berated us since to her not asking questions about the content she HAD NOT taught us meant we knew everything, took months to post grades for even simple assignments, extremely unclear guidelines

Horrible professor. I would give her worse than a 1 if I could. Insanely vague with how she wants things done in her class, never enforces anything and expects everyone to have the syllabus memorized down to the calendar. If you can take another class, DO IT. You'd be better off transferring than taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She never once actually TAUGHT anything, pulls assignments out of her butt, is extremely unclear and vague will instructions yet expects students to be perfect. Extremely rude to all students, lacks communication, and posts her body on TikTok all the time, so maybe that's why she never answers emails. No matter what, avoid her and her classes.
Run while you can. Nivia does not know how to teach the class to present and expects ONLY perfection from her students. Run!

Nivia is by far THE worst teacher I have ever had in anything in my entire life. Extremely hard to understand, gave vague descriptions of projects and then expected absolute perfection. Rude to students, unforgiving, and just very unpleasant to be around. She made what should have been a relatively easy class into a nightmare.

Nivia is an extremely harsh and unfair grader, and she expects students to act in a professional manner when she isn't professional herself. I would like to speak on behalf of every student that has taken Nivia's course; we all believe that it was a mistake of ever teaching at Kelley, and it would be best if she didn't teach at IU.

Late with grading assignments and what she says in class frequently contradicts what assignments say. Her overall attitude towards the class makes it very unpleasant to have her as a professor. Very harsh grader for small mistakes and makes the entire subject of business presentations extremely unenjoyable. Do not take!

Do. Not. Take. This. Class. With. Her. Any other class, I'm telling you. Nivia is horrible about providing grades in a timely manner, will actively put you down in front of classmates, and will find every reason not to give you an A. When someone asks about grades she'll simply say "Is anybody failing?" Save yourself the headache, please.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
The 350-word limit is not nearly enough to describe the absolute travesty that was this class and this teacher. Attached is 750-word breakdown of why you should avoid her class at all costs. 

Use tinyurl . c o m  / NiviaEscobar (no spaces) and read the document. You'll thank me later.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Run. Don't do it

Regularly condescends students, initiates pointless arguments with students, defensive, stubborn, gives vague/misleading assignments (or doesn't post an assignment at all!), then berates you for not doing exactly what she had in mind. She's really petty and frustrating. I'm not one to leave negative reviews, so trust me on this one: avoid.

Fred is a highly engaging professor! If you come to class prepared to participate, you will do well and enjoy the course. As an MBA course, expect heavy group work - but the readings are pretty light.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Fred is a great professor! He's understanding, fun, and wants his students to get the most out of the class. His tests are not too difficult, either.

Great professor in that he really knows how to connect with students and convey concepts in a way they will understand.  The discussions during the lectures were the best I've had in KD.  There was a fair amount of work involved in the course but it  was worth it.  Grading was fair.

Super knowledgeable. He teaches from the perspective of reality - what's actually going on in the world, not sterile ivory tower concepts. Lectures are good, but the real value in taking any class with Fred is to engage him in discussion. Do that, and the learning floodgates will open.
Can't stand this class with him
He basically doesn't specify what he wants and then he gives you the lowest grade possible even after saying you've done a fantastic job!

This man is probably the best teacher I've had... Makes the topic of Entrepreneurship extremely interesting, and fun at the same time. I look forward to attending every class. Great professor. Recommended to everyone...
Great guy, interesting lectures

Rick is an awesome teacher and his lectures go far beyond the IU-set material. Brings in a lot of examples from his career as an attorney that make the material interesting and enjoyable. One of the leading experts on Crypto stuff, and a lot of conversations about current events which is fun
Professor Fair was the best, had amazing stories from his time as a lawyer. Had a great time in his class.

Fair has been my favorite professor I've had in Kelley. He has had one of the most interesting lives of anyone I've met. He had a new story every day and found a way to tie it into the material. The class was easy, but it was very educational. The majority of your grade is made up of a test and a final project. Would take him again in a heartbeat.

Good lecturer and very knowledgeable on business law, but he grades so tough on every assignment we get whether they're tests or regular assignments. Also, tests are insanely hard and even with a notecard you could still have no idea what's going on.

The best professor so far and my favorite!!. Very understanding and very nice. I'd say take Professor Fair if you have the opportunity to. Maybe you'd feel the class is hard, but once you speak to the professor he makes everything easy for you

He's a really good teacher, knows his stuff, casual lecture, but can get dry because it's law. Very very test heavy, you have essay questions that are graded hard. You need to know all of the content for the exams, minimal study tips given but the slideshows give all of the information. Definitely go to class.

I enjoyed the professor and the material. However, the course grade is based on only 100 total points, making each assignment count heavily. Expect substantial reading, graded reading questions, and rigorous essay exams. I recommend checking the grade distribution beforehand so you know what to expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class as an easy gen ed. Whole class is out of 100 points from 2 essay midterms, one essay final, a group rating, and reading questions that must be correctly answered every day to get credit. Readings are easily over an hour for each class and the essays are graded harshly with no opportunity to gain back points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This gen ed is the hardest class I've ever taken. 1 question quizzes every single class count for your attendance, if you get the question wrong, you don't get the point for the day. The question is about something that happens on ONE page of 30-100 pages of reading. I'm currently trying to replace it. No gen ed should result in a failing grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is very passionate about history. This course is rather easy, especially if you have taken any AP history courses in high school. Very good professor and person, and would highly recommend taking this course.

By the way he lectures you can tell he's passionate about history. This course dives into a lot of important historical events. Do the readings or you won't do good on the quizzes in the discussion and it'll affect your grade as well. Also, he will occasionally call on someone to answer a question which is usually obvious, so don't be worried.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell Prof. Guardino truly enjoys history and teaching. I took his class to fulfill a gen ed requirement. Do not take him unless you love history. Expect upwards of 15-30 pages of reading per class. Exams were in essay format, but not too bad because he allowed a double-sided notecard for outlines. Overall great, but very heavy workload.
Great professor who cares about the subject.
Loved peter, great teacher

Do the readings! Weekly mini quizzes over readings in discussion, and participation is expected. Lectures have the content you need, but take notes so you have the necessary information. Gives you slides but they are just support, not content. Exams are essay format and gives the questions as a study guide. Do the bare minimum and you will succeed.
Do the reading before discussion and you will be fine. Lectures are long and boring. Tests are easy and as long as you somewhat prepared you were guaranteed at least a B on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class only graded on three essays and your attendance/reading checks done at your discussion section. Essays are your tests and based on lectures. Gives you plenty of time to study and wants to see you succeed. He does have a sense of humor and will implement it into lectures which makes them fun. Other than that it's a boring class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this class if you need GEN ED credit! It's not that hard, but his lectures can be boring. However, attendance points can help boost your grade at the end of the semester, so go to class. He is very nice and understanding. If you are struggling, keep him in the loop, and he is happy to help support you. One of my favorite professors so far!

Exams are essay layouts, lots of reading in preparation for weekly discussion section. Other than that attendance is necessary, and class is really interesting if you are someone who liked history in highschool. Just prepare well for the exams and you will do fine, really recommend if you need a class for your Gen-Ed credits
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For a 100 level history class it's a ton of work. Seating chart, attendance is taken, and he occasionally calls on someone random to answer. Lots of readings every week and then a quiz during discussion. I would recommend for anyone who enjoys history or is a history major, but for anyone else I would stay clear of H101.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Guardino was honestly very passionate about this course. It was the Social History of War and he clearly enjoys teaching. He was very intimidating to go up to, but was super accommodating and nice. He gave 1 question reading checks every class, so be sure to do the readings! Overall a great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gaurdino created a seating chart for my 150 person class, and then when asking the class a question, he decided to call on someone at random from his seating chart list. Other than that though, lecture is easy and tests are in the dorm of essays. Be prepared to read for the discussion section though, as there are mini quizzes every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Guardino's class Modern Mexico involves a hefty amount of reading and it is graded based on only 4 assignments, but if you are interested in the history of our southern neighbor I highly encourage you to take this extremely engaging course. Guardino and his class have influenced me in my focus not only for my major but for my career.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Good teacher, the class is not very difficult if you do the readings and stay on top of tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Guardino took a section of history (1900-1945) that most people learn about from elementary school and made it actually interesting. He made me enjoy the twentieth century, which I never had prior.

It's easy to get a C in this class, but challenging to get an A. There are usually several readings every week, which you will be quizzed over. Tests are essays over a topic, and can be graded easily or tough depending on the AI. Overall, recommend for history majors, but not for those looking for an easy elective.
Honestly a pretty good professor.  The one essay tests seem really intense, but going through all of the prompts honestly teaches you a lot about the subject.  Not easy though.
Terrible. Long, boring, vague, monotonous lectures. He made history dreadful for me, and I used to consider myself a history buff! AI's grade your tests and they are hard graders.

2 day lecture, 1 day discussion. Lecture - sit & listen to PP lecture (take notes), Discussion - must read all stories in prep for discussion section as there is a 1 point pop quiz at the beginning of class. The readings may very well consist of 200 pages/ 10 sections, but the quiz question will simply be a very small part of one of those sections.

Assigns too much reading. Squeezes students into the first 8 rows of a huge lecture hall for the sake of attendance. Bases students' knowledge on a whole week's worth of reading on a single question during discussions, which only applies to one reading as opposed to all of them. I put too much effort into this class considering it is an elective
Nice guy and pretty funny . Not your typical class of scantron tests over the lectures. Based on 100 points TOTAL so very hard to receive an A. Have to go to class and discussion.

There are two textbooks you're supposed to buy but you only use Sources of Twentieth-Century Global History so I wouldn't buy the other one. He gives you what is going to be on the test, but tests are still pretty hard.

not willing to reschedule exam times unless you have an emergency. exam was the day thanksgiving break started and he wouldn't let anyone take it at a different time regardless of your class or travel schedule.

Professor Guardino clearly loves history and can talk for hours about it. His class is not the easiest to get an A in, but if you do the work and prepare well for the tests, you will do fine. Definitely utilize your discussion leader and meet with them outside of class - they help A LOT. Overall I would recommend this class.
Definitely knows what he's talking about! He makes the topics covered interesting.
Very intelligent man, lectures for this particular class weren't necessary for the class itself as the class essentially revolved around the final paper. But none the less, he's a good professor.

Lectures were pretty boring, unless you have an extreme interest in what he's talking about. Tons of reading that gets pretty monotonous. Discussion leaders can help out a lot if you get a good one that is willing to help.

Class was interesting sometimes but it's history and some lectures were boring. A lot of reading required. Also it wasn't the easiest class to get an A in  so if you're taking it for the easy A, it won't be like that. Out of 136 kids in my class, only 15 got As and 38 got A-s, so it's not just a class where you get the A. Easy tests though.
Lectures are intersting. He is a smart guy and puts a lot of effort into his work. Tests are easy.
Smart guy, lectures can get a little monotonous and boring, but the tests are relatively easy.
Danger! Danger! This dude has issues.

lectures are unordered and meandering, with no clear direction of where he's going or what exactly the topic of the day is. takes student suggestion well, however; made mid-semester evaluations and took students ideas to improve lecture seriously. easy bluebook tests.
He is such a caring and genuine professor who made a boring course interesting and engaging.

I would 100% recommend Professor Ford for Compass 1. He is a really sweet and caring guy who genuinely cares for his students. Class work was not hard at all, probably took me like an hour at most a week to complete his work. If I had this later class time without Ford, I would dread going.
Easy class, easy grader, cares about his students. The lecture is as interesting as it can be given the course material is pretty boring. Overall great.

Professor Ford is amazing. Class is simple and easy to follow, yet he provides good feedback and is always available to help. He genuinely cares about his students and their development. Lectures are interesting and filled with stories throughout, and you learn a ton from him in a low-stress class.
Great guy, easy class.
I have only good things to say about Professor Ford. Genuinely cares a ton about everyone regardless of if students reciprocate that level of energy.
makes class fun. great speaker. really nice guy

Professor Ford definitely wants every student in his class to succeed, and he makes sure to design his course in a way for that to happen. The only work outside of class are weekly assignments that won't take more than 20-30 mins. There aren't any exams, but he takes a while to grade the work. Other than that definitely take him for compass.

Great professor! He made the classes was pretty engaging for how redundant the information can be sometimes. He really cares about his students and their futures. The assignments aren't bad at all and everything you learn from him really helps to set you up for the rest of the semesters! Overall, great class and professor!

Prof. Ford is a sweet guy and you can tell he has a true passion for what he teaches! He always has  group activities prepared and the assignments are straight forward if you look at the directions and rubric. This is the easiest freshman Kelley class you will take and Ford will give you a good grade for following instructions.

Professor Ford is someone who cares about his work and it shows. He had important things for us every single class and he presented information in a way that kept us engaged and made us walk away as better business students. He outlines grading criteria for every assignment well and he is easily accessible outside of class for any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ford is an amazing teacher. He really cares about his students and is so understanding about everything. As long as you turn in assignments on time, follow the rubric, and show up to class, you should get an A+

Professor Ford is super engaging, understanding, and prepared. You can tell he is passionate about teaching and cares about building a relationship with his students. The overall class is not challenging, and the workload is much lighter than in other courses.
Professor Ford's lectures are extremely engaging. The course load is much lighter than other classes, but you still come out from the class with valuable skills gained.

the best professor i've ever had. he knows exactly what he's talking about and is always prepared for his lectures/lessons. he is super helpful and is very inviting for office hours. his class and workload is not hard at all and you dont need to spend more than an hour a week on his class. easy A

Professor Ford is a great guy and teacher. You can tell he genuinely cares about his students, and as long as you put effort into the course, he will put effort into you. His lectures are interesting and he gives you insightful questions. My only issue is that it takes months for him to return an assignment grade.
Very nice guy, very good professor. I had some kids in my class talk over him while he was lecturing which kind of pissed me of, since he is passionate about teaching and ensuring that we learn.
Good guy, passionate about compass and about his students.  He defiantly wants the best for them.  Not the most thrilling class but it's helpful and easy.  Overall, you should defiantly take him.

Literally can't ask for any more from a professor. Super nice, cares about his students, work is easy and there isn't much of it, and attendance policy is very easy you just have to go to like 75% of classes. I can't even think of one negative, take him if you can.
Prof Ford is a great compass teacher. He gives great lectures and is a light grader. However only con is that the assignments are really tedious, but not hard.
Prof Ford is a great compass teacher. He gives great lectures and is a light grader. However only con is that the assignments are really tedious.
I loved Prof Ford, he was very kind and good at teaching course concepts! Easy A as well as long as you show up, pay attention, and do assignments on time.

Ford was the best professor I had this semester. Class was fun, engaging, and enjoyable to attend. Attendance is required but you get 3-4 excused absences before a grade deduction/automatic fail (due to only meeting once a week). He graded pretty easily and there were no tests or quizzes. Highly recommend taking him for BUS-T175.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great prof for T275, just show up to class and pay attention to what the homework is

Prof Ford is super nice and really sweet. However, I feel his classes weren't particularly useful until later on in the semester. A lot of his homework is busy work and it takes a long time to get your grade back, it's easy to do well tho. Nice guy but doesn't provide a lot of value for your time. Easy grader for the most part. Super approachable.

Any negative reviews of this professor are simply due to the students inability to turn in assignments on time, not a reflection of Professor Ford. He enforces the same rules as almost every kelley professor. Great lecturer/person with an inspirational upbringing. So much to learn from him professionally and personally. Highly recommend his class.
Professor Ford is a kind and caring professor, I enjoyed going to class and Professor Ford's passion made class enjoyable. I would recommend Professor Ford to any student taking compass

This class starts off with assignments every week and slowly gets less but the assignments become more work. Ford is a really nice guy and the right teacher for this class. Take notes because not all of the slides get posted and notes make the projects easier. There is no final for this class but some projects are worth a lot of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ford has served as a personal and academic advisor for me since my freshman year solely because of his genuine and kind-hearted nature. He truly loves teaching compass, drop into his office hours and just chit-chat with him! He loves connecting with his students and is a fantastic letter of rec writer.
Show up to class and complete assignments for easy A+
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ford was the best! He made classes fun and engaging, but some of them dragged on a bit. He has clear expectations for his assignments, but most of them are just for completion.

This professor was amazing! The class was very easy but valuable. Ford is very approachable; if you go to office hours with questions about the big assignments and follow his corrections, it should be a guaranteed A in the class. He takes attendance but only uses it if you ask for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ford is cordial and lectures well. T175 is a fluff class, so it isn't too much work; however, I did find the content valuable. Prof Ford doesn't grade too harshly--the biggest grade is a LinkedIn profile, and he gave me 100%. He does mark attendance, so it is important to attend class. Best wishes!

The class is pretty easy and there is usually one assignment per week. The content we learned in class didn't always seem super practical. The teacher was pretty nice but could sometimes come off as a little judgy.

He stinks, do not take him and I hope he sees this. Pretends to care but does not in anyway, especially for kids trying to get into Kelley. Gets angry and annoyed when you try to get help and does not budge on anything. Makes a LinkedIn profile the main grade and if you mess up on one thing he will not let you resubmit or edit it. He Sucks.
Professor Ford is a very nice and caring teacher, and as long as you follow what he says to do for the assignments you'll be fine. Highly recommend Professor Ford for Compass 1.
Wants students to succeed in business world, and makes content feel important.
Super caring and nice. He teaches really well, and makes class time very useful and meaningful.
Came to class prepared, held reasonable expectations for students, taught material fluently and didn't waste my time. On top of all this, he did it kindly and made sure we all were okay.
A great professor that cares a lot about his students and about the material that he teaches. Would def take a class with him again.

Pretty decent dude. He takes his job seriously but not in a bad way. The class itself was honestly just boring but really nice dude. Definitely an easy A, but JLLC classes usually are. Talks a lot and has a lot of discussion based classes. I would take again, nothing to complain about except for boring classes but that's honestly out of his control
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Compass is pretty much a fluff class, but Ford is a good prof overall. He genuinely cares about his students and is really approachable as a teacher. He isn't so great at responding to emails, so if you have a question, go to his office hours and he'll be happy to help you.

Professor Ford is a real gem! He is so caring and sweet and makes sure his teaching environment is a safe place for students. He encourages participation and is extremely supportive of his students. The class itself is very easy and if you have any questions, you can email Professor Ford and he will typically answer within a few hours.

Professor Ford made the 7 am class fun. This was my only in person class during COVID and he did enough group work to where you got to know your classmates. He was always welcoming and cheery. Be prepared to talk in class because he does like participation. Not quizzes and Compass 1 is just a good class for background knowledge in the future.

Not really a fan of Professor Ford. He kind of pretended to care about the students and their lives, but at the end of the day, not really. Was not helpful when I went to him for help or asked him questions. If it required more than one response, he wasn't happy to help. Easy enough class, but take it with another professor.

Although I only had prof Ford for a six week course, he truly was one of my favorite teachers this semester. He encouraged students to participate and was passionate about the work he taught us. He is strict about grading though so be sure to do your homework well and on time.

Hes def the best compass prof. Just do the work for about an hour a week and go to class. His lectures arent terribly boring and he gets people to participate in a non intrusive way. Very aware of social change and social identities if thats important to you. Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Ford was an incredible Kelley Compass 1 professor. He really explains the course well and helps students develop their identities that will help them succeed in the future.
amazing overall prof. just do the work its like 1 hour a week and it's mainly on LinkedIN

Basically, for compass show up and you will be fine. Joshua was ok the lectures can get boring but the material is good to know. Please participate in class it will make things go a lot faster. He is an easy grader and provides a lot of good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He was an okay teacher. The lectures were pretty boring but he was a relatively easy grader. He did okay considering it was his first year teaching. Other teachers are probably better than him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved her! She is really passionate about anthropology and makes the class was really interesting! Also, all of her exams and quizzes are open note which makes it pretty easy. The only critique that I have is the labs are a bit annoying and unhelpful and they also have no drops so you can't miss any. Otherwise though, she's awesome!

This is the easiest class ever. However, Frederika is a BAD professor in being professional. She doesn't respond to emails promptly or enter grades accordingly. We haven't had updated grades since January. She is kind; however, she also makes up various excuses to cancel class and office hours ALL THE TIME. Labs are easy but repetitive.

lab's hard. My grade tanked cuz of my TA. Why they grading like they hate us? They don't help when ur confused.Their response to questions, "am i doin this right?" "by _, u mean _?", r just zero confirmation. I leave more confused than I came in & my grade tanked 1-2% down each time. (I dont even know my attend grade cuz she dont update so, YOLO)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This is fairly an easy class, heavily dependent on Lab, Quizzes, and final exam. I just hate how long it takes until grades are put in and how emails are left unanswered. My friends and I have emailed this prof/our TAs countless times and they don't bother to respond unless you confront them in class/lab.

I had her for A211, she had a very tough semester due to extenuating circumstances but showed up when she could and gave very interesting lectures. Assignments weren't very challenging and she cared about the subject.

Rika is very passionate about Human Variation and knows A LOT about it. But, she is bad about grading. It's December and our midterm hasn't been entered yet...
The readings are necessary but the lectures are the most important, (which are heavy but make sense)!
Be prepared to track your own progress and keep track of your attendance for reference
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She takes way too long to grade the assignments that she assigns and gives a large amount of assignments. You won't know your grade until very late in the semester when it's too late to change anything.

While Rika is a great lecturer, she does not grade in a timely manner and gives way to many assignments. The weekly readings took about an hour, which you were then given a quiz on later in the week. She has a project plus other writing assignments, making something due every week. I spent way more time on this class than almost every other class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is an easy A and she helps with that. Assignments are clear and easy to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The material is exceedingly interesting & the workload isn't too bad. The labs can be difficult, but there's only one a week & your TA can answer any questions you have. Canvas is informational & easy to understand. Some of the lowest grades are dropped at the end. When the entire class was behind, Rika was very accommodating. Great professor!

Maybe it was just a tough year for Rika, but class was constantly cancelled at the last minute, and it was hard to reach this professor outside of class. Class continuously goes over the time limit, so schedule accordingly. Lectures were engaging and thoughtful. This professor cares about her students and is willing to make accommodations.

Rika was very hard to access outside of class and she always cancelled her office hours. Things were always posted late or not all, especially grades. Lab activities were often very strenuous and unnecessary, and you had weekly discussion posts using Kritik. The course was fine and I managed to do well, but the material was not easy. No final!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Shes a great professor who is really knowledgeable. She keeps lectures interesting by always making jokes. Takes forever to grade tests but theyre all multiple choice with extra credit. Just show up and study the slides before the exam and youll get an A.

Rika is an awesome professor and I would definitely recommend taking ANTHB-200 with her rather than the other profs. Tests are super easy and straight from the study guide. Show up to the AI's office hours and you will get a 100% on the labs. She's really sweet/caring too!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Rika is a great lecturer. There was not a single class where my mind wandered or I got bored because the lecture material was fantastic and her delivery was riveting. I took this class just because I needed another N&M, but if I had been in here as a freshman instead of a senior, I might have chosen bio-anthropology as my field of choice.

Rika is a great lecturer - she knows a lot about the subject and doesn't just read off the slides. However, she cancels office hours a lot and takes months to grade assignments. Overall, the class should be easy as long as you look over the lecture slides and put some effort in
Rika is very knowledgeable and super caring. One of the most understanding teachers I have ever had.
Lecture is very boring and labs seem juvenile. However, the class isn't very hard and the professor is nice and funny.
Professor Kaestle was honestly such a nice person and really cares about you and your grade.
Shes really funny, personable, and cares about her students. Her lectures are very informative. Tests are the big thing in this class, so show up for lecture and study!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Grades hard on assignments, but the material is all very clear and the exams are made simple. Really funny, helpful, and approachable instructor!

AVOID HER. She cancels constantly and takes FOREVER to grade. I learned nothing in this class. When she is there to lecture, she just rambles. The midterm was delayed three weeks because she had missed too much, then it took four more weeks before I had my grade! She skipped office hours without letting anyone know. She's too much hassle!
Kaestle is great! Love having her as a prof. Makes expectations very clear and is always willing to give you extra help.

She is a great teacher. She is very easy to talk to and always willing to help. Lectures are interesting even if you don't really like the material. She's very clear and assignments and tests are easy. She can be a little unorganized at times, though. She is one of my favorite professors.
Really fun and great sense of humor. Extremely knowledgeable and just a fun person to talk to. Opened my eyes to Anthropology.

This semester she had a lot of health problems and was always cancelling class last minute. But when she was there, she gave super interesting lectures. Very knowledgeable and great sense of humor! My favorite prof by far. Would recommend to anyone. She is the reason I chose anthropology as my major.

Professor Kaestle is a wonderful and very knowledgable professor. Unfortunately, every other class is cancelled for whatever odd reason--half of the time I showed up and she called off at the last minute. Also, it has taken the ENTIRE semester to receive any updates on any grades. Basically, interesting class and prof. but very frustrating.

I love her! Good sense of humor. Others complain that lectures are boring but I was always so engaged! She is enthusiastic & makes it interesting. Tests are M/C &easy - info is straight from the lecture; plus you review for the tests in section which is super helpful. Labs=easy. Essays prepare you well for the tests. Great class! Highly recommend!

The lectures are painfully boring. I would regularly snapchat pictures of people sleeping near me. Be careful about the exercises, they were graded very precisely. I did absolutely none of the reading, so you could probably go without purchasing the textbook.

Dr. Kaestle is very enthusiastic about teaching the material and goes out of her way to ensure that her students are getting the most out of her class. She's very helpful and caring about her work. She helped me so much with this class and is part of the reason why I enjoyed it so much. Would definitely recommend to anyone.

I LOVED this professor.  I only took this class because I needed an N&M credit and didn't want to end up in chemistry or another math. The labs are fun and the papers you do are not difficult at all.  The tests aren't too difficult, but they aren't exactly a walk in the park either.  If you can, get this professor.

I had her for the Intensive Freshmen Seminar "Brave New Biology" and she made the transition into college so much easier! The class is super easy and started me off with a 4.00 GPA. She shows you around town and the assignments are clear. She's also forward and a pretty easy grader. The lecture is boring and i passed out once, but still good!
Dr. Kaestle is truly one of the best professors I have ever had. She is so enthusiastic about everything she teaches and she makes class enjoyable to attend.

Dr K is one of my fave profs ever! Syllabus/Grading system very clear, slides & all other resources posted online. ACTUALLY USES oncourse, quick to know grades. Bumped up my grade because I was soo close to the next grade letter. She's AWESOME. Labs are actually really fun! And she's quite funny. Very smart. Definitely an IU treasure. Love her!

She reads word for word from the slides and posts them online.  Essays arent too difficult but are graded harshly.  Tests have too much material but are overall decent.  Prof. K is funny and laid back but the lectures will put you to sleep if your not into bioanth so better off not going

One of my favorite professors.  Very laid back and easy to talk to.  You can tell that she enjoys the subject.  Does her best to make it interesting for students.  Plus, she posts review sheets and gives exam review sessions before every test.  As long as you pay attention, you'll pass.
Great teacher... gives out few assignments and tells students exactly what will be on the test.
Dr. Kaestle has been one of my favorite professors ever. She is so enthusiastic and has a great sense of humor and her class overall is fantastic.
She was one of the best profs I had in undergrad! Very engaging lectures and funny!
No Comments
Excellent professor. Don't waste her time she won't waste yours.
Dr. Kaestle is very enthusiastic about her topics and has a way of getting things across to her students. Labs help. Always willing to meet for consultations.
No Comments

The class was easy, but uninteresting.  The material had no depth and the course treated students like they were still in high school.  She has a good personality and enjoys teaching, but rarely goes beyond the lecture notes.
Always heard she was a great prof & so I waited until she was teaching B200 to take it. Glad I did, she teaches clearly, is v. intelligent and has an oddball sense of humor, which I appreciate.
She is fabulous. She totally inspired a love of anthropology in me and she is just a really great instructor. She really knows her **** and she really knows how to explain it to others.

The reviews of him had me absolutely terrified to take this class, but he is not nearly as bad as everybody else says he is. The exams are basically identical to the practice exams, which is really nice. Offered extra credit for every week you went to all 3 classes. Not too hard of a class as long as you put in some work.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: makes this class a lot harder than it needs to be- lived off practice tests. Lectures uploaded online are hard to hear, so you must go to class. slow talker for 9 in the morning.

You just have to put in a little work and you'll be fine. The exams were similar to the practice exams and knowing how to do the problem sets were also beneficial. Your grade is made up of problem sets, exams, quizzes and the final so little room for error. They can also be harsh graders on the exams, little partial credit.

Start studying now if you have to take this class. The lectures are a waste of time just study the practice exams and learn everything on your own. The discussion you have to get lucky and hopefully they give you the answers to the problem set otherwise they just cook you. Study 10x more than you think you have to.

This class SUCKS. It is confusing and the lectures do NOT help at all. You have to learn everything on your own. No one goes to class and you have to get lucky with your AI. It's not clear what to learn/memorize and it's so hectic trying to study for this class. He puts the wrong page numbers for a book that barely helps you learn the content.

Overall very boring. By the last week there were 10 people in class and it feels like you don't learn anything. The exams are garbage in garbage out and you forget it all. The exams are exactly like the practice exams but he doesn't really ever teach you how to do the homework or exam questions. You have to learn it all on your own.

Reading his reviews before the beginning of the semester made me so worried about taking this class. He might not be the most interesting lecturer of all time but I think it's clear he knows the material and the exams are exactly like the practice exams. We also got an exam drop on top of that. I thought the class was super manageable.

Prof. Forrester is a horrible lecturer. By the end of the semester, only about 10 people were showing up to class. The lectures are all recorded, so it is easier just to watch them on 2X when they are posted. The class overall wasn't too bad, but Prof. Forrester makes no effort to make his class enjoyable or helpful at all.

Great course but the content is difficult. You will do well in the course if you study the practice exams and discussion homework because that is where the exam material comes from. Discussion are super helpful and I would go to lecture because he takes exam questions from lecture content as well. Overall great professor highly recommend.

I don't think he actually cares about teaching at all. He lectures and is not concerned whether students understand what he is saying or not. There a few resources for the material. This class felt like a waste of time because it was difficult to learn anything.
Good professor, exams can be hard but the practice exams will help. Get help from discussion TA's, they can help float your grade with the discussion worksheets. Some are better than others.

Beware of him. Has been teaching for too long and couldnt give a flying.... about your progress in this course because his lectures are not reflective of his exams or even discussion material for that matter. Hardest class I have taken in undergrad - and I have taken Biochem, Orgo 2, Calculus, Neuroscience and so on. Even weekly quizzes difficult

Nothing in the lecture prepares you for this course. It is incredibly difficult to find outside resources that are helpful because he seems to make up his own way of doing things. Realistically he doesn't care at all how you do, as he has been teaching this course for so many years.

Attend lecture! Lecture notes aren't posted, and video recordings aren't posted either, so if you want to succeed in this class, attend lecture!! Use the problem sets as exam study material. Practice exams are extremely similar to actual exams, so if you understand the practice exams, you should do well on the exam. Very nice professor!

If you miss the lecture there are no additional resources to make up any loss work. No completed note templates, recorded lectures, nothing. Lectures are extremely boring and he does not go into enough depth on certain topics. Honestly my AI did a better job at having me understand topics than him.

Dr. Forrester has clearly been a professor for this exact class for too long and it seems like he really needs to update his teaching style. His lectures are very long and boring and yet my notes somehow never seem to have the information that I need to do the practice problems for discussion. My discussion UTA carried me through this entire class.

Wayne is a pretty cool guy. I don't love genetics, but he tries to keep us entertained. Note templates are a bit all over the place at times. He uploads his lectures, and exams are practically identical to the practice exams he provides. The quizzes were tough, but weren't a huge % of our grade. Do the practice problems and you'll be fine.

Tbh, you have to work in this class because if you don't it's so easy to fail. Write down everything in the lectures, your homework is graded for accuracy (go to office hours), and there are 3 major exams with a cumulative final at the end. He isn't the best at lecturing because there are a lot of holes in his notes. The exam averages were 70s.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Forrester is a great professor, but there was some topics that he did not explain clearly or would briefly explain them and then give us a problem that had nothing to do with it. The exams aren't bad, they're very similar to the practice problems he gives and he gives you old exams to study. There is a vocal section on exams with no word bank

He's a very nice guy, really encourages students to ask questions and do their best. The way he explains stuff is sometimes very confusing. Definitely ask him about anything you're confused on - he will explain stuff more in-depth if you ask. It was a hard class, but also super interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Because none of the other idiots on this page care to go into detail, if you don't like fill in the blank exams do NOT take him. Otherwise, he knows what he's talking about but his assignments are long and tedious and he's really hard to pay attention to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Forrester is a great professor. I really don't know why his reviews are so low. Study the material (ALL PAST EXAMS) and you will do well. Point blank. This semester he made us take weekly quizzes which were challenging but made you stay on top of the material. Study for those quizzes, they are more challenging than the tests.

I don't find genetics to be particularly interesting, but Professor Forrester is a pretty cool guy. All of the discussion worksheets are participation so you're essentially given a free 104 points. I recommend putting a really heavy focus on the previous exams when studying. The final, which is 40% of your grade, is hard. Study ALL PAST EXAMS.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Wayne's pretty great. He's not a thrilling lecturer, but he makes up for it by posting ALL LECTURES online, so you never have to be in class if you don't want to be. Do the practice exams; the real exams are basically identical. He drops 1 exam too. 1 discussion WS every week for participation. The Hawaiian shirts and reggae are also a win!

Material is pretty dense at first in lecture but if you rewatch the lectures that he posts in Kaltura you'll see that everything makes sense. You get to drop one exam, exams are just like the practice exams he posts, and he's a pretty knowledgeable guy. Discussion worksheets are basically a free 20% of your grade. Overall would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Genetics with Forrester was the hardest class I have taken at IU. Lectures were only helpful for learning the vocabulary for the exams. He did not prepare us for the discussion worksheets, and I spent the whole semester trying to teach myself. The exams did not reflect the practice exams and felt unfair. The setup of the course needs correction.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lots of tests and the class overall is easy but the tests do not have anything to do with lectures. Honestly, studying for this class is a waste of time because the final has no similarities to what was taught in class. Not a man of his word on grades, either.
Forrester knows what he is talking about and makes it easy to learn genetics. Its not the easiest topic to teach but his exams are fair. He is very helpful in office hours as well.

Not a fan. He seems to design the exams so that you can't finish in time. People complained, he didn't change. The discussions were minimally helpful and by minimally, I mean not at all. He isn't a bad guy, I just think the set up of his class is not the best for learning.

Has discussion classes that are listed when you register for the class. Super annoying. All the lectures are posted online but the note templates on Canvas often don't match up with the lecture slides.  40% of the grade is the final. But you can drop one of three exams throughout the semester. To me, the positives didn't outweigh the negatives.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: As someone who has always hated genetics, I was dreading this class. Professor Forrester made it bearable though. He clearly knows what he is talking about and is always willing to take questions.   I found the exams to be difficult, but manageable. I always felt like they were more difficult than the practice questions he posted.

he gives extra credit on exams if the class average is around a C. Bewear the final!! It's worth 40 percent of the grade  (200 points out of 500 in the class). the other 200 come from 2 midterm exams, and the other 100 from learning group worksheets. Don't need to attend lecture, as he uploads lectures online. Class is bearable if you study tho.

Forrester is awesome. Plays reggae music before class, tries to make genetics problems interesting, and really knows his stuff. It's easy to get behind if you miss lecture, but he posts them on the class website and is great at explaining concepts. Practice problems and past exams give you a pretty good idea of what to expect for exams.

Deceivingly difficult class. Learning groups that aren't pre-scheduled (annoying) are easy - major grade savers. Tests are like problem sets, but somehow significantly harder. Never went to him for help - didn't seem to want to deal with struggling students. Worst grade I have ever gotten in college. Final worth 40% of your final grade - very hard!

I struggled with this class because there was a lot of discrepancy between the practice problems and the problems given on the test. I got perfect scores on learning group worksheets and failed almost every test. LG worksheets may save your grade. Get to know your AIs well. Half the class dropped by midterms. Loved the topic but loathed the tests.
Prof Forrester is a great professor and often plays reggae music before lecture.  If you make sure to do the problem sets and go over old exams, you should do absolutely fine on exams.
Great teacher, extremely fair. If you practice the problems given in learning group you will have no problems on the exams they are practically identical.

His redeeming quality is that he makes the lectures available by video online, but the lecture format does not match the exams. Learning groups are more helpful than class but annoying. Success in this class requires extensive time out of class teaching yourself. Also, I was in the hospital during an exam and was not allowed to make-up the exam.

He posts lectures online, gives learning group worksheets, yet I am still questioning why I did so badly in this class. I think it might be the exams, if you forget small things, you can loose major points. Watch out for that.

Forrester is awesome! He makes genetics bearable and lets you know what will be on the exams.  Learning group problem sets are an easy 100 points so make sure you go every week.  Also, he records all his lectures and posts the podcasts after class, so you don't even have to go!
Genetics sucks. It's boring. I hate it. Easier than molecular bio and I think Professor Forrester is a good person to take it from. Just be prepared to fall asleep in lecture.

Great professor! Lectures are clear. Posts lectures & recording online, but attendance still helps immensely. Very helpful in OH and very willing to meet outside of OH. Lectures are not totally consistent w/ exams and problem sets, but DO ALL problem sets BEFORE LG and work them over, along with practice exams. Go to OH and you will succeed!

great professor.  Lecture attendance is a must, but if you do the problem sets and understand them you'll do fine.  Great class with a great professor who explains things really well.  I would recommend him very highly for this class!

Genetics was not an easy topic, but with Professor Forrester I managed to get at A. I rarely went to class because he puts all the lectures online: both the slides and his actual voice recording. It's tempting to get behind but if you stay on top of the lectures and do all homework and tests, this class is not too difficult for an upper level bio.

Lectures are not mandatory but you need to attend to do well. However, he is incredibly boring and not very helpful in office hours. He throws stupid details into the test that barely covered in lecture. I don't recommend him!
great professor! really helpful and the class is very straightforward...if you do the work you'll get the grade you deserve.
Gotta love Dr Forrester. Would certainly recommend him.
nice
It is my opinion that this is a snoozer. I would rather study bison migration in the 1880s or advanced EZ Bake oven electronics.

Oh Wayne. Genetics is one of my fav subjects and Wayne was awesome. Starts class with Reggae music ever day. Lectures are ESSENTIAL. Tests are straight forward and much like problem sets. If you go to learning group and lecture, take down the notes and study them before the test, you'll get a good grade. Highly Recommend

He's very nice professor, patient and helpful. But his notes are not well-organized. I got an A+ in his class because I studied for the exams by going over his lecture notes, problem sets, sample exams, etc. He usually gives the same type of questions on his exams and his final exam wasn't as hard as I expected it to be.
Take him. He is a wonderful teacher and is so caring for his students. This is a great gen-ed to take if you are a business major as well. I highly, highly recommend Professor Koop!
Great class and great professor! Take this class with him!

He is a super nice guy and amazing an teaching! You do have to take quite a few tests but they're open note and usually the weekly quizzes have the same/ and or similar questions, so you can use those to help study. Super chill lecture, would recommend attending because the only thing that prevented me from an A was my attendance!
One of the best professors I have had personally. Very nice and respectable. Open note assignments.

LOVE THIS MAN!  I took this for my nursing prerequisite coursework, and man am I glad I chose him.  He lays out all of what he expects very early on in the course.  His testing is all open-note, and all of the quizzes/tests are tied to the reading and lectures.  His expectations were also very fair with many drops and accommodations.  He was great!
LOVE THIS TEACHER!! TAKE THIS GUY

Professor Koop was my favorite professor this semester. He cares about all his students and got to know us very well. He is a very nice and understanding guy who makes lectures fun and makes class something to look forward to. He's easily accessible by office hours and is completely willing to help with anything.

Professor Koop is great! He cares about student success and is very funny to listen to. All quizzes and the final is open note. If you take good notes, you will be just fine. I liked the discussions as well because it connected what we learned in the classroom to real life. If you get a chance to take a class with him, do it!!!

One of my favorite professors! Honestly hilarious and makes class enjoyable and interesting. All quizzes are open note and the final exam. You can also miss five classes throughout the semester! Highly recommend taking as an easy gen ed!

AMAZING, extremely funny guy who genuinely cares about your outcome in the class. His assignments are extremely well done. I didn't particularly enjoy doing his discussions. They weren't hard, just very redundant. However, everything else was immaculately put together for student success.

Professor Koop is honestly the GOAT. This was my favorite class of the semester. He makes lectures funny and super interesting, never boring. He posts all his lectures with the transcripts online, so just go to class, and use AI to turn those transcripts into organized notes. Open-notes Quizzes, final. 2/7 quizzes dropped. TAKE him at any cost!!

Professor Koop was amazing! The class is lecture based but it's simple content and he makes it interesting. Grades were 7 open note quizzes, which he drops your worst 2, and the final which is also open note. Also small group discussions which were very easy grade boost. He does take attendance but he gives you 5 free skips. Great class and teacher

The class was fairly easy, but a lot of the content is read in the textbook readings (so take good notes!), Participation, especially for discussion days, does matter and it can tank your grade if you don't go. He's a super chill and understanding professor. However, he doesn't take late work (class is quiz and test heavy).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class was pretty easy. He literally lets you use notes on exams (and the final). Attendance matters but it's pretty easy to just attend for the points. Honestly, just a goofy guy who seems to actually enjoy doing what he's doing. I don't think he has any beef with anyone.

Great Professor, very understanding and considerate if you have issues affecting your ability to do class work. Ethics and Public Policy was pretty reading heavy and the exams are very heavy on the readings. Don't be worried about taking her class, she's great
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Failer as a professor cares about your learning more than just doing the class. She slows things down, and assignments are so easy that they take maybe an hour or 2 max a week. Readings matter slightly, but not how many other classes do. For Failer, they're merely a deeper intake than the class lecture presents.

Professor Failer seems to be a really compassionate person but there is no structure to this class. The study guides for the test do not compare to what you learn in lecture and may become overwhelming--we had a test with terms but never went over terms ever. If you like grades fast don't count on this class. Readings are EXTREMELY long.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor was knowledgeable and was passionate about the content. It is very interesting. The TAs were the worst part. Grades can be harshly graded depending on the TA.

Professor Failer is sweet, funny, and terribly chaotic. TA's grade everything, take forever, and are very inconsistent. Depending on your TA, discussion can be painful to sit through. Grading is very harsh for a 100 level class. Your grade comes from 5 assignments. I still enjoyed the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Failer is a nice woman who cares for what she teaches. With that being said, lectures are unorganized and slide shows are not posted. The TAs grade extremely hard and return grades slowly, which matters because your grade is basically based off three exams and an essay. Workshops are uninspiring and a waste of time. IF PRE-KELLEY: AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring; no information is posted. In discussion, you are simply expected to regurgitate what was said during lecture (despite emphasis on free thought). Grading is done by TA's, and inconsistent. Only 4 significant grades, including a paper that you are expected to figure out on your own. Failer often cancels with little warning.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lots of readings, but the lectures go over them pretty thoroughly. She seems super passionate and knowledgable, but is scattered and disorganized at times. Grade is from your discussion, one paper, and three exams (including the final).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is really boring, but the professor is just okay. She goes over the same slides every lecture and you can go without even going to the lectures and still pass the class. Just do the readings, look at the discussion questions she posts in the syllabus, have a good idea for each answer, then at the discussions, hope they pick the best one.

Drawn out lectures that are unorganized and all over the place. 4+ case briefs a week. She is horrible at communication and rarely responds to emails. Papers are based on confusing questions with no clear rubric or grading criteria. TA ran moot courts are horrible as he had no idea what was going on. Overall would not take this class or professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class content is not difficult. But this professor is disorganized, interrupts students all the time, boring and overall somewhat incompetent. The TA we had grades harshly. There are a lot of case briefs to submit. While she is passionate and obviously knowledgeable and credible, she is also just a bit clueless. don't take.

Ignore the optimists, this class is awful. Grading is based on vibes, rubrics are useless bullet lists, and lectures make no sense. 4+ case briefs a week that she won't be able to go over because the lectures are all over the place. She told us her expectations for the papers in April. If confusion and disappointment had a class, this would be it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Students in this class will struggle. Not because it is difficult, but because the professor is all over the place in terms of organization, notes, assignments, and lectures. Students are expected to meet expectations not specified in rubrics. Notes are poorly formatted and lectures seem all over the place. The canvas online assignments are a mess.

Judy Failer is the most amazing teacher  in this department. She is so knowledgeable, kind, and wants nothing for her students other than they leave knowing something they didn't when they walked in. She's got her own style for sure! But if you listen to what she's saying you WILL learn.

You are expected to read whole books in about a day or two. For the exams and papers, if you don't have the same viewpoint as the professor, then forget about getting a good grade. They tell you to be an original thinker but force you to regurgitate what the professor said in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor is not bad. The class is horribly boring and uninteresting. There are 4 case briefs a week, along with long drawn out lectures that are extremely hard to sit through. The foundations of the class are weirdly interpreted theories. Not my favorite class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Failer has a brilliant mind and is clearly passionate about the material she teaches, although she seems scattered often. The TAs and her are also very slow graders. Overall, a very nice woman with a lot of knowledge and passion.

If you are a pre-business student do not take this course! All grading is done by TA's who grade very unforgivingly. I was in a position where I did poorly on the first test but still struggled to raise my grade due to the weighting of the assignments. I enjoyed the material, but the grading was very harsh for a 100 level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers
