reviews.comment: Failer is a good lecturer but if you don't go to the lecture there's no way to get the content. Group dicusssions are helpful but everything is graded by TA's which sucks because they all grade differently. If you're a straight a student be prepared for that to change.

Disappointing class. All grading is done by TAs, who vary in difficulty of their grading and their interpretation of the rubric. Papers are due before the workshop you discuss content in, which doesn't make any pedagogical sense. No one was even willing to review papers to help you improve. Do yourself a favor and don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Failer is enthusiastic about content, but she's NOT ok with questions. Her TAs do everything, and she doesn't respond to emails at all, even for medical absences. The TAs each grade 1/3 of the exams and it's super inconsistent between each. She refuses to post lecture slides even when asked. There's too much reading, one was 300+ pages.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: don't take this class unless you're a masochist
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Failer is very passionate, and is silly at times, but lectures don't make a ton of sense. Goes through slides very fast, theyre confusing, and she doesnt post them online so going to lecture is necessary for notes + class is very reading based. Readings are long/hard to comprehend, there are few assignments overall, and grades take forever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hardly did any of the readings. The tests are based off of the readings so prepare to pay attention for the lectures on those. Great person, loves to teach, can sometimes get off track. Tests were kind of difficult, the information we needed to answer the questions sometimes were not clear in the lecture. very open to answering questions

Professor Failer is very passionate about what she teaches. While she doesn't post slides, you can always take pictures of the presentations. I would recommend taking her higher-level classes since they're more cohesive. The class is very text-heavy, and graded on think-piece essays but she's very caring and open to her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She assigns hundreds of pages of readings and never responds to emails. She refuses to post her lecture slides even when you request it to study, and many of the slides include content on the exams. Her TAs are nice, but they don't seem to communicate with each other and the grading is extremely inconsistent between all of the TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Failer, though knowledgeable and passionate, lacks effective communication with her students. She flies through her text-heavy lecture slides, and refuses to post them despite student requests. Learning primarily relies on lengthy, challenging readings exceeding 150 pages each night from texts that are old and hard to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Failer is very enthusiastic about teaching, which makes her class enjoyable. However, the only downside of her lectures is that you can barely ask questions. I remember many questions getting pushed aside due to time reasons. Despite this, she is available during her office hours right after class, so passing her course is not impossible.

Professor Failer is so kind and intelligent. As a senior seminar professor, she was amazing. She understands that, as seniors, everyone is very busy and stressed. If you ask for an extension, she will surely grant the request. She does assign many papers, but its an intensive writing section so you can't really expect anything different. Loved her!

Failer has her TA's do everything for her. Her lectures don't really follow the slides (NOT posted on canvas) and it is VERY reading heavy. 3 tests and 3 workshop papers for a grade but papers are due before the workshop class even though they give tips for the paper during the workshop (after it is due). You cannot ask her questions during lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You can tell Prof. Failer genuinely cares about what she teaches and the students who take her course. While most of the grading is through her TA's, she is pretty available for additional help. I would really recommend going to most lectures because it will make future exams so much easier.

Prof. Failer was very caring and available. The readings are heavy, but she goes over most of the content. Her study guides are very clear and helpful, and the papers were very attainable and easy. It is important to go to the non-mandatory lectures because you get a lot of good notes from it.

She is very enthusiastic, and her lectures are more interesting than most others. She is very transparent with what she looks for in tests and essays. There is a lot of reading, but not all of it is necessary to succeed. She handles controversial aspects of the material well. I would recommend this class to anyone who doesn't mind a bit of writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: She has her grad students grade everything and all papers were due BEFORE the discussion class on Friday, even though they would give us tips in that class on what to write about (which was really irritating because the paper had to be turned in before the class started). You can tell she enjoys the subject, but she rambles on alot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Failer is very passionate about what she teaches. Course expectations are super clear. She makes difficult assignments much easier- very easy if you just show up and do the work.

Seems like a very nice woman but is NOT a good professor. The amount of work assigned for the class is extremely excessive, and you get next to no credit for completing assignments that take an hour+ to complete each. The lectures are long, rambling, and confusing, and she doesn't post the powerpoints. Grading on assignments is also inconsistent.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're taking POLS105, try and get this professor. Just make sure you memorize the talking points about the texts from class and regurgitate them on the exams/papers you write and you'll do really well. Going to the lectures and paying attention is essential, but reading the texts isn't outside of finding quotes for your papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She teaches extremely fast and in my experience if you try to ask a question during class she gets an attitude and shuts you down. I had a medical emergency and missed a week of class and she was the only teacher who refused to work with me and allow me to catch up. The grading is inconsistent. Lack of communication between prof. and TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor and the TAs were extremely helpful and enjoyed teaching this particular class, however, I put a lot of time into the class and into the readings, so if you are interested in this field of study, I recommend this professor because she will prepare you well. I could tell she was really passionate about this class material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: So caring and enthusiastic. Really cares about her students and does everything she can to suit the course to our needs and circumstances. Highly recommend her upper level classes :)
she was very lenient and did her best to make sure the class always did as best as possible on tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Definitely one of the best professors IU has to offer! I took her class to fill a requirement and ended up loving it, would recommend taking this course!

I took her class 379 Ethics and Public Policy and she was amazing about making sure the class was fair for everyone! She definitely cares about the students. One of those teachers who really just wants you to learn and succeed.

She is literally my favorite professor ever, I would buy her flowers and chocolate, honestly the school year ending and not getting to see her anymore is sad, she cares more for her students than any other professors combined and I am not exaggerating. Biggest heart I have ever seen.

I love Judy, this is my second class with her. Reading other comments, there are defiantly fair critiques. However, if you show up, participate, read, and apply yourself, this class is really not that complicated. Just think about the context of the class and essay question for papers. She is one of the most caring professors at IU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Failer was never available for our class and missed many days so would rush material and make no sense during her lectures. The class is based upon your own research as it seems the lectures are just ramblings about random stuff. If you need easy credits don't take this class. I dropped the class with a B+ because it was unbearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awful. She had a family emergency on the first day of class and didn't show up, which I completely understand and empathize with, but she didn't notify her students or AIs. She's rude and condescending to both students and her AIs. If you can take this class with another professor, I'd do that. She's very enthusiastic, but a poor teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Failer is one of the worst professors at IU. Shes unorganized and confusing. She also changed the format of the final a week before the final and is also refusing to give us the PowerPoint slides until 3 days before the final to punish the kids who skipped lectures even though she just talks too fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. Cannot stay on track. Just goes on and on and on about nonsense. I have gained nothing from this class and literally had me consider changing my major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Let's just say she had me rethinking my political science degree within a week. I had to take this as a degree requirement. DO NOT TAKE AS A GEN ED. not worth it if you're not poly sci. Lectures are all over the place, just like everything she says. Hard to stay focused when her speech is all over the place. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hated taking this course with this prof. She is nice and clearly cares about what she is teaching, but you will be graded on very little assignments to make up your grade, so no room for error. It is Oct 25, and I still have yet to get a single grade in the class (except for one assignment graded for completion). Do not recommend at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Failer goes very fast in lectures and the PowerPoints don't make much sense. The study guides are very hard to know what to study also.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are interesting, and as long as you take notes you should be good. Prof Failer is interesting. She's sweet, and you can tell she likes what she's doing, but sometimes she's all over the place. She's trying to figure out how to use the computer and then goes back to a slide we already talked about. Definitely go to the lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: makes no sense ever I genuinely don't know why I'm in this class
Dr. Failer is very kind, but also all over the place and the grading is super arbitrary. She has a lot of courses at IU, so hard to avoid but I would if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Failer's lecture cadence & presentation structure can be hard to follow, but her passion for the course shines through. Always willing to take questions or explain a point. Exams were very straightforward. No extra credit offered. Really interesting content, and would recommend the course for that alone. Got an A & gave 5-6hrs/week class included.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: This class was difficult but I ended up with an A+. I made sure to attend office hours, asked questions, regularly followed up when I didn't perform as well as I wished on the essay/exam, and attended class via zoom the whole semester. If you are looking for an easy class, don't take this one. But it's a good law school prep class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took this class in an effort to learn more about political theory. After reading all of the material and checking up on the numerous amounts of announcements given sporadically, I can honestly say I got nothing out of the class. My TA always seemed confused and never provided helpful feedback. Overall a terrible class.

Very unhelpful instructor. She reads from the book most of the time, very disorganized with the Canvas page, never relases rubric despite students' requests. No useful feedback on assignments. I didn't even get to see my grades for the last 2 assignments. Particpation points suddenly disappeared at the end. Don't take her class.

Prof. Failer is extremely kind and showed true care for her students. However, lectures were often confusing and rushed through. Additionally, the grading scale and various rubrics put out were similarly confusing, providing more stress than reassurance. The course was interesting, but seemed an attempt to reinvent the wheel.

Professor Failer was condescending and her class was unorganized. She made several disrespectful comments to students throughout the year. Her lectures consisted of her just rambling on for 50 minutes with no clear guidelines. No powerpoints or slides, just her writing on a notepad. Discussions were pointless and the TAs seemed lost tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Failer is an okay professor. Very lecture heavy. Her lectures go on and on while you are struggling to type every little thing down BECAUSE YOU HAVE NO CLUE WHAT WILL BE ON THE TESTS! Her TA's are terrible. Incredibly hard graders for gen ED class. Don't take this class if you think it'll be easy and are looking for an easy A. Wont happen

Ethics & Public Policy is a fun class, but its difficult. There is a lot of reading of political philosophy. Lectures are OK but are definitely mandatory if you want to understand the material. DO bring something you can quickly take notes on as you should write down everything she says. Dr. Failer is very considerate and loves her job.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Failer is amazing and truly cares about her students. Shes one of the sweetest, most caring people I know. Alongside that, shes very available and goes the extra mile to help students succeed. The material is interesting and the moot courts are fun. I enjoyed writing most of the papers too! Great class and I would recommend any class with her
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Judy was my favorite professor this semester. She's funny, kind, and really knowledgeable on the topics she teaches. You do case briefs, which can be tedious, but the lectures are based on the cases so it is beneficial to read. She doesn't seem to take attendance but she collects case briefs without warning so if you aren't in class, you miss out.

Definitely one of the best professors I've ever had. She's so caring about her students and genuinely wants everyone to do well. She assigns a lot of reading, but if you just power through it it isn't too bad and you can generally get most of it out of the lecture. Would definitely recommend taking one of her classes at some point.

Professor Failer gives some of the most interesting lectures. I took intro to Political Theory and I was worried it would be boring, but it was just the opposite. Dont bother reading the material, it takes way too long and in her lectures she explains all you need to know. That being said, DONT miss and take good notes!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Failer is easily one of my favorite professors. Her lectures are always interesting and the tests are always fair. If you simply attend lecture you will do well in this class.

Overall, a pretty good teacher. Her lectures were very interesting and 90% of them were easy to understand. A couple were confusing but she always encourages people to ask questions and loves to answer them. There was a lot of reading assigned for this class but it wasn't super necessary. It might be best to have taken an ethics course already tho

Very nice woman and a pretty good teacher. She definitely knows what she is talking about when lecturing and the lectures themselves can be somewhat entertaining. The only bad thing is that she writes the subject points on the board and expects you to write down everything she says after as notes without saying when she is moving on.

After 3 years in the political science department, Professor Failer is possibly the worst professor I have had yet. She's completely disorganized - no powerpoints, outlines, or even much writing on the board. She just rambles, on and on, without stopping and expects you to write everything down, which is next to impossible. Nothing is clear here.

The lecture portion of the class is great! There is a lot of reading. Beware however, the TAs that I had were HORRIBLE. I do not believe their grading style was inlign with what prof. Failer would have wanted. They were also very unclear about why grades were received.

DO NOT take Introduction to Political Theory with her if you're looking for an easy GenEd.  That's what I did, and even though I'm actually quite interested in the materials, her TAs grade so unbelievably hard on completely subjective things that it's a killer.  And, to top it all off, they are totally unclear on why they grade the way they do.

Professor Failer is the best instructor Ive had at IU. She genuinely cares about every one of her students and is invested in their success. Incredibly intelligent, but goes out of her way to make sure that everyone understands course concepts. Dont pass up a chance to take a class with Failer, shes amazing.

Judy is very passionate during her lectures. She knows her stuff tries to make even the most driest material seem interesting. 3 one-page papers and 1 five-pager. The discussion classes were very boring and the TA's weren't very clear on their grading criteria. Readings can be found with a little googling.

This is basically an intensive writing course without intensive writing credit. She assigns between 4 and 8 cases a week, each of which you are required to summarize in 1-2 page "case brief" essays. This is on top of around 25 pages of regular essays that are also required. Easily adds up to 80+ pages of writing over the semester. Not worth it.
Great professor, tries very hard to make the information manageable. Gives you whole book assignments, tells you basically everything you need to know in the lectures, don't skip
She's really helpful and explains material very well. There was one big-ish projectpresentation but it wasn't as bad as it sounded.

Failer is enthusiastic and very knowledgeable about political theory. Her lectures are based on the readings, but I did alright in the class without doing all of the reading. There wasn’t much homework (three short papers and one large). Unfortunately, she was sometimes disorganized and even failed to respond to my emails for weeks at a time.
Professor Failer dumbs the material down to an annoying degree, but it's an easy class.  I didn't do any of the reading or go to class and I still got a good grade.

Professor Failer was wonderful! She truly cares about her students and is one of the most fair professors ever. The material is not easy but she is extremely willing to help. She allowed us to have an open note midterm and final which was wonderful!

Don't take her Y105 class if you are looking for an easy GenEd, her TAs are tough graders on almost entirely subjective material. Failer is passionate about her class but still fails to make lectures halfway interesting. Inconsistent and canceled more than a few classes for personal reasons.

Failer is an excellent professor - definitely my favorite one in my time at IU. Take her if you get the chance. Her lectures largely cover the readings, and will help you understand them, even if you fail to read some/all of them. Y304 case briefs will definitely boost your grade. Can be a tougher grader, but knowledgeable, helpful, and exciting.

She was such a great professor to have! She really cares about what she is teaching and loves the material she covers. She makes the lectures fun by including jokes but still covers all of the necessary material.

She has the attention span of a squirrel and definitely think she's the smartest person in the room. Class had no structure, and she would interject and interrupt as students were trying to make points. Didn't get grades back til the last week. Avoid her.

Taught an interesting and engaging senior seminar class on constitutional law.  Naturally, some of the students wanted recs for law school-she promised several students letters of rec and NEVER wrote them-even when reminded often by multiple students!  Unfortunately, her willingness to help her students in that department is nonexistent.

She is so passionate about this class it is ridiculous (in the best way possible). Easy class if you attend the lectures (and the discussions!). The tests are all the same and fairly easy, and you only have to do 3 one-page papers, as well as a 5 page paper!

Failer is clearly passionate about the material she teaches, but the class is structured so that a student doesn't have to actually do the readings to understand them...they tend to be covered in lecture. However, I think she is a great professor and if you have the chance, you should definitely take a class with her!

Fairly good teacher, but I found that it was fairly easy to get a good grade by just regurgitating her opinions from the lecture. She (and her TAs) aren't the easiest graders ever, but it wasn't too hard to nail the content if you studied notes from the lectures.

Prof. Failer is awesome! She is so passionate about what she does and loves teaching. The class was very interesting, just make sure you do the readings and come to class prepared. I hope I can take more classes from her in the future!
She is great and knows what she is talking about.
save yourself the time and work, and don't take her class unless you're a poly sci major.

Great professor. Very knowledgeable in her field and is fun to listen to. She expects papers to be structured a certain way and she explains in a lot of depth her expectation. Easy A if you show up to lectures and pay attention to what she has to say. Good at leading discussion.

Prof Failer's class is so inconsistent. Her syllabus does not reflect what is required of the class. There are no notes to write. she just babbles for an hour and fifteen minutes, and we are supposed to write notes from her gibberish.

One of the best profs in the political science department, but a very tough grader until you get the idea of what she wants. Case briefs will boost your grade a ton, and volunteer for a moot court; they're actually fun and will boost your grade on that paper by a full +/-. FYI: Failer is the sponsor for the Truman scholarship for IU
Grades papers tough but helpful with extra credit case briefs to boost your grade.

Outstanding professor. Papers for the class are graded critically, but she holds students to a high standard, which encourages hard work. She always prepares her lectures extensively, but allows questions to clarify the material. The class is structured very interestingly, with moot courts and task forces instead of solely lecture. Great prof!
I had Professor Failer for ethics and she was amazing.  A very sweet lady and very understanding and helpful! I highly recommend this course!
good at making you analyze concepts in depth - tough grader, but it is worth having her at least once.

Her s not have possibly been any more boring, she pretends to value students input but just pushes her interp. of the materal as the right one every time. The assignments aren't difficult if you tell her what you think she wants to hear. 2 hour lecture each day and she refused to give breaks.
She is an awesome professor, tough, but fair. She really gets you to do the absolute best you can. Very nice and makes class interesting
Extremely disorganized class. I never got anything back graded!
I had her for Con Law and Ethics; she's very knowledgeable on topics, and genuinely a nice person.  While she may grade a little tough, you learn alot in her courses!
Tough, tough grader - kind of felt like I couldn't do anything to please her.
No Comments
Very clear. Always willing to help after class. Thought-provoking assignments. Good class discussions. :-)
The class is really interesting, but grades are not easy to come by.
No Comments
she is into what she does and always willing to stay late to help you understand
Discussions are stimulating but papers are graded severely.
Grades unfairly. Do not take.

Professor Goodlander was a great directing teacher. She employs a lot of group projects so be ready to work together and always show up to class (attendance is mandatory). This course required a LOT of time outside of class to work with other students with only a little class time reserved, so be ready for that! Had a great time learning with her!

I would recommend anyone to take professor Goodlander for this course. Intensive writing is a hard class as is and she made it so interesting and genuinely fun to write. She gives many opportunities to pass. Intensive writing has a lot homework but she made the class a lot easier and fun to participate. Definitely take her if you need this credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Despite her primary academic area being theater, I thought she was a great literature teacher. She gives so many opportunities to earn a good grade, and class was always really interesting.

Absolutely hated this class. Feedback is NOT clear (while guidelines are), and the revisions count as a completely separate grade, so don't get too hype about those. The papers are busy work and a waste of time. While reviewing for the exam she refused to go back due to "time constraints" and sped through review, only to let class out 40 min early.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Loved this class. She's very clear what she's wanting from you for the papers. She allows revisions and is a fair grader. Lectures are really interesting and as far as a IW and GCC course goes, this is one of the more interesting and easier ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She has a passion for theatre history but it seems to be more about her own research than education. Reached out to her multiple times for assistance but she answered my questions with vague statements. Typically, I am an A student but struggled greatly to do well in this class.
Dr. Gantz is the best. He is very knowledgeable and taught me a lot about media, academia, and life. He rebuilt IU's NSAC class, a must take for advertising students. Also he is hilarious.

I had Prof Gantz for 6 weeks because my original teacher took medical leave. Our weekly quizzes (no exams) focused on minutia and there were two occasions where the quiz answers directly contradicted the textbook. When I reached out to him about this, he told me he hoped I got the other points and never gave me the credit. He killed my grade.

Definitely my favorite professor in the telecom department! His dry sense of humor is great. He lets you know he'll grade you like seniors, and he does have tough tests.  Moreover,  his lectures are interactive and interesting. I learned a lot; he really gets you to critically analyze the advertising world.
worst  prof I've ever seen tests are unnecessarily hard, and he was standing there announcing what you got in the test

I was really disappointed with this class and he's the only professor. Tests were unnecessarily difficult. He doesn't use OnCourse which is frustrating and unless you go to every class and read every reading, it's tough to do well. Also assigned a paper due the day after Thanksgiving break.

Professor Gantz is probably my favorite professor this semester! He's extremely knowledgeable on the topic, has a good sense of humor about himself and others and somehow gets the class to laugh at 8am! His tests are somewhat challenging.HOWEVER if you attend class regularly, take notes, and do the assigned readings you will do GREAT.

One of my favorite professors at IU thus far. T441 was one of the few classes I looked forward to going to each week. Gantz is tough but fair and really makes you think. He's always available during office hours. I appreciate that when you discuss things with him, he'll throw you a bit of a challenge just to see if you can defend what you're saying

He is really passionate about the subject but doesn't take the lives of the students into consideration all the time. Gave a test the monday after spring break and a huge group project during Little 5.

Such a good professor! I had him for L201, he was so good I am taking him again for another class. I was not good at law, but GO TO CLASS and you will do great. Best professor! Professor Hsu taught me so much about myself that I wouldn't have known if I didn't take his class. He is extremely educated in the law and a great lecturer. He always kept me engaged in the content, even when it got dry. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!

Professor Hsu makes it very difficult to focus on so many aspects of the course material. Answers a million hypothetical questions and makes it difficult to pay attention to the actual material behind the course. Makes students quizzes take-home but you never see the right answers. I am positive that he'll improve as this is his first time teaching

It was a 6 week class and there was massive amount of  material to cover, and he would post review material, a day before the final exam. He did the exact same thing quizzes too! On top of that, he would not post the modules and lecture notes, until after the lecture!! He is a sweet person tho!

Teacher isn't good but isn't thaat bad either. Class is mandatory but you don't learn a whole lot from lectures, the labs teach you a lot more. The tests can be a little hard but if you study they are easy and the rest of the class is lowkey drones so the curves are insane.

Categorizing this course as "introductory" is so misleading. He never shows up to class on time, and his lectures are so unorganized and counterproductive. Homework/assignment instructions are never clear. He releases unhelpful study material only 2 or 3 days before exams, as if it's supposed to make a difference.

This is genuinely the most confusing, frustrating, and aggravating class I have ever taken, despite it supposedly being an "introductory" course. The professor is unorganized, never shows up to class on time, and his lectures are literally so inefficient. You WILL leave class feeling significantly more confused than you were the day before.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: As a computer science major, this is genuinely, and I truly mean genuinely, the worst class I have taken so far. Mitja does not do anything other than read the slides word for word, yet expects you to completely understand the topic after a few slides. I am begging, whoever is reading this, please avoid any class that has his name attached to it.

He's more concerned with proving to students that he knows more than them than he is with actually teaching the content. Refuses to use basic examples for an intro class. Arrives 5-10 minutes late without fail. Bans laptops in lecture but fails to provide any value from what hes saying because of his poor English and examples beyond an intro level.

Lectures are as boring as can be. He kind of just fumbles around, attempting to show examples while going over 50+ slides, which he never even makes it through fully. Exams tend to be identical to the reviews, as long as you can memorize those, you should be fine. Homework is time consuming and covers topics way beyond the suggested "Algebra 2."

I've only been in this class for 3 weeks and I hate it more than words can express. They don't grade any assignments manually and have an “aUtOgRaDer” machine do it for them. Homework has incredibly unclear instructions. They claim you only need basic math skills beforehand which is a lie because they use incredibly calculated math.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was easily one of the worst classes ever. The professor was completely ineffective, explaining concepts either in a rushed, useless way or overcomplicating them into nonsense. Lectures dragged painfully slow, barely covering half the slides, leaving students confused, bored, and frustrated. A total waste of time—avoid this class at all costs.

This is an absurdly difficult class for an "introductory" course. The course is terribly structured, and the homework assignments are unclear at best. The course says you only need "high school algebra" to do well, but the homework covers many advanced topics in mathematics, biology, chemistry, and more.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture is a gigantic waste of time. Homeworks cross the line between challenging and downright frustrating - written very poorly and hard to comprehend. Also, despite them saying you only need a basic understanding of high school algebra, be prepared to deal with calculus, linear algebra, and complex numbers regularly on assignments. Frustrating!

This course just sucks. There's no structure to it BUT I had to sit through Mitja's class for 2 weeks when Hamid was sick and I will say he is just way better. Not sure why he's rated so low because Mitja's actually interactive with the slide and attempts to teach unlike Hamid.

Took last semester. Described as an "introductory" course with "no prior experience needed" FALSE. Only take this class if you know what you're doing and can teach yourself. Lectures only cover half of material needed. The rest is expected to be learned on your own time. Homework is a nightmare. Complexly written, no clear instructions. Good luck!

Horrible horrible horrible horrible horrible. This is one of the worst professors at IU. I recommend he changes professions. For people without much experience in CS, YOU WILL STRUGGLE; in fact, if you don't go to office hours, you are guaranteed to fail. Lectures are extremely easy compared to the homework, which contains extremely difficult math.

Nice guy, but about as stale as an Ikea furniture collection. He would probably work there if he werent a coder. Homework is 50% of the grade, but dont be fooled; you will learn to shamelessly copy code from fake friends you will make along the way. Lectures are pointless. I could learn more from my dreams than from attending them. Feel bad for TAs

Hmeljak wrote the content for C200, but my lectures were taught by another professor. The class is like 50% assignments, 50% midterm and final. Lectures rarely were relevant to the homework that week, and I nearly never went. Focus on understanding and completing homeworks on your own, and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you've ever wondered what a stroke is like, this class is it. Avoid lectures. It's time you can never get back in your life. If you must go, bring a pillow so you won't hit your head when you lose consciousness. Completely inept at teaching. I'm genuinely curious as to why he chose to be a professor and how he has a job. Truly a fever dream.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class over the summer and was impressed how much information I was able to retain in such a short time. If you do not go to lecture you will fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Easily the worst professor I've ever had. He shows up late to every single lecture, never checks his email, and seems like he doesn't communicate with TAs at all. Genuinely don't know how he still has a job. Also the homework for this class will take up 12 hours of your week and doesn't even help you get better at coding.
All of the lectures are already posted, and he rarely even gets to half of the slides. I would focus more on going to office hours and getting the hw done
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Awful

I've not had a more difficult class than this before. You do have quizzes graded for participation, which are important not to miss. I believe I attended them all, and the professor gave me a bonus point (11/10) which boosted my grade from a B to an A-. Attend the labs, do the homework in chunks, review the slides. Best of luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Robotically reads slides without much explanation. While attendance isn't mandatory now, surprise pop quizzes are worth 15% of final grade. If you're considering the class, self-learn (YT&W3) and coordinate with peers for pop quizzes. Daklic might be a better choice. Communication between the TA and professor isn't great, and I skipped lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This course was horrible. Professor constantly made it through less than 30 slides leaving the rest for us to read, which would be fine if there werent 70-90 slides every class. Made lots of jokes that didnt land and then would repeat them throughout the week. Had a poor hold on the class, one student would waste 15 minutes of lecture every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: "Lab" assignment after every class, assignment due over the weekend, and expects you to do the weekly readings. Also is a strict grader for the assignments. The assignments have weird instructions and he won't cover key concepts until you ask. Just a weird guy. Always shows up late and has an excuse every time. I'd avoid this class. Joke of a prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The class itself is meh, not too bad I guess. I think he just gives too much homework for a 3 credit class and his lectures are not good. Very boring lectures, only reads from slides. Doesn't explain key concepts on homeworks. Has a lab every lecture that could take some time. Expects us to also do weekly readings. Just an annoying professor.

DO NOT take him by any means. If you can, take Daklic, the main course instructor. Mitja often is hard to understand and I skipped his lectures and went to different ones from others profs. He rarely goes over examples in class and gets sidetracked a lot. Just an overall bad prof.

Always late to lectures. Doesn't seem to be communicating with the CompSci department. We started actual learning 3 weeks after classes had started. Jokes don't land, and he makes a lot of those. AI's are also pretty unorganized because they aren't briefed by their professors. Makes it so hard to want to be in class and attend lectures.

Very awful and a joke of a professor. He assigns way too many labs and problems sets and does not release them until the last minute rather than giving us the whole weekend. He expected us to complete more labs within a 6-week period which was way more than in the fall/spring. On top of that, it would take up all of our exam study time. Ridiculous

Terrible professor. He does not release the lecture materials nor the assignments until the last minute!!!  The only reason I took this course over the summer is bcuz it's a prereq for the courses I'm taking in the fall. Otherwise, I wouldn't recommend it over the summer as it goes extremely fast-paced.

This guy is clinically insane. His instructions make absolutely zero sense for anything and he just expects us to understand what to do.  Not even a hard class, just a very bad professor who should rethink his career choice.

Dude kicks people out of class for their mask slipping off their nose once or twice. Barely understandable most times. Gives the worst formatted lectures I've ever had. Watch out for the weekly homework, cause he never actually teaches you what you need for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor has a very poorly structured class. I do not enjoy any of the lectures knowing that I will have a task that could take hours to complete and he calls it a "lab". On top of that there is a homework assignment to do as well. He is not down to earth and does not like talking to his students. Nothing is graded and it is week 6 of classes
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Took summer class, first 4.5 weeks were a piece of cake. Last 1.5 weeks crammed like half of the course (graphs) and were pretty awful. For context, I also started working the last week because I expected the difficulty to remain about the same. Also, didn't like the textbook (Weiss java). The CLRS algorithms book was a more useful reference
All the expectations were clearly communicated. Workload isn't too bad compared to other classes. The coursework is pretty interesting
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Let me just list the bad things about the class: 1. You don't get to see your grade until the end of the semester. 2. There is a lab for every lecture and is due that day or the next 3. Does not prepare you for the final project 4. The final project is 55% of your grade and he only give you 3 weeks to do it with an outrageous amount of work to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Gave out homework with only a few days to do it so you couldn't go to office hours. AIs didn't know what was happening more than a week in advance. Didn't recieve major grades for a month and a half. Lectures were confusing. You have to read every assignment, but if you don't go to class you'll recieve a zero because you didn't do the lecture task.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: NO grade until your final, most of the work learn it your own.

Grading assignments took upwards to a month to complete, lectures are not very interesting to watch, had to have a meeting to figure out if a PRACTICE ASSIGNMENT could be graded, only gave extra credit at the end, was TERRIBLE at posting updates on stuff important to class, couldn't even upload a practice exam used in-class before final.

Worst class I have ever taken at IU. This professor would release homework assignments at the end of the week when there were no more office hours to utilize, and trust me the office hours are needed! He never released the grades, so I was stuck wondering how I was doing in the class all semester long. The AI's are lazy. Do not take this with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great teacher, offers lots of extra credit, consistent homework load through out the semester that isnt too bad, lets you use a notecard on exams
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Just gonna post a warning for all future Hoosiers: this class has a ton of group projects. Some of your groupmates will be terrible. If you're not comfortable with that, don't take this class...

Most of the time, his homework is unclear to the point where the TA's also don't understand what the homework wants. His lectures consist of what we previously learned and are hardly helpful on assignments. He allows you to resubmit assignments for better grades, but grades are put in so late all at once that it is hardly helpful.
Mitja was a respectful and effective lecturer. He did a good job of fitting a larger course into just 8 weeks.

His assignments were never up on time, he reuses material from other courses and doesn't bother to change the incorrect information, when he did upload the assignments they were all worded cryptically. The icing on the cake was he has a re-submission policy, but we had no grades to try that policy with until last day of the class.

His lectures had almost nothing to do with the homework and he never explained things well. Very awkward professor, seemingly nice guy, but he never even introduced himself or told us anything about himself. Never told us how to pronounce his name either. Not very personable, lectures were pointless.

Best professor to take if you're pre-kelley. Offers more than 20 points of extra credit and exams are similar to in-class material. If you take notes, ask questions, and go to class, getting an A in Graf's class is easier than you think.
Too many canvas announcements, assignments feel like busy work, and lectures aren't useful for those that took AP Macro.
Sitting through his lectures, unless for some odd reason you REALLY love Econ, makes you actually want to listen to nails on a chalkboard.
Great teacher, class was pretty easy.

Self obsessed and actively does a lot of things to hurt students trying to succeed. Will never make any accommodations for anything that students actually need and is so stubborn he wont ever lesson to any suggestions.
Unfortunutely, he does more talking then teaching :( So his class is very stressful. He has potential, but...I'm not sure he can improve at this point.

Pay attention in lectures. Graf makes sure to provide time for questions, and lectures are how to learn the content. Lectures prepare you extremely well for exams, although exams are hard. Extra credit makes up for the harder exams than those of other professors.

Professor Graf is an amazing professor who tries his very hardest to make long lectures about a subject that most don't like engaging and interesting. Take advantage of the extra credit opportunities and make sure you study extensively for ALL of the exams. They are harder than you expect.

If I ever get a chance to take this class again, I would. His exams were really tough but he gives out tons of extra credit to help make up for your grade. I averaged around a 76 percent on the exams, but all the opportunities for extra credit and easy points made sure I finished with an A- in the class.

Professor Graf is a super nice guy, and gives lots of extra credit. His lectures were always pretty interesting (coming from someone who doesn't enjoy Econ). He likes to throw curveballs on tests, so make sure you study hard and go to the CL sessions! He gives lots of study materials, which is useful, but he doesn't make it easy to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Econ is genuinely a harder course at IU, but Graf was always highly regarded. He gives a ton of extra credit opportunities to try and help those who need a B+ or higher for Kelley. Even though the topic might be hard to grasp, Graf is definitely knowledgeable, and he is a chill professor. I recommend him over some of the other professors for B251.

Professor Graf was wonderful, but the course was challenging. If you didn't take micro in high school, be prepared to spend a lot of time on Youtube to learn. Lecture was fine but sometimes boring, but Professor Graf made it as interesting as he could. Extra credit saved my grade considering the test questions were sometimes very niche.

Take Graf if you can! Graf is one of the best professors I have ever had! He makes his lectures interesting and has activities but his tests are harder compared to other teachers. He is willing to help and gives a lot of extra credit (I think he gave around 37 points). The amount of extra credit balances out. Do the work and you will be fine :)

Great teacher who genuinely is interested in the material covered and cares about students. Lectures can be a bit boring especially if you took economics in high school, but he still makes it fun and easy to understand. If you attend lectures, read the textbook, and take advantage of the extra credit he gives out, you should be fine.
Despite my grade, he was a phenomenal professor. Very passionate about Econ and will help you in any way he can. He gives tons of extra credit to help your grade too.

super hard exams but lots of extra credit to help. his lectures were long but i thought he kept the class engaged. biggest takeaway is really study for exams, he throws in lots of questions meant to trip you up, just memorizing the terms isn't enough. can't stress how much extra credit opportunities there are tho

The best Econ teacher at IU! He offers extremely generous extra credit that students should take advantage of. The class should be a breeze if you took Micro in high school, but students new to economics may find the concepts challenging at first. Professor Graf reminded me of my favorite dorky uncle (in the best way possible)!

Amazing professor! If you took Econ in high school you'll be completely fine, even if you didn't it's still doable. So much extra credit too. Pay attention in class and do the top hat reading and you'll be fine.
Just lock in on tests and you'll be fine.

If you have taken AP Micro in high school this class isn't too difficult. Read the textbook alongisde lectures, it makes the material a lot easier to understand. Lectures were a bit boring, but he taught the concepts pretty well. Overall, the exams were a bit difficult compared to other professors but he offers a lot more extra credit as well.

I like paul graf as a professor, i just personally didn't like the lectures. I find it hard to follow and stay focused for the hour and 15 minutes. tests are hard but he gives a bunch of extra credit which is great

Great lectures—sort of boring, but it's economics so you can't expect much else. Funny guy, passionate and explains things very well. Grades reasonably and course is very structured, so you should not run into any problems. Also, extra credit opportunities are numerous. If you study well (exams are self-studyable), then you will be fine. Take Graf!
Test extremely difficult for no reason and class doesn't prepare you for them

Mirco Economics was one of the harder courses I took this semester. Lectures and long but Graf does a good job keeping class engaged. Tests are all multiple choice but do require ALOT of studying. What saved me is the absurd amount of extra credit given out. Out of all the economics professors, I would recommend Graf.
he gives a lot of extra credit, just be ready to work hard

Class is pretty light, but the lectures are boring. The textbook does a great job of explaining the concepts and is good for studying. Tests were not super difficult and Graf gives a lot of extra credit.

If you attend the lectures and take notes, you will do completely fine. It is important to study for at least a week before the exam, because there is a lot of content. His lectures are engaging, and he gives real-life examples to help with understanding. The tests are not impossible, just challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: its less about the professor more about the class. Genuinely the hardest thing EVER. B251 sucks it's so hard exams are SO HARD. I debate my life choices walking to class every Tuesday and Thursday. I know so many Kelley and pre Kelley drop outs bc of ts. notes are posted blank so u will show up, boring and hard to pay attention to. weed out class
BRO MAKES NO SENSE
Really sweet professor, good at teaching what he does. Didn't find his class bad at all, and he does give EC.

Horrible lectures, not engaging, completely useless in-class notes. Only the textbook matters, tests are the hardest I've taken in my life. Too many gotcha questions, actual content does not help regardless of the effort you put in. Genuinely insane tests, do not take this class, take Schwendel if you want a normal class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I would recommend Professor Graf. He is very kind and wants to see his students do well. He often makes jokes that make the lecture not seem as long. Pay attention and go to office hours for help.

His exams are much more difficult than other B251 professors, but he gives a ton of extra credit so that his grade distributions still end up being the same as other classes. His lectures cover pretty much the exact same material as the textbook. Study a LOT before the exams and know the textbook like the back of your hand and you'll be good to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All lectures. Make sure to go to class or you will lose easy points. Class is hard but every B-251 class is hard. He gives lots of extra credit.

Nice guy, lots of Extra Credit. Material is easier than B251 but tests are harder. Mandatory attendance (TopHat with location verification) and u need to go to get the completed notes. If u put in the studying for each quiz and exam and pay attention to the slides the class is lwk light. If u slack it will be harder. I'd take Graf again for 252.

I would say if you did well on ap micro in highschool then take graf, you'll already know most of the content so the tests won't be too bad, and he gives TONS of extra credit to carry your grade. He's a great guy, but doesn't explain the content super well, and his tests are harder than other profs. I mostly relied on prior knowledge for exams.

Professor Graf is an amazing professor. I had him during the Fall 2022 semester and he always hosted the most interesting lectures. He also gives plenty of extra credit, so if you mess up an exam, you can still pass with a good grade. My exam got lost and he spent 30 minutes looking through stacks of tests just so I could get a grade. Amazing guy.

Very passionate about econ, good lecturer but can sometimes feel confused or bored but I think that's more on me.  Not an easy class and the exams make up most of the grade, but he gives a ridiculous amount of extra credit.  Funny dude too, Graf was one of my favorite professors this semester.
Easily the best teacher I have had at IU. Great lecturer and provides considerable extra credit opportunities to take stress off of exam performance. He's the reason I chose to add an economics minor

Prof Graf is a great professor. He is super engaging and he makes his lectures interesting. Graf has a sense of humor that makes the class fun.
His grading policies are strict and TopHat attendance is taken, so make sure you have it set up right because you will not be counted present even if you show up to class every time.

I actually hate econ but he made it okay and understandable. I had him for his hybrid class and based on what I heard, I would take that instead of having him for the huge lecture because it's more flexible. Gives extra credit which is nice, and is available to ask questions especially before exams.
Professor Graf is a very good professor and cares about his students. Make sure to try very hard on the tests. I think he is the best econ professor.

I enjoyed my time in Professor Graf's class and will make it a priority to get him when I take B252. I thought that he did an excellent job with lectures, but they did sometimes get a bit boring. Rather than dropping so many quizzes and attendance to give you grace, he gives it in terms of extra credit. Do every attendance, quiz, discussion, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Graf attempts to make econ fun and exciting, when it really isn't. He gives lots of extra credit and makes sure to assist students who want to do better and get a good grade. If you're motivated, you can do well, if you simply don't care to do your work, you will do poorly. This class depends on you not Dr. Graf.

TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! The class is hard, but if you take the notes the way he does and pay attention in class he pretty much tells you what to study for. Ended the class with a B, because I didn't take my notes like him for the first section. 3 tests, last one is cumulative. make up like 60% of your grade combined. If you can take hybrid do it!

Graf is a great guy and he tries his best to teach but for someone who hasn't taken micro before, the class was pretty hard. He goes too fast in his lectures to make notetaking worth your time. I'd recommend only showing up for the TopHat points and then taking notes on your own from the E-Book. Be sure to get all extra credit and you'll be fine.

Funny guy who wants you to succeed. It's as if your fun uncle is teaching you Economics. Tests are tough but an insane amount of extra credit is offered. Would pick him over any other teacher even though his tests are said to be the most challenging.
I loved Prof. Graf, and you can tell that he genuinely loves economics. He's funny and wants you to succeed. Gives a lot of extra credit, but Exams are tough.

Very good professor - you can tell he cares about and genuinely enjoys what he teaches. Be sure to do the extra credit opportunities and come to class. Tends to talk and explain concepts very quickly if he runs out of time so beware of that. Overall a phenomenal professor

Very funny and knows how to teach economics. Concepts are made to be easily understood. Lectures are very enjoyable and there is a lot of opportunity to learn and grow in the class. He forces you to think out of the box and apply concepts to the real world. Very fun class.
Very good lectures that kept me focused.

Prof. Graf is an amazing person. However, econ is hard to begin with and Graf overcomplicates topics making it even harder. The class is entirely on power points which typically aren't finished in class. The tests are hard but curved. He offers extra credit, and attendance is taken twice daily, with a is a weekly quiz. It's very possible to succeed
Never really got to know him but seemed like a cool person. Gives a bunch of extra credit but he truly just overcomplicates all the topics from ap macro and micro.

I enjoyed Professor Graf. Although the concepts in the class are pretty challenging, the energy he has makes it worth while. Be prepared to take notes and study, though. You will not do well if you don't prepare for exams. The extra credit he gives at the start of the semester is AMAZING though.

Professor Graf is an engaging lecturer who makes economics interesting. The class has a lot of extra credit opportunities to boost your grade, but the tests can be challenging. I found unstuckstudy and ChatGPT helpful for study prep.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. No curves for exams, and 5 points of extra credit only. This is not the first time of taking an Econ class, he makes everything confusing, even in the exams. He said he likes doing that because he can see if you have really understood the concept or not. Nonsense. Do not take his class.
I think Graf is the best econ prof for B251. Lectures were easy to follow and tests are not bad at all. He gives insane extra credit, even with not so great test scores I did well in the class.

Professor Graf is a cool professor, but Top-Hat in this class sucks. I haven't missed a single class but I don't have half of my Top-Hat points. Also, don't to the practice exams, because it is not helpful at all. The tests are challenging, and he doesn't curve it at all. Be prepared for the tests.

Loves his job and is nice and caring to the whole class. Not the best at teaching either sometimes not clear. Econ isn't the most interesting thing especially for 1h15mins. Test Heavy and a bit hard. Extra Credit will carry your grade so be ready to do all of it.

I found Graf funny and felt like he loved economics. There is tons of extra credit and it is very easy to really boost your grade with it. There's a lot to be said about the tests but in my experience I was able to get atleast a B on every test with only a day or two of studying and just taking good notes in class. I have not taken econ prior.

Prof. Graf makes Econ a much easier subject to understand. He wants to see his students succeed and helps us do so by having extra credit opportunities that require us to further our knowledge in the course. He could go more in-depth during lectures, but he also wants to make sure he can cover all of the difficult material in class.
WORST PROFESSOR. WILL MANIPULATE UR GRADE WHENEVER HE WANTS EVEN AFTER THE SEM. DO NOT TAKE HIM
Graf is funny and very engaging in economics. By far the best B251 professor and with the extra credit you should be able to get an A by simply going to class and doing the quizzes.
He did a great job explaining concepts and trying to keep the lectures entertaining! He also was very considerate of the students that might have been confused! Great professor overall!

Econ is not my strong-suit, but I'm glad I took the class with Graf. The lecture topics were difficult for me to understand, but he did a great job with explaining and it's clear how passionate he is. If you're lost from the lecture, use the ebook - it helped me a lot! He also gives a TON of extra credit. Study, attend class, use the resources!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Graf is probably the BEST econ professor you can get. His lectures are somewhat boring but he makes the the content very understandable. He also gives out a TON of extra credit that you should do no matter what. I did all the extra credit and ended the class with an A (averaged a low B on the exams). Be prepared to study for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Graf gives a large amount of extra credit if he didn't the whole class would be failing. Graf is caring and a very nice guy but the class overall is extremely hard and the thing that prepares you the most for the tests is the Tophat readings. The lectures did not help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Graf's nice but goes through slides too quickly and makes everything more complicated than it has to be. If you haven't seen the material before it could be rough, but if you've taken it before it's light work. So much extra credit, it's unreal & I ended with over 100%. Go to the CLs and do a few reps of the practice quiz/exams and you're good.

Graf gives a lot of extra credit so as long as you do good on 1 or 2 tests and decent on the other, get your assignments in, the class isn't too bad. A lot like high school microeconomics if you took that. Just make sure you attend class and do the top hats

Difficult concepts. Nice guy but speeds thru lectures. Lots of extra credit- can get good grade even if u do shit on tests. This is the Easiest b251 class you can get bc of the EC, almost 30 points. Take graf over the other teachers.

Professor Graf is a great guy, that being said his class was very difficult for me. The practice material and quizzes did not help prepare for the tests at all. I would get all the answers right on on the practice tests and quizzes and still get a C-D on the tests. I still ended up with a B+ due to the large amount of extra credit though.

Graf's class was very structured and he gave so much extra credit that I was never worried about my grade in the class. There isn't much work outside of class either. One part I didn't like was that he would sometimes run out of time at the end of class and send us the rest of the notes, but these concepts were often the more difficult ones.

Graf's very enthusiastic and friendly and gives enough extra credit that you can get a B+ even if you only recieve D's on all exams. However his class would be way too difficult for anyone who hasn't taken econ before. Tons of extra credit to make up for it tho. Study the e-text.

Prof Graf is a great professor! If you can, take the hybrid online class through him, and try to get a smaller class size. I put minimal time into this class throughout the semester and studied before the exam and ended with an A. Make sure you read the textbook religiously and utilize all the practice material you get. Exams are hard and complex.

I took Professor Graf because I heard he was the easiest to get a good grade in. I would agree with that; he gives lots of extra credit, which is a great cushion for the rough exams. He is a great guy, funny and keeps the lectures light, but a terrible teacher. I felt he taught the material very complicatedly, making lectures a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Graf is a nice guy, but the class is way too hard for no reason. He doesn't post full versions of the notes and there are quizzes every week. Exams are hard and not like the practice exams he posts at all. He does give a good amount of extra credit.
Hard

Prof. Graf gives an insane amount of extra credit. He does not post the full notes online, so make sure you write down anything you wont remember. There is plenty of opportunity to get help through tutoring services and collaborative learning. The second exam is much harder than the first, exams are NOT like the practice exams he posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Graf gives a truly insane amount of extra credit during the first three weeks. Class is difficult if you put no effort in, but if you pay attention and study it's not that bad. Graf is an extremely personable guy who is very good at lecturing to 300 people. His attendance policy is kinda strict (a point per class). Would recommend him.

The absolute worst professor ever. I went to office hours every week and did all the extra credit and still ended with a C+. He did not care about the efforts that I put in. The tests are extremely hard and the reviews have nothing to do with the tests. The tests are meant to trick you so do not trust the exam reviews that he gives.

Best professor for econ out of all the others I've seen and heard of. There's a ton of extra credit. Got a D on my first two exams and got an F on the last one, passed the class with a B. I still had to put in lots of effort and work. I attended all CL sessions and did all extra credit. Participation is graded, never missed a class.

Professor Graf is a good professor, it's just that his lectures mainly cater to those who actually care about the subject. He is generous and gives out TONS of EXTRA CREDIT at the beginning of the semester, so take advantage of it. I definitely would've stayed in the class and done better if I had put in more effort.

Graf is a really great guy. He is fair, responsible, and on top of everything in his class. It can be challenging if you fall behind or it's your first-time learning econ, but Graf gives a ton of extra credit. 

Go to every single class (for EC), get 100% on every Quiz and Packback. These are free points which I regret not taking full advantage of.

Although Graf's not lenient when it comes to missed deadlines, he offers A LOT of extra credit and will bump your grade up at the end of the semester if you're close enough to the next letter without you having to reach out to him. However, attendance is graded. Nonetheless, there's no reason you should take any other B251 professor.

Graf was a good teacher. I really liked his class and the fact that he offers so many extra credit opportunities, which if you can you should do them all! The only difficult part was that there is just so much content to go over it can feel like an extremely large workload when reviewing. He is the best economics teacher you will be able to take.
He was fine. Find friends in the class for help and with different assignments. Going to class helps and actively taking notes. This class was harder than B251
The professor is great, he is trying his best to give extra credits. But the materials, Econ, is little bit hard for me.

Graf is an amazing lecturer and I enjoyed his class. Some concepts can be boring but he acknowledges this and does his best to get through it. He always engages with students and promotes discussion. He also gives quite a bit of extra credit, though exams can be a bit tough. I had never taken a real econ course before this and got an A just fine.

Great lecturer if you attend every class. No reason to look at textbook he goes over all of it in class and always was very kind to all students. Definitely take him if you can for B251 you won't regret it.

I almost never know what is going on during Graf's lectures or exams, but he gives out so much extra credit that you can bomb a few assignments and still do well. Complete every extra credit assignment, and you'll likely have a 100 going into the final. Overall, he's a fun and understanding professor.
Mans gave me a teapot. Also got so much extra credit, I ended Econ with a 103%
Wierd guy, likes to teach the subject tho.  Got to study really really hard for the tests to do good.  Pretty easy to get a 3.0 or better.

Prof Graf is great. His tests are difficult so be sure to read the textbook and take advantage of every practice resource. CTS review sessions are also good. He gives A TON of extra credit so it makes up for the hard tests. Go to class to get the participation. He is caring, funny, and fair.

You NEED him for Econ. Do not take anyone else. He gives so much extra credit and is a very good lecturer. The quizzes are very hard, but you get two attempts and see your answers after the second, which other teachers do not do. He is super nice and helpful.
He is decent at teaching the material but he is not understanding at all. Will not budge to fix grades even when the problems begin and end with himself.

Professor Graf genuinely enjoys teaching and loves economics. His lectures are infused with helpful examples and sarcastic humor. He is my favorite professor this semester, and I admire his dedication to fairness for all his students. Exams are difficult, but if you attend lectures and complete homework, you'll be fine! Highly recommend!

One of the best professors I took this sem. Graf gives a lot of extra credit and does not take it for granted. I did all the extra credit and it helped save me from stress when it came to the final for the class. If you took AP macro/micro in hs, this class would be relatively easy. Pay attention during the lectures and always ask questions.

Very good guy and seems enthusiastic about what he does. Gives out extra credit like candy so get as much as you can, it'll help if you bomb one of the 3 exams. Lectures can become boring and it's easy to lose focus but he does his best to keep everyone engaged so just focus in for the class period and you will do great!

3 exams in the class, lots of extra credit. I finished with a 95.48 and had an 83% average on exams. He doesn't curve but he sometimes tosses out a couple questions. I did all the EC. I would only study the day or two before and prioritize Top Hat (the textbook). The CTS econ review sessions are helpful too. Overall, very doable class if you study.

Prof. Graf was really good all around. Lectures were great and he is passionate about economics, can be funny too. Tests are tough and not usually curved but extra credit is offered to make up for it, through TopHat and CL Sessions. Many practice quizzes and resources available for studying. Put in enough time and effort and 251 will be manageable.

Professor Graf went above and beyond to keep my class engaged during lectures. You could tell he genuinely wanted his students to succeed which is why he gave a lot of extra credit. The material could be a bit challenging at times but he always gave us a lot of resources to use to practice before tests.
An all around really great teacher. You can tell he really wants you to succeed but also makes sure you are learning as much as you can. Such a great guy!

This is the best econ professor. Don't get me wrong, B251 is a difficult class, very content heavy but I couldn't have done it without Graf. His lectures are amazing and interesting. Try not to skip too many classes. There's 3 exams throughout class. Make sure to study and get all the extra credit that you can.
He is very passionate about the subject and gives tons of extra credit. This is one of my favorite classes. Extremely respectful, approachable, and loved by his students

Graf gives super difficult tests, but he also gives a lot of extra credit that helps to offset the tests. Make sure to take advantage of all the extra credit you can. It was evident that Graf is super passionate about econ and wants to instill that in his students. His lectures are decent but cover a lot of material in a short amount of time.

I am a Junior now and took Professor Graf first semester of my freshman year for Econ. To date, he may still be my favorite professor. His mix of quality lecturing and humor along with true care for students he was teaching created a great environment for learning. I absolutely highly recommend taking him, specifically for 251.

To all the freshman trying to get into Kelley don't underestimate this class. Professor Graf is a funny, knowledgeable man but the departmental exams will haunt your dreams. If you're reading this and have/plan to copy off of your friends' weekly quizzes you'll likely contribute to SPEA's increased enrollment for next year. Good luck :).

Professor Graf is super kind, offers a lot of extra credit, and is always willing to help. CL sessions were really helpful. Personally I struggle a lot with macro, and he was always willing to sit and work with me. It's hard to do badly in a class with a Professor that cares so much about his students. Definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Graf really makes understanding economics easy with entertaining and substantive lectures. The only parts I didn't like about his class came purely from the large class size and already having a microeconomic background. Overall, an easy class as long as you take time outside of class to understand the material more thoroughly. Great Prof

A MUST HAVE PROFESSOR! Professor Graf is truly a great professor. If you show up to class, go to CL sessions and take notes, you will get the grade you deserve. I am not saying this class was easy by any means. Sometimes the tests felt like they were nearly impossible but if you do all the extra credit he gives you, you will do just fine.

He is an engaging professor making class materials interesting. Graf tended to run out of time and couldn't finish lecture notes. Instead, he sent out completed notes after class. Tests are difficult, but if you go to class, do quizzes, and read the textbook, you'll be fine. Compared to other professors, he is one of the best.

Professor Graf is a pretty good lecturer and has a good understanding of the class. The actual lectures are arguably a bit confusing if you don't look at the material beforehand. Paul balances extra credit with exam difficulty, so you should be able to pass if you show up to class and/or CL sessions.
Graf is interesting in lecture and gives plenty of extra credit to help you succeed. Attendance is required but you won't find a much better lecturer in the ECON department.

Professor Graf is a really caring professor who wants to see his students succeed. He is more than willing to offer over SEVEN PERCENT of extra credit, which can be earned by doing just a little bit extra. The CL sessions he holds don't seem to be too helpful, but he is very good at explaining concepts and tough material. 12/10. Comedian too.

Professor Graf is a great professor! His classes are tough but he gives out so much extra credit it makes up for it. Also if you go to office hours and get to know him he is more than willing to round your grade for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Boring and practice exams are nothing like the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Graf is hands down the best Econ Professor ever. He gives so much extra credit that it is truly hard to fail his class. Tests can be difficult but if you go to class, and do the quizzes, you should be fine. Do not miss any extra credit, you will need it in the end. If you really want to learn Econ and get a good grade, enrol in his class.

Not an exceptional professor by any means. High school economics teachers are much more capable than professor Graf. However, the class is extremely easy. To get less than an A in B251 with Graf is a challenge I didn't attend class the whole semester, did well on tests and did extra credit outside of attendance. Finished with a 99.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Absolutely loved Mr. Graf. Really cares about his students and is very passionate about what he does. He gives out extra credit like it's candy.

He gave a ton of extra credit scores so no need to be worried if you did all of them. Moreover, his lecture is very interesting and funny helping students felt comfortable in his class. However, his test is very difficult and he gave limited practice tests. It hard to get a high score, but if you worked extremely hard, you could make it.

Econ is hard for some, but Paul does everything possible to give students the best scores. Offers a mountain of extra credit if you attend and participate.
