Lectures can be long, but he is good at teaching difficult concepts. He is available for office hours and is there to help. If you attend class and study, it should be an easy A.

The material itself in the course isn't super challenging but he presents it in a very boring way. A lot of extra credit is provided in the class, but that is because he barely curves the tests, even when the class average was very low. The tests are very difficult because he does not provide good resources for studying.

Good professor overall. Lectures can be dry, but he's funny and actually cares about students. You have to read the textbook outside of class to really do well but he also gives a lot of extra credit. Class isn't too difficult if you show up and do the work, I would say the tests are very doable just from reading the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pretty much universally accepted as the best B251 professor by far. A lot of that is because of the ridiculous amount of extra credit he gives. I believe the course was out of around 500 total points, and homie gave us almost 50 points of extra credit total. For the content, its basically just AP Micro if you took that in high school.

All B251 professors have their pros and cons. Professor Graf's biggest pros are that he gives a lot of extra credit, and you will learn more than you will with other professors for this course. The consequence of learning more is that the exams are harder. But again the extra credit involved will help you if you mess up on an exam.
Professor Graf was easily my favorite teacher this semester. He is an awesome teacher, makes all the assignments extremely clear. Gives a ton of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Graf is one of the harder B251 professors, but he is aware of it. He acknowledges that it is more difficult and provides extra credit opportunities to make up for it. Attendance is mandatory and you receive points for it. Though the class is tough he will make you laugh and keep the lectures laid back while still keeping it productive.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easily the best professor for b251. He gives an insane amount of extra credit.
He really knowns what he's doing and he definitely will make you laugh mid lecture while talking about marginal analysis and cost.

Super sweet and caring. Writes his own textbook (it explains things rly well tbh; just super long chapters). Lot of small assignments like attendance, weekly quizzes but the major points are from exams (all b251/252 classes are like that tho). Talk to him outside of class, he logs all student encounters and it def helps in the long run.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Graf is a caring professor and knowledgeable in his field. His lectures would often go on tangents though. He seems to genuinely care about his students (not all profs do) and wants students to be successful. His class offers more extra credit opportunities than most classes.

Very nice professor who truly cares a lot about his students. He took a lot of time to explain assignments and was willing to do whatever it takes to help students succeed. He gave a ton of extra credit which was great. The exams seemed a lot more difficult than what we did and class and in comparison to the practice exams.

take econ with him the extra credit really helps your grade I ended up with an A and I struggled with ap macro in high school. I learned a lot since he has tutoring sessions outside of class. gives practice exams to help prepare that are very helpful. definitely have to work for your grade it's not easy but he makes the best of it.

Professor Graf really cares about his students and takes time to answers tons of questions during class. He also gives an abundant amount of extra credit which really helped me because the class is very difficult. Tests are hard, and his lectures can be hard to follow. However, really enjoyed him as a professor.

Great teacher, although my learning style did not go with his teaching. I struggled with first test, be sure to pay attention and know your stuff. No complaints about the teacher, he does a great job and gave 50 points of EC, or two letter grades. Definitley saved me. Haven't struggled with a class as much as this one, but just challenging material

I loved economics with Professor Graf. His lectures are interesting and challenging at times but he takes time to answer questions and truly wants his students to succeed. He did a great job teaching a brand new course and the material went together well. I would highly recommend him for anyone looking to take B 252. Great is an understatement!

Prof. Graf is an all-around good guy; however, is exams are very challenging and do include information that is not mentioned in class. He does offer a good amount of extra credit that I would fully utilize to help your grade in the long run. Definitely will have to put in a good amount of work to obtain an A.

Although Prof. Graf is nice, this class was beyond frustrating. Please don't be fooled by all of the good reviews. His tests are extremely hard and there is often material on exams that were never covered in class or practice problems. He does offer extra credit, but not enough to save your grade. Don't take this class, it's not worth it.
Professor Graf includes content in his tests that are not presented in lecture or in homework.

I enjoyed Graf. He always had good lectures, made them fun, and knew what he was talking about. He cared about his students. Some of the content was boring a lot of the time, but he had an enthusiasm for econ that made it more fun for the students.

Prof Graf was one of the best professors I could've had for micro. Though his lectures were usually pretty dry, he definitely made a great effort to use personal anecdotes and examples to make things much more interesting. He gives a lot of extra credit. Tests are pretty difficult though, so I would review your Canvas quizzes.

Professor Graf is an incredibly knowledgeable and kind professor. He cares about his students and their progress in the class. He gives a lot of extra credit in the beginning and end of the course. The tests can be challenging, so its important to read up and thoroughly prepare for them. The textbook is a bit confusing and at times contradicting.

Offers a lot of Extra Credit for you too keep your grade up, he gave us about 50 points which is a letter grade bump in the class. You will need to read the Modules before the lecture as the lecture is mainly used for review and announcements. The test were kind of hard but if you study you'll be good. Overall, he really cares about his class!

Literally everyone in the class says "Love you professor Graf" before leaving the zoom meetings. He always has your back and I honestly dont know what happened in this class. He also offers so much easy extra credit. Love that man.

Professor Graf was such an awesome professor. Yes, the content is difficult, but he gives you so many opportunities for extra help and extra credit. Take advantage of the multitude of resources he gives you such as the lecture videos, textbook, and CL sessions. Exams were tough, but it all works out in the end.
Take good notes. Do the extra credit. Listen to the man. Ace the tests. As simple as that.

Paul Graf is a solid choice for macroeconomics. He really cares about the classroom environment and wants students to get the most out of the class. His tests can be tough but he gives a lot of extra credit. Lectures are kind of dry but the subject matter is interesting.

So Econ is not my thing (social studies ed major so more of a history person) and I took this class spring 2020 (covid), and Prof. Graf handled everything beautifully. Cares a ton about his students, lectures are funny (lots of dry humor), very good at using real life examples. Gives an insane amount of EC, use it. Only reason I passed was the EC
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Wasted a ton of class time repeating announcements every class, rushed lectures and sometimes doesnt finish. Have fun doing canvas lectures but on a 3rd party site you have to pay for, and using a different garbage online textbook for quizzes. Also loves to write test questions to confuse you instead of test you. Pretty bad, avoid this man

Took Paul Graf for Micro + Macro, and he is a phenomenal teacher. Although these courses are difficult, Graf truly does care about his students and wants them to succeed. He was always able to help me understand the material, and pushed students to do their best with a challenging concept. Easily my favorite teacher on this campus, and a great guy

Prof. Graf is one of the harder micro profs, but he is also the best. You will learn so much from his class and he relates micro to your everyday life. He makes the course worth taking. He offers a ton of extra credit to balance out bad exam scores and also multiple attempts to take the weekly quizzes. Highly recommend and overall great guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Overall Graf is a good teacher for micro economics. He offers some extra credit, but expect lots of reading, weekly quizzes, and difficult exams. I would recommend him just because I have heard he is one of the better micro teachers and is very willing to help struggling students. His classes are huge and can be boring but is important to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I got a D test 1. He took the time during office hours to talk me through my options and he ended up recommending I stay in the course. Did well. Lots of EC helped me but not all econ professors give that. His lectures, while plentiful, aren't dry even though he teaches economics. Lots of work but that is the nature of the class. Graf is the man!

The class is really not too bad, if you read the textbook along with the lectures and do some practice. Graf is a really good guy who truly cares about his students, and because of this he gives a lot of extra credit.

Every week there are at home quizzes that cover the weeks material gone over in class. These quizzes are extremely hard and hardly relate to what you learned in class. He gives out a bunch of extra credit- make sure to do it all. As the class goes along, it consistently gets harder and harder, so be prepared for your grade to keep dropping.

While he really knows his material and tries to make it interesting, his lectures are a bit long winded and confusing. The class lacks organization even though he spends the first two whole weeks going over course logistics. His tests aren't terrible, but he never curves. Overall, Graf is not a bad prof, but he's definitely not for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Required quizzes every week that do not match lecture notes. Tests are designed and worded not to grade your understanding but to give you every possible answer as an option that might trick you. Being that this is an intro class and required for some students who do not wish to be econ majors it should not be this difficult!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Although Intro to Macro is a difficult course, I think Professor Graf did a pretty good job teaching it. Be prepared to work hard each week on the material, and I suggest you do all the extra credit available to get the highest grade possible. I suggest sitting in the laptop section in the classroom so you can type into the redacted notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Graf is a pretty good teacher, but economics is so confusing and difficult and the wording of his tests is very confusing
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Taking Paul Graf for E201 and E202 is a game changer. I recommend him to all my friends. In what other class can you have a 85% exam average and end up with a solid A in the class? Get your TopHat points, go to CL, and do the extra credit for an easy 10% boost to your grade. On top of that, he's probably the most entertaining prof.

Professor Graf is probably one of the best professors I had he is caring and always willing to help the student out. E202 is a pretty hard course if you take it on campus so if you get stuck go to his office hours it will help a lot!
I am preparing the Economics part of the CFA exam. That makes me realize how helpful Professor Graf is. I still can remember the knowledge he taught even two years passed.
Great professor, awesome personality. Only problem I faced was that his weekly quizzes were a thousand times harder than what we taught in class. Be prepared to read for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's a quirky professor whose lectures are probably the most interesting out of any of the other econ classes. He recognizes the class is challenging, so he gives out lots of extra credit at the beginning and some at the end of the semester. Take advantage of this. Study a week in advance for the exams. Go to class. And a B at the least is possible
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This had to have been one of the hardest courses Ive taken. Econ is just something you get, or dont get. However, Graf is one amazing guy. Hes truly passionate about economics. Dont take EC for granted. GO TO CLASS. Go to CL!!! He doesnt want you to fail and he knows the material is hard. You gotta work your ass off for a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor but hard class regardless of who teaches.

Graf is a great man and great professor. He really knows his stuff and is always willing to answer questions. He makes a somewhat boring and dry subject interesting and for the most part engaging. His tests are difficult, especially the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is an amazing prof. He is very knowledgable and really cares if you understand the material. I would highly recommend going to office hours. Going to class is very important because he takes attendance and uses top hat to ask questions during lecture. This class is difficult but if you are willing to put in the work you can get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He can come off a little intimidating but once you go see him in office hours, he is super friendly! I'm taking him again for Macro and would highly recommend, he's fantastic. He makes econ interesting and he gives really good real life examples. In his office hours, he helps a lot and explains everything very in depth. He is also really funny!

Prof. Graf is a good professor teaching a bad subject. He gives a good amount of extra credit and tries to make lectures interesting. Be prepared to spend a good amount of time on readings, quizzes, study plans, etc.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Graf is amazing professor. I couldn't imagine taking E201 with any other prof. I'm planning on taking him for E202. He makes the class enjoyable to attend, and he gives out a ton of extra credit. There are weekly online quizzes that can be a pain, but as long as you pay attention in class you'll be fine. Attendance is also mandatory in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Graf is probably the best econ teacher at IU. He makes things super simple and was a lot easier to follow than Professor Self. I have been to his office hours a handful of times and those are super helpful. He is a great teacher and takes time to make sure his students are following along and getting all the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: His lectures made things way more confusing then they needed to be, but hit so much material I can't imagine how behind I would've been if I'd skipped class. The final is killer, so pad your grade as much as you can early on

Only reason to go to lectures is for extra credit. The weekly quizzes he assigns have nothing to do with the lectures. The only positive thing I have to say about this man is that he's funny and gives extra credit, which is the only reason I passed.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Graf is hands down the best e201 professor at IU. He gives so much extra credit at the beginning of the semester, so be sure to take advantage of that because it will act as a cushion once the test grades go in. Honestly, if you show up to every class and start studying for tests a week before the test, this class will be an easy B+.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Gives lots of extra credit at beginning of semester-take advantage. Very good teacher, come to class and do some studying before tests and you'll be fine. Not a difficult class and Graf is an excellent teacher. I plan on taking his section for E202 also.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: For Econ he's a great professor to have! At the beginning of the course he gives you a chance to get extra credit to provide any cushion that you need. Make sure you understand the material early on so you don't get behind.

I got a B in this course, but could just as easily received an A. Tests are 70% of grade, there is grade replacement for your prior tests if you have a high final grade and attend most of the classes, do most webwork, etc. He is hilarious and easy to pay attention to. You should make friends for clicker questions, webwork, and studying. Book is meh

If you go to class and simply fill out his redacted notes (which include 90% of the material already) you'll do great. He gives so much extra credit that you'd have to try not to get a good grade. He does get off topic on lectures sometimes but stick to the notes and you're fine. The book is extremely helpful even though I only read before tests.

Professor Graf is so powerful that has the ability to delete the review here. But anyway, I still gonna say that his lecture is just mean to make you confuse. He frequently talks about not relative stuff in the lecture, and I do not understand why he always complete his sentence without breaks. Final grade score can replace the test 1 and 2.
Interesting lecture,  no curve for the exams, but you can earn  extra credits.

Graf is a fair professor in terms of his exams. However, if you are not willing to put in the time for this class then your grade will suffer. The worst part of this class for me was group projects because you are not allowed to pick, and my group was incompetent. Reading the book and doing Myeconlab before exams is extremely helpful.

Professor Graf is a good teacher but he doesn't always go through the material thoroughly. He is interesting but sometimes you can't understand the entire concept. You have weekly quizzes and optional discussions you can go to. He is helpful if you go to office hours. 3 exams that are about 70 percent of your grade.
Large class. Clickers daily. Quizzes weekly. Group projects monthly. Exams every other month. Class was long, boring, and often not helpful when compared to the book.
Paul's lectures are difficult to understand and often overlooked/sped through due to his side comments. At least S201 is a small class.

As a guy, I life Professor Graf. He's goofy, funny, and clearly knows what he's talking about. Almost too much though. He speeds through lectures as if you're supposed to understand everything at the drop of a hat. 2nd test was impossible with no curve and overall his lectures are kind of pointless. Hated this class overall, but as a guy, he's cool
solid choice for a macroecon teacher. Very reasonable and is there for students when they need him. Going to class is especially important for this course.

Professor Graf is a really good instructor. He makes a great effort to make everyone in his classes successful despite their large sizes. Really knows what he is talking about. Presents material well, however the exams are difficult. Expect low averages on exams but it can be made up with some extra credit

Nice guy, class wasn't terribly difficult. 3 relatively straightforward MC exams that make up 70% of grade. Clicker points every class & an online quiz due every Friday.  Have to put in time to understand the ideas, don't expect to succeed if you don't. His lectures aren't great, read the book and watch Econ videos to grasp the concepts. Its doable

This guy flat out doesn't teach. His exam 2 average was 62% and the final average was 59%. Doesn't curve. He spends more time talking about learning objectives than actually teaching. He also has stupid group projects. Unsuccessfully tries to teach Econ with a powerpoint. He has clicker questions so you have to go even thou it's pointless.

He gets way too off topic in class so we rarely got through the material we were supposed to in class- usually he would speed through the last 30 minutes of class (in which most of the complicated material is) so you don't actually retain that much from class. I had to teach myself most of the concepts using the book.

Graf is a bit of a goofball, sitting in class feels like watching a weird econ sitcom, but worst of all you're being forced to do it since he's the only e201 prof w/ mandatory attendance. Aside from disliking lecture, I found this class very easy. Attend, do well on the the few tests that there are, take online quizzes, and you'll probably get an A

Professor Graf was alright. It is definitely helpful to read before class and to pay attention in class. Even with all of that, it is going to be hard to get above a B in the class as his tests (they're departmental tests) are hard even though he tries his best to prepare students. Out of all the econ profs, he probably is one of the better ones

Graf is a professor who really cares.  However, his lectures can go off topic, and the book, which is required, can be difficult to read, and sometimes not that helpful.  His tests are hard.  Weekly quizzes, and clickers in every class.  Since the material is challenging, you really have to work for it in his class

If you're faced with Self, Olson or Graf - go w/ Graf. I had Olsen before and dropped the class b/c the only grades were tests. With Graf I'm succeeding b/c he gives extra credit for going to CL, clicker points for going to class, and quiz points. His tests are fair and he is a nice guy. Independent studying will get you far, extra credit adds up!
The lectures he gives are not relevant to the material at all. Nothing in his lecture appears on the quizzes. The book/myeconlab will be your best friend.

Paul Graf is a good professor, but if you don't want to pay to many focusing on this class, do not choose it, the textbook in this class will be very expensive and useless, but it's required, students need to attend class every time and they will have the little quiz every time, there're too many things you need to do in this class, waste lot time.

Graf is my favorite professor that I've had. He's funny and he really wants you to pass. He offers a ridiculous amount of extra credit and a bunch of points outside of tests. Basically if you do poorly its your own fault. Make sure you go to lectures because he has clicker questions everyday. Overall great professor.

He talks unrelated things on the class. Going to his class is useless, you need to read  by yourself. His book which is required by his class is not a very helpful and clear book. He has quiz every week and not easy at all. Just don't take his class.

Professor Graf was a really nice guy. He was pretty funny and always made sure he answered any questions students had. There are clicker questions every day so you really can't miss class because they're a big part of your grade. In-class group work was annoying. You can't just listen to his lectures and do well on the tests, you need to read.

Graf is a great teacher. He explains things well and is super helpful during his office hours. Economics will always be a tough class no matter who the teacher is, but he definitely makes it easier. Definitely recommend!

I really likes Graf a lot. He genuinely takes the time to make sure no one has questions and he's more than happy to explain. He really cares about his students and made Econ easier for me. Online quizzes were hard but the tests weren't too bad.

Graf is very passionate with what he is teaching, you would definitely learn a lot from his class. Dont miss any lecture and do what the class is asked for, studyplans and quizzes--there are extra credits built in. I took his E202 as well and I got an A.

I took the summer class and it was a bad decision. I think I would have done better if this was during the semester. I got my first ever C in this class. The tests were very difficult and it seemed like he wanted his tests to be a big secret and not give any hints on what to study. Questions are very tricky on tests. I say avoid

Nice guy but a poor teacher. Class notes were useless. I had to use the textbook more in this class than any other in order to teach myself the material. Test questions were extremely difficult/wordy and very different from the homework. Tests written to feel like a "weed out" class. Very frustrating class.

Graf is a great person, but he actually is not good at teaching and explaining the material. Word on the street is that he is better than self, and those are the only two options so I'd pick Graf, but just know you will have to put in a lot of effort.

He spent half the time telling us what we were gonna study on a particular day rather than actually studying. Apart from that he tried waaaaay too hard to be funny instead of putting the same effort into making his subject matter easy to understand. If you're the kind of person who goes to class to learn you'll hate him.

Currently 40 minutes into lecture, we have not yet approached  relevant material, he's spent 75% of the time forcing jokes/attempting to be popular, and we've taken 3 mandatory opinionated polls. You don't have much of a choice of Macro professors, but if you're the kind of person that comes to class to learn, you will hate this guy.
Professor graf is very passionate and funny in class. Love his class very much.

I took this class online. The lectures were condensed and easy to undertand. It was great how you could rewatch anything you needed to. This class is tough so youre gonna have to read the textbook thoroughy and use all of the resources on MyEconLab. Dont slack off in this course, its difficult but doable if you stick with it.

Professor Graf is funny and obviously knows what he's talking about. He's passionate about the subject. He could be more clear in his explanations BUT he always asks if there are questions. Do the quizzes online but more importantly, the study plan online. Read and go to class and you can succeed.

Graf is very energetic and enthusiastic about the material which makes the class enjoyable. It is ECON so the material is not going to be easy, but with the amount of help and study materials available the class is structured to benefit you if you put in the work. I would definitely recommend Graf
He's a great professor. Helpful, enthusiastic about the subject, and funny. Keeps you entertained and intrigued. He is happy to explain things many times if you truly don't understand.

Good professor.  Keeps things entertaining in class.  Draws extensions of microeconomic principles to college life. WARNING: You'll probably have to take weekly quizzes on MyEconLab.  Don't take these lightly.  Doing practice problems in the resources section helps better than reading the textbook, I've found.  Grind it out and you can pull an A.
good.
He's alright, nothing great. Learnt more about Econ in highschool.
Graf was a great professor and always made the information fun and easy to understand

Prof Graf is as helpful as any you will find, but at the end of the day no teacher can make broad concepts "easy." Don't look at the 200 level, look at yourself. If you are serious and well organized, you will have no problem with the course.I took the online hybrid and only attended class on exam days and had more than enough resources to succeed.

He's a nice guy, but the material is incredibly difficult when it gets down to it. Tests are the most difficult ones I've yet encountered at IU - I never found the most efficient way to study for them. MyEconLab is not the way to go, I can tell you that much. His office hours didn't do much for me, he wasn't very helpful.

He's cool in class, very goofy, but don't be fooled by this-- he's not very understanding of things, ie. HW is due before class starts on the dot. If class starts at 3 and you turn it in at 3:01 (for WHATEVER reason) he'll take it but when you they come back graded he adds a little note saying its a 0 bc it was "late". Also goes way off topic ALOT.

Graf is a great professor and really knows what he's talking about, but the material is just difficult. I feel like it would be more manageable if the class wasn't given in the form of a giant 300-person lecture.

From what I've heard, he's probably the best E201 teacher to take. His tests are fair as long as you do your online quizzes and study. Gives easy extra credit opportunities if you come to class, but attendance isn't mandatory. Really helpful if you go in for office hours, and will bump your grade up if you're boarder-line and have gone in for help

This class is tough but professor Graf does a good job in explaining the material. He's def better than the other e201 professors at IU. Sometimes his lame jokes are funny and he's very passionate about econ. Hard class but good prof.
The material is very difficult, but he does his best to make it manageable. He is understanding on grades too
He is a nice guy, just a difficult class. It helps to read the book because sometimes in lecture he overcomplicates things a bit. I would recommend him though.
Explains the material clearly and is relatively interesting.  The class wasn't terribly hard.
good enough
Subtleties

Looks like Seinfeld but knows what he's talking about.  Kind've a nerd but explains concepts clearly enough and holds review sessions that are helpful before each test.  I suggest taking Graf because if not you're stuck with Professor Self which is the worst teacher for econ at IU

Probably one of the best profs in the econ department. Offers a lot of extra credit and tells corny jokes. However, he can be a little confusing sometimes, so make sure that you read the book carefully and prepare from that. And do CL!
if u just want an easy A,take his class,or you'd better reconsider cuz he knows little about the material.

Prof. Graf's micro class is very straightforward. If you use CL and MyEconLab you will do well on the exams. The tests are directly related to class material. There are a lot of opportunities to get help and a lot of good study resources given to you. Go to class for extra credit points. Professor Graf is nice and genuinely cares about students.

He is a great professor. I enjoyed his Macro class very much. While I have heard some reports of his Microecon class being subpar, that is not the case in his Macroecon class. He explains material very well and makes concepts relevant through examples. The tests are not tricky or impossible like many ECON tests.I would recommend him highly.

Very fair and straightforward class.  Lectures can be bit confusing as Graf tends to go on a number of tangents during lectures.  As entertaining as that is, it doesn't really help learn the material.  The powerpoints are really the key to success.  The tests are reasonable and he offers about 3% extra credit and CL counts for 10% of the class.

Professor Graf is awesome. This class is not hard, as the people before me seem to have thought. I took Self for micro (he was awful) and now macro is so easy! If you read through the stuff in the book, all the concepts make sense. And he's quirky which makes class entertaining.
Cool professor, kinda funny too. Class isn't that hard if you try a little.

You can tell that he is a genuine person that does really care about his students. His personality is very quirky and that makes the classes much less boring. I find myself laughing at his jokes and side comments at least once every class. Good guy.

I have had Prof. Graf for micro & macro and have enjoyed both classes. His classes stay pretty interesting, make sure you go to get the notes, because that is 90% of the test. Class doesn't seem hard, but it is difficult to get an A.

He is very clear and is very willing to help. He slows down when he know students are having trouble. My only problem with him was that he didn't offer CL sessions when I was in the class, but that may have changed now.

He is an awesome teacher, i recommend you take his class!! His test are very fair and CL is worth more in his class than other econ classes!!! He also gives easy extra credit, just show up to his class!!
Great examples that simplify the material. Very straightforward class. The only time I had trouble was when I didn't pay attention and took bad notes. Even then, though, it's not hard to find help.

There is no other professor like him. If he sees that you have put in some effort, he will try everything in his ability to make sure that you understand the material. HE CARES ABOUT HIS STUDENTS. HE DOES NOT CURVE!!!     THAT'S A GOOD THING SOMETIMES.
Genuinely cares about his students and wants them to do well. Fair teacher. Would recommend

He's a fair teacher, and if you put in the effort, you'll do fine.  I hardly studied at all and I missed a couple of classes and was getting a 53, and he doesn't curve.  I got lots of help from him and ended up with a C+, with help from the book.  So if you're looking for a fair teacher, I'd say he's about as fair as it gets in terms of effort.

Amazing teacher (best I have had so far at IU). Makes the material interesting, offers a little extra credit, gives out candy occassionally. If you don't do well in the class it's because you aren't showing up to class.
Didn't get the grade I wanted, but I enjoyed her classes. She was really helpful with my study abroad application and career advice too.
Tests are difficult.. but grading schemes are distributed across projects and assignments. . But she's a nice person and offer helps if you ask.

I have a 4.0 GPA and earned my first C in this class. Lectures are long, hard to follow, and often unclear. Tests include material not covered or posted. The midterm and final were extremely difficult to prepare for. Limited support or extra credit. Consider other options if available.
She is a great kind person. But the exams are difficult.. Lots of group works, but the projects are fun.
Overall, a great professor with not much material to read. Exams can be specific and projects are graded fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ma is a genuinely sweet and nice person. D271 is tough course, she offers lots of support with office hours and emails.

Professor Ma is such a sweet and caring professor. While the class material itself could be a lot at times, she makes it fun and interesting to learn. She was readily available to help over email, office hours, or after class to make sure any student got the help they needed. Loved her!

Professor Ma is an amazing person and lecturer, but her coursework is heavy. She changed her grading standards so her exams are difficult and her assignments are toughly graded. You have to balance the final project with heavy lectures from each class which can be confusing. Lecture notes aren't posted until after covering them so notes are hard

Genuinely my favorite professor ever!! So incredibly sweet and supportive, and she is so understanding of people's situations. I was scared looking at the previous RMPs since a lot of ppl said she was a tough grader, but she offers lots of opportunities for extra credit and exams are easy!! 10/10 would recommend

When I saw her reviews on here when I started the class, I contemplated switching professors. I am really happy I did not. Professor Ma is a really nice professor, offering big extra credit opportunities. For tests, just read the slides. Fill out the participation log and just practice for the presentation.
She's very caring. I like how she ran presentation classes. It was fun to do investor report
She is a really nice person. Exams are easy. Final projects have a big group, so that was not easy, but overall workload is very low. She puts so much energy into every class, and I liked that
I liked Hyewon a lot as my instructor. She gave very clear instructions, reminders, and other support.
Good lectures lots of interesting stuffs. Easy exams, doable final.
Good contents. Tough grading. She seems a good person tho

I don't even write RMP ratings, but I've heard there's some unfair hatred directed at Hyewon, and I'm here to support her. She's by far the most caring professor I've ever met. Don't put your lack of effort and laziness on her. I really enjoyed her classes, and I wish she taught more here. She deserves better than the negativity.

This is definitely not an easy course, but a lot to learn. Hyewon's very friendly and caring. I missed some classes, and she even gave me private lectures for one full hour to help me catch up. I heard that some received pretty harsh grades for the final projects, but she gives me very detailed guideline and personal support for that.

She is incredibly inspirational and caring. I absolutely love her teaching style—it's engaging and well thought-out. She's always so responsive to any questions, even on weekends, which really shows how dedicated she is to her students. It's clear that she loves both teaching and working with students, something I find pretty rare here at IU.
I also don't understand all the hatred on her. She's so caring and sweet. Love her style too

I do not understand the general dislike towards Hyewon. She is by far the most caring professor I've had at IU. However, I can understand how someone would easily get below an A in D271 because points are hard to get. Exams are well covered so there is no reason to do poorly on exams. I had an issue with my group and Hyewon was very willing to help
She is very sweet and caring she even says good job and well done to every single student after exams...but assignments and project were not easy. In general I think its okay

I had an amazing experience in this class! I also really enjoyed having her as my professor for this class, I liked the way she ran classes, assigned homework, conducted exams, as well as how much she took the students point of view into account when doing everything... Overall, it was a great class, and I am glad to have taken it with her!
Her lectures were very interesting, and I have learned so much from her teaching. She gives very long personal feedback for each assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am so happy I chose her class. Not only was the content incredibly engaging, but I really appreciated her teaching style and how genuinely knowledgeable she is about all of the content in the course.

In a class where many people were doing well in exams, you would think that you would finish with a high grade. Unfortunately that is not the case as this professor does not clearly state the necessary items required for the final project, leaving it a mystery. For exams, just look at the slides. Be a teachers pet, she favors them crazy.

C The first two exams are easy and worth 40 points. However, the rest of the assignment and group project are so hard. N You wouldn't get point easily and she also posts grades lately after class end. Before the final grade post, I got soild A, when she post the rest grade, I drop to B. Are u fk kidding me? MD

Seems chill, nice, our friend. Says class will be EZ. But then only inputs grades at the end of 8 weeks, grades HARSH and screws us. not transparent at all. would still take her but use every extra credit oppp and put 200% effort and detail into every assignment. for example, the key task of global manager, write 3 pages and cite 10+ sources
Literally the worst. Wanted so hardly to be our friend and make nice, and then ripped us all to shreads. Dont be fooled, she never wanted to help us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: worst teacher ever. Told everyone in the beginning that we would all do really well in her class then failed everyone once the semester ended. Also took her months to put grades into grade book. DO NOT TAKE!!!
drowning. under. the. water.

don't take her. just no. you can average a 90% on the exams and still barely get a B-. You would think you have a good understanding of the material until she grades your final project as if you're on shark tank.

Save yourself and choose any other professor. Tough grader doesn't even begin to describe her. Your work could be perfect and even if you included everything on the rubric she will take points off because "it wasn't deep enough". She also waited to add the grades of all our assignments and projects after classes with her ended.
Said in the beginning of the course "I think everyone will get an A." Then proceeds to grade assignments/projects as if there is a hidden rubric somewhere we had to read but didn't know about.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Clearly a new professor, don't take her. Gives lot's of extra credit but grades it harsher than actual class assignments, also unfairly allocated extra credit (an error made on her part that my team's grade suffered from). Graded 80% of assignments last minute making our final grades ambiguous.

Do yourself a favor and do not take this professor. Exams are easy but class work/projects are graded harshly. My group followed the rubric/instructions, used the info taught to us in class, but she failed us all and it dropped my grade an entire letter. Also she graded everything after the class ended making grades very hard to dispute.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had Prof for summer A311 and I am so happy i did. He is one of the most laid back professors I have had at IU. He made things straightforward. You wont regret taking this in the summer!

Hoffman was insanely good considering I had his class at 8 AM on a Monday. The class itself is hard with the exams, but he does his absolute best to prepare you for them. He actually cares about what he discusses in class and has lots of real world examples. From what I've seen, he is the best professor you can take for A311
The goat must take for any course.

Prof. Hoffman is an uniquely talented teacher. A professor should be passionate about a topic, but equally important, a good professor can portray ideas in an engaging (and not pretentious) manner... even complex financial structures and mergers.

Cannot speak highly enough for him as a teacher and mentor. Strongly recommend. One of IU's best.
Definitely one of the chillest accounting professors out there. Exams are a bit difficult, but definitely manageable if you go to class and prepare. PJ is the way to go for A310
Dont have to go to class but final exam is all short answer so must go to class.

Prof. Hoffman is an amazing person to learn from. His lectures consist of real-world examples which are much more useful than just reading textbooks. If someone wants to learn textbook materials, they can read on their own time. He connects conceptual knowledge with historical trends which makes his lectures more engaging and valuable.

Didn't learn anything in his class - talks about stuff that has nothing related to the material. Definitely a waste of money and time. Wish someone else more responsible in teaching could teach the MSF program.
Just a great guy overall, very funny and caring for his students. The material is tough as expected.

Best grade distribution for A311. Not only this, he's likable and makes me want to actually show up to class for lectures. Very funny which is a rare feature for accounting professors. Happy to have taken him.

Professor Hoffman was the best professor Ive had at Indiana and probably in my life. Hes phenomenal when it comes to explaining the content in ways for us to understand it, but keeps it interesting at the same time. He is absolutely hilarious and cares about all his students, and his assignments all have purpose. Great guy, the absolute best!

As the Director of the Civic Leaders Center, Paul is not one to shy away from keeping freshman students at IU civically engaged. His seminar course provides ample opportunity for networking from exceptional speakers, and it is his connections that create the welcoming environment to this class. There is also an ample amount of absenses allowed!

He will spend most of the class talking about his experiences and how it fits into the class. Will have to read quite a bit for the class, but he allows unlimited notes for the exams and is very fair. I'd take him again and again.
took this last sem. it was so much work. if you are looking for an easy class for the CLC, this is NOT IT. was looking for a breezy class but ended up with that
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Has a decent amount of reading that is required. Will cold call on you, so you should be prepared. Sets clear expectations for the class but will work with you if you are struggling.

Paul is an awesome professor and even better person. Way too nice to be a professor. If you read you will get an A+ but you can easily get an A if you come to class and use Oyez. His tests are easy and he allows unlimited notes. Highly recommend for all students especially CLC members.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Class was pretty easy. Attendance was mandatory and you would have to mention things discussed in class in a weekly paper (a point or 2 that you particularly disagree/agree with). Graded easily however and you could pretty much fake it if you can sound smart. Online take home exams were easy and open note. Finalpaperwasgradedmuchharderthanmidterm.

Prof. Helmke is a wonderful teacher. He is incredibly knowledgable about his field, and his experience as a lawyer, elected official, and leader of an advocacy group strengthen his teaching even more so. His class offers a great mix of discussion and lecture.

I love Paul!!! Civies, PLEASE take this class! The material is very interesting, and Professor Helmke makes class discussions engaging and productive by drawing on his extensive knowledge and experience. One major paper towards the end of the semester, but as long as this is not procrastinated, this is not difficult.

Professor Helmke is probably my favorite professor I've had so far at SPEA. He has a huge amount of life and work experience that he pulls from to make class very engaging and lectures fun to listen to. Overall he's an amazing professor and a great guy.

Professor Helmke is probably my favorite professor I've had at SPEA so far. Paul Helmke has a huge amount of life and work experience that he brings into class to help teach the material, and it makes class very engaging and lectures fun to listen to. Overall an amazing professor and a great guy.

If you want a class on paul helmkes life history, this is the class for you. His favorite subject is himself and he will  constantly bring up facts and stories about himself that he wants to talk about until somebody asks him about it. 
class work isnt too awful, but since attendance is required I found this class very hard to sit through.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Helmke is great. He has given me a newfound love for history. He assigns court cases that are interesting to read about and if you miss a reading he goes over almost all of the material in class, but doing the reading helps because answering questions/sharing thoughts can get you participation points. Also gives a bunch of EC options.

AVOID THIS CLASS. All class he brags about himself and rarely connects material to readings, which are heavy and frequent. Attendance is required and you have to write a paper every week on what you learned in class (which is hard since there isnt much). He also gives pop quizzes based on reading and uses trick questions. He also cold calls.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I loved this class. Professor Helmke made class fun. Grading was not very tough. He will call on people if no one volunteers, so I would recommend just answering as much as you can. Also, there is a mock trial in the course, one research paper, and one presentation. Additionally, there is a midterm and final but they were not too stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Paul loves a lot of things. He loves himself the most, but teaching law is a close second. This is a great undergrad intro to law and the constitution, and recommended if considering law school. It is very reading, writing, and participation heavy, but this course is unparalleled to any other. Great class, great prof, great experience.
Amazing class and professor I would definitely take one with him again. No reason why anyone would not like class with him! Extra cred available, learn a lot, and cares about his students.
Love his classes. if you like to talk politics and law in terms of current events, this is a great class and teacher. plus you get to watch his Stephen Colbert interview in class

If you are in the CLC, make sure you take Prof. Helmke's class. He is a class act, a great teacher, and a real mentor. Come to class with a good understanding of the reading, and PARTICIPATE! The class is much more fun that way. I can't say enough good things about Professor Helmke!!

I love Professor Helmke. He is such a genuine person, he cares, and his lectures are so interesting. You absolutely have to do the reading but the readings are actually really interesting and getting to participate in the discussions makes it so worth it. He does a good job of balancing leading the discussions but letting us talk. I love him.
If you have the chance to take a class taught by Professor Helmke, do it. By far my favorite Professor ever.

Prof Helmke is a great professor and person. He often draws from his career in politics in class, and his courses are informative but easy. He's a really genuine person and ill go out of his way to help his students. Would highly recommend!

Great professor. The class is kinda just a basic overview of the Bill of Rights, which isn't super difficult or challenging, but he facilitates good discussions. Talks about himself a little but he really has some cool stories and life experiences. Would definitely recommend his class, especially for CLC students.

This class is usually only for current CLC members. As long as you keep up with the reading and take notes you will have the test as they have been open note so far. Be prepared before class as he cold calls when people don't volunteer. Overall, Prof. Helmke is a fountain of knowledge and you will have a wonderful time in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great class, specifically for CLC students. Extremely knowledgeable of the law. Lectures require lots of participation from class and cold calls are often. Great class; just wish he would focus more on his side of the lecture rather than ask for our opinions.

Paul has a ton of experience and is oblivious to his narcissism to a point of total hilarity. If you ask him anything about himself, he'll spend the rest of the class on a tangent. Classes are easy, all discussion-based and open-ended. He's unclear about assignments but gives A's for nearly everything. He's a chill dude overall, loved the class.
Professor Helmke is one of the best professors I have had at Indiana so far. He is there for his students and loves to share his interesting past. Course is not difficult if you pay attention.
Best professor at IU by Far!!
Professor Helmke is an extremely engaging professor and has a lot of experience to bring to the class. If you have the opportunity to take a class with him I recommend doing it.

Paul is a good professor. He expects a lot of reading but if you keep up with it the tests are extremely easy. Gives plenty of extra credit on both tests and extra assignments. Not much homework other than reading. Did I mention reading?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Paul's class is really fun if you actually do the reading and participate. His papers and memos are graded fairly and he usually looks for places to give students more points. He wants everyone to pass so if you go to class, try your hardest, and complete the many extra credits you should easily get an A.
You learn a lot in Professor Helmke's class and if you do the work, he's a pretty easy grader.  You have to come to classes prepared to participate.  His class presentations are awesome!

Professor Helmke is not your average professor. He has amazing life experience that allows him to teach with an amazing perspective. His tests were very easy if you study, and you must read the assigned cases to know what is going on in class and therefore pass the tests. Class discussions were extremely interesting. Favorite prof this semester.
did you know he was the mayor of Fort Wayne? Also he may ahve met Bill Clinton once in law school.

Professor Helmke has been one of the most accommodating, interesting professors I have had since coming to IU. I took his class as a member of the Civic Leaders Center, and it was mostly focused on reading and discussing court cases and how they applied to the constitution (with an emphasis on the Bill of Rights).

I took his class as a part of the Civic Leaders LLC. The class was primarily discussion based so be prepared to participate. Helmke can be vague with instructions at times, but he is a generous grader. Getting an A in the class isn't tough if you put some time in. Overall, Helmke is a great guy and I gained a lot from his class.

Paul is a wonderful guy! He has a phenomenal work history (president of Brady Campaign in DC and mayor of Ft. Wayne) and is very knowledgeable about law. He loves to organize mock trials in class and always opens the floor for class discussion/arguments. He lets you know exactly what the tests will be like and grades the final paper leniantly.

Do NOT take this class with any other teacher. Professor Holden is by far the best professor. No attendance, practice exams are very similar to real exams. There were more people in this class (with no mandatory attendance) than some of my other classes that require it. He makes lectures fun and those along with readings are worth your time

TBH i hate the content of this class (law just doesn't interest me), but Holden is such a fun prof that he makes it a lot better. Any other Kelley kids who dont rly like legal stuff, Holden is by FAR the greatest option you have.

John Holden is the absolute best. I could not recommend him more for L201. He made the lectures enjoyable to attend because he is super engaging and just a fun person to be around. His tests are hard, but you get to take an optional final that replaces your lowest test grade. There is a project in the last 3 weeks that is pretty easy and cool.

He was an amazing professor & I seriously cannot recommend him enough. The exams were exactly what he told you they would be, and he was really fun to have as a professor. He made class super engaging and if you have the opportunity you absolutely should take his class!

Every slide deck is straight white with arial font and the occasional picture but that doesn't take away from how easy it is to pay attention when he lectures. One of the nicest professors I've had and I would highly recommend him to anyone taking L201. He made one of the harder prereqs so much easier for students. Holden is the man.
He like chili's. 10/10.

Prof. Holden was great! His class was very well taught and although some of the lectures were long if he finished early he would let you leave which was awesome. Overall, if you want to get an A in this class just show up and pay attention.
John Holden was an awesome professor. His class was one of my favorites so far in college. It has encouraged me to pursue law and I'm really thankful for this class and professor.

Professor Holden is the absolute goat for L201. Straight chiller and exams are not cumulative. He makes the class interesting and you will learn a lot from it. Would recommend Professor Holden for any student taking L201.
An absolute chiller, Professor Holden was the best professor I could have possibly asked for in L201. On top of that, his lectures were energetic and he loves Chili's.

Got a B but could have done better for sure if I had put just a bit more time in. Not too hard of a class. Holden is the goat. Great guy and I have actually learned a lot about a subject that I was not interested in prior to the class. Recommend over any other L201 professors when talking with my friends.
10/10 Professor
Best professor in Kelley. Just a straight chiller who happens to also be a professor.

Great guy, chill but informative lectures. Cares about his students and teaching ability. Tests are not cumulative, read the textbook and you'll be fine. You should go to lectures, but if you can't he presents the slides on TopHat real time.
Shoutout Holden man so inspirational. Dude's a chiller and the class is pretty easy.

Prof Holden was great. The tests really aren't a huge grade impact, and they aren't cumulative. At least some of the questions on the practice exam are on the test and the practice questions are very similar you know what to study for and expect. He's laid back and a good lecturer.
She is super good at explaining concepts and always willing to help. The class grade are not solely by exam.

She is a great professor. She doesn't post her slide decks, so if you miss class, you'll have to use different resources. 3 practice exams are nearly identical to the real exams, so you will know exactly what to study and what to expect to see on the real exam. Overall, the course didn't require a lot of time and was quite straightforward.

She was pretty nice and offered a ton of support in office hours. While she can be hard to understand at times, the class wasn't difficult if you understand a basic level of Excel. Just keep up with the easy homework and quick checks because it's easy to forget those. Exams were just like the practice tests so it was easy.
Stats is an easy class if you go to class and actually follow along with excel. This is a self-study but if you just follow along on the in-class assignments, class is a breeze.

From what I've heard about other stats teachers, Professor An is the best option. I'm not a fan of stats but I felt as if she made it easier. You can also succeed in this class if you suck at tests because homework is highly weighted. Is she a fun professor? No. But stats is boring so she was just fine. Easy to succeed with her :) Good luck

An absolutely amazing professor for an absolutely difficult class. S301 is by far the hardest i-core prerequisite but Professor An makes it worth it. Her way of teaching is so straightforward and easy to understand and the cheat sheet on the exams is a life saver. 100% take this class with her I will never regret not taking her. Loved this class.
She was extremely helpful and passionate when teaching. She always answers my questions in depth.
Caring professor who explains things very clearly. While she does have an accent, she is very understandable & annunciates her words. The class moves fast, but she does her best to help students.

She's a super helpful professor who so badly wants for her students to succeed. Her accent can be a bit annoying sometimes but you'll learn what she's saying after a few classes. Homework is for completion, in class activities as well, but GRIND the practice exam to do well on the actuals. They're VERY similar.
pay attention to the activities, focus on the practice exams, and go through the textbook. the lectures are fast and confusing but it isn't hard to do well in the class.
Professor An always brought positive energy into the classroom. I enjoyed her genuine in the material and topics.

The speed of S301 is incredibly fast and having no idea what is happening during a lecture is pretty common especially towards the end of the course. With that being said she was always helpful in office hours and definitely cares about the success of her students. If you can get into E370 I've heard it is easier.

I went to every lecture, came to class knowing the material, and still did horribly on all the exams. If you want to succeed in this class, read the textbook. The only reason I saved myself was to get a 100 in every section besides tests, and did well on the final. Watch videos online and do practice problems!

Despite the other reviews, she is definitely manageable. The final was just questions pulled from the previous exams, so if you just redo them, you should be fine. She does talk in a very condescending tone, which is extremely annoying, especially at 8 am. Her lectures are not helpful, and to be honest, I played Roblox the whole time.

I really liked Professor Hill, she is very passionate about chemistry and her notes are great. I would print off her lecture notes before class, and you can fill them out along with her. She records her lectures in-case you miss something. Attendance is basically mandatory though with her tophat formatting. Content is more difficult than first sem.

She did well at teaching her students content necessary for exams. She gave us practice exams which were helpful, but the real exams were slightly different. Go to class and do top hat questions and you'll get points. Do homework! 80% correctness will get rounded to 100% at the end. Overall fine for gen chem, I know others have differing opinions.

She teaches the second part of this course which is a considerably harder part of the course, and she isn't a great professor in my opinion. Honestly, I had to teach myself a lot of her portion of the class. However, it wasn't that hard if you just take the time to study and apply yourself.

Never looked both ways before crossing the street when coming to this class. She is JUST NOW submitting the grades from like the WHOLE SEMESTER. If you like to calculate what you need to get on an exam before you take the exam do NOT take this professors section. Grade went from 70% to failing in 10 mins after she finally submitted grades.
Exams were pretty tough compared to her practice exams but she's very friendly.

so bad, does not reply to emails, does not send out announcements, practice exams are nothing like real exams, goes out of her way to trick you with the exams, she released the final review on Wednesday, and the final exam is literally Monday. She doesn't even seem like she understands chem. avoid and take with literally anyone else

Literally don't understand a word she says. She moves way too fast through lectures and cannot even keep up with herself. The exams are nothing like what she teaches. The material we learned in the first half of the class, taught by a different professor, was harder material and I still did better on those exams than hers.

This is the second chem class I've had with prof Hill and she is the reason I don't like chem. She talks to us as if we're kids and I feel the opposite of smart when I leave her class. Her exams have made my grade tank compared to the first part of the semester and she makes it our fault instead of her own.

Future students, do not take this class w her. No amount of studying, YouTube videos, going to office hours, or prayers will save you. I am literally fighting for my life in this class. If you're on a scholarship, take this class with another teach. This teach's entire life goal is failing you and ruining your GPA.

Sarah hill does not care if her students understand the material or are going to succeed. Her practice exams are nothing like the real ones. During lectures she moves very quickly and takes shortcuts when showing examples.

This professor goes out of her way to make life difficult. Like?? Withholding practice exam keys until the last minute, just to add stress to a course grade composed of 62% exam points?? It should honestly be unacceptable.

Course structure was frustrating. The professor often used a passive-aggressive tone and lecture notes were missing key information. There wasn't enough time to digest complex math concepts. Lectures and practice focused on procedural problems, while exams were heavily conceptual, creating a mismatch that made preparation very difficult.

Ever since I took this class, I'd wish for lightning to struck me She teach u nonsense things that the exams wont even covered. Notes n practice exams were mainly math problems, BUT COME THE EXAMS N ITS CONCEPTUAL WORD PROBLEMS?!

I have sent this professor multiple emails over the course of this semester and have not gotten a singular response to any of them. This makes it incredibly difficult if you are also unable to attend office hours due to your schedule. She is also NEVER prepared for lecture.Take this class with literally anyone else if you can. 0/5 stars.

The tests are nothing like the practice exams. Lectures seemed basically pointless since they boiled down to nothing but math (without enough time to digest the material). I stopped going to lecture altogether and taught it to myself better than she ever taught it to me.

worst prof. she makes her exams 10x harder than the other prof in the first half, tries to trick you. her practice exams have so many errors which she only mentioned errors 30 min before the exam. she puts tophat Q's on the screen so students cant google the answers during class.
April 5, 2026 review is big lie.

reviews.comment: If ur a slow learner, struggle w stem, or naturally smart in hs, I hope the deity ur worshipping is on ur side. If they don't seem to answer your prayers, well, they won't when ur asking for help in this class. Especially not w this teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: probably the most unprepared professor i've ever had. she never printed era's on time, doesn't respond to emails, and was never really in class to answer questions, specifically labs. if she was in class, she answered questions pretty passive aggressively. also there seemed to be a lot of miscommunication between the 3 c103 teachers.

Professor Hill acted like she didn't need to teach the class. She was never prepared for our classes, she never answers emails, and she always has her AirPods in. She hasn't graded anything for this class, and we have been done with classes for almost a week. She would never give us our work on time. If she's a professor, don't take the class.
Professor Hill was unprepared and unprofessional during this entire semester. Such a slow grader and does not care about the students in this course.

Professor Hill did not care about this class at all and it was obvious. It took her 5 weeks to grade one ERA (lab reports) and days before the final exam she still hasn't graded 3 of our ERAs. She never publishes the homework enough time in advance to not stress me out. She never responds to emails. Would definitely not take again.

She won't respond to your emails BUT she is very nice in person and will help you with any question you have about any problems. She actually gets up and starts teaching you with the whiteboard; you can tell she enjoys teaching chemistry.

She's horrible at responding to emails, even after I mentioned it to her in person many times. I've had a couple of friends who have had the same issue with her, and they have also brought it up to her many times. She uses the excuse that she "missed the email" and will tell you to send her another one, but won't reply to it either.

I am taking physical chemistry, P360, but that is not an option when giving a rating. Sarah Hill is just not that great of a professor. She is late to class most days, she reads off of notes the entire time, and honestly the class is just boring. I would recommend taking the much harder, but probably more enjoyable, version of P Chem. Chem-C 361.

Lectures were straightforward. If you have to miss class get ready to teach yourself the topic because the uploaded slides are missing half the content. There are lecture recordings but they're always uploaded after the next lecture so you're perpetually behind. Also notes are heavily ipad/tech favored and you WILL be left behind if handwritten
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her practice exams are nothing like the real exams - the real exams are 10x harder and are always conceptual rather than the math she had you do on the practice ones. She bounces from topic to topic in lecture and also tends to mess up A LOT in class. Asking a question makes you feel stupid as she talks to you like you're a child. So unprofessional

Professor Hill's part of the class was good in regards to thermochemistry, but once reaching kinetics, it became much more difficult to follow. The lectures started becoming more math than concepts and the lecture slides were kind of bland which I think made it more difficult. She is caring and gives practice exams that are helpful as a guide.

She seem like a nice person, but her style of teaching just isn't very helpful for learning the content. Most of the lectures just include her doing math problems with poor explanations. Go to office hours if you are struggling to understand because the lectures will not help.
Absolutely awful. Exams are horribly hard, talks to you like she's talking to a five year old but teaches horribly. Lectures are awful. Literally about to make me change my major
Does not explain things clearly. Practice tests are nothing like actual tests despite her claiming they are. I normally enjoy chemistry but this class was such a drag.
Just a reminder if you ever see this Sarah. We do NOT need to be talked to like we have two brain cells. Regular tone is perfectly sufficient.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You know that one clip from mean girls where regina george crashes out and writes in her burn book about katie. Yeah, that's exactly how I feel about her. Her practice exams are NOTHING like the exam, and her notes are awful.
Her tests were completely different from her lectures. Her lectures were math heavy while her tests were concept heavy. This made is extremely confusing. Her lecture notes were just awful
Do not take her. Her exams are a lot harder than the practice exams. Her notes are all math problems and there aren't a lot of concepts.

Switching from one professor to Sarah Hill was like diving into a pit of snakes. Her notes are maybe the worst things I have ever seen. Her explanations are horrible if there at all. Prepare to teach yourself because she will not be teaching you ever. Exams are horrendous, the practice exam doesn't prepare you and her notes sure wont either. GL.

reviews.comment: genuinely her notes are so bad and they make no sense and she doesn't really explain the concepts very well and the mastering chemistry assignments do NOT reflect her notes. she wastes a lot of time doing demos that take up 0.001% of any exam (they are so irrelevant) and her exams are actually difficult and she does not prepare u well enough, GL.
Sarah Hill is the best. Her lectures are great and helped me understand topics of chemistry I was unsure about.

The homework is the hardest possible thing I have ever done in any class ever. I am a very gifted 4.0 student and her homeworks do not align with what we learn in class. It's like learning addition one class and doing derivatives on the homework. Like where do all of the intermediate steps go??

reviews.comment: There were some shaky spots with how material was understood, and overall shortcomings to me as a student, but overall she is balancing a class of roughly 400-500 students, and she handles it very well.
hardest class ive ever taken.

reviews.comment: Professor Hill is incredible at explaining the concepts in Chemistry, she will re-explain multiple times if you don't get it. Additionally she actually works through the math involved in solving the problems during lectures. Hill is very accessible, as she offers plenty of office hours to help and responds to emails.

She was the worst. Talked to us like kindergartners. Pretended to bounce off walls. Never, ever replied to emails. Can't answer questions from class, because she doesn't seem to understand chemistry. Nothing she says or does makes sense. And - you'll get no help from the chem department, so don't bother trying. CHEM at IU hates students.

The lab lectures were not mandatory and you do not have to attend them to still get an A, just make sure to do the lecture videos. She is rarely involved outside of the lab lecture and you will rarely see her. She is very nice and helpful if you email her.
you really don't need to go to her lab lectures if you watch her videos about how to do the lab but the videos themselves are pretty dull so you might want to watch them on a faster speed.

Professor Hill is pretty unreachable most the time, but that's because she has a life and kids outside of this lab. I only went to the lecture the first week and still was pretty ok. That just means you have to watch the online videos closer. Labs were fun and my AI was super helpful.

Prof Hill was very unaccessible outside of class and rarely responded to emails. Her lectures were very boring but not for participation. She often didn't explain the labs well and made mistakes while teaching. The lab AI's were responsible for grading and they were great and helpful. Prof Hill didn't interact much.

While Prof Hill doesn't do much in-person work, your AI will be giving you a majority of the feedback. When I did reach out to her she did take a while to respond. The labs aren't difficult if you prep your notebook before. Work with your peers if you are confused, they are the most helpful.

Didn't answer a single email, the lab was 2/3 online and the lab videos were blurry and illegible most of the time, she doesn't seem to know what she's talking about, and office hours were not helpful at all. Even though this semester was weird due to being online, I still don't recommend her as a professor.

Professor Hill hasn't answered a single email the entire semester. I have emailed her important questions about the Chem labs she barely understands and recieve no answer. She isnt consistent in knowledge because shes messed up the % error equation multiple times during her online lectures. Unless youre already great at science dont take her class.

She honestly did not teach anything. Your AI at your lab section was more helpful than she was. I did not go to one lecture on Fridays because there was really no point. The lab practical exam was ridiculous.

Professor Hill was okay. The labs for 103 are easy peasy. She tripped over her words a lot and Im definitely not judging that but it made it a little hard to understand the material she was talking about at times. Overall though, fun lab! My AI was super nice!
So much unnecessary work but it was overall an okay class

The weekly lectures were not necessary to go to because every powerpoint was put on canvas and there was no attendance taken. The pre and post lab worksheets were usually pretty straight forward and didn't take to much time. The lab reports did take up quite a bit of time. If you follow the grading rubric posted for each report, you'll be fine.

Dr. Hill has made C127 a lot easier to do well in- clear lab report criteria, open note or take-home tests, extra credit, etc. Lectures are helpful but not mandatory. She has office hours often so it's good to go to her for questions, especially if your AI is not as helpful.

Dr. Hill is great, she is available outside of class and willing to discuss grades, comments, and concerns. She is likely to assist quickly too in order for all of her students to succeed in their academics. She is the revamp that the Chem department needed for C127. The 2 cr. hr. class work is equivalent to about 5 cr. hr. course load. AI grades..

reviews.comment: She motivated us to speak, so discussions were really good. Come prepared, though. It pays off and the readings are interesting.

reviews.comment: The prof incorporates really interesting examples. She's also nice and accessible
There's an incredible amount of detail, but it's clear and accessible.

Exceptional and passionate lecturer! I may have received a B, but that is my own doing. Your grade will depend on your attendance and how you perform on the pop quizzes and unit tests. Show up, do the readings, and you are sure to get an A (she gives you the answers in the lectures!). Her expectations are very clear, so there are no excuses!

reviews.comment: Dr. Inouye is an exceptional educator who cares deeply about the material and her students. Her grading is clear and fair, helping you stay focused and grow. She provides direct feedback that refines your writing. The course is rigorous but rewarding, challenging you to think critically on tough topics. Highly recommended!

reviews.comment: Great class, thoughtful prof. I come back to this material alot

first professor i've ever had that i truly hated

annoying voice
