reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Inouye cares a lot about the subjects she teaches and it shows. The class is easy if you just put a little bit of effort into it and engage yourself. The exams and quizzes are easy and she tells you ahead of time everything that's going to be on it. There is definitely a little bit of reading but I spent max an hour a week on this class.

I hated this class at the beginning of the semester because I sat in the front and Professor Inouye lectures VERY loudly so I constantly had a headache and couldn't focus. Once I moved back a few rows, I was better able to concentrate and ended up LOVING this class. It was my favorite class that semester. No textbooks, but there are some novels.

Professor Inouye was, for the most part a good professor. I took her class titled "What is America?" and it was by far one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. If you go to the lectures and at least skim the readings then you will get an easy A. Some of her grading criteria was a bit confusing so beware.

As long as you do the reading this is a very easy class. Very few graded assignments. Sometimes it was confusing what was expected on assignments, especially the essay and the identifications on the midterm/ final. Just make sure that you go to every class. A lot of questions on the midterm/ final come from class discussions.

Prof. Inouye is really nice and encourages class discussion above all else. I had trouble however understanding what she expected of us on the midterm, paper, and final which were the only grades she gives and if you don't do well on even one you could have a hard time getting your desired grade. A lot of reading.

Fairly easy class.  Lots of reading and heavily tested on lectures.  Discussion for a class like this seems stupid to me.  I found professor Inouye a little cold.  Durring office hours she seemed to think no one was attending lectures which was not the case at all.
She is very big on analytical learning which is very good for the topic but this means very few graded assignments, lots of discussion and lots of reading. She is available for office hours.

Inouye is nice & knowledgeable about the subject, but sometimes her questions are oddly worded or unpredictable in how she wants to be answered. Also, a lot of reading for a 200 level class, but bearable. Pretty good to get a solid B so long as you go to class and halfway skim the readings.

Passionate professor and clearly cares about students. However, his grading for the midterm/finals are VERY ambiguous. I received a poor grade on the final changing my grade from an A+ to an A-. There was no rubric for it so I have no idea how I could have done so bad considering I had an A+ the entire semester essentially. Just be weary
really fun classes, easy to follow and understand

Attendance wasn't tracked, but I still showed up to every class because he's so passionate and energetic about what he's teaching it's enough to just listen. Genuinely easiest class ever, you would have to TRY to fail. Love him he's great and SO intelligent.

The absolute GOAT. One of the most kind and funny professors I have ever had. The reading quizzes are annoying but you can take them as many times as you want. If you do the work, you're guaranteed an A.
He's a great professor!
bro everybody here is lying do not take him he is not that funny. And also does not use canvas so you dont even know ur grade until he submits it to the registar.

Place yourself in space and time! Irvin's class is educational, interesting, and demands a manageable amount of work. Irvin cares to get to know every single student, he makes an learns everyone's name, and something about them. Take advantage of extra credit opportunities like posting class notes and out of class activities.

Favorite teacher, great structure to class, easy participation points, will allow you to post notes to a discussion board for extra credit. Projects are easy when you pay attention. Readings are easy bc he posts questions he'll ask in class. textbook readings not as important but its a good source to cite for projects. Taking his Revolution class
super funny

Prof. Irvin might be one of my favorite professors I've had thus far. His lectures are interesting and entertaining, and he seems like a genuinely great guy. Irvin is a nice guy, but he talks forever. His lectures are supposed to be discussion based for a lecture, but doesnt really work that way. He takes attendance in a lecture of 80 people, which leads to people gaining absences when they werent. I would never recommend a class with him.

reviews.comment: Had him for C121 and would not recommend. He rarely responded to emails, no matter how many were sent, and seemed uninterested in supporting his students. One of the most caring and passionate professors I have ever had. Def is a polarizing professor, as he explains things really fast, but is super helpful in answering questions especially if you go to office hours. He is the perfect professor for someone that actually wants to learn quantum mechanics!!

I've never heard a professor brag about a 60% average on an exam, but here we are. 90% of the stuff on the exam and HW isn't discussed in class, be prepared to do a lot of outside work, you will want go to TA office hours if you want any chance of passing. The only good thing I can say about him is that he's passionate about what he's teaching.

Poorly explained complex topics either in analogies or just purely writing formulas.

He forgot to schedule my testing accommodations .

he was horrible. worst teacher/ professor i've ever had. answered questions with the mindset that the student should already know. so many people were struggling that the highest grade after the first exam i heard was in the high 60s (i asked about 15 people). seriously run.
hardest class ive ever taken

reviews.comment: This professor was my only option for C117. If you can take this course in a different semester to get a different lecturer, DO IT! He does not do a good job at explaining introductory topics to students and his in-lecture examples are difficult to connect to the concept at hand. I have heard him verbally berate students in office hours.

If you aren't going to put in effort outside of class, you will struggle. Lectures were organized well but often too fast. Homework's took awhile, and were MUCH harder than exams. I enjoyed his approach, but put in a lot of work outside of class in order to succeed. I think the largest problem is his inconsistency to level with students.

for any positive reviews, you should know he's currently being investigated for discrimination against students with disabilities. tells disabled students they must choose between accommodations for exams and other classes bc he won't move exam time for a test he doesn't proctor. the experience was traumatizing. please don't take his class.

Not a good professor. He tends to say "everyone understand? yes? okay we move on." when probably most of the class has no idea what he had just said. Exams are nothing like practice exams... every time I went into the exam I felt extremely prepared, then read the questions and have never seen anything like it before.

Not a very good professor. He brags about exam averages being 60%, and how his class average is a C-. If you ask a question in class, get ready to be put down and feel like an inconvenience. In exam 2, he had so many typos we got 15 points back. Also had really hard lecture quizzes that were not easy to understand because of typos. -20/10.

He was not a very good at covering the material thoroughly. He would go through practice problems, but he would not go step by step. He would just show the whole problem worked out and expect you to know how to do it.  Homework problems were very time consuming, and you have to go to office hours several times a week for help on the problems.

He flies through material and does not answer any questions. He just points at the slide and does not work through any of the problems. Tests were ridiculously hard for no reason. Do not take this class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sincerely, don't do it. I like not to judge a teachers right off the bat, but this course is a horrible experience. All he does is point at work problems than work them through in front of you and expects you to grasp what's going on. The homework is nothing compared to his story-like lectures. For your success and mental wellbeing, zon't zo it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lecture & exam material is very hard to understand. Even though he seems to be passionate about his work, he doesn't know how to convey that properly in his teaching and overcomplicates things. AI's do a great job, but there is only so much that they can do to help a mass amount of students that don't understand the material as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a good prof. Reads off the slides and doesn't explain. Homework was extremely difficult and lined up with nothing during class, even AIs didn't know what to do. If you have a choice take this class in the fall with a different prof.

Don't understand why the chemdept won't help students.  Any review here blaming the student for not trying hard enough is Prof. I's writing. He had major typos on 2nd exam cost each of us 15 pts; he won't do anything about it. Other questions made no sense; AI's cannot help. Dept Chair won't help. Students negatively impacted by his ineptitude.

Many students don't bother to try and then blame it on Professor Iyengar. He does often skim during lectures, but this is college, you obviously have to put in work outside of class. If a student has a question he will go through the slides just to ensure that their question has been properly answered. He also seems very passionate about chemistry.
people need to give him more of a chance he is a great teacher

The students in this class fail to try and just blame the teacher, students complain when they don't even work to pay attention or understand the material in class, and when they perform poorly they just blame the teacher. His lectures are okay and he skims over stuff, but always explains something if they need it.

Please listen to us. You will never meet his expectations. He brags about exam averages being 64% (NO RETAKES); takes pride in student failure. 30%+ credit removed from homework question credit for getting a homework question wrong ONE TIME. No safe space to make mistakes. If you ask a question, he will respond with an interrogation.

Bad professor. Skims over material, does not fully teach concepts and gets upset when people ask questions. Super unapproachable and talks so fast and has a thick accent so it is impossible to understand when he is "teaching". DONT TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There's so much I can say that has already been said. All I'm going to say is all the reviews are correct, **do not take this class with Prof Srini.**

Not to be racist but bro's accent is hard to understand. Doesn't work out lecture problems step by step but just reads it out. Question? Come to my office hrs/don't worry about it. Bro, some ppl don't got time for office hrs It's almost like he expects you to know half the lesson b4 coming to the lecture. Better off learning by urself.

Not good, lectures do nothing for learning I have taught myself everything so far from the textbook. The exam was rather difficult and there isn't a curve even though the average was a 64% on the last exam. He is rather hard to understand and going to lectures is pointless.
He is genuinely such a nice guy. His class is hard but he works harder to make sure you understand
okay honestly he slayed give him a chance

The powerpoints are absolutely horrible. He only puts the general idea of a topic in the slides and doesn't elaborate. The examples he provides are child's play compared to the homework he assigns. You'll encounter problems that he didn't provide an example for or didn't talk about. Be prepared to read the textbook often and teach yourself.

He only covers the general idea of the material, and there are no examples provided to help you better understand how the general concepts actually work. The homework is also consistently very difficult.  If you want to achieve a good grade in this class, be prepared to spend many hours outside of class basically teaching yourself the concepts.

Im sorry but he is really incapable of being a teacher. He is not open to questions realistically as he provides rude responses his curriculum is very unresponsive and unengaging and overall is not well fit to be teaching any subjects. His course schedule is sloppy and he treats his lectures as busy work for himself

Iyengar had a great personality and passion for teaching. His lectures were very entertaining because he would provide analogies for hard to understand concepts.

Exams and homework were challenging, but practice exams accurately reflected the exams. Grading criteria was very clear and allowed for extra points and drops.
lil bro was a trashcan
He was an ok teacher. He cares a lot about his students and was willing to work with them if they needed help.

There weren't any practice problems done in class and if you wanted to learn, you had to spend hours watching youtube videos to understand concepts. Lectures were pointless and all learning was done on my own time with outside resources
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He nor his Ai have responded to emails sent months ago, the lectures had nothing to do with the homework, the textbook didn't help with a single thing, the exams had 7 typos minimum, he never communicated anything, he was hard to understand, and talked insanely fast. I took the L on attendance points because lecture became a huge waste of my time.

This professor is absolutely terrible and I wouldn't recommend him to anyone. Doesn't round grades up and seldom answers emails. Although attendance is mandatory and counts towards your grade, there is no point in going to lectures since he only covers the surface of every topic. No problem examples on the slides and no practice exam for the final.

He teaches the second 8 weeks of chem117. he talks so fast its so hard to follow up the lecture, be ready to teach yourself, his exams are difficult. a lot of mastery assignments, slides are difficult to follow. but there is an extra credit on the exams which can be helpful.

He is kinda rude during class to people who ask questions. He is passionate about what he teaches but he sometimes gets caught in tangents and doesnt talk about what is needed. He doesn't practice problems on his slides which is very unhelpful (he will sometimes write them on a chalkboard but his handwriting isnt good). The slides are hard to read
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Going from a good chemistry professor to this was a terrible experience. Expect to have to teach yourself the topics, because the lectures are only going to cover the surface level of the many, many homework questions you'll have to do. I bowed out about 2/3s of the course and suddenly I became a lot less stressed and depressed.

I went to every lecture but learned nothing. He constantly used analogies that went way over my head and his exams are so annoying because of the constant typos. It genuinely seems like he makes them the day the exam is scheduled. He assigns a ton of online homework questions at once and won't tell you. He did have some extra credit on exams tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His grading policy was not clear at all. He taught the second half of the semester and didn't tell students how he was changing the weight of points, and he didn't update the syllabus. His lectures weren't clear. You can tell he is passionate about his work, but I wouldn't take this class with this professor again because of the inconsistencies.

Professor Iyengar is a nice guy, but he speaks fast and it's hard to follow the lessons. I have tried multiple times meeting with him in person, but he has avoided setting a time. I don't know whether this is lazy or because he doesn't have enough time since he is teaching 600 kids, but either way it is inexcusable.

Professor Iyengar is a nice guy, but there are so many things with his teaching style and this class in general. I have tried multiple times meeting with him in person, but he has avoided setting a time. I don't know whether this is lazy or because he doesn't have enough time since he is teaching 600 kids, but either way it is inexcusable.

Two words: good luck. Slides are nothing like the homework or exams, so be prepared to read the textbook. I ended up with an A only because I focused on youtube videos and the textbook rather than going to lecture. Lecture was just Prof Iyengar reading off slides and not worth it at all. Go to office hours, this class requires a lot of effort.
Very hilarious and funny man. Very passionate about chemistry.

This course and professor was the worst. Couldn't understand him during lecture, not only because of a heavy accent, but he would speak really fast all of the sudden, and not repeat information. It was hard to understand concepts, so I fully stopped going to lecture. Be prepared to learn everything on your own. If anything, learn during discussion.

The professor outright told us that we would learn through the homework so you basically have to teach yourself and there's also three lecture quizzes that you have to complete that is posted after each lecture. The only thing that really saved me in the class was the groupme.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had him for the second half of C117 and he was better than the first guy. He is very enthusiastic in lecture and pretty funny. His exams were very straight forward, if you did the practice exams you would do okay. The material in the second half of this course is easier than the first half.

His slides are disorganized and tests can be difficult. He explains the concepts, but doesn't really explain them to help you in a test setting. This class requires a lot of outside work. The only thing that really saved me was having taken AP Chem in the past.

Dude's slide were hieroglyphics. Heavy accent makes it difficult to hear what he's saying. Most people stopped going to lecture and learned the topics off youtube. Professor for first semester was better, although boring. Not finished with this class yet but this class blows and so do the professors. The group me, youtube, and chegg will save you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had disorganized lectures. Not the best but they got the job done. I think he was an okay professor; the material covered is just difficult. Do the homework and go to office hours if you have questions. We weren't given a practice exam for the final so that was stressful. Overall, okay professor but tough class.

I ended with a grade that I dont think represented how hard I worked for this class. You will not know your final exam until the final grade distribution is released. He is very condescending and does not boost anyones grade like the other c117 professors. Do good on the final exam or it will show. It sucks that canvas was immaculate
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had him for second half of the semester. Compared to the other prof i had at the beginning of the semester, i did 10-15% worse on exams. practice exams nothing like actual exam. if you have a good prof for the other half of the semester you should end with an A or B but good luck lol.

Terrible teacher. The IU chem department simply doesnt care about their students because they gave this professor for this hard class. I got a B on all my exams (class average was around a 65 %), and got an A on the final, but I still ended up with a B in the class. Terrible grader and the worst professor I have EVER had!

AVOID HIM. Grades were not available to us until after the final was graded. We were all left in the dark. When I had emailed him about this he said that a real grade couldn't be computed bc the final was a lot of points. :/ Also we never had live class, only pre-recorded. Not helpful when you have small clarifying questions.

The gradebook was literally never accurate until after the final exam. He has a somewhat thick accent so that can make listening tough. Syllabus was not accurate. Online homework due dates were seemingly random. Online version had proctored exams. Can't use notes or book on exams.

Prof. Iyengar teaches only the second half of the class. I did well in the first half, but struggled when he took over. He simply reads the slides, which are very unclear and have little information. Lectures teach you very little, so reading the textbook is necessary. Homework and exam problems are never taught in lecture. Very frustrating!

Terrible professor. Took C117 online and he is not enthusiastic at all. Its almost like the chemistry department wants the students to fail so they gave us him. He does not explain anything at all and is simply the most boring person ever. Do not take this professor unless it is the only professor left.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Srini's class's very hard. That's not the problem. He's very unprofessional. Not sure why but this department hires faculty who are have absolutely no social skills. Srini must have been hired using the buddy system cause you need social skills to be a teacher. Anyone can be a researcher. If you are a Chem major switch fast. this dept is awful.

Professor Iyengar has been one of my favorite professors so far. He tries to make sure you actually understand the content and is happy to approach problems in a different way to help you understand. He also explains things in lecture so that you can actually understand the material, not just memorize it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: My main problem with Professor Iyengar was the tests and homework. A lot (if not most) of the questions on the homework and tests were over material he never went over in lecture. This was frustrating considering the tests and homework make up the majority of the grade. The lectures were really boring and he didn't explain things well at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is pretty funny and is easy to ask for help. Generally pretty okay teacher.

The most disrespectful person you will ever meet. He doesnt teach and its rude to students when they have a question. The way he talks to his students should NEVER be allowed. Ridiculous that he gets away with it.
very rude to students. Tried to be fair as possible, but just was flat out rude when you would personally ask for help.

He's a good teacher, I just don't like the way he does things. Lots of homework, you have to go to lecture to get participation points. Generally makes it easy to understand concepts, will answer questions. Overall a nice guy.

I liked Prof. Iyengar at first because he was enthusiastic about chemistry and kind of made class engaging. It wasn't until I went to office hour that I realized he was disrespectful and unprofessional. He is rude to students trying to understand concepts, and puts blame on the students for the mistakes he makes. Would NOT recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I used to like Iyengar until I personally spoke with him. The way he talked to me and other students is unprofessional and to be frank, rude. I don't think he's a terrible prof, but he did not cover all of the knowledge needed for the exams in lecture. Then when kids would ask for clarity he would interrogate them on their knowledge instead of help

His lectures are easy to follow but they sometimes don't really teach you everything that you need to know. He is also a bit aggressive in office hours and email. Not terrible but sometimes seems he has no respect for students.
He trys and fails over and over. Had to find a much better teacher on youtube.

Horrible. If you can't follow spoken calculus and phyisics don't take a class with him. He writes FAR too little on the board. Also be prepared to be compared to his middle-school-aged son, who "understands this stuff," with "stuff" being quantum mechanics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Srini's class is really hard. S117, in my opinion, is one of the hardest classes at IU. And he knows that. The grade distribution shows this. Even through the averages on the exams is in the C-/D range, almost everyone gets an A or a B. Take this class if you really want to understand quantum mechanics and already have a good understanding of chem

He shows enthusiasm and seems to genuinely care about his students. However, his pedagogy is so incredibly inconsistent that it is almost better to attempt to teach yourself the material rather than expect his lecture to provide any sort of information about the exams.

Potentially one of the hardest classes offered at Indiana University when you consider the students are freshman. Having said that, getting an A is very possible if you put the work in. As a freshman, this class stressed me out a lot, but afterwards I was glad I took it as it prepared me to work hard in college.

Iyengar is probably the nicest and most eccentric professor you'll ever have. He is an Indian that LOVES chemistry. However, the more excited he gets about a topic the stronger his accent gets, and the more difficult he is to understand. His handwriting is AWFUL. He has to explain each letter/equation, which he hates doing.

One of my favorite professors of all time. I would eagerly await his class every morning. He does a great job of explaining the ideas in a clear fashion and gives real world examples to help understand them even more. If you want to do well in the class you have to understand the material, not just memorize formulas. Also he likes participation.

Professor Iyengar is an awesome professor! I really enjoyed his class. Even though this was an honors class, I didn't find it too difficult. The lab portion requires a lot of time and the grading (by AIs) on reports was inconsistent and unclear. Lectures were very interesting, and he makes them really enjoyable! Would highly recommend this class!

I was really sick at the start of the semester, so the class was near impossible and I don't remember a lot, but by the end of the semester I got by with a B because of how curved it is and how much easier the material became (AP Chem helped a ton). Iyengar's hard, but enjoyable, and I think it would've been a great class if I'd been able to study.

This was literally the hardest class I've ever taken, but also the most rewarding. While not required, taking AP calc and AP chem definitely helped. My biggest tip would be to ask questions if you're confused. Iyengar will enthusiastically answer your questions thoroughly.

Professor Iyengar stirs up a mix of emotions, some like him, some don't. I, however, am a fan of Iyengar! He is extremely enthusiastic in class, sometimes over the top, but just wants his students to understand the presented material. His exam for the class was more than fair, yielding the highest average of all three exams! I approve of the Gar!

Very good professor. He goes over everything thoroughly at a reasonable pace. He is enthusiastic and engaging. The problems assigned are very helpful. Just make sure to read the book, and you'll do fine on the test.

C117 is a hard class and you are warned of that from the beginning. Do the readings BEFORE class and all the practice problems before the exams. His lectures are as interesting as they get, and he genuinely cares when the class is confused. Exam is not too difficult if you take the time to study. Definitely recommend him. Awesome professor!
Iyengar is my favorite human being on the planet. He is the funniest person in the world and should be in a category above everyone else. I am lucky to know him.

This class was terrible. He went out of his way to tell me how poorly I was doing even though I was consistently one of the top in the class. If you're not first, you're last. He is spiteful and degrading, along with being a terrible teacher. Even when told by the AIs he didn't cover material in class, he would test over it. Most people would bomb.

Don't take S117 unless you have taken AP Chem, AP Calc, physics AND statistics in high school. He assumes you have a TON of background knowledge that most people do not, everyone is so afraid of him that no one wants to ask questions, and the expectations for the tests are never explained. By far the most disorganized and hardest class I've taken.

DO NOT TAKE S117 UNLESS YOU LOVE PHYSICS AND ARE WILLING TO STUDY FOR HOURS A DAY. I was a 4.3 student in high school and this lass single handedly jeopardized my chances at admission to med school.  Be Careful

My favorite professor this semester. He can be loud during lectures. His accent is very understandable--the only common pronunciation mistake is "w" and "v" switching. He managed to make me much more enthusiastic about chemistry. This class is perfect for people who like physics and math because he teaches chemistry from this perspective.

He is very passionate and often makes mistakes in the lectures because of being so excited. He also likes yelling, which makes it hard to understand whether he likes the class or not. The exams he gives are difficult, but comparatively bearable. Overall evaluation: you know what to expect if you're in the hons class.
Not good at lectures... I heard he's helpful during office hrs. You have to sit in the back because he tries to make the lectures "exciting" but just ends up yelling alot. It's annoying.
Sometimes it's hard to understand him, but overall he tries really hard to make sure that you understand the concepts that he's teaching/explaining

The chemistry department does do that but iyengar is very hard to understand and yells alot. I would suggest not taking C117 period, especially with these two because they make an already difficult subject extremely difficult.

The professor was fine.  The hard part of the course was actually just its setup.  There are a lot of pitfalls that the Chem department dug for people's grades to be buried in. I started out with a solid A in the class,and by the time everything was said and done I had a C+.EX:You'll be docked points if your lab section does better than most others
Iyengar is awesome! He screams during lecture, and his tests aren't that hard.
He is a hard to understand at times.
Decent professor.  Funny accent but will repeat himself many times if the class doesnt seem to understand.  Not too bad of a professor but not great either.
nice guy. really explains things well. will explain multiple times if ppl raise their hands and ask. funny accent and emphasis when talking but good prof. overall

Very animated professor -- gets extremely excited about the material and consequently becomes extremely difficult to understand. Tests are poorly written... many corrections after the fact. Prepare to work hard if you take him! Difficult 100 level chem class!
He was a really interesting professor, and he explained things well! He was also always very helpful.

.All the writing assignments are out of 500 so if you miss some points your grade is going down. Doesn't even tell you when he assigns quizzes on Sundays because he usually doesn't. Actually hoped a train would hit before my walk to his 5:30pm class. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS! if you think it's an easy A YOURE WRONG!

readings each week, you have to make a discussion question and reply to 2 each class. not that bad considering theres not any other work outside of class. small quiz in class for attendance over reading material. if you go to class and at least have a general understanding of readings, youll get an A. I'd take his classes again for sure
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Do you prefer saving your sanity?

Coming from a (now ex-)straight A student for seven semesters, Dr. Ipsen is knowledgeable on the course material, but his grading is harsh. He's paranoid about ChatGPT usage, yet grades harshly if papers don't read as if they're ChatGPT-written.

I spent more time on his class than CHEM 383: Human Biochemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: B226 was a very engaging course despite being online. Dr. Ipsen assigned a very reasonable amount of work every week. My one complaint is that he is overly suspicious about the possibility of students using ChatGPT, but this did lead to our midterm and final getting canceled. TA's grade most of the writing assignments, not Dr. Ipsen.

This course was all online. It consists of like 3-5 videos each week that are 10-60min long, with quiz questions embedded in it, so you actually have to watch. The "textbook" is a normal book, reading it or skimming actually helps. Grading was fair and overall pretty easy a enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ipsen was an absolute delight as a professor. I had him during the Covid semester. Even during this time, he still made the class very interesting. If you do the homework, you should have no problem getting an A in his class. Whenever I had a doubt, he would respond to my emails. Best gen ed professor I had at IU.

Professor Ipsen is a god among men. This class is great and really interesting! Professor Ipsen is super kind if you do the work and participate every once in a while. I met one of my best friends in this class so there is that too. If you read the book and know the terms, the exams will go well.

Ipsen is a pretty smart guys that def knows what hes talking about. the graduate TAs can grade reasonably harshly on the assignments, argue them if you know you did better than the grade. As long as you spit back the information from the book youll be fine. On the bluebook tests write specific random facts of whatever you saw in the book
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class was very interesting and he was very passionate about the subject. Attendance was not required and he posted the slides, but he thoroughly went over the text which was helpful for the exams. He was a good professor and gave students everything they needed to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A very interesting class taught by a professor who is clearly passionate and knows exactly what he's talking about. It's a lot of reading and short writing prompts but if you attend lecture and read the book it will be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring but help you remember the reading. The class is just an explanation of the Cosa Nostra book with his interpretations. Assistants grade the homework hard. Great grading scale
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ipsen in awesome- gives a lot of extra credit in class, has weekly writing assignments, gives out review packets for exams. Important to show up to class, good note taking skills are essential. Shows fun video clips in class. He can be a bit dry, but it's obvious he cares a lot about his students. There is a good amount of memorization involved.

He taught the material well but there was a lot of note taking. You have to go to class because his powerpoint won't make sense otherwise. You have to read and write essays a lot its super annoying. Not that difficult but a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You would think a class about the Mafia would be interesting and atleast keep your attention. However this is the most boring lecture Ive ever had. Get ready to read and write.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't mandatory, and he puts the slides online anyways so you don't have to go. However, the tests are very difficult. He gives you a ton of names to memorize/learn things about and only chooses 8 of those names to put on the test. Take advantage of the extra credit and make sure you buy and review the book before tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Basically, you need the Cosa Nostra book. When the midterm and final come around, read the sections of the book over again and take notes yourself based on the slides. If you do that, you get an A. Don't need to show up bc slides are online, but if you do, you get extra credit taking Top Hat quizzes on the readings which you can easily google them
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The Mafia class is hard, but extremely interesting. Professor Ipsen is very knowledgeabl, but intimidating. His assistants grade very hard. There are 9 very short written assignments (only have to write roughly 2 paragraphs) and two exams. However, there is a lot of material and people covered so you must be ready to memorize and STUDY! Not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Love him!! Such a genuine, awesome guy. He definitely knows the subject matter and is very passionate about it. Lectures repeat what's in the book but you still get a better understanding going to class and get to do random extra credit quizzes. Have to actually study and read for the tests though.

Carl was obviously very passionate about what he taught and truly loved what he was doing. He is a very knowledgable guy and although the readings were interesting, lectures could be pretty boring. Although if you read you didn't have to go to class, it was mostly a recap of the readings. Exams require a lot of studying if you want to do well.

He is a really nice guy and super passionate about this class. The material has the potential to be really interesting if you put in the effort. Get ready to ready everyday! But don't worry... the text book is full of insane Mafia stories that are actually entertaining. You don't have to go to class if you read, unless theres a quiz that day.
The class was very interesting, but I would typically get lost in his eyes several times per lecture. His looks are a distraction, but the content and structure of the class kept me interested.

Carl is a super nice guy. He is willing to work with you if you go to his office hours or even just email him. He is super understanding. His lectures are kind of long and a little boring, but it is all helpful for the exams. The exams are a lot of information but Carl is willing to answer any question you have before. He is a super nice dude.

Very interesting class- Carl is very passionate and knowledgable about sicilian mafia and the class expectations are really straightforward. 2 Blue book exams the whole semester and 8 writing assignments- if you do them all the course is pretty easy to get an A in. Also offers extra credit clicker questions that are straight from that day's lecture

The class is easy as long as you do all the assigned readings. The lectures are over the readings and I can honestly say I learned a lot about the Sicilian mafia. He's super passionate about Italian History and it comes through in his teaching. If you're struggling, go to his office hours and he'll try his best to clarify things.
Really a great teacher with an interesting topic for his class. Loved every minute of it.

This class was not what I was expecting. I was expecting an interesting class that I would enjoy going to, but Ipsen made the class very boring. Attendance is pointless except for the extra credit given on random days.

The lectures are VERY boring but I enjoyed the class due to the topic (mafia). I would advise to go to his office hours, When the end of the semester comes around and youre on the borderline of grades, He is very understandable.

Attendance is not necessary ( unless you want an A, if you do buy a clicker for the extra credit) Read the book, and study the powerpoints and you'll pass and not have to sit thru the BORING lectures!

This class is pretty easy overall.  He does go on some tangents during lectures but its obvious none of it will be on the exam.  It is pretty easy to guess what will in fact be on the exam.  If you read the book, do the 8 short writing assignments, and go to class a B or B+ is easy.
Very boring and difficult.  He is extremely knowledgeable, but rambles and gives useless information.  The only way to pass with a good grade is to shell out $50 for a clicker for extra credit.

This guy is awesome. The class can be a little boring and tedious at times because there is a lot of reading, but he is an interesting teacher to listen to. He is really nice and will do a lot to help you. I'd definitely recommend him.

The class was interesting and he does a good job using different medias to explain things. The class is not mandatory to attend but I strongly suggest going to understand the reaings. Read the book and attend class and you should do fine.

Carl was extremely informed on the subject, had a lot of firsthand experience, and had an odd sense of humor. A good class to go to, the extra credit is totally worth it. Because the topic is fairly obscure, Wikipedia cites only this book for many mafia topics, which appear on Wikipedia. The book is cheap, so get it, but you won't use it much.

This class is not about the American Mafia but rather the Sicilian mafia. However, the information he provides is extremely interesting even if his lectures are boring at times. He is extremely knowledgeable and has lots of first hand experience. Read the book and look over notes in order to do well in this class.

Professor Ipsen is very knowledgable in the subject and more importantly very passionate. While his lectures do tend to be boring he is personable and nice one on one. The class is fairly straight-forward, read the book and take the tests. He uploads notes but they are not necessary, its easier to highlight the book as you read.

This class ended up being kinda boring. Take your own notes, because the ones he puts up are pretty much worthless. Tests are blue books. Make sure you do the writing assignments. He gives extra credit points throughout the semester, but you have to actually go to class for them.

I was really disappointed with the way this class turned out. I went in thinking it was going to be a really cool class, but it turned out to be super boring instead. There were a few interesting topics, but for the most part, it just wasn't all that great. Make sure you read the material and do the assignments, and you'll do ok.

He's a great teacher and is extremely knowledgeable. Class isn't mandatory, but the discussions in class are interesting. Topics on the test are clearly laid out and fair. He made vague topics much more defined for tests. Previously had no interest in history, but loved this class. highly recommend him if you have to take a history class

Great Professor who used an assortment of media to help students understand the Sicilian Mafia. Notes from class really do help along with the reviews in studying for the midterms and tests. I recieved a A+ in the class really just due to my reading comprehension skills.
Good

Going to class isn't that helpful for the exams, just read the book and take notes.  Tests and grading aren't super easy, but he isn't hard.  You do have assignments and it isn't a totally easy class, but he was interesting

I thought this class would be a lot more interesting then it was. Going to class is useless just take your own notes on the reading and study a lot for the tests. Make sure you do the assignments too.

Very knowledgable on course topics. This class is a lot more complicated than just watching the Godfather. Very detailed insight into how the mafia shaped Italian history. Can be a bit of a tough grader, only 22 out of 280 students got an A or A- on the midterm. Do no take this class as a freshman! Have to study a lot but not too hard to succeed

Carl is extremely interested in the mafia. He knows a lot so he expects you to know a lot. U have to study for the two tests and they can be graded a bit hard. Overall hes a very good teacher and its a good class. Just study a lot for the two tests and do the assignements. i reccommend the class.

okay so a class about the mafia sounded interesting, far from the case with this guy, class can put you to sleep in a matter of minutes, he rambles about things that dont matter one bit, his notes are awful and don't help you whatsoever so dont take them...take your own notes from the book, our 1st test avg.= 58%...STAY CLEAR OF CARL..save yourself

Mostly discussion class.  He relates to students very well.  Very knowledgeable.  Readings were a little long and his paper grading is tough but all in all he's a great professor.  He likes plaid suits.  Others mentioned his tangents; I personally like them, they are nothing else if not interesting and at least it mixes things up a little.

That stereotype of the stuffed shirt professor? Look no further. His "Modern" Europe class began in 1795 and when it came to the 20th century, we BLAZED through it...but we spent half of one session watching an opera by Wagner. I feel so cultured - not. Friendly, but a tough paper grader.
he's ok.
He's incredibly easy if you do your work in discussion sections, but this is a very boring course.  He obviously cares about his students, however.

Ipsen is very passionate about his subjects (sometimes leading him to go on tangents), and knows a broad array of information. He is sometimes a little disorganized in his lectures, but he is always friendly and willing to help his students.
He was helpful and was open to suggestions from students. All in all it was a very boring class with equally boring texts. I would recommend taking another class.
Boring lectures, not very knowledgable. Would not suggest him.
He likes to go off on tangents, and sometimes spends far too much time on one subject/slide and not enough on another.
He was a really good prof, made everything very interesting.  Tests were essay and long but I learned a lot from him.  I would definately recommend him as a prof to others!

Very helpful and fair. Congenial and bright. Excellent writer. Cares about his students. Needs to reorganize course, and sometimes talks too much about his own work. Would take another class with him.
Very good Prof!!!  Tests are a little tricky, but not bad!
essay test, not too bad, nicest guy ever, good prof too.

Great Professor. I took the online class and enjoyed it. Like other reviews have said, he's a native speaker but very friendly. Volunteer to participate each class and you'll do good, even if your Spanish isn't the best. If difficult to contact online, go to his office. I looked for test/proj dates in syllabus, and assignment due dates in VHL.
One of the best professors at IU! He is super encouraging and caring towards his students. He's a native speaker which helps so much in learning. Easy grader and super funny. Take his classes!!!

Israel's class was awesome. Easily among the best professors I've ever had. His use real topics made me actually good at Spanish and got me excited to attend class. He's also super understanding and kind, and is a native speaker. This allows him to give insights that non-native speakers might skip over. Take any class with him if you can!!!

One of the best teachers I have ever had. He is so kind and funny; I would very much recommend him. I had him for S280 and it is a very participation-heavy class, as long as you participate and just do the hw/read you'll be fine, he is a super easy and understanding grader. I had a great time in his class, and he is always motivating his students!

Hands down best professor I have had. He is sweet, understanding, caring, and funny. His homework was interactive and we often had time to work in class. Group projects were always fun. I took him for 281 and 309 and had a blast.

I have taken an online class by this professor. I have not met them in-person and I can't say how they teach in person. My online class seems disorganized by not posting assignments on time or having assignments open. It is a guessing game on what I am suppose to do. I'd be weary if they teach an online class you have.

Israel Herrera is the best professor I have ever had. He is very encouraging, and motivates his students to be the best they can be. He is also really fun and keeps his students engaged. There is a fair amount of homework, but no more than any other Spanish class at this level. I highly encourage everyone to take a Spanish class with him.

I highly recommend having Israel for this course. He is a little unorganized and hard to reach through email, but he is a genuinely amazing teacher. Being a native speaker, he is quick to realize mistakes but is very good about helping you to learn how to be better. He is very motivational and has a big focus on the classroom community.

This class would have been easier with another professor solely based on the fact that he does not grade or respond to email well. Because of this its hard to make up assignments, and know what your grade is going to be. He also always finds ways to take off points which is annoying. Overall nice guy but could be more organized.

Israel was an amazing and incredibly caring professor, and extremely empathetic to our personal lives/situations. I looked forward to his class every day and his personality. Classwork was fairly reasonable, though due dates were at times muddled and confusing.

He was overall an easy grader. There were small assignments almost every day. There were a couple of essays due throughout the semester and had to be handwritten, except for the final essay. Participation is required he will call on students that have not participated in a while. There were times when he was unorganized and confusing.
Israel is the best Spanish I have ever had and I'm not exaggerating. He is very kind and inspirational while still making sure his students work very hard. I enjoyed his class very much.

Prof. Herrera is such an energetic and inspirational person. He really loves his class and makes sure to give each and every student good feedback on how to improve. The class has a lot of reading though so if this is your first full immersion class, be sure to practice. The effort is definitely worth it. Also plenty of extra credit opportunities!

I was a little intimidated by this class at first, but Israel creates a fantastic environment where students can grow and learn without fear of failure. His passion for teaching was evident from the first day of class, and he does a great job helping students feel comfortable using a new language. The only downside was having to hand-write essays.

Easily my favorite professor Ive ever had. He cares so much about his students and is just so kind. He is a little unorganized and for the class I took, majority of assignments had to be handwritten (including the essays) so beware of that. Overall, he is incredible and I would definitely recommend his classes!

Honestly, just a phenomenal professor. Tries his best to get everyone involved in class, and it honestly just ends up being a lot of fun. Always encouraging and helpful towards students. Easily the best Spanish teacher I've ever had. If you have the option to take ANY course with him, do it. You certainly won't regret it!

Israel really cares about his students and loves Spanish. He creates a great class environment and is always willing to help if you are struggling. If you take 280, do the given practicas and check answers right before the test; they are almost identical to the sections on the test. Also reread Lazos and LCMS stories. Israel is OUTSTANDING!

Israel is probably the best Spanish educator I have had to date. I have learned so much more from his one semester class than from my four years of Spanish in high school. His office hours are easily accessible and they help you so much. Don't be afraid to ask questions and talk in class. It is a quite a bit of work but he's also very fun.

Isra is easily one of the best Spanish teachers Ive ever had. Grammar is a dull subject but he manages to keep class fun and interesting. He cares about his students and does everything he can to make sure they succeed and understand the material. Hes passionate about motivating students to pursue a major or minor, and successful at it too!

Israel is may be one of the best professors you can get for HISP-S 280. He is a native speaker, so it is hard to understand at times, but he still keeps the class entertained with his many phrases. My only issue is that he is a slow grader so you will not know your grade to the very end of the class. Overall, he is outstanding.
Awesome... no way else to describe him

Israel is an amazing prof! He encourages students and gives great feedback, he brings the class together in "familias", he has a strong passion for helping students succeed and makes himself available. Israel inspired me to turn my Spanish minor to a major after I considered dropping it altogether. If you're struggling or want a fun prof, take him!

Israel is a professor who really wants you to succeed. He makes himself available outside of class. He also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities to increase participation grades. His feedback is always positive, and he keeps class interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Israel is an OUTSTANDING professor. He shows a real passion for teaching his native language to others. He is a pretty easy grader which never hurts. I would highly recommend that you take his class.
Israel is very good, takes questions well and cares about students. This class is basically high school Spanish 5 so a lot of review.
Israel is the best!!!!

This professor was very very nice. He made lectures fun and tried to connect personally with each and every one of his students. Tests were the same level of difficulty as other spanish classes at IU. Not a tough grader at all and all around great guy.

Very encouraging and overall great person. He provides many extra credit opportunities, if you do anything somewhat related to Spanish outside of class he'll give you points for it. He cares a lot about his students and their success. He even offered to write me letters of recommendation for scholarships to study abroad. Favorite professor so far!
Israel was a great person and was also a great professor. He really tries to get his students interested in Spanish.
He is the best!! I recommend him a lot.

He really cares about the topic and his students. He is a really good teacher and he makes the class feel more like a community. If I take another Spanish course at Indiana University, I would go out of my way to make sure it was with him. He makes time and gives you any extra help you need. Awesome guy.
very nice, fun guy, played music before class on some days.  loves teaching spanish,  I really enjoyed his class

Israel is a very good spanish teacher. The class is not difficult, but requires you to study, just as any spanish class would. The tests are departmental, so every test will be similar no matter what professor you have. Israel is hilarious and calls the class "la familia". He does his best to make class fun. I recommend him.

Spanish is his native language so of course he speaks it most of the time.  He does know how to speak english, however he doesn't speak it very often, and when he does it's a little hard to understand.  However, he tries extremely hard to make sure that the whole class understands what is going on. He's also very funny One of my favorite teachers!

He is a nice guy but his class is frustrating. Nothing is ever really accomplished in class and he is unprepared. His class is not really all that hard, but it is hard to study for because you  hardly ever know what is expected of you or what will be on the test.

Very nice guy and will take time to answer any questions. Straight from Columbia though and has a very thick accent which can be hard to understand at times. Not the best English, but he makes sure you understand. Interesting class material.

Aspires to be an ENGL professor and not a POLS professor. 212 was the only class that I was told my writing was not good enough tanking my 4.0 GPA; even went to the writing lab 24 times and was applauded each time for my writing. I DO NOT recommend this class to even my worst enemy. Keep a 10 foot pole between you and this class or just dropout.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Lectures nonstop for the entire 1.5 hour class, with no slides. No idea what to take notes on. Very condescending. Encourages students to brownnose, which leads to shameless sucking up from people in the class (this is the worst part. it makes class unbearable to sit thru). No idea what midterm is like until you get it. 

Do not take this prof.

Professor Isaac routinely checked in with students and made sure we were doing okay during midterm season. Also  met with me after I got a nasty grade and helped me understand what I did wrong and how I could improve. Read the readings and participate in class. Also meet with him if you have any questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: tbh GREAT lectures if you want something interesting envolving open disscusuon but be ready to read allot and be ready to listen some bullshit and accepting others point of view this is what PS is about ACCEPT others even if your far right or far left. his rubric and approach on teaching is unique and your graded on take home exam with open notes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This man is so beyond extremely liberal. If you lean right, stay far away from his courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not super right or left, but we almost exclusively read left leaning essays and was frustrating. Very limited assignments and very discussion heavy.very hard to distinguish the actual facts and what he believes to be true. Really nice and funny guy but if are looking for an impartial and wide ranging conversation, you won't get it with him.
Insanely liberal views. Lectures are very boring and he is very passive aggressive.

He doesn't post any lectures nor uses any slides during class lectures. He also does not give out any assignments that are for grades so it's all test based. He also does not post any lectures or notes from any class.

I truly loved Prof. Issac's class. There are many long readings to do for each class and he calls on you randomly at times, so be prepared! The class was graded on a midterm and final, but if you participate, he is more than willing to boost your grade. He can come off as a bit presumptuous, but overall, he is an intelligent and caring professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would never take this class again... or any class taught by him for that matter. Awful grader, awful lecturer, definitely has favorites. Rude and disrespectful if you ask him anything!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Every poli sci student MUST take a course taught by Professor Isaac before they graduate. Though people complain about lack of visual aids, the content of his lectures is enough to grab your attention. He will change the way you view current political events. Lots of reading but I never did them and still got a good grade. Just pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Isaac is extremely arrogant is unapproachable. He doesn't use PowerPoint, instead he just rambles for over an hour. Reading is ridiculous for a 200 level course. Grades consist of a midterm and a final which are graded toughly. Avoid unless you are extremely interested in the course material.
Views are ridiculously liberal.  Blind to open discussion on FACTS.  Abused his position to intimidate if you disagree with his position.

I can understand that his approach to teaching may not be for everyone, but if you genuinely have an interest in the subject he is lecturing on, and appreciate someone who truly knows and cares about what they're talking about, don't miss the (fairly rare) chance to take a class with him. Great guy who appreciates students that want to succeed.

Sort of cynical toward student, but also very genuine, caring, and extremely knowledgeable about class topics. His lectures were very interesting w/o powerpoints to distract, but he assigned a ridiculous amount of reading for a 200 level.  Gave basically no busy work and only a midterm and final.  Decent guy

Prof. Isaac's lecture are extremely long and dull. No visual aids and nothing to follow along with, just a lot of him talking at you. He can be quite snarky and he comes of as arrogant at times. Seems to genuinely care about the subject, but unless you are very into it yourself and willing to do a ton of busy work, don't take this class.
Kind of a jerk but not a bad teacher, exams directly reflect the material covered in class
Very snarky and unpleasant. Always in a bad mood and he plugs his jazz band whenever he can.

Lectures are long and tedious, he can sometimes come off as mean or aloof, and when he calls on people he often makes them sound stupid, and makes biting comments about people that are funny but mean. The grades are all midterm and final, and those are graded roughly. I'd say stay away if the topic isn't immensely fascinating to you

I had him a few years ago. He was not helpful or clear.  Plus, he would not allow students to ask questions during his lecture.  I was considering grad school in political science until I had this guy.

I think Proff. Isaac is really smart and challenging. If you come to him on a personal level for help, he will find a way to do it. For those who say he is pompous,they obviously aren't attending class,because he just isn't like that! He assigns lots of reading, but it winds up paying off when you do your dissert. He is an amazing teacher.

pretentious and arrogant. he likes the sound of his own voice and discussion is dominated by him and any students who also happen to be pompous windbags. For the amount of reading and writing you're expected to do, you'll learn very little, My most valuable lesson from his class: tenured professors who publish a lot tend to be bad teachers. Other than 1 or 2 kids who were his obvious favorites, he paid little attention to the students.

Extremely smart, energetic, and passionate, if a little scattered at times. He comes into discussions with the goal of challenging you, so don't expect an easy A. But the payoff is enormous, if you're willing to put yourself out there.

He lost my final project. Told me I didn't turn it in, later he found it. He never appologized. I would have just let it go at simple mistake but he was  a total jerk about it. I had to get the dean of Poly Sci in on the situation to get my A. Stay clear!
No Comments
Modern Political Thought. It's a dry subject. But Dr. Isaac presented as well as anyone could! Very understandable and willing to help.
One of the best profs and classes I've ever had.  Lots of reading, but worth it.

Lots of writing in this class and waking up at 8 am to walk 20 minutes away for discussion wasn't fun but she's still a good professor and knows what she's talking about. Would recommend for a dual gen-ed.
Amazing lectures, so engaging. Interesting topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good lecturer. Pay attention and show up and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Imhoff was a fine lecturer and the exams were not difficult. Readings outside of class are helpful as you will be asked to randomly answer a question over most of them for a grade, and to cite them on your exams as evidence. Overall, an interesting and relatively easy GenEd course that I reccomend taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: AMAZING professor. I'm genuinely surprised she doesn't have a higher rating. Took this class as a GenEd and loved it. I was always excited to go to lectures. Lectures are interesting and time went by fast because she is a great lecturer. I would 100% recommend professor Imhoff.
She needs to go through University's inclusion and diversity training.

Very decent class for both an A&H and World Culture. So glad I took this class for the credit. There are readings. Only actually read a few and still somehow got an A. There are pop quizzes about the readings though, so be careful on your decision to do the readings. However, reasonable grader. Very reasonable class. Worth the credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Solid elective that was interesting that counts for world culture and arts & humanities credit. Definitely easier classes if you don't care what elective you take.

Online lectures via zoom were very boring and hard to get through. Interesting material, but boring teaching style. Have to read a lot of excerpts and court cases, so be aware. Lecture attendance not mandatory but in discussion, u will get a bad participation grade if u don't show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: After reading the reviews, it was surprising because I had a different experience. We are in a COVID semester, and she's hard to communicate with. It says it's a 100 level class but should be 300. A bit condescending, wishy-washy, and treats us as if we're below her. She knows what she's talking about, but the class takes up hours of your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Seriously, she's such an amazing professor. One of the most stimulating classes I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Probably one of the sweetest women ever. She is so passionate about her material and is good at making her lectures interesting. Some of the reading material can be a little boring, but make sure you do it because she randomly gives a one-question pop quiz (which isnt hard, it is about foundational information from the reading). Awesome professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Imhoff is really knowledgable on religion and intersectional issues. If you're comfortable with the subject matter, you can skip class every once in a while without falling behind. Her class was super interesting and influenced my choice to add a Jewish Studies minor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Nice lady, makes lecture interesting. Really knows her stuff. I liked the class I took with her. Lectures are usually very interesting, even though the subject matter can be boring at times. For R152 go to discussion, it's important and worth a lot of participation points. Lots of reading, the usually aren't too bad. She's also kinda hot too
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A bit of a tough teacher, but worth it. Best professor in the Religious Studies Department. Interesting Lectures, good classes to take.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--SO MANY PAPERS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Imhoff has lectures that will prepare you for the tests. I literally have not done a single reading but show up and take notes every day and have an A in the class. The only difficult part of the class are the essays. Would recommend, and this counts for A&H as well as World Culture credit.  Side note: I find her voice annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There is a reading after every class but they are not too bad and the pop quizzes that follow are pretty easy. Take notes and you'll get an A.
Incredibly friendly and passionate about the subject. The readings are a bore but lectures aren't so bad.

Jews and Race in America- fantastic class if you like analyzing documents and discussing. Prof Imhoff is awesome, but you have to be willing to put in some effort, don't expect to enjoy class if you don't contribute. She's a lovely woman, very nice and very smart.

She is very funny and always had stories to share. Her quizzes weren't hard if you went to class and or studied the notes she posted. She always helps during quizzes and cares a lot. I loved her and would absolutely recommend and take again.

Even though she is quite loud and unorganized at times, I find her lectures very enjoyable and interesting because you can tell how passionate she is about it. If you ever need literally anything, school or otherwise, her office hours are one of the only I have found worth going to ever.

She is genuinely one of the best profs ever. She's super sweet to all of her students and she's funny and interesting during the lectures, but be prepared because she's a bit eccentric. I'd say that you need to study a little bit but not much as long as you go to lectures, even though attendance isn't mandatory. Super easy tests too

Irene is an amazing woman. She constantly let me retake tests when I was I'll and was always there to help anyone who needed to get their grade up. She writes awesome letters of reccomendation and I would love to take her class again.

Honestly,it's a nice class to have as a first-year student. Irene was one of those professors who wanted you to succeed and followed through with that. Attendance was not mandatory, and all the lectures were posted online. Her humor is so out of pocket. No final and her quizzes are just like the notes—great professor and class to have as a gen ed.

Irene is truly great. She can be hilarious and honestly would be even more hilarious if IU wasn't actively trying to censor their professors. I'll be honest though she is incredibly disorganized and at times I noticed she was passive aggressive to students, including myself when I was in her office hours. Overall though, I highly recommend her
So much extra credit. Just do all her assignments. She is so funny. No final.
I did not go to her lectures. She posted all of her notes online. Easy class to take if you need a Gen ED credit.
Professor Vlachos-Weber is simply the best. All that needs to be said.

I'm a senior, and Irene is by far one of my favorite professors I've had in my time at IU. She's hilarious and you can tell she really cares about her students. Her lectures are always entertaining and quizzes are pretty easy if you study the notes she posts on Canvas. I would highly recommend taking a class with her if you can!
LOVE HER SO MUCH. She really cares about her students and takes the time to listen to what they have to say. She makes her classes very enjoyable, attendance is not required but you will want to go.

Irene is the best! She can definitely be a little scatter-brained but she truly cares about her students more than any professor. She made P101 so nice and easy to digest. She also drops your lowest quiz grade, and there isn't a cumulative final for the course. Just make sure to get your studies done and don't procrastinate studying for quizzes.

Irene is a good professor. Her lectures are informative and engaging, and the assignments are easy. However, she sometimes seems a little scattered and can be hard to reach by email. The class is easy, and you could definitely pass without ever studying if you showed up to lecture. All in all she is a good professor and the class is worth a take.
Irene is the funniest professor I've ever had. She also deeply cares for every single student. She will help you through anything you need! She was truly a breath of fresh air within my classes.

She is the most caring and nicest professor ever and she keeps the class engaged with her sense of humor. I have never genuinely laughed at a teacher's joke but she's hilarious. The sweetest person ever and makes everyone feel seen.
She is the best and nicest professor I've ever had in my whole life. I wish you could teach all my classes.

Irene is amazing. Super funny and always keeps your attention. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you'll definitely want to go because the tests are tough and in person. She posts notes online, but they don't replace being in class. The best part is you can ask her about exam questions during the test and she'll guide you in the right direction.

The amount of hand-holding in the class is mindnumbing. I feel like I am back in elementary school. We spent 3 days talking about how to take a multiple choice test and study for it. The entire first exam is just "for fun." The class is an easy A, but I feel like I haven't even learned anything yet and we are getting ready for the first exam.

Irene is a very nice person. If you are looking for an easy A, take her class. If you want to actually learn the material that is supposed to be taught in P101 and be adequately prepared for upper-level psych courses, take someone else. Sometimes she teaches at a middle school level and spends ways too much time on simple topics.

Irene is genuinely the BEST!! I took her class over the summer through the groups scholars program and loved her so much. Every day is a lecture but it was never boring. She is very interactive with our class and cares so much for all her students. Her UTA's were also very helpful and always available if you're struggling.

I mean...the reviews speak for themselves. Most hilarious professor Ive ever had and Im literally dying to take another class with her. Do study a little bit for the quizzes she does cover a decent amount of stuff that you'll need to remember. Wonderful woman, incredibly interesting class. No regrets at all.

She is so great, all of her lectures are very understandable and she's very funny. She truly cares about students and all of the tests were exactly on what we covered. The homework was also very manageable.

I never actually went to this class so I don't know much about the person, but all her notes are posted online and her quizzes are really easy (answers are word-for-word from the notes). She even drops your worst quiz grade. Attendance isn't mandatory, which is nice.

Irene is just straight up the best. She is such a caring individual and really wants you to succeed in and out of the classroom. She is always willing to answer any question you have. Her lectures are hectic but oh so much fun; she is constantly cracking jokes and really enjoys the things she is teaching.

Yeah they say you remember professors and she is one of them. The criteria is laid out very well and for quizzes, just honestly look through the notes because her notes are exactly what you should know on the tests, even highlighted. If i could put her in my pocket and take her everywhere with me I would, 10/10

Irene is the BEST PROFESSOR EVER. I seriously have never met a professor that has made me want to learn more and to want to have as a mentor. Irene is such a personable professor and person, seriously the sweetest soul and treats you as though you are her child in the sense of caring for each student. RECCOMEND P101/P102 EVEN IF NOT PSYCH MAJOR!!

Irene made my college career. Never have I had a professor that cares so much about the content but convey it in a way that is so engaging and accessible. I'm taking Neuroscience now because of how she did this course. I'm not only a better student because of Irene, but I'm a better human too.

Great professor who cares for her students! Her lectures are extremely engaging and are very enjoyable. I disagree that you can skip every day and get an easy A. At least in P102, there are in-person quizzes and attending lectures is very important for context. The quizzes are not super difficult, but you will probably need to study to get an A+.

Take this class. You don't have to go to class for an A, but I always do because she's so funny. Going to class is genuinely like watching standup.  She tells random stories but always ties it back to the lecture in a fun &memorable way. There's like 5 hw assignments; somtimes we do them as a class & everyone who showed up gets credit.
Irene is one of the best professors I have had. Just go to class and study and you should get an A.

Irene is literally the most caring, attentive, and funniest professor I've ever had. Her lectures are incredibly engaging, and she goes above and beyond to ensure every student understands the material. She is truly exceptional.

She is very accessible out of class and cares a lot about her students. She teaches hundreds of students but puts the time in to meet with them, brings extra pencils during tests amongst other things, and is incredibly understanding. One of the best professors I have ever had.
Though she can go on tangents that are not related to the lecture, she is an incredible prof. No one cares about their students more than she does.
She's hilarious and amazing. If you need help, she's so willing to help and even though she has so many students she'll go above and beyond to make sure you get help.

Irene is by far the most caring, fun, and understanding professor! When I was having a tough week, just talking to her allowed me to find better test-taking and studying methods. Though she gets on random tangents in class sometimes, I enjoyed learning psychology through her relatable examples. She truly cares and helps every student that asks!
Funny, inspiring, will show genuine care towards her students. 10/10

irene is the easiest professor at iu, she is very understanding and caring. you dont even have to show up to this class to get an A. I would totally recommend irene over any other professor for psych.

The most understanding and wholesome professor/teacher I have ever had. Truly cares more about her students more than she cares about the class. Extremely understanding about attendance, all quizzes were online. Cannot recommend her enough.
Irene is the BEST professor at IU!!!
