She is a fun and great teacher

Absolutely amazing teacher! She has so much fun and is always so motivated and excited to be there! It is amazing that we still learn so much about psychology why she tells us stories! You so totally rock Irene!
Irene is the best!  And cute.
She's excellent!
Irene makes the class very interesting.  She keeps us entertained with her numerous jokes.
i love this instructor!
Amazing! I love her! You should try and get her if you are taking P101 or P102!!!
I go to class becuase i WANT to. You rock.
She's one of the best teachers I've had in college so far.
very animated and fun!
Irene is awesome.  She really cares about students and helps them with any problems they need.
She tells lots of stories about her kids. She's also very friendly to people who talk to her after class.
Irene is the best, she rocks.  She is so funny, I love how she uses her family as examples of psych disorders!  You have to take the class, you will learn so much.
Irene is such a great teacher.  She always goes out of her way to help students out and continues to help them even after they are no longer in her classes.
She is fuuny!
She is funny and very nice!  One of my favorite classes!
No Comments

Irene rocks.  She goes out of her way to make sure you can get the best grade possible.  She is the only professor I know that would grade a test right after you take it, so you can enjoy your weekend away knowing your score.  Irene is the best ever.
Oh my cow, you have to have to have this teacher! She's absolutely hilarious and still gets her material taught!
Very eccentric. But an easy class.
awesome
VERY awesome!!! get this prof!!!

Not a great professor. Tried reaching out with questions and attended office hours, and the exam never made any sense. Gave out study guides that didn't relate to the content of the exam. Much of the exam is what you do in class, so be sure to pay attention to that. Overall, not a very good professor and a hard class. Try to take with someone else
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This professor wasn't bad teacher, but they had mostly all lecture classes and the only homework we had was to read like 10 pages of textbook per night (Which took a lot more time than I was expecting). There also were only two tests, so make sure you prepare for those a lot because they make up a huge part of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was an unexpectedly hard one. I have done very well in each spanish course taken previously but this one. The professor was very unorganized, took awhile to grade things, and slow to respond to emails. They were also condescending when giving feedback on writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Honestly feel bad giving this rating bc they definitely care about their students and dont mean any harm. class is very unorganized, instructions are so unclear, have to put in so much effort to understand their feedback by going to like every office hour. if u take this class be ready to have it be one of ur main priorities.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Very entitled in the way that they grade, particularly within essays. After writing for semesters, I am confident in many of my abilities and have never faced problems with different professors. Basically, they told me my writing was awful and they didn't understand how I had gotten along writing this way for years.

This class was difficult, but doable if the effort is there. They are a strict grader, but for the most part fair. Regardless, they are very caring and always willing to help. Lectures/slides contained a ton of words/info. Try to participate, take notes, and know the readings well, as the tests were dependent on that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson was a really good professor. I went to some of their office hours and they were always very helpful and nice. The only thing is that sometimes grading criteria wasn't always clear and the slides have A LOT of words on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Johnson is an incredibly knowledgeable and passionate professor. Yes, there are a lot of readings, but each one is valuable in its own right. Dr. Johnson clearly cares about the material and is very deliberate with their selection. I really appreciated their intersectional approach to the course. They are genuinely invested in your growth!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Schwendel is a wonderful professor! The content is hard because econ is a hard class, but Schwendel truly cares for his students. He gives LOTS of Extra Credit and I personally like the way he formats his class vs how Graf does. I highly recommend Schwendel and Graf is good too, just DO NOT get Lantis.
TAKE SCHWENDEL OR GRAF NOT LANTIS. Bunch of extra credit and easier worded exams for schwendel. Lectures are boring but easy grading.
Professor Schwendel is a great lecturer! He cares about his students success and designs his class as such. There is a lot of extra credit but the tests are hard. Would recommend.

Great professor, used examples in class to make understanding some of the concepts much easier. I've always been bad at econ but his teaching definitely helped. He also gives out a lot of extra credit so utilize that.
Good professor, gives very good lectures and examples within class. Try not to zone out or talk, which is hard because lectures are long. Gives out A LOT of extra credit, so take advantage.
Econ is a hard subject, but it prepares you well. Make sure to study, though, and show up to get extra credit.
Tons of extra credit (4-6% boost directly to your grade). Tons of resources and study materials. Sometimes lectures were a bit boring, but his class is not hard if you attend.
Schwendal is a great professor, just don't talk during class. He has a lot of great anecdotes he uses to explain economic principles. Very well spoken.
Passionate about Economics, and likes to get the class involved. Explains concepts well and posts slides online. Gives a lot of good test prep and has review days.

HATED the material. Loved Schwendel. Great guy, he gives so much extra credit it makes the class doable. I failed every single exam and still passed. Went to office hours and he gave great advice, econ just wasn't my strong suit.

Probably one of my favorite professors, has a 0-tolerance policy, but it's just the nature of such large classes, and he provides a LOT of extra credit opportunities. Lectures are engaging and very much a storytelling format. Stay up to date on content!!

Great professor! Super approachable, I highly recommend going to office hours. I did bad first midterm, went to offie hours before final and second midterm and did so much better on thos two. Go to all extra credit CL session and get the attendance points and you will be okay.

Schwendel's a fun econ professor. He's funny, tells stories, and brings random ah brainrot into his lectures for no reason. Honestly, show up to class + the CL sessions, do all the extra credit, and study for tests not the night before, and you'll get an A.

ALOT of extra credit. Uses a lot of storytelling to teach concepts- can easily zone out if that isn't your learning style but his tests are fair and clear. He teaches well enough to understand the content. If you ask questions in the class, he is more than happy to answer them. 2 hours for final exam(other professors usually have given less)

Real smug guy, kinda weird to talk to acts like he's better than others, kind of professor that's actively looking for ways to take points off in exams. Content was somewhat interesting but too broad, class wasn't necessarily hard but he would grade weird? Regret taking
He was a great professor and helped understand with many examples given in class.

Genuinely have never had a good conversation with the guy, hes incredibly sassy and thinks he knows everything. hes a decent lecturer, but genuinely impossible to talk to or get help from without getting a condescending or snarky reply. Overall I wouldn't recommend him at all, he overcomplicates everything and generally isn't a nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Econ was a challenging class, but Schwendel made every topic so easy to understand- super entertaining & helpful. He really cares about his students and his lectures are so well organized to teach every type of learner. Pay attention, stay up to date with assignments/readings, and take advantage of all the extra credit offered and you'll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Good teacher pay attention

Schwendel is one of the best teachers I've had. Tests aren't too hard, just expect questions covering everything you have learned in the unit, do well on the practice tests, and you will do well on the exams. My favorite thing about Schwendel is that he actually cares about his students and wants them to learn and take something from his course.

It's definitely easy to zone out during his lectures, but paying attention will help more than anything else. Also, the CL sessions are easy extra credit, and more practice is always helpful. The tests are kinda brutal, but totally manageable if you study, you need to study. Also, don't underestimate the Q&As those are graded 0 or 100. Great prof.
Really boring lectures and class grades are structured terribly.

Really great teacher to have. Class is long and can be very easy to zone out, but if you pay attention, you will do good. Lots of extra credit, so just show up and get it done. Tests are the majority of the grade, so study hard and lock in for them and do review, since it is very similar. Class is challenging but fair if you put the work in.

Professor Schwendel is a sweet guy who seems to really care about his students! He provides lots of examples and metaphors that are really helpful for understanding concepts. He also gives so many opportunities for extra credit - your grade can be raised by up to 6% at the end of the semester. I would for sure recommend him for econ!!!

Schwendel is a great professor and makes difficult topics more understandable through his lectures. Make sure to come to class. The textbook isn't very good, but do the readings to get a baseline before class, where he explains and expands on each topic. Is very engaging and clearly cares about his students doing well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Makes the lectures as interesting as they can get through a storytelling kind of method. Very nice guy, has a lot of extra credit opportunities in lieu of any exceptions with missing work and all that.

Prof Schwendel sets you up for success, but I would highly encourage students to take advantage of the extra credit opportunities and study well for exams. He was my favorite professor from freshman year because he was really good at explaining difficult concepts and was always willing to help students.

Lectures can get long and it becomes easy to zone out. Don't sit in the back if you want to succeed in this class. Average exam scores were in the 60s. Plenty of assignments and lots of opportunity for extra credit. If you fall behind once, you'll be behind for the rest of the class.

Professor Schwendel was a great lecturer and storyteller. He cares about his students and wants you to do well. The class is dense, and the exams aren't gimme's. I took both AP Micro/Macro in high school, so I found the class easy, but I still studied for tests and attended every class. He makes sure everyone is on the same playing field. Recommend

Really good prof.

For Econ I don't think you can get a better prof. It's a hard subject and depends on you. 

Papers are similar to what he says and quizzes he gives throughout the course. 

So much extra credit, I did well on first two exams and went into the final with a 110 percent or something.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely a really good and caring professor. He offers a ton of extra credit, and he is good at explaining concepts through stories. The exams are not hard if you study with the practice tests, weekly quizzes, and CL questions. Make sure you go to class, not only for the EC but also because it's easy to fall behind.
So difficult and annoying for no reason, couldn't adjust for 1 point, made me not get into kelly by 0.1% because he was being stubborn. even when I showed proof for my claim. absolutely useless

John's a good professor and it's clear that he has a real passion for economics, it's just the fact that the tests are impossibly hard and they're worth around 75%, so study hard. Really hard. He does gives a very good amount of extra credit (5-6%) though, so make sure to capitalize on those, because you'll need it.
Tests are hard, lectures don't help at all, final is cumulative.

Take him for B251. He offers a ton of extra credit for showing up to class. His exams are very fair, and he gives practice tests that are nearly identical to the real thing. He makes up his own examples that can be confusing at times, but if you take his advice and make your own examples you will do well. He'll stop lectures to answer questions.

I would take Schwendel over the other econ professors, he gives a good amount of extra credit and his exams can be challenging but are fair. He is a good lecturer but sometimes can ramble or go off topic. However, I think his slides are super helpful and there is so much practice to help for the 3 exams!

I like Schwendy! He's a good guy and seems like he loves economics... he wants us to do well which is also nice. There is so much extra credit so your grade will be fine. He answers alot of questions which is nice and is always open for help. Take him for econ :)

Professor Schwendel isn't a good professor plain and simple. He goes off topic every single lecture and is typically telling students to stop talking. The lectures felt very pointless, as I never really gained anything when I attended. The exams are unreasonably difficult and are very tricky. All I have to say is GOOD LUCK.....
The class is very hard but he does a very good job explaining things and is very approachable. There is plenty of extra credit as long as you care enough to do it.
I don't like economics but he made economics interesting. He really cares about student success and it shows through his teaching. 10/10 professor.

The course was okay, the professor just kind of talked alot of class and I found it hard to find what information was actually important. The exams were unneccesarily difficult. Offers a lot of extra credit and recommend CL sessions, but because this course is required I would take it with a different professor if you can.

Prof. was great. He gives so much extra credit it is insane. He is also really easy to talk with during office hours and I would recommend just going and meeting him it makes the class more enjoyable. His class does have super long lectures, but that is just econ in general and he at least has some fun stories that add to understanding the content
exams are tough, but if you prepare with the extra material he provides you'll be fine. overhated.
Lecture is kinda boring. Lots of extra credit (6%). Study for tests and do homework and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Can't explain the material very well and gets off-topic. He would talk about Wisconsin, glass blowing, or telling students to be quiet.

ECON 309 was a very good class. I learn't a lot about Inequalities in Economics. He challenges you to critique and beware of data. It is also more subjective than most Econ classes. You will write 3 in class essays (he gives you the topic ahead of time) and take two tests of which he preps you. You do not need to know much Econ to do well. Justread
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great lecturer, they were entertaining, attendance was extra credit but tests are tough. Make sure to pay attention in class

Amazing professor, you can tell he cares from his stories that relate to what you're learning next, to the amount of extra credit he provides. (It's like 10%) He has a lot of energy and is willing to sit down and talk things out with you especially during office hours. I've spoken to many others who've also had him and they loved him.

Loved this teacher. Not the best at explaining math so its so important to go the the CL sessions, just do it. extra credit is great, go to class and pay attention, For exams, go by module, First read the Tophat chapter, then redo the CL questions, then retake the quiz. This class is not hard unless you make it out to be.

Professor Schwendel is one of the best lecturers I have had at IU, and he explains topics and ideas really well. Super caring and approachable, gives 7% extra credit (going to class is extra credit) and he is super clear on guidelines and topics on exams and quizzes. He even acknowledges when there are errors, and doesn't penalize students for it.
One of the best professors I have ever had. His lectures are so engaging, and he teaches very well.
can't teach well and gets off-topic. loves talking about Wisconsin and the bucks (nba team).

John is a very good professor. The course material can be very challenging as the semester progresses, but he does a very good job at highlighting key concepts and explaining the chapter content. If you want to succeed in B251, you need to go to his lectures. Overall a very good professor for one of Kelley's most challenging 1st year classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Schwendel is one of the best profs I have ever had. I had to take B251 over a 6 week summer course to get some credits and he made it a breeze. He explains everything thoroughly, multiple times and gives practice problems and examples. Participation was for extra credit. Expect a quiz on non exam weeks, and tophats. 10/10 recommend.

Everyone always talks about how Graff gives more extra credit when in reality Schwendel give the same or more. Attendance and econ discussions are extra credit. If you do anything attend the discussion. Great job at explaining the concepts and the whole class is easy if you just listen. To study for the test use the practice exams and the quizzes.

Schwendel's passion for teaching economics definitely comes through in his lectures. He explains concepts in depth, using real life examples to help explain why they are relevant. The class is structured so that 70% of your grade is made up of exams, but he does offer a generous amount of extra credit (~7%). Overall, I would recommend him for B251.

Professor Schwendel was a phenomenal professor. His lectures were extremely helpful and he was sure to give out some extra credit at the end of the semester. He is one of, if not, the best B251 professor at IU.

Amazing professor but gets annoying. He yaps about glass-blowing and super obscure subjects for 60/75 minutes. You HAVE to pay attention otherwise you will get confused quickly. Attendance is optional, but definitely do all the extra credit and you will thank yourself. An easy class if you actually spend time studying.

very interesting man. spends the majority of the lecture yapping about glass blowing or the state of Wisconsin. never actually answers your questions. says the word "intuition" approximately 30 times an hour. attendance is extra credit and he posts all the lecture videos so I just put them on 1.5x speed and did the entire course from my room.
Not a very hard class. Lectures are very boring but help reinforce concepts. Gives lots of extra credit, so it should be easy to do well in this class.

ECON is a tough subject but he tries to make it better for students in his class. There are a few extra credit opportunities. Definitely take them up as it helped boost my grade and go into office hours if you are struggling as he is always willing to help. His tests are very tough though so definitely study ALOTTT!

He is very passionate about econ and tries to make boring content seem fun. You can tell that he genuinely cares about his students and offers multiple opportunities for extra credit. With that said, the exams are fairly difficult and you really need to pay attention in order to do well on them.
Great professor who's passionate about the subject and is very willing to help students out. Plenty of extra credit opportunities.

Very passionate about economics and greatly enjoys teaching which made the class less boring in my opinion. The lectures are long but he also records them. There is a good amount of extra credit available if you take the time to do it. I had a very hard time with the tests though even after going to every class and studying a lot.

He's honestly a pretty great prof. You can tell that he is passionate about econ and cares for his students. He gives a good amount of extra credit opportunities. Would recommend attending his lectures as they as helpful AND count for extra credit. Recordings were helpful to look back on. Overall a great prof but his exams are a little tough.

Prof. Schwendel is a great professor. He's obviously very knowledgeable about econ, and provides many examples and practice questions within lectures. Lots of extra credit opportunities are available, and he gives extra credit just for attending lectures. The exams aren't easy, but there's no curveballs on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: ECON-B 251 is a hard class. With Schwendel, you have to put in the work to do well. He sets up the class in hopes that everyone does well, with a fair amount of extra credit. GO TO ALL OF YOUR LECTURES AND PAY ATTENTION. Schwendel explains stuff well, but if you don't understand stuff from the get go, you'll regret it later. Go to his office hours!

He is a great professor! The class is tough but he makes it easier. Gives a lot of extra credit - take advantage of it! If you attend all lectures (and CL sessions), do well on the quizzes and put in the effort, you can do well. His office hours are also very helpful. His exams are not very difficult with very few tricky questions.

Professor Schwendel is a great lecturer. I loved the way he taught as he really knows his stuff. But boy was this class tough. You will have to apply yourself in order to get a good grade but he offers a generous amount of extra credit (roughly 5% overall) I warn prekelley students as this class can be a make or break. Overall tough but good.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolute d***hole, refuses to tell students what exactly will be on any exam so you are forced to read through the entire textbook because the entire textbook is "fair game". No exam reviews terrible practice tests where none of the questions are similar to the exam.
He is an awful professor and his class is significantly harder than the other teachers. He doesn't teach with real-world examples and there is no curve.

Prof Schwendel is a fantastic teacher, although the class material could be a little bit confusing sometime, but if you put in the work, come to class (sit in front), do the extra credit, CL sessions, and come to his office hour with questions, then you will do fine in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking Schwendel for any economics class. His tests are nothing like the review material and his lectures are off topic and half the time, don't make any sense. He does have several extra credit opportunities, but even with that, it was difficult to keep a decent grade or let alone bring up a grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Told me to "figure it out" when I went in for office hours. Otherwise his lectures are pretty boring however he does give a good amount of extra credit.
He was a good professor and his lectures were very helpful. Course had a decent workload with weekly quizzes.

This class is hard even for people who took AP micro and macro in high school. He gets quite off topic during lectures, going on rants, etc. He is a really nice guy though. The lectures are not helpful to many at all. Study the Tophat and take notes on each complete module.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great guy. Early in his career. Gives a lot of Extra Credit, but you have to be proactive to take advantage of it. Take notes in lectures, read the tophat, take advantage of Extra Credit. This review is pre final exam, and because of my past exam scores and being proactive for extra credit opportunities I can get a 52% on it and finish with an A.

Schwendel makes economics interesting and simplifies concepts to match the real world. However, the material he teaches isn't the easiest, and your grade is extremely test-dependent. Two midterms worth 22.5% each and a final worth 25%. He does give a lot of extra credit though so be sure to utilize it. Otherwise, he is a solid professor
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Schwendel is 100% the best option for B251 at IU. He was a great teacher and really cares ab ppl learning.

Schwendel gives great lectures with helpful in-class participation and uses fun stories to help teach topics. Class is easy to follow and he gives opportunities for extra credit. He is very accessible outside of class and is keen to help students if you make the effort to come in to office hours. Fantastic and so helpful. Would 100% take again.
Actually loved the way he taught. Took him in the spring of last year and was one of my best teachers. Always super passionate in lectures if you listen to what he has to say. Great teacher

Horrible. The best advice I will give is do not take this professor. Does not curve tests, the test averages are typically around 70% which he justifies as "good". Gives irrelevant examples regarding his former job as a glassblower and tractor driver. Gives irrelevant examples from past jobs. Take a Graf or a grad student and receive a good grade.

This was not my favorite class, but I did love Scwendels in class examples as they were easy to understand show he cared about us understanding the material. He does not curve though and if you can take a grad student I heard they grade everyone A's. But if you cant Scwendels is great back up.

I don't understand why people don't like Schwendel, he's a good professor that teaches the conepts very easily. I had friends who had Graf and I would say Schwendel's exams are much easier than Graf's. However, he doesn't provide as much extra credit as Graf does if that's something you care about, but Schwendel does provide extra credit.

Quality professor really. Very professional. Very articulate. Knows everything about what he is teaching. Always prepared. Takes time to clarify things if people ask questions. Only bad thing could be that the tests are difficult, but as long as you prepare, you will do well.

Dr. Schwendel was an outstanding professor for B251. Many people complain that he does not give out as many "free" points as some of the other professors, but if you want to truly learn economics, he is the one to take. He is extremely knowledgeable about the topics in the class, and is always happy to answer questions. Put in the work, get the A.

This is not a difficult professor. Although his tests may be harder than the other econ teachers, if you attend class 80% of the time he will add 4 points to your final grade. B251 is not a difficult course if you actually pay attention and take notes. There are practice tests which he provides as well as the weekly quizzes to study from.

I had no prior knowledge of econ. Therefore his classes was VERY hard. he goes super fast and gives little to no extra credit. He also rambles about nonsense during lecture. His tests are nothing like the material covered and does not curve and does not care even if you try hard and go to tutoring.

I loved his lectures and always felt like they were very interesting. My biggest problem is the tests often did not feel like the material we were learning. I would score great on practice exams and then I literally got a 57% on a midterm. He offers CL sessions which are extra credit GO TO THEM, they are very helpful.

Schwendel is fair for B2251. Lowkey not that good in lecture bc he goes soo fast but is helpful in office hours. Too much work and some of it is clearly busy work. Not horrible though and actually is really nice. Doesn't curve which kinda sucks but does offer extra credit. Prepare to do a lot of work but he's pretty good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Coming from someone who didn't take economics in high school, his class was very easy to follow and he has plenty of examples to teach the material. The only reason I'd recommend another professor is because he doesn't curve tests or give much extra credit.

He's great, however, if you have no knowledge in economics, you could find his class a little too fast. Coming from someone who already did economics in high school, the fact that he went through everything quickly was nicer.

Professor Schwendel is honestly a great guy, he was very helpful outside of class and this really helped me in the long run. I just wish there was more extra credit other than CL sessions, considering he doesn't curve tests. Regardless, I will take him for 252 if he teaches it.

Schwendel knows his stuff, but his grading is what ruins this class. Not curving any of his exams and only giving one chance on the weekly quizzes while other professors give multiple will make you lose easy points.

Professor Schwendel isn't the best choice for B251. His lectures are tedious with the amount of in class TopHat questions he makes people answer, and he doesn't curve his exams because he thinks a C- class average is good for him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: everyone who gave him a low rating is clearly just not willing to put in some effort. yes, he is tough in the sense that he doesn't curve, but he is a fantastic professor who explains things very well. just because the subject is boring doesn't mean that he is. he is one of the most caring and intelligent professors I've ever had.

Professor gets it  little harsh, because all the econ professors have different ways to boost grades. He doesn't curve, but gives a decent amount of extra credit. His grading scale is different, your grade gets automatically rounded to the next letter grade. Tests are a bit on the harder side. Overall he is a great professor and good at teaching.
Grades a little hard but I think all B-251 profs do. Really engaging lecturer and a friendly guy. Emphasizes understanding the material over anything else. A great addition to the IU roster.

The class itself is not horrible, but Professor Schwendel is the professor you should take this class with. If you are looking to get a good grade, you are not going to get it with him. He doesn't curve his exams and only gives you one attempt on the quizzes.

Schwendel is someone you should stay clear of when taking B251. He doesn't offer a curve for his exams and his lectures are dry and half of the time don't make sense. He offers extra credit, but it doesn't end up having as big of an impact on your grade as you think. You end up teaching yourself the entire semester.

Impossible to see you true grade in the class because he locks grades throughout the entire semester. Gives you a excel sheet to compensate for that but it even says that it isn't fully accurate either. He also doesn't curve exams so get ready for a very poor exam grade if you don't grind for a whole week before the exam.

He refuses to curve any of his exams because he says that he ends up giving a lot of extra credit. But in reality, that extra credit doesn't have as big of an impact as he thinks. He also thinks that if you get a B- in the class, he is doing his job well. Terrible mindset for a professor to have not wanting his students to succeed.

The fact that the professor did not acknowledge that 95% of the students needed a curve to do well on his exams and his excuse was that a B- was a "good grade" and "normal" for this class. This professor would like to joke about our final grades and say that his extra credit was sufficient, but in reality it was not at all. Big talker but L teacher

Do not take B251 with Professor Schwendel! He does not curve any of the exams like other professors do. And then tells you it will be okay because he gives some extra credit at the end. He also locks your grade on Canvas so you are not able to easily calculate grades you need on exams or the final.

There are a lot of good qualities about Schwendel, but also a lot of negatives. His lectures are not dry and are pretty engaging. He offers a lot of extra credit. But his quizzes are quite difficult and sometimes have material that we didn't really go in-depth in class. He also never curves his exams which is a huge negative.

Unlike most of the other econ professors in the department, John Schwendel does not curve his exams at all. He says that its because he offers a large amount of extra credit he makes it more difficult that it should be to obtain all of that extra credit. He also makes it impossible to accurate calculate our final grade. Avoid him at all cost!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Schwendel tries to make his lectures engaging, but they just become very tedious with all of the in-class TopHat questions. He offers a lot of extra credit in theory, but they usually come from the weekly quizzes and he only gives us one attempt. He is adamant on not curving his exams because he claims that a C- average is him doing his job well.

Professor Schwendel is a great professor. His lectures are very engaging and he does his best to make them fun and interesting. He tries to get the students involved through various in-class activities. He also offers lots of extra credit and does his best for his students to understand the material.
Econ in general is a hard class. he doesn't curve the test but gives a lot of extra credit. pretty good teacher and tries to make class fun if you study you will get an A

Professor Schwendel is a great guy and professor. He makes his lectures interesting and engaging with TopHat questions. He uses examples that college students understand. Although his class is difficult if you pay attention and go to class it makes it easier!
John was a new professor this year. For his first year o thought he was a very solid choice for B251, he definitely cares for his students and makes sure extra credit is available!
Very boring class and probably the more difficult professors out of econ teachers. Hard to follow or listen to but gives a good amount of extra credit. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be prepared to have no idea what your grade in the class is, as it has to be calculated through a complex Excel sheet. He also refuses to curve exams, and the tests are tough. Generally this isn't a well-liked class, but he didn't do it any favors.

Schwendel is a pretty solid choice for B251. He gives a lot of extra credit which is nice but he doesn't curve tests which is pretty big. You have to pay for TopHat and PackBack which kinda sucks but all profs for this class make you do that. Attendance is mandatory and there are participation points so you have to stay the whole time.

This guy scews you over with not curving grades. He provides extra credit in other areas, but not enough to get a good grade in this class. Although you probably won't get an A in his class, he is a good teacher. His assignments involve tophat, packback, and quizzes. Don't choose him if you want an A.

The lectures are really long and informative, but he makes sure to incorporate the most entertaining information there can be when talking about Economics. He is very understanding and is available outside of the classroom if you need help. Exams aren't too bad, just make sure you attend class and gain those tophat points.

Prof. Schwendel is one of the nicest professors that I have had at IU. It seems that he really wants his students to succeed. Plenty of extra credit and opportunities to earn points. Clear on what he is looking for. Lectures can become dry and it is easy to get lost in his words but putting in minimal effort in outside class goes a long way.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Schwendel is a really good pick for B252. He really enjoys what he teaches and comes up with good real-life applications of the concepts through stories. Econ isn't the easiest subject, but Prof Schwendel offers a lot of extra credit making an 'A' or 'B' very obtainable if you are willing to put in the work. 10/10 would recommend.

John Wood is a bad teacher. He doesn't know how to actually teach the content. That part isn't the problem...he didn't show up to class like 8 times and didn't give us any warning. My class was a 20 minute walk at 8 am, and it sucked when he didn't show up. Avoid taking him at all costs. I had an A because I already took Calc in high school.
Professor Wood is a good professor, but you have to be willing to put in the work. If you go to the office hours and try, you will be fine. People are way too harsh on him.

This guy is the worst professor he cancelled around 8 classes this semester and let us know 15 minutes into class then will also randomly assign classwork while you wake up and guess if he even gonna show up. After all that he can't even round my grade up 0.08 to get a B+. Never answers any emails.
very nice guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Wood isn't the best teacher. He was a substitute who came in for my B110 class because the other professor had some personal issues. Dr. Wood did not know what he was teaching. He also never wrote down notes with us, he would just verbally tell us what to do which is not how math works. Don't take a class with this guy unless you want to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The problem with him is that he doesn't respond to emails and doesn't have office hours. He also told me to email a different teacher about something in my gradebook, when he is the main teacher. He teaches terribly. He doesn't explain grading criteria clearly for tests either. Worst Math teacher of my life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Expect to do worse the more you show up to class. This guy couldn't teach an 8-year-old how to walk.
I do not know what is going on in this class

he is not as bad as the reviews say. i'm in b110 with him and he replaced my old prof. he is very good at answering questions and actually wants students to participate in class. these reviews are too harsh.

I would rather put a sewing needle under the nails of my toes and kick a wall as hard as I could or jump in front of a bus. He can't teach he knows the info but he has NO CAPACITY WHATSOEVER to teach and shouldn't LEGALLY be allowed to.

Once we were doing probability and I was confirming we put our questions in the table. Wood's response was uhh. mmm. well..uh.. not exactly.. uhmm well and just muttered and walked away. I called one of our TA's Sydney over and asked her the same question and got a simple, "Yes, exactly." which is just a taste of getting taught by John was like

He's sweaty, anxious and the symptoms of social anxiety. He stutters,stops and skips explanation in others and when he's not he's speeding through so quick math majors are lost. It got so bad we started recording the lecture  because he wouldn't slow down. On review it was teaching the lesson over again because that's how confused we all were.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If I could rate John Wood I would give him a -100/100. I only put 1 because they wouldn't let me put 0. John Wood is thee worst teacher I've EVER had the displeasure of having in academia. He's so bad I filed a complaint with the mathematics dept and as a sophomore in college is a professor that caused me to fail a class for the first time ever.

I have a list of issues with this dude:

1.) never responds to emails. like ever.

2.) Even though I love teachers that are passionate about what they teach, john would give us so much random unneeded information that just stressed me out

3.) cannot teach to save his life, I taught myself everything

4.) literally if you fail 1 exam you're done.

Class structure sucks but all profs have to teach it the same so it's probably not his fault. Guy is clearly a graduate student, nervous, knows a lot but teaches a little too advanced. Can show you things different ways if not clicking. Nice guy, has office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If you are forced to take finite DO NOT take this guy. He is a grad student and it shows. He does not know how to teach the material and he cannot answer questions asked in class. Additionally, he looks terrified every minute he is in the front of the class. He is awkward, jumps around, will never email you back, and is constantly out of breath.
Did not teach the material, couldn't answer questions asked in class, and was not available for office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It was alright. Every class felt too long and the topics go on forever. Teacher is a grad student so not an experienced teacher but knows his stuff. Can show how to do things a few ways. Web work sucks
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this professor. Lectures are impossible to understand and jumps all over the place. Teaches it in a way that no one can understand or follow along with. Comes into class rolling out of bed and out of breath. When you ask him a question, he never knows how to explain or the answer really. Don't recommend taking this class with him
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Office hours were always very helpful to me, but lectures are thorough and if you take good notes that will most likely be enough. The class meets a lot, so you'll probably get to know John pretty well if you try. Beware though, he likes to describe math as 'interesting' and 'fun'. Take that how you will.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The fact that tests are notoriously difficult is not highlighted enough in ratings. On top of that, there is deduce to learn as well. Prof. Siek is deeply caring, knowledgeable and ready to help. But do not expect the class to be easy. It is the hardest core CS class. Make sure to put in 12 hours of studying during the last 8 weeks of sem at least.

Very knowledge and caring professor. The tests were indeed difficult but doable. Also I took the honors version not the traditional section. So our was much smaller class size. And we got to interact with him on a more individual level, and we had less TAs too.
Highly Recommend! It takes a lot of effort to get through but from what I experienced and can tells about other lecturers. Jeremy is by far the best! Make sure to attend office hours!

Class is CSCI-H343 not CSCI-C343. Prof. Siek is a literal GOAT. Really enjoyed taking this class with Jeremy! He is highly knowledgeable and knows a lot about of data structures. I'm hoping to take compilers class with him too! Highly suggest.

One of the best professors I've taken. My only complaint is his proof programming language, Deduce, has a steep learning curve and inconsistent documentation, the assignments with Deduce are what brought my grade down to a B. However, you will learn a lot from his lectures and come out of the course much stronger.

This is my favorite professor at Indiana University bar none. I love this guy and you can tell that he cares. I am going out of my way to take his classes (even if they may not exactly align with my specialization) and I suggest you to do the same.

I came not expecting much from this course and treating it like a required class for interviews. I learnt about deduce, an assistant which he invented. IU is the first uni to teach deduce, and I really started liking theory because of him and the way he taught it. No wonder theory and deduce is difficult but worth learning.

Words can't describe how amazing, caring, best Jeremy is. Very organized. He has a scheduling meet to his students. I would suggest taking any Computer Science class he teaches, knowing that the tests are really difficult. Because he will by myside to be help and be there for me when I need him. I don't think I've met someone like Professor Siek.

Professor Siek is just a class apart. Taking his class, he always supported me, and answered any questions that I had. He even encouraged to explore compilers, pointers, and other technical stuff. He helped me build my base in Computer Science at IU.  I even changed my specialization from AI to PL cause of him.

Professor Siek is probably the best professor you will have at Luddy. You can see this by all the other positive reviews people have gave for him. My ONLY negative is that he makes you use his Deduce language in some parts of this course which can be tricky to learn (reason why I got a B instead of an A).
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. Siek is an absolute Genius. So lucky to have taken two classes with him, and learn so much from him. He even records lectures in case you fall sick! Have taken him twice, and as a senior can vouch that he is THE CS PROFESSOR. Have never heard a single person (students and faculty) dislike him. He is actually that good

Probably my favorite professor and class at IU. Compilers is not for the faint of heart but an amazing experience. Siek knows the material well, gives you a free pdf of the textbook, and is excited about what he is teaching. If you get the chance to take this or any other class with him, DO IT.

We are using deduce in Professor Siek's class. His teaching methodology reflects a genuine dedication to student success. His seamless integration of theory with real-world examples not only makes the subject matter more interesting but also reinforces a deeper understanding of the concepts.

Far and away the best prof I've had during my time at Luddy. Really caring and open to help as long as you approach him. Helped me out a lot when I was having a tough time in the course. Could not recommend any more.
Professor Siek's lectures are engaging and inspiring—challenging material made accessible through his clear explanations and genuine care for students

I took this class expecting tough material, but Professor Siek exceeded my expectations. I felt engaged in every lecture and his approach to explaining difficult concepts boosted my confidence in Computer Science.

I found Professor Siek's course both challenging and rewarding. I appreciated how he broke down complex topics into clear, manageable lessons, and his genuine support made a huge difference in my learning experience at Luddy. I had a great time minoring in Computer Science. He also helped me learn a lot about Luddy School.

Taking Professor Siek's course was a total highlight of my semester. I loved his which made every lecture feel amazing. His energy and real-world insights kept me engaged, and I genuinely looked forward to each class

Professor Siek's lectures were straight fire—every class felt like a chill sesh where I was leveling up my CS game without even trying. His vibes were always on point, making even the wildest concepts seem hella doable

from what i gathered, professor siek is on another level—his lectures are low-key lit, blending serious insights with a vibe that keeps you hooked from start to finish. no doubts compilers are very tough! in the end you will learn a lot.

The tests are extremely difficult, but if you dedicate enough time, do all the practice problems, all labs, and HWs, and actually understand what is going on, and review all lectures that he posts. Everything should be good. Jeremy Siek >>>

The class is very difficult, but Prof. Siek makes it worthwhile. He breaks down each concept so beautifully. That you learn and understand everything from a fundamental level. If there is one professor, you should definitely take a class with: It has to be Prof. Siek. He even provides class notes, and built a website for course. He is exceptional.

Consider very fortunate to be able take a course with Jeremy Siek. He invented Gradual Typing!! Typescript is based of what he invented. So lucky to take classes with him. I've taken both C343 and P423 with him. He is truly the best professor within Computer Science department. Highly Caring. Extremely Empathetic. He is a GOAT afterall.

I took Compilers with Professor Siek in Fall of 2024, and I loved it! It was my first time having Siek as a professor, and I had a phenomenal experience. He was incredibly knowledgable and more than happy to answer any questions with plenty enthusiasm. Highly recommend (course is not a cakewalk though!)

Compiler's is considered one of the hardest classes, however Seremy Jiek does an amazing job of making the material digestible and easy to understand. Be warned though that making the compiler itself leaves you with more gray hairs than Jiek by the time you're done with even a single assignment. Also do the extra credit it's fun.

Siek is a great lecturer, but you have to be willing to put in some work of your own. He's very available outside of class, and office hours are super helpful. Would recommend making sure you 100% understand content before turning in a lab assignment (or at least before the next lecture). Stay super on top of content and you'll be great.

Professor Siek is one of the best professors I have had. His lectures are very engaging and interesting. Even though there is no attendance, I highly recommend attending all lectures. This is a very important course and the TA's are also amazing and will help you get through it feeling ready for the future you have in cs.

Great proffessor. LOVE him! Very approachable, and cares for his students. Helps you out with everything that he can. He wrote his own textbooks used in class too! Very knowedgeable and gives excellent feedback. 
Also took compilers with him not C343

Prof. Siek is great, if you pay attention in lectures and do the assigned readings, you WILL get a good score on the exams. Labs are hard and projects are very hard, especially because the TA for the honors section couldn't explain anything, even the simplest concepts, so we basically did not have a TA

Dr. Siek is so knowledgeable and cares about his students. If you want to succeed, you have to be ready to work HARD in this class. And do NOT start your labs the day it's due- give yourself time to get it done and office hours are your best friend. Midterm and final are really hard- start studying early and take the practice exams seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: An outstanding, well-spoken, and highly knowledgeable guy. Gives off a "cool dad" vibe. Fairly large homework load but no busy work. You'll do atleast OK on the exams if you complete all the projects/labs
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: On godddd this is the nicest, coolest, and smartest professor in SICE. Prof Siek understands the material is hard, but wants you to succeed and will take as much time in or outside of class to make sure you understand the material. Really good lecturer and the kindest man ever. Love his dog too!!!

Very intelligent and extremely good at teaching complex concepts. Has a lot of charisma. Is easy to talk to which can be difficult to find in a cs professor. The coursework for 343 is by nature difficult. Class is fundamental and is expected to be a lot of work. Study the material, read the book, and ask questions. Office hours. Dont fall behind.

Jeremy is easily one of the smartest yet most approachable people you ever did meet, and that suits him well to teach this weeder computer science course. His lectures are actually interesting because the material flows rather well, unlike with some other CS professors. He also gives a great balance of homework vs. projects. Take C343 with HIM!

One of the best courses I have had at IU.  Yes he expects a lot, but nothing an undergrad with 2-4 CS courses can't handle if they put in effort.  He bases C343 from MIT open course ware, which is nice because there are supplemental videos.  If you don't want to work hard then don't take this class.  If you want to learn a lot, take this class.

I'm pretty sure the three posts below mine were made by the same person who is bitter after getting a bad grade in this class. Siek was an awesome professor in my opinion. It was tough, but I learned more in his class than I did in any other course at IU. He is a diamond in the rough of IU's computer science department.

Professor McManus made the marketing material clear and digestible. Compared to other I-Core Marketing Professors, the practice tests are not as useful in accurately representing the test material. Easy class to get a B, but if you're striving for an A you will have a hard time.
Professor McManus is very kind and a great professor. She uses examples that kept engagement throughout class and were genuinely interesting. Would definitely recommend her class!

Pretty easy class and fun yet relaxing because the work isn't tough but it can be interesting. She is super nice as well. However, she claims that you shouldn't worry about the exams because they aren't a big part of the grade which is not true. They're 60% of the grade so you need to take them seriously to get an A and if you care about that.

Easily one of the best if not the best ICORE professor, Kristy is an extremely kind, caring, and understanding person who takes the time to get to know her students. Marketing is typically one of the most underattended of the ICORE sections, but she makes learning marketing enjoyable and interesting!

I have never been so happy with a professor. I loved taking her class, and she makes Marketing enjoyable for people that do not like it. She really cares about all of her students, and she wants them to do well and learn the material. If you do not take this class with her, you will regret it. She is the best!

Look for another section. She takes the class too seriously despite not teaching a single thing. Communication is poor; feedback only points out faults without helping you improve. Office hours are a waste; she's unprepared and unwilling to help. She even posts notes discouraging students from reaching out. Avoid for your GPA and sanity.
Extremely picky with grading. Very tough grader. She's really nice, don't take if you want a comfortable A.

Prange is great and her classes are not bad the grading isn't that tough its just mostly 0 if you miss a part which could affect t the grade I got A- instead of an A just for not having partial credit for some topics just make sure that your presentations are decent and going to office hours is a great way to boost your grade for the presentation

Overall, a great teacher. She was nice and respectful, easy to talk to for the most part, and relatable, so the class wasn't always boring. I think she was a picky grader sometimes on the criteria for presentations, so just put forth your best work. Probably one of the best teachers for BUS-C 104 tbh, so I would def recommend her. Loves IU too!
Prange was a great teacher. She creates a great environment in her classes for C104. Would highly recommend her.

Professor Prange is great. She made what is often a scary class tolerable and at times fun. I feel like I grew significantly as a presenter/collaborator in this course. She gave good feedback on presentations and was willing to work with the skill levels of all students. I have recommended her course to students taking C104 in the coming semesters.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a good person and makes time for students outside of class. It takes a while for her to grade big presentations, but it's understandable with how many students she has. However, she is a very tough grader. She is very specific about certain things and if you want a good grade you must GO TO OFFICE HOURS.

GOAT, such a nice and understanding teacher. She puts effort to make her classes fun and taught me so much about presentations and I honestly can look back and say she improved me as a person and presenter.

I wasn't sure about this course, but if you have to take it, I think her class is pretty nice. She's an easy grader. One guy in my group forgot his part and started cursing before just giving up and moving on, and we still got an A on the presentation. Class can be slow sometimes, but she doesn't give busy work. Would recommend!

I was already confident presenting before this class, but she helped me feel even more confident. I feel so prepared for other class presentations now, this class was extremely helpful and worth it. You have a group and she picks them based on a google form. My group was great and we had no issues. Super easy grader as well. Group got 100% on final

Very solid C104 Proffesor, compared to what I heard my other friends had to deal with. If you put a little effort into your presentations, and take pride in making something nice, you will succeed in her class. She's very understand and gives good feedback, and is always willing to help her students. You get out what you put in.
Great prof and wonderful person! Def the pick
Best professor I have had at IU! As long as you put forth effort and do the work you will be fine
Great Professor, def your #1 Choice!

Professor Prange is not only an amazing professor but person. She truly cared about her students and it showed each class. She made sure her students were engaged at all times and her energy was always at 100% even though we had a later class.

She is an incredibly supportive professor and makes it clear she wants her students to succeed. As long as you show up on time to class and put effort into your presentations you will do well. She is also very personable and easy to talk to, and because of this, she creates a positive and supportive atmosphere in the classroom.

Professor Prange genuinely cares about her students and gives great feedback on how to make your presentation abilities better. She isn't too hard of a grader so if you do your work and really put in the effort it isn't hard to get an A. Would love to have her again in the future

Very nice woman but super strict about attendance. 2 absences a semester and if you're more than 10 minutes late she counts you absent no debate. Other than that if you just put in basic effort you're good.
The Professor we all wished we always had. Simply the GOAT!
Felt at first that she graded harshly, but the class got easier as time went by, overall it was pretty helpful.

Being honest, Compass 2 is going to be a lot of busy work regardless of your professor, so that's no knock against Prange. She's really sweet & will definitely take extra time to help you with career stuff. Although Compass is pretty boring, she tries her best to get past the boring stuff and incorporate fun activities in class.

Makes class much harder than it needs to be. Does not return grades in a timely manner, went into the final week of class with over 50% of grades still not given back to students. Does not communicate well with students. Overall would not recommend.

Takes attendance. Assignments are worth 80% of your grade but deducts points for no given reason. Says she doesn't just give out A's and it's true. She will give u a C for a compass class which is dumb. Makes the class so much more work than it needs to be. I would have taken anyone else besides her.

Horrible horrible teacher. So much busy work and while busy work is a staple of Compass, she takes off random points here and there and assigns a boatload of useless work. She takes her job teaching the stupidest class in Kelley waaay too seriously. Recommend she retires ASAP.
Professor takes class too seriously. Her grading structure is very, very hard. However, she is a good speaker and helps you build some skills.

Kirsten is an "OK" teacher. I think she does take the class a little too seriously and tends to make things more daunting than necessary. There is, of course, a lot of busy work which is a staple of the Compass classes, so be ready for that. I do think she cares for her students and wants them to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prange was pretty solid as a professor, definitely given the class she was teaching. Compass is notoriously a very boring class with a lot of busy work. This class was no different, but thank god that Prange didn't make it any worse than it had to be. Generosity with grading aided her case a lot as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He is too old to be honest, and his teaching style is old, stale, and like an Oxford professor in the way he demands high quality writings. He does not leave room for leniency. He may also be biased toward his students based on unethical components(ethnicity/religion). He should be looked into. -IUB
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is a generally nice guy, but the content became repetitive and boring and he didn't put any grades in or give feedback on the essay, midterm, or final until the last day of the semester. Lots of reading and reading quizzes every class, but you learn very little additional info in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Basically talks about nothing all class, assigns a lot of readings, grades slightly harsh, and treats you like you're "unintelligent" to say the least whenever you ask any question.

Took JSTU-L 270. Quizzes every class for attendance. Short essays for final. Homework is reading a few chapters of books or poems. The class itself seemed interesting at first, but there was too much content shoved into the semester, and I lost interest. Said he would ban tech next semester because nobody was participating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's not a bad guy at all by any means and is pretty reasonable. That being said, you should expect to do a lot of reading though alongside writing essays you'd expect in an intensive writing course. In general, unless you're really interested in this stuff, I'd just take the classes you need and leave it at that. You'll to read A LOT, trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I highly recommend Dr. Katz. He is a wealth of information and so eager to see his students succeed. The material he selects for his classes is very informational and intriguing. But, there is a lot of reading. He promotes dialogue and encourages students to ask questions. His class on The Kibbutz in Fact and Fiction was amazing. I learned so much!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I highly recommend to not take this course with Professor Katz. His lectures are extremely boring and a waste of time; many times spending 75 minutes speaking on one chapter in a book. His grading is horrible, never telling you what was wrong with papers. He doesn't teach students HOW to write the way he expects it, more so just penalizes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Legitimately this man's classes will go down in history as some of the hardest you've ever taken. AP Calc? Organic chemistry? Haha those will seem easy in comparison to this man's designs. You'll tell your children one day about the triumphs you braved getting through this. Good luck to the brave hearted.
It's honestly impressive how long this guy can speak about the exact same thing. He's a sweet guy, but I'm a senior and this is easily the most boring class I've ever taken.

Besides being an interesting professor, he is a genuinely nice person.  Went above & beyond to help me understand material and wants his students to succeed and also learn something from his class- to spark an interest.

I've taken his classes several times. I always found him funny, interesting and interested in his students. He has a daily quiz that tests some aspect of the readings... they aren't difficult, but you'll usually only know the answer if you've read what he assigned for the day. He also allows make-ups for all the quizzes.
Hebrew class was fun with him.

This class was so boring. He rambles on about things that are off topic and doesn't care if people look even remotely interested. This class also had an incredible about of reading that was so outdated that it made it painful to sit down and read it. Stay away from this class- apparently he's better at teaching Hebrew.

Best L201 professor at Kelley by a mile. Extremely clear grading criteria. 10 short quizzes rather than 3-4 long tests. Material is explained thoroughly and there are no surprises on the quizzes. Prof. Keller not only cares about her students but the material she is teaching. Go to class, spend time studying, you'll get an A.

Professor Keller is the best L201 professor at Kelley. All topics are clearly outlined, and the quizzes for each chapter actually follow material taught instead of aimless tests. 9-10 shorter quizzes rather than 3-4 long tests. If you attend class regularly and put in 30 extra minutes outside of class daily, you will get an A.

I actually took 293, but loved the way she taught it. She's super approachable and knowledgeable, and I found the lecture content to be interesting and engaging. As long as you follow along in class you should have no trouble getting an A.

I recommend Prof Keller. She is professional, knowledgeable, and caring. Her lectures had relevant applications, she gave lots of practice for the theories, and she created a comfortable environment for participation. Her grading is clear and straightforward. Overall great!

For BUS-L 100 she uses specifications grading. There are no tests only quizzes. You must get an 80% to master the quiz, and master 9 of 10 quizzes for an A. She has 3 retakes as well. I took the class online and learned a lot. She has lots of required participation on TopHat that help with quizzes. Make sure to take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class had a unique grading system that made it easy to work around my schedule. A lot of content is covered, but Professor Keller explains it well and provides numerous examples (some educational and some fun). I would highly recommend taking this class with her.
