reviews.comment: The teacher is nice but the class setup is pretty poor. The final is worth 80% of your grade the final review is really similar to what you'll see on the exam. People do poorly because they don't show up and take notes or go to the final review.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jamie is your only option so whether you want her or not is irrelevant. The class in general can be tough because the final is worth a very large portion of the grade. Be somewhat proactive and spend a couple of days really studying for the final and you'll be fine.

A100 is the only class that kept me from a 4.0 GPA. I felt like each 8-week class varied greatly in difficulty, with 1st semester's 1st 8 weeks being awful. Several questions on my exam had no correct answers, and the exam's content barely related to the class. She's an ok professor, but her exam felt impossible to succeed on.
If u attend the lectures, she will often tell u what questions will be in the exam & will help u prepare. good professor. make sure to read the book and actually try in the weekly quizzes
She is knowledgeable, but the teaching methods are not strong. It is so easy to not pay attention in class. The final is worth 50% of your grade.
she doesn't teach well at all and always has an attitude

I understand why everybody dislikes Jamie, but the class itself is not particularly difficult to get through. Skip the lectures and really read the textbooks. She provides mid-term and final practice days where her TAs solve through a sample test. These sessions are super helpful so make sure to sign up for them when they open.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just not the best as an introductory Accounting class, especially for a school with a nationally top ranked accounting program. Heavy on conceptuality, not big on actual numbers. Few things to be graded by, and final is worth a big percentage of the grade. Every business freshman has to take this class and she is the only professor. Read the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Seitz teaches A100 as if it is a review course and not an introductory one. She often skips over crucial material and rambles. Learn from my mistakes and skip lectures all together. If you read the book and go over and understand the checkpoints you will be ready for the final which is worth 50% of your grade and only 20 questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She talks more about her trucking company than Accounting, it's actually crazy. If you want to learn about a failing truck company that's losing $ then she is the perfect professor for you
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class information is not hard to understand overall. The lectures are close to pointless. The lectures information are poorly placed within the lecture and she just talks a lot about what is shown on the slide. Study the top hat information and go to the extra help sessions that is how you pass.

Although she is a very kind person once you get to speak with her, her teaching is pretty hard to follow. I attended all of the lectures, took notes, and completed most of the assignments on time, had a 101%, failed the final and ended with a 61%. I'd recommend asking questions ASAP and reading the book. do NOT rely on learning from her lectures!!

Professor Seitz is extremely intelligent when it comes to accounting but explains as if you already know the material. The TopHat chapter readings are the Bible in this class. There are 7 total chapters. Read and take notes and then reread and add to those notes. Go to reviews and lectures are optional. Read, Read, Read !

Professor Seitz rambles in class about her husbands trucking company and tries to act like she is intelligent. She doesn't care about her students growth and your entire grade is basically one exam. I stopped going to class and learned the material entirely by myself, rarely even using the IU coursework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: just no.

Seitz is a good person but not a good professor. Lectures get very confusing, especially if you don't know how accounting works. The textbook is your bible for this class. I would strongly recommend understanding how accounting works. The Final was easier for the 2nd 8weeks sesh than the first. Attend the lectures (might be mandatory).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A100 is a relatively easy class as long as you attend the lectures and read the textbook. Her lectures can seem useless as she will go on strange tangents, but they are a must if you want to know about specific test questions. She is also fairly unavailable as every business student has her (Idk why they do this).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed attending Pro. Seitz's lectures. They didn't always cover the exact material as the book or what should be expected on the exam, but she taught in a very engaging way. Those who view her in a negative light are the students who expect their grades to just be handed to them. Pay attention and stay caught up and you will succeed.

She is a nice person, but she is not the best teacher. Better to read the textbook than go to class. Everyone goes into the final with a 100% (or more if you do the extra credit) but the final is difficult. Discussion sessions with the TA's are nice and there are extra review questions on Quizlet but get ready this is not an easy A class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, Professor Seitz is not a bad teacher. If you pay attention to her lectures, she does tend to emphasize certain things that will appear on the final exam. You do have to learn a lot on your own by reading the textbook (essential for doing well on the final). Read textbook before class, so her lectures can be used to reiterate the material.

The final exam is the biggest part of the class grade, which is stressful. But the rest of the class assignments are super easy, so you should be able to go into the final exam with an A. She moved really fast in the lectures, so it is important to read the textbook to fully learn the material. Teaching assistants were awesome and super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class isn't too bad. I had some health issues and wasn't able to attend some lectures, but I studied the textbook and used the extra study sessions which definitely helped. If you read the textbook and take notes in the lectures, then the weekly quizzes should be a breeze. Work hard and you'll get the grade you deserve.

In class, there is a lot of information in a small period of time, so I basically did a self-study on A100 through the chapters each week. Weekly mini-quizzes are the only assignments, and it's easy to do well on those. Overall, she is a really inspiring business professional.

Because she doesn't look like most Kelley professors I bumped up the rating from a 1 to a 2. All of your grade hinges on one test so if you're not prepared you'll likely meet the same fate as Seitz trucking. This class is similar to your high school Accounting class except you won't learn anything and won't spend much time talking about accounting.
Terrible teacher. You can get a better grade just reading the textbook and doing practice problems, she can't teach you about anything other than Seitz Trucking and Holding (which went under)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She gets a lot of hate for no reason. The final exam is not that bad. She gives extra credit and it's easy to go into the final with over 100%. Her lectures are pretty solid, but I would definitely read the book still. All complaints about this class are coming from people that crammed the night before, ignore what others are saying about her.

Jamie is a nice professor but the class isn't fun. To do well in the class read the book and really understand what you are reading. Attendance isn't mandatory but I find that it helped me understand concepts better. Attend the peer help meetings. They review how to do the checkpoints and podcasts and will also go over potential final questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jamie is a wonderful person, super kind and always says hello! That being said, she should not be a lecturer. Right now, shes the only option for A100 but if you can get another DO IT. I can tell you more about her husband's trucking company than I can accounting because that's how lectures are spent. If you read Top Hat VERY closely you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's not that bad, but if you can pick another professor, you probably should. She does not do a good job making sure you understand the material for the final. She gets sidetracked, and you are better off just not going to class. She is confusing and doesn't cover the material well. Pick someone else if you still have a chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took great notes for the first 4 weeks (of an 8 week course), but after that my interest in the lectures fell off and I only showed up to be somewhere at 10 AM. I got an 80% on the final. The final is 50% of your final grade but the other 50% is free, so all you need is a 70% on the final in order to finish with a B.

Test is literally 50% of the grade and she doesnt prepare you for any of it. Why is the intro to accounting class just an introduction to almost every topic in accounting? Why not just introduce the beginning topics and actually give students a good background on them? Shes nice and the class isnt hard she just sucks at her job.

This teacher does not properly teach you what you need to know for the final. All she talks about is her husband's trucking business. Not a good professor if you are trying to get the B for Kelley or if it's in your first semester class schedule.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Seitz is passionate about the subject and if you do the readings you will do well on the quizzes. Make sure to be prepared coming to class. However, the exam is 50% of the grade and tests on very specific concepts. Reading notes and reviewing quizzes is not enough to prepare if you want a good grade in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures were basically pointless to go to she barely taught anything and we were always let out early. Professor stressed the class was only about the accounting theories and not math so we did at most one math problem a week in class and the final was 70% math which most students did not know how to do at all.

You have to teach the entire class to yourself before the final because she does not go over anything thats on the final during the class lectures. Goes on pointless rants and teaches us things that are not even useful for the class.

Don't bother going to lectures. She spends the lecture on a random tangent or discussing her husbands trucking company. I did get a 106 because I took notes on the textbook, had two Peer Tutor meetings and went to a review session at the place by Mother Bears. It is not impossible, but you are better off studying and taking notes from the textbook.

One of the more difficult freshman classes you will take while not being taught by a great professor. Her lectures made it more difficult to understand what was going on and eventually I stopped going to class and just taught myself for the final (which is 50% of the grade). You'll learn more than you want about her husbands company too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, this class is hard for people because they make it hard on themselves. I recommend reading the textbook over twice before the exam because everything in it is on the exam. I got a 98% on it, and that is exactly what I did. Also review the weekly quizzes because some of the questions will be word for word the same.

To do well in this class you really need to read the top hat text book and look over slides. She doesn't really teach well in class and goes over pointless stuff like excel when excel isn't even used in the class. You kind of have to teach yourself
Be prepared to hear about Seitz trucking

Doesn't use a mic, felt like a mom yelling at her kids for 70 minutes. Barely tought anything, better off studying only from the textbook than attending class. All work was easy until it came to the exam worth 50% of the grade with no preperation.

There was barely any sort of revision material for the final, which is 50% of the grade. I had a hard time studying for it, despite attending her boring, meaningless lectures, in which she goes on talking about her ADHD and her trucking company. Poor grading criteria, and she's the only A100 teacher to make it worse. Prayers up for anyone taking it

I like her as a person because she is very kind and tries very hard to be a good prof. However, the final is 25 questions and worth 50% of final grade. She offers no prep for exam, and exam is extremely hard. Furthermore, going to class confused me more than it helped me.

If you take A100 with professor seitz. Goodluck, She is terrible and barely teaches anything. The test is completely random and 1/2 of the test we didn't even learn. She gives weekly quizzes but none of it applies to the test. You basically will have to teach yourself everything because she doesn't. 


Goodluck, 

Pray you do not get her for A100

Jamie Seitz is one of the worst professors that I encountered at IU. She constantly goes off topic during her lectures, talking about her trucking company and blaming it on her ADHD. Good thing I had already taken accounting in high school or else I would probably have been screwed. Be ready to teach yourself all the concepts because she sure won't

Jamie's lectures are so confusing and all over the place. I went to almost every class and only learned from reading the textbook and studying from the checkpoints. Going to class was always so confusing. You get through the whole class lost, only to have to cram for the final having no idea if you are prepared. Good luck. This class sucks.

Absolutely awful. Did fine enough the whole class and then failed the final and I got a 68% in the class. You need a 70% to pass by Kelley standards. I hated her so much I decided to change my major and leave Kelley than take A100 with her again. Took extensive TopHat notes, understood, and failed. This was awful and good luck to anyone taking this

Barely went to class because I would only get more confused. Ended up teaching myself the whole class from the book and did well on the final. Would honestly say going to class could be a waste of time for some people, you just have to teach yourself.

Lectures are extremely boring and she frequently goes off topic. I stopped going to her class and taught myself the entire curriculum a week before the final and got an A. Just take notes on the tophat textbook and practice the questions from tophat and weekly quizzes. The only grades are the podcast assignments, weekly quizzes, and the final.

I learned nothing from Jamie's lectures as they were all over the place. After the first week I just stopped going and just read the textbook and ended with a b-, which would have been an A without the 50% final that is put together just like her terrible lectures. She's a nice person but not a good professor.
Hard to follow in lectures, try to keep up week to week with material, good luck

Jamie really is not as bad as people say she is. Honestly ya lectures are kind of annoying but she told us day one that if you cram the night before the exam, you will get an A just fine and this is true. A good 4 or 5 questions on her exam are on the check point. She curves a ton! If you do not like her attendance is not mandatory or necessary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: K this might be a hot take but I dont think Jamie is nearly as bad as everyone says she is. Shes the reason why A100 is much easier even though her lectures arent good. She didnt make us do daily assignments or anything so the homework in that class is very easy. I also had talks with her one on one and I felt like she really cared about me.

Seitz is a nice and caring person, but it can be hard to follow along with what she is saying. There's also (unfortunately) no resources for additional practice/tutoring, so read thoroughly. Take your time on checkpoints, ask questions before/after class as needed, and study up for the exam and you will do just fine.

It wasn't that hard for me and I don't think it would be that hard for anyone if they read the textbook, The textbook literally explains every detail. I would say the class was average in terms of difficulty and for advise on the exams, practice the textbook questions and checkpoint.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Seitz is clearly very knowledgeable about accounting. However, she doesn't do a very good job teaching the material. The only quiz/test/exam is the final. Only 21 questions on the final. I figured there would be more practice doing actual accounting and practicing the ideas but the class is very definition and formula heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class has easily got to be worst structured class I've ever taken in my life. No one is ever clear on what the content is, how to study, or what she is even talking about in lectures. During class she constantly jumps from topic to topic without explanation, leaving confusion for literally everyone to figure out for themselves. Good luck.

Absolutely no final prep material given at all during the course and what she teaches doesnt prepare you either. Textbook barely correlates to the exam either. Taking the class for a second time as she is the only prof for this course, was hoping it would be better this time and it is absolutely not.

Skims through everything during class and does not provide enough material outside of class to know what is going on. Half of your grade is your final exam and there are very few assignments leading up to it. She's rushed all the time and goes on tangents, wasting time of our already short class. She needs to streamline and prioritize content.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: None of what she says makes sense the textbook was written by the previous A100 teacher and what Seitz teaches in class isn't similar to the textbook. The quiz questions are very hard and are difficult to do even if you attend class and read the book. Essentially, you leave more confused than you entered.

Jamie seitz has an annoying horrible lecture style. I am unable to focus on the sound of her voice as she drones on and on barely explaining the accounting principles I so badly want to learn. Unfortunately, our university has decided she will be the only professor teaching this class. For students, that spells failure.
Only cares about her trucking business. literally uses this class to promote it.

Had a bad time in this class. Missed the first podcast reflection, took me from a 100 to an 89, did as best as I could on the final and got a 68, and she never curved my exam, even after I told her the "bell curve" didn't change it. Never responds to emails. Pretty bad professor, too bad she's the only one at IU.

Dr. Seitz was an okay teacher, and she was undoubtedly knowledgeable and passionate about what she taught. However, she didn't teach what was on the final. Furthermore, the final was worth 45% of our grade, and we were given no study materials. I spent 20 hours leading up to the final studying, and I got a 68%, results may vary, but I'd be weary.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your only choice for A100 as of now, but a solid one. Tries really hard to make her students passionate about the material, but absolutely no practice resources are given before exams, as she "doesn't believe in them". The lack of tangible resources is the only real obstacle in this course, so keep up with each reading and you will be fine.
Going to her class was completely useless because she only talked about her trucking company. All you need to do is read the textbook and you should be fine.

I thought Dr. Seitz was a very good professor and had a ton of real world accounting experience which helped. You need to do well on all the assignments in order to do well in the class since the entire grade is only out of like 200 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was okay and if you haven't taken accounting before you should probably go. Should study a lot for the final.

Had a 98 all of the 8 week class and studied and understood the content very well. Did not do that because of Sietz she rambled on about her trucks most of the time while the PowerPoint had very little words and she made no sense when teaching. The final was literally impossible. One question on there had not enough information to do the problem.
you have to teach urself the whole class. claims she's "understanding" and "cares" but is actually one of the least understanding and caring teachers i've had in my entire life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She just pretty much talks about her trucking company half the time. She talks faster than my ears can even hear. Her lectures only go over relevant stuff for a solid 5 minutes per class. Blames it on her ADHD but I think she's just insane. Good luck on the final lol you'll need it
Terrible class

All over the place. I found one in every 4 classes useful. Too many times did I receive a lecture on the trucking industry which has nothing to do with the class content. Weekly quizzes are easy as are the podcasts. The final essentially composes the entirety of your grade. I found content easy but not because of Seitz.

Seitz can get carried away often times while teaching and spend up to half the class talking about either her son or her husbands trucking business. I do have to say that she is pretty good at breaking down concepts, but don't be afraid to ask her to repeat stuff because she does move fast. Do the work before class and study hard and youll do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A100 was reworked this year and Dr. Seitz was a new teacher at IU. You learn most of the material through reading the textbook, although I think the lectures are helpful. She does seem to go on tangents and get off track, however they do relate to class material. FEW opportunities for graded points, make sure you do well on weekly "checkpoints."
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: There are quizzes every week, she calls them checkpoints and they are only 5 questions. Overall you just have to read the textbook on TopHat and go to class and it shouldn't be hard. The only difficult part is the final which is 45% of your grade. Also, attendance is not mandatory but going to class makes it a lot easier.

Dr. Seitz is a great person, but not a good teacher. She barely goes over anything during class, and half of what she does go over doesnt relate to class content. What she taught in class did not reflect the content on the final. Final is 100 out of 220 points in the class, and you arent given any study materials. Be ready to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Seitz is a great person, but not a great teacher. Be prepared to teach yourself most, if not all of the material. Take notes over the chapters BEFORE class, she flips through slides quickly. Most importantly, create your own study materials, you won't be given any.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a great guy who truly cares about student success, but the class is not great. He covers way too much material, and exams are significantly harder than the homework. The curve and extra credit aren't enough to save your grade if you struggle with the tests.

He is a great professor. Super patient/clear in lectures and respects students' time, also has a pretty lenient attendance policy in my opinion. He posts a lot of resources on canvas. Beware the class is very test heavy, but you should be fine if you really do the practice tests. I really liked taking the class with him, recommend.

Do not take Lantis, You get under 2% extra credit for the whole semester (where other professors it's 8%) He over explains and complicates topics for no reason, also Is a huge stickler about the top hat codes, and overall takes this way TOO seriously. I often found myself wishing I got hit by a car before class. Take Schwindel instead

Lantis is a solid professor. The class is pretty boring, but if you put in the work you can do well. The class is very lecture heavy, and Lanty makes sure to use up all 75 minutes. He can be pretty rude, but if you look past all that, hes a decent proff. Take schwendel for the a+ take lanty for b+ and take groff b and take glaum for the f

I recommend taking Lantis for Econ B251. His lectures weren't that beneficial, but his practice tests were very similar to the real ones. He also gave easier tests compared to other teachers and gave bonus questions on the test. For my class, he rounded grades too.

His tests are so much harder than the other Econ classes, so that alone wouldn't choose him. Barely any extra credit for his class compared to others. Tries to act "cool" but isn't. Would choose someone else if possible. Not the worst choice, but definitely not a recommendation
He has done a great job this year with the difficulty of the class, I would advise on getting better at conceptual understanding. Highly recommend Professor Lantis.

Lantis is a really good professor. He will everything to help you get a good grade (coming from a pre-business student). He takes time to talk to and respond to student's emails. DO THE PRACTICE EXAMS until you know them like the back your hand, will literally allow you to do the exams on autopilot. Good extra credit (1.8%) by going to CL sessions.

Professor Lantis is tough. He makes topics very confusing and overcomplicated at times which makes it hard to study for exams. He isn't the most helpful when you go to office hours for questions. Go to all of the CL sessions because you can get extra credit for them, always go to them from the beginning because you don't know when you'll need it.

the tests take most of the weight for this class and his tests aren't easy and are not the same level as the problems he shows in class and for the quizzes you can study hard enough to get a good grade, but I would not recommend taking the class with Lantis

Lantis is a pretty good professor. I definitely agree with other comments about him overcomplicating topics, which makes lectures confusing. His practice exams are very similar to the tests which helps a lot since he doesn't give extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His tests are not what he teaches in class. He confuses students and makes sure they fail with little curves and no extra credit. Do not take him. Take Graf instead.

Just take another prof. His first exam was brutal with the class average of 70%, he curved that exam by 1 point so only 2%. Very small extra credit compared to other profs, 1.8%. Overcomplicates concepts that are simple. Because of the weight the Impact of the first exam can make it very difficult for a come back especially if you need a B+.
Professor Lantis is one of the best professors for econ. He gives extra credit questions on exams, is an easy grader for discussions, and gives the easiest exams.

Fine professor. I felt Prof Lantis overcomplicated simple concepts which was confusing on the exams (exams were much more complicated than practice ones). You need to learn his teaching style and when to stop taking notes when he begins to add extra terms. I got a D on the midterm but an A- on the final from learning his lecture style. Manageable.

Lantis is the man. He is pretty funny during his lectures and super responsive to emails. His tests are very similar to the study guide he gives you. He offers CL sessions that make a difference. Overall, great dude class is easy if you do the study guides and keep up with the quizzes.

I personally felt like his practice materials did not reflect the actual quizzes except for the final, which made me struggle in terms of underpreparing. I would recommend taking other econ profs because they give SO much more extra credit.

Lantis often overcomplicated simple concepts in his lectures and did not teach what actually mattered. However he gave plenty of practice material which is super similar to his tests. First test was pretty hard but the next two were super simple. GO TO CL SESSIONS the .15 credits per session adds up. Overall would reccomend!

Lantis is a good professor who makes economics easy to learn. Sometimes his exams would be harder than the practice tests he gave. Go to the CL sessions, take good notes, and do all the practice problems, quizzes and practice exams before an exam and you'll be fine.
trust me, dont take him. The exams have questions that I swear I couldn't find anything similar to in the practice one that he gave us.
He did a very good job balancing concepts with practicality. Gave a ton of material to study for exams.

This was a very difficult class. He's very rude when questions are asked during lecture and he teaches a lot of stuff that isn't in the textbook. Lectures are boring but very important if you want to succeed. Attend the CL sessions for extra credit every single week. Practice exams are nothing like the exams so know how the graphs work.
Best B251 professor. The final is not cumulative. B251 is a very test heavy class no matter what professor you take. The class will not be easy but show up and learn and you will be alright.

Great class if you show up and take notes. Lots of lecturing but the tests are not cumulative, up to 1.5 pts of extra credit, practice tests mostly reflect the exams. If you have questions he's helpful in office hours. Use the quizzes and practice problems he gives to study. I got a 76 on the first exam and a 96 on the final because I studied well
Hard af. There are questions on the exam not in the textbook at all.

Lectures can be a bit of a bore, but Lantis explains the subject very clearly and in-depth. I struggled in AP econ and Lantis made it much easier, he's a chill guy. Go to CL sessions, do the practice problems, and you should be fine. The midterms were harder than the study guide, but the final was ridiculously easy and exactly like the study guide.

Tough class but really interesting (when you know what's going on). He tends to go fast so attend lectures and pay attention and everything is straight forward. He's a real straight-up prof but actually real chill and understanding, and accommodating (office hrs and such). Class was 2 exams, a bunch of long STATA problems sets and a few quizzes.

The lectures are very long, and the professor often explains the same idea in many different ways, which can make it hard to stay focused on the main concepts. The exams are also much harder than the practice problems, so it's difficult to know if you're truly prepared. Overall, the course feels challenging and time-consuming.

I thought he wasn't very nice at times to students asking questions in class. He explains well in lectures but they can get really boring. Go to CL sessions and do all practice problems/exams. The exams are harder than practices so make sure you really understand the practice exams and not just memorizing answers.

It might be the fact that Kelley is pushing professors to grade the "weed-out" classes progressively harshly, but don't take Lantis for econ thinking it's an easy A. He refused to curve a midterm we had due to an average score of 76 being "too high". 

Technically gives a lot of available resources, just not much compassion beyond that.

He's a very good professor. He provides many different tools and resources you can utilize to succeed in the course, including a tiny bit of extra credit. His lectures are fairly boring, but he does try to show different ways to understand concepts if you don't get it.

I took his Econ B251 class this semester. He's a really nice guy and clearly loves teaching, but the fast-paced lectures were tough to keep up with since I'm not very familiar with econ. I ended up cramming for exams, usually scoring in the 70s but still above average. Heavy on lectures, graphs, and conceptual problems.

He's a good prof, gives 1.8pts of extra credit. in class codes for attendance to access in class quizzes, but not mandatory. He gives lot of help like module practice problems and module quizzes, and practice midterm/final exams. I just suck at econ, so my grade isn't good, but overall, he is a good prof - has lots of office hours and TA/GA hours

The practice tests are very different from the actual exam. I go through the practice in 10 minutes, do all of the practice questions for each unit, and go over my missed questions in the weekly quizzes. I still got a 76% on the midterm because the exam combines multiple topics into one question which isn't really shown on the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As someone who took AP Econ in hs and generally doesn't need to study much to get A's, this class is HARD. Lock in early. He offers 0.15% for each CL session you go to, if you go to all 12 you get 1.8%. Go from the start, you can always stop if you don't need the points. I wish I went earlier than I did. Exams are hard and not like practice exams.

I'm not sure I liked him—you can't tell if he cares. Exams aren't like the study guide, and his grading/questions are odd. Only a couple assignments a week, but they're tough and matter a lot. You'll need time outside class since he's not a great explainer. Overall meh I'd recommend another Econ teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His ability to teach, explain, and aid in understanding of materials is significantly lacking. There are 3 exams which each have 25 questions and are 200 points. While there are other grades, you must do well on these exams to do well in the class. The exam material is not similar to the practice exams he posts or the weekly quizzes.

B251 with Lantis has been nothing short of painful. Having to self study every single unit for this class has been tedious. In class lecture will not cut it. You need to do lots of out of class work to succeed. The exams are not super similar to most class material (not completely awful but rough). Exams are based on true deep understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Least favorite professor I have. Class is boring and he does not make an effort to be kind or welcoming. Very sarcastic and is rude when asking clarifying questions in class. Practice quizzes are not similar to exams AT ALL. I understand more from one campus tutoring session than I do from half a semester worth of his class. Would NOT recommend.

This class is overall really hard, but you need to take it with him or Groff. Study as the class goes, as someone who usually gets good grades without studying TRUST you gotta lock in. Also, he's kind of rude but don't take it to heart. The tests just get harder so make sure you understand all the concepts fully and study every day.

AWFUL. I took his econ class because he had a very good rating on this site. ITS WRONG. Kelley is encouraging teachers to grade harder, his practice tests are NOTHING like the exams (I got 100% on all practices and attended the review sessions just to absolutely FAIL the exam. Does not care about you and will not be kind or considerate.

I don't understand the good review's. It seems like Lantis wants you to fail as the practice tests are way easier than the actual tests. There are also quizzes at the end of the week that are very hard to score 100% on and will lower your grade. He does a good job explaining the material, but doesn't give hard examples like on the tests.

Very straightforward teacher with a clear routine—he teaches econ through both slides and visual examples. He offers a good amount of extra credit and the practice tests match the difficulty of the real exams. He's also open to questions and holds dedicated review sessions before each exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He doesn't take accountability for his mistakes, like forgetting to post assignments or quizzes on the dashboard. Instead of admitting these errors, he blames students and says things like 'you should have known this.' His lectures are also hard to follow because he rambles without clear direction. Horrible professor take someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very hard to understand what is going on. he explains something 7 different ways instead of focusing on enhancing the skill. very lecture heavy and bounces between thoughts and almost seems unprepared.

I don't know why people are saying Lantis is a bad professor. If you come to class and pay attention, he really prepares you for the exams. I got As on both of my midterms and utilized his office hours which helped a lot. Also go to CLL sessions. Pay attention. Come to class. Practice exams help a lot for the tests. One of my favorite profs.

Lectures are long and boring - easy to lose focus during 75 minutes of straight talking twice a week. The grade mainly depends on tests, which are nothing like his study guides and are made harder with little support. CL sessions are also at inconvenient times and locations. Overall, I dislike the class and his teaching style, but he's a nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not the best professor. Isn't great at teaching. Practice tests are completely different from the real test. Because they are multiple choice you could get half the question right but still completely get the question wrong because it is a two-parter. Only way to pass the class is to get the CL session extra credit.
Don't take him other professors are better

As a Pre-Kelley student, this was by far the hardest class for the B grade. Professor Lantis gives you everything you need to help you do good on the exams. Go over every practice questions, know why each question is right/wrong, because those are very similar to the ones on the exam. 10/10 Professor
certified goat, if you got him be happy and make sure you go to the extra credit things the 2.5% raise of your grade at the end of the year will bump your grade up

I took B251 as an online class this summer. Attendance wasn't mandatory due to recorded lectures but was strongly encouraged. Prof. Lantis was often available for office hours and cleared up any confusion. The course isn't too difficult but some material is challenging. Overall, great professor! I strongly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Hold yourself accountable to pay attention in lecture and do extra practice. Enough points with extra credit, top hat participation, and Canvas quizzes that are very similar to his practice problems. Second exam is tough but the rest are conceptual so just knowing the material and studying in advanced is key. He reviews in class so ask questions.

Doesn't give a lot of extra credit and lectures can be draining at times. Grade is almost entirely based on exams. I did well in the course, but it was honestly more helpful to relearn the material outside of class.
Very easy to learn from. Gives lots of examples to help you learn
He's just a G
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lantis is a goated teacher. He does his best to make every lecture enjoyable and is extremely well-versed in the curriculum. His exams are a bit harder than the other classes, but he provides ample resources for you to succeed. GO TO THE CL. They make a big difference at the end of the semester, and they are the only extra credit you can receive.
Would 100% recommend for B251! He makes it easy to learn and his practice exams are almost exactly like the midterms and finals. If you try a little, you should get an A.
Lecture gets boring like any other lecture, but Lantis does a great job at teaching what we need to know for exams and giving us enough practice to understand the content.

Awesome guy and great professor. I struggled early on but going to the CL sessions (which are for extra credit) and being able to access all the lessons through his YouTube was really helpful. Overall hes a chill guy and I would recommend him, especially compared to the other profs.

This guy was the only low grade ive gotten at this school. His tests were nothing like the practice and even though he was knowledgeable he went extremely fast and never answered questions. Quizzes were also unnecessarily hard. Even after studying all content its still possible to get a C on exams. Take Graf.
that's my guy

Offers up to 3% in extra credit through optional collaborative learning sessions, gives lots of practice material including a practice midterm that is very similar to the actual exam, gives engaging examples in class, and is very accessible and responsive outside of class time.
Did not do a good job preparing for tests. The practice test are very different from the real tests. It seems like he does not prepare you for the tests he himself is writing. Would not recommend.
Not understanding at all. Don't recommend taking econ with him.

His practice exams are like the actual exams, which is helpful for preparation. His lectures can  feel fast-paced or out of order, but he is accessible during office hours and CL sessions, where he clarifies concepts. 

Be prepared to put in the effort— even if you've taken economics before.
i just hated him
His test questions can be confusing sometimes, mostly because of poor wording. Grading is not too hard, and he is pretty helpful. Lots of extra credit available.
He was great and helped you when you needed it. If you just do the work and go to office hours you will be fine.

Great professor, clearly very caring and knowledgeable. Did his best to make his lectures fun and relatable, but sometimes concepts during lecture were mildly unclear, in which case going to his office hours occasionally was fantastic, he explains everything very clearly. Extra credit in the form of going to extra learning sessions, up to 3%.

Really great professor. Offers lots of extra credit through CL sessions and extra test questions. I had never taken econ before but every concept was explained very clearly. Makes the class pretty easy for it being a required Kelley class. Midterms and final is just like the practice exams. Take B251 with him if you can

Prof. Lantis is a wonderful lecturer. Econ may not be the easiest subject, but if you show up to office hours to review quizzes and tests, create an outline of notes before class, (he posts slides and recordings!), and go to the extra credit CL sessions, you will be just fine. He is a kind and accommodating teacher. Take this class!

This guy is so chill. He gives a lot of extra credit and is super nice. Econ isn't a hard subject and he helped by making it even easier. His study guides were perfect in prep for exams too, as they were basically the same questions with just different numbers.

Very good professor, his lectures were interesting and relevant to exam materials. He provided lots of practice material that looked just like the exams which was nice. Very understanding and good professor.

The greatest professor i've had at any level of education. Truly one of the greatest guys and professors of all time. I was in his 8:00 AM section and was quite nervous, but his lectures were clear, funny, and enjoyable. HIGHLY recommend this guy. Never thought Econ would be for me until I took this class with Lantis. Proudest A- of my life.
Absolute GOAT of a professor, never thought I would enjoy an econ class until now.

Great professor. He responds quickly to emails and is available often for office hours. Practice exams are very similar to actual exams. Weekly quizzes are open note and every lecture is recorded. He gives less extra credit than some other professors but still offers .25 for each CL session. Overall great professor and I highly recommend.

Professor Lantis is an amazing professor overall. His lectures are informative and cover all the content necessary for the weekly quizzes, which are open notes. He offers many office hours and responds to emails promptly. The exams are straightforward and similar to the practice exams. Out of all the econ professors, his exams are the easiest.

Professor Lantis is amazing, the best prof I had my first semester. His lectures are very detailed and are always posted on YouTube in case you miss it. He offers extra credit up to a 3% boost (very useful). Overall he's very charismatic and a genuinely nice guy and probably the best choice for B251.

Professor Lantis is AMAZING and wants to see students succeed! I appreciate that he held office hours multiple times a week and quickly responds to emails. The tests are straightforward and there aren't “trick” questions. Attend CL sessions for good practice and extra credit points. Final is also not cumulative. ABSOLUTE GOAT, 10/10 recommend!
truly a great guy

This is genuinely my first review of a professor ever. I genuinely have never been so thankful for a professor in my entire life. I actually took his BUS E-370 for the summer and went through some personal difficulties and Professor Lantis was very understanding and adjusting. He lectures well and gives a reasonable amount of work too!
I loved this professor. His lectures are not as horrible as it could be for an Econ class. He responds fast to emails, and is very caring. His practice exams are very similar to the real one.

Great professor. He offers office hours and is always willing to help his students. His practice tests are very similar to the real tests so make sure you know why the answer is right and why the wrong answers are wrong.

Robert Lantis is a very good professor. He is straightforward and makes it understood what needs to be learned for the quizzes and exams. He makes it easy to study for the exams by giving practice test which are really helpful. I would 100% recommend this professor if you can take him, he makes a hard class like Econ a little bit easier for sure.

Overall, the best professor I have had at Kelley so far. SO clear and direct along with the tests you are given. He does not try to trick you on tests like the other professors. As long as you go to class, take notes, and pay attention you will succeed. He responds so quickly to emails and offers office hours several times a week.
Dude taught a Ball State and was the GOAT. Bro was so good at teaching. Look him up on YT his videos are nice if you cant show to a class.
Professor Lantis did a good job explaining topics and using relevant examples to keep his students engaged. If you can get him I highly recommend him for B251.

This was my toughest class. However, that is because it was at 8 AM and I couldn't focus... which is why I'm glad I Had Professor Lantis. He was engaging and his quizzes/ exams are decent if you take notes and read the modules. I hate Econ with a passion and was able to get my B+ for Kelley. Little complaints like the other Econ teachers.
A fun class while at the same time being easy to get a good grade just by going to class and paying attention.

Professor Lantis is an awesome Econ teacher. He just came to IU from Ball State, and he is funny, relatable, and kind. He takes time to explain hard concepts in a relatable manner. Attendance is done by TopHat for participation points. Lots of extra credit opportunities and he loads you up with grade boosts at the end of the semester.

Amazing professor. Consistently gave good feedback, always willing to help if you're confused, goes over and beyond to help students learn the material and earn a good grade in his class. 100% recommend taking his class.

He is a good teacher for B251, he posts all of the lectures and practice quizzes. He also does office hours and is good at explaining any questions you have. Attendance isn't mandatory but he does TopHat questions to track/grade attendance. He gave a lot of extra credit if you complete all the module quizzes and go to class.

reviews.comment: BUS PRES SPRING 2026. Toughest grader I've ever had. Learned a lot but she finds new ways to take points off every presentation. I felt this class was less about presenting well and more about not getting any points taken off.
Professor Landis is a horrible professor that does not care about her students.
boring class but nice teacher

Her grading system is very beneficial, essentially if you get 80% or higher on any major or minor assignment then you get a grade of "complete" or incomplete if you do not, which makes it easy to do well. Very clear instructions, very kind and understanding professor, very approachable and easy to contact outside of class hours. 10/10

The professor is extremely kind and the class assignments are straight forward. They all have rubrics which tell you word for word what you need to do to get an A. The assignments aren't very hard and they're actually beneficial towards getting a good resume and cover letter for internship applications.

Great professor, a lot of busywork, but it's all related towards helping you with getting internships/jobs (interviews, resume, cover letter, etc). All of my outside of class communication with her has been helpful. Only reason you don't get an A in the class is if you don't do the assignments and show up to class.

reviews.comment: Well this class can be a bit boring and dull as it covers many basic lessons, professor Landis did her best to make the content interesting. However, any questions I had outside of class or in communications I received through canvas, she always seemed to be unwelcoming and condescending.
Professor Landis is the best! Understanding and a bit humorous in manner! No odd amounts of busy work, just show up to class and it's very smooth from there.
Professor Landis is really sweet. She outlines what you need to do very clearly. She does however assign a bit more busy work than other compass teachers.

Professor Landis doesn't require a lot of work, and focuses a lot of students getting to know one another in class. In comparison of work, Professor Landis doesn't have nearly as much work and you just have to show up.

Prof Landis is super nice. She's a relatively easy grader and makes Compass seem less of a waste of time. If you talk with her before/after class or during office hours, she is willing to help you with your career related goals. She helped me set up a networking meeting with someone she knew in the very specific field I want to work in.

Landis is a great choice for Compass 2. Easy grader, put in the work and you'll get an A. She's helpful outside of class with questions and wants you to succeed. You can tell she's passionate about what she teaches. Most valuable part of Compass 2 is the cover letter & interview prep, so I'd recommend taking it before recruiting if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Landis is a very nice professor. She cares about her students and does everything she can to help you succeed academically and professionally. Compass is the easiest Kelley class in all of your years. If you show up, pay attention and give assignments a small amount of brain power, you'll get an A. She makes it easy if you try.

Rachel is really sweet and considerate of her students. She's a solid choice for Compass 2- she doesn't grade too harshly. She also wants the class to be relevant and helpful for students. Overall, I enjoyed her as a professor.

Overall, Landis is a solid choice for T275. She's a very fair grader, so just put in the time to do a good job on this class's assignments and you should get an A. A lot of the content of Compass's lectures is just common sense advice, however, Landis did provide a lot of helpful information (Resume, cover letter, and interviews in particular).

reviews.comment: Professor Landis is the nicest professor at Kelley. She cares about her students and their success.

Professor Landis is a very sweet, caring person. If you ever have questions or doubts on assignments/expectations she will gladly help you with a smile. Compass is an easy A-class as long as you show up to class and do all the homework assignments. Teamwork is important in this course so try to get the most out of the experience!

I had Logan in I101 my first course at IU and in I494/I495 capstone as my final. Why so negative? They must not have done the work. While I agree there is no way to get an A in Capstone, he is knowledgable and understanding. Maybe the capstone lectures dragged a tad, but hes LEGIT. I actually enjoyed the lessons coming from HIM. Thanks Logan!!!!
The lectures themselves were pretty easy. I101 is a very easy class itself. The attendance is very much required. Generous but strict absence policy I'd say. Labs are breeze.
Doesn't teach you. Grading is VERY strict. They will find ANYTHING to make you lose points.

Stay away from this Professor as LONG AS POSSIBLE. He is probably the worst grader and completely inconsiderate. Grades assignments so its impossible to get an A. Always gives 8/10 and below so imagine your grade starts at an 80 and goes downhill from there. Tanking our grade on easy assignments and simple tasks for no reason. you've been warned

Attendance is very much required and his late policy is really strict, but other than that he is a nice guy and a good professor. I101 is kind of a pointless class, also lab is taught by TAs, but it is a free A as long as you show up, do the work, and learn. Fair warning, the lectures can get boring sometimes. He also gives extra credit.
he's a good guy
Professor for 494/495, I101. Okay professor, but not as bad as what everyone is saying. Be prepared and try to learn the programming languages before taking 494/495

Horrific. Worst prof at IU. Arrogant and not very helpful. Capstone lectures just went in circles and circles. I don't think I can take another team building activity after doing it for a semester with Logan ✋

I was really surprised to see reviews calling him rude or arrogant. Seemed like a funny dude in my experience. i101 was a pretty good and quite easy course. Lecture was the easiest part and most weeks had some pretty interesting and engaging topics. Definitely a lecture I looked forward to and it's only once a week. Study sessions can be helpful.
He was a bit plain and boring

Honestly, professor Paul was one of my favorite professors so far. Despite all the negative comments he has received, I think his personality and caring for his students is great. He truly wants you to succeed and that's something you can easily tell from him. Although it wasn't always him grading, I finished the class with a 100%. Overall good guy
strict about cellular devices.

i dont care what others say, he's great and his class isn't THAT difficult and he's good at explaining, i dont know how y'all can describe his 101 class as hard, i think thats just you, you might be the problem
i like logan a lot but i did really well in the course and still ended up with a B. he doesn't really reply to a lot of emails outside of class either which isn't fun but hes a good teacher.

Either logan or the school is removing ratings that are speaking the truth on him. No doubt one of the worst professors here at IU, extremely inconsiderate and does not care about his students outside the classroom. No empathy or compassion for teaching. Dude seems completely unaware that 70% of the class is there for gen ed credit, just terrible.
Had logan for i101 didn't have too many interactions with him but he seems like a nice guy.

Single-handedly the worst professor ever! EXTREMELY rude and condescending. Continuously talks down to us like we're children, expects us to learn everything outside of class then punishes us for reaching out to other professors for help. The grading makes no sense - you can only get a 90 at best if you do EVERYTHING they ask you.

Logan Paul is by far one of the worst professors at IU. Logan is difficult to work with, critical, and negative to students. He is also unknowledgeable in terms of class content and rude to students. The grading policies are terrible, and his feedback is even worse. Logan should not be in charge of students' futures whatsoever. Avoid if you can!!!!

You're not allowed to use technology in an INFORMATICS lecture, so that should tell you something. Also, the lectures felt useless when it came to doing the real work of labs, but he himself knows what he's talking about.
Not only my least favorite teacher

Strict no-phones policy, lectures are dull with a peculiar ice-breaker routine, and mandatory scanning process. Labs, however, are enjoyable, and the class is educational. Easy for both N and M credit, but aim for Chase, not Logan.

I really loved the lab portion of this course. I got a lot out of them and it made the homework assignments attainable. The lectures were more about the overarching themes of the course and, while you are not going to be quizzed over the lecture, they are interesting to listen to.

reviews.comment: Logan's lectures are amazing. Although we are not actually quizzed over the lectures, they were very interesting and not bad AT ALL for a 4 credit hour class. As long as you do the stuff in the labs its an easy A which can also can be seen if you look at the grade distribution for this class online (type IU grade distribution into google).
i101 lectures were very boring and unrealtated to the labs.
He made the material interesting and explained each section in depth making sure that you completely understood each part.

Not a great professor. Lectures are structured around topics that you WILL NEVER USE in future Informatics classes. He uses this weird attendance system where your Crimsoncard needs to be present to be counted for attendance, he is the only teacher who does this and if you forget your card or something goes wrong good luck getting credit that day!

Super easy class but man, I have not been in high school for 2 years and this guy treats you like a high schooler. He told someone in class to put away their laptops because it is distracting them. I have not heard garbage like that since high school. Too much for a class with elementary school difficulty but easy 4 credits for comp sci majors!

Logan doesnt teaches and treats the capstone class like a middle school class. The lectures are spent talking about how to be a good teammate rather than going over relevant information for the class. reviews.comment: Honestly He does not teach you anything about coding in this class and expects you to teach yourself through the internet the whole time. reviews.comment: The professor you have for lecture for this class doesn't really matter. I really learned stuff in the labs, which I thought taught coding very effectively for true beginners. The lecture professor I felt was sort of annoying about getting people to participate and I didn't really care for them. But you aren't graded on the content of them.

I had Logan for i101 and now again as a prof for i303. We have weekly group assignments due (they're not hard) and weekly discussions due. We have a final white paper as well, but the course load isn't heavy. Logan's hilarious and easy to talk to and 10/10 recommend.

reviews.comment: The lecture component is of the class is pretty straightforward. He focuses on giving overviews of things rather than going extremely in depth. Outside of class, the assignments aren't that heavy, expect a few multi-paragraph papers at most

SUPER nice and approachable, but teaches too quickly and relies WAYYY too much on W3 schools and Google - i I could have saved several thousand and learned from W3 at home. Attendance policy is ridiculous. No such thing as an excused absence - I had an A, but due to job interviews I could not reschedule my 98% turned to a C.

Also, god forbid you sleep or use your laptop in their 200 person lecture hall because they will call you out.
Take his classes
She is very nice and flexible. But if she thinks you used AI or cheated on writing she will not be nice and will even Fail you. It was a good class lots of discussion. Old school style class.
Easy class, you just have to read and actually try for your writing. She's very flexible and understanding.
She wants you to learn and think. Great lectures and creative lessons. I'm enjoying this class, she is kind and every day is interesting.

She is an amazing lecturer, kind, and compassionate. She has designed this course so that it is not difficult to participate. She tries to learn all names, and cares about everyone's success. Quizzes are not timed, and answers can be found in the texts she provides. The readings are interesting.

Professor Lepselter blends innovative instruction with engaging discussion, offering a transformative learning experience. She is among the finest educators I've studied under. Diligent students will find her course enriching. Her influence resonates beyond the classroom.

She is very nice and caring about her students, but the quizzes were timed and kind of hard, especially if you didn't do the reading. Your whole grade is based off quizzes that drop your grade if you even miss 1 point because they are 20 points each. There are two exams that are easier than the quizzes, and the readings were not interesting.

reviews.comment: She is a great professor and very caring and tries her best to help her students. I got an A in the class because I got a little bit lucky, however, the class was pretty easy. She made it pretty easy, but you need to go to every class if you want to succeed. Great professor and I will definitely reccommend her to others.

reviews.comment: Probably the most caring professor Ive ever had. She makes the class easy- and is so passionate about what she does. Thank you professor lepselter for being the absolute BEST!!!
Susan Lepselter is the best professor I've had at IU. Great readings, great lectures, great discussions, great exercises, great feedback. Take her classes!
Her lectures are brilliant. Also a nice and interesting person.

Wonderful professor and great lecturer. She knows how to approach every topic in a thought-provoking way. Do the readings because the class discussions will be interesting and you'll be tested on them! She's very intelligent and open to listening to her students. She assigned a few essays but she gave room for creativity. Highly recommend!

Professor Lepselter is one of the best professors I have had at IU. She was really nice and made sure to connect the material to pop culture so that we could get it down. She was really fun and always cheerful.

Susan Lepselter truly saved my semester! She understands that many of the students in her class are taking it to fulfill their gen ed requirements. Although there is a lot of reading, she does her best not to overload you. I accidentally wrote down the wrong date of the midterm and she allowed me to retake the exam the next week. Highly recommend!
She is awesome. Enthusiastic, supersmart and makes you think. She's the kind of prof who makes you realize why you're in college! Also gives good review sheet nn for exams.

She made discussion lively and fun, she is open to your opinion of you back it up and also you learn a lot. She has a lot of clips and I like that she incorporates clips students find into lessons. She is also nice and helpful. I really enjoyed this class and it changed the way I thought about things.

She is very sparatic and all over the place with her explanations. Class was incredibly annoying and difficult to follow. I would not reccommend her to a friend. She couldn't even work simple programs like PowerPoint. Very frustrating.
Very Nice

takes her a while to return tests & papers and she will probably cancel class 2-3 throughout the semester but she is very nice and not very hard. read over the stuff and go to class (which she doesnt take attendence but it helps) and you'll be fine. i'm in my second class with her right now and she's a class you don't really have to worry about!

Be prepared for lots of rambling and unclear expectations. Canvas is confusing, instructions are scattered, and grading isn't always explained. Discussions don't feel very open because the professor often interrupts or pushes her own views. Good intentions, but not a very well-run class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: A great professor who cares about her students post-graduation. Is very creative and can model great instruction on-the-spot. She will advocate for you years after you graduate.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is one of the worst professors I have ever had, probably the worst in my graduate school experience. She gives very little guidelines or details on assignments, and then takes off points for things that wasn't even on the rubric. She forgets when she "okays" paper ideas and topics, and then ultimately deducts points when she can.

The classes weve taken with Prof. Nyikos are really repetitive and boring. She tries her best to connect with the students and is a really sweet person, but as a professor shes lost her edge. If you do have to take her class its a fairly easy grade, her rubrics are vague though, even though she expects a ridiculous amount of detail.
She is a very helpful professor. Encourages hard work. Always informs the class regarding the upcoming events: conferences, workshops, symposiums.

She is awful. She comes to class unprepared. She doesn't seem very bright, cannot infer information to save her life and will take off points if you do not write every detail and I mean every detail. She rambles, she interrupts students and she does not seem to know what actually works in teaching foreign language.

Very sweet lady, although she is  not very organized.  She genuinely cares about each student as an individual, which is more than can be said about many, many professors.  Her (very frequent) emails can get annoying, but she is trying to help.  Class is generally student-run, and she does ramble for extended periods of time during class.
Nyikos is incredibly unhelpful, flighty, and an overall poor teacher.  This is kind of a scary thought considering she is a prof in the school of ed.
Good beguiner teacher.
Makes her students play like robots. Arguably the worst violin professor at IU Jacobs
Great teacher!

She was one of the best teachers I have ever had. She has teaching, and teaching about teaching, down to a science. If you take her classes seriously, they are not "easy", but in my opinion, that's a good thing.

Mimi is one of the premier violin pedagogues in the world. She is incredibly knowledgable about the violin and cares very much about all her students. If you study with her, you will learn more than you thought possible about the violin. (Incidentally, I don't feel that piano accompanying class students should be allowed to rate her.)
I agree with the earlier messages, all she does is regurgitate what she has stolen from others. She'll drain the love of music from you just like a vampire would blood.
don't ever accompany this studio!!  I second the witch idea.
she's a real witch. stay away. she'll mar your love for music.
she's fantastic and i couldn't ask for a better teacher.  she really works and breaks down your technique for you to build it up again.
The last two ratings were DUMB...she's the best string teacher ever, just check out her former students and her teaching materials, you just can't get any better than Mimi.
not sure how she got on the faculty in the first place
i got tired of being told to "ZOOM" or "SWOOSH" when i asked her to explian certain bowstrokes.
Horrid experience. No instructions and does not actually care about the classes he teaches. Never responds to email. The department ought to revaluate his employment.
So confusing with his expectations, when you ask him a question about it his responses make no sense.  I would not take a class with him again

I could write a whole essay about this man and all of the ways he is not a good professor. For every class we have at least 6 things of reading, most 10-20 pages, so we're reading up to 100 pages for every class only to not discuss any of it. And he expects a lot without explaining WHAT he expects so we have to figure it out alone. Nobody likes him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lecture never made any sense. Assignments were all without instruction. Never graded anything. Stay away.

Muyumba never had clear assignment instructions. He rarely was contactable. I didn't have a grade the entire semester until past the deadline, and was disappointed in said grade given I completed all assignments, attended nearly every lecture, and frequently went to his office hours. I deeply cared and engaged in the class… I'm disappointed.

We had 3 mini essays and 1 final essay for the class. Never gave proper instructions on what he expected for each essay. Did not grade the mini essays 1 and 2 till the before mini essay 3 was due, and so there was no way to improve properly. NEVER GOT GRADES BACK SO DON'T EVEN KNOW HOW OR WHY I MISSED AN A. can only get A/B/C theres no b+/a-.

so much i could say. the lectures never made sense with the topic, there was no flow. Finals are in two weeks and we have one grade, out of 10, which some people say they haven't even gotten back. no one understands what's going on. he doesn't go to his own office hours. very intelligent but shouldn't teach. don't take a class with him.

He's clearly very well informed on the topic but the class lacks any structure. There are so few assignments and he doesn't put grades in until the very last minute or literally after the semester is over. He also has a tendency to be kind of condescending when people don't give his ideal answer in discussions and people were unwilling to speak up

Professor Muyumba is a great guy and I did enjoy his class, but the grading criteria for his movie reviews are quite difficult. You will definitely want to talk with him as soon as possible about getting your paper written the way he likes it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is a nice man who doesnt enjoy teaching. Lots of reading and assignments. It is the last week of school and still nothing in the grade book. He is a harsh grader. Assignment instructions are vague. He was condescending when I didnt know the answer or what he was asking. Did not motivate me to improve but expected a lot from us regardless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Someone else said he's a nice guy who hates being a professor, which is accurate. Super smart. We only had two assignments, which was nice, but makes the grading pretty unpredictable. He expects a very high level of proficiency in class performance, so I was afraid to speak up in class because I felt like I was wrong/dumb most of the time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's an intelligent and eloquent guy, and our discussions were great. But most of the class didn't know what he wanted from our essays. He graded us, harshly, based on a rubric he didn't show us until after we turned in our essays. He seemed to not have enough time to teach our class. We were a month into the semester before he made a syllabus.

Grades were rarely given back so that students could make improvements for the next quiz or essay. He consistently skipped office hours and rarely responded to emails to set up an alternate time.  If you are someone who likes a lot of feedback on your work, I would not recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Basically Muyumba is a really smart dude who does not want to be a teacher. The lectures are occasionally related to the text but more often than not you just talk about whatever happens to be on his mind today. Be prepared for him to tirade about a Facebook post.  Gives no assignment feedback.  the class is better suited to a cafe than a classroom

Enjoy getting feedback? Want to improve on your writing? Want to know your course grade? Then don't take this class! We had no grades put in the gradebook - ever. I didn't get my papers back until AFTER the class was over, not giving me any way to improve my writing. Do yourself a favor and do not take a class taught by Muyumba.

This class was the hardest class I have ever taken. I, along with a good chunk of other people in the class, had no idea what was going on most of the time. He was friendly and doesn't call on you in the discussions which can be interesting, but the topics are hard. There is also a lot of reading, be prepared to read a novel a week.

You definitely have to put in work in Muyumba's class. He teaches you an entirely new way of writing, which is hard at first but VERY useful both in the class and outside of it. Class discussion is fun and he puts more emphasis on critical thinking rather than grades. Great class

This class had zero structure. The only big assignments are review essays where you're supposed to review a work we readwatched. The instructions for these were abstract and vague; on the first essay, I believe the highest grade was a 715. Then he let us pick our grade for the whole class because he didn't "want it to be about grades." BS class.

Rambles through lectures, reading off slides, yet almost nothing she discusses is on the tests. If it is, it's the most complex version possible. Exam averages were often a D. Attendance/participation/homework can save your grade. The cheat sheet wasn't even helpful. I learned more from AI than from her lectures, and she often had a bad attitude.

To succeed, you HAVE to do the readings AND attend lab sections. I personally like a flipped classroom, but it's not for everyone. She gives out her own textbook for readings; however, it does have spelling errors and words things weirdly. Make sure you are using the right link for in-text questions, or else you may lose 30 points (like I did).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Honestly everyone fearmongers her L211 but its literally fine. The course is flipped so it is a lot of work but I feel like meeting only once a week kind of cancels that out. Dr. Mehta is very nice and she has open office hours so she's able to help you pretty much whenever you're free. As long as you do all of your work you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: It was a difficult class. Not the best experience ever but it's manageable. The only thing is that the entire class is self-taught. I think shes on tenure so she just doesn't care. I wouldn't really recommend it but she is one of the most disliked professors in Pre-med, pre-health I will say. She's no Sara Mata but still not great.

The L-211 class she teaches is a flipped classroom, meaning you do your work/studying outside of class and then come into class prepared to apply that knowledge. If that method doesn't work for you, then don't take a flipped class. Professor Mehta is a good professor but can be overshadowed by student's just not enjoying putting in the work.

It was clear Mehta was very knowledgable on the material but she did very little teaching. Her two hour Friday lectures were rants and the groups teaching each other the different subjects. Exams had very little to do with the actual material you taught yourself. Avoid taking this if you can, flipped classroom isn't worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Mehta had a fair grading policy and gave extra credit (a tiny bit) but her homework load with the flipped classroom was excessive. Some weeks I spent upwards of 10 hours watching lecture videos, reading the textbook (full of typos and conflicting info), doing problem sets, and more. Her quiz (really exam) averages were never above a D.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Mehta seems to be very intelligent and has good intentions but her class is terrible and she is an awful teacher. She assigns a lot of homework that is not helpful and nothing prepares you well for the exams. She also has typos in everything INCLUDING EXAMS MAKING THE QUESTIONS CONFUSING. Her Friday lectures are two hour rants.

Dr. Mehta is a reasonable and caring professor. She is always ready to answer questions or explain concepts. Yes, this class comes with a lot of homework, but if you focus and put effort into the readings and study guides, you'll do good on the quizzes. The flipped classroom structure may be hard for some, but I found it to be very effective.
Awful professor, makes homework and tests impossible and concepts way more confusing than they will ever need to be. DO NOT TAKE THIS WITH HER UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE.
A rambler, makes everything 1000x more confusing than it needs to be

Don't take this with her, take it with Carl Bauer. Too much homework far exceeding my other 400 level classes. Every piece of material you get is worded just to confuse you anymore. She makes you read the textbook, take notes, watch hours of lecture videos, do study guides, and problem sets for just one week (up to 6 hours of work).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Let me say, I was so worried for this class,  and everything was fine. You can av. a 70% on tests and still get an A. She really great in office hours and Spencer is a great AI!
