Tests were all multiple choice and fair (we really do learn everything on them, you just have to apply what you learn). It all depends if you like a flipped class or not.

A very condescending person, she's a great example of someone who knows a lot about their subject but cannot teach. The flipped classroom causes inefficient learning and wasted time. Materials are often from different sources which confuse each other. Quizzes focus on extremely minute details. No access to corrected worksheets or study guides.

She runs an inverted classroom, yet the workload exceeds most of my other classes (including 300 levels). The weekly meeting isn't bad, but you have to know every concept by heart and memorize any minor example to do well on tests. Only take this class if you have other easy classes or are incredibly willing to study hard and attend office hours.
Even if I studied the material taught in class front to back, it never prepared me enough for the quizzes. Very frustrating.

Enrolled in molecular biology the week after first week of class b/c I needed to add another class. Counted all 5 of my assignments during that week I wasn't even enrolled as "missing" and put 0's in for everything which dramatically lowered my grade. Very inflexible about missing class even though I needed to get surgery. DON'T TAKE THIS WITH HER.

This class was straight up weird. I averaged a 70% on the exams, but ended up getting an A in the class due to the final project, online quizzes & extra credit. Honestly did not feel like I learned a lot in class- Prof. Mehta was kind, but not a great teacher-- another victim of the "flipped classroom" model unfortunately :(
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Mehta overall is a good professor.  Her grading policy is very fair, with majority of the grade being homework as opposed to exams, and she offers various extra credit opportunities.  I will say this class I a lot of work outside of class, but both herself and the AIs are very ready to answer any questions you may have.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Mehta tends to do a flipped classroom which puts a lot more work on the student's end. The problem sets and study guides take a long time to fill out, and the problem sets are graded for accuracy. On a positive note I think her grading policy was very fair, where homework assignments and participation make up a lot of the grade.

Her class includes a lot of homework and quizzes, but if you engage with the material and focus during lectures, it's manageable. She offers extra credit and isn't a bad professor. The low ratings likely reflect her 2-hour lectures, which some find boring, rather than her teaching. If this is your only option, don't let the low rating deter you.

Incredible professor. Probably my favorite at IU so far. Although the material is difficult, Dr. Mehta is extremely intelligent and it's inspiring to make you want to be at your absolute best. When you get to know her she cares a lot about her students' success and is so respectable for her research and great personality. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!

Save yourself. Her class is the actual worst. You will be expected to read a nonsensical textbook (it is complete word garbage) and watch the most confusing lectures ever (you'll spend an ungodly number of hours doing this). Friday classes are a 2 hour ramble session. If you have to take it with her, I wish you luck because you'll need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She has no clue as to what she is doing. She assigned us exams with a group project, along with packets of homework and quizzes at the same time. This class is run like a joke. AVOID her , she will expect you to spend more time on this class than orgo or physics which is simply unacceptable. There is also no organization of the canvas page
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The "online textbook" provided is a hodgepodge website with varying information, so when you are teaching yourself the information (because it is a flipped classroom) learning becomes extremely hard. Some weeks you will spend 6 hours going over lecture material not counting a lot of other assignments you have due. Very hard exams.

Mehta is one of the worst instructors at IU. She teaches using her own book that contains SEVERAL grammatical errors and contradicting information. It was supposed to be a "flipped' classroom, but that really means you will be watching (4-5) hours of lectures/readings + homework, only to go to her 2-hour yap session lecture at the end of the week.

I am so sad to see less than positive reviews for Dr Mehta on here :( I thought she was amazing! Very kind accessible outside of class. She explains difficult concepts clearly and I thought our assignments/readings sufficiently prepared you for quizzes/tests. There is a good amount of reading and work/prep outside of class, but I learned so much!

This class blows. I never understood how it was expected for the entire class to teach themselves molecular biology before your once-a-week class. The tests have absolutely no correlation to what you read because her textbook will not have problems like the exam. You WILL go into class confused and come out confused. Don't do this to yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is brutal.  The concepts are hard and learning out of a book makes it no better.  Not even joking when I say it took me 9 hours for homework each week.  Not even counting the online quizzes that were required every 4 weeks.  Now shes making them in person so good luck yall.  Shes a nice person, but it is just genuinely too much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class was very difficult. Yes the material can be challenging but the professor explained it horribly. She made the information way more complicated then it needed to be. This class was so far one of the hardest classes I have been through. I feel if their was a better professor than I would have excelled more.

the course isn't even done yet but i just wanna say her book rots my brain, the word docs are jumbled and overly complicated, and the lectures are mind numbing. the TAs explain stuff very surface level. every lecture i feel could be condensed into a few bullet points but goes on and on forever, making it unnecessarily confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: The structure of this class is terrible, molecular biology is hard enough, but having to teach yourself is DIFFICULT. Her textbook is horrendous; it's an online book created by her with no highlighting or noting abilities.   Her lecture videos are too fast, and confusing. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This class is awful. The structure of the class, the textbook, the professor, everything. If you have to take this class, I feel for you. The textbook is confusing, the lectures are confusing, and the quizzes are even worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The class is disorganized and poorly taught. The textbook was not even complete during the semester, and the study tools available for quizzes were not adequate. Also, the material covered did not seem to actually prepare the students for the level of difficulty for the questions. Dr Mehta is helpful 1-1, but the class structure is really hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mehta made the class so much more difficult than it needed to be by limiting the resources available to students (all you really have is her horrible textbook). The content is interesting, sure, but the way in which Mehta presents it is horrendous and creates lots of confusion. She is a nice lady, but her teaching is bad. Really bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lecture videos were long and confusing. It was a lot of material to take in at once and was a big disorganized. Class met once a week and you were expected to know all of the material from the lecture videos and the book. It was hard to figure out where to look for the material we were learning. Quizzes were a bit difficult but were online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid Mehta if you actually want to learn about cell bio. All we have in class are weekly assignments, weekly quizzes, and meeting once a week, none of which help us learn anything about cell bio. The TA grading is almost as random as you can expect. The final paper is the most annoying thing you will experience and does not help you learn at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: For the love of God please do not take this class. She makes the class way harder than it should. We had online quizzes all semester and we had an in-person on paper final and we would have such long readings to do every week. If you're taking bio with Mehta, it better be the only class you're taking that semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is ridiculously hard for no reason. The quizzes are not definition based and they go over things that are barely discussed in class. When you only meet once a week makes it hard when she quizzes you over experiments and other things. The textbook we used she was also writing while we are in class so it isn’t even finished.

I loved it so much I became a TA. The class's HARD. The concepts are complex. It's as big a weed-out as Orgo. The exam questions are puzzle-based so you have to understand the concepts, rather than memorizing facts (like the MCAT). She does everything she can to give resources for students who want help. Open-door policy, forums, extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Online Savvy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: So yea, it was an easy A because a lot of stuff gets dropped, but shes a horrible professor. Sometimes expects too much from us, as if were getting our PhD. Avoid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Sapna made it seem like reviewing not only the lectures but the assignments would well prepare us for the exams. The exams were very indirectly related to the exams and were mainly passage based with little correlation directly to the material we were studying. If not required, I would not suggest taking this class at all, it will cause anger.

Horrible professor. I did well in everything the entire semester and finished with a grade I didn't want because she makes her exams so ridiculously hard. It didn't matter how prepared you were for them, the questions were impossible, and I think she was just trying to spite all of her students for some unknown reason. Truly, do not take her.

Truly never hated a class or teaching style more. The material is the same stuff taught in high school biology. While the material is presented straight off of a power point verbatim, exams are all passage based, hardly relates to the material taught, and medicine based. Our own AI doesn't always know the answer to the questions.

What can I even say about Sapna that hasn't been said already? She is a bad teacher whose lectures are extremely dense and hard to follow. Her tests are also unnecessarily hard. Worst teacher I've had at IU so far. Let's hope it's only uphill from here regarding my professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Even though I got an A+ in this class, I can say with certainty that Professor Mehta is the worst college professor I have ever had. She was a PowerPoint reader throughout the entire class and her exams didn't properly test you on content but rather were intended to trip you up. Overall, I would recommend taking this class with a different teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Mehta reads directly off her powerpoints in lecture with few exceptions. These exceptions are sure to end up on the exam and if you weren't paying attention at that specific moment in time, that's a question you are almost guaranteed to miss. She makes exams to purposefully trip you up instead of testing what you learned in class. Overall 4/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Mehta is my favorite biology professor I have ever had. Lectures and slides are crystal clear. If you go to her office after your test is graded, she will kindly walk you through each question you missed and encourage you to try new studying techniques based on what you struggled with most. Just be honest with her and you will learn much!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Mehta is very knowledgeable on this topic. My problem with her class was grading. There are only 3 homework assignments and 4 exams in the class, that's the grade (with a few small-value grades). But her questions are completely free response and you don't even know what she's asking! and grading is very specific for these ambiguous questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Mehta clearly understands the subject material very well. However, she does not do a great job of communicating it to her students. The exams are made purposefully to trip up students instead of testing them on the large idea. Overall, the class is not something I would take again with the same professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is absolutely horrible. Its quite hilarious that there really isnt a backbone to this class given that its Molecular Biology. Mehta lacks the concept of connecting the topics she teaches. Having this class at 8am made it difficult to find the motivation to even attend class due to the extreme monotony of the lectures.

Mehta is a knowledgeable professor but she makes sure that only the ones who work for it get exceptional grades. You have to be ready to take down everything because you may not hear it again. Plus whatever you miss is exactly what is redacted from her posted slides. This format makes the course hard to study for, but not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: going to lecture doesn't really help much. she usually reads right off the slides but some blanks need filled in. the homeworks and exams are so hard. The exam questions are usually hard to even comprehend what she's asking. points easy to earn to keep grade up ex. practice quizzes, warm ups

GO TO CLASS! You have to work with this material! Just sitting in lecture and not re-reading, questioning, and applying material will get you nowhere! Its application exams and TRUST ME it is so much better than regurgitating information. I remember this stuff to the core. If you truly want to invest in your science career take her course.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class was very lecture heavy. With no textbook, you're left to rely solely on lecture notes when it comes to studying for tests. The homework and discussion worksheets were confusing at times. You may as well not go to lectures since she mainly reads straight from the slides. Try to attend occasionally to get points for the in-class activities.

Homework and discussion assignments are much harder than what she teaches in lecture, but they do slightly prepare you for tests. Tests are hard no matter hw much you study because you only have her lecture notes to reference. Take any other professor if possible - she makes this class unnecessarily difficult

Here's the thing with Mehta: her lectures are incredibly boring; she reads right off the slides. Her tests are all multiple choice, but half of the questions don't really make sense. You can skip class and still pass as long as you don't miss the in-class activity every week. Lots of extra credit. I could handle her again, but she was just annoying

Terrible teaching structure. Lectures are the only form of instruction, and assigns homework due for correctness that does not follow the lecture. Has homework assignments due in person every friday, no help at all on studying for exams. i had to read over hundreds of pages of lectures. Very poorly taught class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Might be one of the most dry professors at IU. The lectures are like listening to someone read off of a script for 50 minutes straight. You will likely be lost in lectures and no longer have interest in molecular biology.

Professor Mehta knows the concepts well and all the info you need to know is in the lecture slides but going to class to get them explained helps with difficult concepts. Exams and worksheets are often poorly worded and sometimes homework is a bit too hard--she expects us to apply the information to an extreme degree. Expect to work hard.

I really honestly have no idea what the other reviewers are talking about. Her English is completely fine and she isn't hard to understand. I went to office hours a few times and she was really helpful. Go to class and you'll do fine. Because there's no textbook, it's hard to study for the exams if you didn't go to lecture and get all the info.

Very hard to hear, very hard to understand. Poor grammar usage. Difficult tests, very difficult problem sets, very basic notes. No textbook, so you're at the mercy of her lectures. Doesn't seem to care about students, seems to not want to be at office hours. Not helpful at all. Do all you can to avoid any classes with her. A 1.1 rating is too high.

Her lectures are very repetitive and use a lot of words to convey what amounts to an insufficiently small amount of information. Furthermore, no textbook is used, so students find themselves at the mercy of the lecture notes, which are somehow written at a level more befitting of high school biology students rather than a 200 level course.
Terrible. No practice problems are ever given, so you have absolutely no idea what to expect on the exams. She reads straight from the lecture slides, so don't even bother going to class.

She is a very bad lecturer; monotone, nonlinear format, unclear explanations. Tests and problem sets are often poorly worded as English is not her first language. She does post the lecture slides though. Easy extra credit is offered and is necessary to get a good grade. If you can, take with another professor. If you cant, study the slides.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: In her Spring 16 L211 section (her first time teaching the class), only 24/161 (14.9%) students got an A/A-. Of them, just 11 (6.9%) got a solid A. 88/161 students got C+ or below. Ridiculous:  worst grade distribution in recent years by far, and over half the kids get C+ or worse  Her bonus pts arent a boost -theyre NECESSARY for a shot at an A.

This professor is very unhelpful when you meet her in office hours. She changes times except not on the syllabus and also doesn't show up on time. Quizzes with the same number of Q's randomly are worth between 5 and 40 points with no motivation. Exams are pure memorization, no thinking just recalling lecture notes; POOR class if you want to learn.

Is an okay prof but provides absolutely zero clarity in any rubric she offers. The exams are hard but you honestly only need to do well on one to succeed in the class. Lecture is okay but I feel like it would be far better if the notes were done on an iPad and with the supplementary slides instead of sharpie.

Pohl's teaching style can be confusing if you aren't aware of it prior. It's not the most difficult to get used to, but there are times when it's not as in-depth as necessary for exams. Exams were super easy and were identical to practice exams. Another nice thing was that the final exam was replaced by a group project, so take that as you will.

The lectures were fine, but there were not many study materials outside of class, so a lot of learning came from using the textbook independently. Professor Pohl was very kind and approachable. I also liked having a final project instead of a final exam, and she adjusted grades after Exams 2 and 3.

Not a great experience overall. The lectures were hard to follow and the course felt pretty disorganized, so I ended up teaching myself a lot of the material. The exams were much harder f than what was actually covered in class and in the practice exams. I would take it again only because of the grading structure, not the teaching.

Dr. Pohl is nice and the class is easy for a high level chemistry course, but the grading and expectations are all over the place/very unclear. She doesn't follow the textbook and her notes did not provide enough information for students to actually learn the content. Exams had mechanisms never mentioned in class. Easy A tho so take that as u will

Extremely frustrating professor to deal with. She takes notes with a Sharpie on the doc cam when she could be using slideshows provided to her for free that go along with the textbook for the class. She often gets lost in what she's teaching and is not open to any criticism. She should not be allowed to teach this class again.

She is quite literally, the worst professor I have had here at IU. Her lectures involve dogs, strange analogies, then you are asked questions on exams that are completely separate from what you learned. The average on our final was a 61%, and she didnt curve the class. I did well, but sold my soul to the devil to do it.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Insane. I took this class over the summer and I can confidently say it is the hardest I've ever taken, and I'm a senior with (before this nonsense) a 3.8 GPA. Unnecessarily difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took English W131 and it was very easy. If you follow the instructions for the writing assignments, you will get a good grade. I liked how we got lots of freedom in our essays. I'd say this class was easier than all of my IB English classes in high school. Defiantly choose this class for a good grade. The teacher is kind, but sometimes unclear...
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely the worst. Directions for assignments are insanely unclear.

They are a kind and caring professor. This class does require you to write a few essays, but you have plenty of time to complete them and they help you through the process. I don't love writing essays, but the professor made it bearable and not too difficult. The essays are annoying, but manage your time well and you won't struggle.

This class was ultimately not difficult and shouldn't have been time consuming, but the professor's disorganized and confusing approach made it extremely frustrating. Prof was not accessible outside of class, directions were always unclear, and our grades ended up not even being weighted (which is totally different than what the syllabus said).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Although you can tell that this professor cares about their students, they made this class extremely stressful and frustrating. Their instructions for the class were consistently unclear, and they were never accessible outside of class, which added to the frustration of many students. I would not recommend this professor or take their class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I do think this professor means well and does care for their students. However, I wouldn't recommend them. They gave extremely extremely vague directions to the point where my peers and I were constantly confused about what was expected of us, they rarely responded when emailed, and a lot of instructions felt pointless. It was easy but frustrating!

If you see this professor's name on a course, RUN. This was probably one of the worst professors I ever had. nothing makes sense, all instructions are vague. VERY terrible grading scale, practically all assignments are weighed equally including papers??? Attendance policy is bogus, more than 3 absences is an automatic 0 very unfair and stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had her for a leadership class. Very good teacher. Nice, caring, clear grading. Despite it being a one credit class, she taught great stuff about leadership that I still remember. Non bs class and professor

Nevitt is a great teacher and a caring person but C104 is not an easy class. I recommend her class because her lectures are interesting and she works magic for some kids. If an easy A is the goal you won't get it in bus pres or any other class at Kelley.

Professor Nevitt is the best professor at IU. She is a communication expert and she made me a better speaker. There are a lot of presentations and you do have to show improvement over time to get a good grade. You have to turn stuff in on time, go to class, and work hard for an A. Kelley is a world class school and she's a world class teacher.

She is really good and was one of my favorite professors at Kelley. She cares. Kelley is a hard major and if it's too hard, there are other majors out there with easier classes. I chose Kelley to be challenged and to be taught by the best. I got that.
She's an insanely tough grader with lots of inconsistency. Feedback isn't accurate and most of the time she will find something to take points off your presentations for.

Lots of presentations (~1 every week). Grading was pretty tough. She doesn't give out any full scores. I barely ended with an A. She's super nice though and her lectures are really good. She clearly knows what she's talking about. The attendance policy is pretty strict - you can only miss 3 classes.

She's nice, supportive, and pushed all of us to become better speakers, but grading sometimes felt a bit inconsistent. You would do something one time and she wouldn't take points off for it, but then the next time she would. That being said, I learned good speaking habits in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She was super sweet, I highly reccomend.

best prof ive ever had. never met a more caring, motherly professor. truly genuinely cares for her students and their wellbeing in and out of the classroom. does not grade tough at all, all you have to do is get up there and show her you tried. you would be crazy to not take c104 with her.

I really enjoyed Professor Nevitt! I thought I was going to hate C104 because I don't like public speaking but she made the class a breeze. As long as you show up to class and like practice for a couple hours before your presentation it's chill.
Great professor to take for this class. One of the nicest professor out there.

Prof Nevitt is one of the best at IU, and this class was my favorite of the semester. She doesn't hand out A's, but she really made me better at public speaking in the most painless way possible. Great class and great teacher; highly recommend. Just go to class, make an effort, turn stuff in on time; you'll get an A and enjoy class too.

1. Very kind amazing person
2. Don't take her for bus presentations she grades super hard compared to other professors because she is new to that class

One of the best professors at IU. She is one of the nicest people I've met and makes the class really manageable for all students. Lectures are interesting. Don't miss a class though because I missed a class because I had the flu and she had me do the most ridiculous makeup assignment. Other than that she is the best!

Professor Nevitt was amazing in my class. She was very approachable, understanding, and helpful. She was very sweet and always smiling. She did not make class boring and a struggle unlike certain other professors. She is a great person and a great professor!

Compass is not the most exciting class but Prof. Nevitt is clearly very caring and enthusiastic about her students. Just show up and do the work and its an easy A. She will not make the class tough on you like some other Compass professors might
Professor Nevitt cares deeply about her students and their future success. Make sure to come to class and follow the rubric on assignments to get a good grade.

If you have the chance, without a doubt take Professor Nevitt for Kelley Compass I. Her character is professional yet warm, friendly, and kind to each one of her students. The class is cake, but I would recommend becoming close colleagues with her for future recommendations and advice

It would be very hard to believe that Prof. Nevitt is not the best Compass 1 teacher at IU. She's very professional and cares about your professional development, while extremely kind, friendly, respectful, uplifting, and informative. This class will help you understand yourself, potential career paths, and you'll build a strong LinkedIn profile.

Professor Nevitt was one of the kindest profs I have ever had. I took her for BUS-T175 (Kelley Compass 1), and in all honestly it was an easy class. You meet once a week for 75 minute lectures, and for that reason attendance is mandatory. Not much is expected from you to be able to pass the class, just show up, engage, and do the few assignments.

Everyone needs a little Prof. Nevitt in their lives. She was so inspirational, an easy teacher, and kept class fun. I am going to try to take her for Compass 2. Although attendance matters, class is once a week so you can manage. Love love love her! No homework except big assignments (class time given) & no final.

Easiest class you will ever take post-high school. You will come out of the semester with a solid LinkedIn profile and knowledge regarding how business interviews and recruitment are conducted. Always learning something new in an easy and light environment, if you have Prof Nevitt, you will not be disappointed, as her reviews show.
The sweetest teacher I have had. 100% recommend her.
Prof. Nevitt is so nice. You learn so much in her class but you don't feel pressured because she is so good at giving amazing advice. Take her for Compass 2, she is seriously so amazing.

Prof Nevitt is the best compass teacher you can have. Her assignments are pretty simple and don't take up a lot of time. Lectures are sometimes boring, but its an easy A. Just show up to class and you'll be fine.
As long as you show up to class you'll be fine... Professor Nevitt makes the class very easy to succeed in.
Jessica is kind and has reasonable expectations of her students. Class is easy and if you show up you will get an A.

The easiest professor for Compass One. She knows you have other things to do and uses your class time well to teach. Homework is a minimum, much less compared to other Compass One professors. Take her if you can.

Class with Professor Nevitt was always a pleasant experience. Although, lectures could sometimes be a bit boring and repetitive. If you're taking Kelley Compass, she's one of the best choices. Be prepared for lots of small group work and participation, but overall the class should be an easy pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Nevitt is one of the nicest, sweetest professors I've ever had. She's always smiling, her voice is so calm, and she's so caring. Compared to other C175 classes, we had very minimal work. An easy 100% with Nevitt if you turn in the work. Skip class and you need to write a full-paged single spaced paper. But I missed 3 times and the papers were easy.

Professor Nevitt's a great choice for Compass 1. There's only about 1 hour of work per week on average, and the assignments are very easy to get A's on. She's also super sweet and will gladly help anyone outside of class.
Professor Nevitt is one of the kindest professor Ive ever had. She gave great tips about LinkedIn especially. As long as you participate and do (easy) assignments T175 is guaranteed A.
Super strict about attendance, but she's really nice and helpful. The class is super easy as long as you show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Please take her classes she is an amazing professor! Fair grader and she truly cares for her students!

Professor Nevitt is very kind and caring. She will never call you out in class but rather encourages students to participate in a non-confrontational matter. She cares about her students and their success in the future. She will not round grades or give extra credit but if you attend classes and do the homework you should be on track to get an A.
Great teacher, just make sure you turn your assignments in on time or else it kills your grade.
Amazing professor. Cares a lot about her students and genuinely wants them to do well. Highly recommend!
SHE IS AMAZING TAKE HER
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jessica is a good pick for Compass. Shes a good professor and organizes the class well. The subject matter can be a bit dull at times but that is just how the class is. Time-wise, the class doesnt take much other than the big 3 projects, which all take multiple hours. They are assigned well in advance so you have plenty of time. Attendance taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher and super easy grader. Would highly recommend for Compass 1

Great choice for professor if you do get a choice. Very caring, always smiling, has a relaxing voice, and is not a very tough grader. She definitely knows what she's teaching well as she has tons of HR experience. I learned a lot and the LinkedIn project is very helpful. The attendance policy is strict but class is only one day a week so no biggie.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Compass feels like a blowoff at first, but is actually super helpful in finding your place at Kelley. While the attendance policy is WAY too strict in my opinion, Jessica makes class worthwhile. She's always smiling, and ready to embrace her students. Very receptive to interactive students. I felt like she cared about our progress, good class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I've had some rock star professors here but she might be my favorite. Super knowledgable. Since this class has a component about creating a LinkedIn, I checked the LinkedIn of all the profs who teach it, and hers was the best easily. Pretty clear why - she's an HR and comms guru. Genuinely cares about us. Also, and not that it matters, but very hot

The objective of this course is to help students get on the right track while searching for a career. Jessica genuinely cares about helping students, and she is extremely encouraging. The work load is very light, with a few readings and assessments but all are very beneficial. I learned a lot from this course and enjoyed myself while doing so.

She is on of the nicest professors I have met on campus yet. She makes you feel welcome within the first class. Her teaching style allows you to relate to her easily and makes it easy to understand the overall course.

Professor Nevitt's class is the best I've had at IU. She is in HR and has a lot of knowledge. She helped me through my first job search, salary negotiation, and interviews. I wish she taught more classes, honestly. If you have a chance to take any class she teaches, do it!

When I took this class, I was really skeptical because I had the Kelley compass class. In Jessica's class, I felt like every assignment helped me decide what major is best for me, and that it wasn't just busy work. I also felt like I was being guided by an expert because Jessica is so knowledgeable in her field.

Mrs. Nevitt was the one of the best instructors I've had in my 4 years at IU. She wants all of her students to succeed and is willing to go out of her way to see that through. She's always available for her students even after the semester is over and gone. Also, if you want an easy A, take this class, preferably with Jessica.
Jessica is honestly the best professor I've had. She cares about students and knows what she's talking about. She has funny stories and a great smile.

Professor Nevitt was great.  She helped me outside class to with my internship search, and thanks to Q299 and Professor Nevitt, I got the job I wanted.  She really cares about her students and I definitely recommend her class.
I learned a lot in this class.  Jessica made the subject interesting, and she was a great teacher.
X420 is an awful class, but Jessica was great! She is also gorgeous and made it very easy to focus during class! :)
Very nice lady. Rather pretty. About 40 years old. You are on the luckier side if you get her. Had her for HPER-H 160 lab (First Aid class).
Amazingly hot and nice, definitely get this instructor for your lab section.

I'm officially almost done at IU, had to go back and say this was one of the most draining classes I've taken! The material is easy, but it's like she's got to prove to the class she's smart by just adding sm info that won't even be on test. Encourages ppl to drop her class, tried to get you to mess up on quizzes even though it still effects grade
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is really easy if you read the textbook and do the practice quizzes she provides. I didnt go to class that much and mostly just read the book instead. Tests and quizzes are the only thing in the grade book but she drops a lot of grades and offers a lot of bonus points on each!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures seem super long but they are not mandatory.

She was wonderful. Her lectures are very informative and easy to follow, she explains things very very well. Also, she is quick to respond to emails. You only needed to attend class when quizzes or exams were happening. She drops several of the lowest quiz and exam scores. As long as you take the time to study, you'll do just fine.

Dr. T is very knowledgeable about this subject and she knows what she is talking about. There is no extra credit and the only grades are exams and quizzes, but there are bonus points and she drops the lowest exam and quiz grades, also attendance is not mandatory. As long as you focus on reading the slides you will do good.

Hybrid Abnormal Psych was fine. Context: I'm a senior neuroscience premed student. I took this class cause I thought it would be easy. It is. All of the lectures are online, one assigned every class day, and you have a quiz every 2 or 3 lectures. There's extra content to read, but she drops a lot of quizzes and 1 exam. Just do your work.

Hybrid Abnormal Psych class was extremely difficult. She will send announcements for quizzes and the quizzes are often about super specific memorization rather than conceptual. Tests are also really difficult. The class should be interesting but she makes it uninteresting and really difficult for no reason. Weighted only on quizzes and tests
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's mean and takes students skipping class personally as if we aren't grown adults in college capable of making our own decisions. When you have a question in the course she's unwilling to help and will just tell you to look at module resources and the slides. She likes to trauma dump too which isn't what I signed up for in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Thomassen is beyond brilliant, and spending just five minutes with her, you'll see that. The class is entirely exams and tests, no fluff. If you're not a good test taker, there is NO chance you'll pass. I had to W because I am not a good test taker. I also disliked how there were no textbooks to refer to if you are struggling.

DO NOT TAKE HER HYBRID ABNORMAL PSYCH CLASS! She uploads lectures to canvas and expects you to watch those and buy the required textbook. When quizzes are taken place in class they are nothing like the material that is given. She rambles in class and it is extremely hard to learn from her because she is all over the place.
She was very focused on herself and her own life and taught more about that than the course materials. Did not inspire me to learn or to come to class because she wasn't teaching it.

Amazing professor! Lectures are so interesting and keeps your attention the whole time. Quizzes and exams are very fair, as long as you go to class and pay attention you'll be all set. She was also so hilarious and smart would def take her class again.

Loved her and her class; she genuinely wants you to succeed and will do everything she can to ensure that. Content itself isn't super difficult, mainly very fast-paced and a lot of memorization + understanding of different parts but if you fall behind it will be very hard to catch up. Plenty of extra credit opportunities.

Absolutely loved her, so knowledgeable and funny. Very fun to talk to her in office hours or after class. Very awesome teacher and would recommend. Definitely a lot of outside of class work to prepare for lecture, but she is very clear about all of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Best class and professor of my whole college career. Class time is completely interesting and really worth attending. Quizzes and exams are straightforward if you go to class.

No attendance, no participation, just multiple choice. 9 quizzes, best 5 count. 3 exams, best 2 count, plus a final but it's not cumulative. Class is long but there's a break, even after exams, usually 10 minutes. Class goes by pretty fast. Early but it's nice to get done early. Professor is somewhat entertaining.

quizzes are so hard. she drops a few, but it's like she makes them hard on purpose so she has stuff to talk about when reviewing the quiz. all the answer choices make sense for the question, so it's like ughhhh.

She takes students not coming to class personally, and basically punishes the rest of the class by scheduling quizzes right after people miss because she's butthurt. During lecture, she provides students with fun facts, but we are never tested on them so it doesn't feel helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not very helpful. She crams in way too much material; not relevant material, but random facts designed to "catch" you on her quizzes and tests. If you go ask her for help, her most common advice is "drop the class." Her Canvas site is disorganized and full of obscure videos and articles she expects you to read.

Always very positive and energetic.The grading system with quizzes every so often and then reviews right after was really helpful. She's hilarious and real. Ignore the haters. The worst part of class was 2 girls who sat in class chatting and snarking the whole time.
Good class, Dr. T is amazing, but it took more study than I thought it would,just  be aware. Textbook is not super helpful. Go to class! That's key. Study the slides, and don't miss quiz reviews.
Great professor, solid class.

Classes like this remind me why I came to college. I hate missing class. it is one of the bright spots in my day. She has so much compassion for people with disorders, but in a real way, not looking down on people. She teaches from experience as well as facts. She often stays after to chat, and is generous with her time.

Dr T teaches an amazing class. She has stories and anecdotes that are funny and relatable, and she is clearly passionate about teaching and about her students. Lots of bonus points and chances to improve your grade. Probably better than 90% of IU classes.

I found Dr. Thomassen to be patronizing in a way that she probably thought came across as quirky/relatable, but really just made her look unprofessional. She would oftentimes would have errors in her tests and quizzes. Someone else mentioned it as well, but the trauma dumping mid-lecture was also wilddddd. The class content was interesting though.

i love this prof, super knowledgeable and funny, but the exams are pretty difficult. even after studying a lot and feeling confident on the material (and leaving an exam thinking i got an A+), i continued to get Bs on the exams. i would recommend her as a professor, but keep in mind it won't be an easy A course.

Prof. Thomassen is always engaging and makes class entertaining with her stories and jokes. Exams and quizzes can be hard and require studying. Luckily, some exams and quizzes can be dropped later in the year. No homework but looking over some additional articles or videos in the modules is beneficial.

Professor Thomassen is likely the best professor I've ever had in my undergraduate career. Engaging, kind, and inspirational, especially concerning psychology and us as students and as people. If you go to lectures and read the module resources, you'll for sure pass this class. Highly recommend you take this course.

This is a very thorough class so if you are interested in psychological disorders and wanna learn a lot then this is a good class for you. If you are looking for the easiest most fun class, this is not the class for you. personally I like Dr. T, I think she is funny and a decent human being.

I love Dr. Thomassen. I think she's a great professor and she's super funny. We didnt see her very often because I took her class as hybrid, so we only were there for quizzes and tests. However, she provides lots of bonus points on both. The lectures are very long, but if you make quizlets and look at the supplemental resources you'll do well!

DO NOT TAKE IT. Take Irene instead PLEASE. This class is extremely lecture heavy it's like 100 slides for one topic. Studying for exams is impossible and there's no extra credit. In the syllabus it says “you might think it won't hurt to ask for extra credit, it does”. You'd have to spend a majority of your time studying for quizzes and exams.

Quite literally one of the worst professors I have ever had. Terrible attitude towards any student that is unhappy with her teaching style. I reached out to her with concerns and she responded to me with links to tutorials on how to properly study and suggested I drop the class if I was not a fan of her class. Avoid this professor if you can.
Excellent lectures.Don't miss class.Take notes on the slides.Grading policy is very forgiving, just hang in there.

The lectures were interesting and made me want to come to class,even during bad weather. Dr. T is very caring and the class has a good set up. The quiz reviews are helpful if you missed class. Pay attention in lecture because she always tells you what you need to know for exams.

Dr. T is a super engaging speaker and her lectures encourage participation (the class goes a lot better if you do). she also really cares, I bombed one of the first quizzes and she reached out to me and gave advice on how to succeed in the class. if you stay on top of the readings and studying it is relatively easy to get a good grade.
I took this over the summer, so the lectures were online and so were the quizzes and exams. It was fine, but it was pretty intense, so be prepared for that.

If you follow what she tells you to do, you will do fine. I took it twice a week, so lectures are long but she had a break in the middle. A lot of the class gets A's because she has a lot of bonus points, with lots of chances to improve your grade. I would take another class with this professor except I am graduating.I just needed a C for credit.
Enjoyable lectures, she provides the slides so you can take notes or if you miss class. Do not miss quizzes because she reviews answers afterwards and that is the key to the exams.

I changed my major to psychology after taking this class. Very thoroigh and so fascinating. Keep up, study notes from lecture regularly and you will be fine. Upper-level classes are so easy after Dr. T's intro. Seriously intelligent and caring professor. She really cares about student.
Go to class and you will do fine. It's a lot, but Dr. T is an amazing professor. This was one of my favorite classes at IU. She is the best!
Awesome lectures, goes way beyond the textbook, which you really don't need, if you use the lecture notes to study and go to class. She always tells you what you need to know.
While Dr. Thomassen can be a bit strict, her lectures are informative. Stay engaged, use unstuckstudy ai for study prep, and you'll do well. Challenging but rewarding class.

She is the only instructor in psychology who does not teach her online summer classes asynchronously. All she does is lecture at us through zoom. She also only gives 6 minutes to take an 11 question quiz. I've taken a class in pedagogy and this a terrible teaching technique. Take this class with another professor who doesn't just pretend to care.

She is unreasonable and I regret taking her for my summer psych class. Gave us 6 minutes to take 11 question quizzes, and barely any time for reading tests questions too. I feel like I was set up to fail because quizzes and tests are all we're graded on.

Favorite professor at IU. She gives many quizes with bonus points available on each and only keeps your best 5 scores. Her tests are completely over lecture content and super easy if you go to class and pay attention. She is also super kind and encourages students to give input.

The grade is based on quizzes and tests only. She claims that her lecture is required; it felt like a waste of time to attend. She has a lot of "required" canvas articles that were an even bigger waste of time. If you take her class, read the textbook (which costs like $60+), read her slides, and make quizlets

I loved having Dr. T as a professor. Her lectures are very detailed with a lot of information, but you'll come away really feeling like you've learned something. She only kept our best 5 quiz scores (out of 10ish) and dropped the rest, and 1 exam of the 3 (not including the final) is dropped as well. She genuinely cares about her students too.

This class was so lecture heavy but she never could stay on topic during her lectures. She trauma dumps and it makes the class uncomfortable. The class is only based off of three exams and in class quizzes. She singles out people in the class and has no filter. She is not scared of being mean and will say rude comments straight to your face.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I never rated any professors but I decided to rate this instructor.

- SUPER STRICT WITH LITERALLY EVERYTHING 
- She don't allow students to work together, no groupchat-s even though there are no assignments. Idk why
- Her exams are always harder than other psychology classes even though it's only 300 level.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super nice person, just a hard class in general. She's great though and crazy smart about what she talks about. Truly worth taking her for P155 I think. A great head start for a psych major compared to taking P101/P102.

This class doesn't require any short responses but the test itself (multiple choice) is still confusing and takes a lot of time. 

During exams, she released  students who are done before others in a group and it's really distracting and annoying.

I love Dr. T! She's very knowledgeable about this topic, which makes learning from her super easy. There are weekly quizzes, but she tells you when they are so you're not surprised. Exams aren't too hard and she gives lots of extra credit questions. No homework and I never opened the text book.

She's a really good lecturer and makes it very clear what you need to know for exams. Ignore the complaints on here, it's all people who didn't put in the work or got caught for academic misconduct. Yes, she can be intense but every time I've talked to her one on one, she has been very kind.

Dr. Thomassen is an amazing professor and very knowledgable, but she is not the warmest person and can be kind of snarky with her students. She is an amazing lecturer, so make sure you attend class even though there's no attendance grade. Studying/memorizing her lecture slides and doing the same with her resources is the key to success!

Dr. T was one of the best Psych professors I've ever had. She is super witty and brings character to her lectures. She is also very clear on grading and gives several chances for grade improvement and review for exams. However, ABSOLUTELY DON"T MISS CLASS, you miss so much and this class is very lecture heavy.
She is so funny and teaches you all of the material you need. However, the lectures are FAST and DENSE. Put your head to it and give it study time and you'll do well, and feel super accomplished
Psychology is not exactly what I thought it was, but Professor Thomassen is amazing. A lot of people complain about their psych professors, but I have no complaints.

Amazing professor. Lots of stories and jokes in lecture, which make the time pass pretty quickly. Super nice and very fair about grades. Frequent quizzes are used to review, and some scores are dropped so some low scores or missing class won't matter so much, but don't miss ifyou can help it.

One of the least compassionate professors I have ever had. Her TAs are are far more helpful and empathetic than she is. They also can explain the material better than Thomassen can. Her lectures are incredibly confusing. She goes on random tangents and can't focus on the important material. Take anyone but her for P101, P155, P315, or P324.

Though her exams are difficult, as long as you attend lectures, you should be just fine. She genuinely cares about students and engages her audience constantly. However, YOU MUST GO TO LECTURE. She is really good about warning/giving tips for exams and quizzes during lectures that you won't get from just the slides. Great lady 10/10.

Honestly, Dr. T is an amazing professor! She really explains the material so well. But do NOT skip class. That is where you get specific tips about what will be on quizzes and exams. There are a lot of those, but each quiz or exam doesnt count for much, and some are dropped. More bonus points are added as the semester goes on.

I learned so much. Dr. T is very aware that students may have these issues, and she does not mock people with disorders the way some professors do! She is very caring, and is a great professor. Grades are all quizzes and exams, but you drop some scores. She knows so much about each disorder, but fortunately is clear about what you need to know.

She is a great teacher!I liked this class a lot and never missed but my grades were bad. Dr T noticed and met with me and we talked about what was going on with my testing. She made some suggestions my grades went up. I have never had a teacher notice when I was struggling before and work to help. She sent me encouraging messages all semester.

Very strait-forward class. Go to class, because she tells you exactly what you need to know. This is important, and will help you. Also, use the study guides and lecture notes. The Canvas things help. She drops scores and has bonus points to help your grade. Good lectures, interesting class.
I learned so much in this class, and Dr. T is amazing. Only quizzes and  exams, no papers or projects. She just counts your best 5 quizzes and also drops an exam.

If she spent half as much time working on updating and refining her teaching instead of working to make her class as rigorous as a bio or chem class, she might be a decent teacher. It's almost like she has an inferiority complex or imposter syndrome. Luckily I took P102 with another instructor and they convinced me to switch back to a psych major.
Great professor! Dr. T is very caring, and teaches a good course. Lots of quizzes and exams but she drops scores. Good to talk to for career advice.

Her class is all multiple choice, which is nice. However, it was near impossible to meet with her to go over. She is the only psychology professor I've had that doesn't have scheduled office hours. She sends you to her UTAs for help. Shares way too much information about her family in lecture. It seemed like she enjoyed catching cheaters.

If you actually want to use this material in future classes, be careful. A lot of what she teaches is out of date. True professors in more advanced courses have shown her wrong multiple times. It appears she wrote all her material the first time she taught, and hasn't changed a thing since. Her slides are extremely crowded, disorganized, as well.

Lisa will brag about being a "teaching professor" and winning all these awards for teaching, then will turn around and tell struggling students to drop her class instead of doing anything to actually support them. She is more paranoid about catching "cheating" students than actually ensuring they have mastered the material. Take anyone else for psy

I LOVE Dr.T. Have taken two classes with her -- always super understanding, supportive, and engaging. Clearly loves her students and what she does. Quizzes are super indicative of exams, takes breaks during lectures, keeps it real without being rude. Understanding of health issues. Drops some scores at end, always has extra credit. She rocks.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class is NOT the same as P101. It counts like P101, but it's for psych majors and is twice as hard and is a 2 in 1 pre-req for 300 level classes. Unfortunately my advisor told me the same. It is not. It is interesting and the professor is good but it moved fast. I could not drop, because bschool.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: All you are graded on is 5 out of your best 10ish quizzes and 2 out of 3 best exams and then a final. So much reading outside of class, but she'll never talk about it in class and then test you over it. I would not take another class with her again, if you have the option chose someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. Very passionate and excited about what she teaches. The class has a lot of information and moves at a pretty fast pace, but can be manageable. Your grade is really only dependent on quizzes and exams, but only the best 5 quiz/assignment scores are kept and 1 exam is dropped, so there is a lot of room for improvement.

I do not recommend her as a professor if you have a different choice. She uses only exams and quizzes for grading. We read so many papers online that we are quizzed on but she never talks about them in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tests and quizzes are not easy at all. She goes fast on her lecture notes. Takes a lot of time outside of class.

She's a doll! At first she was very serious and a little bit scary, but things have losened up as the semester went on, and she's really sweet! Basically it's lectures, quizzes, and tests, but she drops some scores. Attendance isn't counted, but don't miss, and pay attention in class because she basically tells you waht is on the exam in class.

I love Dr. T! She is very caring, and always keeps students up to date with helpful info.This class is very thorough and in depth about psychological disorders. The first part is theory and history, the rest of it is about the disorders. Straightforward exams and quizzes. Go to class, use the study guides, and study the slides - she posts them.

Lisa grades off of solely quizzes and exams, quizzes are entirely random and writes them as she feels. Well the drop policies are nice, she is fairly unprofessional and rude, I have never had a professor send out so many announcements about urging failing students to drop the class 8 weeks into the semester...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i'm not sure why Dr T has so many bad reviews. i don't mind going to lectures because i typically find them really interesting. she gives you all the resources you need to do well, if you do the reading and keep up with the reading questions & lecture content you'll be fine. the quizzes are a little stressful sometimes but i found them beneficial

This class was a lot tougher than any other P101 class, I spent more time trying to get a good grade in this class than any of my other ones by far. She is a nice lady and was fun to be in class with, but her grades and tests were overall hard.

Prof Thomassen is a fun woman with a great class structure. she has lectures most days that are downloadable with space for notes, she provides many examples, a textbook to read, modules with videos, and practice quizzes. she only keeps your top 2 exams and 5 quizzes/assignments. you don't always have to be in class. as long as you study youll pass

Dr. T is good, she is funny, interesting, and is a knowledgeable prof. However, she moves very fast in lectures so it can be hard to take notes. Quizzes can be hard but she drops over half of your lowest scores. Attendance isn't required, but if you miss a class you will probably be lost. If you pay attention you should be fine.

Dr. T is an amazing professor. She is incredibly knowledgable and passionate about psychology. The only reason why anybody would give her a harsh review is if they did not listen to her advice/syllabus, come to class, and study. Studying and attendance are definitely mandatory for this class, but it isn't hard. Would 100% recommend!!
Shes really great. At first i felt iffy but shes really great, funny and if u understand her lectures ull love it. Definitely recommend

Dr. T is an intense professor, but she knows her content and keeps lectures interesting. She has multiple assignments but only takes the top few. Her exams are fair but her quizzes were rough. The quiz would be on a projector and she barely gives a minute before moving on to the next question. Besides that, I definitely recommend her.

I could not stay awake during this class it was so boring. Dr. T just went on and on about stuff that wasn't really related to psychology. You can tell she's a good person, but I don't like her style of teaching. Very knowledgeable but gets off topic VERY easily. Her 50 minute lecture felt like 2 hours and idk why.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super caring, does require study. Fair. Does file misconduct reports as you can see by haters who got caught lol

Interesting class, but it helped me realize I'm not a psych major. Having said that, I talked to her and she helped me find a major that is a better fit for me, and gave me some tips to help me pass the class. She was really helpful, and not nearly as intimidating as I thought. I don't understand some of the comments here at all.

A ton of information in each lecture, which can be a bit much, but she is a great professor. Lots of chances to improve your grade. Recommended if you are able to go to class regularly, because she tells you what you need to know in lecture.

Professor Thomassen is a tough teacher. But, she's a really good teacher. I purposely changed my schedule to be with her again. She tells you from the start there are a lot of quizzes but she only takes the top 5. Tests aren't extremely hard as long as you study. She does a pop quiz when attendance gets too low. Just go to class and pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: For a 101 class this class is way too much work. The first day of class she said we would need to spend 8 hours outside of class studying to receive an A. That is ridiculous, I have never had a 300 class where I have had to spend 8 hours outside of class time on studying. She is way too arrogant.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Literally one of the rudest professors I have every had, she does nothing but pretend she wants you to succeed while laughing in your face if you notify her that you're struggling. Let's not forget the constant trauma dumping instead of teaching 75% of the time. Save yourself and take this course WITH ANY OTHER PROFESSOR POSSIBLE

She is a great professor and keeps the lectures very interesting. You will have PLENTY of opportunities for extra credit, especially during quizzes. You do need to be prepared to read the book, as lectures are based on what you should have read in the book prior. Tests are not that difficult as long as you put in the work. Overall great professor!!

She is a really great teacher and her jokes make the 8:45 lecture enjoyable. The tests are pretty straightforward, but she also includes some topics that were not covered on her slides and only in the textbook. There are lots of quizzes and 3 tests total, but only the top 5 quizzes and top 2 tests are taken as graded, the rest are dropped.

Dr. T is very knowledgeable, solid choice. If you've taken AP Psych before, this class should be an easy A for you. I was able to skip a solid amount of lectures, study up a little before tests, and get an A. She gives lots of quizzes, but they will really help your grade in the long run because she only keeps your 5 best quizzes and 2 best tests.

Her lectures, while covering material I already studied before going, were funny and kept my attention. If you've taken ap psychology before you could probably get by without going to all the lectures. If you prepare for the tests then the material won't be too challenging. Watch the videos she gives you before the tests.

This class is all quiz and test-based; however, she really wants her students to succeed. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I'd say that showing up as much as you can truly help with your grade!! She did do a pop quiz once because of so many absences. The class is a bit tedious and her way of teaching is a bit fast for me, but I do really like her!

I loved taking this class with Lisa. She explained everything well and gave us study guides for each test. She encourages everyone to come every class, but does not take attendance. Lecture slides are posted. You do multiple quizzes and a few assignments during class but she only takes your best 5 and drops the rest. 10/10 take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this class and the professor.
All objective exams and quizzes, which are fairly frequent. Stay caught up and you will be ok.
Not a blow off class but Dr. T is really nice and fun. She has a sharp sense of humor, which I appreciate. She always encourages students and wants her students to do well. Grades on a curve.

I have had Lisa for multiple classes and she IS a good person. You must read the lecture slides b4 class (she even suggests this) bc she goes so fast, so you have to learn yourself a lot. my biggest thing was she is RUDE; every time grade came out she was always discouraging to kids who didn't get a A, she also goes on tangents ab her life a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I liked this class and Dr. T, but there was a lot of reading, if you include the textbook. Skim the text, study from the lecture notes, and you should be fine. There are sometimes questions over the modules, but she usually talks about the main points on class, so take notes on that when she does, to get those right.

discussing class work and collaborating on an assignment is not academic misconduct if it was not previously established. dont take this class unless you want to have absolutely no interaction with your peers.

I have no clue why her rating is so high. She is the most rude person I've ever met, she thinks she has to be in control of everything and never ever gives people the benefit of the doubt. Don't try asking any questions because you'll just get yelled at for not knowing the answer. Makes her class way harder than it needs to be.
Doesnt seem to put effort into teaching

I would not recommend. I missed ONE quiz and she personally emailed me suggesting I drop her class. That does not set a good tone for the rest of the semester. There is little understanding for students and this class stresses me out ( ironic for an abnormal psych class).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr T is super nice, but can be a tad condescending at times. This is an intro class, but you do have to put in the work and really study. She really cares about the well-being of her students and has a really cute dog!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The least accommodating prof I've ever had. Basically laughed when students expressed concern/anxiety over short time lengths on quizzes/exams. She's called out and embarrassed students on zoom (no names but if they're in class that's so rude). I've taken super difficult classes and those profs have been way more caring and helpful

Do NOT take abnormal psych with this prof. You will regret it. Only grades are tests & quizzes. Time limit made me anxious to the max. Hated going to zoom classes, even though I normally LOVE psych classes. She was disrespectful when students asked questions. I like the subject, but HATED her. Take this class with another prof to enjoy abnormal!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: RUDE. Exams/quizzes are all over the place and so specific. Extremely hard to succeed in this class no matter how hard you try/study.

If you have to take this class, I highly advise that you take it with a different professor. I only took this class because I was interested in the topic but she made it miserable for me. She is very very rude. I expected to like her because of the good reviews on here, but I realized she writes a lot of them herself.
Most interesting when its over a problem that you have. Read the book, go to class, study before the quizzes and exams. She drops some scores and grades are curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Plan on doing the work, not a blow off class. Lots of quizzes and exams, so you have to keep up. Drops some scores, gives bonus points. Overall reasonable choice if you are interested in the subject.

Make sure to do all the readings, random stuff will appear on the exam, even if she mentioned it for 2 seconds in class. Also, she expects you to have every little detail from the book, module, and her lecture slides memorized. It really is unnecessary and unreasonable. When we all do bad, she tends to blame us.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The worst psych professor I've had at IU. She doesn't give enough time to succeed or even finish quizzes and exams, she gives ridiculous amounts of material to study in a week, and when an entire class is struggling she says "nobody cares".
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Thomassen is a great professor and really helps you learn the material. You need to put in the work or you won't do well, however, if you take the time, you shouldn't have a problem getting a good grade. Her class is quiz heavy, so be prepared and have studied before going to class on quiz days.

Thomassen is a professor that is very knowledgeable and passionate about the topic. I think she wants people to learn and understand the material. However, this is often overshadowed by her want to get through all the material as fast as possible. Will not slow down, hates taking questions, and won't take even reasonable feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: All of my classes are online. if it werent for this class I would be so depressed. All of my classes are boring and hard. This one is interesting and about real life. The professor really tries to help you understand the subject. I hate online classes. Some people cheated so now we get less time on quizzes to stop it but its ok if you study.

This was fully online, but still felt like a regular class. It was a lot of work with the reading and Canvas and lots of notes to study. I thought this would be a blow off class but its frankly a lot, but honestly, it was a really great course. It was surprising what I did not know. Im glad I took it. Dr T juggles, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very rude. Not respectful. People have said exams/quizzes make them anxious because there is NOT enough time whatsoever and she literally just laughs??? Like this is a psychology class where we talk about anxiety, yet she laughs at people for that. Also if you ask a question she thinks is stupid, she'll sigh really loud. Very very rude.

I am taking this course right now, fully online. She is not understanding about adapting to this course. She goes way too fast during broad lectures then tests in depth. It feels like her priority is making quiz/tests harder on her students verses wanting us to actually learn the information.

The time given for the exam was not enough. During quizzes you cant go back to your previous question while the quizzes are also 10 questions for 15 minutes. This class is a lot considering it was during the summer while a pandemic was going on. She was not considerate of this. She has an attitude when you email, and will not try to see your POV.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took 315, 102, and 324 with Dr. T. There are very few assignments in her classes and her tests require studying, but are very reasonable. If you go to class, you shouldn't have to study a lot. She gives quizzes (usually with warning), but drops some. She is hilarious and makes the material interesting.

I loved having Professor T for psychology 155. It was my first time taking a psychology class and she taught everything so well. She has modules that apply to real life which are really interesting. She isn't too hard if you study because she gives lots of quizzes. So I recommend her even if you just want to learn more about how people think.

She is an amazing professor. I know she reads these sometimes lol. But she is so funny and if you go to class and listen to her you will pass. She gives out plenty of extra credit questions on quizzes and tests. I never studied and passed the class. If you read the textbook you will do even better, but honestly, it is not needed.

Hilarious professor that relates lectures to real life situations while being comical which is engaging. She makes class fun and cares about her presentation in order for students to gain what they should.

Dont take this class if you don't want to work hard. She makes you work for it 100%, if you are lazy like me avoid this prof. She is an amazing person and great teacher and is always engaging students, but expects you to work very hard and will check that you do.

one of the best teachers I've had. she def makes you work for it but she explains concepts well and knows how to teach. she cares and will help you if needed. she is really quirky and funny so you'll look forward to class. The more classes you attend the better
She cares about her students and want them to succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Great prof with good sense of humor. Class can be challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. T is a very good professor. She only gives tests and quizzes, so be sure to know the information like the back of your hand, as she does give very good distractor answers. She only keeps the 5 best quiz scores and drops one exam. Make sure to do online practice quizzes to get hints about Q's on the upcoming quizzes. Overall good prof!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Thomassen is a solid choice for psychology. She isn't a professor who hand you a A, but she knows how to help students to do well. Her methods of teaching can truly let you learn so much about psychology. By the way, she is really funny and engages with students a lot during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really enjoyable in class and makes the material interesting. She only gives tests and quizzes so you actually have to know the material to do well in the class, but overall she does a good job of teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Thomassen is an excellent professor! She teaches the material clearly, and in an entertaining way. She's always engaging with the students and never makes class boring. She's very generous with grading, but will get you with the pop quizzes. Overall a fantastic professor, and one I'm excited to have again!

She took abnormal psychology and made it one of the hardest classes i've ever taken. You have so much reading each week, it's impossible to complete. But she tests you on very specific facts from those readings so when i did read all of it, i still couldnt remember because her questions were so specific. She was also condescending to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. T is one of the most entertaining teachers I have ever had. However, the class isn't to be taken lightly. While she is an awesome person, her tests can be challenging and she can be a bit nitpicky on grading the assignments. She does give bonus questions that should help you. Make sure to nail the first couple of quizzes as they are easier.

She was amazing! If you have to take any psych class, I would highly recommend her. She is very good at adding plenty of bonus questions and freebie points on quizzes. She assigned textbook readings but all of the needed information was on the accessible powerpoints, only needed the book when a few questions on a quiz were based on the reading.
