reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was not necessarily difficult but prof was annoying. Goes way too fast when reading slides which makes lectures impossible to get all the information down. She never posted the slides that were gone over in class too. The homework and group project are easy but I simply never went to lectures because it was a waste of time.
The class consists only of lectures, and she goes through the slides too fast to complete all the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is just lecture and professor cruz nichols goes way too fast to keep up. Your grade relies heavily on the midterm and final but I found studying on my own proved to be more beneficial than trying to take notes in class.
Her tests are so material heavy there is no guidance of what to even study. All very confusing. Class itself is boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was boring. She makes you take notes and speaks really fast and doesn't ever post her notes. She also is just unreasonable and not easy to reach after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was a good professor, really cared about the students, and explained things in a way that made them easy to understand. She appreciated questions, answered them in a nice way, and never made anyone feel stupid. She was also very understanding regarding attendance. You have to do the readings to get a good grade but an A is easily achievable.
Lectures are a bit boring, but easy A!

Nice professor, boring class. Grade is mostly determined by midterm and final project. There's not much homework, and the quizzes/discussions can be turned in a week late for full credit. There's a few extra credit opportunities which is a nice grade boost too. Overall easy A for an S & H credit.

These other reviews are wack. Professor Cruz-Nichols was very well educated, and very gracious. Each quiz and assignment were online, and everything had an 1 week grace period meaning you could turn in anything a week late with no penalty. Sometimes instructions were unclear, but overall this is an amazing professor and really good class.

Assigns a lot of work that does not always makes sense, tries to push a political agenda even though this class could very easily teach about both parties she only seems to care about one which seems very unprofessional
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class has a ton of reading even though it's an intro class. The lectures aren't great and it's hard to keep up with all the work. There is a lot of material so it's hard to know what to study for the exam, which was 20% of the final grade. It's a 100 level course but it definitely takes more time than my other classes
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Treats the course as if its a 300 level course that we all are majoring in even though its a 100 level. Will not give a study guide for exams worth 20% of your grade even though you will go over so much materiel you wont even know what to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Cruz Nichols! The lectures were interested, she was super well-informed, and I enjoyed reading the papers that were assigned. There wasn't too much work and I learned a lot about the current political climate.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class was probably the most difficult course I have ever taken. She is a very nice Professor, she just expects a lot from her students. For this class we were required to read graduate level articles and they never really made sense to me. I am also not a fan of group projects and I was assigned to a group where most of the work fell on me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: His explanations were good and he made sure everyone understood content before moving on. Exams were fair and homeworks were not too time consuming. Lectures were a bit boring but he did his best to encourage us to be interested in it.

I don't think the he made the course difficult, I think it's just a difficult class. He does go a little fast during lectures, but he lets you take pictures if you need to. He's good at making sure everyone understands the material.
Worst professor ever. Class is extremely hard, he is really inorganized, and exams are even worse. 40% of the grades are exams and he doesn't prepare u well enough for the exams.

He means well, however he is extremely unorganized. He has no class outline, posts homework due the next day, and tells no one. He also spent a lot of time on one easy thing in the lecture, then has only 15 minutes left, and completely rushes through the second one. He is also completely inaccessible outside of class. Test are open note
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took 303 with him. Nice + funny guy, he means well. But he's super unorganized and hard to follow. Went to every single lecture, sat in front, took notes, and still struggled on the tests. This course doesn't really teach you stats, he teaches you how to program using R. No tentative schedule and randomly posts homework. Not great at communication
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Valdivia is a really nice guy. If you attend class, you will definitely pass. However, the material itself is fairly hard. You'll have between 7 and 10 homeworks, so be ready to dedicate around 3 hours per week outside of class minimum. This class is the main weed out for the STAT undergraduate program, so of course it's going to be harder.

If you go to class every single day and participate this class is easy. Open "note" (you can use canvas) tests. If you miss class you'll have to learn the code by yourself which is not easy, so just go to class. Overall a great professor and the class expectations are very reasonable. Everyone with poor reviews probably didn't go to class often.
Whatever you do, DO NOT TAKE 303 with this professor. You will be fighting for your grade the entire semester. He will just give out zeros as grades even if you attend every single class.

I took 352, not 350 with him. The class itself is the real weedout for stats majors, not 350. It's tough, but very much doable. Be comfortable with calc (mostly PDE's). There's a lot of HW and group work, but he gives the option to only show up for exams. I wouldn't do that though, his lectures form questions.

His lectures were very straight forward. Any code that you needed for the test he clearly went over in the lecture. You can watch the lectures whenever and have a couple of assignments each week (most of them are quick checks that you can redo). Valdivia is willing to work with you and an A is easy to obtain if you watch the lectures.
I think he has knowledge in stats more or less, but doesn't know how to efficiently explain them to students.
Nightmare. No more words to say

Arturo is a nice guy, but his lectures are pretty all over the place and his explanations are not super clear. He does assign a big homework assignment every week, and depending on your TA you may be graded well or not so well (like me).

The class is not easy, like failed the midterm, but Prof. Valdivia really made opportunities to improve your grade. If you go over exams with him 1-on-1, he'll likely give you back some points. He gave extra credit to people who went class at the end, and he lets you drop the lowest hw grade. Talk to him if you start struggling and he'll help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a genuinely good guy and wants you to succeed. The book he assigned is not useful at all but his lectures are clear and helpful. Overall, recommend his class and would take his class again

Pros: - He is a nice guy. Personally, I like him. - He provides lots of homework. That is fine. We can learn a least something from HW. Cons: - His lecture is not organized. - His explanations are not clear. He is not good for graduate level courses.
He is a nice professor. But the book he signed is not clear and not enough to explain the concept. His lecture goes fast. Be prepare to study yourself.
He is a great professor that is engaging in class. He is also really just a nice guy. Lecture could be more organized. 9/10 would take again.

He's nice if you engage with him. That said, his lectures are extremely unclear and his grading is somewhat harsh. He sometimes mumbles and will often write something on the board and immediately erase it before you get the chance to copy it down. The textbooks he assigns don't really clear up the material either, so you'll need to self-study.
He cannot teach. This man is lack of basic empathy. Avoid him or torture yourself.
Quizzes or groupwork not announced in advance and he is proud of it. Lectures are not in logic order. Rudechill and frustrating. He is my 100% nightmare. Dont want to see him in IU anymore.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: For me the drawbacks were that attendance is mandatory, and we can't see what questions we got wrong after we take the exams. He was always available to help if needed. I strongly encourage anyone who is taking this course to read the textbook, as at least for me this was the best way to learn the material outside of his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Arturo I think really tried, but the material was terrible & he was better at doing the material than actually teaching it. He cared about his students but made the class impossible. Getting a C in this class took a lot of effort. It was however nice that he would drop the lowest test score.

This teacher may be the worst IU instructors I have ever seen. He graded our final with an average of 60%. Our class is a graduate student class. His grading criteria was so funny and lame. And he is so ridiculous about grading. Trust me, if you work hard on it, you may still get an unpleasant and unsatisfied grade. Worst and nightmare.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class, he curves the tests and really wants you to succeed in his class.

Before I took this class, I read the reviews of him on here and was really scared of what I was in for with his class. But he proved all of his bad reviews wrong! He is a VERY nice guy, he wants to make sure everybody understands the material, and he makes you feel very open to ask questions if you don't understand something. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lectures aren't always clear and assignments can be outside of what has been learned which can be pretty stressful, but Arturo is very helpful in preparing for tests and grades leniently. I have learned a lot in this class.
Worst professor at IUB. Disappointed. Highly recommend not to take his courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Provides clear explanations and is willing to help students. I'm unsure as to why his other reviews are so low. Those comments are not reflective of my experience in his class at all.
Worst instructor ever. His lectures are so unclear, I have to self-study a lot.
Exam questions have excel formulas for a piece of paper and you're supposed to pick the correct number based of the excel formula with no other help...I think that's all that need to be said
DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. WORST CLASS. WORST PROFESSOR. NO HELP. TESTS ARE CRAZY HARD. LECTURES ARE LAME. YOU END UP WITH ZERO KNOWLEDGE GAIN. IN ANY CASE, AVOID THIS CLASS AND THE PROFESSOR.
Just don't do it . . . unless you like to torture yourself. Or only care about math as a concept and not as a useful tool. Ruined an interesting topic.

Easily the most disappointing experience I have had as a student at IU. The only thing you will hate more than his tests and homework are the mandatory lectures. I make a point not to miss any classes however these lectures really tempt you to take a dive in front of the B-bus on your walk to class. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.
Every morning before class I load 1 bullet in the chamber, spin, pull trigger, get dressed and go to class.

Arturo is not the worst professor in the world, but he most certainly is the worst one that I have ever had. His lectures are worthless, homework is nothing like quizzes or tests, and I can honestly say that I know less about statistics than when I first came into the class. Thank you Arturo!

350 characters is not enough to describe what a horrible professor this man is.  Literally every "resource" including powerpoints, online textbook, and himself is completely useless.  It's impossible to do well on homework or quizzes by yourself.  He makes you feel like you inconvenience him by asking questions.  Absolutely ZERO teaching ability.

Arturo is not a good professor. He's very confusing and difficult to understand. This is a tough class that doesn't seem to be very closely related to business. The class uses business based problems but that's about it. The material won't help much in a business career. I would recommend taking E370 or another alternative.

This guy is an awful teacher. Homework is very difficult, quizzes and groupwork are unannouced so attendance is mandatory, which would be fine if his lectures were useful, but they're not. Exams are very difficult and even after studying thoroughly I still did poorly. He is lazy, completely unenthusiastic, rude, and very unorganized. Avoid him.

Valdivia's homework policy alone is reason enough to avoid his class.  The homework is near impossible to complete accurately with the requirements he sets, and he does little to help students.  He is somewhat difficult to understand yet thinks everyone should be understanding him.  The worst professor I've had at IU.

Mme Vance is one of the most influential, inspiring, and encouraging professors I've ever had, heightening my affinity for the nuances of French language and expression. Thanks to her detailed and engaging teaching, I feel like my command of the language has significantly improved.  I would highly recommend taking a course with her if you can!!

She's a great professor! She always emphasizes that your understanding comes first; if you need a bit more time to get with her and ask questions about homework, she is willing to be a little flexible with due dates. Always answers questions well. Syntax is hard, but her lectures and feedback on exams/homeworks made it much easier to understand!

Syntax was a very difficult class. However, Professor Vance made it so much easier to succeed because of her office hours. She explains things clearly in class, but syntax is something that needs to be explained more than once. You'll do super well if you take advantage of how available she is. Tough assignments and tough exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great professor! Isn't afraid of being a little off track of syllabus if discussion is valid and needed. Fair grading and explains everything well. Very genuine and caring about your success in the class. Would highly recommend any class she teaches.

Awesome professor. Her class is really interesting although confusing at some times. She will always explain in english when people are super confused. I definitely recommend taking her class. She's super nice and a great professor.

Vance is really disorganized; the class had almost no structure, even though she taught STRAIGHT from the textbook. She often had problems understanding what we were asking her or just didn't know how to answer us. The grading was really picky and specific.

Boring and very confusing. She answered questions when people had them, but sometimes we didn't know where to start. She doesn't explain things well at all. Very easy grader, though, and a sweet lady overall.
I love Barbara!
Terrible teacher......Very disorganized . Needs to work in a flea market

She is a great teacher who cares about her students and wants them to get the best grade possible. Unfortunately I had her for a very boring class, which she structured poorly. If she were teaching a class besides advanced grammar I would recommend her for anyone. If you take her F313 class, you will have to do a lot of teacing yourself!
Excellent Professor that really cares about her students and is dedicated to making sure they understand.  AMAZING PROFESSOR!!!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Took M 106, Math of Decision and Beauty. Not as easy of a class as is advertised. VERY homework heavy but usually can complete during recitation.

Nice guy, but he is not good at teaching. I have never done bad in a math class until this class. His notes do not correlate to the homework or tests. Retake for the 1st and 3rd are even worse than the first test. The examples he skips in lecture are the ones closest to the test. Office hours made me want to cry bc he confused me Failed tests twice

Nice, funny and tried to make lecture enjoyable, but, lecture isn't very enjoyable when there's several math errors in the notes/HW or in his own work. There were units where almost every homework had an "impossible" problem, he doesn't communicate with TAs tho. I had him for M106- Class is super easy if you are reasonably good at math/reasoning

The reviews here I feel don't represent the professor very well. I feel like he's a good guy and wants his students to do well. Other reviews also talk about the test being hard but he provides previous exams from years past and the ones he is giving us seems much easier, also gives a real good curve.

Super confusing, and I got a tutor AND used AI and none of the practice exams looked like the actual exam. He had to curve literally every exam because it was so hard. Honestly though if u want to pass and ur not great at math just make sure to get 100% on the homework, weekly "quizzes" and do ur best on the exams and u should be fine.
Exams are hard to study for. Was told to use AI, which was used to make the exams (clearly)... Practice exams are out of date or don't relate to the required material.

Anyone saying hes a good professor must be a math genius because if you didnt know what he was talking about during class, which many didnt as we were all helping each other, you were practically screwed for the course. He makes lectures very confusing and hard to follow, and has many many many mistakes making it even more confusing than already is
The only thing I learned was how to sleep in an upright position.

You need to be on 119 gallons of Monster to stay awake, much less pay attention in this class. If you want to have long lectures and teach yourself the topics afterward, this class is for you! Homework boosts grades but doesn't help understanding. 10/10 will not take again!

If you dont already understand the content hes teaching good luck! He makes everything so confusing, and does not explain the content well. The homeworks definitely help to boost your grade but they can take a very long time and many times barely relate to what we had done in class. Chatgpt will become your best friend just like it is his!!!!!!

Overall a solid professor. Attendance is not mandatory, but there are weekly "quizzes" that basically act as attendance, although you can easily still pass without doing them. Notes are posted online at the end of the week, and not too much homework is given out (30-45 questions a week).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Honestly he's a rly good professor i just suck at math lol. He gives you plenty of note templates and has practice tests you can take before exams. He started doing attendance quizzes halfway through semester but it was nice cause they gave you extra points in the Quiz category. He obviously wants all his students to pass, but you gotta work for it

Attendance is typically taken once a week in class with a quiz. If you have a background in Calculus, you will do fine; if not, you will need to go out of your way to do well. Professor Villatoro is good at explaining topics and is usually available to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I dont like math but he made it seem a little less terrible. his lectures can be interactive so I recommend going. all notes are published, filled in and not filled in. GO TO OFFICE HOURS, he loves people coming to them and will spend time to make sure you understand beyond just doing the homework problems.

I had taken this class just this yeah, he is very accessible outside of class. Office hours are frequent and he is always willing to help out. There are usually three assignments a week, if you just do the work and ask questions you'll get a good grade. I enjoyed my time a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He explained concepts really well, that along with the number of examples he did in class was super helpful. Definitely recommend doing the homework, because those are typically harder than the exams, so if you can do those you should be good. I took a calculus course in high school, failed, then got an A in this class, he's doing something right.

The lectures are very fast and long. If you don't get the content it's very hard. The Hw does help your grade a decent amount. Our final was the friday before break at 5:30 and we had a final at 10 on homecoming. Super inconvenient timing.

Villatoro was a great teacher, I was able to follow along and learn very well. He teaches through examples going through every step of each problem. The class has 4 tests, all curved and two being retake able for full credit, the rest is homework graded on completion. Hes enthusiastic and all in all a good teacher. I enjoyed the class.

Called himself a "good boy" twice in the same class.

Would not recommend.

Unfortunately I did not have a great experience with this professor. His lectures were hard to understand and I found myself constantly asking where he got a certain number. He would constantly make mistakes while explaining problems making the lecture even more confusing than it already was. 

This class taught me pure rage.

It was a really great experience taking course with him. He has great passion for math and really cares about his students' success and whether his lectures are clear enough. Even if you do not get it during the lectures, you can always ask after class or during office hours in which he takes his time to explain it carefully for you.

Prof Villatoro was very funny and made the lectures easy to understand. He was very understanding and caring. I recommend taking this class with him. If you do everything you need to do and go to office hours for help, you should do well in the class. I really liked him.

Joel is an amazing instructor for calc II. He has clear passion for the subject and values the importance of teaching. Assigned homework is very reasonable. Test difficulty is reasonable as well. Sometimes makes mistakes in class but they do not interfere with learning. Overall, heavily recommend for both calc I and II based off my experience.

He made Calc II such an enjoyable experience, I was pleasantly surprised by how well he was able to make the difficult topics actually approachable. He has a dry humor and is a relatable teacher and would 10/10 take him again. (attendance wasn't mandatory, but you should always try and come to the lectures to fully grasp the course.)
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Villatoro is very kind and passionate about teaching! However, his lectures can be hard to follow due to overcomplicating concepts because of his vast knowledge on the subject. Also, he often makes mistakes during class, which can be frustrating, though he does his best to correct them and clarify confusion.
Enjoyable professor.
Is very passionate about math, and able to explain things pretty well. Made Calc 2 be an actual fun class.
Makes way too many careless mistakes in class and students must correct him, making learning very difficult. It is annoying at this point with this many errors every class
I took M212 but that wasn't an option on here. I loved this class and professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Villatoro is a very nice professor but his lectures can be confusing at times due to mistakes. However, he usually catches them and clears up any confusion. He provides practice tests which are slightly harder versions of the real exam and he has group quizzes. As long as you use all the resources provided to you, the class is manageable.
Professor Villatoro encourages questions and tries to explain thoroughly. He often makes mistakes in class but tries to correct them.

Joel is a hilarious professor that has good lectures, although can be sometimes confusing because of mistake but he finds these out quick and corrects himself. Calc 2 is a hard class and i recommend him without a doubt.
This guy is a genuine square and don't even bother asking him for a 0.2% round.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Both of the A306 teachers are pretty much identical but if you actually pay attention in class, I guess Demere is better than Clark. Attendance is required (tophat) but i just zoned out for every single class and then learned the content each unit the night before. If you can lock in last minute and cram, then you'll be fine (exams 75% of grade).

This class is mostly self-study. He talks really slow and only reads off the slides. Discussions are so important to go to actually learn the material. Most of the TA's are very prepared and knowledgeable. Lots of memorizing formulas. Grade is based on the tests mostly. Definitely utilize office hours and SI sessions they're very good!!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best options for A306. He gives pretty good lectures but they can be kind of boring. Takes TopHat.
He's fine. My only problem is that he talks sooooo slowly. It's almost impossible to sit through an entire lecture.

He is a nice guy. Lectures are quick, so it is important not to get distracted. Discussions help a lot so it is important to ask questions then. A lot of self-learning, but there are plenty of resources outside of class to help. Be prepared to study a lot and the exams make up most of your final grade.
Great professor, prepares you well in general. The most helpful problems are from the discussions so make sure you understand those. He does talk slow which can make class boring

Very clear lectures and does a good job communicating what parts of each unit are most important / will be on the exam. Very exam-heavy course so as long as you study a lot before you'll be fine. Honestly don't know why people tweak about this class, read the textbook and do the practice problems during Discussion and you'll have success.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Demere is a super nice person, especially if you go to office hours. However, I think that he would be a fantastic sleep podcaster. His voice is genuinely so relaxing that it is the only class I have ever fallen asleep in. But, if you're good at staying awake, take him! Also A306 is so hard with any professor! Beware

Professor Demere is great professor for A306. You only meet once a week. Exams are 75% of your grade so make sure you are studying. Go over all the pre-lecture videos, homeworks, and practice exams and you will be just fine.

Professor Demere is a good teacher and the class is more generous with extra points and curves than I expected. Every exam was curved by at least 1 question and the entire class received a multiple percent boost at the end of the semester. Overall the class was fairly difficult but nothing crazy. Prepare to study a decent bit outside of class

Simple class all about Tableau. Class was typically half lecture and half interactive. Frequently ended early. 3 easy quizzes every week. Final project and exam are worth most of your grade and you probably won't know what to expect. He is nice but mostly serious.

He is very caring and wants you to succeed. He teaches at a slow pace and teaches Tableau very well with his walkthroughs. Attendance is encouraged as his final has questions about in-class discussions and he also grades on participation/professionalism. Content can sometimes be boring but he often ends class early. Definitely take him for A314
Best class for students who want ChatGPT to grade their work!

The class consists of busy work assignments created by AI, graded by AI, and then a lot of your grade comes from a group project with random teammates which is also graded with AI. She is also a pretty tough grader. The class isn't impossible, but she definitely makes it harder than it should be, and kills all motivation to try.

The professor uses AI for making assignments and giving assignments (too reliant on AI). Also, there is alot of busy work in the class which is unnecessary. The quizzes in class don't make any sense. Be aware that there is a midterm and final aside from the case work. Her grading is also confusing it isn't consistent.

One of my favorite professors at IU. If you attend class and follow rubrics, you will get an A. I agree some of it can be busy work, but I still think I learned overall. She is very understanding and willing to help, especially if you form a relationship with her in the beginning.

She uses chatGPT to do literally everything in this class, didnt even bother taking out the Chatgpt watermark on one of the assignments. Grading criteria are all made with AI, and she constantly contradicts herself when it comes to grading and assignment expectations. This class is also just straight busy work. She is a very nice person though.

First off, she literally uses ai to write assignments. She gives homework at LEAST 2 times a week, usually way more. I feel like I haven't learned a thing in this class and her grading criteria is so weird

Waste of time class. Only assigns busywork, constantly contradicts herself of the "rules" of assignments, you're graded on her random whims, and she uses chat gpt to make assignments because she doesn't bother to remove the end and beginning parts of ai responding to her prompts. Makes me wonder if AI is grading us too...

Great professor - really kind and created such a welcoming environment in class. Everyone became friends real quick and that made the final project easier.

Grades pretty easily as long as you stick to the rubric, so if you attend class its almost impossible to get below an A.

Will miss her a lot after this semester. TAKE HER for biz writing!!

Winston cares too much about attendance. Your grades will be disproportionate, and they will value in-class assignments more than finalized projects, which are worth 75 points, compared to multiple 5-point assignments. Overall, nice human, OD professor. I would not recommend her, she cares way too much about the little things.

She is very smart & knowledgeable, but it isn't enjoyable to be in her class. She doesn't show your grade in canvas till the very end of the semester so you really don't know where your grade is at. She doesn't answer emails when asking about grading.
Its a tough class, but she is all over the place and not organized. She doesn't really explain things well. I learned the whole class on my own teaching myself, not from her.

Prof Watugala is the goat man. Tests honestly made me want to cry but if you study you will do well. And she gives you the materials needed to do well. Also, unlike other f303 profs, she actually has real world experience and isn't some boring academia person that makes you want to sleep. Overall best f303 prof in the game would highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Peng cares about student understanding and uses fun class games to explain concepts. A pro is that the exams are fair if you attend class and finish assignments. A potential con is that success depends heavily on active participation rather than just reading slides. Overall, it is a rewarding experience for those who show up.
If you are a quiet student who aced k201 and doesn't tend to form a connection with the teacher, Peng is fine. But if you struggle a bit, Peng has 0 personability or care for her students.

Good professor overall and is very knowledgable about the topics. Sometimes I feel the lectures could go at a faster pace. Everything in this course is pretty easy aside from the projects. Make sure you start the projects earlier in the week so you can ask questions before they are due. Overall, I would recommend taking this course with her.

Peng cared about her students. Gave out a note sheet during class that will basically get you through the projects and quizzes. She's more than willing to help. Attendance isn't required but I would say is pretty necessary. She always comes prepared for her lectures and understands the material super well.
Gives note sheets that make the class way easier. Super helpful and genuinely cares about her students.
Peng is a great teacher, she knows the material very well and answers questions greatly if you have any. Most of the assignments are group based anyway, so she makes class very manageable.

Professor Schlegel is an amazing educator and highly knowledgeable professional in her field. Her classes are hard and take a lot of effort, allowing students to gain respect for the discipline of physiology and giving them the opportunity to become 'expert physiologists' as she likes to say.

Prof. Schlegel cares about student learning and growth. The class is very hard, and you should expect a LOT of work. However, the class is very beneficial to anyone who wants to go into the medical field. We did a lot of case-based learning which helped me to understand physiology in the real world.

Dr. Schlegel is a great person, and wants you to succeed. This class is HARD, no doubts. It will also require 3x the time, effort, out of class meetings, and group work than you've probably ever done before. However, if you're going into the medical field AT ALL, it's worth it. Get ready to work super hard, you'll be glad you did... eventually

To start with the "bad news", this class is stressful and a LOT of work. However, Dr. Schlegel is amazing and I loved the class! This class is probably one the best ones to take in preparation for medical school. However, if you are not going on to some medical graduate program, I would probably take something less stressful.

If you have a weak group, drop out. I succeeded because of my group, but would not have survived without them. Exam averages are in the 40-50% range with 10-15 page case reports due the same week and 2 huge presentations.  In class assignments, lab assignments, and outside work/ reading make this class one of the hardest I've ever taken at IU.

Professor Schlegel is a wonderful lady. She really cares for her students and WANTS them to succeed. That being said, this class was a train wreck. No one knew what was going on, including the TAs. The amount of coursework is incredibly heavy and the exams are downright impossible to interpret. Oh and 75% of the class is team work. BUT she curves!!

Your success in this course is dependent on the strength of your group as the entire course is group work. Lectures are dull and not helpful for exams. Course has too much work with large papers being due every Friday that overlap tests and other projects. Prof doesn't heed concerns of students. Individual exam averages were all around 50%!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The absolutely WORST professor I have ever had in my life. Lectures are unengaging, and lecture slides are take directly from the book. Group work is a huge part of the course, but groups are assigned at random, so take that as you will. So much work is given that AIs couldn't get it all in before the final. Avoid this professor at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend to anyone. I have never taken a class so terrible. Poorly organized, learning objectives not clearly communicated. High expectations but guidance on projects/reports/assignments is minimal. Harsh, inconsistent grading. Most work done in groups, which presents a lot of challenges. So much work, there are just under 3000 points.

This was truly the worst class I have ever taken at IU because of the poor organization and appalling teaching style. Professor was incapable of presenting information clearly or of communicating expectations for the mountain of assignments she gave. Everything was group work. AIs agreed that exams were poorly written. Absolutely horrible.

Hard, arbitrary grader. Do not know what she wants from you. It sucks because she is obviously a very nice person who cares about her students and knows the subject material, but I have never been more confused and stressed in a class. Like the person, not the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Absolutely intolerable to listen to her lecture. It's clear she knows what she's talking about and I'm not hating on her as a person as she actually seems quite sweet. However, during lectures she will talk for an hour and say literally nothing. She teaches nothing during lecture and the exams are super specific leaving you lost when studying.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Class and lectures were extremely boring, most of the work in class was busy work. There were assignments due every week and due on the same day as the exams. Papers were harshly graded and if you are in a bad/lazy group you are in trouble since 80% is group work. The exams were impossible, no amount of studying prepared you for them.

you can't miss a day of her class or else you will be really  behind. her power points are totally useless, you must copy down everything she says to get an understanding of the material. P451 took up 70% of my course work last semester, often times with two long papers and a test in the same week. difficult class and teacher.

Tons of work. All of it group work. However, you will learn a lot in this class. Beyond the physiology, I felt a lot more comfortable looking up primary research after this class. While it was a lot of work, I see it really helping prepare me for my future. The AI's are really helpful, Schlegel is less available.

This class was very difficult and required an insane amount of time (which was spent in a group). Her expectations seemed a little unreasonable at times, but the AIs were incredibly helpful. I learned a lot in this class but probably wouldn't have taken it in retrospect.

I learned so much in her class and learned it through a whole new way of thinking. The case study, group format approach is great and even though the tests are difficult with low averages, grades come out well in the end. Must take course for any premedical student. Extremely difficult, but worth it

If you aren't a bio major, dont take this class. Incredibly difficult. The entire class frequently finds ourselves looking around at eachother with faces that say "what the heck this is torture". awful class, she means well and is smart but is useless as a professor. it feels like a 400 level course

Terrible professor. Does not know how to teach material in a way that is helpful to any student. I am a science person, and I was extremely excited to take the class, after the second week I dreaded going to class because it was a complete waist of time. She is nice, and means well but should not be allowed to teach. DO NOT Take her if possible.

She is the worst prof ever. She doesn't teach one thing and you Google every quiz or project you do. Her exams are ridiculously hard and it turns a Freshman level class into 300-400 level class. Our first exam's class average was a 63% if that tells you anything.

She is a very friendly teacher as long as you make the effort to talk to her. Everything is in group format which is kinda nice bc you have the knowledge of 5 people.  If you dont have any background in biology it is extremely hard.  The tests are really hard but she gives you many opportunities to raise your grade and get random point. Go to class
Tough for non-majors. Attendance is pretty much required, and it's in depth for a 100-level class. She's quiet and not real personable, if it wasn't for the TA, the class would've been a disaster.

Turns an intro/100 level class into a 300 or 400 level class. I only took this class to fulfill a requirement- I am not a science person- but this professor teaches the class as if we are all biology majors. A background in biology is basically necessary to keep up, it's quite unfair. Heavy workload. Her TA's are very helpful.
Professor Xiang is a wonderful option for BUSG 492. Very fair and kind to students

Very unclear and disorganized instructions. Be prepared to teach yourself very difficult concepts. One of the least clear, least considerate, most stressful professors I've taken in 4 years of school. I have never left a negative review for a professor ever, but the amount of lost hair and stress caused by this professor compelled me to warn you.

This is not an easy class, but you would get a good grade and learn a lot if you are willing to work. She is a nice instructor, always prepared for class, caring, easily accessible outside the classroom, and encourages students to ask questions in lectures.

Awful. Do not take her class if you can help it. She does not teach, she simply puts words on a slide and reads from it. You're supposed to be learning how to run regressions in Stata, yet she does not take 1 day to teach Stata. She only provides screenshots of what it should look like. Your final project takes 20% but you have to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kind, fun, and caring. If you pay attention you will do well in the class, she wants her students to succeed.
Professor Xiang is a wonderful option for BUS-G 492. Very fair and kind to students

Professor Xiang is very caring and sweet. She does not get overly personable and is pretty business. Her lectures can become boring and monotonous over time and many people miss her classes because of her generous 6 absence policy. She is very available to meet with students after class and at office hours. She gives extra credit for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Graded pretty tough and lectures were very boring

I had Professor Chen for Compass and I would not recommend her. The rubric isn't super clear on instructions and she grades only off of that. She will randomly take points off and won't explain why. Lecture was brutal to sit through. If you want to keep up your GPA DO NOT TAKE!
Not good with communication about grades and grading, will randomly dock points for things based solely on deliverables when it was a presentation heavy class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not recommend her AT ALL especially hard to listen to in-class!!! The points were consistently taken off for very weak reasons which weren't even on the rubric criteria. When trying to speak with her after to gain clarification, she was passive aggressive and responded 5 mins before 5pm so she would be out of office for further questions.
She does read from the slides a lot. She's very sweet and pretty accommodating about assignments. Make sure you do your work according to the rubric and the slides she shows in class.

Professor Chen was a great professor who tried making something as boring as business writing interesting. I would recommend her she is definitely one of the better professors I have this semester. She is clear on her expectations and as long as those are met you should be able to do fine in the class
Just do your work. easiest class you will take sophomore year. dont mess up. I got an A

I took the summer variation of 204, but Professor Chen made it as enjoyable as it could be for 8:45 AM. The content was straightforward, and some seemed a bit too easy, but it ramped up more as the class went on. The report at the end was the most notable part of the class. Being given only a week to complete it was rough, but it was a quick class.

Easy class and not a lot of time required until last project. Multiple group projects so be prepared for that. Has a lot of little useless assignments but easy points to get just annoying. I would recommend this class if you want an easy class. Easy grader and does take attendance.

I've never had such an easy class be so painful to attend. If you want to protect your GPA, take this class because it really isn't tough but it is super painful to attend and do the busy work assignments. A ton of of listening to her talk off her slides, useless reading, and poor examples to learn from when writing your major assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overall, the course was hard. However, Prof Chen made the course extremely painful to attend. She would spend most lectures speaking on things that don't matter or could be covered in the fraction of the time. Taking this course will probably mean a good grade, but just be prepared for the in class experience to be painful.

Professor Chen is the best professor I've had so far (keep in mind I'm only a freshman). She is a lenient grader and is pretty accessible outside of class. Definitely a good choice for C104, the only complaint I had was that sometimes the feedback was a bit confusing. So long as you put in some effort, it should be pretty easy to get at least a B+.

Professor Chen was a very flexible teacher. Anytime you need an extension she will give it to you. The only drawback is she never gives out 100s for bigger assignments no matter how well you do. I was never stressed about this class taking it with her. If you put in all the work you will end in the range of A-B+

Professor Chen is a caring and amazing professor. She really cared about our success and gave lots of good feedback on presentations. Pretty easy grader but will never give out 100%. Created an environment where you feel comfortable and confident to present and she is always accessible after class. Also her outfits are so fire.
great teacher

I'd recommend taking C204 with Professor Chen. She is flexible meeting outside of class and cares about her students. She also replaces quizzes and tests with a little more group work, which gives you more experience working on teams. Just make sure to work well with your group on group projects.
Great teacher, very entertaining and handles big classes really well

丁老师 is incredibly nice, encouraging, and supportive. Her Chinese class isn't particularly easy, and some of the topics for fourth year are a little boring, but overall having her as a teacher is a great experience. She's very funny, engaging, and accommodating if you need help.

While I found the text less effective than in third year and can't pinpoint why, I greatly appreciate how engaging Xiao Ying is as a teacher. She clearly communicates expectations and is very understanding. However, attendance is crucial—I skipped six times and nearly failed, so showing up is essential for success in her course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really good professor who cares and works with you, although the chinese class is general is very difficult with tons of homework and memorization

She can seem a bit intimidating at first but she's really fun. She'll joke around sometimes but keeps a mostly professional atmosphere. She really makes sure you understand the material. I would definitely recommend her for first year Chinese!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is a fantastic teacher! I'm glad I had her for my first year of Chinese. If you dont like working outside of class to learn a language steer away. You need to preview the work ahead of class, if you do this the class is very easy to get an A. She explains the grammar thoroughly. If you want to be challenged and accomplished take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The content itself is extremely difficult, but she is a very generous grader along with the other assistant instructors. As long as you complete the homework and show up to class I don't think there's anyway you can fail. She is a very good instructor as well as very kind and considerate to all of her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Under normal circumstances I would have failed this class. She makes it nearly impossible to fail the class so long as you do ALL the homework. You need to study at least 15 hours a week to understand the material. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU WANT AN EASY A YOU WILL HAVE TO STUDY TO GET A's ON THE EXAM.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her name in class is Ding Laoshi. She is amazing! There are dictations twice a week that you REALLY need to prepare for. This is a very challenging class. Takes LOTS of time out of your week, but worth it in the end. Pay attention in class. The lectures are pretty engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: She's savage, yet she's fantastic. She teaches well, and she's very compassionate when it comes to students. Clearly cares about what she does, and I look forward to more classes under tutelage.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Overall I think Ding Laoshi is a good teacher. 102 covers several difficult grammar points but she does her best. Similarly to 101, there are dictations twice weekly. If you need help she or the drill instructors are available to help.

She is a fantastic teacher! I'm glad I had her for my first year of Chinese. If this is your first time taking Chinese, be prepared to do a lot of work - around two hours a night - if you ever want to be skilled at it. The tests are fair, and are graded very leniently. Because this is a language, don't fall behind, or it will bite you in the end!:)

Lyu Laoshi is the best teacher! His lectures are hilarious, and I never knew what he would be about to say next. The rapid-fire way he teaches to get you to participate really allows you to pick up language quickly. He is also always open to questions or to come in for office hours. Everyone should take a class with Lyu Laoshi!

Professor Lyu is amazing! I would def recommend taking his class if you get the chance. He makes lectures so fun & engaging. He's very funny and makes jokes or gives random fun facts. He emphasizes speaking & practicing often so partcipation is important in learning a language. He'll call on people randomly & u have to engage w others time to time.

He is very involved and animated in his lectures, and he is so funny. Definitely be ready to participate and speak during the lectures. He is very patient if you make mistakes. Also, he is very helpful and encouraging during office hours, so if you can, I would suggest signing up for those as often as possible.

Prof Lyu makes learning super enjoyable. He explains concepts and grammar in way that's easy to understand. He helps students a lot, is very kind, and really cares for his students. His lectures are super energetic, entertaining, and funny. 
One of the best professors I've had so far! Definitely would sign up for his class again!

Genuinely love this professor! There was never a dull moment with him and every lecture was memorable and useful. He gives students many opportunities to do well on the assignments/exams. Although he will make you speak Chinese in class, which can initially seem intimidating, it is all because he wants to challenge you and make you learn.

When I stepped into their class, I was captivated by their dynamic teaching style. Not only are the lectures incredibly insightful, but he has a remarkable ability to infuse humor seamlessly, making every session enjoyable. Beyond the academic realm, his genuine care for students is evident. Lastly, he will always try to challenge you in class!

Hands one of the best Professors at IU. He genuinely cares so much about the success of his students and gives them so many opportunities to do good on tests, which can be hard, but if you pay attention in class, you will be fine! Lastly, he is hilarious and makes every lecture enjoyable and memorable so you will definitely learn something!

He is a great professor! If you are looking into him for 101, don't be scared. He is a little lively at times, but he is great at teaching and makes learning Chinese tons of fun. Would suggest him to anyone!

Tie was always very nice and has interesting and sometimes funny lectures. There is not much reading in this class, some articles, but besides that your homework is watching and analyzing movies! It was great to finally watch important Chinese films and get credit while I do it! Tie is a great teacher and not harsh on grading.

Overall not a terrible professor. Feel as though the grading is super unfair. It is all done by the AI. Was constantly told that professor Xiao graded on a “curve” and didn't believe in 100s.  Basically the entire class depends on your AI. He also won't post the lecture slides so you must attend class to get the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great class and very interesting if you're interested in film and/or Chinese history. One page reflection for each film (9) and a reading paper for each reading (4). Watch around one film every week and discuss it in class. Often taken by Chinese or international students. Recommend this class and professor!
Very nice, understanding, interesting, invested, and lively teacher, would take again.
He was very nice and instructive, very lively and nice. I highly recommend.
He is definatly a teacher you want. He is tough on grading but still amazing

This teacher is absoulutly amazing. His lectures are full of information and material that you wouldn't find elswhere. He is funny, enthusiastic, and just the best teache4 I have ever had. Definatly recomend and would take again.
Amazing lectures, and even though I got a bad grade I know it was my fault, he was full of energy and very intelligent. 10/10

Professor Xiao is very enthusiastic about what he teaches and is clearly very interested in his student's success. While the discussion isn't mandatory, I would suggest you participate as it's very obvious that he's excited to teach you Chinese literature. I learned a lot in his class and the assignments he gives are easy and concise.
Proffessor X, was amazing! The people who gove bad reveiws did NOT pay attention. This professor is the best I've had. I would recommend this class to all future students!
The best
Even though I got a bad grade, it was definectly my fault. He tried to help me as much as he could.
I mean... he has no downfalls.
Best teacher ever!
This was the best teacher ever!!! I will do this again if I could. The best!!!
I mean, it is the class you want.
I've taken two courses with him on the topics of Chinese film and literature. His selections of assigned reading were both broad in scope and interesting. Highly recommend.
So this professor really isn't even willing to be helpful. He refuses to be understanding of student situations such as late registration, and in class is not astute with teaching.
SO good at explaining concepts and really funny. Love Boyuan

The practice tests are super helpful, attendance isn't required, and the teacher is funny and relatable. There might be a slight language issue barrier, but the class, assignments, and tests are a nice medium compared to other math courses. Late penalties are strict, though, but it's just the course standard and not set by the professor.
This professor uses traditional teaching methods and is hard to understand, his lectures are slow and dragged out and you could honestly learn more from the textbook.
Lovely professor. Super nice, caring, sweet, and very lenient if you need to submit something late. The class overall is easy and fun. I will definitely take another one of her classes.

she's like my favorite human being on this planet tbh. cares so much about her students and really makes sure you come away learning a lot!! lectures aren't great but i cannot exaggerate how amazing this woman is. and unless you literally do not show up to class you will easily get an A
Yuri cares a lot about her students and works hard to support them. The class overall isn't that much work, but the lectures can be boring at times. The final project was really fun!

She wants her students to succeed and she understands when people are sick/cannot make it to class/not do work and lets you make things up. Her classes are engaging since there is an in-class activity every class and everything is take home. The only thing that makes this class a bit harder is that there is an assignment due before every class.
My favorite professor ever, I love her so much. So thoughtful and caring, knows what she's doing and so accessible for questions! If you have the chance to take a class with her I highly recommend

Professor Kim is very good at what she does, and the class was easy to follow along with. As long as you put in the effort to do the homework and labs, you'll be just fine. She is very kind, and I really enjoyed getting to learn from her.

Dr Kim is the absolute best! I wish I'd known about her courses earlier in my time at IU. I loved her teaching, and she was always so kind and approachable. She really ignited my passion for mapping and GIS, and I'd recommend her courses to anyone who can take them.
Nice lady but she is hard to understand so I didn't learn much. Though, the content was easy and all exams are online so it's easy to get an A. Daily homework before class, but it's simple stuff.

I love ArcGIS because of Dr. Kim. She is very sweet, caring, and smart. She clearly knows what she is doing and is respected because of it. This is my last year at IU and I am glad I was able to take a class with Dr. Kim. Not many professors respect their students on a level that she does and I am grateful for it. Thank you, Dr. Kim!

Very kind teacher, does everything she can to help you and is passionate about mapping. She puts a lot of effort in and is definitely one of the more caring teachers at IU. I accidentally missed an assignment and she generously let me do it for full credit. She also rounded my grade. Overall, very good teacher.

I took Mapping our World with her and she's so sweet and super nice. Gave out all the class resources before the week started. Easy Grading. Not that much work, and gave easy weekly tests instead of a midterm and final etc. Very nice person.

I took physical systems of the environment with Yuri and it was one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. There are labs due once a week that the lab teacher will help you on and they're not too bad. The tests are SO easy. I finished the final exam in 8 minutes because all the tests are only multiple choice and she gives you the questions prior
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Do all of the extra credit opportunities and your grade WILL go up at the end of the semester. I did well because I did extra credit! Her lectures are so boring. Go through the slides after class to actually learn the content. Exams are like the practice exams- so do those and you'll be fine

Prof. Chooi does give up to 10% extra credit, as long as you show up to lecture and complete the extra credit exams. Her lectures are very difficult to follow, her slideshow is not clear at all. To get a good grade you will have to spend a lot of time outside of class learning the material. Show up for discussions, I learned a lot from the UTA's.

This class was unbearable to sit through. She reads everything directly off her slides making lectures (which are mandatory) impossible to pay attention to. No point in taking notes because the exams are nothing like what was learned in class. The extra credit for this class wasn't even worth it and average test scores were about 70% with a curve.

The only good thing about Professor Chooi is the amount of extra credit she gives to the students as along as you show up for lectures and do the extra credit exams. Professor Chooi's slideshows are not great and hard to understand. Everything I learned in this class was outside of class from a tutor and the UTA's that teach the discussion.

Dr. Chooi is a caring professor, she wants her students to do well. The lectures can be alot since there is tons of information to cover, I would recommend printing or downloading the slides to add notes since it goes quick through slides. She offers extra credit, just make sure you attend lectures. She also is really helpful during office hours.

Not a difficult class, study and it will probably be easier than any other offering. Yes, lectures aren't super engaging, but just do them on your own; she's great since she makes it easy (so much extra credit). If you are pre-med take this, if not, (wanting to go for a PhD) then maybe go take the honors version.

Dr. Chooi seems like a nice person but she is not an outstanding professor. She mostly reads off the slides and she goes so quickly there is no point in trying to take notes in lecture. However, this class is absolutely passable. There is so much extra credit that it will absolutely pad your grade. Attend discussion, you can learn the content.
Loved her as a professor super funny and you can get up to 10% of extra credit

Professor Chooi was an okay professor. Her lecture slides can be 100+ slides. She likes to put things that appear once on a picture slide on the tests. Her lecture videos are more concise. The extra credit is insane, but you have to have perfect lecture attendance to gain extra credit. It took my grade from an 85 to a 95.
Does not care. Puts in minimal amounts of effort, exams are all trick questions, and most of all class is designed for non-success.
her review slides won't help you. 3/4 of the exam is on random other things not on them. you have to know EVERYTHING.

Professor Chooi seems to be very intelligent but she is difficult to understand even though she barely has an accent. Her lectures are rants where she goes off topic and can be confusing. The exams are very difficult with MANY TYPOS. The lectures are pointless except for attendance because you can get 10% extra credit to the final grade.

I had to withdraw from the class, however, for the time I was in it, it was a very chaotic class. The lectures were mandatory but I never felt like I learned anything from them as the language she used he never fully explained, or went about it in a recursive, difficult-to-understand way. I urge you to take someone else if you have STEM classes.

Reads straight off the Power Point & doesn't explain or take questions. What's on the test sometimes not on power point. Doesn't respond to emails, instead, embarrasses you by making a public announcement about your message on canvas. Show up to class because even though attendance isn't mandatory, it's extra credit and you'll need it.

There's nothing horrendously bad about professor Chooi's teaching style, but none of the lectures that I attended were even relatively engaging. There's very little provided to study for exams and they constitute a huge chunk of the grade in this class making them incredibly stress inducing and difficult. Would not recommend.

Her lectures are awful which sucks because they are mandatory if you want extra credit. She uses 100 slide presentations that manage to have almost no useful content on them. She flips around a lot and hyper fixates on super specific things. Her exams are very poorly written with questions on hyper specific details. Extra credit is incredible tho

My grades are a result of not attending classes. Many extra credit opportunities, Chooi makes lectures fun with jokes. Plenty of notes to take on slides, lots of out of class opportunities for help. Sends out weekly updates before class starts, classes aren't easy but Chooi definitely makes them bearable. Attendance is mandatory, but worth it.

Professor Chooi fails to teach well. She puts up to 80 slides of information into one lecture and there is too much information to decipher what will actually be on the tests (which haven't been updated in at least 4 years). Proof: 35% of her students earn an A with while 70% of the students with the other 2 professors. Limited by character count..
She is super nice and likes to make lectures enjoyable with jokes. But, the course itself was very difficult. The exams were so hard and the lectures could get so tedious. I do not recommend it.

I thought that Chooi was a good professor, I think that the lectures for this class with her could be kinda boring so if that is something that bothers you don't take her. But overall her extra credit is so good and literally saved me in this class in the final exam so invest in that.

Prof Chooi is a pretty monotonous lecturer. Class can drag, although many lectures got out early. Show up to class, pay attention, do the extra credit tests, and you will be ok. When studying for tests, look over the extra credit test and quizzes because a lot of questions come back or are really similar on the actual test.

Chooi has a lot of opportunities to learn the material and get help outside of lecture. She also sends out what we'll be focusing for each week before the week starts, so you can start ahead. You just have to put time into the class and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are hard to hear if you are not in the front and the tests are very difficult.

At the beginning of the semester I tried to pay attention during lectures. By week two, I gave up. She put many of us to sleep by reading verbatim from hundreds of slides. I resorted to cramming for all of the tests and the final for a couple days per exam and did well (especially with extra credit). Overall, she seems very nice but is a droner.

Chooi is pleasant, but seriously unclear regarding all material, including the final exam. The study material will provide one answer, the notes have another, and the tests (well, good luck). The class is pretty difficult, especially for tactile learners like me.

I took this class as an Advertising major needing 1 more science credit and expecting this class to be on the easier side (it wasn't) as it is intended for non-bio majors. The style of "teaching" is reading directly from the 80+ slides yet making attendance mandatory. Test scores range from 30%-90% so it's different for everyone.

You have weekly lecture and disscussion quizzes that are based on the previous topics that you learned. Overall, the lectures can get pretty boring and to professor states the same thing word for word for each slide. In addition, if you get higher than 60% on the gen-ed quiz, you can get extra credit through extra credit exams that are worth 10%.

Weekly discussion quizzes, weekly online open internet lecture quizzes, four exams, and three extra credit exams. Overall the course isn't too difficult and the extra credit helps because they offer an extra 10% but it's a lot of notes and lecture is pretty boring. Slides are posted online but attendance is taken daily via tophat. Chooi is okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chooi simply does not lecture over the material well at all. She is prone to skipping over slides in a 80+ slide presentation throughout lecture, making it extremely hard to follow along with and understand. The class really requires you to teach yourself. Although having 10 points of EC (if you participate) is nice at the end of the class.
Exams and quizzes often incorporate material that was never taught or is very minuscule. Great professor, bad lecturer
Yean was a great teacher. She throws some humor and personal stories into her teaching that allows the students to engage with her during lecture.
Guided notes were difficult to follow and BPEs were much easier than the exams a lot of the time, however Yount is very knowledgeable in the subject and UTA sessions/office hours were helpful.

She is very knowledgable on what she is teaching and explains things well. Definitely need to put in a lot of time and effort when studying for exams and the BPEs tend to be easier than the actual exam. With a lot of effort it is definitely doable and I though it was an overall very interesting course and set up well.

I chose to write my own notes along with the lectures which helped a lot because the guided notes were a bit confusing. The tests require a LOT of studying and hard work and even then sometimes the tests still went rough. This class is tricky but doable, study study study! Dr. Yount really cares about her students!

I think I would rather walk barefoot through a blizzard than sit through another one of Amber Yount's lectures. The lecture is completely boring and the "guided notes" are awful. This class is the reason I changed my major....goodluck incoming pre-nursing students!!!

Professor Yount is extremely knowledgeable and approachable. while the lectures were packed with a lot of information and not always the easiest to understand, I found her office hours/review sessions to be very helpful. As long as you put the effort in, she's there for all her students and is very helpful!

She was so kind and really cared about her students. But, her lecture notes were not easy to follow along with. They would not always align with what she was showing on screen, and the wordings were more confusing than necessary. Her exams were harder than the practice tests in my opinion. TopHat was used everyday so attendance was necessary.

I liked that she had guided notes for her lectures but sometimes I would be too busy trying to fill out the guided notes instead of paying attention to the material. However, you can tell she likes what she teaches and is very helpful during her office hours. The lectures are also posted online which was great for studying for the exams.

The notes that she provides for lectures are super confusing and not really helpful. Although, she is really helpful outside of class. If you show up to office hours and reviews, she will spend as much time as possible with you until you understand the concept.

In physiology the teacher switch in about the middle of the semester. I started the semester feeling very confident about my physiological understanding until Yount took over. She complicated concepts extremely and goes on multiple tangents making her hard to follow during class. She rarely makes sure we understand the concepts and goes quickly.
Super great professor -- definitely recommend!

Youle is an excellent lecturer.  He is engaging and very intelligent.  He creates a comfortable space and encourages particiption.  He is not the most organized, but it rarely becomes an issue.  Would highly recommend
Great professor for G350.

Professor Youle is an incredible professor for G350. The content in this course is difficult and technical. However, Professor Youle kept the lectures very interesting, relevant, and clear. He is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is highly supportive of his students and wants to ensure that you understand the material. 10/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best stats teacher I have had. Finally understood the concepts. He is so enthusiastic so lecture is not boring, and sets all of his students up for success.

If you can take a class with Youle TAKE IT. He is genuinely an interested and funny professor who really cares about students. He is not a hard grader but that is just because he sets up the assignments for students to succeed. Highly recommend him for any class, not just G400.
Extremely smart and nice guy, explains complex topics very well, very available, has only open note exams, brings in really cool examples to make the content feel alive. He's the goat.

G492 with Youle was great. He teaches pretty quickly but it sure to slow down, spend more lectures on a topic and apply it to a research paper when people need more info. Try to take G350 and G492 with him, it will help decreasing the knowledge gap between semesters.
Highly recommend Professor. His lectures are interesting, easy to follow for an online class and brings in real world examples. Would take again.

I hate G492 as a class but Professor Youle is such a king!!! I loved having him, he is really good at breaking concepts down and makes students feel comfortable. I would definitely try to take it with him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This applies to G345. Great professor. He makes an otherwise lackluster course relevant by tying class materials to the real world. Exams ask broad and thoughtful questions about the economy. Super nice guy on top of that! For G345, Youle is the only option!!!!
A great professor who cares about his students. Hes more worried that his students understand the material than he is about anything else. He was a pleasure to have as a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Youle is a great professor! I was intimidated coming into the class because of my inexperience with stats, but Professor Youle made the class very manageable. If you put the effort in, you will be able to do extremely well in the course. Professor Youle has been one of the kindest professors I've had. I would recommend him to anyone! :)

Shixiong was a great teacher. He is soft spoken so it is hard to hear him at times but overall its not bad. He writes easy exams, just do all the homework and you should be prepared. Some material he goes over is irrelevant to exam material.

I have only had him for 3 weeks, but I am going to write this review anyways. This guy means what he says when he offers specific advice to study for tests. Listen to him, and you will get an A on your exam.

Physics with Prof. Zhang was completely painless. Just know how to do the in-lecture and prelecture problems and you'll be golden for the exams. His explanations are concise, consistent, and easy to follow. He is a really sweet guy and genuinely wants students to understand the material with as little stress/confusion as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Chill dude. Hard to understand at times because he is quiet. Nevertheless, he keeps his exams simple and similar to lecture problems as compared to other professors.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This is for Marketing Strategy (M450) not M304. She goes way too fast over things, horrendous lectures that were very boring and impossible to pay attention to, easily least favorite class of the semester. Absolutely hated Markstrat game and spent so long on group meetings for it.

Straightforward class, in class lectures are important to attend (mandatory attendance). Content and exams are straightforward. Friendly teacher. Study for exams as they are straightforward from class lectures but if you miss a question getting partial credit is hard. Chill class.

She's super nice and accessible outside of class. While the no partial credit can be a bit rough, the content is easily digestible and she clearly enjoys the subject matter. Lectures are super tolerable and occasionally even interesting
She was chill.

I have her for M450 and she is awesome! She is available outside of class and very willing to help. Sometimes the content can be boring but it is obvious that she is super enthusiastic about what she teaches and that makes the class way better.

I am currently in her M450 class, and she is Great! Even though her material covered in class could be boring, her class material is very straightforward. She offers a lot of extra credit so it is easy to get a good grade. Also, the Markstrat game that takes up a lot of the course is really fun!

These reviews are respectfully so drama, Professor Godfrey has been great all semester, although sometimes the material is boring, she tries to make it more interesting. She is so kind and very available to meet and chat. I like her as a person and a professor! I recommend

Despite what most of these reviews say, I think Professor Godfrey was a great professor. She clearly explained concepts, the exams were taken straight from the slides, there was plenty of extra credit, and she was more than available outside of class. You can tell she tried really hard to get along with students, always talking to us before class.

Made the class more challenging than it should be, in terms of grading material. She gave us a bad grade on the Homework without even stating what she was expecting, and she gives us no sort of preparation for the exams. The material in class she covered was so basic and she made our exam hard. Avoid her if you can, her class is just annoying.

People on here need to respectfully get a grip. The class was demanding in some respects but that was more than offset by the very generous extra credit. As someone who had a relatively poor understanding of the concepts and still did well in the class, it's hard for me to throw any shade Professor Godfrey's way - and I won't. She is solid.

Godfrey is enthusiastic & gives lots of extra credit, yet her lectures are confusing, ICEs are time-consuming, she gives vague answers, and the homeworks & exams are tough. She helps you prepare with before-class quizzes, but concepts are confusing when she is constantly making mistakes and correcting herself only days before the exams.
