reviews.comment: You cannot understand him and he moves fast. You can't understand what is going on and I don't think he does either. Good luck teaching yourself the whole semester on econ because you are not getting help

It's very difficult to understand what the professor is saying and he moves very fast in the lectures. The lectures are literally pointless and you have to teach yourself everything through the book. I hated this class. The only good part was he gave a good amount of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you want confusing, awful, and uninspired lectures that do not help on quizzes or tests, Marco is the perfect professor.

This professor, although a nice and thoughtful guy, is definitely my least favorite here at IU so far. Although this isn't his fault, he does have a tough to understand accent and talks quietly without using a microphone which makes it hard to hear. He does mandatory attendance polls at the beginning of class and uses the paid software Packback.

I loved AC! They were very caring, and it was clear to me that the course really mattered to them. They're a slow grader which can be frustrating, but they are also a very forgiving grader. If you attend class and try your best to participate, you will do well. I met with them a few times during office hours and they were incredibly helpful.

AC is a very kind and personable professor. The class itself was horrendous, as there was an extreme amount of busy work that almost always needed to be completed over the weekend. The content was confusing, but that is more of an issue with John Arthos and the course. AC is quite good, and I wish they could teach a course other than this one.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: AC is awesome. They are genuinely really kind and funny. You can tell they like teaching and care about their students. They're not always super clear about what they want from us on assignments, and they don't always give the best feedback. But I genuinely enjoyed interacting with them and would recommend them.

Honestly he's a great teacher and wants his students to pass. His lectures are boring but you don't really need to pay attention. He posts videos every week that are more in depth than the actual lectures, so you can go back. His tests are confusing but if you meet with him before he'll help a lot. If you study and meet with him the class is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Fine teacher just lecture heavy and test is essay format. So if u just study a lot and don't go to class ur fine or other way around final project is graded easy but is j annoying

Class is 60% exams which are made to trick you with 3/4 answers being partially right. Does all lectures on VERY boring videos and wastes time in class not revising those topics. Grades the essay and final project very hard while providing little help in preparation. Class is boring in general and he makes it worse by asking bad worded questions.

The exams in this class, while open note, were pointlessly tricky and confusing. Additionally, he is a bit of a boring lecturer, and it was hard to tell what he wanted on the two group projects and the final paper. Nice guy, grade turned out okay, but was a little more stressful than it had to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Three online exams worth 60% of your grade with only 15 multiple choice questions and an in class essay portion. Questions are extremely specific and very much up to your own interpretation. The group debate and essays are a pain.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor isn't the worst but he's not the best either. This professor made it so obvious that he was a Republican and trump supporter. There's nothing wrong with that, but he brings up Trump and politics at unnecessary times. He also gets distracted while teaching and writes a lot of pointless information on his slides. Solid 5/10

Professor Deslatte is a very nice guy. He makes lectures interesting because he is very passionate about this subject. This class is very test heavy but if you take notes from the lecture slides BEFORE you get to class and add extra stuff he talks about during lecture is VERY helpful for tests. Test can be challenging listen and do the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have mixed feelings about this course. While Deslatte is very obviously committed to his students success, my classmates and I often felt a bit tricked by his exams. He really is a nice guy, but he isnt always very receptive to student feedback. Be ready for lots of reading material or you wont do well here.

Tests are really hard, but the study sessions help. He really knows his stuff, but sometimes gets caught up in talking and gets off topic during lectures. The Canvas page is super well-organized and helpful, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Get ready for hard exams, which is the only neg thing about him. He's one of the most caring profs i had. He would make Kahoots for exam reviews and you can tell he's really passionate about teaching. He's just overall really cool and nice. The class shouldn't be terribly hard if you take the time to watch lectures and ask questions. Great guy!
He is the worst ever. I would like to give him 0 if there was an indicator. He is smart but he has no talent at all in teaching students.

Prof. Deslatte is a nice guy but his lectures are dry and extremely boring. He does not manage time well and ends up rushing through certain parts of the lecture. There are only 3 exams- which make up 25% of your grade each. NO curves (even if the class average is a 59%). EXTREMELY difficult tests, no study tips and IMPOSSIBLE to prepare for.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty nice guy but he has a lot of assignments. Super easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There is definitely a good amount of homework, but nothing is difficult. All of the information is given in the lectures so show up. But overall the professor is very knowledgeable and passionate so it was a pretty enjoyable gen-ed if you like music (mainly Classical music btw, don't expect modern music).

Super easy class, all quizzes online. As long as you do the work, its an easy A. Attendance is mandatory but you are able to drop 3. Provides opportunities for extra credit as well if needed. Classes can drag on, but overall easy class. Professor Riedford is very passionate about what he is teaching and you can tell he cares a lot.

Aaron is an excellent, engaging instructor. He provides lots of feedback to his students and has high expectations. Not only that, his content is great. The guy is definitely knowledgable but never puts down students. Nothing but respect.

Took INTLI343 w/ Ponce -- if you're interested at all in migration & global studies, TAKE THIS COURSE! He is passionate about the material and lectures are always engaging. Doesn't just teach out of a book; includes youtube videos, group activities, etc. Course notes 1x week but isn't too bad; aslong as you get the theme(s) of the text.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class: Origins and Evolution of Int'l Law: Was basically taught out of the 3 required books. He is okay at explaining material but we weren't really taught anything, all the information we received was just what we read in the books. Would not recommend if you aren't interested in the history and colonialism aspect of int'l law. Books provided free
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His classes are interesting and he is a very good lecturer. He is open to talk to students and re-explain expectations. He does have a strict-ish attendance policy and is a tougher grader. Do not take his class unless you are willing to dedicate some time to it.

While Prof. Day is def monotone and a little cynical, he's incredibly smart (kind of to the level where it can be hard to understand) and funny. If you ask, he's incredibly willing to help you. He can be unclear about assignments, or at least gives you very little rules, BUT he's not a harsh grader at all. If he ever messes up, he makes it right.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's safe it say that Dr. Ron Day is the worst and laziest prof. I have ever had. He can't teach his way out of a wet paper bag and it's obvious he doesn't want to be there. It's astounding this man received tenure. I feel I am wasting my time and money. His performance in class is an embrasment to academics everywhere. Run for the hills if you can

I had undergraduate English with Professor Day in 1991 at USF. He was the hardest working, most available professor I ever had the pleasure of studying with. He  was always willing to match my energy and enthusiasm for the subject. Decades later, the impression he left still influences my work as an attorney, and my ongoing love of literature.

Prof Day is brilliant. If you are less than brilliant, you will not enjoy his class or teaching style. Yes, he's pretty cynical. Yes, this is a core/required class. BUT you're in graduate school. Take some responsibility for your own education. Do the reading and participate in class and you'll benefit from his incredible depth of knowledge.

People who complain about Professor Day probably came to grad school expecting to be hand-held and spoon-fed an education.  Participate in class and visit him during office hours, and you'll find that he cares a great deal about students and has a lot of good advice.

As others have noted, Professor Day is brilliant and his strength is research. He teaches Graduate courses, so they should be intellectually challenging. For me he made a fundamental course interesting. To label him a malcontent is ridiculous. He just gives the students a realistic, not idealistic view of the librarian profession.
Day was brilliant and insightful.  If you just want to learn rules, don't take him, but if you want to learn how to be a good librarian and what that means, he is the best there is.
This man is a malcontent.
Professor Day is articulate and understands his subject matter. He is a very good teacher.

Awful. Just awful. A waste of time and money. He doesn't care at all about teaching. He whines about EVERYTHING. He is cynical about the profession of librarianship and only gets excited about philosophy.

Ron would be better as a small class instructor. He does better with one-on-one discussion and small groups of 5 or 6. A large class like 524 is not his forte. He is one of those professors that is too intelligent for much conversation below his level, so I would suspect that a higher level or PhD class would be better.

Take this class with someone else if you want to learn something!  Instead of covering the topic, Day keeps talking about his experience at Wayne State, his former director and other things that don't pertain to the course.  A waste of money!
Prof. Day does not feel comfortable teaching this course.
Super smart professor, extremely knowledgeable in what he teaches. The class was not difficult as long as you showed up, however he did not grade most assignments until the end of the term.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Falsely promised extra credit, it was only applied to certain students and screwed over a few students grades due to this. Also lectures for a very long time. Not very engaging. He is knowledgeable about the stuff he teaches though I guess.

Really good class that I would recommend taking. Professor Sela is very knowlegable about his areas of expertise, and he is a very engaging lecturer. Most of the grade came from group presentations and papers. My only complaint is that sometimes he wouldn't give full points on homework without explaining why or including any feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The exams are take-home essays. 4 quizzes. Attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class, if you try you'll pass. Take his Heroes of Islam class- it really is his specialty. He has a cool life story and knows so much. If you're an Intl major, or studying Arabic, this class is 100% for you!
He's a genius. Speaks 16 languages. Sometimes hard to follow in lecture because he's a genius but his office hours are great. A must-take.

Grades based off of participation but does not give you a chance to participate. Lectures are horrible and long. The final project is a group presentation and he grades hard. The class was out of 100 points only, not leaving any room to mess up. I do not recommend taking this class with him.

While he is obviously knowledgable, he cannot teach. He solely lectures to the class, and does not create an environment conducive for discussion. Also, be prepared to be constantly insulted. Class was very easy, though, to a fault.

For an introductory class, he does a remarkable job of sucking any interest out of students. He asks for participation but doesn't allow for it, he just lectures the entire class. He clearly knows the material - and thoroughly, but he does not deliver it in an engaging, accessible manner, which makes lectures very had to sit through.

Absolutely necessary to take a class with Sela while at IU. He offers a wealth of knowledge which is very accessible to serious students. If you're an undergrad, be ready to be challenged and to think outside of your comfort level, but be confident you will walk out of his class, a very much more enlightened and grounded individual.

He obviously loves the topic, however, he is not extremely good at teaching it.  He often gets off topic and can stay off topic for the entire class.  Expect to do much of the learning outside class on your own.

Rough for the uninitiated, but great for serious graduate students and academic undergrads.  If Central Asia is at all interesting [Turkestan, Samarkand, Bukhara, etc.] this class is totally necessary.
No Comments

Good professor, but I wouldn't recommend taking C103 unless you have to. Very difficult content that's hard to understand if you don't have an interest in philosophy. Lectures are also hard to follow sometimes. However, both him and the TAs are not harsh graders and want to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Stalnaker was very knowledgeable about his material, but the material itself was difficult to understand in this class. Lots of reading and participation in discussions about those readings is very important. He himself was very relaxed and compassionate, and lectures were long but interesting.

This class was much harder than I anticipated it to be. It was a lot of difficult reading and the papers were tough. If you are genuinely interested in old philosophy and religion, you may enjoy this; otherwise, it's not enjoyable. The professor is nice and cracks jokes, but its quite difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: He is an amazing professor who really cares about his students and material. The reading was hard at times but manageable. Go to lectures to understand the material and to do Top Hats for class credit. The final exam was pretty easy because you can write the essay before hand, bring notes and books.

I didn't really love C103 but he was very helpful and I learned a lot from the class. Very interesting lectures, though sometimes a bit confusing for an intro class in my opinion. LOTS of required reading so be aware of that. The TAs for this class were great too. If I had to take another philosophy class, I would do it with Prof Stalnaker.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: Lectures were interesting to an extent, I found myself falling asleep a lot in this class which doesn't really happen to me. If you like learning about philosophy you'll enjoy the class, but you have to be invested. I was not, and so I got my lowest grade at IU thus far. You have to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great lecturer! Was really engaging and made me want to learn more about a subject that I considered boring. There is a lot of reading outside of class but the lectures make it easier to understand the texts. Discussions were for the most part a waste of time but were mandatory. Interesting class.

Very nice professor. While the lectures can be tough to understand if you didn't do the readings (like me), you can still brush up on the readings when writing your essays. Very interesting class if you're into religion or philosophy. I found it easy.

He is an incredibly nice and passionate man. Lectures can sometimes feel unrelated to class readings (which the whole thing is structured around), but for the most part they help you understand the readings (which can be tough at times). Discussion section helps for understanding too. All in all, getting an A is doable if effort is there.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Stalnaker is an incredible teacher. He knows his stuff and it's clear that he is dedicated to what he teaches. Readings are tough sometimes but his lectures make everything so clear. I'm a stem major, but I respect this man so much that I have done every reading and even taken notes on a lecture he recorded on a day he canceled class.

The class consisted of reading lots of philosophers, east and west. The lectures were amazing, as Stalnaker is engaging and makes you want to learn more about a subject I personally don't find that interesting. He definitely wants you to learn. The discussion sections were okay, but at times would be boring (depending on AI).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I don't like philosophy but the lectures are so engaging and insightful and he makes it so easy to understand that I'm actually interested and enjoy learning. Also there's a LOT of reading but it definitely won't be the worst you'll get. (honestly, if you skim he'll cover a lot of the info really well anyways)

Lectures are amazing, so insightful!! There is A LOT of reading and it can be a bit difficult to understand, but the lectures do a good job of clearing things up! This course really makes you think about life and how some philosophers suggest we "perfect" it.

An absolute gem of a professor! He quizzes every lecture- this is how attendance is counted. We only had to write 3 papers for the whole course. NO EXAMS. He is more than willing to meet outside class if clarification is needed. He is supremely passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches to a point where it is inspiring. STRONGLY RECOMMEND.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He tries to make lectures amusing and often goes over the readings in detail. You don't necessarily have to read if you show up and take notes at all of the lectures and are good at faking it on papers. I highly suggest him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Stalnaker is an awesome guy, but his lectures are very long and cover a lot of material. The topics covered in class are interesting but require intense readings twice a week. Nice guy but easy to get bored or lost in class if you aren't actively participating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Some boring lectures but overall intriguing!! He's really funny in class and tries to interact w students a lot. Lots of reading, and papers instead of tests. They take some time but really aren't too bad. The reading can be hard but make sure you know what it's about because there are tophat questions over them every class. Very easy to talk to!!

Aaron is a gem of a teacher. He can be awkward at times, but you know that he truly cares about his students. Do not worry about your TopHat grade, typically he curves at the end of the semester. Be ready to write for this class. There are 2 papers during the semester and one final paper. But, he is clear with what he is looking for in the paper.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Stalnaker is a solid choice, I took religion and ethics and it was decently difficult. Just pay attention and go to the lectures. As far as the discussions, theyre only interesting when were debating. Liked him a lot hes a great guy. Worst part were the readings you have to do before class, some are kind of long and extremely boring.

For C103 he only teaches the lectures, but his lectures were really interesting, and he is really passionate. Great class as an overview of philosophy, and it did cover eastern and western thinkers. There were three 120word papers, and for the final we were allowed to type up the paper beforehand and copy it in the booklet during the test.

He gives you a ton of reading then expects you to understand and answer discussion questions. Attendance and discussion questions are marked every class period, but in the end, they don't count for much
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Stalnaker is one of the best teachers I've had. He genuinely loves hearing from & interacting with his students and although his lectures can be boring, his passion about the material makes up for it. He's super approachable & helpful when you have trouble understanding material. Such a nice guy & I look forward to more classes with him.

Professor Stalnaker's lecture style feels as if he's just reading the class the Wikipedia page. The class was pointless, and the only plus side to this class was the moments in which Professor Stalnaker (awkwardly) tried to roast students. It was neither interesting, nor informative. I would never recommend a class with Professor Stalnaker.

Lecture is beyond boring and repetitive. Professor Stalnaker can be very awkward at times and reads off of a script the whole time. I was very excited about this course but I did not learn much. Not a great variety of discussion sections either.
Easy A, but I did not know that during the semester and caused lots of stress.  The papers are extremely ambiguous and confusing.  Lectures were quite boring. Lots of outside reading.

Professor Stalnaker is such a nice guy-- definitely a little awkward at times, and his lectures do tend to get wordy, but overall R170 is a great class! He relies on his AI's to do the grading but if you find a problem with the grade, go to his office hours and he'll change it.
He's great. Always has a smile on his face and you can tell he really enjoys what he teaches. Always patiently answers questions, even in a large lecture. I could listen to him talk all day!

Amazing professor! Such a nice guy and so enthusiastic about what he's teaching. If you get a chance schedule a time to meet with him and just talk. He loves getting to know his students and will sometimes even offer extra credit just to chat. The class requires a lot of reading and there are pop quizzes but it's not that bad. Papers are tough.

Stalnaker  assigns articles to read before each class and they've ranged from a couple pages to 20+. He occasionally gives pop quizzes on the reading material too. This wouldn't be so bad except that it's one of the few forms of grading you get here-- tedious essays and random pop quizzes, plus a small bit of extra credit. Good luck getting an A.
Great Professor! Made himself very available to anyone who felt they needed help. I really enjoyed his class. Made very debatable topics interesting. I would highly recommend taking his class.

Prof. Stalnaker is the best professor I have had so far at IU. He makes the material so interesting and genuinely wants his students to understand it. His class is the only large lecture class where I have felt comfortable raising my hand to ask a question. I actually learned stuff in this class and your grade will reflect that.

One of my favorite professors I've had at IU. He makes the material and class interesting and engaging, and is clearly very interested in making sure all students do well. Also makes the tests very easy to do well on, while still ensuring students learn a lot. Would highly recommend this class & professor.
Great teacher, clearly interested in subject and students.
He was great and made the class very interesting!
One of my favorite professors so far! He makes his lectures interesting and is a down to earth and knowledgeable guy.  His classes will make you think and improve your writing.
Great Professor and very interested in his subject. The books he assigned really changed the way I see the world around me. He presents the material the way it was meant to be presented.

Great professor, very intelligent and pretty engaging, really helps clarify the difficult philosophy/religion readings in class. Relaxed and friendly with students, he facilitated discussion well even in a big lecture. I would definitely recommend him.
Great guy teaching an efficient class.
Too much reliance on group speculation about topic.  He is a boring professor.  Reads from a print out the whole time.
No Comments
Excellent
Really nice guy, interesting class.  Keeps the atmosphere relaxed and informal.

I initially expected a difficult grade, but the class was manageable, and I didn't need to study much. Having taken BC Calc previously gave me a strong head start, but the material is very very doable if you focus on understanding it conceptually. The professor's style works well if you stay on top of the core concepts.
Goodluck! You'll never want to go to this class

This class is by far the best math class I have ever taken. Calculus I is generally a hard class but with the overall class structure and lecture style, this class was pretty chill.

Overall there are 3 exams and 1 final. The practice exams are basically the exams. Go to class and do the homework and you will be fine

Take Calc I with Dr. Agarwal!!

I took Linear Algebra with Sanjana this past semester (MATH-M 301). She was an INCREDIBLE teacher, definitely one of my favorites so far. She truly cares about her students, and gives very clear lectures. I would love to take another math course with her!

If you have to take calc, take it with Sanjana. She's your best option out of the professors. She gives practice tests that are usually similar to the exams. The HW is way harder than the exams. She LOVES students who put in effort and she truly wants to help you learn. Go to office hours + MLC. Study book questions and use My Organic Chem on YT.
Best professor for calc1

Trust me, if you have to take calcules and if Ms. Sanjana have seats on her course, don't think and just enroll it. She is very good at teaching and she cares her student a lot, she really wanna everyone get a good grade. I'm going to take Calcules 2, it's too bad she won't teach that.

I had Prof. Agarwal for Calc 1, and it was great. While the material is very difficult, that is just how Calc 1 is regardless of the professor. She prepares you very well for the test-heavy grading (about 70% comes from 3 tests + and a final). Be sure to actually go to class and office hours, they are the best way to learn and review the material!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is easy when you use online resources

cares about students, very approachable, understanding, and kind
If you do the homework and come prepared (usually 1 question for in-class work check) you'll be fine. Explains concepts, good at gauging if class understands. Homework is usually 3 sections, around 25-30 problems a week but v quick. Practice exams are the exams. Best math prof here.

The class itself is really hard, and many times people don't know how to do things, but if you ask questions and try to understand she is a really good teacher. The tests are pretty hard, but she is fairly good at preparing you for them. Hard class, pretty good teacher.
Gives very good lectures that prepare you well for the test. The tests were not very difficult and the lectures were engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Lots of homework and everything in class is graded by AI. Most students do not know what they are learning during class. Never take this class.

Prof. Agarwal was super nice and understanding one on one, but at times she seemed just as confused as the students. Her lectures were super disorganized and it seemed like she just went up there and rambled about the concepts without very much insight.

Very sweet and caring professor, just hard to follow. Her teaching style is very confusing. Spent way too much time in class over explaining concepts and left little time for actual homework problems.

While sometimes her teaching strategies confuse me, if you understand how to do problems on the homework and understand her practice exams, you will be fine.  She is a very caring professor who wants her students to succeed. Go to class even if it's not mandatory. I spend my class time working on the homework assignment for that section.

Although she is a very caring professor, I found it very difficult to learn. Her teaching is a bit messy and would make me confuse simple concepts. She does care a lot about her students, but again her teaching style is frustrating. Attendance is not mandatory at all.

If you're taking 211, take Sanjana. She is the best calc professor who goes through examples in class, walks around to make sure everyone understands, listens to students' feedback, and gives great practice exams. Sanjana does not just teach, she makes sure you understand the materials and always reminds students to talk to her during office hour.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class/lectures were completely useless. Bad at teaching

Professor Argarwal is so sweet and caring. Before almost every class she would ask us fun questions like our favorite flowers or food to keep us engaged. She did give a lot of questions when it came to homework, but I learned it was only to help us. Go to the Math Learning Center often to do your homework and this class shouldn't be anything crazy.

The only issue I had with her was she would go very slow through the first part of class and give us an example to do on our own and walk around for a long time. Then she would try an get through half of the lesson at the end of class. She does have the students best intention in mind, and she wanted everyone to do well.

Professor Agarwal was very timely inefficient when it came to the lectures. She would waste time asking silly questions like what my favorite ice cream flavor was. She would save the hardest, and most seen on the test, information until the last 5 minutes of class. The only reason I had an A was because of prior calculus knowledge.

I attended all of her lectures before Exam 1 until I realized how poorly her time management during lectures was. Since I had already taken Calc in high school everything was review and easy for me so I skipped these lectures. Overall she is very nice but I found her lectures to be way too slow and frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Almost all calc professors here are really bad and she isn't an amazing professor, but she is definitely better than most. She cares about her students and her lectures are helpful and all of the exams are multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think that Pedram expresses an interest in the subject and does his best to communicate with students. I liked how he explained all the material from the week and included people in class discussion. I also really appreciate how he made the class entertaining and was understanding with makeup work.

I really like the way Pedram taught, he was readily available for any questions or concerns students had. It was very easy to understand and follow along especially for a language course. He was also very enthusiastic about the course material and genuinely seemed like he loved teaching.

This was my second semester with Pedram. He's very lenient, funny, understanding, and nice. It was really fun and the class was well structured. There were plenty of ideas to get us using the language everyday, and there was always something new to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Although he is a grad student he was a very inconsiderate and rude professor. I and all my classmates dreaded class and continually asked for help and got yelled at because we didn't understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The BEST professor ever. Offers you the choice of either 5 papers or two exams (I chose exams and got an A). He has clear grading criteria and is very accessible in and outside of class. The final was also a presentation/paper that wasn't bad to write and was actually interesting if you find the class interesting (which he does a good job at).

Professor Agley was a very caring and kind professor. You have the option of taking 2 exams or writing 5 short papers. I chose exams, and they werent too bad (he gave a study guide), and he curves them. I recommend taking this class with him because its only 8 weeks and he made it super interesting! He also never keeps us the entire class time.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor made lecture interesting with video and guest speakers. Gives you the option to write papers or take 2 exams. Very fair grader
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: no textbook, just few short readings. no tests, 7 written papers based on readings and lecture (500-1000 words). final project that you can choose between writing a long paper or doing a presentation. I got "?" as feedback from AI, I talked to him and he improved my grade. good prof and and writing assignment is mostly your opinion.

I had Jon for Drug Use in American Society. The class was great, and was an easy A. He tells you on the first day of class that you dont need the text book, and there are no tests in the class. The grade is based on 7 easily graded papers and attendance. Jon is a really cool guy, and i loved having his class. One of my favorite teachers at IU.
Awesome teacher who makes learning fun and easy for people even for people who don't enjoy class. He's always willing to help.

He's incredibly laid back.  The class is supposed to be like 3 hours, but he never keeps us that long.  The most important thing is there are NO TESTS!!  He teaches through assignments and not tests.  Great class and great teacher.
No Comments

Definitely the most memorable class I have taken at IU! Nic is very friendly and seemed to actually care about his students. There was no textbook which is a plus. I thought it was cool how you can do anything for the projects. It was useful to build my portfolio in one of the assignments. Stickler for tardiness but other than that he's chill

Nic was great for web and mobile design. He has tons of experience in the field, so you'll learn a lot, especially if you ask questions. He has a grade for attendance but he lets you make it up at office hours so emergency absences are a-okay. You really have to go to lecture to know what's going on, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I took interactive data viz. He teaches class with easy to follow along data viz tutorials and for the projects provides videos of tutorials to follow along. Fairly easy as long as you do your work. Not sure if I can reproduce the projects on my own though.
This was a speech class. I hate presenting, but Charlotte Agger is such a sweet person. She is so nice. I loved having this class with her and would do it again.

Professor Agger is soooooooo nice! She is your go-to C104 teacher for sure. I enjoyed every conversation with her and she is genuinely caring. She understands that public speaking can be difficult and if she sees your improvement, she will give you better and better grades. Definitely one of my favourite teachers!

My favorite professor so far at IU. Like a lot of people in the class, I didnt like public speaking at all, but Im much better off and its because of Prof Agger. Not afraid to tell you what to improve on, but she really cares whether or not you get better. Nicest lady in the world, always loved coming to class, would recommend her to anyone.

Charlotte was an awesome professor. She was not a hard grader and gave really good feedback telling you exactly what she wanted. She didn't really care about the content of the speeches the grades were more on the gestures. I would definitely recommend taking C104 with her it wasn't very hard and she made the class enjoyable.

Professor Agger was great. I learned so much in this class and she always provided great feedback. She made the classroom environment comfortable and gave encouragement throughout each speech. Definitely take it with her if you can!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Agger was awesome. I enjoyed just talking to her during class because she is funny and interesting. The class was easy because there are a lot of easy assignments. She can be a difficult grader, but if you follow her instructions as a speaker, you will be successful. Overall, I loved the class and Professor Agger.

She is the most approachable professor I have ever met. Very helpful with clear comments, her classrooms have a very chill atmosphere and her teaching style makes it work. Classes tend to be more open to discussion, Considering that speeches generally make most people piss-scared, Charlotte's teaching style can aid ease you into public speaking.
I'm a second semester freshmen, and she is my favorite professor so far.

Best teacher in IU for me so far. She's incredibly kind and approachable, and she's very supportive. She makes classes very fun and enjoyable. In terms of her class, she is very clear in what she expects for each assignment. C104 is not an easy class, but if you follow her grading rubric and format, you will surely get an A for her class.
Excellent Teacher. I learned a lot from her class. Super nice and genuine teacher. One of my favorite classes I have taken so far at IU.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Agger is probably one of my favorite professors that I have encountered at IU so far. She is a real and genuine person. She really cares about your improvements in your performance in the class, and as long as you keep doing well you will pass the class. Her lectures are interesting and keep the class engaged. Highly recommend!

I really like Professor Agger! I've always been bad with public speaking, but she helps a lot. If you try in her class, it will show and she will give you the grade you deserve. She's also very friendly and easy to get along with.
Super friendly... flexible... clear grading rubric... engaging atmosphere... highly recommend!

Professor agley is extremely well versed in public health and cares a lot about what he does. The lectures, however, seem to go on forever and he often goes on 30 minute long tangents about nothing in particular. You will get an A if you go to class every meeting. Attendance is a huge grade
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Agley has the most experience in the field he teaches and is truly passionate about public health. My main problem with this class was that his lectures and what is in the textbook/what you're tested on are very different. For this reason and the fact that the tests were relatively hard, I did not do as well in this class as I would have liked.

Dr. Agley is a pretty cool guy. He does know a lot about public health and seems to boast about it sometimes, but overall he's easy. The exams are a bit challenging but he throws you so much extra credit and even curves the exams. Show up to class and make sure you look like you're paying attention or he'll call you out in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: he knows an unbelievable amount about public health, sometimes lectures were a little boring though. tests are challenging compared to the rest of the course being easy.

Dr. Agley is hands down the best professor I have ever had. He is incredibly passionate and smart. His tests are difficult, but the curves he puts on his exams are very steep. I have taken multiple classes with him and have loved it every time. If you are passionate about public health, you really need to take one of his classes.

okay I will agree that tests are often harder and sometimes unrelated to lecture, but I made it out with an A and barely studied for any of them. The people in the previous comments just didn't understand common sense concepts in the health field. He is the cutest little old man and I think worth defending. this class is not by any means impossible

He often goes on tangents completely unrelated to lectures (which often aren't related to tests anyway). Attendance was mandatory but as long as you sign the sheet he doesn't care if you leave in the middle of the lecture. I didn't buy the textbook because it was expensive and it wasn't related to my major so I only ever reviewed the study guides.

He makes it clear that the majority of the stuff on the test is in the book. However, the book is an easy and interesting read. His lectures are very insightful and inspiring. If you don't care about public health, don't take this class.
Not the level of an intro class. Not very convincing to enter public health field. Exams have little to do with lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Let's just say I regret the decision I made to take his class every single class I attend. Lectures are boring and dry but attendance is taken, his tests have absolutely nothing to do with lectures, but again, attendance is taken. Everything he talks about has nothing to do with anything, UGH.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: took this class because it was required and i needed an easy A. if you're looking for an easy A, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. tests are impossible and i only got C's on them because there were huge curves on them. lectures have nothing to do with tests but attendance is taken so you have to go. take this class with another professor

Dr. Rawleigh is an amazing professor and a great choice for W131. She is very kind and sets clear expectations for her students. Workload is very reasonable for an 100 level class. Reading HW before every class. You only have 3 absences so use them wisely. 3 essays, 1 revision, no quizzes/tests. Show up, participate, do the work and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed her class a lot! She's super kind and understanding, especially if this is one of your first classes coming into college. She makes her expectations very clear. You've gotta write 3 essays, then for the final project you revise one of them. Just show up, participate, turn in your assignments and you'll be completely fine!

Professor Rawleigh was by far my favorite professor. She is very understanding. I thought the class was overall pretty easy. You half to write three essays but honestly if you put the work in you will be fine. My biggest advice is do not fall behind in class as she is very strict on late work and attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is so nice and so willing to work with students. Take his class.
I took Folklore 101. This professor was so kind. He is my favorite professor. He really cares about the wellbeing of his student. Awh I'm gonna miss him
he is so cute i just want to hug him, he's so kind.
Such an awesome and kind professor made my first semester at IU so much better! If I could have him every semester ever, I would take it in a heartbeat, I don't say goodbye to him :(

Twalha is and will always be my favorite professor. He made everything so fun and interactive! If you have any interest in learning a foreign language, I recommend this class with everything in me. I have never enjoyed a class more. As long as you show up and participate, you are guaranteed to succeed. He is always ready to help! Best class EVER!

2nd Semester of Swahili with Twalha. This guy is still the GOAT in case anybody was wondering. I would just stress participation. Twalha is very easygoing and you will do great in his class if you just put forward a little effort. Assignments are very manageable and you never feel overwhelmed. Again, I'd highly recommend taking a class with Twalha.

Professor Abbass is the GOAT. He's chill and cares about the course. He doesn't give a lot of work or tests, and when he does, they are super manageable. His classes are usually smaller, so it's more interactive. You'll be completely fine in his class if you just try.  I would definitely recommend taking a class with the legend Twalha Abbass.
Was a good class
Lectures were heavy and at times sad about global climate change
Great class.
Was a great class
He is funny and a great teacher.

Don't need to pay attention in class, but make sure to attend as it's a large portion of grade. No extra credit offered but also not really needed since we had take-home quizzes. Participation is graded in the Friday discussions so make sure to raise your hand every so often. Very few assignments and the group final project is super easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: A really eye-opening class if you are interested in climate change and stuff.

Abdul was a great teacher, funny and thoughtful. Some thought he was strict about attendance. I don't agree. He shared early on that students could skip 6 classes with no effects on their grades. That is like 25% of the total attendance. Lectures at time went long and occasionally boring though with lots of theoretical content.
I liked this class.

Nice guy and passionate about topic; strict on attendance; readings are very long and boring; open note quizzes but you need to know the content because questions can be analytical; final exam was 7 page hand written final (3 questions 2-2.5 pages per question); you need to participate in discussions; doesn't feel like a GenEd/easy class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Abdul was a funny guy, makes dad jokes very often which is nice to see now days in professors. Biggest issue was that the lectures were not needed, just went over the basic summaries of the lessons. Exams are easy if you pay attention at all. He is not the best at communication for exams or announcements though. Pretty easy overall.

Lectures are boring and just talks about summaries of stuff we read, super long readings, the participation, TH attendance and, roll call attendance are 3 different things which effects grades. Doesn't work and communicate to do work that could help improve a grade.

I liked this class a lot as it discussed global climate crisis and how it impacted not just human health but of other living beings. The lectures were good but on the longer side. Some with more visual content were more interesting. The professor was really kind and very approachable, very quick in responding to  emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a funny guy, but lectures are ass and too long. You don't have to do any of the readings just kinda listen in class.

reviews.comment: never grades anything in a reasonable time. She is always late. Always go on tangents. Doesnt answer email.

Always late to class and constantly talked about her personal life in class. Alongside this, I received all of my grades for this course in December, and when I went to look at my scores/rubrics, she had already deleted the Canvas page…
The class was ok

Abramson is a very knowledgeable Humean scholar. Alot of your learning is dependent on your independent reading of the materials. Lectures follow concepts that are scattered throughout the philosophers she coversHer classes would not be for someone who needs hand-holding, as she is pretty unavailable outside of the classroom hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Abramson is very knowledgeable about her subject, and her lectures reflect that. They are both interesting and helpful for understanding the readings. However, Professor Abramson is also horribly disorganized and nearly inaccessible outside class. Take her class if you are interested in the subject, but other professors are better.

Horrible at her job. She constantly complains about how overworked she is, which is very unprofessional. The lectures are boring and are rarely connected to readings. The homework/readings are never clear and I have often read the wrong thing because she decided to change the schedule without an update.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Abarmson is a gem. She is so sweet and helpful, currently in her class and enjoying it. Of course, going to class isn't required but it is very helpful, considering its ethical discussion. Highly suggest taking her courses.

Kate Abramson is an amazing person! But a not-so-great professor. There were only 3 papers throughout the entire semester, so there wasn't a lot of WORK to do, but she does assign unrealistic readings. So just be ready to read a lot if that's what you're interested in! 
She also hardly ever responds to emails, so try to talk to her in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Abramson's class is fairly disorganized and she tends to go on a lot of tangents, though she is an understanding professor and a sweet woman. She's helped me when I need her, though I don't think I'll be taking another one of her courses.

Graded from 3 assigned essays, supposed to be given back with comments 7 days after turning in. First essay: given back month and a half late Second essay: given back month and a half late with 3 days left in semester Third essay: never given back, said she graded all of them, asked her for my copy, never received it. Does not respond to email

This is the worst professor I've had at IU. I will no longer be taking any philosophy classes because of her. Her lectures have no structure. I left every lecture wondering what I was supposed to learn that day. Her revision policy also doesn't work if she doesn't give them back to you until two days before they're due. DO NOT TAKE! GPA RUINER!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is an easy A class, it's essentially participation as long as you show up and do the papers. If you're taking this class out of interest, the only person she really covers is Hume. Sometimes she would spend the first half of class talking about things completely unrelated to the syllabus, albeit passionately, but it felt unhinged at times
Kate is the best professor I have ever had, one of the most intelligent people I have ever been around. She's changed my life and how I see the world.

Terrible teacher. No powerpoint or notes. Barely anything ever written on the board. No organization and terrible flow during lectures makes it very hard to pay attention. She just rambles on and sometimes takes very long and unnatural pauses. Says a lot of words without really saying anything. Would not recommend. She does know the material though
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Has no idea what she's doing.  Always late to class, and probably the worst lecturer I've ever had.

Definitely smart and knows the material very well, but doesn't excel at teaching it. Lecture moved so slow that it was hard to hold concentration long enough to understand the concepts. I once counted a 28 second pause in the middle of a sentence. Student discussion of the material does not happen.

Clear lecturer.  Professor Abramson's grading style is one of my favorites, where for each paper, there is a due date for a rough draft, but for the rest of the course, you can revise it and meet with her to keep improving it.  She gives you a grade each time and really helps to improve your writing and also gives good opportunity for an A.

I absolutely hated this class. Took it during the summer for the IW credit, Professor Abramson was always late, never returned papers on time, and taught as if we were all philosophy majors when the majority of us had never taken a philosophy class in our lives (there are no prerequisites but there really should be).

The best thing about this class was that the papers could be revised as many times as needed to get a better grade. Her presentation of the material was very unorganized and she wrote very little on the board. She was very forgiving when grading papers though.

She was always late, didn't keep appointments or return emails, didn't return papers and tests. I had no idea what grade I had going into the final.  Her lectures were very difficult to follow, and she raced through them.

She canceled class a lot. And she never returned our papers on time. We were always behind and had to skip several readings. All of the readings were posted online and if you wanted an actual book you'd have to spend hours searching for the right one online. She doesn't respond to E-Mail. She knew the information really well, but she cannot teach!
shes usually late, likes to pace, very flighty, laughs a lot, and tends to cancel a lot of classes

Jared is a solid lecturer. While the homework and exams are very difficult, I think people need to realize that it is not Jared's fault that required us to use Gradescope and Edfinity. Blame the math department, not Jared. He explains concepts in Calculus relatively well and help break a concept down to digest it better.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Able's a pretty good calc prof and he gives really good methods for grasping different topics, and he gives practice tests very similar to the real deal, and each test is also curved. He always posts his completed notes after every lecture too. Tests can be hard, especially the later ones, but as long as you start off strong, you'll be fine.

Amazing instructor—so grateful! Jared made all the good parts of math show up in easy-to-grasp pieces. He doesn't expect you to know things ahead of time and goes step by step. Even with a quiet class, he brought energy and lots of material. Homework is very fair, more difficult than the tests. Go to lab and push through the tough problems.

ngl, this guy was the best math teacher I've had, as long as you work for your grade and use the resources he provides you'll be okay. The class is hard in general, so if you don't like math you're not gonna like the class, but he is a very good professor to have for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Able gave pretty good lectures. We did have to buy a textbook for the class, but I found an online PDF of it for free. Attendance is not mandatory, but he encourages participation. He always gave practice exams that were almost the same as the actual exams. As long as you do the homework and the practice exams, you'll do fine.
Assigns the worst online assignments out there.

Professor Able explained things in a way I was able to understand, but the material itself was just very difficult. If you have to take finite through IU I would recommend him, but if you are able to, take it through Ivy Tech.

You can't blame the teacher for having to teach a hard class. Please understand that you're going to have to put in the work for this class, no matter the prof. Able was very willing to meet outside of class and was easy to understand during lectures. Never mumbled, spoke loudly enough, etc. Just study and come to terms with Finite being hard!

I would put in hours of studying and tutoring and I couldn't do well on exams, his tests were nothing like the homework. I tried reaching out before I dropped this class but he didn't really help. In class he would continue with a problem without realizing he was wrong until halfway. This is your sign to take Ivy Tech Finite

Finite is a hard class, but I do think Prof. Able is a good teacher of it. He explained concepts well, and as long as you attend class, take notes, and complete the homework, it's not too bad. Attendance isn't mandatory, and exams are curved. There are four exams, and 2/4 can be retaken.

The homework takes a lot of time. Usually, it takes me 2-3 hours to finish the homework. Try not to miss class because you can easily fall behind if you miss a day. He does curve the exam and there are retakes only for exam 1 and 3. The midterm and final have no retakes.

Jared spends his lectures rambling about concepts that will not be on the exam, yet expects you to understand all the material from the chapter, even if he didn't go over or mention it at all. The tests that he writes are harder than other finite teachers, and the resources he gives to study are not good.

Jared seems like a nice guy and honestly tries his best, it's just not very good a lot of the time. He will go on long tangents about the material and will realize he is wrong halfway through and practically act like "you get the point". He writes on these 4 chalkboards in front of the class that are slow to erase and write on and get confusing.

The lectures were focused on the wrong material and 80% of the time he would stop halfway through and realize he made a mistake. He is passive aggressive and reluctant to help. His tests are incredibly hard compared to those given by the department. STAY AWAY!
Although the class overall was difficult, his lectures were very helpful and the homework lined up with what we learned in class. Exams were difficult but nothing I wasn't expecting.

Jared is good for calc. Ur not gonna find a prof that teaches such a large and standard class with an amazing review and honestly jared was pretty good. Talks a bit quiet but explains things pretty good. My issue with this class is curriculum itself but Jared is honestly good for this class. I dont think anyone would rlly regret taking him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but not a great teacher. Does not really teach the material well, and can make topics harder than they need to be. He sometimes even did example problems, and halfway through realized he did it wrong. Overall grade was extremely dependent on test scores and the department exams are extensive. Lots of webwork too.

Professor Able is a great guy, a little goofy, but generally very nice. He is not the best calculus professor and as others have mentioned, doesn't break down the material as much as he should. He skips around on some important topics and delves way too deep into smaller, unimportant, items. You don't really need to go to class but it helps.

This professor is very nice but he is hard to follow. Often times, he skips steps that he presumes the students understand. He also does not write his own exams or midterm. The homework is rarely like the lectures and definitely not like the exams.

reviews.comment: Goodluck

reviews.comment: Take any other Finite Professor,
