reviews.comment: Professor Able gave decent lectures but it was sometimes hard to follow his thought process. M118 is a pretty hard class not just because of the content but because of how your grade is distributed.

Jared is nice but also doesn't seem to completely understand the concepts he teaches. I didn't have pacing issues, but the lessons could be better explained. The homework he assigned was harder than the actual exams, and some of the problems couldn't be solved without the use of resources we aren't supposed to use. Study lots and good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, he was not a bad teacher, but he did not understand the material that he was teaching. I do think that he was slightly more helpful than other teachers. I did go to this office hours a few times and every time he told me that he did not really know and left me with more questions.

I switched to Able's session from Hendrickson's M-118, and Able was a much better lecturer and professor overall. The lectures are very important even though attendance isn't mandatory, and you should do several practice tests before each exam. Overall, though, Able makes the material fairly easy to understand and pace was not a personal issue.

Rushes through a lot of the material and sometimes he is not even sure he is right about what he is teaching. The class is itself is kind of hard and test heavy, but Able doesn't make it easier, hence why a lot of students take it at Ivy Tech and transfer the credit. Webwork will sometimes include problems about material he didn't cover.

Able means well and seems to know what he's talking about, but it's hard to do well in this course when he doesn't seem to know how to teach. He's hard to hear during lectures and much of the information barely makes sense even though I take copious notes. He also assigns tons of homework and most of the course's grades rely on difficult exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Assigns lots of homework, however it does prepare you for the test very well. Very good lecturer and explains topics thoroughly. He often lets the class out early. He also doesn't give you a bunch of information that isn't even required, he tells you what you need to know.

This class is test heavy, as the tests account for 5/6 of your total grade. He assigns a lot of homework but it only accounts for a small portion of your actual grade. The homework is a lot more challenging than the actual tests. Professor Able did a good job explaining topics but only used a chalkboard and was occasionally hard to hear.
He probably assigns double the homework compared to other M118 teachers and it's insane how impossible some of the questions are without calculator but he isn't a bad teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Able does mean well. Several times in class where he is even unsure about what he is teaching us. His test are hard for no reason. He also assigns hours worth of homework each week, but ALL of the homework for the entirety of the semester is only 100 points. This class is very exam grade heavy. I do not reccommend taking M118 though IU!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Able goes through material at a rapid pace during lectures and makes it hard to understand the sheer amount in such a short period of time. The homework he assigns are also very time consuming and tests are very difficult. Beware of homework due dates. I would recommend looking for better professors.

He don't really involve student input and questions during lecture and is generally facing the chalkboard while mumbling. The Webwork is ok, but due to inadequate teaching, I have no idea on some of the questions. He also just puts the Webwork under canvas and doesn't put due dates on individual assignments. Tests long and the reviews don't help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's super friendly, but it is visible in the sparse participation that only few understand his methods, including myself. My friends' notes from other classes are clearer and more explanatory than the ones I receive from him. He over-complicates things, and most of his students complain that he doesn't know how to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Able moves quickly and expects only the best from his students. Creates difficult tests and long homework assignments. Often rejects students' questions and moves on when the class is not ready. That being said, it does prepare us more for midterms and finals. However, we receive lower grades on exams 1 & 3 due to his tough exam creation.
he's a good lecturer, especially for a class like finite. he explains the topics very clearly and is always helpful in office hours. if you want to do well in finite i would recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Jared keeps things short and simple. He always lets class out early and only tells you what you need to know. His WebWorks are not too intense, and I hate math in general. He is a nice guy and accepts any and all questions. Despite not liking math, I would take his class again.
Exams were fair and the study materials were helpful. Took for law of personal finance. Made hard material easy to digest.

Can't recommend her enough! Very easy ethics prof. Keeps the class engaging. Only one exam but the reviews are exactly like the exam. Does in class participation but 3 get dropped. Some group projects but easy. Only "work heavy" is the end of semester paper but just don't wait till last minute. But I really loved her and would def recommend her.
Shes literally one of my fav profs i have had
Liked her a lot.  Brought in current events.  Sometimes went too fast in class, but then had a class of just review before exams.

I originally heard she was boring but definitely didn't think that when I took her business law class. She was funny and had good examples from real life. She also brought in current events, which I hadn't really been following.

Can't select the right course--but this was for her entrepreneurship one.  Liked the real-life examples from her businesses.  Very light on the readings but you had to do some negoations with other people in the class.
Solid business law professor. Online tests and almost no homework

Stemler is one of the best professors I have had in college. She is understanding and genuinely wants her students to succeed. She is always there when you need help and I highly suggest taking L201 with her! Study for the exams and you will do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Stemler is hilarious, accessible, and caring towards all of her students. She is definitely the best/easiest teacher for L-201. Get Stemler!!

You want Stemler for L201. Always brings great energy to her lectures and is entertaining in class. All of her exams are open-note and online. Definitely an easier workload and exams than other L201 teachers.
Shes really helpful and responds very quickly. Makes sure you understand the concepts properly. Easy exams. Would definitely recommend for L201!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Stemler was by far the most engaging professor I had during a virtual year and one of my favorites throughout all of college so far. She comes to class prepared with thought provoking questions, real life examples, and enthusiasm for the subject matter. Stay on top of the readings, attend class, and engage on your "on-call" day!

Professor Stemler was an incredibly dynamic and engaging professor. She checked in on us regularly to make sure we were going at a manageable pace and were understanding the material beyond rote memorization. Her detail examples and personal anecdotes made the classes applicability evident from the beginning. I recommend her to everyone I can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Stemler's course was a major inspiration for my ongoing interest in law. Her lectures are very engaging and add clarity to the assigned readings really effectively, including through fascinating case discussions and examples from her own career. She makes the topic fun and is extremely approachable. One of the best at IU.

Had a bad experience with Stemler. She was routinely underprepared for class. Long reading assignments posted 1-2 days before class, she could've easily put them up 5 days before. Told to read some sections, then in class she tells us those sections don't matter. You need to read to do well. She simply has very little respect for students' time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: During the pandemic, you'd expect a professor to have more empathy and adjust their teaching style. Not Abbey. No recorded lectures, she'll respond to your email days later if ever, and if you miss a lecture or even a minute of the lecture you'll be behind. She uploads practice tests the day before an exam. DON'T TAKE HER this next semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Abbey Stemler is the best professor I've ever had. She's an almost tenured professor, an attorney, she owns restaurants downtown she's truly inspirational. As a Kelley Honors course, it will be challenging and overwhelming at times. However, Stemler's passion really radiates and kept me interested throughout every lecture. Pay attention & read!!

Stemler is easily one of the best professors I've had. She is hilarious and makes the arguably mind-numbing topic of law interesting. The course is dense because of the subject matter, but she really works to make sure her students succeed. Also just like the coolest person ever! Ask her about her (several) businesses, travel, or podcasts.

Professor Stemler is one of the best professors in Kelley! I'm so thankful I took her class. I learned so much about law, and the assignments were all very fair and comparable to other classes. Study & do the homework. While I never read, I still felt very prepared for class. Just put in your best effort, and you'll be fine.

Loved her. She's a great teacher but be sure to keep up with the readings or you will fall behind and get overwhelmed. It's a hard class but tests are open note and she's a lenient grader because she knows the material is tough
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Personally, one of my favorite professors by far. She make difficult, dry materials fun and enjoyable to learn. However her lectures are fast pacing, I would recommend taking notes through a laptop. I would recommend her class to a friend.

I really enjoyed taking Stemler's class because she brought real life examples into the classroom. I've taken too many classes that are all about theory. I was able to ask her specific questions, and she always had the answer and could apply it to an actual case. You definitely want to go to the lectures and visit her during office hours.
Good professor.  Has a lot of energy and really likes her subject.  Class was hard, not impossible.  I'd recommend.

Abbey is a pretty good professor. She seems pretty rushed when she's teaching so it can be hard to follow at times. Her tests are pretty fair and all open book, but they are very long so you can't really use your notes and book effectively. She does a good job engaging the class and makes the topics interesting. I would take again and recommend.

She doesn't respond to emails nor grades half of your assignments on canvas. Also, be prepared to come to class because the in class assignments count as attendance. The only plus to this class is that the tests are open book, but it's still timed so that's not really helpful. She's a really smart lady but an absent minded teacher.

After taking part in Stemler's class, I was a bit shocked that the school of business would take in such a mediocre professor. She moves quickly through topics and is often very unclear in what she wants the class to know. If I were making decisions behind closed doors, she would no longer be teaching here. Kelley deserves the best, not her.

She is all right. Class is just lectures with fill in the blank notes. It can get really boring. The final is open note and open book, which makes it much easier. Don't get the textbook, I was fine without it.

Her lectures are print out and fill in the blank which is super convenient! She's really young and fun which is always a plus! Definitely take her if you're somewhat interested in Law. Attendance isn't mandatory everyday but she would randomly do in- class assignments to check who was in class.

Abbey is pretty cool, and from what I understand, she's one of the better L201 professors. She's great about organizing her class and assignments in a way that actually benefits your learning, so you don't have to do a ton of "self-managing" studying, which is great for people who aren't used to this whole college thing quite yet.
Professor Stemler is a little disorganized, but overall a great professor. She made class both enjoyable and relatable, and is a fairly easy grader! I would definitely reccomend this course.

Professor Stemler sets her students up for success. Every lecture includes a fill-in-the-blank outline. All you need to do is pay attention and fill in the keywords and you'll understand the material. There are a good amount of interesting assignments as well. I suggest sitting towards the front because this professor is gorgeous.
Abbey is an awesome teacher. Just attend her class and you can get an A.

Stemler was a very nice professor who genuinely enjoys what she teaches. I could study an hour before each quiz or exam get at least a B. Notes are fill-in-the-blank (which make for easy learning, but sometimes boring lecture). Each class was worth attendance points. She can be a little frazzled sometimes but is always willing to help students.
She is a great professor.  The notes are fill in the blank to help show you what exactly you will be tested on.  Some studying is needed in order to get an A but overall the tests aren't terrible.

Abbey is a good teacher. She knows what she is talking about, but if you are not interested in law I don't recommend this class. I thought her online quizzes were very misleading at times, but her tests were fair. It requires some studying in order to get an A.

Professor Stemler is an amazing Law professor. Her notes are fill-in-the-blank and very easy to follow. She makes the topics very interesting and tests are fairly easy. She is an overall awesome professor. I highly recommend taking her classes!
Reads straight from her notes, awfully hard to understand.

Fantastic teacher. Notes are fill-in-the-blank so you can listen while remembering key words. She makes difficult concepts easy to understand. Tests aren't designed to stump you. You receive the grade you earn. She is one of the best teachers at IU.
Very nice

overall a pretty easy class. Shes really nice and willing to help. Tests are not too crazy, notes are not too involved. Im not really interested in law but she did a good job maintaining my attention. Another plus for her is that she is willing to help you if you get in trouble or something... she provides good legal advice, and thats nice of her.

She is an awesome teacher. She made the subject very interesting and understandable. It is a hard topic to begin with but she made it pretty easy. She has notes printed out that you fill in blanks. She has reviews during class before all the test. No cumulative final. Gives practice problems that are very similar to test questions. TAKE HER CLASS!

I took her AAAD - A132: Recent African American and African Diaspora Literature course. It was a small class and was very discussion-heavy. She's super kind and genuine and I would definitely take her courses again.
Amazing professor, I would recommend taking any course she teaches if its anything you are remotely interested in.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's awesome! really cares about her students inside and outside of class. We napped in class one day because she saw we weren't getting enough sleep by the time we were turning in assignments lol.

Professor Abegunde will notice if you're grasping the concept.  Never hesitate to ask her questions even if their controversial.  She's a poet, and an amazing person. If I had to continue taking courses (senior) I'd take another with her.

I would take a class with Professor Abegunde again any day. She offers more opportunities for extra credit than any other instructor I've ever had, and she does it because work outside of her classroom is meant to be just as enriching as inside of it. And it is. Love her class, learned a lot. Take something with her!

It was a privilege to take a course under Professor Abegunde. She is one of the most brilliant minds and kindest hearts I've ever known. I walked away from every lecture and assignment more enlightened than the last. Her class isn't hard AT ALL if you give her and the community (the class) the respect they warrant. Highly recommend!

She knows what she's teaching. Your professor for K201 doesn't really matter, but if you do the work (discoveries and case apps) and come to class, you'll be fine. If not, the book and other students can help you understand everything you need to. Professor Abbot gives practical examples and really helps you visualize the formulas if needed.

Many people complain about Megans way of teaching and that its too slow. As someone who got into the school with a 2.8 HS GPA, she was doing fine. But she does teach like an elementary school teacher and shes also passive aggressive at times. Listen and show up to class and youll be fine. Both K160 and K201.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had Megan for online lecture for K201. In all honesty, I can't tell you a single thing I learned all semester. Hard to listen to lectures due to her elementary school teaching style. Her Koin questions have no relevance and are unnecessarily hard compared to other lecture sections. To do well all you need to do is study the Quizlet before the exams

I had her for lecture portion of K201 at 9am on fridays, and maybe it was just me but her bubbly-ness at that time of day was jarring and I hated listening for 50 minutes. She kind of talks like an elementary school teacher. Lecture is boring and feels pointless regardless of lecturer so the dry material isn't her fault. Just answer the koin Q's

I had Abbott for the online lecture portion of K201. Wasnt the biggest fan, as she literally just read off the slides during the vast majority of the online lecture. However, I dont blame this entirely on her since online lectures are boring either way.

If you don't know how to use a computer, you should take K201 with Megan. She explains everything so slowly that it takes an entire 50 minute class to do two problems that I finish in the first 10 minutes if I've done the reading before class. Drones on forever I sit on my phone all class and got a 100 on the access practical.
Amazing professor! Prepared me for K201!
Megan is great! Made K201 so much easier. Show up, don't fall behind and ask questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She teaches very clearly be sure to always show up to class and on time or you will fall behind. She also gives a lot of help to her students

K201 was a pleasure to take with her as a lab instructor! She taught very clearly and probably aided in me getting an A in the class. Always do the reviews and discoveries and dont get behind on those! Only thing is I wish the lab checks wouldve been a little easier sometimes. Other than that, very solid choice!
Megan is always willing to help. She teaches the material clearly. As long as you do the work assigned in a timely fashion, you'll do well.

Dr. Ramadoss is a really good professor. It's a tough class and he is a bit technical, but really helpful with office hours. The homework was graded strictly, make sure to do well on it. Tests are curved.

Ajay should prob not be teaching lower level math courses. He is brilliant but not very clear about material and course structure/grading. Decently unorganized throughout the semester. I gained more from the textbook than from lectures. Definitely do practice problems for the exams. Homework/quiz about every week. Try not to  depend on the curve :)

Does not deviate from the textbook. He's nice and clear, but if exam averages are 51%, then I don't think he should be teaching it. Good guy, but he is not cut out for teaching low level math classes.

He is a pretty good professor. Calculus is a hard subject and while he gives a lot of homework and several quizzes, they actually help you a lot since they prepare you really well for the exams. Exams are insanely hard but the curve is huge so don't despair until the final grade comes out.

This guy is strict but the best professor I had at IU. Amazing, thought provoking lectures that still resonate with me over a year later. Somebody should give this guy a raise because he deserves it. If you are sensitive to the complicated matter he teaches, avoid it. But for everyone else, this class is a must take.
Excellent teacher. I really enjoyed taking two of his courses (239 and 339). I learned a lot and I love the way he thinks. Reasonable exams. Gives you prep docs. Kind and fair.

I walked into this class with little prior knowledge of history in the Middle East, which definitely made this class a little tougher for me. However, if you stay on top of your reading and go to class you should be fine. It's clear that Professor Sinno really cares about his students and wants everyone to do well.

Professor Sinno taught me so much about the the Middle East, a topic I never before had an interest in. He truly wants all his students to succeed, but will have high expectations of them. Be prepared to work hard and do all the readings. If you participate in discussions and take good notes, you will do well. Definitely worth taking.

Make sure to show up to class, attendance is mandatory and for points. He grades papers generously and compromises with the class on grading and due dates. lecture based with slideshows to keep it interesting. VERY liberal viewpoint and it shows in his lectures, but he is very respectful to other positions. Requires you to buy a 15$ book off amazon

Professor Sinno is excellent in terms of IU professors. He is a respectable, funny, and kind man who cares very much about his students. I had interest in taking the class because I wanted to learn more about the middle east and I could not have asked for more. He did a better job at teaching than any other teacher. I will truly miss prof sinno ):

AMAZING Professor. Prof Sinno's course is fun to take because of his knowledge and interest in the material. Lectures are engaging and interesting. He provides study guides for all tests from day 1 and tell you exactly what he is looking for to get a good grade. While class is helpful for tests, most material used for tests comes from the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Sinno is AWESOME. He is extremely knowledgeable and is excited to share his knowledge with the class. His lectures are engaging and full of content. His attendance policy is harsh but fair. I'm not sure why any of these reviews are negative, I'm not even studying political science and got an A+ in his class.

Prof. Sinno is a great professor and an expert in his field. The lectures were probably the most interesting out of all of my classes. One downside is that his exams are pretty difficult, though he offers extra credit. If you're at all interested in history, politics, etc. then you would probably enjoy this class, even if its online.

Professor Sinno is the kindest soul ever to exist. He is very passionate about the topic of this class and he teaches it with first hand knowledge and experience. The class is very test heavy and you definately need to attend the lectures, but if you take good notes and do all the readings, the quizzes, midterm and final won't be that hard.

Quite simply one of the greatest professors in Bloomington. Truly inspiring. He is the type of professor who you do not forget, someone who can really bring out the best in students. If you are lazy, it might not be for you. But if you care about getting an excellent education in Bloomington, definitely enroll in one of his courses. Outstanding.

There is a lot of hate on this board towards professor Sinno.  I honestly find that weird.  He is strict but very nice and a first class teacher.   I learnt more from him than any other at IU and I appreciate that.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: While I enjoyed Sinno's personality and clear knowledge of the course, he sometimes came off very arrogant to students clearly struggling with concepts. The attendance policy is very harsh- if you're a second over five minutes late, you can't stay. Tough weekly homework assignments. The midterm and final project were also very challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sinno does not effectively teach all of the material required, especially in a class such as Y205 that requires quite a bit of knowledge of Excel. As well, Sinno has an incredibly harsh attendance policy where if you are late he will block you from coming to class. Very arrogant as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Sinno is very disrespectful to students.  His course is challenging, but he gives opportunities for extra credit. His exams are lengthy and involve long essays to propose solutions to the world's crises, and perfection in 1 hour. If your writing is not up to his "standards", he will grade you likewise, but leaves absolutely no feedback on exams.

Sinno knows the material extremely well. I found his lectures interesting, but at times a little basic. The class only has tests and no homework or essays which was nice. I though the tests were pretty straightforward. Sinno can be quite offensive on rather sensitive topics. I don't recommend the class if you have strong feelings on the middle east

Solid freaking professor. His lectures are full of energy. It's clear he has a passion for his work. Expect to put in the time to do the required reading. If you do the work and take advantage of the extra credit opportunities, there is no excuse for getting less than 100% in the class.

This is by far the worst teacher I have ever had. You can never understand him, he makes rude jokes, and is the least helpful teacher when it comes to explaining is random and confusing grading. He makes absolutely no sense. Worst teacher.
Information he requires you to know for tests is pointless and time wasting. Nobody cares about the specific populations of 14 countries.
very smart and engaging.  I often left class continuing to think about stuff.  I liked that he pushed us to work hard.  It paid off with an A+.

This class was focussed on the last 75 years in the middle east so do not expect it to be on current events. Sinno grades hard and you have to do the readings to do well on the tests. Do not take this class unless you have an interest and plan on working hard. Sinno is very smart and knowledgable on topics but this was not an easy 200 level course

Honestly, this is a very interesting course. The material covered in class may be seen as biased, however it is not. If you are wanting to expand your knowledge about the truth of middle eastern politics and issues, it is a wonderful class. HOWEVER, dr. Sinno is RUDE and arrogant. This is one of the hardest classes you will take. Mostly essay exams
Really interesting
I'd take a course with him every semester if I can
Wickedly smart and interesting.  I went to college to rtake classes like this.

This guy is extremely biased. To sum up his Middle East politics class: America is evil, Israel is evil, the Arabs are wonderful. This class was nothing but absurd lies and propaganda. If you actually took the time to read the textbooks assigned, you would be able to tell how often he gave outright false explanations for historical events.
Great teacher. Presented all the facts and history on the region in the Middle East. I wouldn't say he's biased at all,he just doesn't care if he offends anyone by stating the truth.

He is not biased.  His job is not to protect "feelings" of whomever is politically committed but to share knowledge.  Everything he says is accurate so it is a pitty some pro-whatever people feel bothered.

Highly knowledgeable, but incredibly biased in his presentation of events esp regarding the Palestinian-Israeli conflict. As someone who majored in Jewish Studies, it is amazing to me that he is not more sensitive to both sides of the conflict and presents it in such a discriminatory manner.
World-class.
Best prof ever.  Those who are not interested enough in topic may think class is too demanding but amazing experience if you really care to learn.  I wish every prof was like prof Sinno.
Very difficult class, especially for a 100 lvl one. Arrogant professor but has interesting ideas. Do not take this class if you are not very interested in the subject.

He is the best teacher I've had at IU. The classes were very interesting! You must come to class but you don't want to miss it. He teaches controversies and he's good at presenting it on the fence, in my opinion.

I never thought a 200lvl class could be so difficult. I'm a senior triple majoring but this class blew me away with the incredible amount of detail he requires on exams, much of which means nothing to the overall class. What bothers me most, however, is that he is so insecure in something that he doesn't treat students with respect. Grow up Sinno.

I met him when I was a freshman and took his large course.  Since then I took two more courses with him.  All along, even when I was not enrolled in his courses, he supported me and helped me make the best choices for me for internships, career and graduate school.  I owe him a lot and want to recognize him as a great educator.

He is amazing.  I went into the class knowing nothing about the Middle East.  I left feeling like a master.  He pushes you and makes you work, but you will be a better man because of it.  He also is great at bringing in guest speakers.  He also does a good job of giving you both sides of the argument so that you can have your own OPINION
Very arrogant, doesn't have a great attitude.

I am surprised at all the compliments Sinno has received on this website. I am aware that Sinno is talented and capable of shooting down students he disagrees with. Interestingly,I have seen him get completely crushed and shut down by both Benny Morris and Mark Regev. He can't deal with people who are above his caliber. Hence he takes it out on kid

Sinno is easily one of the best professors I've ever had. He has a clear, sophisticated understanding of the topic at hand. I like that he asks students for suggestions on how to improve the class lectures. That said, I find that too much emphasis is placed on his subjectively-graded tests. He has to make the tests more fair, or redo the syllabus.

Hard work, tough class.  Don't go in there with an attitude, it won't do you any good.  Great Professor, and despite some of these comments, he may be biased but he does not enforce his opinions on you.  He encourages you to find your own opinions based on hard facts.  If you have a hard time learning the truth...don't bother.
awesome in every way. helped me more than any professor ever did even afters class was over.  I just want to thank him

Those who may consider this professor biased are usually biased themselves.  If you can listen objectively and take in the information intelligently, you will find his courses to be extremely enlightening and well structured.  YOU WILL WORK VERY HARD IN THIS CLASS, but it's under a fantastic professor.

Excellent professor.  If you don't want to work for your grade, don't register for this class.  It's demanding, grueling,and downright tedious.  But, you will be a much better student in general after taking this class.  It will bring your work ethic to the peak, or it will break you as a student.  This professor is one of the best I have ever had.

He's nice and firm at the same time...you can't **** him he's too smart but is also nice helpful and polite to anyone who is same...cute in a suit :) but prefers casual denims. On days when hes really into the lecture  I can't keep my eyes off him...very passionate and has a powerful mind
You have to work for this guy, it's totally worth it.  Learning should push you!

liberal propaganda? gospel? hardly. It's a very interesting course and I would recommend it if you are willing to put forth the effort, it's not exactly easy. As for it professing the evils of Americans, not true either. The professor is actually very nice, extremely opinionated but very nice.
Loved him as a professor, loved the class.
A really biased class, but worth taking if you are interested in the Middle East.

Has a lot of good information but is VERY biased.  Only presents one side of issues as law.  It's always nice when someone in the class occasionally offers the other side, even though he just shoots them down.  You will learn a lot in this class but be wary and take some of it with a grain of salt.

This class is terrible. The entire agenda is a bunch of liberal propaganda. Every moron in this class sits fixated on him, taking in every word as if it were the gospel. Learn to think for yourself, you liberal drones! The point of the class is to teach us how the muslims are "misunderstood" and that Americans are evil.
Its my favorite class.  You learn about the Middle East the way it really is, not the way politicians and ideological crazies want us  to think it is.

In Y200, US media propaganda is a major theme. Last HW reading claimed mass media is rcist and leads to misunderstanding and hatred of Muslims. It was extremely insulting. History was distorted to strengthen arguments. Sadly, this is likely to go on. The syllabus states the goal that we leave 'better informed and more sophisticated news consumers'!

In Y200, media propaganda is a major theme. Last HW reading claimed mass media is “****” and leads to “misunderstanding and hatred of Muslims”. I found it extremely offensive. Unfortunately, this is likely a class theme. The syllabus states the goal that we leave “better informed and more sophisticated news consumers”. I plan on withdrawing.
had him a coople of years ago. great teacher and still go to his public lectures when he gives any.
Sinno was cool and knew his stufff but u have to write well in test

The hard facts taught by a talented and smart Prof who knows the Middle East like the palm of his hand.  I was never bored in 2 hr meetings because he kept it exciting.  Tests were tough but he curves the grade so average is B- which makes it fair.  I appreciated the guests and his enthousiasm.  He gave awesome public lectures too.  Challenging.

I serve in the military and found this class to be super useful...the hard ugly facts of war are sometimes hard to swallow but it is better to know them than being ignorant...very structured and powerful course...we are lucky to have people with his knowledge

One of the best profs ever.  Caring and awesome in office hours.  Always a smile on his face.  He teaches about very challenging topics and yet does great job.  Tests challenging so class for people who care to learn.
I don't recommend taking a class by Sinno.  He doesn't care about other people's opinions.  His tests are very difficult too and graded unfairly!
Yells at people if they express an opinion contrary to his own. Flaming liberal.
Love this class.  He brings guests and very informatiuve
Absolutely the most intriguing, intense, passionate man I've met in my life.

I had a hard schedual so i figured I would take a 100 level to balance my load a little bit,but this ended being harder than my 300 level classes put together. He has an accent and talks fast so its easy to miss things which make it hard to study. Interesting, but very hard.
The best course I had at IU.  Honest.
No Comments
Tells it the way it is

He gave some hard tests and really forces you to do the readings.  For a passionate and enthusiastic teacher I fell asleep a lot.  He is helpful after class but i wouldn't ask questions during class. he gets mad.  I sure learned a lot a his y200 will make your other courses seem like a breeze because you will learn so much
Awesome lectures.

Prof Sinno is a smart and good teacher and his are engaging classes.  I took his Y200 & Y396 and felt I learned more from them than the rest of my IU education.  Sincere and caring teacher but don't mess with him or diss him because he takes no crap and will put you in your place.  He returns respect with respect and is very helpful and nice

Excellent and helpful teacher.  Take his class if you want to understand Middle East today.  Don't take his class if you are someone ideological or close minded.   He goes the extra mile for us including holding discussion sessions from his own time and inviting distinguished guest lectures like the ambassador of Iraq.
No Comments
good teacher - too one-sided

Let's be honest.This Sinno is a decent prof.  His classes really push you and they're worth it if you do the work.I got a lot out of this class.Would I take him again?Maybe, but only if I didn't have other things as the main focus of my schooling.If you have time,the will, and the interest take him.
Very Tough...A Ton of Reading...Very Biased.  He does have great insight, but he just believes his ideas are always correct.
do not take this class...he is so opinionated and it overtakes his ability to teach. doesnt want to be bothered by his students
he is biased

This guy is difficult. He has an extreme enthusiasm for his subject, but not for students.  He doesn't like to be bothered, and he almost has a perverse joy in being vague when you ask him a question.  Also, this 107 course has the most reading I have ever had. There are other better profs to take.
No Comments
No Comments
Great teacher and he cares for students
He's the best, I changed my major to poli sci because of him.  Smart, insightful, exciting.
He is ok. Moves VERY fast. If you dont know your stuff you will get behind quickly in his class....
Saurabh is extremely helpfull. He looks damn cute. He has a good sense of humor and know exactly how to teach.
Saurabh Rocks

Japanese Cinema is a really good course, but a bit challenging with all of the exams, except for film papers. The professor is very sweet and it is highly recommended to take that class again, if you are interested in pre-history of Japanese cinema, anime and yakuza.

She was awesome! Lectures were engaging and made coming to class enjoyable. She knows so much and is nice to talk to. There was a reasonable amount of work with reasonable grading. Would definitely take a class with her again.

Very participation-based class on Japanese Film, though participation not taken for grade. Recommend if you don't mind finding a new depth of appreciation for a subject you previously found shallow. Participate in class discussion and take decent notes to pass the exams, and lots of reading (be prepared to skim) but otherwise easy to enjoy class.

Instructor Airriess was lovely and I am taking another one of her classes next semester. This course required you watch one film a week and do manageable readings before class. The material was engaging and useful but not overly complicated. It overlapped other culture classes often which definitely makes you feel like youre learning something.

Instructor Airriess is a great teacher! She makes the material easily understandable. She focuses more on making sure you understand the concepts than knowing specific information like names and dates. When it comes to the assignments she's not a strict grader, just show that you've done the work and understand. Taking another of her classes!

This was one of the most engaging online classes I have ever taken! The course was perfectly organized. Aida's pre-recorded lectures were excellent, and all the tests and assignments were an accurate representation of the course. I particularly enjoyed the breakout room work on Zoom. I also loved the way we used Socrative app. Highly recommended!
The course material is not overly interesting, but as long as you study and pay attention in class you will do well.

The sweetest professor that is passionate about what she teaches and cares that her students enjoy it too. Has amazing personal experiences that make your learning more entertaining. Although lectures can sometimes drag, quizzes and tests are very easy and its always interesting material

Aida is a great Professor, if you show up and participate in class and review her PowerPoint slides you will be very successful. She is very accommodating if you make her aware of any situations. I would definitely recommend this class even if you arent a music major! No music background needed. She has such a positive and enthusiastic energy!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Aida is my favorite professor I've had at IU. 10/10 recommend taking one of her classes

Pop Music in Europe/Asia is not a hard class. Taking the class is worth it considering it provides both A&h/World Culture Gen Ed credits. There are a lot of tests and quizzes, but they are very easy if you devote a little time to study. Lots of extra credit. Don't need to read the textbook. Lecture is rarely ever dull.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Aida Huseynova is without a doubt my favorite professor I have had at IU. She is knowledgeable, motivational, nice and resourceful. I particularly enjoyed her stories about her work with Yo-Yo Ma and Mark Morris. The video conference with the members of the Silkroad Ensemble was an unforgettable experience!

Aida is very kind and passionate about her classes. This class, while the material can be boring for non-music majors, is very easy and there a lot of bonus points available! If you need a world cultures class and want an A, take this one!

Awesome professor! Her expertise and personal connection with the subject provided invaluable context. I can't imagine the class being taught by anyone else. She treats each and every student as a person before she treats him/her as a student. Constantly motivated me and inspired me to do better work.

Professor Huseynova is a very kind and thoughtful professor and is an expert in her field.  This is not an "Easy A" course if you arent interested in the material like me.  I spent most of my time studying for this class.  We had quizzes every Monday and found myself studying all weekend for them just to get B's on them.  Good place for A&H WC cred

A privilege to have the opportunity to take her course. Expert in her field, passionate about the subject. Teaches every minute of the 75 minute class, incorporates group activities consistently. Always takes time to go the extra mile to help her students. I know more about the Silk Road than my own major because of Dr. Huseynova and the course!
Gave lots of extra credit opportunities. However, her use of the english language is not great...

Music of the Silk Road is an interesting topic. She invited many musicians in the field, so that we can have a feeling of live Silk Road music. She is extremely helpful about our situations and a great teacher as well.
She is good. Also, she gave lots of extra credit for encouraging expanding your music theory knowledge. Helpful and willing to teach. You will enjoy her class.

Aida is the sweetest lady and Z111 is a nice class to take to get A&H credits. The material isgone through very quickly so attendence is very important because it all builds up. She gives many chances for good grades and bonus and is very understanding with conflicts or if you don't understand. Truely loves what she is teaching.

Knowledgeable. Encouraging. Loves her subject. Truly likes students and seeing them learn! Available and approachable. Responsive and well organized. Coursework well structured. Concepts clearly explained! Infinitely patient in explaining concepts. Quick turnaround on assignments and email.
Easy class! Easy and fun~ if you need any a&h class, Z111 will be the best choice.
Overall, Aiko is a super sweet lady. She is super soft spoken and it definitely is hard to hear her sometimes, but she grades easy and tries to make the class less painful.

Aiko is an under-appreciated professor at IU. She values student participation, and she loves when people are engaged in discussion; if you are quiet by nature, she will encourage you to speak up in class, and provides a welcoming space to do so. Additionally, she is very aware of your abilities, and very sympathetic to all skill-levels.

As everyone is saying, she is very soft-spoken but she is more than ready to help at any given time. Professor Aiko is amazingly available and is always more than ready to help no matter the situation. I enjoyed her class very much as well as her!

Aiko is amazing. You'll find that she does speak quite softly, but if you are serious about learning French, she won't let hard work go unnoticed. All homework is done online with 3 attempts. She is the cutest little Japanese francophone you'll ever meet, and she genuinely cares about your success. Don't be mislead by those who didn't seek her help

She speaks so so softly. It was often hard to hear. She also moves quickly and speaks only in French; if you aren't at a high proficiency level, you may want to avoid this class. Instructions weren't ever clear about writing assignments, but class was almost always just discussing our readings. Interesting, but a little stressful.

Avoid her class! She is hard to understand--she speaks very softly and says a lot of things that don't make sense, and her instructions are very unclear. Like her class, the textbook sucks--its a disorganized mess of random grammatical points. I've never had such a poor course experience in all of my time in college!

She's very softspoken and talks very quickly, not exactly the makings of a great language professor. The class consisted of going over the workbook, as said before. She honestly wants to help the class, but no one asks questions... Tests are very easy, and there is a final project over an article written in French, any of our choosing.

Professor Aiko is certainly one of the most remarkable instructors on the IU campus. Her effective method of teaching has helped both my classmates and I to develop a perfect understanding of the history and development of poetry in France. She is really enthusiastic about teaching French, and always accessible in office hours.
Not one of the best professors. Doesn't give help and doesn't allow you to look for help from other sources. Definitely better professors exist for this class.

She doesn't really cover the grammar points in class, so make sure you have notes from provious French classes to guide you.  Class consists almost entirely of her going over the answers to the exercises assigned as homework.  Though she is nice and will try to help you, there are better profs for this course.
She is very nice, and I feel like I learned a lot. She tries to engage everyone in discussions, but she is okay with you if you don't understand. She is kind, and really wants everyone to learn

She speaks rather quietly and quickly, sometimes, but she is clear and concise in her points. She's easy-going, too. She is patient and helpful. I find that getting an A/B in her class is not difficult. Just go to class and do the homework. Really, I didn't even have to study on the midterm. Just show up and pay attention and you're golden.

She is very quiet and uses very proper french grammar. Course material is not that interesting but it's doable. Grading sucks because she grades out of 100 points so everything really does count as part of your grade. But, on papers she lets you turn it in for the first time, she corrects it and gives it back to you, and then you can turn it inagai

I loved Aiko. She is such a nice, energetic, and knowledgable lady. She always makes sure that everyone understands the material. However, she sometimes goes a bit too in depth with exceptions to certain concepts and confuses people. She is extremely helpful during office hours and her tests are pretty straight forward.
Aiko was very kind and willing to help. Sometimes she doesn't realize that students are lost but if you give her a shout out she doesn't mind rephrasing ideas.
she's really patient, kind, and offers many chances to do well in the class. make sure you do all the work, and you'll pull an A! ask for help.

David is the man. Teaches through examples that you will see on homework and exams. Homework and quizzes worth 25% but he never gives quizzes. He is very good and a fun teacher. Class was an hour and 15 minutes and we usually got done in 30 minutes.
Easy class. He's a really great professor and uses a lot of helpful examples. Also puts all notes online so if you don't go to class it's really easy to catch up. All homework is online
David is a very helpful professor. He doesn't like to use the book much at all, but that just means you should be attending his classes and office hours as much as possible. Great professor
Ai is a great M118 Professor to Have. He ends class early often, is very helpful, and very clear.

Favorite professor of the semester. Gets straight to the point, doesn't hold class any longer than it needs to be. It's a very hard subject but he is very helpful; always responds to the NUMEROUS homework-help emails I sent in a timely manner, also scheduled last minute office hours before a test. Nice guy; I have nothing but positive things to say

He tries to get the point across without being boring. He speaks english well, unlike may other finite professors. He wants the students to do well. Unfortunately, it is a very challenging class for many students. Not his fault.
oh boy..
Akshay is a good and caring teacher. It was his first time teaching the class so some things were a little confusing or on a learning curve, but attend the classes and pay attention and it is fine.
Absolute GOAT! friendly and caring , He went out of his way to help students. Made the course worthwhile! Highly recommend!

He was my favorite professor I had. K201 was hyped up to be a very hard class to me, but Akshay made the class super easy and clear. If you go to class and follow along you will have no problem. He's also super nice and willing to help

As far as k201 profs go he's one of the best. The grading criteria doesn't give him a lot of leeway for students but you can tell he tries to help his students to pass. Thick accent was difficult at first but you get used to it. Only gave a couple lab checks the whole semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is caring and treats you human being, he was patient even when I said I didn't understand a topic for the third time. He doesn't get my name right even now🤣

He really cared about me, Spoke to me for 15 minutes explaining the courses and about my mental health. I will take his class again definitely after I feel better. His interactions with his TA is extremely fun to watch
If you just do the work in his class you will get a good grade. He cares about you as a student.

Very lively and caring teacher and he makes such a boring class actually engaging. I'd highly recommend him for K201 if you feel like you are competent with computers, as you can choose how much of the class you do on your own.
He was good!

Akshay's classes was interesting and fun , he treats all students alike and sometime goes to everyone before class and asks how they are doing in course and if they needed help. He goes extra mile to help his student and don't let him fool you , he is really good at chess , sometimes plays a game or two in the big screen with his TA and always win.

Akshay was absolutely fantastic. He was very caring for his students and was very funny. He knows what he is talking about and genuinely wants his students to succeed. Attendance isn't mandatory but there are occasional pop quizzes with the lab checks, so I would suggest going to class. The class itself is not hard, just be prepared to study a bit.
Very funny for such boring material and he will go the extra mile to help when needed.

Akshay is a funny and caring professor. He definitely knows his stuff and gives a bunch of real world examples to dumb down concepts. This class in general is not hard and with Akshay it's very fun. He makes all the material so much easier to understand. Make sure you do your assignments on time and with correct naming on everything with him.
Akshay classes are fun and lively , he incorporates memes in the slides making it easier to understand the topics. He cares a lot about students.
he was a good teacher

Akshay was a great professor and his class average for every exam was around 5% higher than all other sections of K201. His lab checks were half online and half in person, so attendance is highly recommended. The course material was not too difficult, but you had to do the discoveries, reviews, and attend class for case applications to pass.

Where do I begin, Akshay has been an amazing teacher with great lectures. Although the course has some difficult materials Akshay helped our class work through it. He is a great teacher with a passion for teaching.

Really knows his stuff. Explains things in unique ways that make the concepts taught in k201 easy to understand. Lectures were fun and interesting. He joked a lot as well which made the class less boring. Really wants his students to succeed and always does his best to help. Great professor.

Professor Akshay is a teacher who is always prepared and ready for class. He makes his class a very inviting environment where everyone is laughing along with him. His ability to convey material is comprehensive. i would definitely take this class with this professor again.

Akshay is not just an incredible professor, but an incredible person. He always goes out of his way to help students, especially those who need it most. This stems from his genuine desire to see students reach their full potential and succeed, something all professors should have. Can't recommend him enough.
He is caring and goes outside his bounds to help.Classes are funny and interesting.
Keeps class environment lively, always tries to help students as best as he can, overall does a good job of trying to explain class material as best he can

Definitely the best possible professor you could have teaching J101. Super kind and funny, and her lectures do help a lot with the grammatical sides. It can be difficult if you dont have any Japanese experience before hand, and attendance and participation are essentially mandatory. But its more than manageable.

Her teaching style is very fast paced through learning the language. She cares about her students and treats them fairly and with respect. During the lectures she discusses and teaches the lesson material very clearly and makes sure a majority of students understand before moving on.

Yasuko Akiyama is a one in a million professor. She truly cares and wants to see you succeed in learning a new language. She will do whatever it takes to help you succeed. She is encouraging, sweet, and honestly genuinely funny. I think it is unfair to give 5/5 reviews, but she is really the perfect instructor. Be ready for a tough course though!

Akiyama sensei is among the best language teachers I've ever had. Her lectures are engaging and fun. Sometimes she comes up with songs meant to help you memorize the material, and while they do feel a bit silly, they're overall fun and do actually help. She is very kind and approachable, I can't recommend her enough.

Akiyama is the best professor I've ever had. She made learning Japanese fun! Be prepared to sing in class, though! Akiyama, if you are reading this, thank you for everything you've done. If it wasn't for you, I would have dropped this class the second it got too difficult. But you motivated me to finish out strong, and with a good grade!
Fantastic professor. With her class, you will not 'learn' but become one with self and the Japanese language naturally. The class was very interesting.

Professor Akiyama is the best of the best when it comes to the EALC department at IU. She wants the students to succeed and has office hours most days of the week. She gives inspirational speeches in class and I truly cannot recommend her enough. J202 is a tough course, but she makes it worth it!

Akiyama is fantastic, really cares about her students. Makes learning tough material fun, adjusted to online really well. Pays attention to students needs, occasionally offers extra credit. J202 is tough but if you put in the work its worth it
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Akiyama is one of the best professors I have ever had, she gets to know each of her students and really cares for how her class performs. She also is great at working with her assistant instructors to make sure the content is top-notch. I would say though that like all EALC classes, skipping is detrimental to your understanding and grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Akiyama really cares about her students and is always willing to help if you don't understand. She has amazing lectures, and really cares about making sure you know the grammar points, vocab, etc (makes learning Japanese fun).

Fantastic professor. Genuinely cares about each student - not just academically, but personally - and her teaching style is easy to understand. Super accommodating and accessible outside of class, just talk to her. Keeps the lectures fun and engaging. Fair warning: she'll make you sing!

One of the nicest professors i've ever had. She truly cares about her students and how they do in her class. If you struggle even a little in the class she will do everything she can to help you out, all you have to do is talk with her about it. Great professor and her teaching style is very easy to understand. I would highly recommend her!

I feel like this website attracts students who love or detest their professors, making it a less than accurate representation of the average student's experience with a teacher. But in Akiyama's case there really is no middle ground. She is one of the best people I've ever met and an outstanding professor. I will miss her more than anything at IU.
I absolutely love this woman. She makes otherwise tedious Japanese lectures enjoyable and funny! Whenever I'm discouraged or having a hard time, she is genuinely caring and it actually moves me T.T
The best teacher! She genuinely cares about her students. She is an excellent foreign language teacher. If it wasn't for her guidance I really would have dropped out!

Akiyama is such a great professor. Her lectures are always fun, and everyone else seem to enjoy it as well. I'd always feel comfortable going to her office hours because she's super helpful and is just over all fun to talk to. There are A LOT of assignments, but they really aren't hard at all. Also, in class participation matters!

Akiyama Sensei is overall a great teacher, her class is interesting. However her grade policy is a little bit strange. The exam only take about 30% and the essay is 15%.  The rest are all in-class performance and quiz. If you are late for the class for even 5 minutes, you will not be given the quiz and get an automatically 0.

Languages classes will always be hard, but Akiyama Sensei is amazing! She really helps people when they struggle learning a hard language such as Japanese. I, however, don't enjoy when she tries to make us socialize with everyone.  I personally don't like it teachers force people to make friends. She also wrote me an AWESOME letter of Rec. LOVE HER

Akiyama-sensei is one of the best instructors I have ever had, in college or otherwise. She's caring, helpful, and a lot of fun to have class with. Some of the activities (for J301) might bring you out of your comfort zone, but they'll help. She does speak quickly, which can be hard at first, but it'll do wonders for your comprehension.
Akiyama-sensei is very helpful. She is very passionate about her field and I love that. She is very understanding and very patient with her students.
She's one of the loveliest and sweetest professors I've ever had. Learning languages can be so hard, so I can't say if her class is hard or not! Do your best and you will do fine!

Akiyama-Sensei is the most incredible professor I've had. She really wants you to succeed and is willing to help you. She explains things really clearly and I have loved being in class with her. As long as you do your work and keep up with the schedule you should be fine.

A very nice man, and a Professor who appreciates whenever you're participating and doing your best. One thing I didn't like was how 65% of the grade had to be determined only at the end of the
semester.

Taken as an intensive writing course, get ready to WRITE! But he isn't a harsh grader and a very kind professor. Is not very good on tech and saves all grades to the last-minute, but not to an unbearable amount. I love the class content, I just wish it was taught somewhat differently.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is great! Yes he doesn't post grades on canvas but he emails you your grade for each assignment (theres only a few) and its not hard at all to get an A! Just show up and listen/participate. There are no wrong answers and he is very kind and understanding. Highly, highly recommend this class!

This professor threw the students into the topic of the class in the harshest way possible. Not having a grade until the end of the semester combined with not having the study guide for the final until the 14th week out of 16 caused the entire class to fear for their grade. The course material was interesting but so poorly executed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never knew my grade the entire semester because he never posted anything. Final project and final exam. Told to us about final exam less than a week before it was scheduled.

Professor Adesokan is great! He is a really nice guy and is understanding of students and their other commitments. One thing he really prioritizes is class participation. He will stand there for 5 minutes until someone volunteers to answer the question, but you can really tell he cares about what he is teaching, and is knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: very funny and nice. Respects information students bring his seminar based class. Our big assignment was a GIS based creative project essentially and we had alot of freedom. LOTS OF READING tho but its all interesting

I never have taken the time to rate a professor on here, but Dr. Sarathi 100% deserves a 5! This was one of my favorite classes to take and he actually makes the lectures interesting! Another thing is that he really cares about his students! I would absolutely take this class again!

Dr. Sarathi is definitely one of the best professors I have ever had. He is very interested in what he is teaching and respects his students. He really cares about you and wants to make sure you will succeed in the class. He makes lectures interesting and is very funny. 10/10 recommend!!!

Dr. Sarathi is very easy to get along with but makes you read some pretty lengthy assignments. His tests aren't bad at all because he curves them. Just pay attention during lecture and take notes because there's a lot of info.
Dr Sarathi is a very intelligent and respectful professor. He is always open to questions and is very helpful. Also absolutely hilarious during class.

Akwasi is a great guy. He is really nice and funny. I love how he incorporated movie Mondays. It's just that sometimes he would talk fast on powerpoints. He doesn't post the slides so you gotta go to class or you'll miss the notes.

Ok!  Prof A.B. is awesome so just GO TO CLASS. Get to know him.  Listen to what he has to say because you are guaranteed to get either an A (if you truly earn it) or a B (if you attend class- he does take attendance everyday). If you haven't taken one of his classes, then you are crazy!!!

Dr. A.B. is probably one of the greatest professor's at Indiana University, because he teaches his students valuable morals, and it is blatantly obvious that he cares about his students, and he wants his students to do well! Overall, the class is taught in a way that seems extremely easy to follow.

Ridiculous test questions, its not that  they're difficult, just pointless. His lectures and class notes are just his rambling thoughts. He's never clear about your grade. We got out of class early. He does provide notes so textbooks are optional. He asks what you grade you want. i think he gives it to you as long as you have perfect attendance.

Very awesome class, if you go to all the lectures and discussions and at least try on the test he will reward you at the end of the semester with a good grade. He's a great professor and always wanted to help students when they needed help.

Has not given a student below a B- in the past three years for this class (and that's as far back as I looked up.) However, class is extremely tedious, the tests/quizzes are very difficult (if not meaningless...since lowest grade is a B), and I'm pretty sure I didn't learn a single thing in the class.

Class is a complete waste of time and made an interesting topic a boring and tedious one. Out of the entire semester, only 4 class session were lectures. The rest were him discussing what was to be on the midterm/final. Prof. is generally very unhelpful and although he only gives A's and B's, his grading is very unfair for those that actually work.
He gives his students either an A or a B in the class, but his tests and quizzes are hard. You feel like you are failing the whole semester. Very stressful course.

This is a good easy class! His tests are hard and confusing and I literally got D's and F's on them, but his first and middle initial is A.B. so he only gives out A's and B's in class! Also you basically don't have to go to the last 2 weeks of class because he curves your grade so you don't have to take the final. DO ITTT!
if you want an easy A, take his classes
he is real cool

This guy is condescending and full of himself and his class. The course is pointless. He drags everything out. It is not even hard content, he just likes to hear himself talk. I am convinced that he grades biasedly - he likes teacher's pets.
Yes his lectures are dull but the class is not that hard. Just study for the quizzes and midterm and pray you get a good group for the projects.

Very nice professor, but the class just isn't beneficial. The lectures are brain-numbing. I'm still trying to figure out what the point of this class is, I didn't learn a single thing. Take the other option for the credit.

Super nice but lectures are boring. Group projects aren't bad as long as you do you do your part and with a good group. Only hard thing about this class that made my grade go down were the quizzes and midterm exam, don't slack on those and actually study. Offers extra credit, USE THEM saved my grade. When you ask questions can give vague answers.
THATS MY GOAT

The first half of the class was a snooze-fest. The second half also was not good, however, easier than the first half. The group projects in this class saved. my grade because the quizzes and exams are not easy. Coming out of this class, I don't feel as though I have learned anything.

The first half of this class can sometimes feel mind-numbing learning about all kinds of modern technologies, but the second half is very hands-on and involves lots of group work, and becomes pretty fun. Frank is super super nice and will be there for you. Can *sometimes* be slow to respond to emails, but he is very caring overall.
First half of the class is confusing and annoying, second half is pretty fun. Akaiwa rambles a bit and makes it tough to focus but he's sweet and means well.

Professor Akaiwa is a really nice guy. He cares about his students and is passionate about the subject matter. However, his lectures are extremely boring. He rambles on a lot about random technologies that only he understands and gets super excited while the rest of the class just sits and listens. I feel like I did not learn a lot in S302.

Akaiwa began the semester assigning a group project over material the entire class had little understanding of. Exams are open note but still incredibly difficult, as he spends most lectures rambling on and on about random technologies that excite him. Fortunately, there are 4 projects at the end of the semester that saved my grade in this class...

Dry lectures but a super nice professor when you talk to him one on one. Group project heavy. Open note tests and quizzes that are still difficult because they test on small details. Get ready to Ctrl+F.

I've had Frank for K315 and S302. As a senior, he's one of my top 3 favorite professors I've had during my entire time at IU. He cares about your success as a student but also outside of academia and is always down to chat. Super willing to work with students. Down to earth. Keep up on the slides and homework and you'll do fine! He's very fair.

One of the worst professors Ive had in terms of communication and ability to read a classroom, currently working on the first project and have emailed him on 3 separate occasions looking for help and no replies. In the classroom he flies through the material and you can barely keep up with understanding the code and what it means, not good @ job
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the best professors that Kelley's has. Makes sure you fully know what is going on with examples and keeps class very entertaining. Highly recommend him for any class. Not to mention one great guy.
Very nice guy. He is willing to help his students succeed.Go to his office hours; it helped me a lot. If you do everything he tells you, you will do fine in the course.
Frank is really excited about the material. He is very flexible and wants every student to do well. Go to his office hours! He loves helping students out.

Frank is a really good guy once you get to know him.  He absolutely knows his stuff, but he dumbs it down a lot in class so it can be boring at times.  I don't know how useful lectures are, but you definitely have to put in the time outside of class if you expect to learn anything.

I chose to take this class as an elective for my supply chain major because I like computers and I like business so I thought it was an easy match.  Boy was I wrong!  The class requires alot of time, is boring, and is not easy.  XML and Process mapping are extrememly boring. I've gone into office hours but would NOT recommend this class to anyone!
Extremely boring although he seems like a nice guy...X201 is just completely useless and the exams have the most irrelevant questions on them

Frank is useless and incompetent.  Class is not relevant to the final, he just rambles about pointless stuff.  You have to memorize the book to get good grades on the lecture, get your 15 bonus points and stop going to the lecture class.  One of the worst teachers i have come across so far at iu
One word: Boring.
No Comments
Ya he's nice.  But he really thinks he knows more than he does.
He is the nicest professor ever and is always willing to help students. He is also willing to compsomise due dates and is very generous!

Dr. Anderson was an incredible professor, she made hard topics easy to understand. She also gave leeway to students who had demanding schedules, and the biweekly quizzes truly helped me test my understanding throughout the course.
Fun labs and the professor seems to really care about her students and their success
Dr Anderson was organized and set up the class so well. The resources given were informational and helped with learning.

This class was manageable with clear expectations and organization. Grading criteria were provided, and labs made up most of the workload. TAs were helpful throughout the course. Overall, the experience was okay, though it wasn't a course I would take again.

I loved this lab. This class was so interesting and also very easy. It's extremely fun and also easy to follow and understand. Honestly, just show up and you will get an A. This lab makes me excited for future labs to come!
The labs were really well organized and interesting. Professor Anderson checked in multiple times through the semester which I appreciated.
She wasn't directly in the lab but the way she sets up assignments is super easy to understand and she is always checking on students to make sure everything is going alright.
I can't say enough good things about this professor and class! She cared so much about us as her students and our learning. The course set-up was perfect!

Although not a super big part of the class she was very helpful and available for questions or if issues came up during a lab. The course was set up for quick grading and was very easy to succeed at if you put in some effort.

You don't see Professor Anderson very often during lab, but she's readily available to meet with students. There are lot's of extra credit opportunities, and honestly not that much work to do outside of lab. The labs were fun and AI's this sem were spectacular!

I would def recommend this class. Outside of lab assignments, there wasn't a lot of work to do. Most can get done the day of lab. Dr. Anderson was great and her TA's this semester were equally awesome.
Dr. Anderson was very helpful and open to discuss any questions that I had. She was also easy to get ahold of when needed, plus her TAs were equally amazing.

Professor Anderson is awesome! I loved the course setup. Watching the lecture videos before class and then doing the assignments together during class helped me learn way more than I would have on my own.
The labs were fun and interesting. Although I didn't interact with her much, Dr. Anderson was very helpful when I did reach out.
Fun class... mostly led by AI.
The class is pretty much led by your lab AI, but the class itself was fairly easy. The quizzes were kind of hard but outside of that you could easily get 100s on everything else

I LOVED this class! Dr. Anderson made a topic that I never thought could be interesting into something I genuinely looked forward to learning about every week. Dr. Anderson is super personable and understanding. She even learned everyone's names!  The course was so well organized but also flexible and laid back.

Professor Anderson actually cares about student learning! Class time was primarily used to work on assignments as a class and to discuss concepts students were struggling with. I loved the flipped classroom style, and the flexibility it offered. She emphasizes improvement in her class which I found to be super encouraging.

I can't say enough good things about Professor Anderson! I am currently in her evolution class, and she goes above and beyond for her students. Class is super engaging and has covered really interesting topics so far. I am looking forward to the rest of the semester.

I would rather be dropped into a bucket of poisonous snakes and scorpions than take this class. It is extremely difficult, she is very scatterbrained, and the tests are extremely hard. She is also not open to any feedback.

reviews.comment: I found her to be generally unlikable. She would sometimes make inappropriate jokes. On top of that her class was generally unorganized and her lectures were very hard to follow because she would jump between topics often and quickly. Her exams took a very long time to complete. I tell the people I care about to not take a class with this prof.
What is fun? Her definition of fun can be a lot different from normal people. I strongly recommend not to take her class.

Useless ever. I know Andrea is passionate about what she is teaching, but it does not mean that she is good at it. She teaches something that is not necessary. One more thing that makes students hard to understand is that she goes back and forth. Her lecture is not organized, her exam is too difficult, and the problem is she is so proud of it.

Never take her class. Especially A422 is an elective course. First, too many homework Second, she is so proud of teaching students in a difficult way Third, who schedules an exam on Saturday from 4 pm to 7 pm?
