reviews.comment: Bro is always high and loves to laugh

Easy Kelley GPA booster. Class can be informational if you want to learn, but all quizzes are open note. Also, attendance is based on a code, so by the end of the semester no one will be in class. Professor Arcot is a great guy and I would highly recommend you taking it with him!

Nice professor, very approachable about anything business/finance related. Lectures are mandatory and can be boring sometimes. All exams and quizzes are open-note. Ensure you understand the financial problem calculations, as those make/break your grade.

Very good teacher and willing to meet outside of class for anything business related. Easy A. Lectures can be boring. I recommend getting to know him. Cares about his students. Class material is also very helpful so try to pay attention if you can.
Super chill and sweet guy. F100 is pretty easy as a whole and the only reason I didn't finish with an A is because I missed a lot of classes but Prof Arcot was a consistent positive of the class.

Professor Arcot is an excellent professor and you can just tell that he loves his job. He is there for you and is happy to help you at any point. You learn a lot in the class as long as you pay attention and it is definitely a class you should take if you find Finance interesting.
Amazing professor!!
great teacher, very nice guy, exams are open note and not difficult.

Boring lectures but Arcot's a really nice guy. Make sure to try and actually learn the content so the quizzes and practice problems make sense. Most ppl cut it rly close with a final grade of 93 or 93.1, so don't slack during the semester. Trust, if you want to get A's on assignments and in the class its best to be able to solve problems YOURSELF.
Prof Arcot was a great professor but his lectures are pretty boring. You can't get a reach of him outside of class and he does not reply to any emails.

Not to be dramatic, but I would die for Prof. Arcot. He's the absolute best and it's impossible to not smile in his lectures. F100 was more focused on learning the basics of finance and about careers in finance, it wasn't super work heavy, he genuinely just wants to help you learn.
Professor Arcot the goat he really loves his job and is always energetic. Plus his accent is fire. "Finance!"

Professor Arcot is extremely funny. He often mixes witty jokes into his lectures, which make the relatively mundane content bearable. He is quite understanding, but can seem a bit direct or a little too honest. He encourages students to participate, although most rarely do. He's also always willing to chat after class about finance or any material.

Love this professor. Not many people laugh at his jokes but I'm usually dying on the inside during his lectures. Easy A and definitely a good class to take if you are unsure about choosing finance as a major and want to get a basic intro to technicals.

He is a very funny professor. His exams are very similar to the practice exams with different numbers. He posts the completed slides and Excel spreadsheets from the lecture. There are Tophat questions for attendance and correctness, but he gives you the answer before you submit. The exams are on Canvas, and you can use Excel.  Take him for F305!
unc status
Best prof at iu!
Arcot is the best choice for f100, lenient with grading and pretty friendly. This class does help if you're unsure about choosing finance. Extremely easy to get above a B.

Arcot is a great teacher. Easy grader, good lectures, and a good understanding of the material. Try to go to class often so you don't miss content. He appreciates understanding how to teach the class better. If you miss a grade, just ask him. No harm.

Awesome professor that really makes lectures interesting. This class has no sit-down exams and all graded work is open book. F100 covers a wide breadth of topics but Prof. Arcot makes the content fun to listen to and easy to understand in an ELI5 way, even for those with zero prior background in finance.

This class is not much work. Such an easy A. The lectures can be drawn out but you can tell the professors care and know about what they are talking about. There are bi-weekly quizzes and a final but all are open note and done online outside of class. There are quite a few group projects.
Professor was very kind and caring, participation/attendance mattered a lot and made a big difference in grade. grades are all based on participation, final group project, quizzes, and exams

This dude was a horrible professor. I don't know for what reason but he loves to give out low grades. If you don't show you are deeply passionate about what he is teaching, he will use it against you. Very unorganized and frustrating class.

Took this class expecting it to be fun and interesting, it was far from that. I had Professor Arnaudo for the Arts of War class in the now-defunct IFS program. In general, participation, attendance, and engagement matter most. Simply stay away. And find your Coll-C credit somewhere else. How this class fulfills it is beyond me.

Marco was really interesting to listen to. He made a lot of the lectures super interesting, and was very animated. He did require a lot of participation which I wasn't too happy about, and he was kind of a tough grader. However, overall I feel like Marco made the content of the class more fun.

Prof. Arnaudo was amazing for the Arts of War class in Intensive Freshman Seminar. This man has a true passion for history and war. Highly recommend taking this course, you legit get to play board games during class. There is a lot of reading but that's what you get with 3 credits over 3 weeks. If you read and participate, its an easy A.

Dr Arnaudo is very knowledgeable, and a fun guy. The topic can be way more engaging than I at first thought. Almost no absences or tardies are tolerated, and the reading is a lot every week, with quizzes every Friday. More demanding than you might expect

reviews.comment: Cloak and Dagger with Prof Arnaudo was the best class I've taken at IU. The course is well-built, with one concept leading seamlessly into the next. Arnaudo gives you all the information you need to know in order to succeed during his lectures, so don't miss them and take notes!

reviews.comment: Alright so this class has a stupid amount of reading for a 100 level. Yes, they're fun spy novels and movies, but if you are taking other heavy classes, don't take this one. It's a novel, maybe two, per week .. plus a movie. There is a quiz every week and it's not critical thinking, it's quote quizzes. Disappointed.

I thought it was a fine course, but not very clear and good for a critical approaches. There is a LOT of reading, but I enjoyed most of the books (not all). It's a hit or miss if you'll like it, or not. Lectures don't completely supplement the quizzes/final, but are interesting. Arnaudo is fun and is very enthusiastic about the topics.

For a critical approaches course this class did not do much critical thinking. We were mainly evaluated on our ability to recall characters from the book. This class was also had a very heavy work load. There was a novel to read every week, and a movie to watch every week, and almost a quiz every week.

Dr. Arnaudo poorly structured this course, and as a result it was an extremely disappointing class. The lecture is not related to the reading, is not particularly interesting, and performs a schizophrenic overview of topics that are semi-related to the class. The discussion sections were useless - just asking to repeat what was said in lecture.
Awesome, funny teacher.  Interesting lectures and great books & films.  Attendance taken randomly, but not too often.  If you need a topics course, choose his!
worst professor ever!!!

Best class ever is Cloak and Dagger! Do yourself a favor and take this class, the books are good and the films are to die for. Professor Arnaudo may look like Mr. Bean and dress all in black every day but he's still a great teacher.
The man keeps you interested every minute of class.  He's Italian and looks like Mr. Bean.  Cloak and Dagger was the best class I've ever taken.

I really like Prof. Arnaudo.  His lectures add alot of interesting background information to the novels we read.  I would definitely recommend taking "Cloak and Dagger" as a TOPICS class because the literature and lectures were both interesting.

Fantastic Professor. He's here to help you, mae you better, and he truly cares about his students. His lessons are easy to follow, the information is always relevant, and he is always very respectful and kind to students. I hate math, and I'd take his class again anytime. Truly a great man and teacher!
Very good teacher. Cares about students and remembers names somehow without interacting with him. Do not talk while he teaches

This prof is confident, engaging, explains stuff clearly and is very responsive. It's too bad the course itself is basically derivative gen-ed fodder for people who need a math credit (me) because it could far more productive with better topics.

The professional is very knowledgeable and knows how to effectively teach concepts! Only complaint is that there is weekly homework but if you know what you're doing, should take less than one hour + is good practice. Would STRONGLY recommend!

Although he was my lecturer and not recitation leader, he made it so that we were understanding the material in class. With 100% of homework and 100% of quizzes completed,  you are looking for at least a C, even if you do bad on tests. Easy grade!

Dr. Lahiri wasn't my specific lecturer but was the director for my class. Have fun teaching yourself everything from YouTube videos. Mini-Lectures are boring and slow. On top of all the excessive readings! Way too much for a level 100 course.
TA's are WAY too harsh on grading (I had Kim Bryan)! You think you understand it until your grade drops a ton!

reviews.comment: Art was a good teacher. His lectures could get boring sometimes, and I once even feel asleep during a video lecture. But, his class is very easy. It relies heavily on discussion posts and quizzes (all of the answers are on quizlet). But if I could offer one piece of advice: STUDY FOR THE FINAL because its all short answer. Make a study guide.
This online class should be an easy-A, but the final is 2 hours and is all open answer. Hardest final I took this semester and didn't do well because I ran out of time, WOULD NOT RECOMMEND.

I really enjoyed this online class. He's grading criteria is clear and he gives great feedback.  Most of the mods are open at the beginning of the semester, so you can do the mods at your own pace--which I enjoy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Long lectures that can be interesting sometimes. Lots of discussion assignments and other writing assignments. Was sorta boring but not too bad. Made me feel like intro sociology is full of stuff I already kinda know.

Took this class because I had to of my major and thought it was going to be so interesting, but it was awful. His lectures are extremely boring and he rambles on and on. The assignments were annoying and somewhat pointless. I wouldn't take the class unless you have you. If you do take it. Make sure you attend lecture and try and take good notes....
Prof. Alderson is a great teacher.  He is very knowledgeable and patient, and if you don't understand something he will go the extra mile to make sure you do for the test.

He's knowledgeable but can't seem to bring it down to understanding terms. Closed off, unapproachable, not talkative. Difficult way of presenting info and lots of reading to do each week. Tests seems easy but come out against you. He's happy if everyone get's a C+ to B on a test which is the real problem in my opinion. I advise a different course.

As long as you show up to class, take notes during lecture, and do the assigned readings, you will do fine in this course. The exams aren't easy, but they're not difficult either. He provides you with study guides for each of his exams that are a general outline of lectures. He's a great guy, and I would definitely recommend his class.

He's a great professor. He is friendly and very clear. He expects you to take notes directly from his lectures and will not post them on oncourse. You have to come to class and pay attention. Tests are a little difficult but not impossible. I think he's a good professor though and very informative!

Prof. Alderson is a great teacher. He makes the class super interesting. He does lecture quite a lot but keeps it open for spontaneous class discussions as well. If you do the readings regularly, you'll do well in the class.

This class was hard for me. I got away with a B but that's because of attendance, his "papers" and readings. His exams are pretty hard and extremely wordy! His papers are a lot of busy work. If you love Sociology then I guess take the class, but if you don't have to DON'T. attend class, do all readings b/c of mini pop questions from reading
Social inequality class enjoyable, nice teacher, approachable, weekly readings assigned, three papers, three exams

It might just be me, but this class was very difficult. Alderson is very helpful and is willing to help you out if you need it. The tests are extremely difficult but some topics (last third) are really interesting.
Repetitive lectures.  Would be more interesting if it involved some thing other than him lecturing on the same point for an hour and fifteen.
art is a boring teacher.  he will stretch a half hour lecture into an hour and fifteen minute lecture.  pretty good teacher tho, kinda interesting.
Wonderful professor- best class I ever had.

Readings can be a bit thick, but the subject matter is interesting. Prof is a very good *lecturer* which can be rather boring--not much discussion or class interaction. But if you go to class and keep up with the readings, studying for the exams will be easy and you'll do well.
Very tough. Not an enjoying class, stay away.

Professor Averitt is a newer prof. and you can tell. She tries really hard to connect with her students, and I definitely recommend attending office hours to discuss concepts or writing assignments. She basically goes over exactly what the reading discusses, but if you participate/ask more questions, she'll go into more depth. Very approachable.

Super passive aggressive and condescending. It's like she doesn't want to hear anything her students have to say. I took another class with her before this and hoped that she would be better around this time, but she wasn't. Sucks because she seems super knowledgeable and intelligent but I honestly think she just doesn't enjoy teaching.

You can tell that she's passionate about the subject but she's not good at teaching. Found myself very confused in class and ended up studying most of the material by myself. She's pretty understanding.

Pretty hard given that it was a 100 level class. The lectures and discussion were a waste of time and most of the concepts covered were purely theoretical. However, there are a lot of drops/extra credit that are being offered which bumped my grade up by a whole letter almost
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I can tell Ms. Averitt loves what she does, and that's always a great teaching quality to have, however, this class is pretty difficult. Unfortunatley I don't believe she is the best at explaining things. I felt I had to teach myself a lot outside of class

The professor is actually really nice, and if you're interested, you could go to her office hours and talk as much as you want. This class however, it's particularly hard. Critical thinking is such a broad skill that one could possess but her way of teaching as well as lecture materials seemed rather confusing. Beware of memorizing key terms!
Professor Baker was a very chill and jolly professor who always has a smile on his face. While Q295 isn't very interesting, he does the best to make the class enjoyable.

Baker is a great guy and very, very jolly. Maybe too jolly... But in all honestly I really hated this class but it is required for CASE, so whatever but he is a pretty good professor and is super nice. Very little real work for this class.
Prof. Baker was amazing. He's a very kind and understanding person who gives great career advice, and as long as you put in the low effort work outside of class you should be fine.

Professor Baker was always super kind and shared helpful career advice! It was easy to ask him for help or clarification, and he loved hearing peoples' interests. He was very knowledgeable and cared a lot about the wellbeing of his students.

She is a really good teacher if you take an extra step and participate in class and ask for feedback. She did change the syllabus halfway through the class to make it where you had to ask questions in class to get participation credit, but as long as you ask about one per class you get full credit. Not too hard of a grader just be smart about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor changed participation requirement 3 classes before semester end. Each student had to ask 5 in-depth questions. With 40 students, this meant 200+ questions in 3 classes - impossible. Grade based on participation, final group presentation, 2 exams, and peer evaluation. Do not recommend.
Do not recommend

The grading criteria is completely hidden from students. She never uses clear rubrics, except on participation. Almost nobody in my class received the grade they deserved, and everyone felt like they were hopeless for getting a good score. The average for participation in this class should not be 50%, projects should not average 80% or lower. It

Do NOT take. She grades unnecessarily harsh, almost as if she's looking for reasons to take points off. 5% of your grade is participation and she grades it harshly but there's not many chances to really "participate" in class. Way too much work for a 1.5 credit class.

Do not take for D271. Went into final presentation + report with 100% and finished with a 90% in the class. 30% of grade is the presentation, and no matter how much you align your work with the rubric, she will give a low grade. No one in my class finished with an A

She is challenging to reach outside of the classroom. Moreover, she has not updated the grade book and has already submitted final grades without making a formal announcement. Canvas states that my grade is an A (94.06%), and she submitted an A- to the registrar.

Rubric didn't even match the class. Submitted our final grades without even telling us our grades to our final project and assignments. Does not know how to structure a class and doesn't care about any of the students. Do not take her, I would recommend taking another section over her any day of the week.

This class was awful, and the expectations were ridiculous for a 1.5 credit course. There were 2 exams, 2 team presentations and a 5-page single spaced paper in addition to weekly quizzes. I would avoid taking D271 with her at all costs as there are much easier options.

She's nice at first but after the first exam, she ignored my emails and acted annoyed with us. First exam class average, 50 questions with 50 minutes to complete, was 72%. Doesnt require attendance but has 2 group projects and group members dont show up. Randomly changes correct/incorrect answers after exams are submitted. Dont take this class.

1. Tough quizzes need a lot of readings
2. Tough exams, 50 questions in 50 mins with more than four choices. There are also questions with no correct answers
3. Tough grade in presentation. Our whole group is deducted about 7 percent of the total grade in the presentation, which means you need to get FULL SCORE IN ALL  QUIZES AND EXAM to get A

Should not be a professor. Has a disorganized Canvas site (syllabus % weights don't match up with what's given, hard to access rubrics), and takes FOREVER to grade. Does not have a rubric out to grade presentations, which is unfair when points are lost. No curve on specific exams and I do not know a single person that has an A. Avoid at all costs.

She is a knowledgeable professor and cares about what she is teaching. Great person and she is quite fun to have as a teacher. However, in our course (4210), the exams took unreasonable amounts of time and extensive research to write the essay questions. Prompts are way too long and confuse you more about the response. Lectures are unorganized.

Dr. AuBuchon is really fun. Her exams aren't easy, but if you pay good attention in class, study from the notes, and read the book, you will definitely get a good grade. I learned a lot from her class!

Taking K300? Avoid her at all costs. Lecture is so unorganized, labs are hard, she randomly springs homework or quizzes on you, and worst of all, you don't feel like you learn anything! If you go into office hours, she'll help you and is SO nice, but then you get bad grades on the homework that she answered every single question with you on. Avoid.

Overall very unorganized, and you really don't learn at all. Many emails were responded to weeks later or not at all. Doesn't have time to meet with you if you can't go to office hours. Doesn't show for scheduled 1-1 meetings. Teacher shows up late to class. Doesn't really teach content in class, but expects you to know everything after one class.

She comes up with class activities, materials, and changes things last minute multiple times throughout. She also expects everybody to entirely understand the class material after one lecture, or one explanation and she doesn't understand why we havent gotten the material down yet. (We have other classes and a social life...)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor A was awesome! I loved her class. It is definitely a harder class, but it is very interesting. You will need to read the chapters in order to pass the tests and you will need to go to class to get the lecture slides. She does offer a lot of extra credit and easy point assignments. I would definitely take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She rambles on and on during class, so you have no idea what to write down.  She goes super fast, and of course she doesn't post her lectures online.  Her TA grades SO harshly!! On the first assignment the average was a 60, and her tests are all confusing.  At least all of the questions have more than one right answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is terrible. I have taken her class twice now and they are the worse psych grades I've received. She grades crazy hard for no reason and she leaves rude remarks on your papers. She acts like she's a 17 year old girl and often gets distracted and talks about nonsense. Her tests are intense and even her "easy assignments" are far from easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best teacher ever! She is so passionate about the subject and goes the extra mile to make sure students understand the material. That being said, she doesn't hand out grades; you have to do the readings and attend class for a good grade! Love her personality an teaching though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a down right rude person, if you're not one of her favorites at the beginning you will hate the class all semester long. One of the most difficult introductory courses there is, according to our own TA. She doesn't care about her students, does the bare minimum with them. 10/10 don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Professor AuBuchon is such a good teacher. You can tell that she is really passionate about Psychology and teaching which makes the 100 times more interesting/enjoyable. She's really funny and makes the class really comfortable. You won't need your book as long as you go to the lectures because she covers everything for the exams in class.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Didn't spend much time on any particular topic but memory. Having the results of the election in her class wasn't that fun - tends to moralize. Average in every sense of the term.
Did not at all enjoy this class. Extremely difficult exams and quizzes due to confusing and unclear questions. Would not recommend friends to take her classes.
She is terrible.  This class was 100 times harder than it needed to be.  all my friends taking this class with other professors had easy A's, I studied like crazy all the time to get a B

Read the assigned readings before exams. Make flashcards, basically a vocab memorizing class. Didn't particularly enjoy class material, a lot of useless info on lecture slides, rarely went to lecture and did decent in the class. Great extra credit opportunities, do them!!!!!

Professor A is cool, definitely knows her information, gives good lectures, but this class was much harder than it needed to be for an intro class. My friend was taking a class with a different professor and told me the professor said that Professor A teaches this class at a 300 level. Go to class, read the readings for the week, you'll be good.

I really really like Dr. A and think she's so passionate about the class and what she's teaching. The actual class i thought was really hard though and made me feel like I shouldn't be a psych major. I studied for WEEKS for the tests and still didn't do well. Questions are tricky. But I did love the class and her teaching.

Slides are basically useless and she consistently goes over on class time. "I don't care if you remember this on the test, I care if you remember it next semester."  She thinks class is for all pysch majors when most take it as a pre-req. Intro courses are supposed to be easy, but not this one. Upperclassmen, beware.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is such an amazing professor!  She genuinely cares about the success and learning of her students, and she makes it easy to integrate the required material into your everyday life.  I'm trying to get my next psych course taught by her just because I enjoy her class so much!

This may be one of my worst experiences with a teacher at IU. She is very unprofessional and is very rude to be honest. An introductory psychology class should be an easy A, but she creates her questions on quizzes and tests to trick students not to actually test students on if they understand the material. Very rude, would not recommend.

She was such a great professor! She teaches in a way that is fairly easy to understand and she always able to answer questions. You do have to work, though, but it is that way with any class. I would definitely take another class from her again. Would recommend to anyone taking this class!
I thought she was fantastic. Fav professor so far. Just show up and pay attention. Don't bother to buy the book though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Absolutely avoid at all costs. She is interested in her students failing rather than succeeding. She is very rude and not caring towards students and seems to be power hungry. This is an INTRO course and she pawns it off saying the questions are "conceptual".

Doesn't curve ANYTHING. First exam average in class was a 51% on it and she still wouldn't curve it. Barely does anything as a professor. Her slideshows are very disorganized. Seems as though she wants you to fail and is very uncaring and rude even when you come talk to her and get help from her during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Considering that this class was an introductory course I expected the weekly quizzes to be less intimidating than they actually were. Her grading capabilities lack and she may be extremely interesting she is extremly picky about how she likes things done.

Dr. AuBuchon was a great teacher.  She made Statistics easy to learn, and I am not a math person.  She focused on the concepts behind statistics and their applications in the real world.  She was really helpful in her office hours and was very good at explaining things in different ways if I didn't understand initially.

Does the bare-minimum of her job, which is to lecture and give tests (four of them, and they are your entire grade). Lectures are energetic and you get the sense that she really loves psychology, but she is not interested in whether you're learning or not- she just wants a captive audience to listen to her. Doesn't seem to like students frankly.

The best professor I have had at IU so far. She was always there to help me whether that be after class or during office hours. She is young and can easily relate to all students. No quizzes or homework, plenty of extra credit and she drops your lowest test grade. If you have to take P101, take it with AuBuchon!

This class wasn't bad at all. Professor AuBuchon really works with the students. There are lots of extra credit opportunities. Just read the chapters thoroughly and take notes (or get them  from someone better than you) and you'll do absolutely fine.

She is not a good teacher. Her lecturers aren't clear, her slides are barely useful at all and the material is incredibly disorganized. Most of the points for the semester are crammed into the last two weeks of class (extremely stressful). Don't take stats with her if you can help it.
Knies was a very solid Econ professor. He is very young and can relate to the students. He explains concepts very well and tries to get everyone to understand. Only thing is he will not curve tests.
Best teacher I've ever had, as long as you do the work and show up to class, he'll make sure you pass 10/10

Good professor, nice, and energetic. Lectures directly from the textbook. You can easily pass the class by reading the textbook and not going to lectures. Sometimes his lectures were more confusing than the textbook explanations so I would look in the textbook for more clarification.

Prof. Knies was a great professor. It's clear that he's passionate about the subject and his lectures are more tolerable than most professors. He is able to simplify difficult concepts and is always open to helping students. Prof. Knies is a lot better than some of the other Micro professors at IU.

Prof. Knies is a great economics teacher, but since this class was asynchronous and lecture heavy, it was difficult to stay motivated. This class is based on 6 exams with homework only taking up a small portion of your grade, so I did not receive the grade I wanted. Even though this was online, I could tell he really does care about his students.

This professor is highly intelligent, humorous, and explains things eloquently. With that said, I would avoid taking this if you don't HAVE to. You have to remain locked in at all times, and keeping up with readings is nightmarish if you want to do it legit and not skip your way through.
Lectures are heavy and there's a lot of reading. Attendance matters. Craiutu is extremely knowledgeable and passionate and makes content interesting. I would highly recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Craiutu is as real as it gets. If you don't want to really learn don't take his class. This is what you come to college for, get smart.

Great Professor. I strongly recommend this course if you are interested in political philosophy. Readings are really tough if you have zero interest. Professor Craiutu is great at lecturing and keeps lecture entertaining. Avoid if uninterested otherwise go for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have mixed feelings. Most readings were dense and very challenging but, at least to me, super interesting. Lectures included a lot of student participation and didn't have enough structure for me. Exams were all open-note, timed with short answer/essay questions that felt like topics for 3-4 page papers, and often wanted very particular answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Aurelian is very knowledgeable about the topics he discussed in class and was able to incorporate some comedy into his lectures, which made things easier to digest. Attendance is a huge part of the grade so make sure you're there. Quizes were the rest of the class (2 quizzes, midterm, and final) and all were in the same format where you chose Q's.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only take this is youre really into learning about the HISTORY of politics. The professor was nice but I found this class very boring. The readings were long and dreadful. I felt as if this class was quite difficult for an intro level course. Maybe course would be more engaging in person?

Professor Craiutu is the best kind of professor. Though he asks for a lot and is prone to grading papers fairly tough, he is incredibly constructive and helpful. I am so grateful to have had Prof. Craiutu this past semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Craiutu is the best professor I've had at Indiana University so far. He is very passionate about his courses and the content. Leads excellent class conversations, allowing students to openly discuss their views and values with complete respect for varying opinions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Craiutu really cares about the subject matter and his students. Do the readings, show up and pay attention to lecture, and be a decent writer to do well in the class.

Criautu is a great prof he definitely likes what he does and wants you to learn. The material for the class is really dry though, and theres little breadth in the backgrounds of the tests. Its all the same type even though they sometimes disagree. Cant really blame him for that I guess, its a lower level class so he likely has less control

He is a very entertaining professor and makes the class fun and interesting. The readings were super long and they were assigned at each class, so it was easy to get behind. You will not be able to pass the class if you don't do the readings. If you are interested in political science, I would recommend this class.

Funny, and incredibly focused on student learning and growth. Had to read 60-80 pages per class, sometimes more, but lectures were always interesting and the readings he selected were great. Takes attendance each class, but makes it clear when in-class participation is mandatory. Several essay quizzes and tests, not super easy to get As.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is essential for anyone who wants to call themselves learned. Craiutu cares about students' learning. He doesn't go easy; there's 100 pages of reading each week. But the upside is you will come out of this class a better student and a better person. Seriously, if you're only going to take one Poli Sci class at IU, take 381 with Craiutu.

Craiutu is a very good professor. He genuinely cares about students learning rather than memorizing material. There are TONS of reading and this class requires lots of work. But, the quizzes/tests are very fair and it is possible to attain a good grade on the quizzes. But, he doesn't ever give 100% on the quizzes. I really recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Only professor at IU I have been willing to get on rate my professor and write a review for. Class is very fair, not as difficult as its made out to be as long as you put in some work and pay attention in lectures. Class will have you engaged the whole time and you'll learn more in this class than any other political science course. Favorite prof
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really liked his class. Very difficult, so if you're looking for a gen ed. credit I'd look elsewhere. You live and die by reading what's assigned and taking good notes, since that's all you can use for the difficult quizzes. My AIs for this class weren't the greatest and were very inconsistent graders so be wary of that. Otherwise, great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For an intro level class, one of the best lecturers I've had at IU. With a class of 100+ participation should be difficult but he handles it well. Discussions are productive and funny at times. Content isn't incredibly difficult to grasp but quiz grades are very reliant on who the AI's are. Would take again
My favorite professor by far, Mr. Craiutu is an amazing person and an amazing teacher. I have learned so much from him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Craiutu is an amazing teacher, and gives the best lectures. Really have learned a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing!
Amazing proffesor. Would really recommend!!!!
Amazing lectures. Great proffesor.
Professor Craiutu is an amazing teacher to work with, makes you work to achieve goals in the best way, and overall is my favorite!

As a business major, I took this class to satisfy an A&H credit. I found the material to be challenging but rewarding. The class required lots of reading and note-taking on difficult texts. Professor had interesting and entertaining lectures. Professor missed class a couple of times and left the lectures up to the teaching assistants.

As a political science major, this is my favorite professor at IU. I've heard people complain that Classical Political Thought was hard, but I don't know if a single person has called it a bad class. Personally, I felt like I learned so much and was engaged the entire time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took Y105 with him, really enjoyed the class. You only get one unexcused absence, which kinda sucks, but the lectures are actually pretty interesting. He's a really funny guy and makes some boring stuff interesting. Tons of reading, and you have to take good notes for the quizzes/exams (they're open note, but you NEED your notes to pass).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Aurelian is an amazing professor, and I have learned a lot from him!

Professor Craiutu is excellent at breaking down concepts in political theory and explaining them. His lectures are engaging and he really opens the floor for student discussion. He's also very accessible outside of office hours, and I can't stress using those enough. He's been very helpful and and given me great advice for my grad school search.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the best Professors at IU. Thought provoking, inspiring, and challenging for sure. Do not expect to get a respectable grade in his class if you are not going to class or doing the readings. Reasonable amount of readings and assignments considering the courses he teaches.

Best professor I've ever had. Amazing lectures, engaging, thoughtful material, and makes you a better student. I wish I could take every class of his. There is a lot of reading, but do not let that keep you from taking the class. He always goes over it in the lectures and in office hours to help you understand it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This seminar course goes over the most important texts in Western political thought. The professor is super knowledgeable and also very interesting. He takes care of students' different research interests and major backgrounds. Generally he leads the discussions well. Sometimes his interpretation of ideas seems not deep and profound enough.
Amazing professor. Really cares about the material and his students. If you are willing to do your part, you won't regret taking his class.

The texts are often extremely difficult to read since some of them are published as they were originally written in the 17 century. Lectures are super interesting, but you have to thoroughly read and re-read every page, take notes and actually spend an immense amount of time "digesting" the readings. Writing skills are important, tests are essays
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Craiutu really cares about the material he's teaching and wants students to be engaged. He's also pretty funny. There's a decent amount of reading but it's not too difficult. I liked the course because it covered things we still debate today (e.g. democracy, freedom) but showed how people's ideas about them have changed over time.

Treats students like adults, let us play a major role in discussions. Just be sure to read. He provided good background, and made lectures entertaining. Respectful of dissenting views. He also did a good job incorporating current events into the class without compromising the material. It's nice to have a professor who takes ideas seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Wow what a fantastic professor. Took this class just to fulfill an A&H and he ended up inspiring me to change my whole academic route. Great selection of texts, you get out of it as much as you put in though. If you want an A, you'll get an A. His graders were kind of annoying and arbitrary in their grading but nothing that couldn't be disputed.

Good professor but class was way too difficult for a 100 level. Readings were hard to understand and assigned every day ranging from 40-100 pages + notes. Do not take if you're just looking for a fun and interesting class. I ended with an okay grade but stressed the entire semester about it.
Class is hard, prof. does a lot to help you though. Still very hard for a 100 level class.

Absolutely amazing professor, absolutely amazing class. This is NOT an easy class by any means, but it is definitely worth it regardless. You'll learn a lot from the readings and prof. Half of the grade was participation & attendance, one quarter final presentation, and one quarter your reading log. Put effort into the reading log. LOTS of reading.

This class was difficult and required a lot of work but was absolutely not impossible. I ended doing very well in the class because I put in a ton of effort but it definitely paid off. The readings are really challenging but the quizzes are not too bad and the grading is extremely fair. If you put in solid effort into this class you will fine.

You'll walk out of at the end of this class with a fair grade that reflects the effort you put in. A lot of reading, but keep a good reading log and you'll be fine. 6-7 quizzes are given with your top four scores counting, along with a mid-term and final, all of which you can use your reading log on. An extra credit quiz was also offered at the end

The difficulty level of this class isn't due to the professor- it's due to the fact that you're reading ancient texts that may not seem as clear to us as modern day readers. As long as you listen in class and keep a reading log with adequate quotes, this class shouldn't prove to be impossible as some have previously stated.

Craiutu is a good one: he gives thought-provoking lectures, knows the subject thoroughly, and is passionate about the material. He did have a habit of giving assignments at random, which was annoying. But he respected everyone's viewpoint, and was often very funny as well. He's like the Pericles of PolSci professors. I recommend him to you.

Craiutu is an amazing professor. He should be on a stump teaching near Athens. But he is willing to talk over any issues you have, he is very understanding, very passionate, and knows his field very well. He is one of two professors who have shaped my college career with their lectures, and I cannot recommend him enough. If you care, he'll deliver.

As a lecturer, he is great and brings ancient issues full circle to modern day events. It's impossible to have any idea how you're doing in the class, however, because he does not enter grades and sometimes mentions curving grades at the end. There's little feedback, so I felt as though I didn't improve as the semester progressed.
Great Professor. He made class very interesting and was always willing to answer a question and help out. Definitely one of the best professors I've had at IU

Absolutely awesome. He is always willing to answer questions during his lecture.  His lectures are well structured and his tests are not too difficult if you come prepared. Do the readings and make sure to have complete reading logs. You will not pass the class otherwise.

I took y382 and y281 with him and got B+'s in both.  He follows the great books/classic liberal arts approach.  You will read Locke, Tocqueville, Machiavelli, Plato, Rousseau, Rothbard, Mises, Hayek, Marx, Mill, etc.  Just read the readings (you will be doing yourself a favor and not just for the class) and bring the main points to class.
Excellent professor. Homework is very time consuming and consists of heavy reading and comprehensive reading logs. Class is interesting and mandatory.
You need to read, participate, and keep a reading log in order to do well in the class. That's it.

Professor is awesome. You'll feel like you're doing bad at first, but he gives out chances for extra credit at the end. You'll read great works you'd probably be too lazy to otherwise. Sometimes the reading is hard to stay on top of but manageable (and logging quotes). Participate, and you'll own the class.

Professor Craiutu is very intelligent and has a sense of humor. This is a difficult course; 3rd-and-4th-year political science majors said this course was as difficult as their 300-level classes. There is lots and lots and lots of reading, but if you put in the time it isn't that bad, and it's worth it.

He makes you work hard, but you will learn a lot if you keep up with the reading and the reading log. He gives people the grade they deserve - there was a lot of opportunity for extra credit. He is very intelligent and funny, he really understands the material. The class discussions are incredible. If you're interested in the topic, you'll love it.
Heavy reading, but the class discussions are awesome. Take good notes and do the reading log else you are promised a C or lower

Aurelian's great. If you're not up to the task of making yourself heard, you might get your feelings hurt and come to the conclusion that he's got an "intergalactic ego."  That is, he's pretty clear about what he wants students to get out of readings, and one really has to press him if one wants him to go elsewhere. But that's our responsibility!!!

Heavy reading (it's a political theory class after all), don't expect to be able to slack off. He appreciates students who are engaged in class discussion. Lectures were interesting and very helpful when it came time for the exams - TAKE GOOD NOTES. He is passionate about the material, so don't just sit there like a bump on a log.

Dr. Auger is an awesome professor with my experience in her L520 class. Her lectures are organized and well-prepared. She is good at facilitating discussions in class. She is always available to work with her students and give feedbacks on your projects etc. She is also very friendly to talk to. I love her!

Dr. Auger's lectures can be dry, but they are always comprehensible and polished. Despite what people say here, her grading criteria is quite clear. In fact, she grades very generously; but she does expect her students to be dedicated and advanced linguistics majors. If you're not one such major, you will probably not do very well in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS WOMAN. truly the worst professor I have ever had at IU. She has a thick accent, so it's sometimes hard to understand her lectures. She gives you criticism on assignments but its not constructive. Has no clear criteria for grading whatsoever, she gives you bad grades on things despite your hard work. awful professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not clear, gives vague instructions, takes forever to return assignments, hard to hear & understand, does not set course up logically, not understanding of flakey project partners, assumes we have more statistical knowledge than we do, gives readings but no exams on them. All group project based. Work hard and you'll do well, but you won't enjoy it

As much as I wanted to enjoy this class, I can't. Professor Auger isn't necessarily a bad professor, but she's not good. Assignments are extremely vague, and when asked for help, she is dismissive and frustratingly critical of your work. She teaches this like a blow-off class and grades it like a capstone. It's disheartening.
No Comments

C388390 very similar. Knows a lot on Roman history and always tries to answer questions during lectures. He's laid-back and pretty funny, so attend lectures not only for the info but because he makes them interesting. Expect 1 long or 3 short papers per semester, 2 exams with term definitions and an essay. Fair grader. Easy pop quizzes if you read

So basically this professor is amazing. He loves what he does, he loves to teach, and if you are even the slightest bit interested in Roman history, you will most likely get an A in his course.  Just do the readings, show up to class with something to say regarding those readings in line with the themes he presents, and you're good to go.

Great teacher, clear presenting of material.  If you do the work it is an easy class.  Grading is, in the end, based on attendance, quizzes, and tests, so go to class everyday.  Which is fine because it is a fun class.

One of my favorite professors at Kelley. He really knows what he is talking about and ensures that his students understand the material after learning each topic/concept. He is very patient and will always happily answer any questions and he is also very funny!
Boring and hard to follow lectures, takes awhile to grade things, misleading exam wording. Is a vert nice and genuine person though

Professor Lalwani is an AMAZING professor. He explains material well and will always respond to an email within an hour even if its the middle of the night. HIGHLY suggest taking him for any course possible.

A top-tier lecturer, although a bit slow-paced, is very engaging, and you rarely feel bored. However, there is "extra credit" if you attend the first two classes, so if you sign up late, you are out of luck. Also, he doesn't bump grades, as everyone does quite well in his classes, so yes, I was

He is such a sweetheart. Once gave me a cough drop in class when I was sick, and gave us starbursts when we got answers right. The material was super challenging to me personally, but I thought he made it very easy to understand throughout the semester. Take him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lalwani is very clear in his teaching of the material, making even the harder sections easy to understand. I appreciated his effort to ask for feedback and implement it in class. He cares about his students' success and is always willing to answer questions both in and outside of class. I highly recommend taking him if you can!

He is one and was one of my favorite professors at Kelley and IU. Cares about his students a lot, he is awesome and really makes things easy to understand. I have seen a review say he isn't available or willing to help, which coukldnt be further from the truth. Professor Lalwani is an awesome professor that cares about and helps his students

Professor Lalwani is fantastic, he really genuinely cares about his students success and explains the topics extremely well. He consistently asks for feedback from his students and applies the feedback to his classes. He is one of the best professors at Indiana! Take any chance you can to take one of his classes.

Professor Lalwani is awesome! one of the best professors at Indiana University. He really cares about his students success and is willing to sit down outside of class consistently to help you succeed. He is extremely nice and very helpful if you approach him.
I enjoyed going to his class. His use of real world examples solidified my understanding of marketing concepts. I would recommend Professor Lalwani to any student majoring in marketing.

Doesn't teach certain math areas in class and gives confusing questions on final exam that were not well explained through examples and not in the textbook. Does not make himself very available through email, says he has "too many students" to write individual responses. Exam questions are tested on areas only verbally mentioned one time in class.
Dr. Lalwani was one of the best professors I had at Kelley. I learned an insane amount from his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Genuinely interested in the students' learning and development.
This professor was one of the most passionate I have had in Kelley. It is clear that he really cares about the subject and the success of his students. I really appreciate his dedication and passion.

Prof. Lalwani taught my final course as an undergrad at IU. His genuine care for his students was amazing- he truly had our best interest in mind.  The start of the semester is a bit heavier than the end; the last few weeks involve a simulation game which is one of the coolest things I've done at IU.  One of my top 3 professors I've had.
He's a major chiller and good K303 professor. Go to class and you are for sure guaranteed an A.

Professor Palley was a joy to have for K303. Even through course changes and new grade reduction exams to make the course seem more difficult, he was reasonable and supportive, assisting us through the process the whole way. He made lectures fun and ensured that we had all the information needed for projects and exams. Great prof!

He seems like a nice individual and he always brings snacks on exam days which is very nice, but he is not a very good teacher. He doesn't explain things clearly at all so you have to rely on the TA to answer additional questions. Overall, would not take K303 with him again because I had a hard time grasping concepts with the way he teaches

Dude is unironically the best professor in Kelley. He answers questions and clearly cares about what he teaches so much and about his students a ton. He brings us snacks on exam days, and sometimes for no reason at all. Definitely take K303 with him bc its the only class he teaches thats not a masters class.

I have no idea what happened in this class. It got to a point where I was so lost, office hours were extremely intimidating because I didn't even know what to ask. I used YouTube a lot during this course, and the people on there explained the same concepts from her modules in a much less confusing way. Don't expect this class to be useful lol.

Professor Nelson puts a lot of effort in providing feedback and creating good resources. I appreciated it a lot when so many online classes seem like you have zero interaction. You will get a better grade if you pay attention to feedback. This class is much more focused on academic writing and technical correctness then you'd probably expect.

She wants you to think she is smart, so she says things in the most complicated way possible, then makes you feel stupid for not understanding. I am usually a pretty good student, but she makes me not want to open my laptop. I am scared to join office hours because I am scared she will judge me for not understanding. Just do not take her classes.
Professor Nelson was very nice, but a tough grader. She explained the material very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She doesn't want to see you win like some of the dawgs they have here. The room is colder by her presence. The lectures don't add more to explain things. YouTube will be your best friend in this class.

She's mean, rude, and disrespectful. That's fair game but quality isn't there. I've attended free courses that provide more quality than this. I found my own code online for R. I read the textbook. I Google formulas. I do everything myself. This is not a course that's reflective of the educational quality of this institution.

If your idea of DEI is distilling everything down to race or you are the kind of person who  can fake it write what the professor wants to hear Professor Nelson's course is for you. If you are not into dividing everyone by race alone and/or want to express your own options that might be contrary to the course material I would stay away.

Extremely woke and views everything through race and the political lens. She commonly talks about political topics and her assignments require you to explicitly talk about race from only one angle. She uses her courses as a platform to expound upon her personal political beliefs. Very in professional for a professor.
Unnecessarily tough in grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Nelson is extremely nice and caring. This class was pretty difficult, and adding delays to graded assignments and feedback was the cherry on top. You must pay attention to feedback when given and definitely attend student hours to ask questions you will undoubtedly have.
I had a rough time with this class because it was definitely complex material, but Professor Nelson was so gracious and made sure that if we needed help that we could get it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Wonderful! I am not a math person but was required to take her Statistical Analysis course during the start of COVID! She was so helpful, flexible, and always checked in with us weekly to talk and to make sure that we were all doing ok, with the class material or otherwise. It was difficult material but she was always happy to help!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment:
This was by far my favorite class throughout my 4 years at Kelley. He challenges you mentally,
strategically, and professionally, but I felt I was learning skills I would need after graduation.
Probably the best professor at the Kelley school. I use things from this class every day. I wish I could take the class again.

Richard is the best professor I have had at Kelley. The material is not difficult, but the lessons are invaluable. Richard taught me so much about how to feel fulfilled, not only in your career but in life. Take this class if you want to challenge yourself to view the world through a different lens, you'll thank me.

So much non-sense in his class For instance, he will give you a fill in the blank asking you to recount the name of a theory. Like bro, it's a negotiations class. TEST US ON THE APPLICATION... I've taken other negotiations classes before and in them, I learned more and had to do less outside of the classroom work.

I would not take him again.
One of the truly outstanding professors at Kelley. If you have a chance to take a class with Richard, take it.

The most caring professor you'll ever come across, and with the coolest backgrounds you'll ever hear. He covers materials quickly, but if you come prepared with the slides printed out and take diligent notes you'll do great. He's always available for any questions, and he encourages participation in class. It's way more engaging that way. He rocks!

Richard was, without a doubt, the best professor I had at IU. His classes aren't necessarily an easy A, but he truly cares about each of his students. He was always extremely accessible outside of class hours, in person and via email, for any questions about school, careers, or life in general. I feel beyond lucky to have had a professor like him.

I don't typically take the time to write reviews on here, but I really felt it was necessary to do so with Richard. He is singlehandedly one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures are fun, the content you learn is SO important, and overall he is one of the most fascinating humans I've ever met. Take the class. You won't regret it :)

Professor Ash is by far one of the best professors that I've had during my time at IU. He's incredibly smart, and his British humor makes lectures entertaining. He keeps students engaged during class by including them in discussions, but does occasionally cold-call. The only negative is that he's a strict grader and makes you really work for an A.

To reiterate the comments before. He doesn't do well with online courses. Assignments were changed on the fly and groups had to rewrite papers days before due dates. He has few assignments so your grade drops significantly with one mistake. He is a competent individual who can; hopefully, learn from his mistakes with this course and improve.
He's an alright professor. Lectures are interesting, but a very tough grader. Directions for assignments are unclear. Learned a lot about strategy in his class though.

Amazing professor! I took his class one year ago, but still kept in touch up with him till now. When teaching about global expansion, he really encouraged us to express own opinions and motivated our global perspectives. But make sure that you won't skip the class since it's a highly interactive class.

If you have an option, do not take Strategy with Dr. Ash. His grading criteria is not clear at all. His lectures are pretty entertaining but his directions are terrible. So many group projects and you do not pick your teams.

Richard Ash is one of the best professors I've had at IU. He cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He is a decently tough grader, so you have to really put in time into learning the material and applying it. Overall, I would highly recommend anyone considering taking any of his classes to definitely take one!

I honestly was scared of his class. There were never very clear instructions on the homework, so I would go to class unprepared and he would randomly call on people (basically none of us knew what was going on.) If we had more of a heads-up on the readings he expected us to do, I don't think it would've been as bad as it was.

Ash is awesome! He's a tough grader but if you put in the time and effort needed you will do well. I remember his group project was tough and a bit dry and he asked very tough questions during the case. The exam was open notes which was a plus.

The guy is a genius, he's funny if you like a dry British sense of humor and clearly has made a lot of money in a short span of time. His lectures are as good as they can be. He was a mildly difficult grader- easy to get a B- harder to get an A. I'd recommend him for BUS-D271 or Effective Negotiations (Z404)

Richard Ash is a brilliant man who clearly knows a tremendous amount about the ins and outs of international business. His lectures were engaging and very interesting, unfortunately he is also a very strict grader. You will have to struggle extremely hard to get your passing grade but he'll at least make sure you get a lot out of it.
Incredible professor. If you're thinking about taking Z111 at Indiana University, please take Atanas! One of the most caring, respectful professors at IU. 10/10.

He is a great teacher and genuinely has a passion for teaching students about music theory. The class is very easy. He assigns these homework assignments that are tedious but manageable. He is a funny teacher who is glad to help students outside of class.

One of my favorite professors! Makes the class very engaging and easy to understand. He genuinely cares about the wellbeing of his students and wants the best for them inside and outside of the classroom.
Great guy! I enjoyed his class a lot. Even if you do not know anything about music, he will guide you through everything. He makes things easy to understand and keeps everyone engaged.

I would never take his class again. He doesn't treat his students right, he would get mad at them for simplest things. He gets annoyed very easily if students misplay the instruments. He also have bias on students so he treats some kids worse than others.

I was in his ukulele class. He knows people are taking the class for fun and focuses on teaching a wide array of uke texhniques and teaching us basic music theory. The music theory can be a little confusing for those who don't know it, but he's patient. Easy grading, few assignments. Show up, be respectful, and have fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: I took SPEA-E 183 last semester with Dr Attari and she is one of the best professors I've had. She genuinely cares about her students and makes her exams as easy to understand as possible. Few group projects but she lets her TA's grade so that annoyed some people but overall great professor definitely don't hesitate to get to know her personally!

Shaz is a gem of a professor and an inspiration. You should get to know her, she even offered the whole class to join her research lab and write letters of rec. Easy class, a group project, two online exams, but really interesting topics and discussions. I felt close with my classmates by the end, something which is special for a university class.

Professor Attari wants everyone to engage during lectures; however, most people just stare back at her. There are not many assignments throughout the semester which is nice and the exams are online and open note. I would highly recommend getting to know her because she cares about her students and welcomes any feedback about the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Attari is certainly a professor you should take a class with at IU. Her work and career are inspirational, and she is great to have a discussion with about any topic under the sun. I would go to class even if it's not mandatory or seems unnecessary. It's rare to have this great of a professor.
Shaz is the best. Participate in this class and interact with her; you'll get more out of it!
She is so knowledgable and caring! Highly highly recommend. You learn about a lot of different topics and how they relate to sustainability.

Shaz is my favorite prof at IU. She truly cares about her students learning about real-world issues rather than rote memorization. Her lectures are engaging and funny, and the few homework assignments and tests are fairly easy if youve paid attention in class. I highly recommend taking a class with Dr. Attari.

Basic college english class, long essays with adequet time. Heavily pentalitizes those who procrastinate as the ideas and prompts are not easily understood. Very fun class and amazing teacher. Would take him again if it wasn't for english.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I've ever had. The class isn't easy because of the course material, it's easy because he makes it easy for you to succeed. Gave me lots of resources to complete my assignments. Very approachable in his office hours and he genuinely wants to get to know you. I'd take this class again just to be in the same room as him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Atassi made me excited to write my papers giving us lots of creative freedom. He is a caring and overall great teacher. Most of your grades come from your papers, but he gives constructive criticism and sees the best in your writing as long as you try. Stay engaged and you are bound to love his class.

Sami is the best English teacher I have ever had in my entire life. He's the first English teacher that has ever had respect for my time as a student and an actual passion for teaching the class. As someone who has struggled with English my entire life, I did not struggle in his class. His lesson plan's are super simple and easy to understand.

Honestly Sami is one of the best teachers I have ever had in my life. For the first time I felt like I actually learned something in English class. He gives fantastic feedback on papers. Sami is also an extremely caring professor and always finds a way to make class enjoyable. His class is what all other classes strive to become.

Sami is what I wish all teachers were: down to earth, caring, and, most importantly, he strives to create critical thinkers. He deeply cares about his students and their wellbeing. He is flexible and leads class well. Show that you care about his class, and he'll help you achieve what you want to get out of it. Make sure to participate.

Sami is the man! He is super easy going and really funny, while still getting you to think on your own. He helps students find deeper meaning in all aspects of media, pushing students to think thoroughly and rewarding them with a fair grades. If you care about his class, he will care about you and your grade will definitely reflect that.
He's very nice and it's an easy class to do compared to taking eng-w 131

Horrible, she is so judgmental and makes you feel horrible about not knowing how to do something even though she throws you in the deep end without any instruction. She never explains what she expects and then gets very angry when you don't read her mind. the other instructor for the other section builds up to the projects while she expects pros.

Awful. Just plane horrible. It's her first year at PSU, and boy is she making a reputation for herself. She cannot comprehend the use of canvas, or that she cannot say one thing and do any other. The amount of times my class time have been wasted because she said something in passing, and thought it overruled what she posted in canvas.

This professor hopes that her students do poorly. She is condescending and brags about her "blunt" personality trait. Her exams are extremely difficult even when open book and she does not provide any extra credit to assist when you 'earn' a poor grade. Good luck to those who have to take this class with her.

The prof. graded so hard. She changes the rubrics without telling anyone and makes up new requirements for assignments and exams. Make sure to clarify what she wants because she will most likely not tell you and grade you poorly. The class itself did not teach me much.

Hated going to class because she expected us to perform according to expectations (which weren't communicated) and seemed to feel pleasure in witholding information if we didn't perform like she wanted. She docked 10% on final project for not attending during last week (I was horribly sick) even though attendance policy allowed it.

This teacher does not care about the success of her students. She actually hopes for their downfall and will not put in the effort to see them through their journey in the arts. She loves to argue with her students about the assignments they submit and takes pleasure in seeing them fail. Do not take this course with this teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: When in this class, she rambles on about things that do relate to textiles but lectures in a way that is not understandable. She makes students feel dumb for asking to clarify. She also will grade very hard for the littlest things and makes it seem like your work will never be enough. I do not suggest this professor. Worst experience ever in school

This class is my least favorite class and she makes me dread it every single week. There is no reason I should have a C in a class that is this easy. She is so stubborn and thinks she is always right even though she makes so many mistakes. When she is grading she takes an INSANE amount of points off for the stupidest things. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

Atencah is a graduate student. She is knowledgeable, but she doesn't know how to teach/encourage students to learn. She does not give enough in-class time to finish labs, her office hours are only 15 minutes, and she is not understanding of extenuating circumstances. Assignments aren't hard. The lab is interesting, but Atencah makes me dread it.

To have a teacher who doesn't speak english as a first language teach a beginner level math class was dumb. Test a brutal no matter how much you study. If you get a 7/14 with the curve it's a C... shows how great of a teacher is. He uses the textbook definition of everything so it isn't easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Would definitely have him as a professor again. He makes him self available outside of class whether its office hours or by email. A great guy! does an excellent job when he lectures as he writes the notes as he's doing it.

Ata describes the material in a way that is easy to understand and he genuinely cares for his students. He made sure to answer everyone's questions and held regular office hours in case extra help was needed. I would definitely say my math skills are stronger thanks to him.

She is an awful professor. Instead of taking time to explain the things that really matter, she tries to cover far too much in a single class. Her exams consistently include content that was not covered in class.
She's not a terrible teacher. It's a tough class and she does make it easier the sense that she is clear but there are better options out there.

Ms. Attenborough was a pretty good professor. Finite is a really difficult class, but she explained the material well, and  her Webwork sets weren't impossible. In addition, she sincerely cares about her students and is really helpful when they have questions. If you have a chance to take her Finite section, do it.
She was extremely helpful! Knew the material well, never actually taught me but was a TA for my class.

She always screwed up her examples in class, forgot formulas, etc. It was supposed to be a prep class for Calc 1, but nothing I learned in there helps for Calc. You'll do fine if you have friends to help you with the homework, though.
Superb.

Hardworking, open-minded and smart Professor with so much to give. Straight A if you come to class daily prepared and ready to actively participate. She brings music, art and poetry to her language classes in a professional and inspiring way.

Best Arabic Language and Literature Professor I have ever had. She knows what she is doing and she is very enthusiastic about teaching Arabic language and poetry. Requires many many exams and oral performances but all paid off at the end of the year and the class was impressed by her energy and inspiring love for Arabic poetry.
Amazing woman. She is so nice and always made my day brighter. Arabic is hard but she tries to make it understandable.
Such a fantastic teacher, her enthusiasm is contagious. hands down, one of the best teachers the NELC dept. has.

Atwood loves the Mongols but by the end of this course you will hate them. Lectures are excruciating to sit through and always go over. He babbles about pointless crap the entire time. He cares about what he teaches but does not realize that no one else in the room does. Easy A though, but you will dread going to the lectures

Empire of the Mongols was literally the most boring and pointless class of my life. He assigns like 100 pages of confusing and boring readings a week and requires you to buy 4 books. Lectures have nothing to do with the assignments and besides his random attendance, are pointless to go to. No exams though so that was good.

Worst teacher I've ever had. He's not necessarily a difficult professor, just extremely boring. He doesn't do anything but go in front of the class and blab aimlessly. Lectures are completely pointless. I was literally getting a B in this class but still withdrew because I could not stand the class. It's impossible to stay awake for a whole class.

I was impressed with Professor Atwood's enthusiasm for Mongolia and enjoyed his lectures. The essays were a breeze to write because you could gain a lot of insight though Prof. Atwood's anecdotes. I didn't read as much as I probably should have though.
Terrible Professor. For a 100 level class asks quite a bit. Lecture is pointless and boring. If you thought this would be an interesting class you would be mistaken. Avoid at all costs.

Lecture is pointless. Papers and quizzes are in learning group. Btw, when you turn in papers make sure you turn in a paper copy as well as the emailed copy or the AI's always seem to "not get the email" and then they don't bother to tell you. For the record, an incomplete for the class wrecks your GPA... Don't take the class.

Overall, boring class. Lecture itself it pretty much irrelevant because all of the actual assignments and tests are in the learning group sections that you have once a week. Out of 4 books, I read maaaaybe 30 pages and did well on the papers because the grading scale was super easy. Easy class, wouldn't really recommend it though.

Took this class because I wanted to learn more about the Mongolian empire-the largest empire in the history of the world. Now just hearing the word "Mongolian" results in projectile vomit. The entire semester, Atwood didn't utter a single sentence w/o at least 3 uhs or uhms. The man makes watching your fingernails grow seem like the Super Bowl.

This is by far the worst class I ever took at IU. Professor Atwood was extremely boring and his AI's are power hungry. The papers are relatively easy because the AI's typically give you your thesis.  I never read and did well on the 12 pt. papers.  This class was more work than a 300 level  Contemporary German Culture Class taught in German.

Yeah, this was terrible.  The lectures were boring, discussion was boring, nothing interesting.  Atwood loves his stuff, but he can't make it interesting for anyone else.  It was easy though.  I went 800 words below a min word limit on a paper and summarized the book when I should have analyzed and got a B, but that was the discussion leader.

I would rather watch mold grow than go to this class. It was excruciatingly painful to sit in this class, which he NEVER ended on time and you had to be there cuz he graded on attendance. Avoid this class at all costs I has mora work in this class than abnormal psychology, it was horrible

I don't know why people are complaining about the great wall of china course. All you need to do is memorize 15-20 names and dates the night before quizzes in order to get A's on those.
