reviews.comment: Dr. Black did an excellent job of making an asynchronous course as personable and interactive as possible, and of packaging a massive course topic into manageable, coherent units that gave us a more complete picture of Native American history. Not a difficult course at all, but engaging and thought-provoking. I only wish we had been in-person!

There was quite some number of readings every week, but there were several options provided (you can choose your readings). She is extremely helpful as well, where she gave the greatest flexibility in the assignment submissions. The class content was amazing and will challenge your long-held beliefs about history in America.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Black's course "Introduction to Native American History" was awesome. She is so passionate about what she teaches and really cares about helping students out and ensuring they understand the content. Plus, she's super funny and relatable which always made me look forward to class. One of the most down-to-earth professors I've had.

Don't take this class if you're intimidated by strong women. Professor Black is so amazing. There is a reading for every class period and you discuss it. At first, discussion for me was scary, but Professor Black does a great job of making sure you feel heard. The material varies, so you stay interested. I can't say enough great things about her!

She was a really nice teacher, she was funny, easy to understand, and unafraid to state her opinions to the class. She tells history not by numbers (which are hard to remember anyway) but by theme which make is far more interesting. A history class by her is sure to be memorable and entertaining!

Professor Blacks class was such a joy to be a part of. The class environment is very interactive and relaxed, I felt respected and appreciated. Its INSANE that IU offers so few Native American courses, this one is a must.
Read all the comments. Please stay far away from taking any of his classes. Very stuck up, doesn't care about students. Seems like he Enjoys watching students fail.
His lectures were confusing and his commentary on your work will be rude (not constructive at all) if you do not do well on it.

He frequently makes mistakes, and blames it on students. He is very rude via email if you reach out for help blaming you for not understanding. Doesn't have a clear rubric so his grading is purely subjective. Good luck, don't take him please!
Frequently makes mistake in pre recorded videos as well as live lecture, which makes it very confusing. Don't ask him for help as he will be rude and go at you for not understanding.

Very knowledgeable.    Assumes we know a lot of things, so difficult to get the basics.    Moves around materials a lot as well, found it difficult to keep track of what Professor was doing on the excel spreadsheet.   Often says "I dont necessarily like this", not sure how we are supposed to handle that information.
Nice Professor, very tough grader. Hard to pass class.
Good luck.

One of the worst professors I have had in my entire life. Assignments are extremely vague and unclear, he is disrespectful to students and is extremely unaccessible. The class is centered around excel and it is clear that Professor Blocher has limited knowledge of the program. He often makes mistakes in class and keeps going. Avoid at all costs.

Professor is extremely bad at teaching. And not approachable outside class. Extremely rude. I share the same feelings as others. Often cold on emails and does not responds with actual answers. Does not accepts his mistakes and rather puts it on students. I'd not recommend him at all. Avoid at any cost

I got a ton out of Dr. Blocher's class. It did require a reasonably high level of autonomy--you're expected to do the readings, and if you struggle with those, you may have to work a few of the problems independently--but I found myself operating with a long leash and able to apply a lot of what we learned in class in the "real world" very quickly.

Cannot hold a thought. Keeps jumping between topics. Doesn't finish sentences, hard to understand. Exams are way too long and too complicated to finish within given time. Very unpleasant to talk to. Avoid at all costs
Extremely rude and unprofessional person. Doesn't know how to talk to people. Uses very condescending tone. Shouldn't be allowed to be anywhere near the teaching profession.

Professor doesn't care about explaining the logic.  Examples shared in the class are way different than what you get in homework/exam. This professor is not approachable at all. If you send email with doubts, all you get are counterquestions and one liners but for sure you will not get the answers to the questions you asked.
Nice guy, but overly harsh grading although assignments seem to be graded by the department. Ridiculous grade cutoff policy that is not clearly defined in syllabus.

I share the same thoughts as other recent students. Initially, I looked forward to this class. Prof. Blocher moves quickly, often making mistakes, which causes additional confusion in live sessions. The lessons do not align with the exam materials, and when approached through email, he is often curt and cold.
Look for another professor don't waste your time and money.
Lacked guidance for exams
I did not enjoy professors lectures or the course and grade structure.

C520 would be a tough class for those who don't use excel regularly, as the professor moves quick over some things in order to cover all of the material. However, he is good at showing formulas to see what he is doing. Overall, I think he is a great teacher for this type of class. Buy the textbook only if you need supplemental examples.
Never made sense

He taught the class with Rex, Kari and Aaron Perry. He is extremely unapproachable and has demeaned students during the lectures. His answers are often short and curt and he doesn't bother to explain things. Side note - buying the textbook is a waste of money, the class was heavily lecture based vs. reading based.

Excellent lecturer and very adept at teaching in the online format. Good pace during lecturers, covers material clearly, and gives clear guidance on assignments and exams. One of my favorite learning experiences. Equal credit goes to his co-lecturers.
Great

Doug was a good professor. He was responsive to questions through email and in class. He tried to explain concepts in a few different ways so that everyone in the class could understand. The step-by-step solutions of example problems he did in class were very helpful. I would likely take him for another course if possible.

Doug was a good professor.  He was responsive to questions through email and in class.  He tried to explain concepts in a few different ways so that everyone in the class could understand.  The step-by-step solutions of example problems he did in class were very helpful.  I would likely take him for another course if possible.
He is very helpful and his class is mostly participation. His exams are difficult.
Dr. Blizard isn't that bad. As long as you do some reading and outside work, you'll be fine.

If you know going into this class that it requires a lot of time and effort, it's manageable. It's absolutely necessary to take notes in class and I recommend reading the textbook as well. The tests aren't too difficult but she's very specific in her grading. She does give partial credit and credit for second-best answers, though.
This professor did not explain anything, exams you were on your orn for, no study guide review or anything. Barley helped when going to office hours

This class is not bad if you try. I went to her office hours multiple times and I really recommend doing so before exams. For me, quizzes were harder than exams. She does highly recommend you take notes, and I can agree. Writing good notes helped me learn the material better. She's pretty kind and will help you if you ask her questions.

I didn't think this class was that hard. Prof was clearly very passionate about biology. She was kind and somewhat engaging. The quizzes can bring down your grade but I thought the exams were fine. I never read the text book and didn't feel like I needed to. Take notes and pay attention in class and you'll be alright.

If you show up to lecture and take notes, Dr. Blizard's class is totally manageable. The tests aren't just definition based -- you have to apply concepts, but Dr. Blizard prepares you for this really well through lecture and discussion assignments. She presents information in a very clear, digestible way.

This class was so extremely hard for no reason (especially for an introductory course meant for freshman). The exams were horrific, she gave us little to no study material, and she grades so incredibly harsh it's insane. All of the other instructors of BIO111 talk about how terrible she is and how low her students grades are. Good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She treats this class as if it's a filter class. I've taken many bio classes throughout highschool and for an INTRO class it is unnecessarily demanding. Notes/lectures are unhelpful yet required. Quizzes/tests are purposely worded confusingly, even if the material is easy. Prof. Blizard is kind and asks for feedback but doesnt apply it.
Absolutely terrible. Impossible to get full credit on anything. So so picky on grading.

I worked so hard in this class. I studied ten times more than I did in my Chemistry class and yet I got a 98% in chem. She is so stuck up and when given feedback, doesn't apply what students ask. There is no review for test and the questions are nearly impossible to get a 100 on. It's her way or the highway. She is overall a bad teacher.
Worst professor for biology. Was not helpful when you go for office hours and focuses a lot on topics she is interested in. Good luck on the quizzes and exams. Do not take this class with her.

Aside from what other reviews say, as long as you participate, take notes, show up to class and meet your AI or Blizard for help, you'll do well in this class. She was extremely helpful and cared to help out her students, and it's needed to put in the necessary work to come out of this class with a good grade.

Overall this professor was not great. What was good about her is that most of the time her lectures were interesting, and passionate about the content she teaches. However, she is an extremely tough grader. Exams and quizzes are difficult, you will never get full points ever. Assigns a lot of textbook readings, that I found to be a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do not take this course or any class with this professor. Does not provide any guides, outlines, or assistance to the students. The lectures focus on examples rather than course concepts and then before exams will tell you you don't need to memorize course concepts, yet it is the entire exam. Switch to human bio for major so you don't take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just look at her grade distributions compared to the other lecturers for this course. Expects way too much without communicating what exactly she wants and seems to not comprehend that this is a 100-level course
This may have been the worst course I have ever taken. She tweaks on kids for “cheating” . Top hats are graded on accuracy. DO NOT TAKE WITH HER. 111 is not supposed to be a weed out course.

This is the worst class I have taken. She only reads off her slides during lectures and most of that content aren't even on the exams. She has multiple open-ended questions on her exams and if you don't put exactly the answer she wants you will get no credit for it. This class is miserable with her and I would try to stay away from this course.

The most paranoid prof EVER. She doesn't trust ANYONE - not even her own TAs!! She legit regraded questions on an exam because one of the TAs grading it had not taken off enough points. Her lectures are freehand notes and she does not record her lectures. And as others have said - answers to test questions are what SHE wants, even if they openended

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.She is very rude and does not care if you are going to pass her class or not.If you have something important going on or emergency she will not care no matter how important it is.The exams are NOTHING in the lectures and doesn't give you any guide on what to study so you go in the exams clueless and will more than likely fail

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! Prof and TAs grade extremely hard. They will have open ended writing, but accept only one answer, and multiple-choice questions that accept many options to purposefully trick and mislead students. Many struggle to meet her expectations and the harsh attitude she has for a level 100 class. Worst class I have ever taken.
I just didn't like the class content, and the lectures and class structure made me hate it even more.

When signing up for this research program, I was  excited to enroll in a course that explored my interests. However, that was crushed by this professor. She is very nit-picky to the point where she will remove .1 points from a written response on a paper or presentation. There is no leeway for mistakes. It is impossible to receive a fair grade.

Misha is very kind and well spoken, but she doesn't like students talking during class. She gives out a lot of participation points, so make sure you show up and are actively engaged. Everything you need to know is covered in lecture, so I barely used the textbook. Tests are harder than the quizzes, but there are some extra credit opportunities.

Destroys interest. Professor does not know how to structure a class nor the exams. The exams are open ended but graded as specifically as possible. Tests have 10% multiple choice and the rest are short answer, long answer, or fill in the blank. Setting students up for failure with the absolute lack of study resources and lazy class material.

PLEASE do NOT take this class with this professor. Her lectures are long and tedious, and extremely difficult to understand. She is a very hard grader especially on the weekly quizzes (20% of your grade). I sincerely believe she doesn't want her students to succeed. You will have to teach yourself most of the material.

Do not take this course with Dr. Blizard. Exams are written as if they are for a 300 level course. Most questions are open ended and you never receive full credit unless you put the answer she wants exactly. I went to office hours once to ask a simple question about the course, and she was very hostile and never answered my question.
This professor is very stuck in her was even though she wants to help you this class is very hard to pass without looking at the textbook and using the AIs as a substitute for the teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst course I've ever taken. I was accused multiple times of cheating and was called out many times in class. She's not "chill" at all and her questions in class are grades on accuracy not just participation. Be prepared to have to work harder in this class than in any other class.

This professor is the worse teachers I have ever had. She makes questions on the quizzes that were never discussed in lectures, and most of the questions are opened ended so you never receive full credit. The tests are written as if they are a level 300 course when this is just a 100 level course. Please do not take this course with this professor.

Dr. Blizard "teaches" content and provides course/discussion work that is not applicable to exams. I and dozens of other students were accused of using chatgpt to write our short answer on a quiz when it did not happen. She blames the poor exam grades on the students instead of reflecting on her teaching when a majority of the class is struggling.

Professor Blizard is both rude and abrasive. She unreasonably suspects students of cheating without evidence, creating a hostile learning environment. Her lack of trust and negative demeanor detract from the educational experience, making the class more stressful than supportive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Does not grade based on effort or time put in, only get a question right if your wording is exactly right, will accuse you of using chat GPT if you use big words even if you didn't use it.

Would not recommend this class. The professor treats this class as an upper level course. The quizzes are basically nothing that we learned in lecture, it is mainly over the textbook. The exams are 90% short answer, 10% multiple choice, with the multiple choice she'll put "multiple answer choices" but there ends up only being one right answer.

I feel as though Dr. Blizard genuinely does not want her student to succeed. The tophat questions are sometimes over things we just learned or haven't learned, we got accused of cheating on TAKE HOME/OPEN NOTE quizzes, if you don't put the exact answer she's looking for on the exams, it's wrong. READ THE FREQ. ASKED QUESTIONS FOR EXTRA CREDIT!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Blizard teaches this course as if it is an upper-level biology course, despite it being a 100 level class. She makes the exams unnecessarily difficult and expects very particular answers on the weekly quizzes.

Unnecessarily hard and unfair class. I have lost all interest in ecology and biology because of this woman. Not only did she accuse students of cheating (on open-note, take-home quizzes) but she does not want her students to succeed in general. Do not be fooled by her friendly demeanor in lecture

This is the hardest class I have taken at IU. No where near an intro class and she makes it so much harder than it needs to be. Have to go to class and the top hat questions are not just worth participation and attendance they are based on accuracy. Professor makes all tests open ended, biased, and have one right answer. do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class does not set students up for success.

I recommend using rate-my-professor before enrolling in any class, I will not make this mistake again. The professor treats this class like an upper-level one. The grading is extremely particular, for example on most exams I only miss around 2 questions, but I only receive partial credit for the rest since she is so particular about answers.

Do not take this class. Prof & TA's are very harsh graders for all work. Tests involve open ended questions but only expect one answer. Weekly quizzes covers more of the book than the actual course content, and have too many answer choices. Class is treated like an upper level class and not a level 100 class.

This class has made me come to hate ecology altogether based on how it was "taught" and the professor  "teaching" the class. I came into this class excited but everything about how the course was set up made the excitement disappear. This professor acts like this class is an upper-level biology course when it's only 100 level. Horrible experience.

Super sweet and understanding. Easy class if you take time to do notes, read the textbook and pay attention to what she has to add. Tests are in class and closed note but not difficult. Make sure to complete the weekly homework assignments and she gives lots of extra credit opportunities as well.

She was a great professor. Cares what she is talking about and material is interesting. Attendance is only taken once a week and as the semster went on it rarely was. A lot of times not all the slides would get covered in lecture but the exams were easy, just look at the study guide.

The class was very easy, but the lectures are boring and drag on for a while. There are 4 exams that are pretty easy if you just study the day before. However, if you can get into another CJUS 100 class, do it because her class is the only one with in-person exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Block is a really good professor. Her class in itself is kind of boring so considering the fact that I didn't try at all, I'd say an A- is pretty good. She gives tons of extra credit so be sure to do it all. Trust me, you don't want to be studying for this gen ed class when you have a math exam, so DO THE EXTRA CREDIT.

Dr. Block is really passionate and helpful. Unless you are very interested in the material, this class will be pretty boring. She takes a long time to go over slides and drags it out. The tests weren't hard and your lowest one is dropped. I found it easier to learn from the study guides, but the chapters in the textbook are really long if you read.
Dr. Block is really sweet and cares about her students. I would definitely take this class again.

Dr. Block's teaching is very easy to absorb and her lectures are not hard to understand at all. Like other reviews, you can use part of class time to do other things as she posts the slides but she will sometimes reference things she mentioned in class on exams, so still pay attention. She asks a lot of questions to the class also in a good way.

The lectures aren't very interesting and I would mostly use class time to work on other courses and copy the notes at the very beginning. On the upside, it's an incredibly easy class. Exams are all online and open book. If you do the study guides and attend class, it's really easy to get a good grade. There's also a few extra credit opportunities.
Her lectures are so great and class work is so easy!! She's so nice and understanding plus this course is super easy to follow.
This class is not a useful way to spend time but is extremely easy. Lectures are not engaging at all and assignments are busywork. Do not use AI on paper, professor caught multiple people.
I would recommend this class. Her lectures are very easy to follow and everything is posted online. Classwork is super light, and all exams are remote online and multiple choice.

Dr. Block is a great lecturer, she is very passionate about the course. The content is organized well. Expect to read every weekend and answer corresponding questions online for a grade. Exams are all online and taken outside of class, the lowest one is dropped. There is one big essay. This is a good class.

Dr. Block is always happy to answer questions. Lecture not required & she will post some lecture slideshows on Canvas if you can't make it. Dicussion sections are required, so go to those- tests are also given in there. There are 4 major exams, an ebook is provided, and she always does exam reviews the class before. Very straightforward!
Dr. Block was super nice and her lectures were so fun. She always does practice problems for us like the exam. I would take her class if you can, even if you're not a criminal justice major!
Easy going teacher! Interesting GenEd class. Tests were multiple choice and straightforward. Professor Block was easy to get a hold of and made the topics understandable.

Dr. Block is so nice and this class is very easy. She does lecture very slowly, and often doesn't get to everything on the posted slides, but everything you need to know for tests is in the textbook, so just read over that and fill out the study guide and you'll be good.

Dr. Block was an amazing professor, it is really hard to fail her class. Show up to lectures and discussions and you will pass with a good grade. Just listening to lectures you will learn and go to the review sessions it'll help!

Dr. Block was amazing! The class is very textbook-heavy, although the textbook is not overwhelming. It was much more helpful to read the book than to go to lecture. The tests are entirely designed based on the book, if you read the book you will get an A! Staying ahead on the online textbook assignments will help a ton! They are super easy
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved this class. The organization was perfect and by just doing the work and going to lectures I was never confused on the material or what I was expected to know, especially because we got the exam study guides before lessons started. Dr. Block is also upbeat and passionate in lectures so I was never bored. Fantastic intro class.

I took this class as a fun GenEd. The lectures are always good and interesting. There is homework every week but it's not too difficult. The worst part of this class was the discussion led by the TA. TA was not great and always seemed scattered. Don't let that stop you from taking this class as an easy GenEd.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed Nick's Spanish I class. I learned so much during the semester about Spanish vocabulary, sentence structure, and grammar. He explains the content very well at a reasonable pace. Assignments and activities are well-structured and engaging. Hopefully I'll have Nick for a future Spanish course.

His grading eased up as the semester went on, but at first he was a tough grader. He emphasizes participation and the first exam went into very specific material that was impossible to know unless you memorized literally everything. His exams after the first were easier. The course material itself can be a lot but not too hard.

Nick was a great instructor! He cared about his students and wanted everyone to succeed. He was entertaining during class. Sometimes he did not explain the literature very well, especially because the class is almost completely spoken in Spanish. Translating literature to check what I had learned was often necessary.

Great teacher! Just make sure you follow the rubric and syllabus exactly, and you'll be good (ex: don't go above the max word count on papers, name your files exactly how it says to). He's really awesome to talk to after/outside of class if you need extra help, grades quickly, and gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He does talk pretty fast in Spanish but if you want something explained in English, he's super approachable to ask after class. He really wants you to only speak Spanish during class time and if you don't you'll see it come out of your participation grade. Stay on top of the ancla and canvas assignments, study the vocab and you'll be fine.

He sometimes goes on short tangents while speaking in Spanish really quickly, and those are always funny. He's just a funny guy in general, too. Class itself isn't bad, not too much homework, just make sure you participate. He's good at explaining things and is really encouraging. Also, he doesn't grade too hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's very nice.

The lectures are barely relevant to the assignments and class time is mostly busy work. Gives critiques on your work though most of the time it consists of you re-explaining things you've already covered or done. I came out of this class not having learned anything new due mostly to the instructors teaching methods.

I had no other choice but to take this instructor as it was the only way it would fit into my schedule. And like you are I checked rate my professor and saw the many bad reviews. I decided to go in with an open mind and positive attitude. Surely everyone was overreacting right? wrong. This instructor is what everyone says she is. #fireher

She is one of the worst professors I have ever had. The rubric said in class is different then the one online. Instructions are never clear, and grades are based on her intellect, not the majority. The TAs were confused about what assignments were. Never take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've taken 245 and 346 with this professor. The project and lectures are similar to all the other HCI/D courses. She's very passive aggressive and rude in her feedback. The project rubrics are confusing and have very broad instructions. You'll probably get an A but the feedback and boring lectures you'll have to sit through won't feel great.

You spend most of the semester in a group project with unclear instructions on every assignment. Each Monday class you present your assignment to her and she basically tells you that your assignment sucks and does not tell you how to make it better. Good luck to those who choose to take this. Dropped a minor casue of her

There were no rubrics because, "they were too hard to make." Assignment instructions were not necessarily what the AIs are grading. The professor and the AIs will briefly go over revisions, then dock points for things they didn't tell you in the in person feedback. The AIs are the people that are grading the assignments.

The professor is disorganized, doesn't use grading rubrics-very confusing. For group projects, you only get three questions to answer, but just addressing those won't earn good feedback. The criticism is unfair without clear guidelines. If possible, choose a design class with Phil Jordan—he's organized and provides detailed rubrics for assignments.
Her class is very unorganized and confusing. I dont know anyone who understood what she wanted from us.  The fact i paid money and this is what i got is frustrating.
Definitely not my favorite professor
Worst professor at IU. Very confusing class and she's very condescending. When I complained to my academic advisor after this professor's behavior. She apologized and said she regrets not warning me.

Confusing class for minor, disorganized, misalignment between student and main teacher, mind-reading needed, unclear lessons, heavy reliance on student teachers like I300, strongly advise against due to unclear assignments and group projects. NOT CLEAR RUBRIC OR GRADING CRITERIA also DONT BUY TEXTBOOK

The assignment criteria is extremely confusing with three bullet points of information on the assignment. The teacher then gets mad when the class doesn't meet her expectations when no examples are given. The class is all group project based and it requires a lot of revision after critiques because the assignments are so unclear.

This class made me and other classmates drop our minor in HCI. It actually made me not want to pursue HCI or UX anymore despite coming into IU and informatics to pursue it. The course is extremely disorganized and the lectures are boring. Our assignments are literally 2 bullet points of instructions without any other context,very unclear. RUN AWAY
Has her student teachers grade and teach everything basically, ong with it being identical to her I300 class

I have personally never taken a course and felt like I was losing braincells while in class. The lessons are absolutely pointless. Very nice lady. The way the lessons are taught are extremely disorganized and don't get anywhere. Instructions are never clear. Difficult to understand but that is OK and not one of my complaints. Nothing good to say.

Professor provided valuable feedback on our projects, directions were often unclear but if asked, she will explain.  AIs/UIs are more important in this course, as they grade and provide input on projects. Professor maintained loose control over the classroom.  Learned a lot in this course.

This class was a confusing mess & the prof didn't make understanding the material any easier. She spoke very quietly and has a thick accent, luckily she wore a mic but it was very difficult to understand what she was teaching at times. Overall, I wouldn't recommend this prof for this class. Try to get a different prof if at all possible.

No one understands what she speaks because she has a heavy accent. The instructions are always vague and confusing. The rubric on the TA's Canvas sometimes are different from the student's one. More than half of the assignments only worth 1 point while you need to speed lots of time and effort on them. The worst class I've had at IU so far.

Nice lady, it's true that she could talk louder and has a bit of an accent which makes something hard to understand every now and then, but it's really not as bad as everybody else on this page is making it seem like. Though, mine was in an average classroom, so maybe it's worse in a lecture hall. She was helpful in individual/team conversations

Professor Blevis leads a wildly confusing class, which is not helped by her thick accent that makes it hard to understand what she is saying. In terms of the class itself, assignment requirements are confusing, AI's do not know what is going on/how to help you, and the assigned readings are overly long and not worth spending time on. 0/10.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Assignment expectations were unclear. Blevis is soft-spoken and would not use a microphone in lectures, making it difficult to understand what she was saying. Class itself was disorganized; AIs frequently didn't know what was going on in the course, and the professor failed to clarify expectations. Overall, it was a frustrating and wasteful course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class as a whole is just poorly designed, but Prof. Blevis doesn't make it any easier. She doesn't speak up during lectures and she has a foreign accent, so it can be very difficult to understand what she is saying. Even when you can understand her, she's usually just reading straight off of the slides and doesn't elaborate on the concepts much
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very kind, funny, and helpful. Lots of group work and interaction. He often didn't correct mistakes when we had to talk to the class, which minimizes the stress, but isn't the most helpful for improving. But otherwise, I thought he was great and prepared us well for tests. I was always smiling in his class even when I wasn't interested in the work.

Professor is the chillest dude ever. He is very understanding and an easy grader. The assignments are easy and the exams are also easy as the study guide he gives has all of the questions on it. He also tries to make the class really fun and get everyone involved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super nice guy! Very understanding and he teaches well to make sure that everyone understands.

He is a very sweet man who cares a lot about his students and their success. I am really glad that I was able to take a class with him this semester, he was very understanding about some of the problems I endured, he also is very helpful and will take the time to explain terms and things if you're not understanding them.

He was such a joy freshman year and really made sure if it was your first time doing Spanish at IU that you felt you weren't behind. Very encouraging of questions and the style of group discussions helped connect w/ your peers while practicing actually using the language. 10/10 would take again lol.

One of the nicest professors I met at IU. This class is very lecture-heavy, but he does that to make sure everyone understands. As long as you come to class regularly, do your weekly assignments, and participate regularly, you should be able to get an A.

Was my favorite professor from my freshman year! Super sweet and understanding, met people where they were at with spanish. Class is 10 times better when you actively participate in groups or class discussions and makes it less awkward for everyone. Highly recommend taking a class with him.

Nick was such a good professor for S200. He always encouraged the class to speak in Spanish but if you're struggling you can easily ask how to say something without feeling bad. He wants everyone to succeed and makes learning fun with activities and gives lots of handouts to help understand new concepts with grammar.
She is a great teacher, but a lot of her class is sitting, and having her read off PowerPoint.

I really enjoyed her classes. She really makes the topics interesting to learn about and you can tell she cares a lot about her students! Her classes are really informative, useful, and fun! She really emphasizes the importance of having fun while learning. I met so many new people in her classes because she pushes us to work together
Made lectures fun, always takes the students opinion into account and is flexible and not afraid to change things up. Played games in class and learned a lot.

Professor Bjørnstad is amazing! I really enjoyed his class and learned so much. He definitely challenged my spoken French, but the participation grade is based on effort. Sometimes I found his grading overly difficult, but ultimately he was very fair. Great lectures and he really helps you understand complex topics/readings. Attendance matters!

The class was interesting enough (especially the final project), but Professor Bjornstad is a tough grader and there are only about 10 grades for the whole semester. I went to his office hours several times; however, I was just left more confused and stressed over how exactly I could meet his standards.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you ever get the chance to take his class on tragedy, please do it! This has been one of my favorite classes I've taken at IU, taught by an amazing professor. While there are a lot of readings, as long as you try your best to understand them, you will do well. If you put in effort, Prof. Bjornstad will make you succeed. TAKE THIS CLASS!

I liked Hall and his class more as the semester went on. Easy to do well in, difficult to do great. Readings and viewings almost all interesting. Grading criteria is not clear, and his paper prompts are gargantuan. However, if you give a decent effort, you will do well. Final project seems overwhelming but is not too bad, even a little fun to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: After reading the reviews for this class, I did not expect to spend that much time on this class. However, there are multiple readings or films you have to watch every week. Additionally, the main projects and papers can be tough and the grading is very vague, no rubric was given for the major assignments. I would look for an easier Coll class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took F300 with Prof. Bjørnstad and highly enjoyed the whole experience - the class discussions, the reading assignments, the thought-provoking questions, and the challenging yet rewarding writing assignments. I enthusiastically recommend taking one of his courses - you will definitely improve your communication and critical thinking abilities!
Professor Bjørnstad is great! I took F300 with him and he made it a very interesting class. He cares about your progress in French and gives good feedback.

Professor Bjornstad is an amazing professor. I had him for FRIT300, and I thought it would be an insanely hard class. He definitely makes you work for it, but its all to help your French improve. There are no tests, only 4 short papers throughout the semester. He is incredibly kind and always willing to help!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I think this class would've been better if it weren't entirely virtual. The class was mostly based in group discussion, which was frustrating when no one really understood some of the tougher readings. He was also very strict on attendance and participation, even with COVID. I still got an A in the class, but I really had to work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Bjørnstad is amazing! He's a well-respected professor, and really cares about his students, not just in an academic sense, but outside of class, too. If you have the chance to take his honors section on tragedy, please do! The final project was probably one of the best things I had the chance of working on.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He makes lecture very intriguing, on every assignment he provides feedback, and the work load is not much.

Professor Bjornstad is interesting and always seems excited to teach. He gives helpful and specific feedback and is happy to help if you're confused about something. There's a lot of reading and writing, but if you make an solid effort and ask questions when you need to, you'll probably get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Bjornstad is a fantastic person who is very energetic and excited to teach. The course itself was very homework heavy with weekly readings and discussions. Overall, I learned a lot and would take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Our section of HON-H233, "Tragedy: When Life Imitates Art," was very reading and participation heavy. Hall was an excellent professor and seemed to recognize when true effort was being put forth.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took French Grammar (mandatory for majors) but this prof made a dreaded class into a really helpful and good one.  Grades fairly though not always clear why he grades the way he does, always willing to help, and though lectures can feel long he really targets what you need to know.  Also gives extra credit throughout the semester.

He is sometimes a little hard to understand, but is always more than willing to help you. Praises you for going to office hours, which is always nice, because I usually feel like I'm bothering teachers. He is so sweet, a great guy and fun teacher!
Professor Bjornstad is the best French prof I've had at IU. He is clear, willing to slow down and explain, and overall a great guy. He wants you to succeed and enjoy the class!

Prof Bjornstad is very helpful and clear. When it comes to history, the professor will make it or break it for me and he is a lively discussion leader that made me enjoy it. He keeps you interested and thinking. He also switches to English to highlight important things if he thinks you're lost. He's a very nice guy.

Prof B is extremely enthusiastic about the material. He is a bit reserved and his lectures can be dry and seem to drag on. However, he is always willing to help with any problems/questions and he rewards genuine effort.
Go to class, do readings, and you can learn a lot!

He was nice and taught a lot in class but you are expected to do a lot and they grade the tests quite strictly and always say you didn't write enough. Another reviewer said when they are grading it feels like they are only looking for wrong answers which I agree with. It does not feel like a 100 level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The teaching style across the instructor's curriculum is overly directive, often crossing into micro-management of daily tasks. Must avoid him.
He cares but get ready to work.
OMG, hysteria

Lot's of reading. Lectures aren't necessarily mandatory IF you utilize the slideshows, but he does have a participation grade and WILL remember your face. Tests are easy, but he is a tough grader. Put in the work for the grade you want, Professor Scheuerman is incredibly smart and is always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is serious and expects you to be as well. This is a really solid course! Do not take if you want to blow it off.

I don't recommend unless you need to or are a political science major. It is not terrible, but very inconvenient and not reflective of a 100 level course's work. I had to devote more hours to doing and reading the work in this course than I think necessary, and it feels like the graders are looking for wrong answers rather than for right ones.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Semester grade was composed of only 4 assignments which are not clearly defined as Bill does not utilize canvas to show assignment details but rather only sends them in announcements.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Pretty average professor. Allows the opportunity to ask questions in lecture but can go a little fast sometimes. Discussions are important to go to for the tests, they usually give you an idea of what questions are going to be asked. I did well enough without reading, but the final paper really requires you to have read something.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very knowledgable and academic, somewhat stubborn but is willing to hear dissent and make your point heard. He's kind of awkward, but if you do the readings and are okay with participating in the discussions you should be on track for the A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I liked him, but only take this class if you are genuinely interested in Poli Sci and want to read and learn about Locke, Mill, Marx, Hayek, etc. I really enjoyed it and didn't think it was unfairly hard, but I struggled to get an A-. Interesting guy, really smart academic, but a tad elitist, and is just waiting to shoo you out of office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The readings are very pompous, making use of "big words" that are really unnecessary. They're also needlessly long & confusing. They could be short & still make sense. The exams are long answer, but no rubric exists, the professor seems to grade based on how he "feels". Attendance is mandatory but the professor does not track it through Canvas.

reviews.comment: Scheuerman keeps class interesting but there are very few assignments and they are graded pretty harshly. If you only study his lectures and not the reading you will NOT get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A helpful introduction to political ideas

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU ARE NOT A POLITICAL SCIENCE MAJOR OR A RELATED FIELD. The content isn't boring, but the lectures are (extremely). No need to buy the 5000 lb book: the texts are free online. The tests aren't too difficult if you read and study the slides. Sections are good for better understanding the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: he's a good guy, kinda dorky, but the material he teaches is really interesting.
A demanding but illuminating course.
Do not take this class.

This is the second class I have taken with him,he really understands the material and will do whatever to make sure you understand it.  You HAVE to keep up with the readings and go to class to even have a chance of getting a decent grade in the class.  He gives test reviews and notes for every lecture, though make sure you take notes on everything
Kind of arrogant. Not a bad teacher but not the best either.

he is really funny and lectures are exremely helpful. he covers a lot of material and if you don't go to class you will probably not do too well. but he keeps things interesting and was very well informed about his subject.
Good teacher, very smart and an interesting sense of humor that helps. Lectures seem to last forever sometimes.

Professor Bichay is a great professor. I took POLS-Y 121 Capitalism and Democracy. The textbook is a novel that is actually interesting. Attendence is optional, slides are posted. Exams are hard; there are takehome reading quizzes designed to trick AI. Three two page current event memos graded lightly. The class is easy, just don't use AI.

Prof. Bichay has a rare mix of being a great professor and having a great personality. His lectures were always a joy to listen to, and I learned a lot more that went beyond the content of the course. I actively looked forward to going to class each time, and I was never disappointed. Great class, great professor, great times.

Bichay has a talent for teaching. The class is really easy as long as you show up and review the PowerPoints. Midterm and final are very doable. Other assignments are very easy. He clearly states what you need to know for quizzes or write for other assignments. The simulation was very fun! If you have any interest in Europe, I definitely recommend!

Y205 is the only mandatory class for PoliSci majors and is somehow the most boring class ever. However, Prof Bichay made this class worthwhile. If it was not for him, I would have fell asleep every lecture. Bichay is very engaging and can make such a boring class somehow enjoyable. Props to him because deep down I think he knows we find it boring.

I can't lie, POLS205 sucks, but Bichay is a cool guy. The class material can get mindnumbingly boring, but his actual lecturing is good and he is tremendously smart when it comes to stats and politics. If you're a PoliSci major, he is your way out.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures were super entertaining. This class is the bane of most poli sci's majors existence but his lectures made it bearable. He understands that statistics isn't really a polisci major's strong suit & that the only reason most of us are in that class is because we have to be, & he wants us to succeed.

Great professor in a not-so-great class. This course should be a short introduction to a different course. He tries his best to make it interesting and succeeds most of the time. He uses memes, videos, and tells jokes to keep us engaged. Every concept is explained well. Goes over assignments and tests in class so you can learn from mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Bichay was amazing. This was my second time taking Analyzing Politics, and Bichay made it so much more clearer and easier to understand. Related complex ideas into relatable topics so things were easier to digest. Great guy to talk to and overall funny guy. Attendance policy is not too harsh so you can miss a couple classes if need be.

This guy is awesome. He's clearly very passionate about superheroes and film scores, so I really enjoyed hearing from someone who cares so much about the topic. The tests weren't too bad, and it really made me see film scoring in a completely different way.
He is super passionate about what he does and pretty accommodating. I recommend for an easy gen ed!

Boring lectures but the professor is very nice. The work is not bad at all. You do not need to pay too much attention to the class to do well. The work only takes about 3 hours every weekend if you can buzz through it fast enough. There are no tests except for one online final. Chill prof, easy work, and easy lectures you can do other homework in.

He is very nice and understanding about group project deadlines. There is a lot of homework, but it's very easy and since there are a ton of assignments, it's very easy to get a good grade. If you like superheroes, then you'll be fine.

As a business major, I took this for GenEd credit and it was definitely a decent amount of work outside of class, but none of it is hard. He is very passsionate about music, and his classes are all lectures. The Attendance is mandatory through tophat, so make sure you go to class. As long as you pay slight attention and do the homework its easy
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this for a GenEd credit. Please pay attention in lecture and don't miss class becuse notes are not posted after lecture. The textbook + homework will help you succeed on the multiple choice part of the listening quiz. He is super passionate about music, making lectures engaging. There is no extra credit or curves, but easy to do well in.

Professor Bishop is extremely passionate about music and a great teacher. Long lectures where he just talked the whole time and attendance is mandatory/recorded using tophat. Homework about twice a week, but it was very easy to complete. In class paper quizzes also easy if you do the hw. I would recommend taking this class with this teacher.

I took this class as an 8 week, 3 credit class to fulfill a gen ed. I was anticipating it to be more work than usual, since it was condensed, but the amount of work was outrageous. Get ready to spend 10+ hours a week outside class watching movies, doing asynchronous lectures, and completing random busy work. Okay professor, but crazy workload!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. This is a Gen Ed course with more work than any of my other classes. He is not accommodating if you need to miss class and will make you watch and take notes on the entire class recording. Everything is busywork and takes so much time. Spare yourself the trouble and find an easier A&H credit.

This class has too much work and it's all unnecessary busy work. I know it's only 8 weeks but it's kind of ridiculous. I am a senior in Kelley and this class has twice the amount of homework as my other classes COMBINED. Do not take it if you're not up for this much work.
Too much busy work, needed to spend lots of time on HW
Lots of lengthy busy work

He's quite an interesting character, but the class was not too difficult. As a business major, I succeeded so anyone can take this for a GenEd requirement without a problem. The listening quizzes have hard multiple-choice questions but if you READ the textbook to study, they're easier to answer. I'm sure there's a better course for the GenEd but...

Music in global cinema is such an easy gen ed and you get A&H and world culture out of the way. the work in this class is easy. Only "difficult" thing is allocating time to watch movies and the cue sheets might be boring but the work is not hard at all. Highly recommend this gen ed.

He was very understanding with attendance when I was sick. He is an easy grader and allows you to make a "cheat sheet" for the midterm and final exams. He is very passionate about the material and is lecture-heavy.

It is beyond difficult, originally it was just getting used to academic Spanish as you would get used to academic English. But its a ridiculous amount of readings needed everyday. Also this is not a Hispanic Culture class, its a Hispanic History class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: While this class was interesting, there was a heavy work load with an excessive amount of participation expected. Very nice professor, but you have to work for a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She's a great professor and welcomes all questions and conversation. I thought her class was very enjoyable, though it was sort of heavy on the reading. Her class is set up very well and expectations are very clear from the start. It does require a lot of effort but it is a very interesting class to take!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I constantly found myself very confused and stressed throughout this course.The professor gives long, complicated lectures and rarely makes time to answer questions (and when she does is not clear).There is also an excessive amount of reading and many assignments with unclear requirements and harsh grading.I also found the professor rude at times.

She assigns an extensive amount of long readings in Spanish for homework. She lectures for so long but is ineffective at teaching the material. She sometimes judges students when they ask questions. Her exams are absurd and difficult. She is a bad teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Profe is really passionate and knowledgable about what she teaches. You will need to put in quite a bit of effort for class since there are a lot of assignments and participation does matter. The exams are long and tough (and so are some of the assignments) but as long as you are paying attention in class and taking notes, you should be fine.

I am an "A" honors student. I did not do well in this class. She is a nice person, but a terrible professor. She is not clear in what she is teaching, not helpful when you have questions, not clear in her expectations, and meticulous in her grading. Bad combination. Horrible class.
Prof B is kind and accommodating, though I found myself confused by the content at times. Prepare for pop questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A306 was my favorite class this semester because of Prof B! She is so sweet and caring for students- truly wants everyone to succeed. I went to office hours frequently and she was always happy to answer any questions I had! I am so sad she is retiring, truly a fantastic professor. A306 isn't bad at all overall if you put in the work- you got this!
Prof B was an excellent professor. She was very sweet and caring. This class was super easy.

Good teacher and caring for students. Only complaint is test heavy and tests were only 20 questions so could not miss a lot but test questions matched what was taught in class. Did a good job explaining and would take her again. I am an accounting major so I do enjoy it more than the average person. Took a lot of studying but can get a good grade

Accounting classes are infamously difficult and I did find this one to require more studying than A100 & A304 but Prof B is very sweet and her lectures actually do help reinforce the textbook content. You have to do some work on your own but she is a great teacher and is very approachable!

i really liked her, and I think she is the best prof for A306.. the class is going to be annoying regardless, and she's a sweetheart who calls everyone hun... the class is a self-study, but going to her lectures can help sometimes

She does not teach well at all. I had to teach myself the entire course. The final for this course is the absolute worst part. It is a cumulative exam for the entire course - 10 chapters. There is vague direction given for what is going to be in the exam, with absolutely no practice exam materials besides McGraw Hill. Worst Final to study for ever.

Even though I do not have a good grade in her class but I love her. I learned a lot in her lecture or her. I love seeing her at KSB and I am willing to learn Accounting or come to class because of her. She is amazing and I don't understand why the ratings is low here. Prof. B cares a lot about her students. I love her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof B is so sweet and genuinely so smart. All accounting classes are known to be super hard, but her exams are very very similar to the examples you do in class, so there are no surprises

Prof. B is super nice and caring towards her students. She always pushes students to visit her during office hours for help. The information during lectures could be a bit confusing, but the tests were easier compared to a304. She has a quiet voice so get a front seat.
Overall it is an easy class as long as you pay attention to the lectures.  The tests are not that bad as long as you prepare right for them and an 'A' is pretty attainable.

Professor Biagioni is a super nice professor and cares about her students. Class is test heavy (80%) and only 20 questions on chapter tests and 30 questions on final. Focus on reading and understand examples from lecture notes as well as discussion groups. A lot of concepts need to be understood but overall, not bad if you put in the work.

306 was a difficult class and the exams were very tricky and encompassed small and nit-picky information. The exams also total 80% of the grade and none were curved. Prof B was a good professor but the Homeworks didn't strongly relate to exam material which was frustrating. I wish there was another metric to balance out exams taking up 80%

This is my second time taking this course. Prof B is incredibly knowledgeable and caring. She is so nice in office hours. My complaints with the course are not on her, my complaints with the course is how test heavy it is (it is this way with Healy too) and how difficult the exams are.

She does not curve exams, and exams are worth 80% of your grade. Even if you do good on exams, getting 1 question wrong will tank your grade. Having 4 exams be worth 80% of your grade doesn't accurately reflect how students are doing in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof B is such an angel!  So caring and such a sweet human -- accounting is, well, accounting.  But, she dumbs it down so much.  4 tests worth 80% of grade, they're all curved.  Lectures are pretty slow sometimes, but she's hands down better than Mike Healey (had roommates with him who complained every day; Diane's grade distributions are better).

Prof B is an extremely caring professor who wants to see all her students succeed. She is always open to help if you ask and regularly curves exams. However, the 4 tests count for over 80% of your grade and they can be difficult. Go to discussion as the problems there are similar to test questions. It's not easy to get an A but entirely doable.

Prof B makes accounting as interesting as it can be, and she is incredibly nice. You can tell that she genuinely cares about her students and the material. Although the class is hard, there are tons of resources you can access to get help and succeed. Stay on top of the material and you will be just fine.

LOVE LOVE LOVE. She is so kind and caring and genuienly cares about you especially if you reach out to her. She isn't too boring of a presenter and she knows what she is talking about. The class is pretty easy just reach out to her for help, she would love to help you.
Prof B is so nice. She always wants to help and as long as you have the lecture material down and practice what was went over in discussion you'll be fine! Take her for A306.

Prof B was the best professor I had this semester. I love that she was eager to get to know her students, usually going up the rows to talk to us before class. Her class is well structured. Don't make the same mistake I made for the first exam: studying from the online textbook. Every single test question is based on the course packet!
THE GOAT!!
She was an amazing teacher. All of her content related to her exams. Her exams were easy. She is always there to help and her discussion classes helped a lot.

Hands down amazing professor. I believed I hated accounting before her class, but I ended up enjoying it over all my other classes. She explains concepts in a way that is easy to understand and retain. Discussion is actually useful and enjoyable. Exam questions come straight from discussion and class, attend class and you will do excellent. AMAZING

Do not get thrown off by the bad reviews. It is not her it is accounting. Every class is test and homework heavy. She has the best A306 grade distribution and she writes the exams. She is very good at explaining the material and will do her best to work with you. A306 sucks all together but compared to the other profs she is your best option.

The class itself is hard but if you put in the work and apply yourself it is not that bad. Prof B is 100x better than the other options for A306. Her lectures simplify the content and then it is up to the student to take the basics and apply them to the homework. There are tons of review problems under the test prep module.

Prof.B was an amazing teacher. Her Lectures in my opinion, were very engaging. 

Here is my tip for people that struggle to study in this class. Do this for each chapter: 
1. Review the lecture notes
2. Review the smart book 
3. Review the Connect Homework 
4. Review the Discussion problems

This is the best methodology to study the class material
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof B is a sweet old lady. However, this class is ridiculously difficult. As someone who made an A in A100, I was shocked at how my efforts in this class resulted in a C. Prof B doesn't give practice exams, and once you finish the practice problems on Connect, you can't redo them. This makes it hard to study. Exam problems are different from HW.

Prof B does not explain anything. I did every single practice question for each test and still did not do well. She herself said she makes the tests too hard, but refuses to give an adequate curve. I would never recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The worst teacher I have ever had. She doesn't teach anything to you in class. I really only learn the concepts and how to actually work things out in the Discussion class with the TA. Would not recommend her class to anyone unless you want to stress too much when studying for tests and want to constantly get frustrated in lectures.

Prof B is the worst teacher I think I have had in my entire life (no exaggeration). She gives zero attempts to make her lectures interesting; is really lazy; and blames the entire class for not understanding a poorly taught concept. The only positive takeaway from this course is the discussion courses that are taught by graduate students. She sucks
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Get used to learning by yourself. Spend a lot of time reviewing if you want to get a good grade.
One of the worst jobs I've seen adjusting a course to online. Exams are much more difficult than any content covered by her (you learn everything in discussion) and she designs exams to trick you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible teacher. We had to teach ourselves everything. It is very obvious that Prof B does not care about students. She is very lazy, used lecture videos from last semester, and met with us on Zoom for 30 minutes a month. The Zoom sessions were useless, they had no substance. It sucks that we don't have another option other than her.

Prof B's class this semester was quite challenging and demotivating. She used recordings of past lectures and had us watching videos with no interaction, and lecture class only happened once a month. Discussion classes were helpful but never felt as though they were giving us what we needed for the exam. Her office hours were quite limited.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Participation matters

reviews.comment: A202 is a hard class and Prof B does her best, but I would have appreciated more support this semester. The lecture videos are good, but if she had held more extensive review sessions before exams like Julie Head does, I think that would have helped many people with the exams. She seems disconnected from her students and like she doesn't care.

The way this class was put together was absolutely trash! Prof B was very unorganized and did not care about her students at all. For her exams, which are ridiculously hard because she does not cover the "new concepts" in her "recordings", we use a lockdown browser, show our surroundings, and have a single piece of paper for rough work.

Prof B was never available, and 80% of your grade relies solely on exams. She only had class once a month and it was pointless because she didn't teach. You have to watch the pre-recorded lecture videos on your own time. She seems so sweet, but she will not curve anything even if the majority of the students do poorly on the exams. 0/10 recommend.

Prof B dropped the ball this semester. She used old recorded videos and relied entirely on them. Class was asynchronous, and calling it a hybrid is entirely untrue. We rarely met for class, and since she wasn't even filming videos, I'm not sure Prof B did anything at all. The content is hard enough, and I would've liked having an actual professor.

I am awful at accounting already but this class just made it worse. Prof B is a slide reader and never goes into depth. Online classes were supposed to be synchronous but she opted for the lazy path which was to prerecord videos so she didn't have to spend time with multiple classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof B is the only teacher for A202, but she teaches it incredibly well. Accounting isn't the easiest thing to grasp, but she provides ample help to get a good grade. Has office hours by appointment only (at least when I took it), but is super willing to help you with any questions that you may have.

Prof B forced everyone in the class to install Respondus spyware browser so we could be tested... it broke on an exam for me and screwed up my grade. She didn't let me retest, which was infuriating because I knew the material. The Respondus browser is just badly designed spyware and demanding students install it is unacceptable

"Prof B" was shamefully unprepared for the online teaching environment. Even though her class was supposed to be taught LIVE over zoom, she decided to just record lectures on her own time instead and send them out. They were ALWAYS longer than the time allotted to the course. She completely lacks empathy and thinks all students are trying to cheat.

Diane is your only choice for A202. She's not the greatest teacher but that doesn't make the class impossible, you just have to put in work. Do the readings and GO TO DISCUSSION. Discussion is all practice problems and is where you actually apply what you learned (preparing you for the test). It sucks having it on Fridays but it's worth attending.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Seems like a nice lady, but this is the most confusing course I have encountered. Her lectures make the material seem like its a 2/10 difficulty. Her homework makes it about a 5/10. Discussion groups get you up to a 7/10, and tests are probably a 9/10. It truly feels like there's 4 different classes going on that only vaguely relate to each other.

Prof B struggles to show and walk through how to do things. Most of her lectures consist of pointing a laser at the screen and just talking about what to do. This makes it incredibly difficult to just look at the course packet and know what to do when you are dealing with more complex homework problems. A lot of stress.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class itself is not terrible, but she does not do the best job when it comes to explaining it. I was somewhat shocked by the inconsistent difficulty of the exams; some tests will have averages north of a B, while others will have an average around a D+. Her lectures and homework are not indicative of the material on her exams. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I literally dreaded this class. The required course packet is relatively informative on A202's basic concepts. However, test questions are often 10x more difficult than the basic sample problems she puts in the course packet. Prof B's lectures are very dry, and it seemed like I had to teach myself the majority of the material.

I'm not sure why Prof B has so many bad comments... she is very passionate about accounting and cares that her students do well. The lectures help explain the textbook in a simpler matter, and all things considered I really liked how she taught the class because of how simple she structured it. She's just a really nice lady!
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof B is absolutely the worst professor I've ever had. Her lectures are pointless and her notes make no sense. She is super unhelpful at office hours and contradicts her TAs.  Her tests are extremely hard for absolutely no reason. On the first day of class, she said "I am not funny or nice." And she was totally right. Avoid her and her class!!!

Didn't love Prof B when I took her class, but realized just how bad she was when I took A201 with Julie Head and learned what a good accounting teacher is. I really don't think Prof B is a good teacher. She gives a great curve at the end of the class,  but it's only necessary because she doesn't teach the material well.
Big Fan!
Added a curve to the overall FA16 course grade. She knows her class is tough and will go out of her way to help you be successful.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Don't fall into the negative hype that surrounds prof B. Yeah, it's a tough class, but she doesn't go out of her way to make it so. There is only three tests, so not much margin for error. Wait till she says "leverage" for the first time. You'll crack up. Awesome teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof B's negative reputation is utterly unwarranted.  You will work for your grade, but she is very clear in her expectations and explanations.  She goes above and beyond to help you out.  It's obvious that she loves her subject and truly *cares* about her students. Attend lecture!  You can get by without going but it helps enormously.

Prof B is a sweetheart. She explains things extremely well, but her tests are tough. The first one is the easiest, but still try to do well; it will help your grade tremendously because your grade will drop with the second two tests. Look over the notes before the quizzes because there is no partial credit, you'll either get 10, 5, or 0 points.
Do the practice tests and understand each problem completely. If you do, the exams are not bad. Toughest one was the second exam.  Conceptual questions are usually from your course packet.

Prof. B gets a really bad rep, but she does truly care for her students & is really nice. Make sure you do really well on the first test to give you some cushion because the second test is definitely the hardest. She is honest and will tell you that straight up. I am not an accounting person, but was able to do decent in the class with some effort.

Gives in-class examples and practice problems to prep you for the exam. Sometimes gets carried away with stories about family. Usually available before and after class. If you go to class, follow along, and do the homework you'll have a much better chance. Each test question is worth 1% of your final grade, so you have to study carefully.

She is awful.  I had to teach myself the class, because she doesn't know how to teach.  My class' average was an 83, and that is a direct reflection upon her teaching ability, or lack thereof.  Going to class is pointless.  Just get the course packet notes from someone who already took it and just teach yourself.  Good luck.
Easy Class. But make sure you finish the homework she assigned before each quiz and exam. The homework did not count for points, but it was really helpful.

I thought the class was enjoyable, and the way she describes the material is pretty clear cut. You gotta put some effort into the class, however, cause it's not an easy A or B. Do all the homework and go to any office hours if you have any questions. Also, prepare A LOT for exam 2, as it's the hardest of the 3. There is a nice curve for it though!

Don't really understand why people don't like Prof B. She is really goodhearted and cares about her students. She doesn't know how to write a test thou, exam 1 average was a 90% and exam 2 had to be below 60%. Overall she teaches the class well. If you did well in A201, this class should be a breeze. Prof B is actually pretty great!

The material was very unclear. Professor B is a really nice person, but you won't have much time to interact personally with her in a big lecture. Sit in the front, read before class, do the homework problems, do all the practice tests before the actual tests, and you'll be fine.

This isn't a difficult class per se, but you can get derailed if you don't do well on the first exam, because the second is much harder. If you have a guaranteed way of getting notes from someone, then there's no reason to go to class. You'll be fine if you read the course packet before the exam and do all the practice exams (many questions reused)

Prof B is a nice lady, but not the best at teaching. Some of her examples are confusing and the exam questions are tricky and sometimes extremely ambiguous. It's not easy material so it will take some effort, but she is there to help and so are the TA's. With a little effort this class is not as hard as most people make it out to be

Avoid at all costs. She has no idea what she's doing and doesn't even explain the concepts to you. The point of the professor is so that you can have someone explain the concept to you but she just confuses you more. You can sit at home and read the book and learn wayyyy more than you will ever learn from her.

If you're a Kelley student, take accounting classes in the summer at IUPUI or IPFW or equivalent. Easier and I learned more. Diane is a charming person but not a very good professor (as I find is true with all accounting professors in Bloomington). She reads directly from the powerpoint and provides few examples that resemble her test questions.

Reads off ppt. No use in going to her lectures. It's pretty much a self study course, cuz the prof isn't too good at lecturing. Big curves because almost every one scores super low on midterms and finals. I you really want to learn more about accounting, you won't learn anything from her.

Prof. B. was helpful with individual questions before/after class, but I was rather confused by lectures alone. She pretty much read PP slides in lecture rather than providing additional information, and she didn't explain steps well in in-class examples. Some friends used the textbook to teach themselves instead. There was a helpful curve, though

Course is badly organized. Exam questions are ambiguous and full of mistakes. Textbook answer key is wrong and confusing. Teaching quality is good but the poor course organization makes this class painful. If the course organization was improved and the discussion sections were actually useful I feel like she would get better ratings.
How can you expect a teacher to teach you when she screws up every question on the test.
You will fail on her class unless you only take A202 in the full semester. Promised!

She is the worst teacher I have ever seen!!! There is no need to go to her class. It's a waste of time. Whether you go to the class or not, you have to teach yourself before the Exam!! You will have more than 300 pages to read before exam. So, never, never, never choose her. Please!! And she will never change the way she teach!

Very poor professor.
