She goes over one book problem per week in class (the main one that the chapter is written about), and is very happy when the class scores a 77% (most people have below a C right now).  Take any other accounting professor if you can. Course is completely self taught.  No one even goes to class anymore.

DO. NOT. TAKE. HER. If you have the option to take this class with someone else. DO IT! for the love of God she is the worst professor at IU. literally all she does is go through the slides and at the end of the day you have to teach yourself EVERYTHING! do the practice problems before the test, that will help but again... DO NOT TAKE HER!

Professor Gardner is truly amazing. I just want to sit down, have coffee, and chat with this guy. He's very knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches and engages students well in each lecture. Only grades are the midterm and final, but he prepares you very well for each. Learned lots and would eagerly take him again if I could.

Very passionate professor. His lectures are pretty great, but he can go on tangents and will spend the entire class answering questions. Theres only a few grades, and they involve pop quizzes. He essentially gives you the final and midterm ahead of time, so there not that bad. Pretty solid dude outside of class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bovingdon is a very smart man and I think he may overestimate the student's taking this 100 level course. He relies heavily on historical examples in his lectures to explain topics, so if you don't know the examples you are screwed. There are no opportunities to get your grade up, mostly midterm/final grades. Extremely reliant on textbook!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Bovingdon is a wonderful and engaged lecturer who tries very hard to communicate all relevant information to students. There are not many papers in the class but you do have to read and show up to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gardner is an extremely insightful and intelligent professor who clearly cares a lot about what he teaches. However, he throws two pop quizzes at you which are both worth 10% of your grade and take about 5 minutes each. If you want to succeed in INTL-I 100, skip the readings and just go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this as an S&H credit just to fill my gen ed requirements but I'm very glad i chose to take this class with prof Bovingdon. He is very passionate about what he teaches and is very open to teaching different world topics that may interest students. As a stem student, intl relations isnt my thing but he made this class extremely enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The professor is really knowledgeable and is super interesting to listen to, but the course (I-206) only has a few graded assignments and Bovington isn't the best at communicating assignments and objectives clearly. The professor is also objectively quite liberal and doesn't shy from sharing his political beliefs, which might be a problem for some
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great Professor. Taught the information and was very passionate about what he taught. My favorite professor and a great intro professor.

When I started at IU, I was an International Studies major. This class changed that. While Prof. Bovingdon was definitely passionate and knowledgeable, this class was a boring 5-month slog that killed my passion for IS and made me switch majors. The only grades were two quizzes and a final, so very small margin for error. Terrible class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved him! He is clearly very passionate about this topic which made it super fun. I loved going to this course. This course may have changed my life. I am seriously considering changing my career path to go into city planning. Wish I wasn't a senior so I could take another one of his courses.

Gardner is extremely fascinating to listen to because he is intelligent and passionate. However, his grading methods, attitudes towards students, and setting standards for an intro class like its a senior level seminar was rather disappointing. This was a required course for my major and was upsetting to know my teacher did not want me to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Barely any assignments leaving no chance to fix grades 
Grading was harsh and uncompromising
Impatient with all his students but still shocked people didn't go to office hours

Gardner is clearly a smart guy, but the setup of this class was extremely frustrating. Final grades were almost entirely based on the midterm (took well over a month to get back), the final, and another assignment. Although he offered office hours and showed interest in students, he was generally condescending when approached outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Would not take a class with this professor again. Its graded purely on midterm, final, quizzes, attendance + participation. Had a 77% showing on canvas so I was studying and striving for a certain percent on the final and on the last day of the semester he changed the weight of the grades and my 77% quickly dropped to a 63%. Still no final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He makes an effort to get to know everyone, even in his large classes. He is more than happy to re-explain something if you are having trouble understanding certain topics. He cracks jokes which makes the class energy very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Super awesome prof -- cares about his students and is super engaging. I will for sure take a class with him again!!
Great professor. 10/10 would recommend especially for CEUS. He's passionate about the subject and makes class engaging and based around student needs/ interests.

By far the hardest 100 level course I've taken. Gardner seems very knowledgable and I think he has good intentions, but I wouldn't recommend this class. Especially if you don't enjoy writing. The grading is harsh and takes a long time to get feedback. The text book is literally like the bible for this class, and it's incredibly boring.

Extremely well-educated and passionate about the subject he teaches. Goes out of his way to encourage students to learn, lectures are very informational & insightful. Grades constructively and offers detailed feedbacks Has a fantastic attitude.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Clearly a well-educated man, passionate about his subject. Lectures were extremely engaging and he made the classroom a comfortable space to speak up. Changed my perspective of the world and I absolutely adored his class.
Fantastic professor, very immersed in teaching, knowledgable Cares about the students, passionate about the subjects Get ready to read & participate in class, though

A very respectable professor. Very passionate about teaching. Encouraged participation, and was very knowledgeable. The only down side of this class was that he didn't assign very much homework which made bringing up your grade difficult. The midterm and final were fairly easy if you studied for them.

Fast paced lectures, makes note-taking difficult. Given readings are long & hard. Prior & outside knowledge about the cultures and politics is needed to fully understand the material and to receive an A. Discussions are uncomfortable & difficult due to many different beliefs & students trying to voice their opinions without offending others.
I really liked Professor Bovingdon, but I found this course to be kind of difficult for being 100 level. You'll have to work for an A, but Professor Bovingdon will make that work worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bovingdon is the best professor I have had at IU so far. He is a legendary lecturer and just a legendary person. His lectures aren't mandatory but I found myself going to every single one just because of him. I can see how much he cares about the topics and how much he wants us to care. Couldn't suggest him enough!
One of my favorite teachers at IU. His small classes are always way better than his large lectures. A lot of reading every week but he cares about the readings and makes them interesting.
I've taken three classes with Gardner. He's a great lecturer and fascinating to listen to. Reading and attendance are expected. Prefers to use Socratic seminars than just lecturing to the class.

Dr. Bovingdon is the BEST and Ive had many great professors. He engages the class through discussion and free thought. Class is reading heavy & the readings are very tough, but you get more than what you paid for. Hes brilliant. Do not take unless youre junior year or above unless you want to WORK. You will want to show up to class as its fun.

This is the worst teacher I have had since I started pre-school 16 years ago. This class should be called "International Philosophy," not "International Studies." There was absolutely no guidance as to what was expected of students on tests. Furthermore, the professor imposed his political views on the class as if they were facts. DO NOT TAKE THIS.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The discussion for this class was terrible, not a fan of the prof and teaching style... All he did was pose questions for you to consider. There is limited grades for the class, but they are all forms of writing assignments. The discussion that accompanied the class was very good, but attendance to it was crucial.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Bovingdon is a very passionate person but often is very overbearing and somewhat aggressive when he presents the information. Each lecture has a powerpoint and I would recommend taking notes because they will come in handy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I loved taking his Intro to International Studies class. Lectures were interesting and fast paced. If you're not there, there's no way to get the lecture slides. If you put in the effort you'll be fine and he'll notice. Best professor I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Worst class I have ever taken. Grades extremely hard and barely has any grades for the class. If you do bad on one thing there is no way to bring the grade back up. Participation and attendance for the discussion is extremely important. The lectures are heavy and hard. I would not recommend this class to anymore, not even my worst enemy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's a really fantastic professor definately worth taking his classes Pros: extremely knowledgeable, very discussion based rather than lecturing, he takes your feedback into account Cons: lots of reading some of which are very boring, academic writing style, tests/papers can be hard if you're not great at memorizing authors and concepts
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Bovingdon is a great professor, but this class is hard to follow sometimes. The class is a bit boring but very informative. Be ready to read. You'll have to read the assigned  articles and book to be able to follow lectures and discussion class. The midterm and final come directly from the study guide, so make sure you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Horribly unorganized to the point where his class was extremely frustrating.  Changed the syllabus as he went, took 7 weeks to grade midterms, teaches from an extremely biased liberal viewpoint, acts like his opinions are fact, and straight-up told us he doesn't care about course evaluation feedback

I took a course on oil, islam, and geopolitics with him, and you could tell he was very knowledgeable on the topics and always encouraged questions. His lectures were interesting and overall he is a very good professor. His tests seem intimidating because of the many assigned readings; however he provides very helpful study guides.
Always tried to keep the class interesting. One of the most knowledgeable professors in the department and goes out of his way to find answers to questions.
his lecture is interest; what he focuses is how to activate student during the lecture.

Gardner is so great seriously. He is really funny and very understanding. His class is very interesting and it's easy to stay focused. He is a little scatterbrained but he knows it and would never let his mistakes hurt your grade. Overall very good and would definitely take more classes taught by him.

Easily one of the best professors I've had so far at IU. He takes a genuine interest in his students and wants us to succeed. He prefers a Socratic seminar-style lecture, which is highly conducive to sharing ideas and expounding on the texts. He's always willing to listen and is entertaining to listen to. I definitely recommend him as a professor.

Best professor I've had at IU. He is genuinely interested in his students and so passionate about what he's teaching. He also loves answering questions we have. Class discussions are really engaging and thought-provoking. I love coming to class because I know I'll leave having learned something new everyday. Phenomenal professor.

Bovingdon is THE MAN. I knew & cared little of Xinjiang prior to his class, but he taught w/so much enthusiasm that I actually ended up enjoying it. Loves questions & is genuinely interested in your thoughts/opinions. If you're deciding what class to take, take his, b/c you will like going to class & he will keep interested even for a 3 hour class.

AWESOME! He's so passionate about his area of study and makes every lecture exciting and informative. He welcomes questions and actually takes time outside of class to look for any answers he doesn't know. He's really good about letting students know about related special events on campus. He's a great professor and seems like a cool person too
Hands down the best professor I have ever had. He is intelligent, passionate and a great lecturer.

I had oil, islam, and geopolitics with dr. bovingdon. he is perhaps one of the coolest professors at IU. he's extremely interested in his student's interest. he loves questions and will find answers even if he doesn't have them. take his class. he is seriously one of the coolest and most interesting people i have ever met.

I had OIL, ISLAM & GEOPOLITICS with Prof. Bovingdon & it was one of the best classes I've taken. He is smart, interesting, and a Silver Fox ;) Too many readings for a "104" class but the tests turned out to be pretty easy. Attendance wasn't required- yet I went to almost every lecture because that's how interesting his class is! Highly recommended!

If you can take a class with this professor, do it!  He makes everything interesting and you'll learn an insane amount. His only downside is that he sometimes gets a little too excited and goes off on tangents.  Interesting ones, but tangents nonetheless.  Hands down the best instructor I've ever had at IU.

This man is EXTREMELY intelligent. He has a very extensive vocabulary and teaches very rapidly, so it is hard to keep up. But, he is very interested in what the class is thinking. He begs for questions and nearly jumps for joy when one is asked. Also, he will do whatever he can to answer questions, even if that means researching at home overnight.

He's very passionate about his subject, and really informs you a ton during lecture.  However, sometimes he seemed to present too much information, especially on his powerpoint slides. And for a 100 level class, there was quite a lot of reading (sometimes over 100 pages a week).  Regardless, he is an excellent lecturer and speaker.
The best professor I've ever had at Indiana.
A fantastic and engaging lecturer. The class is great, with though-provoking readings and fascinating lectures. One of the best professors I have had so far at IU.

Dean Bosco is a very good professor who succeeds at breaking down complex legal topics to undergraduate students while not talking down to the class. The textbook is expensive (~$250) and the reading is very dense, but if you are interested in the topic, he is a great professor to take. The exams are not easy, but if you prepare well it's alright.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lectures. Explains concepts really well and is fair with grading and additional make-ups. Does update Canvas rather slowly but he is the assistant dean of HLS. Slides are comprehensive. Take notes on what he says in class and you'll be set for the papers.

This class is all lecture and above-average difficulty for a 100 level. I got a B in the class only attending lectures ( I missed a few of them too) and taking notes. The grade is based of attendance, the midterm, and final (no assignments). If you take the class the most important thing is to attend the lectures and take notes!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bosco as a person is very nice and everything but the class itself was horrible. For it being a level 100 class is extremely ridiculous. Grades are based on 2 exams and attendance. Lectures are very heavy and to add on the exams are difficult as well.

Bosco is a good guy and is genuinely passionate and knowledgeable about what he teaches, but the course should not have been this hard. It was a 100 level course and was unfair to have just the midterm and final as grades, especially if you aren't a great test taker. Do not take unless you are extremely passionate.

He is a nice guy, and he is passionate. But his exams are ridiculous for a 100-level class.
 I'm a sophomore and I wanted to take this class because I love intl studies but lecturing and assigning a midterm, then lecturing and assigning a cumulative final is not a good way to teach. Your grade is only based on two exams and attendance.
PHENOMENAL professor! He is so insanely passionate about his teaching, not a dull moment in that class. You can only miss 4 lectures per semester!

Bosco was a stellar professor. He had interesting stories to back up concepts and had a structured approach to class. I felt like a learned something new every time I left. 1 research project, and 2 tests determined the final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His humor and engagement he has with the class during the lectures makes what might otherwise be boring material into something much more interesting. Some professors force students to speak when they don't want to, Bosco does so in a more natural and forgiving way which makes paying attention actually worth it.

Overall Professor Bosco was very engaging, very knowledgable, and personable. He is fairly fast paced with material, and much of the time is spent lecturing. It was entirely up to me how much effort I was willing to put in, the course I took was "you know it or you don't". He is very good at keeping things simple and understandable
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took his INTL100 class spring 2020. Although he follows a bland power point, Bosco's lectures don't get too boring. Sure, there is a lot of information, but he does a great job engaging with the class and being humorous. Does assign quite a few readings, however not necessary for a good grade. Go to class and participate in discussions.

Professor Bosco was very late to grade the only four assignments in the class, and the feedback was not useful. Grades for essays were mainly up to his discretion. There was very little direction. Not very accessible outside of class.

Loved prof bosco. excellent professor and really interesting lectures that weren't dry or boring at all. Class not too difficult as long as you take notes and attend class. Highly recommend this course and prof bosco.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: SUPER engaging professor, clearly passionate about the topics he teaches. You read an actual law school textbook, which seems dry and difficult at the beginning, but actually is quite fun and informational once you get the hang of it. He is occasionally hard to reach by email if you can't go to his office hours. Overall, fun class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bosco is a wonderful human with experience in his field. Take all of his classes.

Hes amazing! One of the best profs Ive ever had. Ive taken two of his classes now and I wish I could take more. Hes so knowledgeable and passionate about the subjects he teaches. His lectures are very funny and laid back. Hes incredibly approachable and available outside class, even just to chat. He cares so much about his students. Great guy!

Professor Bosco is my absolute favorite professor at the Hamilton Lugar School. He is incredibly knowledgeable in international law and is absolutely hilarious and makes going to class a joy (the only class I never skipped). The textbook is a law school book and is daunting, but his lectures are very spread out. Legal analyses are very difficult!
One of the best professors that I have ever had. Makes the class fun, really drives home points, and cares about his students. 10/10 would take again
I would recommend taking any of Professor Bosco's classes. His lectures are interesting and cover all of the important material he assigns you to read.

Professor Bosco is my favorite professor I've had in SGIS. He's a very engaging lecturer and very knowledgeable about international law and legal systems. Be sure to do the readings and come to class. Your grade relies on five things - participation, two short writing assignments, a midterm, and a final.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Bosco has amazing lectures that keep you engaged. Used a law textbook which was expensive but very doable. His tests weren't hard and there were only two short writing assignments, one of which was cancelled. Just showing up and taking notes will give you what you need to know for tests.

Professor Bow was the best teacher I've had in my four years at Kelley. He's incredibly enthusiastic, interactive, and great at grabbing attention and encouraging people to participate. He's also always there to help students, both in class and beyond. I'd recommend him to anyone.

Professor Bow cares so much for his students. Going into this class, I wasn't expecting to learn anything and just coast by to meet graduation requirements, but he made the class very engaging. He makes a big effort to learn all the students individually, and he is one of the best professors I've had at IU.

Professor Bow is the most memorable instructor I've had at IU. He takes time to talk with EVERY student before class. His enthusiasm and humor make the class exponentially more enjoyable. Understanding and willing to be flexible with individual students. Ensures each student is prepared for "exams". You'd have to try hard not to do well on them.

It is hard not to pay attention when Bryce speaks, you can hear the passion in his voice, and it is engaging! Furthermore, he is very clear in his instructions, and I never felt lost when doing an assignment. 

My only complaint is that 4.5 hours is entirely too long for a final on top of other finals and a full-time job.

Professor Bow is a cool guy however, he is really bad at giving instructions. The assignments are just busy work with not much class material involved. He does give a lot of extra credit, which is kinda necessary because your team members will probably screw you over for the team projects. You NEED to do well on the quizzes to get a good grade.
If you show up to the zooms and take notes you will get a good grade
Good professor, very energetic and keeps the class engaged.

Repeats himself a million times about the same things which wastes so much class time, almost 20 mins a day. Always criticize students who ask questions and finds a way to point out a flaw in the student or their question. Makes you hesitant to want to ask questions and makes the class environment very uncomfortable for everyone.
Class is a pass/drop. He was super SUPER enthusiastic which was actually a bit annoying. His tophats were the best though so eh

Professor Bow is very nice and energetic. Teaches well with good energy. Not very many grades for this course so stay on top of projects. A little tough on grading, submitted a video that was 10s over because I liked the topic and he took a good amount of points off for it not being the correct length. Other than that, easy class and nice professor
Great professor, he has great business knowledge because he has learned real world skills through actually having a business. Brings energy,enthusiastic as one can be. By far my favorite professor.
Bryce is a nice guy and great presenter, however, he gives too much bs homework and expects you to tie it back to class material. He gives very vague instructions and nails you on grading.
great professor! amazing energy in his lectures

Prof Bow likes to befriend his students. If you sit in the front row and interact a bit he's more likely to grade you leniently. He brings the energy to lectures, but is more interested in side convos than being slide heavy. The quizzes count for a big chunk of your grade, so read through the book on your own before those are due. Overall good prof
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: It is very important to show up to every class. You can get lost easily, but she does post the slides. Exams are mainly 'can you interpret the data' type questions. And math heavy. Excel workshops are every once in a week, worth a lot of your grade so ATTEND!
Very easy class, just show up and you'll get an easy A/B, the cheat sheet is very helpful. Not sure about the TAs I never used them but mine was pretty nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a nice teacher that does her best to make sure students understand the materials. It is best you try to attend every single lecture. TA are nice overall, but I do understand some frustrations that ppl have personally so take it w grain of salt. I think she's a new prof so she's still figuring what work best for her. Just catch up with class.

No study guide for exams, TAs outline general concepts, & students are allowed a note card. My main issue is TAs. They're nice, but you can tell when the energy is different. Watching who get actual help vs who doesn't is kinda (ik im evil) funny also sad. Im lucky to EXCEL enough. Yall should too if u wanna keep ur dignity intact w/ ur classmates.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am not in luddy/anything computer, but it definitely does help a lot if you have a passion or are majoring/minoring in it. I did not, hence, I'm constantly struggling to stay afloat alongside my other classes. I admit that is my issue for zoning out hahaha. It's an easy A/B as long as you GO to class, attend office hours, and review notes.

Bowman made stats interesting/not boring. Content was more theory based than math, and she gives a lot of material to study with (ex: slides). There's discussion where TAs help with the Excel assignments. She explained things well, sometimes went fast but would repeat/slow down if asked. Listened to feedback. Also, you get an exam note sheet
This class is interesting. IN CLASS ACTIVITIES ARE A MAJORITY of your grade in this class. Generous drop policy, but attendance is very much required as it basically decides your grade.
Talks too much and has too many assignments. TA (one specifically) took his role way too seriously. Attendance was unfortunately mandatory or nobody would ever go.
Fine, wouldn't take again though
Lots of in class group activities

Dr. Boss took over our class near the beginning of the semester. He is a very caring and respectful teacher, but my class did not like to participate. This led to awkward pauses where he would ask students to think about a certain idea by themselves. Otherwise, he explained terms and ideas very thoroughly and kept everyone on the same page.

Jake was such a great professor for my class. It was his first semester teaching it, and I felt like he was a seasoned vet. As a freshman, X159 was invaluable. We had field trips, guest speakers, and many discussions to help us navigate the college life and beyond. It was such a great class, and Jake is an AWESOME professor and person!

Dr. Jacob Boss is the most inspirational and caring person I have ever met. He wants you to fall in love with learning, and he does just that. There are no lectures, it is one big discussion where everyone is welcome and accepted. I cannot encourage you enough to take a class with him, he changed my life. There are no tests or quizzes.

The most caring, passionate, dedicated professor Ive ever had. When class was canceled because of a power outage he showed up to sit in the classroom and let people know, and people just stayed in the dark because they didnt want to miss the chance to talk with him about the readings. That says it all.

Life changing class and professor. Works with you instead of against you. This is how all classes should be. Very knowledgeable on the subject and group discussion allowed us to see other peoples points of view.
Jacob was a great teacher who really cares about his students and is very open to feedback. If something in the class isnt working for you, he will work to fix it. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Jake was my AI for original sin. He was always available to help. He responded to email faster than any teacher I've had. He really cared about us and didn't talk to us like we were children. Going to his office hours was really helpful because he gives straightforward feedback and doesn't talk down to you.

Jake was a breath of fresh air. I'd pretty much given up on school before this class. There were a lot of readings, but the variety was good and the old religious books were balanced with current events and videos of rituals and performances. Basically as long as you showed up and participated you were good, everyone got pulled along by his energy.

Non-traditional but fantastic. Genuinely wants students to care about the topics, structuring classes and homework accordingly. Lectures were interesting but never more than a fraction of class time, instead leaving the bulk of it to student-lead discussion or other interactive activities.

Do NOT take this class if you want to keep your sanity. Says you can miss two classes, no, you can't. He still deducted my grade. Gave me a B for participation, but in his feedback, he said nothing poor about my class engagement. I learned NOTHING about France or its culture. And finally, this class lowered my GPA so much, save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Accuses of AI, with lots of reading. Attendance and participation matter so much. Honestly didn't even learn much about French culture, more about the anthropological network and media configuration which is a very confusing topic for a GenEd. Going to class and talking, giving new ideas is mandatory to preserve your grade, but it's not worth it.

Vincent could be condescending at times (he was always accusing us of using AI because our written French was "too good") and he tends to forget that you have other classes to worry about as well. The rubrics are basically nonexistent, yet he gets upset when you cannot magically read his mind. I also had to miss another class to take the final.
This class was a steep learning curve for a GenEd. I was halfway through the semester and didn't even realize I didn't understand the class until then.

I don't think that this class is for everyone...or anyone. There is so much that I want to say that I can't. Let's just say that only the strongest get through this class unscathed. Be prepared... in class and mentally.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I don't even have the words for this class. be prepared to be flabbergasted is all I have to say. Good luck Soldier.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I do not recommend this class. The Professor is not professional in the classroom and does not offer clear guidelines in and out of the classroom, for reading, assignments, and basically everything. Don't take this for a GenEd, there's much easier classes to take that won't tank your GPA or make you feel stressed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: If you want your sanity, don't take this class. Even if you are the best in the class, it will never be enough. There is little help or direction in assignments, and he gets angry when he is the one being unclear. He takes points off for missing a single class, he gives lots of reading for each class. Don't take this for a GenEd it'll drop your GPA
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Bouchard was great. He was very sarcastic, and the class was mostly discussion-based so get ready to talk every day. Because of that, doing the readings is definitely required.

I will preface by saying that I am not good at french, but I try. Obviously this class is taught completely in french but he recognized the students who are putting in effort. His grading was more than generous and he really based it off of your understanding of the culture, not your french ability. I could not recommend him more.
Very interesting and funny teacher with a lot of knowledge and passion for his job. Take a class with him but don't be afraid of awkward silence.

Professor Bouchard is an amazing professor who is very knowledgable about his respected area of study. He heavily encourages class participation, so as long as you are willing to talk a lot in class you will enjoy this course. He is a relatively easy grader and is very caring towards his students. Overall great professor!

The other F225 rating summarizes this class well. Everyone has to do a short presentation but it's not bad. Showing up is the most important part of your grade. If you contribute 1-2 times every few weeks you will get a good participation score. Papers are long but they are only as difficult as you make them be (you get to pick your topic)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good professor, very easy class. Just show up, skim the readings, ask some questions, participate a little, and you will get an A. Docks for skipping w/o a reason, but he is a very easy grader, and will give essay deadline extensions almost always if needed.

Ok, definitely show up to class. If your French is good, you will be fine. If it isn't that's ok, you really cannot fail this class unless you don't do anything. Usually 20-40 pages of reading and a 2 paragraph discussion post before each class, but honestly just skim the reading, because class is all discussion based really. Definitely not hard.

I loved Professor Bouchard's course in West African literature! He really invites you to engage with the material and raise questions in discussion. Although the class is heavy on homework, participation, and attendance, it's not hard. He literally says just ask one question and you're fine. I loved his class, his research paper was super fun too.

Super tough grader, but never made it clear what exactly he was looking for. Disorganized class structure. Participation in class is very important, yet I always struggled trying to come up with something to say to the absurd things we discussed. Anyways, the best part of the class was that he often struggled to get the subtitles to show.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would go to the bathroom in the middle of his class just to escape and get a break.

Has a heavy french accent, doesn't seem to know what he is talking about, gets off track pretty often. He is nice, but if you don't participate in class/actively pay attention he will dock you on your grade pretty badly. He is a really tough grader. 5/10 wouldn't take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lots of reading. Very available for help and a pretty cool dude, but you definitely need to come to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The material is taught in a very unorganized manner, which makes it difficult to follow and understand. Lectures are boring, and grading is really tough for a lack of clear guidelines on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He puts a unique spin on an old class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He's honestly very annoying. Readings are boring, lectures are boring- Take 300 with someone else
She is a very understanding professor and had fun, engaging classes. I HIGHLY recommend, I'd take this class again if I could

Professor Boveja was very kind and helpful in helping students understand what different careers could look like. She used good, clear examples and tried her best to engage students as much as possible. Class itself was a breeze, honestly too much so. But, she herself is a wonderful professor.

This class is super easy 
The professor genuinely cares about students and is very understanding 
All homework is available way in advance
She is really nice and easy. Very understanding.
Dr. Boveja is really nice, and hardly makes you do more than 1 hour of work outside of class!
This class was not hard at all and felt that Dr. Boveja genuinely cared about her students. She is very flexible to work with you and would recommend taking a class with her if you can.
Great professor

Dr. Boveja is the nicest professor I have ever met. She is so empathetic and wants to see you succeed. I also had her for stress prevention and management, which was great. Her material isn't very difficult if you put forth the effort. She cares for her students and will work with you to make sure you do well. I couldn't recommend her enough.

She is honestly the most empathetic person ever. She understands how her students feel and actually listens to feedback. The class itself was super interesting and her projects are lots of fun. Literally, if you just show up and pay attention, it is a very easy A and I respect that. She honestly inspired me to look into a career in public health :)
Story Lab 2 taught by this instructor is a living nightmare. You will be drowning in work and get no help when you ask for it.

If you're in the Media School, you'll likely have a class with her or her husband. Though she can be disorganized, she's a GREAT professor with extensive media experience. Take a smaller class with her if you can. You'll work hard and learn a TON. Her large lectures with TAs are fine, but her smaller classes are great. Get to know her either way.

I really liked Bonnie. Many will complain and blame her for their issues, but most students actually just dislike the class projects itself. She is very clear on instruction and she brought in amazing guest speakers. My only complaint is that I wish she allowed us to use students as subjects for our group projects.

Professor Layton is nice, means well, but, FAIR WARNING if you didn't come in with any prior editing, video, or design experience you're in trouble. 3 big projects big and tedious. Random selected groups, if you get put with people that don't try, you're screwed. Her AIs grade very tough. I was fine, but be ready to devote a ton of your time here.

Prof. Layton was great, and (in my opinion) is the best professor for C250. She offered many extra credit opportunities, which helped boost your grade if you missed more than the 3 allowed class periods. Her TAs graded very tough, but she was very understanding with extensions. One negative thing was that she is very against devices in class.

Four group projects over the semester, no exams, participation points every class and lab. I prefer Bonnie over her husband (she also has less quizzes). The class can be very basic and tedious at times but if you have to take this class it is good to get a feel of a variety of media. Talk to Bonnie if you have issues, she is pretty lenient.

Overall was nice but could be a little aggressive at times. Very good professor however. She knew a lot about the topics and was able to teach it very well. The class is challenging though. Lots of homework and lecture heavy so be prepared. Her TA's/lab instructors were tough graders which made the class that much harder.
She is a super sweet woman and is passionate about what she does, but she puts too much emphasis on attendance and not having electronics out that it feels like a high school class.

Professor Layton was maybe the most boring professor I have ever had. She seems like such a sweet person outside of the classroom, but she teaches this class like high school and you will be SO BORED. She puts way more emphasis on attendance and not having any laptops or phones out than the actual material. The TAs grade way too harshly.
Professor Layton knows a lot about the topic, but teaches this course like a high school class

not a huge fan of this class structure or the lectures in this class; felt a bit nervous to approach the teacher/ask for help; lectures are ehh in terms of substance and the labs are so tedious for such a basic intro class. was super stressful and turned me off of story lab 2 completely

Professor Layton was very good. She was always very helpful whenever anyone had questions and always tried her best to make things very clear for assignments and stuff. For C250, if given the choice between her and other professor Layton, take Bonnie's section

Professor Layton is a great teacher -- Storylab 1 is a great starting point for learning media-specific skills such as using the Adobe Suite and collaborating with others. Yes, her class can be a pain at times, but if you show up to class and put in the effort, you may find you actually learned something.

She has so much personality, and it shows in her lectures! She really cares about you as a student. Also offers A LOT of extra credit, which is nice. I would love to take another one of her class in the future.

I think she teaches the class quite well and cares about a lot of her students. She is sometimes a little boring in lectures, and if you have taken previous journalism classes before, you will pass with flying colors. The textbook is all online, and you don't really need to read any of it. She could improve the photography section.

Professor Layton is super nice and brings amazing guest speakers to class. She always asks if we have questions and makes the class engaging. You do have to go to class and lab if you want a good grade, though. I will definitely take another class with Professor Layton!
Loved this class!! Brings in awesome speakers and really cares about her students.

Professor Layton off the back shows she cares for her students and the field of journalism. Her lectures are informative, but C250 contains most of the graded knowledge within the text book so read! In lab, she is always ready to strike up conversation about journalism and your own future endeavors. She is an amazing professor.

Professor Layton 1 on 1 is great and super helpful, if you attend her office hours she can be really helpful. However in class she is vague on assignment criteria, has super inconvenient due dates, and grades at the pace of a snail despite having multiple TAs to help her. Expect to be confused, disappointed, and question your major. Good luck.

I'm sure this class would be fine with a different professor. It seems as though she has made sure to make sure regular assignments are due at the most inconvenient times. Along with covid, I feel as though I really haven't learned as much as I should have for what this class is supposed to be. I would not recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class probably would have been fun in person, but online it's difficult, assignment-heavy, and unclear. Many assignments had unrealistic expectations, especially during covid. Responds late to emails, your best bet is to attend one of her Zoom help sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She never responds to emails, is so unclear about assignments and projects due and when you ask her for clarification or help she will tell you to ask your TA or UITS, if she even responds. For the love of god do not take her, slack off once and your grade is already on the line. Not to mention the most unhelpful Professor I have ever had.

Warning, MSCH-C 226 is very art heavy so if you are not looking for a photography/graphic design class, save yourself the trouble. I believe this class would be very fun in person, but as an online class, it is very difficult. This online is also not Covid-friendly, instructors will expect you to conduct normal procedures or you will lose points!

Bonnie is really knowledgeable in her field, but isn't super understanding of how to change her class to be more covid-friendly. We're still expected to go out and interview people, even with covid. She's nonetheless a good professor with a ton of field experience, so if you're interested in photo/film/digital journalism, take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I think this is a great class to learn about photography and videography but it's a lot of work. Considering the circumstances (COVID), I think she and her AIs still expect too much. We are forced to go out and speak with strangers even with COVID and the labs and participation points are literally only worth 2 points but the work is worth way more

I love Bonnie! She is extremely nice and will go out of her way to give you feedback. Can be tough on criticism but really just wants the best for you. Always has a great attitude and is just a very genuine person. I highly recommend her!

I love Bonnie as a person and she has TONS of experience in the field so definitely pick her brain about her past career. Her class was a little sporadic and sometimes the semester schedule was really hard to follow. The way she explains things can be a little confusing. But, overall, a really good person and a caring teacher.
Very boring lectures. If you are not willing to read the powerpoints outside of class don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Bonnie is great! She teaches a really fun course, and it's very engaging. You learn a lot of unique material in a short amount of time. The projects are a lot of work, but she gives you a lot of time and a lot of guidance on how to manage your time well. Labs are important.

Bonnie has a ton of experience in the field and really wants to see students succeed. Labs are useful and AIs know their stuff; Bonnie is a real help too. Every lecture and lab has some sort of participation grade, but they're very useful, so just go. Best media instructor I could think of, yay Bonnie!
The assignments were fun and interesting, but the lectures dragged on a little.
Confusing. Just confusing.

Very motivating and helpful professor. Always so full of energy in class and is truly passionate about journalism. She is more than willing to go out of her way to help students, especially outside of class. Tough grader, but very fair. One of my favorite professors.

She is an extremely motivating professor and will do anything to help her students do very well.  She cares about each assignment, student and journalism from the bottom of her heart.  She is experienced in the field which allows her to bring real world advice and knowledge, making her a better professor. She is one of my favorites, an inspiration!
Helpful, experienced, and really does want her students to succeed.
What a wonderful lady with a wealth of experience that is enthusiastic about helping students learn and grow. Super easy to talk to and just all around nice to be around.

Bonnie Layton is not an easy professor, but she's incredibly helpful and fair. She'll go out of her way to help any student on their project, she's always willing to meet outside of her office hours, and she wants to see her students succeed. You'll have to work in her class, but you can easily do well. She also was really flexible with due dates.
Very motivating professor. I highly recommend her!

This class was great and useful, I highly recommend. He teaches important IRL things like investing, credit, and buying house and cars. Class is fairly easy everything is online, exams are open note. He was also super helpful I had an issue with my exams and he met with me and figured out what went wrong and gave me make up points for all of them.
Great professor. You'll learn a lot from his course! Just make sure you complete everything and get it done on time. A lot of busy work but it isn't terrible.Tests are open book.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: If you don't do the readings you might screw yourself over. The exams are online but each exam is generated differently so you can't look up questions. The exam is online and open note but don't be fooled the questions aren't online anywhere. I recommend reading the textbook online and making sure you do all of chapter practices.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I liked this  professor. One of my problems was that the homework assignments and readings felt somewhat unrelated to what he taught in the lecture. You definitely had to study and teach yourself some stuff outside of the lecture to do well on the exam.
Goor professor. Online class makes it hard to be focused. Test heavy with relatively hard exams if you think you can just find everything online. Actually need to study for exam even if online.

Prof. Musumeci was always very understanding and answered any questions. The class was supposed to be once a week and around 2.5 hrs, but instead, he split it up into an hr online lecture, and the rest was posted in a video two days later. There are only 2/3 assignments per week and a total of four exams where he posted plenty of optional practice.

Prof Musumeci is nice but not a great professor. Lectures are just slides from McGraw Hill that don't exactly align with what are on exams, attendance gets pretty low as year goes on. Homework is just McGraw Hill and worth only 2-8 points towards your grade. The majority of your grade is dependent on the exams which are pretty difficult and LONG.

Mr. Musumeci is a super nice guy, but what he teaches doesn't seem to apply to what we need to know. We were taught definitions and things that felt off-topic to the exams, which were mostly math. If you can teach yourself things well, then I would suggest this class as it can be easy if you learn the topics from McGraw Hill by yourself.
Learn how to do PV calculations and this class is a breeze. Online structure makes it hard to focus so find a quiet place. His tests are predictable but still difficult

I would not recommend this course. The lecture was solely on definitions and processes where the exams were entirely math. As a result this class became self taught. Similarly the assignments and practice exams are different than the exams so preparing was difficult. The time given for exams was unreasonable as it was challenging to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams make up 80% of your grade and the remaining 20% is homework that is only 2-8 points each assignment. I was unable to completely finish most of the exams in the given time period because of how many questions there were. Exams are almost nothing like the practice exams either which was very frustrating.

This was my second time with Professor Musumeci and I was even more disappointed. Your best option is to use Chegg. Everything is from McGraw-Hill. Learning from just lecture is nearly impossible. Honestly lectures were pretty pointless. Exams makeup most of your grade.

He doesn't really teach so much as present slides provided by McGraw Hill. The same goes for all homework and exams. It's probably best to just read the book and occasionally attend lecture. A nice guy, just wish he added more than he did for this class.

Love this class! Super helpful material that will go a long way once you enter the real world outside college. Professor Musumeci is very kind and replies to emails very quickly. He makes his lectures as entertaining and relevant as possible.

Highly recommend this class and this professor. He cares about his students and wants them to learn the material instead of just memorizing the material. If you attend class and listen to lectures you will do well in class and also will help you in life.

Professor Musumeci seemed like a very nice person, but for me the lectures were hard to follow with everything that he wanted us to do and download on our computers. After the first test I knew I would not get the grade I wanted in his class so I chose to withdraw.

Extremely disappointed with his laziness as a professor. Exclusively uses McGraw-Hill for slides/homework. He does have knowledge in his field which could be useful with one on one convos. The homework can be broken and it resulted in a much worse grade than what should be. Its an easy class, but I expect my tuition to attain higher caliber profs.
Professor Musumeci is very kind and has a lot of real world experience in the subject that he teaches. Ready to help anyone and always makes the chapters easier to understand.

Thought he was a little arrogant at first, but he has a ton of real-world experience and does know what he's talking about. Class avg test score is a B; you have to put in work, but it's definitely doable. He cares about his students and is always more than willing to help you out, from going over test questions to setting up your own credit card.

Good guy but an awful professor. Rambles through lectures and doesn't give any time to stop and let the class take notes. Makes the test unnecessarily difficult for no reason as if he wants us to do poorly on them. Do not recommend for F260.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. If you can take any class with him you should. I know this isn't his normal class but if he happens to teach it again this is a must take accounting elective. He's so accommodating and so understanding. I'm so happy that I was able to take this class with him. I for real couldn't recommend a teacher more than Lance he's amazing

The fact that he's recently graduated makes him stand out as a lecturer. He understands our perspective and teaches us what we actually need to know for exams. He's very straightforward during class and makes it easy to understand.

Lance is an absolute dog when it comes to the K-201 course. He not only teaches you what you need to know but also the tricks he's learned to make certain processes so much easier. 1000/10 would take again, made the course fun and easy.
One of the best K201 instructors. He is young, approachable, and can relate to students. His test averages are always at least 10% higher than the rest of the course.
Lancy Pantsy is the actual goat

He is knowledgeable about the subject, and if the lesson ends early with class time left, he offers to do after-class work together, which is very helpful for the class. My class's test averages were always at least 10% more than the average throughout all the classes. Really recommend!
K201 was a really difficult class but Lance teaches really well and makes K201 a lot easier than most professors.

Mr. Bradshaw was simply fantastic. He understood K201's difficult coursework and exams and how to teach that to freshmen meaningfully. He never wasted student time and went out of his way to help anyone in his class. He is quick but detailed. Easily, the best decision you can make by taking his K201 lab class.
Great teacher for K201, made things easy to understand and answered any questions we had

Lance is the most phenomenal K201 professor offered, and he is a must-take for a smooth and easy experience in the class. He's incredibly caring and actually caters his classes to his students, and is very helpful during office hours. Very grateful to have been in his class, amazing person and teacher. Could not recommend him more.

Lance is the best professor and person you can get. Not only does he makes K201 which is a supposed "weed-out" course easy but he is always there to help you and actually seems to be one of the few professors who cares if you succeed. He is a must have if you are taking K201
I would 100% take him again.
Easiest K201 professor by far.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lance is good, only drawback is his voice!

Lance is one of the best professors I've ever had despite him being a Masters student. He taught us well and always told us how hard each class was going to be. No messing around with busywork either once we were done he let us out which was sometimes only 10 minutes after class started. 10/10 would recommend.
The goat of K201, greatest professor at IU. Great at teaching, kept class simple and a great environment.

Best teacher ive ever had. Will sit with you as long as you need during office hours until you understand the material. Explains everything so simple it makes the whole process better. He just recently graduated from kelley so hes super knowledgable about everything and is easy to relate to. If ur worried about taking k201 definitely the prof for u
If you take k201 take it with Lance his average exam scores were always 10% higher than every other class and you will learn the most with him

Absolutely 100% recommend for K-201! He is an incredible instructor and is extremely knowledgeable on the K201 course. K201 is a difficult course for many people but it is his goal for all students to succeed! If you have to take K201 I cannot recommend taking it with him more!

DO NOT TAKE. take literally anyone else. takes forever grade. grades so hard. by the time he puts grades in, its too late to improve. doesnt tell you about important deadlines or if he does he only mentions it once. does not answer emails. Really amazing teacher but I will say the class gets really boring. Honestly you dont have to go to class if you dont want to but make sure you study outside of class. The course expectations are uniform across classes, so you always know what you need to do. I would recommend him for K201 any day!

The course itself has well-defined grade boundaries, so the expectations are clear. If you have any questions, the professor or the TA would be more than happy to help. Jamey Brooks was excellent; he has a dry sense of humor and is meticulous during his explanations of the course content. I would recommend him any day!

He's a great professor. He actually does database and spreadsheet work in his other job at IU, so he really knows what he's talking about. People make K201 sound harder than it is. He is a great instructor, and you can basically learn everything you need for the class just by listening to him. Also, he is a super nice guy once you get to know him.

I had this professor at 8 am and he was always ready to teach. The concepts were easy to follow and make sense. However, if you don't pay attention during class the whole time you will be lost and it's hard to catch back up unless you know what your doing. Highly recommend doing the Discovery on the E-Text before class.

I love Professor Brooks. The guy is super chill and has a great sense of humor. He's also very willing to help his students out. 

The ONLY issue I would say is he does grade harsher compared to other professors. Mainly in the fact that the quizzes and checks you take throughout the semester are 1 attempt while my friend had multiple attempts.

James is a suer good professor, he definitely knows what he is talking about and knows what he is doing. Super good at explaining things for a hard class like K201. I would definitely recommend taking this professor if you get a chance.

Good guy and knowledgable about excel, has a pretty dry sense of humour. However some of the other instructors do appear to be a lot more engaging. A solid instructor but probably shouldnt be your first choice. Def very skilled at excel tho. Wouldn't reccomend him for ms access however.

Jamey is fantastic for K201. Explains everything very clear in class. K201 is just a lot of work but if you do all the outside work and go to class, you'll be fine. Pretty serious but still funny and approachable seems like a great guy. If I could take another class with him I would.
Take her for W131. Great teacher helps a lot

Overall Ms. Brinkman is a great teacher. She is very caring and wants to make sure her students are okay. She is also a very nice person and if you need help/extentions on anything just talk to her and she will be understanding. She is not a tough grader and gives good feedback on your work. Overall I would definitely recommend her.

Incredibly kind and willing to help students with any paper needed. Essays become more demanding as the class continues, however, she also opens up more resources and allows more time to perfect them. Enjoyable lectures with fun and unique in-class activities are often.

Overall an incredible professor, she makes sure to take time to help students to understand the material, and inspired us to make papers on topics that typically aren't talked about from some backgrounds. Really influenced the way I think about a majority of subjects.

reviews.comment: This is absolutely the guy you want to be teaching you, incredibly insightful, as long as you pay attention, engage with lecture and attend class you will do exceedingly well. 2/5 of the final grade are basically free points, 3/5 are other major assignments that you are able to do well on if work is put in.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He cares for his students

Best professor I've had by far so far.  Cares for you as long as you care for the class and you can tell is passionate about what he teaches.  While the weekly reading assignments can become tedious, it is worth it to have Dr Wallace as a professor

This guy is genuinely the funniest professor you'll meet. His lectures are loaded but he makes them entertaining. I actually took C218 last year as a freshman but he had a class that was a 300 level and called Sports, Media, and Literacy. Overall his class was the same structure as C218. Dr. Wallace is an outstanding professor who cares about his students. Lectures are extremely engaging, and I never wanted to skip class. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Wallace is phenomenal. He is so kind, funny, and actually cares about your lives. He treats you like college students and is a big help when you need him. The readings are a bit lengthy and the weekly quizzes have some questions that come exclusively from lecture. As long as you participate, show up, and keep up with work, you'll get an A

This dude is honestly awesome took his class and liked him so much that I took him again for another class the next semester. I have never had a teacher with such engaging lectures; it doesn't even feel like class.

One of my favorite professors so far at IU. He is so nice and funny and makes class interesting. The assignments are straight forward and easy. The final exam is also easy, and I am not a media major, so this is a good Gen Ed too if you like sports.

Great class and awesome guy. He's strict about some things (dont use AI, dont have your airpods in during class, etc) but in general a smart, funny, encouraging, and relatable professor. He's been my favorite professor here since the first class. The weekly assignments can be annoying but very manageable, it's mostly opinionated, and the readings are all applicable and interesting. 10/10

Great professor, insightful sociology course. So good I signed up for his 300 level course, and so far am enjoying it just as much. Not too hard, but not an easy A either. Easily one of the better professors I've had at Indiana. He truly cares about himself and his students. If you put in the work, show up to class, and ask questions you will get a good grade in the class. I highly recommend this class

reviews.comment: great class, learned a ton. you can tell he puts a lot of effort into teaching and making the content interesting and understandable for us. he always raised interesting questions about sport and society and the class really changed my perspective on a lot of things

Wallace is the man, plain and simple. My fav professor and class at IU. He's brilliant but also authentic and encouraging. Dr. Wallace is amazing. Honestly ended up learning so much more than I expected and I actually enjoyed coming to class. Although he rambles and has long-winded lectures, it is not a hard class and he grades fairly. Terrible Class. Least liked professor at the school.
Interesting individual

Professor Burge made every lecture super interesting and he's super passionate about his area of study. There was quite a lot of outside reading, but it wasn't overwhelming. I looked forward to class with him.

reviews.comment:
Professor Burgins was my favorite professor I've had this semester. He has a great teaching style and creates an environment where students are able to thrive and comfortably talk in class during discussions.

Be prepared for handwritten notes due every week. He's very laid back and has a great sense of humor. You can use notes on exams too.

I loved this class. Genuinely the best course I have ever taken in all 4 years at IU. Scott truly cares about his students. He wants us to not only be better students, but better humans.  He was always so entertaining and fun. As someone who hates going to class, I attended every single class because I wanted to be there.

Scott seems like a really tough guy, but he's one of the kindest men I've ever met. He'll be real with you. Be prepared. BUT! He appreciates it when you're real with him too. He's a guy you can and should level with. Be ready to learn and grow when you're around him. A great professor and a stand-up guy all around.

Genuinely seems like he wants you to fail in this class, just rude and demanding and not straight forward. Slow at grading, ambiguous, and tends to degrade the student body and others as a whole in the middle of presentations bc he thinks it's funny

There's a lack of professionalism imo. The grading for assignments lacks clarity and rubrics, leading to confusion among students. Feedback lacks clarity and seems hasty, giving vague yes or no answers to questions. Seems like others like him quite a bit though.

Funny enough guy, but he is an absolute control freak that lacks a sense of direction and professionalism in the class and with his material. Prepare to write 10 pages of handwritten notes that are graded subjectively with no feedback

Scott is an amazing professor in many respects. He always manages to keep the class interesting, sharing plenty of his own personal stories from real world experiences, throwing jokes around in there often. My two things I would advise you to recognize when taking him:

2) prepare to spend 1-2 hours a night writing notes

He gave a decent amount of the grading to his T.A., who would count off major points for small things and lowered my grade a letter.

Professor Burgins class was definitely more difficult than the other professor for v236 (ex: you got a 0/50 every class if you didnt participate, but attendance wasnt even counted in the other class). Other then that, he cares about his students and as long as you attend class and take notes you'll get an A.

The workload can be a lot but it is consistent. 1-2 daily check-ins a week and handwritten notes due every week. Grading and class criteria is very clear. As long as you do the work, the quality does not seem to matter as much, you will get a passing grades. Tests were also very easy and were straight from the lectures, just take good notes.

Straightforward class. Mandatory notes, however they are directly based on test. workload 2 to 3 hrs a week. Lectures are actually really interesting. Professor Burgins is the funniest professor I've had at IU. Lectures constantly involve asking students about opinions/experiences. He learns peoples names, and actually cares unlike other professors

He is my favorite hands down. He wants you to take handwritten notes only, and no electronics in the class at all. He starts the class with a question. He really cares about his students & it shows. You can take the notes during class or on your own time. As long as you submit the notes you can use them on tests! No final:) my favorite professor!!!

His atmosphere and energy is unmatched and he makes class very fun and interesting. I would definitely take this class again, but beware for weekly homework's!

Professor Burgins is an awesome guy and a great teacher. I have really enjoyed taking his class this semester and will definitely take more of his in the future. He does a very good job just teaching you everything you need to know. This class forced me to take good notes and I am thankful for it. If you can take a class with him, definitely do it!

Professor Burgins was very engaging and made a mandatory class enjoyable. I really enjoyed his and the energy that he brough everyday. Scott is overall a really good professor. He is engaging and fun to listen to, he makes a mandatory class enjoyable and is very accommodating. No huge surprises and the requirements are very straightforward. Participation is key.

If you do not like writing, DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE. It is solely based on writing. To get an A, you MUST participate in class and do all the assignments on time!

He expects a lot from students, but I learned so, so much from him. It's worth putting the effort into his class. And he lets you rewrite big assignments to improve your grade.

Very generous with extensions. Makes a class that could be hard really manageable. We often got out of class early, and he gave us multiple days off. I would definitely recommend him as a teacher for C204.

TAKE BUNGER I LOVE HIM!! He's actually the best bus writing professor out there. He cares to get to know all his students and your lives outside school. AMAZING professor. easiest for C204. other teachers are harder for bus writing trust me take Bunger no matter what

Great guy, Great teacher, definitely recommed.

Amazing professor! So sweet, so kind, makes such a nice environment in class. Although he might go a little slow compared to other C204 classes, it it so nice because we have less work and only focus on the important tasks.
Respectably, Professor Bunger is the only option for C204. Take it with him.
Professor Bunger is the best professor I have had at IU. He genuinely cares about his students and their well-being. He is very personable and all around just a great guy.

Professor Bunger is my favorite professor I have had in college. He is funny and a witty lecturer. His background is in law and it shows through his writing and speaking abilities. He often brings his dog in class and has great taste in music. All around great guy.

Bunger is super chill, takes the time to get to know you individually and gives loads of time to complete assignments so the class is very low stress. Brings his dog to class sometimes too, would 100% recommend

I really loved Bunger's class, but at times it was very unserious, and he felt more like a student than a teacher. Not that that is a bad thing, but when it comes to grading and feedback it kind of lacks... But, if you are looking for a chill professor who brings his dog to class and does extra credit kahoots, this is the man for you!

If you are taking C-204, I would highly suggest taking it with Bunger. Not only did he make his lectures enjoyable, he will get to know your class by first name and ask questions to everyone to ensure that he grows a one on one relationship, very caring, very nice, and super funny. I always looked forward to going to his lecture!
Amazing, best teacher ever!!!! So funny and helpful. Makes his lectures extremely engaging and interesting.
Andrew is an absolute beast. He makes class fun and enjoyable. If you want to have a great time, take Andrew.
Don't expect this class to be easy or fun. People will say this but it is untrue, the test materials are the same except you wont be prepared. Would recommend looking for another professor.
Best professor I've had at IU. Highly recommend taking him for C204. Make sure you take advantage of going to his office hours, they really help!

Bunger is by far the most personable professors at Kelley. He genuinely cares about his students and values their well being over academic success. If you have any extenuating circumstances, do not be afraid to communicate with him. He is incredibly accommodating. He is a great teacher and explains concepts well. Definitely go to office hours!

Prof Bunger genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. I have had many good conversations with him during office hours and before/after class about my goals after getting through undergrad. He's always willing to help his students out to whether it be advice or just talking through one of his assignments. 10/10 would recommend.

Besides being one of the most caring and respectful people to meet, bunger strikes you more as a mentor or friend who's trying to teach you something you can utilize in your life later on. He is very likeable because he understands a student's life. If you want to get an A , make sure you hop on zoom for office hours and let him review your work.

Prof Bungers is one of the best Profs at Kelley, He cares about his students and finds ways to actually make you improve. You never know where the direction of the class is going to go and he actually used a variety of platforms to effectively make this best online course I've ever taken. Go to office hours and participate in class, you'll do well

Professor Bunger is one of my favorite professors in Kelley. He truly cares about his students, and he wants each and every one of us to grow as individuals and professionals. Really cool guy and good professor - I would definitely recommend.

Professor Bunger is one of the most caring Professors that I have met in this school. He focuses on teaching students what is like for business writing. I am an international student so I sometimes feeling struggle when writing a report or email professionally. I recommend everyone to take C204 with him!

Bunger is the nicest, most caring professor I have ever met. He is so understanding of his students and what is happening in their lives. He genuinely cares about the success of his students and will do anything to help you succeed. He is one of the easiest c104 and c204 professors in Kelley and gives the least work.
Good guy, but test didnt cover material in class.

reviews.comment: Andrew is one of the best professors I have ever had. In my opinion hes one of the most caring and down to earth professors at Kelley. Hes incredibly smart and goes out of his way to help his students. I learned so much in C204 and am extremely lucky for having Andrew as my prof.

Easily the best professor I've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students' wellbeing and is just a cool guy in general. I actually looked forward to going to his class because he made it so fun and enjoyable. I 110% recommend taking him

reviews.comment: To say that Bunger is a great teacher is an understatement. He is a tough grader, but he gives good feedback. He is a really great guy, and he was very easy to connect with. He is very funny and personable, and made this boring class much more bearable because he is a great guy. Favorite professor I have ever had
One of the best professors I have ever had. Everyone should take him for c204. He genuinely cares for his students and wants each and every person to succeed.
Great teacher and really helped me grow as a presenter and is overall a cool guy.

I'd recommend Professor Bunger's course for three reasons: interactive lectures,access to feedback, & genuinely cares for his students. Additional Note: To get an A in the course: attend every class session and do all required reading. In hindsight, I think every hour I put into the class was worth it, as my skills have improved & I learned a lot
It was his first semester switching from Compass to C204, but he did well and gave great feedback especially in our group work.

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor of T275, great person. He does grade the homework.
