kind of geeky, but because she gives you the notes the class is a breeze

He never answers a question directly. There is no way to study material and there is nothing you can do about it. I'm prepared to fail this class. His class is 2 hours long and he talks about NOTHING, there is no structure, he just spits out random information that is so irrelevant.

I've not taken any German classes from him, only literature, but I think he's a fantastic professor in that reguard. Some of the most interesting discussions I've had in my time at IU, and his level of preparedness along with his expertise made for an amazing class experience. Only complaint is that he sometimes rambles and gets off topic a bit

Overall this class is an interesting study of German culture. Rather than a typical chronological approach your learn through course topics. The professor is a tough but fair grader. The best way to succeed in this class is follow the syllabus and engage with the lectures. Chaouli has a great understanding of the material and I learned a ton.

The grading system is very misleading! Don't even worry about trying to test out "what if scores" on canvas because Michel Chaouli goes off an entire different grading system that should not be allowed at IU. Pop quizzes every day in class so make sure you show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The good grade distribution for this class on IU website was misleading. Even with doing all the required reading the quizzes/midterms were way dificult. Only 10 multiple choice, and 4 huge essays on the midterm that are graded way too harshly. Also went to office hours and he laughed at my essays. Rude. This is coming from a 3.9 student
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor McBride's class is one of the hardest classes I've taken so far, but also one of the best. I found that he was a hard grader, but everything was fair, he gave out homework that you could keep up with and was helpful with any questions you have. Sometimes his lectures can drone on, but you can tell he cares about what he's teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor McBride is a good guy at heart. He truly cares about marketing and has some good experiences to talk about. But, the tests for M370 was beyond difficult to the point that a good portion of students failed. The lectures didn't really give any learning materials, just basic slides that had no meaning that he would talk on for a looong time.

I would avoid taking McBride at all costs. The lectures are painfully boring, the exams are so difficult. I know he might be your only option for marketing I-core but if you have another one go with them. His exams are also in class and 50-60 questions long so just overall very difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: McBride is probably the most boring professor I have ever met. He makes attendance required because no one would come if he didn't. Also, his lecture slides are basically useless, random graphs paired with information from the textbook which makes his lectures have absolutely no substance.

Looks and sounds like the teacher from Ferris Bueller. Super Boring super monotone. Cold Calls. Has to enforce attendance because nobody shows up to his terribly boring lessons. 90% of his class is him droning on whatever or just having students answer inconsequential questions.

Chris makes the class so fun and entertaining, and everything you learn in class will be beneficial once you get in Romania! By far one of the best experiences of my life. Rank Romania high on your preferences if you want an easy class with a teacher who prioritizes fun and learning! Best X272 prof by far

Prof Cook cares so much about student success and that is evident through how he instructs his students. He gets to know everyone on an individual basis and creates a learning environment to help all sucede. I plan on taking more courses with him.

Chris Cook is the funniest professor I've ever had in my life. First 8 weeks of class is fun learning about Romania in the classroom. It may seem to start slow, but get excited for in country because once we got there we had packed days of company and culture visits everyday. He gets great staff members to come and there was never a dull moment.
I could not have asked for a better professor on a trip like this. He ensured we learned as much as possible in a short amount of time.

Professor Cook made this class incredibly fun and meaningful. The assignments during the class were all beneficial and helped me learn a lot, and the time in Romania was very well planned and was an amazing time. I would highly recommend going to Romania with Professor Cook.

Chris was an amazing professor who put a lot of time and effort into planning the class and the trip to Romania. He cared about all of the students and was very supportive. Everyone should take this class with Chris and go to Romania with him!!

Chris was an awesome professor - he taught our class so much about the Romanian business environment and about how to be considerate travelers abroad. He was very fun on the trip and set a great example of a business professional - would take this class and travel to Romania again!

Professor Cook is an incredible professor, and one of my favorite teachers. The class is tough and requires a lot of work, but he is laid back and makes the lectures a lot more enjoyable. He is relatable and understanding if you have any conflicts outside of class. If you have to take Cost Accounting, I would highly recommend taking Professor Cook.
barely taught any material. Would ramble on all class about nonsense not even related to class. Had to learn everything on my own

Cook is the kind of professor you remember even after graduating from college. Thanks for making accounting unbearable Generally IU has some kind and intelligent profs who invest a ton into their students. Unfortunately, Cook isnt one of them. He doesnt treat teaching/and his students seriously.

Avoid this teacher if you can. He is the guy who makes the final impossible, but curves up. This sounds kinda good with the curve, but he doesnt actually read your exams. He had 1700 short answer questions graded 3 hours after we took the final. Unlikely he truly read them at all, if you know what I mean.

This is one of those upper level classes where you are learning things like "cash flows" again for the 10th class. The final exam is 35 impossible short answer questions. Despite having almost 2000 short answer questions to grade, Cook graded all exams in 4 hours and I dont think its physically possible he actually read all the exams.

Chris Cook is a bad lectures who requires a lot of reading and teaches NOTHING. Everyone taught themselves before the exam, and his questionable tactics (when interacting with students) should be looked into immediately!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Among the lowest ranked Kelley instructors for a reason- this man probably has a worse attitude than his teaching style (which is already pretty awful). Agreeing with the previous reviews: AVOID AVOID AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you cannot get into another professor's A325 session, I would wait for a semester before jumping into cost accounting. The material is difficult, but others do not take participation into consideration like Cook does.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm in his cost accounting class this semester. At first i was biased from reading reviews on here, but as time went on, i realized that... WHO LET THIS MAN TEACH HERE!? Kelley, IU, if you're reading, please remove him from a teaching position because ive never had a lecturer like this guy.
Cook has a bad personality overall... I didnt think the class was hard but the exams are quite messy

Cost accounting is a hard course in itself and Cook made it worse. Nothing he talks about in class makes any sense. Exams are unbelievably hard and he is a tough grader. Honestly if I had a choice, I would never want to work with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Would NOT recommend. He explains every chapter in a manner that is more complicated than it needs to be while also leaving out critical key points. It was clear that he is not confident on many of the basics of A325. He is arrogant and consistently praises himself & guides class discussion towards his own personal life and his own accomplishments.

this guy's still teaching 325? get out. you're enrolled in his class? get out. took him last year during the spring semester, what a joke. unlike other "unprofessional" or bad/boring lecturers, this guy adds a bit of condescendingness to his classroom.

Easily the one of the worst lecturers at IU- I didnt like his personality and the in class stuff is kinda hard to follow. I would take it with another person because I heard cost accounting shouldnt be a hard class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: A325 was my least favorite class in college- because of Cook. He talks about football on a daily basis and dismisses other people's opinions (both sports- and non sports-related). Upset that he's teaching at Kelley, a well-known business institution.

Do not take him. We have homework before every class and quizzes every week on MyAccountingLab which is not a user-friendly tool! His teaching style is confusing, increasing the level of self-study you need to do. Exams are extremely hard and totally depend on how much self-study you do. Do not enrol in his class if you have a choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Surprised to see how many people are still using this website/actually rating profs. But Chris Cook probably deserves this. In response to the person who said he changes all grades to 100%: simply not true! He expects you to answer questions at least twice a week, if you dont? you get a 0 for participation

He tries TOO HARD to appeal to the students (because he knows literally nobody likes him) and talks CONSTANTLY about what a nice guy he is for not giving out an exam after little 5 weekend. Please do yourself a favor and AVOID! worst professor ever and a good exam date doesn't offset his AWFUL personality!! other C325 profs give easier tests anyway

Yes, I did receive an A in this course. However, Chris Cook receives an F for his teaching style, professionalism, and homework assignments. He earns no respect from anyone in the classroom.  His lectures are extremely difficult to follow, and he is somewhat too personal about his private life. I would strongly recommend for you to look elsewhere

Prof. Cook spends half of scheduled class time telling lame jokes that rarely inspire any response. He can be rather unprofessional in that his tests and lectures are unorganized and vary in difficulty. It is rather difficult to receive a good grade in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great professor as he is one of the fairest I've had. For example, he gave us a day off for little five week and moved the test around to help us have a good time. Although there is a lot of homework as long as you try to  do it he will change all of the grades to a 100%. If you're lazy don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's an interesting guy and tries to be really cool, but the class is tough. The lectures are somewhat confusing and tests are tough. Records participation and attendance. The myaccountinglab work is not very helpful. This isn't an easy class to begin with, so another instructor would probably not be much better.

1) He uses Pearsons accounting lab, which is the worst possible way to teach accounting. It is not iterative whatsoever. 2) He assigns homework on subjects before giving the lecture. 3) The weekly quizes are also on Pearsons and one was over  a chapter we never covered 4) he wants to make his class hard and grade distribution sucks 5)***AVOID

He's ok but I would take it with someone else. His lectures are confusing and he makes jokes rather than being clear and concise. He also uses Pearson My Accounting Lab for homework and quizzes which is a terrible teaching tool. The exams are tough but thats expected in a 300 level course. No practice exams or useful study materials for exams

This class was way too much work for cost accounting. Two homeworks and a quiz every week isn't needed if you're a good teacher. Wastes time during lectures trying to be cool and "humbly" bragging about his life. Also the tests are close to impossible no matter how hard you study.
WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD! Does not know how to teach! Tries too hard to be cool and funny and spends less time on teaching. Do not take him if you would like to understand accounting.

Dr. Ruiz is simply the best professor I've had at IU. Super energetic, always asks if anyone has questions, and cares about every single student in the classroom. You don't get many professors like her. You also get a cheat sheet for tests. The course is exam heavy, but the cheat sheet, homework, and quizzes set you up well.
what a nice lady

She is amazing and caring. The course is difficult, but you will get an A4-size cheat sheet. She is one of the best accounting professors at Kelley. She gives partial credits for free-response questions on the exams. I am honesty so grateful to have her as my A329 professor. She has the best lectures, super helpful OH, love her SO MUCH!!!!
She is average and very unnaccomodating! She is very unapproachable to some students and overly nice to some.

Any class with Maria Clor is a must take. Every lecture feels interesting, and she usually has a unique way of teaching each week. She kindly invited the SPARC Team to present in class about advising (those guys are the best). Plays Taylor Swift songs before class.  My only criticism is she kept asking me to follow @luddyadvising on instagram.
Best professor in the business. Take as many classes as you possibly can with Maria, you will not regret it.

I recommend T100 strongly. The lecture can be a bit boring for some classes, but it's a very very easy A+ and 1.5 credit hours. Professor is nice and she is entertaining. Typically there is one assignment to do per lecture but they typically take under 10 minutes each and are accepted late. If you got lower than an A you are honestly cooked.

The course was very easy and her grading was very lenient. The lectures are pretty boring and there's usually one per day, but it's moreso the course material that gets boring rather than her presentation of it. Overall she is very understanding and caring and does a good job at keeping the class engaging and entertaining for what it is.

Frank Cloud is a very nice guy who loves what he teaches. He drops 2 of the 5 exams you take and is always available when you need a question answered. I would recommend going to his lectures because he goes over short exam questions that are very similar to the ones he puts on the exam. His AI's are also amazing and very helpful!!

Always accommodating and a very nice guy. Chill class, and he drops 2 out of the 5 exams you take. Gives good feedback on the short answer assignments due weekly. I would recommend attending lectures because he goes over exact test questions. His AI's are also very great and helpful.

This professor is clearly passionate about biology and kind overall, but the course felt overly difficult for an intro-level class. Lectures often went too in-depth and were hard to follow. The TAs were very helpful though. Exams had limited study resources given, and having three exams in the three final weeks was horrid.
He's a really nice guy, he just sucks at explaining things. His tests are unnecessarily hard and has the worst grade distribution for all managerial accounting teachers. Take someone else if you can

Pretty good at explaining the concepts in lecture. Attend discussions because they solidify everything. Clark makes sure we get our questions asked and answered. He really encourages people to come to his office hours or go to review sessions as well.

Overall decent professor. He's mostly good at explaining the concepts in the one class a week. Definitely go to the help/review sessions M-Th nights. I had a solid B but started going to every review session the week leading up to the exams and ended up with an A. Also the weekly discussions are crucial, I would be lost without them

Jeff is a very clear lecturer and makes the concepts easy to follow. The discussion sections are really helpful to practice the lecture content, but Jeff gives you a good foundation and encourages you to ask questions.

The course is hard but he's a super nice guy and his lectures are pretty good. He is also very clear in what he's teaching and how to do certain things. He probably has the most conveniently organized and helpful Canvas and the resources in it. Would definitely recommend taking his class.

The department makes this course difficult, but Prof Clark is a great teacher. He explains concepts well & spends time making sure students understand the material. Be prepared to spend hours and hours studying for exams though. I'd recommend taking him
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
his voice puts me to sleep

probs why im gonna fail lol
Cool guy frfr
He's good at basketball. Baller and great 3 point shooter, great teacher too

His lectures are straightforward, the homework is super easy, and he gives out plenty of resources to prepare for tests. The class was light, 8-10 homework problems per week and 1 pre-class video per week (10-20 mins, but you can put it on 2x speed). Yes, it's test-heavy, but the tests are MCQs and you have plenty of time to work on them.
I got an A-. good luck. these classes such
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was worried after seeing the previous semester about Professor Clark, however he was great! The exams are the only thing that really affect your grade so study for them. He prepares as well as he can, and gives practice questions using AI. He also takes student's opinions and tries to adjust the course which I appreciate.

Professor Clark was great! He wants his students to learn, so he provides them with the resources to do so. His lectures are very straightforward and he encourages students to ask questions during class. Be prepared to attend class to get the notes you need for your packet and attend discussions to be best prepared for class. Great professor & guy!
Great teacher

Lectures are a little grueling because he is so monotone, but he genuinely cares about his students. Currently studying for the 2nd exam and here is what he has done so far:

1. Realized he didn't emphasize something enough --> emailed students to review the concept 

2. Kelley says HE can't make a practice exam, so he made two using chat gpt

Not a fan. Boring lectures and exams were clearly not written for undergrads. Lectures consist of him reading off slides and they are essentially useless. Get ready to learn all the content basically on your own, or take Prof. B. This class should not be as hard as he makes it.
Class average on the exams were around 80%, and he curved the entire class grade by 4%. Overall, decent professor with fair exams. I'd recommend going to discussion as I found it to be very helpful.

friendly but it was his first time teaching the course (and undergrads in general) and it was painfully obvious. the lectures were boring and not useful (and he rarely finished his slideshows on time if at all). class averages on exams were not high, and he didn't seem too concerned by that. take prof b if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The average on his tests were around 80% and he added a 4% curve at the end of the course. Content isn't too difficult and the discussion sections helped a lot.

Lectures were went through the content very quickly by thoroughly. Many students struggled with the tests but I didn't think they were bad as long as you studied the discussion handouts and extra practice. Super nice guy. Very doable class and would him as a professor
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were went through the content very quickly by thoroughly. Many students struggled with the tests but I didn't think they were bad as long as you studied the discussion handouts and extra practice. Super nice guy. Very doable class and would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Solid guy, but goes crazy fast so its hard to pick up stuff. his exams are very fair and dont try to trick you, you can put minimal effort into studying and pass, the third exam is pretty tough. It kinda sucks paying 50 bucks for the course packet which is free in A304. Good prof, but it was his first time teaching undergrads and it shows.

Clark is a nice guy and fine prof, but content was very quickly moved through and never benefited from lectures. Discussions with TAs definitely help more. Overall, the course is just very difficult and test heavy. Manageable if your willing to put in the work. Utilize peer coaching through Kelley, that helps a lot.

Was his first semester teaching the course, he was just okay. The exams were pretty hard and 80% of your grade. Hard course overall and you will be studying a lot. I would recommend taking it with Prof B instead if you can. He was nice though!

Since this was his first year teaching the course I don't believe him to be a good teacher. It more felt like he was speaking at us and not teaching. Course is hard regardless, average 100% on the homework to help for exams.

Do not take her. She is so mean to her students and incredibly passive-aggressive. She is never available to meet outside of the class time and you cannot reach her via email either. I honestly have never dreaded a class more than this one. Do NOT take any classes with her. It's not worth it.

Do not take her class. It is so bad. Never dreaded a class so much at Kelley. I literally think that they are trying to fire her because she keeps being evaluated. All she does is complain, and her class is much harder than the other L  375 classes. Do not do this to yourself.

Needs to be fired. The content is easy because everything is open note and online but she is unbelievably rude to students. Doesn't know the content and just reads off the slides and is furious when you try ask questions. Easy to get an A+ but so unprofessional and it's honestly painful to sit through her lectures.

The class was SO easy all exams and quizzes were online and open-note. But... she was a terrible professor. She was so mean and was not available outside of class at all to help. She was so vague in what she wanted for assignments and was so nit picky about grades. It was still an easy A and worth taking the class for the grade.

One of the worst profs at IU. Lectures are terrible and communication with Dr Hamilton is near impossible as she never responds to emails and is "occupied" during her own scheduled office hours and won't meet with students. Other than that class wasn't difficult. 100% not equipped to prof. at Kelley or any college for that matter.

She is unapproachable and passive-aggressive. She is also unprepared: frequent typos in her slideshows which can confuse students (mismatching definitions) and online quizzes/discussions are posted late more often than not. Lectures are boring, so it's frustrating that attendance is mandatory. Avoid taking a class with her.

The easiest A+ I have gotten in kelley. All the tests and quizzes are online with a lockdown browser. Class time is useless as Clovia sits up and complains about stuff. She has a short temper and calls out students for no reason. Overall easy class since everything is online but horrible teacher.
Just bad
Take her. All tests and quizzes online from home.
Boring proffesor and lectures but all tests and quizzes are online. take L 201 with her because every other student with other proffesors have to dedicate so much time to studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Take this proffesor for L 201! All tests and quizzes are online. Other proffesor have students struggling but this class was so easy. Lectures are stupid and I didn't pay attention but tophat attendance is taken. I promise the easiest way out of L 201 is with this proffesor. TAKE HER!!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and don't take this professor. Very boring lecturer and tough grader. Blames students and does not take any responsibility if we do poorly. Class is out of 100 points so every point affects your grade. Quizzes are online and aren't too bad, but that is the only thing she has going for this class.

She is an absolute joke of a professor. The class is a joke too. 20% of grade is attendance. No enthusiasm. Insanely rude. All quizzes and tests are online. She doesn't even know what shes talking about most of the time because all slide decks are not hers.
If you take this course be prepared to be bored to death. She shows ZERO enthusiasm for the course. At least the exams are online, the only thing going for this course.
Class is worth 100 points so there is little to no opportunity on improving your grade. Only offers one extra credit point which is an introduction of yourself at the beginning of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Insanely rude. She literally admits she doesn't have sympathy for students. She taught grad school and acts like a bunch of sophomores are grad students. The class is only out of 100 points, so u have to do very good on everything. Don't take her for L201.
She was very nice but a harsh grader. Easily accessible and would help you with everything. A lot of the assignments were AI generated and pretty annoying.

Kind person, average professor. She's always open to answering questions both inside and outside of class, but the grading feels inconsistent, and feedback isn't the best at times. She doesn't overload the class with work, and it's very easy to stay on top of things, but the class feels harder than it needs to be.

She is a nice person but not a good teacher. We are given pointless AI generated assignments in class and expected to do 90% of the work on our own time. She also grades really harshly but doesn't give feedback about how we can improve

Do not take this prof. Genuinely so unreasonable and provides extremely unclear criteria for assignments. Refuses to give full marks and seems to grade based on if she likes you or not. For a class that's supposed to be an easy a, you'd be better off taking anyone else.

Sarah Clark is a very nice professor who cares about her students. She didn't assign that much work and keeping up with the class isn't hard. However, she is a very tough grader and will dock you many points for tiny things. Also, about 7 assignments went in after the class ended so it was hard to tell what you needed beforehand.

Very nice person, not a good teacher. It seems as though her advice is nitpicky and she gives out bad grades just to lower the c204 grade distribution because it's an easy class. It is almost impossible to get anything over a 90 so your grade just sits between a B and A-. Do not take this class if you want to save your gpa.
She is super nice and doesn't assign that much work but she is a very tough grader.
Very nice professor and willing to help. Very harsh grader the first couple assignments. Can be vague on instructions but not an easy A whatsoever.

Professor Clark was so so nice and wanted everyone to do well. Quickly learns her students names and about gets to know them. Lots of class time covers examples of assignments and allows time for work especially towards the end. Assignments were overall helpful for real world. Was a fair grader. Should pick her for C204 if available.

Professor Clark was a very kind and caring teacher. She did have a lot of work but it was super easy. The group projects weren't bad and classes were a bit boring. But, it was super easy and she was actually very helpful. You can't really make bus writing fun so it was not her fault it was boring. If you want to get good at writing she's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Clark was a great professor. If you have to take C204 definitely go for her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Super nice and cares a lot about her students. If you go to office hours to review a paper before its due, you will likely get a better grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This teacher is decent. Seems very kind towards students but sometimes talks too much even when class is over. Sarah is also a tough grader due to her swallowing her pride in writing for multiple companies in the past. If you're working hard in the class, the grade you can at least pull is a B.

Her lectures are subpar and I sometimes found it difficult to relate it back to what was being assigned. The structure and timeline of the case project needs to be improved, was very unsure of what was due and when. She is an extremely hard grader. I mostly averaged a 90 on papers with minor "errors" or subjective wording discrepancies.
Rambles a little too much in her lectures and class is quite unproductive.

Professor Clark is very nice and cares deeply about her students, but her grading is very tough and I never received anything higher than a 94% on any paper. Her lectures are very random and not very useful which is the main reason I wouldn't take her again. She rambles on about nothing and the class feels like a waste of time.
Professor Clark is genuine with her students and gives great feedback. Unlike other professors within Kelley, she takes the time to establish a relationship with each of her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is one of my favorite professors. Be ready to contribute during class, but she is very personable. I consistently use writing skills from her class in my business writing.

Professor Clark is really a tough grader. I took business communication and every assignment got an average of B-, thanks to my group and we did a nice job on case project, I can just touch the line of B. She didn't tell us why give this grade and I guarantee that when she is grading, The beginning level is B-

I enjoyed this course and thought it was interesting, however it is only graded on four things: 2 presentations, the midterm essay, and the final essay. She gives good feedback, however throughout the entire course we have no idea about our grades. Attendance isn't really mandatory, but don't skip too much bc you will fall behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Prof Pinaud is very qualified and passionate about this class, but if you want an easy A I wouldn't recommend taking this class. The class itself is graded on 10 things, and sometimes the grading criteria is unclear. She does not take attendance but shows a preference for students who show up. The class is discussion-heavy and has lots of readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Pinaud is awesome and does very important work, and I thought that class discussions provided great insight into her field. Be sure to be prepared because readings are discussed in class, and she cold calls. If you skip regularly you will be called out in class. Otherwise she is a great professor if you're interested in learning ab genocide.

Easily the best and most interesting class I have ever taken. Initially, I was shocked by Professor Pinaud's bluntness, however, after a couple weeks realized how much I appreciate it. She clearly knows a lot about what she is talking about and pushes her students to do their best. The assignments gave so much freedom to really explore our topic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The class was reading off of a slideshow and she flipped through so fast that you could not write everything down in time and the slides weren't posted either. Class grade was based on four essays with no rubric and  little to no feedback was given. Content seemed to be based off of her own interests and studies rather than a historical analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She has a "no-nonsense" attitude and can sometimes come off as intimidating. The class isn't really that difficult as long as you read, she prefers to have free-flowing discussions. So even if you didn't read the discussions are still engaging and there is a lot to comment on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took INTL-I 306 with Prof. Pinaud fall 2021. She is a smart and knowledgable professor but this class was hard and very demanding. Multiple readings per lecture, doesn't use powerpoint or anything, and just relies on talking. Interesting subject but very unenthusiastic professor. Has stark opinions and will put you on the hot seat if you disagree.

I highly discourage anyone from taking a class with Pinaud. She is condescending and regularly discusses her disdain for students and teaching. She is very vague with all of her assignment guidelines and gives no feedback when taking points away. 

She is also a harsh grader. Do not expect a good experience with this professor.

Avoid this class! I do not recommend this professor at all. She is very knowledgeable in her field, but every class you are required to do readings that are up to 20-80 pages. Your overall grade will be based off on two presentations and two exams (written). She is very passive-aggressive and rude. Literally the worst class I have taken!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She 100% knows what she is talking about in her field. There is a lot of reading in her classes and her exams are less than 20 questions and come straight from her power points. If you don't pay attention in class she will call you out, but she is very willing to help anyone in need. Ask questions, take notes, pay attention and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Pinaud is awesome. She is so so smart and accomplished, and both are evident in her lectures. Its a tough class and the only grades are exams, but if you work for it, youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class! The only grades are 4 test that are all under 20 questions so if you miss 1 you are screwed. Half of the class dropped after failing the first test and then she said we needed to try harder. Also the readings she assigns are very long and difficult to understand.

Worst professor I have had at IU, hands down. Exams are worth 25% of your grade and consist of 13 questions. 20% of the class failed the first exam and when asked what we could do to improve our score, she told us to "try harder." Extremely condescending and rude to students. Lectures are just a reiteration of the readings. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class was based off of three test grades and the tests were only 15-20 multiple choice questions so make sure you are prepared. However, if you do the readings (which can be long) and review the powerpoint notes they are very easy. Her voice is pretty monotone and the lectures are pretty boring but she knows what she's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I was really intimidated by this prof at first. She's a no-nonsense type and she's not afraid to call you out for slacking or poor performance. However, I wouldn't call her a tough grader. There are only a few things you're graded on, but I got A's on everything. Do the reading, speak up in class and you'll be just fine, plus you'll learn a ton.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: There's a lot of reading for this course, but it's bearable and most things are pretty interesting. There aren't a lot of grades so you have to do well on tests and a presentation. Pinaud knows her stuff and expects you to do the reading. Not the easiest class but what you get out of it depends on how much work you put in.

Do not take physiology with professor Clark. Not only does she not explain lecture slides well, she moves at too fast of a pace. Understanding the context is very difficult to grasp and understand. Practice exams that are meant to mimic as preparation for exam's are nowhere near what actually ends up being on the exams.

You will definitely hear many horror stories about this class and there is some truth to them. Physiology is a difficult class by itself. The way Dr. Clark has her class set up is to try to help you succeed in this difficult class. Her class is very lecture heavy and you will most likely feel overwhelmed with information.*lots of extra credit*

She is not a bad professor, with the content you are expected to learn, the teaching style is definitely not for everyone. If you put in the recommended amount of studying hours per week you will do okay. All exams are curves, and there is plenty of extra credit opportunities. Physiology is a very lecture and informationally heavy class.
She is not a good professor. If you are a freshman and pre nursing major don't take her class.

I was able to get an A without attending any lectures and only studying a few hours the week of the exam. Dr. Clark makes the grading more forgiving compared with other courses by offering a ton of extra credit, large curves on exams, and making exams worth only 50% of the grade. For that reason alone I would choose her again for this class.

Clark is not a good lecturer and is bad at explaining content. She focuses on details that become irrelevant and leaves important concepts vague and doesn't care if you don't understand. Test questions are tedious and don't align with the material she covers or the reviews making the exams incredibly difficult. Don't take this class with her.

Prof. Clark is amazing and gets a bad rep mainly because the course is hard. It is absolutely possible to earn an A. She offers lots of extra credit and curves exams. Exams are based strictly on lectures and she records them. I ended with a 95% and could've put in more effort. If you read before class, listen, and work hard, you will do well.

This class will honestly be very challenging if you're a freshman. That being said, Pat Clark gives out lots of extra credit, and the material on exams is strictly from the lecture. If you are studying for her exams, do not waste time combing through the book; just rewatch the lectures and be able to recite information without the notes.

Honestly, she's incredibly sweet, and I enjoyed our few interactions. I think she just gets a bad rep because of the course itself, but she offers tons of extra credit. I would advise that you plan to put in lots of studying into this course. Utilize the UTA's and don't be afraid to ask her for help. I didn't, and now I'm planning on retaking it.

I'm begging you...DO NOT take physiology with Pat Clark. I would beg for the bus to hit me every morning so I didn't have to go to her class. Obviously, I wasn't looking for an easy A in a physiology class, but she made the class extremely difficult for no reason. You would have to go to at least one study session a week to even learn anything.

Hear me out... I would recommend Pat Clark. People are only complaining about the course because they want an easy A. Physiology is no easy course so regardless of the instructor, you're bound to study a lot. Additionally, those who said they study a lot but end off with a B+ or lower are just lying because I haven't studied at all and have an A-!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do NOTTTTTTT take this class with Pat Clark if you are Pre-Med/Pre-Dental/Pre-Nursing because your GPA will suffer. Yes she gets a bad rep...because it's true. She does not specify ever, leaving you with a vague idea of what to pay attention to for exams. I studied HARD and I still got a C with her. Take the class with someone else!!!!

She gets a really bad wrap, but she is a very good teacher. The course is difficult, but that is to be expected in a course like this. If you are not studying for multiple hours every day this is definitely not the course for you. She gives a lot of extra credit opporuntities and if you do not do well on tests you can still succeed in this course.

I think Dr. Clark is a good professor. The material is tough, but she is straightforward with what's going to be on the test. She gives lots of opportunities for extra credit and even curves the test. I think the material is just tough and that's why she gets a bad wrap. She is always accessible and willing to answer questions.

Professor Clarke is a great teacher and a super genuine person. Her class is difficult but you should know going into it what to expect. Her exams align with the lectures. I'm taking this for a pre nursing class. She wants you to succeed, giving out extra credit and curves. You get what you put in, you should expect to study 10 to 15 hours a week.

Dr. Clark is an amazing professor. I'm a nursing student taking this for pre-reps and she will teach you so much and is a genuine person that will always listen to you. Exams are not hard as long as you put in the work, however a lot of studying is needed to do good. She gives good curves on the exam and always try's to help you out for the better.

Pat is obviously an intelligent woman, and she is genuinely nice. But her test questions really don't align with the material she posts on lecture slides and that's why I think people tend to fail. To whoever said along the lines that you can't say she is a terrible teacher if you get bad grades because you don't put the work in is FALSE.

DO NOTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTTT take her, you will BE BETTER OFF TAKING ANYONE ELSE. I don't know what anyone else in these comments is talking about. Especially if you're a senior trying to graduate. The material is heavy, UTAs explain things differently- and I mean material NOT PROVIDED BY HER, and it's just a mess. Please, save yourself.

Dr. Clark seems really intimidating at first, but she is such a nice and caring person. She is also super funny and is always willing to help. This class is very challenging, that is a given, but you knew that before coming in. You can't say a teacher is terrible when you get bad grades because you don't put in the work.

She is a nice person but worst class I've ever taken. Probably be the reason I don't get into the nursing program. Lecture heavy with way too many details.Makes everything way harder compared to other physio professors.exams were hell, looked nothing like the reviews. Asks so many trick questions.has a ton of out of class work.

Is this class easy? No, and by no means am I saying it is, but if you go in with the right mentality and show up to class  all the resources are provided to succeed. Dr.Clark is so nice and you can tell she puts in so much work to help people succeed. There are multiple TA office hours every day and her door is always open. Ask questions!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Clark is an amazing professor! Get past the fact that her class is hard, you knew that going in. Don't hate the player hate the game

Dr. Clark is actually a very kind person. I'll be the first to admit that I was intimidated by her and the class. Once you go to her office hours or even just talk to her at the end of class, you will see that she actually wants you and other students to do well. Obviously this is a hard subject and it is very important to know what you are doing.

Physiology is a hard class don't get me wrong, but the professor is very nice. If you don't put in the work you will not do well. You need to actually try to learn the information. If you actually talk to Dr. Clark, you will find that she is actually very kind and she really does want you to do well. You have to put in the work to get good grades.
She is a very kind and caring professor! The other reviews are just people who don't want to do the necessary work!

Obviously the class is hard and challenging but Dr. Clark is very understanding and very kind. Her office hours are super helpful and all the UTAs are super good. She offers a curve on the exam but the tests are still hard. If you work hard you will do good in the class.

She is such a caring proffessor and clearly wants everyone to do good and wants to help people as much as posssible. Obviously physiology is a hard subject so there is difficult tests, but she gives you amble opprotunity to do well.

Physiology is a difficult class and is really challenging, but Dr.Clark is extremely kind and always wanting to help. She's easy to reach and is normally in her office with the door open willing to talk. I would take this again.

Professor Clark is clearly very smart however she goes over way too much in such little time. Her exams are nothing like practice, and there is genuinely so much homework and outside work it's insane to keep up with especially for someone with multiple classes.
I have no idea how I got the grade I got, but Pat Clark is easily one of the worst professors I've ever had.

STAY AWAY!! I don't care if it is the only time you can take it. Make room for the other professors class! Soooo many lecture slides for each exam. Grueling test questions which she does NOT prepare you for. Not really sure how I even ended up with an A as I failed multiple exams. Probably the huge exam curves she HAD to give. PLEASE STAY AWAY!!

This class sent me into a health crisis and nearly killed my passion for medicine. For your sanity, DO NOT take this class with this professor. She takes each chapter a step further than necessary and expects you to draw on higher knowledge from chemistry, biology, and anatomy. She is not approachable and doesn't care if her students succeed.

Dr. Clark is one of the best professors I have had the privilege to learn from. Her course is more than just memorizing. She teaches so you truly understand the material. Although the material taught may seem harder than other professors, it is all for the sole purpose of making sure her students are knowledgeable by the end of the semester.

STAY AWAY FROM PAT CLARK. This was my hardest class by a mile. My lowest grade received at IU was a 96, until I took this course. I would put hours upon hours in studying for exams EVERYONE failed. I ended up finishing with a 79 and will probably not get into the nursing school because of Pat Clark. Please fire this woman.

Do not take this class. the exams are nothing like the study guides she gives. there are questions that we went over once in class and never again, if even that. she expects you to know everything the day we learn the material. she gives a lot of extra credit/curves but it's only because everyone fails and she doesnt want to lose her job again.

I took this class and it was absolutely HORRIBLE. If you think studying for other classes is bad, be prepared for this one. The other classes had simple terms explained to them in condensed form, while Dr. Clark went so in depth that there was up to 300+ lecture slides per exam. Prepare for a decline in your mental health after taking this class.

A TA told me that with her a C is an A in the other professors class, because she goes out of her way to make it harder on us! She acts bothered if you don't know material on the first day it is taught to you. Not to mention everything is graded insanely. Can go word for word through rubrics on lab reports and never get an A. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS
Terrible professor!! Beware! She makes the course seem like it's at a graduate level. I have never had such a horrible professor at IU!!!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS otherwise good luck! She clearly is a smart women however is a horrible lecturer! Her tests are meant to trick you. She also had us learn way more information than the other class and blames us for not knowing stuff when she overloads us with information. Please take the other professor or take it through Ivy tech..

Without a doubt the worst professor I have ever had. Seemed knowledgeable on the subject but could NOT clearly teach or prepare exams. Exams were insanely hard. Lectures were confusing and 10x harder than needed to be.  RUDE professor who made it clear it was your fault and not hers when you were confused. 
DO NOT DO NOT take the class with her!!!!

DONT take this class; either take it with the other professor or go to Ivy Tech. literally the worst class I've ever taken and I am a premed student. She does not care about students at all, she is blatantly rude, has no intention of helping, and thinks everything is the student's fault. criteria too much and she expects you to memories everything

Pre-Nursing Students Beware!
Pat Clark is a wonderful person but a terrible professor. If you haven't taken anatomy before this class get ready to learn it in more detail than A225. The exams are extremely detail oriented and difficult. There's little guidance, no real support, and barely any extra credit.

One of the worst professors at the university. She just lectures about vague concepts for physiology but then creates the most difficult exams. She also just sucks at teaching in general, she doesn't explain concepts clearly. She curves all her exams by like 20% hoping she doesn't lose her job but hopefully she does. Take the course without her.

I wish I had the option to take this class with a different professor. SO TEDIOUS about the smallest/insignificant details, especially on tests. Everyone in our class did so badly (due to her instruction) that the exam had to be curved by *20 points*. Super blunt, does not tolerate "dumb questions". My advice: go with different proffessor.

He's a really great teacher. I did well un K201 which made K303 easier, but he always made sure to explain each new function or topic thoroughly to the class, went through examples, and did problems on the board after giving us a chance to try it ourselves. Final project was annoying, but not his fault and more time consuming than difficult.
Super nice guy, just gotta pay attention and you will do good.

This teacher made k303 so much more bearable and made me actually enjoy the subject. he is so caring, as well as a very thoughtful teacher. his lectures are super clear and he is always willing to help his students succeed. I would 100% recommend prof. Collins.

One of the best instructors at IU. Has real-world experience and makes K303 way easier to understand. Enthusiastic and extremely knowledgeable. He's strict with grading but he will definitely make you better at Excel. Super nice and professional. Take K303 with Professor Mike!
One of the best teachers at IU.
Interesting class: He made lectures engaging through real-world applications and videos, and he graded projects fairly. A lot of the semester is working with your team in class.

Collins makes Excel very easy to understand and the class structure is set up so much better than K201. You absolutely have to go to class to understand the material and get points, but as long as you do, there is virtually no work outside of class. Collins is very helpful and always open to answering student questions.

Prof Collins is a really nice guy.  He's not the easiest grader of the S310 professors, but he teaches really well and is enthusiastic.  He assigns a lot of videos with quizzes though, and they can be kind of a pain.  Overall a good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Really funny guy and great professor. Also very accessible outside of class and super helpful at office hours. I would definitely recommend taking him if you can.
Mike's great, definitely one of my favorite professors at Kelley.

Mike made an 8am as enjoyable as it could be. He really cares about how his students do in his class and wants to ensure growth from the beginning to end of the semester. Read the book for the sake of tests, but it's only about 10% of the tests. But overall, for the sake of your well-being, take Michael Collins.

Mike's a super nice guy who provides good detail in his explanations. This class involves a lot of videos to watch outside of class, but overall isn't that bad. As long as you put in the work, you'll be fine.
He's a really great professor and the tests are easy as long as you understand the material. Projects are harder than tests and they take a very long time, but they're a good way of studying.

Prof. C is one of the best teachers I've ever had. I came into this class hating excel, but he changed that by the end of the semester. He explains things in a way that makes excel so intuitive. He answers question clearly and is extremely fair when dealing with students. Even if you have to take an 8am, make sure you sign up for his class.

If you got an A in K201K204, you will breeze through this class.  Mike is a cool guy who can be a little boring at times but answers all questions and has a ton of real world experience. If I would have no problem taking a class of his again. Clear, understanding and communicates effectively.

Mike Collins is an amazing professor. He's extremely helpful, impartial and is always willing to help students. He makes the course even easier and more enjoyable than it already is! Head over to HH 431 for all projects and you'll breeze through the course.

Constance Cook is a pretty good professor. The class is insanely boring and lectures are painful. But the class is also insanely easy with just busy work. The attendance policy is aids. Stance is very caring and she is always happy to answer questions. Overall a very good gen ed to take, especially for those who love Leonard Berstein. Go STANCE

she is great taught us for the first few weeks then the prof changed to a boring instructor the class is an easy A and it shouldnt take much of your time it just has a lot of busy work the grading is super and it is easy to get a 100%
Extremely boring material and presentation. Strict professor who thinks everyone is just as invested in this stuff as she is, busy work on busy work, don't take this course- it's just not worth it

Super easy gen-ed. She clearly cares a lot about the content and likes what she does. The lectures are actually kinda interesting. There's no tests. There is one paper that you have to write that's pretty common in all of the music gen-eds and then a final presentation that's really easy. There's extra credit offered. Attendance has points.

You have so much busy work in this class, especially at the beginning. Lots of Norton homework that's really annoying to do and takes a while. There's also a bunch of weekly quizzes and discussions. In the online class you have to type things into the chat for attendance but lecture itself is not really important.

Boring Boring class, really easy but very mundane, and the attendance policy aids in that, only two classes are allowed to be missed. If I was IU and was looking to cut costs or make things more efficient, I would make this an online class, lecture basically teaches you nothing.

This was the most disappointing class I've taken at IU. While it was easy and I earned a good grade, the professor constantly started early, went over time, and rudely shut down student questions. She even rushed final presentations we'd worked on all semester. I dreaded attending, an overall horrible experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Professor Roosma, but I think the online version of the class is the same, no matter who your professor is. Such an easy way to complete your A&H credit without having to stress about your grade. Professors are very nice, and the class is very easy.

My online class had another teacher teach the class while Prof. Cook was in charge of grading the assignments. Honestly, this class was one of the easiest classes, but the thing is there's a lot of unnecessary busy work. If you know music prior to the class, you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I have so much respect for Professor Cook and her Music of War and Peace class. This class was very useful and I'm so grateful that teachers like Prof Cook still teach these classes, especially with the current state of the country and universities.
Literally the most boring class I've ever taken. Take the class if you want a free A though. Mind-numbing busy work and you can't be on your phone during class.

Constance Cook was a really caring, accommodating professor, who was happy to grant extensions when needed, and always answered emails quickly. this class was incredibly easy as long as you get the points for attendance.
Had the most boring lectures I've ever seen in my entire life. Never got back to emails and graded extremely slow.
Lectures were extremely boring, lots of busy work, but overall an easy A.

She is a super sweet, caring lady, and the class doesn't require a significant amount of effort. Cons: She is rather incompetent with technology. She does not allow phones or computers out during class, and will scold you if you do. Lectures can feel very repetitive in that she forgets and covers things multiple times, so things get boring.

She's definitely been one of my favorite professors by far. She is kind and understanding, & if you discuss anything grade-related with her, she listens & will help you out no matter what. I've never felt more comfortable talking to a professor before. She's so passionate about music, but please don't go on your phone in this class. She hates it!

Professor Cook is one of the most caring professors I have met. Come to class and engage, answer a weekly discussion post, and complete online listening quizzes and you're set! She wants to work with her students, and has repeatedly told us she offers extensions when needed.

Dr. Cooper is genuinely one of the most caring professors I have ever had. Not only is he very knowledgable in his specific field, but he also makes it apparent how much you as a student mean to him. None of the work he assigns is impossible, and most of it is fun or interesting. I couldn't recommend him enough, truly one of a kind.

Dr. Cooper was truly one of my favorite professors on campus. Incredibly knowledgeable in his field, and he clearly loves his students and wants the best for them. His expectations are very high, and he pushes you to meet them. This is not a slack-off easy A class, but you will come out with completely transformed views on music and culture.

Dr Cooper has been one of my favorite professors at IU, and for a gen ed class, outside of my major completely. Dr. Cooper is one of the kindest professors and you can tell that he is really passionate about black music education. He expects a lot from you and wants you to learn and do well, but in the end, it's totally worth it.
Great professor, extremely knowledgable about the topic. Made every class very interesting and engaging. Fair grader.

Kindest and most generous professor I've had. Dr. Cooper really cares about his students, their well-being, and their grades, and really wants them to be engaged during class. Definitely read and take notes before class because he expects participation. Other than that his class was mild. He is so awesome and super educated.

I would recommend Dr. Cooper to anyone. You can tell he cares about his students and wants them to do well. This class does require you to read a little bit, be prepared to read before every class so you can participate, but other than the reading this class was amazing. I will be taking another class with Dr. Cooper soon!

Dr. Cooper filled the class with meaningful content and discussion. The material is not too hard, though you have to read before every class in order to participate in class and he expects you to know the basic facts and content. Interesting class and an amazing teacher. Would recommend Dr. Cooper to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Tests? Not many--Would take again

reviews.comment: Very intelligent! You can tell he has a passion for what he teaches. I strongly recommend taking one of his classes. You will leave knowing so much more!

Dr. Tyron Cooper is one of the best professors on Indiana University! If you have the opportunity to visit him you should! You are willing to learn at least one thing when you talk to him. Overall great guy who is very inspirational and life changing. But he does expect you to get your work done and try your best! Do this and you are good to go!

TAKE HER!! Often she would grade hard, but once you understood what she was looking for, you will be fine. Make sure you put in the work and go to her office hours and you will get an A. Can grade based on favoritism I feel so go to those office hours even if its to ask a 2 minute question and a small conversation.
Professor Land was an amazing professor. Would highly recommend her for C104!

Professor Land is a good teacher but def grades hard. Her feedback can sometimes be vague. The most important thing is practicing for your presentations. This is a tough class but if you spend time and effort you will get an A

Professor Land cares a lot about her students and wants all of them to succeed. However, the honors rubric was quite challenging with tough grading on presentations. Make sure to be very well prepared for your presentations. This class will make sure you learn these presenting skills and you will learn them well.

She is super nice and approachable. Is super willing to work with students and gives clear feedback after every presentation so you know what you have to work on. Its not hard to do well in her class as long as you pay attention and practice your presentation. As long as you follow the rubric and practice youre bound to suceed.

This was my favorite class this semester! Professor Land gives detailed feedback and genuinely wants her students to succeed. As long as you put in the effort she is more than willing to help you and you will do well in the class. Would definitely recommend taking her for C106.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
Professor Land is an amazing person! She genuinely cares for her students, and it's clear she wants everyone to succeed. 

Her feedback/grading can be strange, and sometimes it does seem really specific. Overall, it's a laid-back class and chill. Just make sure your team is on the same page for group projects. 

Definitely recommend this class!
I loved Professor Land's class! She is the sweetest lady, and is always open to providing support and advice. As long as you are putting in your full effort, you will do just fine in her class.

I do not have enough space to express how much I adored having Professor Land. She is truly a one-of-a-kind teacher who cares for all of her students. Everything is laid out in the syllabus, and if you respect her, she will respect you. You have to put in the effort, but she has helped so many students come out of their shells. She's the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good teacher. Doesn't grade too hard. You will get an A if you do the work. Not much work except for presentations. I recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Land is pretty chill overall, sometimes her feedback is a little nitpicky but if you put in genuine effort you'll do well.
She was a chiller fr
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: C106 is a required freshman year course and I would recommend taking it with Land. She makes class fun and engaging. There's daily reading but it isn't that much, heavy on presentation and participation. Lots of group work but overall would recommend.

Professor Land is a good teacher and a good person who clearly wants to see everyone improve through the course. She does her best to create a low pressure environment for those who may be nervous about public speaking. Her grading style is sometimes a little nit-picky but her feedback is generally pretty good.

She's so nice! I struggled initially with the grades but if you really talk to her and meet during office hours, she'll help you out a lot and it definitely helped me get the grade I did. Also class was very fun I wasn't tempted at all to skip haha
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Strongly recommend taking any other honors teacher! Never got above an A- on presentations and she never gave good advice on how to improve. Very inconsistent grading. She took massive points off for very small factors, and was always looking for something to criticize just to take points off. AVOID. TAKE ANY OTHER HONORS TEACHER
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Land is one of my favorite teachers to date. I recommend integrating humor and trying not to be a robot to do well on her assignments. Your grade is heavily dependent on the skill of your group, but Land is a fair grader who will help you succeed if you show effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is utterly incompetent. Her grading is inconsistent and unfair. It's as if she doesn't even bother reading assignments, and takes points off for whatever she feels like without properly telling us the requirements for deliverables. She is not lenient with grading either. Her score on this website is very misleading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this professor's class. Her rate at my professor was so high, so I decided to take her class. However, she turned out to be one of the worst professors I've ever had. We are graded on the most ambiguous aspects of all deliverables, and she gets mad whenever we ask about our grades. Horrible professor and terrible grader.

Paige is actually one of the WORST C106 teachers. DO NOT TAKE HER IF YOU CAN HELP IT. I ended with an A- by less than .1 and she WILL NOT round up. She genuinely does not care about teaching her students how to present well and the class is incredibly hard to improve in. I received the highest grade out of my group and I genuinely hated her.

Land is overall NOT a good teacher. She is extremely unfair when grading and is unapproachable when you ask her to talk about the grade you received (gets mad and short). Also thinks discussing a grade on a presentation (not asking for a grade change) is unprofessional. She made me feel more uncomfortable giving a presentation than I felt before.
Paige is a fun and enjoyable teacher to be around. I thought she graded very fairly and made sure to help whenever I needed it. Just do the work, prepare for presentations, and show up.

She definitely cares a lot about her students but is a tough grader. Make sure you follow the rubric very closely or you will probably receive harsh feedback. In the first few presentations, you are allowed a notecard just in case.

Warm, friendly super approachable lady. Class size of 24 so it's not scary to present. Can grade a bit harshly so put in effort... most of the class makes it out with As so as long as you're working hard it will be fine. Grades very close to rubric.  Class is not much work besides the presentations.

She is a very smart teacher. She's great for feedback, and if you want to genuinely become a better speaker, she's a great teacher to help you with that; she's very experienced and honestly gives you great feedback. Just make sure you read the rubric many times over, individual and w/ group. She will round up close grades at the end. Very friendly.

I would rate Land higher if she didn't cancel class so often. We missed a lot of impromptu speeches, which made the midterm and final speeches worth more. However, Land did bump my grade to an A due to my peer evaluations. Overall, she is a very nice teacher. She can be a hard grader, but she gives good feedback and extra credit.

Paige Land was amazing. I had her for C106 and honestly she felt more like a friend than a teacher. She was very clear with what she wanted us to get out of with the class, and helped each of us improve and be our best we can be. I enjoyed going to class every day. If you can take honors do it, there's no difference besides an extra presentation.

The teacher is extremely kind/friendly and reassuring during your presentations so you feel much more comfortable. The class is mostly group presentations so make sure to set up a guaranteed weekly meeting time so people don't scramble to meet. The research portion isn't too tough and she grades pretty closely to the provided rubric.

Professor Land was so kind to me throughout the semester. I always had a fear of presentations, and she could definitely tell, but despite that she was always encouraging me and giving me great feedback and by the end of the semester I could actually be proud of what I presented and gained so much confidence. Paige is the best!!

Professor Land has been awesome. She gives you everything you need to know to succeed in the class. She gives feedback on presentations and then you can evaluate and make necessary changes to improve for future presentations. Class is team heavy and plan on meeting often with your team. 3 team presentations and 2 individual presentations
Paige is amazing. She is funny and extremely knowledgeable. Do not feed her B.S though because she can see right through it!

I was battling from a low grade from an early presentation and showed her that I cared and wanted an A. She helped guide me and appreciated my hard work and effort. I am forever thankful for her ability to communicate with me and would recommend her.

Professor Land gives great feedback on presentations, clearly outlining your strengths and weaknesses. Focusing on what she says to improve on will help your grade on future presentations. As long as she can see that you put effort and practiced your presentation, she will give you a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She clearly outlines everything you need to do to be successful in the course so make sure you read the rubric and stick to it. It is ESSENTIAL that you have a good group because group presentations is a big part of your grade. Overall Paige is very kind and easy to talk to.

TAKE PROF LAND! She really wants you to succeed. She outlines exactly what you need to do to get an A. If you do it, you will get an A. Easy as that. She's also just a really friendly face. If you hate public speaking like I do, she makes it feel bearable.
I would recommend her if your taking business presentations. Make sure to go to class and follow the rubric and you should do just fine.

Prof Land is super nice! make sure to go to optional classes, it helps with the professionalism portion of your grade. Choose your group carefully, you'll be spending a lot of time with them. Super clear feedback and what is expected, just check the rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Paige Land is a great professor for C106. She cares about her students, and if you chat with her before and after class, she's more than willing to help you get the grade you are looking for. All in all, great professor

Paige Land is a good professor but because this class is an honors class, there's a lot of presentations. She is an easy grader since no one in the class ever got below like an 82 on a presentation. The homework is annoying though because it does take some time. But she usually finishes class early
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's nice enough, but grades incredibly harshly even on assignments not worth tons of points. Even the top scores won't be perfect. Extremely nitpicky and towards the end of the semester she gives you no room to breathe. Personally I'd go find someone else to take this class.

Paige is a great professor for C104. The textbook is online and attendance is mandatory but I really don't like public speaking and I got an A- in her class. She's very caring and is very clear on what she's looking for on the rubrics. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Land is the type of prof that you don't think you are learning much until you compare the opening speech to the final. She responds to emails very quickly (usually under an hour) and is always accommodating. I would gladly take a class with her again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Land was one of my favorite professors to date. She is outgoing and wants to see you succeed. She is easily accessible outside of class and can easily meet with you. If you have the chance, take this class with her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Land is a fun person to talk with. Her class makes you feel relaxed. But don't let that fool you, she's actually on the harder end of business presentation and will grade your presentation hard if you don't do the work.

Contrary to all the reviews, I had a negative experience. She is not an extraordinary professor. I really think she is unreasonable during grades and quite a few times even rude. She doesn't help a student if he/she is not doing well on their presentation. If you are bad at presentation, she's not gonna put efforts to improve your skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really dont understand Paiges high reviews. Her lectures are not helpful, she just sits in her chair and reads off the screen. The lectures she gives have little to no information I didnt know before C106. She is oftentimes unreasonable and doesnt tell you things you need for assingments, and then docks you points. Take it w/ a different prof

Paige is one of the sweetest, most caring teachers I know. She is super fun and wants only the best for her students. As long as you try to be a good group member, make nice visuals, and put in your best effort you'll really enjoy it with her!

Paige is a wonderful teacher. She gives wonderful feedback, and really wants to see her students succeed. This class isn't always easy, but you will learn so much and come out with wonderful professional skills.
Best professor for C106; Uncomplicated class structure

Paige's feedback is great on each presentation so you know what to work on for the next one. In the honors class the lowest grade was either a B or a B- but more than half of the class got A's or A-'s. The way to get an A in this class is by practicing your speech until you perfect it before the day of your presentation. No text on slide deck  A
I really enjoyed taking business presentations with Paige! She was one of my favorite professors as a freshman!
Great professor, really cares about he students. Definitely one of the easier C106 graders.
reviews.rating_tags: GROUP PROJECTS--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Land was an awesome professor!  By far one of the best courses that I've taken while at Kelley.  She is funny, down to earth, and will support and challenge you to step outside of your comfort zone in order to be a much better presenter.   Team presentations were really stressful and there are a lot of points riding on those speeches.

She is an irresponsible professor. She made several absents during the spring semester. Due to her absents, class schedules totally messed up. Also, directions of the assignments are not clear. She is also extremely biased.

Having Paige and my presentations instructor made the class much more enjoyable than the traditional public speaking class. She creates a fun and safe environment, and was always more than willing to help or even just to talk about life! Loved having her for class.

Paige is a nice lady but a very tough grader for an entry level class. She will mark you down tremendously for her "opinions" which isn't fair. For example, she grades all your powerpoints based on design, and expects you to come up with your own designs. I spent hours designing my slides and got marked down 25% because she thought it was a default

Everybody dreads speech class, but Paige makes you feel comfortable. There are two huge group presentations, which account for a lot of your grade. She picks the groups and tries to make them fair and on an even playing field. I would recommend Paige ten times over-- she's really enthusiastic and makes the class far less boring than it could be.

Pretty solid prof. Would probably take again.  If you get a good group, you are good to go. Only gripe is that she didn't round my 92.4 to an A. But whatever, not a huge deal, I was happy just getting an A-.

Paige is my favorite professor from my freshman year. She is young which makes her easily relatable to her students and really cares about her students. She wants you to do well and will help you whenever you need it. She is very fair when it comes to grading speeches and realizes you won't be a perfect speaker so she doesn't grade super hard.

I dreaded giving speeches before Professor Clark's class, but she helped my overcome my fear. Grading is clear, gives great feedback on speeches, and very clear on expectations.
