Ok this teacher is like chill if u take the emails in the beginning of the semester serious. they r worth liek 10% of ur grade. if u get As on the emails then ur good but just befriend her and go to office hours. office hours help a lot bc she will explain what u have wrong and how to fix it so it is chill. its an easy A if you do the assignments.

C204 isn't supposed to be a super hard or time consuming class. Professor Kelly makes it a lot harder than it needs to be. She grades based on whatever she feels like. She is such a hard grader for no reason. Do not take C204 with her if you want an easy A.

I had Dr. Kelly for C204. Overall, she's knowledgeable and she explains topics well, even when they're not super engaging. She grades according to the rubric for every assignment. No exceptions. She's very caring and easy to talk to. Overall, pretty good.

Very tough grader. No round ups granted. Lectures are lengthy and not engaging. Much of the in class lecture material is not useful to learn. Only 2 absences allowed, any additional and a 900 word essay with citations is required. Would not recommend.

Do not take this professor for business writing. This class will be a nightmare when she starts grading very harshly, and you have other things to focus on. The lectures are very boring, and the grading is unnecessarily hard. The good reviews are from the people in the teams she likes, who are nerds and over enthusiastic about this boring class.

Don't listen to people claiming she assigns a ton of homework. Homework is just smartbooks, short 100-word emails, and grammar practice, aside from the group project. Lectures are boring, but the class is easy. Deidre gives great feedback, and you will only struggle if you get a bad group, but that can happen in literally any other class.

Take another professor if possible. She gives out a ton of busy work and is a stickler when grading. Also when you have two days left until your final report is due and it says on the syllabus it is a work day, she will make you spend the time presenting your report to the class instead of working on it when it is worth a big chunk of your grade.
Considering this class was supposed to be an easy A, this is my far the most homework ive had in my 2 years here.

Pro: you don't really need to pay attention in class, grades pretty fairly based on the rubric, very helpful when seeking feedback
Con: lecture heavy, homework everyday, a lot of reading assignments, takes effort to do well in the class

Do. Not. Take. Her. She is harsh in grading. She acts nice in class, but very rude otherwise regarding assignments. She gives WAY too much homework, and takes everything too seriously. You have to follow her instructions so closely to receive an A. Please change her if you can, otherwise you will be struggling to even get an A-.

Genuinely terrible professor, probably one of the harshest graders I've ever seen. Her guidelines are always poorly outlined, and her opinions with what's been stated can clash and be completely different in person vs how she grades you. Would strongly recommend taking any other teacher as there's an unreal amount of busy work in the class

She is a good person but takes her class way too seriously and believes she is always right. I would avoid her for c204; she had horrendous averages on projects. Her smart books take forever as they are 40+ concepts, equating to a minimum of 80 questions.
Horrible job at explaining the guidelines for assignments. Very tough grader - she is very very strict at this. Every single assignment is due at 1pm instead of 11:59 - watch that on canvas calendar.

This is not a professor I would recommend at all. The material itself is not hard; however, it is extremely time confusing. She grades like this is a Harvard law class, but instead it is Business Writing - which is in most cases one of the easier classes before I-CORE. Her feedback is not helpful and will mark things wrong - when it's right.

Take another professor, don't make business writing hell. This class is supposed to be an easy A, and she makes it a difficult B. No reason to take this professor, not one good reason. Also offers no grade rounding and doesn't put in grades until the last second.

Seriously, find someone else. If you are reading this, you have already considered her for too long, plenty of other options. Way too strict and (in my opinion) sexist towards men. Way too many assignments and does not care about your success. Now, stop reading and change your schedule.
Grades everything way too hard. Talks for the entire 75 minute class period straight and it is extremely boring. Very hypocritical when it comes to feedback. Take any other C204 professor if you can

The most mid-class I have ever taken. He is clearly intelligent in the topics he teaches, however has little regard for student time. He provides 0 drops for attendance. He also claims that if you study the ANKI, you will do fine on the tests, which is untrue. He tests very random topics or things that are said 1 time in class or in a video.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Rowe-Magnus is very smart and seems to care about his students a lot, but the lecture was the most un-engaging class ever: all he does is read the slides and play a few videos. If you do the anki flash cards you'll more than likely do well on the tests. He drops your lowest grade from assignments, quizzes, and exams.

I was in the M200 course. The exams are lecture content only and pretty easy if you study the Anki cards that he provides. The exams are 95% anki cards and 5% video-based and or in-class-based information. The class can be as easy as you make it to be but do not wait until the day before the exam to study.
Makes it very clear what will be on exams. If you listen and study, you will do fine.

One of those professors that is sometimes too smart for his students own good and lectures very fast. Good thing he reposts all of his notes and lectures, so it is easy to go back and study for his tests. He seems very helpful when you have questions on homework or quizzes, and he is understanding when students struggle on tests.

Even though he claims that if you study the highlighted pink sections of the PowerPoint that you'll do good on the exam, it's partially true. There were some questions on the exam that had NOTHING to do with microorganisms and disease. Then he acts surprised that we all scored low. Thank the heavens that this class isn't that important for my major
Unorganized and without direction, I had no idea how I was doing in this class. Somehow pulled out an A.

Purposely tries to trick students on pop quizzestests - and then acts smug about it. Book wasn't really needed, ppt slides were right from book. Sometimes disorganized (arrived late to the final!). Tests are scantron. There was one big project which wasn't hard (Read a paper and present on it). Ask questions during presentations to earn points!

Lots of articles, and tests are a large portion on articles. He's a cool guy and a respected prof, but he will make you work for the grade. PARTICIPATE. He isn't a raw score grader and leaves room for his own subjectivity. He grades are more on attendance, participation, and high pop quiz scores than exams. Unofficial mandatory attendance.

Prof. Rowe-Magnus is a tough teacher, but participation and interest counts a lot. His exams are pretty tough, so studying is a must. Pop quizzes count a lot too. Make sure you keep up and you'll do okay - this isn't a class you can blow off. He is available for help if you need it but can be confusing, so the readings can help too.

The people that took his 211 class sound like a bunch of whiners.  Be grateful he doesn't give completely verbal notes.  In M480, there are group presentations worth 20% of your grade... very easy.  Exams (multiple choice) are really easy if you study... Especially because of the 100%-85% A grading scale!  Pop quizzes, assignments... the usual.

Whole class is him reading directly off the slides which makes for a very boring class. He says he wants you to learn the material, but the way he presents the information and how he tests you makes that impossible. You have to memorize everything and regurgitate for the exams.   If you want to learn, then take a different professor.

The textbook was useless in that his slides were often verbatim textbook text; however, he condensed the material and only cared about his slides. In the end I ended up with an A because he changed the syllabus and gave me over 100% on the final. He is condescending and doesn't engage students. He just stands behind his desk and mumbles his slides.

Not hard to get an A.He gives you 30% of ur grade.The quizes wernt graded just for practice and the rest of the class was based off the exams which were multiple choice.All you had to do was study the slides the test questions were directly from them.Yes his class needs some work its his first time teachig here he shanged the syllabus to it easier

I get why others don't like him. Honestly, he deserved some of the the criticism. I had absolutely no idea what my overall grade was till the day it came in. However, I did well by reading and understanding the slides and then practicing the concepts. You can succeed if you are a dedicated student. If not, the sciences may not be for you.

Those who are complaining are the people who didn't study or prepare well for the tests. He isn't disorganized, he takes the time to put together slides for the class from which the info on the test is directly from. He gives you 30% of the grade if youre in class. He's a fine professor but molecular is a hard course.

THIS CLASS IS HORRIBLE. we don't even know half of our grade because he refuses to put in the quiz grades. the exams are impossible and lectures are useless.  if you need to take this class, wait for a different professor. this class is just unnecessarily hard.

One of the worst teachers I've ever had. Might as well just read the textbook and learn it on your own because you'll probably learn better than listen to his lectures. He can be quite condescending at times.

I would not recommend this professor. His tests don't cover biological processes - they cover specific details of biological processes that might come from a single sentence of a long, dense powerpoint. If you want to truly learn the subject, do not take his class.

True, he does mumble and reads word for word the slides. However everyone who is doing so poorly shouldn't just blame him. I have an A in the course and that's from studying those slides with textbook to clarify the slides. He is though VERY disorganized. He changed the structure of the course constantly and has no definit method of grading yet.

HORRIBLE PROFESSOR. He doesn't teach the material and basically throws everything at you and expects you to know it all by the time an exam comes around without explaining it.  His tests are extremely specific, yet he goes into no detail during class.  The power points are extremely dense, but he reads them WORD FOR WORD. RIDICULOUS!!

THE WORST PROFESSOR EVER. Read word-for-freaking-word off of the slides. Believes that the students should just know everything and not be taught. Doesn't have office hours and says to NOT ask questions in class...NEVER EVER have this professor.

Honestly the worst professor I have ever had at IU.  I was well aware this class would be a challenging course, but he makes this nearly impossible.  He just reads the slides word for word.  He mumbles most of the time so you can't even hear him.  Avoid taking his class at all costs.

Worst teacher I have ever had at IU. He regurgitates exactly what is said in the book, and does not take time to explain the concepts. The power points he uses are provided by the publisher of the book. He assumes the reason his students aren't doing well in class is because they don't study, not because of his teaching style. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS

He didn't even have office hours until the very end of September. He doesn't have weekly study guides like his syllabus states, and also was very condescending when almost 70% of the class failed his first exam. The material he gives us is very basic, but the exams he writes are super specific. Avoid at all costs.

He is by far the worst teacher I have ever had at Indiana University. He uses slides that are given to him by the text book company and just reads word for word from the slide. His exams are poorly written. There's a difference between a hard exam and a bad exam, his are just pathetic. Avoid this class at all cost.

NEVER TAKE THIS PROFESSOR! She is super unorganized. She expects you to do the impossible, when she is clearly not ready to put any efforts into the class. Awful feedbacks that are meaningless, takes forever to grade, and requires you to have her 7 pages requirements into 600 words essays which is impossible. This woman should not be teaching.

Dheepa is a decent instructor. She is funny and chill. Her tests can be difficult, but she often curves and gives extra credit. Not my favorite class but you learn a lot. Dheepa is good at handling dialogue. You can get by in class without reading because she constantly reviews.

She is knowledgeable about course material. Class consists of lectures and discussions. She teaches through novels rather than history books. Gives a take-home midterm and blue book final. In addition, short papers are assigned and a larger research paper. Attendance is mandatory if you want to do well in the class.
She's so awesome and sweet. Really cares about the subject.

The way the class is set up is that she teaches the Medieval art for ARTH A101. Super interesting class, and her and the other prof were very good lecturers. Took some adjustment because they do it differently, but still good nonetheless. You have to study a lot for this class, though, a lot for a gen ed too. If you like art/history, take for sure!

She gives very good and helpful feedback and is incredibly knowledgable on what she teaches but I found the workload towards the end of the semester to be too much for a gen ed. I had to spend more time on this class's final project and exam than chemistry...
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: take an easier gen ed - nice teacher though

She was a very nice professor, but if you do not find the topic as interesting as she does, it will be hard to follow along. You have to take good notes and show up to every class otherwise you will not have the information you need for the exams. The final project and 3rd exam were not placed well next to each other as they are within a week.

Diane Reilly is truly exemplary at teaching. She takes subjects, that may not be of much interest to her students, and masterfully structures her classes to make learning motivating, engaging and easy. Additionally, she genuinely cares for her students and is very reachable outside of class. Very few teach as well as Diane Reilly.

This class is definitely lecture heavy. If you're into this stuff, you'll love the class. You definitely need to show up or you will struggle. Professor Reilly is very knowledgeable and accommodating. I really enjoyed this class, but make sure you're willing to go to class.

Professor Reilly was one of my favorite professors so far at IU! I am not an art history major by any means but her class was interesting and I was always excited to go every time. She explains things clearly and makes her expectations known. She was absolutely slay.

She is a very nice lady but is also a pretty fair grader. The content is a bit difficult in this class but it seems as long as you show you have an understanding on the test or presentations then you won't do too bad. I was really worried at first but as long as you show up to class and write everything down then its fine.
Lectures were rather lengthy and dry, but we were expected to memorize many small details. She is a nice woman, but can come across condescending. Overall not too bad but nothing special either.

I honestly really enjoyed Art History and didn't find it that difficult. She lets you bring in a 4x6 notecard for every test so you don't even have to memorize the names or dates of the items. She's very knowledgable on the subject and I enjoyed learning from her.

This class is HARD. You have to take really good notes and pay attention or else you will not know what is going on. The lectures are dry and long and there's a lot of assigned reading (which I'd recommend doing to understand better). You get a note card for tests which SAVED my life. But, lots of quizzes, papers and homework. Nice lady though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was extremely clear cut and the easiest I have taken. I really enjoyed Professor Reilly's lectures,  and despite her being a bit condescending at times, she was a great professor and I would definitely recommend this class. Great way to fulfill A&H requirements.

I took this class thinking it would be a breeze after reading the other reviews. Let me put it simply, its not. you have to do your work if you want a good grade, and attend every class and unless you thrive on art, you'll have to work hard.

A lovely professor in almost every facet. Great legs, great stories, and great ideas on everything she teaches. Easy paper grader and really, REALLY nice in person. She's also a very good lecturer and powerpoint maker. Take a class with her if you get the chance.

Prof. Reilly is fantastic! She's SO easy to understand and really gets that HER class is not the ONLY one we're taking! She's extremely knowledgeable and informs you on what you're going to be tested. She's very enthusiastic and has a fun and intelligent sense of humor. Recommended!
Very sweet woman. Knew her stuff and was definitely better at teaching her half of the course than Van Voorhis. Would take her again if I could.
Wonderful teacher. Would take every class with her if I could.

She is very interested in her subject, clear on what she is teaching and what she expects from her students and she has a great sense of humor. I stopped reading any of the handouts or textbooks she gave out about a week into the class and found that just going to class was good enough. And she's cute too, what more would you want in a professor?

Maybe I just had her for the wrong class, but she seems like she should be teaching kindergarden! I wish she would teach at a level more appropriate for college students, and stop treating us like imbeciles. She is very sweet though, and I know that she means well.

Maybe I just had her for the wrong class, but she seems like she should be teaching kindergarden! I wish she would teach at a level more appropriate for college students, and stop treating us like imbeciles. She is very sweet though, and I know that she means well.

Diane is awesome. She is a brilliant woman who wants nothing less than perfection from her students. If you like to skip, don't even consider her class. She is strict on attendance. She conveys info very clearly and you're aware of what is expected of you from day 1.
holds excellence as her standard. expects it from her students! funny and bright in class. wish she would get a new wardrobe though.
Excellent professor! Very clear and helpful

Would not recommed, there were pretty lofty expectations that were also slightly vague. Lots of reading, lots of classwork, lots of essays that would have to be professor-approved theses. Tough class, nice professor, difficult grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dinverno is a great professor. She is really open to answering questions and responds to emails very quickly. Make sure that you participate in this course and come to class because it will help you when it comes to writing the informes and the midterm/final essays. Be prepared to read A LOT in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: While she's a kind and invested professor, be prepared for very hard grading. I got the same grade on all 11 of our homework assignments, which was roughly same grade I got in the class. While she's fair, be prepared to never get over a 95% on any assignment ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Melissa is kind, knowledgeable, and easy to talk to. Participation matters a lot in her class, so she'll call on you even if your hand isn't up. Doesn't upload anything related to participation until the very end of the semester and takes a long time to grade most things, so just talk w her if you don't know where you stand. Great prof and person!!

Melissa is a sweetheart and I love her as a professor, but she is a harsh grader. Participation means talk a lot every day. Essays need to focus on analyzing certain passages word by word (not just general themes). She grades really slowly. There are very few grades in the course - oral presentation, midterm essay, participation, and final essay.

She is awesome, but you have to really work for your grade. Participation means speak up several times per day, never pause. Can get by without the readings but I wouldn't advise it. Will give you all positive feedback and still give you a B in the class. Requires literary analysis skills that are not easy to produce for non-lit majors.

Prof. Dinverno is such an awesome literature professor. H328 not only improved my Spanish skills but also my lit analysis skills, which is why I really valued it as a course. Furthermore she is a super sweet and understanding person who cares about her students, but who still takes class and assignments very seriously. Loved the class and her.

She's a good teacher but challenging.  Class is completely in Spanish, so be prepared for that.  Also you get a decent amount of reading and homework for every class.  The plus side is she doesn't give tests, instead she gives projects.  I would recommend this class if you are ready to work and wanting to develop reading and speaking skills
Good class, but lots of material to cover. She uses movies on occasion. Sometimes we didn't even talk directly about the reading, other times it was critical to in class discussion.

S328 with Dinverno is great if you speak poor Spanish and are fine with a B in the class; however, if you actually enjoy Spanish class and have some talent, be warned. She gives inane homework assignments, forces classroom discussion in her own predetermined direction, and gives everyone the same grade (B). I was highly disappointed in this class.
chooses interesting topics, if you ask for something she's VERY helpful, friendly classroom environment
Best professor in the Spanish Department.
Best professor I've ever had.  Makes me want to go back to school just to take her classes.  I lived in Spain and her class helped more than I ever could imagine to prepare me.
best teacher in the spanish department. highly recommended.

Teaching-wise, he's good. He uploads the notes and exam questions come straight from the study guides. Easy A. HOWEVER, he is HORRENDOUS at responding to emails. He mistakenly graded me absent, and when I emailed him multiple times about it, he never responded nor changed the grade.
He is so sweet also took for methods of experimental psych and exams are not weighted heavily and study guides are straight forward

Professor Hu was pretty chill. His lectures could be stale sometimes, but the concepts weren't very difficult. Only gripe I had was that I tried contacting him about a grade I got, but he straight up didn't email me back lol, so that was kind of frustrating. Just pay attention, don't miss any assignments, do the study guide, and you'll be fine.

I honestly don't understand the negative comments. Dr Hu has been a great Prof. He canceled class a lot but he posts all the lectures so you don't fall behind. He is very kind and sweet and likes art and shares it. He adds personal stories into lectures that helped in exams. As long as you study and use his study guides you will be perfectly fine.

Prof. Hu is extremely chill. He is very easy-going and understanding. Lectures were unfortunately very boring, they are basically just him reading off the slides. Always felt like we were behind schedule in class and he is god awful at responding to emails. But the class is straightforward. Your grade is representative of your effort/attendence

His presenting was not great. He is pretty monotone and there's a lot of material, but he doesn't explain it the best. I usually was able to learn the material for the exams through his study guides, but I feel like I didn't actually have in depth knowledge of the material. He cancels class A LOT, which was frustrating.

He just reads off of the slides (extremely quickly), but assumes you already know what he is talking about. He uses TopHat to make exams based off of arbitrary homework from a textbook we don't even use in class, so when you take the exam you fail (even if you've been to every lecture and paid attention). He's a nice enough guy but a bad professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: When it came to assignments, this professor seemed to always devalue our work. We were instructed to write a 3-5 page introduction paper over Thanksgiving break that amounted to 5 points. Another example that felt incredibly dismissive of my work was when I spent 6 hours on a 5-point assignment. My email from 3 weeks prior was never answered.

He's a really nice guy, but he cancels class all the time unexpectedly and he's horrible at responding to emails. I emailed him twice a week in between and no response and its been 2 weeks since I've emailed him. His lectures are just read off the slides, he doesn't know how to explain most things in depth. He's a cool guy but not professor.

He was a great professor, didn't go too fast and always did Tophats for attendance. At the end of class he would ask the most blurry/ unclear topic so that he could revisit it and explain it in another way for the next class. While he didn't grade himself, his TA could be a bit of a stickler. Easy A if you attend class. No homework.
All test and quizzes are online. You can take the quiz unlimited times until you get all the questions right. Participation is on top hat. Easy class although there is a lot of material.

The class itself moves really fast, so you won't do well if you aren't reading and keeping up with lectures. There are a couple of extra credit opportunities but he isn't super good at answering emails or questions. Okay prof, hard class. Good luck

class is so chill. All the tests and quizzes are online and he often gets sick so class turns into an online lecture. need to answer top hat questions for participation. He is very nice and gives you the opportunity to make up assignments if you forget.

This class was super easy. Only 3 exams and they're all online. Weekly quizzes which aren't hard either. He assigns a textbook but you don't really need to read it. He's super caring and loves what he teaches. He was sick for like 3 weeks out of the semester so we had online lectures a couple times too. Definitely recommend this class with him!

Professor Diaz-Campos was awesome in HISP-S 326. He's easy to reach out to and always makes sure everyone understands everything. There's homework to do before class every day but it's not very heavy. The tests are kind of long and weigh a lot on the grade, but he provides a lot of study material and if you just study for the test you'll be fine.

He tries to teach too much in one single semester, and we have to figure out the many contradictions of his own so called research, which he believes it is engraved in stone.  He is dogmatic and always anxious when students raise intelligent questions.

Good lecturer, though you can see the contradictions of his materials. Pushes the envelope and does not remember where he started. Take a class with prof. Felix-Brasdefer, bc' he is more relaxed and U  learn about pop culture if U keep the eye on the news and spectacles. Don't recommend Diaz Campos, bc you may not want to keep studying linguistics.

This was an interesting class and Prof Diaz-Campos was helpful and kind. He makes sure to call on people to record participation grades so be prepared for that. He was very available outside of class and replied to emails quickly. Overall solid class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed his linguistics class, and despite his extensive knowledge of the material I felt that he did a good job breaking it down and making it understandable for us. At times the weekly reading assignments were a little heavy, but I never felt that it was too much to be tested on, even in the honors section. Very enjoyable experience!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He is not a bad prof. or person but he presents an excessive amount of material that may be unnecessary. When he wants to prove the point, he overloads the students with info. that in the end was irrelevant, or worse, he returns to the original point ; then we know that there was no need to throw all that info. at us just because he was anxious.

He definitely knows the material and expects you to as well, but he was always willing to answer questions and the criteria for tests and projects was clear. He will just randomly call on people all the time (after letting you review assignments with your table) which helps make sure everyone is engaged without stressing you out! Would recommend

Professor Diaz-Campos is a really intelligent guy, but sometimes he goes into too much detail over things that are not on the exam. Make sure you read and do the assignments. If you need help, go to office hours. He will help you.

Campos is an expert in his field and it shows in class. I took the honors version, so it may have been more difficult than some, but he moved too quickly with material and did not know how to communicate concepts well for students.  There was a constant vibe of panic among my classmates as none of us felt prepared for anything.

Manuel is one of the best Spanish professors I have ever had.  Not only is he sweet and hilarious, he is also super smart, organized, interesting, and fair.  The textbook, which he wrote, is full of wonderful information for Spanish students.  His exams are really easy, but the group projects can be tedious.

Great professor - knows his material very well and enjoys teaching it. As a person, very funny and likable. At times, the quizzes could be a little tough but nothing too crazy. The group projects were time intensive. The most interesting material comes in the last few weeks.

Manuel is a spectacular professor. He uses a variety of resources (textbook, empirical studies, YouTube videos) to demonstrate linguistic concepts. The group project was challenging, but Manuel provides good feedback for improvement. Sign up for Manuel's classes if you are interested in Hispanic linguistics!

He often talked about how he didn't believe questions had right or wrong answers they took points away for not answering correctly. The questions he asked were very confusing making it hard to give the answer he was looking for

Although I still have a few weeks left until I complete H105, I believe that Professor Dierks is one of those professors who's lessons will stick with you after the course ends. You do write A LOT, BUT he's not at all looking for a "right answer." Dierks truly just wants you to be able to form/support your own thoughts based on various sources.

Very unique class and takes a while to get used to. He uses his own website which is annoying and you have to calculate your grade manually because he grades with letters. Class is a lot of discussing and answering questions. After a few weeks you get used to it, and he's actually pretty funny and caring. He also hates AI with a passion.

Professor Dierks was amazing. He might not be everyone's cup of tea, he had a lot of specific humor. My classmates didn't like him, but I thought he was so funny. He taught history in a way I had never been taught before, which changed my worldview. When I was going through hard times, he was super understanding and offered me a lot of support.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you dont like history this class will most likely be a struggle. However, if you give the benefit of the doubt to the professor, this class will take you on a ride which challenges how you perceive history.

He has a very fun personality and tells a lot of jokes. His lectures, however, are not very interesting. It feels like he cares more about writing than history. He asks extremely vague questions on his essays that are very difficult to answer. He doesn't post grades on Canvas, which is extremely frustrating.

As others have previously stated, your grade in the class is dependent on how well you perform on the four analytical essays. On paper, it sounds nice, but the essay prompts are too broad and make it difficult for one to answer. Overall, the class wasn't as fun as I had expected, coming from a history fan. Very nice guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Thinks just because he cares so much about the topic that everyone else would too. Asked for help through email and was completely ignored and instead complained how my work was below other students

I had to take this class for my major, but if you aren't required too and aren't super into hearing someone lecture from a PowerPoint and not go into further detail then this class isn't for you. He seems like a great guy but I'm just not a fan of his teaching or grading style. Grades take FOREVER to show, and still isn't your typical grading style
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I love this professor, he is a great guy and really cares about the subject, but his essay assignments were always a bit unclear. Very broad, vague questions that needed long, specific theses. I think there was a lot of unnecessary confusion over the writing assignments. That being said, its an easy A with standard effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Dierks really cares about his students and about the content he teaches. He is also constantly relating topics back to real world day. Although if you don't have interest in American History, you probably wouldn't find the class enjoyable. I would take him again, he's a super cool dude.

I don't like his style of teaching, he gives little context to what we are talking about, he poses questions in a very difficult way, and he's a harsh grader for only giving us vague prompts. Also I feel like I haven't learned much about American history besides race theory.

I can see how some students like this Professor and his teaching style; however, it was not for me. His lectures were somewhat dull, with a couple of mandatory questions each day, and their contents were boring. The 4 written responses are very niche topics, none of which I found remotely interesting. Only take this class if you like US History.

Prof. Dierks seems like a nice guy. However he is a terrible teacher. He gets up in front of the class, lectures for an hour, then proceeds to not explain anything. Your entire grade is pretty much just 4 papers. The class was called American Empire and we did not talk about empire at all until week 5. He then presents an incredibly biased view.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was awesome totally recommend, just a nice guy to even talk to.
Really caring and nice dude. His discussion were enjoyable.

Lectures are participation based and prof always asks thought provoking questions. This class is very engaging. He even had me get up in front of the class and recite the Gettysburg address. Loved this prof, highly recommend.

He's a great professor and one of the most understanding people that I know. I only took H101 so his grading may increase in difficulty with other classes but it was not very hard. The lectures and the homework were thought-provoking and I ended up really looking forward to his lectures. If you have the chance to take him, do it, he's a real gem.

Prof. Dierks is the genuine and kind professor I've ever encountered. After missing class due to unforeseen circumstances, I emailed him apologizing for missing his lectures and he was so understanding. If you love history, you'll love his lectures but they aren't for everyone. There are papers rather than tests, which make you think and reflect!

The only class I ever looked forward to attending. Specifically says he's not interested in testing anyone's memory abilities ("You're all college students, you've proven a million times how good of memorizers you are"). Encourages students to think for themselves, rather than aggresively type notes down and not listen to the lecture. 10/10.

He doesn't teach; class time is mostly spent in breakout rooms where we essentially have to teach ourselves by answering questions he assigns. He expresses his left leaning opinions over things that don't pertain to the subject. I think I learned more about the American Revolution in high school for 2 weeks than I did all semester in this class.

Easily the worst professor I have ever had at IU. Uses both Canvas and his own personal website that is incredibly inefficient and difficult to navigate. Posts readings 2 or 3 days before they are due. Makes you stay in a breakout room for 20 minutes to answer 2 questions. Syllabus is incomplete/often inaccurate. TA does most of the work. Avoid.

Although I am just a freshmen I already know this will forever be one of my favorite professors. He is funny, engaging, but most importantly, he genuinely cares about his students. Will recommend to everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dierks is extremely good at giving you assignments which allow you to advance yourself as a writer. The source documents also give you a view into what history was really like. The class is unusually structured, yes. However, he is full of passion and makes class interesting. His grading is also incredibly lenient. If you fail, it's on you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love Dierks. He may not be a great lecturer for big class, but he is a very knowledge and thoughtful historian, who leads me think more beyond the class and our age. His class makes more senses to history majors. He does not just teach us history, but also share an approach with you to explore history. Highly recommended. Very easy grader

Difficult to judge. He's enthusiastic and the lectures are more like large discussions which makes for a good class. Readings are relevant selected weekly by the instructor. There are not tests just papers. The main issues is his view on the subjects are often so narrow that so much is left out that only his view is allowed. Very skewed version.

Knows his subject extremely well.  I had a difficult time in the class, but it was mostly meant for Ph.D. candidates preparing for quals, not M.A. people who weren't going farther; I didn't have as much theoretical experience as most students, or I would have gained more from it.  Highly accessible, routinely replying to emails within hours.

At first, I disliked him because he rambled a lot. But I ended up loving this class. There were no tests, just papers, which was awesome! He is extremely knowledgable. This professor gave me a whole new outlook on history. Would definitely recommend!

He has disorganized lectures in which he seems to think out loud to himself with no apparent direction. If you want to learn about History, don't take this class. He informed us that the only thing he wanted to teach in this class was better writing skills. The 4 essay topics he assigns are vague and difficult to write about.

Dierks is the absolute worst professor I have ever had. No feedback on anything we turn in, and he posted the course policies (grades, attendance) in Week 13 of the semester. He is the most useless person I have ever come across, and everything is confusing and unclear. I would rather sell my first born child than EVER take a class with him again.
At first I hated the class but then I ended up loving it, he really wants to help students get the best grades possible but his lectures can be confusing
I'm not really a history guy but he was extremely interesting and the lectures were the high light of my classes for the week

Terrible class and professor. He rambles about nothing the whole class everyday. I learned nothing about history at all. There are no tests, just papers about very broad topics that make they incredibly difficult to write. Don't take this class. It's horrible.

Do not take this class unless you are a history major. You will not learn facts about American history. You will only write papers on bizarre topics. If you do not enjoy writing, this class is a big mistake!

Do not take this class if you are not a history major! You will not learn facts about American history. You will only write papers on unrelated topics. I struggle with writing so i struggled with this class.

Not sure what the rater from 3/9/11 is talking about..his essay topics are EXTREMELY broad as others here have noted (e.g. "discuss the way Americans' social status changed over the course of the 19th century") & he gives you more than enough material in class to be able to write an A+ essay. Go to class, take notes, talk to him. He's a great guy.

This course is not about history, it is about Professor Dierks forcing his beliefs upon his students, usually condescendingly. Homework and essay questions are unclear and always have a heavy slant toward his own beliefs. He seems incapable of discussing anything, from historical writers to works of art, without criticizing its quality.

Professor Dierks probably knows his stuff, but that is overshadowed by the fact that he asks vague and irrelevant questions for homework due every lecture. There are no tests, but four papers which are also broad, vague topics which I found difficult to write for that reason. Avoid him, if possible.

Dierks is a brilliant man who really cares about his students.  The papers make you think but they are only 4 pages long- I did each one the night before and got an A in the class. If you are good at writing you should have no problem getting a good grade in this class.
He's a nice guy who cares about getting his students involved in the class.  His lectures are hard to pay attention to and the only grades are four papers and participation (each category being 20%).

his only grades come from papers which depending on you AI and your writing skills can be good or bad.... He's pretty criptic and always asking abstract hypothetical questions for no apparent reason.. Oh and he requires you to prink out about 30 pages of readings for each discussion that I couldn't fit in any normal sized folder by the end.
If you want a history class this isn't for you.  If you don't like having someone push their political beliefs on you, don't take this class.  He has made me hate history.
Dierks is a genius but for some reason cannot ask coherent questions. For example one of his questions was "so do you think you exist or don't you?" Very smart man with a wonderful grey vest

Wonderful professor.  The class is by no means easy, in fact it was probably my hardest history class. But he is always willing to meet with you outside of class and is interested in how you do in the class and how you are outside of it.   He really challenges but if you struggle he is always there to help out. Remembers you after the class ends.
I HATE DIERKS!!!!

1. Interesting Lectures 2. Left-Leaning Bias 3. If  you want to know a lot about history, don't take this class; it is mostly to reinforce writing skills (no tests, just papers).4. Very interested in the well-being of his students and is always willing to help.
He's a really nice guy and is caring of his students although he has 225 of them. He's real helpful if you email him... class isn't too boring either.
Horrible, made me hate class
Very insightful, cool teacher who really cared about his students.  A little fruity at times, but not bad.  Class involved a lot of essays but no tests.

Rudest professor I have ever had. Should take a class on how to talk to people and how to write an email that has a greeting, a body, and a polite ending. I am shocked she has made it so many years in academia without anybody checking her tone and way of talking to people.

One of the most disorganized classes I've taken. Tests were stressful and based on group discussions, with no rubrics. She usually came off as condescending and set unrealistic expectations. The whole class was just group presentations, which she constantly interrupted. There's rarely any homework, but honestly, it's not worth the credits.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had her for intro to environmental toxicology, and it was rough. Lectures were scattered, we rarely finished the material, and grading took MONTHS. Tests were unrealistic and rubrics are nonexistent. She was defensive and condescending to all. Don't subject yourself to this torture. However, you can tell she loves the content.

Most unorganized class ever. Class itself was easy, but little to no lectures. Most of class time spent on presentations by students. When asking her a question, she comes off very condescending and rude.

Dr. Henshel is a terrible communicator and difficult person to work with. She does not explain assignments or expectations clearly at all, is defensive, and generally unhelpful to students. Students are mostly left to navigate the difficult assignments on their own, while she gives unhelpful lectures during class. I wish I was exaggerating.

As a professor teaching a communication course, she is ironically an extremely poor communicator. There is regularly confusion on what we are supposed to be doing, and for the group projects if you run into issues, it may go unsolved unless the TA can help. She is not necessarily mean, but certainly doesn't seem to be accommodating or invested.

Diane may have talents, but they do not include graduate level education. One of the most un-organized, condescending, and manipulative people I have met. If she is teaching a CAPSTONE you should avoid at all cost. Her CV is full of several CAPSTONE's work that she later publishes to self promote her myopic point of view.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Dlamini's courses enlighten us about the world as a whole and the fact that behind every cultural practice there is meaning. she helps students shed away the stereotypes they had about Africa, and brings more light and understanding into this continent. I would take her courses over and over again, because I gain more than just subject matter.

Dr. Dlamini is the NICEST human being! She is always there for her students and is willing to do anything to make them pass. She is a fun professor and is well respected. I would take more classes taught by her if I could!

Mama Dlamini is so much fun! I was planning on taking a foreign language just for my major but now it has become a passion. She is attentive and energetic, which allow classes to fly by without the drag. I have learned so much-- I can write full sentences in isiZulu and feel confident. Mama welcomes questions and is always available for extra help.

Mama is a wonderful, hardworking professor who her keeps students engaged and feeling like part of a family. She always has energy and is more than just a professor-- she is truly a mama! If you're interested in learning an African language in a way that is musical, interactive, and feeling like you're part of a family, take this course!
Dr. Dlamini is a great professor. Taking her lass has helped me even in my personal development. I highly recommend her courses to anyone who want to learn more about personal development too!

I enjoyed being in Dr. Dlamini's class. She has a way of making you love her class and when she teaches us dance, I am always amazed at the way she is always full of energy. I came to her class very shy, but now I can perform in front of an audience! Whoa!

Professor Dlamini is an amazing woman. In the intermediate Zulu class she made us write papers in Zulu and I never thought I could do that, but after her strategic planning I did it and amazed myself. I just love Mama's energy and interesting approach! Ngiyabonga Thank you)Mama!

I have always thought that learning an African language is difficult, but that's nor so if you have a professor like Professor Dlamini (Mama). Her teaching style is fun and we end up getting good grades! I enjoy learning Zulu!

I really liked Professor Dlamini and enjoyed her class because it enlightened us about other cultures. She explains in a way that makes you realize that the USA is not the whole world, there are many good cultures in Africa!
Professor Dlamini is teaches more than the academic subject matter. She helps and encourages her students to make an effort and be focused in their work resulting in their excellent performance.

Teacher is very easily distracted and doesn't have much material for the class. Most material is reviewed before each class and becomes excessively repetitive. The teacher is from Africa and doesn't have a strong grasp of the English language.

Dima is really good overall! The work is a lot, and he expects a lot from you, but if you do the work and participate as much as you can in class, you should be okay. Class moves very quickly so prepare for that.

Friendly professor with an emphasis on participation. His Hebrew classes require speaking 1 on 1, in groups, and in front of the class. The only issue is lots of homework between each class, but it's great to meet a Jewish community.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Good teacher, but if you skip class, FOR ANY REASON your grade will suffer, bad.

Dima is an amazing professor who cares about you and wants you to learn! He is definitely a tough teacher, but if you put in the effort you will be successful and he will honor you in that hard work. Would definitely take again.

Enrolled in the IU Summer Language Workshop for Russian 2 with Dima as one of my professors, and he is just amazing. He has a degree in pedagogy, so he knows how to teach. I wont lie  he isnt an easy professor. You have to try to do well in his class, and he will push you. If youre not used to working for it, you wont have a good time.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had. Rude & completely inflexible. Taught Russian by never explaining anything in English, like he spent TEN minutes explaining the word "something" in Russian when he could have said it in English in 1 second. Didn't teach grammar or vocabulary. Tests were horrible. People cried daily in this class. Worst class ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He seems to not care too much into your skill level, instead jumps right in day one with Hebrew. I had no background before the class, and began well enough, but as the class wore on, he became much tougher and seemed to shove those who couldn't keep up under the bus and leave you on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at IU. Lectures are engaging.

If you like dry humor and care to learn about the subject, I would recommend taking it with him. If you would rather not have to study a lot, I would not recommend it, but in my experience, I walked away learning a lot and found the topic to be interesting.

What can I say about Dmitry man. He comes off as this nice guy, right? Just a little bit of a nerdy dude that's into finance but mostly has academic experience. Never really set foot out of a classroom, bros just been studying. That's nice and all. However, what's NOT nice is when he absolutely destroys us with exams and ruins our GPA.

The class is going to be hard no matter who is teaching it but he makes it super easy to follow. You should go to class because he explains things in detail but if you have to miss you can email and not lose points. the exams are tough but not impossible and don't kill your grade either. Best professor i've had so far easily.

Professor Cheborarev is one of the most intellectually demanding and rewarding professors I've had at Kelley. His class was incredibly challenging but also the most impactful. He doesn't just teach you the material; he makes you earn your understanding of it. You'll be pushed, but come out sharper and more confident.

The class is hard no matter who you take, but I recommend Professor Chebotarev. There's no excel in exams, but he truly prioritizes the students' learning and is happy to help outside class to explain further. You need to go to class though since a lot is covered in lectures. He's also unexpectedly funny at times which helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is challenging, but he's an excellent teacher. I'd recommend him if you want to understand the material truly and are willing to take time to understand concepts conceptually.

Dmitry is one of the nicest professors I've had at IU. He does a great job of breaking down complicated topics and making them easier to understand. Although the exams are hard, they are curved heavily so a bad score doesn't kill your grade.

Dmitry is one of the best professors you can take for F-303. Even though his tests are a little hard, he would not ask questions outside of the lecture. The material is generally tricky; however, he does his best to explain concepts and genuinely cares for his students. Other reviews about him being rude are absolutely NOT true.

Dmitry is by far my favorite professor at IU. It's clear he's very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject and goes above and beyond to help his students. Other reviews aren't wrong in saying that the class is difficult, and other professors have easier exams. However, if you want to learn from a professor who cares, take Dmitry.

Take any other professor! Does not allow excel on exams, participation is graded by cold calling and the accuracy of your answer, and your final grade is determined comparatively to other students in the class. The hardest class I've ever taken and the professor is incredibly demeaning and blunt, calling half of the students failures during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All questions are unnecessarily hard. Tries to trip you up on problems for no reason, and you can not use excel for anything. An answer will be right and he will say "choose closest answer" and it could be completely different from what you found. Other teachers allow excel and have way easier questions for tests. Great guy but avoid at all costs.

Dmitry is simply an amazing professor. His class is naturally challenging, but he does everything possible to assist students in any way possible. He is extremely caring about his students, and is also extremely knowledgable on what he teaches. Overall my favorite finance professor at Kelley. Class is challenging though so expect to work hard.

Dmitry is an awesome guy. He teaches the class well but explains things a bit more complicated than it has to be. He also throws calculus around in a way that makes it hard if you are not good at calculus. Take the time to review lectures after class and attend office hours. This is a class you will struggle in.

Dmitry is a fantastic professor. His lectures move at a challenging but completely manageable pace, and he takes time to re-explain topics if necessary. In addition, he has in-class exercises (no points) and fields questions. Clearly cares about material, makes it interesting and relevant, and uses funny analogies to make difficult concepts simple.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lubensky is a GREAT guy, but races through material in class. Office hours aren't very accessible. I honestly did better teaching myself. Lectures were overwhelming/stressful. Exams are worth 100% of your grade. Homework is assigned though. It's long, expected, and only counts for some extra credit. Dropped the class to take with someone else.

Easiest L201 prof hands down. Drops your lowest exam score, gives a cheat sheet on exams, and no cumulative final. I was able to completely skip the last exam and last like month of class. Her exams aren't that many chapters are super easy to prepare for because she makes outlines of everything on the exam. Barely studied/put in effort and got an A

She is a new professor and it was extremely prevalent throughout this course. On the first 2 tests many students were cheating and she didn't realize, but when she did all she did was put a lockdown browser. All she does is read off of her slides and her tests are pretty hard. DO NOT TAKE UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCE.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Up till recently, she did not know people were cheating on her test. Realizing this, she did not take much action besides just making the test a lockdown browser and switching the code every class. Does not know how to teach and just reads off the slides. Tests are tricky, and you cannot backtrack. Do not take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's a great person if you talk to her one on one, however, *as someone who doesn't have much interest in law* her lectures are quite boring and long. I honestly slept through a lot of the lectures, but if you read the textbook, do the practice problems, and go to her office hours, you should be fine. (I just didn't, so I got a B lol)

Professor Douglass is incredibly kind, supportive, and invested in her students' success. Some early bad reviews were just from low first exam scores. HOWEVER, L201 is a hard course! And she listened to feedback, adjusted the curriculum, added many extra credit opportunities, and greatly improved the class. She's hilarious! Highly recommend!

She's the kind of professor that I think you would love if you like law but if not you probably won't like her class. She goes really deep into cases and I assume it's helpful but honestly I find the material too boring to pay attention for more than 5-10 minutes at a time, and her lecture style makes it hard to follow. Cheat sheet on exams tho!

-She gives in person extra credit and a cheat sheet
-Cannot teach she reads off slides so self-study
-The textbook is wordy

Professor Douglas was one of my favorite professors this semester if you can take her for L201!!! She allows you to have an entire paper front and back cheat sheet for exams, the exams are similar to the practice exams. And she also posts when we will have in class assignments so you can for sure get credit for those if you go to class.

She is so misunderstood. She has improved so much since the start. Gives out extra credit sometimes. No homework. Get a full outline for each test, a full front and back page cheat sheet, and you get to drop 1/4 tests. Her lectures are kind of boring, but she is super great at receiving feedback and answering questions from students. Def recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: New professor. Doesn't cold call anymore. Reads off the slides that textbook makes for her. Speaks like we are all lawyers so no one can actually understand what she is talking about. Get a cheat sheet on exam and get to drop exam L201 is hard in general...her lectures INSANELY BORING...also on exams you dont get to go back in questions
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: So boring, but tbh we get a whole printer paper cheat sheet per exam, get to drop one exam at the end, and attendance isn't mandatory. the only thing is that she has this god complex since shes a lawyer and is really od about certain things. her voice could put me right to sleep. i wouldnt take w her u can def find better profs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor - loved taking her class and thought it was very easy just reading the textbook. Did not pay much attention in class

the best professor ever. yes it's exam heavy, but she is EXTREMELY prepared, VERY articulate, really cares about the material, is very knowledgeable, and is very welcoming of questions. any reviews that say otherwise are students that barely show up to class or spend class time doing literally anything but paying attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: First year and young professor and I think it took her a min to get the hang of things but now she's dialed in. She's very smart, answers questions, and supportive. She does expect participation, so not a bad idea to read cases/textbook to prepare for class. Offers extra credit. Drops lowest exam grade. In-class assignments are participation based.

Started out rough since she cold-called but that lasted one week. He started giving good study guides, extra credit, cheat sheet, and is not too strict about IRAC formatting for in-person assignments. Overall is a hard course so you have to read and take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Some of these reviews are too harsh. She's a new professor and had some things to figure out at first but she definitely got the hang of it. No homework, just in class assignments (that's the only attendance). Four exams and she drops the lowest grade. Offers extra credit for raising your hand in class. You get an entire notebook sheet on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her class is so much easier than a lot of the other L201 profs! Practice exams are super similar to the real thing, she drops your lowest exam score at the end of the semester, and she genuinely cares about her students and will meet with you. The class average on our last exam was like a B+ which is higher than I've ever heard of for L201.

Super smart and lecture content is usually just slides, but she always expands more on the content and is incredible at answering questions. Prepares you well for exams and really wants students to succeed

There are 4 exams and she drops your lowest score at the end of the semester. She reads off the slides a lot but then she elaborates. She met with me twice outside of class before the first exam to answer every question and it helped a lot. Her "cold calls" aren't serious cold calls. You can say you don't know. The material is just hard, so study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I have read the reviews and I think that they are way too harsh. Professor Douglas does her best to make the class interesting and engaging. Yes it is a lot of work but this is a college course its not supposed to be a breeze. My only critique is that her slideshows could use some pictures but other than that I have really enjoyed her class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The professor simply reads off the slides that are prepared before class and doesn't explain challenging topics or ideas. You, in all honesty, would be better off teaching yourself the elements of this course. The exams are rigorous and nothing like the supplied study materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I feel like these reviews are a little hasty. This is her first time teaching the class and shes clearly a young professor. She elaborates beyond the slides, and she does cold call, but its not hard at all she literally gives you the paragraph to read the answer from. Tests are hard, its college. Just actually take notes and study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Practice exams are so easy and literally common sense but the actual exams are worded very complicated and much harder. She cold calls in lectures and expects students to have a detailed answer aftering reading 40 slides in the most monotone voice I've ever heard. Attending class is so boring, pointless, and frustrating.

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

Within this class you do a United Nations module, wherein you select a country and then have to write weekly assignments over the positions of that government on a range of topics. Lectures about the UN and its subsidiaries. Be prepared to read and write a lot, diplomacy requires a lot of words. One quiz, weekly assignments count the most though.

Professor Spechler has a captivating teaching style that keeps her classes interesting and enlightening. Her classes are lecture heavy, but she frequently opens the class up for open-ended discussion. I have taken several of her classes and each of them are crucial to understanding international politics and relations.

Professor Spechler is a gem in the department. Her lectures are engaging and she explains everything well, makes sure you understand. Always down to answer some current event questions. Theres lots of reading for a 100 level class. But would nevertheless take a class with her again!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Spechler the best professor I've had at IU. She cares that her students get excited and interested in the course material more than anything. I've had Professor Spechler for two classes now and she's been amazing. Do you have to come to her class and pay attention? Yes. reviews.comment: I have loved taking this class with Spechler. She really makes you work hard for the A, its not an easy class. But it is very rewarding, lots of fun, and Spechler gives great lectures. Highly recommend.

Dr. Spechler gives a good, informational lecture. Readings are very important and tests are hard if you dont spend a copious amount of time preparing. The paper is rough but fun. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very good lectures. Best professor I've had at IU. You get to do a simulation that is lots of fun in her classes. Would highly recommend. reviews.comment: She's very intelligent and an expert on Russia. Her class however was annoying. There was way too much reading and a lot of it was superfluous for her exams. I was the only A so if you're not smart and do not have a good memory (a ton of material on tests), stay away.

Absolutely amazing professor. I plan on taking her Russian politics class in the spring. She really knows her stuff, but attending class is essential to get notes. Way more assigned readings than any other class, but she does talk about a lot of them in class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Spechler is amazing. She is one of the smartest people I have ever met and definitely the best prof I have had at IU. Even though she is getting old, she is still extremely passionate about her subject and it is obvious. Readings are difficult, but trust me she knows what she is doing and of you do the readings you will learn SO MUCH.
Assigns a ridiculous amount of reading, more than any other class I have ever had. Lectures were fairly interesting. Class was fairly difficult but not impossible.

Professor Spechler is absolutely fantastic. Her classes aren't easy, and the assigned reading was more than my other classes but together. However, it was worth it. Her knowledge of her field is excellent, and she does a great job teaching. She also works hard to keep students engaged in class and discussing the material, to their benefit.

Prof is very knowledgeable in their field, but not an effective teacher. Lectures are not on-task (Rambling). Lecture notes not very useful. ExamsPapers micromanaged so that the TA(s) have no discretion in grading (to your detriment). Reading ESSENTIAL to passing, yet amount of reading   2 classes of 300 level equivalent topics. AVOID Spechler!

Pretty tough class, but still intriguing. Topic was based around warfare between nations and was very interesting! However, the tests were difficult, even when she does give you the questions beforehand--and note-taking as well as reading is necessary to get a good grade.

Yeah yeah, she's hard. But that's what makes you learn the material. If you're willing to put in the work, she's a fantastic teacher. However, if you have only mild interest in the topic she's teaching, then maybe you shouldn't take the class because you will have to work extremely hard to get an A.

Prof. Spechler is the most amazing professor I have ever had or could possibly have. She's the most interesting lecturer I've ever seen and really tries to engage students. She's extremely well-versed in the field and you can tell she loves teaching it! As long as you do the reading and the assignments, you're golden!

While Dr. Spechler is incredibly intelligent and the lectures are engaging, I was floored with the workload and the grades distributed. I'm a Junior Poli Sci major who'd never gotten an A- before, but this class killedme. It bordered on being a smaller version of an Honors thesis seminar. Intellectually fascinating but not worth the hard won B:(
Grandma Spechler is too old to be teaching. Does more nit-picking than grading. Very hard grader with lots of reading. No visuals with rambling lectures. She does know alot about her field though.

no visuals and just talks, hard to identify what is relevant and what is antidote. Took the first exam all my answers were correct but still C all activities happened at the end, last 3 class periods high expectations for course but very disappointed should be classified as a psych class not a poly sci major regrets taking this class wish i didnt

Professor Spechler is the best professor I've had at IU. She is truly loves what she teaches, and conveys that through her style of teaching. Don't get me wrong, this class is tough. If you don't study, you will fail. But if you're willing to put in the time and are interested in international relations, I'd highly recommend her classes.

Assigns a ridiculous amount of readings and provides no visual aids for her lectures except a brief outline on the board which she doesn't follow because she gets off on tangents. Very little feedback about grades. Unless you like taking a class that is a full time job in itself I wouldn't recommend.
If you love international relations, she's a great professor. Really loves what she does, sometimes over enthusiastic. Do the reading, and you'll get a good grade

I've taken two classes with Prof. Spechler. She is one of the most intelligent and helpful professors I've had. Yes, her classes can be challenging, but I guarantee you'll be appreciative of that later on. I especially recommend her to poly sci majors or anyone interested in IR. You read a lot, the tests can be a challenge, but you'll learn SO much

Professor Spechler is amazing!  Her class is a lot of your, and you absolutely need to do all the reading, but if you do the reading (actively) you are almost guaranteed an A in the course!  She tells you exactly what she wants, and she really tries to make sure you take the most from her class!  You have to be interested in the topic to survive.

She is a terrible professor. She does not tell you your grade at any point in the semester. SHE IS TOO OLD TO BE TEACHING. Reading is ridiculously long and lectures were unbearable to sit through. Avoid her at all costs if you value your time and grade.
Great professor. You have to read a lot, but if you care about international relations, it will be easy reading.

Spechler's class was my absolute favorite class of the semester. I worked very hard to earn an A, but the amount of material I learned in the process was well worth the sweat. She is insanely intelligent in what she teaches, and her lectures are enthralling.

She literally talks at you the entire time with no visuals or media, and expects you to read massive amounts of repetitive information. AVOID her if you love your GPA.

Prof. Spechler is one of those professors where if you figure out her game, you'll get an A. Spechler knows everything about Russia, a lot about nukes, and tells you EXACTLY what she wants in papers and tests. Just go down the lists, and you'll do well. Very agreeable professor, with a good sense of humor.
One of the best Political Science classes I have taken at IU, and it's my major. This woman really does know EVERYTHING about Russia, and is extremely nice and helpful.  TAKE NOTES

I took Prof. Spechler's Model UN class. She really is an expert in her field, is always fair and understanding, and willing to work with you or give you a second chance if you deserve it. If you're interested in the UN, EU, or international politics, take her classes. You'll have to earn your A, but you'll learn a lot.
Expert at what she teaches, and she knows how to teach it in a way you can understand.  Very interesting and engaging.  Difficult, but completely worth it.  Lots of reading.
Very good teacher but very difficult. Not an easy class but fun. She makes the class interesting and entertaining. Expect to do a lot of reading.
If you're looking for an easy A, Dr. Spechler is not for you. She's tough but extremely fair, and you will definitely learn a lot from her. But be careful cause this woman knows EVERYTHING.
No Comments
She will go out of her way to help you with anything you may need explained. Generous with extensions. Thorough, a little boring, but really worth it,
Wonderful professor.  Very tough, but that is why we are there.  Great professor, you'll like her.  You will have a lot of reading but its worth it.  The UN meeting is the best.
One of the best and most intelligent professors at IU.  Highly recommended.
too much reading. too hard. boring as hell.
i agree wholeheartedly with the above comment
