steer clear :p

Tests are open note with ample time and no analysis. Little is posted online, and the lectures are device free. This means that the class is primarily about attendance, notetaking and note sharing instead of learning. For a history course, it misses most analysis and serves more as a survey of counterculture in (almost entirely western) music.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you're willing to take time and go to every class/ study, take this course. If you're lazy and skip class you're going to hate the tests. Also, I personally despise the heavy metal genre and succeeded at this class because I worked hard. You'll be fine if you actually try. NO NOTES POSTED AFTER CLASS so go to class to succeed. TIMED WRITING

This professor is very entertaining and knows what he is talking about. If you want to do well in the class, you must show up. There are several essays. Tests are lengthy and free response. Overall, the material is interesting, the difficulty is moderate, and you are introduced to some good music. I would recommend this class.

This course was new for the semester and Professor Dodson did a wonderful job with it. I loved his enthusiasm for the topics we were discussing. There was always some sort of song playing for students to walk in and out of class based on what we were learning. Such a fun course and I LOVED it and LOVED Professor Dodson. Take this course if you can!

Lectures are pretty interesting, he is a good lecturer. BUT has way to many readings from early 16th/17th centuries that go on and on in old english and expects you to read/know them. Being a history major I expect some of this...but not 10 pages per article of nonsense of which there are 3 of them to read per class at least.

Prof. Dodson is an excellent lecturer. He's well-organized, intelligent, and eloquent. The class is challenging and Dr. Dodson is skilled at asking students pertinent and thought-provoking questions. He assigns a good load of reading, but for the most part it's fascinating stuff--primary sources and great novels. He's my favorite professor at IU.

Professor was okay - seemed like he'd be fun to hang out with if talking about subjects other than that of the class.  The class itself was new and experimental, kind of lacked focus, and was difficult to follow.

Excellent teacher!  Lectures are packed with interesting and insightful information not in the textbook.  Essay prompts are always interesting and thought-provoking.  Shares his personal research interests with the class.  Friendly, funny.  A great teacher!!

Wonderful professor.  Lectures and readings are very long though.  However he makes it bearable with is humor.  Willing to meet with you to address problems and issues with the class.  Very nice and understand man.  The content of the course was good as well. Although there was too much reading..lots of novels.

His lectures can be extremely long, but they're peppered with humor and sarcasm which make the subject manageable. One novel/lecture theme= about 7 novels and a paper with each, but otherwise a worthwhile class

She grades pretty easily as long as you have some understanding of the material. She gives study guides for all exams that are very thourough, but most of the info isnt used. She is very passionate about art and will answer any related questions. It is very test heavy and the final consists of two parts.

She's very sweet and the lectures are really easy to understand. The tests are easy if you pay attention in lecture (I barely even take any notes) and review vocabulary. There's a test every 2-3 weeks and an essay, so I spent practically no time outside of lecture for this class. I definitely recommend if you're looking for an easy A&H credit.
Nothing bad to say about her--lovely person & lectures were good. Would highly recommend this class.

I had to take this course for GenEd credits and I expected this class to be super, super hard. Luckily, Professor D is super down to earth, really funny and sassy, and will always be a shoulder you can rest on. She is really understanding and really cares about setting you up for success. Slight learning curve at first but it's manageable.

Took her class as a freshman year GenEd because I thought it would be a chill time and cool subject—ended up being one of my more work-intensive classes (START THOSE PAPERS EARLY!) with a crazy time-crunch exam format. If you have good memory and a genuine interest in art, you will find something of value in A102. She and the TAs are awesome!

I adore Maria's lectures; she is such an engaging speaker with clear moral values. She does have a Catalan accent, but I feel that it adds to the course material. Her academic vocabulary is absolutely insane and has widened my own vocabulary. She doesn't fear a well-placed swear at times. Maria is so funny, stylish, and engaging.

Maria is the best. Her lectures actually helped me really understand art as a Pre-Med student who took this as a Gen-Ed. Hilarious and gracious. Attendance is not taken, except for in discussion, but I suggest going to class because she's great at what she does and so funny!
She is so sweet and funny and knows how to relate to students. She is a very easy grader and also super understanding if you ever need extra help!
I highly recommend taking classes with Maria. She is very funny and makes class interesting. I take her art history class and I can tell how passionate and knowledgeable she is about art history.

Goated Professor, while my class had a lot of terms that you needed to know that you might struggle to learn if you didn't know the terms in advance, that's not the professor's fault. She is very funny and always there if you need help in the class. One of the nicest professors I've had to pleasure of having.

Dr. Domene is awesome, I loved her! Her class is pretty easy as long as you attend lectures to take simple notes on the artworks and key terms. She wants everyone to do well, so she is willing to offer retakes or extra office hours. She is also so spunky and fashionable. She is a queen and you should take her class!

(For ARTH-H 100) Maria is great, but the course structure is ridiculous for a gen ed. ~5% of the kids in the class are art majors yet the quizzes and exams require extensive knowledge on the content, so you'll have to study for days. 40 artworks + 60 terms to memorize EXTREMELY in-depth plus a short answer question on the final for perspective.

Took this class my first semester of college as a gen-ed. I didn't have a huge art background but the class was really organized and lectures were good. Most of the grade is quizzes and short writings, but grading is lenient as long as you're able to support your claims.

Although she is a very kind professor, her grading criteria makes absolutely no sense. I would do the same exact thing on every exam and my grades would range from a 99.5 to an 81.5 despite performing at the same level. This caused me to end with a B+ in the class which was very frustrating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is SO funny and an engaging lecturer for the most part. I had an A+ before attendance took me down a letter grade and she is a very fair grader IMO. Only problem is she assigned a giant research paper due during finals week... when we also have a final exam.... why....

I love Professor Domene-Danes. Her class is very easy, what you don't get from lectures, you can get from readings and personally, I think she taught it very well. She makes it interesting and the professor is a very good professor. She tells you what you did wrong in an assignment, not as a punishment but as a way for you to improve. She's amazing
LOVE HER!! very fun professor who loves what she teaches
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Makes you want to come to class because the artist she discussed are so interesting ,even when its early history. She is just a really good lecturer and professor overall, def recommend

Love this woman. Very funny and knowledgeable. Her class is lecture based; additional readings were not really necessary, so I don't recommend buying the textbook. Really easy to do well is you show up.

Maria is a gem -- so kind, intelligent, and full of knowledge. I had Picasso with her and enjoyed it so much. Her lectures are mandatory (you lose points after 2 absences), but she was very entertaining and insightful. The only grades are 4 term tests (done through canvas at home, no proctor) and a research paper. Take Maria at any chance you get!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: My favorite Professor @ IU! Just attend lectures and take notes and you will get a great score! Extremely considerate and accommodating to student's work loads with other courses! Lectures are so interesting and she is funny and cool!

Actually took A327, but the course isn't listed on here. Lectures were super engaging and always very interesting, plus professor Domene-Danes is overall a great lecturer. Exams were primarily about understanding larger concepts, so as long as you kept up with reading and attending class they were fairly easy (but very time consuming).

Have had Maria online and in person. Her lecture slides are accessible if you miss class but lack a lot of the information so it's better to just go to class for her analysis of art works. I skipped over half the semester but researched/studied enough out of class to get by. Tests are all memorization and knowing how to analyze art work. Study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I love her so much, shes super smart and really funny :)

Maria is not a horrible professor but definitely makes this class way to hard. Goes over around 40 different artworks and will test you over just 5 but it is necessary you memorize all the 40 artworks or you will fail the tests because they are random IDs of just 5 of the 40 artworks. I took ARTH101 and it was way better and less stressful

Literally the hardest class I have ever taken. You have to memorize many pictures and state the date time year and who painted it plus terminology essay questions. Thought this class would be easy, but it is the hardest class I have ever taken. Quizzes all on paper taken in the class, lots of memorizing. Might drop the class. Horrible lectures.

Maria was absolutely fantastic. Her quizzes and tests were open-book/note. Although her slides weren't very detailed, whatever I didn't learn in class is mentioned in the book. She's a generous professor and can tell she loves what she's teaching, while also being good at teaching it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hes a nice guy, but his assignments break constantly and the questions are extremely vague. The assignments don't even matter due to the assignment reviews only giving you one point on the score for actually doing the assignment and more-so grade how much you remember from the assignment you did 2 weeks ago and never covered again.

Andrew Holland is a pleasant person and clearly has a deep understanding of the topics he teaches, however he can't teach. His courses are very disorganized, yet are extremely technical. He gives vague questions, then expects hyper-specific answers, and just doesn't know how to setup a course.

On the surface the professor seems like a nice guy, very easy going and fun but the structure of his class isn't the best. Grades are rushed and Game projects aren't graded as they are but against other projects including high achievers. You could put so much work and effort into your project and still receive a bad grade. Would not recommend

Like everyone else he's a nice professor but just super unorganized. The ICEX's we had in class never worked everyone in class always had problems with them, the actual assignments barely relate to the information talked about in class. Never gets back to emails in a timely manner. Doesn't give back feedback on grading. Just a nightmare of a class.

Very unprofessional professor, he's a nice guy and will try to help you but he is awful at getting back to emails, the structure of his course, and just overall is all over the place. First off the auto grader is never working so he always sets those back, he never announces anything so attend classes will be a necessity. Take only if required.

While a nice person, Mr. Holland is a terrible lecturer. Almost every in-class exercise he set up resulted in the majority of the class having technical issues, which he then put onto the TA's to fix as he moved on with almost no one else participating. Never responded to emails, provided no reasoning for grades, couldn't relay information well.

Andrew is a very nice guy, but man his classes are not fun. I had his Info-230 class on Tuesday and Thursday. Tuesday he would just give notes which do not show up again until the final. On Thursday he has an in-class exercise where most of the time, students are having issues with the assignment. The communication is awful too.

He seems nice, but the class is such a hot mess. Everything is disorganized, the autograder is broken 90% of the time, so sometimes the coding assignments are pushed back, and sometimes they're not. We're told things very last minute. There is also 0 communication, over email and on the discord server. The class is passable but such a pain.

He's a chill/cool professor. I am not sure if it was his first semester teaching this class, but the lectures were interesting. He can do better on explaining or teaching since most of the instructions were vague, or he expects us to know the terms he uses. Most of the in-class exercise days were stressful; everyone always had tech problems.

The professor is nice during class, that's where the benefits of him end. His grading criteria is insanely steep, only perfectly working code stands a chance of getting any points. Lecture bore the entire class to tears, the content is so dense that it's hard to learn any one thing. Only take this class if you have, God bless your soul.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: there's 1 exam only 20% worth of ur grade, 1 big project at the end. there's 1 mandatory class every week, 1 optional. overall solid professor that gets u out of class early from time to time too. 1 thing to keep in mind is that his questions are a bit annoying with "which statements are false"

The class is fairly easy and attendance isn't required except for a few days. Exams are hard. All MC questions are "which statement is false" then a,b,c,d and e being all are true. All exam questions come from his slides so attending lectures can be helpful to get his explanation for slides. Two papers, one with group. Easy grader if you try.

Scott is passionate about what he teaches and it is clear through the way that he conducts the class. Exams are tough, but he communicates what is going to be on them, so just study what he emphasizes in class and you'll be fine. Attendance isnt mandatory with the exception of a few days, but dont get into the habit of skipping classes.

Scott is the greatest professor at Kelley. He shares his personal experiences and has a lot of professional experience to back it up.  He helps students develop professionally with career goals.  He really cares about his students.  He will help you with any professional or education needs you have.

Scott may be the greatest professor at Kelley.  Not only is he a great professor who keeps class time interesting, he cares about his students.  If you build a relationship with him, which is not hard to do, he will help you with any professional or education needs you have.  His class is also very interesting if you are passionate about SCM.

If you attend lectures ready to learn and leave yourself with a decent amount of time to study for exams you should be good to go. None of the information he teaches is all that difficult to understand, but skipping lectures will make it feel impossible to learn.

I don't think I learned anything in this class. I think some of his material is made-up because you can't find it anywhere on the internet. The exams were memorization and every question had All/None of the Above. He seems like a nice guy, but I hated his class.
the lecture makes no sense and his ppts are awful. bunch of words with made-up acronyms.
smh.. don't take it from him if it's possible.
Don't take this course from him if it is possible. 2 tests that leave nothing in your brain. It is just memorization that you will not use when you go into your career.
I started hating Supply Chain because of this class. Tests are horrible. Felt like I learned nothing after the test. If you are SC or Ops major he is the only one teaching this course so good luck..

People either love or hate him. I found him to be arrogant and petty, forcing assigned seats and wrote memorization tests. The class itself isn't difficult, and he is pretty forthright about whats on the exams, which is decent. I took him again for P431 mostly because the other prof was harder and you might as well take the (easier) devil you know.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice and very fair!! Exams were hard and pure memorization. Attendance are required though!

Avoid this class if possible. Every question on the exams have either "none of the above" or "all of the above." is lectures make no sense and his tests are extremely hard. You have to read a book for no reason and also do a large case at the end with no questions. Don't take it!!
Loved his class. I thought he was a great lecturer and made what could be dry material interesting. His energy every day was awesome and he clearly cares about his students. The EC is nice too!

Dobos lays out all of the information for the course in a way that is very easy to understand. He genuinely cares about your grade and pretty much tells you what is on the exam so if you don't pass or get at least a B or above you were most likely just never in class or didn't put in the effort.

Very fair teacher overall. He is very understanding when it comes to excused absences etc. The lectures were at times long and boring, however, he makes good use of examples to solidify his points. His tests are no joke. He loves the "D. None of or All of the Above" option. You  have to memorize and know your stuff to get an A, but its an easy B.

Most boring lecturer ever and talks with his hands wayyy too much.  The material he teaches will make you stab your eyes out in this class.  On the pop test we had for X170 only his section was extremely detailed and everyone left it blank.  Not a fan of him as a lecturer, but he's nice.

The class is purely memorization.  You will get lists and have to regurgitate them on the exam.  Attendance required.  You literally learn the same information in almost every class, but he has different lists about the same subject.  Really nice guy, but very boring class.

Dobos is a really nice guy, but doesn't seem to know much beyond the slides he goes over. The class is pure memorization of the slides and regurgitation of it on the tests. Save your money, and do not buy the textbook.

He's very serious but completely fair. I didn't take class seriously, missed too many days, etc., and he still treated me well. I'm taking another class with him this semester because if you don't screw around he's a great teacher. If you're used to slacking off and then sucking up; good luck.

Treats you like a 5-year old. Sits in the back of the room while lecturing. Will call you out about cell phone use. He's not really that great of a teacher. Every multiple choice question ends with "All or none of the above." Good luck, avoid him at all costs.

Had Scott for P320 as well.  Best Professor - Cares about students, treats you fairly, and teaches a wide array of topics that are very informative.  He shows applications through videos and great books picked for the class.  He strays away from quantitative analysis...which I think is great

Really nice guy. Class is organized. He is easy to understand and uses a lot of examples. Exams are a little hard, but you'll do fine if you study. Attendance policy is more strict than most professors. He will try to work with your personal schedule if you talk to him before hand. Don't buy the book, you don't need it.
Class is very organized. Tests require alot of studying but overall, easy to do well in the class. Don't buy the textbook, you'll never need it.

Very fair instructor.  Always uses examples for every topic.  Tests are pretty tough even after he gives you what he is going to choose the essay from.  Lets you make up exams if you speak with him before.

Professor Hollinden is by far my favorite professor that I have had at IU. He is caring, funny, and wants the students to excel. I wish I could take more and more of his classes. Happy Retirement Professor!

I had a blast, I've gained so many new favorite songs and always enjoyed his hilarious lectures. I would take this class over and over again. Happy retirement professor! Wish I could take one more class with him.

The Music of The Beach Boys is in my opinion the best course offered at this school, Professor Hollinden is extremely knowledgable of the history and the music and I cannot recommend this course enough. The music is spiritual on the speaker system and I would take this class over and over again if I could. Happy retirement Professor.
Awesome class with an amazing professor.
THIS DUDES THE GOAT!! Best professor I have had at IU easily.

Mr. Hollinden is a really great prof. His lectures are VERY engaging and he clearly knows a LOT about what he's talking about. He is really funny and lectures in a way that feels like you're having a really interesting convo.

This class isn't easy! Ur grade is based off 4 exams (one retake). But he is very clear about grading criteria. Just study
Make sure to attend class. Funny guy and outlines what he may ask questions on during his lectures. Just pay attention and get some laughs and you'll get a free A.

What a dude. He's seriously hilarious and will go off on random fun topics which makes the lecture easy to listen to. As long as you pay attention the class is easy enough. This is his last year so if you're reading this Professor I hope you have a great life because you made my Tuesdays and Thursdays so much better.

This man is truly incredible. I took Z203, and this class was so easy and enjoyable. His lectures are absolutely hilarious, and the class itself has become iconic at IU because of this man's enthusiasm, humor, and wisdom. Changed the way I listen to music forever. Hats off to this legend, thanks for a great semester.

King, took his Z201 class, and he proves to be extremely knowledgeable and funny. If you go to every lecture, even though it is not mandatory, and listen to the music as you learn it the class is so easy. Worst part is giving up almost all other music throughout semester to know the songs so well, but turns out a lot of them are now in my playlist

Writing this for Z201
The best professor I have ever had. Extremely funny and it's clear he knows his stuff. Kept us engaged with jokes and has a passion for the music.
Attendance is not mandatory, but if you don't show up you will fail.

Interesting class, only four tests throughout the class (an additional optional one to drop the lowest grade). It's easy to get an A if you start listening to the music early on and make sure to study the facts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He did a really great job of keeping everyone interested, it was really fun going to lectures and listening to all the music.

Prof. Hollinden was great, really knowledgeable with rock music. Attendance not mandatory, but lectures are great especially if you like the music. Take the notes and study the music, only four tests and 200 points that make up the entire grade. Fun GenEd.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Unarguably one of the greatest professors I have had. He kept the students engaged using jokes and asked our opinions on the songs he played. It was so obvious how deeply he cares for this subject and how knowledgable he is. I loved going to class! I will say, however, if you take this class, keep up with the listenings and notes for the exam!!!
Solid prof. One of my favorite. Took a strong interest in her field and was genuinely invested in student success. And she is well published.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This proffesor was probably one of the best i've ever had. Her course was very direct and difficult so if your a bad student, dont take it. This class if for people who actually care.

The most disorganized person, let alone professor, I have ever come across in my life. She never has a clear thought and teaches about primary sources, not historical events. Clearly has a lot of knowledge about the subject but she never has a clear thought. Insane amount of readings due each class and expected to know about each one for exams.
This proffesor is wonderful and I'm so happy that I got her. She is my mom and all you other people being mean should stop it. 10/10 parenting and teaching skills!!

I would advise you not to take this course. This professor is very nice, though the course itself is rather disorganized. There is so much reading and information thrown at you for just a 100 level course. My 300 level courses didn't take up half the time that this one did. Find a different way to get your diversity credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Gave us the option between a final paper, or a written final. We picked paper. We got both.

She assigns so many readings. She wants you to agree with your side and isnt really open to other things.  The readings are horrible. She expects you to read tons of random papers. This should not be an entry course. There are mandatory questions every day over the readings. And she adds things last minute like we have no other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I feel bad for the professor because she made zoom a thing for this class. This causes the complaining toddlers to get confused and they get bad grades because they are confused. Readings are not bad, if I am being real, you do not even really have to read. The daily questions are extremely easy. The papers are also easy. Stop crying :'(
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course includes HEAVY reading. Each lecture includes students being handed a microphone and told to speak about their opinion on what we read. She has very heavy set opinions she wants you to abide by. If you even at all have a different opinion, she will reword it(key quote, "So in theory, what you're saying is.") Note: you learn nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is honestly one of the worst classes I have ever had the displeasure of sitting through. Getting assigned on average 60-100 pages of random speeches and papers, then being assigned a short answer question that has NOTHING to with the reading is one of the most soul crushing experiences I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is very nice, but avoid this class. Get ready to read 60 pages before every lecture and listen to students give their opinions for the majority of in-class time. There is a daily question over the readings and they're mandatory for essays. There is no reason an entry-level course should be this much work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr.Libby is truly a great professor! He seems a bit intense and intimidating at first, but once you get to know him better and understand his teaching style, he is very kind and wants the best for his students. His lectures are very fun and conceptual, which makes 'boring' work very digestible! Also, points for the amazing hair. I love it.

This is probably my favorite class I have taken at IU (B200 obesity and hunger). Dr. Libby is very knowledgeable and a super entertaining lecturer. He introduced things in such an interesting way and explained things about the food system I didn't even realize existed. I loved my group it was honestly a good time. LOT of work but worth it
Dr. Libby is so passionate about what he teaches and it makes a huge difference. He makes class very interesting, and is very helpful with coursework. He really wants to see students succeed!

Tough grader, but super passionate about the topics he presents. I NEVER thought I'd say a professor's lectures were interesting, but his really were!! This class made me love the Human Bio major and i'm so happy I got to take the Obesity and Hunger topic (if this is an option, take it!).

Dr. Libby is intense when he lectures, but when you get to know him he is really kind. I stayed after class and talked to him for over an hour last semester and we talked about poverty and climate change and my family and other ideas and he gave me advice on future plans. He is a great teacher and nice and not at all like I thought he would be.

I loved Dr. Libby's class! It was super engaging, with hands on. The content was relevant and changed my view on the food system, giving insight into daily eating habits. Though he's a tough grader, his feedback is helpful. He dislikes passive voice and sentence fragments. Was a great intro to my freshman year and made me feel prepared. He's funny!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Libby was a great professor who genuinely cared not only for the subject but also for the growth of his students. The IFS course was writing-heavy, but the work was fair, and the feedback was helpful for improving academic writing. He included many excursions and dinners, making his class and the program a great introduction to college.
I loved taking Libbys b200, b300 classes. He always got my attention right away in class, told interesting stories to make his points. He's a scary hard grader though.

Dr. Libby had NO clear grading criteria, incredibly unstructured lectures, and was such a harsh grader. You will lose points if you miss ANY lecture, as there are no drops. Class time was not used to prepare us for our final project that was worth a very large portion of our grade. He took off many points for every essay exam, yet had no rubric.

I HATED libby as a professor. He is an extremely tough grader and doesn't provide clear feedback for anything. This class shouldn't be ruining your gpa. It could be a super engaging and interesting class if the professors weren't TERRIBLE. WOULD NOT recommend.
Overall a terrible instructor. Wouldn't recommend taking this class with him if given ANY other option.
By far one of my favorite professors at IU. I would definitely take all my hubi classes with him.
I took his IFS class, and it was a blast. He is very engaging and seems to care a lot about both the topic and the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: LOVE THIS DUDE. He was engaging during lectures (even via zoom, which is hard to do) and made the material very interesting. Definitely recommend this guy
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hes a solid prof! He graded the essays on all the tests and gave decent grades. His powerpoints were basically useless though, so beware of that. He makes lectures interesting and i would recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Libby was one of the best professors I've ever had. He was inspirational but also created fear in my heart forever. I was always excited to go to class and thoroughly enjoyed the content as well as how it was presented. Dr. Libby is a very chill prof but won't take your bs. Be ready for class and ready for any criticism he gives you.
Made a simple topic absolutely fascinating. His tough but helpful feedback really improved my writing. Want to take more of his classes.

Dr. Libby was awesome. The course was 3 credit hours shoved into 2 weeks, but he was fair when it came to assignments and he was easy to approach with questions. He also works hard to get to know his students and their interests. I would totally take another class with him in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Take the obesity topic if it's availiable. Libby is very energetic, quirky  and gives a great lecture. If you participate he will know your name and will love to talk to you about your thoughts. Very friendly, and very helpful. Quick grader. He has cool hair as well. Beware a group project that is worth a large part of your grade. Do the readings.
Great guy! I would take all of my Human Biology classes with him.

Very great guy, who has a wide range of expertise. He co-taught my bio class and was by far the better teacher. Very good at lecturing and draws you to pay attention. Would recommend him to anyone. Will meet outside of class and also help with anything even if it is not class related.

Good Teacher, grades leniently. Class was very interesting and Libby was always willing to help. He tried to ensure that everyone in class understood the point before moving onto another topic. Though he did give a lot of homework, that was not an issue because it was always interesting an related to the topic. He also used class time very well.

Professor Libby is very insightful and knowledgable on the topic. He offers a ton of information, and you learn by going to class. The course consists of three projects and 20 hours of volunteering. Overall, this class is great!

He's a really insightful, interesting teacher. His comments are helpful and thought-provoking. He's a tough grader on papers, but I really enjoyed the class and was introduced to a lot of concepts and writers that I had not experienced before.

he was a very very nice guy, i had him for 131 but he did not teach in a typical 131 style. still am not sure what he expected for our papers but he was a great teacher and really enjoyed the class - makes you think a lot!
VERY INTELLECTUAL! I ENJOED THE CLASS VERY MUCH, BUT HE GRADED SOMEWHAT DIFFICULTLY ON PAPERS AND THAT MADE ME NOT LIKE THE CLASS AS MUCH.  STILL A GOOD CHOICE.

He is so smart and funny. Sometimes professors don't seem to care about what they teach...that is not the case with Professor Libby. He is very compassionate about what he teaches and he likes his subject!! He is extremely helpful and such a great teacher. I am so thankful to have taken his class because it was such a great experience.
No Comments
Goldman goes above and beyond to include people and make lecture interesting, even on boring topics. Grading was exam heavy with a final group project as well.

I really enjoyed his lectures, they didn't feel super heavy and the slideshows were pretty helpful. Provided clear study guides as to what would be on the test, super open and clearly cared a lot about the class and the students.

I took IFS with Dr. Goldman and had the best time. He made all class content really accessible for non-music majors. There were some complicated readings, but we always went over them in class thoroughly. He was very communicative, and genuinely wanted to interact with his students. Would 100% recommend this kind professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Would recommend! Kept lectures fun, interesting and interactive.

Prof was really knowledgeable about energy economics and teaches really relevant concepts while fostering a conducive class environment. Exams were very, very fair and ample practice was given. The policy debate was an interesting capstone and we also had a fair mix of in-class simulations and guest lectures that made class engaging!

Highly recommend G455 to anyone at IU. Prof. Butters does a great job of making energy policy and economics interesting while staying unbiased in a highly politicized industry. Grades are also fair and representative of effort.
Amazing Guy!!!!

One of the best professors in Kelley, Amazing and funny guy very passionate about what he is teaching and telling us. He is also very kind and fun when it comes to being able to convey the complex things he is teaching. If you can for any class take Prof. Butters!!!!
Butters is definitely better than the average teacher for a Kelley math class. Good at explaining concepts. I'd recommend doing the assigned textbook readings if you want to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Likely to be my favorite professor in the Kelley School of Business. He is extremely caring for his students, and always makes himself available out of class to ensure his students learn the material to the best of their abilities. The class is structured extremely well; the homework is extremely helpful, and isn't too much either.

Professor Butters is a fresh face in the Business Economics department within the Kelley School of Business. He teaches econometrics in a very engaging and digestible way. He is young and relatable, but not lacking in experience and excellence. Beyond this, he invests a lot of time in his students- even in projects beyond his own classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Very entertaining lectures. Keeps students engaged, attendance isn't mandatory but you'll find yourself wanting to go (and you need to if you wanna do well on tests). Very knowledgeable on his topics. One of my favorite classes so far.

pros: no attendance/textbook, online midterm/final, very chill, 3 extra credits
cons: barely writes anything on the slides so u NEED to be in class, midterm was unbelievably hard, TAs take turn grading ur paper so expectations are diff each time, final wasn't as hard
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best courses I've taken at IU. Prof. Weaver is hilarious, knowledgeable, and keeps students engaged. The workload is light—brief writing assignments and occasional exams. You'll need to attend class, as outside research or AI won't cut it—but that's okay, because the course is genuinely enjoyable!

His course is the most fascinating I have ever taken at IU. He's a very smart guy with a great sense of humor and his lecture style reflects that. Not many assignments, but they are graded very fairly and are also very interesting. Would highly recommend this course to literally everyone ever.

There's only a few things he grades and exams take up most of your grade. You have to be in the lecture to know how to answer the exam questions so make sure you are there even though he doesn't take attendance. He made the class very interesting and easy to understand and not that tough of a grader. Loved this class!!

Weekly one-page paper, no required readings or attendance but attendance is important to get a good grade on exams and knowing what to write in papers because he is very specific and Chatgpt and the internet will not give you the right answer. Great professor and lecturer, very entertaining and helpful to answer questions in and out of class.

He is a great professor and explains the concepts very clearly, and he's just a cool and fun guy. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you don't go to class you likely will not pass. He has a few slides each lecture, but they won't help unless you take notes on what he is saying in class. Not much homework, but your grade depends on a few things.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't mandatory but make sure you go to class (especially on weeks papers are assigned) because YOU WANT GOOD NOTES!!!! All assignments (there are only 8) and tests are open note and he gives you all the info needed to do well on them in person during class. Loved his class and his personality overall. 10/10

Cool professor, took for A&H credit but nonetheless, he made lecture interesting. Class was four essays plus the mid term and the final. If you can write essays and are well at test taking, this is a fairly simple class. There's also readings he posts before every class, never did them and skipped class sometimes and was fine in the end. Recommend.

If you want free credits - take this class. Weaver has some interesting segments around most of his lectures, so if you want to actually get something from the class, show up. If you simply want free credits with little to no work, this class has few writing assignments but are all easy and essentially opinion based. Interesting class, solid Prof.

i really enjoyed this class, however you have to actually go because the questions on the exam and the weekly assignments are strictly based on the in person lectures. professor Weaver is a good lecturer and the weekly assignments are not too hard if you attend class, there are 8 weekly assignments and 2 exams, and that is it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: hes honestly super cool. he gives high school english or social studies teacher vibes yfm? if you miss class you probably will fail bc he doesnt give slides until the week of midterms and finals. you rlly have to pay attention to get useful notes. he doesnt care abt attendance tho. theres only 4 papers and 2 tests (midterm and final)
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Weaver is a super cool guy teaching a super cool class. The discussions you'll have are just so amazing. The class starts off a little boring, but don't worry it gets super interesting later. Weaver assigns a lot of readings, but you don't need to read any of them. If you go to class and take good notes, you'll do great on the open-note tests.

I took Intro to media psych as a gen ed with no insight to the class. I will say, this is my favorite class this semester. While it's a very basic lecture based class, it's not hard and very interesting. The mid-term and final are open note and online so he makes it easy to get an A, as long as you take good notes. I would recommend for A&H credit

I was disappointed by this professor. His slides never had much information on them, just bullet points with general topics. When students asked questions he gave vague responses. I would say this class is an easy A, but I personally did not enjoy the professor's lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I always look forward to Professor Weaver's lectures. He explains things very in-depth yet his lectures are never boring and are very interesting. He is also very easy to talk to outside of class. IF YOU DO NOT GO TO THE LECTURES YOU WILL NOT RECEIVE A GOOD GRADE. All of the tests/papers are directly related to class content not on the PowerPoints.

The format of the class was great! Professor Weaver covers an array of topics in such a short time span. However, I didn't enjoy his specific teaching method. He talks very slowly with long pauses between thoughts. This made it exceptionally difficult to stay engaged. He has PowerPoints but often only covers two slides in a class period.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Weaver is very knowledgeable on race and media, and has interesting lectures! Super nice. He doesn't take attendance, but if you constantly skip/dont ever pay attention, you will not do well. Midterm and final are difficult, but if you pay decent attention, you'll get a good grade. 4 short papers, 2 tests. I would take his class again!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class had no attendance policy but I went and it was the only way you can pass the exam. The lectures were very entertaining and I played on my phone for a lot of it as long as you get the information down you're fine. The few assignments we had were easy and did not take long. The midterm and final were hard but with a big curve fine.

Had him for his IFS class and it was a an amazing experience. Super chill guy and the content was interesting. You have reading every night and a research paper due but the readings don't take any time at all. Totally would recommend if you're doing IFS.

There's textbook so it's important to show up to class. As long as you show up and are engaged it's not hard to do well in Weaver's class. I showed up to almost every class and made sure to take notes during lecture and got an A+. His lectures are engaging and interesting which makes it easy to pay attention. Overall Weaver is a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Weaver is a solid choice for Media 101. Doesn't require readings, lectures are interesting, and assignments are super easy. His midterm and final are seem to be way easier than their counterparts in other sections of the class.
Mr. Weaver is a cool dude and Media 101 is the easiest class ever, easy a for sure.

Mr. Weaver makes the material interesting, but truthfully going to class every day is not required to pass the class. Just make sure you have someone to copy notes from because the tests are mostly based off the notes in lecture. So, if you wanna do well on the tests definitely go to class. Discussion section assignments are frequent but easy.

Class is super easy, really just show up, take some notes, and look over them before the tests. 1 asgt. per week done in small discussion class, and so far half of them have been group projects/participation points. The material might be bland sometimes, but he makes it funny. Guest lecturers have all been interesting as well. Easy A.

He is great! He is so nice and helpful! Before signing up for him with this class, he would email me back very quickly about my concerns with another online class while I was abroad. In this class he is funny, very chill, and for the most part entertaining. There is only 1 assignment per week and tests are easy. Attendance isn't counted, but go.

I really enjoyed having him as a teacher! He's funny and tells great stories. He helps you to remember the material by giving real life examples. He has a good voice to listen to as well. Be sure to take good notes, the power points aren't very helpful because they are pretty vague.

T101 is pretty much the biggest blow off class I've ever taken. Such an easy A. I believe he's the only professor that teaches it as of right now. All the class material is pretty much common sense; I didn't go to half the lectures and still got a 96% on the final. If you're looking for an easy A, this is the class for you.

Weaver is hands down the best professor I've had at IU. I had him this semester for T-205 and T-101. He is hilarious and makes concepts easy to remember with real life examples. If you ask him a question he goes out of his way to get you the information you need. Awesome guy, really just want to be his friend.
Really good guy.  Took 2 classes of his. Never got an A, but he's one if the very few genuine professors I've had.  Like to have a beer with him.
He was really bland and often class was boring. The tests aren't super hard if you study. Paper grading depends on the AI's largely.

Many people say he is a great professor and grades easily and has a lot of fun with the class: I beg to differ. This class was very boring and was difficult to pay attention. If you are going to take this class, make sure you take good notes because his power points are too vague to study from.

Pretty good teacher. He explained everything very clearly, the tests were straightforward, and the papers pretty short and simple. The topic was really interesting and he was pretty funny. Good class, good teacher, though I have heard that Bryant is much more entertaining.

Really interesting class. I am glad I took it because i found it so interesting that I want to minor in it. It is clear that he really knows what he is talking about, and he works to make it interesting. Sometimes he shows clips and makes jokes so as not to lose the class. Overall, a great professor and class!
Interesting and funny
He is SO funny and nice. He tries to keep class interesting but can be boring sometimes. Overall I liked the class and really liked Prof Weaver.
Boring. Very boring. Monotone voice. The class is over an hour, and i was tempted to skip every time we had class.

I had him for a summer class with admittedly an unusual format, but it was obvious he's an excellent teacher. Very informal and makes an effort to connect with his students. The grading was fairly easy, and if you paid attention in class and participated, you'd do fine. I'm hoping to take another one of his classes myself!
Came off as being an obnoxious jerk which really turned me off of the class. Probably would have been more interested if someone else taught it.

Great professor!  If you go to class you will get the notes and do fine on the tests and papers.  Keeps lectures interesting and students engaged.  Would recommend him for any telecom class he may teach!

Such a great professor and probably one of my favorite classes.  It is really interesting but you do actually have to go to the class to get the notes.  If you attend the class then you will definitely do well.

Exams are way harder than they should be. Out of class assignments are pointless and take ages. Lecture is okay but skips over the niche details that she focuses on in exams. Honestly would be a much more enjoyable class if the exams werent as hard.

boring lectures, slow speaker. I never knew biology was this funny!!!!! she laughs at everything. tests ask about things barely talked about in class or discussion. tests are very hard, even though they are multiple choice. tests are also weighted more heavily than classwork, so it has been hard to maintain an A.

Prof. Dunn drags on in lectures, and the lectures are incredibly boring. Primarily reads off slides and adds very little extra verbally. Exams were moved to in-person compared to being online like they were previously. Expects students to use AI to study.

Her lectures are hard to sit through. She draws out her words and says "Umm" at least 50 times a lecture. The first exam is general microbio, so make sure to get a good grade. The rest of the exams are  much tougher and are purely memorizing lengthy/random biological pathways of diseases. Overall, I did not find the class enjoyable.

Her lectures are boring & her exams are TOUGH. You have to really study to do well. Grade dropped a lot from the group article assignments bcs of the strict grading with no rubric. You have to pay attention during her lecture, record it yourself bcs she doesn't, and write lots of notes. She did offer an exam retake and extra credit. Raised to an A-

Megan is one of the worst professors that I have had. She clearly doesn't understand her own material as she as to read off the slide for everything -- even if a student asks her a question. She has to go back to the lecture to look over the information. She doesn't give clear directions on the assignments given and then takes off random points.

Participation is crucial. Lectures are not recorded so please attend class. The weekly homework takes a while, but it overtrains you for the tests, which are all online. There are very few extra credit opportunities. She is a slow speaker, but is thorough with her explanations and loves answering questions in class. A bit awkward but she's so kind.

Goes over slides and answers questions in class. Mastering Bio homework every week, but it does help to understand the material better (not hard whatsoever). Exams are all online. Provides guides for each chapter which may or may not be helpful, just depends on how you prefer to study. Overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Dunn was a good prof. Attendance was mandatory as she asks top hat questions during class, but I'm unsure if they are counted towards final grade. All exams are open note and online, but are still difficult and worth studying for.

Dr. Dunn was okay at best. The exams were all online, open note which was nice. Lectures can be hard to follow along with if you have a short attention span, but her slides and information are very straightforward and help out for exams. Mastering can be difficult (we got behind early on and were expected to read the textbook as our only help)
Pretty simple class. Just attend lectures and discussions. Tests are online and open note. Discussion worksheets are simple and do not take up a lot of time. Ask questions and go to review sessions!

Professor Dunn's lectures can be boring at times, but her slides are straightforward and very helpful for exams. The exams were online and open-note, which made the class much easier. Professor Dunn offered opportunities for extra credit, through exam reflections and the OCQ, and the discussion worksheets were easy to complete.

I think Dr. Dunn is a good lecturer, she has very organized slides and as long as you really listen to what she says during lecture and write it down, you will have all the information you need for the tests. Her tests are not easy but if you go to office hours and make sure you understand all of the homework, you can do well in this class.

DO NOT HAVE PROF DUNN 
She was so inconsistent and beyond unfair. This woman decided to change the in-person class to asynchronous with her awful lectures and then decided to do in-person testing. I don't know how long she's been a professor at IU, but I think it's her time to leave. She should consider kindergarten teaching.

Take with a grain of salt, but apparently this class was supposed to be in person and open note with the rest of the biology department. Dr. Dunn started the class online and asynchronous. We eventually moved in person but tests stopped being open note, again going against the rest of the L112 classes. Lectures were boring. Nitpicks in discussion.

Dr. Dunn is a great professor, but the material for this class can be very heavy. There will be about 9-10 powerpoints with dense information and her exams are only 20-25 multiple choice/short answer questions that are very surface level, so you study a lot of information and the test ends up being light but still difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I always felt like I understood the content after the lectures and homework assignments, but the tests always seemed to be significantly harder. Just worded in a difficult way. This class is definitely time consuming, and the schedule is not changed around at all even if we have an exam that week. Professor seems nice though.
This class sucked so hard. Every exam was harder than the last. You will most definitely cry every time you do homework.

This is the worst Professor for L112. Her lectures are not concise and are extremely boring. Despite the textbook, Mastering Biology, lectures, and discussion worksheet, it is impossible to succeed in her class. Her tests are way too specific and difficult for an intro class. She does not want her student to succeed and is always egotistical.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Dunn was fine and she seemed genuinely interested in what she was teaching, but her lectures were not concise and they were incredibly boring. The tests are hard, but if you study (even a little bit) you can do decently on them. There are a few opportunities for extra credit, and you can skip lecture and still get the attendance points.

For this class, it helps to have a little prior bio classwork (high school level). The assignments are on Mastering Biology (weekly) & really boost your grade. After each exam, she does exam reflections for EC (minus the first one). I only wish her lectures were more concise & flowed with one another more. However, it's clear she is knowledgeable.

Good professor overall. Engaging enough, but not over the top amazing. No real complaints. I would take her class again. I'm not a science major, but looking over the study materials the day before the exam was good enough to do well on the exams. Attendance is only 2% of your grade.

I personally thought prof Dunn was a really awesome professor. It seemed like she enjoyed what she was doing. I felt like she was very good at teaching us material. The exams are very fair as well. Sometimes there are questions that would have been really hard to remember but overall if you study tophat and SG & DG

Great professor! Even though the topics are heavy because it is biology, she does a great job explaining them. Test questions can come directly from homework and discussion work sheets. Drops the lowest test and lots of opportunity for extra credit. Would definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great choice for 112! Really nice and has straightforward notes and straightforward tests. Drop lowest test score. Class structure makes it easier to get a higher grade. Some extra credit too. Would definitely recommend for 112

Extremely boring. Her lectures make you want to fall asleep. But the kicker is you have to pay attention to them because sometimes she talks about stuff that isn't in the lecture notes that she then puts on the exam. Out of about 8 powerpints maybe 100 slides she chooses extremely specific things to put on the exam, overall concepts matter less.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's not the most interesting professor, but if you pay attention and put some time into the class you should be able to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I honestly don't get why she has not great ratings... she's certainly not an easy grader but you could get like 5% EC in my molecular class. Honestly what I would expect in a college science class past the intro level. Lecture and exam heavy. You'll need to work for it, but it's not impossible. She's friendly, go see her if you're struggling.

Dunn is nice and helpful if you ask but her lectures are unbelievably boring. I could never pay attention and just did other homework. So you will probably end up learning most of the material on your own. The tests are not easy and that's coming from someone who took AP Bio, so make sure you study.
Reads directly from the slides and omits words from slides so you have to pay attention to get the full notes. Tests are hard and every week there is a quiz due.

Horrible, horrible professor. I'm not sure how she got chosen to teach 211 but I hope for everyone's sake she never teaches it again. Thank goodness for the AI's because without them the class would've been even worse.

This class is a tough class that goes into depth about the proteins and other molecules involved in genetics. However, if you regularly attend class and read about the material you don't understand in the book you will do fine.

I honestly believe she's a genuine person , but she is truly a horrendous professor. Her lectures consist of her reading her power point word for word in a voice that is monotonous af and the text book she selected was almost just as bad. Almost the entirety of semester points come from tests and she provides no practice problems or practice exams.

I find her lectures kind of boring and that I can't learn well from them- but if you get the notes you need in class I was able to learn from the powerpoint slides on my own. She is nice and well meaning, but for some reason her teaching style just doesn't mesh with my learning style.
Maybe she was better in the upper level classes. I thought she was good. Quizzes were really hard and detail heavy. But everything else was easy and I ended up doing fine.

She always read word for word from the powerpoint making classes seem extremely long.  We had quizzes every week about some minor detail covered the previous week.  Tests were hard, but with doing well on the quizzes and homework, you can do well.

She is terrible at giving lectures. Every week you have a quiz and even if you show you know what you are talking about, you will get marked off for not having exactly what her grading sheet has. You can only miss 2 on the tests to get an A and the questions are tough. This is my second year in college and this has been one of my hardest classes.

Dr. Dunn is an awful professor, she doesn't know what she's doing. Her grading is insane. For the discussion group quizzes, she grades very very specifically, even if it's clear that you fully understand the material from your answer, she will still take off points. I even tried to appeal one of these grades I got, but she would not reason with me.

All I did was read the textbook and take the online tests provided by the textbook and I got A's on all the tests. Listened to maybe half of the lectures. I did go into her office to talk to her once and she was really accommodating.

Megan Dunn is perhaps a below average orator, but nevertheless she stands as a shining example of a rarity in most college courses these days. She is a professor who genuinely cares for her students. If you study and do not attempt to half-ass your way through this course you will do fine. I recorded As on all my exams with relative ease.

I'm a first semester junior who earns As and Bs, until I took this. She reads directly from PowerPoint slides and every few slides takes a word out so you can write at least something down. It's unclear what will be covered in the quizzes & you only get credit if you have exactly what she wrote for an answer. You can only miss 2 on a test for an A.

Dr. Dunn has good intentions of teaching, but can't act on those intentions. Discussion sections are made difficult by quizzes where the answer won't be right unless it's what she has. Lectures aren't great, she reads off the powerpoints. But if you read the book and put in the work, anyone could pull off an A.

You have a quiz every week in your discussion section and every discussion section has a different quiz! This class is difficult if you are not that good at biology because there are about 25 questions a test.  Read the Chapter before the class each time!

Too smart of a professor, overcomplicates every problem. Will mark off participation for not making eye contact. Absolutely no talking during class. Went to every lecture and claude is teaching me how to do every exam problem. Graded participation & attendance. Luckily gives a few of the exam problems in the practice sets and the homework is free.
Inconsistent

Okay.. I think she is super nice like kind. I also think she really likes the topics of class. But I did not learn a single thing in class. I went to class and sometimes walked away more confused. But she gives good non graded practice problems. She makes simple concepts 10x harder than they are.

Worst Kelley professor I've ever taken. No practice for exams besides non-graded practice sets that she doesn't even go over, basically you're left in the dark to figure stuff out on your own. 3 cases through the semester which are easy but are honestly a massive time suck. Sena makes concepts you've learned in F305 sound like monkey speak. AVOID!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Durguner is likely one of the worst professors at IU. She makes a mockery of the material in F-305, and explains easy concepts in convoluted ways. All of the previous knowledge gained from I-Core is wiped away in this class. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

The exams are EXACTLY like the practice problems she gives so study those and you'll be ok. Participation is 10% of the grade which is kind of annoying but just show up and try to answer at least the easy stuff. The class can be taught to yourself too so you can never show up if you don't care about the 10%.

Hard class, but do not need to go - just helps learn concepts. Test are all quantitative so you should do all the practice problems. ALL of them, because the test are 20 replicas of those problems, sometimes word for word (those have some conceptual questions that will be on the test).

She doesn't let you use Excel, which makes the class much less helpful. The lessons in class are all conceptual and the tests are all quantitative, so you feel unprepared for the tests. Class time is useless and I felt more prepared for the tests when I didn't go and taught myself how to do the problems.

Far harder than all the other F100 teachers and makes the class far more confusing than it needs to be. She is simply not good at teaching and I was lost pretty much the whole year despite attending the majority of classes. People literally average 40-60% on the tests before the curve which says enough in and of itself.

Super knowledgable and passionate professor and does a good job of teaching the material without overbearing us with knowledge. She doesn't tell you your grade until the end which is annoying but she curves all 4 tests by a bit and it's all based on her lectures and isn't too difficult.

Although professor Durguner knew her material very well, her method of teaching sucked. She made her students use financial calculators instead of excel for complex calculations. This hampered the learning process tailored for this class. Test material was not covered in class. Instead, she gave tough non-graded assignments to practice for tests.

Stacey is an amazing professor. This was a new course and she did an amazing job organizing it. She cares about our success and is extremely personable. I am taking A225 with her next semester and am looking forward to having her again. Strongly, strongly recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was difficult due to the material, not the professor. The lab was harder for me than the lecture. Professor Dunham was very clear and had good lectures, she recorded them and posted them afterwards so missing class was not a massive deal. Overall, she taught very well and was a good professor.
Tough class but a very good professor

Crazy unorganized of material. I think that they just shove all the material into each because they are "professionals" in there work so they think that just show us a picture of the material and make a joke about it that it makes us professional at it too. Don't make the mistake go to Purdue. Football doesn't matter in Indiana

This was a very hard class, if I had any other professor that wasn't her, it would've been a guaranteed fail. My advice is to take the two first blocks very seriously. It's only gonna get harder and harder and you don't want to put it off

I loved this class! It's definitely challenging at first, but you learn how to keep up with everything and study for exams. As long as you stay on top of your work, re-read your notes, and STUDY!!! you'll be fine. Quizlet was my best friend :)

This class was not hard at all. Lots and lots of memorization, but the professors and UTAs/UTINs are there to be resources and are very willing to help you. You'll study a lot for this class to memorize things, but the exams are not challenging. Take advantage of the block practice exams and the weekly quizzes for studying purposes. Similar to exam

Dr. Dunham is one of the best professors I have had at IU. I really enjoyed taking anatomy with her, it is tough and memory-heavy. 5 lecture exams and 5 lab exams, the labs are significantly easier. Learn how to study for this class as early as possible!! It took me until 3/4 of the way in to learn how to study properly otherwise an A is possible!!
While the course is very demanding and has a lot of information to cover, Dr. Dunham does a great job teaching the content and helping students.
The 5 exam is a good set up. It makes the content for each exam not too bad. And if you miss a lecture she posts the lecture video too.

While this class has a reputation for being especially challenging, I feel that if you are dedicated to working hard an A is achievable. There is a lot of content and while some of it is hard to grasp at the end of the day it is all memorization. Dr. Dunham is a great professor and passionate about the content. Use the additional study resources!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dunham is incredibly kind and encourages all of her students to pass. Im glad to have had her as a professor. The class itself isn't extremely hard, and if you make sure to study all of your notes often, you'll be okay. I'd argue that the new 5 exam format helps make the exams less content heavy compared to the previous years structures.

Unbelievablely unorganized. New format this 2024 Fall Semester and it was taught so poorly. It was 2 exams every 2 weeks with jampacked lectures that didn't even mention everything. Struggled a lot and the exams are nothing like the practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So lucky to have her as a professor for such a difficult class. She gives a lot of extra credit opportunities that also help you learn/retain the material. She's really good at explaining concepts in class and you can tell she genuinely wants all her students to succeed. Definitely take this class with this professor.
she was a good professor for how difficult this course is

prof dunham is a very nice and caring person. she makes anatomy very easy to understand, its a difficult course in general so be prepared to study a lot and put in the work. prof dunham is very available for questions and help and is very approachable.

Dr. Dunham was amazing! She knows what she is talking about and all of her students respect her. She makes a tough class enjoyable, and easy to comprehend. Lots of extra credit opportunities and exams aren't too hard if you put in the time. Although attendance isn't mandatory, she will do in class activities that count for credit.

This is a very difficult class with a lot of material. But Dr. Dunham is amazing and really wants all of her students to succeed. She was always available outside of class and was very clear and direct with lectures.

Overall a good professor there is just a lot of information (of course). There is only 4 test and lots of extra credit and most of the time you do the extra credit in class and submit it online. They give you a note outline watching online and in class lectures. When studying for the test memorize every single little detail on the notes.
Propst and Dunham were amazing professors, the class is hard just because it has so much material to cover but it is broken up nicely. Expect to study a lot

Dr Dunham & Dr Propst are great teachers. Attend lecture. That's how you get extra credit & it's valuable to hear their explanations of the material. Study regularly. Many aspects of this class are designed to help you, but you do need to put in the work. Use all of your lab time & ask your AI for help when you need it. The AIs are amazing.

Dr. Dunham's (& Dr. Propst) class was my favorite 2nd semester. It is a lot of studying but they give you everything you need to do well. At least 20 extra credit points, take home quizzes and freebie point assignments. 800/1100 points come from lab & lecture exams. Lab is typically easier since it is just identification. Lectures were interesting

good, unorganized but I wish she taught all semester. the material was obviously hard, as expected, but be prepared for exams. really no room for error, if you get one bad grade, expect a whole letter grade drop.
She is very helpful and her lectures keep you very engaged. I wish she was able to teach the whole semester.This class is hard, but as expected, just spend A LOT of time studying.

LOVE this prof! She's super personable and very easy to talk to. Her lectures always kept me engaged. IF YOU TAKE ANATOMY - go in to the open-labs over the weekend/during the week to get extra practice. You'll have to work very hard in this class, so keep that in mind.

Her lecture videos are helpful, if she would ever post them on time. She is extremely unorganized and would often come in midway through lab with materials she had forgotten. She was never available outside of class. I would title her an absentee professor. Expect to be doing your homework and lab preparations after 11 at night.
Her lecture videos are kind of boring, but she is extremely accessible outside of class and really cares for her students! She was a great lab director, especially amid Covid-19.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Dunham was the lab director for my course. She was very organized and kind. She is very helpful if you miss lab with a valid excuse, and genuinely cares about setting students up to succeed. If you put the time in, succeeding in the course is simple. It is very clear what you need to know for the lab exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Stacey is an all around great professor. However, she has an attitude when students are asking questions. She gets so defensive when people challenge her statements. She needs to learn how to separate her emotions from the subject matter at hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: He was an amazing professor, it was one night a week and he did his best to get you all the information and prepared you well for your exams
Good class, Good guy, Good times.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Very fair. Slides are very easy to learn from. She provides all necessary resources to learn the material well. This class is not hard. This is the thought process of most people in the comments: Don't go to class, start studying a day before exam, get bad grade on exam = Blame teacher.

Super nice, tries really hard to engage her students and is passionate about the content. Participation is very important which is very furstrating because the material is so difficult. Amazing professor. Cares a lot about her students and there success. This class will be extremely beneficial if you actually put the time and attention into doing assignments.
