reviews.comment: Bro for one the class runs late, but he gives a 10 min break which I guess helps. His lectures are extremely boring, and sometimes he rambles about random things. Playing the games is fun, and I've made pretty good friends here so that's a plus of taking this class. Overall he's kinda mean and very boring and doesn't breathe life in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was pretty good overall, but I would say he brought down the enjoyment of the class. The lecture was VERY boring to sit through, for some reason he talked absurdly a lot about philosophy, it was basically a philosophy class as much as it was a gaming class. Also lowkey felt like he was advertising his books and stuff to us.

I was excited for this class in the beginning. That stopped once the lectures started to revolve around philosophy and the way he views the world. The worst part was him openly mocking neurodivergency on a platform he required all of us to join. I did not feel respected as a person.

Direct quotes from Castronova in a public server:

“I don't have time to look up every new term or letter that leftists invent to proclaim their self righteousness.“
“Any group that censors pro life views deserves mockery and contempt.”

Openly ableist, hypocritical, and unprofessional. Please watch out if you are a neurodivergent student.
Castronova is an excellent teacher. He wants you to succeed and he'll do what he can to get you there, you just have to try your best. As long as you're showing effort he'll work with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Has a superiority complex like none other. Tries to implement logical fallacies and arguing techniques into an intro level class about games because I am not sure if he knew what else to teach. Requires a pass or fail assignment that is 10% of our grade with a 90% failure rate. Average for the assignment was a 4.3 with 80 students in the course.

Turned in our evaluations super early (five weeks before the end of the year) and then suddenly became extremely unhelpful and difficult while grading all of our assignments from the entire semester. Part of our grade was answering questions on the white board in class and he would go through and not give a lot of people credit which hurt grades.
He definitely puts himself first while teaching. I took this class because I wanted to learn about game design. Good luck anyone who takes this class with him. I dropped ASAP.

He doesn't care about student at all. He plays nice though the whole semester, but he will show his real face right after you turned in the evaluation form. I got a F in his class and I have already appealed my grade and I'm definitely gonna report his behavior to the department.

He is a very tough professor but he will help you if you show up, read, ask questions and are there to learn. He is an economist with actual field experience in emerging markets. He will actually teach you things that will change the way you see the world. Do not take this class if you are a lazy student. You need to work hard and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: zhi you san ci kao shi, mei ci zhan bi 33% shang ke sheng yin xiao, kao shi mei da gang, mei kao qian lian xi ti, kao shi ye hen nan, wo de jian yi shi bie shang kuai pao! ting shuo shi ge hen li hai de xue zhe, ke shi jiao ke jiu shi yi tuo si.

Not recommended No homework for students to study, tough classes, and exams. He only has three exams to count for grades, with each occupied by 33% of the overall grade. The only material you can rely on studying is his class notes, however, if you don't comprehend the textbook before class, you will get into trouble understanding the class notes.
Lectures were hard to understand. No homework at all so it was hard to know how to study for the exams. Professor is knowledgeable but the class is hard to learn. Worst grade I have ever had at IU.

Do not ever take this professor. He doesn't provide slides to his students, he doesn't provide study guides and he does not care about his students. The worse possible teacher there is in the econ program or even in IU. It is apparent that he doesn't care about your learning but just the score you get from the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst Professor I have ever had at IU by far. Very knowledgeable, but a horrible Professor. It is apparent he does not like to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: worst professor at IU. Classes have no structure and you can hardly hear his voice when he lectures. Don't bother going to class. Use that time to read the book.
Interesting lectures if you're into the subject. Gives really good explanations on the topics. Make sure to pay attention and take good notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Incredibly hard grader, one of the hardest I've ever had at IU. Fairly reading heavy, but they are pretty helpful for understanding the material, more so than the average class. Overall E337 was a somewhat stressful experience, but if you try you'll pass.

E322 was one of the most interesting and difficult classes I have ever taken at IU. Buffie expects mastery of the concepts. I would HIGHLY recommend supplementing class with the textbook. He does not like repeating himself but goes through explanations quickly of complex stuff. SLOW HIM DOWN and ask lots of questions- ask him to repeat and expand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This professor is a jerk. I missed an exam because of my grandmother's funeral and he would not let me make it up and gave me a 0. His excuse was that grandparents are not "immediate family." Was forced to drop class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Buffie wants you to master the information. It's that simple. If you're not willing to take the heat, don't put it on him. If he knows you care, he will help you out. Succeeding in this course is one of the most rewarding academic experiences this school offers. Take the challenge.

Buffie can initially come off as really stern, but he's actually a pretty easygoing guy and is definitely one of the smartest/most experienced professors I've ever had. (Ex.: He had to miss a few classes because he was in Ethiopia working with the IMF.) E337 is tough, but definitely passable. Just GO TO THE LECTURES.

Miss class & fail. Miss class & get denied office hours. Can't understand low tone of voice or read illegible scribble on blackboard. Extremely difficult class, had him for E322 as well and did not grade nearly as hard.

Buffie has been really helpful in macroeconomics this semester. He is hard to understand at times in lectures and he moves through material very quickly, but he is always willing to do review on his own time, which I think is awesome. He's hard but not impossible

This was my 2nd semester with Professor Buffie. He is NOT easy. You CAN'T miss class or you will fail..his tests are STRAIGHT from lecture notes. I ended up with my only 2 b's in college in his classes but I've never learned more from a person. If you are dedicated to learning and very interested, I recommend him.

Really brilliant guy. Tests are not hard if you go to class and study the notes. Reading the ereserves and text helps too. He uses an adjusted grading scale and curves that no one in class understands, but it will definitely improve your grade. Like most profs at IU, he will look at the trend in your test scores and give a final grade accordingly.

Unavailable for e-mail; not even on syllabus, incomprehensible in lectures (illegible handwriting, hard to hear [should invest in a microphone]), no fixed grading scale, exam grades are hard to obtain. Oncourse usage-non-existent. This professor should not be teaching a challenging course though he is "qualified" by his publications and education.

I have now had him for e322 and e337 and he is by far one of the brightest professors I have had. He may come across as tough, but is willing to engage students in discussion. Your quality of analysis will definitely benefit from taking him.

Great but very tough Professor. If you go to class you will learn a lot but may not get a great grade because he is a tough grader. Clearly knows what he is talking about, but speaks in strictly econ jargon at times. Again, great class, but tough.
Very engaging professor as he relates everything to current events.  Tough grader on essays, but overall not too bad.  I would highly recommend taking a course from him.

Buffie's Honors Intro to Macroecon is one of the most challenging courses I've taken. He's an agreeable character as long as you don't sleep in his class and take thorough notes. He has almost no patience for slackers, but will help anyone who has paid attention. He loves the NY Times and makes an appreciated effort to provide current examples.
really knows what hes talking about and is genuinely interested in the subject. i won't lie it is hard not to fall asleep during class and the tests are really hard. be prepared.

Great class, great professor. Very open to class discussion and questions. He is very easy going, and he is very willing to answer questions throughout the lecture to help everyone understand the material. Also, he is very clear about what will be on the exams.
I haven't studied harder for a test... wow.  But I haven't learned near as much in any other class.

Lots of reading. I once left my group's table to focus better reading the ruleset of a game before an exam and he made fun of me for 5 minutes telling me I had no friends... 

Extremely right wing QAnon conspiracy theorist type of guy. Avoid if you can. If not, godspeed.

He doesn't wear his mask and weaves through all the desks getting closer than six feet to all the students. Assigns entire BOOKS every WEEK. Feels like he's using course material from another class and vaguely connecting it to games? Made us read Plato - a philosophy text- and the Buddha Sutra - the holy text of Buddhism- for some reason???
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Every lecture he gives makes no sense. His analogies and metaphors do not connect with the material, and he is always off in his own world. This teaching style is very lacking. The class is super easy, barely any work, but he is very much full of himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great class and you must participate to really enjoy it! You learn about game systems and expect to be competitive and work together while learning!
Fun, interesting course. Nice to chat up about games and systems.
Good games and systems here.

I took one of his classes last year and he was awful, but this year he is awesome. Really fun and interesting, with awesome games and good ideas to help students. He threw a pizza party at the end of the year for us. Like a boss.
Class material is great but this professor is terrible.  Avoid.

He asks at the beginning of the semester, "My class is really hard. It's not easy to get an A. Are you sure you want to stay" When he says this, what he is really saying is, "My course content, teaching, and grading methods aren't the best. Do you really want to stay?" Don't waste your time or money on this professor's class.

This man is the embodiment of arrogance and ****baggery.  He at one point in class walked out not to return.  He left after 80% of the class had missed a test question and he wont listen to why the class missed it.  The next class he told us that he has an anger management issue and would've failed people if he remained in the room.

Worst professor I've ever had. Shows no respect for students and is the most egotistical person I've ever met ("Were you ever called a genius on NBC news? I think not"). Has a terrible temper, and has stormed out of class. Terribly organized and has an atrocious grading system. I honestly feel he has no right to be teaching at a university. Avoid!
If you expect to a blow-off class this is not one of them...a lot of work, very subjective grading. Tests are pretty straight-forward
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

One of my favorite professors! Really knowledgeable about the subject and very much willing to discuss things with students. I was bummed I was graduating and couldn't take more classes with him. This class has the amount of writing you would expect from a 300 level history class, so be aware of that. IU needs more awesome Rome specialists!

This guy is brilliant! However, if you're not a history major you probably won't like the work load. He gives clear, concise, and well prepared lectures which really prepare you for the 12-15 page paper. The AI's comments on my paper were not very helpful, but I feel that the grading was extremely fair. Take this class if you want an intriguing and genuinely fun experience whilst being challenged.
His class is very interesting and he manages to keep Ancient Civ light while mentioning everything I hoped to become acquanited with. Stellar course, excellent prof.
Great professor...really smart guy and he lets you use a note card for his essays on tests!
Probably the best professor I have ever had. He knows the material very very well, and he comes to class incredibly well prepared. He is incredibly enthusiastic about ancient history.
Watts is an outstanding lecturer, knows the material and historical context very well, and is well prepared for classes.

Great teacher, knows a lot about the topic. He lectures the whole time, but if you are at all interested in Roman History you shouldn't get too bored. The primary sources are not necessary to read, although they will greatly assist you when it comes time for midterms and finals, and also the papers. I became a History Major after taking his class.

I took 3 courses with him- I found him very interesting to listen to, and I enjoyed participating in his class discussions.  I got by without reading all the primary sources but they are helpful when writing papers.  I was a history major and found his exams and research papers difficult, however I learned a lot and became facinated with Roman Hist

I really love this class.  He tries his hardest to make every day fun and interesting and his quizzes at the beginning of lecture are really easy as long as you went to the last class.  Attendance isn't required, but I would suggest going, since his online notes aren't much besides pictures.  He's a great guy, although he's a tough grader for tests

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!! You pretty much have to go to class on Thursdays for the quizzes. Be prepared to write an 8-10 page paper plus a short paper. He's extremely boring and his A.I.'s are snooty just like him. Be ready to fall asleep in class. Bring a pillow. SAVE YOURSELF!!

Watts is so funny and random.  It's really boring material, but he tries his best to make it interesting.  The two tests you have to take are really hard, but the two long papers are just O.K.  I suggest you keep reading if you have the time so you won't be lost, but it's not mandatory.  The Thursday quizzes are easy if you attend class reguarly.

He has a montone voice.  His class is absolutely the most boring thing ever.  He just reads from a paper and covers more information in one class than any class I have ever taken.  He expects you to be a historian before entering his class.  If you are not a history major stay away from any of his classes

I am a 3.5 GPA non-history major student.  His monotone voice mixed with simply reading from a paper, put me to sleep every class period.  He failed to clarify citation on his first paper and ended up giving me a D- on the paper.  The citation was the only thing wrong.  Expects perfection.  Don't recommend the class for non-history major students.

Best teacher I've ever had teach a large class. He knows his stuff and is really interesting. If you like history, especially roman/classical history take his class.  But in a class with a couple hundred kids obviously it isnt very personal, but thats the nature of the beast i suppose

Knows his stuff, but a little boring and long-winded.  He should moniter his AIs more closely, and/or change his grading standards, because the expectations for an introductory class were unreasonable, especially for papers.Also, forcing an entire huge class to write the same exact paper sucks. Some variety would have helped, esp. for us non-majors
By far, the best history professor on this campus.

Vague feedback on papers, poor discussion leader.  Very passive aggressive in imposing his political views on his students.  Very subjective in his grading and he clearly had favorites.  Make sure you do well on the first paper because if you do poorly, poor grades are likely to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Gubar was a really nice guy, he just didn't ask the best discussion questions. He would follow up his own questions with answers that he came up with, and then expect us to respond to his answers. His grading scale was also unclear. You won't know how well you are doing until the end of the semester.
There was lots of reading, but the actual class was really easy to pass. The main thing is to make sure you participate. If you participate, you'll probably get an A.

Gubar is a very good discussion leader, he is very random in his grading. I took a class with him, didnt read any of the material, got B's and C's on the papers but I got an A- in the class and have no idea how. Participation is huge, he likes to be able to close his eyes and recognize your voice.

Lots of reading (about a book a week), but a general knowledge of the subject matter is all you need for discussion. Grade consists of 2 15 page papers on any topic, 2-3 random short writings, an in-class final essay, and participation. Prof wants you to succeed plus pizza at semester's end. Best Honors course, you have to try not to do well.

Gubar's intensive writing class involved a lot of reading but a manageable amount of actual writing. He chose good texts that spanned a variety of topics and interests. This prof will get to know each of his students, so you benefit from showing up to class and speaking up.

I had prof gubar for ideas & experiences II. I found the class to be enjoyable overall. there were times where i felt a little overwhelmed by the reading, but thankfully the majority of it is quite interesting. also, once you get the hang of what he expects, its pretty easy to keep up. the grading consisted of 5 or 6 papers

Took this a couple semesters ago.  You need not read the books.  I didn't and ended up with an A.  His grading is random.  He is a good discussion mediator.  His accent is as Bostonian as it gets.  Take H212 if you liked high school English discussions.  Don't take it if you value more constructive education like, say, anything else.
Ed Gubar is a truly excellent professor. He takes the time to work with students on their skills and their plans for the future. He has had an enormous impact on me, and I am very grateful to him.

Gubar is a good guy who genuinely cares about both the students and the subject matter.  (Our course was about politics and the media.)  His class involved a lot of hard work, but my writing has definitely improved as a result -- and, yep, my awareness of the media's effect on society has increased.
Professor Gubar has valuable criticisms for written work and his combination of film and fiction made for a semester well-spent.
Gubar is the man, even if the J-school acts like he doesn't exist sometimes. He is helpful and offers a unique perspective on journalism. The film class is awesome.
No Comments

Ed is accomplished in his field. However, his lectures were surprisingly unorganized. He consistently bounces around on dates and times, and his exams were graded subjectively/ tough given his prior descriptions. He is knowledgeable, but his reliance on videos put me to sleep every other class. I know a lot of people still enjoyed his class.

Every class is a lecture, which is fine except he just reads from books which is extremely boring. The occasional video is shown. He only takes 4 grades the entire semester, so if you do bad on a few you'll be in trouble. Very tough grader, though the AI's do most of the grading. LOT'S of reading, way too much in my opinion. I don't recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Linenthal is one of those professors who clearly has a deep love for his work. He was extremely understanding and forgiving. The only thing I didn't like was that the class met three times a week, with mandatory attendance, and the lectures were about literally nothing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ed is one of my favorite teachers I've ever had at IU. He hates technology and simply lectures from memory and readings. He will show videos and movies that pertain to the topic. You have to read a lot, but the content is interesting and you will do fine in the class as long as you pay attention to lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Ed is an amazing prof and great person. Highly suggest going to his office hours, you'll get to know him and get great tips on whatever paper you're writing. He's very genuine and doesn't brag at all about how he's a complete legend both in the department and in the field. Doesn't use much tech but his lectures are so great they don't need it

Dr. Linenthal is an absolutely awesome teacher. He is extremely knowledgeable about history, extremely passionate, and extremely talented at making history exciting for everyone. He is extraordinarily kind and down-to-earth and he has a great sense of humor. If you take a class with him, he will make you want to be a historian. He is phenomenal.

Prof. Linenthal is incredible. He's extremely knowledgeable and hilarious. He doesn't use PowerPoint, instead he just lectures for an hour and 15 minutes, but he's so interesting that I never got bored. Grade is based on exams and a paper but he gives you the exam questions beforehand. You also get EC for perfect attendance

Very in depth lectures, but not necessary to attend. He gave a grade boost if you didn't miss any class. Lectures were kind of a drag, but Linenthal was very knowledgable about this subject and very funny. We had no exams but several different 3 page papers written over books we read for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Linenthal is incredible. Just look him up and you can see the long list of accomplishments he has had, it will blow you away. I have had him for two classes and will gladly take another! He is kind and will take the time to get to know you. Be prepared to read and write quite a bit, but it's all very worth it, I promise.
Terrible teacher. Didn't feel like I learned anything from him. Used books to teach for him and expected you to know everything that he wanted you to know for the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: As a science student, history courses are expected to be boring and drag on the entire semester. But not this course. The topics and materials that are covered are SO interesting . He gives to 10% extra credit for perfect attendance, which is always great. He was actually apart of this history and knows many important people. He loves the subject!!
He gives anyone who has perfect attendance 10% extra credit on their final grade so it is very worth while to go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ed is by far my favorite professor at IU. He is incredibly accomplished and is the Michael Jordan of his field. He is makes history so interesting and challenges you to think differently about the way you think about the past. He also likes to get to know his students and if you are on his good side your grade might go up. Take his class if you can

Edward Linenthal, aka "Eazy E," is hands down the greatest professor at IU. Mr. Linenthal knows how to keep students engaged and always makes the classroom a fun learning environment. He's absolutely hilarious and has a heart of pure gold! When he retires, Indiana University will truly miss this remarkable man.
Amazing.

Amazing professor! You can learn so much from ETL. He's down to earth, funny, and incredibly knowledgeable. Worked with the Smithsonian Museum as a consultant on some of their World War II displays. Go to his office hours and have a chat with him, he's very welcoming and helpful. Took two classes with him, would love to take him every semester!

Professor Linenthal is one of the best professors I have had at IU.  I have taken two of his classes, WWII and the Peoples and Holocaust in American Life.  He is very knowledge and passionate about what he teaches. While grades are determined by the TA, his assignments are interesting.

Awesome class, even better professor. Loved his lectures and even when I was very sick with mono I made sure I made it to his class. Assigned readings may seem like a lot, but they are great. One tip-don't be on your phone or laptop during class, he hates it!

Professor Linenthal's lectures are very engaging and eye-opening. Normally, this isn't the course he teaches, but you will get a lot out of this class. There are two exams and one final based on answering a single question pertaining to the course. Depending on who you have as TAs, your grade will be determined by them.
Best professor I've ever had...he's the dood
ETL is a fantastic professor who keeps lectures interesting, even his sometimes confusing tangents are worthwhile.

Professor Linenthal is very genuine, and just an interesting person in general. He has worked on the Enola Gay exhibit and has written a few books... I've told my friends I want to be like him when I grow up. He doesn't use powerpoints but LOVES videos to articulate his points. Be forewarned though, you'll be writing 30 pg. journals 3 times a sem.

Professor Linenthal is just a genuinely interesting man... I tell my friends I want to be like him when I grow up. He is really bad with using powerpoints, but his videos are moving and his personal experience make the course richer. Definitely take it if you have interest and like to write... 30 page journals due 3 times a semester.

He is definitely my favorite professor at IU - very interested in the subject, fantastic use of media in addition to great class readings.  I looked forward to attending his class every week, and he keeps you thinking long after the class is over. He's also very friendly and helpful in office hours, overall, just a great professor.

Lectures are often pointless and boring. He gives helpful review sheets before every exam. Be wary of the TAs. They have all the deciding factors into your grades. Participation grades in discussion are not structured.

Prof. Linenthal was my favorite professor at IU. He taught a small seminar class on contemporary religious history in America, and he assigned terrific readings. He was really engaging, and fostered a very open atmosphere for discussion.

One of the best professors I have ever had. English is one of my worst subjects and I did well in his class. It's not an easy A, you have to work, but the grading is fair. Very willing to help you out if you are having trouble. Great guy all together.

This class is a really great, fun class, especially if you have to take a CAPP class. HOWEVER do not(!) take this class if you are only interested in zombies because of The Walking Dead. You will be very bored. You need the books, but normally only a tiny section per book is used. Try to borrow or rent. Prof Comentale is amazing, smart, & funny.

One of the best teachers that I have ever had. Incredibly funny and definitely knows what he is talking about. The class is not easy, but if you read and take notes and pay honest attention, you should be fine

He is a wonderful professor, very nice and helpful. I enjoyed going to class just to hear him speak. But it was not an easy A. We over analyzed EVERYTHING.I believe it was graded harder than an entry level class should be. The test material was unclear and we only had 50 minutes to write 2 essays and answer multiple choice. LOTS OF READING as well.
This guy is incredible. Hands down best prof in the English department

He is ridiculously cute; everything about him. He is super nice and down-to-earth. His lectures are very interesting and he makes his students really want to learn. I definitely recommend taking at least one of his courses.

Prof. Comentale is one of the better professors I've had at IU.  He is extremely helpful and gave me really good feedback on my writing and even took time to meet me outside of class to talk about graduate school.  Super nice, modest, down-to-earth guy.

First off, this guy is a closet genius. His office is practically overflowing with all the books he's read not only on lit, but on psychology and far-out stuff like critical race theory. He REALLY knows his stuff and does a great job of relating all these things to the novel or topic at hand (music, genres, whatever) - and he's clear, at that.
I love analyzing literature but we blatantly over-analyzed much of the assigned readings in this class. This professor is a cool guy but was an ineffective teacher.

If you have the opportunity to take a class with this professor do so. The class was not an easy "A", but if you attend lecture and read the material then you can at least get a "B". This professor is very helpful, really loves what he teaches, and makes the class interesting. Only negative: required movie nights not mentioned prior to enollment.
Professor is fun - great lectures - a required course, but worth it
Awesome zombies class - smart and fun - taught me a lot of different topics - history, anthropology, novels, film, science, medicine - cool!

Ed is one of the best instructors I've ever had the pleasure of being taught by and I would recommend him over and over again to both literature majors and those simply looking to take a literature class. He's an awesome professor and an extremely interesting intellectual.

Interesting class, but this professor is self-absorbed.  Also, while I did well in his class,  I felt that his comments on my work were dependent on his mood and how busy he was.  I agree with the student who said that he is less open-minded than he would have you believe.  Take a diff. class - the English Dept. has better professors.
Ed is an awesome teacher
Literary Modernism - Dr. Comentale was my favorite professor of all time.  Unbelievably brilliant, engaging, and into his subject.  Stellar.  Flawless.  (To say nothing of his GQ hotness!)

My favorite teacher in my 3 years at IU.  Really interesting and a great guy if you are actually interested in discussing what he's teaching.  A little self indulgent but overall a brillant teacher.  Definitely take his Brit. Lit. Subculture class.
He is the man.  Everyone should take his class.
He talks A LOT, but overall L346 was a good class.  If you work hard (and make sure he knows it...go to his office hours) the class is not bad.  He's easy on the eyes, too. :)

One of the most pretentious, nonsensical courses I've ever taken was his literary modernism class. Seems like a decent guy, but as a professor he is way to into the sound of his own voice. If you appreciate rationality, steer away from this one.
It's great to see a male professor who's so egalitarian and truly a feminist-more of a feminist than most women I've see at IU. He's one of the most progressive professors I've ever had.

Prof. Comentale is the best professor I've had at IU. He is brilliant, always interesting and challenging, and constantly tries to challenge ossified thinking. Anyone who thinks English is a BS field should take a class with Prof. Comentale.
Helpful and challenging.  Listened to all students comments with an open-mind.  Funny, does not accept crappy work but in a good way.  Great class.
No Comments

Prof is uncomfortable with being on an equal intellectual footing with women.  Tends to pay more attention to men's comments and engages with them to a greater extent.  Self-centered, both personally and research-wise.
Very New Age.
Grades hard on papers but totally helpful with students.  Teaches really difficult material but makes it interesting.
Very smart, really good in class.  Funny.  Can be serious about papers; generally not willing to accept crap work.

Prof. Eckes is very knowledgable and engaging. She used to teach high school, so she's not boring! This class is highly applicable to anyone who wants to be a teacher; lots of real world connections. There is a paper and a project, but grading is fair/not too harsh. Exams are easy. This class makes case law fun and manageable! Would recommend!

Suzanne is an amazing teacher who's extremely knowledgable on case-law. Her lectures are incredibly engaging, and so are Francesca's! Complete all of the readings. You will be quizzed at the beginning of every class, and it all comes back again on the final. This class is extremely applicable to the real world & I would take it again, if I could!

Prof Eckes is amazing. She really cares about her students and goes above and beyond to make sure the material makes sense. This class was great. She is smart and nice. There is a decent amount of work for the class but she is very clear on how she wants it done. I would love to take another class taught by her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Suzanne is great! She's very knowledgable about the course material and has had lots of experience in the field. She makes sure that you know your rights and how to find them when you start teaching. Very interesting course!
Great professor! Made class very interesting.
She is brilliant, and class is never boring.  There is are attendance points, but assignments and exams are easy if you do the reading.
Very great teacher and approachable!
No Comments
No Comments

I really loved listening to all his lectures. Not only was the material interesting, but he made it really fun to learn and easy to understand. Yes the exams are rather difficult and attendance isn't mandatory, but it helps a lot. He also has a review session a few days before any exam where he will go over every single thing the study guide has.

A great person with a big heart and sense of humor! Lectures were entertaining, but when it came to the material we were tested over…I don't think it was taught. The exams are hard, and it is near impossible to get full credit on the final (all written) unless you are a mindreader! Love the man, but he grades tough!

He makes his lectures extremely interesting, you can tell this is something he is very passionate about! I really enjoyed his class and was even sad to see it end. The exams are definitely not easy and you have to study a decent amount (its a lot to memorize), but all the information has been taught and is not unreasonable to include. I recommend!!
Dr. Hirt's class is fun, I enjoyed social psych a lot. Attendance is not mandatory but it helps a lot. There are weekly quizzes. The exams are a bit tough because of the free response questions.
The sweetest man alive. So animated during lectures. I would totally take him.

He's a good guy. Test questions are tricky and not straight forward. Going to class, doing the quizzes, and reviews are not enough to get a good grade. You basically have to know everything from the book and slides. It's not an easy A, or even an easy B. I wouldn't recommend this class.

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic and easy to listen to. He offers test review sessions and is very willing to help his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Easy assignments and easy exams. Very enthusiastic during lectures and always available if you need help. This class is an easy A

Had this professor for consumer psychology, we only had two exams plus a final that included 17+ pages worth of definitions on just one exam! don't take this class like seriously dont do it ....... im serious!!.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: A very good psy professor with traditional powerpoint lectures. Nothing too fancy, but very good quality and presentation. There were 4 tests, combination of multiple choice and short answer. The tests were challenging but fair. Overall a very good class with no unpleasant suprises
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable on the things he teaches. He has fill in the blank notes and a few assignments. His review sessions are very helpful.

Great professor, clearly loves what he does and is so engaging that you can't help but pay attention. If you do all the reading, which is a lot, and go to most of the classes, you can get a near perfect score in this class.

He obviously loves the topic he's teaching! He posts the slides, but they're posted as a fill-in-the-blank, so attendance really is needed. The tests are pretty straight forward if you've gone to class and paid attention. Basically, if you want to actually learn the material- he's absolutely fantastic!!

Ed Hirt is a good professor. He goes through the powerpoint at a perfect pace and always gives enough time for everyone to write everything down. He's extremely passionate about social psychology and he's VERY knowledgable on the subject. The 1st test can be rough,but once you get used to his teaching style it's a breeze. Recommend taking his class
He is so passionate about his work and is my favorite professor compared to any professor i've ever had. Go to class and take notes & you'll get an A
Dr. Hirt is extremely passionate about social psychology and in helping his students.
Go to lecture. Everything on the test is covered in class. The textbook is next to useless. Great teacher, tests are straightforward, but ensure you understand the important information.

Nothing bad can be said about Professor Hirt.  His lectures are clear, extremely organized, and interesting.  He is an understanding and caring person who wants his students to do well.  He's also very enthusiastic while teaching.  Extremely helpful review sessions are given before each test. Easy to do well if you go to class. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!

Professor Hirt is a great instructor. He keeps the lecture interesting, provides a study session for each test, and is happy to answer questions any time in person or through email. Highly recommended!

Professor Hirt is really thrilled to teach and it shows. He really keeps students engaged and is a funny guy. He's also very helpful towards students wanting to participate in research. Tests weren't super difficult and I loved the class.

Ed Hirt is very passionate about teaching this class! You can tell that he really loves what he does. If you go to class on a regular basis and read your text book, there is no reason why you shouldn't do well in the course.
Very good teacher.  He is incredibly enthusiastic and is a really good teacher.  If you study you will do absolutely fine in this class.
Has great notes for lectures and essential review sessions for exams.

Professor Hirt is definitely one of my favorites ever at IU. He is extremely enthusiastic about the topic of social psychology (the field that he conducts research in). Tests are moderate- not easy but not too hard- i highly recommend him for any psych class. he is also extremely helpful if you go to his office hours!
No Comments

Professor Hirt instructs Social Psychology, and he makes the subject very informative and interesting throughout the semester.  He's very helpful if you have any questions, he's more than willing to take time outside of class to help.  He always holds review sessions prior to his exams.  All around, just a great guy.  I totally recommend him.

Metaphysics is a hard course. However, he gives hand outs which is great study material. It is not hard to get good scores on test as long as you study hard before the tests. The lectures are a bit hard to follow sometimes as it requires more time to think the idea through before he finishes talking the session. Overall, he is a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor, loved the class, would recommend

Bridger's lectures seemed to me quite phenomenal, particularly relevant in an introductory philosophy course. Beyond that I found the man himself to be informative and straightforward, while entertaining in a dry, philosophy professor kind of way. Easy course, but only if you are ready for the type of thinking philosophy requires.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cool professor, passionate about what he does and teaching it. Very engaging and wants students to learn despite half the lecture hall being full. Participation isn't exactly necessary, but it is a nice grade booster to have. Super nice and approachable too. Exams are cake, you make a study guide, so it forces you to look through everything. 10/10

Newman is really nice, and his lectures make sense if you pay attention. You can also follow along pretty intuitively if you miss a few lectures and have to use just the slides to make up the content.
YUMMY. Great LinkedIn. Love the modern mullet! It inspired me to attend class every day, whether it was scheduled or not.
He is amazing. If you can take his classes, TAKE IT!!!

He is a very fair, engaging professor. He makes his lectures accessible and all attendance points to be made up in full. His exams are very representative of what he presents in class and are worded very clearly. I enjoyed my time in his class.

Dr. Newman is a very engaging and funny lecturer. I was rarely bored in class because he uses fun demos to help supplement the lecture, and values student feedback. I will say that make sure you do attend class, even if it isn't mandatory, because at the end of the year he adds participation points that can really make or break your grade.

Loved this class with Dr. Newman! Genuinely great guy who cares about students and wants to make sure everyone understands the material. He emphasizes student development and participation, and kept lectures engaging with light humor and videos to emphasize concepts. Also very easy to reach outside of class for any extra help. Great class!
Made class really entertaining

Dr. Newman is wonderful and very smart. The material is pretty difficult and hard to grasp initially, so I recommend taking notes before class and treating lecture like review. The exams are hard but he uses scratchers so it's basically a partial credit multiple choice exam which is very nice. He likes to keep lecture fun so I recommend going.

One of my favorite professors at IU, he knows what his is talking about and wants you to do well. The course takes studying and self motivation to do well, and I would recommend attending lectures, but there are ways to make points back if missed. There are many resources like lecture videos, practice quizzes, review days, and more.
Believe me when I say this professor is simultaneously super intelligent and understanding. LITERALLY A BLESSING FROM GOD FOR EVERY STUDENT!!!

Amazing professor. Very clear about what he wants you to know for exams. The material he shows in lectures is exactly what will be on the exam and there's practice tests. The review sessions are extremely helpful. His lectures are very engaging and visually stimulating so it was a lot easier to stay focused in this class than any other I've taken.

Newman was pretty good. I thought the class as a whole was pretty hard, but he tries his best to prepare you for exams. He likes to make us "think" on exams instead of giving clear cut questions, which was annoying sometimes. However, he does offer some good study tools including making your own exam right before the real one. Overall, I recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: such a amazing lecturer, so knowledgeable and passionate about the topic!!!

Dr. Newman is fantastic. You can tell he cares about his students, as he tries to miss class only when 100% necessary. He is accessible outside of class and very understanding, allowing you to make up for lost attendance by doing an optional quick attendance quiz online proving you know the material.

I loved listening to Dr. Newman's lectures. The subject is so interesting, and he does a great job breaking down some very complicated concepts into simpler terms. There is a book for this class, but as long as you go to his lectures, you shouldn't need it.

Prof Newman was a really good professor. He was accessible and understanding and made his expectations pretty clear. He did go on tangents during lectures which put us behind schedule constantly but he was always willing to listen and answer questions in class. Would def recommend taking neuro with him!
He gives really interesting lectures and is very funny. He really gives you all the tools to do well and wants to see you succeed. Overall just a great professor

Professor Newman made this class as straightforward and clear as possible. He always told you exactly what he wanted you to know and was open to questions. Weekly assignments/quizzes are not difficult if you watch and understand the lectures. Not an overly time consuming class considering the level of material. Good content, pace, and workload.

His lectures were clear on what he wanted to know. He was also very knowledgable and open to questions during lectures. If you're looking for a professor with clear expectations and interactive lectures, I would definitely take his class.

Loved Newman. Honestly, show up to lecture and follow along with the slides give nand you will pass easily. Grades are based on lecture quizzes, these quizzes are then combined to make min tests and standard 4 exams ( that also include some of the previous questions). EASY
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: His notes are NOT self-explanatory, so either read the book or attend lectures and listen to him explain. Welcomes feedback, but he also gets defensive and doesn't budge (e.g., saying something like "Yes, this exam question was unfair, but I'm still not giving you guys the points back"). And he doesn't round. Overall, though, he's a great prof.

Ehren Newman is overall an amazing professor. First, he is super hot and that makes lectures very enjoyable. His lectures are very well designed but you need to attend class if you want to do well. He really listens to student feedback about exams and is definitely trying to help all he can to get his students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ehren is a really cool professor. He explains everything in a lot detail to make sure his students understand the material. The exams are kind of difficult so make sure you study a lot for them and they are also worth 80% of your grade. Make sure you go to class everyday for tophat questions because they count towards 20% of your grade.

This class is a very interesting class, but sometimes what we needed to know for the exams was unclear. The total points in this class include 4 exam prep homework (worth around 18-25 points each), clicker questions (graded by participation and correctness), and the 4 exams. Make sure you go to class because his tests are based solely on lecture!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is a very difficult class, but nothing you can't handle. Ehren Newman provides great lectures that pretty much cover everything you would need to know for the tests. These tests are pretty intense, but if you study the PowerPoints and spend time with Ehren Newman after class to learn the stuff you don't completely understand an A is possible!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Newman said on the first day of class that he wanted to serve as a mentor for all of us students, and since then he has done exactly that. This is a lab course unlike traditional lab courses. This course allows for creativity of ideas, and Dr. Newman does all that he can to teach us about the design and implementation of real world research.
So hot. Loved him.

The class is made up of only four tests including the final,  but he reviews playing Jeopardy the class before the test. 1st & last tests were the easiest!  Uses scratchers instead of scantrons for partial credit on tests.  10/10 would recommend! He uses clickers for questions to review material.  Jeopardy and clicker questions helpful. Great prof.
so passive aggressive and not respectful to students. dont really understand her problem
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I would say the best teacher for L201. If you have her make sure you do well on the first Exams and you are pretty much set with an A in the class.

Professor Eikenberry's L201 class is difficult, but the way she grades is helpful. You can drop exams or projects that you don't do well on. The tests are pretty challenging with essay questions. During lectures she gives out extra credit for participation, so definitely take advantage of it. Overall, this class is tough, but you'll learn a lot.

Do the readings before class and take good notes during the lectures. Extra credit is very generous for each test as long as you participate in class. Both group projects are pretty easy and I thought the mediation project was very fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: The beginning of the semester was loaded with required readings and pop quizzes, she also will cold call in most classes, and participation is very much expected. She lets you weigh your grades which can really help improve your chances of getting an A. I would also say the amount of work required for her sections is more than that of others.

ONLY TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU WANT TO GO INTO LAW. If you are just taking it because its an Icore pre rec and you dont care take another professor. She is funny and nice, but NO other sections have open answers on tests, their MCQ is much easier, they don't have projects. Questions on the exams are harder and all the exams are cumulative

Professor Eikenberry assigns 1-2 hours of work prior to lectures. The class has multiple projects, assignments, and an exam. Participation is important in her class; she often cold calls. She allows you to weight your grade for specific assignments to help your grade. She is very caring; show effort, and she will help you! I would recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Eikenberry is a really sweet lady, but she makes the class way too difficult! There is at least 20 pages of textbook reading twice a week, and on top of that, there are quizzes and ABA's (Application Based Activities). Only take this class if you are VERY interested in law!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Specifically for L375 only: Shawna is a very outspoken liberal and forces her opinions on her students. L375 had very little to do with ethics or law but rather focused on racism, sexism and every other ism. If you are not a liberal you will struggle in this class. Id recommend taking any other teacher as it will be much easier.

Professior Eikenberry was nice, she gave out extra credit every single day for participation. Her exams are a little bit hard but nothing that studying won't help. She let us pick our own class percentages in terms of the rubric and how much everything weighed. Super helpful and just wants everyone to succeed.

Prof Eikenberry's business ethics class is worth taking, especially when comparing to the work some of the other ethics professors give out. There are quite a bit of readings, pop quizzes, and attendance is taken every class. With that being said, most days you will just discuss the readings the whole time and the assignments/ tests werent too hard
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Shawna is a nice person, but personally I didn't vibe with her teaching style. The material is confusing and she doesn't necessarily explain it well. There is a lot of homework and a group assignment every class. This class was difficult and was not made easier by the professor, unfortunately.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Shawna Eikenberry was a great professor to take for L201. She has a good sense of humor and is very interactive with the students. You can get extra credit points for speaking in class. I would definitely recommend taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is a great professor, one of my favorites I've had at university. Lectures are interesting (as can be for a law class) and she does a great job of engaging with the class and making incentives to participate. She's also very understanding and empathetic. Put in the work she assigns (There's admittedly a lot), and you'll get an A.

LOVE HER! I have class w her right now, its NOT easy but she makes it fun. Shes actually really cool, a chill down to earth professor. Everything she says in class is on the test, you dont really need to read (theyre just to understand the concept better) class is still really tough, better take it with her than anyone else! Best prof ive had at IU
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is overall just pretty hard but Prof. Eikenberry does a good job of trying to highlight the key things you need. You have to read so much for this class but she offers extra credit and all you have to do is speak in class. She also gives cheat sheets for tests that make them not as scary. The group project is awful so get a good group.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class is very reading heavy and expect difficult tests. But other than that Prof Eikenberry was very helpful in lecture and during office hours. She gives daily quizzes that you are to complete before class and offers some extra credit for class participation. Overall good professor but just a difficult class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Shawna's smart and is a great professor. I learned a lot from her, as she makes sure her class is engaging and interesting. She has a dry sense of humor that takes a while to pick up on, but once you do makes for a funny class. Her tests are challenging, but I always felt like she prepared us well for them. You can get EC for class participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This women is not only the worst professor I have ever had, but one of the worst people I have ever come across in my life. reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. Eikenberry did a great job of bringing in current events into our discussion of ethics. It was a very fun class and I would definitely take it with her again!

Honestly, great prof. I wasn't too sure about Y324, but she made it both enjoyable to sit through--despite being lecture heavy, and known that she is knowledgeable in this topic! Though exams were ROUGH (tbh just study, you can't wing it) I would take this class again in a heartbeat; however, she does go a little quickly through slides so be aware.

Professor Braman is a great professor and she, along with Y304, is a must have for those wanting to go to law school. Attendance isn't mandatory but I believe it's pretty important if you want to do well in the class. Y304 can be tough but she is extremely knowledgeable about the content and how to teach it.

I have taken two courses with Professor Barman and she is absolutely wonderful. Y304 in particular is a must take for any students wanting to go to law school, as it gives a snippet of what the experience will be like. 3 exams and a short paper. Tests usually have a slight curve, and are always fair. She only tests on things taught heavily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Braman and her courses are must takes for pre-law students!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a great professor. She makes her lectures interesting and engaging. The readings she assigns have to be read to do well on the tests and that is key since tests are almost the entire grade. However, the readings are not too long and test questions are not too difficult. Also, if thinking about law school, definitely take a class of hers.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great topics covered, yet grade based on 3 papers (1 extra at the end instead of the final to replace another) and participation and attendance starts an an 85% and can go up or down from there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Eileen Braman is extremely knowledgeable on the course topics presented, and she cares a lot about Constitutional Law. However - she is not very open to opinions contradicting her own, and she is quite unorganized when presenting lectures. Additionally, the class consists of only two grading aspects: 3 papers, and attendance/participation points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I thoroughly enjoyed Professor Braman's class and lectures. Y304 is based on 3 papers and there are a few pages of reading per week. Papers were graded tough and I was never sure what the criteria was. I still managed a B+. 
Prof. Braman is passionate and dedicated to offering students the best education possible.

Professor Braman literally wrote the book on legal decision-making, and she uses her legal expertise to give interesting lectures. If you take notes and read the book, you will do very well. Her exams are involved and require a strong understanding of the material, but you will end the semester with a wealth of knowledge about the Supreme Court.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As long as you do the work, you should be fine. She has slides for all her lectures. You must show up to class bc during her lecture, she adds insightful information that are not on the slides. Exams are fair since she prepares you well for them (study guides). Papers are graded fairly. I've taken 3 courses and I do think she is a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Braman is a fantastic lecturer and very knowledgeable about course material. She works really hard to prepare informative, engaging lectures. This was her first semester giving papers instead of exams, which I liked. Her TA was a bad grader who didn't give feedback but essay topics were interesting and built off of course topics well.

Great teacher, I am glad I took the class. If you wanna be a lawyer, take this class. It is very important and the material is useful. Probably my favorite course i have taken at IU. The teacher is passionate and definitely a smart lady. She also cares about her students and is more than willing to make accommodations if u reach out to her. 11/10!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Braman is one of the nicest professors I've had, but most of the time I couldn't force myself to go to the lectures. The class is regarding material that I'm fairly interested in, but I dreaded going to this class because it was so boring. We wrote papers instead of taking exams, and the grading did not match the feedback given.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I dont know how shes not more highly rated. She takes what could be such boring topics and makes them thoroughly enjoyable. You can tell she loves what she does as well. She may be a tough grader but if youre actually there and thinking critically for you papers, theres no one to blame but you if you get below an 85. One of my favorite profs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Braman gave very interesting lectures, and helped to present a very clear picture of the course material. She is very enthusiastic about the subject, and is also a very helpful resource for learning about law school and practicing law.

Professor Braman is clearly very knowledgeable in her field. She has clearly studied the topics extensively, but she is simply not a good teacher. Her powerpoint slides lack key information and she will not do a good job of explaining what she is talking about. There will be stuff on the exams that she barely mentioned, let alone explained.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's extremely knowledgeable based on lectures, but I can't help but get the feeling that she's going into each lecture as if she's never reviewed or covered the material before. This is because she, uh... cannot go five seconds without, um... filling empty space with, um... uh... plenty of filler words. If this annoys you, stay far away.

She is one of the best professors at IU. Her classes are so interesting and fun to be in. Participation is necessary but as long as you read the summaries before class she won't get mad. Attendance is also very importance since the grade is based on 3 tests and one essay. If you go to the classes you should be good but if you skip, good luck...
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Do not take a class with this professor. She wants students to participate a lot, but when they do and attempt to ask questions she gets flustered and upset. She grades extremely difficult, even when you answer an exam question correctly she will take off a ton of points for missing very specific words-even if not necessary to correctly answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Bramen is a decent lecturer and very helpful. Make sure you go to class - she says things in  class that end up being multiple choice questions on tests. Not too much work, just study hard for test and write verbatim what you learned in class. Don't put fluff. She is particularly helpful if you want to go to law school.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Braman does not excel at lecturing. Her class is very heavy on participation and discussion which is nice but she doesn't have much respect for opinions that are different than her own. She mispronounces and messes up court cases making it hard to follow the lecture and confusing when it comes to getting a good test grade which is the whole grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I really like Prof. Braman! The tests are difficult, but I just make sure to know everything on the study guide she gives out and I've gotten A's. She's a good resource if you're thinking about law school.

Professor Braman was a great teacher. She is very intense and intelligent. If you attend class and do the readings, you should be able to earn a good mark on the exams. The multiple choice questions are particularly easy. When it comes to the essay questions, make sure you write exactly what she wants and don't forget anything.

Professor Braman is difficult to understand when it comes to what she wants on her essay tests-or she expects to much. In a pure lecture course asks for too much reading in my opinion. Her TI for this semester was too tough of a grader as well. I would not recommend anyone to take her courses. She is very disrespectful to her students in lecture.
Super tough class!

Prof. Braman seems fairly knowledgeable, but is highly biased toward her own particular opinions and will blatantly cut off and shout over students when they're participating in class if she considers their opinions invalid. She also frequently stumbles over her words and mispronounces constantly, which is quite distracting.
Eileen is amazing!  She teaches well.  She stammers sometimes but what you learn in her class will benefit you a great deal if you are considering law school.
She is VERY difficult to understand and goes through mood swings.
She's awesome. She will call you out if you're all wet. But overall a great professor!

Bramante is really interesting and really knows her stuff. However, her essay tests are hard, and she's really specific about exact wording. Sometimes it's hard to understand her test questions. Also, she is a nice person buy she will be extremely mean to those who ask 'stupid' questions.

Great professor! Really passionate about the topic. I've taken two of her classes, and she does a really good job of explaining the material.  Tests are exactly what you would expect, and it's difficult but well worth the effort!

Take very good notes because a good amount of test questions come from something she'll say in class but not have on the slides.  Studying for the tests can be frustrating but that's law for you.  Just read all the chapters thoroughly.  She knows her stuff but does have trouble expressing herself which makes note taking even tougher.  Tough grader.

I have not seen anything that would suggest her intelligence is above average.  She does stammer a lot and does appear to go through mood-swings.  See tends berate some students for asking relevant questions, and then play with her pet students who are just wasting time.  Not a bad teacher, but does appear to show biases against students.

An incredibly smart woman, but I never know what she wants from us. Grading system is ridiculous, and I don't think even she knows what's going on with grades. She does try to be clear but is stuck in political scientist mode and doesn't really comprehend when students are having trouble understanding concepts she teaches.

Definitely a smart professor. Tries really hard to be clear, but sometimes she talks so fast it's hard to get everything down in your notes. DEFINITELY read all assigned chapters. Tests are mainly based on class lecture notes, so it's extremely important to go to class!

The professor does know her stuff, but she does have a hard time expressing herself.  However, she always happy to help you if you don't understand something.  The tests can be very difficult and tedius, TAKE NOTES ON YOUR READINGS!  Overall, this was a good teacher and a good class.  But don't get on her bad side!

I liked this class a lot. The subject matter (Constitutional Law) was quite challenging but Prof. Braman did a few little things that made it easier. Always a great help during office hours. I love this woman... sigh.
She really knows her stuff and is really amazing about helping you with anything during office hours - just ask!
While the class was fairly easy, Prof. Braman has huge difficulties expressing herself. It was quite distracting but she definitely knows her stuff.

Is so excited to teach that the trips all over herself trying to talk about it. She's very passionate and apart from occasionally talking herself out of breath, is an awesome professor! Gives very fair exams and if you study, you'll do well. Is understanding. Runs her classroom like a law school class; if you're thinking law school, take Braman!

I very much enjoyed her class. It was really difficult, but I learned so much. She loves people who participate and get involved, and her lectures are always enthusiastic. She has a real passion for what she does and sharing her knowledge. You should take her class(es) if you're considering law school.
Sometimes has trouble explaining things but very interesting and enjoyed her class.
Great Professor, sometimes has difficult time making herself clear but is extremely knowledgeable.  Expects a lot from students but if you come to class and put in obvious effort, you will get an A
The class was interesting but the prof is hard to understand and does not make herself very clear.
No Comments
No Comments

Professor Eitan is a lecture-heavy professor. His lectures are usually boring; and he will try to engage the class to participate, yet not many do. He is a really nice guy and is always willing to help his students. His quizzes are very easy if you do the homework, but his exams are tough. There are questions you are not well prepared for.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome!

Goldman is a great prof, he did a better job explaining finance than any prof I've had. Feel free to ask questions, he has a way of making fun of people that ask stupid questions without even trying. Honestly though I've gone to him for advice on finance crap outside the classroom material and he is extremely bright and knowledgeable.

She has no clear expectations, she does not know her own syllabus, she forgets things she told us, she never puts up readings in advance, and she often puts students on the spot in class and in office hours. She doesn't even teach us anything, and it's unclear how her readings and guest lectures even relate to to the theme of the class.

Professor Juilen expects are too much from her students and gets extremely annoyed when students don't complete the insanely long readings. She also has the tendency to post assignments for the next day lecture late the evening before, usually around 8 or 9 o'clock.

This is the worst teacher I've ever had. She is not a very good teacher and her teaching method is very poor. She accuses people of not reading the material all the time. I strongly recommend not taking her. Also she is hardly ever in office hours, standing students up. Very unprofessional.

Prof. Julien is one of the best profs I have ever had as IU. She does expect a lot of her students and her classes are not easy, but she absolutely knows what she is talking about, and is very willing to consider outside ideas about the text. If she isn't sure how your comment fits, she asks you to elaborate, she doesn't shoot you down.

The class was interesting, but she is strict and not very receptive to others' ideas.  She actually offended me a couple times, just in how she made me feel like my comments were stupid (they weren't, trust me.)
He is retired now, but I wanted to say that Professor Eiderman was an AMAZING teacher for Calculus! He was funny and very good at explaining harder topics. I hope he is doing well!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is retired now, but I wanted to say that Professor Eiderman was an AMAZING teacher for Calculus! He was funny and very good at explaining harder topics. I hope he is well!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are super hard to understand, mostly proof based. Read the textbook and you'll be fine. He grades tough, but fair. Try and talk to him as much as possible because he'll give good advice.

Dr. Eiderman was very sweet, but this class was difficult and dense. I found lectures to be not so helpful, as he had to rush through content to cover everything. Do the assigned problems ASAP after class—not the kind of HW to do start-to-finish the night before it's due. Also beware that the content gets harder at the end of the semester.
He is the sweetest professor ever and always willing to help if you asked. He is very knowledgeable about math and his lecture is also very helpful.

Prof Eiderman is hard to understand at best, mean at worst. I wouldn't recommend him for 211 unless you've take calc before. I took precalc in high school and still didn't understand half of what he said. He gets mad if the class doesn't do well on exams, which is very unmotivating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend Dr. Eiderman for M211 if you've never taken anything beyond pre-calc. He was fine to teach the actual material of the class, but if you lack background in calculus he tends to overcomplicate things and make it more confusing. He also has a very strong accent, but he is a sweet guy and tries his best to help if you ask.

There was weekly homework and quizzes which was very difficult to manage at times, but he wrote very easy exams, and I would not say the class is hard to succeed in. Teaches directly from the textbook, so I was able to miss class a lot and still keep up. Highly recommend Vlad.

He is very kind and approachable outside of class but his class is based on the fact that you have had previous experience in calculus further than pre-calc. He seems to assume that most things he teaches are common knowledge or that we should know it coming into his class. This class very concept heavy so be prepared for a lot of proofs.

Professor Vladimir Eidermann is one of the best in the math department. He is so caring and willing to help you along the way. If you skip classes and don't care, then you will find his quizzes and exams tough. If you have any chance to take a class with him then take it without any hesitation if you are genuinely a hardworking person.

Professor Eiderman is by far one of my favorite math teachers I've had! He is very accessible outside of class and loves when students come to his office hours so don't be afraid to go if you have questions. He is very smart and has a genuine love for math and I would recommend him to anyone!

Although the class was challenging, Professor Eiderman is an exceptional teacher. He demonstrates a genuine concern for his students' academic performance and is willing to provide assistance during his office hours, even if it requires extra time.

Amazing professor. Does a great job breaking down and explaining material while giving plenty of examples. Homeworks and quizzes are pretty simple if you pay attention in class and he is willing to do homework problems at the beginning of every lecture. Exams are difficult, but not impossible if you study. He has helpful review sessions for exams.

Professor Eiderman is great. He does give a lot of homework though and his tests aren't the easiest (except the final which is common across all departments if I am not wrong). However, he does curve the final. He is also really sweet and is always willing to go out of his way to help you. I would recommend him but you do have to be willing to work
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This teacher will ruin you
always went over time and never acknowledged it. He gave lots of homework even during finals week and only help review sessions outside class on weekends or late at night.

In high school, I took Trig and PreCal, so I shouldve been ready for Calc 1. I had this class last semester, but had to withdraw. The material was too difficult, and it catered to the people who took AP Calculus in HS. I felt like I knew nothing compared to everyone else. He does seem like he cares, but it doesnt matter if he teaches poorly.

Professor Eiderman is a very sweet man, the class is just very difficult without any background calc knowledge. He expects you to have a lot of previous knowledge and also loves proofs even though we never need to use them.

Knows the material really well and teaches far beyond the textbook. Grades hard on homework and exams, make sure you learn the material well and brush up on integral tricks. Band together with classmates to check homework, it will save your grade and help study. Lively professor who's a pleasure to take a class from. Best of the math department!

Professor Eiderman is a very nice guy but his class is tough. It is difficult to understand him during lectures. Do not recommend if you didnt taken AP Calc in hs because it is nearly impossible to learn this material without past knowledge that he expects. Tests are very hard and hw is graded tough. It is best to just take M119.

Eiderman is really nice and always willing to help and answer questions if you have any, especially during office hours. However, he's not the best lecturer. I found that there were a lot of things he just couldn't explain in a way that I understood. Homework assignments are a huge part of your grade so check your work! Weekly quizzes, 3-4 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: My favorite math professor at IU. He wants all of his students to succeed and grades accordingly. All exams are open note & open book. Very passionate about the course and understanding about the pandemic (even let me retake a test after I forgot to show up). Does not accept late work though, so make sure to stay on top of deadlines.

Professor Eiderman was the worst educator I have ever had. If I hadn't already taken AP Calculus, I would have failed his class for sure. I received a 4 on the AP Calc test and would like to think I have a good understanding of the subject. My homework grade is what pushed me down to an A- even though all of it was checked on Slader.

I had this professor for m211 and he was the best! He has exam reviews on the nights before the exam and those are really helpful (he literally brings the exam there and does problems exactly like them.) If you go to office hours he will help you out a lot! I highly recommend this professor

Professor Eiderman is clearly an intelligent person. He did expect everyone to have previous calculus experience but he still explained key topics well. He mainly used lecture time to show us proofs but he had amazing review sessions before every exam that basically gave you the outline of the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a great professor, especially for math! He is Russian, but is fairly easy to understand and tries to make class entertaining for students.
