You can really tell that he is passionate about math. He also gives OUTSTANDING review sessions before all tests, including the final, that I would absolutely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such a nice guy!! He always makes himself available if extra help is needed. He really wants you to succeed. Exams are hard and there is a lot of homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is the best professor I've ever met in university, always smiling and so ready to help. He is everyone's grandpa because he is so caring for students.

VERY sweet old Russian man. He's everyone's grandpa. And don't worry, you'll get use to his accent very quickly, no matter where you're from (and no matter how bad you are at understanding them). TOUGH grader though. Homework is SUPER IMPORTANT. Basically only thing that keeps you afloat because exams are stressful and not easy in the slightest.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Eiderman truly wants each of his students to understand what is going on in his class. He offers optional review sessions before each test and he will stay and help students until all questions are answered. He is so passionate about his work and is one of the most caring professors I have ever had. I highly recommend taking his classes!

He's one of the most enthusiastic professors I have ever had. He loves teaching and math, however I did find his class hard. He often makes mistakes when explaining things or he isn't clear enough because of his Russian accent. His exams got quite hard. First time not getting an A. He's very available for help, though!
Incredibly difficult tests and confusing homework. Spent most of the semester lost, but I didn't use office hours. Accessible outside of class and a sweet guy.

Professor Eiderman is a great teacher. Go to his office hours, he is extremely helpful and often times stayed past his posted hours in order to make sure that me and other students had all of our questions answered. He grades pretty hard overall (not a fan of curving too much) but tries very hard to give partial credit. Get ready to prove things.

Had him for S211 and loved every minute of classtime with him. It is obvious he loves what he does and wants to explain everything in depth. This also means he typcailly can overfocus on some tertiary subject and not get around to some of the other concepts that students might struggle with. Go to office hours! He to pass you but is a strict grader
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Has a russian accent, but is extremely willing to help students. Decent lectures, highly recommend going to class, it is the best way to learn the material. Homework is a reasonable quantity but is graded for accuracy so make sure its right! Homework is worth more than quizzes!! I suggest purchasing a membership to chegg website for book solutions

He cares about his students and if you put in the work you should do well. However I would have crashed the course if it wasn't for the AI, quizzes, and homework grades. That being said his teaching style wasn't for me. He loves proofs and would be a great teacher for honors class. But this class doesn't require them and he focuses on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Like any other math course, you need to do the homework (there's a lot, but it really helps) and attend lectures to do well on his tests and in his class. Also, he's very passionate about calculus and willing to help his students; he has review sessions for his exams and have additional office hours opened around exam time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Eiderman is one of the best professors I've had here. (You get used to his Russian accent btw.)  I wasn't sure about him at first, but he really just wants his students to do well, and it shows. He can be very animated at times. He's taken entire lectures to answer a question before. He expects a lot out of his students, but in a good way.
Sixty problems in weekly homework. Confusing lecture. No extra credits. Almost no curve. Tricky tests.
Often hard to understand and in individual help. Has difficulty communicating for personal help. Nice person and always smiling though.
Pretty good teacher.
Eiderman is a great professor - very animated, eager to help students, always tries to make class engaging, and he's a pretty funny guy too. I would definitely recommend him.

Definitely take this class instead of W131.  Although she goes strictly by the rubric and can be unclear in her expectations she is really open to help and is a laid back nice teacher.  Learn to adapt to what she expects and you'll do well, and improve your writing.
Overall a really good teacher. Very helpful although slightly cooky. She has very high expectations of everyone but it definitely pays off in the end!

Her guidelines for W170 are strict and her expectations are high.  Not bad qualities, but coupled with her way of expressing what she *really* wants students to learn/understand clouds the entire course. Expect to be challenged and have your writing style criticized strongly.

Eve is an excellent teacher! She really helps you apply what you learn to what you're writing. I believe that this class will further help me in my college education. She really tries to connect on a personal level like most other teachers will not. Follow guidelines clearly, attend office hours if you have ANY questions she's always there to help
great teacher. i actually enjoyed english.  fair grader
Very helpful, nice and funny. Pretty easy if you follow the guidlines. Taught me a lot and I really enjoyed her class.
She is a nice and funny teacher. She talks a lot. You can tell she loves english.

If you enjoy very tough exams (averages around 65%) with no curves, lengthy and time consuming assignments, boring lectures, and the assumption that you're an expert in statistics (his speciality), then you'll love this professor! Otherwise Id stay far away.

I don't know why everyone complains. I took this professor and found him to be great. Very straightforward, do the homework, go over quizzes and lecture slides and you'll probably be fine. The curve is quite nice as well.

One of the hardest teacher in my academic life. Expects you to read textbook in advance. No sample exams, helpful though in office hour. ( Expects you to do HW that he has not taught yet) Class Average for First exam was 45%. Figures says it all

Was my TA for Macro.  Would help me with homework, provided great explanations to questions, answer keys were extremely helpful.  Wonderful at his office hours.  Would gladly take his class again.(Still wears a lot of purple shirts.)

One of the best teachers I've had hands down! Go to his office hours and you will do fine.  I struggled towards the end but going to his office hours i think he was very nice about my grade. Plus he is very attractive!
THE WORST PROF EVER IN HISTORY OF BGSU!!!! I dont understand how he got hired.

His quizzes were ridiculously hard, but going to his office hours really helps your grade. He gives a little leniency on your final grade if you are a good student and talk to him about it.  After taking him, I realized I enjoy Econ.

Gives a ton of pointless six point quizzes that do nothing but destroy your grade, does not make things clear and makes you feel dumb if you don't understand, final exam is comprehensive over about twenty chapters and he gives no review or study guide, and you have to write two short naturalist essays one that is due the very last day of class.

Ryan Eiben is tough but fair.  He is one of the hardest teachers I've had but that doesn't make him bad.  I went to his office hours and what he didn't make clear in class was much clearer in one-on-one sessions.  I'd take him again.
awful

things wrong with Ryan Eiben: -only wears purple shirts. -laughs at own jokes waaay too much. -worst teacher i have ever had. i learned more from my friends final exam study guide from another teacher than anything he ever did. no study guides, minimal help on homework. the only thing I liked was his grading scale. 55% to pass?? saved my ass!!!
Makes simple instructions hard and only has early or late class times for this section.
He makes what should not be that complicated into what takes hours to learn on my own.
Terrible

Difficult homework, quizzes made to fail students, boring lectures, near impossible exams. Rude to students who don't understand concepts immediately; makes you feel stupid. Impossible to pass without hours of tutoring. Offers non-answers for help and can't accept students may be struggling because of HIS methods rather than laziness.

I hate to say but this class is worthless.  In all honesty i learned more about economics in an hour review in an unrelated class than i did in the entire first six weeks of this class.   The review sessions are helpful and i would recommend going but if you want to do well on the test you pretty much have to figure things out for yourself.

Young prof who likes to relate econ to the world. However his teaching methods are horrible and his homeworks are extremely hard. He refuses to give out grades or keep track of them. He is the worst prof I have had a BG. Basically, try to find another teacher and if your stuck with him, just drop the class and wait to get another prof next year.

Not so bad first couple weeks. However, I think his teaching methods completely suck. He needs to learn how to use a powerpoint because his graphs he draws suck and he has chicken scratch. I think his voice is annoying because he puts emphasis on his s's and it makes me cringe. Take someone with more teaching experience.
Our class average on the first exam was around 65% He told our class that this was our fault and not his.

This professor is awful, he can not relate to his students. I went a few times to his office hours and he seems to not like it when you ask him for help and he also grades really hard and makes impossible to get an A in the class. I failed the class even though I did all of the assigned work and showed up to class every day.

This teacher is awful! He doesn't care about your grade and he is NOT helpful with homework. He won't answer questions about the HW. His tests are hard and he expects you to know things the first time they are taught. He is an awful teacher and TRIES to explain things with pictures. It's stupid.

He uses everyday examples to explain the economic theories which is very helpful.He gives office hours to explain things after classes for those who had problems which is great.And by the way, he is the cutest teacher I ever had. Seriously, he's hot! ;)
Ryan is interesting to listen to if you dont pay attention to what he's saying. He is excited about the material but does not explain it well and he doesn't seem to want to be a professor.
Lectures not really of substance, he pretty much just babbles about nothing. The class isn't that hard if you go to tutoring.

The WORST prof I've had at BG. His teaching method is using examples and not explaining. He is very sarcastic and gives a lot of pointless quiz' that are made to kill your grade. Assigns terrible papers and tests us on things he never went over in class. He screamed at our class and kicked us out. Then said we would get a quiz we cannot pass.

The final probably was the easiest of all the test he ever gave. However, the wriiten part contained a chart I don't ever remember him going over an dthere were a few questions that were crazy off the wall.The executive summaries should count for more than they do

Mr. Eiben was nice.I took advantage of his office hours and left more confused than before I went. I hated the papers. I thought they would help my grade because I am stronger in writing,but the topics were stupid. I rather he give us a topic instead of ask us to make up our own to apply econ to. He's passionate about econ, not good at teaching it.

worst prof ever! do not take him! he doesn't care if you fail. he gives you a quiz every single day based on the reading and it's impossible. his tests are ridiculous. the papers he makes you write are ridiculous. DON'T TAKE HIM!!

The first time I took ECON203, I had to drop it because of the professor.  I was able to understand the material that Mr. Eiben taught.  I did think that some of the homework was difficult.  The test were not that bad.  With the curve, I got Bs on all the test. The test were from what he covered in class (which came directly from the book).

This guys is a bad teacher because he is unclear in explanations, his tests have nothing to do with homework or described course material, he also has unreasonable quiz expectations.That being said, he is a nice and well meaning guy but a bad teacher

A completely worthless teacher. He can't explain anything. He can't write on the chalkboard coherently. His tests ask compeletly random questions that we don't go over in class. His homeworks are very unclear and come out of left field. There's no way of really knowing how you are doing in the class until the end of the semester.
Overall, a very knowledgable and interesting person. He cares about students preferences and is willing to work with you. He is awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: This course really helped in prepping me for graduate school.  The class room setting was very similar to that of graduate classes.  Dr. Eklof was willing to look over papers before turning them in, and gave useful feedback on drafts and graded papers.  Do the reading, pay attention, and his classes will be easy to follow.

Coming into this class I thought I was going to hate it, but Dr. Eklof is so knowledgeable on Russian history he made the class somewhat enjoyable. Get on his good side early on and this should be a somewhat enjoyable class.

He really knows a lot about Russian history and is happy to share it. Sometimes goes on tangents. Tests are short answer/essay and will be a lot easier if you attend classes and listen to the lectures/take notes.

Lectures are boring but mandatory; go to them or you will do poorly on exams. You must do the readings and pay attention, but the material itself is not difficult. He is overall an understanding guy who realizes that you have other things to do. If you like history definitely take a course with him.
Disorganized, rude, unhelpful.

Professor Eklof's knowledge of russia and russian history is unparalleled -his interest in the topic is likewise contagious. He is understanding and caring, helpful and a joy to listen to. Work hard and be patient - he is a gift.

Essay Exam on the entire 20th century with no study guide or guidelines to help you prepare. The entire class is doing poorly and is still reluctant to have any curve even though it is blatantly his fault. Also terrible at teaching and lecturing. Thinking about taking it up with the board cause this is ridiculous.

The class wasn't that interesting, but Eklof was a good professor. He really cares about his students and wanted to get to know them. He is easy to work with and understands that you have other class so he sets the pace to the class. The lectures are super interesting, but he has a dry sense of humor that is great if you get it.
This man doesn't know how to teach a class. He says he's being doing it for years, but still doesn't know how long he wants essays to be. Incompetent. Never take this class.

Eklof is an awesome prof. He is very understanding and helpful. Just chatting with him let's you know that most of the comments on here are from those who can't make it in a real college course. Pay attention and do the reading, you'll enjoy the class and do well

Great class and great prof. Appropriate level of difficulty for a 300 level class. Lectures are a little dry,  but it's better if you have background knowledge. Tests are pretty easy and papers as well. Loved it.

Professor Eklof has been by far one of the most interesting and enthusiastic professors in my time at IU. He is passionate about Russian History and makes the class very interesting. Don't be afraid to talk to him after class. He is a very interesting and intelligent person to know.

He is very scattered and it's true he gives out a list of >20 topics that may be on the test, but if you pay attention in class you'll be fine. I was able to do all the complimentary readings on online without purchasing the book and come out with a B+. He is also understanding of issues you may have you just have to make the effort to talk to him.
Came to class with his belly button showing! could be suffering with ADHD. readings were interesting but extremely boring lectures.

Lectures are very dry and boring and impossible to take notes on. He does give u an outline of the lecture but even that is unclear and unorganized.  tests are impossible to study for because he gives you 25 different essay topics and picks a couple.  my HIST-A379 class was easier than this, and more enjoyable. STAY AWAY!!!
dry, boring, unorganized, and limited.

You may be overwhelmed at first, but you can do the min. amount of readings and you will be fine. He sometimes rambles but he reiterates a lot. He is a little disorganized, show up to class and you'll be fine.
he mumbles and rambles on and on and is hard to follow and impossible to take notes on. doesn't provide any visual aids (power point) and is extremely dry.

Readings for D308 were interesting, and while Prof. Eklof might at times seem a bit "scatterbrained," he is extremely knowledgeable and gives great lectures. If you do the relatively little work he asks of you (though there is quite a bit of reading), you'll see Russian history from a very different perspective after this course. I miss this class.
Enjoyed his lectures and reading material.  Didn't find he was unwilling to talk after class or during hours like a lot of profs at this research-driven institution.

He makes over $70,000 a year and doesn't show up with a completed syllabus. On top of that he's rude, generally unavailable. He lives in his little tiny specialty, and has forgotten about the rest of us, including students. Save your time and money: take something else.
Scatterbrained but very intelligent and honestly wants students to learn.  If you have problems with him, it's probably because you're not trying.
He's mailing it in, and you will suffer thusly.
No Comments
No Comments

in class lecutres and notes had NOTHING to do with exams or papers. grading was unjustly harsh. i never had any idea where he was going with anything. he is impossible the reach as well and can be very rude

Prof. Eklof was a great purveyor of knowledge in the classes I had with him, which include seminars on Soviet/Tsarist Russia.  Again, Eklof is a misunderstood man, for he is quite cerebral and can lose a student who truly doesn't have the mettle to make it
is a little too "close" to his female students
Shoot me for taking this class. SO UNCLEAR!!! I have pages of handouts he gave us to take notes on and NOTHING is written on them. Avoid this guy at all costs!!!
very interested in material, helpful, can be unorganized, good teacher
Often unorganized, but very intelligent and committed to his students. Assigns great reading material. Goes above and beyond to offer help or advice.
one of the lower life forms on campus
Inconsistent in his grading but always really helpful during office hours
Well organized and informative.
No Comments
Elkof's a good guy, but he checked out years ago, teaches on autopilot
She is super enthusiastic about mythology, and it really reflects on her students. This class is awesome, would highly recommend.
Holy peak! Very easy class, make sure to go to lecture. Test were very easy as long as you take notes effectively. She is very passionate about the subject and it shows, class was always interesting!
She is goated, as long as you take notes during class and study for the tests, you're guaranteed an A...do not skip lectures because her notes will not be posted on Canvas or anywhere.

Easy class. 3 exams and all were very straight forward from the study guides and lecture material. Weekly discussion posts and 2 projects were very easy too. She literally drops your 5 lowest scores from the grade book so that should help with overall grades. Overall pretty easy, just come to class because it will be confusing if you don't.

Overall very easy class. A discussion every week and some projects and exams. Attend class and take notes and you will minimum get a easy B. Does very helpful review for exams and outlines exams and projects clearly. Very kind and would take again

She cares about her students, but her teaching style is very boring to many. Make sure to go to class and take ample notes - you will rely on them heavily for studying. Coursework is very manageable but make sure to study a lot for all 3 exams.

You only have three exams, all multiple-choice. There are four versions, but they all have the same questions, just in a different order. Also, on top of that, her assignments are due at 8 pm on Fridays. If you miss an assignment, your grade is genuinely toast, like you can't really come back.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would say this class is average, but the professor makes it hard. The content can be learned easily if you actually study, like I would study for at least 4 days before, but on the other hand, she doesn't give you a single study guide, and the test, if you do get a bad grade, will drop your grade by a letter grade or two.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mooradian wants you to learn and cars about student engagement. Classes can be a little monotonous, but it is good for exposure to many aspects of exercise science and you can learn a lot in a small amount of time. Great way to get immersed in the field to really see if you are interested in exercise science or not.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just does not simply understand how to teach.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Freshly got her PhD, not tenured, and not well liked among other profs. and all of that is very clear.

She was overall a good professor, but her lectures were super boring. She tries so hard to make them engaging but it doesn't work. She said to order a textbook, I did, and never used it. She doesn't take attendance, but will randomly take participation points. Tests were pretty straightforward, sometimes.

She has very clear grading criteria, which I liked, but the class is very lecture-heavy and can tend to be boring at times. Exams are multiple choice, which is great, and there is an in-class review before every exam. She takes participation grades at random, but you don't know when she will be doing those. The slides aren't posted fully completed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: A very kind person, not the best professor. Lectures are boring & are just her reading off the slides that she never posts complete. Exams are fine(ish)-- multiple choice, but no study guide is given, so prepare to reread every single note you took. Otherwise, homework is easy, and she's available to meet if you need anything, don't stress much.

She doesn't really explain topics in depth and does not seem to know answers to questions about things that are deeper than surface level. Would highly recommend taking structural before this class. I would not take this class again unless I had to.
Shes alright but lectures are just piled with so much information she doesn't go into depth about anything. Tests are easy though, so the class is pretty light
Don't play with her, she's #unwell. Literally 0 understanding. It is not human, expects perfection as in completing your assignments the day they open, and checking them until they're graded.

This professor does so many notes but they just confuse you more.. Boring lectures full of her just talking but not really explaining. Has low exam averages but she is happy that it isn't failing. Doesn't provide study guides or outlines on what is going to be on the exams. Most students retake this class multiple times to pass it.

Her exams were very straightforward and almost exactly like the in class review. There wasn't too much homework and it was very manageable. She did go through lectures pretty fast and didn't upload the complete notes so it's important to show up or at least get notes from someone. Overall I thought the class was interesting and very manageable.

Took Dr. M as a graduate student online. Thought her lectures were a bit long but the readings always tied into what you learned. I don't get all the negative reviews, maybe her teaching method is different for undergrads. There are quite a few papers for this class but as long as you follow the rubric you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Test way harder than they needed to be. Show-up to every class because that will be the determining factor for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Mooradian has extensive knowledge on the topics of class, but that doesn't make the class anymore bearable. A bulk of the grade is online weekly assignment, and every day in-class group discussions that force you to show up to class. In class the lectures are 80 slides long and incredibly boring. All contact to Dr. Mooradian goes through her TA

This class is mostly online and graded based on the amount of points earned, so it is important to actually do the work outside of class. There is an attendance grade, but the lectures are horribly boring. Mooradian is knows what she is talking about, but is not good at communicating it to the class. Even so, it is super easy to pass.

She is an awful grader. She doesn't do much grading personally because when you email her questions about your grade and her response is " I do not do grades ask the TA". Her class is all attendance! Do all outside assignments because there are very little points. She also didn't get our final grades in on time so that was interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Mooradian has a wack grading scale. You have to get at least a 94.1% to get an A because she grades off of her own points scale. The majority of the class is busy work, which sucks. Also, she reads directly off of her slides so that's all you really need to look at, but you do get points for in class discussions, so you should show up.

The class was pretty easy in retrospect. Do all the online quizzes and discussion and show up to class and that is the grunt of the work. The tests in this class require you to review her powerpoints and notes, but they are not too hard. Dr. Mooradian isn't necessarily a great professor there is a lot of busy work. She reads off the powerpoints.

Showed up late twice, forced us to stay late to finish her lecture. Bogus career services homework assignment, she gave us no due date, most of the class got a zero because one day she said we needed to have it by the end of class or it's a zero. Absolutely zero late work with her. Almost no points in class. She doesn't even get enough scantrons...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests? Not many--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Elizabeth is not a good professor at all. She is very adamant about the things she is teaching, but she does NOT have any research to back any of it up. I have never in my college career been treated with disrespect in a class like I was in her class. She treats us like we are back in middle school. DO NOT TAKE, IF POSSIBLE.

You get participation points for going to class so you mostly need to go, but you get 3 excused absences which is nice. Online quizzes almost every week, easy 5 points. Exams cover a lot of material but aren't hard if you read lectures. Final project was cake work. Overall easy class

This professor actually made me mad. I was treated more like an adult back when I was in high school than I was in this class. The assignments were pointless, the tests were vague and horrible, and the final was literally just busywork. Requiring attendance at a career services orientation at the start of the semester really topped it off, too.

Why would you want to make an effort in a class in which the professor treats you like you're still in middleschool? From yelling at you if you "pack up before class is over" to making you attend a career services orientation for credit, this professor really does a great job of making you feel like you're 13 again. Would not recommend.

One time someone in my class was laughing, and she stopped class and yelled at him, and she constantly calls out students for the smallest things. Her lectures are so boring and a lot of what she says aren't on the exam. Just memorize the case debriefs entirely to get an A, otherwise the class will be difficult.

I'd advise not taking her. The class isn't too hard but she yaps about irrelevant things half of the lecture so you don't know what to really take away from it except what's on the slides. She crashes out every other class when a student in the back row laughs at their phone or talks to the person next to them which is pretty funny. Hard to listen.
Her class is not worth going to. Everything you need to know is on the slides. Also gets mad at students for doing anything besides staying silent.

Ellie teaches the cases, Steven her husband teaches the lessons. Ellie talks all lecture and it is easy to get lost in her words. She is quite rude to studnents and often doesn't understand that we have lives outside of class. If you ask a question not during OFFICE HOURS she will not be helpful. Overall did bad on one test but rest was easy.
I wish you the best of luck... It will become very obvious who the better Kreft is.

Mafi-Kreft is hard to understand and calls out students mid-lecture to ask them pointless questions. Dismissive, rude, and disrespectful when asked questions. Puts little effort into her lectures & reads verbatim from a script. Why Kelley has both Krefts teaching one class is beyond me. One of them or better yet both of them should be replaced.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Literally stands in one place and reads from a script. will randomly cold call. class is mandatory for the tophat but I dont think I gained anything from actually being there bc I could've just read the slides. not a hard class tho
Very boring, stands in one place and does not move. Reviews exact script from textbook.

Mafi was difficult to understand in the lectures. Steve would make analogies to simpler topics to help his students understand hard concepts. Mafi seemed like she was reading straight from a script and will call out students who are talking about the material in class, trying to understand what she is saying. Heavy accent.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wouldn't recommend. Ellie reads from a script and doesn't move for entire class, while cold calling student during an incredibly boring lecture. Virtual office hours which is very impersonal. Say I should come and speak with before class for 5 minutes instead. Many hours of outside study is required because lectures don't explain the content.

She works with her husband Kreft for this course. She is definitely not as good of a lecturer as her husband and can be quite boring. It is hard to stay engaged. Course is super exam heavy, but they give you exactly what to study. As long as you put in the time you will do fine. Make sure to really know the cases for exams!

This women having a job is the biggest joke of the 21st century. Deep accent,  not funny at all, and constantly wasting time calling on 10 kids asking useless questions wasting our time and money all because she thinks she has power as a professor. Truly a disgrace to teaching although she seems to have a passion for the material. Steven 100/10 tho

She calls out on people and expects them to always have the right answer. I can understand calling out on people during class, but if the answer isn't correct she disregards everything you say. What's the point of calling out to people the whole lecture if you rudely interpret them and dismiss them simply because you don't agree with them.

Wow. If you enjoy sitting in a lecture hall stressing about your other classes only to have your teacher call out other students instead of talking about the material then you'll love this class. Honestly you're probably better sleeping in an extra 40 minutes and reviewing the slides for 10 minutes then actually going to the lecture.

Ellie Mafi-Kraft was an excellent professor. She really knows her stuff and makes herself very accessible to students. If you pay attention in the lectures and study for exams there is no reason why you couldnt get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ellie is the best professor at Kelley that I have met so far. She is caring and humorous. She stays after lectures to answer questions, and she is easy to reach for help out of class. She and Steven hold extra office hours before exams. I enjoyed having her class so much, but you have to work and practice to get high scores for G202.

While many students claim G202 is hard everyone can agree that Ellie is an absolutely wonderful professor. The only reason people struggle is because the tests involve lots of conceptual and critical thinking. If you can look at a graph and think oh if this happens then this will go this way because people are thinking this, you're golden.

Ellie is probably cooler than 90% of the students here. She plays french techno to get everyone hyped up before class starts. Good professor, no complaints. However, the tests are so difficult. It's almost all trick questions where like 1 word is different in each answer, I think you would be better with open ended to explain concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ellie is awesome, so caring and  an energetic lecturer.. Both her and her husband Steven are great professors and you can't go wrong either way-- they teach the same exact things. Tests are more challenging (review the cases) but there's plenty of extra credit with bonus practice problems and easy points from the cases.

Great professor. Attendance is not mandatory nor is it really required to get an A. It is definitely worth your time to go to class during the days of the Case Debriefings. If you take good notes during the Debriefings and cram the slides (available on canvas) before each exam, you should do fine. Do the 5 minute extra credits before each exam!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: It doesn't matter if you take G202 with Ellie or Steve. Both are great professors with similar personalities and teaching styles. She has a slight french accent but I never had any trouble understanding her. There is no textbook and her slides have quite a few blanks in them so make sure you go to class or find a friend to get notes from.

Professor Kreft is really sweet, and she's always ready to help you out even if you make the slightest effort. she makes the case discussion debriefings engaging and interesting and explains them really well.  Literally holds office hours everyday when an assessment os coming up. Great person and professor!

Professor Mafi-Kreft is an excellent teacher who takes the time to really get to know her students. There are 7 "pop-quiz" assignments throughout the semester for extra credit. You get one point for putting your name on the paper. She gives you everything you need to do well in her class, you just have to take a little time to review before tests.
Expected her to be a better professor.  Poor direction. Seems to follow a script

Nice professor but super confusing. Cannot really explain the material. Did not have her for G202, so she may be fine for that class. However, when you take upperlevel classes with her, she has a hard time addressing your questions and explaining the material. Be ready to teach yourself.

Ellie is a very nice person.  She is French, but easy to understand and is funny at times.  She will go out of her way to help you and shows a big interest in her students.  The class isn't hard, but the exams can be tricky.  There are often applications of concepts on the exams that we did not talk about in class.  Overall an excellent professor.

Professor Mafi-Kreft is nice and helpful. Class is not mandatory, but it is helpful to go, and we sometimes received extra credit basically for coming to class. She is willing to answer any questions students have, and the material is pretty interesting. My recommendations are to attend class, do the readings, and go to review sessions to do well.

Ellie is extremely nice and very wiling to help anyone, but she just forgets to  cover a lot of the material that is covered on the tests, and she often doesn't finish the lectures because time runs out. Her husband Steven writes the tests, and I have friends in his class that say he does better job of teaching. I would recommend Steven over Ellie.
Extremely nice and helpful. Has a French accent but it's completely understandable. Easy class but don't slack off near the end. If you want to get the A, finish strong.

Great teacher. Only alternative is her husband who teaches the larger lectures. I have heard she does a slightly better job of teaching to the test. I studied 1-2 hours for every test and received high A's on all of them. My friend in Steven's class studied much longer and did much worse. Great teacher.
While she is very nice and somewhat helpful, she is not very clear in what she wants you to learn. Tests are somewhat random. I would recommend someone else.

She is awesome. Entertaining lectures and good explanations in class. Go to office hours, because tests usually have numbers applied and she does not do examples in class for those. She can explain any problem you may have and is always willing to help. And...she's French! Bonjour!

Very fun teacher, loves her subject and her classes. The course itself is too small in scope (only 2 credits, should be 3) and she could do with more than a 50 minute lecture. That aside, she really knows what counts and what will be worth knowing in the real world.

I LOVE HER! She's funny, she always looks nice, and she's extremely helpful. She makes sure it's worth coming to class and appreciates those who does. She's also really enjoyable to talk to. If you pay attention and have a will to study, its definitely an A. She's just the best. One of the best profs of Kelley!!
Extremely cool teacher! Very nice and helpful. Funny too. Picks cool topics to discuss, good dresser, adorable French accent. Highly recommend her!

Extremely nice and cares about her students. Go to class for extra credit and she'll tell you what you need to know for tests. Always willing to help in office hours. Relates topics to current issues. Study for tests and pay attention in class and you'll get a good grade.

Very nice- Lectures can be a little boring, but it is helpful to attend as she emphasizes the areas you will be tested on. gives 4 quizzes and lets you drop the lowest(they are easy 10 multiple choice and 2-3 short answers). The practice exams help a lot! Overall its a good class and she is a good teacher...
The key to an A+ is to attend class and participate. Grades fairly and is always willing to help students during office hours.
Good teacher, study for exams, go to class, participate and its an easy A

A professor with extremely high expectations and standards but sucks at giving instructions so expect to only pass this class with an A if you can read his mind. Has you lead a discussion week but posts his thoughts multiple times that week before you can get a chance so good luck actually leading the discussion. 3 credits but should be 6.
The professor uses generalized wording and is not clear on his expectations. The syllabus says one thing but he expects another. He is very responsive but still lacks clear communication.

Professor Engbers cares about students, he makes himself available to online students, provides clear assignments and discussions and provides quick feedback.  I learned so much in this class and was really able to connect with other students..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Such a great professor. Clearly extremely passionate & knowledgeable about public management & nonprofit organizations. Always willing to hop on a Zoom call to offer feedback on essay drafts or to answer any questions over email. I would take more of his courses if I could -- easily one of the top 3 professors I've had in my entire SPEA program.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Trent is a great guy. There is an insane amount of work when it comes to writing. Attending class makes it way easier to write the papers. He grades hard but is very willing to help you and meet with you. I would definitely recommend his class- I learned a lot and the material is very useful for a management degree.

The actual WOAT. Genuinely dread going on Tuesdays. Expects professionalism, yet treats students like children. On average, freaks out on a student every 2 weeks for needing to use the bathroom in a 75 minute 200 person lecture. She is very intelligent but impossible to lock in for. Better to fade Tues when possible and go on Thurs for Steve

The class was bearable with Steven, he makes it fun, engaging, he's great. Ellie on the other hand, wow. Super weird about rules regarding leaving the class even if it's for the bathroom. All you need to know is the info on the slides so you can just zone out when she's talking.
It's not that she doesn't know the content and reads from the slides too much. She should read from the slides more and go over content that actually gets tested.

Lectures are incredibly boring, all information is on the slides and she just reads off of them. Speaks very slowly and very demanding of the class. Drags on simple topics and gives too much information during lectures that is unnecessary for learning and understanding. Would not take again

Literally cannot understand half of what she says. There is a reason why she only teaches the case (She don't know anything). Constantly calls out students for going to the bathroom talking about "professionalism". Real professional calling someone out in front of everyone. Every day i would drive to her class without a seatbelt on.
just take another class. yells at u if u go to the class late
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I dont understand what she says

Completely disrespectful towards her students. She often has called students "space cadets" to their face. She yells at you for using the bathroom and I have seen her single students out that arrive barely late by stopping her lecture that has barely started to give the students "a piece of her mind". Would never recommend this prof.
We pay so much money to attend this university, we should be able to use the restroom when we need to, we are not high schoolers.

She just called out someone TO THE ENTIRE CLASS for trying to go to the bathroom and said he needs to practice professionalism. She said "you are a healthy young boy, you can hold it." So extremely odd.

I disagree with those who left comments saying her English is bad, but that is the only nice thing I have to say about this professor.

For someone who values professionalism so much, to come into class on the first day and declare that her "being a difficult person" is just something students will have to deal with is extremely hypocritical.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are extremely boring and difficult to sit through. She sometimes goes on random tangents that are meaningless. I also HATE this... She sometimes will randomly call out people for leaving class in the middle of lecture. My 2 cents.. It's their money and education so if they want to leave so be it. I just think it's very distracting.

Steven was awesome, one of my favorite professors. Ellie not so much. She doesn't help very much with the case, goes off topic and calls out students for random things like going to the bathroom or arriving two minutes late

All she does it talk about random (typically inappropriate in a college classroom) things that have no impact on the class, can not speak english, does not teach, and runs the class like a 5th grade teacher. would never take her again even though Steve is a good professor. Ellie just rides off her husbands coat tails to be a prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She would be fantastic at leading sleep meditations. She is not fantastic at being even kind of interesting or testing on anything she yapped about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Oh jeez. Goodluck
Not good. I wish you luck

Don't even bother coming to the case debriefs. Complete waste of time. She literally just sits in the front of the class and reads basic summaries of the cases off the slides. She is also sometimes passive aggressive / rude with students. I am writing this in her class right now, and she just called someone out for going to the bathroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mafi-Kreft is hard to understand and calls out students mid-lecture to ask them pointless questions. Dismissive, rude, and disrespectful when asked questions. Puts little effort into her lectures & reads verbatim from a script. Why Kelley has both Krefts teaching one class is beyond me. One of them or better yet both of them should be replaced.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The Krefts who co-taught this class, were incredible. Study, do the quizzes, and do the homework, and you will do well on the two exams. I would take them 100 times out of 100. They are really awesome teachers.

No matter how hard I tried to stay awake, I would be off dozing and napping by the time she got 10 minutes into the case debriefs. The debriefs themselves ain't bad but there is no reason to dedicate an entire class to elementary synopsis of the cases. I suggest you bring a pillow.

Her lectures were the most unhelpful things- she'd yap for 75 mins about what we already read about a company then we would be tested on the smallest detail that was on the slides. Every test question you miss knocks 1% off your grade and the curve is very minimal. Classes were a huge waste of time, and I learned more reading the slides myself.

Where do I begin.Taking G202 with Ellie Kreft was the most miserable experience of my life. From her blasting Daft Punk when the entire class is asleep to her standing behind her desk blatantly reading off of her unhelpful slides. She can't keep a class engaged at all. Every time I went to class I thought WOW what a waste of time. Love Steven tho!

I feel that the office hours where I would clarify any questions that I had regarding the self test quizzes really helped me to do well on the G202 exams so I am truly appreciative of that. I think Professor Mafi Kreft also made me feel respected when I was in office hours.

If I were to imagine purgatory, it would be her lectures: music blasting so loud you can hear it from the hall, elementary regurgitation of 15 year old cases, and coping with being assigned the useless half of G202 by writing case questions based on the most obscure trivia imaginable. There's a reason Steven's ratings are the exact inverse of hers.

Professor Mafi-Kreft more like Professor Yappy-Kreft. She spends the whole 75 minute lectures yapping about the case studies at a third-grade level of analysis in broken English. Her speaking is extremely hard to understand but I didn't even mind because when I did understand her I felt like I was getting dumber by listening!

Sophomore weed-out class, too much information in all of the slides and exams are only 25 questions. They pick out the smallest and most random information from the slides, mix it into an entirely different question for the exam. Recommend taking the class in the fall as the spring term, final exam is during Thursday of little 5. Goodluck

Mrs. Kreft....More like Comrade Kreft.  She spent 15 minutes at the beginning of one of her classes explaining to everyone that she is not in fact a communist.  All im saying is that people who are not communists generally don't have to explain to their entire class that they are not communists. Her husband is pretty chill though.

Most boring class I have ever taken at IU. She provides zero value in her lessons because her entire lesson plan every class is regurgitating basic facts and comments about the case studies we have already read and interacted with. Bottom of the barrel professor.

Her lectures are often directionless, and even though they cover simple cases, the content she teaches often doesn't match what is asked on exams. Your grade is almost entirely decided by your exam score, so you have to learn what kind of minute details they will ask, not the actual important content. Most of our classes ended 15 minutes early.

She refuses to help students and simply cares that her class is considered "challenging" despite the content not being difficult. If you're struggling be prepared to get an automated email saying it's the quality of hours studied not the quantity. She is rude, doesn't adapt to student's needs, and is unkind.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this class with Kreft if you want to listen to an unreal amount of irrelevant things. First class was about their love story.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Ellie as a prof was pretty much one my least favorite professors in Kelley. Half the times she'd call you out and ask you to do the most random things mid-class.

She & her husband,Steven, do not provide any clear guidelines for the exams and the questions are usually all over the place without any clear pattern. 

Would NOT recommend!

Ellie is not the greatest lecturer. She frequently cold-calls students despite her poor lecturing skills. She teaches the class with her husband, Steven, and he is clearly a much better teacher than she is. The tests are very hard and makeup 75% of the class. Office hours are only over zoom, so if you want to get to know the teacher, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Proud cold caller and communist. Attendance is mandatory, but you can get away with studying for the test the night before. All exams are word for word from the slides and online videos. It is important to not question her opinions.

Ellie is the most immoral professor I've ever had who loves to put students in uncomfortable situations. During a class, I had to take an emergency call to discover the passing of my grandma. As I walked out, she mocked me in front of the 250-student lecture hall. I walked back in with tears in my eyes, for her to make fun of me again. Unbelievable

Her slides are great for understanding the material. However, she does cold call and will berate you for not knowing the answer to the question. She does slow the class down due to stubbornly refusing to proceed till she receives a satisfactory answer. Would not recommend her. Disables canvas grade total.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Genuinely the worst professor I have had at IU. She has no business teaching at Kelley. She is overall just a mean person, calls people out in class and publicly makes fun of them if they get the answer wrong. Never take her. 
I have nothing but praise for Steven, he is awesome and funny and I actually enjoy going to his section of the course.

G202 is almost completely reading based. I learn better through lectures but unfortunately, Prof Ellie's lectures never really stuck with me. She cold calls and it's really awkward when student got answers wrong. The grading system is a nightmare. You have to calculate your final grade and discussion grades come out after exams. DO ALL EXTRA CREDIT
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Mafi-Kreft and her husband were passionate, professional, approachable, and understanding. Lectures were engaging, and they simplified complex problems in more digestible pieces. Put in your best effort, do all the work, and you'll pass! I would definitely take a class with them again!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ellie is widely known as having a mixed reputation -- she cold calls EVERY class.  If you don't know the answer, she will often give a passive aggressive comment, like "Why don't we think about what you just said for a second."  She just reads the slides and thinks she eats -- her husband Steven teaches one day and she does the other day each week.

Steven is an incredible lecturer and I think Ellie gets unfairly compared to him. She cold calls but moves on if you don't know the answer. I think her "snarky" remarks are more due to the language barrier than her being mean. When reading these reviews I thought she would be much worse than she is. This class is setup for you to succeed overall.

Ellie will cold call every class, and if she doesn't like your answer she will put you down and be very passive aggressive. That being said, you don't necessarily need to do to class as long as you engage with all the online materials, especially the cases!! I think she can be funny at times in lecture, but not when she is being rude to students...
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cold calls! Cute outfits. I like Steven better than her.

You will need to take Ellie to get Steven, and vice versa, but I much preferred Steven over Ellie. Ellie will make her students feel uncomfortable in a class with optional attendance, which does not bode well for her. However, it's somewhat simple to do well in the class and the lectures are actually extremely interesting.

3 "Quizzes" are VERY important, but not deal breakers. ~83% test average and 100% on everything else should get you to end with an A. It's easier than it seems, at least for the 2 credit version of the class. Go to class on case review days (once a week/every other week), no need to go for spotlight lessons. Curve per "quiz" is about 10%.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Ellie knows her stuff, yet she seems to find joy in cold calling students and making snide and snarky remarks whether or not the student answers right or not. She is accessible through her once-a-week online office hours. Attendance isn't mandatory but I recommend going to Steven's classes and watching all the videos they post on canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do the extra credit, it's easy practice and almost identical questions show up on the exam. Other than that, read the cases/debriefs and watch the videos and you'll be well off. They say the exact same thing and they're right. Attendance isn't totally worth it unless you want them to reinforce the concepts then it's useful.

Ellie is knowledgeable on the content and presents it well, however she randomly cold calls on people during class and is not respectful of your answers. The class is easy to do well in, but Ellie has an attitude. It's not out of mal intent but its annoying. Ellie and Steven co-teach so it doesn't matter who you schedule on iGPS.

Nice person, bad professor. Class was useless and a repetition of the pre-recorded videos used so they didn't actually have to teach. Despite studying exactly the way they told us to, exams proved difficult and weren't much like the example questions given. Cold called students with the sole intent of embarrassing them in front of others.

She was kinda weird as a lecturer - she called out students and embarrassed them in front of the class. The lectures for the most part are a waste of time - the same information is posted online so coming to class is optional. The quizzes can be really difficult if you don't study the right material - make sure to watch the office hours videos

Used to love Ellie but towards the end of the semester, she's become increasingly more passive aggressive. Furthermore, her attitude comes off as though she enjoys calling students out and embarrassing them in front of the whole class. She'll make personal attacks in front of others and tries to control the class by cold calling on people.

Elli is one of the most caring professors I have had during my time at IU. You will succeed in their class as long as you study for exams, watch their online lectures, and attend class. They give you every way to succeed possible, so you just have to apply yourself. I definitely recommend her!
Kind people but poor teachers

Stephen and Ellie are amazing professors. The length of time given for the exams is unrealistic, but overall it was a great course. To better prepare for exams I wish they could give additional optional memos that students can practice on.

Professor Engels was great! The online class was overall very easy, and the course structure was easy to follow. The lecture videos were informational, and the two main projects for this course were interesting. There were no exams, only online quizzes. I loved that Professor Engels left personalized comments on assignment submissions.

I love Jennifer, I've had three classes with her, and each class is refreshing. She doesn't make class hard on purpose, she cares about her students and would rather talk/teach than assign a lot of work. Tests are easy A's, and the book is only used once in a while. Take her for any class!

This class does not seem like a 300 level class. It was very easy and sometimes kind of boring, but the professor is so sweet and nice. The lectures are kind of boring and only sometimes have things to turn in for points. Don't need the book at all.

She is very kind and caring about her students and the topic she teaches. If you want an easy A, take this class, but only if you are willing to go to class every time. Tests are word for word and she gives reviews (the answers) the class before the exam. Great class but does in class assignments, DONT MISS THEM!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved her. She was by far my favorite professor in the department. She was always willing to help students and was very easy to communicate with.

This was one of the most boring classes I have ever taken. Jennifer is really sweet and I can tell that she cares about students. But the material was very easy and it didn't feel like she was an expert on any of the material. Could have learned everything and more from a textbook and it would have been just as entertaining.

Jennifer is super sweet, but her lectures are pretty boring because she just reads off of her slides most of the time. Her class is really easy though! She has in class and homework activities that are super important!

Engels is a total sweetheart who has students' best interests at heart. Reads directly off lecture slides. Day before exams she has a review day (you can have an index card with notes for the exam). Lectures are a bit dry but it is impossible to fail her class. Discussion groups can be fun too depending on your leader and peers.

Professor Engels is one of the nicest people that I have ever met. She goes out of her way to use diverse teaching methods in an attempt to keep her students interested, she holds really helpful review sessions before her exams, and she allows the use of a note card on exams to help relieve test anxiety. I will miss her so much!
Conversational, easy-going and very well versed upon the subject matter. One of my favorite professors, especially for an 8am class!

She spends the whole class before the test reviewing the material and the test has way more on it then what she makes you think. She seems nice but literally reads off the power point, doesn't seem to have any actual knowledge about the class she's teaching.

If you take F347 with her, be prepared for an extremely easy but also very boring class. Her lecture consists of her reading off the powerpoints and almost all of the material was covered in F150. Don't buy the book. I never read it and hardly paid attention in lecture and still got a B, and would've gotten an A if I'd done all the work.

Jengels (as we affectionately refer to her) is one of my favorite professors at IU and serves almost as a second mother to her students. I especially enjoyed how hip and with-the-times she presented herself.

Class is easy and she tries to make it interesting but lectures consist of her reading off of the powerpoints. Class can be fun if you apply yourself but otherwise students typically did other homework during her lectures. It is too bad because she seems to be a good professor.
don't buy the book, just the workbook. class is mandatory but attention is not. easy easy A if you just go to class.
This class is super easy! She is super nice, but literally reads off the powerpoints. Very unorganized. Book is pointless to buy, just the workbook. Usually did other homework in this class.
Very easy and straightforward and cares about students
Professor England is the goat. Lectures are very helpful, and he's always willing to help and answer questions after class. He provides all the resources necessary to succeed in the course.
Mr. England was a great professor. His lectures were very good and it's easy to follow along. The tests aren't that hard if you do the exam simulations. Very kind as well.

He goes through the material at a decent pace and makes everything easy to understand. He's very easy to talk to and very approachable. The class goes by pretty fast since we cover a new chapter each day but the material isn't difficult as he guides you how to do things, and will give you shortcuts that are very beneficial to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The nicest professor and he actually acted like he cared about his students. He also seemed like he enjoyed what he was teaching.
takes time to explain things, very nice and funny, made K201 much easier.

This professor was great! I was nervous for K201 because of all things I heard about it but his classes were engaging and easy to understand. The curriculum was very organized and the textbook was a huge help. He also has a TA and 2 peer tutors in the classroom which makes it very easy to get any questions answered. Overall, amazing teacher!

Prof. England is thoughtful and explains course content clearly. Complete chapter discoveries and reviews for practice. He is easily approachable and his lab checks were simple and never difficult. Overall, a great professor to have for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very good professor. Made having my 8 am manageable. I would 100% retake K201 with him.
Mr. England is a very good professor. He made having an 8 am manageable. I would 100% retake the class with him.
The professor in K-201 doesn't matter much, but he's very good and goes through the material very well.
Great professor. Keeps class fun and interesting. If you pay attention and do all of the work, you'll get an A. Make sure to do the discoveries and do not fall behind.
Cool teacher. Particular about grading but very straight to the point. Double check your work always and never miss a class. Very helpful so don't be afraid to ask questions.

K201 is not as hard as people made it seem. There are just a lot of heavily weighted exams but if you study you will be fine. He is a very nice professor but most K201 lectures are the same because it comes out of the book. He does not call on people in class though which I have heard a lot of professors for this course do.
Professor England is amazing. He cares deeply about his students and is passionate about what he teaches. He will always be there to help you and genuinely cares about you.
a very chill professor and out of the k201 teachers, he is very understanding. he makes dad jokes in class and truly will help if you need.

Mr. England is super sweet and is always available if you need help. For this type of course though, repetition is your friend for everything. Try to get 100% on all of the GP's. The tests are not too hard if you really focus in class and practice a lot outside of class. Would definitely recommend this professor though! Also, go to K-Cove!!

Prof England did a great job of making the K201 material clear and accessible. He answers questions regularly and quickly, and he is always prepared for lectures. If you do the prep work outside of class, you will do great in his section.

One of the best professors out there. He was always super nice and kind. He explained every concept well and thoroughly. You do need to study, so make sure not to fall behind but you should be totally fine, and he is super easy to approach with questions. Would highly recommend him.
Really chill and straightforward with his teachings. Lab checks were very light compared to what other professors gave their students. He is easy to approach if you're ever confused.

England is an ok teacher but he makes it seem like he doesn't want to be there, the energy is very low. He's not great at explaining the concepts it's more just following through what he does on screen to your screen. I don't know how he compares to other teachers, but the class is ok as long as you don't fall behind.

As a professor, Chris England was very good at teaching and made class worthwhile. However, K201 was extremely difficult as a course and the most challenging class I've taken so far. I am glad I had Chris England teaching, or I would've been even more clueless for the graded projects and finals week studying than I already was. STUDY to succeed.

While K201 is a difficult class for most, Prof. England makes it extremely understandable and simplifies topics very well. I don't believe attendance was enforced, but I would recommend going because although he teaches from the online textbook, his explanations are needed. Ask questions, he won't move on until everyone understands the material.

Fantastic prof who's really nice and welcoming. Can explain difficult concepts in an ELI5 way, so much so that you don't understand the e-text because his explanations are much simpler. Go to class, but also take time to re-read the portions he went through in class to 'connect the dots' and self-review. An A should be no problem with Prof England.

He makes K201, which is a hard class because of the content, feel easier and less confusing. I had his class at 8am and he still was energetic and passionate about the students learning the content and making progress.
Very helpful. He wants to see all his students do well, If you go to class he really makes sure you understand the material.

Challenging class, but it is made easier by putting in consistent time and effort. It is also made easier by having a great professor like Chris. I just did standard admission into Kelley and was worried this class might be a roadblock. It took a lot of studying, but between that and Chris, I earned a B+.

K201 was a difficult class for me but England made sure that we spent class time efficiently. He tried lightening up the mood in class and running through various test simulations for exam prep. Overall, solid professor.

Professor England was a great K201 professor! He made sure to teach the concepts in a way we could understand, he would give us advice on Access or Excel even if it wasn't explicitly stated in the textbook. He's willing to sit down with you to help you with Access or Excel in class or through Canvas email and replies back in a timely manner.

K201 is a notoriously difficult class, but Professor England did an outstanding job at teaching the course material and making sure students understood. You can tell he cared about the students' understanding. His Canvas was very well organized and made it possible to find everything you needed to succeed. Brilliant Professor!

I am so glad I had Professor England for K201. He does a great job of explaining the material. You know you are well prepared after his lectures and he makes sure that he doesn't overcomplicate the class. I cannot recommend him enough if you are going to take the class.
Good guy. If you lock in during lectures you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: is not accessible outside of class, never answers emails
Great lectures and every class has something cool or funny to learn about. Blends technology and history and opens eyes to see the world in a different lense.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. is a great guy, funny, and knowledgeable about content. Be ready for weekly written assignments paired with some lengthy readings. TAs were not very good about getting grades in, but if you give thoughtful answers on assignments, you will get 100% on each. Not mandatory, but you need to attend lecture to succeed. Can be incredibly boring.

I don't hate the professor, he's passionate and can be funny. He's very lecture heavy so if you aren't interested in the history of technology it gets very boring. If you just want to take this as an S&H gen ed don't do it. There are much easier gen eds you can find. It takes him forever to grade and there are only two exams so good luck.
Extremely passionate and an easy guy to ask questions/talk to. However he takes very long to grade. Show up to lectures and youll do fine. Only one hw assignment per week.

I am currently enrolled in this class. We are one week away from our second, and final, exam and I have yet to receive a single grade. No homework has been graded, our exam has not been graded. I have spoken with many others in the class and they have the same issue. I have no idea what my grade is and the final exam is in 8 day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really passionate about what he teaches and the lectures are actually interesting. ATTEND THE LECTURES! He's telling the truth that you'll do well on tests if you go to every one. The only downfall of the class is that there's two tests, so be careful!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great at giving lectures. Funny, intelligent passionate about what he does and truly interested/invested in what he teaches.

I thoroughly enjoyed Nathan's lecture style. He is very informative and doesn't have too much texts on the slides. I thought he did an excellent job conveying the material, and the test material was fair.
Horrible professor with the heavy and pointless lecture. He only has 2 exams in the whole semester. So if you fail one of these, you will be get a B only.

Lecture attendance was optional, discussion was mandatory. There are no exams, only 4 quizzes and 4 out of class assignments with a final assignment. He's a good lecturer but is very factual throughout the entire class period. Overall an easy class.
He is not only really knowledgeable about the material, but he is also passionate about it. He is primarily lecture based, would highly recommend for anyone.

He gives comprehensive lectures on the history and growth of information technology. His lectures are interesting if you're interested in tech, otherwise it might be a little dry. He sometimes assigns reading assignments. The textbook is 50% utilized. Exams are blue-book, so attendance is necessary. If you skip class, good luck.
Interesting lectures, reasonable work, easy going guy.
Was a great graduate E&M professor. It was clear he put a lot of time into organizing the class and the grading was more than fair. Office hours were helpful. Highly rec for grad E&M

Enrico is a nice guy that genuinely seemed to care about his students.  Tests were curved to an 80 and there are a lot of free points to cushion students grades. However, this is a difficult class and requires a serious time commitment to do the homework.
Great teacher, readily available to students and very helpful!

The class wasn't easy, but Enrico did his best to help students who reached out. Lecture time was used pretty effectively, and the tests were fair (multiple choice with the ability for partial credit if you showed work). He's extremely smart, and sometimes would go over our heads without realizing it, I think. Overall, good professor.

This class is decently hard. Often times in lecture it would be easy to get lost because he will talk over your head on accident. He's extremely willing to help you out though. My AI saved my life... Exams were multiple choice. He's also pretty funny.

Mr. Vesperini was a great teacher. He is an extremely passionate and driven teacher which is evident through his lectures. The lectures may seem long but they are crucial to understanding course content. Test questions were more than fair and homework assignments take less than 10 minutes. Overall, I would suggest this course.

He was great, the class was very easy, I don't know why everyone is complaining. Easiest A I got while at IU. The lectures can get a bit boring sometimes, but the content is super easy and the exams were online...

For a course called "Stars and Galaxies," we probably talked about stars and galaxies for 25% of the entire class. The rest of the material is so much physics and math, so unless that's your thing, I don't recommend. I liked how the test could be taken remotely, but that could change. Overall, super boring and weirdly hard for an intro class.

The lectures are BORING, but necessary to attend b/c there's in class assignments each lecture that add up and have the potential to make or break your grade. The material was WAY more mathematical and science based than I expected. I struggled with this class & wish I would have chosen a different N&M credit.

Extremely boring professor, at any given moment roughly 10% of his lecture audience will be sleeping because Enrico fails to make astronomy an engaging subject for beginners. Enrico makes you do in class questions that he never explains the answer to, leaving you on your own.

This guy's solid. Not great, but it helps that the material he's covering is pretty basic. More than willing to meet with students and go through things multiple times. Don't feel bad about showing up a bit late as the first 15 minutes or so of each lecture are usually a recap of the previous one.

This class was pretty basic but has some difficult areas and I thought he did an excellent job of guiding our class through them. He understood that not all of us were science majors and gave a lot of credit for effort. He has a thick Italian accent but he still manages to get through. Very patient and easy going!

Was knowledgable in her field but fair warning, she talks very slowly. Overall a fairly easy class as long as you don't mind group work, and she gives a lot of extra credit. I wouldn't take her again because  I could not stand the slow talking, but as an instructor she was fair and good at explaining content.

Easy A+. Gave so much extra credit. The TA was okay but strict, I mean if it weren't for him then I think a lot of us could of gotten away with a lot more stuff i.e. some people cheated/took pics. There is a lot of work but it is easy because even if you don't do anything or put together mediocre work you will still get a B or A on the assignment.

I would rather watch paint dry than spend any more of my time in her class. She has the same stage presence as a young Dane Cook (not good) and seems as if she does not want to be there either. This teacher has not kept up with modern technology nor has she done research on what she is grading and teaching.
I really recommend taking this class with this professor! It was enjoyable and I loved how knowledgable she was about a lot of IT related areas!

Heaviest french accent known to man. Chalk board only. can read handwriting. Rewrite exactly whats on lecture slides. Doesn't know some topics and will tell you flat out. Doesn't know how to work technology. cant make an "easier" test to save her life.

I had her for P201, she does care and tries to be encouraging before exams but she made topics much harder to understand than they needed to be. She would start off doing practice problems but as the semester progressed we fell very behind and stopped doing them. Her exams are significantly harder than what is shown in class.

Several ideas mentioned in p221 lectures were topics covered in Calc 3. While the exams did not require you to use calculus, it made lectures become confusing. She always seemed in a rush, making lectures feel very frantic. The learning we did in class did not reflect on exams, because we had 4 different professors emphasizing different topics

At certain times it felt impossible to succeed in this class. We had 4 different professors throughout the semester because Professor Passemar was never there. Each lecturer had a different teaching style. I think all the other lecturers were easier to understand and better at explaining these topics. She is a good person, but not a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While she can be kind, Prof. Emilie Passemar is a terrible lecturer and fails to explain fundamental physics topics clearly. We did not get to Calculus IV topics in this class which was frustrating! Further, her tests do not reflect the homework well and way too long (the final was 3 hours). Overall, take someone else for Physics 321 if you can!

While she can be kind, Prof. Emilie Passemar is a terrible lecturer and fails to explain fundamental physics topics clearly. Further, her tests do not reflect the homework well, making it difficult to achieve a high score. Overall, take someone else for Physics 222 if you can! Also beware of the 8-10pm exams of P222, its a rite of passage!
