This thing (not sure of gender) is the sorriest excuse for a "teacher" ive ever encountered. She treats this entry level gen-ed course like its law school. Horrible assignments that aren't relevant to the course content. Waits until the semesters is over to grade assignments so you dont actually know your grade. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Really loves to speak her mind about nonsense that no one cares about. Her templates for graded assignments take 30 minutes of prepping to be usable, and she'll still take away points if there's a mistake. Physically cannot make a lesson exciting. Quite literally my most mentally taxing class and I am in multiple 300-400 level classes.
shes not good

Meg does not communicate homework or certain criteria well at all during lectures, is completely unhelpful, is an extremely harsh grader even though this is a 100 level class with people who may not have had experience in public speaking, gives terrible feedback, and is generally very egotistical. don't make the same mistake i did.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very openly biased in her views. When you have a speech you get the feedback on your outline the night/ day before, giving no time to fix what she does not like which is usually most if it. The class is difficult for no reason and she is unwilling to help efficiently. Ridiculous assignments. Overall the worst course Ive taken, STAY AWAY!
I would rather stare at a brick wall for 50 minutes than listen to Margaret Gardiner try to teach. Unfortunately, I have to do both during the duration of this class.

Honestly I was a little upset to see the harsh rating when I loaded up Meg's profile. She has honestly been nothing but great and is deeply passionate about teaching and helping students learn. Wait... no I'm lying. Margaret is basically the golem from lord of the rings if he was like triple the horizontal size and cajun.
grotesque in all its mediums

do not take this professor PERIOD. She will have 7 assignments all due on Sunday. The class is very participation-heavy, you will get a bad grade. A minute of silence at the end of speeches will go by before you're ALLOWED to go back to your seat. She is a tough grader and will take 5 points off for stupid things. DO NOT TAKE HER!!!!!!!!!!!!

seemed nice until I emailed her about the assignment & she ignored my whole question to tell me to look at the rubric. RUDE. And no, my question was not something she covered in class. Her office hours are legit before the class. Makes you stand until someone asks a questions on speech day. Overall very unserious professor.

Absolutely by far the worst professor I've ever had. Expresses her biases in class which goes against the IU Code of Conduct, would not grade anything until the end of the semester , and I overall learned nothing from this class. If you have to take the course as a requirement, DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!!!! I am saving you the stress.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. The most frustrating professor. She grades brutally, and provides un-constructive criticism on assignments. This course is one that all students at IU must take, and for many it is their first experience with public speaking. She does not care, and will score you harshly. It feels impossible to succeed.

Worst instructor I have had by far. Waited until very end of semester to enter grades dating back to January. Thought I was going to end with an A until she finally put in a ton of grades. She is an unreasonably hard grader. If you have to take this speech class, please do yourself a favor and take it with someone else.

Worst instructor I have ever had in IUB. Rude and condescending, and a brutal grader. Very unhelpful in class and in office hours. Does not update course grades in a timely manner and cannot easily be reached through email. It is almost guaranteed you will not do well in this course with her, even though its intro level. Never take her class ever.

Margaret Gardiner is the worst professor I have had at IU. If you have to take a Public Oral Communications course, do not take it with her. I am currently in multiple 300 and 400 level courses, and this 100 level was my lowest grade. She does not respond to emails, and grades remarkably harshly. She is not willing to provide help if needed.

This woman was not respectful of the fact that this is an introductory level speech class and expected students to be amazing imminently. She was an incredibly harsh and did not give good feedback. She was slow to respond to emails and was not interesting in class.

Her class could be interesting, however, she made me feel quite uncomfortable. She wouldn't respond to emails and wasn't very helpful when I asked questions. She unfortunately graded assignments at the end of the semester so you wouldn't know your grades. She had a very strict rubric that didn't make much sense and gave unconstructive criticism.

Class met once a week and you'd think lectures would only be limited however she'd have hours of lectures you need to get done outside of class. Lectures were alright but really boring, and the assignments were alright. The issue were the exams. The only prep we had for the exams were just the assignments we did which were only like 2 assignments

She seemed very knowledgable about what she was teaching; however, she did not teach her knowledge well. She tested us over things that were not taught about, she never corrected herself, and she was outdated with the material she taught. She also showed up to class late and was not good at communicating through a hybrid course. Very unorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she can be very blunt

Vicky is easier compared to many professors I've had at IU, but she is very particular and difficult to please. Her assignments are easy in Public Health Nutrition, as are her exams if you pay attention and study a little. Prepare for a lot of outside volunteer work with this course. The Grant Proposal project is tedious and she will grade it hard.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Vicky is an amazing professor.If you are a Dietetics major, appreciate her eagerness to get you read for the REAL WORLD. Most college students enjoy being 'spoon fed'. Vicky doesn't cater this behavior because it's not realistic. Pay attention, take good notes and participate-- you'll do great with her.

Vicky can definitely be a moody person but you must stay on her good side if you are in the dietetics program. She writes one of your letters of recommendation for internships, so speak up in class, do well on assignments, and be respectful.

It takes a while to get used to Vicky, but she really is a kind professor who explains things very well.  She is always willing to go back if you don't understand something.  She can be moody, which is never fun, but you just gotta push through it.  Her tests are not terribly difficult, but don't go into the test without studying.

Vicki is the head of the dietetics program. If you're in dietetics you WILL have her in many classes. Shes not imposible to get along with but is a pain in the ass. She assigns multiple projects overlapping, w little guidence, & high expectations. She's rude and its "her way or no way" she lives for her job and expects you to live for her class!

Advanced Management Accounting is inherently more challenging than Financial Accounting. However, Professor Sprinkle makes the material manageable and offers a generous curve. It's a great course for students interested in pursuing a path in corporate accounting, and it's also quite feasible to earn an A with reasonable effort.
He is the best teacher I have ever had. Go to class and he will give you very good insight and great grades.

Sprinkle is my favorite professor at IU. He does everything in his power to make sure you will succeed in this class. Even if you do not enjoy accounting, you will still find this class interesting, as it is more focused on evaluating a few interesting parts of managerial accounting rather than broadly covering a bunch of topics.
Best professor in acct department. Very nice person, respect and care every student. No homework at all plus huge curve on exam. Really enjoy his class.

I haven't taken an exam in Geoff's class yet, but he is the nicest, sweetest professor/person I've ever met. I won't have the opportunity to take him again (because I'm a senior), but I will treasure every class period I get to spend with him this semester. Thank you, Prof. Sprinkle- for being the best!

Geoff is a great professor because he wants you to succeed and is genuinely nice. Class material is somewhat difficult but Geoff is fair and will give you a decent grade if he sees effort. The class is overall very fair and well designed.
Very nice professor overall. Willing to help you through every possible means.

Nicest man you will ever meet. He truly cares about the students success. He says all the time in class that he wants to make his tests fair because he wants you to come out of the test and call your parents and feel good about it. Every single problem on the exam (except conceptual) had been done in class or in discussion. Great guy and so helpful

Professor Sprinkle is not only a wonderful professor, but he is great person. He truly cares about the well being of his students. He knows the Kelley School of Business policy of grades lower than a B- and basis a generous grading scale based on test performance. He ensures you do well, this semester a 55% was a C-!

Professor Sprinkle is probably the nicest man I've ever met. Managerial accounting is a very difficult subject, but Sprinkle makes it easier. The whole class is based on 3 tests that are almost solely based on the homeworks. Definitely take Sprinkle if you can.
Really nice professor! Class material is not easy but he makes it clear! As long as you do prepare for every class you will get a good grade.

I absolutely HATE accounting and always have BUT Professor Sprinkle was great.  He grades on a curve and the lowest grade you can get is a B-.  He recently changed his class so there are 3 exams instead of weekly tests, but the exams are EXACTLY like the homework problems he assigns. Overall, great teacher and TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN.
Professor Sprinkle is awesome! The class is graded on a curve, and there are no exams. The weekly tests are pretty easy. Just go to class and you'll be fine.

I did not like accounting coming in and I'm not keen on it going out...but I understand it a WHOLE LOT better than I did because of Prof. Sprinkle. Very open and helpful with the patience of Job, he knows his stuff, if you want to learn managerial accounting he's your man...if you don't WANT to, but HAVE to he's DEFINITELY the guy to go to!
Without a doubt the best professor I've had in my life.  He is genuinely nice, helpful, and completely fair.  If you are able to take A207, do it.  Best decision I ever made.

I'm not an accounting major, so the daily quizzes in A207 were overwhelming.  But Sprinkle was always there to help out before, during or after class.  His grading scale is very generous.  He loves "Top Chef."

Without a doubt the best teacher I have had in my entire life.  It is obvious that Dr. Sprinkle legitimately cares for his students and will do anything he can to help them not only in class but in life.  Don't pass up an opportunity to take his class.

He's a great guy and easy to talk to, however, he often moves too quickly, and his handwriting is bad, so it's sometimes hard to follow along. There's a quiz every week and only one test--the final. He'll try to help you out if you need something. Doesn't give lower than a B.

Sprinkle is the best professor I have had.  He truly cares about every student and will go out of his way to help you.  He is the most down to earth professor I've had...he is really nice guy both as a professor and as a person.  If you can get into A207 don't pass it up...you'll regret it.  I can't say enough about what a great guy he is.

His classes are boring, but he is a nice man and he gives you credit for showing up.  Find a way to keep up with the homework and you'll do fine on his exams.  His questions are usually straight out of his slides and his homework/study problems.
Tough class, very tricky exam
No Comments
Tough class, but he never gives below "C".
absolutely a hard class. Don't be fool by his friendly face. The exams are much harder than he claimed. You'll realize, at the end of semester, he is actually kinda cunning.
He's really nice, helpful, and takes interest in students. The class can be boring sometimes, but he tries to make it fun.
Both a great professor and a great man.  Highly recommend.
He is such a nice man and really cares about the well-being of his students.
Very helpful and friendly...hope to have him again someday as a professor
No Comments
Very good - loves what he does, it shows.
No Comments

Cares a lot about her students, but instructions are not clear and are very confusing. She tries her best to keep things organized but it often ends up all over the place, making it difficult to follow and complete assignments.
So sweet and genuinely cares about her students. Tests are all online (even the final) and you take them at your own time. Attendance isn't rlly mandatory. There is lowk no reason to not end w an A.
Amazing professor, very caring and has an adorable dog that may attend class.
She is a great professor and cares deeply about her students success.

Professor Getz manages to be entertaining and informative; although she does like to read off slides. She encourages class participation and is very forgiving in her grading and attendance policy. Tests are open-note and open-book, but other assignments require a good bit of research and reading. Very accessible outside of class.

Dr. Deb is a great professor. The class is very easy to manage and the assignments are not difficult. The main things you are graded on are tests (which are open notes), chapter summaries, and a final project that you will work on throughout the semester. Dr. Deb is accessible outside of the classroom and wants your feedback to improve her course.

Dr. Deb was a great professor to have. She did have us communicate with one another a lot to keep us engaged. Class was mandatory, but she rarely took attendance and offered zoom if you were sick or just had something else going on. All exams were online, including the final.

She is so nice and cares about her students. The material of her lectures were pretty basic and easy. There were some lessons that were interesting but some others were pointless. Super easy class to get an A in and there is not much coursework to complete.
Really good teacher and all tests and assignments are online.

I love Prof. Getz as a person, but as a prof. she isn't the best. Her lectures were confusing because she made the slides as we went & never really explained anything. We spent 1/2 semester setting "goals" for being a youth worker but never actually learned how to be a proficient one. Super easy class, it's just chaotic & disorganized.

Attendance is not mandatory and the professor was super nice! Prof. Getz grades very fairly and I passed the class with an easy A with minimal effort. I'd honestly just do the work and you'll get the grade you deserve. She also comments positive feedback and tells you what you need to improve on. There was also no final exam but a final project.

Be aware she did not grade our Winter course, personal financial health and wellness, during the instruction period. It was very frustrating. The course was published as a replica to fall 2021, and she talked a lot about a bunch of non-existent workshops expectations. It was all very confusing, and she rarely responded to emails!

Overall, the class is fairly easy. You don't need to attend the lectures since majority of the assignments and coursework are online, however, if you need additional help Prof. Getz is available before or after class and during office hours. The assignments take less than a few hours to do (depending on the assignment itself) but it's an easy A.
Fell behind at the end of the semester, and took the time to reach out and help make sure I did everything I could to get my grade back up.

Dr. Deb is the most caring person ever. She is there if you need to talk about ANYTHING. Her exams are online and open everything. Class is easy, based on a project. DON'T get behind on the study guides, though. Do them while she lectures-they take forever. Would recommend this class, for sure.
A great person but lectures aren't very informative or valuable. A 93.99% is somehow an A- still for a blowoff class which is confusing for an IU course.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring and dont do much of anything

Dr. Getz is an incredible professor and woman. I truly enjoyed being in her class and the material taught was great as well. She truly cares about us as students wanted wants us to succeed. The only part I didn't like was all of the mandatory participation and small group work.

Dr. Getz is very caring and accommodates well to her students needs. Some of the chapters she taught did not match up with the week stayed in the syllabus. A couple of assignments were a bit confusing, but she is always available to talk to. She understand that students have other classes and a life.

Dr. Getz really cares about her students. She is very passionate about what she does and has a lot of knowledge about professionals working with kids. She can sometimes be a little unorganized which can be a little frustrating. Overall, I was very glad I to have had her as a professor. You will enjoy her class.

I like Getz as a person but her class was really disorganized. Her lectures didn't match up with readings so it was hard to know how to prepare for her tests. She assigns chapter summaries which are over 5 chapters at a time so be ready to read a lot. Each class is 25pts attendance so you have to show up even though lectures were pretty pointless.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Getz was the most unprepared teacher I've ever had. She was nice enough but the entire class was very disorganized and confusing.

She had never heard of Purdue OWL and was late for our midterm. Claimed to be organized but consistently had her dates for Assignments wrong. Preacheddemanded spell check but had misspelled words on her slides.

A329 is a tough class, but if you show up to each class, participate, do the homework, and study, you should be fine. Professor is always willing to answer questions in class and outside of class and he responds quickly to emails. Prof Giesler also gives great study guides/topic lists and a double-sided personal note sheet is allowed for exams.

Geisler is very sweet, he learns the name of all of his students, but that does not make up for the absolute disaster his class is. He downloads the book slides, which are awful. He is extremely monotone and I could not learn a single thing in class. His homework is so unbelievably difficult and he provides zero help. Do not take for your own sake.

By far the worst professor I've had at Indiana. He reads directly off of his notes, doesn't teach at all, and rushes through every single thing he goes through. The HW problems he gives are extremely hard and he doesn't give an ounce of help on anything. DON'T TAKE HIM YOU WILL REGRET IT

Professor May is nice and knowledgeable on the subject, with that being said the class was really boring for me so I tended to not really listen to well over the lectures. There is an assignment before every class but they are easy and she grades light. If you need an art and humanity like I did I would recommend this class despite it being boring.

She's a very nice lady and you will get an A if you put in any level of effort whatsoever on the homework. However, she frequently starts class early and ends late. Make sure to have enough of a buffer in your schedule to account for that. The language is easy and fun to learn, though.

Although GER-E162 is an easy class, professor May lectures for a majority of the class time. She's often hard to follow, and goes off on tangents. She expects her students to watch long movies and read entire books before each class, and the majority of the class would agree that the material is boring and unrelatable. However, she's very kind.
she truly wants her students to do well. She sometimes puts the homework up late but she allows you to turn it in the next day if you missed it.

Gergana has a real passion for language and making sure you like what you are studying more than others. Class was taught easy enough that you'll enjoy it and want to learn more and actually gave you information to build Norwegian skill.

I love Gergana! She made Norwegian fun and approachable, and I feel like she is a genuine friend. Make the effort to get to know her, sit up front, and have fun! You will have to put in effort, but its worth it.
Professor May was fantastic and I am looking into taking more classes with her. She is incredibly nice and helpful, and her lectures were much more interesting than most classes that I have taken.

Attendance is mandatory, and her lectures can be boring at points; however, I really liked it. Consisted of pass/fail reading quizzes, 2 pass/fail papers, and a graded final paper. You DO have to read but the tales are very interesting, and if you do this you will pass easy with an A (not blow off tho)i recommend to those looking for a GPA booster

Lectures are all over the place and so random. class is not structured at all. says there would be frequent pop quizzes and there have been 3. didn't enter any grades until 2nd 8 weeks. only attendance, papers, and tests fulfill the grades

Learning objectives completely unclear, class organization is haphazard at best, impossible to tell how you are doing in the class until she gives a grade halfway through the semester. Gergana jumps around topic all the time during her lectures and ends up rambling off-topic for most of class. She is clearly knowledgeable but she's hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Gergana is and will always be my most favourite professor I've ever had! She cares deeply for her students, and makes you want to work harder in her classes. Would recommend highly to anyone taking any classes with her.
Really great over all helps you throughout the process and always makes sure everyone understands what's going on

Excellent teacher. Gives helpful feedback on quizzes and homework which helps you improve and doesn't take off points for every little mistake. She demands a lot of in class participation which dramatically improves your listening and speaking skills. Would recommend for anyone interested in taking Norwegian.

Such a nice professor! Does a good job of incorporating outside elements into the class - like bringing in local Norwegian fiddlers or having teach the class folk dances. The subject matter was pretty boring to me, but she has enough enthusiasm for a whole class. A very kind grader too. Just a great prof, highly recommended.
Gergana is by far my favorite professor I've had so far. Very helpful and insightful, and really forges a connection with her students. Very highly recommended.
Gergana is probably the best professor I've ever had. She's extremely helpful, kind, smart and interesting. I highly recommend taking a class with her!

Please don't take this professor. Everyone was dropping the class, I thought I could tough it out (always had A/Bs) and I was wrong. He writes his own textbook and it makes 0 sense. The test questions were so confusing and I had a friend in another econ class look at them and he didn't understand. DO NOT TAKE PROFESSOR GLOMM!!

If you are taking econ as a pre-requisite, don't even consider him. Do not take his class. He makes EVERYTHING possible SO unclear for us students. He has very old-school ideologies about the world, not just class. Always voices his opinion about anything, doesn't teach doesn't teach DOESN'T EVEN TEACH.
Genuinely the worst professor I've ever had. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS

Just makes everything way harder than it needs to be. You can't get help, either, because he teaches whatever he wants with no structure. He's old and forgets everything and his explanations will just confuse you more. If you're pre-Kelley, drop this class like a hot potato or start scheduling your SPEA classes next semester.

Please, save yourself- especially if you're pre-kelley. It's possible to do well, but just not worth it. You would learn the same amount in less time with another prof. His exam class averages are 60%, he often doesn't give students points they earned, and he does not answer emails. So bad at explaining materia, even during office hours/CL sessions
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not as bad as people make him out to be. More difficult than other econ professors, but if you read his self-made textbook which is literally just the lecture notes, you'll be fine.  Very accessible outside of class, gives extra credit if you go to CL sessions and the in class quizzes are basically free points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: NotebookLM everything paste all his notes in there and don't worry about group projects grades those are actually impossible to get a good grade. Tests are not bad first one is the hardest second one is easy final is medium difficulty just notebooklm videos and quizzes
Horrid professor take with literally anyone else!

Such a bad professor. His lectures are just incoherent rants. His self-written textbook doesn't prepare you for exams. The content is completely different from other B251 classes so there are no outside resources to help you with this class. He doesn't respond to emails and his TAs are no help either. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!
Please don't take it; one grade can destroy you.

He is the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. He made his own textbook for the class, which had canvas quizzes for, but then also assigned another textbook for us to read and had more quizzes on that. He doesn't explain anything, talks about random stuff that has no correlation to economics, and thinks that he is better then everyone else.

Gets a lot of hate because, yes, his course is more difficult than other B251 profs'. However, he is accessible outside class hours and clearly passionate about the subject matter. If you put in the work - a lot of work - you will get duly rewarded. I don't recommend him for pre-bus students.

He's not as bad as some people say he is, but he assigns way too many quizzes, and the research paper is annoying, especially if your group doesn't help you. I'd take B 251 with someone else if possible; however, if you are stuck with him, you'll be fine as long as you put a lot of effort into his class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Just don't its bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take this class with this professor especially if you're pre-Kelley; he uses his own poorly written material over a textbook; has less extra credit opportunities than other professors; last two exam averages have both been in the 60's; only one to do a writing project & gives vague guidelines for them. Very nice and pleasant guy though.

If you put in the work and effort, reading his textbook before every class, reviewing materials, and listening and taking notes during class, you will be fine. It is a hard class, but Professor Glomm is very passionate about the course, also very nice and funny. If you also go to TA hours and his office hours, you will get extra credit and help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He cannot teach well; the only thing that was interesting the entire time was the final day, when he wasn't even talking about economics. He uses his own notes as a textbook and uses the actual textbook for quizzes. The tests have nothing to do with the textbook, and include random numbers from the lecture.

This class was automatically assigned to me as a freshman, and I am still pissed off that I ended up with him. He spent 90% of his lectures talking about random personal things, and he didn't shy away from expressing his opinion. If you have the option, do not choose him or drop the class if you're assigned him.
Glomm never talked about anything related to the course. He would go on tangents, talk about religions and politics, and is incredibly sexist. I do not recommend you take his class.
DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY!! But if you get auto enrolled like I did, then just make sure ONLY to study class notes. The tests have nothing to do with the textbook, though its like 90% of the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took AP micro and macro economics in high school and his textbooks make absolutely no sense. I already happen to know some of the concepts we're learning but if I didn't I would get an F in the class. He writes his own textbook and the Pearson quizzes are extremely hard and have no relation to his exams. Group projects graded super strict

No slides, have to teach yourself outside of class, and includes an extra group research paper that has to be resubmitted and regraded through the semester. Lessons are not focused on test questions, and he kind of just talks about random things that he slightly relates to the lesson in a very not useful way.

Super confusing course since he goes off of a completely different curriculum. Questions on exams are irrelevant to the actual topics and he uses references to in class examples that could easily be glossed over when studying. Don't take please!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Awful professor. If your prekelley, drop. Does not teach the normal curriculum for economics. Test questions make no sense and even ai doesnt get more than 70%. Lectures are full of random rants and zero preparation for the tests. Do. Not. Take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
RUN - if you can
if you have the choice of taking it next semester, DO IT

if you are stuck in this class, few things to note:
- unlike AP Macro and Micro (mostly new material)
- 3 exams (including final) which are very hard even if you study

the way he structures the class makes it VERY Hard

glomm himself isn't actually that bad
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dude is genuinely the worst teacher I've ever had. If I could give him a 0 I would. He talks about random stuff most of class, that is not even related to econ, he writes his own textbook that doesn't even make sense. The things he puts on the tests aren't even in the text book or about what he discusses in class. Don't know how he has a job

Do not take Glomm. Trust me. He teaches his own textbook in class and the tests have nothing of it on them. He also rambles about nothing in class and then out of nowhere comes back to the material. Most classes I don't even know what to take notes on because I dont know what I need to know. Do not take this class.

**DO NOT TAKE**Genuinely the worst professor/teacher I've ever had. Racist, sexualized students, and astonishingly bad at teaching. No explanations, no thought behind lectures, questions are worded in "his own way", with that way being nonsense. The fact he gets paid to "teach" blows my mind and how he still has a job is incredible.

Does not give any grading criteria for any work or project. Does not use Canvas page in any conventional or meaningful way, vital info is scattered everywhere with no care for student comprehension. Makes up lectures as they go along. No structure to curriculum. No grades posted 2 months in. Overall very aloof and in no way helpful to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He has a unique teaching style, with content being derived not from the textbook, but from course material that he has created, so it maybe a little biased to his perspective. He gives group projects, hates the use of AI, and it's not going to be easy to get an A or even B+ at all! But he is very caring, and ready to help, but gotta make use of it!
Glomm is incredibly difficult, and his classes are not worth taking. Save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: No grading criteria. Grades based off whatever he's feeling in the moment. No feedback. Won't post instructions for projects & only tells you one time in class. 5/7 grades are group projects. Won't put in grades until after drop point. Tells you to go to office hrs but will talk for an hour & not answer 1 question. Lectures/textbook made up by him.

This honestly is probably the worst professor i've had at IU. His projects literally have no rubric and he will give you zeros for assignments even if you correct them because they're not what he wants. If you don't want to fail, i would drop. he just put grades in after the drop date so that people are stuck in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be prepared for your ears to bleed. One of the worst professors at Indiana University.

I wish I could give a rating of 0, genuinely. Gerhard is probably the worst professor I have ever had the displeasure of dealing with. He doesn't give ANY rubrics, grades are arbitrary, and he is SO cocky for someone who doesn't know how to do their job. He should retire at this point before he wreaks havoc on the lives of more innocent students.

Worst teacher I've ever had. His textbook is self-written, full of incomplete and incoherent thoughts. He never has a point and is noticeably sexist. His lectures were so disorganized and pointless, all he did was rant about unrelated topics and he never EVER finished a thought. I learned nothing, I am so lucky to have passed this class, STAY AWAY.

I have to disagree with the previous posters--if you're interested in actually learning the material, and being challenged, then this is the professor/course for you. Prof. Glomm doesn't make things easy, but in the long run, I feel like I'm better prepared for future econ courses than I would otherwise be.
Just an awful teacher- the textbook did not help either. Be prepared for a lot of self study. Also, he goes off on random tangents in class and his attempts at humor are just bizarre.
Very difficult, complex concepts with sketchy explanations at best, and in a voluminous multitude, with little or no correlation to the book assignments... which he then expects you to complete
Terrible.
I learned an amazing amount. Even if he is "intimidating", he wants you to succeed in his course, and will help you do so.

Prof.Glomm's language: "I'm here the one asking questions!" Which means you as a student better sit still and keep quiet. Students are not encouraged to ask questions. Expect long formulas copied from a list without explanation behind them.
He should probably make his course more challenging.  He's incredibly helpful, and full of great advice that one should strive to follow.
No Comments
No Comments
Intimidating, but fun.
No Comments

Professor Ghoshal is extremely supportive and understanding. He is kind and approachable and always willing to go the extra mile to help his students succeed in his class. I would gladly take more classes with him if I could and strongly recommend him both professionally and personally 👍🏻
Im a senior, never rated a professor so far. Currently, a pass is a 45% because of how poorly the class did on the midterm; my friend received a zero and still wasn't far from average.
He is a genuinely caring teacher who goes above and beyond to support his students and help them succeed.

I am so displeased with this class that I had to make an account on this website just to add this professor. He does not know how to make a curriculum for a class. Before the midterm, we were only assigned *1* homework assignment, which has yet to be added to the gradebook. Practice exam was useless, lecture notes unreadable, avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were long and full opinions being preached onto students making it difficult to sit through. Short answer quizzes weekly, worth 50% of your final grade and answers were specific based on what the professor believed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As long as you do the reading and participate in class, this will be an easy win! Pragya was dedicated and passionate, and is great for discussions! Easy to reach out to and doable assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: For Screening Gender and Sexuality, Pragya was a wonderful teacher and was great at facilitating conversation. The beauty of this class is that you will get a good grade as long as you at least show you are trying. 10 reflection papers (1 per week - 1 page length) a midterm presentation and paper, and a final paper.

This individual does not provide any information on how to submit assignments but yet he expects it to look the way he imagined. I highly encourage everyone to avoid taking his class, it is boring, attending lecture does not help even though it is mandatory, and for every absence he will take 10 points off.

This is supposed to be a very easy class maybe an average class difficulty wise at most yet i'm a STEM major and this class is my lowest grade. He takes off points off for every little thing. He grades extremely harsh. There is a overload of pointless assignments. His lectures are boring but you have to show full participation at 8am.

Lectures don't help with learning, but are required because attendance counts for a grade. Assignments are hard to find. Extremely hard grader and isn't sympathetic when it comes to covid. Really thought this was going to be an easier class this semester when the workload and expectations makes it harder than some of my major requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is kind and helpful when you ask him questions. VERY tough grader and LOTS of busywork. Not my fav or least fav just meh. The class in general is stupid but that's not his fault. Always answers to emails very fast!
He doesn't know what the assignment is, what it asks for or when its due. Then he takes off points for the most ridiculous things. You'd be better off taking speech in person.
Do not recommend. stupid hard at grading, gives little instruction on assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super Nice! She's a fantastic teacher who cares about her students. We had 2 group projects throughout the class. She doesn't grade too harshly and is very understanding on grading. Maybe sure to keep up with the homework and to attend class (participation/ attendance is its own grade). definitely take her class!

Prof Mirelli's classroom is relaxed but discussion heavy. You have to participate often to get points. She is great at including everyone and giving individual help. Sincerely wants all her students to do well and teaches interesting lessons! Probably my favorite Spanish professor at IU.

Had her for S280. She's really sweet. There's A TON of work (reading, movies, papers, & other stuff). Tests were kinda difficult and not much time was given. Grades on participation, but she gives a lot of opportunities to participate. If you have a good class, it's fun (mine was awkward, so it was boring). Final was just our last test, online.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great professor. Helped a lot at improving my Spanish. Definitely recommended for a great experience. I hope I have her for another course.

Giada is one of best professors I have had at IU. She is funny and younger so she knows how to teach college students. She makes classes interactive and participation is important but easy to get if you show up.
genuine, caring professor who is truly passionate for her students and their learning. class is super interesting and applicable to daily life
Dr. Githiri connects everything in her lectures to real life, it is difficult to not be engaged in her class. I would definitely recommend this class.

One of the best professors I've ever had at IU ( coming from a second semester Junior). Her lectures are all real life examples and class never feels like a waste of time. I feel like I got to know Dr.G as a person through her personal stories and interactions. She is incredible and works so hard to make sure her students succeed. I love Dr.G!!
Taking this class online, the professor was great and the work load was very easy and very manageable! Prof Githiri had great lectures and was very accessible via email.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. G is 100% my favorite professor I have ever had. I genuinely could not recommend her enough. I finished with a 100%. She does not give any exams or quizzes. The only homework is discussions which don't take long. She does use tophat for attendance most days, so go to lecture. She is SO funny and caring which makes it easy to attend lecture

Professor Githiri is caring and respectful of her students. She is really hilarious, makes class enjoyable, and really wants her students to succeed. It's an easy class if you do the homework, quizzes, and take notes.

TAKE DR. G!!! She is hilarious, engaging and an overall amazing professor -- I hope I get to have her again while at IU. Participation is mandatory, but the class has no exams (1 final group project).
Dr. Githiri is an excellent professor. I took Community Health during the semester we were sent home, due to Covid in spring 2021, I would have loved to finished the course in person.
Dr. Githiri was awesome during this pandemic! It is obvious she cares for her students. Definitely take her class if you have the opportunity!

Dr. Githiri is a bit disconnected & lacks clear communication. She doesn't send out any announcements, so check for assignments often. Most of the work is group assignments, so you can split it up between your group members. When emailing her, I've received unhelpful responses. She seems to grade for participation, which I like, so I'm indifferent.

If you have to take this class online be ready for a lot of work and very few lectures. Starts off easy and then out of nowhere you have to do a bunch of group projects with very little direction. Assignments will take you a minimum of 1 hour and there are about 2-3 due each week
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: She is the nicest professor I have had yet. Very caring and takes it easy on you in the pandemic. Do the assignments and you will do very well in this class. Always willing to help when you ask. The weekly lessons take no time and since I found this topic interesting, I was ready to engage with it. No final exam either, just a paper and video pres.

Virginia is so funny and sassy, will definitely have you laughing in class. I took one of her in person classes a year ago and just finished with her online class. She has not adapted well to 100% online but you can tell she cares about her class and her students. One of my favorite professors, would always suggest taking a class with her!
Love her! I enjoyed taking this class and her humor makes class entertaining, would take it again in a heartbeat, she made me appreciate my major on a greater level.
Dr. Githiri was super sweet and definitely cares about her students. Not only that, the class was super easy and as long as you show up and do the assignments, you will easily get an A.

This class is literally so easy. All you have to do is show up to class and do the top hat. Professor Githiri is SO funny and makes the class more enjoyable. There is a small group project at the end but she gives you class time to do it so you don't have to work on it outside of class! Take this class even if you don't have to, its an easy A.

Dr. Githiri allowed me to appreciate my major and find the meaning behind it. I was able to grasp the main concepts and see how my job in the future is going to help people. I liked that she made the lectures interactive this made me want to show up for class  the projects corresponded with the lecture which allowed me to do my research.
LOVE her

Dr. G is hands down one of the best professors i have ever had. She is hilarious and gives good real life examples of everything she talks about. She knows how to make is feel comfortable during topics that may be uncomfortable. She knows when to be serious and when to be fun. One of my favorite classes and professors ever.

Guys, Dr.G is one of my favorite professors ever. Super caring and funny, lectures sometimes end earlier because they're so easy but are very helpful. If you get a good and caring team for the assignments and projects, this class is a super easy A. Loved her!

Dr, Githiri is the best professor. She makes her lectures so fun and easy to learn. the homework assigments are more busy work, not difficult at all. Tests are straightforward if you pay attention in class. Participation points earned through class so attendance matters.

Dr. G is by far one of the best professors at IU. If you are having a bad day you want to go to her class. She will have you laughing in the first 3 minutes. She has grades in pretty quickly, responds to emails in a timely manner, and is willing to work with you if you missed an assignment or have something going on. Take this class.

Amazing woman, so kind and knowledgeable.  Doesn't go out of her way to make class difficult because students are already interested in the subject and she wants to encourage their success.  Hilarious, with interesting career experience.  Never missed a class because of how captivating her teaching style was.
Loved this class. Just do the work and you will do well. I plan on taking another class with her.

Incredibly nice and knowledgeable. The class is an easy A and she makes it fun enough just through her own mannerisms and stories. Also good about stressing the real-world significance of the material If Dr. G teaches your course, consider yourself lucky and register before it fills up- and it will do so quickly.

Dr. G is by far one of the best professors at IU. It's very easy to pass her class, she's super nice and funny, lectures are interesting, and exams are straight forward. For my class she even allowed us to use an index card. I would totally recommend Dr. G for any class she teaches.

Dr G is really funny. She has good info for lectures. All her classes are easy and designed for you to get an A. I took two of her classes and I feel like someone would have to make an effort to get anything below a B+. Majority of points are from group projects. You will most likely have a presentation instead of a written final

Never pass up a chance to take a class with Dr. Githiri. She is by far the nicest teacher I've ever had. She responded to emails fast, was very clear about assignments, and graded easy. She is funny and everyone liked showing up to class. Stress free class with the best teacher!

Dr. G is the best! This was my second class with her and I loved it.  She respects student's time and ends lecture early.  Takes attendance on occasion.  Don't buy the textbook.  Exams were online and the group project was really easy, while learning a lot.  Great course! Absolutely take it with her!
Dr. G is great.  She keeps her lectures short and her exams are online.  Course saved my semester GPA. Got a 100% in the course and hardly tried.
Great teacher! SOOOO NICE! She is very helpful and funny. Very easy class, she grades very easily. Great class.

She is the best.  If you're a public health major, def take a class with her.  She's hilarious and class is easy as long as you go and turn in the assignments, which are never complicated.  She also has real world public health experience that she uses as examples in class which really helps you see the types of jobs you can get with your major.

Makes no effort to teach, and I mean that literally. The average lecture is setting up zoom for 10 minutes, taking attendance for 20 minutes, and then the rest of the time is narrating his way through setting up the class website, calling on students to ask them random irrelevant questions, and reading assignment instructions.

Extremely nice professor but I feel like he's not built for teaching. Half the lectrues are spent with him narrating what he does ("I will click on this website and then click here and then do that and then..."). He also spend the first 35 minutes talking about attendance and rambling about assignment deadlines. Hes a smart guy but not good teacher

I could spend more time articulating Dan's horrendous communication than focusing on any one of his lectures. He has no filter and knows no bounds to being passive aggressive. Lectures are miserable. Remember that your professors were hired for their knowledge, not their basic most communication skills.

Professor German is easily one of the best professors at IU. He genuinely cares about his students and clearly loves what he does. His passion for teaching shows and he truly wants all his students to succeed. He puts in the effort to make sure you're learning and is always approachable when you need help.
He only has high ratings because he gives out easy A's. This man can't teach to save his life. I thought H212 would be better than C212, but I was wrong

Professor German is easily one of the best professors I've had at IU. His expectations are clear, and you can tell he genuinely cares about his students. He's super approachable and always willing to help. If you get a chance to take his class, definitely do it.

One of the best professors at Luddy surrounded by truly excellent graduate staff. He truly cares about his students actually learning subjects from my experience. There is no “bad” question in his class and he is extremely open to sharing his wealth of knowledge and walking through students at any pace without judgement.
very passive aggressive. available for office hours to make up any assignments, if you want to get grilled on the topic for missing it when it was due.

He's an easy A usually. Our midterm was on 27 chapters; we had only covered 5 of them at the time. Our final was composed of 2 final projects and our writing two front-to-back pages on paper per chapter, for a total of 54 pages. still got an A, but took me way too much time. He uses the same broken code from a decade ago and asks you to copy it.

Great class if you don't want to learn anything. He gives you the code solutions for nearly all the homework. Look, I tried. I really wanted to learn stuff, but he's honestly not good at teaching. He'll get caught in random tangents that go nowhere that'll just confuse you. So why not just copy and paste what he gave you?

Professor German is super helpful and makes himself very available for extra support. The course can be a bit disorganized, but he genuinely wants everyone to succeed. unstuck study and office hours were key for staying on top of things.

Lectures are terrible, as he spends pretty much half of the time just setting up and taking attendance. His class/assignment layout is the worst I've ever seen, and it looks like it has been used since the early 2000s. Don't take this class if you want to actually learn anything useful.

You will not learn anything you didn't teach yourself. The class structure is awful. If you want an A with little effort, take the class. Otherwise just take C212. Ratings for professors that give out easy A's are inflated by students who don't care to learn anything.
If you like to learn I'd 100% recommend this professor. He is a little tuff but as long as you try your best and attend class you will pass. He's a very reasonable and funny man. 1000/10
Adrian German is very funny, cares about your learning, is extremely passionate and knowledgeable on the topics, and definitely wants to see every student succeed.

Funny guy who will literally do everything he can to make sure you get a good grade as long as you are willing to try. He holds office hours literally every day waiting to help people who are behind, I've never met a professor more willing to help than him. Overall, he's awesome.
at this point, I WOULD TAKE ANY CLASS HE TEACHES.

Midterm covers the entire semester of material, even material from the second half of the class that he hasn't taught yet. So you need to memorize 26 design patterns when you've only learned five in class so far. And then, you need to play a game with him where you guess your exam grade and you lose points if you guess wrong. Awful.

Literally love him, took his class and last year! He is great, and actually cares for you, and even teaches you agains and again if you go to his office hours. He is everything you need in a professors. He is an exception from the typical arrogant Luddy professors dying for DOD money.

His lectures are hour long rambles with no substance. He'll spend an entire lecture helping a student do an assignment that was due three weeks ago. Nice for them, I guess, but it's painfully boring and you have to go for attendance. Way more time is spent fiddling with your websites instead of the actual material we're supposed to be learning.

His rating is only high because he gives out easy A's, but you won't actually learn anything. The homework is just following old, unclear, and incomplete directions that you'll need to attend office hours to understand. Lectures are a slog. He'll spend the first half hour of every class taking attendance and setting up zoom. Attendance is required.

He has the best office hours system I've seen, always available for a meeting. He lets you go to class in person or on zoom. I do feel he makes his class to easy. He gives out solutions for every assignment, which can be good or bad depending on your preference. Lectures are useful sometimes, but can also be all over the place. Overall he's good.

Professor German is a helpful and funny guy. The class was a little disorganized, and expectations on assignments were often fuzzy, but he is extremely available for additional help. You get what you put into this class, and the grading is very easy. Submit all assignments and ask for help when needed, should be a guaranteed A.

You will pass the class as there are no due dates and the answers are practically given to you. You will not learn anything unless you can really teach yourself from the books. Lectures are really boring as he spends 20 minutes taking attendance and just rambling, and is all over the place. Does not really teach well and just reads off the books

how is he rated so highly?? nice guy but not a great teacher. the directions on everything he assigns are so confusing. you'll do everything the directions say on an assignment and then later get a 75/100 to find out you had to do something else that wasn't even listed in the directions

Took this class last semester. The way he teaches the class is really strange. His directions are extremely unclear and so trying to know what you actually have to do in the labs and homework is a pain. He's funny and nice and a good guy but his teaching style is all over the place, confusing, and unclear

I personally really did not like his teaching style; I found it hard to follow and his criteria/what he was looking for was really vague. That being said, the class is a lot of work but he genuinely just wants you to learn the material. He had the most forgiving turn in policy (2 weeks after the due date no penalty no questions asked).

He definitely has a unique teaching style and his lectures can be pretty confusing at times, but he genuinely wants everyone to get an A and makes it super easy to earn full credit. I've also never seen a professor dedicate so much time to office hours, so you will not have a problem clearing up any confusion. Highly recommend!

German is a very rare breed. He is hysterical for one. For two, he couldn't care less whether you turn anything in or not. If you go to his office hours enough times, he'll just do the homework for you and give you an A. The amazing thing is, even with his lack of requirements and extreme flexibility, I still learned so much from him. Truly rare.

If you put in effort Prof German will bend over backwards to help you pass. The class is difficult, but the amount of opportunities given to students is amazing. I graduated in 2015 so it's been a long time, but I remember him letting me retake a quiz I'd bombed during office hours. If you make an effort then so will he.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor German has awesome programming skills. He is very accessible and helpful. He has an appointment system, and you can see all his available time through the system. He is available almost every day until late at night, even during the summer and winter break. If you study every day, I am sure you will get a good grade. Best professor ever!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: German's lecture is easy to understand. And he is very patient so if you get any question during the lecture, just go to his office hour, he will try his best to help you. And he doesn't want his course to be tough. Even if you did a bad job in one exam, once you think you are well-prepared. You can retake it again and still get the full credit.

Professor German is fantastic. He cares deeply about his students and you can tell he wants to see each one of them succeed. German makes himself available to students and goes out of his way to help students understand the material. Fair grader, compassionate, interesting, and knowledgeable. He is truly IU's best. Can't recommend him enough!

Professor German is in the top 1% of Computer Science professors in the country. He genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed and reach new heights. His focus on understanding the student point of view sets him apart from other professors. Take a class with him and with an ambition to learn and you wont regret it.

Professor German was my first CS professor at IU. He really helped build my base and the tips he has given are invaluable. Such as expect errors when compiling and clean up your code when stuck. For that reason I rank Prof German 1% of CS professors. Take a class with him and visit Prof German with an attitude to succeed and he wont let you down

Never had tests, only HW and Labs. Also never had a due date, most kids just put everything off and turned in everything at end of semester. I stopped going to Zoom lectures cause he would ramble. At the end of the semester he just gave out A's to most of the kids, I was missing nearly half of my HW and never did the final project. Nice guy too.

Adrian is one of my favorites Professors at IU, I am not a CS major or minor so I know nothing before taking this class, but he always happy to answer questions. He contributes a lot of time for office hours even during the weekends or after midnight. This is not a demanding class but you definitely need to pay attention during the class.

Prof. German was a great professor, he has this really goofy personality that keeps you engaged and interested in the material and the class and he was always really understanding when it came to deadlines and make up work. I learned a lot of java under him, and I don't think I would've passed IU's Data Structures class without his help.

German is one of my favorite professors in this school. He is diligent since he held office hours basically every day - even when it is the weekends or Thanksgiving week. He loves to help students with their problems. Easy A for this class if you could attend office hours when your confusion happened. Will recommend this professor in that case.

Professor German is the best professor I've ever met at IU!! I toke 2 classes with him. He is very responsive and cares about every single students in the class. I got email back even in holidays. He hosts office hour every single day and you can easily make appointment online to reserve a time slot. Class instructions and grading were clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor German is the best instructor I have ever met at Indiana University. He was always trying hard to know students' needs, and he set office hours almost every day to help his students solve their problems inside and outside the class. Also, the contents in Professor German's lectures are interesting and you will find them really useful.

Professor German is dedicated to the success of his students. His humor, experience, knowledge, and commitment are demonstrated in the sublime quality of his lectures and support. Even with hundreds of students enrolled in his classes each year, he is always well prepared, organized, and available to help anyone. He genuinely cares about students.

Professor German is the best professor I have ever met in all aspects! His lectures are easy to follow, with excellent pace and detail, and opens to questions Assignment/exam grades can be improved in OH, which he holds 8hrs daily, devoted to helping students You can learn a lot and succeed in his courses with all the resources he provides

I also took 211 and 322 with German. German is the most empathetic professor I've had at IU. Whether it be explaining complex topics or helping with assignments, German is always willing to go the extra mile to explain things. He is a great professor and an even better person. There is a lot of work, but most of it helps you learn.

Professor German was the first CS professor I had, and he is one of the most memorable ones among all the others. He genuinely cares more about students learning the material than the students' grades. I have never had a professor sacrifice as much of his time for office hours. He is always available to help, no matter the time. Amazing professor!

German is a super nice guy and the class is very easy, but he is very unorganized and is very hard to follow. He constantly jumps around from topic to topic and gives very vague answers to your questions. You never know what is expected of you and you always feel like you're missing something.

If you want to genuinely learn about computer science, avoid taking classes with German. His lectures are awful. His thought processes are never linear, they're absolutely all over the place. Yes he allows remakes of everything, and you WILL get an A in this class, but you will get nothing out of it and it will be a waste of your time.

He is not great at explaining things. You will rely on the textbook, classmates, or SICE tutors when you're confused. He has plenty of office hours available but he can be kind of... aggressive. He allows you to make up any HW and retake tests so it is possible to get 100 in the class. Beware: to make up HW you must write the entire code by hand.
He's a great lecturer, and makes himself readily available outside of class. He also lets you retake tests for full credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not much more to say than he's occasionally funny because of his awkward humor during lecture. His class average gpas are usually around 2.7, whereas other professors' are closer to 3.1 or so. He doesn't spend much time in lecture explaining relevant material, and gives most of his grading to TAs. Worse than my AP CS-A Java class.

A great professor very accessible and always helpful. Holds enough office hours that you can go to them whenever you need to. A great professor and cares about all his students. Tough but fair as long as you put in the work you can get a good grade.

Literally the best teacher at Indiana University. Super nice and accessible, hosts office hours whenever you need them. Grading is tough but fair. Also you can retake anything. Take this professor you won't regret it!

Much of what is covered in lecture is not related remotely to the homework or exams, which tend to follow the textbook, so if you decide to take a class with him, make sure to read the textbook and understand it. If I had done so from the beginning, I have no doubt I could've received an A on this class, even as someone without any Java experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Caring prof who allows you to make up hw, exams, and projects to improve grade, so not hard to get an A. However, one of my worst experiences. If you have no Java experience, the beginning will be stressful. Exams sometimes test content hardly covered in class. 3rd exam (take-home) and final project focused on concepts not covered in any capacity.
Easy grader. You can retake anything. Easy A. Problem is he is maybe the most boring person Ive seen in my entire life. Schedule your sleeping time during his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great professor, if you need help, you can get it almost anytime.
Dan was a great professor! Very accesible and funny. It's true that he's an easy grader and you can probably get by without learning much but I felt like it was a great balance!

he is probably the easiest professor ive had, really friendly too, he will show you memes when you go to his office hours.  he from romania not germany. funny accent. you can pass his class without breaking a sweat and thats exactly why you will not learn anything, because he won't make you work very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Best professor for Software Systems. Even if you want, you will not miss lectures, they are very interesting. Very generous assignment and exam policy. Always available for any help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed him for my c211 and c212 courses. He is a very nice person and a great professor. Go to his office hour if anything confuse you and he has his office hour everyday and almost all the time. If he is not in lecture, he's doing office hour. You can't find any professor like this.

This professor will be one of your favorite teachers in your college career! He genuinely cares about you learning! Don't be discouraged by his confusing lectures! If you go to his office hours he will do whatever takes to will you through learning the material. His personality is also uniquely hilarious! Give him chance! He's an amazing person!

Professor German is the best Professor I've had at IU so far. He respects his students, learns everyone's names, and goes out of his way to make sure everyone understands the course material. He is a little confusing, but his willingness to help  gives you lots of opportunities to learn. I would, and probably will, take a class from him again.
He has kind of a weird way of explaining things, but if you go into his office hours he is very helpful and makes sure you understand the material. Really cares about his students.

Professor German is one of the best teachers to help with your introductory Computer Science classes. Although he is not always clear, he will help you understand every concept. If you do poorly on assignmentsquizzestests, he will let you make them up and give significant credit back. Confusing at times, but still helpful.

Dr. German is a very smart man and sometimes lectures and material can be very confusing. That being said, he only wants the best for every student and if you visit office hours you will do fine no matter how terrible your programming skills are.

What he lacks in organization during lecture, German makes up for it with his care for students.  He has an insane amount of office hours and is pretty intentional with getting to know you.  If you end up taking his class, GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS.  That's where you will learn the most.

Amazing professor, I was struggling in C211 and he stuck with me and helped my grade out a ton towards the end. Now I'm in his C212 and I'm doing much better, he cares a lot about his students and wants you to do well, but he'll challenge you as well.

He was by far the best professor I had last semester. Intro to comp sci classes are just made to be tough and I felt like I was way in over my head but if you make an effort, He would love to help you. He is a very nice guy and loves to be funny. GO TO OFFICE HOURS, it will be so worth your time. I would 100% take any class he teaches.
German is inconsistent with emails and sometimes doesn't follow through with things he says he will, but he does care about his students plenty and will want to help you do well.

Professor German is by far my favorite professor I have ever had at Indiana University. He is very scattered, and unorganized. But if you truly need help, reach out to him! He is the nicest guy out there and is always there for his students when they are struggling to understand the material.

Professor German is by far my favorite professor I have ever had at Indiana University. He is very scattered, and unorganized. But if you truly need help, reach out to him! He is the nicest guy out there and is always there for his students when they are struggling to understand the material.

He was a great professor! If you are struggling, I definitely suggest going to office hours. I took it in the summer. He really does want you to pass and is willing to work with you to get you where you want to be as long as you put in the effort!

Professor German is a very nice, funny guy.  He really wants his students to do well, so if you put in the effort, you should be able to get a good grade.  My only complaint is that he was he was slow getting assignments & grades back to us.

Great Prof, those who try in his class will succeed. Best Prof I have had at IU. Had him in the fall, and found out he taught one class during the summer, I rearranged all my classes and summer plans just to take it with him. If you have the option take any class you can with him!

This class is extremely easy to do well.  Adrian offers make-ups on EVERYTHING, including exams.  He has an odd sense of humor and is sometimes difficult to understand, but has a very awesome sense of humor.  He truly cares about his class and wants everyone to do well.  You have to put out REAL effort in order to do badly in this course; easy A.

German is an excellent and friendly teacher. Compared to Lara-Dammer for C211, this class was a godsend. This class was taught with Java, covering basics to GUIs to an intro to web programming with Groovy on Grails. I definitely recommend Professor German for this course.

This guy may be one of the nicest professors at IU. His lectures are a little confusing, but they are laid out and uploaded online verbatim, so you shouldn't fall behind. Other than attendance points, there's no reason for this class to hurt your grade. Dan is VERY helpful and is a great professor, so go ahead and sign up already.

Professor German really cares about his students.  He has a huge amount of office hours and responds promptly to e-mails.  He wants everyone to get an A and more importantly, he wants everyone to learn.
BEST professor I've ever had, in any department.  Try to take C211 with him.  He provides the textbooks so students don't have to buy them.

Hands down the best teacher I could ever have. Not only is he willing to put you before everything else in life. But he cares more about you learning, more than the grade. He will give you a good grade if you go and talk to him and show it to him that you care. Attendance is a must. He's also funny with his jokes.

Do yourself a favor and schedule office hours with him. His classes can be disorganized and you may have a hard time learning, but he will meet with you at ANY TIME. He truly cares, and will help you out as much as need be to help you understand. I have yet to have a professor that cared as much as he did. Go to the damn office hours.

His lectures were scattered, unfocused, and generally incomprehensible, but I heard he was helpful if you asked him outside of class. We never got a single grade for anything and I actually stopped turning in assignments half way through and still got a B. He was nice and entertaining but not very effective.
Great teacher who truly cares about his students and his work. Definitely one of my favorite teachers I have had at IU.

Yeah he's nice, yeah he's funny, but that doesn't matter because he goes too fast and does not explain what he's doing. Read the book, get help from AIs, go to peer tutoring. Also, he's terribly disorganized. Don't expect to get feedback on labs or homework. You can probably get an A, but how much you actually learn is completely up to you.

He is one of my favorite professors at IU.  I thought I would have a hard time in Java since I hated 211.  He has a ton of office hours to help you out if you get in a bind.  Keep up with homework as it will bite you in the butt if you don't.

This is a fun professor to learn from. I was afraid I wouldn't learn anything from Adrian, but was delightfully surprised when his wealth of experience made me feel like a novice. His teaching methods rock! The only downside is that he's even more disorganised than I am. His disorganisation doesn't matter because he responds to questions promptly.
All you have to do is show up and you will pass. Assignments are a breeze and you don't even have to think. Highly recommended.

Very nice guy but from my (limited) experience you won't get your money's worth from his class. CS290 was easy but the course quickly lost focus (we started doing random installations) and he began showing up late to lectures habitually.

rambles on and on but is quite funny. didn't really understand much. grade was based on "a conversation to understand if you understood much during the semester" very helpful has office hours like everyday

Professor German is one of my favorite professors I have had so far at IU. He is very knowledgeable, very friendly, and is even willing to help you once you are out of his class. I would highly recommend taking a class with Professor German.
Impossible to understand, doesn't seem to realize that no one can keep up with him.

Professor German is very helpful and seems to have 24/7 availability. He is often late to class but maybe this is related to his office hours. Given his generosity in grading, availability, and answers to problems, it is unreasonable to complain about his lateness to lectures. However, he is slow at getting official grades posted.
He is a cool guy
good
Going to office hours is definitely worth it- he's really helpful plus has a great sense of humor. highly recommend!

He's very willing to help you but he's not particularly clear with his help.  It's hard to really understand him unless you're willing to put in the time or energy.  I spent a lot of time in his office talking, but I would not work with him again.
Adrian is my favorite Comp Sci professor. He's down to earth and more than willing to help you even after you take his class.

Nice guy. Incredibly disorganized. Consistently showed up ~5 minutes late to class, and was more than half an hour late to labs on at least 3 occasions despite the fact that his previous class was 5 minutes away. VERY lenient, allowing you to wait 'till end of semester to turn in assignments, and let us give ourselves a grade at the end.

German is off da hizzook.  Very crazy, easily offended, hilarious.  He has repeatedly been more than 30 min late to lab.  His teaching style leaves much to be desired, but he definitely is willing to make sure you succeed in his class.
had german for A201... disorganized, didn't understand when students failed to comprehend. seemed helpful, but the required book was absolutely no help. (his book)
No Comments
Adrian is a nice guy.... However, he should not be teaching an introductory course in anything!  He lacks the ability to know when students fail to comprehend the material.

Adrian is very unorganized.  He does give many opportunities for extra-credit and truely wants everyone to get an A.  He will do all he can to help students.  He does have a small problem recognizing when the class as a whole doesn't understand a concept.
Amazing professor. I thought I would struggle with this class, and it has been really easy thanks to him.

It's hard not to like this guy, despite his lack of effectiveness as an instructor. An incredibly nice person, he's willing to spend hours with you in his office -- hope you've got the time, or can teach yourself from a book!
Adrian is very willing to help you - has a great sense of humor.
No Comments
Hands down: This man in insane. But he's fun to watch, good class
Programing is not easy and he tries very hard to make it understanable.
No Comments
adrian rules
Dan'
Adrian is a really nice guy. However, he is not a particularly effective teacher
Adrian is a wonderful one-on-one teacher. Try to get him for smaller classes.
Very funny, willing to work with you.
Side-tutoring and is more concerned with student learning material than deadline

Shows up late to class often. Rarely communicated online assignments. Often wouldn't tell us about exams/in-class assignments till a day before. Took a month+ to grade exams. Would never go over vocab. Very disorganized.
shows up late often, workload is easy and the professor is nice. Grades are rare to come in and online homework assignments were not communicated well.

Weirdly showed up late to class every day. Would cancel sometimes. Most lazy grader I've ever had, tests would sometimes be graded 3 weeks after. Easy class, but came ready to learn and lost motivation after teacher couldn't even show up on time. She's nice and all just unprepared

I genuinely did not learn a thing from her. She came to class late every single day and never entered grades. Grading expectations were nonexistent. The class was easy so I guess it was fine?? But least prepared professor I have ever had ngl

She is really great! I took HISP-S 105 First Year Spanish.
Attendance: You can miss up to 8 classes with no penalty. Anything after that is a .5 deduction of your overall score. If you go over 8, no matter the excuse, she will deduct you. 
Homework load is pretty light. Almost everyday but the stuff is easy and takes no longer than 15 minutes

She was an okay teacher, but I do not sincerely feel like I learned anything in this class.
