As an upper level Spanish class, I expected to have to be a sponge, but I ended up having to teach myself the whole semester. Very sweet, but doesn't get much done during class and never lets out on time. Went months without grading a single thing.

I agree with the other ratings. Shes a nice professor but doesnt really encourage Spanish speaking in class. If you really want to improve and practice your Spanish, I would not recommend this professor. However, if you are just taking this class to earn a credit, you should pass easily.
Nice, but not exciting professor. Not great at leading engaging class conversation. Very slow, but easy grader. Late to cancel class. Had trouble scheduling office hours.

She was nice... but this class made me the least confident I've ever been in Spanish. The native speakers led the class and I feel like if you aren't a native speaker, it's hard to keep up. I would suggest a different teacher, esp if you aren't totally confident in your spanish. She was a nice person though.
I would go out of my way to take one of his classes

A very great professor! He grades easily and brings his dog very often. Class discussion are very interesting and you can tell he genuinely cares. I could tell that for him it was truly about us learning and understanding rather than forcing answers out of us. He is also very funny and overall sweet guy. The workload is not too heavy and difficult.

Professor Delgado-Diaz is the greatest professor I have ever had. He is so funny and so nice. He grades super easily. You can tell he absolutely loves the subject he teaches. Very in-depth lectures with great material, and he sometimes brings his dog into class. Love him so much, and I would definitely take his class again.

Great professor, probably the best Spanish professor at IU. He really cares about his students and wants everyone to do well. He makes it an extremely easy A, but I recommend you participate and try to learn from him because he offers a lot of good knowledge. His accent is can be hard to understand at first but you will get used to it no problem.

The best Spanish prof I've had at IU. He really does care and is 100% real--he understands when people have their own problems and always makes exceptions/necessary adjustments. He is very smart and super engaging with lectures. His Puerto Rican accent takes a minute to get used to, but he adds in a lot of English filler that helps for sure.

This professor was awesome! The content of the class isn't to bad and he definitely makes it better. He responds to emails fast and is very helpful with his responses. He is very funny and makes lectures easy to follow. I would definitely take another class with him if I could!
BEST PROF EVER!!! take his class take his class take his class. so funny. great lectures. take his class
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Gibran is from Puerto Rico, so his accent takes a lot of getting used to. He is very funny and tries his best to make class fun and enjoyable. He covers most of the readings during his lectures, but read as much as you can so you are ahead of the game. There are 2 group projects, but they are pretty attainable. I recommend a class with Gibran!

Awesome lecturer! He makes it very easy to participate, unlike most Spanish professors who have to pull teeth to get answers from the class. The book is useful but most of the information comes from the lecture slides. Make sure to attend class or you will lose points and miss important information.

Professor Gilley was a very chill guy that I would recommend taking. However, his lectures can drag on and get off topic. The readings are interesting, and all exams are online. Take if you need the credit!
Dr. Gilley is one of the best I've had at IU so far. The class isn't super hard but he definitely makes you think. Gotta do the readings to get a decent grade
He is very unorganized, wouldn't follow the syllabus, and would test you on the contents that you never learned.

Great teacher, loved this class. He name the topic interesting and as long as you attend the lectures and do most of the readings it is an easy A. Speak up in his class, take interest in the class and he will take interest in you. One of my favorite teachers.

Dr. Gilley was the worst professor i've had at IU. He was rude to students, unorganized, and his expectations of students was high. However, his exams are online which is a real help. SO much reading though... & it's super dull. He does not treat it as a 100 level class.

Dr. Gilley is awesome. He talked the whole class and if you write down what he writes down on the board and read and participate in class you'll get an A for sure. Don't ask stupid questions. Stay on his good side.
He was a great professor! I really e5njoyed going to class. As long as you pay attention and take notes, it's an easy A. Just listen to what he says and go to class.

I would definitely recommend taking a class taught by Dr. Gilley. While they are challenging, he is very easygoing and willing to help as long as you are regularly attending class. He was, by far, my favorite professor this semester. He's very witty and has great stories to tell.

He's an okay professor, but a great person. He lectures without cold calling. The exam is essay and closed book.  He provides you with past exams and throughout the semester will advise you on how to use them. Sounds easy? Don't be fooled. He's loquacious but vague. Get a supplement book for concepts, the cases aren't great examples. Prepare early.
Unstable and volatile. Not recommended at all.

Seems like most of the things you need to learn for the exam are in the reading. Lectures helped very little and were vague generally uninformative. Most of his lectures were about how to take exams and what law school is like instead of teaching torts.
Professor Gjerdingen understands students, and his lectures are very enriching. He always helps students to get better grades.

He's like the kindly grandfather of the law school. He has a humble demeanor. He never makes a student feel stupid about giving the incorrect answer in class. He is the best-dressed professor in the law school (Mattioli is a close second). His exam is an endless issue-spotting brain-dump, but that's pretty standard for torts.
Is always very approachable if you need help, but make sure you have a good amount of time to chat - he is verbose, but very friendly. For exams, write a lot (but keep puffery to a minimum).
Although I was not a fan of the subject material, he did a good job teaching it. Interesting professor with a great personality.

Very clear both in making his points and in letting you know what he wants to see on the exam. Entertaining, engaging and very helpful; he lives to spend time with students in office hours and really does care. He's there to teach, not just to research and get published.

How did he get tenure? He's rather uninteresting. He never says anything of value. And he doesn't stretch your understanding of the law. He keeps referring to "these other types of things" and no one has the slightest clue what that means.

Gjerdigen's appeal is to the 1L who fears the Professor Kingsfields of law school.  Gjerdigen is witty, kind, and always entertaining--in other words, everything the practice of law is not.  Imagine learning law from your Norwegian uncle.  Seek him out for his mentoring, not his lectures.  He shines brightest when he's one-on-one with students.
such a great prof.
Totally reminds of the "Inconceivable!" guy from The Princess Bride.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

What is Common law kitbag, prof? He's a generous and kind prof to int' students. His appearance is just like a lawyer. His class is not so bad for intro to law. He uses his technical term which is not clear to int' students.

He's a really good professor and a really nice person. The reviews say he rambles but he doesn't do it that often and if he does, it all relates back to the slides and is interesting. The class isn't hard and he provides good feedback for the final poster and is very willing to help on the final exam if you need it. I'd definitely recommend him!

Professor Chip would be a great guy to have a beer with as he is super fun and has great stories. But as a teacher he rambles too much and the class can be very confusing if you're not an expert in ecology/environment. That class made me feel way out of my depth. His slides were not always clear about what was important. Great guy, okay professor.
complete lunatic waste of time genuinely guy needs mental help

I know the reviews say he rambles, but he honestly mostly stayed on topic in my class. Plus, if that bothers you, attendance isn't required. The tests are easy if you are willing to sit down and study. The final project is daunting but he is very willing to help you if you are having trouble with it. Overall, really great class!!

Personally my most interesting class, he does ramble a bit but I found it interesting. The exams weren't particularly hard as long as you study, and the final presentation was a group presentation, i.e 1/3 of the class presents and you go around the room to each poster asking questions. He also did a great job providing feedback.

i love this man. chip became the lab instructor for limnology after the previous instructor went on leave, and he's awesome. really fun to be around and knows a lot. i would take anything he teaches and i enjoy the way he explains things in the few lab lectures we had.

This is a decent class and Chip could not be nicer if he tried. The final however was extrmeely hard and time consuming, plus there is a really intense project at the end. Overall, would take the class again and especially with this prof.

Glaholt is a pretty good professor. The class is interesting enough but he rambles a lot in lectures. There are only a few quizzes that you can use the textbook for and only two exams. The presentation at the end of the year was my favorite part of the class but the instructions were not very good and he wasn't the greatest at explaining things.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor, a previous review says lectures are rambling but I found the tangents to be engaging more often than not so it's just your preference of if you'd rather someone be a dry straightforward lecturer or not (personally, I've had too many of those at IU). Attendance and participation is important. Genuinely cares about students.

I was excited for this prof bc he had good reviews, but found the lectures soo painful. He rambles for the full class time and makes learning difficult. Very different from my expectation and made the class difficult for no reason. I did well in the class but felt like I learned nothing bc he over complicated everything.

Amazing professor! One of my favorites that I've had at IU. He genuinely cares about his students and takes the time to learn everyone's names. Participation is a big portion of the grade, but he allows you to make up points by emailing him questions or talking to him after class. Highly recommend his class
I graduated IU in 2014 and he was by far my favorite professor! His lectures were interesting and he tries to give you as many points as possible on your exams. I really enjoyed his class!
Awesome teacher, you can tell he cares about all his students and wants them to both learn a lot and get a good grade.
He's a really cool dude who wants his students to succeed. He seems to get lost in his own lectures occasionally, but he knows what he is talking about.
Really nice guy, very helpful! Moves a bit fast but it's manageable

He's hype. Really chill fellow. The class is easy if you just look at the slides in class and the study guide although the study guide hasn't been updated in years and has stuff not in portion. He explains well also. HOWEVER Attendance is 10% of your grade and DAILY participation is 10%. The topics are super easy though. I wcas high every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: was a super nice guy, and lectures were interesting (very knowledgeable in his fields), but has a voice that truly drives you to sleep. also loved to quiz on niche facts from the course, which was frustrating at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a great professor! The course load was very light. He is very accessible and accommodating for extensions or missed quizzes

I really enjoyed Prof Gliboff because he comes from such an academically-rich background and has so much to say about the material. Definitely try to connect with him personally if you get the chance. He weighs participation heavily so those who don't go to class are screwing themselves over. Do the work and the tests will be a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Unclear standards, will not give rubric but looks like he grades with one. took the course way too seriously for a 100 level class

In one word: 'meh'. The class talked about evolutionary scientists. The main grading criteria is over papers: 2 individual ones and 1-2 group ones. It helps to participate and show that you care about the readings. Definitely means well and is nice, but his objectives/expectations for the class could be clearer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Meh class. Easy to pass, just show up and take notes during lecture. There were a couple papers and presentations, but nothing terrible. Totally manageable with some heavier classes. The lectures can get a little boring but the info is good if you're into genetics. Really good AIs when I took it too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was mostly lectures about the life of Darwin and other early evolutionists. While Sandy is clearly knowledgeable in his field, I found it quite boring. The course objectives were also vague. Oh, and we had to do dissections for no clear reason.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lectures are extremely boring, and he has an accent that can be hard to understand. His feedback isn't very good, but he is a nice guy and willing to meet with you and help. Assigns a lot of reading, but then goes over them in lecture and discussion so it isn't necessary to read them.

I took his Genetics and Eugenics class. It ended up just being a history of major geneticists and eugenicists. His lectures were horribly boring, but he's a nice guy. The readings are often long and semi pointless. For the most part they won't help you on the test. Skim them. If you can memorize and regurgitate, you're good.

If you're looking for an easy A topics course look elsewhere.  Lectures are about as entertaining as the weather channel on mute, tests have few questions so if you miss one, you're docked a dozen points, and reading assignments are about 2 hours long a week.

The lectures are pretty hard to sit through, but I was interested in the material.  There was so much reading, but a lot of it you don't actually have to do because it is just reiterated in lecture.  I didn't like the tests.
Prof. Gliboff's material was relatively hard, but he was always focused on helping you understand the material.
Can be hard to listen to sometimes, usually the course material is interesting enough to stay focused.

Amazing K201 teacher, gets straight to the point but will stop and help you if needed. Class moves very fast and typically does not go the full 50 minutes. Skipping class will make it very hard to get a good grade. Highly recommend for anybody who can keep up with a fast paced teacher.

He moves very, very fast. If you don't like a professor that moves quickly then 100% do not go in his section. If you ask him a question, he always has an answer (especially for the basic Excel and Access questions). His lectures are not mandatory but if you don't attend class you will have a tough time with K201.

Glaub's lab portion is really helpful because he gives you exactly what you need to know for both the Access and Excel exams-- gets straight to the point and doesn't waste your time. He does move fast, though, and lectures are important, so go to class and pay attention (lab lectures only last about 30-40 minutes anyway).
He's a very good professor, the only issue is that he goes really fast, so if you think you can't keep up with speed, I would not recommend him.
Works very fast and very well, knows what he is teaching.

Adam made K201 much easier than I originally made it out to be. While attendance is technically optional, the lectures are the only real-time you can learn real-time and ask questions. It's hard to read about Access and Excel (watching and doing it makes it easier). Sometimes he goes fast so keep up. Lots of extra credit offered to help your grade.

Had him as my K201 professor in his first-semester teaching. He is VERY knowledgeable about K201 and all assignments. Incredibly smart. He is very young (was 25 when I had him). Sometimes it seems that he teaches a little fast, but if you do the reviews and pay attention you can get an A. Students fail K201 a lot but Adam made it easy to understand

The lectures are really long and boring but you can't miss them because the slides are just pictures and you have to listen to everything he says and write it down. The test is fully based on niche questions from details he talked about in class. But Professor Knox is very kind and a great person and an A is possible if you grind for each test.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Age of giants is a HORRIBLE class to take if you're not into art history. Took it for an art credit, do not recommend. Everything felt so crammed at the end, it is so much memorization. Names dates and titles of at least 40-50 paintings per test and incredibly test/quiz heavy. He is a really nice guy and knowledgable, just painfully boring.
LOVE him. Lectures tend to be boring but he grades easily, is very accessible outside of class, and is overall very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Attending every lecture is necessary, slides only include artworks with titles + dates so you have to attend lectures to get notes for them. Quizzes over readings but gives questions in advance so you know what to look out for in readings. Memorize artworks when given them on slides to prepare for tests.

Do NOT take this class if you do not have to. he does not have any notes to take when out of class and even when in class you must write down word for word what he says or you will miss important info. Sends announcements out late when preparing for quizes in class. Grading is ridiculous and seems that he grades as if everyone was an art major.fade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Giles struggles with pacing, and we were behind the entire semester. Most of the time he would correct the exams and quizzes to match where we actually were but towards the end he kinda just dumped about 300 years worth of material on our heads and said good luck. He's so much a fan of the renaissance that we never even got to modern art.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Memorization is key. Take good notes, slides only have pictures on them. Exactly which art works will be on exams are not known so memorize all the artworks. Name, date, artist of artworks as well as writing will be on exam. Lecture materials are important for exams. Textbook material is important for quizzes. There was also one essay given.

Amazing professor with great wit, but incredibly lecture-heavy. He doesn't put any notes on the actual presentation, so you genuinely will not know the answer unless you're in class and can actively pay attention. Quiz nearly every week based on the textbook. This is even harder because his voice and content make you want to sleep.
Super funny, great in depth lectures, attendance is MANDATORY, you will regret it if you miss class. Take lots of notes!

genuinely do not take age of the giants if you're not really into art history. There are always quizzes that you really have to read the textbook for, and he does not record any lectures or post notes anywhere let alone put your grade on canvas. If you want to know your grade you have to email him to calculate it for you.
Great would totally recommend, attendance is mandatory but he's super funny so it easy to show up
Good lectures with a sense of humor. Memorization of materials is difficult but overall good art history class.

I took baroque art with Professor Knox and really enjoyed the class! The lectures were definitely long, and I could see how someone less interested in art history could dislike the class. Just make sure you know what you're signing up for (Memorization and looking at old paintings for 3 hours twice a week)

Hes cool the material is just painfully boring, made me hate art history. Had to fight to stay awake/pay attention during the lectures. If you take notes you'll be fine on exams. Be prepared to memorize stuff for exams/quizzes. Quiz questions are based on textbook and given the night before.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The exam answers are only based on what he says in lecture, or it's wrong. I wouldn't recommend unless you take perfect notes. Not at all like a typical art history class where there is room in exam answers for interpretation.

The only grades in this class are from 4 tests, and 10% in attendance. The lectures are boring and I had trouble staying awake. The lecture slides only consist of pictures, and you have to take notes only based on what he says. The testing criteria is not very clear and he expects you to write specific answers based on what he siad in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at IU by far. Makes class very enjoyable. I actually look forward to class. Has an awesome dry sense of humor.
Obviously cares a lot about the subject and manages to make class actually interesting. Attendance is taken every day, though, so beware of that. Overall a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Giles is a great instructor. He's funny, in a serious corny dad-joke way. You can definitely tell that he is extremely passionate about the Renaissance, so you probably won't get to spend much time talking about modern art at all. Nevertheless, the class is enjoyable and serves as a great introduction to the history of Western art. Be sure to study
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Giles is a solid professor. He keeps lectures cohesive and humorous. Memorizing paintings is key, however they give a lot of room for dates, which is nice. I looked at the textbook on the first day of classes and then never again. The tests are only based on his lectures and the discussion sections.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing lectures. You can tell he's really into this stuff and it makes paying attention in class really easy. All the grades in this class were from tests and one paper, but the tests weren't hard as long as you go to class and pay attention. I barely studied, and got by with just reviewing my notes the night before the exams.

This guy is AWESOME. Super knowledgeable about art history and has real world tidbits from seeing works in person. He cracks jokes and adds tiny details to his lectures to make them interesting and entertaining. He focused on artists' stylistic choices and compositions instead of just making students memorize dates. I learned a ton. I recommend!

Love this man. I hate history but sitting through his lectures everyday was usually pretty entertaining. He is pretty monotone but cracks jokes everyday and is good at gaging the energy in the room. No work required outside of class but one paper, and only in class assignments are exams. Easy A and great professor.

Every day is basically watching a slideshow of art pieces and Giles talks about each. I highly recommend you actually GO TO CLASS because a lot of what he says will be on the tests. Tests are slide identifications, short answers, and comparisons. If you go to class, listen, take notes every day & review each art piece often you will do just fine!
Very clear lectures and great at communicating information!
KNOX ROCKS!!  Seriously, Love this man!!

Giles is a really good teacher but can be very monotone. He really knows what he's talking about and I only suggest taking the class if you are interested in art history. It won't be an easy A, a lot of quizzes and the tests include seeing a picture of a piece of art and giving the name, artist and date. If you aren't good at memorizing don't do it

Professor Knox really made learning about the history of art interesting. He incorporated humor into his lectures, and he never spent too long discussing one painting. Although there are many artists, dates, and titles of the paintings to memorize, he often compares different artists and the techniques and styles used to help make it easier.

Professor Knox is such a fantastic story teller and has a great personality. Unfortunately for me, Renaissance Art History is not my forte but Knox is enlightening, intelligent, and has a great sense of humor. I recommend taking a class with him, whether the topic falls in your field or not. Pretty easy grader as long as you put the effort in.
Great lectures

He's a good teacher and you can tell he is really passionate about the subject. But the class is entirely memorization... You don't really have to even go to class--just download the slides and memorize every artwork. I didn't enjoy the memorization; therefore, I didn't find the class necessarily easy.

Giles Knox is hands DOWN my favorite professor at IU. His lectures are very interesting and he thoroughly engages his students. His lectures are delivered quite elogantly, and I repeatedly used his vocabulary in the papers I would write in other classes. Simply put this man is brilliant! If you get the chance, TAKE A CLASS WITH HIM!
Date memorization is the only challenge on tests. Otherwise his lectures are great.
Giles is a funny old guy with a love for Jan Van Eyck and a rocking bod!

He is a good prof. but you HAVE to be able to memorize! It is all about which AI you recieve for discussions, due to the fact they grade everything. They grade pretty rough. If you are not crazy or love this area of study I suggest not taking it.

Great professor, make sure you go the lectures. He makes the information as interesting as he can, and as long as you make flash cards and study you'll do fine on the tests. He doesn't use the book, so again just make sure you got to class.

"Art History Renaissance to Modern": Excellent lecturer, great sense of humor.  It's not super exciting material, but even if you have no background in art you will learn and understand what he teaches.  The book is NOT required; just make sure you study the slides for the quizzes.
By far my favorite teacher. Knox speaks  eloquently in lecture and inspires all who listen. Furthermore, Knox is very personable and has a great sense of humor. Basically, I love this man.

Behind Facos, my favorite teacher. I love the way he teaches! His lectures & voice are awesome! He REALLY knows his stuff.He even cracks some(kinda dry)jokes, but it's hilarious. Very kind too. I slacked a little in this class when it came to the reading responses, but I still got a good grade in the class. Take him if you can!! Brilliant man.
Prof. Knox was one of my favorites

This guy is pretty funny.  As long as you show up and take notes getting anything below an A in his classes means you are stupid as hell.  Don't bother to buy the testbook at all, or at least wait until mid-semester.

It was hard to stay awake in his 100 level class because he voice just froned on monotonously, but in the higher levels that he taught, he was interesting. He can be very humorous at sometimes too. Just make sure you show up for attendence.

I had Giles both in undergrad and now as a grad student. A102 is an overview...it's a snooze nomatter what. He is super smart in his area of study (renaissance/baroque) and makes class thurough clear;not at all a run-on guy. He's one of the best teachers I've had here. Sense of humor = a dry Conan O'Brian!
Really interesting and cutely quirky.  A good teacher and a really nice guy.
actually, you will fall asleep because of his teaching.  he has a terrible sense of humor and speaks like a high pitched ben stein. not too tough, but hard to listen to.
Very interesting speech inflections, cute humor, and very nice man, (though the room is lighted so that you may want to fall asleep, it has nothing to do with his teaching)

Professor Glaser is super sweet, and makes class interesting. The class is super lecture heavy, and can get boring at times but overall its not bad at all if you put in effort. She gives out study guides before each exam and the exams can be hard at times, but I think she curves them by a ton. Overall, easy class and would definitely recommend.

Prof. Glaser was such a kind and understanding person! I had many sickness issues through the year and she gave me a lot of leniency. There is a 5 question reading quiz before each class which is pretty simple. She also allows you to write a page of notes to use on tests. Overall, I really enjoyed the class.

Class was Environment, Economics and Ethics No exams, changed my whole world outlook. Just in class quizzes you partner up for. Very engaging and a class I looked forward to. She said at the end of the class that her goal is for just 1 person to understand that everything we do is bad for the environment and that person was me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Glaser's class is lecture heavy, and the lectures are quite boring. However, the class is pretty easy. Although, I studied a ton for tests and was pretty sure I failed after taking every single one I ended up getting a good grade, probably because she curves it a ton. Class isnt too hard to manage.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: there are participation assignments every day in class as well as tons of readings and a quiz due before every class. the tests aren't super straight forward. the lectures of extremely boring and don't make a ton of sense. i would suggest chugging caffine before you go into class or else you WILL fall asleep

Overall, Glaser was fine. She wasnt awful and she wasnt amazing but the class is easy and I found it somewhat interesting so that made it better. You read a lot but theyre really helpful in understanding the content. The most annoying this is the participation worksheets she gives out every class because she only gives you like 5 minutes to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is not difficult in the slightest. But, Prof. Glaser's course is lecture heavy, and she is not the most engaging speaker. Assignments mainly consist of daily reading quizzes and participation assignments. Most assignments feel like pointless busy work. If you're looking to take 181, I would go with a different option.

2 quizzes every week based on extensive weekly readings. Participation work required for each class and if you get done early she will not let you leave until class time has run out even if there is nothing left to say. lecture feels as if it drags on.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Every day you have a class with her be prepared to spend a couple of hours doing a pre-class quiz about readings, being 100% attentive during the lecture, and then taking a quiz about the lecture. Not only that, there are so many small grades as well as big grades, it is a lot to keep up with. She acts as if her class is the only class you have.

Very good professor, some stuff is confusing, but overall it's not bad at all. You have a reading quiz before class everyday, and then get a handout of the notes that you'll need to take for the day. Before exams you get a study guide 2 weeks in advance. You'll also have a group project that isn't that hard at all.
She is boring and I think she doesn't understand most of the things she is teaching. I feel like I never get a clear answer from her during review sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a very nice and passionate professor BUT a lot of the assignments she gives are very pointless and they take away from attention of the actual material. Makes students want to ignore her talking to finish worksheets. Maybe its the curriculum that is boring but she does not make it easier to find interesting :(
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Glaser is a fairly decent professor. The course was kind of unorganized and so was she sometimes, but over all I feel like she did her best and was pretty fair in the end with grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The class didn't seem to have any organization to it, which made it confusing to keep up with what was being covered in class. She sometimes didn't seem to be very knowledgable on the material and often, students would correct her on some of her information.

I did environment economy and ethics and this was by far the class where my worldviews were fundamentally changed. I changed what I wanted to do after and it made a great impact. Warning there are 0 absences and in my term we had daily group quizzes however no midterms or final.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many--Would take again

reviews.comment: Dr. Glaser isn't awful, but I would recommend looking elsewhere for a National and International Policies professor if possible. There are readings and 3 point quizzes for every class that end up having a bigger impact on your grade than you'd think. So much material is covered throughout the course that it all feels very disconnected and random.

Has no idea how to effectively teach. Assigns readings that are 15-20 pages of the most boring information. Readings assigned every class, followed by quizzes worth 25% of your final grade. If you don't understand policy issues and how they work already, do not take her class. I wouldn't wish this woman on my worst enemy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Had 1-5 reading assignments due every class. You cannot get away with just skimming the reading material because you have to write about it and she grades it pretty hard. Pretty boring class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I am watching the Olympic opening ceremonies and it made me think of her. I took her class, E400, Sustainable Use of Natural Resources in 1993.  I am sure she would love the opening ceremonies and it's exploration of sustainable development. If you want to take a class and meet a person you will remember 23 years later, take her class!
Online quizzes for each reading assignment, only 3 exams-including the final, lectures are boring but it is an easy A/B class. She is very polite
I loved Christine. Excellent teacher and really nice woman!
Excellent teacher! Very helpful and a extremely nice person. I definitely recommend her class.

Professor Glenn is really a great professor. However, in my opinion, if you aren't 100% interested in the topic of the class you will get lost and confused. She makes everything you need to succeed accessible, but you need to go to class and take notes to be fully informed for tests and exams.

I absolutely loved Connie's Music of War and Peace class. Yes, it did involve weekly papers but most of the topics were interesting. She is one of the most passionate and involved professors I have ever had for a class. She sparked an interest in classical music and the topics were interesting. There were no tests, just listening quizzes.

Professor Glenn is very fair and understands when you don't have a huge musical background. She is very nice and helps when you need it. Not too much homework, and it's usually listening to music and writing a small bit about it. Doesn't make you write full sentences on the tests, my favorite part. :-)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I took this class because I needed an A&H credit, and I've always been passionate about music.  Professor Glen is super sweet and wants to see her students' passion for music. This class has 1 assignment per week, listening quizzes, and take home essay exams.  While that may seem like quite a bit of work, I have enjoyed this class. I recommend!

Connie is adorable and is so passionate about music, hers was a class I looked forward to every week. She assigns a lot of homework and it's time consuming, which sucks, but it's relevant to the material.

She's one of the most passionate professors I've had and is extremely nice. she genuinely likes teaching which can be rare to find. not very many assignments maybe once every 2 weeks but a lot of in class group work. tests can be fairly difficult, make sure you study the listening lists! it's a music history class with music to memorize

Prof. Glen is very passionate about music and generally very nice - that said, it was a lot of work for a 100 level class. It's never clear what is going to be on the exams, and the lectures drag on. She really likes to break us up into groups, which can get annoying in a huge lecture hall. The class is almost like a music history class.
One of my favorite teachers I have had at IU.  Very helpful, nice, easy class
One of my favorite teachers I had at IU.  Very helpful, nice, easy class

I learned some interesting information in the course, but it was waaay too demanding for a 100 level course. Don't take it because it sounds easy, it's a lot of work. Connie Glen seems very passionate about music, but she picks favorites in the class and seems to have little patience with others.
The worst classroom experience ever. She is not clear about what is going to be on the test. She does not treat students fairly. I will never take any class with her ever again.

She treated the class like preschoolers. She would take students' phones away during lecture. She would waste valuable class time getting a 150 person lecture into small groups. Do not take this class with her if possible.

This class was pretty tough for a 100-level course. There is an in-class activity every day, usually involving some kind of group work. There is also an assignment every week, and a comprehensive exam taking an entire class period every 3-4 weeks. Study for the exams, don't miss class, & don't assume it will be fun just because it's a music class.

Easiest class I've ever taken - no tests, one weekly homework assignment, you basically show up and get an A. She brings in some pretty cool performers, too. Very passionate about the subject matter and really hates cell phones, so don't let that be her first impression of you

Connie is such an amazing and passionate person and teacher. Her tests require a lot of studying, but if you do, it'll pay off. She forms relationships with her students and rewards effort and dedication.

GREAT TEACHER! I had her for 2 semesters, once in z101 and then in z373 the american musical. This isn't a blow off class though. You work for your grade but she makes the material so interesting that you want to learn! She cares about her students and loves what she teaches! She hates laptops and cellphones in class so you've been warned.

Connie is so passionate about music and is really helpful to those who are willing to learn. Her tests can be difficult, but only if you don't put in the effort. Attendance is rewarded and she offers a lot of EC to help you out! Wonderful guest singers.

really people? Not only is she like the nicest person in the world, but her tests arent that bad. Just do the readings (which she says everytime) and youll be fine. Great class. Hated musicals before I came into the class, now love them!

I thought Professor Glenn was a good teacher; she is very passionate about music. It's not a tough class if you study, and there are opportunities for extra credit. Some parts of the class might be hard if you have no prior musical experience.

Extremely condescending to her students. The information presented in class is not consistent with the exams, she focuses on stories that interest her rather than musical terms she assumes students knew. Important information is rushed and her mood effected my learning. Very knowledgable about music, but should not be teaching at this level.
Shes cranky but tests r easy when u go to exam sections

Also teaches z100. Most mind numbingly dragging classes ever. Treats all students like they are grade schoolers. Constantly interrupts her guests. I don't normally agree with this statement, but this person is absolutely the definition of "those who can't, teach." Waste of money to have her as a professor. Stay home and read a book.
This teacher appeared fairly angry throughout the semester.  Her attitude is not good for the future of the world.  I wish she would be more considerate and understanding.  13265.

If you want an A, you MUST do the readings, listen/learn the pieces, go to class, and study. I got an A+, but it was definitely not handed to me. She offers extra credit and exams are short answer and essay. Concert attendance/reviews were required for the class. Simply put, if you don't want to do the work, don't take the class-it won't be easy.

Connie knows a lot about music but she treats her students like little disobedient children. Her AI patrols the class for people texting and throws them out of class. Also, Connie interrupts musical presenters constantly, which is VERY irritating. Consider taking a different music class.

Teaches class as if its an elementary school class. Doesn't have respect for students and talks down to them. The class itself is interesting and pretty easy, but you'll wish you hadn't taken it every time you hear her talk.

definitely not a easy course for general education. Even though she gives lots of extra credit, difficult exams evens out the points. and the lecture is so boring. her ppt slides and board writing are not organized.
She would be a lot more comfortable teaching elementary school. Talks down to students, and makes mistakes.
dont take this class!!!!!!! She wont give you any information and will test you with all kinds of information, what a aweful class!!!

Connie is a really nice lady with good intentions. She is passionate about musicals, however she tries to put WAY too much on each exam. She doesn't listen to students requests and makes the tests WAY TOO DIFFICULT. Teaches her musical class as though everyone has seen every single musical covered. Waste of time.

I researched hard to find the easiest A&H class for Kelley, and I think I found it. Listening quizes and tests are pretty easy, and there's an insane amount of extra credit available. I know people that only showed up for test/quiz days and got A's.
All I have to say is find a better class with a better professor to fill your time with.

If you don't have any knowledge of the history of music, you'll find this class VERY difficult.  However, if you do know Beethoven, Debussy, Mozart, and blah, then you'll definitely do fine.  Unfortunately, her notes were VERY unorganized and her chalkboard writing is chicken scratch.  Just make sure you study.  Even a little bit will help.
You got points for each class you attended and she offered a lot of extra credit points.

I took AP Chem in high school so this class was mostly review. Professor G makes lectures very interesting and explains everything well. He gives lots of real-world examples and demonstrations as well. The homework was all digital and took about 2 hours per week to complete.

Professor Goicoechea is an amazing professor. The material in class is presented very clearly and he explains concepts very well. Homework is a bit harder but you should get an A on them. The first test is the hardest, but the others are very easy and he allows you to replace your final grade with your lowest test score. Very nice and helpful.

Dr. Goicochea was an excellent professor. Office hours were where you got the best of him (but go to him with questions about specific problems). 

However, the actual class is on the harder side, but if you revise diligently, you should be able to do fine. I would recommend this course for honors chemistry and AP students.

Prof. Goicoechea is the GOAT. He makes the content very understandable and genuinely cares about his students. Sometimes the workload can be a bit much, but as long as you pay attention in lecture and go to the discussion you should be fine.

He's funny and approachable and really knows what he's talking about. Lectures are mostly just practice problems but they are very helpful. The class is difficult but as long as you have some experience in chemistry it's not too bad.

Not only is Prof G in a different realm of intelligence, but he's also just a super personable dude. Extremely passionate about the complexity of what he's teaching, yet can translate the content to typical college freshmen. Great guy.
Very good lectures: informative,funny engaging. He has a good sense of dry humor, and he seems to care about his students and learn their names. Don't be afraid to participate in class!
Amazing professor. The demonstrations worked sometimes. A lot of dry humor but also practice questions in class.

This class was a bit horrible. The people who did well have a strong foundation of Gen Chem before they came in and it showed. Do not take this class if you did not have an amazing AP Chem teacher who drilled concepts or if you're ready to feel humbled by how difficult this is. Funny and dry humor lecturer though and office hours were helpful.
Very clear with the guidelines for class and is very accessible. I often went to office hours for help and felt that I understand the material much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Goicoechea is great! His lectures are super helpful and interesting, and he's even better in office hours. I learned a lot from him, and would definitely recommend this class to anyone needing to take gen chem. There's a decent amount of homework, but it's par for the course for a college-level chem class. He gives bonuses on his exams too

Professor Goicoechea is the best chemistry professor. He is very knowledgeable and passionate. He is amiable, intelligent, and funny. He is very willing to help. Lectures are extremely helpful and informative. Definitely take this guy's class!

Professor Goicoechea is a great teacher and is highly knowledgeable, but sometimes doesn't quite understand what you may be asking with your questions. Make sure to try and be concise and to the point! Overall very passionate and has consistent office hours. A fun class that has a professor with a dry wit and is a great starting point for chem.

He was a good professor and knew his stuff, but his exams were awful. Every time he claimed the actual exam was just like the practice exam but they were never similar at all. You can do good in the class, but be prepared for surprises on the exams.
He was a great intro professor and I recommend taking a class with him. He is very knowledgeable, but can also simplify a topic if asked. Definitely go in for office hours.
This guy is an amazing professor. Although the material is tough at times, he is extremely nice and passionate for the subject. All around great class and I definitely recommend it.

I had Heath for ASL II. Highly recommend! Worth taking for his storytelling skills alone! He's a master storyteller and opened my eyes to expressions and concepts I didn't know were possible. He always welcomes questions and explains things VERY clearly/simply. He was always willing to explain a different way if I didn't understand something.

Professor Goodall is funny and his lectures are engaging. I enjoyed this course, but it had the same issues as the other ASL classes. Mainly, it was very disorganized and the GA took forever to grade assignments and lacked consistency.

Health is the best! He wants to see you succeed and wants to teach you how to use ASL, and how to be respectful. The best ASL teacher I have had. He is funny, he actually cares, and he really teaches. He does goes strictly from the book however which is not a bad thing. It's never a question about what he is looking for to get a good grade.

BEST best best professor. I found myself actually excited to go to class, which is rare for me. ASL can be intimidating but heath makes you feel at ease and makes sure everyone understands. Be prepared for signed conversations with other students. The expressive exams can be scary but heath instantly eases the nerves! I wish I had him next year.

Heath is my all-time favorite professor at IU. Heath genuinely cares about his students and has a good heart. He makes an effort to build a relationship with each and every student. He will remember facts about you and what you care about. 100/10. I was blessed to have him for 2 years of ASL and I feel like it came so natural to me thanks to him.

Heath is a great professor. As long as you give some effort, you should be able to get an A. Not because the class is so easy, but because he teaches so well in class. There are many pop quizzes, so make sure to show up to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He is awesome! I highly recommend Professor Goodall, great class!
Took P155 over the summer and it was great! She is very flexible and understanding as long as you are genuine and put in effort. Even over zoom she made participation fun and easy!

This is a glorified AP Composition class, yet she grades like it's a 500 level. She is such a slow grader, and then waits until the very end of the semester to release everything, so you don't know your actual grade until then. On top of that, she doesn't show rubrics which makes it impossible to actually know what she wants in an assignment.

She is super nice! I had her for English and looked forward to class. The class uses a lot of technology, so make sure you know how to use it. She grades you higher if you participate. She sometimes cancels classes. She's a grad student, so she's very understanding. As long as you do the work and come to class, you should get an A.

The course itself was overall frustrating and a lot of effort without much reward. Unless you just don't do you're work, you'll at least get a B. The teacher is a grad student therefore I am more understanding but she was not very helpful to making the course flow better. I have heard taking it is easier

Somehow, David Good popped in to my head after 34 years! I remember his lectures being tough to follow. An overhead projector was used back then and he'd scribble in Greek at blinding speed on a transparency, about 10x faster than I could follow.
And yet!... I learned a lot. Multivariate regression. Heteroskedasticity! Bayes theorem!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It is clear Dr. Good really cares about his students and will lose sleep to help you. HOWEVER, his teaching is really fast and hard to follow, if you get held up on something during a lecture your pretty much lost the rest of the time, he does not stop. I consider myself okay/good with math but I really struggled in this class, by far the hardest

I love Prof. Good -great sense of humor! Although the class was the toughest class I've ever taken (I'm not good at math), I came out feeling like I was on top of the world. That is because I worked my butt off. READ HIS NOTES.. ALL THE ANSWERS ARE THERE. Also, watch some youtube Vids for extra help. I do not regret it. It was absolutely worth it!

I went into this class knowing very little about coding and Dr. Gold never mad me feel like I was behind or doing something wrong. He was always generous with praise and gentle when pointing out mistakes which made things so much easier for me and my anxiety. The assignments had pretty clear guidelines and overall the class was low stress.

Sensation and Perception is probably the hardest class I've taken at IU, but his grading system is really helpful! There's no homework or grades other than exams, but I recommend going to class to understand the lecture better!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The teacher made it inherently hard to communicate with and was very passive-aggressive when it come to communication. This was supposed to be an "easy" to navigate coding class but was not and it takes a lot of your time.

His coding class is one of the best classes I've taken at IU. He gave us freedom to learn on our own but made himself available for help when we needed it. Didn't expect you to memorize everything, he encourages problem solving and using your resources. If you get a chance to take his coding class, you'll love it.

Dr. Gold is awesome! Sensation and Perception was the hardest class I ever took in college, but I still got an A because he drops your lowest test grade. Lectures aren't required to go to, but if you wanna have any idea what's going on, you should go. He answers questions as soon as you raise your hand. Super funny too!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Gold made this class super understandable. He would always review tough material until we understood it. If you go to class and pay attention you will do fine

Jason Gold is my favorite professor at IU. He is very accessible and a very good teacher. The material is harder, but he curves the tests and goes by a different grading scale so anything 80 and above is an A, no homework, and he rounds your grade up to the highest percent and hes a super nice guy. He also does research to answer any questions

Dr. Gold is literally the greatest prof. I have had in psych at IU! He is clear on what he expects, keeps lectures interesting, and is just an all around cool guy. No book, he posts articles to read before each lecture (but I never read them and still did fine),  and he has his own grading scale (an 80% is an A-!) 10/10 would recommend

Excellent professor! One of the kindest professors I've had at IU. Class is organized very well so it's not unnecessarily stressful. He organizes each unit with a common theme which makes everything easier to understand and tie together. I'd definitely take another class with him. Two thumbs up!
Test are very detailed orientated. Either go to class or read over power points. easy material just have to memorize it.

Dr. Gold is a good guy and he keeps lecture pretty interesting. The class operates on reading one journal article before lecture, and the tests are pretty much over PowerPoint material. I didn't really learn all that much, and the class was fairly easy, but overall a positive experience.

He's a good teacher.  I also had him for P329 and the P335 class was very similar.  He posts articles to read which are discussed in class.  If you go to class and take notes the exams aren't too bad, but he also has a very easy grading scale.

Pretty good teacher. He is goofy and makes class enjoyable. Tests are difficult but he makes up for it was an easy grading scale. No text book, he posted all the readings and slides from class online. Made a very boring subject much more interesting for students
Great Professor! Made class worth going to, I really learned something in class.  Very helpful and very cute.

Very laidback, preferred teaching method is Powerpoint. Lectures, has interesting examples and clips. Intense subject matter, but attending class and taking good notes helps. If you MUST take an Area A, he's a good prof to have.

LOVE LOVE LOVE Granger. Super chill prof. For each exam gives you 3 practice exams which are basically mirrored copies of the actual exams. Plus you get a one-sided cheat sheet with all the formulas or whatever you want to write down. If you make a good cheat sheet and do all the practice exams ur set. Also all exams combined only 50% of your grade

Best professor!! He's so chill and goes over every in class activity so you get 100% on each one. The exams can be hard but just go over the practice exams a few times and you'll be fine! They're also only weighted 50% of the course grade and the other 50% is basically guaranteed 100%. He's a great professor take him!!!

What a phenomenal professor! Rob clearly understands how college students think and makes lectures so clear and easy to understand. I have never taken a stats course but still did very well because of all the class materials and the way he prepares us. 100/100 can't recommend him enough!
Nice guy who gives you the materials you need to succeed. If you don't do super well on the exams, you can still get a good grade in the class.

Stats is a hard course, but Prof Granger is the best teacher for this class. He's pretty funny and makes lectures worth going to. He also lets class out early a lot. He gives you mostly everything you need to succeed as long as you're willing to put in the effort

Great guy whos super laid back and genuinely cares about the students and their learning. The class is setup to where you can do bad on the exams but still get a B or A in the class through consistent attendance, homework, and the pre class readings / quick checks. Best math class I have ever taken. No prior stats classes to S301

BEST S301 PROFESSOR!! Had never taken stats before and did just fine thanks to him. Funny guy, lets us out of class early, and helps you finish your in class activity. Course is heavily weighted so you can do bad on exams and still get a good grade from hw and quick checks. Can't recommend him enough please take him!!!

BEST STATS TEACHER!! He is the sweetest man and wants you to do good. He is the one who creates the tests for the department so definitely try to get him. You can do bad on the tests and still pass bc of the weight of HW. Get him or get on his waitlist

Business Statistics is a difficult class that many would prefer to take online during the summer. That being said, if you do take it in person, Robert Granger is the GOAT. Tough class made easy through detailed lectures and homework, plus he's nice and cares about his students. He stays after class and has the course grade not focused on tests.

He structured this class very well by splitting the class into a lecture and an activity every day. The lecture gives you all of the tools you will need to complete the graded activity for that day. Rob is a super caring guy and super funny when you catch his humor. If you take S301 you NEED to take it with him.
Best stats teacher out there, take him if you can
Rob will help you success in this course. He's relatable, engaging, and committed to his students' success. He motivates everyone to excel. For stats, choose Robert's sections.

Rob is a really nice guy. He explains everything well and cracks jokes to make lecture entertaining. He prepares you well for exams and the practice exams given before the test are super helpful for studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's a true shame this guy doesn't have more ratings. I can't say enough good things about him. He has such a good sense of humor that it's worth it to show up, just so you can laugh.

Everyone gave Rob a round of applause when he entered the final exam lecture hall. He's a great guy and an excellent teacher. Always available, very good at explaining difficult concepts, and genuinely cares about his students. His lectures are short, but very helpful. Best class and teacher at IU, take S301 with Rob.

Robert = GOAT. He is one of maybe 10 professors at IU that knows how to explain things clearly to people our age. Also, he is a cool sense of humor and goes out of his way to make sure you understand how to do the stats problems. I was worried about stats because Im not great at math, but this class might as well be called Microsoft Excel class.

As a journalism major, I'm not the best at math, but Rob was able to make it easy for me. He's fun to listen to and he responds to your questions in a way that's easy to understand. He's really helpful and approachable, and somehow made stats not terrible. One of my favorite professors!

Robert is great, a super awesome teacher. The TA sucks. Sasha grades so unreasonably hard. If Robert did all the grading this would be my favorite class of the semester. Sasha is ruining my life. Someone please rock her for me thank you.

This class was a breeze. Rob's great and he makes everything about as "cut and dry" simple as can be. If you're a journalism major and need to get your statistics credit, take Rob's class. Don't hesitate for a second. He's a homie and that's tough to find in a statistics professor. Sasha is cool, too. She's a tough grader but it's always fair.

I took every one of his classes, and even though my major was outside his field I can honestly say there was nothing else in my college experience that was as inspiring for me, and nothing else that will stick with me as long.

I took all of Gass' courses and can honestly say they changed my life (and my taste in music). He is easily the most engaging and passionate teacher I've had, teaching with a gripping, transformative emotion and impossibly deep knowledge of his subject matter. His classes are pure music appreciation and the most important education I'll ever have.
He's someone I'll never forget. Almost 20 years out of IU & I still speak of the vibrant way that he spoke about music. The world needs more professors like him.

The best professor I've ever had no question. Teaches many life lessons and is incredibly passionate about what he teaches. Gotta love Glen. Also a very easy class he tells you exactly what you have to know. He's not here to trick you. If you do bad on a test he allows you to take a cumulative final after the regular final to get a better grade.

Glen is one of those professors you always hope you'll have. You'll never meet anyone with more passion for what they teach than him. He has so much knowledge to share and so many stories to tell. He's taught me more about all of my favorite bands than I could ever hope to know and has significantly broadened my horizons, musically. 10/10 recommend

Fascinating lectures, but did not enjoy the class at all. Do not take this class unless you genuinely like rock and roll. You are given an insane amount of songs to listen to and memorize for the test. Don't think you can skip class. Whoever told you that was lying!!! Not a blow off class!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Glass is the best professor I've ever had! Class was taken for a GedEd Credit & VERY glad I took it. Only three exams (well four). There is a fourth exam on the day of the final. It is taken after the final and it is optional. It is cumulative & can be taken to make up an exam or to replace an exam if you did bad. Exam's are easy!!!

Absolutely the worst professor I have had thus far throughout my college career. He is very disorganized and his lectures barely cover what is on the exam. He does not hold any office hours and is very condescending when students asked questions. Left me and others unready for his exams.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Glen is a pretty cool dude and his classes are hilariously easy. Folks will probably drum up google doc pages for test studying, so you don't even have to attend class. Only problem is he's an opinionated codger and presents his thoughts as fact, which is pretty elitist and obnoxious if you happen to be on the wrong end of his hot opinions. So yeah
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: loved history of rock n roll. glen is an absolute G. going to class and paying attention means that you can skip reading the text book. listen to the assigned music as he goes over it so you won't have to cram. really, this isn't that hard of a class, as long as you do what he says to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Fun class, just a terrible grade system where the only grades are 3 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took this class for fun and was not disappointed. Glenn is the best.  He love the subject matter and  it shows. His enthusiasm is infectious! I learned so much about early rock & roll and yet never felt like I was in a lecture. I loved the class so much I'm taking Z202 next semester just because.

I love rock n roll and Prof Gass made me love it even more. He is hilarious, super passionate about what he does, and truly wants everybody in this class to succeed. Hands down one of my favorite professors at IU. If you pay attention in lecture and listen to the songs he provides, it's an easy A.
Best professor I have ever had

Glen Gass is without a doubt my favorite professor I have had at IU. He is so passionate about the material his class covers, and conveys the importance effectively to the class. If you have any interest in rock music, take this class. You will not regret it.
A legend.  The greatest educator the world will ever see.  He is the most passionate human I have met in my life.

HIGHLY recommend taking one of Glenn's classes if you know/care about music even in the slightest bit. I took two of his classes and learned an immense amount! He's incredibly passionate and full of knowledge about almost any musician who has ever walked this earth. If you listen to the songs and take notes in class, the tests aren't very hard.
You won't find a professor more passionate about the material they teach.
Could be the best professor I've ever had.

He's hilarious! He makes class super fun and he really knows what he's talking about. The information he has on this topic is never ending. He gets off on tangents a lot and can get a little boring but he always brings it back.  If you can't appreciate music in any way you'll hate this class and waste your time. If you can then you'll love it!
MY FAVORITE PROFESSOR. He's so passionate about what he does and makes the class so fun. The lectures are long but so entertaining. There's never a dull moment.
LOVE THIS CLASS MY ROOMMATE DOES TOO BIGGEST FANS LOVE U GLEN

Glenn is the man. I don't know if a simple post of appreciation is enough to describe how much I loved his class. If you don't take one of his classes at IU you're missing out. Best professor I've ever had. Genuinely cares about the students. My only regret is that I have not grabbed a beer with the man. I would pay to hang out with him.

By far my favorite class ever taken at IUB! He did a phenomenal job teaching the Beatles and gave me an interest in their music. You learn just about everything of the Beatles and the classes are so much fun to attend. I highly recommend taking this course before you graduate, even if you're not a big beatles fan, you will be after taking this.

He's a great professor, funny guy and makes the material fun, but the class is an hour and a half so it can get brutally boring at points due to a boring sort of section or if you aren't a fan of a certain artist

Glen is a fantastic professor. He is the most enthusiastic professor I have ever had and truly loves what he does. I actually look forward to going to this class (The Beatles) because he makes it so interesting. I signed up for another one of his classes next semester I enjoyed it so much. Tests are not difficult if you listen to the songs.

Honestly confused as to why Glenn doesn't have a 5 star rating because he is THE BEST professor on any of IU's campuses. Probs would marry the dude. He's got a sick tye dye button up also. Passing up the opportunity to take a class taught by him will be the biggest mistake during your time at IUB. Glenn Gass for president 2016!!

I took his class on Bob Dylan, and now Dylan is one of my favorite artists. He chooses the right songs for you to listen to, and makes you interested in the content. He could get a little boring, but the class is pretty good overall, if you're interested in music.

By far one of my favorite professors here at IU! Some of his home videos are absolutely adorable and take away the idea of being in class. Listen to the music and you will be just fine, as he will provide the trivia questions that will be on the exam. Also, go over your notes a few days in advance. I will definitely be taking another class of his!
Glen is a great professor that knows everything about Rock n Roll history ( & Bob Dylan). Take his class now and learn bout great music

Glen is the best.  If you show up to class and do the listening, you will pass.  Glen is very passionate about what he is teaching and incorporates humor into his lessons making you want to go to class.  He changed my taste in music for the better.  He has some awesome stories that keep class interesting as well.

Glenn Gass is incredible! He has singlehandedly ignited my renewed love of music, and he is without a doubt one of the greatest professors I've ever had the privilege of learning from. He's hilarious, passionate about teaching, and he's just all around awesome. TAKE HIS CLASSES. (Especially Z202. Just do the listening and you'll be fine.)

Glenn Gass is hands down the best professor on any campus, teaching any course. He is so passionate and interesting and hilarious. Students love him and I hated the "music type" people before taking his rock and roll classes, and now I'm pursuing a music minor as a Business Major. What will i do with that? who care his class is great!

I am not a music major, and yet Glen Gass is by far my favorite teacher I have ever had at IU. His class is so interesting and he is so passionate about the material. He makes jokes all of the time and the class just eats them up. Very interesting material, nothing required in the class other than listening to good music and taking 3 easy tests.

Glen Gass will run the same way of teaching each and every class. He will turn the lights out, everyone will take their laptops and phones out, and Professor Gass will play music very loudly and display a bunch of notes which you will need to pay close attention to and study as those will be on the 3-4 exams. 1.5 hour class lecture but funny guy.
This man's life is pretty much the history of rock and roll. Take a class with Professor Gass is you get a chance. He loves what he teaches and it shows.
Pretty much spells out what's on the test.  And a great class if you like the music. Supplement with readings to reinforce the lecture. Just don't be lazy and the A takes care of itself.

Glenn Gass is a God. He knows more about The Beatles than anyone you know. He is hilarious. He has amazing stories. He plays music from time to time at The Bluebird. The Beatles course is a real multimedia tour de force. Everything a college course should be. Inspiring. Inherently interesting. Easy as hell. You will not regret signing up for it.

Professor Gass is quite a character. His lectures are filled with amazing (and loud) music and funny anecdotes from his life. Although he tends to stray away from the main topic sometimes, he can be very interesting. He doesn't do the best job at preparing the class for exams but he tries, failing sometimes. Overall, great professor and great class

Glen Gass is what a college professor should be. Passionate, opinionated, knowledgeable. Make sure you attend class - he is very big on class attendance. Not so much because it's part of the grade, but because he genuinely wants to teach us. Listening exams can tricky so make sure you're listening to the music from the start of the semester!

Graduating from IU without taking one of Gass's courses would be a shame. His lectures are hilarious and really informative. He knows EVERYTHING about the Beatles. If you can't enroll in one of his classes for whatever reason, at least attend a class to get the experience. If you're passionate about music, a class with Gass is a must.

Awesome teacher, if you have any interest in rock music history, take the class. If you are into classic rock, you will get an A without much effort. Good times, no reason to skip class because he always made it interesting. Book isn't necessary, but he wrote it so why not pick it up.

He is the best professor I've ever had. I had him for The Music of Bob Dylan and he knew EVERYTHING about Dylan. He always kept the class interested and seemed to truly love teaching the course. I would definitely recommend him for anything he is teaching. Also, if you can't handle too loud of music, don't sit up front.
GREAT Professor! I would recommend anyone to take a class with him before they graduate! He genuinely loves what he is teaching about so it makes the class that much more interesting.
awesome teacher if you can take one of his classes you wont regret it. loves what he does and he's very interesting and fun. keeps the class entertaining. probably my favorite professor yet

Best teacher I have ever had. Everyone should take one of his classes if you ever have the chance. He is one of the most personal and lovable guys out there. Also, he has a lot of awesome home movies.
awesome professor, everyone who goes to indiana university should try to get into one of his classes

I almost cry every night in his world-renowned Beatles class. He makes them so beautiful and human. I'll be honest, I have trouble separating my love for The Beatles with my appreciation for Dr. Gass. He teaches them with such humanity, though. It's amazing. If he teaches any other class with this passion, he is an excellent professor.

I just graduated from IU, and Glen Gass was my absolute favorite professor. I would never skip class because he made the material so enjoyable. The home videos he shared were so fun to see (his family is ADORABLE) I didn't know a lot of the music, so the listening was challenging for me, but as long as I did a little studying every day it was fine.
The best. Totally lives up to the hype. I just wish he would institute a good attendance system so he wouldn't worry so much about the people who skip class. Those of us who were there loved it!
Every person needs to take a class from Glen Gass.  I was in both the 60s class and the Bob Dylan class and it is amazing. Seriously this professor is one of the best at IU!

After three years of college this is by far my favorite professor. Very interesting plus it's rock n roll music so what's not to love? Highly recommend this class. And also book is not necessary, you will probably never use it.
great teacher
best teacher on campus
A cool guy and a cool class. Don't underestimate the exams - they can be tricky if you tend to skip lectures.
Awesome guy and awesome class. No need for text book

If you love music, this class will easily be your favorite! The guy knows his stuff, and makes it fun to learn! If you think this is a blow off class, or don't have any real passion for music,don't take it,It requires a lot of listening outside of class and some struggle. Any music lover will LOVE Gass and you will never want to miss a day!

He is fun to listen to. Lots of note taking. The book and the lectures are exactly the same. I took notes rather than reading. The tests are pretty hard but multiple choice. The listening part of the test takes time to prepare for. The facts part is pretty easy but you must know names.

I had Glen Gass my second semester freshman year for Z-201, History of Rock and Roll in the 60's. It was by far the most awesome learning experience of my life. That is no longer true since I have taken Music of the Beatles with him... take this man's classes. Dylan is up next for me.

Took this class 1st semester freshman year, and going into senior year still my favorite class. Hilarious, passionate, and a joy to be around. I never wanted to miss a class. Definitely taking a class with him again before graduation. The material easy for me because I already love the music, but would be manageable no matter what!

One of the most inspiring teachers I've ever had. Not many people can pour their souls out on a daily basis especially in front of a couple hundred people. Classes are always interesting and a welcome stress reliever compared to other classes
Great Professor. Most passionate professor I have every had. The guy loves his job and the subject. Every class is a new experience.
AMAZING PROFESSOR. HE MADE ME WANT TO COME TO CLASS. IT'S ALWAYS ENJOYABLE TO LEARN FROM A TEACHER WHO IS PASSIONATE ABOUT WHAT THEY TEACH AND GASS IS JUST THAT!
A tad bit overrated but still a great teacher and one of the best at IU

Glen Gass has been my favorite teacher at IU since I took my first rock history class 2 years ago. I'm now in my fourth rock history class, and he is AMAZING! loooove glen gass!!!! take his classes you won't regret it!
Glenn Gass is by far the most amazing man to ever grace the room of Ballentine 013.
Gass is amazing

GLENN GASS IS THE BEST PROFESSOR EVER!  He is so passionate about rock history, especially The Beatles, and it's clearly obvious he loves teaching, music, and history in general.  He also has some of the best quotes out there!   To leave IU without taking a music history class from him would be an absolute shame.
Awesome teacher.  Probably the most interesting class I've taken.  Easy class just take good notes and listen to the Beatles a lot.
Most passionate, inspirational professor ever.  Joy to attend class.
Glenn Gass is the coolest teacher EVER. Never even thought about missing one of his classes. He always found a way to make class fun. TAKE HIS CLASS
The Beatles class is the best!! Glenn rocks, one of the most knowledgeable, passionate and genuinely NICE professors ever. Nothing bad to say about him.

AMAZING PROFESSOR.  I've never seen someone so passionate about their topic.  He made every class interesting and exciting.  He taught the material as if it was his first time learning it.  TAKE THIS CLASS!
Best and easiest class ever
