Dr. Hill was nice, respectful, and engaged while lecturing, but the examples during lecture and Edfinity assignments do not prepare you properly for the exams, and if you haven't taken calculus before, self-teaching is your only option. Explore tutoring or spend time outside class learning concepts if new to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr.Hill I believe is a good person but his class was not a class I would EVER take again. he teaches calc like I would teach addition to a 9th grader. What I mean by that is he already knows calc so well that he basically does the probelms in his head and he doesn't explain how he fully got to the answer therefore just leaving you more confused.

This professor is genuinely awful. Do NOT take this class, even if your advisor says it's easier compared to other classes. Each lecture, he only covers a couple example questions, which are nothing like the homework questions. You will 100% need to teach yourself calculus. The exams are incredibly difficult, and you will absolutely struggle.

He is by far the worst professor I've ever had. He cannot teach math at all. Cannot explain what he is doing. You will struggle. If he is your professor get a tutor ASAP you will need it. Do not have him as a teacher if you get the choice.

Very nice and easy going however the in class work does not translate to the homework. Only did like 3 problems a day in class (not to step by step) and they often were very different from the homework. I'd recommend the group sessions and practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't recommend this professor, he can't teach at all. He doesn't explain how he gets the answer and it's hard to understand what he is saying. His hand writing also isn't good so I suggest to sit closer to the front so you can see. So many homework assignments each week and pop quizzes. He does curves on exams so it helps a little bit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Hill has a very calm lecture and is easy to understand, although I would recommend finding more difficult examples of the topics you learn online as some of the in-class examples given aren't reflective of what you will find when completing the homework on Edfinity.

Not a bad professor for m119. if you learned most of the stuff in high school you'll be even more fit for this class but the content wasn't too difficult, he just lectured kind of slow and unclear sometimes. but he is easygoing and the grading is straightforward w/ all MCQ exams and edfinity. just study and do the practice exams and you'll be good
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Not a bad person, didn't take attendance for lectures, but also if you attended lectures they were not helpful for homework at all. Basically went over like two problems every lecture and only one of those the of questions would show up on the homework. The exams were nothing like the homework, had to rely on the practice exams to study.

he was a really nice person but super mid teacher. if i hadn't taken ap calc in high school I would've been screwed, but my previous knowledge helped mostly. he answered our questions, but every class was a lecture and many times it just felt pointless to attend.

DO NOT take this course with this professor. If you did not take calculus in high school, you will struggle immensely with this professor. None of the exams corresponded with the notes, practice exams, or homework. The final exam was almost completely made out of questions never covered in class or on the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I found there was few correlation with the content taught in class, as well as the homework to actual exams. Unfortunately, I spent an extremely long time having to teach myself calculus. As someone who was 2 years removed from any math class, I found it to be extremely difficult.

PLEASE READ: If u did not take calculus in high school do not take him. What he taught in class had nothing to do with the tests, the homeworks were difficult for no reason. You basically had to teach yourself calculus. Exam 3 was extremely difficult, please do not take him. Unless u work ur butt off.
Boring lectures that have nothing to do with the exams. All he does is ramble on about nothing relevant. Ended up teaching this to myself. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR.
The exam sometimes include things we have never learned and that's why I struggled, he also just write and doesn't really explain well.
UGH UGH UGH

I took calc in high school so I had some baseline, but the class was still decently hard. Lots of homework, and 4 exams, each had a curve and the final could replace one if you got a higher score. Prof. Hill isn't very good at teaching, he has our best interests in mind which is nice but lessons rarely helped on homework

Difficult teacher. Didn't really show you how to work out the problems or explain how to do something, he would just write it on the board and expect you to figure it out. Many homework problems were very different from class examples. He does drop a few grades and curves all exams.

His class was very difficult. He teaches class lessons that don't correlate with the homework at all. The exams are super difficult no matter how much you understand the material. He is a good person, but not a great teacher.

Professor Hill curved every exam in the class making it difficult to fail. Despite this, I could see how his lectures do not necessarily correlate to the questions on homework assignments and exams. it is strongly suggested to go to campus tutoring because what Michael Hill teaches in class is not everything you see on future assignments.

Hill was an ok professor for me because I took calc in high school but for someone who has not I don't think he is the best teacher. He doesn't always explain concepts fully and the homework does not always line up with the textbook material. He replaces test grades sometimes if you do better on a different exam and the quizzes are open notes.

Professor Hill was not the worst professor but he wasn't the best. He either had really good or bad days explaining lessons, sometimes making numerous mistakes and the students having to tell him what he did wrong. I did not understand the class that much but still passed. It is possible but for stem majors take V119.
Generous curves so if you study you'll be fine- definitely make use of Campus Tutoring Services if you want to get an A. HW is nothing like the tests

This professor teaches different things in class compared to what is on homework and tests. Campus Tutoring is good for this class. If you have a B after your first 2 tests, it's impossible to get an A after.

In my opinion, Professor Hill is very caring and wants to help you. He is so easy to ask questions to and explains things well. But, if you don't have a sufficient background in calculus, then he won't be good for you and you will have to teach yourself outside of class. He also gives a lot of review time for exams which is nice.

He really taught me nothing even if you go to class, he does maybe 1-2 examples of problems in class and never goes over them again. Nothing he teaches is in the homework and is about 10x harder than what is in class and doesn't have anything to do with what we did in class. Tests are multiple choice but doesn't help if you didn't learn anything.
no

If you have to take M119, take it with Professor Hill. Going to lecture is SUPER important, although they can sometimes be boring. Stay on top of the online Webwork homework each week because if you don't it WILL pile up quickly. At the end of the semester, he gives opportunities for extra credit and curves the exam scores which is nice!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You basically have to teach yourself outside of class. He moves through his lectures very quickly and the online homework doesn't match the notes he does in class.

idk why michael is rated so poorly. yes the class is hard but i think he really tries his best to help his students out. he states things as clear as they can get and gives as many examples as possible in the 50 minutes that we get in lecture. the homework was easy A so they carried my grade and gave me room for the exams, which had good curves.

Although he is likely one of the better professors in the math department, Professor Hill is pretty useless with lecturing. He seems to care, but the content covered in lecture doesn't necessarily correlate to the homework and exams. The curves on exams are nice. Make sure to do the homework!! Using his chapter summaries was the most useful for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Hill is prob one of the better profs in the calc department. He is not a great lecturer, but I ended up doing just fine. GO TO CAMPUS TUTORING SERVICES before the exams for review sessions!! He did do some grade flipping to replace your lowest exam score with your final exam if you scored better. Handy in case you bomb one.
Lectures were very fast and did not gain much information. I would go to CTS so you get a good grade in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He was hard to reach through email (which as a student who was unable to attend office hours because of other Classes was the only way to reach him). His teaching style is one where you have to learn the material through examples, he doesn't explain the formulas at all and breezed through topics quickly. He had nice curves tho (which saved my grade

This class is a lot of work. Pay attention during the lectures and do the homework and you should be fine. Prof Hill would usually give examples of problems you will see on the homework which was helpful. He also made outside resources/his office hours very clear. Take the time to understand the concepts/put in the work and you should get an A.

Dr. Hill is not a good professor. Makes it extremely difficult to succeed if you don't have previous Calc experience from high school. Explains things horribly, and tests are more difficult than others. In order to succeed with him, you need to use Campus Tutoring Service. It will be night and day learning from them compared to Hill.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yes, there is a LOT of homework, but he makes the content super easy to learn. Lectures are partly rules, and mostly examples. If you use your notes when doing the homework it is super easy. There is access to several practice exams for each exam we take. There were so many people in the class that the group chat we made was extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You really need to go to class to get good notes. The webwork (homework) sucks and doesn't always match up with what you learned. The tests are okay if you study and there is a curve on every test. Make sure you do the quizzes every Friday!

Out of all the Calc teachers here he is one of the best. Exams are just like the homework but the homework is harder than any of the problems we do during the lecture. He is accessible so go to his office hours if you need help.

The lectures have nothing to do with the homework. He is a good lecturer but they just have no relationship to the exams and quizzes and homework. Would never take with him again. Get ready to read the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The homework is worth like 20% of your grade and there is so much of it. He does give practice exams which are very helpful.

Covered material clearly and in a way that was easily understood. His lectures were straight to the point. The structure of the class and grading was straight-forward. He was easily accessible in office hours and was always open for questions and willing to go back and review when students needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He's not the best but he gets the job done. He explains most concepts well but there are some that you have to teach yourself or go to office hours for. The homework is sometimes a lot but the practice helps in the long run. The exams aren't too bad if you keep taking his practice tests and take good notes. He's definitely a good backup.

I took M119 in the fall and then M120 w Hill again in the spring. Honestly one of my favorite profs. He grades easy and is very clear about the grading criteria - most important TAKE NOTES! most of lectures are a little bit of material and then a bunch of examples, write down the examples and review them before the exams.

Like most of the other ratings have already mentioned, the work done in class has nothing to do with what's on the homework, which in turn has little in common with what is on the exams. That being said, it is not impossible to do well in the class. Use the textbook heavily, and for each exam go through all of the practice exams given to you.

This class is composed of three things. Lectures, homework and exams. His lectures had nothing to do with the homework, and the homework had nothing to do with the exams. Be prepared to get 50s on all of his exams because that was our class average.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The homework, lecture, and exam questions were all completely different from each other. Showing up to class wasnt even worth it at a certain point as it just confused everyone more. Neither were the homework problems, which were 20% of the grade. Exam averages were staggeringly low. He also didnt update canvas so you were left in the dark.
possibly the worst professor I've ever had. Our class averages for our tests have been 61, 56,60, and 51. If this doesn't explain why he's awful then idk what else would.

Plainly said he is quite easily the worst professor that could possibly teach calculus. Is entirely incapable of going through examples in class and makes mistakes as if he were Stevie Wonder trying to draw a self portrait. Homeworks were longer than entire bible chapters and pertained to absolutely zilch from the test questions or class examples.

Tough class. I always felt like Dr. Hill was just freestyle teaching the entire time. Granted, I take this class at 8:45 and I definitely can't do the math that early in the morning but the amount of simple math errors that Dr. Hill makes during class is nothing short of incredible. I feel like everyone is struggling in his class

In class lectures are completely unrelated to homework and test questions. Never before have I experienced a class where YouTube videos explained class content better than the professor. I have no idea what my grade is, refuses to curve tests until all grades are collected. If you can't get another professor for M119 I'd recommend a 200 calc class.

Less than a week until the final. Still don't know my grade. He put up an "equation" for us to compute it ourselves, but doesn't explain how to use it. Literally is destroying my GPA. Worst professor I've had. Ridiculous. For your own sanity, do not take him. You will spend endless nights trying to learn what he's "taught" you, just to fail.

During the lectures all that is gone over is examples, not necessarily that actual concepts we are trying to be larned. Do the web work, it helps with grades in the long run. The bonus webwork is also helpful. Overall though my least favorite class by a mile, professor doesn't make it any easier or more interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: literally awful. I had never taken calculus before coming here and he expects you to already know everything. doesnt know how to explain anything. tests are nothing like notes or homework. take it online.
so bad. Cannot teach at all.

Just take it online. I am telling you right now I have failed both tests so far and it's not getting better. Even when I steadily went to class, the material on the homework and tests was so much harder on the homework. This class is so hard. It is. So. Hard. Do yourself a favor and take it at Ivy Tech. Please. I wish I could. - The opinion of many
terrible

My first calculus class- its like he expects you to already know how to do everything. Only does examples in class- doesnt actually teach. The trillion hw problems dont reflect what is taught in class. Even reading the textbook doesnt help. He simply doesnt teach he just talks and expects you to understand automatically.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Steve is passionate about quality and responsible journalism. He does a great job of sharing his experiences and insights and instilling in students a desire to explore a range of perspectives of a single topic or idea.

Worst journalism class I have taken at IU. Steve barely gives any directions on assignments, but then gives you a hard time if you didn't do it the way he wanted. Everything is submitted through Dropbox, not Canvas, so it's SO easy to lose track of things. I have not learned hardly anything new with Steve. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNLESS REQUIRED

Professor Higgs is by far the worst professor I have had at Indiana University. On the first day of class he told us he is the "boss" and we work for him. The vibes are terrible. No assignments are actually submitted on canvas everything is put into a dropbox and over-complicated for no reason. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS IF YOU ARE NOT REQUIRED!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Take any class Steve has to offer! He is extremely attentive, has lots of experience and only wants students to learn, grow and succeed. As long as you communicate, he's fair and understanding should you run into issues completing your work. If you're seriously interested in pursuing journalism, he's a great mentor and down-to-earth professor.
He is one of my favorite professors. He will help you become a better journalist and is very understanding and accommodating. Also funny and engaging. Definitely take his class.

Steve is a great guy overall. Hes super experienced. Ask him questions about his career! Youll learn tons. He can sometimes be a pain, but if youre gonna be a journalist/reporter, your editor is gonna be a pain. Do not fall behind on this work, do not skip class, and communicate well! Hes willing to grant extenations when needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Run the other way! He is by far the worst professor I have ever had at IU. He could honestly care less about you and your work. He doesn't understand that students have other classes than his and he shouldn't make a required J School class like an internship. You volunteer for classes like those. Overall its not worth the hair pulling.

I was worried that by taking an online class, I would have no interaction with my professor and that the class would be boring. This wasn't the case at all. Professor Higgs is very helpful and responds quickly to emails. The information we learned in the class was relevant, and overall the class was an easy A.
Steve is an awesome guy. He has a strange sense of humor  and has some funny stories... His class can get a bit boring and redundant sometimes, but I enjoy going to most of his classes.

Steve's a really nice, interesting guy. He knows his stuff, is passionate about journalism and the environment, and was easy to learn from and listen to. Definitely take a class with him if you get the opportunity!

This is a great class to get one credit hour and it is online, but I feel that he adds those trick questions. Although, he is great to work with, especially if you do your research. I definitely will sign up with a class with him again.

I would disagree with people who said he isn't helpful. He really cares about the success of his students and always gave me good feedback for improving my stories. He expects a lot of students, but creates a laid back atmosphere in the classroom.
This guy knows his stuff, but is useless answering your questions. I emailed him numerous times and absolutely nothing in response.
He is really knowledgeable on his subject, but he's kind of absentminded. He's a nice guy and a good teacher, though.

Professor Bouhlal is a breath of fresh air to someone who has struggled in the past with foreign language. His class is rigorous but provides students at all French-speaking levels with the support they need to be successful and actually follow along in class. I really appreciated his investment in his students over the semester.

Prof. Bouhlal is a great guy. He's a native speaker so he knows a lot about correct pronunciation and grammar and he is very understanding when it comes to learning the language. He speaks quickly so you have to pay attention, but if you have a decent grasp of the language its not a problem. Funny guy, good class!
He is a great guy and cares that we are actually learning. Had this class at 7-8pm and he was a big part of the reason I actually went to it.
Great! A hard class but he's pretty easy with grading even though he takes a while to grade it. Overall good.

He was a great teacher and really helped me learn how to speak French and not just write it. He explained the grammar which is always hardest for me in a way that was easy to explain. He also allowed us to ask some questions in English and also explained in English when needed.

I have taken French for 5 years now and he is by far my favorite teacher! He truly cares about helping us learn the language as well as the culture and tries his best to provide good feedback! Overall an amazing person and would love to take another one of his classes again!

He is a nice guy, but a bit disorganized. Even in a relatively upper-level undergrad course, we found ourselves a bit confused by the grading criteria for each assignment and even what the assignment was itself. He is very understanding for absences, but you have to attend most classes.

Took into French under him. Languages can be tricky so its essential to get a good professor and Hicham pretty much there. I found some of his lectures less informative then if they were explained in English, and was a little slow grading, but ultimately he was a good and entertaining guy. Beware of his dog in class some day though!
She's great!

Avoid at all costs. Professor Hines can not separate her personal life from the classroom. She asks inappropriate questions and makes inappropriate remarks to student. She has to be reminded to post assignments to Canvas, and she is always unclear in her descriptions. Her feedback is not helpful for real classroom application. Extremely stressful.

Professor Hines can be disorganized and is not that tech-savvy (although she tries). But, she is extremely kind and genuinely cares about her students. The course itself is very theory-heavy, and like most education classes, you learn more through actually working with students than the course readings.

Professor Hines was unorganized & erratic. She is extremely hard to follow & she goes off on tangents. She will forget to post modules on Canvas weeks at a time & she requires weekly readings, which she does not go over. Her class consists of projects that she does not explain and discussion boards over the readings. Does not prepare you to teach.

Means well but is very confusing and very unorganized. Us, as students, never knew what our next assignment would be, what we had to read, when it was due, if we would have class, etc. Very large lack of communication. The content is not confusing, but the lack of organization made this class extremely hard to manage.
vague confusing frustrating disappointing

Her class boils down to "read this and comment about how it makes you feel." It's way too easy; she doesn't ask for any higher-level thinking. Part of it is because she has an open hatred of scientists. Every text she selected talks about the "evils" research, and when she found out my background in research, she made me unwelcomed.

Her directions were never quite clear enough and there was more than enough reading to last me my whole college career. As a person she was great and personable but some of her teaching approaches were a little unorganized.
Excellent teacher, extremely interesting class, high tech savvy, always accessible, creative thinker and not to mention easy on the eyes

Exams are significantly harder than practice materials and there is a good amount of extra credit provided but averages on the exams are still C-D with the extra credit. Lectures aren't always clearly explained and you should read the textbook to be able to apply what you learn in class to exams. Not a very nice person.

Her tests are significantly harder than the content taught in class and she won't explain content clearly in lecture. There's a good amount of extra credit but it doesn't get weighted as much and the average on some of the tests are below a C

Biochem is not a subject to take lightly and, despite that, I really loved how Dr. Hollenbeck was able to teach this course. There's a lot of outside work that goes into this course and you NEED to reach out if you need help understanding the concepts. Her office hours were extremely helpful with my confusion so definitely go to those.

Very hard exams. The professor explains the same thing multiple times using different terminology, confusing people, and going very fast. The class is passable because everything is weighed equally. One extra credit point is like one point on an exam, assignment, or attendance. The average on exams was 67% and that's with the extra credit
Holy. The first exam was something, it was very application based. She gave a practice exam but it was barely like the actual one.  Only 10 students out of 140 got above a 90%.......

Great at explaining lectures, but exams are unfair and overly application-based without proper prep. Introduced new material right before midterms/final with no review. Disorganized, tough grader, and no final regrades. Needs to better align teaching with testing and be more fair.

From the reviews, she must be an entirely different person in 484, because in 383 she is an absolute sweetheart who always wants the best for her students. Tests are hard but we get almost 25 points of extra credit per exam. She is also very accommodating of personal and religious schedule conflicts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not a good professor whatsoever. Exams are very hard and she doesn't want to get to know her students. Not a nice person really either and answers questions very condescendingly.
Worst professor I have ever had. Do not take biochem with her

For 483 not 484, her exams were terrible. They were way too hard and long. She asks way too detailed and deep application questions. Her lectures were fine, but you'll have to truly study all the time if you want to get a good grade. Office hours 1-on-1 with her sucked because she makes you feel like your questions are dumb. EC barely helps.

She's a decent professor, but her exams were the worst things ever. They were too long, too difficult, and the practice exams she makes don't even help you. I say take it w/ a different professor or prepare yourself to truly overwork yourself for this class w/ her. The extra credit she offers can only help you so much since you have to earn them.
Hollenbeck is one of the worst lecturers that I have ever had at IU. She takes simple topics and makes them difficult to understand. She responds to questions in a condescending manner.

Dr. Hollenbeck is knowledgeable but I wouldn't say she is the best lecturer. She tends to focus in on the smaller topics and quick through the harder topics. She sometimes has an attitude towards students during class also when simple questions are asked and I think she needs to work on her approachability. Accuracy is everything! I wouldn't take.

She honestly is not very nice to students she doesn't know or who don't come see her everyday. Everything is graded for accuracy- there are no "free" points in this class so be prepared to spend every moment on trying to get things correct, only for her teaching team to still take off points. Exams weren't too bad, but I don't recommend.

Hollenbeck is a great teacher to have for biochemistry. You can tell she really enjoys teaching it and does a great job at making the material easily understandable. Biochemistry is a hard course and it will require a lot of time to do well. If you go to class, skim the textbook, and make some flashcards you will do great.

This was one of the hardest classes I've ever taken but one of the most interesting. I loved Hollenbeck and it isso helpful if you attend her office hours. She has much extra credit and truly wants you to succeed. One of my favorite professors.

Loved Hollenbeck as a person, but her exams were horrible. She expected you to know 5-7 chapters worth of material in so much depth for only having spent such little time on each chapter. Gives chances to get points back but they're not gimme points, they're hard to get. Group quizzes are the worst and there's not nearly enough time for them.

she lectures well, but her exams are WAY too difficult for CHEM-C 483. She offers tons of extra credit but it's hard to get them. she curved exams but they were already too hard. the individual part of the group quizzes were pointless. this class is supposed to be similar to C383, but she makes it way harder and you have to memorize so much more.

This class is impossible. Do not take C 483 with Dr. Hollenbeck.
The exams are absolutely impossible and nothing like the practice exams. She is very good at teaching but the level of difficulty in this class is so above an undergraduate biochemistry course.

Amazing cares so much about her students and truly wants them to succeed not only in this class but in our future as well, long exams but loads of extra credit to balance out tough exams. Make sure to study for quizzes, they add up quickly!

She's one of the better chemistry professors I've had at IU, but definitely not the best. The lectures are pretty easy to follow, and we get points for attending. The tests are a lot harder than any of the practice problems she gives us. Be sure to read the textbook and use the practice exam to study.

It's an honors course, so she wants to challenge her students. This class gives a lot of homework which helps to boost your grade. She does not curve exams ever. The exams can cover anything you had access to (i.e., book problems, worksheets, slides not covered in class). The exams are free response and based on the application of the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: There is a lot of homework but that helps to boost your grade in the end. Exams are rough with no curve and I did not feel prepared for them at all as far as the difficulty level. She is very open to questions though and wants to challenge you as it is an honors course. The class was difficult but good if you are looking to challenge yourself.
This professor is very difficult and the midterms are super tough. The averages on them are in the 60's and 70's, and she still won't curve the tests.

All of the midterms are super hard. She doesn't curve any of the tests and her lectures aren't very helpful. You'll go into her tests thinking you're super prepared, but then end up becoming an academic victim.

Professor Hollenbeck is one of the best professors I have had at IU. Her class is graded very fairly, and she truly wants her students to succeed. As long as you go to lectures and office hours, you will do well on the exams. I highly recommend taking C383 with her.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: GO. TO. CLASS. She records lectures online but participation is like 50% of the grade. Do well on HW, quizzes, and participation and you wont stress about tests. 4 exams, and a final but you can skip/replace the grade. A few drops for hw, quizzes, and part. Lecture heavy. Dr. Hollenbeck is awesome and a great professor. She great at explaining.
Fantastic Professor. She cares about students and works hard to help them excel!

I really enjoyed H-117 with Dr. Hollenbeck. About 50% of your grade is from exam scores, but she gives the class a lot of practice questions. She also gives online quizzes each week and will answer any questions you are unsure about. While it is more in depth than the regular C-117 class, I would definitely recommend H-117 with Dr. Hollenbeck.

Dr. Hollenbeck is by far the best professor you will find in IU's chem department. Her exams are tough but fair. If you go to her office hours, you will easily get As on them. She grades very quickly and offers a TON of extra credit. Most of your grade is attendance so show up and pay attention. You'll find out quickly how kind and helpful she is.

After my past year with chemistry professors, I was a bit trepidatious about continuing on in chemistry. However, Professor Hollenbeck really changed all of that. She was the best professor I have had at IU in the Chemistry department and really inspired my adoration for biochemistry. She was always willing to help and answer all my questions.

After my past year with chemistry professors, I was a bit trepidatious about continuing on in chemistry. However, Professor Hollenbeck really changed all of that. She was the best professor I have had at IU in the Chemistry department and really inspired my adoration for biochemistry. She was always willing to help and answer my many questions.
Dr. Hollenbeck is a really great professor but the material was too difficult for a 101 class that needed no prior experience :/

I feel like she was not made to teach larger classes. I didn't learn anything from her lectures, shout out my discussion AI MacRyan, he really made this class a piece of cake. I honestly could have gotten an A if her quizzes weren't so impossible lol.

Dr. Hollenbeck is a great person and even a great professor, but this class is really difficult for a level 100 course. I learned more in the discussion rather than lectures, but lectures are graded and she would often give extra credit for exams.

I liked the instructor a lot, I think she did a great job of explaining her expectations for the course and teaching them. She also was available often and had resources when things didn't make sense. 10/10 professor. Show up to lectures and try!
She is an energetic teacher but I think the course was too difficult for an intro chemistry class
i think this class was too difficult for an 100 level chemistry class :/ but she is very energetic about teaching

Dr. Hollenbeck is a great professor. You can tell she really wants you to succeed in the course and encourages you to try your best. If you go to class, do the homework, and consistently study you'll be fine!

Professor Hollenbeck is a great professor and is by far one of the most caring professors that I have had in a science class. The class is by far not an easy A, but if you put in the work you can get there. The exams are difficult but she provides with with a bunch of study materials and provides review sessions and one on one office hour meeting.
Incredibly knowledgable on course material. Harsh grader, but great feedback

One of the nicest teachers I've ever had. Super genuine and caring towards the students writing. Sort of a harsh grader, but if you take a look at the comments that he gives back and make corrections on them in future papers, you are guaranteed to get an A in this class. Definitely reccomend meeting with him during office hours or after class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: One of my favorite teachers this year by far, Ben is so kind and really makes an effort to improve your writing, I would go to all his office hours before turning in my essays and he really made an effort to work with me. The class is set up well where you have 4 concepts each unit (movies, poems)  then you get to pick and write about that x3 units
Light asf.. just know how to write at an AP level and you'll be fine
Dr. Howell is amazing! I learned so much from him, and the class was an easy A. The exams are a little weird but not hard.
He is a great professor and truly cares about his students. His lectures are easy to read and remember. The quizzes are fairly easy and do not take much time. Easy class to get an A in
Professor Howell is a fantastic teacher; his lectures during class are a lot at times.

This was an introductory course for the THEM major, and it showed. It was so easy and I slacked off so much but still got a good grade. The whole semester was filled with busy work that didn't challenge me at all or really teach me anything. I would say 70% of the material is common sense things. Dr. Howell loves to talk about himself also.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I absolutely love Dr. Howell and the content of his lecture within the F&B lecture class. He gives out his cell phone number so is clearly available outside of the classroom. He does not have rubrics for assignments because he wants us to be creative. this did not bother me but bothered others. He talks alot about Disney but I love it

He is a nice person, but I feel like the test material was unstructured---like some questions didn't come from the book or slides. I feel like a more focused study guide would have helped, as it is challenging to study so much material and miscellaneous facts for a 38-question multiple choice exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Howell is a great professor. He tries to relate all his material back to personal experiences. He worked for Disney, so for anyone interested in working for Disney (me) he is a great connection. Really love all of his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Howell does a few things really well - he makes himself available to students and is generally in a good mood. However, I do not find him very engaging as he merely reads off the slides. He talks a little too much about how great Disney is. MWF attendance is mandatory which sucks. And some of his test questions are pulled out of thin air. Hes ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Howell is an authority in the field of which he lectures! Having spent over a decade in Disney World, and having worked all over the industry, he provides good insight and anecdotes that tie into the lectures well. He is always available to help students and is a great networking resource. In addition to teaching the content, he makes class fun
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Dr. Howell is my favorite professor at IU. He is so passionate about the industry and does so much to help students gain connections and real-world experience. He is funny, nice, and tries to make every class interactive and fun. I've taken all of his classes and, while they can be difficult and do require group work, they are some of my favorites.

Reading all these reviews and I'm like.. what? This guy is amazing. Please take all of his classes. He is so passionate about what he does and what he has done. He is willing to help students understand material and make it far in the THEM major. There is a lot of group work but in the hospitality field you work in a group.

Definitely one of my least favorite professors I've had at IU, especially in the Tourism department where the teachers are normally really nice. If you miss his MWF class six times he takes 75 points (over a full letter grade) off your final grade. Also there is a 300 point project PLUS a final. horrible horrible horrible avoid this at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class is recycled material from his other classes. Some of the assignments are the exact same as well as PowerPoints. Don't take this class if you want to learn about festivals. The only thing that related to festivals from his class was the final project.
SPH 201 Brandon is so friendly and such an expert in the hospitality and hotel field. He's laid back and a great person which makes class fun.
If Mr. Rodgers was in his 30's...

One of the best professors in the School of Public Health. Unfortunately he does nothing when it comes to group members not pulling their weight. He is very kind though, and has experience and is seeking to improve our courses at IU.

He is a really nice teacher who tries to make all his lectures interesting. I had him for Festival and Event Tourism and he has a lot of experience in this field so he did a great job of providing real world examples. Didn't use the book. Attendance was taken but was not factored into our grade for this class. A lot of this class is group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Howell is the most engaging professor I have had. His lectures can be a little boring sometimes, but he does his best to make this class as fun as he can. He gives students an opportunity to review him mid-semester and works to change what students suggest he changes. If you can take a class with him, you definitely should

This was the first class I took after I changed my major to THEM and He is now one of my favorites and I try to take any class he teaches. He is really easy to get ahold of if you have any questions and is really easy to work with. Even though you can't skip his class, (because each one is worth 100 points) I really enjoyed going!

This class is a really easy class, and he's a great professor. If you miss class, you will fail, because all of your points are from class points since it is only 1 day a week. However, he applies real life experience to his lectures, goes over each chapter in detail, and makes it easy to pass a test if you study lecture notes. never used the book.

Worst teacher I've had at IU out of my 4 years here! I'm in his senior level class & he's making all of us take our final exam at 8 am on Friday, while all of our family's are here for graduation. He deducts 20 points after 3 absences, fails you after 6, & takes attendance from the very first class. In-class assignments pretty much everyday.
Dr. Howell is by far my favorite professor I have had at IU so far!

Very easy class, and very straightforward, but I also learned a lot. Dr. Howell made all of the different countries we were learning extremely interesting, and encouraged class participation when students had been to the specific country we were discussing. There's no midterm or final, just a couple of projects, and you know about them early.
Prepare well for the mid-term using the study guide, the professor is great overall

I personally enjoyed this class. Professor Hsia is very kind and knowledgeable. His classes are very lecture-heavy and require attendance. I recommend only missing if you know someone in the class, since he doesn't post slides. Class requires two books; I only used them for the source exercises. Make sure you study for the tests, and you'll be ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good professor, cares about students. Class is very lecture heavy, but as long as you show up and take notes you will be fine. Buy the books also because you will need them for the short essays and the final. He makes the midterm and final very easy to do well on. TAs did most of the grading

I took this class for a world culture credit, and I am glad I did. Professor Hsia is a great professor, and clearly cares a lot about the subject matter at hand, as well as his students. If you put in effort, you will get an A. You don't need to read every night, but make sure you understand the material and buy the textbooks.
The lectures are a lot because you just sit there and take notes for over an hour but he is a very nice and understanding guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Ke-Chin Hsia was kind, humorous, and understanding. I took this class to fulfill a Gen-Ed credit, and I highly recommend. You have to purchase 2 textbooks but you don't actually have to read them everyday. Just read them to complete the 4 Primary Source Analysis papers. Go to lecture, complete the assignments and you'll be fine!

Professor Hsia's WWI class is lecture heavy, but it is not too difficult to find needed information for tests if you take notes. If you take fairly detailed notes, this class should be easy. He is a professor that cares for his students (he let me make-up the midterm because I was out of town!) I cannot recommend this class enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was extremely knowledge about the content, and was overall a nice person. The grading is quite lenient, especially for the papers. Attendance is mandatory, and there are in-class quizzes as well. He does not post the PowerPoints either, so I highly suggest going to class. If you do, the class is incredibly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hsia is a remarkable professor with an incredible breadth of knowledge in his field. His class was about nationalism, communism, and fascism, and his insights were genuinely impactful in my worldview. Be prepared to read a fair amount of complex works (and do extensive research for a final paper), but he does discuss them well in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Great professor who cares about his students. Grading was very generous as well. Attendence is mandatory and there are 3 pop quizzes but they were all relatively easy. Highly recomend.
I can't put everything that is wrong with his class into 350 words, just take this advice and don't take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Hsia was my professor for "Baseball as History", very nice and interesting professor who keeps the class active. The class consists of learning the history of baseball and exploring different countries and their relationship with baseball. Attendance was taken and there was some group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Lectures can be a bit redundant to the reading. That being said, because of this, you don't have to do the reading if you pay attention in lecture, vice versa. There aren't many assignments or tests, but the few writing assignments aren't pages of writing at all. Caring professor, and his almost dry sense of humor made me laugh!
There are a lot of essays and group work. Very intensive class. Don't take the baseball class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: I enjoy Prof. Hsu's course overall. She explains complex concepts using simple examples, making them easier to understand. While most classes include an attendance sheet, she allows some flexibility, which is appreciated. Additionally, she connects previous material to new concepts, creating a sense of continuous learning throughout the course.

Prof Hsu is below average for a standard professor but above average for an Econ one.. Her lectures are long and very boring. She contantly uses phrases like "refer to your memory" and things of the sort when students ask questions. She is hard to understand verbally, but compared to the other professors that teach this class, Hsu is a good bet.

Mrs. Hsu is a great professor for intermediate to Budgeting and finance. Her class is set up well and easy to understand. She makes learning the material easy and is always available to assist you if you need it.

I dont know why Prof Hunts score is so low because she is a great lecturer, kind and super knowledgeable. If you are interested in human rights you will get so much out of this class! One weekly assignment , 2 lowest scores get dropped and theres extra credit opportunities. Only thing I didnt enjoy was the group projs, but they were pretty easy.
Professor Hunt is super passionate and knowledgeable. Her lectures are straight to the point and very entertaining. Don't be scared about the score she is actually a very good professor.

I took Prof Hunts Study abroad class and had the best time. She is kind, available, and so knowledgeable in her field. If you go to class and do the readings you can get so much out of this course. The class is long but is often used to watch movies. Dr. Hunt is the best!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: if you aren't religious, pick one and start praying if you decide to take her class. not only is she an unnecessarily tough grader, but she disables your final grade on canvas until the day final grades are due so you won't know if you're failing. she's also really hard to listen to and a very slow lecturer. pls don't take a class with her.

Professor Hunt is a good professor. She is clearly passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. Her class is very lecture heavy, but I found her teaching style to be very effective and I responded well to it. Her exams aren't that difficult and always had bonus questions. Overall, I have no idea why her rating is so low, her class is great.

She clearly cares about the subject, but the lectures move so fast that understanding the material feels optional. She is an extremely tough grader, yet students were never allowed to see their grades throughout the semester, despite being told they would be released at the end which apparently, is a conceptual idea rather than an actual deadline.
Ran her class like a cult. If you are not willing to play the whole student pretends to care and excited to participate game, you will struggle. She loves a good suck up.

Professor Hunt is solid. She cares deeply about the topics she teaches about, as well as the students within her class if you participate or try. You can get by without reading if you attend class, and she does give opportunity to improve grades. Don't let the rating dismay you, she aint that bad

Attendance matters, weekly assignment, 2 exams, and a final group project. She wasn't my favorite professor in the world and her reviews on here scared me at first, but most of the reviews weren't correct in my experience. She's knowledgeable, answers any questions you have, and makes the exams extremely fair and topic-related.
Test are brutal and even when you feel confident the grading and the level of complexity required is a lot.

Ok, so I took this class my freshman year and the lectures are so boring and it's basically her rambling for 50 mins straight. A huge amount of readings outside of class and is a harsh grader. There is only two exams on paper that are each worth 25% of your grade and just an assignment a week that also requires a stupid amount of reading.

Grade isn't bad if you put in effort, but she is a terrible professor. She grades very unfairly and doesn't give much guidance. Rude feedback, and doesn't explain well why she takes points off. She's very rude and not understanding if you're sick. DO NOT take a class with her. One of the worst professors I've had at IU.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr Hunt is a caring and passionate professor. International Human Rights Law is her specialty, so she knows what shes talking about. Attend lectures, take good notes, and befriend her - always willing to chat after class. Exams are online and open note, so aslong as you take good notes, you'll be fine! Readings are not super mandatory to succeed.

Professor Kate Hunt was challenging to keep up with. The course is given in a way by her that requires too much time outside of class. The readings are very long and focus heavy on a topic or two throughout the whole semester. Even as a woman studying women rights I had challenges cooperating with the class material most times.
Professor Hunt was one of the hardest professors I have experienced throughout my first year at college when it comes to grading.
Class material can be heavy at time. The readings are too much.
Made attendance mandatory and that's where she lost me...

Not an understanding professor whatsoever. Will not care what you go through on a personal level as long as shes living happy. Would not recommend to anyone that might have 1% of extra challenges on their outside world such as work or personal matters.

Dr. Hunt seems like a nice person and is clearly knowledgable about human rights issues. However, she struggles to teach this knowledge and relies too heavily on readings and class discussion from students rather than presenting her own thoughts and ideas. Her grading is also unclear and doesn't give a lot of room for error. Would not recommend!

Professor Hunt is really nice, very educated, willing to give extra help. She gives great lectures and cares about the material and her students. The class was interesting, but make sure you take notes, watch the lectures, and do all the readings because it's a lot of material. The quizzes aren't super easy, so make sure you know your stuff.

As long as you care a bit, you should do decent in this class. Her lectures are kind of worthless, as she just rambles on and on. However, it is essential to attend lecture and take notes on the slides she puts up since the exams are open note and online. She assigns a ridiculous amount of reading, which I did for a while but eventually quit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's a very nice teacher who genuinely cares about human rights and just wants people to be educated in it. The class isn't hard as long as you do the readings. The tests are online so it's not terrible but you have to know your information. Definitely go to her office hours!

Awful professor. She also monitors her page here and tries to remove negative comments about her while posting positive ones herself. Telling people to "ignore the other reviewers" makes it even more obvious.

I would strongly recommend avoiding this professor. She was consistently rude and disrespectful. She had totally unclear grading standards that wouldn't be disclosed until after she grades an assignment. I certainly did not leave this class with greater knowledge.

As a disabled student, I would never recommend taking her class. At a few points she presented things promoting eugenics as neutral and interesting and encouraged my classmates to support the viewpoint. In addition to rarely staying on topic in class or even having a topic. I did very well in this class and I still would not recommend it to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. Class based almost entirely on the readings, which students read and present to each other while she sits there. Unclear grading material and an absurdly difficult midterm. She can also be quite rude.

Do not take her class. She has no standards for grading and when you ask her for the rubric she wont give it. I have no idea why I got the grades I did and her comments on papers are rude. If youre reading this Kate hunt you need to change your class. The worst professor Ive had at IU.

I learned nothing in Kate Hunt's class. It's an easy course with not many assignments, but when it comes down to the final you're screwed because you're supposed to know everything when she hasn't taught anything. All discussion based on the readings no one did and she just sits there saying "mhm yeah"

I wouldn't say Prof. Hunt was the best or the worst in the world. I took S211 with him, and it's easy to fall behind because each lesson builds on the previous one (especially with coding stuff), but as long as you're attending/paying attention in class and staying on top of work, it's doable!

Okay, I wouldn't say Prof. Hunt was the best OR the worst in the world. I took S211 with him, and you definitely need to attend class because each lesson builds on the previous one, making it easy to fall behind (especially with coding stuff). As long as you pay attention and stay on top of work, though, you got it! Honestly just gotta lock in :)

Okay, I wouldn't say Prof. Hunt was the best in the world, but he wasn't the WORST either! I took S211 with him, and you definitely need to attend class because it's very easy to fall behind, but it is doable! The lessons build on the previous one, but as long as you pay attention and stay on top of work, you got it!
4 years later and Paul Hunt still can not teach in a way that is sufficient in understanding how to code.
He is a difficult grader. He will deduct a point, even though it is correct and 100% accurate on the previous course.

Writes a ton of stuff on paper, and projects it on the front screen but it all looks like chicken scratch. Uses Greek letters and symbols with little to no explanation at high speeds of learning. Don't recommend whatsoever.

This class is difficult for a variety of reasons. "Paul" teaches using greek letters and expects you to understand their meaning without any explanation. You are required to watch videos before class in order to complete the homework and to do well in the class, but attendance is mandatory even though you are teaching yourself.

S301 forces you to teach yourself everything before class through videos. The videos posted to help us aren't helpful and aren't similar to the pre-class quiz checks. In class, you complete an activity (only 2 are dropped the entire semester) where you are expected to have already understood the content. The exams are also all fill in the blank.

Prof. Hunt uses a flipped classroom, but provides so little material outside of lectures that it is almost impossible to understand the material without doing extra research. Even though it's a flipped classroom, you still have to both take notes AND do homework outside of class, while doing additional work in class. Not a good Prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Class was easy and she is a good resource to have for opportunities but she is not a good teacher and professor. Rambles about laptops for half the class and lectures feel repetitive and boring. Assignments are busy work that felt like a waste of your time. I agree with other reviewers saying that they could've learned more from an email.

Great resource to have for internships and opportunities but class was a huge waste of time and all she does is ramble on about the same things the whole semester. Felt like her class and her final project was a complete waste of my time. Also be ready for her to complain about laptops for half of the class every other class.

Meh lecturer, I don't feel that my professional knowledge has been improved at all from attending her course. Great person to have a connection to for future job placement though, she receives many requests from companies looking for future HR leaders and they trust her input.

Best teacher I have ever had. The environment she created walking in the room, so refreshing. Every story, piece of advice she gave, encouraged me to want to succeed. If I could recommend this class to every student at IU, regardless of their major, I would. She encouraged me to pursue fantastic opportunities, not just in HR, but also in life.

Cheryl is the best professor I've had. Her lectures are enjoyable and inspirational. She really cares about her students. She definitely likes student that speak their minds during class but is still very kind and lenient with everyone. I will definitely be prioritizing my schedule around her classes because she is that enjoyable.

I have had her for two classes and in my experience she has been the easiest going professor I've had. Her lectures may be hard to sit through and understand but her assignments were easy for me and if you ever need extra time for an assignment or need an accommodation, see her after class and she will be more than willing to do that. Great Person!

Listen I think Cheryl is a great person. However, as a professor, she is not adequate. Her lectures consist of her telling stories that often go way off topic or her complaining something relating to her life. She has also received plenty of feedback regarding this lack of structured lectures and still has done nothing about it. Hard grader too.

Cheryl is one of the best professors I have ever had. She takes the time to get to know her students individually and is willing to help you make connections for internships and jobs if you work hard and take the time to know her. If you want to do the bare minimum this class is not for you, but if you work hard you won't regret taking her class!

Cheryl is grotesquely obsessed with the corporate world. All her lectures could be fit into a single email and it would've been more helpful. She just rants and goes on tangents for an hour and spend no time on the actual topic. The tests have nothing to do with the lectures, so good luck if you don't retain reading information from textbooks well.

Professor Hughes is the most amazing teacher I have EVER had! She is such a wonderful teacher and person and will always go out of her way to help students out. She is a no-nonsense kind of a professor and will always go the extra mile to learn about her students. Her classes are interesting and engaging! Please do yourself a favor and take her!

SO passionate about IU/her students. If you just want to do the bare minimum don't take her. If you have a genuine curiosity about real HR experience and willing to go to office hours and make that connections she will open so many doors for you. Class discussions are great if you like to engage and are grown up enough to handle different opinions.

Shes incredibly disorganized. Its almost impossible to get through one slide deck. She always has a random story and goes off into a tangent. PowerPoints or book dont really reflect the exams since theyre extremely conceptual. Cherns case is too long and she pushes off so many chapters just for you to do them all at the end. V sweet

I've had the "pleasure" of taking two classes with her. Lectures are pointless, as she prefers "using real-world examples" which are really just hour-long rants about random topics that aren't relevant to my professional life. If you suck up to her, you can be added to outside topics and get in with her connections, which is nice if you're HR.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is an easy A but her lectures have nothing to do with tests. Goes on rants the whole class about random stories and often stays on the same slide for an hour and a half. Painful to sit through and if you have another class with her, beware she will tell the exact same stories.

Professor Hughes is inspirational. Her teaching style is meant to get collaboration working , she wants her students to speak to eachother and have respectful disagreeances. You will be expected to read the material. The reading directly reflect the real world application Cheryl talks about this is a critical thinking course not regurgitation.

If you aren't an HR major, don't take this class. Everyone preaches about the connections she has, but they're only beneficial for HR majors. The class sessions are a waste of time. She doesn't cover exam material very well, if at all. I didn't learn anything in this course.

Cheryl is an interesting professor. Definitely someone who has a lot of connections and very willing to help students find internships/jobs, but only if you establish a relationship with her. Her lectures get super off topic and are not at all helpful for the tests so make sure you read the book when you study. Makes you use TopHat which is $30.

You can tell she cares about her students, but her classes aren't conducive to learning. Her lectures quickly turn into disorganized rants and stories, but her tests require memorizing parts of the book. Would be a good connection to have, but only outside of the classroom; couldn't get past her opinionated/semi-aggressive personality to do so.

She tries to make lectures interesting, but it just turns into random tangents about past experiences/students. Her slides in class are basically useless, and her tests require you to memorize the textbook (even though she doesn't think the book is useful?). Going to class is a waste, but takes attendance. Read and study or you won't pass the tests

There is not much homework at all in this class. She tries to make lectures interesting with video clips and personal stories. She really cares about her students and if you put the effort in to get to know her, you won't regret it!

Cheryl truly cares about her students. If you are an HR major, definitely take at least one class with her; she has a lot of stories and a lot of connections from the field. If you are not an HR major, I think it is still worth taking a class with her and building a relationship. There is a lot to learn from her.

Cheryl is a great person and professor. Doesn't cover much of specifics from the book, but rather lectures about her experiences and real-life application/examples. Read the chapter notes and slides if you want to get good grades on her exams/discussion boards online. Kind of vague with instructions, but she's super willing to help if you ask!

Least substantive class and professor I've had at IU. Endless unmoderated class discussion... we spend entire classes talking about Kesha, Donald Trump, the Apple FBI controversy, and whether or not we think it is bad that kids get trophies for only participating. She reads from textbook powerpoints  and shows youtube videos.  Learned nothing.
Great person. Cares about her student. Easy A. Discussions are often unrelated to class. I didn't learn anything during class time and the outside of class work was not challenging.

In her 336 class right now. Love going to her class, actually look forward to it! interesting, interactive, and informative lectures. learn new things everyday! OH AND SHE GOT US CHIPOTLE TO CLASS!!!! WHO DOES THAT!?!?!?!

Professor Hughes gave a lot of real life examples in class where you can actually use the information that you learned in the classroom. She loves to have class discussions where you can voice your opinions and it opens your mind up to other views. She loves to have class discussions rather than just taking notes all class period.

Covered only 2 chapters out of the book she specifically 'made' for the class. NEVER stayed on topic, EVER. I even turned in my final assignment EARLY, and she lost it and gave me a 0100. Don't take ANY of her classes if you actually want to learn something and not just listen to her rantsstories. And I thought she was going to be awesome :(

Best instructor at IU hands down. Truly cares about her students and will bend over backwards for you if you put forth effort to contact her. Great availability, great class setup. Doesn't use textbooks, encourages discussion. I've learned the most in her classes. If you have a chance to take any of her classes, do it. You won't regret it.
Great Professor and genuinely caring person.  Was very helpful in all aspects.  Very willing to help with resumes, internship searches etc..TAKE HER CLASS!
CHERYL IS THE BEST. Not only professor, but you can tell she is a wonderful person too.TAKE HER CLASS!

Cheryl is the best! HR is her passion and she will go above and beyond to help students if they dont understand something, need help, or want to talk & get some advice. all the exams were open note so not too bad, though u may want to READ the book to do well. Attendance is mandatory, but she is a lively instructor so class is never boring.

TAKE HER CLASS!!!!!! If you take Human Resourses with her, TAKE IT. Her classes aren't lectures, more of a class discussion. Open book exams. She wants you to do well and learn A LOT. And that you do. She does everything to help her students.
Professor Hughes is pretty awesome

Do everything you can to take one of her classes. She is an absolutely amazing teacher who loves her students and is very passionate about teaching.  Class is mainly discussion based and tests were all take-home or open book.  I learned so much in this class that was practical to my life and to my future career path.  She is very fun and helpful!

Really great professor. Ive had her twice and would take one of her classes again. she's really energetic so the class isnt too boring. shes really helpful in and outside class. really helpful with internships and networking
She is so easy! The class is boring, but it is easy. She is willing to help her students as much as they need. Awesome teacher, you should take her!

Great Professor, will do anything to help see her students succeed which is becoming rare amongst profs these days.  Make sure if she is an option you get into one of her classes, you won't regret it.
She is the coolest! awesome class!
I dont know what to say but you need take her class.

Cheryl is a nice person, but I hated this class. I did not learn ANYTHING, and I am pretty sure she came to class without any thought of what she was going to say. She would just get up there and ramble on and on about nonsensical things, elevating the absurdness of her story telling until she got some kind of satisfactory audience reaction.

She is so helpful! She has lots of experience in her career and she is a great source for networking.  She is always willing to help students get their foot in their door through her contacts.  She connects class topics to real life experience and helps students understand the real life application of her class.  She was awesome!!

Loved her! She is so easy and helpful and if she thinks something is going to hurt your grade, she will give a different assignment. The midterm was either in class with all your notes or take home which u have a week to do. The biggest part of the class is a big group project but its not bad bc she helps you soo much! Take her class!!

Amazing lectures! This class was not only very informative but I found it entertaining too. Grades are test-heavy but they were pretty straightforward and easy to study for. I would honestly take this class again if I could!

Kurt was the best professor I've had! As long as you go to class and take notes and read the textbook, you should pass the class with no problems. He doesn't give anything outside of class but his lectures are interesting and he makes the class more fun.  There are very few grades though, so make sure to take exams seriously.

My favorite professor I've had at IU so far. I'm not interested in social psychology, but he made it very interesting! I liked how he doesn't post his lectures on canvas because it gave me much more motivation to come to class. Exams are easy as long as you go to lectures and know the vocab.

He was great!!  Attendance is mandatory, everything is given in class and he doesn't post anything on Canvas. If you go to lecture and take notes and read some of the text, you should be able to pass the exam easily. He also makes class interesting and makes the topics more interesting.

this class had a lot of reading and some were interesting, and kurt was good at explaining them. unfortunately, this class was the reason i switched my major. if you're one of his favorite students or participate the most, you'll receive more positive feedback. if not, good luck

he's one of THE BEST lecturer i've ever had. if you're taking his class, make sure you write notes during lectures because he doesn't post slides on canvas. he makes lectures so interesting and he's always down for a one on one conversation about anything you're interested in. there are also in class writing sometimes so come to class! BUT HES GOOD
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Kurt is the best professor and lecturer I've ever had. He is very knowledgeable and his lectures are very engaging. I could listen to him talk for hours, and classes go by very fast. He does not post anything on Canvas so you are forced to go to the lectures. Very test heavy, but straightforward and not hard. I wish I could take this class again!

I LOVE KURT! He's one of my favorite profs here and really is passionate about this class. I love social psychology, but he made this class so much more enjoyable. There weren't really any assignments other than one paper towards the end of the semester, but you can write it on pretty much whatever you want, so it's worth it.

Kurt was my favorite professor yet at IU! The class has few assignments so it is very test heavy. He makes the lectures extremely clear though so if you pay attention you will do great on the tests. He does not take attendance but he does do occasional in class assignments that you can only know about if you attend class.

Kurt is the greatest lecturer I have had the pleasure of having so far at IU. He is incredible. The material is a little bit difficult, but he makes it super interesting. Primarily graded on exams with few in class writing assignments and one essay. You don't necessarily have to go to class (only does attendance sometimes)but you definitely should.
Passionate, funny, entertaining, smart, respectable
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVED this class with Kurt. Im not big into social psychology, but he made the lectures engaging and fun, and you learn a lot about him as the course goes on. He's an open book who is willing to help his students. There aren't a lot of assignments that are graded, so the class is very test heavy, with occasional writing assignments.

Kurt was the best professor I've had at IU. The course is lecture heavy as 90% of the exams come from lectures but his lectures are never boring. Very animate and entertaining lectures. Textbook is separate and you have to read it but only like $20. Not many assignments, only one paper and 4 exams but they aren't difficult. Highly recommend him.

Social psychology is my favorite class I've ever taken because of Kurt Hugenberg. I took his class last fall and I still think about how much I loved his class and enjoyed it enough to come back and rate him a year later. I recommend taking any class with Hugenberg because his lectures are so fun and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A very funny and well-spoken professor. Grades were largely based on tests, but they were pretty easy with studying. The only annoying thing was that he would randomly grade attendance with small in-class prompts that you would have to turn in. He dropped one test grade. In addition, the report was extensive, but fun.

You are graded on very few things and your attendance is marked randomly which he intentionally does on days when the least amount of students are present. The material isn't difficult plus I did well on the essay assignment. I cannot believe I got a B because of the inadequate and lazy way this course is laid out.
He was great! No complaints! You get out what you put into the class!

This prof is very nice! He is almost theatrical in the way he lectures, the class is not really boring! He does random in class writing assignments that can definitely affect your grade if you don't participate. The exams, I think 4 of them, are somewhat easy. If you study the vocab from book & know the studies you're good.

Kurt was an amazing professor. His lectures were always very interesting. He is also always willing to answer questions. The tests are very fair, and if study you will be fine, especially bc they are all multiple choice. Attendance is not mandatory, but he gives in class writing assignments randomly that are worth a lot and cannot be made up
Kurt is a wonderful man and a great professor, but MAN his class was probably the most taxing and difficult of all of my classes. Still worth it, I suppose.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I had Kurt and loved his class. Its almost entirely based on group discussion so you do need to be prepared but its also okay to not understand concepts because questions are encouraged and he loves to see students engaged. If I wasn't graduating I'd take another class with him. And he helped me figure out grad school and was so patient with me.

Kurt is the literal best, like so nice. I loved stereotyping and prejudice because Kurt made it so interesting and engaging. Kurt loves to see his students getting involved in the group discussion (which is 90% of the lecture, so be prepared to participate) and come up with new ideas. Overall this class is great. 10/10 would recommend

He is a great professor. I took 2 classes with him, and he was very supportive and knowledgeable. I hope to be able to work with him or take more classes with him again in the future. Great course and it can be challenging, but keep up with the lectures and review frequently and it will be fine.

You can tell he is VERY smart, knows everything he's teaching super well. if you aren't a bio, or animal science major, I'd probably not recommend this class because I think it'd be hard if you weren't. Going to lectures is very important there's a 2q quiz every lecture but as long as you are in lectures the quizzes are very easy. Really liked him.

This is a difficult class. It is very lecture and reading-heavy, as there are two-question quizzes during every class session that cover the previous session's lecture. A lot of information is covered. With this said, I adored this class and professor. I found the material engaging and interesting, so I did very well.

Okay to be honest this class was not that hard to pass. He does do daily quizzes (only 2 questions) based on previous lectures so if you're not there he won't let you make it up unless if you let him know before class. The lectures can get boring at times. Also I suggest you know the material well before the exams because it's a lot.

i loved his class because i'm passionate about chimpanzees, and he's definitely the most efficient in that subject. the class can bit a bit annoying because there are quizzes every single class, and all of the options seem reasonable, but I think it's worth it if you're passionate about the subject.
