Make sure to keep up with the reading as much of the class is structured around discussion. Also, he is really open to helping you if you need it.  Go to office hours!

I took Prof. Kreilkamp's L202 class as a senior English minor, much later than the norm. I think Prof. Kreilkamp is the perfect professor to teach an introductory course. Though I needed no convincing about my path in college, his enthusiasm could truly be the deciding factor for a student at the beginning of their IU career. He cares.

I really like Professor Kreilkamp. He's really enthusiastic about the books we read and makes class feel like a really fun book club meeting. He tends to ramble on a bit but he's generally entertaining. If you do the reading (which can be lengthy) it's a pretty easy class.

One of the BEST instructors I've had. He put so much effort into preparing students through detailed reading guides and extensive essay suggestions. He took a whole part of class to discuss what students can actually do with an English degree. He's sincerely interested in improving writing skills, and mine are better for it. Stellar, very engaging.

Considering the anticipated level of difficulty of this course (lit theory!), this class was fantastic. The world of theory is huge, and dense, and Ivan wonderfully engaged students, helping us jump right into the material. I also loved that he encouraged us to analyze the world around us (pop culture, etc) through the theory lens.
He is a REALLY great prof, lectures are generally great and he gets everyone talking. Class was really a lot of fun! Be aware that he will call you out for an answer in class
Did not make the material clear at all. He expects students to teach the class through presentations.

This class was very unorganized. I'm pretty sure that I knew as much about what we'd do that day going into class as she did. Shes pretty lenient though and chill most of the time. If you put in a little effort, she'll like you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I thought she was pretty chill for a literature professor, I had a lot of fun in her class and I thought that the topic was interesting. Overall good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: As a comparative literature major, I think she's entirely unprepared as a professor, and I found most of our discussions to be aimless and underwhelming. I've never had a professor disregard their own syllabus to the extent she did, and I often felt as if she had barely read the texts we discussed in class. Constantly late and very disorganized

One of the worst professors I have had. She is late to class every day and we did not have a single grade in the grade book in till literally the day before grades were due for the semester. This class was basically a book club, we did little to no work and class was basically sitting in a circle talking about pointless things.

I have never had such a horrendous professor in my entire life and am absolutely appalled that any university would keep her on their payroll.She never once updated grades, didn't follow her own syllabus,adamantly defended a pedophile in a novel she assigned, and did not provide a single trigger warning for the multiple SA scenes we read. Fire her.

Worst Professor I've ever had at IU. Never available for email and frequently is late to class, also holds you after to make up for her being late. Doesn't communicate about location of class or assignments, and penalizes the class entirely for her faults. Grades very hard and gives you less than a week to read huge books. Do not recommend at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Izabela is so unorganized and everyday seems like she's off her game. She is forgetful and kind of a mess every day. You really need to participate in her class, to keep it going. Not a horrible class if you enjoy the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She was really nice but did not seem well prepared for class. She openly admitted to not having a plan for our class, and did not have a syllabus saying what we were doing in the class. She sometimes took attendance, but also sometimes forgot to. Most of the stuff seemed to be for completion, but not everything. She was really inconsistent.
Easy class and she tells you everything you need to know to do well on the tests/papers as long as you're paying attention.

She is such a sweetheart and you will enjoy her class a lot if you participate and have outside conversations with her. There is a very average amount of reading that usually does not take long, and sometimes you have to watch movies. The writings are usually just one-paragraph reflections that take about 15 mins to write. She's very knowledgeable
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This was one of the worst professors I've had at IU so far. She knows a lot about the subject but that doesn't matter because she only cares about student's writing skill. It is a pop culture class and I felt like I was in an intensive writing course. She had a very specific view on how she wanted assignments to be written
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Prof Potapowicz is interested in the subjects she teaches, and you can tell. If you come interested in learning, she's a great prof. If you don't give a damn, find someone who prefers lecture to discussion. Readings were generally easy, with the exception of movies nothing took longer than 30 min. If you just try, papers and tests are easy too.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Worst class I've ever taken, worst professor I've ever had.

He gets frustrated easily, especially if he thinks your question is stupid or does not understand. Seemed as though he had never taught a beginner class before, and he is so knowledgeable, that it was hard for him to understand that the class was lost. Overall, the class was very difficult for someone who had no background in coding.

Eduardo is a really great professor but, because he knows so much, there can be days where people who don't have a significant background in programming can get extremely lost. This means you're reliant on your own work on homework and other assignments to fill in the gaps. For that reason, approach this class with a little independence.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a difficult class if you show up. Some of the concepts are a little complex, but there's YouTube videos on every subject that also explain it. He loves participation, even if it's just throwing in your 2 cents about the topic. He does give a reading assignment before almost every lecture.

Really enjoyed this class- the assignments were appropriately challenging and interesting, and I'd say I learned quite a bit about modeling. Definitely recommend this course and instructor. As a quick caveat: you should be comfortable with programming before taking this class, as the pre-reqs suggest. There's not really time to re-learn everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Eduardo is interesting. I didn't find him very approachable, but we both may be awkward. I found his programming classes moved too quickly and spent a lot of time working with the TA (who wasn't very helpful, but that's not Eduardos fault). Overall take a programming class for basics and then go into his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Izquierdo is very intelligent and approachable. His lectures were very engaging, straight-forward, and applicable to the real world. Light reading (1-5 pages) and watched 3 movies for homework. Prof. Izquierdo just wants you to open your mind. Go to the out-of-class recommended lectures, they are very interesting. LOOK AT GRADE DISTRIBUTIONS.

Eduardo is an awesome professor. He is an engaging, passionate lecturer and a kind grader. He was not strict about doing things his way; he didn't care how we got the assignment done (including which programming language we chose to use) as long as we got it done.
His tests are very difficult. If you aren't a very good test taker, I would avoid his class. However, his lectures are very interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've had as an undergraduate. Took SOC 101 as an extra credit course after dying from 4 semesters of graduate level chemistry. Worst mistake. This is "101" level course and "101" level material, but all of the grading criteria is extremely subjective and arbitrary. Got an A- in a class where "education" was a vocab word

he's okay. i definitely wouldn't want to take a class from him again. you can tell that he taught an upper level sociology at a different school before he came to UMKC. he's expecting too much from his students in a 101 class.

I enjoyed his class,  his lectures were entertaining and involved his own stories and experience when appropriate.  I felt he was a hard enough grader and expected a lot out of his students.  Overall I would take a class from him again and recommend him to those who have not yet had a class with him.

This class was really interesting and Hubert does give a good amount of work. Keep up with the readings, make sure your phone does not go off or he will definitely ask you to leave. He knows the material, has a genuine interest in the subject matter, loves participation and often tells funny, random stories. Class is pretty enjoyable.
Very interesting class and I enjoyed his teaching style. The class is a discussion of books you read throughout, very thought provoking. A pretty fair amount of work, but I learned a ton!
He's really a great guy, he explains things clearly, and his assignments and exams are fair. Also, he's pretty easy on the eyes so that's always a plus.

There is basically 0 work to do in this class, I'm not sure why everyone else says she gives out more work. Dr. G is passionate about what she does but this class was extremely boring and will make you not want to go if I'm being honest. I recommend taking her, but if there is another professor that isn't attendance mandatory I would choose them.

Dr. G is an amazing professor and I would recommend her Kelley Compass 1 lecture to any incoming freshman. She is passionate and involved in her area of study and as a recruiter herself she offers insider information on her field. She only grades by a few projects in each unit so turning in one late assignment could tank your grade, so be careful!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is amazing. I took her for both Kelley Compass 1 & 2. She always brings energy to every class and has such an adorable personality. She will spend hours helping you prepare for job interviews and teaching you useful tips and skills. The assignments she gives are also really manageable, and she is always willing to help you.

She cares about her students' futures. I thought her assignments were manageable. She allowed 2 absences before a letter drop. She let students talk to her about their grades and was willing to change them once they made corrections. She may not be the easiest teacher, but I didn't put that much effort into the class and enjoyed her wisdom.

Professor Gibelato cares a lot about her students and their success. She makes class fun with music and excitement in her voice. Office hours are constantly provided which helps with the grading structure as there are multiple little details that can be counted off for if not included.

I would definitely recommend you take this class with her. She deserves a major promotion - I took this class with her two years ago, and to this day, I hope she gets promoted past Kelley Compass so that I will be able to take another professional development class with her. Very clear grading criteria, and genuinely cares about all her students.

I think out of all the T175 professors, Dr. Gibelato is by far one of the best, she really cares about her students, although you do have to put some work in for the class, I think the material she teaches actually helps to prepare for future endeavors within the business school. Ask questions during office hours, and you will be fine.
Too hard for a 1.5 credit Kelly Compass class, and she grades very harsh. There are also a lot more work required than other compass classes. Would not recommend.

Izabely is the best professor you could have for this class. She cares about her students and teaches very relevant and helpful information. She is constantly asking for feedback from students to make the class better catered to us. Only thing is she is not great with responding to emails, but she is very lenient and gives extensions whenever.
Not the easiest class you can get for Compass, but she is amazing. Lectures are fun and engaging and she is the sweetest professor you will find at Kelley.
Way more work than any other compass class. Lectures are a complete waste of time but mandatory. Nice person though.

While Compass is supposed to be a less challenging class, Professor Gibelato made it the complete opposite. The first class she assigned us to read a 30-page case study and turn in a corresponding assignment with it. In comparison to my other classes like K204 and B251, this class was a lot more work for a class that is only 1.5 credit hours.

Hands down THE best professor you can have.
Get her if you can. She cares, she is fun, and you will learn a LOT.

While compass isn't the most fun class. Dr. Gibelato sure finds a way to make the lectures fun and engaging. She is a person cares a lot about her class and her students but also sees the human in them (not common @ Kelley). She is literally always willing to help. Pay attention in class, talk with her if you have issues, and you will be A ok!
She makes compass, which is supposed to be an easy class, much harder than it should be. However, if you put in work you can easily get an A/A+.

Dr. Gibelato is a great professor and tries her best to bring out the best in students. She is very kind-hearted and helpful. There are around five assignments that you get a week or more on, the grading is exact, so if you don't follow those guidelines you will get points docked off.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really loved professor Gibelato, It was her first year teaching that year I had her and she graded HARD. Compass is suppose to be an easy A, and she made it not an easy A. However if you were willing to meet her in office hours she was very happy to help you. I do not know if her grading has change since then but she is a good person.

I really loved professor Gibelato, It was her first year teaching that year I had her and she graded HARD. Compass is suppose to be an easy A, and she made it not an easy A. However if you were willing to meet her in office hours she was very happy to help you. I do not know if her grading has change since then but she is a good person.

K-Compass1:

One of the most inspirational professors I met. She emphasizes the importance of realizing important career decisions and she teaches her students with sincere advice followed by her own experience.hardworking professor that is really considerate and there when you need her. Definitely attend her office hours she is a true sweetheart.

She is my favorite professor! She cares about her students so much and helped me not only in this class, but she helped me prepare for interviews, improve my essays and improve my resume. Her class was enjoyable and she is such a sweet person.

Her section may seem intimidating at first but I would definitely take her class. It is more work than other sections, but she actually provides incredibly insightful information when it comes to acing interviews and recruiting. If you do bad on an assignment just go to office hours and she'll change it to a 100. Great person, get to know her.

Sooo confusing and awful trying to figure out what was going on.  She's so unorganized and does not know what she's doing.  She is a really, really nice lady but does not know what she's doing.  Assignments popped up randomly and syllabus was not followed or accurate at all.  I got an A+ because she liked me, idk

The absolute nicest professor I have come across. Her classes are extremely engaging, and I regularly found myself chatting with her for 20-30 minutes beyond class. She cares about every single student in class, personally helping out anyone who has any kind of trouble. Would definitely recommend taking Compass with her.
No exams, but a big group project. If you can, take Jayma for this class. She is so awesome, and you learn so much. Tons of incredibly interesting guest speakers.
She was really knowledgeable about the topic and was a really engaging class. Only reason for A- was that I did not do any of the extra credit assignments. Really enjoyed it and would take again.

One of my more interesting courses taken at IU. I took Sports Law back in Spring of 2021. This professor is very demanding for attention and professionalism. However, should you buy into her presentation of the class, it can be very rewarding. Some of the most in-depth projects and papers were done in this class, yet the final product is rewarding.

Professor Meyer is an incredible instructor - she is deeply passionate about course material, while boasting an impressive legal record and multiple connections. Sports Law is an adept introduction into the legal realm of sports; assignments are somewhat annoying, case briefs and group assignments are graded confusingly, but proved to be helpful.

The class itself is fun but the grading criteria is really muddy. You are expected to do a lot of random power points and in class group exercises; which would be fine if they were adequately explained and we were given enough time to actually complete them.  However, the course is guest speaker heavy which is fun because really cool people come.
He also yelled often, and made so many students super anxious to even come to class. 3 students reported him to the dean and were told that it was just his teaching style.

He truly requires more time than any other class, outwardly humiliates, and will physically hit pictures of your face on walls. It's more about the process than product for him so prepare to fluff, It's NOT for the weak.
Yes, James is a harsh grader but it's worth it. James knows what he's talking about and you really learn a lot from him by being in his class. He wants everyone to do good and helps you get there.

James is an amazing professor. He really shows care about his students and their work and strives to make them work for it. He makes stunning work and is a really great mentor. IU Photo is so lucky to have such an amazing person and instructor! Great prof if you have a passion for photography!

James is not only a respected photographer, but he is also a respected professor and role model. He makes you work for your grade, but he gives you the feedback you need in order to be the artist of your full potential. Taking a class with him is an honor and a privilege, and I could not be anymore fulfilled to have had a class with him.

I was a bit surprised to read some of these comments that ride James off as some professor that takes hiatus' during class and doesn't teach. This couldn't be more wrong. People forget that James is a working artist who is constantly shows work worldwide. To be taught under him is a privilege if you're SERIOUS about art making.

James is widely known for his digital photographs, and has exhibitions around the world. Thus, he will likely miss at least two weeks of classes and you will be working with TAs. Don't fret though, your TAs are likely to be just as incredible as James. If you're lucky, he will bring his dog to class to soften the pain you'll feel during critiques.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class was NOT easy. It was split between him (photo) and another professor (printmaking). He is a fairly hard grader and it was hard to understand what he really wanted from us. Very unorganized class and I often felt very stressed out. Some of the things he had us do ended up being useless information we did nothing else with...

James was a mentor to me and many others in graduate school. He opened a lot of doors for students and treated them as colleagues. Work hard, push yourself, and you will be rewarded for your effort. His feedback is valuable, and he works tirelessly to build a community of learners. He is an accomplished artist as well.
Is fairly unorganized, class usually doesn't know what's going on.  Plays favorites with certain people, & basically treats others like crap for no apparent reasons.  Inadequate instruction n

He should change the name of the class to everyday is a critique day and you wont learn anything in digital photography or Photoshop. I suggest you do all of your work a year or two in advance so the class discussions can actually move forward. Also he assumes this class is your number one priority when its just an elective.

He is a tough teacher, but I learned a great deal in his class. I like him as a person, and he's not always easy to deal with- but most people aren't. He tells you what he thinks and offers you real advice and opinions. I have taken several classes from him and always learn a lot.

james is tough thats for sure, but if you actually take the time to talk to him with well thoughout ideas he is extremely helpful. his class was hard at times. but that was only because he said exactly what he thought of my work. if it was bad he would tell me and if it was good he'd rave, which was cool. an honest opinion is hard to find, hes it.
james took a hiatus from our class for a few weeks, so basically he never taught. his work is terrible, and it's hard to learn from someone when you don't like his work.
this guy is bananas, his work is mediocre and he is way into telling you how much your work sucks.
James is tough.  Real tough.  But he's good.
James can be hard to understand at times, but if you take the time to actually listen to him instead of getting frustrated with him he a great prof.

Technical skills in photograhy are severly lacking and his teaching skills are even worse...  I truly believe the only reason he is teaching at IU is because his once short lived success in Digtal Photography.  This man can not teach!

I enjoyed this class. It was very lecture heavy but makes sense for an 8 week course. He is very experienced and knows what he's talking about. He does Tophat so attendance is pretty mandatory. The tests are kinda hard I would take good notes in class and use his examples. I think he's kind and funny I would take him again.

Professor Davis is very knowledgeable about the subject, but has an ego about it. 70% of your grade is exams and he will quiz you on random stuff he said in class. He yaps a lot and goes on pointless tangents. Pay attention in lecture, take notes and you will do fine.

Lectures are interesting and Professor Davis is very knowledgeable about the content he teaches. There are two exams which take up a majority of your grade that are a little tough. Overall great guy that cares about what he teaches.
Great lectures and fun guy to listen to, exams are tough and focus a lot on little things mentioned in class which is annoying.
I liked Professor Davis! He mostly just lectures, but I found them to be engaging especially at 8am. Just make sure to read the textbook to prepare for tests and you will be fine.
Get ready to do nothing but his class, gives a simulation on the first week of class because he is lazy and all his classes are damn near at midnight avoid like the plague

I thought Prof Davis was really cool and a funny guy. For an 8am class I was actually pretty engaged in his class. I thought the material was interesting. If you're interested in learning more about international business I think you would definitely enjoy his class. Exams are decently tough though. There is some extra credit.

Davis is super passionate & knowledgable which makes lectures interesting, I really liked him. Grade relies on 2 exams (LOTS of content to learn), questions are a mix of random examples during lecture & textbook so you have to read.  Extra credit opportunity and weekly engagement assignments to complete.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: Extremely passionate about the topics and uses relatable examples that are interesting. Textbook chapter readings every week. Exams were not too bad if a decent amount of studying is done. Gave extra credit and gave points back on tests.

He's a great professor and his class was really interesting. There is chapter readings, but they weren't that bad. Just use the quizlets and study on your own and the tests will be fine. There was a lot of extra credit and keeping a good grade is pretty reasonable. There is attendance using tophat and he occasionally cold called.
Super duper easy class. Never did the readings. Just find the quizlets and youll do fine on both exams. He is an awful teacher tho.

There was a significant amount of extra credit offered. His lectures were pretty interesting and easy to follow. I thought first exam was harder, but if you pay attention to lectures and attempt the reading you should be fine for the exam. The readings could get annoying but weren't too bad. He's really nice and obviously cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Majority of exam questions are on Quizlet. Extremely exam-based (75% of grade is the two exams), impossible to do well in the class if you don't do well on the exams. Pay attention in class as examples and videos will appear on exams. Reading the textbook is super important for vocab terms and case studies. Use Quizlets to study and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jim's an amazing prof! D272 to Sydney was really fun and structured well. You're introduced to various parts of Australian culture in a fun and engaging way and get to know your classmates well through various group projects. Homework was reasonable. Trip is amazing though - definitely recommend it!

Davis loves to give examples of everything, which is frustrating because the summer D270 course could be condensed down to 1.5 hours without them. Tests consisted of 80% of the final grade. 15 points of extra credit. 20% for assignments. Don't use AI. The tests are online and I would take the course again in the summer just for that reason.
hes a great and knowledgeable teacher and fun but tests are really really hard

the worst professor I've had at IU. He makes the exams so that you have to study literally everything. you have to: write down every word he says in class, read all 200 pages of the book, and watch every video he provides. 99% of the information you absorb won't be on the exam but you'll have to learn it anyways! his lectures are also very boring!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Davis is great and so passionate! I wasn't particularly interested in global business but he made lectures so engaging and fun! Assignments were not too bad, but hated exams because of random specific questions. I will say midterm is way easier than the final. Nevertheless, there are a couple extra credit work to do which help a lot!
out of all the d270 teachers he is by far the better one. definitely take him because he makes the hard class so much easier to understand.

From an A student with a D-, take anyone else
 -spends class yapping about almost anything but the material to prove how smart he is 
 -answers questions by finding a way to prove his intelligence to the class 
 -tests are related to what you study but trick questions, if you're a critical thinker, fear this class
 -goes over class
 -THREE top hats
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Davis is probably the best D270 teacher of all the professors at Kelley. Tests are a combination of the textbook (super long read), slides, and the stuff he says in class. Attendance is TopHat, but you need to be there to hear the stuff he says in class for the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class was pretty chill tbh. Professor Davis did a good job lecturing and preparing us for the exams, which aren't hard at all if you go over the material and pay attention in class. He also gave 10 and 15 extra points on top of the midterm and final. A lot of the videos he showed were also pretty interesting. Don't take Garica take Davis.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It was clear how little he cared about student success. When I sought advice on preparation and improvement, I was met with complete dismissiveness. Student participation was routinely questioned or labeled “wrong,” discouraging engagement. To make matters worse, he spent an entire class advocating for lying on resumes. Avoid at all costs.

Don't take him. He demands participation in class and when you provide an answer that he does not deem 100% correct he will talk down to you.

He does not provide insights into what he wants to see from projects, weekly homework takes 3-4 hours for no reason, and you have to take a final exam.  

Seek other options.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible professor. None of the material that we learned in class was reflective of what was on the midterm and final exams. Also just not a very nice and welcoming person in general.

Honestly, I think this guy is only a professor so he can talk about how much "stuff" he knows. Every time we have class, he talks and talks and talks about himself and all the things he knows and wont let anyone tell him anything because of course, he already knows it. Doesn't give good instructions, then gives poor grades. so unfair and rude.
Hard class, don't slack off. Pay attention to lectures and watch all the videos in the slide shows. Not bad though

D270 in the summer requires 12-15 hours a week of work; While Davis is very nice and affable, his exams are frustrating - testing anything from the videos, to cases in the textbook, and even in-class stories (in addition to the slides), so be prepared to take LOTS of notes. 80% of your marks are from exams (each qn = 1%) but there's 3% extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment:
fabulous professor but stupid class
he uses a lot of examples to illustrate the abstract concept/terminology covered in the text books and I can always gain something interesting(related to the business) from every his class but the course requirements are toooooo demanding

Davis is a boring lecturer, BUT his tests included stuff he mentions only in the lectures and is not in the book. Be prepared to read a lot if you want to succeed. Very test heavy class, each question wrong is 1% off your final grade, so be prepared to study hard and do all the extra credit opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: D270 is a stupid amount of work for a 1.5 credit class. If you want an A in the class, get ready to put in at least 3-4 hours per week into reading the textbook & doing homework. Exams are worth 80% of your grade so every missed question is -1% off your final grade. Overall this class is another useless i-core prereq.

Decent professor. Gives ample EC. His class is pretty interesting but he does occasionally cold call. You may be quizzed on his yapping on the exams. Exams are 80% of your grade and each question is 1% of your total grade. 80% of the test questions can be found online on Quizlet. Memorize that and you'll be fine. Weekly assignments are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's not a boring lecturer, but there was so much information. Don't study the night before an exam give yourself at least like two or three days. There's information from lectures that isn't on the slides and he also puts stuff from the textbook on the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 80% of your grade is the mid term and the final. That said out of all the D-270 teachers Davis is the best and makes class somewhat enoyable. You essentially have to read two sections a week with one homework assignment. For tests utilize online quizlets, read the cases for chapter, and take good class notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice guy--my biggest qualm is the lack of direction for exams regarding content. Lectures teach you so little & you will get no guidance on what will/won't be on the exam. Exams are poorly written & impossible to prepare for-they feel more like a game of Trivia than a fair assessment. Participation sheet is wildly stupid; attendance mandatory.
Try to avoid him in your schedule if you can
go to lecture, pay attention even if it seems like common knowledge. use quizlets for the exams.

Nice guy although he babbles in lecture. Make sure you read the textbook and understand the videos shown in class as those appear on exams. It's only 1.5 credits so it shouldn't do too much on your GPA. Overall class is pretty boring (and useless IMO) which adds to the difficulty.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No matter who you have for D270, your grade is determined by how you do on the midterm and final exams. Review quizlets to prepare for these, but also attend lectures for Davis, as he does include questions on topics he only discusses in class.

Your grade is so heavily dependent on tests and whether you do well. The exams also have many choices per answer so you should know the material by heart. Also, the quizlets are helpful. The downside to this professor is that he feels the need to assert dominance over his students and calls them dumb which did not feel ok

This class felt like memorization of a bunch of material that won't be used later. Also, this Professor makes the class feel boring and doesn't give adequate material to review for tests. I would suggest using the quizlets for this class and hope for the best. Try and take it with another professor if possible

Course grading is heavily test based, causing unnecessary stress. Not only that but tests are impossible making getting a good grade impossible. The professor also is disrespcts students and don't value their time when in class. Don't trust the good reviews or else you will be fooled like me!

Honestly not a good experience. Not only are his tests not related to the content but he often pulls obscure questions that were hardly talked about to test you. He made the class way harder than it should be. AVOID IF YOU CAN
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Course grading was heavily test based adding undue stress. The professor's disrespectful attitude created an unwelcoming atmosphere, hindering learning. A more balanced grading scale and respectful interactions are needed. Just use quizlet for his exams and you'll be fine.

Tests are 80% of your final grade, and it was so difficult to end up with a good grade from his exams. People do well from quizlets online that are exactly like the midterm and final. The class is harder than it needs to be, but the material and the way he teaches makes it worth it. He is such a sweet guy, and I would recommend taking it with him.
This was the second class I had with Prof Davis. Overall he is a solid prof. His tests are not difficult, and the lectures are engaging but there is a fair bit of reading and prep work for class.

the midterm is based on the quizlets, final is based on the slides. go to his lectures and absorb what you can so you don't have to do work outside of class. a LOT of information for a 1.5 credit but Davis does a solid job at keeping you engaged and making sure you come out of the class with some extra knowledge on IB

He manages to make 75 minutes of lecture time more entertaining and quick than any of my other teachers. He is very passionate about what he teaches and provides lots of good examples. If people rated him poorly on here than they skipped as many classes as they could and did not use the resources available for studying. W teacher, would recommend.

Echo what most people said. The tests flat-out have questions which make no sense, which is what happens when you include stuff like in class videos and offhand remarks in them. Lots of questions are about niche, incredibly specific fields. Shouldn't be a hard class, but Kelley insists on making it as annoying as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The final exam is absolutely ridiculous because instead of testing on key concepts and ideas from the course, it asks questions about obscure non-important details that have no significance to the curriculum.The exam needs to be re-written--it is honestly a slap in the face to study for hours for an exam that has all bogus questions.

There are two exams that are each 40% of your final grade. The class is vocab words, textbook case readings, and provided videos. Outside of that, low attendance is correlated to low test exams which he'll mention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Alright listen to this review because it is the only one that matters. All D270 professors are somewhat mid, Davis is BY FAR the best out of all, and students in his class have more fun than others. Don't take this class with another professor unless you have to. James is interesting and there are great study sets for his exams on quizlet.

Davis is the best choice for D270. It is not an easy class, but he's a kind professor who is very accessible to students. Exams are tough, but the concepts aren't necessarily difficult to understand. I do sometimes feel like I'm in kindergarten when he makes us recite how to say "hello" in various languages.

Professor Davis is the best choice for D270. He makes lectures entertaining and provides several real-world examples. If you want further clarification over the material or extra examples, he is more than willing to meet with you during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: D270 is a hard class no matter what professor you take. The tests are meant to challenge you. The D270 assignments are tedious, but that's something you'll have to do regardless of what prof you take. Prof. Davis is probably the sweetest guy you'll meet. He's very passionate about international business and it shows in his lectures.

Tough class, tougher grader. Used substitution words we hadn't been taught on exams to trick students. Lots of reading and vocabulary to learn, don't miss class. TA's aren't helpful, but if you schedule time with him he will sit with you and help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Davis knows a lot about the subject and enjoys teaching it but is strangely strict for a college course. At the beginning of class, he reminds all students that they need to put phones and headphones away, which reminds me of a high school teacher. Midterm and Final are worth 80% of your total grade so if you do bad on one you're screwed.

This class is unnecessarily difficult for what it is teaching. The questions are unnecessarily difficult. Youtube videos are not exam materials. I have graduated high school and, as I am paying for my education, deserve to be beyond teachers/professors trying to trick students into failing.
Professor Davis spends a lot of class time discussing his own opinions on the topics he should be teaching. I learned very little from the class, and would not recommend him.

Prof. Davis is one of the best professors I have had in college. While the class itself is very hard and has a lot of reading, he does the best job at explaining the material and is very accessible and open to answering any questions you as a student have. He really does want to see you do well in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Davis is extremely knowledgeable about business management. He tells really interesting stories to demonstrate important topics which makes class much more worth while. He is also very friendly and willing to help students with things beyond the course content (job search, networking, industry knowledge).

He is flat-out just not a nice guy. He tries to act like it and maybe he is outside of class, but he is the most stuck-up professor I've had in Kelley. He makes his course and assignments as difficult and tedious as possible, almost as if he hopes to annoy you with them. They have no real-world practicality or benefit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof McMullin was good. He really cares about his students and can help when needed. To be honest this class was a joke which is probably why they are changing it. McMullin took feedback well and was always accommodating. I will say though, that final exam was not even close to the practice exam so study much more than that.
Professor Mcmullin is the best professor I have had at IU. Class isn't super hard as long as you pay attention.
great professor, class was somewhat difficult
Enjoyed learning many new concepts. Would highly recommend

I think that Professor McMullin made a very hard class a lot more enjoyable. It is so obvious how much he cares about the students. He knew everyones names from what seems like the beginning, and I felt like he genuinely wanted me to succeed. Very helpful that he makes videos of him going through the review and case problems.

This was my least favorite class I have ever taken. I had never received a B in college until I took this class, and I haven't gotten one since. Professor McMullin read off the slides in class, was terrible at explaining concepts, and made his exams unreasonably hard. Every exam for the semester that I took it was in the 50s or low 60s.

A312 is just a brutal class. Professor McMullin seems like a nice enough person he just does not make this class any easier. One of those classes where there seems to be endless amounts of curveballs that can and will be thrown at you on assignments and tests. Studying felt pointless as I could just rework stuff I already saw. Idk just end me lol

A312 is a super hard class. Professor mcmullin is a great teacher but be prepared to study hard. He is kind and fair and genuinely wants us to succeed. He does a great job explaining difficult concepts. One of the best teachers at Kelley.
I just took his class this spring and found him pretty doable. His exams are tough so make sure to study the materials carefully.
The exams and practice are extremely unnecessarily detailed and pointless.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Mcmullen is a hilarious professor. Although I felt going to his lectures were pointless, I found myself studying the material more from the work problems given to us on Canvas. Only attended lectures to avoid missing on any in-class assignments we had to do. He does make his lectures entertaining though.

A312 is a tough class regardless of who you have. I have always struggled with financial accounting and was really dreading this class. However, Professor McMullin was an amazing professor and made things finally make sense to me. Very tough grader, but its worth it. VERY helpful in preparing for the CPA exam

Hi there- you're probably searching for potential A312 professors. Do yourself a favor and DO NOT take Jeff. Without a doubt the hardest class I've taken at Kelley. Jeff doesn't teach during class, he cracks stupid jokes and literally reads off slides. In the end, students must teach themselves. Only A312 prof. with a CUMULATIVE final (55% average)

Do not take A312 with professor McMullin. Compared to the other professors, he goes into much more details (the stuff that doesn't really matter) and expects you to know every little detail. The exams are nearly impossible, averages between 60%-70%. He does not explain the material hardly at all, but expects you to learn it on your own. Beware.

Professor Miller is amazing! He makes lectures interesting, is very positive, and made this my favorite class. He offers extra credit at the end of the semester and is very transparent about what will be on the two tests of the semester. Could not recommend more!!!
Amazing professor and I recommend you take him. You learn a lot and his class is easy. Very personable and passionate about sociology.
Really nice guy. He's funny and I actually enjoyed attending his lectures. Attendance is mandatory bc he doesn't post his slides.

Favorite professor I've had. His passion for sociology is contagious and I loved having him. He's super interesting, funny, and caring. I can't recommend him enough. He's happy to talk to students after or outside of class, so visit him and say hi!

Literally will be your favorite class you take at IU. Dr. Miller's lectures are super easy to follow. He is a professional in his fiend, and is very passionate about the content to where you will feel just as passionate as him.
Assignments are very easy to grasp & small. The reading weren't longer than 10 pages & only had 2-3 question with 1 attempt.

Jacob Miller is the boy. He's a great professor and I'd highly recommend him. I had him as a sub so it wasn't necessarily the hardest class due to unforeseen circumstances with the previous professor. Great dude and entertaining.

Jacob Miller is a very knowledgable and funny Sociology professor. He cared about student learning, he does not allow electronics which honestly I didn't mind. If you need a credit for a gen ed or a sociology degree I would 100% recommend his class.

One of my favorite classes! He makes class SO EASY and SO INTERESTING! I highly recommend his class, whether you need it for credit or not because I learned so much from him! One note is that he doesn't allow you to use tech for notes, but it's not that big of an issue since he gives you time to write.
Super easy course and although it is lecture Professor Miller keeps them mostly entertaing! does have a no electronics policy but wasn't too bad actually.
Great person, easy class

Awesome guy! He really cares about teaching his students in a very logical and honestly more enjoyable way that is different from the textbook definitions that are difficult and useless to remember. Not test heavy (only 2) and if it was up to him, he wouldn't make you take exams so  they're not hard or graded harshly. I def recommend him for S100!

I've had Jacob for Intro. to Sociology, but he ended up taking over my Healthcare Sociology class due to an emergency. I cannot say enough good things. He explains things in a way that makes such complete sense, and is so relatable. Doesn't act like he knows everything and students know nothing. So down to earth and FUN

One of those dudes who couldn't care less about all of the unnecessary logistical and repetitive stuff that's so commonly seen in classroom settings. Only cares that he is teaching his students the most practical material he can at the highest quality possible. Awesome dude who genuinely believes his teaching is making a difference.

Professor Miller was amazing! He was so funny, easy going, and kind. You could tell that he really just wanted us to learn. He covered a broad range of interesting and important topics. I'd highly recommend a class with Prof Miller!

Dr. Miller is absolutely incredible. The material in the readings and lectures is easily digestible. He's really focused on making sure you learn. Plus, he is a hilarious person who very clearly is passionate both about the course and his students.

Professor Miller is incredible. He cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. His weekly quizzes were very easy and straightforward. There are only 2 exams but as long as you take notes on the review day(s) and pay attention, you'll do good. His lectures were interesting and he was an all around great guy. I 100% recommend this class.

Mr. Miller is an amazing ,kind, and respectable professor. He has very involved and intriguing lectures that make coming to class fun and worth your time. His TA's are also very helpful and there when you need anything. You can tell he really enjoys what he does, which makes it so much better compared to other professors.

Professor Miller doesn't allow laptops or phones in his class, but it makes no difference because his lectures are really interesting. To get a good grade, all you need to do is show up to the lectures and take notes. Professor Miller knows what he's talking about and enjoys teaching this class, and you can tell. Fantastic gen ed and professor.
Miller was an amazing professor he adds comedy to his lectures and he is very enthusiastic about the course, very easy to learn

Prof Miller is a good professor. He does his best to make sure the topics don't lean a certain way politically but they do sometimes. You can have 5 abstinences until you get deducted and there are only 2 exams. His other assignments are very easy. Go to class, take notes, and study for the exams, you will get an A. Just go to class bruh.

The course was set up very functionally with entertaining readings Dr. Miller wrote as lectures. You can tell he's a great guy who's done lots of research on the topics taught. He's also quite the amusing writer. The assignments don't take long and are straight to the main points. I truly learned so much from his class!

BEST! His lectures are very interesting and engaging, weekly readings are easy and he has a lot of easy assignments with a lot of points to balance out the midterm and final. Advice, take notes on the examples he talks about because studying with definitions and examples is the best way to succeed. (I got a 91 on midterm and 100 on final).

Professor Miller is very active in his lectures making them fun and interesting, this class is great if you're looking for easy credits. Not a lot of homework or hours spent on this class, although it was probably one of my favorites.

Work was extremely minimal and didn't take more than 10 minutes per week. He is a super nice guy and very passionate about his work. Lectures can drag on and be boring, but it was generally interesting stuff. Super great to take for a gen-ed! Only two tests, which are not hard if you pay attention in class.

SUCH an amazing professor! Makes lecture fun & interesting, even incorporating some of his own stories to make the material come to life. Cares about his students and MAKES HIS GUIDELINES CLEAR. Goes over every test before you take it, which was extremely helpful. Laid-back with attendance, allowing you to drop some missed days. Take his class!!!

This class was so fun to take. For being a lecture class I was always paying attention, and never got bored. He relates things to your life today that helps you understand the topics he is talking about. As well as setting you up to succeed, he will answer any questions you have, while also learning and having a good time in class.

Jacob Miller is an amazing professor who is extremely passionate about his work. He loves to tell stories while connecting them to sociology. Not only that but, honestly what he teaches is pretty interesting. When it comes to the class it is all paper and pencil but honestly if you can look past that I would 1000% recommend him to anyone.

This class was extremely easy and Dr. Miller offers fun and engaging lectures to help you learn. There are few assignments and they're all incredibly easy. The two exams aren't difficult either, but make sure you study the notes or else it will actually be hard. I highly recommend him if you're taking this class.

Professor Miller was definitely one of the best professors I have had at IU. His lectures were funny, entertaining, and connected to real-world examples. As long as you take notes and come to lecture, you can ace the exams. He even went out of his way to email me to congratulate me on getting a perfect score on the midterm.

Dr. Miller was amazing! Lectures were hilarious and that made everything way more entertaining than a typical lecture would be. Mans got jokes. He also genuinely cares about his students. Quizzes/exams were easy, everything comes from the lecture. Take notes, do your work timely, and you'll have an easy A.

Best teacher I've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students and his profession. He manages to make an hour-long lecture interesting the entire time. He often had our entire class laughing out loud mid-lecture. Go to class, take notes, and you will get an A.
Lecture as alright, 65 percent of your grade is made up of exams so studying before those can be helpful but everything that will be on the exams he goes over in class.

Dr. Miller is one of the most amazing professors I have ever had. He is hilarious and really makes you care about sociology. Lectures were always entertaining and he's a very easy grader. However, tests are majority of the points in the class.
Miller's class wasn't all that difficult, but I found the content to be boring, and the lectures to drag on and on. Also, he does not allow any electronics, so no computers or iPads to take notes.

Very enthusiastic and cares about teaching. Attendance is mandatory with a few allowed absences but the class isn't difficult by any means. Also pretty interesting and there's not much reading at all.

Jacob Miller is a very passionate guy and his lectures are SO WELL PLANNED he really makes difficult to understand material extremely easy by relating them to memes and other stories. I never wanted to skip class because it is so refreshing to see a prof care so much for his students! Super manageable and takes less then a hour outside of class.

Dr. Miller is amazing! While some of the topics in sociology can be a little abstract, he does a great job of explaining them in terms students can understand, and with a large dose of humor. Attendance is taken every class with a sign-in sheet. Homework is just short readings and a weekly reflection - very manageable.
Dr. Miller is one of the best sociology professors at IU, super funny guy, but don't miss lecture or you'll get behind.

Professor Miller is the way to go! His lectures are super fun and I feel like I comprehended the material so much more just by the way he incorporates memes and breaks down topics. Hopefully you guys get a rate my pet brain break every class like we did!

Dr. Miller is the best, he makes class fun and interesting as it's an hour long. He doesn't post powerpoints online so you have to go to class to get the notes and to write your name for attendance. There is only one HW assignment each week and they are easy readings that aren't tested on the midterm or final. Great class, great teacher!

One of the best professors I have ever had. Such an easy and interesting class. Highly recommend this class and this professor. He is super nice and will help you if you have any difficulties. Only spent about two hours on the material throughout the week. Easy to navigate canvas and get everything complete.

Professor Miller has by far been my favorite professor at IU. He's an extremely nice person, but also makes his lectures really engaging with his humor and enthusiasm. You can tell he really cares about his students succeeding in his course, and the material itself. Attendance is taken, but he makes class exciting to where you actually want to go.
I want other students to know that a professor like this is hard to come by. He is energetic in his teachings and truly cares about his work. 10/10 recommend

Dr. Miller is extremely nice, funny, and very clearly passionate about sociology. He always tries to keep things lighthearted and barely gives out homework (which are basically free points because he'll always give you 100). The only thing I disliked was that there were no other tests besides the midterm/final which may hurt your grade.

Professor Miller is by far the most caring professor I've ever had. Readings aren't hard, only homework is a weekly mental check in, exams are straightforward and you'll do well on them as long as you go to class.
Great professor. Has interesting takes on his subject. Cares about Sociology a lot and wants to make it interesting for all. The class has one major paper, and two tests. Its fairly simple.

Jacob is an amazing professor, you can tell he is passionate about everything he teaches. He makes lectures interesting and he is the funniest professor I know. The class itself is generally easy as long as you pay attention and take notes (you take notes by hand because it helps you memorize the course material better)!
Dr. Miller is the BEST! Take him for any class you can. His lectures are VERY entertaining and fun to be in (even at 9:30am). The midterm and final are very very easy.
Jacob is great! You can tell he really loves Sociology and he makes his classes interesting with stories and real life examples. His lectures were entertaining and the tests were fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy class with entertaining lectures. Since it's an intro level course it's mostly memorizing vocab. Readings at most once a week, usually fairly short (less than 4-5 pages).
Jacob is awesome, super funny and an easy A

Jacob (prefers his first name) is awesome! He is super funny and makes lectures interesting. However, he does get off topic easily, so just make sure you are writing down what is actually on the powerpoint rather than what he says.  No book, but gives articles to read with weekly quizzes. Easy tests. Take him for any Soc class you can!

Jacob is such an amazing professor and person, I really would recommend anyone to take his class. He knows how to make his lectures fun and he is a very interesting person. He is also very passionate about his job and his research and it is clearly seen in his teaching. 10/10.

Jacob is a great professor and is enthusiastic about sociology, however lectures are unorganized at times. Also, he does not allow laptops, but expects you to handwrite extremely long definitions and take notes on topics that he goes through rather quickly.

Jacob is an awesome professor! He is really funny and enthusiastic which makes his lectures a lot of fun. His attendance policy was extremely lenient, but it is mandatory because he doesn't put his notes online. He only gives two exams (the midterm and the final), and neither are difficult if you just go to class and take good notes.

Jacob was a great professor- he really peaked my interest in sociology. He had interesting lectures and had interesting topics for the class to discuss and participate in. Jacob loves to engage the class. He also spelled out clearly what he expected on his couple papers and midtermfinal. 1010 would recommend.

He is so awesome!! You need to go to class, as there are quizzes every week on the assigned reading, but the quizzes aren't hard if you read. The lectures are sometimes boring but he usually gets off topic and just talks, and he is pretty cool and funny. I recommend this class with him!

Jacob is very enthusiastic about sociology and the topics he teaches in class. . Overall his S101 class was fairly easy; there were weekly readings but most were interesting and the quizzes weren't worth very many points. If you need an A&H credit and are looking for an interesting class that won't wreck your GPA, I'd recommend taking one of his.

I took his class over the summer, and he made it quite painless. He is genuinely interested in everyone's opinion and in seeing the students succeed. He doesn't post his lecture notes but he does a darn good job during reviews. His tests are straight forward, and he doesn't try to pull any tricks.
He is an awesome professor! So helpful and relatable!

Definitely take this class with Jacob! He is so enthusiastic about the subject and makes it really interesting. Tests are not difficult as long as you attend the review session beforehand. Textbook is easy to understand and there is little writing in this class. He was a great teacher and I would definitely recommend him for this class.

He's a great professor with a positive outlook for every subject. Very open to new ideas and makes sure you feel like your ideas are important as well. He keeps the class interesting. Take notes and make sure you write them word for word, they won't be found on oncourse. Overall the class is fairly easy but in a way that keeps you interested.

Jacob is a really nice guy. He really knows what he's talking about and is a really good sociologist. His lectures were a little too disorganized for my liking but I still thought he was a good professor. He was excited to be in class everyday and the class was pretty easy. Just study the notes and write the papers. He's a great, smart professor.
Mr. MIller was an awesome professor. He was excited to be in class and a great sociologist! You're in for a great class if you ever have him.

Jacob is an all-around awesome professor. He is very enthusiastic and loves teaching. If you have questions, he MAKES SURE that you understand it. He makes the class revolve around discussion so it feels as though you are teaching the course which adds a cool element to it and makes you actually learn the topics.
Jacob is always super excited about sociology and loves teaching it. he really wants his students to succeed. if you're going to take a sociology intro class, take his!

Super friendly and approachable professor, very helpful and understanding. Class is mostly discussion based with notes. He wants everyone to do well! Definitely not too hard to get an A if you attend class.

He had a great personality and you can really tell he loves what he teaches. He's a funny guy which makes the class so much more interesting. The material he teaches is interesting for the most part. You won't regret taking his class!

Jacob is a very interesting guy with an amazing personality. He keeps his classes entertaining, and we often had big class discussions about fun topics. He never had us do any pointless assignments and kept his class in the right direction throughout the semester.

Jacob is very enthusiastic about Sociology. The course itself was not difficult, but many of the classes seemed to go in circles; they were quite boring at times. Jacob was nice and graded fairly, but he was clearly biased about certain beliefs and, in an attempt to relate to students, made jokes that I sometimes found inconsiderate.
great teacher, fun class, not much else to say tbh

Exceptional professor who brings an incredible level of passion and energy to every single class. Their ability to break down complex concepts and make them digestible makes the course material both accessible and genuinely engaging.

Joyce cares a lot about all her students and really wants everyone to succeed. K201 is a class that requires a lot of work outside of class, but Joyce does everything she can to prepare you for the challenging exams. She is always willing to help you, all you have to do is message her on teams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She spends 90% of class talking about long winded anecdotes that don't quite pertain to the topic. She keeps every class over, while I believe she has great intentions, she ends up spending so much time ‘caring' she doesn't actually teach. I would learn everything myself before she even finished talking.

She's goated, just make sure to READ for the first exam (question on the first exam is literally word for word from the textbook so if you can memorize all the chapter information for the first exam then you're good) and REALLY study for exam 2, 3, and 4.
I really enjoyed her class and thought she made the lecture go by fast which is always ideal. I also felt like she cared about students and wanted people to do well.

Dr. Jewell is really caring & understanding. I love her as a person, but her teaching style isn't my favorite. She speeds through her lectures and a lot of work I did was outside of this class, so be prepared to self study if you have her. K201 is really easy though, so don't worry too much about the class itself.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Yes, Joyce may go off topic sometimes. However, Joyce was very nice and good at explaining things. She would also have attendance checks, which is an easy 5/5, something that other professors usually don't have. Also, what you do in class and on the test are similar.
Really good at explaining the K201 concepts

Will randomly jump back several steps and then back forward in the files. Hard to figure out what step she is on at any point. Ended up following the textbook on my own time and showing up for attendance, but she is very sweet.

Easiest class you will ever take, Jewell explains everything very simply. The only thing that can mess up your grade is the group project. Just do the discoveries and gps every week early and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Jewell is extremely caring and passionate about this class, which makes it much easier to pay attention in class. She is very accessible outside of class and will do anything to help improve grades and confidence. Highly recommend!

Honestly, Professor Jewell was fine at teaching K201, but I never struggled with the content so after learning it I can't really say anything about her teaching. However, I did not vibe with her teaching style. She wasted class time giving metaphors from her own hobbies, when we could be practicing more examples or review.

Professor Jewell is a great professor in a class that is honestly not difficult. Idk why people find such a hard time in K201, the exams are directly the same as class work and projects. I got an A+ without putting in any effort. Just make sure you go to class, the prof will help with easy shortcuts.
She has a very unique teaching style but it is very effective and it's obvious she's passionate about what she teaches and wants students to succeed in her class. Would highly recommend.

Honestly I took this class a second time because the first time sucked and I didn't get it.  That professor was awful.  I loved Professor Jewell.  She talked with me outside class and when I said I was worried about how I would do at the beginning she set up a teams chat with me to get in contact whenever I needed.

Professor Jewell was great for K201 and had many helpful tips to succeed. She knows how to approach students and help them succeed. She is always available for questions and will even stay after class to help. She made the class enjoyable and I did better then expected! If it weren't for her, I would not have passed K201.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Jewell gave a variety of tips and tricks for students to succeed in K201 that weren't mentioned in the book. She does sometimes ramble about neurodivergence, but it doesn't alter her ability to finish her tasks. Take her advice and practice all practice exams and chapters before exams!! If you go strictly by the book, you can still pass!
Very good about allowing high ability students to learn simple concepts on their own while still providing effective feedback on graded projects and group assignments.

Joyce Jewell rambles for the entire lecture about things that don't pertain to her class and just wastes your time until she realizes she has 10 minutes left in class. She then rushes thru the actual content and holds you late.  You have to rely on yourself if you take this class with her. She spent entire lectures rambling about irrelevant things.

Joyce is a very caring and optimistic professor, however she gets very distracted during lectures and tends to talk about things that do not relate to the course. She does not like to go by the book and makes her data and problems up instead. She is hard to reach outside of class, but she is always willing to help her students out with any issues.

Joyce often has higher than average grade distributions, but her classes can be unbearable at times. She often begins class with long-winded lectures about anxiety strategies, neuro divergence, etc. While she explains everything very thoroughly, she often repeats explanations 3-4 times, which can be mind-numbing and puts the class behind schedule.
Joyce is very good at what she does. She prepared me very well for the exams and if my attendance hadn't slipped in the end I am convinced I would have gotten an A.

Professor Joyce's lectures have been enormously helpful. She explains each operation's rationale, emphasizing common errors and confusion. Her vivid analogies make complex concepts more relatable, enhancing my understanding and aiding in exams. Her review sessions are well-planned and crucial for mid-term and final exams.

Professor Joyce's lectures have been enormously helpful. She explains each operation's rationale, emphasizing common errors and confusions. Her vivid analogies make complex concepts more relatable, enhancing my understanding Her review sessions are well-planned, crucial for mid-term and final exams.

Jewell's was one of the best K201 lab instructors. She made it very clear of what you need in order to get an A. Do all the discoveries, case studies (in class), and the reviews. When the practice exam material come out, study it REPEATEDLY. The practice exams are super similar to the actual exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had professor Jewell last year and I miss her class she made lectures fly by and although she was a little bit "crazy" about ironmans she cares about her students too. She made an effort to let all her students know she cared about this course and the mental health of her students. Do not be scared to take her class she is kind human.

She has been one of my favorite professors. She was always there to support and give students the resources they need to succeed in this class. It is a challenging class but she made it worth it. I did awful on the first exam and she gave me the confidence to stay in the class and would stay after class to answer questions. Truly a 10/10

After my time at Kelley, Professor Jewell is the one that sticks out to me as one of the best. Out of all the K201 professors, she is your best bet. She helps students learn and make class interactive. Definitely take it with her.

Joyce Jewell is an absolute gem of a professor. She is the first professor I have had in college that truly cares about her students and will move mountains to make sure they do their best. Everything she does comes from a pace of care for her students. If you have the option to take K201 with her, you are in for a great semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She fits none of those tags but I thought she was pretty good. K201 is a difficult class regardless but she gave lab checks that could only help your grade, unlike some other professors. She really depended on her TA Zach because of her concussion and whatnot but I think she still explained the material in a graspable way herself
The course itself is difficult, but I like the professor

Herself as a teacher was amazing. The material that is being covered is very challenging and she does her best to accommodate to students but the tests are soley through kelley not her therefore she has no control over assignments, but will do everything to see her students succeed and pass. She understands the struggles and is proud of us

Professor Jewell was an okay teacher, I wish she gave us enough time to write down notes in class though. She blamed everything on her "concussion brain" and it was kind of annoying, like you've said it 5 times, we get it. She kind of talked down on us and made us feel like preschoolers. She was meh, but not terrible.

I had heard before having her she was a harder k201 teacher. However I found her class always to go by very fast because she was funny and made the material interesting. I know you can not pick your k201 teacher but do not worry if you get  her. If you run iron mans you will connect with her. Overall I liked k201 and she was a big part of it.

Professor Jewell is fantastic at teaching K201. She knows the material thoroughly and is great at breaking down topics so that you not only understand how to do them, but also their conceptual framework. I feel like many of the negative reviews are just a product how difficult K201 is, but if you're willing to put in the work, she'll be great.

oh my god she sucks at teaching all she talks about is her concussion and blame everything on it IT HAPPENED A YEAR AGO JESUS doesn't teach correctly had to learn from a peer taught myself more than she taught me

Professor Jewell was amazing. It's K201 so it is definitely a tough class but Professor Jewell's way of teaching made the material so much easier and her classes were extremely engaging. She is one of the nicest and most caring professors I have ever had. Highly recommend taking K201 with her.

I loved professor Jewell!! She was super thorough with her lab discussions and made sure students really understood what to do. Although a lot of students struggle with this class, I personally found it super fun and if you go to class it's not too difficult.

LOVED HER! She is definitely one of the best K201 teachers at IU. She goes at a good pace during the class, and the class is hard so it helps a lot. Listen to her tips and make sure you go to class because your grade will show the effort that you put into it
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: i have joyce for the lab portion of this class. she gets off topic way too much throughout class and talks about her personal life very often. in addition to that she basically says every class that if youre not dedicating hours and hours to this course than you wont be successful. i wouldnt take it again
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really can't imagine a professor who explains the information better for K201. The class is difficult and you have to put in the extra work for a good grade but she does a good job at making it interesting. Also responsive with emails and any questions.

I had Joyce for K201 lab and didn't love her class structure. Everything seemed very rushed and never learned anything in class. Her outside of class lectures were the only things I seemed to learn from. They were very lengthy too. She is for sure passionate about her class, however it is very hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I only had her for the lab portion and she was fine. Her lectures are pretty long but she explains everything really well and gives you some helpful exam tips. She wasnt the most amazing professor ever but she wasnt bad either. Id take her again

K201 is a tough course, no matter who you take. She was fine in terms of a lecturer, but she would often get off track. In class if you were having an issue, she didn't address it and would send one of the TAs over, which that's fine but sometimes you just want the professor's input.

Makes this class so fun! She clearly is enthusiastic about what she teaches and that makes you want to learn it so much more. She does such a great job explaining everything so you definitely won't want to miss class.

Professor Jewell is a great professor because she explains her techniques for Access and Excel very well. She gives helpful tips as well as cares about the student as a whole. I learned more from her than I did from any other professor so far at IU. K201 is already a difficult weed-out class, Jewell was able to bring the stress level down.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I enjoyed having Joyce has a lecturer for K201. Her lectures were really easy to listen and covered the material needed to do well on the lecture exams. I received 100% on both tests. Make sure you tune in to lectures in order to receive all the extra credit points available for the course.

I only had Joyce for the lecture session which is good because one can only take so much Joyce at a time. Her lectures were awful. Instead of making sure to cover the material that would be on the test, she spent most of her time making jokes and going off on tangents. The lecture component of the course is useless and everyone agrees with this.

I enjoyed having Joyce's class. K201 is a hard course, but Joyce explained everything well. She was super personable and I felt comfortable asking questions in class. She cares about students, and she would use extra time to review material and give advice for the upcoming exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: What can you say? TERRIBLE! Feminazi! Outwardly display hostility to "A" men. By that I mean Men who know who and what they are and are good at things. Her victim status is apparent. I could never guess why but I am sure she was put in her place a few times with logic and reason. Anyway. Avoid her at all costs. Absolutely terrible. I passed.
I had Joyce as my K201 lab instructor and she was a good teacher. She explained everything fairly well and emphasized that we had to put in work on our own to do well in the class.
She got off topic a lot, bragged about her personal life, and was rude to the AI. Having her class is not the end of the world, but take another lab or lecture if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Joyce spends more time off topic than she does actually explaining the lecture material. I bombed the access lecture exam because there were slides we never covered in class, and then I didn't study them afterwards.
