She is nice, but she needs to realize that people watching just want to hear the lecture, not a bunch of off topic stuff from the chat

The only way to be successful in K201 lecture with Joyce is to do all of the readings before class. Although she gives you answers to the poll questions to earn koins, the lecture exams are on content you have to learn on your own from the book. Oh and also... "Brace yourselves, the 4 week ALDI case competition with 6+ random students is coming".
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The lectures were not that great. She went off topic a lot of the time, talking about herself spending too much time interacting, "joking",  with people in the comments.  Her saving grace is that she tried to explain the main concepts thoroughly, but reading the book is the only reliable way to get all the info and key terms. In conclusion, just no

She's so bad. She is just a rude person. Likes to put people down and only is in favor of students who do nothing but study all day. Wont be the best professor for getting a good grade. her LAB checks are awful they are timed and even if you know things and you show up to class, if you cant finish that section in her time limit she wont give grades

I absolutely loved her! She is easy to understand and very knowledgeable about the subject.  She also cares deeply about her students' wellbeing.  If you go to her after class she will even help you draw up a study plan and she gives very good advice.  After every K201 lab class I felt inspired to study and do my best.

I had Joyce for both K201 Lab and Lecture. She was funny and kept the class entertaining. K201 is known as one of the hardest Kelley classes you'll have to take, regardless of your professor. Joyce was approachable and always stayed after Lab to answer questions.

K201 lecture is not very easy. She gets off from lecture topics very often. 80% of her lectures' contents are jokes. So, do yourself a favor, choose other professors if you can. I learned most of knowledges from the book, not from her.

Ok... here's the deal. She panders.  She gets off topic and stays off topic. She has interrupted her own lecture to sing Happy Birthday to people she cannot see online.  She seems nice, but I have seen her be very mean when people ask reasonable questions. Overall this was easy. I listened to music the entire time and did the polls and got credit.
I loved listening to her because she was hilarious! She made things interesting, and I enjoyed the way she explained things.

The class material is really boring but she does her best to make it interesting. It's an online lecture so it's even harder to pay attention because all you have to do for attendance is answer poll questions.
Professor Jewell is almost like a high school teacher and spends a lot of time lecturing students on things outside her subject. She teaches reasonably well but is sometimes too fast to keep up with.

She knows what she's talking about but I didn't really enjoy her as a professor. I didn't dislike her, but I didn't like her either. Don't get behind or you'll be screwed, and stock up on koins (can be exchanged for extra credit) because you'll need all the koins you can get.

It's not really Joyce's fault that the material she's being forced to teach is so irrelevant, however, she definitely didn't make it any better. Every week I was forced to sit on my laptop and watch a glitchy live feed of Joyce in a room attempt to teach us. She get's off topic very easily, wastes time, and has lots of technical difficulties.
She was a very mediocre teacher who though she was great. If you pay close attention and do all of the work you should be fine, but not directly related to Jewell's teaching style

The K201 lecture sections are kind of pointless. The live lectures are mostly online and Joyce is an overall good professor.  She tends to go on tangents occasionally which can be annoying. She cares about her students and is helpful with questions.  Overall a good professor for a pointless class.
Joyce is a great teacher! She really cares about her students and give great K201 advice and life advice in general. Highly recommended!

The lecture portion of k201 is pretty worthless, the only reason to attend the lectures is for credit. Along those lines Joyce is not that bad, she lectures very casually, and considering its half online, its very easy as well.
THE WORST INSTRUCTOR I EVER MET!!!! Never stop talking her personal life, and spoke fast when she finally begin to say something useful...Just awful, try to avoid her!!!

I really wouldn't say the material she teachers is hard, and she is good at teaching. But it is true, it doesn't matter what happens, I was in the hospital for several days and she did NOT care. You get three no questions asked absences, but it still seems a bit harsh. She was also randomly hard to reach via emails come finals week.
Can not make up quizzes you could literally get hit by a car but still wouldn't allow you to make up a quiz and grades harshly. No technology in the classroom as well...
Do not take this class. She has no heart.

I absolutely loved her and found the class material so interesting. I enjoyed discussing topics with the class. Lots of 'pop quizzes', but she usually tells you about them before class. I think she's really funny and interesting to talk to. Lots of reading, but I found all of it interesting, and also a group presentation that was not too difficult.

I liked her for most of the semester, but sometimes she said things that were out of touch, especially considering her field of work (f slur and d slur). Her lectures were engaging, even though some of the readings were unnecessarily long, but you definitely need to read them anyways because of the pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She was rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof. Maher is an exceedingly cold person who shouldn't teach. The 3rd week of freshman year, my college-aged sister was tragically killed in a skiing accident. During my two weeks at home for the funeral and wake, I missed all IU classes and pop quizzes in her class. Every other IU prof was great. She gave me 0 for every class/quiz. Run from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Very opinionated would judge me and is quite actually an awful teacher.

My 2nd class with Jen and I loved it! She's very funny, engaging, and knowledgable about course topics. Attendance and doing the readings are crucial--quizzes and exams are a breeze if you do the reading. If you're really interested in gender studies and not just taking the class for a gen ed, take a class with Jen.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Maher's G225 class is engaging and rewarding if you put in the work. Attendance is a must, but the lectures are fun and insightful. Paired with the textbook, Unstuck ai proved helpful for exam prep. Overall, an enjoyable and challenging course.
She's the worst
no thank you   never again   she is not for me

Professor is legit so funny. The readings are long and you have around two to do every class period. There are "pop" quizzes given, but are easy if you read. You really have to pay attention in this class. DO THE READINGS or read a summary at least. Absolutely no electronics allowed. Very interesting info every class period, I liked the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I overall really liked Professor Maher. The class was mostly lecturing, but I also thought it was interesting and captivating. There are pop quizzes, but they are open internet so do with that what you will. The midterm and final are open note so neither are too bad. The one bad thing is attendance is required so make sure to be there.

She is the worst professor I have had. Very strict attendance policy. I asked her ahead of time if I could make up a pop quiz if we have one when my GRANDMA DIED so I could go to her funeral and she said "No. That's life, you'll figure it out." So insensitive and rude, don't take this class ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at IU. She is ridiculously funny. Readings can be dense, but she explains them well in class. You cannot really miss class; there are 10 pop reading quizzes, she drops 2 but it will be covered on the exams. This class will make you think. I'm not a gender studies major, but I will take another class with her.

I had a great experience with Jen! As long as you do the reading and come to class, you'll do well. There are pop quizzes, but they are open note/book as well as the exams. She is not very tech savvy, she's a little scatterbrained, and her humor may not be for everyone, but she is an absolute expert in gender studies and I loved her course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I took an IFS class with her and she was great. Definitely passionate about the subject and serious about the classwork, but a chill & laid back professor overall. Really cares about her students. She is strict about the no-electronics policy.

she is very strict about attendance and phone policy. you cannot look at your phone or else she will count you absent without saying anything. she can be funny and the lectures can be interesting from time to time but in general this class is very focused on difficult readings and pop quizzes. your grade is strictly dependent on your test grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easily the least understanding professor I have had at IU. Her lectures are pointless. She calls people out in the lecture and singles students out. She is easily the worst professor I have ever had. Not only is she a terrible teacher, but a bad person in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took IFS with Maher and she was amazing. Lectures were interesting, assignments were fun despite having so many of them. If you're thinking about this class, know you will be working all day every day on it. I still think Maher makes it worth it.

Her attendance policy is absurd. First, she does not believe in excused absences, so I guess don't get sick? If you get 3 absences in the class your grade gets dropped an entire letter grade. Not only that, but she will mark you absent if you even look at your phone for a second. Worst professor I have genuinely ever had.

She is very passionate and knowledgeable about this subject. You must read the book and outside readings as well as come to class to pass. The information is so interesting and requires you to think critically. The exams and quizzes are open book and note, but the questions' answers are not directly stated in the book.
Love Her! Really cares and made my first class at IU such an amazing experience! Would recommend!

Jen is super funny. She is a very harsh grader, but don't let the first bad grade intimidate you, you will improve your writing skills if you take her class. The readings she provides are lengthy but interesting. I enjoyed this class even though it really stressed me out for the first half of the semester
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic and hilarious. Attendance is mandatory (and there are random pop quizzes), but I never had a reason to miss anyways because the course is very interesting. She doesn't cut anybody slack, but she knows what she's talking about and is a great person.

I loved Professor Maher so much!  I took her IFS class Blood, Babies, and Chainsaws, and it was the best introduction to college I could possibly have asked for.  She is an excellent lecturer, an expert writer and critic, and a very kind and caring person.  She introduced gender theory and taught me proper academic writing. Best professor at IU!!

Attendance is absolutely mandatory but worth it because she doesn't post lectures, so if you miss a class, you need to ask a classmate or look at the syllabus and after you miss 3 classes, your grade gets knocked down by a letter grade. But overall if you attend class and read the required readings it's a really easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved prof. Maher. She is hilarious and I always looked forward to coming to class. She was also really great a explaining things and was also eager to answer questions. I learned a lot and if you do the readings and show up to class getting an A is very doable.

In her regular section of 225 she is a great professor. She doesn't share lecture slides and has random pop quizzes, if you aren't in class you get a zero on it. She doesn't believe in excused absences so don't get sick. If you are taking her honors section DO NOT! Her grading is ridiculous, changes requirements of assignments after the due date.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class was extremely engaging. I learned so much! Maher is hilarious and keeps class entertaining with her witty sarcasm. At times, this professor can be unprepared and make students feel belittled. ATTENDANCE IS MANDATORY, so be ready, and be on time. Understanding the readings will carve the path to an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Prof Maher is an excellent teacher and so funny, I really enjoyed her class and I hope to take another !

TAKE THIS CLASS. She is actually the funniest and most engaging professor I've ever had and she actually made me want to go to class. If you do the readings and attend every class then you will get an A. Final and midterm are both open note and only 25 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I LOVE Maher. Her lectures were engaging and fun. She had easy reading pop quizzes that were open note, and she was always available for questions. She can be challenging but will make you a better student. She can get off-topic in lectures. She is not super tech savvy, but it will not negatively effect your grade, and is understanding,

Professor Maher is by far my most engaging professor. Her lectures are always funny and interesting, and lots of people participate. There is a lot of reading, and if you take the honors section, she can be tough on grading writing, but if the subject is actually interesting to you, the reading isn't bad. I always look forward to this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS. She is so so so funny and entertaining which makes class easier to attend. She only allows 2 absences which kind of sucks but I don't want to skip anyway. The only grades are 5 point pop quizzes, novel questions, and the midterm/final which are both open note and only 25 points each. If you do the readings you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Jen was the instructor of my IFS class, and I have to say that I would take this class again! She can be a bit unpredictable, but she is also approachable, fair, and very funny! There was quite a bit of reading and a few group projects as well, but the workload wasn't as heavy as other IFS classes. I recommend Professor Jen!
A very interesting course but there are very few grades. Essays are graded harshly and attendance is very strict.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I felt it was a decent class. Jennifer was funny and cared about her material, but the grading felt way too harsh on papers and the tests were kind of confusing.

This teacher is genuinely awful. She imprints her liberal feminist views on every student. Her attendance policy is crazy and if you miss more than 2 classes she bumps your grade down a whole letter. There are 100 points in the whole class which is extremely unfair considering she grades obnoxiously hard.  DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.
Great teacher, but assigns too much reading for a class thats only 120 points
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I love Jenn. G225 is an interesting class, but does require quite a bit of reading, majority of them are pretty easy reads. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: often judged students and would make people feel uncomfortable.

I really enjoyed taking this class. Professor Maher is hilarious and she provides all of the readings required for her class so no textbook is required. That being said prepare to read 20+ pages every (or almost every) night. She gives random pop quizzes over the readings too so make sure you stay caught up. I highly recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Attendance policy was pretty strict with only two absences even in the middle of a pandemic. LOTS of dense reading. The material was interesting, especially documentaries we watched. She can be very fun but be prepared for work and strict grading on writing!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Maher is the toughest teacher I have ever had. Her attendance policy is absurd. There's more but I ran out of characters. DON'T TAKE HER CLASSES!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: An amazing and kind professor. She is intense but kind, funny, and approachable. She will explain why you lost points and provide ways to gain them back. She is respectful of her student's identity, health, and time. She admits her faults and works on them. I would take her classes time and time again.
Interesting, but not very easy to read.

reviews.comment: The class was interesting, but it wasn't an easy class to be in and the instructor was very nitpicky on my papers and rhetorical analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: well, her class was fun, the Rhetorical Analysis just confusing, and the way they rate your essay just way harder than the English you were expecting, I got an A in my W131 but my essay here was 14/20, don't choose this class, there was much more class easier and much more interesting.

I took this class because of Covid and overall it wasnt bad. Weekly reading responses that you have to mess up badly to not get full credit. There are 2 papers which are graded tough but thats fine. My main issue lies in her taking points of for small mistakes. If you submit assignment in the wrong place 50% off which is a lot for her grade scale

You only have a few big grades. I am a good writer, got an A+ in W131. She gave me C- on papers. She is a hard grader and will refuse to give you an A on the papers. Would not recommend this course for an easy A. Annoyingggg

This professor was very open, educated, and kind! She made her lectures interesting and the weekly assignments fairly easy. The two papers for the course are a little hard to get an A on, but overall she is funny and a great choice for a gender studies class. 8/10

jens lectures are funny but this class requires A TON of reading. shes SO anal about how she wants her papers and theres few grades in the class so its almost impossible to make up points. you definitely have to work for your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Jen is a super funny and chill professor. The class has a lot of hard readings, but Jen will explain them well. There are random quizzes over the readings, but they are short answer and open book; they aren't graded but she reads them all at the end to see if she should bump your grade up or not. Only 2 essays and they are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dont take this class if you arent proficient in writing and English. She literally has been grading our responses based on our writing skills, not on if we learned the gender ideas. She gives interesting lectures but grades all her writing more about how you wrote it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I love her!! She is hilarious and super fun which makes the lectures not boring at all. She is kinda strict on her grading but if you follow directions you'll be fine. Do not take this class if you're super Christian. You will see p*nises in class and it will be awesome.

MAKE SURE TO COME TO CLASS!! Professor Maher is awesome and hilarious. I highly recommend taking Professor Maher. Make sure you have experience in writing and do not mind reading a lot. The class is graded on two essays, a midterm, and a final, so be prepared for everything. Overall, one of the best professors I had. She is not afraid to roast btw
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Jen is a really good person. Honestly, her classes are the only ones where I feel challenged anymore in the IU Gender Studies department. If at all possible, take her class.

I thought Jen's class was fine. She's a very tough grader and sometimes won't give as much specific feedback as you'd like. She takes rough drafts of papers but doesn't give actual feedback on them generally. I really didn't like her grading scale: you need a 95% for an A instead of an A- which I found unreasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had Jen as a professor for my Intensive Freshman Seminar. Even now it was one of the best classes Ive had at IU. Her lectures and classes were fun and fascinating, and Jen was excellent at getting all of us to connect.

I love dr Maher!!! She is HILARIOUS! Her lectures are so much fun and there's no way you'll get bored in any of her classes. She does make you work for your grade though. She is by far the best teacher I've ever had

SHE IS HILARIOUS! most people in her class (me included) hadn't taken a gender class before, next thing we know we're watching magic mike XXL, reading playboy magazine - it's one of the most entertaining classes I've ever taken. She is absolutely awesome.

I love Jen. She is tough, incredibly smart, and hilarious. If you're looking for an easy A, don't take any of her classes. She makes you work for your grade... but she gives amazing feedback and is so constructive in making you a great writer and a better student. I highly recommend taking a class with her if you want to challenge yourself.

Jen is by far my favorite teacher at IU, she is super hilarious and her classes always have a good mood, however get ready to do a ton of reading and be ready to answer questions about them, your grade for G225 will be based in 6 assignments, so make sure to prepare for them because it will be hard to recover if you don't do well in one of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Maher is hilarious and very knowledgeable about gender studies overall, and popular culture studies. There are papers and a midterm and final. If you are not a good writer, do not take course. But, it is very fun and interesting

Prof. Maher was super cool and nice. The class was very interesting and I enjoyed it a lot. We had two rhetorical analysis papers, a midterm and a final, and we also had to choose a corny romance novel and write a paper about it. There is also a fair amount of reading
Very hard grading and not a lot to do to recover from bad grades. Would not take this class again. She is an entertaining teacher but way too hard of a grader just to get Gen Ed credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Jen was hilarious and made this class very interesting. I loved her class, although it was a lot of work and a ton of reading, her lectures were always so entertaining and she really does know what she is talking about and I always understood the readings after going to class. Attendance is mandatory and you will have to work hard for your grade.

Jen was by far my favorite teacher! She's kind of quirky but always made us laugh in class.  She likes to call people out if they arrive late or if you have your cell phone out.  There are only two essays but she's a picky grader.  And lots of random reading quizzes so make sure you read!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Amazing and nice and just the most interesting person ever

Absolutely love Jen. Didn't have any tests, but had two big essays. I love the way she grades them because she is very specific about the way she wants an essay written, but at the same time she doesn't take off too many points for it. She gives lots of grade feedback and is a very fair grader. You have to work in her classes, but its worth it.

Jennifer is hilarious. I absolutely loved this class. Really fun material and lectures are never boring. I really learned a lot but enjoyed every minute of it. Definitely recommend unless you're against feminism in which case you will probably disagree with her a lot. Also, she warns that it's not easy to get an A but it is.

Dr. Maher is by far the best professor I've had in the gender studies department. She's incredibly funny and engaging. Attendance is mandatory and there are no electronics allowed in class. Make sure you do the reading, sometimes there are graded reading responses. People say she grades harshly but I disagree. Ask for help if you're worried.

Professor Maher is very smart, engaging, and funny. The class of hers that I took, however, had a ton of long readings; they were very interesting, but there were a lot. She is also very strict in general, calling people out for being late and stuff like that. Her essays are tough but engaging. A real stickler for the rules.

Shes a great professor in lecture. She is really funny and the topic of the class is extremely fascinating. She is VERY OCD about how she organizes and runs her class. There is assigned readings every class that she will give pop quizzes about. Some of the readings are hard, others not so much. Her class was my favorite by far this semester

Jen was a wonderful teacher for my IFS class. Our class was small and connected well through her rather crude humor. She is passionate and clear in her lecturing and will assign reading with short response quizzes the next day. We used three books for this course. I would love to take her class again. If you do the work, you'll get an A!

Jen Maher was a funny well educated teacher however she was not suited to be a teacher. She does not specify anything for her tests and leave grading of papers to her AIs. She announced that the final was cumulative after our last class and after she cancelled class which would have served as a review class just because she did not want to come in.

Amazing professor. All though she lectures the whole period, I have never ever been bored during one of her lectures. Funny and great personality!! The class would be more difficult without the help of the AI's. Talk to them and use them to help you with papers. If you talk to them you will do well on papers. You must show up to class

Your grade in this class consists of two rhetorical analyses, questions over a romance novel, a midterm, and a final. The AIs do all the grading, so it really just depends who you get for AIs, but so far I've heard they've all been fairly tough graders. The exams are straightforward and not too difficult. Attendance is mandatory. Interesting class.
If you know how to rate a rhetorical analysis, you'll do fine in the class. My advice: do the readings, listen in class, know how to write a paper.

Would not recommend this class.  Class title included "Pop Culture" but most of the class is focused on historical readings that are pretty boring. Comparable to a high school teacher that is obsessed with attendance and cell phone use.  Essays are tough- I received 25% off my essay because of a misunderstanding.  She is not lenient whatsoever.

My favorite teacher I've had at IU so far, as a sophomore. Yes, her papers are a bit difficult, but they're not nearly as bad as people are making them sound. The tests aren't too bad at all, pretty straightforward. The AIs are not the best, not very friendly. But I loved Professor Maher and I am excited to take another class with her!

I really can not believe the ratings she has received. As a senior at IU who has taken many gender classes, she is by FAR the WORST yet. Don't get me wrong, her lectures are interesting, but she is cold hearted and could care less about her students, seriously. And as for grading papers, like it has been said its impossible to please her. Horrible.

She is hilarious and makes class really interesting. I always felt engaged & she explains really well. The tests were super easy, just 25 m/c. On the flip side, writing an essay for her is ridiculous. She grades so harshly and it's nearly impossible to please her. Overall she's a really good prof but just be warned and be prepared for those essays.
Awesome teacher.  Super funny and charismatic!

You are missing out if you don't take a class with her. She is hilarious and makes class really interesting. I though the grading was fair and the exams were extremely easy... only 25 Q's multiple choice.

I was really excited about taking her class before I actually took it. She gives you random reading quizzes, so do the readings. But she doesn't like it when you try to relate your own personal experiences to the class discussion unless you're REALLY interesting. Also, her opinion is the only opinion. Don't even try arguing your own with her.
Hard class. Bad AIs. Never know how to write a paper that will please her. Bad class. Don't take with her.

Very entertaining classes to look forward to and that clarify the difficult readings required. The biggest problem I had was I never knew what she was looking for in an A paper... just seems kind of subjective.

She's a very personable woman, with a lot of funny quotes.  Overall, she can be a bit difficult because she expects you to rise to the occasion.  This isn't bad, but if you want an easy ride look elsewhere.

As a non-gender studies major, I found her a difficult grader and opinionated. She didn't keep her opinions to herself and made me feel uncomfortable. If you have views different than hers and confront her about how you feel in class, she brushes it off. Don't take her courses unless you're a gender major.

i really enjoyed this class but unfortunately didn't get the best grade-she is very knowledgeable and makes you understand and enjoy the material-the assigned readings can be and are difficult, which make the papers difficult to write too. she relies on her AI's mostly and can be hypocritical at times, i have mixed opinions on her

By far the best professor I've had in my undergraduate experience. This is the most interesting class I have taken. I love debating with my friends about the things I've learned from her and her readings. The class is well worth it. But you HAVE to go to class!

This lady ROCKS! She is an amazing professor! Attend class- simply because they are so interesting- and understand the concepts of each author and you will do just fine! She uses movie clips to exlain the concepts too! There are two papers, two exams and you have to read a Romance Novel of your choice- very fun!  She is hilarious! Def. recommended!

Ms. Maher is a first-clASS PROFESSOR!  SHe knows her material and knows how to impart it. She's published in cool magazines and hip essay collections. Plus, she has a dreamy husband and a gorgeous,albeit spoiled-rotten dog. She's very likable if you have good attendance. One of the smartest, hippest profs I've ever had.
She is Funny, opinionated, and easy to get along with...tough paper grader though!

love this class.  she is intimidating at first, but actually extremely accessible to her students.  she makes really funny comments, but the attendance rules are the only bad part.  tests are easy, papers are straightforward.
SHE HAS YOUR A.I.'S GRADE EVERYTHING, YOU NEVER GET HIGHER THEN A B- ON A PAPER.

At first she seems intimidating, but she's not as bad as she makes herself sound. She's very strict with attendance and people who leave early, etc. Otherwise, she makes the class very entertaining and interesting.

Professor  Maher is a very knowledgable, helpful individual.  I enjoy her class very much.  The only caveat is she adheres to the strict attendance policy of the Gender Studies department, so don't miss any classes.   The only criticism would be that group work in any class sucks, so why do it at all?
She is great! She makes complex issues easy to understand.

I REALLY liked this class, and I'm not even a Gender Studies major. The subject material is usually really interesting (reading due every class, sometimes kinda long). Two reg. papers, lots of good movie clips :)Really nice/funny/interesting/clear/enthusiastic. (teaches other classes too)
fabulous  teacher, just fabulous

A nice and entertaining professor. Some of the subject material is pretty interesting and her comments are pretty amusing. Not too much homework, just a lot of reading and a paper. Overall, I'd recommend her. And I think she said she reads this, too. :)
Her class is fun and interesting, not much homework, mostly reading.
do not take his class

The worst prof I've ever had. Tried reaching out to the grader for feedback and Mr sha after our first exam and no answer. I'd get questions right but didn't solve the way he wanted to he marked it completely wrong and as a zero. Save yourself and find any other professor. Tuition = wasted.

He is bad with accommodations first of all and does not know how to use canvas properly. He does not outline the class well and just know he is a tough grader and very strict person to talk to. I would go to his office hours a lot and he did not ever help in the slightest. He is a nice guy but terrible at helping students properly succeed.

This professor is an overall good teacher. Yes he does not give feedback on tests, quizzes, and homework, However, he tells you exactly what you need to do to succeed. He wants you to learn the overall concepts in class and do independent study to solidify them. If you want to succeed you have to put in the work!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I'm hopping on her after receiving a 48% on my first midterm exam. I'm a straight-A comp-sci student and have never failed a test... ever.... until today. The class average for most quizzes is below 50% and I wouldn't be surprised if the average for this exam was below 50% as well. The homework is also super easy to lose points on. I hope I pass.

Sloppy handwriting, quiz every Thursday, very tough grader, doesn't explain clearly, expects us to know already, class not mandatory, but weekly quizzes. Not a lot of office hours, not accommodating for exams or quizzes, no make-ups. No feedback on hw or quizzes. Get a really good tutor or take through Ivy Tech.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Doesn't care about how you do in the class
If you have to take a class with him, drop out. You'll thank me later.
Bro is absolute dog water at teaching, yo.

Professor will show up with one, maybe two examples for each section of the textbook. Will spend a day proving a section and expect you to be proficient enough to do the most difficult questions from the textbook. The exams are also much harder than any examples given in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Awful. The class is designed for you to fail, or barely pass. His lectures are useless, and exams regularly cover material that was never taught.

Have A's, one F. Guess the class. His lecture goes as follows: complete ONE (maybe 2) examples on the board with straight proofs, screams "ya" repeatedly. Then gives you hw and test questions that is way harder or completely different then what he showed on the board. Expects you to be a genius after one proof. I loved math, now I hate it bc of him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you want my honest opinion, this guy does not care how you do in his class. He brings one sheet of paper with 2 equations to every class. He reads directly off this paper, writes it on chalkboard then dissmisses class. I went to every one of his office hours for help and he told me to "read the book."

It is a challenging course, but once you are prepared enough for the class and understand the concepts, the course is ok. The overall grades aren't as high, but he curves, and I'd say although the examples he does are not as hard as the homework questions, he explained the concepts well.

The guy does NOT teach you, you WILL read the book if you want to pass the class. The B O O K is SACRED to this class, honestly just show up to the lectures so you know what to teach yourself because the professor doesn't teach you at all, and expects you to do like 50 problems to study, 25 of which the book doesn't even give you the answers for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Although he curves, how much do the students learn when an average test grade is less than 50%. No study material was given for any exam, harshly worded, and the final exam was insanely hard for being worth 30% of our grade. Getting an A+ in 211 then a C+ in 212 shows that he makes this class way harder than it needs to be. Very condescending too.

He is very condescending and expects you to know everything because it is "common sense" and "very easy. He gives simple examples of problems only to assign difficult homework problems, quizzes, and tests on concepts he never taught. His 3 exams are 6-8 questions with each problem worth about 10-20 points. Switch majors or go to Ivy Tech!!!!

Your grade in this class is 75% exams, and although the questions are similar to what we see in the homework, you get docked so many points for small algebraic errors on exams. If you need to take this course with Professor Sha, prepare to learn everything independently from the textbook and youtube, as I learned almost nothing from his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hands down the worst professor I ever had in the history of Math! He provides no practice exams/review problems at all which is the backbone of preparing for an exam. All he provides is his unclear and poorly written lecture notes but all of a sudden would throw in some of the most difficult problems you cannot expect on the exam.

He doesn't teach. That's all. Sure, he'll put theorems up on the chalkboard and do examples, but they're rarely comparable to what we see on the homework, quizzes, and exams. I learned way more from the once-a-week recitation with his TA than I did in Sha's lectures. Avoid this class; people warned me, and I didn't listen. Be smarter than me.

Goes over the topics using the easiest most basic problems, then expects you to translate that into being able to do the hardest problems in the book for hw, quizzes and tests. I will never understand how something can be covered on a test/hw that was never taught in class. He makes class way harder then needed, he should be ashamed of himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Sha is charismatic and loves teaching math which makes coming to class much more enjoyable. He engages well with students and explains the topics clearly. He follows along with the assigned book which makes the learning even easier. 10/10, would recommend Professor Sha. I will be taking more of his classes in the future.

Prof Sha absolutely knows what he is talking about. The only issue is that he skips 3-4 steps at a time when working examples in class and leaves the class lost. Also, exams tend to be very difficult with a very generous curve for final grades. You will learn a ton but it will be difficult
Amazing prof
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Horrible Professor.

This professor openly states how he aims for a D average on exams. Concepts that were skipped over in class are on the exam. Partial credit for problems is almost non existent. States that this class is for engineering/ CS majors yet skips most of the important content that can be used in Machine Learning / Computer vision. Very rude at times.

Professor Sha was awful for the online semester. He had one in person test for an online class that students had to go to with no virtual option. He did not communicate well, did not answer emails, and was terrible with zoom. Do not take his class.

Professor Sha was awful in an online format. His lectures are very hard to follow, his handwriting is awful, and he refused to turn on Zoom chat even after students requested it. The grader is impossible to contact and left literally no feedback on homework or quizzes. Prof Sha's computer made a horrendous whining noise all semester long too.
Professor Sha did not care about his students this year in the online format. He was a struggle to communicate with. He also never answered emails. His handwriting is also horrendous.

Warning: this course is rigorous and is an exploration that touches the beginnings of analysis and topology with a helping of linear algebra. Lectures are incredibly dense and require a lot of background. Homework tends to be worded unclearly; be sure to ask him as a class and not individually. Don't worry about the occasional 60%-70% on anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the most intelligent professors at IU. He teaches math in an unusual way, which is sometimes difficult to understand, but rewarding when you manage to get it. He's a pro at teaching S312's disparate material in a unified way. Tying everything together at the semester's end was super satisfying. Curve is very generous, too.

If you get the opportunity to take S311 with Sha, do it. He is brilliant and more passionate about calculus than any human should be. His curves are extremely generous too, so don't be worried about the occasional 60% on an exam or 4/10 on a quiz. Do the homework and show up to lecture and you'll get the grade and learn a TON doing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Sha's linear algebra is a nightmare. Weekly quizzes over material that was not covered in class. No study guides or guidance on exams. No feedback on incorrect exam or quiz grades. 3 exams make up 70% of grade. Take this class with anyone else, the curve is generous but not worth your trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Sha's linear algebra class is a mess. He does not explain the underlying ideas behind concepts and then expects you to know them by the exam. Weekly quizzes that don't align with course material. Frustrating lack of explanation on incorrect exam answers. No study guides or practice exams. Take this class with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you aren't naturally good at math and understanding it, this course will suck. Very much test and quiz heavy, often times the tests and quizzes are much more complicated than the material he covers in class. Get ready to watch a loottttt of youtube videos in your own time, because this class is entirely unclear and harsh.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Sha is an amazing professor. He really emphasizes understanding throughout his lectures and teaches you math beyond just formulas . He teaches you tricks and methods that are only achieved through years of experience. His remarks/examples in class are invaluable for depth of understanding. You will become more sophisticated in calculus.

Course difficulty and theoretical level is comparable to IU honors math courses. Works quickly through theory and examples in lecture in a way that loses most people. Bad at clearly answering questions. Homework is time-consuming, and exams can be pretty long and theoretical. Curves the class like crazy at the end, so not too hard to get an A.

Ji-Ping Shas classes generally tend to be much more difficult than they need to be. His classes are averaging Ds on exams, and it seems like he is one of those teachers that really attempts to get a specific (rigorous) grade distribution in his classes. That means a lot of people need to do poor. Exams are 64% of the total grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This professor is definitely knowledgable of the topic; however, his explanations and lectures are unorganized, difficult to follow, and often unrelated to the homework. The tests and quizzes don't compare to the wording in the textbook. Office hours were hardly any help. The grading was extremely hard and there's barely any partial credit given.

Great person and brilliant mathematician; but beware of the summer course. Calc III is usually said to be easier than Calc II, but this only holds during fall/spring. Any 6-week calc course will be much harder than any 16-week one. Material is breakneck speed, homework almost everyday, a quiz or two each week. Not for faint of heart.

Sha is a great math professor. He presents concepts very clearly and assigns homework problems that really help you learn the material. He challenges students to think rigorously about new definitions and often shows connections to other areas of mathematics. (Also, his english is perfect. No native speaker will have any trouble understanding him.)

Good professor. Skips unnecessary steps, which I liked. Always took time to explain the math behind a theorem or concept. He has an accent so you have to pay attention well to understand, but what he says is very helpful. But he was annoying during test reviews about only doing book problems. Homework every week about 4-6 hours, Steward Calculus.
He explains the material very well and is very welling to help. I would recommend people with better math background to attend the class since he does skip some steps.
this is one of the best mathematic professor in IUB. he can talk about everything clearly in class. so we can understand the content when we participate the class.
Sha is very kind, but not helpful with what he teaches.  Skips a lot of steps in example problems.  Will not look at problems with grading, makes you see the graders (who are usually terrible).
Accent takes time to get used to, but overall a decent professor. Gives reasonably fair tests and quizzes, so as long as you keep up with the class and really learn the material you will be fine.

Accent is very noticeable, but not bad at all.  Handwriting is very legible.  My only complaint is that he sometimes goes too fast, but in a 6 week summer session, that's to be expected.  Quizzes and tests were challenging, but he does use a curve.  I would take him again if I was a regular student here and not visiting from another campus.
I couldnt understand him at all. he is horrible on explaining examples and hard to understand his english.

Professor Sha is one of the worst professors I have ever had during my career here at IU. The averages on the tests were f's and d's. He ended up curving but wouldn't tell us what the curve was like until the final grade actually came out. If you had any questions you are turned away. He laughed in students faces daily.. RIGH?
Professor Sha not only gives excellent insight in analysis, but is an amazing mentor as a person and mathematician.
Probabaly the worst professor I have ever had
No Comments

AAAH!! I hated him so much I felt like taking the time to add him. Calc really isn't too bad, but this man takes 40 minutes to explain something that should only take 5. He refuses to go over specific questions, and he's not clear about ANYTHING.  AVOID this professor. "You agree?!?" "No Sha. I do not agree."

Overall, decent professor. The class wasn't anything special ie. not particularly hard or easy. Just beware she makes a lot of typos in instructions and other things, so don't be too worried if you see something not work in a homework or the like since there's a chance it was just a typo.

i had minimal programming experience before taking this course, but I still managed to find success more often than not. professor Li is decently accommodating for hw and help with hw and is clear that if you want to do well in the class, she will help you. attendance is not technically mandatory, should go to as many classes as you can.

Prof Li is clear from day 1 on how to do well in the class. Coding is difficult, so students have to put in effort outside of class to learn. I attended every class, and her lectures were straightforward. The in-class files were helpful for studying. I did well on the exams despite not having any prior coding experience. I recommend Prof Li!

It was difficult to actually understand the material in class. Most of the time, the files' instructions are significantly difficult to understand and she struggles to explain concepts thoroughly, so I mostly used ChatGPT to teach me the material. Additionally, there was very little clarity with quiz/exam structure which made it difficult to study.

Professor Li is a very nice person - wants to see her students succeed and always help. She is accessible and kind and reasonable always. Objectively the material in the class is somewhat difficult and the quizzes, being only a few points are easy to not do so well on. But it is possible to improve and do well.

Li's lectures can be material dense and their is not much time to ask questions. The quizzes are in class and mostly conceptual which I found harder than the actual coding. Their are weekly 2-3 question coding exercises that aren't too bad and daily in-class assignments so you do have to go to class. Overall not a bad class but not a great one.

Bit of a boring class but really attainable to get an A since a quiz is dropped and she curves them. Classes are just lectures that take the full class time, but Jie is very kind and willing to explain concepts as needed. The latest review posted for her is just blatantly wrong. Not a heavy workload, and "notoriously difficult quizzes" is crazy.

Ji Lie's first attempt at teaching S364 has been brutal. The lectures often last to the end of class, and are focused around completing lengthy in class assignments. This and the weekly projects and four notoriously difficult quizzes make the class a heavy workload with difficult high weight assignments. Slides/quizzes are worded incoherently.

The class and professor are easy, only thing that can be difficult is the projects. Sometimes she isn't always confident in the material herself which can make it difficult to ask questions and get help. She is very nice though!

Great class for those who want to learn programming but have limited experience. This class can be challenging with all the work you have to do (daily pre-class quiz, weekly quiz, hands-on exercise, timed long quiz, and a final project). You'll learn a lot from this class if you are willing to make your hands dirty.
She is a great teacher, take her class!
She's the nicest professor I've ever met! I don't know what the previous comment was talking about. She's knowledgeable about the things she teaches and she really cares about her students.

Worst professor with poor spoken or teaching skills. She just reads the slide and babbles without explaining anything. Why Mike frutiger the other professor was not asked to take the whole course is a wonder as he is articulate and knowledgeable. Li acted confident but struggled with tech herself. She lacked internal knowledge or the ability.

Do not be shy or afraid to ask questions. She really wants to help you and all you need to do is just try to do it yourself and make mistakes and ask her for some guidance. There might be other professors that give better easy As for this course, but she will teach you and you are going to learn. I really recommend her! Also attend the classes!

Jie Li is a very sweet professor and cares a lot about her students. Took her for K303 during online classes and she made it very easy. Little bit of an accent, but still easy to understand. All K303 sections offer EC through surveys so be sure to take advantage of those!

Jie Li is such a sweetheart that is passionate about data analytics and her students. She was available to help me multiple times outside of class and gives great feedback on projects. Sometimes she drags out her lectures when she gets passionate about the material, leaving little time to work on graded assignments. Other than that... solid choice!

Professor Li is honestly so nice. You can tell she really cares about her students and she is always willing to help you. She's not always great at using class time effectively--can be a little lecture heavy and sometimes she gets confused--but she really grew on me as the semester went on.

I don't really understand the reviews of Professor Li on here. I thought she was awesome! She really wants students to understand the material and make it relatable. I didn't do to well on a project and I went in to talk to her and she gave me  A LOT of points back because she could tell I understood the material, just made small mistakes.  10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Jie Li is probably the toughest grader in K303 which should be an easy class.  She tries very hard to teach the material, but I just found class time was not all that beneficial to my learning, especially the powerpoints. If possible, I'd try to take someone else. If you're already scheduled with Jie bae,good luck, maybe I'm just an outlier.

Jie Li wasn't a very helpful teacher compared to others (last spring, her students had 30% less A's than other professors teaching the course). For example, a student came in after he did poorly on a project and instead of helping him she told him "You should've done worse on this project". 1/5 would not recommend.

This class is test heavy and exams are hard. Homework assignments are all handwritten, over 6 pages a week. Our class got punished for previous classes using AI and in lab. Flipped classroom was confusing. He offers so many extra credit opportunities, UTA and review sessions do it all. He cares a lot about students and will help you succeed!

Jim Davis is truly a wonderful professor but the class is not easy so you will have to put the work in and show up outside of class to UTA sessions. He is caring and try's to keep class entertaining even through long lectures.

Dr. Davis is an amazing professor. He has high expectations and the class is not easy, but he gives SO many resources to help you succeed + a ton of review sessions every week. He genuinely cares about all of his students and wants them to do well. There is a lot of homework but it is genuinely helpful in learning the material. 10/10 professor.
Tests are really hard so just get ready to really know all the material and show up to lectures
A professor that wants to see you fail.

Had an amazing semester with Professor Davis that left off on a bad note because he did not like our lecture section because some students had used AI and not come to class. Sorry but it's not fair to take it out on the whole class.

Not a bad professor at all, just a hard one. He writes his own tests and they are extremely difficult, a lot more difficult than the other professors'. There are no study guides. Get ready to do a minimum of 6 assignments per week and cry over your grades.

He is a pretty good professor, a lot of extra credit opportunities but a ton of work before each class as it is a flipped classroom. He can be super intense and really did not like our class for a variety of reasons, which he will absolutely let you know any chance he got. There is a lot of out of class time trying to understand it.

Dr. Davis is an amazing professor. P225 is a hard course, so expect to work. However, Dr. Davis will do everyhting in his power to make sure you succeed, as long as you are putting the work in. He gives so many resources from study sessions to podcasts, but its up to you how you use the available resources.

Dr. Davis is an AMAZING professor. He gives you ALL the tools you need to be successful, its on you to use them or communicate if you need something else. He is very accessible. Go to every class. Take the pre-class assignments seriously. Make time to go to UTA sessions/his review sessions once a week. It seems optional but it helps so much.

He was the best professor I had. He cares so much about the students' success and future. He gives you so many resources and opportunities to do well in this course and listens to feedback! I genuinely learned and retained the most I have in a class before because of the way he teaches. Go to the lectures!

Professor Davis is funny and makes class time fun, but it is a flipped classroom. His course was difficult due to the contents, but he clearly explained everything. His tests (for the most part) weren't trick questions, but again difficult due to the course. Davis can be strict with expectations but as long as you follow what is asked he is great.

Dr Davis makes physio so easy. The flipped classroom format is v helpful too. The short assignments you do are quick and easy and exams are not too hard either. The BPE's are more difficult than the exams btw so they help with studying. Dr. Davis is a great dude. Pretty chill and truly shows that he cares about his students.

A very caring professor, I would take this class over and over again because of how awesome Dr. Davis is. Attend every class and come prepared and you will succeed. Go to UTA sessions, review sessions, and office hours. Engage during class with your classmates as that will help you learn the most. 100% would recommend taking his class

Dr. Davis is one of the best professors that I have had. The class is flipped and there's a lot of work outside to do, but the lecture in class is basically a review of the notes you took the night before. He really wants you to succeed and provides so many resources, extra credit points, etc. It's a tough course but he is a really great professor.
low key fw this professor.

Dr. Davis is such an amazing professor, definitely this class is hard you have to put in the work but Dr. Davis is always available to help his students and offers a lot of extra credit. He uses analogies to make you understand physiology. There is also a a lot of homework due to this class being flip classroom.

Dr. Davis has been the best teacher I've had so far. He is really nice and understanding. His class is a flipped classroom, which means you will have a lot of homework. Make sure you start off with a good grade because it's harder to understand the material as you go further into the semester. BEST TEACHER EVER.

I think that Dr. Davis is really good at explaining material in his lectures, however he does do flipped learning. There is a lot of work to do outside of class because you need to watch lecture videos and do the homework. However, Dr. Davis is a really nice professor that gives out a lot of extra credit.

Dr. Davis is the best professor I have ever had. The class is hard, but getting an A in the class is absolutely attainable if you put the effort in. There are plenty of extra credit opportunities as well. Dr. Davis truly cares about his students. He gives you plenty of opportunities to get help on material in the class as well.
Difficult class but Dr. Davis offers extra credit and explains tough material in a way that is understandable.

One of the best professors at IU. Improves on teaching methods between exams and semesters. Easy-to-follow flipped classroom style. Engaging teaching style, even at 8AM. Utilizes teaching team well. Makes class easy to succeed IF you use the resources correctly, but does not make it an easy A by any means.
Cannot recommend P225 by Dr. Davis enough.

this is one of the hardest classes I have ever taken, but davis was always willing to help & encourage me. saw me as a human before a student. do all of the assignments. lots of extra credit available. every. point. matters. I literally got my A- by .03%. (TAKE THE 8:00 AM)

hate physio, love davis. 
& if you're reading this, you got this.

One of the best professors at IU. Extremely caring and always wanting the best for his students. Lots of material is covered in his class. However, the flip classroom design allows for students to watch videos multiple times to understand the concepts. They can be great study tools before exams.

This was the best professor I have ever had. It is a hard class and covers a lot of material in general, but he is great at simplifying topics and creating useful analogies, and an A is possible if you put the work in. There is a lot of work outside of class, it was a flipped classroom, but there are a lot of extra credit and review opportunities.

The content was very hard for me, and my test grade reflects this. However, he is very reachable during his office hours and always will have review sessions either hosted by him, or the AIs. He explains the information well and gives great analogies if you are confused. Definitely glad I had him as my professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Davis was my favorite professor! If you need to take P215 he is the best professor to have! The class was early but he genuinely cares about his students understanding and being able to interact with the material. the flipped classroom may be a bit more work on the front end but his teaching style helped me to genuinely learn!!
He is a great guy that wants the students to fully understand the material. He gives lots of extra credit and runs a flipped classroom. He truly was the better of the two Physiology 215 professors!

Best professor I have ever had. He made a very hard subject surprisingly enjoyable. The flipped classroom style is SO helpful and he genuinely cares about students succeeding. He always has extra credit and consistently makes himself available outside of the classroom to answer questions, provide additional help, or just be there to listen. 10/10!

Dr. Davis is my all time favorite teacher! He runs a flipped classroom. I found the flipped classroom to be to my benefit. Even though his class was early, it was worth waking up for. If you have to decide between an 8 A.M. from Dr. Davis or another professor at a later time, pick Dr. Davis. He has lots of extra credit. 5 major exams. FANTASTIC GUY
Professor Davis is an amazing teacher and really cares about how you perform in his class.

Genuinely cares about student success in the class. Physiology is a difficult subject but Prof. Davis made it easy. Flipped classroom style worked out really well for me, take good notes over the videos and pay attention in class and you will do well. He made himself very available outside of lecture for help. Exams were frequent but easy.

Dr. Davis is an amazing professor. He does flipped classroom which can be time consuming, but SO helpful. If you take good notes from his recorded lectures you will do well, and he gives so many opportunities for review and questions to be asked. He cares about teaching, and he wants you to do well and understand.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class itself is easy, the professor is a little od, won't let kids into class 2 seconds after the bell, and punishes you for missing a meaningless class where you learn nothing

Prof Shelton was a very nice professor who clearly cared about his students. His classes did tend to become "Sports Marketing Buzzwords 101", but he worked hard to make it an active and engaging environment. If you're taking this class, take it with Prof Shelton, but maybe take it online. Same results, less lectures.

Teacher in class is fine, but the course was one of the most meaningless classes I took at this school but Professor Shelton thought it was a grad-level physics course that was essential to the future. Doesn't let students into class even five seconds after the start time, then punishes them when he doesn't let them in with drastic grade reductions

Easy class, he's just hard to get in contact with and will give you a bad grade over the smallest mistake, but not explain why or how to fix it. Took him over 2 weeks to respond to an email; I had to explain to higher-ups his inabilities. I finished with an A but had to argue for all grade changes due to poor instructions and a lack of feedback.
classes were interesting and i found myself engaged

Greatest Professor ever. I really loved his teaching style of treating each class like a game. Doing pre-game, 1st quarter, TV timeout, 2nd quarter. You get the drill. Had amazing lectures and was a great guy. 100/10 would always recommend.

I took M211 but that wasn't an option. Very easy class if you do the work. Some assignments are annoying but nothing is difficult at all. Very easy A+ if you just do the work, no tests or anything other than small reading quizzes. I took the online version.
I took M211, not C218 but that wasn't an option. Just do your work and it's basically a participation A. I'm lazy af and got an A-
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Just do your work and youll be fine. Whatever you put in is what you'll get out of this course
This class was very easy, although the reliance on group work made for uncertainty about how to turn things in. I would still highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This guy was actually really cool and funny. Easygoing and understanding as well. I would recommend.
The class is sometimes online, but participation is graded in a way that you do not have to come to every class.

He's a pretty smart guy. However, he teaches nothing that you haven't already learned before. There is a heavy emphasis on participation, and it will ruin your grade if you don't. Overall, I haven't learned anything in the class that I didn't learn from 7th-grade science.

Julio provides funny commentary throughout the lecture and participation in the lectures is NECESSARY to get an A. Readings and assignments are super easy and there are no exams but there are unit quizzes. Definitely go to office hours if you are interested in the material- his research is interesting and he can find you cool opportunities!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Hilarious--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: AVOID HIM. DO NOT TAKE HIS COURSE. First, HE ASSIGNED HW/CLASS OVER THANKSGIVING BREAK (our only break for the semester). Then, he put in a participation grade at the very end of the semester, giving almost everyone an F, and dropped so many students 1 or 2 entire letter grades. I did all work assigned and got A's for everything, but now have a B.

This professor does not actually teach. He will assign readings and videos to read/watch before every class and then make you talk about them the next day in class for 20 minutes. He then would ramble for the remainder of the hour. He gave work over our only break. He seems to love himself far more than he loves to teach. Never take his class.
No exams (during COVID), fairly easy homework. As long as you take notes on the readings and go to class, the unit quizzes are fine. He's funny, but definitely likes to hear himself talk.

During the pandemic we at IU have received one break, thanksgiving break. Otherwise the semester has been non stop work. This professor is my only teacher who had the audacity to assign work during the one holiday break weve had (btw hes also insufferable, annoying and rude). Dont take this class if you think youll want to respect this man.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Uploads assignments the day before they're due, doesn't say anything in his lectures pertinent to a test or the class, yet sends you into endless breakout rooms to "discuss" the babble he spews, and makes you talk because participation is an important factor. He won't teach you anything a 2nd grade science picture book couldn't. Picture book > him

I dread going to this class and frequently don't even though I'm sacrificing participation points. In the main session he drones on about nothing, and then sends you into breakout rooms at least 3 times to talk about the hour long documentary or 30 page historical text he made you read the night before, and then goes back to talking about nothing.

Great professor, super knowledgeable. The class covers very interesting material if you're interested in the environment and sustainability. If you do the homework and write thoughtful responses, you'll get a good grade. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof. Postigo is clearly very knowledgeable about this course and passionate about his work, in which he does a lot of work with the environment and geography. It is interesting to hear about his work. However, the class he teaches is very difficult and requires A LOT of reading for homework and memorization for tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This was one of the worst classes I have ever taken at IU. I signed up thinking I was going to enroll in a class that had an academic focus, and instead I found myself in a classroom that seemingly only existed to feed the professor's ego. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE WITH THIS PROFESSOR! The other section averaged 2 letter grades above this section.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Poor teaching - rambles on about stuff you won't be tested on. Tests are "multiple choice and short answer," where there are 10 options for each question and there are unclear instructions. Unhelpful at best, condescending at worst. REFUSES to change how he teaches, even when respectfully confronted. Take G208 with a different professor.

Here are my issues: -boring or nonexistent powerpoints with no visuals -confusingly formatted tests -asks for students opinions but doesnt listen or take into consideration -no recent/relevant examples -have to find our readings ourselves -rambles -no sympathy (scheduled an exam right after spring break and refused to change it)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is easily the worst class I have ever taken in my entire life. Postigo is a rude, condescending professor who creates the worst tests. The tests are extremely confusing and even if you attend all the lectures and do the readings, the tests still will make no sense. His lectures are TERRIBLE as well. NEVER TAKE A CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR.

Dont take this class as a Gen-Ed. Tests are confusing and hard. We took two tests this year with the majority of it being fill in the blank with no word bank or other guidance. We were given no study guide until we asked for one. You will have reading quizzes for every class and youll have to find the readings yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Doesnt know how to teach a college class. Very unclear with test material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Krause is amazing! His lectures are actually fun, and he has a good sense of humor! He genuinely cares about how you do in the class! I would 100% take a class with him again.

Jim was honestly a pretty cool guy. He's really funny and very knowledgable on film. His lectures were a tad boring and felt kind of dragged but definitely helpful. The class (lab) was really fun but also a lot of work. I'd take his class again though for sure!

PROS: funny dude, no midterm or textbook, final was easy & online 
CONS: boring lectures, has a fake attendance question so u need to be in class

Genuinely one of my favorite professors I've encountered at IU. His lectures are engaging and he radiates so much joy and passion for every topic he teaches. He has a wonderful sense of humor and is very personable. This class is one that I am excited to attend every time and I always leave feeling like I've learned something important.

There are very few points given in this class, but so much of it is literally just showing up. You'll need to spend a little time out of class while producing group projects, but you get a lot of creative freedom. Krause does his best to extend real in-field opportunities to his students, and definitely knows what he's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jim is awesome. He is the type of guy I would love to work with in the film world. He shouldn't be a teacher though. He definitely knows the material, but he can't explain it. If you ask a question, he will never know the answer, because he just knows the basics. He is super funny, and he does care, but don't expect to learn much from him.

Regarding the lecture, it was amazing. In such a short time frame, you learn a lot. And you are given a lot of resources for studying outside of class, which is a relief. Also, extremely funny guy overall, and you can easily form a bond if you interact individually. Would definitely recommend him to other students.
Great guy who loves being interactive and making sure students care about what he is teaching. Easily helped us with the mini in class assignments he would give in class.
It was made very clear that the lecture was complementary to the lab and it was a short way to get an introduction to what we'd be doing that week.
MSCH-229. There was a lot of information thrown at us at one time, but he made sure to provide us with links, lecture notes, and time aside to ask any questions about anything. Labs were really fun

I think theres too much in this class for him to be able to teach it properly. Youre kind of just thrown in without any true guidance and he heavily relies on you doing all the work outside of class. Hes very nice though and you can tell he knows a lot and really cares about his students. It also gives you good film experience.

Jim obviously cares about helping students improve. He's very clear about what he expects and what the assignments are. However after effects is a lot so be prepared to spend a lot of time on homework every week.
I really enjoyed talking to him, and he gave me a lot of help when I feel lost about projects. His lecture is cool, and from this class, I do learn a lot of things from AE.

Nice and helpful for one on one questions but needs more clarifications of what and what not to achieve nice performance at the beginning of the class. Class materials, besides creative video and tutorial resources, are somewhat boring.

Jim is a great professor! He is super friendly and truly cares about his students. He is very smart and able to explain material in a clear way. The learning atmosphere is extremely fun and casual! I really recommend  taking one of Jim's classes

VERY Unorganized. He leaves during lab for long periods of time and comes back at production time to tell you what you did wrong. Grades hard when he hasn't even taught material fully. Says quizzes are bite-sized and easy, but they are random and they hurt most students' course grades.
Jim is an absolutely wonderful teacher. Some of the technical stuff can be confusing, but he honestly taught me everything I wanted to know. Trust him and pick his brain as often as you can.

Jim is the best production professor in Tcom and IU. Although some of his classes are slightly disorganized, he forces students to learn by actually filming, which truthfully, is the best way to learn how to produce video. He doesn't impose restrictions on content and is a fair grader. Still, you should be motivated to take his classes.

Completely unorganized. 3 Different syllabi for the class. Each from a past semester. Too lazy to update. No one in the class had any idea what was due and when. Quizzes are random and don't necessary deal with anything to do in the class.
No Comments
He is a really cool teacher...one of my favorites

Professor Judge is a super nice professor that makes A304 pretty easy to understand. 3 exams are weighted 25% each, and there is no extra credit, so make sure you are understanding the material in order to get an A in the class. Study the packet they give you, and take notes, and you will be fine.

Professor Judge is super nice, and makes A304 easy to understand. To get an A in the class, I would recommend trying to memorize every learning objective as best as possible. Material isn't hard, but class is 75% exams and no extra credit.

Overall professor doesn't matter too much for this course as there are 2 options and they both teach the same. The course is very structured and easy to follow with plenty of resources for studying and extra help if needed. Lectures are heavy on content but Prof Judge explains things well. Very doable course even if you are weak in accounting

imo the professor does not matter much for A304.  The class is going to be difficult regardless and it is very exam heavy (75% of your grade). However, I believe Judge's lectures are pretty helpful and exam reviews are a good test of your understanding on the material.  Overall, A304 is going to be harder than A306 (in my opinion).
Class is very hard. However, Professor Judge is amazing! Also, homework is very irritating.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Judge is cool, the homework is agonizing though, but it is the same no matter what prof you have.
Homework is long and annoying. Teacher is good, lecture is worthwhile, tests are easy.

I love the format of the course, the in-class notes are much easier to digest than a textbook would be. You can easily get 100% on the homework and cases. Study a lot for the three exams (which are 75% of overall grade) and you'll be good. She's great at explaining the content and being very clear with what will be on the exam. Final is a project.
