They're dismissive, unhelpful, and create an uncomfortable environment where students feel set up to fail rather than supported to learn.

Krefit is one of the most inconsiderate and disrespectful professors I've had—easily among the worst in Kelley. reviews.comment: The Krefts who co-taught this class were incredible. Study, do the quizzes, and do the homework, and you will do well on the two exams. I would take them 100 times out of 100. They are really awesome teachers.

The Kreft's were some of the most inconsiderate professors I have ever had. The Kreft's want their students to fail. They do not do anything to help improve grades in a class based almost fully on tests. They try their hardest to catch kids cheating and even go as far as to take matters publicly and make an example out of them in front of the class

The way the Kreft's run their class is a complete joke. They do not assist their students what so ever. They talk down to their students and have a horrible attitude towards their students. They will not even answer your emails.

Steven was a really good professor overall he was able to talk about the mostly boring content in an engaging way. While his lectures really just cover the quizzes, he takes his time to explain the answers and let you ask as many questions as you can. 

His course direction is super clear and he communicates well. I would take this guy for every class if possible....

Professor Kreft was pretty lecture heavy with the spotlights that he gave for G202 but I feel that he did a really good job of summarizing what we needed to know and that allowed me to be successful for the G202 exams.

Steven you are amazing (sorry the wife drags you down I second the idea of you going solo big dog). You only stay sane in G202 because his lectures are fun, engaging, and interesting. He walks around the class lecturing with an almost standup comedian-like cadence, making even the most mundane topics enjoyable. Can't wait for Ellie to be fired.
Bro is the funniest guy of all time.  His stories are hilarious.  I spend most of his lectures cracking up.  I can't stand his wife though.  Maybe its time for him to start a solo career.

Not a hard class at all but theyre both really reluctant to help. whenever I would have a question, they would always tell me to figure it out on my own or get offended by what I was asking. Would take again and recommend professor. Class was very clear and felt tests matched lecture and given all resources to do well on tests. Liked not having to read from a textbook. reviews.comment: Steve was a great lecturer and provided all the information you needed during class. All the exams are based on the PowerPoints, don't necessarily need to read the cases. Exams were very difficult. Lots of studying will be needed to get a good grade in the class.

reviews.comment: G316 Sustainable Enterprise - chill but stressful. Split 50-50 Kelley/O'Neill kids and differing viewpoints are debated. Not much busy work. However, in-class participation forms the bulk of your grade and is curved against your classmates. They rate your in-class yaps (literally) – you rate theirs; stand strong and participate if you want an A.

I love his lectures, he keeps you engaged and really makes sure you know the content through stories and funny jokes. The course is SUPER exam heavy, but they give you all the materials needed to study. As long as you put in the time to study, you will do fine. He works alongside his wife Mafi-Kreft.
His lectures are fantastic, he drills the concept into you through a joke, it makes the course so much easier. Just put your phone away and listen.

The Professor Kreft is very humorous and engaging, often using vivid and interesting examples from his life to help students understand complex theoretical concepts. Moreover, he teaches very well, and I highly recommend taking his class.

This was the class I was most concerned about taking and it ended up being my favorite class of the term! This prof makes difficult material super accessible by thoroughly explaining and demonstrating problems and clearly delineating expectations; uses real-life examples that make it easy to connect to and remember the material. Super funny!

Steven is a good teacher for a rather boring class. He teaches it with his wife, Ellie, but does a far better job than she does. He has some funny lectures, but the class is 75% tests, and they are all very hard. Great teacher, just a poorly designed class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Steven does the best he can with a pretty boring class. Exams are easy and attendance is required but Steven is funny and does care.

One of the funniest professors I've had at IU. However, the class is extremely challenging. Make sure to redo the top hat and extra credit questions. Disables canvas grade total which is extremely annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, he is a good professor. He makes the class interesting and funny. But that said, the grade is mainly based on tests. They make the test very confusing and tricky and you can lose points easily. They barely curve the tests compared to the other professors (The highest curve was an extra 1.5 points).

Steven is a terrible professor, and also not a nice guy. He is passive aggressive and hardly responds to emails. Exams are the entirety of your grade and are so tricky that you miss entire questions because of one word. I genuinely think both him and his wife should be fired, because they clearly don't care about their students or teaching.

Prof. Kreft is one of my favorite profs. I've had at IU. He is extremely reasonable and lets you know where you can improve. His class is also very discussion-based. He makes sure everyone gets a chance to speak, and he tries to make you see things from multiple perspectives. I would 100% recommend taking any class taught by him, especially G316.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I LOVE STEVE! Best class & best professor at IU/Kelley! Such a kind and caring guy. He made every class super entertaining and it was definitely the most useful class that I've taken. He challenges you to think about sustainability from various perspectives and encourages everyone to participate. Class is small so you have the opportunity to talk.

Tests were pretty hard and although I went everyday that didn't help. It makes no sense to have him and his wife teach the class. She is mean during class and he is mean after class, maybe they're the perfect match because of it. Both are pretty smart but the class is a below average experience that's frustrating.

Steven is a really good lecturer. He jokes a lot to keep your attention. Him and Ellie are very transparent from the start about what you need to do to succeed (which is not much). Ellie gets unfairly compared to Steven but she really is not that bad. I have heard that they do not answer emails but they provide so much info that I understand why.

Steven is the rudest and most passive-aggressive professor I have ever had in my entire life. He did not care about my accommodations and I was crucified for a mistake. If you do not want to feel about 2 inches big, do not take them. This professor is unwilling to actually educate and is just there for the paycheck. I recommend them being fired!

Steven's lectures were always engaging and he would often tell funny stories during them. I always felt like I gained something from being in class, can't say the same for Ellie's lectures and I ended up rarely ever going, just looking over the PowerPoints on my own. G202 is a pretty easy class if you stay on top of readings and study.

reviews.comment: If you wouldn't like two different professors that both don't answer emails as well as not being good at teaching other than their online videos, then don't take the kreft's together. Although the course subject is relatively easy, they made the class much more difficult than it should've been.

I like Steven more than Ellie, he is more sympathetic. That being said you have to take this class with the both of them anyways, so it doesn't matter. Their lectures and slides are better than Powells, and most likely the best you can get for this class. Please please take it with them because it is the best option!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Better than the alternative. Funny and great, can't say the same about his wife but you learn to get over it. Really study for the exams and you will be fine.

Much preferred over the other G202 professor. Steven kept the lectures super engaging and was funny. His spotlights are helpful and I would recommend going to class even though everything is accessible online and attendance isn't graded.

Much preferred over the other G202 professors. Steven kept the lectures super engaging with his anecdotes that never waned no matter how late the class was. His lectures on the class spotlight were very helpful to go to and those who showed up definitely did better on the exams. Steven is awesome and I'd recommend any class he teaches.

I loved this class so much and I think anyone who can take it should. Professor Kreft has amazing insight and he really lets the discussions flow themselves. He is amazing and the course content is something that everyone should know. The whole class is based on discussion, so if you don't show up, you won't get anything out of it.

I disliked this class so much as it felt like they never really cared about their students. I reached out for help and felt like they did not care about anything I tried. I would never take a class from him or his wife again. This class material isn't super hard but they made it hard for me.
Neither Ellie nor Steven were engaging during their lectures or videos

reviews.comment: this class is amazing if you want to explore sustainable business. the class and the prof made the topics so interesting and engaging, even if you're not into sustainability. Steven Kreft really values people's opinions so it's important to share those in class or on the online discussion to receive full credit for participation.

The expectations set for the class were very clear.  Each week you had lecture videos to watch, a multiple choice quiz, a memo assignment which they basically tell you how to do in the live session, and an article/discussion board.  Definitely had to review for several hours for each exam, but they were all straight forward.  Very enjoyable class.

reviews.comment: Steven is a much better lecturer than Ellie. He tends to be much more engaging and it's easier to understand the material that he's presenting. The exams are pretty much your whole grade, so take all of them really seriously, especially the first one.

Steven and Ellie were very lazy and rude. They only teach using online videos and waste class time by telling stories and calling out random students. Steven's lectures are more interesting and less pressure than Ellie's. reviews.comment: Prof. Kreft was overall a solid professor. G202 is a course that could be made very interesting, but the lectures are often a little boring. Other than the case discussions, you really don't need to go to class. They post videos online you need to watch before the exams.

This class is easy if you watch the pre recorded videos and study the extra credit quizzes. The lectures were a repeat of these videos but I would recommend going to class when they went over the cases. Overall he seems like a smart and funny guy.

Steven is very knowledgeable and makes the content extremely easy to understand. Watch the prerecorded videos and make sure you understand the content for exams. They curve a lot and give extra credit. Ellie and Steven co-teach so it doesn't matter who you schedule with on iGPS. Loved the class, very doable to get an A!!

Nice person, bad professor. Class was useless and a repetition of the pre-recorded videos used so they didn't actually have to teach. Despite studying exactly the way they told us to, exams proved difficult and weren't much like the example questions given.

Steven teaches the most random stuff that doesn't apply to this world. His wife is good, but he is beyond stupid. He uses the most stupid analogies that don't make sense. To put it in clash royale terms, he tries activating king tower against a firecracker but just loses a tower instead.

Steven Kreft was incredibly rude in email conversations. My assignments were turned in on time, yet he docked me for points. If that doesn't sound crazy to you I don't know what will.

Steven and Ellie were great at the beginning of the year and I used to look forward to going to their class. I think they're both overworked and take out their frustration on students

Both Steven and Ellie are the rudest, most passive-aggressive, and ignorant professors I have ever had in Kelley. The 3 quizzes are way beyond the scope of what is taught. Overall content was easy to understand. Explains very clearly what is expected out of the quizzes and homework assignments.

Best professor at IU. He cares so much about what he teaches and it makes you excited to be a part of the discussions in class. There will never be a boring lecture and he always listens and loves to hear our perspectives. Hes just a great human man take him if you can.

This class was solely based on 4 exams. They teach a certain way in class then use completely different wording and detailed questions on exams. I failed 3/4 exams and studied for hours. This is the only C in class I have ever gotten. Be ready to study a lot and go to lectures and listen carefully. Take every EC quiz you will need it.

Prof Kreft is a decent teacher, even if the class content is boring. Attendance is not required, just read his powerpoints and practice the extra credit quiz questions to prepare for the tests. Super kind and knowledgeable about sustainability. Participation is really important either in class or in the canvas discussion. I really enjoyed his class and learned a lot, I definitely recommend.

Steven is an amazing professor! He is really knowledgeable on the subject matter of the class, and the class itself is very engaging. Although, the class is graded by only 4 assessment quizzes. To succeed in G202, you need to attend classes and watch the videos.

Steven is an amazing professor. He explains every concept learned in G202 to a depth, providing numerous examples and explaining material in ways that is understandable. Worst professor I have ever had. Steven and Ellie are heartless. Luckily I passed but if you got a 72.99, they wouldn't round your grade up to a C. reviews.comment: G202 is a pretty easy class- as long as you do the work and go to class, you'll get an A. Kreft's lectures are super engaging. There is a case reading every week that you have to write a short (250 word) essay on, besides that there isn't any homework.

So engaging! Was able to make real-world connections and material feel really relevant!

reviews.comment: I loved being in Steve Kreft's class. He's one of the few professors i've had that makes the class's content more meaningful through his personal experiences and stories. Very passionate and funny guy, and he explains the material pretty well.

reviews.comment: Professor Kreft was one of my favorite professors- he has a lot of experience teaching G202, so he knows how to structure the class while still making it entertaining. reviews.comment: I love how he uses real life examples and stories in class. He is super energetic, explained things well, and is hilarious. Overall, a super cool dude and an awesome professor. Show up to class, take good notes, and participate in the online discussions and you'll do fine. Exams are a bit difficult, but only if you don't study for it/take notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Not great. Class isnt too difficult, but my grade got worse the more I went to class. Class is mandatory for Kelley, but he clearly puts in next to no effort into his lectures. Too focused on being the cool and funny professor as opposed to actually teaching.

Fantastic Professor with great lectures. Hes one of those professors that you would want to get to know. Hes got a lot of knowledge to share, just make sure you go to every class and do all the readings.

Kreft is hilarious and an awesome professor. HOWEVER, I would NOT take this class second semester because he is notorious for placing an exam the day after quals (basically a holiday on IU's campus). I wish I knew this before registering for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He has very funny jokes in lecture and does a great job explaining things with examples. Attendance is not mandatory but you will be heavily tested on what was said during class. Taking notes and reviewing before exams would translate into an A

I took Professor Kreft online as part of the KD program curriculum. By far he has the best online class management skills of any course I've taken. He is very comfortable on video and has a great knack for engaging the class in a virtual setting. Exams are tough, so keep up with the assignments and prepare for tests. My favorite prof so far.

Best Professor so far at Kelley. The guy explains exactly how to study and what to study for his exams. While he does change the wording around and make some things more difficult than they should be, he is overall amazing at getting through to his students and is the best at keeping his students engaged I have seen thus far at IU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class is fairly straightforward. The tests are actually quite tricky and its hard to get over say a B+ on them but there are tons of extra credit opportunities that make up for it. He is a very cool guy. Never seen so much energy in a professor.
Great guy and absolutely hilarious lectures. Class isn't hard as long as you attend the case debrief days and pay attention during lecture. There's also a ton of extra credit.

Steve is my least favorite professor I've ever had. Everyone loves him and I have no idea why. His jokes are entirely canned and aren't funny, his attempts to be relatable are cringe-worthy, and when I asked questions one-on-one, he was dismissive, rude, and unhelpful. The quality of his instruction is neither great or bad, but I dreaded his class.

Genuinely enjoyed going to class. Professor Kreft made class interesting and used great examples to keep the class engaged. Hilarious. Helpful outside of class. Use the practice problems he gives you and there will be no issue on tests.
Steve is awesome. His lectures are hilarious and he always finds real life situations that apply to the material. Go to class and do the readings and you'll get an A.

Kreft is a really great professor and his lectures are definitely entertaining. He tells the funniest stories and is always willing to help in office hours. If you pay attention in class and read the cases you'll get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really nice guy and rounds up grades at the end. Going to class is definitely really helpful but not mandatory. The tests are tricky, but the discussions help to boost your grade. Can get a B pretty easily but difficult to get an A.

Kreft makes class fun by playing music, adding humor, and telling stories. He's by far one of my favorites. He connects with students without trying too hard. Study the PowerPoints and do the practice tests. The exams take 1 hour instead of 2 and are not hard if you study. There is extra credit before exams.
Overall really great professor. Gives you every opportunity to earn a good grade but you will have to work for it.

The class is essentially Microeconomics but delves into how government regulation can impact large business and the economy. There is a minor homework load. He keeps the class very engaged through his jokes but make sure to have your phone on silent. Yes there are only 3 tests, but the answers are in red on ppt, in practice exam, and review session
Steven Kreft is the best professor at Kelley. Awesome lectures and learned so much. This class is mostly discussion and was my favorite class at IU.

Kreft is a great lecture and his classes were never dull. However, the class is mainly graded on the tests which can be very difficult. Attendance isn't mandatory, but you need to show up to get a good grade. The class itself is rather pointless though. I got nothing out of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Kreft is an awesome guy who does a great job keeping you engaged during lectures. The class he teaches however is rather pointless. Many times throughout the semester people asked me what G202 was about and I honestly couldn't answer it. The tests are super confusing cause you have no idea what he's gonna throw on it.

Kreft is a great lecturer but the whole class is confusing. I can't tell you one thing I actually learned from taking the class. The tests were tough and you have to understand what he's talking about. You must attend class because that's where you get the notes.

Steven is a great person-- funny, smart, and engaging. The material isn't necessarily hard, but it is imperative that you go to the review sessions. There will be things on the exam that weren't gone over in class. But if you attend the review sessions, do all of the extra credit and assignments, and study, you will be fine!
Steve is a fantastic professor. Great at appealing to his class and making the material enjoyable. Great class, would take again if I could.
Steven has an amazing style of teaching, and the lectures are phenomenal. This is that one class, where attendance isn't compulsory, but still students come. Will definitely recommend him.

He made the course requirements very clear and if you asked for help, he was more than happy to provide it.  As others have said, he made the material much more interesting and was pretty funny.  The tests were tricky but fair.
Great guy and the subject is much more interesting with him. Probably the best professor at kelley
Very clear grading system. Class required a lot of reading. Recorded lectures kept to length specified. Attendance was not mandatory. Group assignment due every week.
Hilarious Professor! Go to his office hour before exam, and you will pass.

Steve's a really cool guy and this is a great course. It's very different from your typical business class and I really appreciate the different perspectives that we get with this course. He's a really cool guy and has a different lecturing style than most other professors.

Professor Kreft is great for online classes in Economics at Indiana University's Kelley Direct program.  He has extremely engaging lectures.  He partner with Professor Ellie   Kreft and they did a great job at team teaching.  I would highly recommend for C530.
Good professor, but can be extremely condescending in one-on-one situations

Great professor. He keeps your interest for the entire lecture (all of which should be attended, as the course moves quickly) and is funny throughout. Tests are tough, but the review sessions help immensely. Random extra credit quizzes during lectures, so don't miss out!

Kreft is hilarious.  Class is always interesting and entertaining.  Tests are 40 question multiple choice (which can make it difficult get into the "A" range), but by no means unreasonable.  Great class with a great teacher.
You can't go wrong with kreft. Easy but interesting class.
Awesome teacher. Highly recommended for G202. Just come to class and pay attention. Read and understand the slides. Definitely read the case studies and case updates.

He's totally cool with his Adidas outfits. But, I think he does not always explain everything clearly. Even though most of the exam questions are from the slides, some of those really need deepest understanding about the whole things. If you're about to take this class, please pay closely attention to the important points from the case studies!

Kreft is one of my favorite teachers. His lectures are great and he is really funny. Tests are hard, and there aren't many points to offset them. Lectures are just powerpoint slides. I would definitely take him for any class.

The topics actually sticks in your mind. Kreft is super funny and actually is a great professor. He not only makes his topic both relevant and engaging, but also does thorough discussions over the concepts and topics. I would recommend you go to all the classes and enjoy it. Best class ever in the KSB!! Would take it again !!

Kreft makes the subject so interesting due to his great sense of humor. One of the funniest classes I have had so far, he doesn't take attendance but it is highly recommended and every class is packed because people enjoy attending it and laughing. Gives ample extra credit. Tests can be a little difficult so make sure to attend a review session
Good professor.

Kreft's lectures are very entertaining. He has an impeccable flow and comedic timing. His tests are difficult.  If you want a good grade, go to every lecture and go to at least one review session for every exam.
not difficult exam but make sure to attend classes and read the cases.

Steve Kreft is probably the funniest professor at IU. You'll love his lectures and his sense of humor. There's basically no work involved in the class, but the tests are hard since there isn't a textbook. I would definitely recommend Kreft though!

Steve is a great teacher. In this class you will have lectures on course knowledge and case studies, and he does an amazing job integrating the cases studies into your current course topics. He is also keeps lectures very entertaining, I never saw a kid fall asleep. Just make sure you attend all lectures, they are great and necessary to get an A.
Everyone else nailed it. Steve is great, and this is not a difficult class if you show up most of the time.
Very knowledgable and engaging professor. Frequently responds during lecture and provide comprehensive and instructive feedback while encouraging further discussion
Kreft is an excellent professor! His class is dynamic and he is hilarious. If you attend class and take notes you will for sure make a good grade. The tests are not that   hard if you read carefully.

I highly recommend this class. Prof Kreft made each day worthwhile – he related lessons to his life experiences, told riveting stories, turned extra credit quizzes into game shows, and actually taught a great deal of content. If you pay attention, do the in-class extra credit quizzes, and use his study guides, the exams are very manageable.

Steve struck me as a good guy and O.K. professor. He gave ample extra credit, made lectures entertaining, and was extremely willing to help outside class. That said, I learned more in the review sessions than I did in class. Really, the only reason to attend class is for the extra credit; try to find somebody in an early class to alert you of EC.

Steve is a decent professor. He keeps things interesting and is pretty funny at times. Because there is no textbook, you really should attend lecture every day because there are points you will be tested on that are not explained well in online resources. He needs to explain the charts in his power points better. They are mostly economic concepts.

Hilarious dude who is always engaging when subject matter isnt always. He gives a TON of EC as long as you show up. Tests are of moderate difficulty but easy if you study (3-4 hours tops) Has office hours EVERY SINGLE day before a test to help kids. Textbook is like $35 too. Fantastic teacher
Really great instructor. No textbook, but you have to purchase online courses, which are cheap. Hilarious lectures, very engaging, one of the best professors I've had so far. Highly recommended.
Very fun and enthusiastic professor that makes the content very interesting! Exams get progressively harder though, and its hard to know what exactly is on them. Go to the office hours before exams.

Kreft is a funny guy who makes lectures entertaining. Unfortunately he doesnt teach what will be on the exam. You have to go to review session to be able to do the questions on the exam. He offers tons of extra credit and the forum posts arent too bad as long as you put some thought into them. Tests dont reflect what youve learned in class
My favorite instructor in IU!!! His class always fun! You will learn a lot of useful things
Love him! Very entertaining class!
My favorite class to attend!
Awesome teacher. He knows the material and explains it well. Definitely go to class! Besides being a great professor, he has a great sense of humor and you'll never be bored.

Classes were interesting, forums were easy. Attendance not mandatory, but you get several EC points if you're present for all the quizzes - enough to bump you up a grade. Tests definitely need to be studied for, don't blow them off because the material seems easy.
Awesome guy, class is very entertaining. The tests aren't too hard if you pay attention and can grasp overall concepts.
Funny guy. Tests are harder than you would expect. Interesting class overall.

Great teacher. Made the class interesting and worth attending. You never know what randomness will happen each class(getting pied, DJ, etc.). I would recommend going to his group office hours the day or two before each test.

Funniest teacher I have had in a while.  Lectures were always full, which is surprising, so you know he does a great job teacher.  He makes the material very interesting and helps you understand it better wit his humor and examples.  I will stop by some of his classes and just listen to him teach and crack jokes. Overall a great guy and a great tea
Hysterical teacher that gives fair tests but the class isn't as easy as people say it is

Awesome teacher..super laid back.  Easy material and he explains it very well.  He holds TONS of voluntary office hours, even two hours before the test on Sundays.  I would go to all of these as they are super helpful.  On top of fairly easy tests, there is extra credit if you go to class.  Interesting stuff..more concept than memorizing.

He is my favorite professor in IUB. He is extremely funny and smart (super smart). Go to the lecture usually and he will give unannounced quizs, and go to his office hour before the exam(important), and you will be fine!

After taking his class I have considered BEPP as my major. He makes the subject unbelievably interesting and fun. I hated econ before this class but he made it very tangible and interesting. Best professor I've had yet.

He's really funny in class and presents a lot of economic principles humorously. Don't be fooled into thinking that this class is just "econ-lite" as I have heard it called. He deliberately words the questions on the test so that you have to read them really carefully. He posts the questions online so download them whenever you can!

he was a funny guy and very caring. the class was not hard either. going to his office hours before exams helps a lot. but what's really weird is that he was so serious in office hours that you can't believe that was the same person who teaches your class. overall i think he is very good and recommend you to take his class.
i honestly thought he was kind of an a**hole. the class was cool but and he was funny during the lecture but during office hours he seemed very a**holish.

I would go back and sit in on one of his classes because he is so funny. It's an interesting class, but it's no slouch. Be warned, the exams get harder as the course goes on. Also, really take your time on the online case discussions because it can hurt your grade. Attendance isn't mandatory, but the xtra credit quizes and jokes are worth going for

Not a difficult class but certainly not a blow off class.  The tests are anything but straightforward but if you study and read the optional readings then you should be able get a B if not an A.  Likes to say "free pizza action" a lot.  Gives extra credit quizzes on random days although you can figure out the days he'll give them after the 2nd test

Really easy class, straight-forward exams, awesome material, easier version of E202, great and relevant cases, a lot of extra credit opportunity, and a lot of enjoyable pranks and jokes along the way. Yay G202 World!

He looks like an entertaining, helpful, & knowledgeable guy at the first time. But be aware! he is the type of person who smiles and stabs you in the back at the same time. Test can be extremely hard for someone. Also it should be a 3 credit course. Office hour is helpful sometime but when he is in a bad mood he can be very disrespectful.

He is a funny, friendly, and helpful teacher. Gives some extra credit. Tests are a little harder than you'd expect, so make sure you take good notes, read the cases, and also read the optional packets. Case discussions are easy as long as you read and get in the forums early.
Funny and entertaining professor. One of the few classes I enjoyed going to! Tests can be tricky, but study the cases and lecture notes and you're on your way.

I love this man. Funniest guy ever, and he's adorable. Tests aren't hard, just be sure to memorize the slides. Best part? He will remind you about all free food action on campus and save you lots of money.
Amazing professor for G202. Hilarious and entertaining. Anyone who can make 170 kids consistently show up voluntarily for what is basically an economics course is a great professor.

Kreft is hysterically funny. If only all teachers had a sense of humor like his...I don't remember a day in class where I wasn't laughing at some point.  While the material may not be interesting for everyone, class lectures are a good time had by all and usually include some techno, laughing, and dance action.
Best lecturer I've had in the B-School thus far. Class format is clear and makes it easy for student to succeed. His lectures are like stand-up comedy and a great way to get extra credit.

He was completely helpful and makes extra office hours available to students. He makes class interesting with personal stories that relate to the material and explains concepts well. I also feel I better understand microeconomics concepts better after this class than before taking it. He is great!

He's a decent prof who gives decent lectures.  He wasn't terribly engaging and didn't make the material that much more interesting, but he is a very competent professor who grades in a timely manner.  He is sometimes a little harsh with the partial credit deductions.

Class is pretty easy. Get him as your teacher for the class. Study the PowerPoints and memorize everything on there and you should be good for the tests. Go to class for the extra credit pop quizzes and also because he is a really funny teacher. Gives a lot of great examples that will come in handy.
this is good teacher

Great teacher, possibly my favorite thus far. He has great examples that are hilarious and helpful. The whole class sometimes just seems like watching a standup routine. Tests are extremely easy, homework isn't bad if you have a smart group (you choose your group), and there's a good amount of extra credit. Best Kelley Pre-Req class.
Fun class. Great Professor. Attend the class.

G202 is structured in a away that will allow you to learn the system after the first unit and dominate the class.  Kreft seems like a great guy in class but was very abrasive in his office hours if you didn't show that you spend some serious time studying the material.Kreft had some interesting, funny examples but this class should not be required.

Great teacher.  Class is very easy if you actually go.  He makes it interesting with some redic examples that you will remember come test time  The book is only used for case studies, if you borrow some one elses to read them you'd be fine

This class isnt really worth your time, even though you have to take it for Kelley. Kreft makes some good jokes, but hes a boring lecturer, grades ridiculously on HW, and is unprofessional and seems annoyed to help you on HW in office hours. My least favorite class this semester.
Fun class. Fun examples.
fun guy.   go to class and everything is easy.   he is tricky on tests though.  he will also give u the answers to homework in office hours
Fun class.  Highly recommended.  Attend all his lectures for pop up extra credit quizes.  Also understand his lecture slides to get good grades.
Most material is review, makes it pretty interesting though.  Grades somewhat tough on homework, but the tests aren't bad, and as long as you understand the concepts you will be fine.
The materials are interesting and logical. He's nice and explains well. The exams are multiple choices, so if you miss a few, you're screwed. His exams can be somewhat confusing.
teh man
No Comments
Least pretentious prof at Kelley
No Comments
I liked this class better when it was called E201, E202, and L201.  Not much new material, he's a joker but seems angry he has to teach such a huge group.  Not helpful outside of class

If you go to class and pay attention, you should have no problem in his class. Everything comes straight from his lectures and a few short readings which he goes over most of anyway. Easy bonus points from going to class and taking all of the quizzes.

Kreft is hard...his tests are very dificult and tricky. He is also a VERY hard grader on his homework and assignments, and his final is cumulative. There is another asian professor that teaches G202...my friends had him, and he's a lot easier and his final isn't cumulative...so take the other guy!
Class is easy tests are hard.
Awesome guy! Very smart and funny, manages to keep your attention. Even though the material is so boring, he makes it fun.
Good guy. Go into his office hours and he'll tell you what you need to know.
does the best he can to take a completely boring class and make it more fun and interesting. lots of bonus points and easy tests!
Prof. Kreft is extremely clear in his explanations, great class!!

The course material wasn't bad but the exams were too in depth in my opinion. There was information on the exam that covered only half of a slide in her lectures. The slides were very disorganized and I think that was the biggest problem. She's very knowledgeable about the neuroscience and is accessible outside of class.

All the lectures were Canva videos which was convenient but there were 2/week and each one was like 2 hours long. Her lectures had no sense of organization. She just talks about random info and doesn't clarify what we're expected to know for exams. Grading was chill but it was frustrating and boring trying to follow along with the lectures.

You can tell from her lectures how knowledgeable and qualified she is, and shes also very kind and caring. Im a senior this year, and Dr. Wisner was of my top 5 favorite profs Ive had at IU. Highly recommend!
she was great! would take again
wisner is an absolute bro 10/10 would recommend this class!
Kind, caring, supportive of her students, and incredibly knowledgeable. Easily one of my top 5 favorite profs at IU.
Dr. Wisner loves nothing more than the human brain! She seriously knows so much about it and is the best educator. Would take her class in any lifetime!!!!

wisner is very knowledgeable and you can tell clinical neuroscience is 100% her area. she worked as a clinical psychologist and has years of experience in this field. she lets you drop an exam which is key. the tests are very straightforward. she is very friendly and available during office hours. overall solid class
Absolutely fantastic professor, truly cares about her students, and loves her profession as much as she loves the human brain.
this class honestly isn't that bad. you get a dropped exam and she teaches everything clearly in class that you need to know. doesn't take much time to learn the material

Krista Wisner is so inspirational!!! She is always peppy, enthusiastic, and excited to teach. I've never met a professor that is more prepared and loves to do her job as much as Wisner. She is a MUST for neuro classes, and the whole class absolutely loved her. Trust me, you won't regret it!

This was my first advanced neuro class, and i was nervous about how it'd go or if i'd be able to handle it. Despite my fears, Dr. Wisner was a fantastic teacher. She took material that is usually extremely hard and made it super interesting. She also does a mid semester eval where she grants one of everyone's wish, one of which was to drop an exam!

this class was a cake walk. with a great teacher and some mediocre study habits i was able to score an A without a problem. if you go to class, you don't even have to pay attention at all and you can do well. wisner was a blessing in class bc she knew the answer to every question people asked, which is a rare trait i've found with teachers at iu

wisner is an angel, and by far the best teacher in the neuroscience department. i went to her office hours really often, and she was soooo helpful. we ended up getting dinner a few times because she is just such a sweetheart. she also offered to help with future career stuff because she cares so much about her students. i'm gonna ask her for a rec

Krista never presents incorrect information ever in class. She knows this material so well, and even better, she knows how to teach it really well. Her teaching style is so good that every student in the class loved her. Knew it so well she didn't even rely on other teachers to come in and teach the class for her

Professor wisner really cares about her students, and she gave lots of extra credit and explained the material super well. Her lectures were very interesting because she made the slides very concise, simple and minimalistic. She's super organized and gets her grades back very quickly after assignments are due. Loved her!

I absolutely loved Krista Wisner. She has hands down been the best professor I've had at my time here at IU. She knows the material really well, writes tests that represent exactly what we've learned, and is always on time to class! She posts the slides far ahead of class so you always have time to print, and her slides are clear/very easy to read.

Professor Wisner is new so this could contribute to her poor teaching skills. She somehow manages to make material that is interesting, very boring when she teaches it. She reads directly off the slides, hardly looking at the class. Sometimes she stands with her back to the class and stares at the slides while she teaches. Not a great lecturer.

One of the worst teachers I have ever had in a skill sense. Completely disengaging. Extremely drawn out lectures based on very simple information. If you're the type of student who just wants a B without having to go to class, this would be for you. If you actually want to learn and be engaged in class, stay as far away as possible.
Dr. Krutilla is a very kind professor, but his classes are very lecture heavy and can feel monotonous if you aren't very interested in the subject. He is very thoughtful in answering questions.
Aggravating.

He is a poor lecturer. By the end of the semester few students were going to his class because it isn't worth the time. I much rather would have taken Ross for BCA. He doesn't explain much, throws around terms without explaining them and goes off onto unhelpful tangents. He doesn't listen to students well and will often misunderstand questions.

He's very kind and knowledgeable in his expertise, but his lecture style really doesn't foster efficient learning in my opinion. The classes are lecture heavy, with him talking the whole time, many times in great length about a single topic. Personally, it was difficult to take a lot from his lectures, especially with the complexity of the topics.
His assignments assignments may be slightly confusing, but he is a good teacher and is willing to discuss anything with students. Also very considerate and does not tack students for attendance.
Sweet guy, but speaks in a monotone voice. Very hard to focus on what he's saying, but if you have a background in micro and macro it's a piece of cake.

He is one of the best professors I have had at SPEA. He genuinely cares about student's learning and is very approachable inside and outside of the class. Sometimes funny. Accommodating of student's needs based on circumstances. Sometimes his lectures are vague and do not follow syllabus strictly so it is important to keep deadlines in mind.

Kurt Seiffert is not a bad guy at all, he obviously cares a lot about the course material. The thing is, his class is so unorganized and all over the place it is impossible to gain anything from it. I highly recommend finding a different course.
The professor thinks we can do 3 hours of work in 30 mins, but doesn't realize that students have other classes to take and not just his. Please don't put yourself in this position. TAs are bad.
dont take this class, all you will do is stress

Take up so much time. He would open an exercise during lecture & have it due 15 min after lecture ends & everyone just rushes. In the middle of sem, he changed the activities to be every single lecture & they take so long in group, coz everyone has to contribute & take time out to meet. TAs are no better. PLEASE CHANGE YOUR SPECIALIZATION.

So I am currently in his C and Linux class. Look Kurt is a great guy, cares about his students, and does help but the way he teaches doesn't help. He bounces around a lot, doesnt break down code and instead has complex files pre-written, then leaves you with 15 minutes to write a tough program which he ends up extending. Learn outside of class.

Class was extremely easy but I feel like I learned nothing because it was very encouraged to just copy paste whatever AI code was in the assignment descriptions. Work load is a little high and class requirements change frequently. Extremely easy to get high grade but grading was extremely behind.

Knowledgeable, but not great at organizing a class. The class outlined in the syllabus at the start of the semester will likely not be the class you're taking by the end, and the structure is very unpredictable. I found the copy/paste in-class exercises to be a unhelpful way to learn and the professor's reliance on AI was a detriment to the course.

Changed coursework mid-semester from 1 assignment/week to 4+. Gives buggy code that teaches nothing and you end up having to fixing everything. TAs are useless. You're stuck with the same team all semester, so hope they're good. He uses AI to write all his assignments. Have to do in class exercises every class. Online midterm/final is good ig.

Not particularly organized and requirements for assignments were often unclear. We had a final project introduced at the start of the semester that we never did because he didn't get it set up. I was fine because I had some familiarity with  C beforehand, but I would advise against taking it if you're not already comfortable with Java or C.

Very unorganized and kind of all over the place. He extends deadlines almost every assignment. He cancels class a lot. The assignments aren't bad, but the autograder is awful. I wasted countless hours trying to beat the stupid autograders. The good news is that he allows unlimited autograder attempts. If you do the homework, you should get an A.

Kurt is a terrible professor. For reference, his class went from almost 50 people at the beginning of the semester, to 7 at the end. He is passive-aggressive when you try to ask questions within his lecture, and he has no idea how to properly create assignments. He would have to go back and redo them because they were made incorrectly. Avoid.

Professor Seiffert is a very knowledgeable and kind man however, he spends all of class time lecturing which can become exhausting over time. There are assignments due almost every week however, he is very lenient with giving extensions as long as you talk to him about it.
Very good proffesor, gives alot of homework that you almost have to do on your own. However, he is very merciful in that if you tell him you cant finish he will extend the deadline. Very good dude.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The prof's habit of changing assignment requirements is a big time drain. It's frustrating to invest time in one direction, only to have it wasted due to his changing demands. Especially when it takes time away from other classes. Even deadline extensions don't compensate for the stress and lost time. Don't even get me started on the autograder.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think the other reviews for Kurt are a little harsh. The autograder is annoying to use but he is readily available during office hours and respond to emails within a day. Definely take more programming classes then the prerequisites this helps a lot!
Doesn't know how to teach

This is the sloppiest class I have ever taken. Multiple errors in the set up of the class. Put the wrong github link so we had to fix that. Many of the TAs who were suppose to be collaborators were not on the set up instructions. Is using the autograder but barely knows how to use it so there are many errors. Nice guy, horrible professor. Retire...
Professor Kunzman is a great teacher. As long as you read before class and participate in his discussions you will get an A. Would def take his class again.

I started to struggle in this class about midway through the semester and almost lost hope for my grade, but after going to him with my issues and asking how I could improve, he gave me some very useful tips and was very understanding. Great teacher and very helpful if you fall behind as long as you take initiative to talk to him about it.
I had prof Kunzman for H101. He enhanced the in-class conversations and helped everyone learn deeply and think critically. Super nice guy. Would love to take one of his classes again.

Super nice guy; made discussions genuinely engaging and allowed you to express your opinions with full honesty. Workload wasn't too bad, one reading per week and as long as you went to class and raised your hand now and then you were basically guaranteed an A.

Provided insight I needed for me to decide if this was the route I wanted to take in my education. Extremely motivating to think critically about values of the education system. Did wonderful job at letting students share their insight. Structure of class worked wonderfully when paired with content. Hard class, but worth it. So kind and caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: This class with Kunzman was my favorite class I have ever taken throughout 13 years of schooling, and I credit it to Professor Kunzman. He is the most caring and thoughtful teacher I have ever had. He cares about his students and challenges me to be a better student and person. He is always willing to help, and I could not recommend him more.

Rob is a really great professor. I had him for my first honors class at IU and was intimidated to say the least, but definitely felt very comfortable within the first week or two. He listens to what you have to say and makes you feel like what you said is worth something. Gives insight and tips for your writing - big paper, but interesting topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a great and knowledgable professor who definitely fosters discussion in the class. It was one of my most challenging classes, but also one of my favorite classes that I had all semester. There is a 20 page final paper with very little guidance, but that also gives you the chance to write about almost anything

Rob is a great instructor and understands what students need to grasp from the class. He sets high standards. BEWARE: i took hon-h 212 which is Ideas and Experiences II. i love the class as it has been very informative and engaging, and the other students are great to be around. There is a ton of reading and a 5000 word essay at the end. js.

Rob is wonderful and amazing. He is extremely helpful both in and out of class, and always makes time for his students. Furthermore, he offers real-world experience and is one of the most knowledgable professors in the Education program at IU. Highly recommend!!

Dr. D is a phenomenal person who you can tell is so knowledgeable on the topics and cares about her students. This class was TOUGH, but neuro is always going to be. I think she made the best of a really really hard class.

Overall, she's a great professor. However, if you are not a good test taker (like me), DO NOT take her class. Exams are worth 60% of your grade, she does take attendance through top hat and there are 2 video homeworks.
straightforward class. take home exams. lovely professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I greatly enjoyed this class and it was very well organized for a completely online course. Her lectures were straightforward and exams fairly straightforward to if you did the study guide. I learned a lot from her in this class and she was very open and kind. I highly recommend her for 346.

Dr. D was amazing for P101. Her lectures were very thorough but straightforward, and guided notes were always provided. She makes it very easy to study for the exams because she publishes study questions at the beginning of the unit that are almost identical to test questions. Lectures can be boring. Drops your lowest exam score out of 4 exams!

AWESOME!! Only had 4 exams during p101, all are fairly easily so long as you spend a few hours studying! Lectures are immersive and interesting. She is so kind when going to office hours and talking after class. Amazing she teaches 200+ students and still takes time to help each one. ALSO, TA's would hold help sessions before exams, very helpful!!!
Super nice! Made for an easy transition to college. IFS is very intensive but Dr. DeBoeuf made it enjoyable!
I had Dr. D for IFS and she was great! Not always the most clear, but she is always willing to help if you need anything. Super easy credit and overall an interesting course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. D made neuroscience very accessible to anybody regardless of how interested you are in it. There are very few grades in the class but she provides great materials for studying and holds a lot of review sessions. Her lectures can be rough sometimes but she even provides guided notes which made the information digestible. Take neuro with her!

Dr. D is great! I really didn't want to take neuroscience (I'm a psychology major), but Dr. D is super chill. Her tests are really straightforward and if you complete the study guides she provides you'll be prepared.

Dr. D is one of my fav professors in the psych department. I had to retake neuro after taking it with Sengelaub and she's such a breath of fresh air! She gives very clear lecture notes that you can download. She has also been so kind during special circumstances. Don't feel scared to ask her for help. I would 110% recommend her for neuro

Professor DeBouef's lectures can become very boring if you have no interest in neuroscience. Some things weren't in the lectures that were on the exam and some of the quiz questions are worded weirdly. That being said, I don't think this is the worst class that you could take if you need neuroscience. The exams are all open note/open book.
Great professor, her class was my last choice ,but I still enjoyed it. She makes the lectures easy to understand and has great slides to look back on for notes. Very nice and caring person.

She makes the material very easy to understand, and her tests are very reasonable. I'm not a psych major, so I was a little nervous to take this class. However, her exams and quizzes contain really low-reaching questions that cover the basics. She said we needed to read the book, but her lectures covered everything so well that I didn't need to.

I would recommend her for neuroscience, I had a pretty easy time with the course considering how heavy of a topic it is. She drops the lowest test and quiz. Also there wasnt any homework- just watching lectures(take notes) quizzes and tests

Dr. D was the best, she made IFS awesome! The class was super interesting. She made the content easy to understand yet engaging. Program was hybrid. For the online portion, she gave us lots of breaks in between zooms so we weren't sedentary, staring at a screen for hours. She is super kind and caring, she really made the adjustment to IU easier.

This professor was extremely sweet, smart, and relatable! She made the course material easy to understand and quite interesting to learn about. We had student notes provided every week along with lecture videos and a Friday quiz over the chapter. The exams were not hard at all if you took notes or even just payed attention! 10/10

This professor was by far one of the best professors I've ever had at IU. She was so engaging and through asynchronous, she gave us time to complete work at our own pace which I really liked. I loved her energy during each video, she is a clear grader, and even though I'm not a neuroscience major I really enjoyed her class

I took Psych 101 with Kristi, so it was very lecture heavy. However, she always managed to make the lectures engaging and interesting. There are four tests and easy reading assignments. The textbook is not really needed in order to complete the homework assignments. She does take attendance but she does not tell you what days she will be taking it.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class was great. Only one homework assignment throughout the entire semester. Tests use scratchers so you can get partial credit for multiple choice answers. She gives you a study guide for each chapter which helps a lot for the test. Lectures are interesting and she is always available to help answer any questions.
Very kind person. Lectures can get kind of boring but are mostly interesting. Overall the class is pretty easy
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mrs. DeBoeuf is one of the kindest professors I have ever had. Her course is straightforward when it comes to material you need to know for exams. Exams are 75% of your grade, and attendance and review worksheets are 25%. She gives you study guides for the exams, which are really helpful too. I fully recommend taking neuroscience with this teacher!
Learning goals weren't always clearly communicated. If you got lost in class during one of his long winded lectures, you were doomed. Class topic is interesting but hard to grasp.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I have never experienced a class like Kurt's before. He will have you questioning your entire life after just one class—but it's great! He is a stickler for formatting and works cited, but if you have questions, just ask him, and he will clarify. Just read the syllabus, come to class, and you'll have a great time!

Kurt is a very tough professor who takes some getting used to, but underneath a tough facade he is a very funny guy who cares a lot about helping his students succeed. The criteria for each speech is difficult to understand and only gets harder with each speech throughout the course, but he provides very helpful feedback on how to improve.

This class is super interesting and I feel like I learned a lot about the rhetoric of science. Kurt is a great professor; he is intelligent, well-spoken, and caring. However, I really did not enjoy writing the essays for this class (which make up basically your entire grade), as doing so caused me a lot of stress.

Kurt is a really intelligent guy, which can be intimidating. His teaching style is not for everyone, so if you don't like feeling like you are wrong I would not take this class. You have to work for a good grade in this class. It is more a writing class than speaking. As long as you follow the structure he wants EXACTLY you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Do not take this class unless you are prepared to be extremely challenged. Professor Kurt was a nice guy if you needed to reach him outside of class or had extenuating circumstances. However the speech structures and research for the class only gets harder with each speech. There is no busy work to save your grade, he also hates grade grubbers.

Zemlicka is incredibly smart and caring. He wants to help you. Very good at rhetoric and arguing, and sometimes is intimidating because of that. Still, I am glad I took this speech class as opposed to the general one. Made me think of arguments in a different way. He takes a little getting used to, but he wants everyone to succeed. Awesome guy.

Not for the faint of heart. Lots of philosophical ideas and you'll leave class feeling like you know less than you did. The teacher cares a lot about the class and is very understanding/ supportive. You are only graded on five papers, class lead discussion, final project, & participation. So there is no busywork which I honestly really liked.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Kurt Zemlicka is an absolutely amazing professor whose lectures have often left me dumbfounded. His ability to engage a class is unmatched. Give him 75 minutes of your life and he will leave you questioning reality. He doesn't do busywork, any assignment is graded based on demonstrating your knowledge of skills and ideas discussed in class.

The professor is a great instructor and that is reflected in the amount I was able to take away from his class. The direction of the class was clear from the beginning and he was able to make abstract concepts understandable. Grades very fairly!

I took this class for an A&H credit, and I hated every second of it. There are hardly any assignments, so you can't do bad on one, unless you want a bad grade. Very abstract class, but the second eight weeks, it did get a little better. I barely understood any of the readings and I hated participating in class. Nice guy, but I hated this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy class but have a lot of group work which is really annoying. groups are random so hopefully you have a good group.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Her class is much more work than the other T 375, but it is still not hard. Does not really matter the professor that you get.

One of my favorite professors. I took individual and societal wellbeing & I definitely think you got out of it what you put in. It's a very introspective course & I had a lot going on at the time I took it. This class helped me tremendously & honestly changed my outlook on life in so many ways. Her lessons continue to guide me in my career journey.

She's a super kind and caring person, but to be frank, she kind of annoyed me. I took the class "Individual and Societal Wellbeing," and we spent very little time on the 'societal' aspect. She loves to get personal.

Prof K is one of my favorite professors I've ever had. She's super sweet and cares about her students. She also always had great stories. The assignments did not take super long and they were mostly just introspective things. The class was not hard, but the content was stuff that I still think about. She's literally the best.

T375 was a chill class but the amount of work given was absolutely insane, especially for a one credit course. Overall, she is a nice professor and very caring, but I wish there weren't as many useless homeworks. It was a pain to do with icore.

HON H237
Dawn was such a good professor and even better person. She really took time out of the class to understand us and make us feel like we were appreciated and understood. The class material really transformed me as a person and surpassed my expectations. I would definitely take this class again.
Hype We stan Dawn
Most useless class I've taken

Taking compass II with Prof. Kutza was a very pleasant experience. Although compass is usually full of busy work, taking the class with her made it more tolerable. She is very enthusiastic and the best option for T275.

Professor Kutza was one of the most caring professors I have ever had. She is very enthusiastic about the material, and she cares about our success as individuals and professionals. Shes the type to walk around the class to ask how your weekend went. She also takes her past students feedback and bases her material on it. I definitely recommend!

Dawn was so caring and understanding when I had a schedule conflict. She showed me compassion and was accommodating. I hope you choose to take her course because she genuinely cares about each individual student. :)

Professor Kutza made my first semester at IU great. She was always accessible outside of class whenever needed and I would recommend her to everyone. In Kelley, she is one of the best professors I have ever met. She is also lovable and tries to make 8ams so much better. Thank you Professor to all that you do!

Sweetest lady EVER! If you have the chance to take her class, do it! I would go in early just to talk to her, and I even began to see her as a mentor. She will go out of her way to make herself available to you, and even if you aren't the best at public speaking (like me) she will help you improve by the end of the course!
Professor Kutza was one of the best professors I have ever had. She was caring and her requirements were specific and clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Kutza is a very caring, sweet woman and although the class itself is pretty dry, she does her best to be upbeat and help students do the best that they can both in class and outside.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The most kind person I've ever met. She's a tough grader but very fair. She wants you to succeed. Ask for help if you need it, she's very accommodating with your issues if you talk to her during office hours.

Professor Kutza makes this class harder than it should be. Most of the work is easy busy work, however, she grades the assignments very tough. She is a nice and caring woman, but I would recommend taking this class with someone else
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof Kutza is so kind and caring. She was very patient with our class. However, she is such a harsh grader. The amount of work she assigned was ridiculous when compared to other T275 classes - for example, while other professors assigned one 500-word final question, she assigned SEVEN. Her assignments take hours, and the highest you'll get is a B.
Dawn is a quirky professor who genuinely cares about her class. That being said, she assigns writing intensive homework and cares about the fluff. Be prepared for busy work and a nice woman.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Great professor. Extremely helpful and gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Her class material was super easy and straight forward, however when it came to grading she was extremely hard.  I never quite knew what she was looking for or what she wanted for each assignment.  She doesn't describe assignments before you do them so a lot of times you're left confused of what you're supposed to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dawn knows that compass is a blow off class. She rarely kept us for the entire class time. As long as you show up, you will get an A.
Pros: Very nice professor, easy grader Con: She assumed I was an international asian student but I am Asian Amerian.

She gave great feedback on the assignments and was definitely able to utilize her past experiences to give students real world examples and advice. I would recommend taking her because she makes the class relevant for those entering into the recruitment process. Not too much busy work and so much better than t175.

Don't try to go against anything she says, she will be ANGRY with you. Put the phones away and she will be happy. Doesn't try to understand her students just expects them to work her way. Also don't ask her to try to understand you, she will just get rude about it.

Compass is not a good class, but Kutza is a pretty good professor. Extremely enthusiastic and knows about professionalism, interviews, etc. She isn't always clear about due dates or expectations for assignments. Kutza loves her syllabus, but I had trouble figuring it out. You could do worse.
Dawn is the nicest Kelley professor I've ever had! She has great energy and she is always willing to help, so go to office hours! I would take another class with her again!

I took MATH221, honestly he is the best professor for it, i had another lady who barely spoke any english and spoke 1000 mph so i had to switch. kutluay is a cool professor and he explains to make everything a little better. if you've never taken calc before the program sucks, honestly the way calc is at UD is unreal but it's not his fault.
The amount of homework is crazy! But he really tries his best to teach and make students understand. Will consider taking his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would've given him a worse rating but his prompt emails and his words of encouragement made me reevaluate him again. He is a nice professor and helps students with the homework and quizzes each day during and after class. One thing is that his lectures are a little difficult to understand because he explains in a round about way.
online class made learning this course impossible

He is a boss. At first I thought I wouldn't be able to understand what he is saying for the rest of the school year but I got used to it and he is awesome. He is very funny professor and nice to everyone. Very comfortable to talk to and ask questions.
Very passionate and helpful.  Quizes are easy as long as you attend class.
Nice guy and has good intentions, but is extremely difficult to understand.

Deniz was an excellent instructor- best math teacher I've ever had. He breaks information down very well. Moderate amount of homework due every other day. Material in the homework/tests is harder than what is taught, but Deniz has frequent office hours, a homework help forum, and is very eager to help. I loved going to his class, even at 8am.

Deniz is an amazing mathematics professor.  I have always struggled with math but he made the material easier to understand and was always available to help whenever I needed it.  Don't make the mistake of taking this class with another professor!

It's honestly so funny how people never want to come to class or complain when attendance is mandatory, and even want classes to be canceled, but all of a sudden it's an issue when she cancels class "a lot". If you don't attend or put in the effort, that's on you. Grow up and stop complaining about nothing just because you didn't get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I am taking her for AAST-A 300, and I don't understand the bad ratings. She's one of the sweetest Professors I've had. A lot of the negative reviews seem to come from students who never come to class but still expect an easy A. It's not hard to just read and write you're in college, just get off of your phone, get off TikTok and pay attention bro

We had class MAYBE once a week, she cancels all the time. When there is class, all you do is group work that has zero benefit. Half the time you are sitting there in silence because she needs to get ready. Does not teach and then expects you to write 2-8 page papers about things that she doesn't teach.

She was very caring, and was passionate about the subject of Asian Studies. She cancels class alot due to chronic illnesses, but tries her best to be available. There's readings before each class that you should do, as we discuss in class each time. The book you read is very interesting and is an easy read too.
She is mean

I took Prof. Kwong for AAST-A 201. She is a pretty easy grader, but the class has an absurd amount of reading, and way too many writing assignments. She also doesn't really teach any material and expects us to lead most of the discussion without adding in any of her own input. Easy A class but don't expect to learn much from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: *my review is of AAST A201* Take this class if you enjoy reading 30+ pages before each lecture and writing so many papers. The course material doesn't match the description of the course, at all. In years past, attendance wasn't required but it is now... Great class if you love constant reading and writing and are looking for a writing course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: There were lots of lectures involved. It's a-okay class, just very awkward.

Very nice teacher, she makes it really easy to understand the material and while there is alot of papers assigned she will give you plenty of time to complete them. I enjoyed the ice breaker questions and interacting with the other classmates
Professor Kwong was a okay teacher. She was a little disorganized, but she is willing to help if you need it. She did have group actives. Super easy class. Thank you Professor!

In all honesty she doesn't seem that committed to the class. Her grading system is horrendous, with it being an 8-week class she has only graded one of 4 papers. There not even papers really, just drafts worth 200 points. Out of all 18 students only 4 show up in her zoom calls. Instead of grading she has us watch music videos to kill time. Smh.

Very easy class, but the way Prof. K teaches is disengaged. She's not a tough grader, she's kind, and there isn't a whole lot of work to do. You don't even have to attend lectures, it's all recorded and posted. But they're not very interesting. It's not her fault the subject mater is boring, but she seems as bored as her students.

Professor Kwong is an excellent instructor. Intro to Asian American Studies is an extremely easy course, yet engaging and interesting. Unfortunately, she had to cancel class a number of times, but she always did her best to ensure that things stayed on course. She deeply cares about each of her students and wants to see them succeed.

Go to class, do the discussions, and participate in class and you'll be fine. It's an extremely easy class since you watch tv shows and movies a lot and write short discussions about it. There is a final paper but no final test.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Very unclear on expectations. Slow grader, do not get major grades (midterm, papers) back until after the semester is already over. Very hard to know where you stand in the class grade-wise. Changes major assignments mid-year (cancelled final 3 weeks before end of semester.) Takes 101 class too seriously. Seems nice, but needs to organize better.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Prof Kwong was a great 131 professor. She was always there to help and had flexible office hours. It is not easy to get an A in the class, however, she grades based on improvement. Super sweet and very passionate about English. Just like any english class, there are many papers. I strongly recommend her as a professor!!!

Professor Kwong is an excellent professor. She goes above and beyond to inspire and aid her students. She always provides feedback to students and is very understanding with absences and tardies. She rarely cancels class, but she brings in cupcakes on the last lecture day. I would 100% recommend this wonderful professor. BEWARE many papers.
I really liked this instructor. He did a great job.
he does not know how to teach a class . hes all over the place majority of the time and he be confusing his own self .

I found that he went too slow in describing the problems and how to do them that I could not understand what to do. He says "um" a lot which also slows his explanations as well. Going to class didnt seem necessary for me. I worked a lot out of class to do somewhat decent on my 3rd exam because I bombed the 2nd but did well on the first.

Although it is Luke's first time teaching he isn't that bad. He usually writes down everything with you so the class doesn't feel rushed at all and he will solve any questions that you need. He does need some time to master his teaching style but overall he is a decent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This was Luke's first time teaching D116 and you can tell. Luckily he follows the textbook pretty religiously so anything you don't understand you can find in the text. Lots of WebWorK, but since the class is slowed down compared to normal finite, its manageable. Hopefully his teaching methods will get better...

Her class is a class all you have to do is show up, fill out a paper, and leave. If you don't get an A in this, idk how you got into college. You can easily talk her into canceling class. However, at the second part of our class she brought in guest lecturers who were very boring- hated it. She lets class out early generally too.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The class was really great. It was stress relieving and definitely didn't cause any more stress. She always let us out early and even let us decide what we wanted to be graded on. If you need a GPA boost, take this with her.
She is an easy professor, and easy to get along with.  She is nice to her students, and I enjoyed having her.

This professor does not deserve to be faculty. He is incredibly predatory towards his students and very creepy. He made me and other students very uncomfortable time and time again. I have zero respect for Justin Kumar and he needs to be fired immediately. IU do something about this please.

Terrible attitude, Kumar's lectures are unengaging, trite. When I raised questions, he defensively suggested I drop the class if I didn't like his approach. Called 911 for a medical emergency. He refused to let me retake the exam.His lack of empathy, class is frustrating and unproductive. And don't say I'm bombing him, cuz I got a good grade.

Dr. Kumar is an encouraging professor and is very considerate. His goal for us as students is to absorb any part of anything we have learned in class.
