reviews.comment: Laura Brown is the best orgo professor anyone could ever have. She is so intelligent and teaches the material in a way that makes the concepts easier. Her exams are hard but you know what to expect because she gives a lot of practice.

LCB is a queen. She's not in your face like Reck, but her lectures make sense and she's sweet and funny in her own way. Orgo II is also the hardest class I've ever taken hands down. You want an A, you're gonna have to eat, sleep, and breathe orgo. Tests are hard, but grading is fair. DONT SKIP CLASS OR DIS! Tough class, but overall worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Caring

reviews.comment: LCB is the best of the best. She cares about you far above your success in her class. That's not to say that this class is easy--it's not. Organic III is HARD, the exams are hard. You'll learn so much in this class. But, she gives you plenty of resources to be successful and she's more than willing to help you. She wants to see students succeed.

Not a super exciting lecturer, but makes sense and gives good examples. Her exams are brutal, but that's to be expected in orgo 3. The textbook we used (clayden) didn't have anywhere near enough practice problems (only like 10 per chapter), and she didn't supplement (unless you count the homework). Overall, nothing major to complain about.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Absolutely wonderful lecturer, with great explanations.

LCB is the best! She was so good that I'm taking another class with her so that I can learn from her again. She makes grading criteria very clear, and gives you all the resources and practice you need to succeed. It won't be easy, but it'll be worth it. She's thorough, thoughtful, and a real gem.

Dr. Brown is one of the best professors I have had. Her lectures are very clear and easy to understand, and she provided us with TONS of practice problems, quizzes, and exams to master the content. The exams were difficult, but if you study and practice you will do fine. This class is a lot of work, so make sure to keep up!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Laura Brown is a great teacher, she is very intelligent and very caring too. She honestly wants her students to throughly understand the material. She can explain everything in simple terms. The class is easy if you simply review every day for 30-40 minutes and study every weekend.  Its not hard to develop a professor crush on LCB, she's awesome!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Extremely nice lady, pretty tough class. Go to office hours (not hers, an AI's) for ALL (yes, all) of the short reports and preferably for the formal reports. Short reports can save your grade. Final was open note but very challenging - required in-depth organic knowledge and based off of lecture instead of lab.

Her lectures were interesting and focused. She gave us packets to go along with the lectures and constantly asked for feedback regarding clarity. She also asked us to answer practice problems while going through them in class, making the class a place to "fail without consequences."

She's a lot of fun. She really knows her stuff, and respects students who try to do the same. She only graded one assignment; she left good feedback and gave to opportunity to get extra credit with a rewrite. The final was a bit harder than expected and partially relies on S343 material. The labs she chose were really cool and used a lot of methods

You NEED to do the practice problems in the book to get an A. Exams are very hard but are not worth much. As far as her teaching goes, make sure you pay attention during the first few minutes of class, if you don't you'll be lost the entire lecture because she moves too fast. She is amazing at one on one help so go to office hours if you're lost.

Very hard professor, but nice and fair at the same time. She is very, very smart so that is quite intimidating and sometimes makes her lectures hard to understand, but overall she cares about learning the material and if you take good notes you can do well in her class.
LCB is the best. Super intimidating though…. go to class and take good notes, and you'll be fine with whatever course
LCB is the best. She can be really intimidating, and she's tough and unapologetic, but she is always willing to help. I think she's very clear during lecture and is incredibly well-spoken.

This course is difficult, and while she does a good job of providing lots of practice problems and office hours, the exams are still rather difficult. Things are usually clear when lectured, but not always. Although I think she is better than a lot of professors, this is still a class where you have to put 150% effort for an A
Terrible lecturer, not clear at all. Doesn't explain anything clearly.
Very nice, but a bit disorganized with the notes. Also a little confusing whenever she disagrees with the textbook. Beware of the final exam - average was a 54%...

She's a good instructor. Her tests are extremely difficult. Thought there would be more partial credit (some questions are all or nothing on exams). This class is tough. Always attend lecture, go to office hours, do your homework. I'm barely passing and I put a ton of effort into this class. Beware of her synthesis questions. Know your mechanisms.

Hardest final I've ever taken... worth 40% of your grade, and the practice final wasn't even close to representing what was required on the actual exam. Isn't very clear on class, contradicts book at many times, and forces useless "only carbon source" synthesis problems on exams that take forever to try to solve. Avoid taking if possible.

Laura Brown is a terrible chemistry professor. Her notes are useless and don't contain the information necessary. She contradicts the book consistently. She always runs class late. We have no idea what is expected of us on tests, and things on tests are not covered in the class or books. She is disorganized and does not answer questions. DONT TAKE.
I did not like her at all. Her exams were very hard. She was a horrible lecturer and wasted a lot of class time. She is a terrible professor.
The final is 40 % of your grade ... Be Aware

I had to retake Orgo 2, and I had her the second time which was such a blessing! She is a fair grader and test-maker. But if you have to miss class, make sure to use Study Edge for the chapter review videos so that you can catch up on the material and know what is going on in the next class.

Dr. Brown is a good teacher.  The class was obviously difficult and fast-paced, but she was very helpful outside of class. Work hard, practice often,and actually understand the chemistry rather than solely memorizing.

TAKE ORGO II WITH HER. It's worth breaking your back to make the schedule work, she is BY FAR the best orgo II teacher IU has to offer, writes very fair tests and quizzes, not at all impossible to get an A, only her 2nd semester and is one of the best orgo teachers at IU; is up there with Reck.  TAKE HER CLASS!!!!!!!!!

Dr. Brown was a good professor, she always made sure she was available for help and going to her office hours definitely helped me a lot. In such a difficult course, it was hard to stay up to the course material but she taught everything clearly and in a way that was easier to understand.
great teacher! shes from harvard so you know shes good. this was her first semester teaching at this school and you could tell she was nervous sometimes, but she did a great job overall!!!
Dr. Brown is a good teacher. Her notes are clear and she teaches at a good pace. Furthermore, she tends to write reasonable quizzes and tests. I would recommend her.

was a decent course and professor, but the work can be grating and does not feel substantial for most of the semester. i also did not enjoy her acceptance/use of ai, yet ageist slights about tech. also made off comments about judging student's intelligence "based on how they speak" which was reminiscent of classism/racism. very nice person beyond.

The class is very boring and will feel like a waste for most of the time. We spent one class singing row row row your boat for like 30 minutes. I genuinely tried to stay interested a put effort into it but it is just too mind-numbing.

You are only allowed one absence without a grade penalty, it's on a flip schedule so all work is done outside of class before the next lecture, professor was high energy, gave commentary on submissions, enjoyed this class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: You can only miss 2 days of class and your canvas feed will be flooded with about 6 assignments a week, but you only have to get like a C to get a S in the class.

Despite being required to take this course, I would say that her class can definitely be inspiring. There is a strict attendance policy where if you miss more than 2 classes, she asks you to drop the course. There is also a lot of busy work like going around campus and attending events that seem to drag on.

Not a bad class for an 8 week class but a lot of expectations are held by the professor for the students. Professor assigned an excessive amount of busy work (7+ assignments some nights), had a very strict attendance policy (will force you to drop if you miss more than 2 classes). Class requires a lot of outside of class work.

She always was energetic and prepared for class. It was always easy to understand her, and if you didn't understand something, she was more than willing to help you understand. She is harsh on attendance, but if you just show up and do the work, it's not a bad class. You will get out of it what you need. There is some busy work, but it's not hard.

I took Q295. I think people are being too hard on the class and professor. It helps people picture where they are and want to go. There's nothing stressful in this class nor are there any big papers. She is a little weird but she's a motivated person. I think that if she was a man acting like this people wouldn't be rating this course as hard.

This class is extremely easy, all busy work but none of it is hard.. think high school career course. Lecture is 100% participation and talking to others but if you just show up and do the work you'll be fine. She's very strict about attendance though and will make you drop if you miss more than 2 classes. Overall, so easy and Id take again

Has no compassion for emergency situations that result in an absence. If you have something as contagious as a sinus infection or the flu, it is still required that you attend class. She is, by far, the least forgiving instructor I have ever encountered.

She's alright for the most part. However, she's very adamant about absences and will force you to drop the class after 2+ missed classes - I was once very sick but went to class anyway to ask her nicely if I could have an excused absence the next day, but all she gave me was "there are no excused absences in my class". Very inconsiderate professor.

Class was a waste of time, but it is more to blame for the curriculum being used than the professor. She tries to act extremely cheerful at all times. Encourages participation strongly: it is the only thing done in class. All assignments could be completed quickly and even without going to class. Would start class early and end late.

The professor values attendance and you only get 4 absences before you get kicked out of the class. It does not matter if you are sick or have a doctor's note, you will get kicked out. Classes sometimes go over time but, you are not allowed to leave early if you have something important to do. Would not take again.

Her class was incredibly easy and incredibly boring. She also required so much useless busywork that took time away from my important classes. She told my upset roommate to "grieve after class" because her friend will "still be dead". Very patronizing vibes. Would not recommend if not required.
She is very hypocritical and ableist:
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Angela was an amazing professor. Although I did have a small class, she really gets to know everyone one-on-one and is always there to help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Angela is a sweetheart, very helpful, always happy. I did not feel like this class helped me to get a better understanding of what I might want career-wise, which was disappointing. We took a lot of surveys about our personality types, but most of these told me things I already knew.... Made us go to career fairs which did not help me, personally.

Most enthusiastic teacher I've ever had! She created an atmosphere that allowed all the students to become friends and we grew really close. She is a hard grader on speeches though-strict on note usage. I looked forward to going to this class.

Very hard grader.  She does not give any mercy. Ever.  She kind of makes up for it by being compassionate.  She knew everyone's name, but that also meant she knew if you weren't there.  Overall a great teacher, and I definitely learned a lot from her!

Great teacher! Made class fun and I got to know everyone in it.  She made it much easier to speak in front of the class.  Even if you messed up sometimes she wouldn't mind....I once had to turn something in late and she was okay with it despite her late policy. Great and fun class despite the public speaking!

Nice lady, pretty funny. Pretty tough grader and can be picky about topics not related directly to your speech (ex: powerpoint slides). Also kept us over 1-5 minutes nearly every class. She does care about her students though and will learn everyone's name.

There were only two exams and two homework assignments. The syllabus was bare-bones with no clear instruction. Lectures were two hours long with no breaks, no slides, and no notes. I did not feel as though I could ever come to him for any difficulties I may have had. He had no office hours. Type of teacher to brag about students failing his exams.

He's been one of the worst teachers I've had in undergrad. This required SPH class felt unfair—he often mocked SPH students for not knowing the juvenile justice system. Lectures were 3 hours with no slides, just unclear talking. Harsh tests and overall not a good experience. DO NOT TAKE WITH HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is very material heavy so do not take if you are looking for an easy A. Get ready to do a lot of writing and reading on SCOTUS cases. Professor is very clear in his expectations of your work and leaves helpful feedback. Overall, good professor but not very fun class. Would have been easier spread out over the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was supposed to be an intensive writing course. The only grades were two papers, two exams, and participation. Participation is super important but is often difficult to understand and sometimes topics were all over. He is a good prof, but this class was hard and he doesnt use slides. Just pay attention and do the work and you should be ok.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Lectures are really interesting, he grades heavily on participation, however, every time a student participates, he'll either confuse them with his response or blatantly belittle their response. The tests are difficult, this class is basically for mini lawyers who love to read and argue with a stubborn prof. Not worth it.

As long as you come to class and do the homework you will do well in this class. You can get up to 50 points of EC for doing a 5 minute presentation. You also get credit for participation. He curves the exams. It's a tough class and it's long but he's very fair and gives a lot of opportunity to get more points if you aren't a great test taker.

P375: The class is extremely boring, especially for being a 2 1/2 hour long class. You NEED to come to class in order to do well because his handouts will not make sense on their own. It's hard to follow along with his lectures because he doesn't use powerpoint slides, just talks at the front of the class.
If you are able to stay organized and do the work, you will do very well in the class. He teaches like I imagined professors would.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Yes this class is for people who REALLY want to read and are mini-lawyers already because the standard you're held to for the exams. If law is seriously your thing, he's perfect gives you cases and tests you on the application. His classes are fun if you're taking it for yourself, but can be overwhelming for people studying general criminal justice
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grading was tough, no one gets a perfect.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class was the worst online, the subject was very interesting but his grading is tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The subject was interesting but he did not do a well job engaging the class. Students were graded based on two exam and a book memo which the class average on the exams were lower than a 50%. Highly recommend not taking the class online.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Although this course is intended to be taken in person. Due to Covid I took it online. Levesque's teaching did not translate well at all into video form. The material was intriguing however the lectures themselves where mind-numbing. Not to mention tedious exams that appears to have stumped a large portion of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Levesque is a great professor, especially for law school bound students. His papers test you on the most difficult material, yet he can always explain it in a simple manner. Overall, a great professor. Highly recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I really like Professor Levesque. He makes lecture fun and interesting. Which isn't easy to do for 2 1/2 hours. He is very big about participating and the class as a whole participates he will make the exams easier and give a better curve. I would definitely take another class with him. Awesome professor.

it is not an easy A class, but with all the information you have to learn in here, professor levesque does a good job teaching it, is well organized, and easily approachable. Seems mean/sarcastic at first but is actually really nice, interesting, and fun--- my 2 1/2 hour long class with him went by faster than some of my 50 minute ones with others

Roger is an excellent proffesor. He is not a cake walk but if you do the readings and participate in class with engaging an useful comments you will make a good grade. Takes input from students and is very respectful of ideas. This is not a class for quiet people, if your quiet you wont do well!!!!!!
Far and away the best, and most interesting professor I had at IU. He is difficult, but fair. If you put in effort, you will get a lot out of him...very nice guy.

He's an excellent professor.  He's just honest and doesn't hide his annoyance with students that have nothing useful to say.  He knows what he's talking about and has the ability to engage students in interesting debates.
horrible.
He's not a bad professor, but the work load can be pretty intense. Sarcastic, but generally interesting.
This professor teaches very interesting classes, especially for criminal justice/law school bound students, I highly recommend him.

Lectures were lengthy and unclear, and the material covered in class did not relate to the homework or on the exams. Professor would periodically stop in class to ask if everyone understood, but wouldn't wait for anyone to reply before continuing to teach. Teaching style consisted of rambling for the entire lecture without any variation.

The HW would take at least 2-3 hours minimum unless you're very, VERY quick with science and math. Do be careful about dates and participation, however there are some drops for attendance and discussions. There is no late credit but he can be understanding with the deadlines as long as they are properly communicated. Lectures can be a hard to comp.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. I took C101 as a required class, the lectures were M,W,F 9:10-10:00 am with a quiz every Friday and a homework assignment that would take about 2-3 hours each week. He does not explain the material well at all. You could definitely crawl your way through this class but would not recommend it.

This professor teaches linear algebra, Calculus III, and Differential Equations from a Powerpoint deck. He did not publish the exams for the course and determined that we would have exams Friday nights and Saturday mornings by telling one student before class (and having that student tell the rest of the class). He does not care about his students.

Professor Li is MUCH better than Professor Iyengar. He can be more difficult to understand, but he is happy to slow down and explain. His handwriting is clear and concise. He does rely much more on math to explain, which is fine. If you are put in S-117 you should be EXTREMELY comfortable with Calculus, if not, take C-117!

When I took S117, it was split between Iyengar and LI. Iyengar was way better and more organized. Professor Li was difficult to understand at times, assigned a lot of homework, and didn't explain things very clearly. His lectures were much less interesting than Iyengar's

When I took this class, it was split between Iyengar and Li. Li's portion was much less organized that Iyengar's section. Also, Li seemed a lot less willing to answer questions and, when he did answer, the answers were not thorough and often times added to the confusion.

The exams are fair and relatively easy, but the homework is downright impossible sometimes (eg. derivations beyond the scope of our knowledge; simply too MUCH homework).  Dr. Li scribbles incomprehensible math on the board for 50 minutes, and I leave class understanding less than I did previously.  He's a nice guy, though. The AI helped us a lot.

Dr. Li is great! He understands that this subject is not easy. He knows what the students are going through- and he is super easy to converse with. The class is fair and if you just do the work, you will be fine. DO THE HOMEWORK!! It's worth 30% of your grade and tests are impartial (similar to practice exams).

He's one amazing professor. He explains concepts somewhat clearly. Also, he passes out practice exams before exams..and it's like almost identical to the real exam with numbers changed and problems taken from homework. Midterm exams are worth less than the homework..there is weekly homework, which sucks, but totally helps you to do well on the exam

The work is okay if you keep up. Exercises are challenging but push you to think. He is brutally honest to make a point but keeps the class engaged. It's an ethics course, so some discomfort is kind of the point.  Not a class where you can coast, but one of the more thought-provoking courses and one of the best professors for ethics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Lemper had great lectures where he would go into further detail and give examples of the topics in the assigned videos. Exams make up all of the grade but one could be dropped. Exams are similar to practice exams so I recommend going over those to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the best professors at IU. Extremely well qualified and super funny. has some of the hardest exmas tho.
He is an outstanding professor, could not recommend him more!

The absolute GOAT. Lemper made every class meeting into a standup comedy show which made some of the more mundane topics interesting to listen too. The class itself isn't too hard, but you're graded entirely on tests which are moderately curved. The class average is around a B but it's worth it for Lemper's hilarious lectures, so I don't mind.

Professor Lemper is an amazing teacher who's extremely knowledgeable. He made classes so interesting and hilarious with his examples, which really helped everyone understand the concepts so much easier. Even though there are only three tests he allows you to drop your lowest score with the average of all three tests. Definitely take L201 with him!

L201 is a tough course that many would prefer to take online. However, if you do take it in person, Lemper is the go-to professor. Extremely knowledgeable as a former attorney, he provides many useful examples to relate to course material. The class is entirely graded on tests, but this also means your grade won't be decided by group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing guy. Would always chat with him before class. Used meaningful examples and gave plenty of practice to help with exams and with decent preparation are not bad at all. Has a great sense of humor which helped me stay engaged during lectures-this also helped me remember tougher concepts and made law more enjoyable.

He records all of his lectures and makes them available on canvas. The entire grade solely depends on 4/5 exams. He provides old exams for practice which is super helpful and makes the exams easier. Overall, I find L201 as a subject itself hard but professor Lemper definitely makes it easier.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grade is all exams so you better study. You get out what you put into it. Tests are similar to practice tests he provides but are very word heavy. Lectures are funny but sometimes the scenarios and examples he comes up with in class or on an exam are so absurd that it can throw you off. Not an easy class at all but I'd recommend taking it with him.

Fantastic teacher and uses some funny examples to help understand concepts. Focus on doing well on first 3 exams only covering specific chapters so you don't have to take the final over all material. Practice exams are extremely similar to exams so understand the format. 2nd exam has more difficult concepts so make sure to not overlook it.

Your grade is only four exams, each worth 25% of your grade. He gives practice exams. He is funny, which makes lectures interesting. I probably could have done better but tbh, I didn't study more than a day for the exams.
Can't stress how great he will make the class for you. Need to enroll with him

Professor Lemper is amazing! I would definitely take this class again. He records every class in case you miss one. You also get to drop one exam. There are no assignments. Exams are curved. He give past exam papers for practice, exams are very similar to the past exams.
His lectures are mind-glowingly amazing. Loved everything about this class.

I cannot stress enough how amazing he is! Seriously is such a great teacher that if you attend class you will only have to study a little bit to do well on exams. He is excellent at providing real and most times funny examples of the topics in class making them easier to memorize and apply. Exams are just like class, no curveballs!

Love Tim! 4 exams with a 5th one that is cumulative. If you do great on the first 4, you don't have to take the final. His practice exams are the ticket to acing your exams. His real world examples make the material easy to understand and his humor brightens my week. He understands that his class isn't the only class you're taking and truly cares.

Lemper is great. L201 sucks, but you've got to take it. Take it with Tim. 

If you pay attention in class, you'll be fine for the exams, they aren't that hard with a little studying. There are a lot of tests, but trust me, that's a plus. There really isn't any homework. There is a book, but I didn't know that until last week and I did fine.

The man. This is who you want for L201. Keeps what could be boring topics interesting to listen to via real examples of law application. Tests are very much bearable & passable if you always attend and take notes. Cannot stress enough how helpful and high-quality his lectures are!

Engaging and entertaining lectures, especially for a law class. Straight forward with expectations. Go to class, study, and you will do well. 100% of grade relies on exams but it is not meant to mess you up.

Prof. Lemper is by far the best professor I've had at Kelley. His lectures are fantastic and he gives you the tools you need to succeed. That being said if you don't go to class and prepare for exams (he gives a ton of help) then you will struggle. Funny guy, great examples through lectures, and makes somewhat boring topics bearable/enjoyable.
Best professor I've ever had at IU. If you show up to class, you'll pass because his lectures are outstanding.

Lemper is the best professor I've had at Kelley hands down. Super funny, actually relevant lectures, and gives great examples to help you learn. He also really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. I tested positive for COVID during the final and he HAND DELIVERED the exam to me at my apartment so that I could still take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof Lemper is easily the best choice for L201. My semester he only graded the class off 3 tests, but if you actually read the book and go to class you will do fine on them. He comes up with relevant, interesting and entertaining examples while teaching to help you better understand law applications. Overall, Lemper is a super chill teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lemper was very accommodating to what is going on in your life. He explains the material very well, and helps explain the terms in simple terms. The only way to get points is through exams, but every exam is straight forward and following along with his teachings. I would 100000% take him again!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tim Lemper is one of the best professors I have had at IU. He cares about his students and wants them to do well. His exams are straightforward: if you do the readings, pay attention in class, and take notes, you will definitely do well! He also uses a lot of amazing examples that help bring the material to life. Overall, a fantastic professor.
One of the best professor at Kelley and IU. Great person, funny guy, and always accessible. He tried to make classes easier than it would be, and don't have much (if any) homework.
Best professor at Kelley
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: IU grades are available online so I did some number crunching. If you take the average student GPA and subtract it by the class-specific GPA, you have a relative estimate for the professor's difficulty. This stat would crown Lemper as consistently the toughest L201 professor. Don't do that to yourself. You can read law on your own. Good guy though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Best teacher at IU hands down.

He is by far one of the best professors I have taken at Indiana University, Bloomington! You will learn a lot from him. He is fun to listen to, and his classes are definitely better the other Law Classes (BUS L 201) as he does not ask you to do the entire course, just the sections which he thinks are need to know!

I like Lemper as a professor and lecturer, but I really struggled in his class. It was difficult for me to take notes on his lectures because he tends to use stories to develop concepts, and the PowerPoint doesn't always stay on track with his lecture. If you miss when he addresses the basic principles of a concept, you're out of luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Informative and willing to go out of his way to assist

Lemper is one of my favorite professors, he really knows how to connect and teach students. Does a great job of being engaging. Go to class, thats where he gives a deeper understanding to the material he finds important. His video review lectures are also very helpful. But be prepared to work real hard, otherwise you'll get a C+ like me

Lemper is one of my favorite professor's I have had at Kelley. Yes, his class is very challenging, but he is always willing to help his students succeed. Not only does he upload re-caps of lectures after every class, he also gives generous curves/extra credit on tests. I strongly recommend going to class, even though it is not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tim is by far the best and most helpful professor I've had while at IU.  He explains each concept in great detail and makes them funny, and he shows things visually as well.  His tests are straight from lectures so if you attend class, you should do fine on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tim is great, there is really no excuse to do poorly in the class. His lectures are extremely helpful and he also provides so many resources before each test including past exams and also recorded lecture videos. If you do poorly, it's really on you for not using all of the resources he gives to succeed. He's also hilarious and very entertaining.

Agree with all of the other feedback.  Lemper is easily the best professor I've had so far - he goes more in depth in the material than any other professor, and as a result you learn a lot.  That being said, it is a tough class.  As long as you study for tests and utilize the materials he provides it should be an easy B to A.  Beware he does curve.

Lemper's awesome. He helped me form my business, has helped me legal questions, and is available to help students who are respectful and ask for help. This is a challenging course - don't get me wrong - but Lemper's online lectures make it easier to succeed. Go to class and listen to the online lectures before tests and you will do fine.

I like Professor Lemper alot. Let me just say that. I enjoyed going to class and I definitely learned more in his class than I did in any other class this past semester. I did well on all 4 exams and had an average of 85% on exams. I ended up getting a C+ due to the hard class activities. If you don't care about your grade but want to learn, go 4it

Pretty complex subject material, but does a pretty good job at explaining it. Pay attention during lectures. Tests are pretty hard, but he usually puts a fat curve on them. Prepare for class because he does like to give quizzes unannounced. Real nice guy though, pretty understanding. Would take another class from him again.

He posts a lot of helpful information on line. He posts videos of all of his lectures as well as the slides and provides a lot of practice exams. The tests are tough but he curves a lot because of it.

Lemper is a cool guy, he uses really good examples in lectures and really helps students to try and understand. His exams are hard though and you will not do well if you don't go to class/regularly study

Easily the worst professor I've had at IU thus far.  His tests are impossible and studying his power points/videos don't help. He makes you feel stupid and unmotivated. His classes are extremely boring and rarely engaging but he tries to be funny to make lecture somewhat interesting. His voice could put you to sleep. Never take J300 with him.
He's really funny and tries to relate the difficult concepts to things that people know already. He knows the course content is difficult and tries to help students grasp the course content.

Lemper knows what he's doing. He is a well-educated Harvard Law graduate who is eager to teach. He brings real life examples to class and goes through problems step by step. Reading the book is optional but definitely go through his power points before exams. Exams are exactly what he says they are - he wants to test if you've actually learned.

Professor Lemper is a great guy and he's really helpful when you go in to see him. However, he is an awful teacher! He barely discusses the material during lectures, goes off on tangents, and only talks about pointless examples that really don't end up helping you at all.

Lemper might be the hardest teacher I have ever had. He knows every trick in the book and feeds off students losing points. I suggest any other teacher than him. The hours I spent on his lecture videos and notes is not worth it. This class is impossible. TAKE A DIFFERENT TEACHER!
Great Prof, very funny, attend class and you will learn, test are hard but he gives test examples in class all the time. One of the best!
Lemper is smart and he will let you know it.  He is a good teacher but is kind of a spiteful person.  Tests are hard.

This guy is legitimately A BOSS. He is one, if not the best, professors I've had. I honestly had no interest in the subject but he makes the class so interesting and entertaining it is actually fun to go to class. Even though attendance is technically not mandatory you will have some pop quizzes at least once a week. If you can take him! DO IT!
He's a nice guy and has no filter (which is entertaining), but the class is a bit difficult.

This is the only professor I have bothered commenting for on this site because he was by far my favorite at IU! You have to go to every class because there are always quizzes and it can be somewhat challenging, but he is very helpful and makes the material a lot easier to understand. He is funny and approachable and made boring material fun.

Wonderful Professor. Great advise. Always helpful. Must go to class to get points for the quiz. Work is challenging but totally worth it. Stays in your head. He uses current examples to help you remember cases.
Makes Class much interactive and fun! Graduated from Harvard law School so, expect test little harder. Overall, above average!

By far one of my favorite professors! Have to go to class bc he has quizzes almost every day. He says you need to read the book, but you dont, and the tests are not difficult if you study using his practice tests. He is really funny & makes the class interesting. I though that I would hate the class, but it was my favorite this semester.
He is probably the best teacher I have ever had! He makes the class so much more injoyable! :)
Cool prof but better be on top of the game other then that open notes exam and study those power points

Professor Lemper is very knowledgeable as he knows the material extremely well. Nonetheless, the exams are very challenging. Interestingly, he changes the structure of the class every semester. The bad thing about him is that he curses excessively, thinking that he's being funny, and makes some unappropriate sexual comments. Okay teacher overall.

Lemper is a lot of fun as a teacher and makes most information engaging. The tests are really hard and you should study using old exams. He says that reading the book is mandatory for doing well in the class, but it's not. Go visit him in office hours because he's really fun to talk to.
Great prof. but you have to go to class. He makes it worth it. This is my hardest class but it is the one I enjoy the most. Having him for law is worth messing up your schedule.

Loved his class, he made even the boring material fun. He teaches the type of class you don't want to miss. He is tough and doesn't give anything you don't earn, but is willing to give a lot of help if you go to office hours and talk with him. Tough, but worth it.
Dude is the man! Great teacher...Explains the concepts tremedously.  I find law to be quite boring, but I anticipated going to each and every class
Professor Lemper is an incredible teacher!
He is awesome! His class is fun and his sense of humor actually worth listening to! Go to office hours and get to know him... worth it!
He is nice but his exams are not; they are extremely tricky.

His tests were relentless and ridiculous. Each semester has a different design, usually voted on by the class. Regardless of point distribution, test format, or course curriculum his power points are the primary notes, you will use the book a lot, and you will need to seriously study to get a solid A or B.

Absolutely wonderful teacher, funny, intriguing, and has lots of interesting stories and knowledge and experience in the field. Although the tests are difficult, he allows the class to decide the structure of the class the first day (we had 4 non-cummulative tests and attendance was extra credit.) Highly recommended. :)

Very hard tests.  Each question is a paragraph and one word can change everything.  The tests are open note but it doesn't really help because they are so long and it is difficult to get through all the problems in 90 minutes.

Very good teacher.  Really helpful, but tough tests.  As long as you study you'll be good to go though.  I posted some notes on Gradeguru.com so if you need short-hand versions of his teaching as a guide for how the class will be, you might want to check those out.  Just search them or w/e.
Awesome teacher. Genuinely one of the best teachers in the business school. Hard tests though. Be prepared to study as there was a 12 point bump on his first exam.
Good Teacher but really hard tests

Excellent teacher. 1 pt extra credit just for showing up. Tests are pretty easy. Very reasonable & easy to talk to. Pretty funny guy. Good at explaining concepts. Willing to curve tests. If you're good at critical reading, you should have no trouble, but I know some people have a tough time with the material.
Simply awesome.  Truly one of the great young professors in the business school.  His personal charm and deft sense of humor mask a staggering intellect.  Definitely worth the price of tuition.

Awful. You can use your notes but they dont help. All of the exam questions are a paragraph long of real world examples and then you have to rush through everything. Attendance every day. Quiz every day.
Take this class it's not that bad. Interesting and doubles for marketing/legal studies majors.  Exams are all open book/open notes too
Great guy. He is down to earth and genuinely interested in his students.  He is very generous with extra credit and also with curving the tests.
No Comments
No Comments

Open note exams.  Good guy. Makes lecture interesting with jokes and stories of law suits he has worked on.  Lots of real world examples. One of two professors I would take for L201.  You don't want to end up in the wrong class.

The Daily quizzes are annoying he looks for such specific answers to get full points. The midterms are very hard but he lets you bring a notes sheet. The final project is also such a tax, follow the grading rubric perfectly if you want a decent grade. You wont do good if you don't go to class so take at your own risk!
The kind of professor that would rather you memorize a few specific sentences rather than actually learn anything.

Talked loudly with students during exams and took attendance out loud half way through the exam. Also an example of an actual test question is "what is the most important river in china?"
A. The Yangtze is the most important and the yellow is the second most important 
B. The yellow is the most important and the yangtze is the second most important

The class isn't actually that difficult, but the lectures can get kind of boring. If you pay attention in class, you should do fairly well on the exams. The final group project is graded pretty tough, so make sure you read the rubric really well. He curves the class at the end and offers some bonus points and drops your lowest two quizzes.
Don't ever take anything from this guy. Instructions are always unclear and has no idea what's going on. Actually an unintelligent individual. Avoid at all costs.

Just had group projects today and he gave incorrect instructions for our group then graded us on a different rubric. He gives everyone an average of 65 on poster projects and average of 65 on tests but docent curve anything. Pick another professor.
Nit picks on every grade. No curves with super hard test. No a fair teacher at all

He doesn't care about his students succeeding. Exams were super hard. He said at the beginning of the semester he isn't trying to trick us and claims his exams aren't hard but then why did the exams not cover lectures notes and reading questions.
Lastly I found the 3 point quizzes every class completely unnecessary.

Claims test are easy and gives you study guides but the don't help. 

Only drops 2 quizzes only giving you 2 miss days.

Grades final project super harsh.

Walks around constantly during tests 

Doesn't curve anything until the end of the year with 2% even with most of the class scoring 50%

Only drops 2 quizzes only giving you 2 miss days.

Grades final project super harsh.

Walks around constantly during tests 

Doesn't curve anything until the end of the year with 2% even with most of the class scoring 50%

Super unfair grader.

'd recommend taking this class with another professor. The instructor is a tough grader, didn't honor my IEP accommodations, and forced in-class exams. Project approvals were frustrating—my group needed 10+ attempts for one part. Very strict and challenging.
Take with a different prof

Very clear lectures, tests were open note and quiz for attendance but super easy. The teacher is great people just get mad bc he grades the final project really hard. He is very helpful with any questions and just overall super nice. Final project is hard but that's only negative

I have never been one to write rate my professors but I felt it was my duty to share how horrible of an experience in this class was. There's a quiz every single class and readings are way too long. Midterms are impossible and u have a project all semester. Extremely unhelpful, I had to email him over 20 times to get 1 part of the project approved

He makes his class very hard for no apparent reason. He is not a nice teacher to his students and does not seem to care about the success of his students. He generally is not a good teacher or person and should have no place working any profession on Indiana University's campus as he does not reflect the values our school has.

Do NOT recommend. If you have to take E183, TAKE IT WITH SOMEONE ELSE! He is unprofessional and rude to students. He is extremely unprepared for class and changes things last minute. Quizzes EVERYDAY that you can miss, but if you have a question on grading, he can't answer it. His TA grades everything, and he is extremely unaware of grading. 0/10

THE WORST professor I ever met in my life. Extremely not care about his student, and take points off on every assignment on purpose to make sure you don't get full credits and A in the class. All other 183 session exams are online except his. He make it clear in the first class that nobody will have an A before curve.

Completely rude and unprofessional with students, could really care less how you do in the class. Will be matter-of-fact in a way that isn't constructive criticism, it's just criticism and will make sure you do not receive full points for anything. If you have to take this course, TAKE IT WITH SOMEONE ELSE!

DON'T EVER TAKE HE'S CLASS. Quiz for attendance, long reading for no points, tough tough exams (tricky questions, even you study hard but you still can't get it right). Other E183 class are all easy A, but for he's class is to darg your grades down.

He 's a chill guy, but very unhelpful. He seems to not care about his students and when someone tried to tell him their preferred name, he told them not to bother because he wouldn't remember it anyway. The reading quizzes and lecture material are easy, he also gives some extra credit. The group project is a pain and he grades it extremely harshly.

hes pretty chill theres a test the minute class starts everyday ab the reading homework. theres a group project you work on all year and he gets pretty nit picky on the grading so follow the syllabus EXACTLY. i honestly dk why he has such a bad rating on here I thought he was fine and he doesnt call on people to participate in class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Liu is a very respectful guy but as a professor theres a lot of room for improvement. Everyday you have a quiz that is given for attendance basically. Theres a group project you work on the whole semester and even if it has everything, he will find something so you cant get an A. When it comes to the midterms good luck!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Liu is the laziest professor I have ever experienced. Given the option of asynchronous or synchronous for online learning, he opted with asynchronous. He does not care about his students' wellbeing or performance in the class; furthermore, has unrealistically specific criteria he looks for when grading quizzes we have 5min to take.

We had a group project that encompassed the entire semester, we had four people in the group one dropped the class (Smart Guy), he asked us the last day why we only had three people? If that doesn't tell you how involved he was as a teacher idk what will. He also had trouble understanding graphs that I could and Im not a professor... Hmmm

While the material and the way it is presented is semi-interesting, he is very condescending and extremely particular when it comes to having the exact right answer on exams and the group project. Any time you would try to argue your answer being right, you will always lose as he is not open to suggestions. Be prepared to practice a lot of patience
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Liu does not care about his students. He provides unclear course criteria and does not explain assignments properly. He provided a grading scale after the first midterm and changed it the day grades were due. No technology allowed in class and quizzes every day for attendance. Do yourself a favor and take this course with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nice guy, yes, but the biggest issue I had was his tests and the end of the year project. This professor is an awful grader. Not understanding at all, will not appeal to reasoning, and changes his mind/grading criteria last minute when faced with an issue. You have to put his exact thoughts word for word on the page or its wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really recommend because it is a very organized class. You have the same format of homework every night, and the classes were predictable. Hardest aspect is the group project, which requires a lot of time outside class. I had a lot of group issues and he was extremely understanding and helpful, definitely wants students to succeed.

Every class has a short article with questions assigned and there is a quiz at the beginning of each class based exactly off of the questions. The material is always interesting and relevant. Professor Liu doesn't make a huge effort to get to know his students, but he is really nice and accessible. 3 exams and no final but a semester group project
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She is brilliant but why does that matter if she literally just reads off her script lol

Reads off a paper the entire lecture. Always has pop quizzes from the multiple chapters assigned that week. Boring readings as well as a boring lecture. Lectures aren't very relevant to the things she teaches. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Professor Lloyd is very intelligent and has a deep knowledge of the subject matter. But the lectures are incredibly boring and hard to stay engaged in. There are a LOT of pop quizzes and a lot of reading so be ready for that. I personally didn't like her teaching style. She just stood up and read from a packet for 50 minutes. I would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: This class will probably open up your mind. But the books are dusty, but if you don't mind reading 3 books over a semester you'll be fine. They're not difficult to read, just very boring. Just keep in mind that some labs you have to take second semester count for this credit. OH, and attend class. Her pop quizzes give definition to "Pop Quiz"
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Evolution and creationism was really interesting. It was a lot of reading and studying, but I actually learned a lot and enjoyed doing the work for it. Dr. Lloyd lectures and you will have an AI that grades your papers, home works and tests so grading varies. Her lectures are really interesting and informative.

Professor Lloyd is very intelligent, but I learned more from my TA in discussion. Professor looks at a piece of paper and reads it to you during class; there is no sort of aid to follow along. There is 1 reading quiz per week. They're pretty tough but got better as the semester progressed. The class is a lot of work but A's are easily attainable.

Such a boring lecturer. I have the hardest time paying attention. There is no powerpoint, outline, or anything to look at. She just stands and talks. And she never goes over the reading that we did prior that night, she will go over reading from a week ago which makes it frustrating when you have to take a pop quiz over the reading from that night.

Topic: History and Philosophy of Medicine. Nice teacher who is pretty brilliant. A TON of reading that is difficult to keep up with, but in-class discussion highlights important points. Very interesting course material; I enjoyed this class. Attend class (mandatory, but ungraded except for pop quizes) and the quizzes and tests will be easy.

This class is a lot of work, as it should be.  However, if you show up to class, take good notes, and do the reading assignments you will do just fine.  She makes the robust amount of information manageable with 4 quizzes that really do prepare you for the mid-term and final exams.
She's absolutely brilliant.  Not the most engaging lecturer but she really knows her stuff. Fun fact: I've seen her referenced in more than one Cracked.com article!
Very nice professor. Sometimes it was a little difficult to comprehend, but her office hours were very helpful. Do the readings, and participate in class and your certain to get an A+.
very very boring lectures even though subject material was interesting. easy tests though and some in class small group activities that made lectures slightly more exciting.
This class was horrible. She says the word UM every second she gets and looses track of thought. Discussion was the only good part about the class. Looks like she put a fork in an electrical socket.

Super easy course.  The first half is history of medicine; well organized, easy material.  Second half is public health philosophy and ethics; poorly organized, random, opinion-based.  Not an interesting class at all, nor is she an interesting lecturer.  4 pop-quizzes with easy questions, some are unfair.  Curved grading scale.  85% = A.

Tough but you will learn a lot.  She does not budge on deadlines, but she out of all my professors prepared me for grad school because of this.  Incredibly prompt via email and available night and day for consultation. For I400 thesis class, she personally made detailed track changes on every one of our 40+ page papers. Great respect for Dr. lloyd
hated the class. I had to hold my eyes open so i wouldnt fall asleep, she was way to fast with her slides. i like the other comments heard soc was a great easy class- NOT WITH HER
No Comments

Everyone says sociology was an easy class, so I took it. They were very wrong. She made the class so vague and abstract I struggled a lot. She has power point up, but changes the slides so fast you don't have time to copy down the VERY IMPORTANT notes. It made me hate sociology.

Professor Lopez Neumann was not a good Calculus I teacher. He failed to explain lecture material clearly, but the homework assigned was not difficult. His tests were satisfactory at best. Be prepared to do a lot of the learning on your own.

If you have him for Calc 2, maybe he's bad, but he really excelled in a class format for Calc 3. He wasn't the best teacher that I've ever had, but he definitely is not the worst. He also made learning the theory for Calc 3 fun, and really tied it together. 
Be warned though, the tests are hard, you MUST study to pass.
lectured off very long powerpoints and did not explain clearly. his tests were very hard and not like what the homework was like. if he's your professor, good luck.
I just want to be really honest and say if you can avoid this professor...please do it.

Classes are only 50 minutes 3 times a week, every class he speeds through the PowerPoint without explaining or making anything clear.  He jam packs so much information into his lecture slides that we never ever get through all of them (usually about 60%).  He leaves no time for explaining anything and everything is extremely rushed.  Tests are 80%
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor focuses on personal anecdotes over teaching, gives vague critiques, and grading lacks transparency. Many students fear asking questions or giving feedback due to intimidation. The environment feels hostile, and constructive guidance is rarely provided, stunting growth.

I had Professor Logo for 2 classes and he is such a good resource. He genuinely cares about you and your work. Get to know him because he is genuinely the best professor I had in the media school. Highly recommend taking the Portfolio Workshop class with him instead of the online version. You get so much more out of it when working with him.

Great professor for advertising students. Very knowledgeable about the ad agency space and cares about his students' work. You will do some projects to practice creating ads towards the end of the semester after learning concepts earlier on. If you have an opportunity to take his class, do it.
He's super nice and funny. There's a lot of homework, but I've found it really helpful. Sad I'm not taking ASL III with him.

Rob is an absolutely amazing professor I can't recommend him enough. He's super funny too! If you're passionate about ASL you'll do fine in his class, as long as your heart is actually in it and you genuinely try its pretty easy.

Rob makes you put the work in, but in return you learn so much. There is a lot of homework but honestly it's not terrible. You HAVE to go to class to learn. As someone who struggled in spanish, i highly recommend taking ASL instead.

Rob is great! I love his teaching approach of focusing on practice during class. It was a little annoying to have more homework outside of class, but I definitely learned more. He is almost impossible to reach outside of class though. He is a great person though and I really enjoyed being in his class!

Rob is a great ASL teacher. He is a good teacher to start in ASL100 because he is big on the little grammar aspects and that will help you have a good foundation later on in ASL. If you participate and come to class you will get an A. He does like to cold call so pay attention. Overall he is a great teacher and has taught me a lot so far about ASL

Rob was a funny and caring professor who loved teaching ASL. However, I will say he loves to call on students, so you must be engaged all of class. If you're late, he loves to pick on you and he is big on coming to all classes. Overall, he's a nice guy and there's not much out-of-class work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a good instructor, but he's hard to contact outside of class, and he doesn't update grades that often. He's not Canvas savvy, and students have had to reach out to TAs to request assistance in fixing their assignments. He's fine for learning ASL, but he took too long to start teaching actual signs. The syllabus schedule isn't followed.

Professor Loveless is an amazing professor. He really does care about his students. He can be a little intimidating at first, but if you just show up to class, and ask for help if you don't understand something he is great help in helping you understand. If you do not show up to class you will not pass. The tests a very easy if you pay attention.

Super great prof. Zoom meetings are mandatory and graded; he will send an email out about what materials are to be practiced and discussed in the upcoming class session. Very patient and funny. Average amount of homework, about 2 assignments a week. Super nice GA (Marriah). Overall, a great, interactive course that you will learn A LOT in.
He is a nice guy, but he is extremely confusing and his "lectures" on Kaltura are usually really blurry and not very helpful when it comes to his zoom meetings, which he requires participation in.

Professor Loveless is such a good guy.. he can be super intimidating at first but really cares about his students. Just ask questions when you're confused and attend his zoom sessions and youll be golden. I would also recommend meeting with the GA when you're confused. For my class, she was really kind, helpful and accommodating

With being online, assignments were difficult because you watch his lecture videos and then answer questions over them and sometimes they arent written clearly. However, prof Loveless is a great guy and professor. He focuses more on the grammar aspect than A100 and because of that I feel I am a better signer.

He is very good at implementing good ASL technique in his signing and enforcing their use in the class. The bad thing is that sometimes he will introduce a concept/vocab list once and then not ever use it again.

I am in the middle of taking his class this summer and it is so beyond hard. so much work and he teaches sign language terribly. even the TA always says she has no idea whats going on. zoom classes are required. he gets frustrated in the zooms when the students dont understand. im sure taking this class in person is different but he sucks.
Literally had an exam once a week. They are easy. But we never learned anything new. Just kept testing over the same things you learn in ASL 1
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Rob was fine. He wasn't great but he wasn't horrible. His issue is that he would use a word once in class, and then put it on the vocab version of the exam. Also, you have exams constantly, and he is really bad at announcing when homework and exam dates. He also changes grades after the GA already grades them, and his grades are usually worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rob is by far the best ASL prof EVER. In his class you learn the details of signing correctly, and this is what helps you actually be able to communicate the language. I have learned SO MUCH this semester and would 100% HIGHLY recommend him. The only reason I wouldn't is if you struggle making it to classes or paying attention during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: THEE best asl teacher out there, if you fail this class you probably did not attend. he seriously is the best, hes such a down to earth guy i recommend him over every asl teacher if you actually enjoy asl
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: So funny and understanding. Does a great job at explaining things, even with the language barrier. He keeps you engaged in class.

Professor Loveless knows exactly what he wants out of each student's signing, and you will learn more of the nitty gritty details of ASL. If you want to learn to sign beautifully, Loveless will show you how. He's caring and forgiving if you try your best. Great guy.
My ABSOLUTE FAVORITE ASL professor!! Rob was amazing! Definitely recommend taking him!
He made it way too difficult. How you do on the first test pretty much depends on what your A100 teacher taught you.

Rob was the worst ASL professor I have had. I would not recommend taking his class. He does not care if you understand. Play close attention to what book you actually need because he told us the wrong book.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Rob is so great. He makes every single class so enjoyable, and he teaches so so well. We do a lot of activities(not graded) and practice with one another. He made me love sign language, and helped me reach my major! he is also very understanding, and lenient!
awesome!

He wasn't terrible, but he wasn't great, either. I had him for a summer ASL 150 course and it seemed that he was very new to summer teaching, as our timeline constantly changed and we all always came into class not knowing what to expect. Overall we did fine but it was very stressful, especially the last week.
Very nice and a lot of the later lectures actually felt useful in a class you wouldn't think would be much. Easy to get a good grade and a GPA booster.
He is great at what he does. He easily breaks down more complex linguistic ideas. He will work with you until you understand a concept. Highly recommend!

Samson was overall a nice guy. He was really relatable and funny sometimes. When it came to the speeches, he wasn't very much help at all. All of the information we needed came from the online lectures, and we wasted too much class time on unnecessary things. He grades pretty harshly on the last two speeches. TAKE YOUR MINI UNITS & BLOGS SERIOUSLY
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Samson was friendly and really helpful. He was always open to questions and was really good at seeing when the class didn't understand something and clarifying. No complaints.

This woman does not know what he's doing. His "art" is not "art." It is repulsive and offended several other classmates and I. Indiana needs to figure it out soon because women like this are ruining our reputation.

If you go to class, you'll be fine. Metalsmithing is a lot of work, so if you aren't willing to put in the work, don't take this class. She gives demos and they take FOREVER, but the information is useful. You need patience with Randy because she is older. Sweetest lady alive though and is always willing to help.

Prof Long is prone to nervous breakdown (3 in 3 years during my tenure) leading to extended abscess thus making it necessary to turn elsewhere for esoteric guidance (turned out to be better for me anyway). Technically adept however her thought process are pedestrian.

Randy is one of the greatest professors and mentors I have had in my educational career.  She is unimaginably devoted to her students development and goes above and beyond to help in the process. Randy has high expectations of her students, including independent research, excellent craftsmanship, and demonstrating commitment to the craft.
Her shameless negativity is the kind of spirit-crushing dogma that one would hope would be absent in a fine arts school.  Technique is one thing, communication and optimism are another thing.

she is completely uninterested in student growth. as a grad student no guidance or helpful criticism was offered or could be gleaned from her. my experience has been one of self taught lessons and personal studies (what I could have done on my own with out paying).

she is completely uninterested in student growth. as a grad student no guidance or helpful criticism was offered or could be gleaned from her. my experience has been one of self taught lessons and personal studies (what I could have done on my own with out paying).

Professor Lucas was great and if you need or want a public speaking credit, I would 100% recommend his class. He was very understanding and made public speaking, which can be scary, very comfortable and less challenging.
Professor Lucas is very understanding and reasonable. He cares that his students do well and is easy to talk to inside and outside of class. I would recommend him to anyone who needs a speech credit.
Professor Lucas was my favorite professor this whole school year. He was always caring and there for all students no matter what time of the day it seemed.

Professor Lucas was very engaging, understanding, and in general created a comfortable space in class. It is pretty easy to get a good grade in this class if you put in the effort to your speeches and midterm. I actually had a lot of fun in this class with this professor and I'd take it again if I could!

Would recommend taking V326 with Prof Lucas. The class was once a week with a break in the middle of class to regroup since it was 2 hours. You have one midterm, and 4 speeches total including a final group project. The textbook is only used for midterm and attendance isn't mandatory but recommend going to class or you will miss material.

Prof Lucas is awesome and I recommend taking V326 with him over anyone else. One test (midterm in week 12), based on the textbook that is supposed to be read outside of class. Not a lot of speeches ~4, but he's a very forgiving grader. 2 group speeches, but not too awful. Go to class, or you'll miss a lot of directions. Class isn't too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Steve was one of the best professors I have had. He made this class a comfortable environment where you feel more comfortable speaking. He always answered our questions right away and always had our best interest at heart. 10/10 recommend!

There is a lot to do reading for her class. I'll be honest, I js skimmed thru them n managed to get full pts on disc anyway. Use the lect notes to help u out on the quizzes n final exam. Theres a group project which is an easy A if everyone did their part correctly.

This class was okay overall. Lectures often felt disorganized and dull, making it hard to stay engaged. A group podcast project is 40% of your grade, and exams are 30%, so this class is graded mainly by the podcast and exams. Weekly discussion questions require 30–40 pages of reading per question, which adds up. I wouldn't personally take it again.

Prof. Stavig was awesome! She is clearly an expert in her field, but she knows how to teach, explain, and engage students. She didn't give letter grades; pretty much everything was completion (with the ability to resubmit). Readings were long, but you can skim and be fine in class. Also had 10 weekly 2-page things for the readings, also very doable
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She is the absolute sweetest. The material we learned about was interesting and she accompanies it with a video or story sometimes. She allows notes on the tests and is a pretty easy grader on the podcast stuff. You get a few freebies if you need to miss class which is nice. You have to read for the discussions and answer like 2-3 questions.

She's an amazing teacher. Same with the TA, Youngmin. This classes requires attendance, no more than 3 absence before she takes 2% from the final exams. There is a group project that will be throughout the semester. TEAM UP W/ GOOD PPL. Plus, 3 quizzes and 10 discussion post to do. An easy A.
Good guy, just so much reading outside of class and the classes are him just reading the powerpoints.
Very interesting class material and a professor who is obviously passionate on the subject, I really enjoy professor Lundell
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: i was most excited for this class and now it has become the hardest to attend. he just reads off his lecture slides, which are just only bullet points and an occasional picture. the topics are super interesting, but the way he teaches it makes it so hard to pay attention. the tests are online but he only gives a minute for each question.

Go to class because he takes attendance through tophat or written dicsussion questions. There are a lot of required texts, but you don't really have to buy as most are free online. Weekly quizze s& tests- you only have a minute per question which is rushed. He also rushes in lecture a lot. Topic was interesting if you read Percy Jackson as a kid.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This might be one of the most mind-numbingly boring classes I've taken in my entire life.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Makes the class extremely hard. There is not enough time to take the tests and the reading if difficult to understand. Do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was lowkey really hard for a gen ed credit. I found it uninteresting and he gave us only a minute per question on tests and quizzes to answer which felt really rushed. Go to class because he does take attendance through TopHat.

Professor Lundell is hilarious and he's super passionate about C205. I took this class fully online durning COVID 2021 so he might be different when in person. But my experience was awesome and super easy. You need to show up but I honestly just looked over lectures, went to class, and read BARELY anything I was suppose to.

This is my favorite class this term! He is such a funny and inspiring professor! He always makes mythology fun, especially when starting the class with clips relating to the topic. He gives a very thorough summary for the reading. There's a lot of reading, but so long as you do it and attend the lectures, you'll get easy A's on quizzes and tests.

I would advise against taking this class. The tests are worth 75% of the course grade, so if you dont do as well on the tests youre pretty much out of luck. The pop quizzes can also be difficult . Way too hard of a class for the A & H credit. Youd be better off taking another class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I really liked Professor Lundell, but his class is way too difficult for an A&H and World Cultures credit. His exams and pop quizzes offer choices A thru E, with each answer choice being quite nitpicky and specific. If you take this class you will read a lot of boring material that is difficult to understand. Very few grades in the grade book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: You can tell that he loves his job very much, but he is very nit-picky about the questions he puts on his questions that can make it very hard to do well on the quizzes and tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You can tell from the first day that Professor Lundell truly cares about what he has to teach and that makes the world of a difference. Honestly, as long as you go over the PowerPoint and listen to his lectures, the tests will be incredibly easy.

Professor Lundell truly loves the class that he teaches. His passion for the class allows him to make connections within his lectures that make a long class much more entertaining. I did well in the class, but paid good attention in class and did lots of the assigned work. If you are prepared to read and pay attention in class you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lundell is a super cool guy, but his class is tough. He lectures all day everyday, with a lot of outside reading and studying required. Pop quizzes suck if you don't read. Tests aren't bad if you pay attention and put in the time to learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Too much reading and full lectures every class.  Exams are 75% of the grade so even though I got almost all the participation points and did fine on quizzes, still didn't get the grade I wanted. Only reason to take it is for WC and A&H credits in one class. Would not recommend this class, makes me hate mythology.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Lundell is a great professor and really cares about what he is teaching. He is lecture heavy but he keeps it interesting. You have to read a lot and there's reading due for each lecture. He has 6 pop quizzes that are only 5 questions and are pretty easy. 5 clicker points a day. Exams are pretty easy as long as you've pay attention to the slides

Lundell is a heavy lecturer. The quizzes take a chunk out of your grade if you don't do the readings but tests are easy to study for b/c of the study guide.  You get like 1 or 2 quiz grades dropped. He's not a bad lecturer though and makes some pretty funny jokes every once in a while.  He plays videos occasionally. Today we watched Star Trek.

He really is a great professor and passionate about what he teaches. Wants the students to succeed just isn't ... that good at it. Exams are tough and the pop quizzes can be brutal. You must be prepared to read. Read. READ. A LOT. Don't fall behind. Best of luck, because I couldn't keep up.

He is a great teacher but the course requires a lot of material be covered. The final covers 7 Greek tragedies so if you aren't ready to read don't take the class. He does his best to make connections between Ancient Greek myths and stories to modern day things as well as making corny but funny jokes. He is a great teacher.

Had Lundell for Greek mythology. He's a pretty funny guy but made the class pretty difficult. You have lots of quizzes. I wouldn't recommend taking a class with him unless you are ready to read and study a lot.

The lectures can feel long at times, but Prof. Lundell does a good job keeping things interesting (but I was pretty interested in the subject from the start). The tests are pretty easy, just reread the slides before the test and pay attention in class.
Great teacher, easy going, and is pretty funny.
An absolute terrible professor. Turned my friend who was a lover of mythology into a myth fiend. I'd pay my life savings to have his degrees ripped from his name. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES!
