Loved this professor!  Sometimes difficult to understand due to his accent, but otherwise a great professor.
Karo is a great professor. Shout out to the OG for real.

Karo's class is average. It can sometimes be hard to understand because he has a very thick accent but you get used to it quickly. He will usually do the assignments along with you in class which is awesome. The content is understandable as long as you come to class. A couple of big group projects but nothing terrible.

The class is fine and Its easy to get a good grade if you just do the assignments. He is very nice but hard to understand at points and class is super early. You can miss class but there are random in class assignments some days.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She's funny. The class are pretty easy IF YOU READ AND REMEMBER what she taught in class. She likes to teach something that is out of textbook------but i think it doesnt be a problem bcs it can give u more knowledge lol.   I RECOMMEND U TO TAKE L104 WITH PROF ODLE!!!
Gives a ton of extra credit even though the class is already pretty easy. The course grade is 90% exams, but you get to drop one. She's funny in lecture, too.

She is a genuinely nice lady but her tests are harder than they need to be. Odle makes her class easier than it seems for a majority of the semester, and I felt like I knew the material until the test was in front of me.

Odle is awesome. She was so so nice and funny. Everyone should take human bio with Odle. Tests are very straight forward. She also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. You can raise your grade by 10% easily if you have great attendance! Take 104 with Odle!!!!!
super nice and pretty funny lady. Gives lecture skeletons that really help and opportunities for extra credit. straight forward tests.

DON'T TAKE IF PRE-MED/DENT. Material she covers is not the material you need for the MCAT/DAT. You need to know systems, and she doesn't cover any of that. I had to relearn all of it. I UTA for Zolan/Beckers now, and the material they teach is much more clear and more important. Odle's lectures were so disorganized too. Really really really bad.

Odle is a good teacher. While her lectures are disorganized and boring her tests are very straight forward and come from the skeletons which she provides. She offers extra credit quizes and tests which can add up to 10% of your grade! Keep in mind that you cant fail a test or you fail the entire class, so work hard and youll do fine.

Professor Odle is very hard to understand. Her lectures consist of pictures only, and she can never figure out how to adjust her mic so you can hear her. Tests are vague and tricky. Class is very disorganized. If you want to pass you HAVE to read all the chapters assigned. I was never excited for class, I wanted to leave after attendance.

There is no curve, only a maximum of 10% extra credit. She's also the kind of prof to make you memorize the main 20 amino acids and put questions about them on the test, when it's really not necessary at this level of biology. I found reading the book 100x more helpful than her rambling lectures, but her lectures are important to follow too.

Make sure you read the syllabus if you fail her final then you fail the class even if prior to it you have an A. I had a B+  and even after the final score wise it took me to a high C but due to the rule I failed the course. So keep this in mind before you take her class

Such an interesting woman with a good sense of humor, but the class is over all kind of difficult. Lectures can be hard to follow. Tests are all multiple choice. A lot of extra credit is offered though (do it! it helps boost your grade a lot!) and she gives practice tests that are very helpful.
If you are reading this, sign up for Joan Lafuze. You'll thank me when you get the A instead of the high C.

Her english is fine. Her tests are difficult in that they are tricky, multiple-choice questions. Although, tests are not unreasonable; they just require a lot of studying. She offers extra credit (EC) exams and quizzes.  Perfect attendance is required if you want any of your EC points. I didn't particularly like the skeletons or going to lecture.

This course is technically for non-science majors, but students without a background in science may find it challenging. I learned a lot in the class and retained a lot of the information. Dr. Odle adds a big lump of extra credit at the end of the semester, so don't worry if your grade is less than perfect before the final.

I wouldn't recommend taking Professor Odle. I'm usually a good student, but her class was way too difficult for a 100-level. Almost NOTHING that she taught was on the tests. The tests were completely random. I worked so hard in this class- had perfect attendance, read the book, studied the notes- but could only pull a B. Think twice before taking.

Dr. Odle has a very low comprehension of some important points of the English language, which leads to very poorly worded exams. While the material is not hard, she seems to barely understand some of it, but I mostly attribute this to a poor grasp of the English language.

You can earn up to 10% extra credit with perfect attendance which really helps. Her practice exams help a LOT. Memorize them and read the skeletons and you'll do well. 95% of the final is questions from previous exams which makes it really easy. Easy B, an A if you work hard.

Chooi is a wonderful woman who I've really connected with during my semester. Unfortunately, she does the best she can to make it easy, but it doesn't work. I do like biology and I worked my ass off, but I will probably still get a high B in the class. Her exams are difficult, extra credit helps, but only so much. I feel I did not retain most info.

Prof. Chooi's lectures are horrible, there is no flow and nothing you learn in class or read about will be on the exams. The only thing that can save you is to have perfect attendance and do outstandingly well on the "extra credit" exams.

Prof. Chooi's lectures are horrible, there is no flow and nothing you learn in class or read about will be on the exams. The only thing that can save you is to have perfect attendance and do outstandingly well on the "extra credit" exams.

It seems there are some mixed feelings about Yean Chooi (oodle). If you are good at biology then you will probably like this class. If you are just an average/non major student, as the description of the class says that it is for, you will probably hate it and do horrible like I did. The information is very quite interesting and her anecdotes are f

Odle is hilarious but her lectures are COMPLETELY worthless.  Honestly, coming to class is only to get extra credit.  Her tests are significantly harder than what you do in class.  The only reason it's so "easy" to get a good grade is the extra credit.

Pretty interesting class. Not that hard if you've had any prior biology knowledge. The extra credit exams help a lot. Have to read the book before tests. If you pay attention and attend, you should get an A.
sorta hard

More demanding than most 100 level, but an A is possible.My advice is read the book A LOT, go to classes, not because their really helpful, but you get extra credit and she'll tell you random facts that will many times appear on the test. the skeletons are useless. and the final is made up of about 65% of the review final so that helps a lot.

The class was fair and interesting. The extra credit exams are a great opportunity to boost your grade before an exam and the homework is not very intensive. Odle was knowledgeable and accessible. The skeletons weren't incredibly useful, but if you pay moderate attention in class and do the readings you'll be fine.

Was a little more difficult that your average 100 level class. If attendance wasn't mandatory it wouldn't be worth coming. She gets on random tangents about her research more than she teachs. The skeletons are not useful, and she won't provide any of the diagrams that consist of 95% of the overheads. No curves. 10% EC exams before real exams.

Overall, just not that great of a class.  Not terrible though.  If you're looking to get an easy A, not your type of class.  Study a lot (not w/ the skeletons) and read the chapters front to back and you'll do fine.  However, don't just review previous exams n prac test for the final like she recommends.  You'll get screwed over.

If you don't read the book before lecture, the material covered in class may be difficult to follow; however, before each exam (not including the final exam), she offers an extra credit exam where you get bonus points AND you can get a feel for what to expect on the real exam... and... shes hilarious!!!

I love Professor Chooi (as she prefers to be called). She is super friendly and tells fun stories in class. Not to mention that our practice/extra credit exams are a good study guide for the test. 85% of what's written on them is on the test.

All the reviews are pretty accurate. Going to lecture is pretty much pointless except for the fact that she takes attendance and loves pop quizzes that consist of 2 and only 2 questions. The only way I got a good grade in her class was by literally reading, taking notes, and reviewing like crazy all the chapters assigned for each test.
There's nothing wrong with Odle, I'm not sure why all the animosity towards her and her teaching methods. I found her tests to be fair. She was funny and smokin' hot too.

Terrible teacher. Doesn't seem to care about students. Extroadinarily difficult and unfair exams. Completely memorize the chapters out of the book and hope for the best. You will not learn anything in this class if you take it with her.

Somewhat decent professor but this class was way too hard for a 100 level nonmajor course.  Expect to study like a maniac if you want to do well in this class.  In retrospect I wouldn't have taken this course if I knew  how much students were expected to know for the exams and how low the class GPA was - over 80% of students received less than a B.

I just finished this class and am so upset. I had a B- going into the final and just took the hardest final of my life. Across the board people said this exam wass extremely hard and unexpected. If you fail this too no matter what your grade is you fail the class. She rambles in lecture and is not a good teacher. Do Not take her class.

The exams are unpredictable and never resemble the EC exams. She doesn't spend that much time going over the material in lecture, so going to lecture is basically a waste of time and attendence is required.

Professor Odle just doesn't really understand how to teach.  She does not explain important biological concepts nor do her exams come close to matching what she discusses in lecture.  I would not recommend her if you actually want to learn something about biology.

She is great fun and entertaining, but easily digresses from course material.  She spends a lot of time talking about who discovered what, and how she knows so-and-so who discovered this process blah blah, INSTEAD of teaching the material.  She gives a lot of extra credit, but it is needed because here multiple choice exams are unpredictable.
No Comments

Dr. Ogan is possibly the worst professor I've ever had. The class was supposed to be a business communication class, but it seemed more fitted as a sociology class, if even a class at all. The tests are all subjective. Participate in class and go to her office hours, otherwise she'll grade you more harshly. Avoid if at all possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Ogan is one of the best professors I have had. She keeps up with recent events in the news and uses them as a class discussion point. She also remembers her students and pays attention to them, which is really nice to have. I really enjoyed her class and it was a good break from the rest of my classes because she forces you to participate.
my pet potato was bored to tears and it doesn't usually cry

Lectures are focused on technology, not actual journalism, REALLY boring. Takes attendence and gives quizzes. Exams are boring and based on lectures and some reading. Can get away with out doing a lot in this class.
SO BORING! She does not make the class interesting at all. There is also a lot of reading.

AWFUL. His class should be an online class but attendance is required...Wikipedia.com is NOT a textbook...and the ENTIRE class is based off that and howstuffworks.com, including exams! Class is a WASTE of time and he doesnt know what hes talking about...he never works problems out in class n laughs at the students when they get clicker points wrong

Great Guy, who is real interested in what he is teaching, makes the class much more fun. For cellphones, he taught a lot of things that were very interesting and completely unknown to me! Every class checks and discusses recent technology news. Real good class experience.

This class was very intersting.  You learn about how lots of things work and how they are integrated into your cell phone.  Professor Ogren appears to enjoy his job and is willing to help when you need it.  Very friendly.  This is a great class to take for N&M credit.

he is the best professor at IU as far as I am concerned. You dont have to work very hard to get A. Just read the materials he provided on line and review the WIKI page. Easy clicker questions in class and regular exams and the final exam. If u dont do well in the exams, u r allowed to write the make up paper (usually everyone got the full cr for th

He is a good teacher and the subject is interesting.  There is very little that you need to do in this class.  The tests are challenging, but you are allowed to do a make up paper for a good amount of test points back.

Sometimes his quiz/test questions can be a little tricky but pay attention, keep up with the readings and you should do fine. You use a clicker and this keeps track of attendance but it also counts towards daily points. It totals out of 4 (2 questions a day, 2 pts each. 1 pt for attendance, 1 pt for the question)
He knows what hes talking about but he wanders a lot and goes kind of fast.  Not my most fun experience.
This class is a waste of time.

Professor Ogren is an excellent professor. Everything in the class is straight forward and there are no tricks. Uses the Wiki feature on oncourse instead of having all the students buy an expensive text books, which works out great. Do not listen to what the students said who reviewed him poorly. They don't belong in college.
HE MAKES NO SENSE! You can tell that he is passionate about what he is trying to teach, however this class lacks one major aspect- HE DOES NOT TEACH! He he not understanding at all!

This class makes no sense! When I asked prof a question about the class material he said "I don't know, figure it out"--a prof is supposed to at least hint the student in the right direction! THis class bites!

This class is aweful! There is no structure to the course and no textbook, instead of a book students are expected to look and know the websites that he provides on oncourse. Surfing the web looking for one stupid little answer is a complete waste of time. Although the prof is nice, and approachable he is not helpful at all.
Very good teacher. He sometimes digresses, but keeps things interesting.  I recommend his classes to everyone.

Prof. Ogren is a good professor whose enthusiam for teaching sometimes borders on the amusing. A fair grader, his exams are straightforward and no one should have a problem getting an A in his class provided you make the effort.

Full respect for this professor. I genuinely enjoyed her class. Class grade was based on 4 assignments: attendance, an exam, a short group paper, and a final short individual paper, all graded leniently. Overall, what mattered most is that you learned from her lectures and asked questions. Am taking another one of her classes. Amazing!

Dysfunctional class with Prof. Ojeda. 90% of grade from two unclear assignments and exam. Due dates exceed withdrawal period, making personal assessment impossible. Grading seems subjective, lectures boring with little understanding. No clear lesson plan, avoid class and professor.
DON'T TAKE HER CLASS. Doesn't even have the decency to respond to emails during finals week. She won't help and only wants to hurt your grade.

I would highly recommend not to take this course with Professor Ojeda. She only graded off of three assignments in which she graded super tough. Her lectures make no sense, and you have no idea what's actually going on. Look for another International Studies course because for whatever reason, you can't get a good grade in this one.
Great teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is super sweet. Lots of reading, but its over pretty interesting stuff. I recommend doing the readings because although she goes over them in class, she doesnt include all the information about them that will be on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I was very excited to take this class, I didn't know what I was in for. You read 20-40 pages for weekly discussions that are worth THREE points. Your grade is based on attendance, weekly discussions, mid term, one paper and the final exam. Which makes it hard to get a good grade if you mess up even one time. She is very dry and seems unqualified.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Prof. Okamoto is intelligent, passionate about her work, and very down to Earth. She speaks to students as equals, rather than subordinates, and is clearly very passionate about her field. Her lectures can be dry, and the level of reading is not for everyone, but I genuinely loved coming to her class (and talking to her during office hours).
She is amazing. That's all I have to say! Take her for M405.
Jenny has amazing energy! She is very organized and makes class painless. Technically, attendance isn't taken. The exams are online and she posts the powerpoints too! Loved this class.

Jenny is one of the best profs I've had at IU. Super engaging and cares about both the content and her students. Be prepared to participate in class, but it's pretty low stakes. Also there's a research project, but it's not too bad as long as you start decently early. Definitely choose her for Consumer Behavior!

Great person and professor! She's very nice and her lectures were super interesting and she was good at explaining things. Exams were online and a little difficult but not terrible. Not a lot of homework.

Prof Olson is one of the best professor I've had in Kelley. She is very knowledgeable in consumer behavior, let along her charming personality and willingness to get to know each student personally. Her classes were always insightful and engaging. The tests and projects weren't so difficult, but make sure you take good notes. A great class overall!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Prof Olson is a really fun professor and is good at explaining the material. She's good at making the content interesting, you can't go wrong with her.
Prob the best professor I've had so far. Super laid back and explains everything really well. To do well in K-201 just go to class and do the practice questions from the workbook. Highly recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: GREAT! He is so funny and wants you to do your best. I loved his lectures and he made K201 feel very very easy.
Such a nice professor and explains everything so well. Great teacher and great class, do all of the work and you'll get a good grade.

Mr. Oh was my lab instructor for K201, and I couldn't be happier that it was him. He clearly taught the material and provided the tools necessary to prepare for the exams. If you have the option of taking Mr. Oh for K201 do it.

Professor Oh is hands down my favorite professor of all time. He does such a good job explaining the material and makes a concious effort to learn all his students names. His labs are full of content but as long as you stay focused you will learn. He loves to joke around and make the class fun. If you have space, take his class. He's the GOAT.
Amazing prof for k201, went above and beyond to make his own presentations and extra practice for exams. Super helpful explaining and super nice guy. Best k201 prof
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a nice and helpful professor and wants his students to succeed. He provides good resources before every exam and teaches you everything you need to know in an understandable way. He tries to know people's names and notices participation. His lectures can move pretty fast, but just do all the optional prep before/after class and participate!

Great Professor, had him for K201 lecture. Weekly assignments are graded on completion and projects are nothing to stress too hard about. The only thing to worry about is the participation assignments, which must be done during class within the 10 or so minutes you get. Ended K201 lecture with a 330/330 grade. Overall Great Guy.
Great k201 lecture professor!
He is amazing

I had Professor Oh for the lab portion of K201. He was always prepared for class and did an excellent job covering the material. The pacing was smooth, the examples were clear, and he did a good job of getting a feel for the room. I had experience with Excel prior to the class, so I thought the content was easy. My class also had a great TA!

I had Prof Oh for the lecture part of K-201 and wish I had him for both sections. Hes really nice and a great teacher. Lecture is the easy part of K-201 focusing mostly on the group project and its online so I didn't really get to know him but I recommend him for either section of K-201

Really great professor who is quick paced and efficient. He is understanding and cares abt students. Always willing to help. Great at explaining logic and getting students to engage. Take him for K-201!

K201 is scary for a lot of people, but Professor Oh did everything in his power to make the class enjoyable and palatable. Just do what he says with the discoveries and find a few people you can go to with questions and to compare work. Everything I've heard about K-Cove is bad so I wouldn't rely on that. You'll be fine.

He is an amazing professor he made this class feel like a breeze. coming in I thought it was a hard class but having him it was so much easier. he is also very good at getting back with you and your requests and one thing is to make sure to follow all the rules and guidelines within assignments. He is very strict on that and won't make exceptions.
He is GREAT! Made K201 so much easier to understand compared to other classes. My test scores were great because I knew what I was doing. Made a hard class much easier.
He uses class time very efficiently and we finished early pretty much every time.
Great guy and cares a lot about students
Such a beast my favorite professor of all time

Professor Oh is one of the best I've had here at IU. He explains K201 concepts very well, and he works hard to help us all learn and prepare for the exams. His grading criteria and class expectations are very clear. So long as you put in the work outside of class (discoveries, reviews, etc), you will be fine in K201. Take it with him if you can!

K201 is a tought class, so be sure to work hard during the lecture portion. Mr. Oh's class is a good way to boost your overall K201 grade, so take it seriously. Attend the lectures and take the group project as seriously as you can. This class is basically 300 free points that will boost up your K201 grade (and you will need it).

Harvey made k201 very interesting, he was clear when explaining the topics and genuinely cares about the students in his section. He doesn't check to see if the discoveries are done, and lab checks are straightforward, open-excel.
Great professor. Very nice and helpful. Cares about his students.
Great professor, takes time during class to allow everyone to catch up. Take him for k201.
Very good professor with straight forward lectures. Would definitely recommend taking him for K201 if you can. Also offers great help and explanations if you ask.
Mr. Oh is fantastic! He makes k201 alot easier than it is thought to be, he is very kind and loves his students! I would take k201 again just to be in his class again
Good professor, try and take him for k201 if you can

I currently have Mr. Oh as my teacher for K201, the class itself is difficult but Mr. Oh makes the material come as naturally as possible. He and the TA's are very accessible outside of class. He doesn't leave any student behind and he refuses to let class continue until all questions have been answered. He is a great teacher and a great guy.
Mr. Oh uses various examples to explain concepts. Attend classes and make sure to complete the discovery and review problems.

I had him spring semester and it was his first semester. I was pretty nervous since it was his first semester, but he ended up explaining everything well. He makes the harder concepts understandable and will even help you while teaching the class.

Although K201 is known as being brutal and this was Professor Oh's first semester teaching at IU, he was great!  He made the material easy to understand and was very humorous during lab to uplift the classroom and make the class enjoyable. Had I gone to class more often, I could've significantly done better. Don't be scared for K201 if you have Oh.

Mix of assignments (field trips, oral presentation, Jeopardy-style test prep that was super fun). Lots of small group discussion. Lectured too fast. Take screen shots of her lecture slides because she doesn't wait for students to finish taking notes on them. Long tests, but with clear grading expectations. Pleasant but formal.
Profe is amazing and I would honestly like to take future courses of hers. She helped me realized I want to double major in Spanish!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Rosenthal was very knowledgeable about Hispanic Literature.  This class is discussion heavy so be prepared before class.  She can be a tough grader so pay attention to details on your projects, papers and assignments.  Overall she is very sweet and I would take another one of her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really incredible class. The content is fascinating and Prof. Rosenthal is very helpful. Participation will make or break the grade. Attending lecture is absolutely necessary! Prof. Rosenthal is kind and available inside/outside of class for help. The course has a lot of information to learn and is dense, but it will be worth it to learn so much.

The material and the class overall is not terrible, however, Prof. Rosenthal was always condescending to me and made me feel uncomfortable in class. I always did the readings and almost always participated in class, yet she still talked to me as if I was struggling in the class. I was scared to go to her with questions and was happy class ended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Classes mostly consist of discussions over the readings, in small groups or the class as a whole. She writes down important points on the boards for students to know what to write down in their own notes. Very fair grader on essays and gives good feedback. Exams are decently difficult but she still grades pretty fairly on them.

Super interesting class, participation really matters(!!!), tests require rote memorization and analysis so don't let that catch you off guard and use Quizlet or something. She offers extra credit - take it!! She's clearly super knowledgeable and wants students to engage with the material. Tough, but 100% worth it.

Like all Spanish classes at IU, you will have to read and participate a lot. Olimpia is very kind and knowledgeable. This was the last class I took to complete my minor and was by far my favorite. I would absolutely recommend Olimpia for any class, she's wonderful.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She's a good professor and is very knowledgeable about cultures and backgrounds. There is a lot of homework due each class (long readings either in English or Spanish followed by guides about the readings in Spanish); most of this information is then re-taught via powerpoint after turning in the homework. Participation is a huge part of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Choose a different instructor if possible!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rosenthal is passionate and knowledgeable about her subject, and she definitely takes her job seriously. However, she doesn't take the time to get to know her students nor share much about herself. If you have anxiety, I don't recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Olimpia is a nice person and made interesting lectures, but her class gave me an anxiety attack every day because your grade is VERY heavily based on participation. She also was a relatively hard grader and never made clear what exactly she was looking for in her short answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Olimpia is very knowledgable and enthusiastic in her teaching. There is a TON of reading in this class. Sometimes the combination of length, complex Spanish, and use of abstract ideas made the readings very overwhelming. Overall though, Olimpia is always willing to explain things more clearly and help students who need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Olimpia was always extremely kind, available for office hours, willing to give feedback, a relatively easy grader but it's a lot of work, primarily reading. and she was alwasy very personable
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Olimpia is passionate and very knowledgeable about Hispanic cultures. Lectures were full of art, music, and other interesting facts. She cares about seeing each student succeed, but is a tough grader and expects each student to go above and beyond with participation. There is also a lot of reading, but it is all very interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Olga is so awesome and anyone in geography related fields should take a class with her. The food geography class is so interesting and she really puts a lot of thought and effort into the class. She is a knowledgeable chef and guided everyone through becoming better cooks and having more diverse palettes. She is hilarious and kind

Readings outside of class have to be done because we discuss them in class. Attendance is very important and make sure to raise your hand in class. She is very nice and communicative. I liked her but did not like the class.

She likes to teach about the topic and is very knowledgeable, but I wish this class were online. attendance is required, but like I said, it would have been better for it to be done online. a family member of mine passed away too, and I emailed her about it, and she never responded to me.

I took GEOG-G325 (Food and Poverty in America) with Dr. Kalentzidou. She is highly knowledgeable in social science, but the class lacked structure. If you attend class and complete the assignments, you will do fine.

I'm currently enrolled in this course and could not tell you a single thing we've learned. Grades are made up of random readings and assignments that have nothing to do with the course and a semester long project that lacks any sense of clear guidelines. The professor walks around the class and makes it feel like your fault you've learned nothing.
She always criticizes your answers and makes you feel dumb for participating in class. She expects you to be experts on the readings after reading them once.

Olga is such an interesting and caring professor. She has creative projects for her classes, and through her Geography of Food class, I gained new insight into the world of food. Talk to her about her life - it's fascinating. Also, she's a fantastic cook, and you'll learn a lot from her if you take a cooking class with her.

The main part of the course is a group project that takes the whole semester. Classtime that could have been used for groupwork was instead used for Olga's random, non related assignments and unhelpful lectures. You also better pray that your groupmates are good students because if not she will force you to carry them them through anyway.

Random assignments would be worth a massive portion of your grade. We had to interview another student in class and write a summary of what they said. This seemingly meaningless assignment was 15% of our grade. Some assignments  had nothing to do with the overall goal of class. The class is almost exclusively group work with few exceptions.
My favorite professor! Everyone in our class and others that have had her really enjoy and like her. Lots of readings every week but easy to keep up on. Course topics are interesting as well.

Olga is generally a pretty good professor.  Definitely nice, lenient about deadlines if you talk to her about them.  She knows a lot about a wide variety of subjects and she usually has interesting things to say about international disputes.  If you're taking International Studies classes, she's a good professor to get!
Super nice, good prof. Cares about students. Class was easy but still learned. Lecture heavy but she keeps it interesting by talking about current events. Easy grader. No exams
Easy class, Prof Olsen just wants us to pay attention and show up to class. If you do that, you'll get a good grade. Tests are online and open book. Attendance affected our grade.

Great professor, its an interesting class that she ties real world examples to make it more worthwhile. I enjoyed this class, am glad I took it with her, and would recommend. This wasn't a topic I was particularly interested in going into it, but ended up being really cool!

Professor Olsen is by far my favorite professor I've had at IU. I absolutely loved her class. If you put in the work and go to class you'll get an A. This was my first class I've taken through Eskenazi and I'm so happy she was my professor because she was the biggest inspiration for me to declare apparel merchandising as my minor.

Professor Olsen is one of the best professors I've had at IU. She's always available to help and is such a nice person. This class can be challenging but as long as you take notes and pay attention in class, you'll be fine. The homework isn't too hard
Super nice professor, her class is really easy but you have to show up. Really enjoyed her guest speakers, and she really tries to help students with personal development.

Professor Olsen's lectures were very informative and she would insert her personal experience. She also brought had a lot of guest lecturers speak which was great. Only negative was that she would assign a lot of work and it would be worth very little. For example, we'd have to watch hours worth of vids for only a 10 points. Otherwise, great class!
A lot of work for a class that doesn't need it. Very hard grader. Doesn't accept late work under ANY circumstances. I had mono and couldn't leave my bed and she still wouldn't extend a deadline.

The course I am taking is Time Series Analysis. 

I think Professor Scrivner is knowledgeable in the topic, but ultimately has not structured the course in a very linear way - it seems some of the topics a few weeks in should have been the initial foundational topics. 

I also think the lectures lack an explanation of motivation or context.

Excellent professor. Terrific asynchronous lectures and examples. Provides graded practice that is key to succeeding in assignments. Works with students to overcome student learning obstacles.  You have the opportunity to learn much more than just the basic material, although you will do fine in the course with simply the foundation she provides.

Reads through slides, but doesn't do anything else to help with learning. Is unable to answer questions about web programming and instead replies with her own questions. The only good thing is that she grants extensions for assignments.

The course (NLP) is online and mostly based on datacamp certifications. There a few video lectures from the professor and they are bad to put midly. Very hard to follow and slow. I got the felling that someone is just reading from notes which just have bullets points. You are not going to get deeper understanding of the course.

Great professor. Good material and she is available outside of class if needed. She does have a few preferences she is very specific about, but if you follow along, ask questions and get involved with the work, you will really enjoy the class. Its all very manageable.

Poorly designed class. Topics were out of synch, and didn't progress in an efficient manner. Objectives were not clear nor were many of the assignments. Professor responded harshly to questions and said we should ask other students (i wonder, then what a professor is for, if not to teach?). Not a hard grader, but not interested in teaching.

Olga speaks many more languages than just Spanish and it was very hard to understand what she wanted us to do in class.  She was a hard grader on the writing portions.  She did give us candy/cookies randomly.  Wouldn't recommend taking her class if you can choose someone else.  I ended with an A but had to get good test and homework grades.

Olivia was an amazing prof. She was super kind, and she clearly cared about her students. She saw us more than just students, but as people. She was flexible when students has personal matters, and considerate of the fact that we had other classes besides her. She is also extremely knowledgeable about what she teaches, and is super passionate.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Olivia is by far one of my favorite professors I have ever had in college! She is constantly there for her students and relates very well to topics we all face in life. She provides great resources for everyone to look back on even after the class and talks about her research , which is very interesting! Fair grader and keeps content relatable.
She grades you on every little thing, very detail oriented, also always thinks she is correct and no one else is, unless she agrees with you.
Very understanding during the covid semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: She was really kind and very helpful. I went in to this class not knowing what to expect and came out as a gender studies minor. She was awesome and a very good instructor. She is very clear on how she grades and gives several tips for assignments during lecture. If you're not big on talking in class for participation points, she gives extra credit

mom, i wanna be him when i grow up. for the love of god, please attend lecture because dr.sporns is such an inspirational lecturer. super passionate about his research and supporting all of his students.

One of the most interesting course and professor. He was on Morgan Freeman's podcast and achieved many interesting things but a very humble person. Grades on few things so important to do them to earn good grades. His lectures based on his own research and others he's familiar with so lectures are always amazing.

Most genuine professor ever. You have the chance to learn about some really cool stuff that Prof Sporns is passionate about without the dooming stress of exams that make or break your grade. The exams are take-home and Prof is more than willing to go over them with you before they are due. The presentation portion is easy 100% if you do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: 3 take-home exams (all the answers come right from the slides), 1 partner paper presentation, and participation. But, don't worry if you don't love to participate in class, you can schedule office hours to talk with him about literally anything for participation. Also an easy opportunity for extra credit at the end. I got 102% easily.

Worked hard to raise my grade close to an A-, but he wouldnt round up and gave me a B+. His class was hard to focus in because it was an hour and 15 minutes long. Your grade depended on the exams and participation. Hard class to do well in if you have ADHD because you will lose focus and you need your lecture notes for the exams. Good luck :(
Best Nuero teacher. Class is not mandatory. Either go to class or read the power points. Only need to book if you confused and need a reference. Test are easy as long as you know the power points
Clear, Concise, Honest, Fair, and Flexible doesn't even begin to describe this man. Always a pleasure to attend one of his lectures.

Very nice professor. Is extremely helpful, and likes to make small jokes throughout the lectures to try and keep the material interesting. Tests are based entirely off of lecture notes and many questions come straight from the quizzes (not graded--he gives these 'quizzes' to help students better understand the material).

Sporns is a great prof. Tests are from the notes. Either read the book or go to class, one or the other, and you'll easily get an A. He's always available to meet up concerning coursework. He's also interested in hearing about any research you're interested in. Great person and professor.
Grade determined by 4 non-cumulative tests, all off slides, there's even extra credit on tests! I dreaded taking Neuro, and I'll end up with an easy A+.

Prof Sporns is an absolutely great professor! Obviously extremely intelligent. He will occasionally crack little jokes to keep your interest because he has this really soothing voice that can put you to sleep sometimes. 100% recommended and the tests are straight from his notes. You really don't even need the textbook, though it can be helpful

I learned a lot from this course and still refer to Dr. Sporns's notes for other neuroscience classes. The prof covers a lot of material each lecture, but the exam questions are pulled directly from the notes. I wouldn't say the course is particularly challenging in terms of grades, but it is definitely interesting.

Amazing prof, he is aware of how boring the material is so he tries to crack a joke every now and then.  His intelligence is obvious and he is working on awesome projects, pretty easy too, don't even have to open up the textbook.

Takes a few classes to get used to his accent, but Professor Sporns is great.  The neuroscience material is difficult, but he is very thorough and doesn't skip the details. Pop quizzes every once in a while, and tests are a mix of MC, fill-in, and T/F, so study hard!

Prof is great! He's very nice, down to earth, and explains everything clearly. The material is quite difficult, but the class is very straightforward. No surprises on the tests, just know the material from the slides well. Study ahead of time, and go to office hours! He's very friendly!! Read the material before class.

Olaf is a friendly, very intelligent prof who makes neuro as easy to learn as possible. Tests are straightforward and cover the lecture slides; you don't necessarily even need to go to class to do well. But it's fun to go just to listen to him talk. He's pretty funny and has a great accent. You won't get a more laid-back prof for neuro, so get him
Hard Material, know the notes very well. gotta go to class. makes it much easier.

Olaf is great! I had no interest in neuroscience coming into the class, but he made it very interesting and easy to learn. This class is not hard - just go over the lecture slides a lot. You don't have to go to class, but I enjoyed going because of Olaf's little jokes every now and then. He's extremely intelligent, and a very good professor!

Lectures were really helpful. He gives you powerpoint slides which are great because there are a lot of diagrams. Tests focused on the main points of the class. Textbook isn't really necessary if you attend class regularly and pay attention.

Hard material but hes really good at teaching it. He makes neuroscience really easy to understand. He is extremely helpful and wants students to do well. Just study your class notes before the test and you will get an A. He posts all notes online too.

It's a tough course but he's a good professor.  He's actually pretty funny if you listen in class.  Homework and tests are hard, but he explains everything pretty well in lecture.  Take him for stats, I've heard he's the best prof you can get.

The best statistics teacher! Very clear at explaining and very down to earth. Very funny and enjoyable to listen to. Wants students to do well and helps you by giving practice tests and non-graded quizzes before tests.

I have taken courses with her for the last 6 semesters. I took three years of Swahili and she is the sweetest professor ever. She also grades relatively easy as long as you show up and do your assignments. She also allows you to makeup and gives good feedback. MY FAV PROFESSOR AT IUB!!

Professor is very dedicated to teaching the course material to you as easy as possible. Learning a new language is never the easiest but this was one of my favorite courses because of the professor. Attendance is taken because new material is gone over almost daily.

Professor Alwiya made this semester so wonderful for me. She is a great teacher that truly cares about students and takes the time out of her life to help you learn the material. There are few tests and one group project. There are not too many assignments and attendance counts! Show up and use the book and you'll pass the class and learn some!

Swahili with Alwiya is a joy. She is so kind and hardworking. She will help if you ask for it. Class sizes are small and attendance matters. There are no tests but instead a few written and oral assessments throughout the semester. The class is fun and fairly easy for a foreign language.

Professor Ondrik's class was always very fun, and was a great way to stay creative, as a business major. Although the class is 3 hours long, and a lot of time is necessary outside of class for shooting images, I thoroughly enjoyed the class. He understands that we are beginners, and offers helpful advice and criticisms.

Deadlines are very set and would not budge, be prepared to use lab hours. Other than deadlines feeling rushed, he is an amazing professor and is very involved with helping students with their questions and concerns. Also has a bit of dry and awkward humor, but personally I think he is hilarious.

Professor Ondrik is very knowledgeable about his craft. Grading criteria and rubric were detailed and informative, and you get feedback on each in-class project as well. Lectures focused on history of photography, discussion sections focused on project prep. Certainly a course worth taking to learn more about photography.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quite harsh for new photographers. Lots of interesting photography history but I wish the class was more technical. I enjoy his sense of humor but he comes across slightly awkward and condescending at times. I can't bring myself to dislike him though. If you find yourself even a little lost at the start of the semester, be prepared to put in work.

One of my favorite professors at IU. If youre actually interested in photography, hes an amazing mentor and gives some really great feedback to help you get better at the craft. His humor isnt for everybody but he knows what hes talking about and is at the perfect level of professional/ not stuffy. Fair grader and interesting projects.

As far as photography professors goes, he's one of the best I've had. A little unprofessional in the classroom and also is a know-it-all (as many teachers are), but obviously cares about his craft. Gives big projects, as well as in-progresses, and smaller activities. Sometimes stressful to get all HW done in time and doesn't budge on due dates.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took Professor Ondrik's class expecting to take a fun, easy photography class that would help me learn more about my camera and shooting techniques. Instead, class lectures were not useful (more abt the history of photography) and overall a pain to go to. If you love the history of photography, take this class. If you dont like dry humor, dont.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Ondrik displays questionable content in the classroom. Attendance is mandatory, although the lectures don't support the lab activities. The professor came to class without a charged camera on the first day. Not a good first impression.

David is one of the best photo teachers I've had. Grades fairly and comes up with interesting projects that I always had fun shooting. Can be stressful getting prints done in time for critique with the printers but that goes for any IU photo class. All-around a great person and professor. Would 100% take another class taught by him!
Very nice professor. Makes the class fun and engaging.
I had the pleasure of taking two courses taught by Nina, and I wish I could have taken more. She is great at making lectures interesting, and maintaining engagement in class.

I have taken three of Nina's classes. Hands down the best professor I have had at Luddy so far. She is understanding and casual, while still making sure everyone learns the necessary material. Super fun professor! Highly recommend!

Nina is probably one of the best professors I've had at IU. She keeps lecture interesting by telling stories but can be strict at times. She understands students are under a lot of pressure and occasionally just cancels class for a mental health day which is really nice. Not a super tough grader either in my experience.
INFO 101 was a great class taught by Nina. She keeps lectures interesting by providing humor and videos, and none of the work assigned is hard at all. This class was an easy A.
Nina is an excellent teacher. She is very caring, genuine, easy-going, and smart. She is young.
Shes a kind and interesting professor. The lectures are long, but full of important information. Overall the class is a very good introduction to some types of coding and ideas in informatics.

Nina was okay and funny comments sometimes but I was mostly turned off of the class because of the lack of organization and clarity with the assignment prompts. I found myself having to ask for every assignment what she was looking for and then got an even more ambiguous answer. The grading was easy enough that it didn't really affect it much
love nina!

Nina was amazing. The class is mostly based on your labs however. The class is pretty easy if you do your homework and study before the exams. Would highly recommend Nina, she kept class entertaining and relevant.

Nina was great. She has tons of energy, is funny, and cares about students. INFO 101 itself was awful. There's so much busy work for this course, and most of it is pointless. Expect 2-3 assignments per wk. Careful, some of the pre lecture preps are really easy 10 minute quizzes, but others are long papers. Definitely look ahead at assignments.

I took I101 as an online class so I never really met Nina or Logan. The class was super easy if you just go to the labs. I had a great AI (Runqi). She was really understanding and easy on grading and was fairly quick about posting them on Canvas. As for the course, I don't think much info in the lecture class was rarely ever tested on...

I don't have any stints against Nina, but the class itself is so pointless. The lectures do not relate to anything we do in labs, and the lectures themselves are topics that Nina finds interesting that may not have any actual value in our majors/careers. The AIs for the labs take at least a month to grade tests/papers, and are not clear on anything

This was the most disappointing class I have ever taken. Being "taught" by Nina meant having random guest speakers  and papers to write about what they said. Lab is worse than lecture. The labs are taught by undergraduate students who are incapable of teaching this course. I changed my major because of how awful it was.
Nina is definitely my favorite professor at IU. Her courses are presentation based and she forms a nice rubric to help prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: We had attendance points for lecture, but even without the points, the lecture checks (homework assignments) require at least one citation from lecture, so you have to go. The labs are easy though, so no worries. Nina does a good job with the lecture, and she tries to be funny. She doesn't talk too fast, so you shouldn't have issues taking notes.
Lectures were your basic lectures, just goes off a powerpoint. Homework is a word document assignment thats due every Sunday night
Honors I101 was the easiest class I've ever taken and it's four credits. If you get the chance to take H101 definitely do it. Absolutely no prior knowledge of coding needed.
I really enjoyed the class, the topics were interesting and the coding was very basic material. I would recommend it to anyone even just barely interested in the topic.

This class is very easy. The lectures do not have required attendance, but labs do. The course content consists of a series of shallow dives into various topics. The lecture topics do not match up with the lab topics. The lectures are borderline worthless because you will only be tested over lab material.

This is one of the easiest 4 credit courses at IU. It's sad because it makes Informatics out to be a joke. Lectures are long and 90% of the class does not show up. There is A LOT of busy work, assignments that aren't even read before they are graded. Nina is not funny. Through lectures, she posts dumb memes and tells horrible jokes
This is the easiest 4 credit class IU has to offer. I loved the lectures! Nina is hilarious and makes the 75 minute lecture go really quickly.
The lectures for this class are no fun at all and the majority of kids skipped lecture every week (so did I). As long as you show up and participate in the labs you will pass the class easily.

Nina is an awesome professor. Although you only see her once a week for lecture, she keeps you interested and cracks jokes the whole time. She also offers a lot of extra credit. If you like technology, this class is a joy to take.

This is the most disappointing class I have taken in my years at IU. The information is scattered and shallow, the class has no clear content or direction, the labs are taught by undergrads with minimal knowledge of the topic, and the exams are randomized questions about minute (and unemphasized) details. A shame that it's a prerequisite. Avoid.

Nostalgic for the days of coloring in the lines and getting a pat on the back? Take this class with Nina. You'll learn to jump through arbitrary hoops, "learn" code from other undergraduates who have little to no experience, and spend the whole semester doing busy work Sunday essays. It's easy to the point of being difficult to justify taking.

This review is more for the class in general for me.  The lectures to this class are boring but the material seems to be easy as of now.  You spend most time in lab rather than lecture in this class.  I've gotten 100's on assignments with a lack of effort as of now.  Great if you are considering a major in Informatics or an easy A.

H101 was really easy. You don't interact with Nina much though; there's weekly online lectures and lots of time spent in Lab. The lectures homework is easy but boring, and in-class lectures are mostly group projectsmoviesfun stuff. Good class to take if you need an honors course and want to explore Informatics.
Nina is a great teacher. She's enthusiastic about the material, and teaches it very well. She is enjoyable to listen too, and makes lectures more fun.

This class is pointless. The lectures half the time consist of Nina just showing you random websites that she thinks are interesting, 14 consist of her talking about herself, and the final 14 is actual lecture. She gets irritated if you don't laugh at her jokes, and can be kind of rude at times.
She's really nice and has funny awkward humor. She's on your side.
Nina's class was very easy and enjoyable. She had a good sense of humor and made everything she said clear during lectures, but I'm still somewhat confused as to what informatics is.
The class is very easy, but you don't exactly learn a lot except for technology in the news.  Also, Nina can, at times, be rude.
Great professor. Very laid back but very clear and precise in the way she explained material. Has a great sense of humor and keeps the class entertained.

Nina was honestly the best professor I had all semester. She's funny, she know's how to communicate with young people, and you can tell she likes what she does. Go to class, go to the labs, do the assignments, and you should be able to pass the class. Lab instructors vary for different section numbers. Overall I give the class a 5 star rating.
Nina has been my favorite professor by far, she really makes the class interesting and enjoyable. I would recommend her to anyone.

Nina is just rad. Don't hesitate to take this class if you're interested a little. You watch interesting videos, do easy assignments, and more or less have a good time. The midterm and final are pretty straightforward, there is a decent amount of material but it's ALL covered in class explicitly and clearly.

I loved Nina! There were no quizzes, some group work in Lecture and mostly group work the second 8 weeks of the lab. She teaches the INFO-I 101: Introduction to Informatics class. The class was interesting and fun. Both the Lecture and Lab are mandatory attendance. She co-teaches the lecture with Dan Richert.
Nina is one of the best lecturers. Even if the material isn't that great sometimes she still makes jokes and is really enjoyable to be in class with. Take as many classes with her as possible!

Nina and Matt Hottell taught my class together. These two were the best professors that I've ever had at IU, and the class was so much fun. Nina is hilarious, and she's also an excellent teacher. She's young and cracks hilarious jokes. Take her classes if you get the chance!!
Super funny but knows what's he's doing and knows how to explain the math! Don't be afraid to ask him if you don't understand because he'll love to explain :))
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I have taken Finite M118 twice before this and failed it both times with a big, fat F. Kiah is very funny and engaging and explains the material so anyone can understand it! I finally got an A in Finite!

An absolutely hilarious professor. Saved the grade of everyone in the class, and kept everyone attending with his charming and hilarious personality. He puts everything you need to know on OnCourse, so if you study that, you can easily get an A. Textbook was not needed at all. This prof really brightened up something as dull as math class.

Regardless of it being math, Kia was an awesome professor. I am now in D117 and was hoping he would teach it. He isn't and now I realise how good of a professor he was, he gives you exercises and answers to them that help you with webwork and the exams. He is funny, explains stuff well and will break down problems further if you have any questions.
He's awesome! He's hilarious and he's really good at explaining the work. He's always open to helping students when they need it. Overall, the class was very laid back. Definite recommendation.
I love his enthusiasm and humor. He was hands down the best math instructor I have ever had.
Instructor is excellent, personable, helpful and friendly.
Was unclear and all over the place. Examples did not reflect that homework.
Great at giving examples, kept the class light with jokes.
Awesome!! He's really helpful and he likes students to be active ;)

WebWork assigned every night, but not due until next class so will always have a minimum of 2 days to do it. In-class instruction is mostly examples that will be on the homework and tests. Study guides very helpful. 2 question quizzes almost daily, but do not count for many points and can be corrected. Great guy with lots of jokes! Fun class.

This class often has many sections, taught by different Professors. If you have the opportunity to get into Professor Tom's lectures do it, you will not regret it. He explains things very well and is always willing to help any students. His TEACH YOUR NEIGHBOR CHALLENGE mirror the lectures, tests, homework. He's super cute tho, and tell jokes

Tom is great at teaching this class. He uses ppt most of the time and they are usually well organized and thought-out. Explains content pretty clearly. Help is very available after class since he usually has a lot of AIs. Very funny.
Tom Is a great dude. Beware, he is very different outside of the classroom.

202 with Ortega was not bad. Attendance isn't required; there are only a couple of grades, including practice quizzes and exams(including an optional final). The exams are completely based on the practice quizzes. If you drill the practice quizzes, you will do absolutely fine in the class. Lectures were confusing, and no technology was allowed.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's adorable and supportive, who gave this lovely professor such a poor grade :( But the exams were tricky tbh, the questions were really flexible.

professor ortega was a good guy but bad professor. his handwriting is messy, his lectures often have errors in them that he corrects during class, and office hours make no sense. find a different professor if you struggle with quant classes.

He is horrendous at explaining topics in his own words. Not sure if he created the notes himself. Contradicts himself during examples. Convinced he doesn't actually know anything about economics and was assigned to this class hastily. Quizzes and exams are SO much more difficult than class content. Reviewing exam content with him is useless.

The lectures were quite short and recorded by a robotic voice that was hard to understand and the quizzes were often on material not covered by the readings/lectures.  Professor Ortega sent one email during the class - at the end to remind us to do the end of course evaluation, no other contact.  There were required discussions, but no feedback.

Poor handwriting that makes it difficult to understand what is on the board meaning it is tough to write useful notes. There are weekly quizzes with questions that are meant to trick you or be difficult just for the sake of being difficult. He is not accommodating at all and will blame you for not understanding material or asking him any questions.

Lectures feel rushed and he just scribbles on the board. We had to ask him to do powerpoints after we all failed the midterm since none of our notes made any sense. Has extra credit from first of school he hasn't put in and we constantly remind him of it. Seems like a nice guy just not a good teacher/lecturer. Worse grade so far in college

Professor Ortega shows PowerPoint slides during lectures and posts these at the end of the week. There are weekly quizzes that are 10 points and require you to watch (1-2) 25 minute videos but the quizzes are pretty straight forward. There are only 2 exams, 3 assignments besides the quizzes. He is a nice guy and is happy to help if you reach out.

He genuinely tries to trick you on quizzes. Even if he admits that you are right, he will not change your grade. All of his lectures (that are up to 5 lectures a week) have errors throughout them. I would not take this class with this professor. It is exhaustive work for a 10 point quiz weekly that are so tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: V202 is a ton of work if you are taking Ortega. Gives homework during breaks and his exams and quizzes are such that you can only view one question at a time and cannot go back to check your answers. His lectures are long and monotonous and get boring very quickly. Choose your V202 professor wisely.

Seems like a smart guy, wish he'd open up more. He never lectured with much emphasis which made it hard to listen. Class is pretty easy with exception to first exam. The open ended questions were graded with subjective standards. I do think he'll become better as he gets used to IU. Second exam and group project weren't very difficult.
She is not very good at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Orla isn't clear with her expectations. She tells you that she doesn't plan to trip you up on assignments or exams, but then does. She grades on a very difficult scale and takes off significant points for not doing something the way she wants. It's her way or no way. She can be rude with feedback and made a few students feel targeted/embarassed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Stapleton is amazing! This is the best D271 class you can take. Midterm is online and the final is written to be very passable. She is very funny in class and overall is just a great class to be in. You will find yourself excited to go to class. She is super caring and will do everything in her power to help you succeed.

Don't be discouraged by taking a business class about Ireland, Orla really makes this class not only enjoyable but is also highly caring of her students and really makes an effort to accommodate everyone's learning abilities. I am not even a business major but she is probably one of the best profs I've had so far.
I loved Orla. She is an awesome professor and I learned a lot from the class. It is also fairly easy as the quizzes are open note and you write one paper, one group project, and one final.

So caring and energetic - you can tell how much she wants her students to succeed. She's relatable and brings a sense of humor to the class. She does a great job of tackling the course material in a way that has you saying "A-ha!" over and over throughout the course. Its very clear her goal is her students success and understanding of the material.

I'm in Orla's second-eight week course for Intro to Sociology, and within the first two-and-a-half hour class, she already had me hooked on Sociology. It's a long course, but she is able to keep the class engaged. She is a good balance of educational and fun, and I've always looked forward to her class. A decent amount of work, not too overbearing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Orla is quite possible the best teacher I've had at IU so far. She makes a dry subject very interesting and is enjoyable in class. She's very funny and socially "up-to-date" as in she listens to modern music and watches lots of movies. She's very easy to talk to and relatable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Orla is super nice, but lacking at getting students involved in lecture. To be fair the material can get dry and is a slow start. My issue is the work for a 200 level course. Weekly readings, 2 books, weekly journals, 3 tests, a final paper due less than 2 weeks after the second exam, and a final. Not the easiest A or really even a B
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She helped me decide to major in Sociology. She is one of the best teachers I have had and I am taking another class of hers next semester. You need to go to class because there are weekly quizzes. She is an easy grader but read the articles she assigns for each class to pass the quizzes. You do not have to read the text book if you go to class.

She is my favorite professor I've ever had, and I'm taking another one of her classes next semester. She knows every single person's name in my class, her lectures are very interesting, and she outlines EXACTLY what you need to put in your paper. She is always available for you if you need help. There are reading quizzes every week but are simple.

Orla is such a caring instructor; she memorized the names of all the students in my lecture class and is extremely polite. Her class is enjoyable and she has a great knowledge of sociology. She specifically outlines what she's looking for in written assignments, so they're a breeze to write. Her tests are simple and easy. Take this class with her!
Gives too much work from the book. I cannot speak Italian well after her class. Too much memorization.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Marianna is the best professor I had during my 4 years at IU. Her grading is more than fair and her lectures are always engaging and thought-provoking. Never did I once feel as though she would not go out of her way to help clarify a concept if I failed to understand. You would be crazy not to take a course with her.
really nice teacher! not hard if you show up to class and participate and do your homework. would recommend.
Helps you grow! Will help you out any way
A+
Its English
Unique lessons, understanding and mind, always a smile on her face.
Fun lessons, interactive, excited to work. Give her raise
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This class is great for those that love to read. 2-3 novels a week but all good choice. Feedback is the pinnacle of learning! Very detailed feedback on every assignment, truly feel confident entering my upper level class. Go racers!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Becca challenged me in ways that secondary school didnt, she encouraged writing and helped me grow. She also doesnt give up
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof oatman was very kind, she takes the time for student and encourages free thought.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Not helpful. Didn't give good instructions.
Fair grader and very interactive 10/10 teeth

Very nice and chill class in general. Online but participation matters, you are graded so make sure to send chats and participate. A few long assignments, mainly short writings, discussion posts, and reflections. Work is easy.
Great professor, didn't have much video game music knowledge prior, but explains the subject so well and makes class super fun and engaging!! Fun class

Professor O is an interesting professor with engaging material, though the 6:30 PM online class can feel draining. While cameras aren't required, participation is crucial—no chat activity can result in a 0/10 for attendance. They are lenient on late work and grade easy, making the course manageable.

Alex Ostergard so far is a great professor. They are very informative, and they explain advanced or lesser-known terms while also providing examples if it's not clear enough. They are also quite knowledgeable of the history of video games and music, while also keeping up with current games. This is an easier class, but not impossible to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I'll never get over her telling me I had a weak personality, very constructive! Amy certainly plays favorites and belittles students outside of this group. If one part of an assignment is not to her standards then the whole assignment is marked as incomplete.If a student has put forth effort that certainly deserves at least partial credit.

Just a bad instructor. If you said anything that was "wrong" in a homework assignment the assignment was marked "incomplete." Doesn't allow technology in class. Has favorites. Will chastise you for missing class. Don't take this class if it isn't mandatory for you; if you do take the class just try to get on her good side.

If you're legitimately interested in marketing, Prof. Osajima is a great resource to get started. Everyone else? Avoid taking this class if you can- readings are required with expensive textbooks, she's a difficult grader and doesn't give good feedback. She also doesn't allow computers, so bring a notebook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed the class, there was a lot of hands-on learning with peers and in individual projects. Amy has extensive knowledge in her field and serves as a great connector. I would recommend the course but not her as an instructor. She is very condescending, blunt, and sometimes outdated with her viewpoints.

Amy's a tough grader if you don't read instructions, and her instructions are all usually very clear. She also uses the textbooks that she asks you to buy. You will do some group work, but none that will require you to meet outside of class. This class teaches you a lot of valuable skills such as InDesign + press release writing.

Professor O wants to see her students succeed, but the way she goes about it is TERRIBLE. Make one tiny mistake on a homework assignment and you will receive an incomplete. Cold calls people religiously. Gets pissed if you ask her to repeat a question. Generally not friendly, will probably make you feel bad about yourself if you get something wrong
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly take someone else if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Taking Linear Algebra with Professor Kent Orr is not for the faint of heart. His lectures are all over the place, he assigns a lot of homework, and his tests can be graded harshly if you're not careful (show your proofs, y'all!). He is very passionate about the subject and is accessible!

Kent is very accessible and visibly cares about the success of students. He will not stop until it is clear the student understands a given topic. The topics can be complex and he may seem unorganized during lectures, but office hours are very useful as he can be flexible to your learning style.

Kent is a good professor, in that if you want to succeed in his class, he will go to hell and back to make sure you do. He can be flighty in lectures and get side-tracked sometimes, but his lectures are always entertaining, educationally valuable, and well worth attending.

Kent gives very engaging lectures. He does mess up some problems but genuinely appreciates students correcting him. He gives a lot of extra credit points on homework and had bonus problems on the midterm and final.
Hands down the best math professor I've had at IU.

"I am the professor, you are the student; I set the expectations, you rise to them" Seems to get off on students trying to earn his praise, RICHARD Before enrolling in Kent's course, you might want to find a video of him to make sure you can stomach his voice. If you can't find one, just play any Ben Shapiro clip over Carl Wheezer singing Montero
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly a spectacular teacher. I can not put into words how much gratitude I have for this man. He has helped me a LOT. Just try hard to learn the subject and you will succeed!

Take it from a senior who's taken a lot of math at IU - Kent was sadly the worst math professor I had in my college experience. He means well and wants to see his students succeed, but he's condescending, constantly unprepared for class, and yells at the class for not understanding even though he can't even explain the material right. Pass on him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: not great at teaching, condescending during lectures, kind of intense, makes the class waaaay harder than it needs to be

Kent is really a caring professor. He's explanation about math is amazing, and his lecture make me think about double major in math and acct. I'm an international student and I literally boomed my first exam, but I doubled my score after spending time in his office hour. Take his class, and you will find the beauty of math.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Kent is probably an idealistic math professor, but he really wants you to understand the course topics. Grades < Understanding . If math is 'easy' for you, then make sure you understand the WHY more than the HOW of solving problems. You cannot do well in this class just by knowing how to solve problems. You need to show conceptual understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Kent really is a gem, and I don't say that about professors often. Kind of comes across as a jerk at first, but his high expectations are perfectly reasonable for a 300-level course. If you put in the effort, he'll move mountains to try and help you understand the material. If you're gonna take lin. alg., you might as well take it with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Kent is story teller. He does not teach a lot knowledge but tell stories in the class. After time goes through a half, he speed through the rest of the information. His notes are hard to read and pretty mess. To be honest, his test is weirded. Numerous definition must be stated as clear as book in the test even it is a computational question.
Kent is smart and caring and funny and just a great human being. If anyone can make finite math fun, Kent can.

Kent is a great guy and really wants to help students but he isn't a good professor. His notes are confusing and he speeds through his lectures. Your entire grade is the tests. There really isn't anyway to help your grade because webwork doesn't give you a good enough cushion. Choose a professor who has more things in the grade book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Kent is such an awesome professor. Very knowledgeable on the topic and extremely willing to help in and out of class. Always tries to finish material one week before exam so you can absorb it. You don't really need the book since all the lectures and homework are online. Not sure I would have passed if I hadn't had him
