Attendance isn't mandatory but the book is lacking.  Go to class, do the homework, ask questions.  Kent is your friend.  If you go to office hours, he will answer as many questions as you have.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The material is complex and there is lots of homework (weed out class).  However, there are lots of free resources on campus and Kent holds office hours where he will answer as many questions as you have.  Attendance isn't mandatory but the book will not get you by.  Go to class, do the homework, ask questions.  Kent is your friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: I was not a fan of his teaching style.  His lectures are very confusing, and I had to teach myself all of the material outside of class to do well in the course.  He goes so much into the theory of linear algebra, but the exams are purely computational.  He gives homework but no answer keys, which is not helpful at all.  Go to office hours.
He is one of the best professor that I had in undergrad. He is always very helpful and he gives awesome feed backs.
Good professor, explains material well and is helpful. Attendance is NOT mandatory, and his tests were decently difficult. Prepares you well of midterm/final.

Kent is a good professor.  He insists on being called just Kent even though he has a PHD.  He gets really passionate in his lectures and people sometime perceive him as being angry, but that's just his personality.  He will go out of his way to help if you ask. His tests were difficult, but he let us replace the first exam with the midterm grade.
The coolest, most friendly, most enthusiastic prof I've ever had. The class was great, and I learned a lot, but the best part is just getting to know this guy.
He does give some quizzes, but they are not a major part of the grade.

Kent is my favourite professor at IUB by a long shot. Exceptional personality, loves his subject and loves his students. S303 is a very challenging course and there are times when you feel like you're just copying down jargon, but Kent will go the extra mile to help you understand the concepts.

Kent cares so much about you, but only if you care about his class and work hard. You have to go to class and study the material and if you do, you'll be fine. Too many students get bad grades simply because they didn't want to sit through class.  His tests aren't hard at all compared to the midterm and final-get your points on his tests and hw.

I've had a lot of amazing professors at IU, but I'd have to say that Kent is by far my favorite. He cares so much about his students, and as such, he expects a lot from them. He holds very high standards, but he's perfectly willing to devote the time to help you if you're willing to put in the time yourself.

Kent can teach about anything and does (even though sometimes you just want to get on with it)! Heâ??s stiff with attendance, and TAKE NOTES and act like you care!!! So much is offered if you do. Need help, then ask him.

Expects students to work hard, but will give students as much help as they need during office hours. Great at answering email. I sent him a question after midnight before and assignment was due and I got my answer back in five minutes. Incredibly enthusiastic, he probably converted half the class into math majors.

He was very helpful during office hours, but the class was difficult enough that his office was usually swarmed with students. I really appreciate that he didn't dumb things down because of a few students who didn't study. He did go off on rants sometimes, but they were mostly amusing. He is definitely passionate about math.
Very good prof. M118 is a tough course, but he did a very good job and really cared about his students. I highly recommend this teacher.

In my opinion, Prof. Orr exemplifies some of the ideal qualities of a mathematics professor.  He's active academically and totally competent in his subject, yet despite having high standards, he was always friendly, willing to devote astonishing amounts of his personal time to his students, and always tried to point out each student's good points.

Constantly felt lost in this class, and when you go into his office, he doesn't help you very much.  Only believes in one method of learning.  The class has not been useful or insightful.  I would advise students to avoid his honors section and take M301 instead.

Challenging, but if you like math it'll be rewarding to have him as a teacher. He's a little hard to follow in class, but if you're confused he's extremely helpful if you ask him, especially during his office hours. Very friendly, enthusiastic, and knowledgable about math and iPods.
He was enthusiastic about Geometry, which definitely made the material more interesting.  I wouldn't say he's an easy teacher, but you'll definitely learn a lot if you do your work.  Good man.

Great professor who explains materail clearly, is genuinely entusiastic about the material, and cares about his students/former students.  One of the best professors to take an honors math class from.
No Comments
hard class.  fun guy who is arrogant at times.  means well & cares if you learn.
Smart, entertaining, demanding, interesting, fair, kind, and truly in love with his profession.
He is the GREATEST math teacher EVER!  I had a blast in his linear algebra class!!!
Orr is a good guy, but sucks as a teacher.  SUCKS.  I actually UNLEARNED math
Really nice guy and an easy class in the honors college. Rarely any homework and he grades easily. Would recommend!
Really nice man that cares about what he does. However, he and the class can be pretty boring. He doesn't use rubrics or anything, but is a really easy grader.
This class is awesome.  You get to propose your own documentary and then in the Spring you make a few of them.  Ron is awesome.
Great guy, great class, way to go Ron!

One of the worst professors I've ever had. He accused the whole class of spreading a "myriad of misinformation" on the subjects of extra credit and what he said would have due for a project. He doesn't tell what he is grading on for anything until it is graded. Doesn't let you know what is due until after it's due. Just a horrible teacher.

Great instructor and personal friend. Did an amazing job of getting his points across while maintaining class interest. Unlike other Telecom   instructors, he was readily available for consultation and  would help clear up any issues. Great instructor and great class. Take it.
Very nice guy, and very good teacher.
Very clear and unbiased.  He respects work and the eagerness to learn from students
Not a bad prof, overall; has a clear bias toward some students in the class.

If you are female or have any interest in film you are lost to this man.  He is close-minded, stubborn and anything but supportive.  Despite him telling me that I had no serious interest in video editing, I'm in LA now working as an editor.
He accused me of cheating on a test that I actually failed, proof that he's senile.  This guy should take a long walk off a short cliff and in the meantime, review a teacher's manual to self respect.
Great guy, fun class, keeps it real with lots of video examples. Vietnam vet
Scooter is a hell of professor even if he has forgotten the important stuff like how to calculate Reynolds number.

Wanted students to learn and to do well. Clear about what was expected and very willing to help. Lab course was challenging but the work was doable and his grading was fair based on overt effort by students
Professor was clear about expectations and fair with grading. Exam study guides were very helpful. A lot of material covered, but overall it was presented reasonably well.
Super fair professor. He is very clear about what you have to know for the exams, and his review sheets are very close to what is on the exam. For a tough course, he is a good professor.
Do not take a course with this instructor.

Horrible professor.  Was never prepared.  Constantly late.  Monotone.  Literally read word for word off of slides that he did not even create.  When asked questions he was not able to provide responses.  I am a neuroscience major and love the science but this was my least favorite class.

Presents powerpoints to students that contain paragraphs of information rather than more easily understood bullet points, of which the book does a better job explaining. Has 5-question quizzes once a week that are over 2-3 chapters and account for a fifth of your grade and can be confusing. Exams are fairly easy though, which is a plus. Avoid him

He is one of the best professors I've had at IU. Attendance was basically mandatory. The study guides are a bit tedious, but at least he gives a study guide. The tests and homework are super easy, and he's definitely an easy grader. Basically just show up for class, do the homework, and look over stuff before the test and you'll get a good grade.

He's a really nice and if you go to his office hours he's very helpful! This class was really easy as long as you just look over all the slides he posts before the test. I hardly ever read the textbook and I got an easy A in the class. He's got a good sense of humor which was good considering that the class could get boring at times.
he is Neil Patrick Harris. Talks just like him and looks like him. He's pretty funny and the class is easy if you show up.
This professor's hilarious. I love his jokes and the info gets across well. I actually enjoyed attending this class when i woke up in time.

He is a great professor! Dont be turned away by the other reviews. Very passionate about the subject and has a good sense of humor. There is a lot of reading but I never do it and I still have an A in the class. Just attend and study the slides and you will just fine.

I really liked Daniel. He has a good sense of humor during his lectures, which some people take for granted when it's 9 in the morning. His tests are very straight-forward, and just by attending the lectures you can ace them all. Lots of reading assignments, but even if you don't do them you can still get an A. Fun and interesting!

Overall pretty good young professor. Tests cover the basics of everything covered in class and in the readings. The readings are long, but if you do most of them and go to every lecture you will be just fine in his class

This class really wasnt bad despite the other reviews. i hardly did any of the readings. Make sure you sparknote the Aeneid and you really don't have to read much as long as you somewhat go to class and study before tests. Easy A if you're smart about it. Teacher tries to be funny and sometimes is. Try to look past the sarcasm.

This is the worst professor I have had at IU.  He gives ridiculous amounts of reading assignments that are pointless.  He expects you to remember every  detail about roman culture with as little time as possible.  Plus, this is just a 100 level class.  Do not take his class! he tries to be funny and he receives no laughs.
Ougie rocks

Prof Pak is awesome. Took his first-year seminar at DePauw University and it was the best seminar out of all of the ones I heard about. Emphasis is definitely on writing so if you don't enjoy writing creatively you will not enjoy the class as much as I did. He praise and criticize your writing in the same sitting, great evaluator.

He opened up my eyes to a whole new world that I have never been exposed to in the past. The films are sometimes boring and some are kinda dark..haha..but usually great. If you want to have the chance to get to become creative in your own right and learn a lot, take this class. He will make you write a lot, which is required, but it is worth it!
Very easy. He doesn't give out much work, and as long as you go to class you should pass easily. He isn't always clear on what he wants but as long as you email him with questions he will email back.
He is very embracing of the creative process, but is definitely wet behind the ears. It is very obvious he has little experience with teaching. Fun professor, but you will be frustrated at times.

Prof. Ouassini keeps class active and fun and he makes certain everyone follows along. He cares about students learning and improving. He jokes around but is very serious when it comes to the work. He is very willing to help on an individual basis. Do the work and you will be fine! Great Teacher.
Wonderful class and instructor. Very enthusiastic and knows his stuff. I highly recommend him.
Loved him! Knows how to interest his students, relates material to 'outside world'. Fair on exams. Added bonus, he is funny. If you can take a class with him, do it!
Excellent professor that cares about his students. Knows how to get students interested in the material. Highly recommend him.

Incredibly nice, friendly, and helpful. His first priority is to get students interested in the material and learning new things. Absolutely wonderful professor. If you have the chance to take a class with him, don't pass it up!
awesome professor.

Professor Vic is lovely! The care they put into their lectures is obvious. The assigned reading is extensive but fascinating, and the conversations are engaging and thought-provoking. The weekly 500-word Friday write-ups are annoying, but I appreciate the check-in. An easygoing, compassionate professor with a clear passion for their courses.

Vic was one of the best and most caring professors I have had at IUB. She went out of her way to care for each of her students whether they had an issue with the coursework or outside of class. I cant say enough good things about her!
Super caring!
This professor is amazing! They were my TA and the discussion sections were amazing each and every time. Definitely would take another course with them.

Vic is an amazing Professor. She is passionate about the class and makes it fun for everyone. I enjoyed coming to class everyday. If you have a chance to take her as a Professor, DO IT! She also is very helpful when it comes to writing the midterm and final exam paper. Vic's the best!

I adored this professor! I am minoring in Gender Studies so I enjoyed this class a lot, but its definitely something to take for an easy A and A&H credit! Very low stress class, I just showed up and participated which she loves! They were always making jokes and is very easy-going! I hope I have this professor again, I feel like we could be friends

He insulted us with profanity after we used technology in class to take notes, then revoked our privilege to use devices. This decision disrupted the normal flow of class & made learning more difficult. Also, he often rambles lengthy stories about his personal life that have 0 connection to the class topics & spends 40-50 minutes on the TITLE SLIDE

Prof. Ox is super funny, and the class is definitely interesting if you want to learn. If not, it's still the easiest class you will take at IU. Attendance is taken by a Canvas question so you can just do that. Most of the grade is attendance and there is a ton of extra credit, it's pretty difficult not to get an A

EALC100 was a very easy and manageable class that can be taken for both AH and WC credits. Oxenboell does a great job at keeping the class engaged in the lectures and does not require much out of his students. There are one-point quizzes for each class lecture (not difficult) but add up in the end and can bring grades down. He offered extra credit.
Very good professor with an entertaining, passionate way of speaking about his material, interesting and easy class overall.

Counts for both Gen-Ed A&H and WC! He's very enthusiastic and makes the lectures interesting. I knew little about the topics covered, but he made it easy to understand. Reading is "required," but, I rarely read. Pay attention in lectures, 1-point quizzes daily. Whole semester to work on final group project, and weekly lecture topic paragraphs due.

Love oxenboell and barley any work. The weekly "essays" don't take too long. Readings are usually not required and he'll kind of tell u if theres gonna be a pop "quiz" (one question) on it so u can prepare. Material is kinda boring but I actually enjoy his class and hes pretty funny too. If u need gen ed credit, take this class.

Makes the lectures fun while also being very enthusiastic in tone. Usually daily 1 question quizzes (EASY as long as you pay attention in lecture you're fine) Had a zoom option. Extra credit opportunities, reading responses are graded, no tests really at all. Final group project.

He was pretty good with the lectures and made them interesting. The content was kind of boring so I guess he did his best. He let some of his personality show through which helped. The tests were SUPER easy, and the papers were all graded super easily, honestly if you pay attention to the lectures and take notes every now and then you'll get an A+
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: was super fun midterm & finals are not hard at all just show up to class & take notes and you're fine. both midterm & final were open note so that really helped. don't really need to read the textbook but is good supplement

Overall hes very enthusiastic and fun. Somehow he takes such a huge amount of information completely unfamiliar to everyone and makes it understandable. Hes not too rigid on attendance either and his tests are not too hard, but not overly easy either. You just have to have ALL of your notes ready.

Oxenboell is a nice guy, but his class is extremely boring. He is passionate with what he's talking about and does his best to engage with the class. However, everyone falls asleep in lectures and nobody pays attention. It's the single-most boring class that I have ever taken. I also found the TA to be more helpful than the professor himself.

He's a great professor who makes the content really interesting and fun. We had a lot of reading but they were all accessible through the IU-CAT system, so it did not cost any money. There are a few short papers (1-2 pages) that are very easy. The midterm was a 5-6 page essay and the final was a 6-8 page essay. Easy as long as you pay attention!

Professor Oxenboell is one of the best professors ever. He is teaches you to teach you new things, not to be a jerk. His lectures are always fun and engaging and every student who has taken him have great things to say. Just show up to class, listen, and you will do great.
Professor Oxenboell is seriously my favorite professor. I took his class just to fulfill an A&H credit and he made it so engaging, I always looked forward to going to class!

The class was not difficult, but he was so easily distracted. He would often go on random communist-like rants that really had nothing to do with the class. He didn't seem to care at all about student growth, more about feeling intelligent and superior. Still an easy grader though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had Prof. Horton for W131. Explains things very clearly and engages with students well. Overall a great guy and a great teacher. However, this class with him is not easy. There is a significant workload and he does not hand out high grades easily. But, he structures his class so that even if you struggle early on you can redeem yourself in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Horton is a very tough grader! Be ready because I have taken this class before with a different professor and got a way better grade then what he gave me. Do not take class with him. He is also rude if you do not understand the assignments when you email him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Horton is really passionate and personable. He is a tough grader, but gives good feedback and really does want everyone to do well. He keeps his lectures interesting, and while attendance isn't mandatory, I feel it is necessary to understand topics and do well on papers.
He overcomplicates a lot, pretty condescending in emails, bought a textbook we never used and seemed way too hard for what a freshman writing class should be. Overall, wouldnt recommend.

I felt that Dr. Horton was accommodating with the online environment but was a relatively hard grader. I expected freshman English to be more of a blow off class, but you have to try hard on each assignment to get a good grade.

Although an online literature course can be pretty tough to read, as Dr. Horton would put it, he is an absolutely incredibly professor who really knows what he is talking about. He made us think about texts and the deeper analytical parts of texts that I really hadn't thought about before. I definitely recommend taking a class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Great guy! Our course was online this semester and Dr. Horton was very accommodating with basically everything. He deeply cares for his students and loves to discuss texts from the course which makes attendance important. Do the assignments and try your best on the papers and you shouldn't have a problem passing this class.

I took English online with Dr. Horton and even though the semester itself went online, Dr. Horton was very caring with the circumstances and was completely understanding. There was a lot of homework (which he himself also called busywork) but that was due to a lack of "in class" assignments and they were easy points.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Cool guy, really laid back and doesn't require much of his students. Easy grader and willing to accommodate you if the circumstances require it.
A lot of busy work

Big fan of Sandra! She genuinely cares about her students,  and is passionate & knowledgable about the material she teaches. Her tests are difficult, you have to study and cram notes/examples into your cheat sheet.

Excellent professor.  My roommate had Peggy Hite the same semester and from talking with him, Owens is much better.  She makes tax accounting about as interesting as it can be.  Tests aren't too bad (you get a 1 page cheat sheet).  Wish she gave more pre-test prep though.
She's nice but does not know the material as well as Winston thus making it more difficult to do well.
She was a very nice professor. I preferred her to Winston and I thought that her lesson plans were great.

Not bad teacher. However, she doesn't make the tests and doesn't teach quite as well as Vivian Winston. Choose Winston over Owen if you can, but Owen is not bad by any means. She's nice and helpful and wants her students to do well, unfortunatly this was her first time teaching A100.
The class is challenging only if you don't read and don't practice; do your homework and some practice problems and you'll be fine

Fantastic Ernie Pyle travel course professor. He truly knows his stuff and is a friendly guy. He is difficult to figure out sometimes, but overall he loves what he does. Definitely recommend taking the travel course with him!

Fantastic professor for the Ernie Pyle travel course. Really knows his stuff and is a very interesting man. He is difficult to figure out, but very friendly and understanding once you get to know him.

He expects a lot out of his students, but he knows what he's doing. He really respects the students, unlike many profs I've had, and that makes his class easier to get through. I loved taking 410 with him. Class was largely debate-style so you're not lectured AT for 75 minutes. I think he's one of the J School's best profs.

OJ is amazing. Yes, he expects students to do the readings, attend class, and put effort in to the assignments; Silly him for asking students to do academic things while at college. He's very passionate and knowledgeable and will help a student improve his writing skills. That's why we're in the journalism school.
The worst teacher I have ever had in my life.  Drop the class, he will make you hate your life.
A good professor. Challenges you, but isn't that the point of learning?
He expects alot, but it's not unreasonable. He's kinda funny for an old prof.
Has passion and discipline.  I believe the instructor et a high standard for students, and this made students want to work at their highest level.
No Comments
Challenges you and makes you think
He is ridiculous. This was a first time journalism writing course and he was awful. Thought he was god. NEVER take a class from him.
Getting a B in his class is equivalent to an A in any other class.
Professor Sternberg was an amazing teacher an explained everything so well, and if you are debating between him and another professor for any class choose him.

Prof. Sternberg broke down Calc 3 into a very manageable course. I would recommend brushing up on the way functions behave as graphs before starting this course. Taking linear algebra before this course, while not required, would also have helped especially at the beginning. Overall, hard class, great teacher.

Best math professor I've ever had. Took Honors Calc 1 with him, class moved at a very good pace, and he explained everything very clearly. Obviously very passionate about knowledgeable. Spent time with him in office hours, he cares about his students and will spend as much time with you as you need. Very encouraging, love this guy. Take him!

Great at giving feedback and answering any questions.The course moved fairly quickly. Goes very in depth with the material and covers plenty of examples. If you do the practice problems he suggests, it helps a lot with the quizzes and exams. Short quizzes are given every Friday. Exams are fairly difficult. Very caring and kind.

M212 is by far the lowest grade I have this semester and I'm fully blaming it on how difficult he's made this course. I was very passionate in Calculus 1 and I got an A in that course, but I might fail this one because of him. Everything that's on the quizzes and the tests are NOTHING like the problems given on the homework assignments.

Sternberg makes boring material fun with his wit and his passion for differential equations. He gives a fair curve on exams. All homework topics are fair game, though, so please make sure you pay attention to the proofs when he goes over them. He is extremely kind, funny, and cares a lot about his students' well-being. Couldn't recommend him more.

He is a very good prof and I would recommend him for pretty much any class. The only reason I didn't rate him higher is because I didn't like the way the class changed after we had to move online due to the virus. Besides that, he is a solid prof who is very engaging and obviously cares about his students. Take him if possible.

Best professor I have had at IU. Calc 3 is always going to be a difficult class, but he made it much easier to understand through his lectures. I would recommend going to his office hours with any questions, as he is very approachable and genuinely wants to help you. As long as you pay attention and do the homework, you should do well.

Prof. Sternberg was amazing! I thoroughly enjoyed Calc III, largely due to his engaging (often amusing) lectures. He obviously loves math while also understanding our perspective and current abilities. Brilliant yet patient, I always felt free to ask q's. For all you math lovers (who isn't one?), I would highly recommmend taking a course with him!

Attendance is not required but it might as well be, Im pretty sure sparsely attending class is a pet peeve of his. His lectures were concise and explained the material in an accessible way. He posts quizzes and homework grades on canvas but doesnt tell you how they are weighted you have to ask him if you want to know your grade. Curves the class.

Probably the clearest math prof I've had. Excellent at explaining theory in an intuitive and stimulating way. Like most honors math courses at IU, the homework can be challenging, but the tests are relatively simple. They're mostly just calculations with 1 theoretical question. His passion for diff eq is clear in lecture and makes them engaging.
Really great professor, always helpful in office hours. His lectures were very well prepared and he clearly wanted everyone to do well.
Great professor. Explains material and prepares you for tests well.
He is very clear on presenting the lectures to the class and knowledgable about the subject of Differential Equations. Take his class and definitely learn a lot on the subject.
Pete Sternberg is the man. Nothing helps in a math class more than a helpful professor, and he's as good as it gets. Take him!
TAKE HIM IF AT ALL POSSIBLE! His lectures are wonderful, he is SO clear and really breaks the subject down. Do the homework, the exams will be a breeze. Fantastic guy to boot.
Professor Sternberg gives great lectures. His homework assignments are appropriate.

Dr. Sternberg is the best math professor I have had. Is is incredibly clear in describing both the "what" and the "why" of things we cover. His homework questions are primarily designed to practice major methods or illustrate additional important material AKA not busy work. He is also a hell of a guy, very friendly and funny.

Really amazing professor!!!He is so nice that he treated me just like his kid,I really enjoyed talking with him in the office hour.Definitely,I would take his class again if I stay here in my junior or senior year.BTW,You can't miss his lectures!

I made an account just to rate him.  Tough class, but he explains things very clearly and with lots of humor. Probably one of my favorite teachers yet.  Take him if you have the chance!! He wants you to do well!

Sternberg is a very excellent lecturer. He has a way of making everything really clear. Although not the he is not the easiest, he allowed me to understand the material very well. I wish I could take all my math classes with him.

An excellent lecturer, and very student-friendly. S212 with him is challenging, but not impossible. He will do anything to help you understand and master class material; he sincerely wants his students to succeed. I am not planning on moving beyond Calculus II, but if I could have Dr. Sternberg for another course, I would very likely enroll!
Excellent math professor.  I wish I could take more of his classes.  Sadly, the rest of his classes are grad level classes.

I really enjoyed her and her class! She does assign a lot of reading tbh, but the discussions in class are really helpful in understanding, and I'd say like 50% of the time you can get away with missing the reading. She is really understanding if you have to miss class or if you are behind on work, and she was really helpful and kind.

dr anderson is such a sweetheart. her lecture style is discussion based, so be sure to do the readings if you want to participate. the grading is essentially just a few papers and quizzes so you do need to pay attention to the readings and discussions in order to write a coherent paper & shes very understanding about illness and deadline extensions

I don't love 17th century poetry but Professor Anderson made it interesting and engaging.  I learned a lot and feel more confident reading poetry now.  Deadlines are soft, she's available for questions, and it's clear she cares.  The reading isn't too bad since it's poetry, so it's short. I highly recommend taking a class from her.

She is extremely knowlagable on the subjects that she teaches and is super nice, and is very understanding if you are missing work.however, but she is very judgemental. If you mess up she will laugh at you in front of class, as well as she is awful at grading things on time.
If you like poetry take this class, if not steer clear at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson is an average teacher. Her lectures are interesting but she does sound like she is about to cry (you get used to it). This semester we had to wear masks in class (fall 2022). You read 3 books. There is some attendance but she's very lenient on "sickness". Just slightly above average overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson really knows what she is teaching. This class was discussion heavy, and sometimes the discussions can feel a little dense. Prof. Anderson was really understanding though with students' mental health and outside commitments and gave extensions if students asked.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Not a bad professor if you want to learn about 17th century poetry which is just a somewhat dull subject to begin with. Can be a tad incoherent in speaking at times but Prof. Anderson is generally very caring. Also, all the poems can be found online so you don't HAVE to buy the books.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: i signed up for anderson's Shakespeare class to get an easy gen ed requirement out of the way but she ended up making the class super dry and difficult. she makes you memorize and perform hamlet's soliloquy in front of the class and publicly shames you for your mistakes. i struggled to get through this class and would not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Anderson is elite in the intellectual art of using the word "problematic" to describe sixteenth century plays. Her lectures could essentially be described as bloviating strands of word salad whispers interspersed by giggles that were simultaneously nervous and pretentious. Her class is at its most enlightening left on mute or unattended.

An okay professor but has the annoying habit of a little giggle at every other sentence. Helpful enough but made Shakespeare a bore when in my spare time it is my passion. Fair at grading and understanding about extensions or feedback though, so not a bad teacher overall.

Professor Anderson is amazing! I took her class on John Milton and loved every minute of it. She is a tough grader when it comes to essays so make sure to review your work and go to her office hours for extra help, but regardless of her grading tactics, she is a fabulous professor and I would definitely take another class from her.

Ms. Anderson made me love what we read because she loved what we read. She was helpful with her feedback on papers. Only downfall is she doesn't really give percentages on your assignments so you just have to keep track of your letter grade. She was enthusiastic and compassionate and always well prepared. I highly recommend.

The three papers you write almost entirely determine your grade. I've never had problems in English classes before with my writing, but she wanted her essays to be written a very specific way (though she never says outright what that is). No numerical scores, just letter grades. Did all the assignments and extra credit and still didn't get an A.

Prof Anderson is an incredible, inspiring person.  She is devilishly intelligent and willing to take extra time to ensure each student is up to speed. She offers encouragement and guidance to students who ask for it, and is more than willing to work with students, but has legitimately high expectations. Loved this class! Very challenging/fulfilling

Prof. Anderson is engaging and super helpful!  She held discussions as opposed to lectures, which made studying the texts much more fun.  She also gave us free tickets to a show of Richard III, which was really kind of her.  If you actually show up to class and do what the syllabus says, you will be successful.  I had no problem earning an A.
She was a great teacher, very traditional in her teaching method and helpful.  However, she was a tough grader so be warned.

Professor Anderson is an extremely well-informed and inspiring professor who is truly eager to broaden her students mindsets and offers them the tools to do so. I loved the way she combined the use of literary and theoretical texts to teach a cohesive course.
When people would complain about teachers that were evil, I really thought they were overreacting. Thanks to Prof Sokol for teaching me that it really was not an overreaction.
professor does not do anything during this course. its almost a flipped classroom like class. work is just busy work and extremely tedious but manageable. just a really mid class and teacher overall.

This class was easy. The lectures are videos that you can skip through and retake up to 20-100 times. The peer reviews are irritating, but fast if you don't care and give everyone a 100. He uploads 10-15 video assignments due every week at Sunday, but you can get them all done in like 20 minutes tops.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice guy and easy to work with. Class was assignment heavy. Very easy to do well if you just do the work. Take him if you want an easy grade.

Don't be fooled by all of the negative feedback on Prof. Sokol. Prof. Sokol is basically impossible to reach outside of class, and will give you extra credit if you DON'T email him. But that's because what is required of you is very clear, and as long as you stay on top of what is asked of you, you will be fine. (Take this course online)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Professor Sokol is a moron and will waste your time. He gives you formulas yet they don't even work on the quizzes. His class is an absolute joke and he needs to retire. Easy grade, but still unbearable.
do not take.

I have never in my life had a teacher or professor be on such a power trip especially for an ONLINE COURSE. He expects you to do an 8 week course doing hefty work that calls for it to be a full semester course. In my 4 years at IU I have never had a professor worse than Dr. Sokol. He does not care about students. reviews.comment: Sorry to say I took this class without checking ratemyprofessor. Professor Sokol does absolutely nothing except upload what I'm assuming are the same videos every year. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class is based on peer activities and review. He does not take personal issues into account so don't turn in your work late. He does't answer emails, and quite literally offered extra credit to all the people that didn't email him. He is very lazy. He was not easy to reach at all which should be something that a online professor has.

This class is entirely lectures, you are given groups the first day of class and that is your group for the semester. You have to do 4 group powerpoints over the topic of lecture (changes every semester). Besides those, your only grades are the homework assignments, 9 for the whole semester and they are easy. Final is a paper.

Took this course in Fall 2017 and didn't leave a review then. Checked today to see, appears he has gotten even worse. Should tell you how strongly I feel about him if I'm coming back to do this. 
Back in the day, we used TopHat for attendance. All assignments and homework were trash, exams terrible. Avoid at all costs necessary. ALL COSTS NECESSARY

I completed all assignments, videos, quizzes, and peer gradings. But because he is lazy and decided to neglect grade queries when final grades were due, I got a C when I deserved an A. Do not take this professor; his teaching license should be revoked indefinitely.
Terrible professor, avoid at all costs! He is extremely terrible with technology and clumsy. Messes up grades, quizzes and will ruin your GPA.

Are you taking P120 soon? Read ahead:

- Engaging material (truly interesting) but Dr. Sokol's approach is FLAWED.
- EXCESSIVE # of emails; dull, monotonous teaching.
- Uses peer grading; threatens probation for high scores he disputes.
- Quizzes require disputed online research.
- Hard work earns you an A+; but class was not worth effort required.

reviews.comment: Avoid taking this class at all costs. Sokol just needs to retire. Most of the class grade is based on peer activities that are so difficult and time-consuming and instructions are never clear. If you give your peer a good grade it can be flagged as academic misconduct. This class was a joke.

P120 is a joke. Makes us peer grade and says "there's no reason to be a harsh grader" but threatens people with academic misconduct if you give a decent grade. Units 5+ require a lot of math for tests but he uses weird formulas, even if you follow his way, you'll still be wrong as he makes mistakes in the answers. P120 is 100x more stress than K201
hes just so lazy hes making us grade eachother the assignments have 0 effort and make no sense

Only lectures with a lot of group work but overall easy class to get through if you put in some work. Overall nice teacher simply not that entertaining as a lecture even though what he teaches is interesting.

This professor has assignments in questionable English (not for lack of knowledge, he's just lazy) and a response time of a half semester (or not at all). Professor did not enter grades correctly or in a very time appropriate manner. There are also virtually no directions or guidance on assignments, so rely on Google to teach you more than this guy
Truly intelligent professor! He cares about your grades and understanding of class material. Definitely recommend him!
I definitely recommend professor Paul. He is so kind and willing to help, and I also never felt bored in this class. You should take it for credit because it is super engaging.

I respect the professor Paul because of his willingness to help students and work with them for their success in this class.  His lectures are pretty awesome and riveting. It is unassailable that you should do your best on projects, but they are engaging and interesting to work on. I definitely recommend him to be your professor in this class!

This professor is so chill. He literally doesn't take attendance until presentations. You get one homework assignment a week and he wants you to use the internet to find the answers. He's really nice. Definitely take this class if you need a gen-ed science credit.

Physics for future leaders was a cool chill class that counted for Natural Science credit. It was a really nice workload and he didn't make you attend, also the topics were really cool.  We didn't have to memorize anything and it was all big ideas about interesting stuff. Sokol was really nice and helpful. Cool dude

Three mid terms and final comprised to 60%, thus if you fail at least one test your grade will be screwed, especially when many people taking this class are pre-med students. Lab takes between 4-6 hours, and is graded such that it decrease your grade.

Professor Sokol is, by all means, the worst professor I've ever had. 60% of the the grade is based on the test, which the professor only wants the score to be around 70 so the least amount of people could get an A. Homework takes a long time and is only worth 4%. Lab has too much work. Textbook is unclear in its explanation of the physics concept.

This was by far the most difficult class I have ever taken as a pre-med student. Orgo, biochem - nothing compares! Prof Sokol may act like he wants his students to succeed, but the exams and way in which the class is set up are in no way set up for someone to succeed!

reviews.comment: If theres an award for worst professor, he would win it every year. His exams are worth 60% of the overall grade but every question is the HARDEST it can possibly be. He is tyrannical and power-hungry and clearly doesnt care about his students or if they learn. If hes on fire, and I had a glass of water, Id drink it.

Exams are impossible to do well on. You won't finish them in the time given due to the paragraph prompts with useless background info and the multiple conversions required for no reason. Sokol is a horrible professor and shouldn't be teaching anymore. Do not take this class.
The worst professor Ive ever taken. Exam are nothing like the practice or examples. Completely absurd and unreasonable for an intro class. Dont take under any circumstance

reviews.comment: I tried to write out a paragraph explaining how horrible and hard this INTO LEVEL class is but no words can describe it. Just don't take this class with sokol you will hate your life.

The exams were nothing like lecture or practice problems. I literally was never able to finish an exam due to the length and difficulty of the problems. Keep in mind I am normally at the top of my classes and this was the worst class and professors I have ever had. Whatever do not take.

Paul is by far the worst professor I have ever had. Once going online because of Covid-19, Paul made the class increasingly harder. The absolute worst excuse for an educator Ive ever had  I seriously dont know how he has a job. The single hardest class Ive ever taken and I learned absolutely nothing. Paul does not teach. reviews.comment: I dont normally despise professors, but this man is the worst teacher I've ever had in my entire life he simply cannot teach physics. If you don't want your GPA to get destroyed, DO NOT take this class and take it in the summer.

Paul has a hard time dumbing things down to a young student's level. If you don't care about physics, you're in luck- the exams contain very difficult problems, but they come verbatim from the homework. Frustrating for those of us who want to actually be tested on our knowledge, but take that as you will. Full lab reports each week take up time.

Worst professor at IU. During lecture Paul does derivations of equations. Thats it. He does not lecture about the material he assigned the night before. He asks ridiculous questions like "is the moon one meter wide? 5 meters wide? 70000 meters wide?" Just a horrible professor all around. Avoid at all costs

I cannot overemphasize my dislike for him.

I've never had a class make me feel so worthless. Avoid him.

Paul Sokol has been the worst professor that I have every had at IU. He does not care about his students and thus is not available outside of class. He is very hands off with any student matters. When he makes his tests, he doesn't make sure that the correct answer is on the test form, and then when you ask him about it he gets upset and defensive

Worst professor I've ever had in my life. I've never had to work so hard in a class ever, but this is the worst grade I've ever received. In the lab, they don't even grade based on your work. Homework hard lecture notes nonexisten, zero drops

The book is awful, teaches physics as if it's your third time studying the same material (like a review). Each exam is 15% of the course grade and he drops no exams, quizzes, homework, or even lab. reviews.comment: I have had many very professors at IU who were terrible, and this one really takes the cake. He gets visibly annoyed when students ask questions and he is not available to help students. I know people who took this class before with other profs, and Sokol's grading is by far the most harsh. He does not care about students. Do not take his class.

I know some don't like him, but I thought he did a good job teaching 309. He made you squirm some asking tough questions on the spot, but that's real life. He knows his stuff and will help you out with all the crazy tough experiments. Lenient with due dates, fair with grading. Plus the experiments were really good ones. What more do you want?
Nothing special at all. Material seems more challenging than it actually is, seeing as how 90% of test questions came from practice exams word for word.
No surprises here, once you figure him out the first couple of weeks you've got him figured out the entire semester.
Read the syllabus carefully and try to play ahead by doing each module ahead of time

reviews.comment: Take this class if you need a GPA booster. It's an 8-week online asynchronous course, and all modules are posted weeks in advance. Just be careful on the multiple-choice quizzes as he asks very specific questions pertaining to lecture slides. Dr. P is very kind and leaves good feedback, and is a great connection to have.

Professor Pederson is a very likable guy, who grades assignments extremely quickly, always leaving kind notes of advice. He was very welcoming, as he personally, and individually introduced himself in the comments of our first discussion. Overall, very impressed with him and enjoyed his course. I would recommend if you want a stress free option!

Class consisted of very long weekly lectures (almost 2 hours) and a weekly quiz, which was 30 mins for 40 questions so it was a bit rushed. Only other assignment was the final paper which was just summaries so it was very easy. The paper was split up into only one paragraph per week so it was not bad. Would recommend this class, great 8 week class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class was a joke. I didn't learn anything, partly because it's fully online. If you want to actually learn, avoid it. Otherwise, it is one of the easiest A's you will get. Just proofread your writing assignments, dude took off 15 points on a 50-point discussion for one spelling mistake.
Not exactly motivating. Wanted to know how to improve and do better in his class and wasn't much help, focused more on what I was doing wrong and how other students were succeeding.

Watch the lectures and you'll get a A+. Paul is one of the bets and truly cares about his students. He's kind enough to keep you on an email thread with current and old students about opportunities in the sports world that opened up. I enjoyed his class.

He's a good professor with a knowledgeable background in the field of sports. 
Take him again yeah

This class consisted of 8 lectures in the span of 8 weeks where every friday night there was an exam. While the lectures were extremely long, if you put the time in watching the lectures, the exams were quite easy. Overall a very nice guy too and responds quickly to emails.

Dr. P is a great professor. Grade is made up of 8 exams, one each week. The content comes from an outline that he provides that you fill out as you watch the lecture. While it is time consuming there are no surprises. Very nice when I reached out to help and replies quickly.

Very knowledgeable about his content. Very long lectures. Grades were weekly discussion posts and weekly quiz. Quizzes were tough but if you payed attention in lecture its an easy A. Not a class you can slack off in. Would take him again if I could!
Great guy. Lectures were sort of long but they were informative and worth your time. Easy class if you put in the work during the lectures.

There was an accidental error in the system and a test was taken for me when I never started it. I emailed respectfully and asked what I could do because it was an accidental mistake that was in no way my fault and he said to "refer to page 6 of the syllabus" and my grade was docked by 11 points. Not a nice person when it comes to accidents.
Great guy. Very knowledgeable about his classes material. Usual amount of work. Lectures are interesting because of his stories/tangents. Will look out for his students.

I put the most work and time into this class by far. Professor Pederson does expect a lot out of his students, he has a lot of experience in the Sport Marketing and Management field and is constantly sending his current and past students new opportunities to get work.
When you guys are taking this courses, you better listen to the following instructions. What I mean is that you have to listen carefully on every lectures because he gives 8 exams weekly.

Dr Pedersen knows his stuff but he expect you to be involved in the class since the beginning. His 8 weeks class has been really tough but I managed to do well. Be professional when you take his class because he does not tolerate immature behavior. There were 8 exams total worth 100 points each, 6 discussions and 1 project. You will have to work.

reviews.comment: Dr.P is honestly a great professor, he genuinely wants his students to succeed and will let you know if he likes your work

Dr. Pedersen has been my favorite teacher at IU. His class is 2 & 1/2 hrs long and he lectures the entire time but each class is extremely interactive. His abnormal exam formats involve questions based off class discussions rather than textbook material which appealed to my learning ability. Very stern teacher, but a great mentor to learn from.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very rude to students, bases test off of random things he brings up during that lecture. If you dont got to EVERY class you wont pass. If you talk points off, leave class for (restroom) points off. Books only used for quizzes and maybe 5 to 6 Qs on test. Not worth the time or stress. Warning to all just dont take the class.

Professor Pedersen was the cruelest teacher I have ever seen. Whether it's from his extremely short temper or how mean he is to his TA's. He seems to try an belittle his doctoral student TA's. Overall not a likeable guy and seems to be a huge narcissist.

Dr. Pedersen is an excellent professor. He expects all of his students to read the book and remember specific details, but if you put in the effort, he will notice. I loved this class, and I earned an A. Since taking his class, I have met with him several times, and he has helped me connect with professionals in the area that I want to pursue.

Pedersen is a cool guy, but he doesn't deal with immaturity. He's a really smart guy who cares about his students and is a really good resource if you don't get on his bad side. The class is easy if you show up and pay attention. Tests are based on in-class discussions, so if you skip you won't do well.

reviews.comment: I thought Dr. Pedersen was a great teacher. I felt as if he was misunderstood by many students who just wanted to breeze through the class. He wants his students to really learn something and he cares about the ones who really want to achieve something. He was very accessible for help outside of class as well and I still keep in touch with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is beyond rude to students and his tests are so stupid, i've attended every lecture and still did poorly . That is because his tests you on random things he says during a lecture rather than actual concepts for the class. One time he wouldn't even accept an assignment of my assignments because I had to leave the lecture early for an obligation.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Avoid Professor Pedersen if possible. Does not test you on concepts, rather what videos were watched in class and what musician the class liked to listen to the most. After he receives more than 2 "stupid questions" about a test, he does not allow anymore to be asked. He belittles your future.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Honestly, I have no idea how anyone doesn't pass Pedersen's class. His tests are so easy if you just sit in lecture and look at the slides. Don't need the textbook really and he cant be a cool guy if you show interest. Attendance isn't graded but if you want to pass the class then go... Oh. and no phones or laptops at all.

Dr. P was awful. He was rude and condescending to the basketball players in class. He had no appreciation for the AIs and would often make kids feel like idiots. His test questions had nothing to do with big concepts, but small details discussed in lectures and random powerpoint bullet points. Lectures were long, boring, and no electronics allowed.
. Unreal how many pointless, time-consuming assignments she gives.

Probably more work than the average C204 class; however, Professor Perry's students learn more than the average c204 student. She teaches how to write in a concise business tone, design reports, and work in a group. I would recommend taking her class if you actually want to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: She took attendance and expected much participation from her class, so be open to answering questions. She is very nice and gave amazing feedback to improve your personal writing style. She assigned small assignments that built up to the final paper, which really helped in the class overall. Take her!!!

She gives more work that other C204 teachers, and a lot of her lectures are very basic and repetitive, I would not take her class again. She is also a very unfair and tough grader and is very nit picky on certain things. I would just take someone else that is easier and nicer. She is also not a very approachable person.

I appreciated having Professor Perry as a resource this semester. She gave my group valuable feedback, and I always left class feeling accomplished. While some assignments were time-consuming and excessive, I gained a lot from this course and am grateful for the creative, supportive environment she fostered.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Perry comes off stronger than many other professors, but holds a great deal of care for her students. She really cares about our success, and does a good job with providing feedback throughout the large case report you complete. This class as a whole is a lot of work, but Perry is a good professor to take it with.

Professor Perry takes some warming up to because she is a strong character. However, she is super upfront and is a super fun professor once you've spent some time in her class. There is a lot of work and she has pretty high standards, but I do feel much better about my writing than my friends in other classes do.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Perry is one of the best profs I've had so far at IU! She teaches so well, cares so much about her students and really helped guide my group in the right direction. She's accessible outside of class and is super easy to talk to. As long as you go to class and do you work on time, you'll do great in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Compared to other C204 professors she gives more work for the Final Project than the others.  Additionally, it's hard to understand what she thinks about you.  It feels like she doesn't like most people yet talks to everyone.  She just doesn't feel super approachable.  However, you will probably learn the most from her.

Perry was a great lecturer and it's clear she knows what she is talking about. Despite having a passive-aggressive attitude sometimes, classes were pretty engaging and I enjoyed them. She gives way more work than the other business writing professors, however it's nice to be done with the EY case a week before any other class. Fairly tough grader.

Homework is too lengthy & detailed for a course of this level. Grading is too exacting. Passive aggressive and plays favorites. When a student is burnt out at the end of the semester but contributed well up to that point, you ask them if they're OK directly versus making them out as the problem by consulting other people they know. Avoid.
great prof. cares about her students. assigns a lot of work but grades pretty easily.

Loved taking this class! It does have a lot of coursework but it is very manageable and easy! Just make sure you attend class and work really well with your teammates to succeed. I would definitely recommend taking her course. She is very nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: I thoroughly enjoyed Professor Perry's class, as she was incredibly organized and created such an enjoyable structure for her course. I would love to take her class again, and recommended her to all of my friends. There might be a lot of work to adjust to, but it is absolutely essential and so valuable. I learned much, and love her!

By far one of my favorite professors! She is always available and makes her expectations very clear. As long as you follow the instructions and do your homework you will do just fine. Her lectures are also way more fun and interactive compared to other C204 profs.

Professor Perry assigns more work than any other C204 professor by FAR. Generally, these assignments are not too bad, but they are time consuming and it makes no sense why all my peers with other professors have it easier. Honestly, Professor Perry is a good lecturer during class, but is very shady in her feedback, emails, and side comments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Great prof and I took her C204 class because she was so good. Decent amount of work, but nothing too crazy for a presentations class. Would highly recommend again.

I like Perry as a person, however, the way she ran this class often left me frustrated. The amount of writing assigned outside of class is quite frankly absurd. When it comes to the final case report, make sure you get a decent group because she acts like there isnt much she can do for you if your group members are unwilling to contribute.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Perry cares about your success. You WILL become a better writer if you take her class!

Business writing is hard to master, but Perry gives you the tips to succeed. If you're taking the hybrid version, make sure to not wait until the last minute to do the assignments (they take longer than you think)! Perry truly cares about her students on a personal level and is most helpful if you go to office hours - I learned a lot and recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Hybrid C204 with Angie Perry was my favorite class at Kelley. She is supportive, approachable, and truly cares about your development as a student. The writing assignments are all very helpful, especially in moving forward with the large EY case. I learned a ton about business writing and would tell anyone to take her section in a heartbeat!
TOUGH GRADER I took the hybrid version of c204, and we got a lot more homework than other class. She's very tough at grading and won't change anything
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: This class is very time consuming until the ArcelorMittal Case. After that, the class is relatively easy and enjoyable. The first half just involves a lot of teamwork and collaboration in order to complete projects.  Angela cares deeply about her students and want you to receive the best grade you deserve.
C104 is easy with Perry as long as you do the work. Several group projects.

She is not very good, and I now know why Kelley has her only teaching Compass, instead of a real class.  She would take points off of my group's assignments for no reason, and I struggled to get an A-.  She comes off as cold and distant, and I dreaded having to see her once a week.  One of my roommates had her, and he felt the same.  Don't take her

It's compass so show up and do the homework and you'll get an A no matter what teacher you have. My only problem with her is that she is a pretty hard grader when it comes to presentations and projects. If you want to breeze by in Compass and not have to worry about this class, take someone else. Tries to validate compass as a "real class."

Perry is an easy grader in this class. She will not dock you too much unless you are simply not trying. I have awful anxiety with public speaking and she really helped with tips on how to overcome it. I would take a class with her again if given the opportunity.
She's really nice and is willing to help. The class is easy but she makes it super fun

She is a pretty solid professor. The class was pretty easy if you show up and actually pay attention. She has a ton of reading for you to do every week. Also in your discussion groups you dont need to really read the textbook. Not a lot of extra credit. She can be mean sometimes if you are on your phone or late to class. Was nice when we talked.
Learned lots of interesting information and she was very well informed. Definitely had to write a lot, but I was able to manage. Lots of primary source readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Contrary to some reviews of professor Pergher, while she has good intentions she can be fairly rigorous in her disciplinary actions.While the course itself may be interesting, it is a minefield of complication, unfairness and an unrealistic expectation of an undergraduate course.

She can be rude and is on top of attendance for no reason. She WILL report you if you log into top hat if you are not there. She also won't let you leave a couple minutes before lecture ends and go through 3 more full slides in those couple of minutes. There is a ton of reading each week and long tests be prepared.
Beware of tophat, that thing ruined lot of people last semester. She did signup sheet on last class before final absolutely dissed everyone. Exams are okay, TA's are great

If you go to lecture and pay attention, or even just read through the slides and readings good you should do ok. Discussion heavy with 3 very long horrid hand written exams with two open ended questions and weekly online quizzes. 10-30 pages of reading a week for discussion. Interesting class, but she's rude. Acts like this is a grad school class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is the LEAST understanding person ever. People would be very quiet and she would scream at them in class. She was always doing something to try and trick you. Her slides were irrelevant and she was not very engaging. They grade harsh for no reason. She would cold call me and then berate me for being wrong. AVOID IF YOU CAN!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Overall, I'd say Prof. Pergher was a pretty likeable professor. She was available outside of class, and the lectures and primary source documents covered most of the content. Although there is a textbook for this course, you should be fine without it as long as you pay attention/ take notes in lecture and pay attention to the primary sources.
Loved her lectures, very knowledgeable.

Professor Pergher does a good job at what your expectations will be for the course. There are a lot of readings but they are very important texts and I love that this class is still offered at IU, and she is the perfect professor for it. The writing assignments are graded pretty toughly, but you learn the skills to writing historical analysis'.

Pergher expects handwriting at court-stenographer speed; slower writers will be heavily penalized and have to really prioritize this class to get an A. Her 4 bluebook exams (45% of the grade) each have 2 fixed questions—one requiring 2 pages, the other 4—completed in just 50 minutes. She only discloses this format long after the drop deadline. BS
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Pergher was very engaging, it's clear she knew what she was talking about. Extra credit was offered for those who came to her office hour. Reading materials throughout the week weren't bad. For exams, memorization and understanding the readings are key since you have to write about it. Discussion class > give assignments that help w/ exam

Professor Pergher is pretty chill and cares about her students. Plus the class is easy. The problem is this class is a lot of work for an elective. It is a ton of reading every single week, and you have quizzes and discussion writings based on those readings. Professor Pergher's lectures are decent, but they can be a little unorganized at points.

Extremely enjoyable class and very interesting. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about what she teaches. There is a lot of reading and writing assignments in your discussion groups. The exams are two short essays in 50 minutes but are pretty easy if you simply show up to class and take notes.

She was a very sweet professor who deeply cared about the material she taught. You don't even have to love history to enjoy this professor and her class. Some assignments were graded strictly, but if you pay attention in her lectures (which are very engaging) you'll be in good shape. Highly recommend this professor for a history class.
She showed an interest in what she was teaching and she was engaging in class with her lectures.

Make sure to spend time on the take home exams. If you rush it could hurt your grade a fair amount as each are 20% of your grade. The discussions are super easy and if you answer the print they will always give you 100%. Lectures are interesting most days but they are quite long so be prepared to take notes for an hour 15 each time.

She's a great instructor and was always excited to teach during lectures. This course requires a little bit of reading, but the sources she assigns are always interesting and bearable reads. A majority of your grade comes from primary resource analysis.

I absolutely loved Professor Pergher. She's very passionate about what she teaches and always clarifies confusing topics when needed. The class requires a good amount of writing for the exams, but if you are on top of your readings and attend lecture it is totally manageable. Overall, the class is very interesting and Pergher is very kind.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Good lecture, moved around the classroom and slides were very easy to follow. Class is enjoyable if you follow along with the interesting/heart breaking readings. She has an Italian accent and a passionate for the class/subject.
Amazing professor who is very knowledgeable and very enthusiastic about the topic. I thought this class was awesome and very interesting. The professor was very personable and helpful as well.

Professor Pergher did a great job of teaching the material and making the class enjoyable. Expect weekly reading, short quizzes, discussions, and some papers once in a while as your workload. Attendance isn't required but I'd still go just because she's so cool. Just actually read the material and do canvas stuff on time and you'll be fine.

She is very knowledgeable and she is willing to help students that come to her for it. However, the assignments are harsh considering that the TAs grade strictly. Quizzes also have a bigger impact on your grade than you would expect. Make sure to look over notes and recorded lectures before taking the quizzes or doing discussion posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures can be boring and seem like a waste of time but going to class will help you with the quizzes and essays that are due. Don't forget to do the weekly quizzes even though they're only 10 points those add up. she posts all the lectures online. will give you an extension if you ask her.

Prof Pergher is amazing and ready to help any student that comes to her. Some of the TAs are ridiculous and grade insanely hard, making the class frustrating at times. Overall great learning experience and will humble your writing techniques...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Pergher really cares about the content she is teaching and makes sure she chooses readings that are extremely interesting and things you want to read. She is very helpful and very understanding with students. She is one of the nicest professors I have ever had!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof. Pergher is an accurate grader, so the students that don't work hard say she's tough. The class is lectures but she really works to engage students. She's very nice and is very helpful over office hours, and grants extensions if you reach out ahead of time. I would highly recommend a course with her, but don't expect an A unless you work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Her lectures for the class I took, Inside Nazi Germany, were very informative and the assigned readings were helpful to give insight into different experiences. There are quizzes once a week so make sure to keep up with the reading. Only two papers in the class and one final project. I would definitely take one of her classes again!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a great teacher who really cares about her students and is a really good and nice teacher. Show up and you will do fine.

She genuinely cares for all of her students. There was a decent amount of reading, but it was all important. The material was interesting. The lectures were engaging and easy to follow. I always received helpful feedback on my papers and responses to help me improve.

I don't know why she has a bad rating, before taking this class I was a bit weary just because of her rating but after taking the class I wish her rating was higher so more people wouldn't have the same hesitation that I did. She was great and even a little funny too.

This class is a lot of reading and writing but the lectures are super interesting and the professor is very knowledgeable about Nazi Germany. She makes the material highly interesting and this class taught me a great deal, even though I took it as a Gen Ed. You do need to be prepared to write, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had a great experience this semester. There was a decent amount of reading, but it was all important. The material was interesting and was presented in a way easy to remember and review later. The lectures were engaging and easy to follow. I always received helpful feedback on my papers and responses to help me improve.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Interesting course material if you enjoy history. you can see the passion this professor has for the course based on her lectures. She knows a lot about the material. She is also very flexible when it comes to the papers. Not a huge work load, just take notes during lectures.

I don't know why there are bad reviews. I am not a history major but I think history is interesting so I took this class. If you take good notes and show up to class its an easy A. This professor is incredibly kind and she really cares about the students and the material she is teaching. She also knows practically everything about Nazi Germany.

Very kind professor, keeps the lectures interesting, and has a passion for the subject. She is also very understanding and extremely knowledgeable when it comes to Nazi Germany. Take good notes in this class to better prepare for the quizzes and papers. Not a lot of homework and easy A if you take good notes.

DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE UNLESS HISTORY MAJOR! Toughest grader on planet earth. If you are an A or B student throughout HS and even college this class will change that. If you want a nice gen-ed history course please for my sake DO NOT take this course. It doesn't matter if you know the info or not you will still be graded like you know nothing.

reviews.comment: Professor Pergher seems like a nice person, but if you take B270 be prepared to take 3-4 pages of notes every class. I did fine without doing the readings, but she really prefers the class to participate and engage.

reviews.comment: I wish my advisor did not recommend this class

reviews.comment: WORST PROFESSOR I HAVE EVER HAD. For one she goes of topic all the time and her lectures are boring. She does not give directions, then she expects you to know how to do everything. Grading criteria not explicitly said. Oh she's also mean
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is so sweet and really wants her students to understand the material

Professor Pergher is one of the best professors that I have had at IU. She is such a wonderful lecturer and you can tell she is passionate about her work and her students. She is always available to help students, and she wants her students to grow. I have taken 3 classes with this professor and I have loved every one of them.

Dr. Pergher was a great lecturer and knows a lot about Nazi Germany. All we did were two papers and two exams, but a lot of reading. The exams were basically writing for an hour and a half straight, on the more difficult side (I'm not a history major). Not horrible if you need the credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am absolutely shocked at Dr. Pergher's ratings on here--she is extremely personable, caring, and genuinely invested in her students' educations. Her class Working in the Archives was engaging and fun, and not too difficult. If you are a history student, you will love her--I'm not sure who all these negative reviewers are, but I would ignore them.

She was blatantly rude to students on so many occasions to the point where people were actually scared to ask her questions about the material. The AI's graded very harshly, taking off points for small, trivial measures. Most of the kids taking the class were just in it for a gen-ed.

The course seems interesting until you're in. It's the most boring class of all time because the professor talks like a robot and is not personable at all. She does not react well to questions or criticisms. Will curve final enough for everyone to pass so the grade distribution does not show true lack of understanding from all students.
She is actually really rude. Easy grader though but she will rip you a new one just for fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The AIs graded harshly, took off random points, were super inconsistent and gave the same feedback on multiple student papers. Prof knows lectures by heart and is passionate, but can be pretty rude in class. Unclear about expectations. Class isn't extremely difficult, but the grading is so bad it's hard to do well. Tons of reading.
