No formal exams and attendance isn't mandatory but it is beneficial to attend. He is also very accessible outside of class. The only problem is you must use formulas that work with older versions of excel.

His lectures are dull, and the material is overly challenging. Students are restricted to pre-Office 365 formulas; using newer functions results in heavy point deductions. Group projects are frequent and time-consuming, often submitted incomplete. Expect to spend a lot of hours on both projects and exams.

Do not take Serex for K327. Multiple other teachers are much easier and have better materials. His lectures are mind-numbingly boring and barely contribute to what you'll do on his exams. His exams usually take at least 10 hours. As well, for each exam or project he makes you write a massive plan which doesn't help you learn anything

Everyone who rates him poorly doesn't come to class and listen to him spoon feed them answers. Everything he shows you is applicable to the real world and his examples are VERY similar to all the projects/exams. Pick a good group, listen to him and follow along w/ the examples and you're chilling. He is literally my GOAT at IU so far

Pro:
- lectures available online
- its hard but you learn a lot
- he wants you to succeed
- problem solving is fun 

contra:
- not so well structured lectures
- course material might at some point be outdated not that valuable, lets see. Still learned a intresting and valuable stuff about Excel

Tip: Make sure u have a group u like!

Easily the best professor I have had at IU so far. Prof Serex helps you develop critical thinking skills that are applicable outside of Excel/the classroom. The class is definitely hard but if you consistently show up and follow along during the lecture you shouldn't have an issue. This class is a must take in my opinion.

His lectures are unbelievably boring and hard to sit through. Most of the class is group work so you need a group except the tests which are individual and certainly not the easiest and very time-consuming. He is available outside of class a lot but he doesn't really help all that much. Take a different prof if you can.

Paul's teaching style is incredibly outdated. Not only is the subject matter very rudimentary for the level of this class, but Paul makes it annoyingly difficult because he restricts half of the new functions added to Excel and otherwise expects you to do things his way or marks them as incorrect. Lectures are a bore as well, do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Serex's K327 classes are VERY difficult. Try to get the other professor if possible. You'll learn a lot of new things about Excel but it's still very hard to do projects and exams. A lot of your grade is dependent on your group. Exams take 10-15 hours on average. At least Serex's available outside of class since he gives his phone # out.

K327 is a very hard class. Professor Serex's lectures are packed; he moves fast. He often rambles about meaningless topics, but he is very caring and helpful if you show effort. Your grade is completely dependent on your group which he allows you to pick in the first week. There is no homework. Exams take 10-20 hours, while projects take 3-5 hours.

Professor Serex's K327 class is probably one of the most difficult classes I've taken. That being said, I think it is the class I have learned the most in at Kelley. He grades on a large curve and many people often settle for Cs. However, you can do very well in the class if you put in the work and budget your time correctly.

Professor Serex's lectures are very dry but packed with content. I stopped attending halfway into the semester and chose to watch the videos online. Your grades come from group assignments and three take-home exams. It is a lot of work so be ready to grind for a good grade.

Tough class but most of your grade comes from group work so that makes it manageable if you find a good group. Honestly, don't think I learned a lot bc I was lost most of the time. Stopped going to class halfway through the semester, but I still got an A on the first exam. Lectures are boring and dry. Professor is nice and gives out his cell number

This was by far the worst course I have taken at IU. His teaching style is terrible. He took 2 weeks teach the same formula without teaching any complex formulas that he required us to use on assignments. He spent 15 mins once because he couldn't figure out how to solve a problem he created. Overall terrible teacher, do not recommend!

Professor Serex has been my favorite professor at IU. He is just a good teacher who cares about his students. Having said that, k327 was probably the most challenging course I've taken at IU considering the content, but the way the class is structured, you should not have much of a problem getting a good grade since all assignments are take home.

Paul is the type of the guy who is serious for most of the time but you just find some of the stuff he says super funny. Tough class, but most of the work are done in group so you have all the help you can get.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: K327 is a HARD class, definitely the toughest I've taken. Paul is nice and approachable but the whole point of the class is to be super challenging; I think he thinks "kids these days" are softies, because his class is intense and has a high dropout rate. However, you can do well just by being smart and resourceful; take it if you like a challenge.
All the quizzes and exams are take home, but pretty hard. However, Paul is always available through his phone and through office hours for any help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: the worst professor i have had at IU! Do not recommend taking him!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Paul is incredibly knowledgeable about Excel. Unfortunately, the assignments provide you with very little direction for you to show him what you've learned. My groupmates and I found we needed to decipher his example solutions to figure out what we actually had to do. He also grades minute errors as harshly as utter model failures.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Paul is the man

Paul is probably the nicest teacher I've ever had. His class is harder than K303, but that doesn't mean you shouldn't take it . Paul really cares about his students and he really wants pass his knowledge and experience on to you. He says he would rather challenge students in class rather than have them be stuck when working in real life. Must take!

He's a really smart guy but boring as hell. I would try to listen as much as possible though because he knows this stuff. This class is just hard and the prompts for the GPs are difficult to understand.

Professor Serex was a fantastic professor. His graded projects could take a long time and his first practical exam was brutal but the rest of the class was quite easy as long as you put in some effort. Funny guy and always willing to help you out if you just go to office hours  and show some thought as to what you are doing.

Prof. Serex is a really nice guy who wants to help students. His lectures can be confusing since the class moves fast, and it is tough to understand everything right away. If you regularly review what you do in class, take part in group projects, and ask Prof. S. questions (which does help), you can do well and get a great deal out of this course.

I am pretty sure he just gives us his old work but he gives you about a paragraph of directions but you need about 3 pages of directions.If you take the class you better enjoy asking him questions because it is impossible to complete the project using just his directions. They aren't hard they just don't contain all the information you need, ever.

At first he seemed a little dry. As time went on I actually really enjoyed his corny jokes haha. I took it as a challenge and did my work, did the practice, understood the gp's, and actually read the 2 excel books and got an A+! It's not bad if you actually take his advice and put in the extra work. Plus my group was awesome!
Sometimes a little dry but super helpful and really great guy.  Grades really easy too

Paul is very knowledgeable about his material and is ALWAYS willing to help you if you are confused. He makes himself extremely available for help on all of the projects and is just an all around great guy.
Boring lectures, but you will learn a lot if you can pay attention. Paul is a pro, and really knows his stuff. He is extremely helpful, and makes himself available for questions almost 24-7.

He knows the material extremely well and being able to call him is very helpful so do it. Try not to take 8am...I made that mistake. Projects aren't that bad, just get extra credit so you can afford to bomb the lecture final. The most boring man alive, he may not always teach, but when he does, he prefers x202.

Paul is a terrible lecturer... 8AM with him is awful, but you NEED to go to understand what is going on. The class is challenging, but manageable. His grade distribution is high and everyone ends up doing well. The practicals are VERY difficult, but he curves them pretty heavily. Overall I enjoyed Paul's class and would recommend taking him.

Paul knows Excel and knows how to get you to know Excel. His real world examples sound anecdotal at first, but really do tie in to the lessons. The group work doesn't prepare you enough for the tests though, so be sure to do all the homework on your own or you're sunk. Final lecture test comes out of left field, but is passable with studying.

Lectures are terrible but you have to pay attention when he goes over material (usually the last 15 minutes of class). Go in for help before practicals even if you don't think you need it. Class is really hard compared to K204 but he curved my final grade 5%.

Real boring teacher. However, class seems to be less work than x-201.  Don't really have to go to class, don't go when he goes over powerpoints, go when he actually teaches excel.  GP's and take homes are the same every year, practicals are a little rough but only 15 percent of your grade. curved at the end, take it to get out of a fri x201 lecture

I did a Revenue analysis that the past 2 CFOs of my company COULDN'T do...cuz of X202. I helped Research Execs from Google, General Mills, & P&G in an excel form cuz of X202. And I got a B in the class!!! Hahah. My raw score was a 71% that got curved to a B! It's not that bad. You learn a lot...and in the work force, that's what matters. Serex rox
So Boring. Bring a pillow to class no matter what time you take it. He talks to just hear himself talk. AVOID AVOID AVOID

He will put you to sleep, but his experience and expertise goes unquestioned.  He's a lenient grader, but at the same time, I often wonder why I would get points marked off.  Either way, he's incredibly helpful (he gives you his phone number-- use it!) and seems like a great resource to have down the road.
Really boring in class.  I'd say over half the class in here right now is on Facebook.  Class is easy enough though, and groupwork isn't bad if one person knows how to do it.
easy class, very bright guy, uses the same graded projects and take home tests each semester, go to class, goes in depth with excel and can be difficult but he gives good grades and tests fairly

This class was fairly easy. You learn a lot about Excel and get real world examples that will help you in your internships. The class is curved a lot at the end and there is a lot of extra credit. The written final (multiple choice) wasn't that bad either.

You learn a lot of advanced stuff. Just show up to class, and don't goof around too much on the internet. He's very accommodating and willing to work around your schedule if you need help or have another exam on exam day. No busy work, and HW really does help. Overall an easy class that will boost your gpa and make you better at excel.

He really sets up the course well. You learn things that you will actually use and you learn them very, very well. His tests are not set up to make you fail, and he really gives you the grade you deserve. You will probably never get worse than a B- in his x202 class. ever. One of the best teachers I have ever had.
He is very helpful during office hours. The class itself isn't too bad, but you have to pay attention of course.
No Comments

Lectures are amazing but genuinely do not take v202 with him. 3 exams worth majority of your grade that are impossible, class average was ~60% for each one. multiple choice answers go from a-j. homework takes forever and is also ridiculously hard that doesn't do much toward your grade. attendance isn't mandatory but id go to class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance is not mandatory, good. The BIGGEST thing is exams are impossible. 6-7 answer choices on questions. No study guide. Most will not get 70%. Homework assignments are worth almost nothing and take over an hour to complete each. So many computer drawn graphs, no pencil allowed. Strict grader

Get ready to draw diagrams. Like a LOT. Probably have drawn near a hundred during my time in this class for homework and assignments. Extremely harsh grader and the exams are ridiculously tough with multiple trick questions. Save yourself the headache and take someone else.
if you dont have a religion, pick one and pray. he is the devil.

Not a bad lecturer or anything but the grading was unreasonable. I missed a total of 30 questions throughout the course between quizzes, exams, problem sets, etc. and still ended up with a B. Something with grading bands is messed up I believe.

Having taken multiple econ classes on similar material and doing well, I find this class unreasonable. The tests have options a-j, and trick questions; the average grade on each exam is 50%-60%. The professor doesn't allow electronics or cold calls and embarrasses students. After the final drop date, the professor said the average would be a C.

Ignore his overall rating here. he doesnt mandate attendance, you will fail if you don't show up to class. Show up to class. Expect to be called on, but dw abt not knowing the answer, he'll help you out. Buy the optional textbook and read the chapter following the weeks content. take this course, dont gamble with a phd student as they cant teach

The worst teacher ever! Avoid avoid avoid. He is a super harsh grader, the average for exams are 50-60%, the homework assignments take 5 hours plus each, and he doesn't care to help his students. He cold calls people in class and embarrasses them when they are confused and don't know the answer. His lectures are absolutely horrible too no one goes

This professor is brutal. There is a lot of homework, which takes hours to do, and he is not a friendly grader. The professor will deduct points on News Analysis and Problem Sets at any opportunity he gets. The exams also have an excessive amount of options and trick questions, which tend to create confusion rather than allow students to learn.

Do not take this professor even if it's the only thing that fits ur schedule he is a miserable liberal that just tries to make you do as bad as possible and the tests are impossible and not worth studying for

amazing at explaining tough concepts super simple w real world examples. Attendance is not mandatory but if u don't go u will not pass. His exams are extremely hard, with questions that have answers a-j. he allows you to make up questions u missed on exams for some credit. ur not in trouble if u have him just do what he tells you to be successful.

His papers relate nothing to the tests you will be taking. You will be given study guides, but it is shocking that they look nothing like the tests. The final is cumulative, so if you did badly on the first two, you are cooked for the last one. Lectures are so long and boring. No technology is allowed. I advise doing anything to stay away.

This professor had by far the most difficult class. I studied more for this class than for any other, and still did terribly on my exams. He docks for the littlest things on homeworks, making it nye impossible to score a 100. His lectures are overwhelming boring and tiresome and he has a No Electronics policy removing the online note taking option.
Tough grader be prepared. Also looks like that monkey businessman from spongebob.

In the fall of 2024 there was a 24% difference in the number of students who got in A in his class vs another professor, a 12% difference in the spring 2024, and 16% difference in his other class. In 2023 he had a 4.7% of the class got in A when another professor had  29.9%. No professor has come close to a gap in grade.

In the fall of 2024 there was a 24% difference in the number of students who got in A in his class vs another professor, a 12% difference in the spring 2024, and 16% difference in his other class. In 2023 he had a 4.7% of the class got in A when another professor had  29.9%. No professor has come close to a gap in grade.

Professor Simon is no-nonsense and very intelligent. Class is lecture-based, and technology is not allowed. This rule is intended for your success. Attending all lectures, participating, printing out the PowerPoints and adding notes is how you stay ahead of the curve. Go into this class with the right attitude and you will succeed and truly learn.

In my 3 years at IU, this professor is by far the worst. His ridiculous quiz policy only records the latest score, not the highest. His exams are extremely difficult, and the study guides are useless as they don't resemble the exams at all. Save yourself the trouble and avoid his classes if you can. PLEASE!

Professor Simon, while clearly passionate about teaching Econ, is actually driving me crazy. In class, I would participate every day, and confidently answer the questions correctly. On the News Analyses, I got 16-20/20 and on the Problem Sets 25-30/30. But on the exams, I got a 35%, 45% and 55%. I am a straight A student  and so irritated with this

All these reviews are right, Prof Simon's class is a tough class to do well in.The material is hard and can be confusing, but I think prof Simon explains everything very well. It is very lecture heavy and if you don't go you are kinda screwed because he goes over everything in class.The class is hard but he is always willing to explain everything.
The exams have absolutely nothing to do with the study guide so don't bother studying. Everyone fails the exams, the grade average for my class regarding the exams were a 54% and a 59%.

Amazing Economic Professor. He explains hard concepts in ways that make it feel like common sense. He is very forgiving in Homework grades and will not hesitate to help you. His tests are difficult but straight forward, plus the class curve is very nice. Overall I have taken 4 economic classes since highschool and he is by far my favorite.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Unlike the rest of the reviews, I actually liked this professor. He is difficult, but really smart and knows what he is talking about. Lectures are very boring, but it's a no-technology room, so you are kind of forced to pay attention. Attendance wasn't mandatory but it would be stupid not to go. The curve at the end of the semester will save you.

BEWARE:I was stuck in his class after at the last minute my professor decided to quit. His class is very lecture heavy and relies on the graphs (which he doesn't provide on exams). He says that he will do a class average shift at the end of the semester to raise grades, but the amount of work you do outside of class is dreadful. Take someone else.

This class will make you hate econ. The assignments are repetitive, the lectures are painful, and the professor is insufferable. Having half of your class in the D to F range is quite disappointing. Furthermore, I am one of the students with an A right now and I still feel the same way about this class.

He makes every explanation 10 times more confusing than it needs to be, even for the simplest of ideas because of his insistence on using the most confusing graphs. I didn't learn anything about economics I didn't already know, and yet it was still hard because of his teaching style. Homework also had useless and late feedback, so that didn't help.
Daniel Simon describes

Professor Simon is one of my favorite professors. He is very smart and does a very good job explaining difficult concepts. Go to class, and go to office hours. That's how I was able to pull off an A. If you do not try, you will not pass. Tests are very difficult, but the curves are generous. I feel like I actually learned in this class.

Whatever you do, do not take his 202 class. There are so many better professors that grade so much easier. They give no feedback on homework either. They will literally put just bad. I am pretty smart and I have a 3.6 SPEA GPA and attended every class. PLEASE PICK A DIFFERENT 202 PROFESSOR AND DONT ATTEMPT TO EVEN TRY WITH HIM.
The exam was very hard. And he will give u lots of homework need to do.

Econ is hard, there's no way around that. Professor Simon knows what he's talking about and provides ample opportunity to understand material. GO TO CLASS! Ask questions and participate in class-- this is how I was able to pull off an A. He is super passionate and will help you succeed if you just give him a bit of effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Simon was by far the most frustrating professor Ive ever had. If youve ever wanted someone to condescendingly explain why things like the minimum wage hurt people of color more than they help based solely on supply and demand graphs. This is the class for you. He needs to control his libertarianism. Expect his HW to make you hate life.

I CANNOT believe that some people have given him a good rating. He is hands down the WORST professor that I have ever had. He spins everything in the most twisted and impossible way to understand, he CANNOT/REFUSES to make anything even remotely straightforward. Let me do you a favor and PLEASE do NOT take this class with him.

Knowledgeable regarding any economics topic. Does a good job getting that across in his lectures. Shows some policy bias but he disclaims it and doesn't talk about it unfairly. A wonderful class for economically minded people. Tough for those who don't care, but still passable. Either person will genuinely learn in his class.

I really liked Professor Simon. Economics is hard, but he was always willing to explain the concepts in as many ways as possible to make sure students understood the material. Lots of homework, but it helps solidify the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Simon is a great professor. He explains things using many examples to make sure that everyone understands the concepts. Tests are difficult but he did curve. He is truly passionate about what he teaches and does a good job of doing it. I enjoyed his lectures even though I dont like econ.

about 40 people in the class. The Midterm exam results: everyone but 5 people got an F and the rest received a D. He curved it 26% (only so the university would not see how HORRIBLE of a professor and test writer he is). He is the worst professor, so rude and only teaches things in HIS point of view, rather than an inclusive way like a GOOD TEACHER
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I am an A student and usually very adaptable to varying levels of difficulty and styles of teaching. This course was extremely disappointing, as it was almost exclusively the same as microeconomics but skewed to an almost impossible to wrap your head around kind of way. I don't think he understands that it is NOT microeconomics.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable professor, explains economic concepts clearly (usually either involving his wife or mangoes). Some of the quizzes and tests are worded misleadingly. I had a very small class so our lectures were sort of discussion heavy. He curves the final which is great. Should have taken at least high school econ to do well in this class

The tests in this class were very hard. The average grade was normally around a 60 percent. Then each week we had a long problem set for homework. There was a final group project and a final. His lectures were boring and I fell asleep a lot (but I took it at 8am). However, he did curve the final grades, which helped.

Took managerial economics cause it fit my schedule, this website had nothing n him prior and he spent some time at some pretty awesome colleges. Partial credit written tests & assignments a pro, teaching style a con as he blows up things out of proportion, making them more difficult than necessary(e.g. something simple like monopolies).

Very nice professor, but be prepared for a lot of busywork and group work. You will be working in your group every day so your grade relies a little on other people as well. But it's very easy to do well in this class since tests are open to a note sheet. A few assignments outside of class, but they're very easy and the same each week.

Amazing teacher, got over a 100 on all the exams by just rewriting some of the notes from the lectures on the cheat sheet she allows for each test. If you show up and put basic effort into the exams, you will get an A. Some repetitive videos before every lectures, but they help provide a basic overview prior to the lecture.
Sienna is an amazing and knowledgeable professor. Lots of busy work, but I can appreciate how organized she is as a professor.

I took Susan for SPEA-V 182: C&I Policies and highly recommend her. She keeps expectations reasonable—no excessive homework—and allows a handwritten notes sheet for each exam, even the final. Her study guides are directly based on lectures, and all lectures are posted on Canvas if you miss class. Super organized and fair. 10/10 would recommend.
Good teacher, the class is not difficult if you do the readings and assignments. She is a very fair professor.
She is very accommodating. There are online readings through e-texts but nothing unmanageable.

So. Many. Assignments. Minimum of 10 assignments each week -- granted, they are relatively easy, but if you are the kind of person to forget about assignments occasionally, do not take this class. Kind woman, dry lectures. The group she puts you in can be a hit or a miss, good luck with that.

I love her teaching style because she does mini lectures to help understand the material, but most of the class is group work based on the readings. You can probably get by without doing the full reading, but you have to at least have an understanding of the material before coming to class. You get a cheat sheet and study guides for exams too!

Exams are graded half multiple choice half 1 written answer. Written answer grading is the most vague I have come across and rarely explained.

Portion of grades are from students rating one another, and bias was clear in my group. There is no opportunity for correction. 

Sent more notifications than my 4 other classes combined. Gives me headaches
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Siena made the class interesting and engaging every time. Furthermore, she didn't require us to buy textbooks and is very flexible. I could meet with her whenever and she even helped to accommodate and reschedule my exam for me. Professor Siena is a great prof to have and a very nice person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Enjoyed everything about the class, the professor even provided us with the textbooks so we didn't have to pay. Professor Siena even helped me to accommodate my exams when she didn't need to. I enjoyed the class and if you take it, definitely try to get Professor Siena.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Sienna makes it really easy to learn and understand material. Nothing on tests are a surprise, and you will do well if you study the study guide. She also allows handwritten notes to be used on tests. There are also a lot of graded assignments and extra credit, so if you do badly on a test, there are chances to bring your grade up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Sienna keeps everything pretty straightforward but she does assign a decent amount of work. For the most part it never takes too long and the tests are pretty easy as long as you study her study guides. There isn't too much lecturing in class either

Prof. Sienna's class is not extremely difficult. She gives you all the answers to tests ahead of time so you are able to study pretty easily. But, even though the class is not difficult, there is an INSANE amount of busywork. We had 4 quizzes due before 1 class. They aren't difficult, its just tedious and repetitive. She is nice and helpful though.

Professor Sienna is great at explaining the content and is successful in making class interesting. The class itself isn't hard just do the study guides she provides and there are also optional review sessions. There is a big group project but she extends it over a couple months throughout the semester, making it manageable. She is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: A lot of reading but she is very sweet and tries to make the lectures engaging and easy to follow. If you show up and do the work you can't fail. Make sure to do the study guides and keep the work sheets from class to prepare for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Really great class. It was very organized and laid out, and the homework was typically the same expectations every day. I learned a lot of information in this class, and Prof Sienna was amazing and caring about the students and made sure we were able to learn the information correctly--in which there's a lot to cover in this class.

A422 is a hard course, but professor Sinha's approach is top tier. While attendance is not mandatory, you should go to every class as does not post the in-class problems sheet after classes. If you go to each class, do all the HW and study the way he tells you to (redo class problems and hw and practice questions adequately) you should do decent.

Roshan is a great professor. It is clear he is keen on adapting lectures to ensure students get the most value out of his classes. This class differs from other accounting classes that rely heavily on lecture slides and rote memorization. Grading is very fair and there is a large course curve at the end of the class. Best accounting professor at IU

One of the few classes where you learn on a daily basis, content is very applicable. Lectures are working through practice problems (no slide decks) which makes class engaging with the caveat of attendance being important. Exams are difficult but similar to in-class questions, also a big curve. Great teacher who cares about students, no busy work.

This class is HARD. Sinha is a good teacher, but the content is very dense. He is aware of this; he grades easy and there is a big curve. Classes are mostly practice-based, but the concepts are very challenging. I would not recommend this class unless you are hardcore into accounting.

Professor Siena's 182 class is very easy, cheat sheets for all four exams give you really good opportunities to get A+ on the tests. During class she gives team assignments and the class is team oriented. She then gives out a guided note sheet to help take notes. She is very caring and respectful to students. My TA's were annoying though.
The best teacher i have had in SPEA. I genuinely learned so much from her classes and she makes you feel like she cares about you which other professors just dont

Engaging lectures with in-class small group assignments. Daily homework but its simple and doesn't take very long, but it prepares you really well for in class. Most effective, caring, and engaging professor I have had. Great class with even better professor. Tech-free, attendance required, but there's no final and she offers extra credit.

I absolutely loved this class! She was so passionate about teaching and it was always a class I looked forward to. For tests, you get a cheat sheet for every exam, which was super helpful. The format of the class is really clear so it was easy to get a routine going. if you are taking this class, THIS is the professor to take it with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Siena is amazing, her lectures are genuinely so interesting, and she is so passionate about her work. Tech-free class and attendance matters. There is a team assignment every day, but the lowest two drop, and you have the opportunity to switch groups. Exams are difficult, 40% is an essay, but you get a cheat sheet, there's no final exam.

She is a very good professor. You were allowed a cheat sheet on exams, front and back. She is very caring but there is a ton of readings and team assignments. Honestly thought I would do a little better but the exams were somewhat challenging. Overall great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Good teacher, but babies students. Does not let you use any devices which tends to be very irritating. Heavy group work and in class assignments so make sure you go to class. Overall, good teacher but class is structured like a high school one.

Professor Siena really cares about her students and the content. I loved her class and thought it was interesting and very easy. She does assign quite a bit of reading but I was able to get a good grade without reading every single one. There is no final exam which is a bonus. As long as you show up for class and pay attention you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is literally the best. Show up, care a little, talk in class, and you will have an A. Completely reasonable amount of work for a grad class and she is the most understanding person ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved class with Siena. She gives helpful video quizzes and reading guides before class that really help you understand the material. Class is super easy because she gives tons of study resources and will help you out if you ask. The only way you can fail this class is if you are lazy. One thing to note is this class is very group work heavy.

This class was fairly easy overall the challenging part was the concepts were hard to grasp the exams are lecture and reading heavy but majority of the exams are reworded in a difficult way to understand. Overall, this professor was great you can tell she really wanted her students to succeed. Group participation matters.
bad do not take class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: There is an in-person exam, and the course is WORK, but I've never seen an educator put more work into the job or learning outcomes in my entire life. She genuinely cares about personal and professional development. She breaks concepts down well and is fair in her feedback. She also creates interesting assignments.
Really great professor, however this is just a horrible class & the guidelines aren't always clear (especially on the research assignment)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Overall, it is a very easy class. There were assignments due before class that were easy to complete. She makes it easy to make up classes by providing tokens and allowing you to redo work. Tests were easy to study for and you knew what was going to be on them. She was very kind and was open to questions always.

Overall, a pretty good teacher. Definitely has a monotone voice that can make it difficult to pay attention. She's not super good at answering questions, or the why's or how's. Tests are pretty hard so just make sure to study.

She's super sweet and accommodating but each class has homework quizzes you have to complete before-hand and an assignment with your team each class. You have the same team through the whole year so pick well. She has makeup assignments and tokens so you can miss class if needed, but you won't learn anything if you don't go or do the homework.

She's super nice, but gives a ton of hw, every class consists of a group project. Do not take this class to finish your gen ed requirement. Tests are pretty easy and i got 85+ in the first three without much studying. Not the most engaging class but not too bad tbh.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Siena is the professor that you want for V182. She does have a lot of homework and team assignments but the class is set up and done very well. The homework assignment are pretty easy and the tests are not too difficult either. You get a sheet of notes front and back for the test. I highly reccomend EC and doing all Daily Chatter sheets.

I really loved this professor, she has a good heart. But her class is very homework-heavy and you must pay attention in class. Taking good notes on the video quizzes is key to getting a good grade by studying them. The tests can be graded harshly but if you talk to her about your grades she will help you a lot. As long as you try you will succeed.

It was a super easy class if you just pay attention to the material given. You're allowed one cheat sheet on all exams and two on the final. Super sweet professor; however, all the material is learned outside of class on your own. You have to do team assignments everyday which is very annoying. Would much rather learn in class than work with a team

I took Professor Siena for her Terrorism & Public Policy class. She is incredibly smart and knowledgeable about the topic. This is not an easy A though and prepare to apply yourself. There is a lot of work, but she structures the class in a way that helps you learn. This is not just rote memorization either and applies a lot of critical thinking

She is definitely in my top five professors here at IU. She is very calming and makes sure that everyone understands the topics. Just like every other policy class. Just listen and read the powerpoints and you'll get an A. This class is not hard at all and only bad students will get a bad grade. She is very nice, doesn't drone on, and no hard work.

You have to do multiple quizzes before each class, she doesn't lecture and it's based on group work. But when you're stuck in a deadbeat group it's hard to learn during class time. She's very rules heavy and nags a lot which can be very annoying and honestly disturbs me during exams when she is going around yelling at people to pull their masks up.

i took comparative and international policy the entire class is group work and you have the same group all year the in class assignments kind of suck and dont help much but for homework you watch these videos and theyre really informative and interesting and you can save up on these token things and you can skip class, cheat sheet on test

While there was a lot of readings for this class, it was a breeze. Took it first semester my freshman year. If you're not wanting work, projects, writing, and reading as a part of your classes then maybe SPEA isn't for you. This class was very typical of other O'Neill courses I've taken the past 3 years, and Siena made it easy to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I have had her for Comparative and International Policy and Terrorism and Public Policy and both have been excellent classes. While there is longer homework they are manageable unless you are lazy. Her lectures are interesting and I have learned more in these classes than most others I have taken

While Professor Siena seems like a nice person, her class is annoying. She gives tons of busy work and then makes students come to class, so she can teach you what you already learned with the busywork. Attendance is mandatory even though you literally learn nothing new. On some assignments, you get all or no points, she doesn't grade all of them.
Tough grader, a lot of busy work and quizzes. Made an easy class difficult and is very picky for this to be a 200 level class. Would not recommend

i loved Professor Siena's class, She teaches Comparative and International Policy and Terrorism and Public Policy. I have taken both with her and I do not regret it. Her class is not hard, but it is really information packed so if you do not read and pay attention then it is your own fault. She gives great study guides and offers help when needed!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Really awesome prof. The class itself has hw quizzes over the reading and the class is study heavy if you want a good grade. The best advice is Do the study guides of the exam they are so helpful and she is super sweet so I would recommend to reach out if you have a difficulty.

A ton of reading and a quiz due before every class. If you don't read you won't do well on the tests but study guides are the tests. Prof Siena is extremely knowledgable and organizes the class really well but if you want an A you have to work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Her tests are way too rigorous for a 100 level course. MC is fine, but there are about 3 short essays per test that ask for an insane amount of detail and makes it feel like a 300 level course. She's also very picky about everything. Quiz due before class every time. Group project is terrible and if you do not get a good group then good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Susan is one of the best profs ive ever had. 10/10 person. 10/10 class
Tough grader and tough test

Shes pretty quirky but a really great professor. You work in a group the entire semester, but she has a good way of setting them up and I became good friends with the other members of my group. The material is really interesting, and her class inspired me to take up a minor in International Studies!

This class was a lot of busy work, and for a 100 level course was way more work than it should've been. She will give zeros if you miss one part. Quizzes and about 45 pages of reading before every class, lots of group work and unnecessary worksheets, and you get 2 absences before you begin to lose points. She's nice but not a great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Favorite professor. I loved this class, even if it had a little bit more work than normal. You have to do the readings, but the textbook is really good. She definitely cares about the students, and I learned A LOT. If you're going to take V182, Siena is the way to go. Looking to take her other classes. Study guides are the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You can tell she is very interested in what she's lecturing about and genuinely cares about her students. She is so sweet and fun to have as a prof, I do not really mind having to go to her class. There is a lot of reading and group work but it's not necessarily hard it just may take you a long time to complete.

Professor Siena takes her class very seriously. This is a lecture-heavy course and you will need to do the readings and pre-class quizzes. This is a required 100 level class that is more challenging than 300 & 400 level courses. I strongly recommend looking for another professor.
She was a very good lecturer. There are readings and quizzes for every class but they were very interesting and not hard to read. It is one of my favorite spea classes so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Siena is a wonderful professor, but this was a wildly challenging 100-level course. Almost everything is done in teams which is either a blessing or a curse. In my case, it worked out well. If you study hard and fill out the study guides for the three major exams to completion, you should do fine, but it won't be easy for everyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She is the sweetest person in the world. However, this class is only a 100 level course is soo difficult. I was cursed with a terrible group for the semester long project. This class is very team oriented. A quiz before every single lecture. Every one. The material is not easy for everyone, but if you work for it you'll be fine. Appreciate her.

I took Professor Siena's Terrorism and Public Policy class, and it was one of my favorite courses I've taken at IU. It provided a wide variety of lessons related to terrorism issues and was challenging enough to be engaging but not overwhelming. Prof. Siena is a great instructor who is intelligent and fair. Would recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really liked Siena because she brought in interactive simulations and videos to help teach the material. She's a very clear lecturer and easy to follow. You shouldn't underestimate the tests, but if you do all of the study guide (it's long), you should get an A.

Professor Siena is one of my favorite professors I have had in college. Her class is very interactive and while it is lecture heavy, there is a lot of discussion that goes on during class. She wants you to learn and succeed and I respect her a lot. Take her for V160 FOR SURE.

Extremely interesting content, and you will learn a lot if you invest yourself. Highly recommend if you are interested in homeland security/counterintelligence. You will learn a lot about the history and structure of terrorist organizations, as well as threat prevention. Tests are pretty essay heavy, but not too difficult.

Really like this professor have had her more than once by choice, because I enjoyed her class so much. I recommend her greatly. I don't think attendance was required, but it will help. Pretty easy, but study a little bit for tests. Anything more than an hour of studying is probably overkill. I enjoyed the lectures, overall great class.

Siena was one of my favorite professors. You had to attend lectures, but it was an easy A/B class. There is no text book, but a lot of assigned articles. The class requires work outside of class, but nothing over the top. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

Really nice professor. Super approachable and willing to work with you. Would recommend her because 1) she's super nice and 2) her classes are set up so that you'll get a good grade no matter what. Just study a bit for the tests and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof Sienna is very organized and incredible at explaining policy for those who don't know anything about it. If you know about policy, you won't have any issues.

The class allows for you to be very interactive with both the professor and students. The lectures from Prof. Sienna are very informative, non-biased, and give a good basis of knowledge for a lot of policy topics. The homework assignments and quizzes are fairly simple and the large tests are not bad at all, especially if you do the review guides.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Awesome knowledgeable and unbiased professor. Got a b+ through laziness, but As are definitely doable. I actively look for course offerings with her when registering ever since this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Every single class so far has been incredibly painful. I sat on the first row and I really would have shot myself if I had a pistol. Its a boring class the most boring class I have ever taken as a Junior.

Prof Siena is really nice and I would recommend taking her for National & International Policy. You have 3 test grades, a paper, and quizes. Tests count for most of your grade but as long as you come to class and listen you will probably get an A in the class. She is very helpful on explaining public policy.

Prof. Siena was awesome.  She has an evenly distributed grading system, the tests are over what she teaches in class, and she goes above and beyond in when help is needed.  Pay attention in class, and the test are very similar to the powerpoints.
Pretty good professor if you know nothing about public policy. Very easy and nice. If you know things about public policy, you will probably sleep through this class and get an A.
The pre-requisite for this class is to open the Old Testament and read about how God destroyed creation in the flood because that is exactly how his class will make you feel

He is very hostile toward students and speaks down on them. Accountability is preached but he can never be on time twice. Also makes a lot of contradictory statements about assignments. Grading is confusing and took him 3 months to enter anything.

This professor is a very difficult grader and rarely gives out above 90's, especially on group projects. Each week, we had individual assignments and mini group projects, which were not hard, but sometimes very time-consuming, and it was hard to get a good grade on them. He is also not accommodating or very understanding.

Tough grader for no reason and comes off very hostile towards his students. His canvas page is so unorganized and messy and doesn't know how to help when you ask. Just overall not helpful and doesn't make himself clear when talking about Public Health, I feel like I didn't learn anything, everything was all just group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: for some reason makes it a point to treat you as an "intern" and not a student, then proceeds to run the most disorganized class i have ever taken with no direction. Pretty much a sink or swim class

very frustrating professor to have. Extremely messy in terms of when he assigns projects. not easy to work with but claims to be. also claims to be very organized but could not be more disorganized. has his moments of being funny here and there but cons significantly outweigh the pros.

Amaury is a very nice guy, but his class is extremely boring, unorganized, and often students were literally scared to ask a question because he would get so frustrated when no one would understand what was happening. I would not recommend this class to anyone.

This class should not be a hard class. However, I found myself stressing over it and spending an overwhelming amount of time teaching myself everything. He gives no guidance whatsoever on assignments and expects you to just figure it out yourself. I would recommend taking this class with another professor. Was even worse having to take online.

ABSOLUTELY take this women's rights class. Yes, it's a lot of reading, but at the end of the day we're all in college to learn. Try to avoid skimming the assigned pages and actually make the time to read them and get the information. I would recommend this class to everyone. The professor is also absolutely amazing, I'm very thankful for this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I LOVE LOVE LOVE professor Siqueira. I have taken three classes with her, and I have learned so, so much in each of them. She is caring and very knowledgable about all things human rights. If you have the chance to meet with her one-on-one in office hours, I would highly recommend it! She is a very inspiring and wonderful person.

She is super passionate about her work. As the class is discussion-based, she would assign on average two 20-page articles to be ready to discuss by the next class period. Besides the pain of having to read so much, the class is pretty easy. She is always prepared to help and talk to students when needed
She is very friendly and available to help upon request. She is well-experienced and cool.

Nice professor, but lectures never made sense. Info on the slides were often all over the place and didn't make sense. Weekly assignment were only worth 1.5 points each, while tests were worth up to 20, therefore your grade is very dependent on the exams. Her AI also seems to do all of the work for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Every assignment in this class is worth close to nothing and is very test heavy. The tests are extremely hard and they do not provide feedback on the questions you get wrong. Both the professor and the discussion leader fail to answer emails or assignment questions.The professor's slides make no sense. I HIGHLY recommend NOT taking this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Absolutely a great professor and so nice, but the grades were very few points and test heavy. Easy to access outside of class. The only main issue was being able to understand her, since she spoke a lot on top of the slides for notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The lectures often made no sense. Accused students of not paying attention. The discussion leader for this course should consider taking over the lecture. The professor was unresponsive to emails or just in general and had her discussion leader do everything for her and I mean EVERYTHING. Was so bad I changed my major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a wonderful professor. Our class was very sensitive to different human rights issues, and involved a lot of different viewpoints and potential ways to address them. The final paper was a lot (25-30 pages), but it was done in a number of steps throughout the semester and she gave good feedback on each to help guide your work.

Professor Siqueira was incredibly disrespectful to numerous students during class. She does not prepare lectures, punishes students for her unclear assignment instructions, and assigns boring and tedious readings. Unavailable outside of class. Takes months to grade every assignment even though very few are assigned. Shows up consistently late. NO!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Did not allow any outside electronics, to the point of kicking people out of class if they were on their phones. Flew through her lectures, did not share them, and required constant reading for a class that could be so much more interesting and insightful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great professor, she's very accessible for help if needed!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: GREAT PROFESSOR PASSIONATE ABOUT HER WORK & really takes the time to get to know her students and provide them with the resources they need to succeed. If you participate and put in the work, youll get an A. Long paper at the end, but Andrea provides plenty of guidance & suggestions to help you improve. Will go out of her way to help students
Definitely cares for her students, will go above and beyond to make sure they are prepared!

Professor Siqueira is a great professor. She is nice and wants to make sure you are retaining the info in her class. She graded a little hard for weekly discussions which were only 3 pts. There were times I had to turn in assignments late for personal reasons and she was very understanding. Youll have to work hard but its worth it!

Took her class fall 2019. Lectures off of a power point that can be confusing at times. Assigns long readings every week that are pretty important for the tests. HIGHLY recommend the discussions as they can be super helpful to break down the readings and difficult concepts you need to know. Great class but will make you work for the grade you want.

Andrea is an extremely interesting person with a lot of insightful experiences and her background is super cool! Shes a great person to talk to, ask questions, or spend office hours with. Her class is entirely based on easy readings. Read, take notes, and participate. There are only 2 tests and one large group project (I got 100% on both tests) :)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She has a very thick accent so lectures are difficult to comprehend and readings are 40 pages too long. Nothing in her lectures is teaching - it's asking the class a question we don't know the answer to and staring at us until there's a guess. And Siqueira doesn't clarify points afterwards. A lot of my notes were questions asked with no answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: What seems like an interesting class soon became one of my most dreaded. She barely does any teaching, instead makes you read about 40 pages a night of extremely dry reading & then just lectures about them the next class. Not exciting, only midterm & final, no graded homework, & complicated group project. Not approachable & hard to understand
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She was a fun professor who discussed important topics! There's a lot of reading and it's essential for exams. Participate in your discussion sections or your grade will suffer. Put in the work and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: By far THE best professor is Dr. Siqueira at IU! She is beyond caring and genuine. She is very respectful to all opinions and opens the doors for multiple views. She is a fair grader, as long as you put in the work. She is easy to talk to for any further information. Her English is easy to follow and understand. Put in effort and you'll be fine.

Prof. Siqueira really cares about her students and the topics of her classes. I took her for her Women's Health and Rights class. The readings were really meaningful and easy to follow. She grades on a few assignments but she's a fair grader. Her courses are not difficult as long as you do your readings and regularly participate in class.

Prof Siqueria is a humorous woman, but her accent makes lectures hard to follow. Be ready to read in this class ALOT but the discussion section at the end of the week helps tie in all of the class information. Few papers but not too harsh on grading criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Siqueria is such a great and intelligent professor. She really cares about the topics she teaches. She shows lots of videos/documentaries so the class can get different perspectives on subjects. I would love to have her as a professor again.

I loved prof siquiera, and her women's rights in healthcare class is one of my favorite classes I've ever taken! I don't think she's difficult to understand at all, and all of the readings for this class were really interesting. There aren't very many grades (take-home midterm and final, a paper, participation), but she's an easy grader

Professor Siqueira is a very nice lady, but her lectures are very boring and hard to understand. I didnt read any of the material and still got a good grade, just make sure do the study guide. It may take a while, but its worth it to do. Ask her questions about it because answers are easier than you would think. A lot of it is common sense
I really liked this professor. However, the class  was only out of 100 points. There is also a huge group presentation/ project! I had to do the work for all 6 of us! Readings every night!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The entire class is based on reading super-dense academic journals and then having class long discussions about the articles. She has pretty poor english speaking skills, so her lectures are difficult to follow. The class is also a ton of work. I would not suggest taking this class if you aren't majoring in a related field.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is very hard to understand and all you do is read 40 page articles outside of class and then talk about them for the whole class period. The tests are all essays and fill in the blank but everything you learn is common sense.
Slaughter was a great professor and made my experience in C104 quite enjoyable. Everything was going well until he was fired/quit due to tax fraud.

If you put in the work, you will earn an A, but he doesn't always grade instantly, and it may get frustrating. Slaughter wants you to be successful both inside the classroom and across campus, he is great to talk to. If you want the easy A, don't take him. If you want to become a better presenter, Slaughter will push you to be the best you can be.

Professor Slaughter is a very nice guy, who enjoys his job. However, he takes a class that should be easy and makes it harder than it needs to be. Simply meeting the criteria of the rubrics is not enough, as he will just find something else to mark you off for, so the goal post is constantly moving. You will likely get a B in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Slotegraaf has a great amount of knowledge in marketing with a good mix of theory and best practice in industry. The class material can be difficult if you are not interested in marketing, but she grades fairly easily and value all aspects of opinions. She's more understandable in person and will help student more if they are motivated to learn

Rebecca mixes the perfect blend of academia and practice. Her depth of innovation from many angles enables her to answer all sorts of questions,  even those not directly related to the content. She is also willing to discuss more with students before and after lectures.

Really nice lady, but it's a pretty dull class. If you go every day and pay attention to the notes, you don't need the textbook at all. Really if you go to class you shouldn't have a problem getting a B or better.
Really just a sweet lady.  Make sure you pay attention to the notes.  The cases are really easy but they're every day so you need to go to class.
Makes you write 2 page papers on every chapter you read which gets pretty annoying
Just go to class and study the notes. He usually gives a review sheet. That is the test!! honestly just memorize it. guaranteed A if you do!
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments

Course expectations are clearly outlined. Tests are fair and cover the most important material. Slaboch was always available for consultation if needed, and provided valuable feedback on assignments. The lectures were fairly interesting, and the professor had a unique sense of humor which provided a certain degree of occasional entertainment.

This professor is the best! He is FUNNY and I've had a lot of FUN with him...sometimes he could be a bit strickt but just because he wants to teach you something. Best English teacher for foreign students ever and moreover he knows Czech :D
He's really funny and he makes European politics really interesting. Definitely take his class.
he's really funny and his class is fun!
great class, cool prof

Thought I was going to hate this class after the first two or three lectures. Ended up being one of my favorite classes of my college career. My writing very much improved because of Chris. The more you put into this class the more he is willing to help you, so speak up. He gets very frustrated if only two or three people talk the whole time.

Required textbook for the class was barely used. He was vague with what was required for the short response assignments. I have to say that my writing improved but not because of the class, rather trying to figure out what was "not obvious" with respect to his opinion. In-class discussion rarely focused on anything and was not helpful.

I loved this class!  Chris will really help you improve your writing.  Some of the materials we read were not the most exciting but I defiantly enjoyed the in class discussions.  Oh! You also get to see Chris’ amazing smile when you go to class!

I thought he was an ok teacher until i got the results back from the fourth microtheme and the second paper due to not understanding the assignment completely and when he was asked to explain, it was still incredibly unclear. I may not be an English student but I wanted to fix my writing and accomplished nothing and didn't fix my awkward syntax.

Chris is very fair, no nonsense (no cute), clear in his expectations, and willing to help anybody who asks. He grades based on the completion of the assignment and how well ideas are expressed - not on whether the ideas correspond with his. He encourages thinking and teaches not merely how to write well, but how to enjoy writing (and learning).

He is a total hipster. A bit awkward at times but at the same time very interesting and will make you think. His papers can be difficult if you don't follow his formula, but he will teach you a lot about writing and how to make a good paper.

Funny and easy going. However, don't talk when he's talking. Sorta difficult grader. Easier if you ask questions and go to him for help on papers. You will need to read the assigned readings in order to write the papers he's looking for. You write a paper almost every week and they're based off one another so hafta stay on top of it. Has bad style.

As long as you read the assignments and do the weekly activity its an easy A. His guest speakers were really interesting. His hearing isn't the best so if you plan on participating (trust me, you do.) then try to sit closer to the front. Whatever you do, don't miss his class, don't come in late and don't touch your cell phone. He REALLY hates that.

Not the hardest class, but an Awful professor. Lectures are completely useless in helping to prepare exams, which are very confusing. He wrote the textbook and it could be the worst textbook ever put together;so full of errors and irrelevance. Also, you must get a 96 to receive an A. Thought it would be a cool class but I wouldn't recommend it.

Awesome professor! Very knowledgeable of material and makes the class very fun! You need to study for the lecture exams but as long as you read the material you'll be fine. If you come to every class you get a 100% on the final; awesome right?! He also has tons of GREAT speakers that come in and talk about their abuses with drugs. Interesting class

He is a great teacher the lectures get a little dull, however, the material is interesting. The tests are easy and as long as you come you will get an A. How can you not like a teacher that regularly does magic trick?!?

This guy is fixated on attendance when his lectures are very dry and pretty much useless when it comes to taking the test. He thinks 400 students is overwhelming, so he makes it very difficult to approach him with questions (despite having 2 AI's for each section he teaches). This guy got his job because his wife works at the university. He sucks.

He's honestly my favorite teacher I've ever had. I can see where people are coming from with the complaints... he has his assistants do a lot of the grading and such. However, he is very knowledgeable about drugs, he loves hearing students' stories and telling his own, he does magic trick, he has a great sense of humor. FAVORITE CLASS EVER!!!

Very strict rules make for a very unpleasant learning environment.  Treats students like children.  The reading is interesting, but expect thirty pages for each class.  Not very helpful or clear with instructions and uses his assistants a little too much.  Worth taking the class, but try to avoid this teacher.

he started our class by telling us he used to be a high school teacher. he should have stayed. he only cares about students following rules and protocol, not about teaching. treats you like a child.  complains about getting emails from students. complains about students being confused. sitting through class is like medieval torture
Good teacher with realistic demands. Liked not taking final. Could trengthen the class with more challenging assignments and less lecture straight from the text.
He is the best teacher I've ever had. He is funny. I learned so much in that class, not just about drug use. He is excellent. I think everyone should take this class.

Slisz has really gone down hill this year. Students last year loved him, I can't see how. Papers are graded unfairly, his lectures have very little to do with the exam content, and he does anything but treat you as an adult. He is definitely the worst professor I've had. If your looking to take a class and earn the grade you deserve, DONT take this

Drug use in american society....easy as can be. He is not a good teacher at all. I feel sorry for his TI but you need to go to EVERY CLASS. If you have perfect attendance then you automatically get a 100% on the final and don't have to take it. I got 199/200 points in the class. EASY A if you want it but he just regurgitates the book which is lame.

Slisz is the worst professor I have ever had. His class is straight from high school health,and he adds nothing to the content. He is hypocritical and disrespectful. He prohibits basic classroom freedoms such as lap top use. His grading system is totally unfair and he makes it very difficult to receive help or consultation. A truly AWFUL instructor
Easy class, but not the best teacher. he's funny, but not when he tries to be.
very easy class... takes notes and if you want an easy A take drug use

Horrible teacher, I'm not sure what these other people are talking about. He is extremely unhelpful; email him or his TA's a question and they'll tell you to ask someone in the class. He never tells you when you have homework due, you just have to figure it out yourself. The magic tricks are few and far between, mostly you just sit there bored.

Funny guy...interesting class, but he's also totally out of touch with modern post secondary academia. He takes points off of your grade if you even glance at your cell phone for the time, he takes points off your grade if he catches you doing ANYTHING other than taking notes with your computer. Really stupid, we're in COLLEGE, not 1st grade.

Amazing teacher.  So much fun and really made the class worth attending.  You don't have to take the final if you have perfect attendance.  He is funny and his class (Drug Use in American Society) was so much more interesting than I ever would have imagined.
Great teacher... he does magic tricks and makes the class very interesting. Also there are a lot of guest speakers which is really fun!!!
Loved this class! Favorite teacher I've had!
Great instructor!
professor slisz is an awesome teacher! H318 is an easy class but very interesting and informative. he jokes around alot, knows the material well, is very nice, and he does MAGIC TRICKS! :-)
No Comments

Drug use in american society... take that class with this man! A great guy and teacher. He is easy, but you take away a lot information. He also takes breaks for stories and magic tricks. He's a very fun, fair and honest guy.
Easy class and very interesting. Professor is very fair and wants to give students A's. He does great magic tricks and makes the class fun.

It wasn't listed as an option, but I had her for L260. Absolutely amazing professor and so incredibly understanding and flexible. An excellent teacher and explainer of things, she clearly knows what she is talking about and she actually cares to hear and consider her students' opinions and questions.

If you are an English major, then it is a MUST to take this class with Professor Skillman teaching it. Her knowledge of poetry is expansive and incredible; if you want someone to make all the complicated nuances of poetry easier to understand, Skillman is your gal. Her feedback on papers is also the most detailed of any professor I have ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Nikki was an incredible professor. Show up to lectures and take her advice and work on it and you will get a good grade. I'm very glad I took the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I can not stress how amazing this professor is. She's is one of the smartest people I've ever met in my whole life probably. She knows her poetry and her vocabulary is incredible. On top of that she is so personable approachable and friendly. She's funny and her smile warms my heart. Most of all she is the hottest teacher I've ever laid my eyes on!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Skillman is so knowledgeable and passionate about poetry, so she really makes you enjoy it. She is easily one of the best lecturers I've ever had, and she really helped me to get into the topic. I could have cared less about poetry before this class. Skip the lecture? Forget it. Show up and take good notes? You'll pass with flying colors.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I literally worship the ground that she walks on. She is hands-down the smartest and best professor I've ever had. She makes poetry so accessible and engaging- I've never sat through more brilliant lectures. She is always available to meet, and she provides some of the best feedback I've ever gotten (although she is also the hardest grader).

Dr. Skillman's course on twentieth century American poetry was one of my favorites I've taken at IU. She's brilliant. Her teaching brought out the best in every student in the class, which made for illuminating discussions. She expects a lot in your writing, but she'll help you get there. She's readily available outside of class for discussion.

She is very knowledgeable, crazy smart, and funny. It is a poetry course, so get ready to read A LOT of poetry. There aren't very many assignments, and because it is an IWC she expects you to do solid work. She gives good feedback and is an understanding professor. She wants you to do well and participation matters. The final is intense but doable.

Professor Skillman is fantastic. I took L260 with her and she was such a great prof that I decided to take L205 with her for my IW credit, even though I hate poetry. She is a bit hard on papers, but she grades based on what she believes you are capable of. As such, she has helped me grow as a writer tremendously.

Nikki Skillman is pretty much everything you could hope for in a professor. She's brilliant, passionate, compelling... everything. Her class changed my perspective of art as a whole. Use her office hours because she absolutely walked me through a paper and let me know precisely what she wanted to see. I'll take any class from her!
She's incredibly passionate and helpful, taking another of her classes next semester because she is just brilliant!

Nikki is the truly one of the most delightful people I have ever encountered. Fiercely engaging and passionate about poetry, she made every class feel far too short. She is fun, current, honest and endlessly inspiring. For fun facts, ask her about her cat's name, and her handmade 20th century poet's board game.

Had a hand-out for everything, which was very helpful. Expects you to care about class, and you should. Got a lot out of the class and really liked it. Very supportive and super intelligent! Loved her.

Love Connie. One of those rare teachers that actually cares about the wellbeing of her students. Very funny too. Not gonna lie, tough grader at first, but you will figure it out quickly. Make sure to answer "why," and you will get a good grade. The class was very inspirational even tho I thought it would be a waste of time. Pleasantly surprised.

This class is insightful and covers a broad range of topics. Mrs. Skinner, along with the other instructional staff, are wonderful instructors that truly inspire students to do great, sharing their own personal stories throughout the class. However, this class is very dependent upon reading materials and busy work. Keep up and you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: U215 is nothing but busy work the first half of the semester, but if I hadn't been forced to take the class I would have been lost my first year. Connie is amazing, funny, and real with her students. She is easily approachable and genuinely cares about her students. We all joke and call her Super Woman. Amazing woman and amazing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: While Connie is a very nice woman, this class is worthless, and she does not do a great job of explaining the significance of what we are learning. I, personally, felt that this class was making me revert back to high school ways of thinking. The way this class is taught is slow, childish, and nothing like college courses should be.

Listen. Connie is a fine professor and I have nothing against her,but this class is BY FAR the worst class Ive taken. It is purely busywork, and I hate it. The only thing that kept me going was that I was getting paid to take the class. But yeah,Connie is fine. She was the only upside of this class. Nothing about this class was hard, just annoying.

Connie is an amazing prof. u212 lecture was hella long, but her discussion and assignments were extremely helpful and fun in a way. I would def take another class with her if i had the chance. SHE IS AMAZING!
Connie is a great teacher! She cares about all her students and is very knowledgeable.
Easy A. Gets very involved with her students and shows you that she cares. Lectures can be a little boring as she can go on a rant and talk forever.

Professor Sklar is extremely approachable. She's very friendly and easy to talk to. That being said, if you didn't hand in assignments, she was very on top of you. She responded to emails in a timely fashion and always stayed after class to answer questions or clarify assignments.

Professor Sklar makes compass an enjoyable class and the whole class is a breeze if you show up and do the work. If you do not attend you will fail. Attendance is key for this class since it meets once a week.
