reviews.comment: Professor Tennessen is very very kind, and genuinely wants his students to do well. Exams were challenging at times, but he drops one exam. Several extra credit opportunities were given to us. Would highly recommend BIO-L112 with Professor Tennessen!!!

Professor Tennessen is a great lecturer! Bio112 is lecture heavy- attendance isn't mandatory and he posts lecture slides/videos on canvas. There was quite a bit of homework but it was manageable! Almost every week there was a masteringbio assignment, discussion packet, and quiz due. He also drops one exam grade and gives extra credit!

He is a great professor! For me, a majority of my grade depended on the exams. He does give extra credit, but you will have to show up to lecture and pay attention to Canvas when he announces it. Overall, it is a very passable class and he is very kind when you ask for help. His lectures are also helpful in PowerPoint format! He did a great job!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: records and posts every lecture and previous years' lectures. one major assignment/week exams are open note/internet online. answers questions and you can see he's passionate about his work. while it would be a class that you could easily skip, it isn't one that I usually would want to. He is very understanding and cooperative, just communicate!
talks way too fast, his notes/powerpoints are disorganized and his tests are really difficult

This professor is AMAZING. 10/10 recommend! His lectures are loaded with information, but he somehow finds a way to make it all interesting and makes it easier to learn. He gives past exams that give you an idea of his questions. Highly recommend this gem.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Tennessen definitely wants to see his students succeed. He gives you many resources to understand and apply the lecture material. Lectures have good explanations of concepts, and he does review sessions every week. Not a difficult class if you are willing to do all the work. Only complaint would be is that he sometimes imposes his views.

Prof. Tennessen is an great person who is very knowledgeable about the subject matter. He is not here to scare individuals away from the field of biology rather give them the tools and foundation to find an interest in it. The canvas page was incredibly well put together and given you put in the time to watch lectures you will do do well.

Awesome guy, made boring lectures into interesting ones. Very understanding and accessible... really wants you to succeed if you actually try (hosts 2hr+ long review sessions before every exam). Go to lecture, pay attention, & study hard for exams and the class is easy. Most people who don't do well didn't show up or actually study at all
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor, made lectures that would normally be very dry pretty interesting. gives out lots of extra credit so easy to get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He was overall one of my favorite professors during my freshman year. All of his lectures were interesting and engaging, and he always made himself available to help if you didn't understand something. He is so nice and he really cares about his students' success. It's almost impossible not to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Good
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Tennessen is awesome. Favorite professor my first semester of freshman year. Not super difficult yet you get a great foundational understanding of biology.

Jason is a really good choice if you are entering Biology. His exams can be a bit challenging but he basically hands out free extra credit points all of the time plus discussion worksheets are easy points. Lecture isn't super interesting but just know the slides he posts online.

JASON TENNESSEN IS THE BEST PROFESSOR THERE IS. Offers 25+ extra credit points over the semester. Drops one quiz and one whole exam. He's super clear on what will be on the exams. He even holds additional review sessions on Sunday nights on the more difficult topics in addition to his regular office hours. Literally the best.

This course material is not easy, you definitely have to put in the work. JT is clear about what is expected. His lectures can be dense but he puts up the Powerpoints before class. Lots of extra credit. Online homework, quizzes, and discussion worksheets are super helpful for exams. Exams are very fair. Great professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Cares a lot about his students, especially considering it's a giant lecture hall. If you do all the work you should be fine. Not too many assignments
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor, flexible and always willing to meet with you.   Gives extra credit. Do the work and you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Jason is so awesome! We cover a lot of material within lectures, but he is very caring about he goes out of his way to make sure we all understand. He drops several exams and quizzes and he offers extra credit. Bio in general can be kind of tough but Jason makes it bearable and he makes an A absolutely attainable.

He's a really nice guy and cares about you doing well in the class. His lectures are extremely  heavy and sometimes he goes through them pretty fast but he is organized and stays on topic. You can tell he is very knowledgeable. He also gives extra credit homework assignments which really help your grade.

He really goes the extra mile to help, as long as you are willing to meet with him. He may be a new professor but he really does put in the extra effort to make sure you understand and succeed in his class!

The lectures were long, and he covers a lot of material in each class, but if you keep up with it and ask questions, the class isn't difficult at all.  You won't use the book at all.  His exams come straight from the notes.  Sometimes it is hard to distinguish what is the important material that will be on the exams though from his long lectures.

For his first semester teaching L-112 I thought it was okay.  The class isn't meant to be easy, but it's not meant to be too difficult either, it's just an intro class. The times he did seem like he didn't want to answer a question is just because it's so basic to him, but he did answer questions. He's really smart and knows what he's talking about

this course was like fine
as long as you do the homework and vaguely pay attention in class youll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The classes are so boring as you just sit there while she reads slides, you don't need to read the textbook. There are only two tests and the final, but all the assignments are fairly easy with clear instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I've had Prof White for multiple classes, she is a generally flexible professor. If you need help, she will help you, whether that be with deadlines, content understanding, or attendance (sometimes). She is great at adapting to her students

Her class is very unengaging, lectures consist of her mostly reading the slides verbatim, and adding very little depth. Very few graded assignments and there is little outside of the lecture, not a difficult class but feels like her lectures don't teach very useful information, and are often repetitive and over-explain simple concepts.

She is so sweet but so boring. She just reads the chapter from her slides, so you don't need to read the textbook at all. Some assignments seem like they were pulled out of thin air, but overall an easy course. I barely ever showed up, and when I didn't I got the slides online. Take this class if you need easy credits.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: WAY easier than my high school classes. I feel like I am losing brain cells in this class because of how easy it is. You don't even need to show up to class in order to do well. So easy, but love Terry--she is such a sweet human being.

No clear instruction. I can't carve out two hours on a Tuesday to go ride a bus. I did not get grades until 3 weeks before the end of class. I wish I could get the time and money I wasted on this class back. I genuinely learned nothing in this class. I would recommend this class to anybody who wants to develop the worst kind of anxiety imaginable.

Professor White only graded one assignment that I turned in all semester. There were lots of assignments and case studies I worked hard on and never got a grade for. I also never got a grade for the midterm paper or final paper. Often times, in our ethics discussions, she cut students off when they said a point she found 'incorrect'.

Absolutely worst professor I've ever had. never take this class with her or any with her. She has left so many of my grades in as zeros up until the last week of the semester when the work was completed and is not easy to communicate with at all. And she is genuinely just terrible at teaching and offers very little assistance or feedback. 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I enjoyed Professor Whites character however she waited to the last week to grade assignments. 16 out of 25 assignments still needed to be graded after finals were over. Those 16 assignments were not taken into account in the final grade, only 9 were. She was an overall OK teacher. She did make the class interesting but we didnt learn much.

I'd never heard so much dribble. For a 400 level class, we never went deeper than surface level. Pretty useless. If you're looking for a few brain dead credits, go for it. Otherwise, check out another course.

Teresa definitely stands out among IU's experienced staff, but not in a good way. She definitely doesn't have the background that the majority of professors at the Media School have and it clearly shows. She's an alright teacher but was clearly confused. There were a lot of incongruencies in quizzes as well.

She took our class to Disney World and Universal to teach us about IMC, but she was sorely under qualified to take on such endeavor. She was enthusiastic, but just not qualified. We took on a lot of meaningless work, she waited until the last week of class to input grades, and should really go back to being a high school teacher.
Professor White did nothing to make this course interesting or engaging. Slides were not posted, lectures were long and necessary to pass the course.

Teresa White is such a great person overall and I loved having her for Media 101. She doesn't post any powerpoints so going to class and listening to the lectures is the only way to get the information outside of the readings. Class was a breeze and the assignments were easy.

Teresa is super nice, but she is a terrible college professor. This course was an experiential learning marketing course with travel to Disney for spring break. She did not plan a thing for us to do on the trip nor teach us a single thing and has zero experience in marketing. How this class got approved I do not know. Avoid her if you want to learn

Took this class with Teresa. Worst experience I had at IU. Papers from the beginning of the semester weren't graded. She turned in our final grades without having half of what she assigned to us graded. COMPLETE waste of our time as students. If you value your time at all- just don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Teresa is really a good teacher. Media Ethics is hard to teach, and she does her best to try and get the class involved. She is a really nice person and is willing to work with you as long as you have a good attitude and do your work. You do have to write one paper and one shorter post each week, and you definitely use the book!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sweetest lady ever. Give reading quizzes everyday at the beginning of class and gives homework based on the reading ever night. if you read the text its not horrible

While simple, Prof. White jam-packs the class full of busy work. Two papers a week. Assignments due weekly on off-days of class. Terrible, terrible,  TERRIBLE discussion facilitator, and does not help you think further than what you are.  She is a former high school teacher, and you can tell. If I were a junior in high school, I would love her.

Media Literacy should be the easiest class in the J school. The lecture content is painfully simple, but the only grades are 5-10 point reading quizzes. If you miss one poorly worded question, your entire grade is screwed. You won't know you're screwed until dead week though, since that's when she decides to finally grade everything.
Awful and horribly unorganized class.  I emailed her around 10 times during the semester and received a reply to one of those.

Worst professor I've had. She still has not put up grades from the beginning of the semester. Her lectures are so boring and useless. If you are looking for a class filler NEVER take this course with Teresa White.
Please avoid Teresa's class if you value your time. She is completely unresponsive when you need her and teaches a miserably boring lecture.

This class is the most painful lecture I've been required to sit through in a long time. The professor is a nice person but she is completely clueless. We're required to write two papers each week. I dread everything about it.

Excellent professor and very engaging class. Lectures are chalk-only and fast-paced but well organized, and reviewing notes makes the material click. Exams are difficult, and practice exams closely reflect them. Participation is valued and can help near cutoffs. Challenging but very rewarding course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If you are not religious, pick one and pray. Hardest class I've ever taken in my life. Super smart guy and nice. Grades very harshly and involves more mechanisms than I thought even existed. Great class though and I learned a lot

Probably the most fun and informative class I've ever taken. Lecture heavy and notes are written on a chalkboard so come to class every day. He really emphasizes the importance of understanding the material than straight memorization. Don't hesitate to go to office hours or ask questions during discussion! His office hours were literally a godsend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You will WORK for your grade in this class. Ted is an amazing lecturer, and you will learn so so so much, but the class is extremely fast paced and it's very easy to fall behind. Exams and "quizzes" are the only points to be earned in the class, but each exam has anywhere from 10-25 extra credit points on it, so receiving an A is doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ted is a great lecturer and clearly very smart. He does everything on the blackboard so lectures are a must as he doesn't post anything on canvas. He also uses the book but often points out inaccuracies he sees. It is a hard class but that's expected. He does his best to make it easier and it is clear that he is a good person and loves his students

Dr. Widlanski is an absolutely amazing lecturer.  The course and material is hard, but he knows that and truly does everything he can to help the students succeed.  The majority of the grade is the exams, but every exam has ~20 points of extra credit to even out the difficulty.  However, you MUST go to lecture.  Everything is blackboard, no slides.

If you made it this far into Biochem, it's too late to turn back. This will be the hardest course you ever take. To succeed, you will give up sleep, social events, and sanity. Ted can be condescending, but he is probably the smartest person on this campus. Attend every lecture. Study consistently. Pray to your deity. Highest value course at IU.

Ted is one of the greatest lecturers at IU; however, you must go to class. I repeat: Go to Class!! I didn't attend a majority of Friday classes; therefore, I lost out on a huge chunk of extra credit. I was still able to pull a B+; however, I would have had an A- had I attended Friday classes. I stayed up multiple nights for each exam, worth it.

Ted knows the best way to teach this class, which means he gives you everything you need to succeed in the class. That definitely doesn't mean it's easy - it's been the hardest class I've ever taken at IU. The material is really cool.

Difficult class but very doable. Exams are a huge part of the course, but with consistent studying, you'll be fine. Ted is, without a doubt, one of the funniest and most engaging professors I have ever had, and his passion for biochemistry is infectious. Understand that you will have to work for this class, but the payoff is worth it.

Ted is a great professor. Yes, he can be a bit rough around the edges, but that does not deter from the fact he cares about his students, as hard as it can be to see sometimes. His exams always have tons of extra credit on them too. This class is very tough, definitely one of the hardest I have taken at IU, but you learn a lot. Go to office hours.

Extremely smart, and doesn't waste time in lecture. Everything he writes on the board is important. He's very transparent about what's expected of you on the exams. There's no guessing game with Ted. Also, try not to write or say anything stupid.

Ted is one of the smartest profs I've had at IU and he's also the best I've had at IU. Amazing lecturer but this class is HARD and its very easy to fall behind. Ted is a great guy who truly cares about his students. If you're having trouble either inside or outside the classroom he will give you good, genuine advice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you don't go, be prepared to read A LOT. Also, some mechanisms that he goes over in class aren't in the book or aren't specific enough. He is also kind of an ass, so its best to go to office hours& get on his good side. Also don't know where "he hates pre-med students" came from, I think he hates everyone equally.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very knowledgeable on the material and makes sure to stay abreast with all of the latest research. He expects you to know many mechanisms. The tests are all free response. He can be a bit condescending. There's always plenty of EC on the tests, and the quizzes are EC. Getting at least 450 points isn't be as hard as people make it.

Widlanski is one of the smartest and best professors I've ever had. The class itself is one of the hardest classes I've taken, but he makes it bearable because he explains the material really well. He has a unique sense of humor, but he's funny once you get used to it. You will learn a lot in this class, more than just biochemistry.

Widlanski is not only scary in person, he's a scary grader.  He taught biochem by drawing all of the mechanisms by hand on a chalkboard.  It was very hard to find organization and logic in the lectures as they went.  There were four tests and the majority of the questions were all or none as far as points. I would recommend someone else.

I loved Twidlanski! His class was extremely challenging and you really needed to know things down to the nitty gritty details to get full credit, but he's extremely fair and willing to help.  I think he enjoys teaching, but doesn't appreciate premed BS. NEVER ask if something will be on the exam (the answer is probably yes anyway).

Taking biochemistry with Dr. Widlanski should be avoided if at all possible. Be ready to extensively memorize mechanisms, receive almost no partial credit, and fight very hard for a respectable grade. I personally scraped by with my only C as an undergrad and almost screwed myself out of medical school. It can be done, but it won't be any fun.

This guy is the stereotypical PhD who'd love to be in the lab full time than "bothered" with having to teach. HATES pre-med/pre-dent students, and has no qualms about saying so. Terrible teaching methods - basically, he rants for 50 minutes about how much more biochem he knows than everyone else. Had lots of good chem profs at IU - but he's not one

Avoid if at all possible for C483. He basically told us that he hates all students in this class because they are just premed students trying to get another A (not serious biochemistry majors). Tests were nearly impossible, and Ted didn't really seem to care if we learned anything about biochemistry at all.

Probably the worst teacher I've had at IU. Rude, snarky, puts way too much emphasis on memorizing mechanisms that are easy to look up and not enough on actual applications. His notes are all over the place and constantly criticizes the several-hundred-dollar textbook he made you buy.

Hands down the worst professor on IU's campus. He was rude, gave mechanisms to problems that were not correct then counted them off on tests. Does not tell you what you need to know for the class. According to him, the text book is never right, and neither is online, yet he doesnt give you the answers in class. Rudest teacher at IU as well.

Ted gets way too much flack from students who think they deserve A's without studying (read here pre-meds).  If you genuinely want to learn the subject matter of whatever he is teaching, then he will help you.  Be respectful and he will respect you back.  That being said, Ted is a great professor who tells you exactly what you need to know.

Ted is a demanding professor, but it seems to be his way of keeping you honest.  You earn his respect by performing well and asking good questions in class.  Act scholarly rather than infantile and you will enjoy his class. Warning: you need to study non-stop!

Ted has a very rough exterior but he's really a great guy. I actually like his funny cynical attitude and how pissed off he gets when people walk in late; make me chuckle. Anyway, for an O-chem class Ted's is really not that hard.   Pellerito might be a little easier. Do EVERY problem in the text and memorize pretty much All of the reactions.

Yes, the class was hard.  But it was very clear what was going to be on the test and wasn't on the test.  I only was in his class for biochem II, but he seemed very interested in helping people and even held extra review sessions before a test.  His class definitely weeds people out. Come prepared to memorize your whole textbook.

Have you ever imagined what it would be like to have Dr. House from foxes "House" be your teacher? If so, take this guys class.  He comes complete with the exact same attitude, the exact same damaged leg, plus super tight tee-shirts and biker jackets.
Great professor if he is interested in the subject.  Works very hard to make sure you understand the material.  I wish i could have had him for other classes than just biochem.
ted. wid. lanski
He's an intelligent guy and a decent professor, but he looks down on students all the time and does NOT treat them with any respect. Unless you're an A/A+ student, don't expect him to be nice to you.
meanest teacher, abrasive towards students which is surprising I would feel this in a 300+ person class.  Very unapproachable and condescending

Ted is the worst teacher I've ever had. Clearly doesn't care about undergrads. He berates his students and his teaching style is essentially 'look at how much more I know about orgo than all of you.' The notes he makes in class are hard to follow and are often irrelevant.

Professor Widlanski talked down to his students. Exams were taken during 50 minute lectures, which was not nearly enough time for an orgo exam. I would definitely recommend waiting it out for a better professor. Even if you're up for the challenge, his lectures are terribly boring and unorganized.

By far, the worst professor I have had at IU. He teaches very advanced chemistry that even the AIs had difficulty explaining and understanding, while failing to teach the fundamentals. He is very condescending and will make you feel inferior if you ask for help. If you ask a question about your exam, beware!! You WILL lose points! Run away!

Extremely tough professor. Be prepared to dedicate lots of hours outside of class to study and teach yourself the material. In Spring 09 none of his exams averaged above 60% but he ended up curving grades at the end of the semester.

Tough professor. Be sure to develop good study habits before taking this class, Ted will not spoon feed you the material. If you want a good grade, your going to have to work hard for it and just suck it up. Exams mainly focused on a higher understanding of the material so memorization will not cut it. Don't be late to lecture!

Ted is a jerk.  He constantly makes you feel inferior and as if you are stupid for only being in Organic 1.  He also constantly cut people's grades.  I know someone who had an A and went to a D because they asked a question about an exam.  Very very very unfair.  Very very very hard grader.  Do not take this class and you will continue being happy.

Expect to teach yourself organic. He even states "I'm not your teacher, I'm your coach." Read the book, do the problems and don't expect him to teach you anything. His tests are horribly written, is very NON-specific with them, but expects incredible specificity from you. Refuses to clarify any question on the test. He should NOT be teaching!!!

He could really care less if anyone learned. A horrible representation of IU and of Chem. He taught the class backwards and didn't teach the fundamentals until the last few weeks.  He would leave out huge details in his lectures on purpose. Freq yelled at students and disrespected anyone, whenever he so pleased. He's a bitter, horrible teacher!!

Unbelievably bad professor. He's rude, unapproachable, and--worst of all--is a terrible teacher. He clearly knows his stuff, but he's not interested in trying to make it understandable for undergrads. Seemed like he was at war with the class; he wouldn't give answers to practice problems and was generally vengeful. Avoid him at all costs!!

He lectures clearly. It is evident what he wants from you in class and if you follow his instructions and should be alright. Do the textbook problems, even though they aren't required because they are VERY helpful for the exams. Sometimes, he takes problems straight from the hw on exams. Use his office hours, he's nicer then and more understanding.

Wid is the worst teacher I have ever had. He doesn't care at all how you do in the class and isn't helpful what so ever. He tends to think the book is wrong and teaches is own random topics. His exams are way too long to do in our 50 minute class time. It looks like half of the people have dropped which I would have done had I known he's so awful.

Absolute worst professor imaginable.  You must study for the exam's format, not the material, as you will have only FIFTY MINUTES to take them.  Curved?  Nope.  A majorly mistyped question?  Every time.  And for the love of god, don't sneeze in his class.

Ted single handedly ruined science for me. He is a horrible teacher who makes tests much harder than needed.  I wish i would have known how god awful this teacher was so I could stay as physically far a way as possible. Everything I learned in the class is from the text book, which according to Ted is "Wrong" half the time.
He is a TERRIBLE teacher

Arrogant and much more interested in showing off how much he knows about chemistry rather than expressing interest in actually teaching anything. The book was the only hope for learning a thing. I am sure he was a lot nicer when he was obese.

He is horrible! Tests are honors tests! He has no empathy for anyone! Don't dare be late for class, sleep, or ask a question about the test...he will FREAK! I ruined my GPA w/ this class! I should've dropped by didn't so learn from my mistake and STAY AWAY!!!!

Hardest class I've ever taken. I did not drop it but it takes me a week and a half to prepare for exams and I still barely get a B on them.  He doesn't care about the success of the students in his class and he thinks of himself as a "trainer" instead of a teacher. Stay away!

Professor Widlanski's organic I lectures basically gave me an anxiety disorder. He is clearly used to teaching an honors class and shows no empathy whatsoever. Also he expects ridiculously hard tests to be taken in 50 minute class periods- I had 2 hours for C117 tests! I dropped his class and took the W, hoping for a better professor next semester.

Horrible, horrible. Botched up the one hardest chemistry class we have to take in our undergrad career. Many of us will suffer a bad grade on our transcripts b/c we unknowingly signed up for Ted's class. Very unclear, practice tests are old HONORS tests, doesn't clarify notes in class, just writes and expects you to read his mind. Stay away!!

Clearly knows Chemistry well, but awful at teaching it.  Rushes through material.  The ONLY way to succeed in this class is do book work, his lectures will help you very little if at all. His classes are an assault upon your brain, and I have had him in both honors and regular chem.
He's a horrible professor...rude and doesn't clarify himself at all.  But he has the pectoral muscles of a Greek god!

Awful. There has been an uproar amongst students in the chem department about this man, yet nothing is being done about it. He used to teach honors organic and I think he is still stuck there. I will be retaking this class asap. Avoid at all costs!
He's rude and arrogant

He was by far the WORST professor I have ever had! What I learned from the class was not a result of him teaching me it-it was the result of pouring over my textbook and consulting with others! Put off orgo if you can for a different professor!

This professor is absolutely terrible. During the first lecture he openly stated "I do not care about your grade in this course." When teaching, he simply talks to himself. Not to mention, he pocketed research money intended for another department for his own use in research. He is a horrible, helpless man.

He is heartless.  Tons of people have dropped and are losing sight of med/pt/pa/etc-school dreams due to this man's "teaching". I did really well in 117 but am struggling in this one.  Yells at students for drinking coffee, coming in late, and dozing during lecture-we are college students.  What does he expect? Worst professor I've had.

AWFUL PROFESSOR. STAY AWAY.  I would recommend putting off orgo a semester just to avoid him-you will get a better grade.  The class averages on tests have been a 58% and a 55%.  I can't read his handwriting, he tends to ignore raised hands, slops through the material.  The text my last hope for survival, I feel completely unprepared for CHEM 342.
worst professor I have ever experienced at IU. Completely rude and a terrible teacher, Do not take his class if you ever want to have a future.

Professor Ted was great! He was funny and very helpful throughout the semester.  There is no denying that his class is challenging but in all fairness it is an honors course and it isn't for everyone. All in all I had a good experience and learned a lot!

Be careful with letters of recommendation from this guy.   I  did extreamly well in his class but still got an average letter from him, and he didn't send letters to a number of places he said he would.  A usually excellent classroom teacher, but not very interested in students obtaining professional success for themselves.

This man is ridiculous.  I took his honors orgo class and failed his first exam but  busted my earned a B as my final grade (w/out his help). To make a long story short, I asked for a recommendation letter and instead of saying no he wrote one that was not good at all.  I was told by the PhD that received it to never get a rec. letter from him agai

He isn't especially helpful or clear, but I learned more in his orgo class than I have in any other class. Ever.  But that is a result of my working hard because the class was very hard, not because of him. Take it anyway.

Attendance taken by in class assignments, but a lot of them are dropped, most of the grading is just participating in class which is nice and she is pretty funny and engaging and makes the pretty boring content of i202 actually fun to go through, barely any homework
Decent professor, but the class was dry and not super interesting, which I will try not to blame on her.

Dr. Jen was an amazing professor for I202, you can tell that she genuinely is passionate about the material. Most of your grade will come from 5 papers and the final, so make sure that you are ready and prepared for those. Each paper is about 4 pages. She is really accessible outside of class, and always ready to help!
Very nice and she loves what she does. I'd recommend actually going to class I have over a 100% from the extra credit. Not sure how you could do bad in this class it's pretty straightforward.

Professor Terrell is awesome and loves what she does. Lectures were engaging and fun and attendance is not mandatory (or even taken at all). There are only a few assignments for this class, which could be seen as good or bad. If you do the work on them and follow the rubric, you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. Though most of our classes are lectures, which can be boring, professor Terrell brings a lot of enthusiasm into every class, making the lectures more interesting.

Really does care about her students, and has pretty interesting lectures (If you are interested in the subject matter). Very low workload, one "Journal Entry" weekly (with a 3 day grace period), online midterm, and the final is just a paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: She is an incredibly sweet professor. You can see the passion radiate off her and it is infectious.

I really liked having class with Dr. Jen! She tries to make lecture engaging and interesting. The class is mainly busy work assignments and then a final paper. She tends to ramble and we don't get through everything frequently but I still enjoyed her lectures. You can really tell how much she cares about her students too.

I took Disney: Tech, Tourism & Leisure with Jen, and it is one of the best classes I have taken in a while. I loved her enthusiasm in class each week. She genuinely cares about her students and makes class a fun and interactive environment. I learned something new and useful every class.

I loved having Dr. Jen for I400 this semester. You can tell she loves what shes doing and also cares about students actually learning material and not just about assigning grades and homework. I definitely recommend taking Disney: Tech, Tourism, and Leisure with her.

Dr. Jen is an amazing professor. Her name constantly comes up in conversations about favorite teachers. Her lectures are very conversational, and she does a great job adapting course content to the students' interests.
The professor was nice, but I didn't find this course related to info ethics at all, and nor did I found it helpful. Way below my expectation. Do not recommend.

She is such an amazing professor and one of the best professors I have had at IU. She is incredibly nice and her classes are just wonderful to be in. She has such a nice personality as well. She really loves what she lectures about. She really cares about her students as well. She is just awesome all around!

I had Dr. Terrell for both I202 and I453, she's a great lecturer and highly recommend taking her classes. As long as you put in enough effort you'll be fine. Very welcoming atmosphere that she creates in her classes.

I had her for Advanced Ethics. Take this class it was so much fun diving into ethics in media and books abotu media. TAKE ANY CLASS JEN TERRELL OFFERS great professor and she really cares about your success in the class/college

Dr. Jen is easily one of the best professors at IU. She is so passionate about what she teaches and knowledgeable. She also challenges students to see the world and technology in a different perspective. She's also very caring and accepting, which makes the atmosphere of her classes worth taking as well.

Dr. Jen is one of the best professors I've had at IU. She has a doctorate in Informatics and goes strongly in depth about social informatics. Her lectures are/were never a waste of time, she's a great personality and is extremely genuine.
Jen is a great professor. Lots of opportunity for extra credit and her lectures aren't a waste of time ever. She really does her best to make it interesting and engaging.

Jen is the best professor I have had since being at IU. She is extremely passionate and understandable when it comes to lectures, and she takes her time to explain all aspects of the course to you. Her team as a whole is wonderful. Attendance is graded and there are only two or three take-home assignments all semester. One test and one paper. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She was awesome all semester. She really cares about ethics and the course (she created it). She made sure to talk to us as equals and made sure we got the most out of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Be wary this class is constructed in the world view of the graduate ais and professors who designed the class and is more so a class on social justice than on computer and information ethics. Many of the teachers do not even have a formal background in technology and tend to oversimplify and abstract technology and political theories.
Dr. Terell is awesome. Show up and do the outside class assignments and you'll be fine.

Teaching style is lecture-heavy, with some outside assignments. Dr. Jen, to me, is a fantastic lecturer. The way she explains things is clearly and easy to understand, and the structure of the course allows for easy learning. Just show up, don't cheat, do the assignments on time, and use the slides to study.

This is definitely as easy A and Jen makes it more fun. Just go to class and pay attention and you should be good for the quizzes and papers. It definitely isn't much work but do the readings she posts. She gives you about 3 extra credit opportunities so those guarantee you an A.

This class is an early class for me, as it is hard to wake up attend class Jennifer makes this class worth going. Every class I walk away with new insights. She challenges your thinking. She puts a lot of effort into making this class interesting and I tend to share a lot of the class content with my friends and family. Great Class, Great Prof.

This class is an early class for me, as it is hard to wake up attend class Jennifer makes this class worth going. Every class I walk away with new insights. She challenges your thinking. She parts a lot of effort into making this class interesting and I tend to share a lot of the class content with my friends and family. Great Class, Great Prof.

Loved, LOVED this class. Super interesting lecture content, and pretty dang easy if you just do the readings (which are normally around 4 pages). Raise your hand maybe once per class and you and Jen will basically be  best friends.  Honestly best Info class I've taken so far- convinced me to minor in HCC. Cool class, cool professor. Would recommend

Jennifer was one of the best professors I've had at IU so far. Lectures are optional but definitely help if you go. She makes learning easy in her classroom. Papers are a bit difficult but if you ever need help with anything she is there. There are 4 extra credit opportunities given out, no doubt you should get a good grade in this class!

She made the summer class super easy.  As long as you were there and did the work.  All of the quizzes were open book, note, internet.  The papers were self-explanatory.  I would definitely take another class with her.

I would recommend not taking I202 with her. There are readings every week and she barely goes through them and when she does go through them she goes way to fast and hardly explains everything. The papers in the class are not very clear and the final and midterm are all over the readings. I would avoid her if you can.

Took her for online W131 best choice ever. Such a sweet professor and easy and chill class. You can get three skips. Homework and essays are never hard, very lenient about asking for extensions and help outside of the classroom. 100% recommend.

! If you want an easy A, take her, she is very lenient compared to the syllabus. If you are communicative with her and stay engaged her in class, she is willing to help out and bend the rules a little for you! I appreciated the flexibility she gave for extensions since I had so much packed in my schedule and she wants you to do well in the course!!

I LOVE HER!!!!! Such an easy and fair grader if you follow the rubric. I took W131 and recommend this class to everyone. It's over zoom, but you are allowed 3 absences. 3 projects over the course of the semester and then a final portfolio of what you would change about your projects to make them better. Highly recommend if you get the chance!!!
IF YOU HAVE YOUR CAMERA OFF FOR MORE THAN 15 MINUTES YOUR GRADE DROPS A LETTER. Literally keep your camera on, class is easy as hell. My grade dropped a whole letter because of that stupid thing.

Teacher really enjoys what she does and makes online class very enjoyable. A lot of easy homework to get a good grade so as long as you submit your assigbements on time and do what the basic requirements should be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Super nice dude. The only thing is he grades hard. Get ready to get a 4.2/7 on some random assignments. Honestly think he uses chat to grade.

Professor Thomas was a fantastic professor who laid out expectations for every assignment. He also met with every group during multiple classes in case competition season and graded the final project easy. Very personable in and outside of class time and his lectures provided examples he knew we would be familiar with. Good source for rec letter

Amazing teacher. If you can take his class, take it. If you make an effort to meet with him during office hours it will significantly help you understand what needs to be done to do well on assignments.

Without a doubt the hardest C204 teacher in Kelley. Other teachers grade way easier and assign less assignments. Do anything you can to not take this teacher. He will kill your gpa for no reason. His feedback doesn't really let you get any better and has an inconsistent grading scale that he will defend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Grades way harder than other C204 professors for no reason. Feedback makes no sense and rubrics are impossible to understand. Just save yourself the trouble and take another professor's section.

He's super understanding and would even extend the deadlines for assignments if he knew we had exams/big assignments for other classes. He tries to make sure that we do as much work as we can in class so we don't have a lot of homework. Would def recommend him if you're in Kelley and have to take C204.

Great professor give very clear guidelines on assignments and projects and is available for consistent and helpful feedback. Also is caring and is sometimes willing to change class structure based on the students such as giving extensions or pushing back certain assignments till later.

This semester was his first time teaching bus-c 204. His grading was tougher than all the other professors and his feedback was more geared towards an English class rather than a business course. He also has no business experience, which made his lectures very boring.

Professor Thomas was absolutely amazing. Although W121 is a writing heavy course naturally, he does his best to space out assignments so students are not overwhelmed. Most of our essays were based off of the Sopranos Tv show so if you like the mob and villainy, youll love this class!

Amazing teacher! He was a fairly harsh grader, but I loved that! Every time he it caused the class to hush and listen to his inevitably inspirational comments. He was very passionate about his class and was a good guy overall. I wish I could have Chris as my instructor for every English class in the future. Highly recommend.

By far my favorite professor so far at IU. He is truly passionate about teaching. Since he is younger it is easy to relate to him and he tries to do the same with his students. He will help you in any way possible. Professor Thomas helped me appreciate writing again and actually enjoy it.
Good guy and pretty easy grader.

Tests expect high levels of precision in answers, but scores are curved. Just attend lectures and discussion sections + make sure you have a moderate understanding of the handouts and you'll be fine. It helps to have basic knowledge of philosophy-lingo before taking this course. I personally found it easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy! He does get off topic alot during lecture but it is very obvious he loves and is passionate regarding what he lectures about. The class is very test heavy but he prepares you very well. I took intro to philosophy as a freshman and it can be difficult to follow if you do not find this stuff interesting. Overall hes great and funny.

Professor O'Connor was a great lecturer and seemed like a really interesting dude. He got off topic a lot. The content of the class was dense, and I found it to be very difficult to learn (memorize). This is not an easy gen-ed, and grading is tough, but I think the class was worth taking. It was the only A- I received as a freshman.
DO NOT TAKE AS A GEN ED. There are so many easier classes out there. Notes were very hard to understand and decipher. 50 minute lectures dragged on forever and didnt make sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: get ready to take the hardest tests ever. Grading doesn't even make sense, he looks for answers so specific that you wouldnt remember them if you had the answer key. Reading is so boring, and if you have an interpretation other than his, you're wrong and good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting course. Weekly quizzes during the discussion section. Readings help with those but are not that necessary for exams. The professor tries to make the class engaging and can be funny. Gives a study guide with the exact test questions. Use the PowerPoint to fill out the study guide and you will get an A on exams. super easy for a gen-ed.

Interesting content, clearly is passionate, but is hard to stay engaged in lectures. Tough to even get a word in sometimes. Holds writers to a "high standard" but not much feedback on writing itself -- hard to grasp what he's looking for/how to improve. Seems like a really friendly and smart guy, just not a very collaborative classroom + confusing.

My friend summed up this class perfectly, "He has little respect for the philosophical capabilities of his students, and he loves to hear himself talk. This leads to lectures with no open discussion... His exams consist of regurgitating arguments instead of philosophizing."
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. O'Connor's course was boring the majority of the time. Lectures are boring and consist of Tim talking the whole hour. Attendance is not mandatory for lectures and all the notes can be found online. There are four grades total, two exams, a paper, and writing assingment. Exams are quite easy and are exact same as the study guide.
This class is simply cool. Some of the topics will spin your head, while Tim pushes you to think, think, think. We had more fun in this class than any I've been in. Take any class he teaches.

Dr. O'Connor is my favorite professor of all time. Genius. Lectures were fantastic. Reading was from the top level sources. Great variety of topics covered. Spent tons of time with my outside of class and through email. Nicest guy too. Recommended for upper-level students w/ experience in philosophy. If you don't understand, go to office or email.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: for context, I'm a straight A student and salutatorian of my class. Took this 1st sem Freshman year. by far the hardest class I had to get in an A in, with biology chemistry and sociology. The professors lectures were unorganized and not helpful to class. reading reactions-easy. AI graders and seemed subjective. class was out of 100 pts. NOT EASY!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: First Day of class Professor O'Connor removed A+ from the grade scale and claimed no one was going to receive an A+ in his class, and very few, if any, would receive an A at all. Do not take this class for an easy A. Readings are long and difficult to comprehend at times. Seemed like an OK guy but I felt as though he wasn't there for his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's super chill, friendly, and knowledgable. Highly recommend.

Dude is an absolute chiller. 231 is also very easy if you're fine with doing some writing. He uses a e-textbook for most lectures and asks you to read it for homework, but it doesn't matter if you do or not.
1 of 1 couldn't of asked for a better teacher

Professor Townsend is one of the kindest and smartest teachers I have ever had. He is always willing to help you in whatever way works best for you and you will never leave his class without understanding what needs to be done or how to do it. All of the assignments and essays are fairly easy. Attendance counts and the textbook is online.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Colby, honestly, his class was great. We had to get one book, barely used it though. Only have two papers and they are on the same topic, very easy to accomplish. Especially with how much time he gives. He's sweet and tries to make the class entertaining. Two assignments a week but more than manageable. Highly Recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
I took W131 last semester and dropped it because my last professor made me absolutely HATE writing. Props to Professor Townsend to make me enjoy and better my writing again! 
One of my favorite professors!

Best English Professor I have ever had. He really made me feel like my writing was valuable and motivated me to do better. If you want to get a good grade and also become more confident in your writing, enrol in his class. He is very understanding and will work with you and help you with any issues regarding the course. I loved going to class.
One of the best Professors for English W 131.
(HISP-250)- Professor Robinson is a fantastic educator. She's very helpful and understanding and uses a great balance of Spanish and English in class.

She is so caring and actually cares about her students. Quizzes are online, but there are in-person exams, oral exams, and writing exams. She is really good at her job and will change the course to make it better for the students.
She is very kind and a good teacher.
Profe Tory is an awesome professor! She makes class fairly easy and is always willing to help with assignments. Definitely recommend.

Profe Tory was incredible and so much fun to be around! She made sure we all understood the material while we were in class and would make sure to take the time to help us. She also would help us with the homework if we ever needed it and it was never too much homework. I would recommend to everyone!

I absolutely love Profe Tory! I highly recommend her if you are taking Spanish 105 or 200. She explained the content well and she truly does care for her students. I have nothing bad to say about Profe Tory.

Professor Robinson is an amazing teacher. She genuinely cares about all of her students and she is always willing to give extra help outside of class if you need it. If you have to take Spanish I would 100% recommend you try to get a class with her.

Profe Tory is one of the kindest professors I have had so far. Not only this, but her lectures are clear and concise and she ensures her students understand material thoroughly. I totally recommend taking a class with her if you have the chance!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The day before the exam, he suddenly changed the format, leaving us completely unprepared. His so-called review session consisted of just a couple of irrelevant remarks. He even admitted himself that he graded the exams arbitrarily. And if you wanted any feedback like where you needed to improve, he certainly couldn't provide any
He was an okay prof.

Professor Rabovsky is very knowledgeable about what he teaches, and he is very thorough in his lectures. However, there is a LOT of information to take in, and you are graded mainly on your 3 exams in the class. Show up, take notes, and study, and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take him! He seemed nice and gave good face to face feedback on group paper when you go to him. You have very few assignments in this class and 3 exams. Exams are 75% of your grade and are all multiple choice. If you're a good test taker this would be good for you but if you aren't STAY CLEAR of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super good at explaining things. Is lecture heavy
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Miss you professor kennedy. You would be proud today.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had in Kelley. It's impossible to learn anything from his class if you don't have a passion for tax, and know bunch of random facts about the US tax system.

Provided the best real life examples to remember class topics and taught me not just a lot of tax technical content, but how to be a great tax professional.  His style, however, is not for everyone.  He has the best stories from his career in tax.  Tom is probably better for someone with a career interest in tax.

Doesn't really follow any kind of a structure when teaching in class. All over the place. Assumes that you know a bunch of random things about tax for some reason, and goes off those things a lot of the time. Has a lot of interesting opinions, but not particularly related to the things that we need to be learning for the exams.
Doesn't really go through problems or help you with the mechanics of tax. Take Peggy instead, i've heard she's leaps and bounds better.
Professor Walker is a good teacher. If you attend class regularly you will get an A. All of the quiz answers are given in class so just show up.

He's a great guy, but he's not a good undergraduate teacher for this course. Instead of showing the math, he essentially just has you memorize a bunch of formulas without going into the meanings. He says you don't need the book - you do. But, the practice exams are the same as the real exams so he tries to make it easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I loved Mr. Walker! If you take Econ115, GO TO CLASS! This class isn't that hard, but you need to go to every class. I thought that sometimes he wanted very specific answers to questions, my advice is that include any and all information related to the question or he'll dock you points

Very insightful and thoughtful professor. Loved going to his lectures. Content is meaningful and pertinent to real life. If you take notes and pay attention, exams are easy especially with his reviews. I highly recommend Prof Walker and his class Everyday Economics.

Prof. Walker is a very positive and encouraging instructor. If you pay attention and take notes, the exams are easy. If you know everything on his review materials, you will ace the exams. Many items are exactly the same as the review material "examples". He's really great! Boring subject not so bad with him as instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Walker is highly underrated! Economics can sometimes be a dry subject, but he does his best to make lecture enjoyable. Homework is light, usually turned in once a week. Literally puts the exact questions from lecture and homework on the tests. Mr. Walker wants you to succeed! I recommend taking his class.

Walker is the best professor I have had at IU so far. He is really laid back and thoughtful for his students. This course is what sparked my interest in economics and has been really helpful in core classes. I really recommend him and his new course: Everyday Economics 115
Fantastic Professor! Keeps class interesting and relevant.
The worst professor I have ever had. After the second month I started skipping his lectures and still got my A! You should really delve into the books on your own, because this guy is useless...
Great professor. Made the material interesting and included a lot of real world examples. Gives a nice curve as well.

He always gets sidetracked during lectures so ur basically on ur own. He is also a tough grader which sucks. And exams were worth like 75% of the grade, no matter what u did it wasn't enough. If there is another philosophy class available with another Professor, take that one.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Redundant and went off on tangents about unimportant things. However, if you ignore the lectures and go to your discussions, you will do fine. The readings were very important to the success of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Tim is a really nice guy who cares about his students, however it's really hard to follow what he's saying in class. The slideshows he prepares have good content on them, but he always explains them horribly. Tests are 75% of grade and it's basically all on you to learn the material. What you are able to learn can be pretty interesting tho.

This professor has very confusing lectures that honestly don't make very much sense. I was taking this class to satisfy one of my gen ed credits, this was NOT a good choice. He treats his students when it comes to the exams as if they're advanced in philosophy. His exams are super hard, and graded very heavy. Don't recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS! He makes what could be and okay class so much more difficult because he's incredibly harsh when grading exams which are your whole grade. There are no lecture slides he'll give a handout that is basically useless. He goes off topic 80% of the time which is inconvenient. He's super nice just not a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is genuinely the worst professor I've had in the entirety of my college career. On the first day of class he claimed the class would be student led and discussion based, however he allots maybe 10 minutes to student questions in which he interrupts, adds his own biases, and answers with useless unrelated responses every time.

Tim OConnor spends half his time teaching and the other half ranting. He gives daily quizzes which have proven to be difficult. His TAs grade papers and exams harshly as well. If you enjoy banging your head into a brick wall take this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Really cool topics. O'Connor's funny and smart, and open to your ideas. He looks like he's having a lot of fun.

He has little respect for the philosophical capabilities of his students, and loves to hear himself talk. This leads to lectures with no open discussion, as O'Conner would rather waste time smack-talking other philosophers than call on students with questions and counterpoints. His exams consist of regurgitating arguments instead of philosophizing.
Everything on the exams are taken straight from the lectures
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof. O'Conner was my favorite instructor this term. Very smart, and usually pretty entertaining. The readings could be very hard to digest, but he tells you everything you need to know in lecture, and you can download his powerpoints. He also responds promptly to email and clearly answers questions.

Not easy to take it all in, but the ideas were really interesting, most of the time. Aristotle was fun, Kant was rough. If you go to class, the powerpoints lay everything out clearly. Tim is very smart, and he's also funny.

Tim is a great guy and means well, but his lectures are very boring and he rambles on far too often. The AIs try to salvage lecture material in discussion but it doesn't always work out. He quizzes over the minute part of boring reading material.
Interesting material. You get what you need from lectures - what's not covered in class is not on the exam.
The readings aren't necessary, as long as you go to class take notes and fill out the study guides its a pretty easy class.
Don't need to read just go to class and take notes and all the tests will be easy. He gives study guides that are word for word the questions on the test

Incredibly energetic and passionate about the material. Wants you to succeed. This was easily the most fun and mind-blowing class I have had at IU. Warning: it's not easy! Go to office hours, talk to him after class. He's very approachable and seems to live for talking about philosophy. I hope to take him again before I graduate.

You can tell that he's a really really nice guy. He's just not meant to teach an introductory class. He goes off rambling in lectures and it is very hard to pay attention. He does make it possible to do well with study guides and office hours. Overall if you are a business major like me, then I don't think you will like the class.

This guy just won't stop rambling. Totally just thinks out loud in his PhD jargon. Extremely hard to understand, and grades pretty harshly for a freshman topics course. Not recommended. I did ok only because the AI, Allen Gehring, got me through it.
His students run his class, not him. He lets them ramble and has no control over his own class. Also, seems to be a self-hating closet case.
His class was very challenging and demanding, and i studied for a whole week and still got a C- on a test. He's very nice, so go to office hours & he'll remember that when it comes to grade time.

Let's students that have wild theories with no backing ramble on. Also, has pop quizzes to punish students that don't read books that have nothing to do with the tests. Not a hard professor if you keep up with the material. Does not seem to value students' time... only his own.
HORRIBLE TEACHER. makes you not want to go to class. half the class dropped after the first test.

I took medieval philosophy with him. He's very energetic and makes it fun. You should read the material outside of class and he's more than willing to help. Warning: Professor O' Connor isn't priivy about human nature and the brain - if you aren't familiar with science you'll actually believe some the arguments you go over are true. They aren't.
Easy class, but he certainly doesn't care about his students.  Just study the notes and you'll ace the exams.
No Comments
harder than necessary
um...your screwed

Amazingly knowledgeable man.  One of the top schollars in Free Will.  Not an easy professor, but is very receptive to participation in class and office hours visits.  Slightly dorky, but in a very amicable way.  Recomended.
He makes absolutely no sense.  He is a nice guy, but his tests and papers are hard and what he teaches does not really apply.  He also is horrible at lecturing.
Tim's one of those professors you either get, or don't.  It's that simple.  I got Tim's methods fairly quickly, and did well in his class.  Not a good professor for non-majors
Good professor but his tests are hard.  Helped persuade me to change my major to philosophy.
Terrible teacher, grades did not adequately show what you had learned in the classes, only had a few tests and one paper, that determined your final grade.
He was great at teaching the specified matter, and developed enough of an interest in philosophy in me for me to major in it.
has no idea how to explain anything to his students.  everything is so jumbled in his head when it comes out it is unintelligible.  terrible prof.
It was a pretty difficult class, but Tim is very helpful and a great lecturer.
Intro to symbolic logic is pretty hard, but Tim is doing a great job of helping me through it.  I thought I was going to fail the class, and now I think I will end up with a B.
IT is a hard class, you need to study, and be prepared to drop if neccessary.
Pretty good teacher, but you better be dang good at test taking. My grade for this semester consists of 3 tests and attending discussion, that's it.
No Comments
He is a hot potatie!!!

Dr. Pappas made a seemingly plain course into a very hilarious 9am class! He is very understanding that most students are in much more complicated courses, so he sticks to a simple schedule of homework due on Monday and a 5-10 minute quiz on Wednesday (for example). I highly recommend his 2-credit course and would take it again!
I would highly recommend this class to anyone interested in medical sciences. He is a great professor. I took the class at 8am, and he always made the class enjoyable.

Great professor, made the material much more engaging. Lectures made sense and there was a clear grading criteria. Made lots of jokes and puns, too bad class atmosphere was dead at 9:00am and nobody was laughing but he kept it going till the very end and I appreciated that. Highly recommend taking this

This professor is amazing. He makes the material fun for people who are taking this class as a gen-ed or people taking this class as a minor requirement. He's a super great guy. He loves what he does and talks fast when he gets excited about certain topics. He's super knowledgeable. Definitely one of my favorite professors. 10/10 recommend.

Travis knows a ton about the material, but his lectures can be a little boring and he talks pretty fast. He's a really nice guy though, and you'll definitely learn a lot. Exams were online but still kinda hard, while the homework was fairly easy. Overall, I'd recommend his class.

This class was a bit dry at times, and I did not feel like I learned a lot about extreme weather; however, I gained a better understanding of how to read and interpret a research article. Travis is extremely accommodating (he canceled our last assignment out of the blue), but he does like group projects so make sure you find people to work with.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Earth Dynamic Atmosphere was a fun online class and the professor was very helpful with the video lectures. The homework and discussion boards were easy, but the test were not.

You will have to read a paper every week for the class. They can be fairly long. You don't have to know every detail, but the class is mostly based on discussion, which is where the grade comes from. Participation in class is key to a good grade. Travis is a very helpful and caring professor, and is good at explaining things
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Travis is so nice and understanding. He cares a lot about students' feedback and understanding of class topics. Class was not hard at all, but I enjoyed the discussions we had. We read two papers a week and had homework that went with them about our understanding. Interesting class.
Really difficult class, but you genuinely learn so much through the projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Loved my IFS class with him! Grading isn't that hard, you just need to make sure to actually put in effort and time on your assignments. He also really cares and is willing to help if you need it. 100% would recommend

Of all the professors in Informatics, he was my favorite and loved every lecture and project. With Travis I felt respected and appreciated. His classes helped me with interviews and to feel more confident for post-graduation. TAKE HIS CLASS because he teaches you a lot! If you care he will too.

Not finished with the class yet, but easily one of the best teachers I've had. Genuinely enjoys what he does and assigns projects that are relevant to real life. Encourages student ideas and pushes them to turn those ideas into real business plans or products.

I absolutely LOVED TJB, his class has been my favorite at IU thus far. All of the assignments are team and project based, and very realistic and hands on. I actually learned valuable skills in this class. My favorite thing about Travis is that he is very clear with course objectives, and rechecks AI grading to check for inconsistencies.

Travis is fair and reasonable. Although half of your grade is made up of group projects, he allows you to "fire" group members who slack off or "fire" yourself to work as an individual. Various opportunities for extra credit. Office hours are worthwhile, but you'll be there for longer than you'd anticipate.
Take the class with ANYONE else
BEST TEACHER EVER! Cannot recommend him anymore. Truly care for his students. Easy class if you show up. Everyone take his class.

Best professor I've had at IU. Class is relativity easy but attendance is the majority of the grade and it is long but he keeps it interesting. Especially if it is. Smaller section since everyone is asking questions and engaged.

Love this guy, attendance is 40% of your grade the rest is in class quizzes and tests that are relatively light.  No homework outside of class the only thing you'll need to do is show up, take notes and do some light review.  Gives tons of extra credit, super easy A

He was one of my favorite professors/teachers I have ever had. I LOVED this class and genuinely looked forward to it during the week. Travis is so funny and interactive with the class and his dog Jake is the cutest thing (his dog he brings to class!). If you take this class you will not regret it! Attendance mandatory but it was always worth going!

he is great if you want an A has a personality that you either loved or hated, I LOVED him, the grades are only for attendance and tests 6quizes and 3tests which are fairly easy and mcq, the only  thing is that he doesnt share notes and if you missed a class you are gonna have to get your notes from another student, gives extra credit that=quiz

Travis is the best! He teaches in a way where everything just sticks with me and makes sense. He also just presents all the information in an interesting and digestible way. He is very strict on attendance but I didn't even want to miss his class. There's also no homework and the quizzes and tests are very reasonable.

I adore Travis and want to take all of my SPH classes with him. He's hilarious, so real, knowledgable, + passionate about the class topics. Attendance is important as he doesn't post lecture slides. No tech rule but I found it beneficial. No reading or hw bc he tells you everything you need to know in lecture. I always look forward to his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Lawson is awesome! Class is like a stand-up comedy show most of the time because of how out of pocket or funny he is. He also brings his dog, Jake, who is an adorable border collie/german shepherd mix I believe. Overall a great class!

Not only did I receive closure from events from my past, but this course helped my future. I have brought friends to his lecture and showed family members my notes. I believe that everyone paying tuition at iu should get to experience this course and an instructor like Travis. Just come to class cuz EVERYHTING is inperson.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hands down best prof at IU. He actually made the topic of public health incredibly interesting and I found myself WANTING to go to his class. He brings his dog Jake sometimes and he's the best dog ever. Such a good prof as long as you go to class and pay attention to what he's saying (he emphasizes the important things 2-3 times) you will get an A.

I would actually die for this man. He is the most relatable and funniest professor I've had at this school. Genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He makes learning about all areas of public health easy and interesting. Travis is the BEST!!!!!

Just make sure you go to class because his lectures are literally the key to passing with more than a B in this class. He is amazing! Three exams in total and 6 quizzes(could be 7 or 5 depends) curves!!!! This class is so worth every second because he actually teaches the class and not just lecture.

I truly loved his class. If you have any interest in public health then I really would suggest taking this class with him. He does not give out any homework, he is super funny, and the lectures are very interesting. He is very passionate about what he teaches making it easy to learn. However, he is strict on the use of electronics in the class.
Favorite professor I've had so far. His lectures are very interesting.

I really like Mr. Travis a lot! Almost all of his content were interesting and I can see how it applied into my life. However he loves to go off topic and sometime we're spending the a big chunks of the class on some irrelevant questions. But overall he is the GOAT.

Dr. Lawson is super kind and clearly understands what he's teaching. I have zero complaints on how he runs the class and he also gives no homework. As long as you pay attention to the lectures, this class is very easy.

No phones/computers allowed in class but for good reasons, and all notes are on paper. If you pay attention and listen his lectures you will do well in class. Super nice and is always available to listen to you if needed. Very fun teacher and you can tell he cares about what he is teaching and about his students.

You aren't allowed to use any electronic devices while in class but it's all for good reasons. If you go to class and stay interested you will receive a good grade. He is a great and very experienced professor who knows his stuff.

NO PHONES allowed during class, do not even try. You also have to use paper & pencil to take notes. I LOVED him. One of my favorite classes & best professors I've had. He is SO funny & made the 2.5 hours so enjoyable. 3 tests & a weekly quiz, but if you pay attention they're not hard at all. I would recommend him to everyone! I'm fr gonna miss him.

Ended my 2.5 hour, 8 week course early often. NO PHONES allowed during class and have to use paper & pencil to take notes. Attendance is mandatory, but you get 1 freebie. Quizzes once a week and 3 tests total (all multiple choice). Easy if you pay attention during lecture, repeats important info a lot. Knows what he's talking about, and very funny.

Prof. Lawson is seriously one of the best professors I've had. He is super knowledgeable ab anything. REALLY admired how he encouraged students to ask questions no matter how relevant. He genuinely cares ab our safety and emphasizes harm-reduction strategies. So easy to talk to & hooked me up with a good connection for my future career!

travis is one of my favorite professors. hes absolutely hilaroius and i always enjoy coming to class. he is anti technology so you can only take notes by hand and no phones allowed, but its honestly worth it. definetely will be taking another class with him
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely such an amazing professor. You can tell he cares about his students' education. Encourages questions and knows a lot about all different types of subjects. Very transparent about what our quizzes and tests would look like. Also has very funny jokes! Definitely will take another one of his classes.

Just want an easy A? Take him. You'll do fine if you never disagree on anything. But if the traits "egotistical and unkind" annoy you, stay away. Examples: Belittled the entire class for sending "useless and pointless" emails about a grading inconsistency he never explained. Unironically said "I know A LOT of things" every class. Choose wisely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved him! SO funny and smart and knows EVERYTHING
gives great feedback and will make you a better presenter.

Prof Kerle is super nice! She grades a little hard and is very specific with elements of your delivery. Know that most of your presentation is graded off delivery. But she really cares and helps out a lot! Her tough grading has made me a better presenter and honestly I thought I was a pretty decent presenter before, but now I feel a lot stronger.

Kerle' really cares about her students; as long as you show up, put in the work, and ask for feedback (she loves that), you'll get an A. Group projects are unfortunate, since you could get stuck with a poor team, but she understands that and accommodates it.

She challenges you strictly but is genuinely supportive. She helped me resolve group issues and coached me to speak slower. I barely made an A (93.37%), but the high standards make sense. My only issue is that everyone on your team gets same grade. It's like giving Mario Chalmers the same salary as LeBron just because they're on the same team.
Super nice professor who helped me a lot with my public speaking skills and encouraged me to think outside the box.
