Kerle was an amazing prof with great feedback! She grades pretty strictly, but she gives you a rubric beforehand. A lot would say she's too strict with formatting and technical stuff, but I honestly think her teaching made me a better presenter. Grateful she was my professor!

Professor Kerle is an honest grader, which is why some people may dislike her. But in my opinion, her honesty made me a much better public speaker and made me perform well in Business Presentations. I really recommend taking this class with her because it will set you up for success in your future at Kelley. She really cares for her students!

Professor Kerle was very encouraging with feedback. Sometimes she can be confusing but I really enjoyed taking this class. It's a Kelley Pre-Req, so you'll have to take it. Her final speech is a lot easier than all of the other professors, just go to class and try the best you can, and you will end with an A. I highly recommend her as a professor!
Professor K was always encouraging and a highly interesting lecturer. While I absolutely hated the class, she made it a whole lot better because she was always there for support.

Prof K is awesome and super nice. Cares so much about her students and gives TONS of feedback after each speech. She wants you to succeed. Go to her and ask for help if you need. Make sure not to cram before each speech. You will enjoy the class if you prepare and try your best. She doesn't grade too hard at all.

Professor Kerle' is a very caring professor, she always provides a ton of feedback to students and makes herself available. If you put in the time and effort in this class, you will easily do well. She doesn't grade super tough but does stick to the rubric which she makes clear. Attendance is tracked but doesn't count for much.

Prof K was by far my favorite professor. She was very caring and genuinely wanted every student to succeed and improve their presentation skills. She was not a harsh grader! Gives very thorough instructions and provides examples from past semesters. I definitely recommend taking her section of the course.
One of the best teachers I have had so far. I am glad to have had her as my business pres teacher.
Prof. Kerle was a good teacher overall. She is tough on her grading rubics. Just come to class and do the work and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Honestly I loved Prof Kerle. She truly cares about her students and would do anything for them if they needed. Can be considered a "hard grader" but I personally did not think this as every grade you get is deserving.
Non stop presentations, graded heavily and harshly on rubric and structure. A- must be the best grade possible

Once of the best teachers I have ever had. She is very transparent when it comes to her feedback which only makes her students better. She also follows her rubrics very closely which is difficult to adapt to at first, but overtime makes her students more efficient and effective presenters. I would definitely take her course again.
Just dont take her for this C104 class or you will regret ur whole life
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor, u wont learn anything from taking this bad professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Nice teacher that gave good feedback. She genuinely cares about improving your speaking skills. Otherwise I thought she was tougher than the other BUS-C 104 professors and is pretty strict about students following her rubric. You definitely have to work to meet her expectations.

Hardest c104 prof by far at Kelley. Grades way harder, rubrics are very complex/strict, and presentation prompts are harder than other classes. She doesn't let you pick your teams, and you aren't allowed to use the confidence monitor (the screen in the back of the room the displays your powerpoint). Oh, and SHE DIDNT ROUND MY 86.7 (b) TO AN 87(b+)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor! I love her class and she is really willing to help. The grade that you will get equals how much hard work you put in.

Professor Kerle is a really hard grader and not flexible at all. you cant miss class or if you have an exam on the same day as a presentation you cant do anything about it. it sucks. otherwise she's really nice and gives good feedback.
Really fun class.  I got kind of screwed over with my group, but other than that I did not have to spend much time outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She's a bit of a hard grader in the beginning, but by the end of the semester you'll get the grade you deserve. I received B's in the beginning but ended my semester getting an overall A. If you use the rubric as a guide to your speeches and you can talk without sounding monotone or memorized, you'll do fine. Def recommend, was my fav class

This class requires effort, and may be a little challenging for students who are shy of speaking in public, but it is so worth taking it (plus its a requirement.) Prof. Kerle is an amazing teacher, but she's not gonna be easy on you.

I actually really enjoyed having Trisha as a professor. She's probably the only teacher iv'e had that has made me actually laugh out loud at her jokes. Super down to earth person and knowledge. Exams are somewhat difficult but I think that goes for any law imo. I would def recommend to take her to others.

Very kind teacher who cares about the material. Lectures can get boring but she interjects with her own stories as an attorney. She is a very light grader and allows for a 1 page sheet on all tests. The tests were all very fair and she goes over what is going to be on it. Pay attention and you will do well.

Gives plenty of time for assignments, even if you were unable to complete them on time. Very understanding professor, she adds her own stories to the lectures which is nice, especially for a somewhat boring topic like law imo. She goes over what's on the exam and provides a 1 page cheat sheet, just do the work and you'll get a A-B

A great, caring, respected, and knowledgeable professor who really wants you to succeed in this class, her lecture might be a bit boring, but she tries her best to make it fun. Clear grading criteria; not an easy A, but if you put in the work, you will be able to receive an A.

Professor Bushey is easily one of my favorite profs at IU. Her class is interesting, she curves grades, and her lectures were entertaining and educational. I have depression and a chronic physical condition, and when I communicated with her, she gave me plenty of flexibility and grace to get my work done. She was so supportive. Take this class!!!

This class was one of my favorites! Professor Bushey uses many stories that she has encountered in law school and in her career to make lectures very enjoyable and funny. She is a great person and a very funny lecturer. The 3 exams are relatively easy and focus on big picture ideas. The case briefs are super easy and the quizzes are as well. Great!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: They really are a great person and professor. They are also very reasonable about deadlines and gives generous extensions if needed. This class helped me improve as a writer so much and was one of my favorite classes.

Laura has been my favorite professor. They give solid feedback and genuinely care about students lives and their understanding of the topics. They went to extreme lengths to make sure we had time to review feedback from them as well as other students. I looked forward to this class and I am kinda sad that it is ending.

Interactive teaching style, very understanding. The way they set up class time and assignment due dates is very helpful and actually lets you use class time to work and get peer feedback along with feedback from the professor themselves.

Extra assignments that don't work towards the 3 short assignments and 3 essays, which is 40% of your grade is why most of the class was clueless about the structure of the assignments. There are also no clear grading criteria and you are expected to submit a draft on Tuesday but submit the final by Friday so there is no feedback.

Prof. Tscherry is probably one of my favorite teachers I've ever had. They are so caring and will do anything to help you succeed, and will work with you on flexible deadlines. They are incredibly intelligent and the class is just a fun class, especially if English is your thing. If you have argumentative writing w Tscherry, it will be a blast.

Professor Tscherry is incredibly intelligent. Her lectures are so clear and she offers great feedback on all assignments. An A is definitely manageable if you go to class and do the readings and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Tscherry cares for the class and students. With that said she is very understanding and can help you through the course if you are struggling. There are no tests, just papers and some homework with plenty of time to complete. I would definitely take her class. It is an easy A if you go to class and do the work.

She is an amazing professor. She is ALWAYS available and willing to help. This is an extremely hard class though. Do not take this until you feel comfortable with Japanese and linguistics. Th class consists of assignments, quizzes, and a final paper/presentation. Very hard but interesting class.

Makes fun of students. Rude. Not willing to help students. A real joy of a teacher :/                    I love learning Japanese, but somehow she was able to make it an awful experience with her bad attitude.
Was very demanding and appeared strict, but cares a lot for her students and goes out of her way to help them learn.

I had Tsujimura Sensei for two years and I enjoyed her class. Yes, it was difficult and there was a lot of material to memorize in a short amount of time, but I actually learned it and retained it. (I forget it now but haven't had any one to speak Japanese with!) I wish other language departments would use methods like hers more - it would help.

Japanese linguistics class was incredibly challenging, and not because of the Japanese aspect. If you are a FRESHMAN, please do NOT take this class without SOME prior knowledge of linguistics! Very fair grader and teacher, though; very kind and helpful. J421 was VERY challenging. Please be aware of this aspect, and TALK TO YOUR ADVISOR!

This class was hard.  Not like "Oh, I have to write a paper" hard, more like learning 40-60 new words and 2-5 grammar concepts every week and she expects you to use them fluently the day after they're introduced.  Said in class she expects you to spend 3-4 hours a day every day on homework and practice.
Very good professor, also very good looking for her age.
No Comments
goes too fast for being an "elementary japanese" class. although workload was extreme, it was beneficial in the end
She's a teacher who likes to make fun of people if the student cannot answer her question!!!
I think she's awesome! I really liked the Japanese language class and I love the Japanese Linguistics class too!
Lectures from book, sometimes miscommunicates, good professor
phantastic professor, the lectures introduce to major literature and film, he makes these relevant for  today

turk is a great professor who cares a lot about h233! he likes to go on random tangents making it hard to pay attention some times but the class is genuinely interesting. he gives easy pop quizzes and is a very easy grader on the 3 essays required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is a super nice guy and is clearly knowledgeable. However, he tends to ramble in lecture about unrelated things, so we end up missing out on time to discuss readings that we need to know about. Beware of random pop quizzes; he says they are easy but often contain tiny details from readings. Do well on the essays, as he is strict about grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Turk is an amazing professor who cares about the course material. Deadlines can be unclear and there are few grades in the class. He likes to give out pop quizzes to gauge how prepared the class is, but they are typically straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Turk is a kind and caring professor who loves what he teaches, although he does spend the entire class lecturing. He's more focused on your understanding of the material, but make sure you speak up in discussion as that plays a large part in your grade. Three short papers graded generously and a final exam that's pretty straightforward.

Professor Turk is am awesome professor who really cares about his students' development. He can definitely ramble during lectures, but overall he really understands the course material and wants the class to understand too. Make sure you do all the readings so that you can participate in discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great course!

He's a great guy and truly cares about the topic but he gets off topic a lot. He spends the whole class lecturing and almost nobody listens. His exams you DO need to study for but it's all simple material. Papers are almost always promised A's. Just put in minimal effort and you'll likely get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's very caring and compassionate, and he genuinely wants his students to do well! He can sometimes get carried away during his class discussions and talk for a VERY long time, but he is knowledgeable and interesting to listen to. I was very grateful he was lenient on due dates and grading essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Johannes is fantastic. He is ridiculously intelligent and really loves what he teaches. It's easy to do okay without putting in much work, but the readings and lectures are really interesting and you learn a lot if you pay attention and do the assignments.

He is very smart and passionate about literature, which is very apparent by his lectures. His tests are pretty easy if you read the books and go to class. The only thing is that he tends to talk for a long time, and everybody seems to be intimidated when he asks questions. Otherwise, he is a solid professor and a nice guy.

Pretty disappointing class - supposed to be German lit but we only read maybe one or two actual German works - the rest were by non-Germans, inexplicably. He was a nice and knowledgeable guy but I was bored to death. He can lecture for over an hour without stopping to discuss things with the class - which is strange in a 20-person literature class.

He's so smart, and he doesn't even realize it. He's very passionate about the pieces he chooses and wants everyone to be affected by them. His quizzes are very easy, the readings are decent length, and even in a 2 1/2 hour long class. I was kept entertained. I highly recommend taking one of his classes.
Good Teacher, which is rare when a german teaches german. A little eccentric, but just talk about bavaria and fc bayern and you'll be fine.
He was one of the nicest professors I have ever had. His classes aren't particularly hard because he is really good about being helpful, and repeating things untilthey are understood.

Johannes speaks passionately and clearly. Knowledgeable and comfortable with the materials. Easy to come see outside of class. (And certainly nice to look at!!) However, talks for too long, while ignoring students. Either because he's passionate about telling us about the topic, or because he's nervous, and trying to stay in control.

Lacks any confidence whatsoever, takes it personally when students don't show up for class regularly and don't do their work. There is a really tense atmosphere in the class because he's so self concious. He tells you you can only re-write one paper, but if you ask him he'll let you re-write anything

Nice dude with a chill dry humor type of personality. Law backgroind, knows his stuff. All the info is learned from in class lectures so write down EVERYTJING he says (suggested textbook readings tho). Graded only by tests, first is hard but 2&3 better. Honors class so expected to be on top of it. Doable class much better than Rubin. I'd take again
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There are only exams in this class so attending lecture is very important. Take a lot of notes in class. If you need help just ask he is always willing to answer questions.

One of the best L201 professors. As long as you go to class and take good notes on the examples he mentions, you will ace the tests. He also gives extra credit if you participate in class. You don't have to do the readings but it helps to understand how the concepts are applied. There are only 3 grades though and the final is 50% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best choice for L293. Turk's lectures are super entertaining, and he makes it easy for everyone to get extra credit. Exams are relatively straightforward, and he makes it worth coming to class. Only reason I didn't give 5/5 is that he doesn't round final grades, and the class grade is based on 3 exams. You'll leave with a new appreciation for law.

I really enjoyed this class with Turk. If you ask him a question he'll ask if you want to actually understand or if you want to know what's needed for the test. Basically, you'll get out what you put into this class. Turk has a lot of personal experience and gives helpful stories. He also gives extra credit for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Similar to L201, L305 in Prof Turk's class is clear and interesting. Turk provides great anecdotes and examples in class. Participate and you will be rewarded with extra credit. His exams are not difficult if you prepare. He is a really great professor who cares about your learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof Turk is my favorite professor by far. His straightforwardness provides this maturity and frankness to the course. His exams are easy if you study the slides, and he provides generous extra credit for participation. Prof Turk's lecture style might be a bit monotone, but where he lacks in variety he compensates in intrigue. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Matt Turk seems like a good guy. He also seems like he cares about the material. His lectures are intensely repetitive and difficult to get through. Additionally, the class has only a few grades and little margin for error. The combination of these two things makes for a poor experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I don't think Professor Hasan was a great professor. She goes extremely fast and gives a ton of work for the amount of time you have. She is very nice and is very available for help outside of class, but I don't think her lectures are very great.

Goat! Best teacher I had in IU, super patient, care about students, reply email super quick, and try her best to help and answer your question! If u can't get good grade from this course that means your are not trying and not using your resources
She really tries her best but the lectures just go really slow. The content is also hard. Take someone else if you can
THE GOAT OF KELLEY. Bro is an absolute banger. Talking about any topic is hilarious with his humor which is officesque. The class is pretty easy and tests aren't bad at all.

It's a dry class, and Turk is a dry lecturer. Despite that, he tries really hard to make lectures engaging. I hate that the course is graded by only two exams - you have to perform extremely well to get a good grade. He'll always help if you ask for it. Show up to class, participate, and he gives you a grade bump at the course end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Turk is awesome! I had him for L201 last semester and what started as my worst class became my favorite. He has a great sense of humor he brings to every case, topic, and discussion and truly was an industry expert on everything covered. I highly recommend him, and he is super accessible outside of class time. Definitely show up to lectures!
Very funny, but subtle humor. He teaches very clearly and straightforward.

Great Professor! He was very accommodating with absences and taught the content with a dry sense of humor, which was nice since some sections could get a little detailed and tedious. Grades were based on two midterms and a final.

Really enjoying the class thus far. The entire class is based on a midterm and a final, but the midterm was very reasonable if you go to class and take good notes. Everything he tests you on is discussed in detail in class. He has a good sarcastic humor to bring light to topics that can be dry, and overall a very qualified dude to be teaching this.

Learned a lot from Prof. Tuohy and gained a new appreciation for music. She was super easy and gave you study guides that would have nearly identical answers to quizzes and exams. The papers usually were over interesting topics. You learn a lot if you put in a little effort.

Professor is very sweet and motivational but her exams are way too diffucult and she doesnt allow you to work on assignments ahead of time and will usually give you 5-7 days to write a 5+ page paper. Dont understand why her exams are that hard. Also she will lock your overall grade for atleast half the semester so you cant see what you have.
I really like Dr. Tuohy. She has great enthusiasm for Ethnomusicology and it shows really well. Easy grading from the AIs and all of them are very approachable and willing to help.
She is an awesome teacher! This class is intriguing and fun. The work is not intense or hard to keep up with. She is also very understanding and will talk to you about anything you need help with.
She's a nice teacher. There is a lot of reading material but as long as you skim and get the basis of the reading, you'll do fine. Very straight forward, 100 level class.
Prof Tuohy is a great teacher and really friendly and eager to help. She listens to students and understands issues that may arise.
I LOVE her! SO much fun, but her classes are a little too easy.

True sometimes she jumps topics, but she's nice, and easy going, and grades assignments easy and gives easy quizzes, i didnt do the reading for either of the two quizzes we've had yet i only missed one question on each
No Comments
It's Maddness. I don't think she should teach this class, half the time you didn't know what topic she was covering...there was so much material to read and it was ridiculous.
Great professor, Always there to give feedback and support. If you go to class it should be no problem getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Personable; professional wall often cracked with great humor; slides are dry (presentation is also at times). Reading intensive. Extra credit opportunities. EASY tests if you've read the material & followed along in class rather than squatting on a cell phone. Good attendance can bump a "borderline" grade up a letter- use that. Feast for the eyes!

Nice guy, funny, and young. Cute, too. His class is easy and lectures are boring/long. He's a good teacher but he's a very tough grader. Does give extra credit often, which is cool. He takes papers seriously and test Q's are worded terribly. Study, show up, pass. Overall, okay professor. Fun to look at though.
Chris was great. Gives quizzes sometimes but warns you. Tests are easy and he does offer several extra credit opportunities throughout the semester. Very nice and helpful guy.

He gives quizzes that is usually related to assign readings, but he always let people know in advance that there is a quiz (or sometimes he gives problems directly). He also gives study guide for tests and basically everything in the test is in the study guide. Don't be scared by the syllabus (exams, quizzes, papers...), SOC100 is not hard course.
Awesome guy. He clearly loves sociology and lectures are manageable. Only 2 tests and a few quizzes but he usually gives you a heads up. Go to most classes but if you miss some not a big deal.

Mr. C. is an excellent teacher. He clearly cares about his students and about being the best teacher he can be in order to prepare his students to be teachers. I highly recommend taking his section of P251.

I didn't think I'd enjoy an online course but our discussion forums were amazing.  Mr. C was good about answering questions and was flexible with assignments.  I learned a lot from the readings and highly recommend this class to anyone who cares about improving their teaching.
No Comments

He is an amazing teacher.  This is his first year teaching the course, and he has gone above and beyond to help all of us in his class.  He is always making things clear and going over all the material so that everyone understands it well.
Very nice and helpful, understanding that his class is not you're only class. Makes the class organized and interesting. Enjoyed it a lot more than I thought I would.
He is absolutely adorable, and he knows what he's talking about. I love Neal!
Kiss kiss. Adorable!
First year teaching at IU, but he has a lot of experience in the field. Great teacher; very funny, kind, understanding, and patient. Be sure to have your scenes MEMORIZED! You will love him!

The way the class is set up is that she teaches the Ancient art for ARTH A101. Super interesting class, and her and the other prof were very good lecturers. Took some adjustment because they do it differently, but still good nonetheless. You have to study a lot for this class, though, a lot for a gen ed too. If you like art/history, take for sure!

Professor Van Voorhis is one of the sweetest and funniest people I have ever met.  She is always very open to answering any questions.  The workload is extremely light but attendance is super important.  The tests were extremely easy and the lowest one was dropped.  She is an amazing professor to have in class and get to know.

What. A. Queen. Very knowledgeable & super funny. It can be a little memorization heavy if you're not at all interested in the material. Make a quizlet with the key terms and the key monuments. Read through the key themes once & hit quizlet a few times before the test and you're all set. Drops the lowest test grade!!! Take Julie 100% !!!

Enjoyed the content covered in C-206, the tests weren't too bad and she drops your lowest one. Attendance is mandatory and you are quizzed on content from lectures so go to class!!! The final project was kind of dumb though and should just be treated as a test.

Could be just me, but I felt like there was a lottttttt of information to take in and I often struggled on tests though I had studied for hours. She's a nice lady and doesn't give a lot of homework, but there's a lot of information to try and remember.

Professor Vanvoorhis was a super nice lady. Her class was one of the easier ones I've taken. You get a notecard to use on every test. She explained things clearly and was funny! She is very passionate about her job and is a great teacher.

Professor Van Voorhis makes her lectures so entertaining, and while she goes off on (interesting!) tangents, she works to make up for the lost time without forcing her students to teach themselves outside of class. She is extremely knowledgeable and the exams are easy if you pay attention during lectures. Highly recommend!

Professor VanVoorhis is extremely funny and understanding. This class was enjoyable, and I actually learned a lot. Her class is relatively easy as long as you attend her lectures and study for 30 minutes before each of her exams. She also drops your lowest exam grade. Her lectures often go on tangents which is the only flaw I can name.

Basically, if you go to class, you'll have no problems. Professor Van Voorhis is incredibly knowledgeable in her field, providing personal experience and excellent commentary. There is little homework and no textbook, and an A can be achieved with minimal effort.
You'll learn sooo much from Julie. She is extremely knowledgeable and hilarious! Best class I have ever taken.

Dr. Van Voorhis is an absolutely amazing instructor. She is tremendously knowledgeable about classical art. She is extremely passionate and she lets her passion show when she is teaching. She also has a great sense of humor and keeps the lectures interesting. The class I took with her was also extremely easy. Just pay attention to all the lectures.
Grading is subjective on quizzes and writing assignments. You can go from an A to a D with no logical explanation. Wouldnt recommend.

Julie is truly the most amazing professor Ive ever had. She engages with students and is very understand with any issues you might have. Her lectures can be boring if youre not interested in the topic but she makes them fun and entertaining. Shes also not afraid to call out bs like some of my other professors are, and I really admire her.
Really good professor. Lectures can be boring, but assignments are not difficult. There are a lot of quizzes so make sure to be prepared for them.

Julie Van Voorhis is incredibly knowledgable in her subject area and also calls out the bs that other professors in this area just casually accept as fact. She's super cool and I would gladly take another class taught by her (this is my second).
This is an extremely easy class. if you need an easy Gen Ed or any reason to take this class, take it. only 5 QUIZZES no exams. quizzes are two questions basically. two easy papers. easy A!

Don't take CLASC206 with her if you have no background in Art History.  I took it as an intro course for the Classical Studies major, and I did great on the position papers since they had to do with Archaeology, but the quizzes aren't graded on any objective material, it's hard to figure out what she wants.
Easy, entertaining, interesting. No textbook, just pay attention.
Julie is my favorite art history professor. She is clear, nice, funny and gives minimal work. Textbooks aren't needed, just good notes. Easy to get a good grade.
Great professor! Great class to fill a general education requirement. Class wasn't very hard or time consuming, and Julie is a great person to teach this class.

Her voice can be really boring, but the class is really interesting if you can stay awake. She's very kind, helpful, and definitely knows the material. I'd highly recommend. Don't buy the textbook, though. I didn't use it once.

A lot of other reviews have said Professor Van Voorhis was a boring lecturer, but I found her to be quite funny and very clear on what she expected. I knew nothing about art prior to this course and I ended up excelling. Definitely give it a chance. You do have to study for the tests, but it's easy if you put forth effort.

Although she is a boring lecturer you need to be in class to learn the material as the textbook is rarely used. Attendence is not mandatory but is taken into account if you need your grade bumped up. The tests can be a pain as they are subjectively graded by the TA's.
She was  really nice, but a little boring sometimes. The material she talked about kept me interested. The class was basically easy overall.

Not as good as Reilly. Very boring and monotonous. Usually I don't have to read the book, but for her I had to b/c I would literally stop listening to her. Only attended to make sure I didn't miss anything important. Very relieved when Reilly started teaching! Nice woman, just a boring teacher.

The way she talks is a little boring, but if you take some (i emphasize some) notes and go to the discussions you'll be fine. Also do well on the final paper. It's the only major project and it's an easy grade booster.

Awesome teacher. Be sure to take her Topics in Art History: Rome In Film class. It's a lot of fun and you get to watch a plethora of intresting films. The class was quite enjoyable and I highly enjoyed Professor VanVoorhis' lectures.
Great teacher. very easy, no textbook! just have to go to classs, whatever she says in class will be on the test.
The way she speaks put me to sleep. I was bored most of the time, and she spoke to us like we had no idea what was going on. She seemed nice though--
She knew very little about ancient egypt and got alot wrong.  the tests were easy if you know much about egypt...so if you want a jerk off class then take it.  But I wish I had not waisted my time.
Kinda boring, but easy to understand.
Prof. Vander Schee does a great job applying the lectures to assignments, projects, and the business world. His feedback is ample and constructive as he truly wants to see all his students succeed!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Great course, insightful week over week applications. Felt like I could actually translate what was in the class to the real-world. Professor himself is also very kind and knowledgeable in the field. A safe and insightful environment. Highly recommend.
Professor Vander Schee was a great professor who gave informative lectures and made the content clear to understand. He also never failed to fill us in on his quests to Chipotle! Highly recommend.

Professor Van der Schee was a great professor who gave informative lectures and made the content very clear to understand. He also never failed to fill us in on his quests to Chipotle! Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I thought he was a decent professor. Very nice and pretty funny. I didn't think he was incredibly helpful when I had questions outside of class, but most of his assignments and work are pretty strait forward. Attendance wasn't really mandatory, but there was a participation grade.

Vander Schee and this M501 course were both outstanding. The course followed a linear curriculum that allowed students to develop digital marketing skills through platforms that industry professionals use, applying them weekly to a company-based project. The instructor fostered a venue for rich academic discourse and gave calculated feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Vander Schee is an excellent instructor. His Digital Marketing class was informative and well worth the time. He gave clear guidelines for assignments, and provided detailed and constructive feedback. Instead of a final exam, the course concluded with a group presentation and project, which was a valuable way to apply what was learned.

This is for M303 not 370 but he's truly a great professor and is really funny. You'll work with a group basically all semester and there's small projects every week, but they're really easy. I loved taking the class with him

Took Vander Schee at IUB for the marketing component of I-Core. I seriously can't believe it's his first year here, and he did an amazing job. If you show up to class every day, you're guaranteed an A. He explains concepts very well, shares great marketing tools which will be helpful on the case, and has funny Chipotle rants. Best choice for M370!!

Varon as a whole is a good teacher; be prepared to participate in class by reading the things he assigns. It's a lot of reading involved and might be time-consuming, especially when having other assignments from other classes. The only thing I didn't like was at the very end, being the group project. It was randomized, which sucked.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had. Prof. Varon is very respectable and teaches and directs discussions well. My class was very text heavy with a lot of online sources he provided, but he helps you understand them. My section was focused on video game narratives and it was very fun. Few grades with a couple papers. Gives good feedback on essays
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: I like Professor Varon. The readings he gives are interesting. Just make sure to do the reading and you will get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I really loved Prof. Varon's class. The lectures were discussion-driven, which comes with the usual baggage--if nobody's done the reading, the lecture is a drag; if even a few people come prepared, it can be really exciting. He offered clear feedback and was sure to tell us what to expect for assessments. He's a gem!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: readings after every class, which are somewhat interesting. not very clear on how he grades essays or how he wants them structured. more of a discussion than a lecture. super nice and comfortable environment. the class isn't too difficult as long as you do the readings and pay attention during discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Varon is very passionate about teaching and the topic of the class. The class was very discussion based and if you don't like speaking up in class I would suggest not taking this class. The homework wasn't too taxing and the essays were graded pretty easily.
Really nice guy, but the class lacks structure. We had interesting discussions, but not a lot of content from him about the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This course was enjoyable & interesting. Prof. Varon encouraged lively discussion, though he would sometimes jump in the moment there was any hint of conflict between students. Overall positive, but I did sometimes feel like my comments were shut down with little, if any, consideration, just because someone else said they disagreed.

Class lectures were very interesting and entertaining. I enjoyed attending the class. Professor grades very strictly and you must participate in class discussions. The required readings were good novels and I would recommend this class to others.

material is so, so interesting and the texts are great and engaging. his lectures (altho it's more discussion than lecture) are great, and he made the class worthwhile. tough grader, go to office hours for guidance on essays!! he's really easy to talk to outside class. midtermsfinals are easy as long as you know what the point of each story was.
Professor Varon is a great professor, though he can be a tough grader and expects a lot from you. It's very likely you will learn a lot about reading and writing in his class.
Good discussion class. Learned a lot about Latin Americans in literature and workload was not too bad. Very engaging material

What a nice guy! I appreciated how clear he was on test content, and I always felt prepared for the exams. Labs were great and complemented the lectures well. The lectures were sometimes hard to focus on, and when he would use the dry erase board his handwriting was hard to follow along with. Still a great guy though take him!

This class is really well structured. The assignments are really educational, and often fun. 

Vel is very kind, but his lectures were often hard to follow, then boring. I think he just needs to slow down a bit and perhaps revise the slides to introduce concepts in a more digestible manner. It was easy to lose focus and zone out the rest of class.

Nice guy but lectures are a bit boring. HW has very detailed instructions. The extra credit opportunity mentioned could be a bit difficult if you're new to assembly isince it's solving puzzles using assembly code. Tests are multiple choice and you can bring a cheatsheet.

I breezed through this class. Didn't even go to lecture 95% of the time - I did have pre-existing knowledge, however.

Most of your grade is derived from the (autograded) homework. There's a huge extra credit opportunity about halfway through the semester (300/200 possible score on an assignment) that will do wonders for your grade.

Lectures can be boring but the lab assignments are engaging and where you'll be doing most of your learning. Lab assignments use autograder so you know what grade you are getting before its due. Exams are multiple choice. There's a generous extra credit opportunity where you can get 50 or 100 bonus points.
he pretty much just reads slides to you. you'll have to teach yourself��

I took Malbasa's Intro to Python course. I thought it was a great class that covered all the basics of python. He clearly cares about his class and wants you to learn. He is available outside of hours. Starts slow, but quickly builds into you creating applications and much more complex programming. I spent a few long nights on reading & HW.

Curriculum is designed to be gentle at first. It ramps up. Don't get complacent. If you do the following in this order, you should have no problem: Watch all the videos, print the presentation slides and have them for reference, do the exercise problems and keep them for reference. Start early. Ask questions because he's very responsive.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The professor's lectures are very good and easy to understand. The way course is laid out is very seamless. Understanding of python is build gradually. He is always available for you if you any question.

Dr. Malbasa is a decent teacher. He makes time for students. There is a lot of reading, lecture and homework. If you are not that familiar with Python, the amount of homework makes the course quite challenging. I had to set aside 2 -3 full days per week just for this class, but I did learn a lot and now Im a Python programmer!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I'm taking his class online. He's kind of monotone in his videos and reads almost word for word from the slides. That being said, he does present things in a straightforward and understandable manner. Lots of homework that gets challenging as the semester goes on. Seems nice in his messages, apologizing if things sound confusing. I like him.
He's a nice person, but be prepared to listen in lecture. If you get lost, don't be afraid to ask questions.

I took the online Python class. The videos he posted online were fairly simple in scope, made it difficult to hear everything he said, and left you to do a lot of reading on your own or to ask other students for help. I would recommend that you go to his office hours with questions, as it was difficult to reach him by email. Good class; lot of work
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Tough material, but a great professor. He knows how to read the room, and cares about his students understanding of the material. Homework and projects can be difficult but not impossible.

Lectures are long. As of this review, you can skip class and receive an A, so long as you attend the labs and self teach yourself. This applies to every C212 lecture, no matter what professor. Grading can be subjective and appealing grades depends on your reasons. Professor himself is a nice guy if you try to get to know him. Office hours plenty.

He is a visiting lecturer from another school. I'm not sure if he knew what we were doing in lab, because he would lecture about content that we had covered weeks before on the homework. After the first couple of classes I stopped going to lecture other than review days for tests and I did just fine. Lab teaches you everything you need to know!

He has a lot of sass and generally seems like he doesn't care in his lectures.  I suggest not going to any of his lectures because he'll give you a pretty hard time if you ask a simple question, plus he just reads off pp slides.  Be prepared for a class where you'll have to self-teach, and this'll be apparent after the first test.
Super cool guy and funny, but lectures are really boring. He is an easy grader though if you put effort into the assignments.
Dr. Velez is the goat. He's a really funny professor & makes every lecture both entertaining and educational. If you show up to lectures and take notes on review day you'll get an A.

He's really funny and makes lectures entertaining. Not a lot of grades in the gradebook, but he's been adding more assignments for us to get some points in. Tests are online and open note and he does random attendance quizzes so it's not required, but you might miss out on some points if you aren't there.
The best prof ever, highly recommend.

The professor was decent but the way he taught the class was ridiculous. The whole semester is a big group project and if your group members do not understand the material you are screwed. Two exams, four group assignments, and a final presentation are the only grades, all members get the same grade. Very confusing material but decent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Velez is funny and lowkey  you'll do well as long as you pay attention to lectures. Exams are pretty easy and lectures are based off the textbook so if you pay attention to those you don't really have to read. The middle of the course is a lot of group work so make sure you pick people you can rely on. On the whole the class is pretty easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Velez is an awesome professor. He really loves his students and also wants everyone to do well. If you go to class and take notes you will definitely pass. He gives good study guides before the tests and the final is a 800 word paper. He is funny and his class is really interesting. Take anything with velez!

Professor Vander Schee is always timely and prepared. He is an extremely tough grader and gave me a suprising grade on my final presentation compared to what I thought was earned. He is nice enough, but is nit-picky and cold calls.
Was a very supportive and understanding teacher, recommend him highly. Everything was very clear on when things were due, what was due, and everything else.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Vander Schee is a wonderful teacher, very personable, and approachable. His lectures and slides are easily digestible and he is always willing to explain more if needed. Honestly, his class didn't even feel like class because the subject matter is relevant, interesting, and steadily paced. Highly recommend taking with this Prof. Vander Schee!
Just an amazing Course and Teacher. Show up and try and you will do amazing.
Professor Vander Schee is passionate about the content, gave us lots of work time, and was good at explaining topics I was confused on.
Professor Vander Schee was a very kind and welcoming Professor. He remembered students names, making us feel valued. Further he provided very clear guidelines to help you be successful in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This course with professor Vander Schee was very straight forward. Almost every week followed the same structure which was nice to have an expectation and routine. He provides detailed feedback on the assignments you turn in and he is available and willing to help you if you have any questions. The class was interesting and clear.

Professor Vander Schee was great because he was genuinely kind, personable, and approachable. He created a comfortable class environment where participation felt natural, not forced. Most boring class every and quite possibly the worst teacher I have ever had in my life. He needs to be fired ASAP.

Despite being a nice individual, he is not the best teacher. The lectures are taken from the tophat and he does not answer questions that well. Although he includes discussion points which are a nice grade booster and gives useful practice tests.
Don't expect a curve
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is undoubtedly the worst professor/teacher I have had at Indiana University. His lack of ability to speak English makes his lectures impossible to understand. The questions on his exams are nothing like the practice exams or exams given by other Econ-b 251 teachers. Definitely recommend staying as far away from this guy as possible.

Did not prepare us for the exams or curve. He never replied to emails or could answer any of my questions in class. Barely any extra credit compared to other professors for this class, and the one extra credit assignment he did give was so difficult even tutors couldn't figure it out. Does not curve tests and they are extremely difficult.

Run. If you are one of the unlucky people to get this professor, drop the first week. I have never had a worse "teacher." Every class he is difficult to understand, quiet, and boring. It is a lecture the entire time, reading directly from the PowerPoint. Longest class of my life. He is unable to answer questions and will do problems incorrectly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had, he deserves to be fired.

Vladimir's classes were incredibly boring, essentially just reading out PowerPoint slides. That said, he knew what he was talking about and the material was very basic. I know some other people had issues with the class being difficult, but I never found it challenging, just mind-numbingly boring.

Professor Menshikov is quite possibly the worst professor I have ever had. His lectures consist of unenthusiastically regurgitating power point slides for an hour and a half. His tests contain a lot of short answer questions while the other professors are strictly multiple choice. He is also a little full of himself.
Very smart teacher, but over critical in grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy but a tough grader. He didn't curve the class till after it we took the final and when it was curved it was a heavy one. His teaching style was confusing at first but I got used to it. However I left this class very confident in my abilities.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Starts talking in depth about stuff the first day and he has a VERY thick accent that makes it hard to keep up, especially the first couple weeks. He's a really nice guy and funny but you can tell he'd rather just be left alone to do his studies here at IU. This is the hardest class I've ever taken and I'm a straight A student. Don't do it. Don't.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do NOT take it. If you do take it, be ready to teach yourself. The only people who tend to do well in this class have already taken AP Calculus or higher in high school, or are completely self-taught. It is highly likely you will not learn anything from the lecture. The professor wasn't a bad person, just could not teach & overcomplicated it all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Vodosek is such an amazing professor and his class structure is amazing. He is genuinely one of the most organized professors I have ever had. Class is pretty much the same daily with a lecture and then small group activity. Be ready to show up, participate, and read. All exams are online (yay) for real take him for D311
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Vodosek is such a chill guy & this class is really not all that hard. All the tests are online and if you go to class, participate, and complete the assignments with even just a little bit of effort you'll be on track for an A. He brings real world events and news into the classroom so if you are interested in international business I'd recommend.

Read the textbook in preparation and take heavy notes for the ALL ONLINE EXAMS - really nice professor; just show up to class (attendance is a big part of the grade) and be prepared for lots of group work. Current events are interesting and Vodosek is very well versed in his field!

This course was very reliant on the textbook, including Professor Vodosek's asynchronous lectures. That said, content was quite interesting, the class discussions were solid, and I took a lot out of the coursework despite extensive professional experience in global business. I would definitely take another class with Professor Vodosek.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: One of the kindest and sweetest professors I have ever had at Kelley. Genuinely cares for all his students and makes participation points accessible to introverts. The hardest part of the class were the debate papers but other than that, he makes it easy to get an A. Everyone I know that has taken a class with Vodosek loves him!

Professor Vodosek is an amazing professor. He is very kind and caring. You must read all the material he assigns to get good grades. I have learned a lot in his class, and I would love to take other classes he offers.
Way too much work for a class that is next to meaningless. D312 was a much better course. Couldn't recommend Markus Vodosek less.

Took him for D311, not D270. Easily my least favorite professor I've had through 4 years at Kelley.

Incredibly boring lectures although he tries to make it better by putting us in groups and giving us meaningless assignments. Unfortunate that this is a required class for the international business co-major. Terrible professor - don't recommend
Great Professor for D271 business in Europe. Extremely sweet and understanding
Very kind and decently interesting lectures. He grades on a clear criteria and doesn't make exams overly difficult.

I took Professor Vodosek for Doing Business in Europe. When I tell you this class was dry and he did not help, I really mean it. While he seems like a nice man, he does not inject life into the extremely boring material at all. There is a ton of reading and a group assignment every class- honestly wish I had taken a different D271 class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Very sweet guy who cares about his students wellbeing. The course is not difficult and I learned a lot. Exams are essay-like but not difficult if you take notes and use the book. He is a very understanding person and will work with your schedule. Very discussion based class.

This professor is so awesome and the class is so easy. Optional attendance and pretty straight forward topics. He is also so amazing! He's a great person and cares a lot about his students. He is very understanding and does everything he can to make this class easy for us. HES THE BEST!!!
He cares so much about you actually learning the content. He relates to class at a deep level and is very understanding. It is an extremely easy A, but also an interesting course.

Genuinely one of my favorite professors of all time. He is super nice and EXTREMELY understanding. A ton of the class completely relies on the readings but its not horrible. Class is more of a discussion and grading is based on how thoughtful your writing is and not your answer being "right" or "wrong". Definitely take his class if you can.
Professor Voyles is open to feedback and grades very easily. This class itself doesn't feel fully worked out but Voyles teaches it well and opens the class to discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Voyles is so nice, and he genuinely cares about his students as well as the content that he teaches. Each week, he goes over a chapter in class and then there is an online quiz for students to take. There were about 3 really long assignments. He gives an extra credit assignment at the end of the year that really increases grade averages.

Very clear with instructions and deadlines. She is super willing to answer questions and accommodate if tech issues arise. They changed the K303 course material this semester so sometimes she didn't have the most knowledge on certain new things (PowerBI), but still super helpful in figuring things out as we went. She also brought great energy.

Professor Votolato is amazing!! She makes K303, a topic that can daunt some, very simple. She is always willing to answer questions and goes the extra miles for her students by being available via teams. Our class is mainly projects, which can be challenging but are simple if you take time in advance of the due date to work on it. She is awesome!

Katie is so laid back and made the class environment not stressful at all. She is always willing to help students, inside and outside of the classroom. She is super understanding and overall a great person. She made K303 seem easy and always encouraged everyone to get their work done.

She is a decent professor but never really wowed me with her teaching skills. K303 shouldn't be that hard to get an A in but for some reason, her projects were graded way harder than other professors. Me and my roommate had different profs and would help each other on projects, they would routinely get 5-8% higher on every single one, idk why.

Honestly K303 is a pretty easy class, but what I will say is for the few confusing concepts she isn't the greatest professor. You can kind of tell she's just their to collect a check and is pretty lazy, and good at coming up with an excuse of why she can't help you at a specific moment during work sessions. I would try to find a better professor.

Katie was the BEST. She was so nice and wants every student to succeed. K 303 isn't a hard class but taking it with a good proffesor helps. She helps during Checkpoints and on projects as well as answers questions for the final project. Definetly recommend

Professor Votolato is probably my favorite professor I have had at IU. Her workshop class is very interesting and she does a great job connecting students with professional opportunities. Would highly recommend her for any course she teaches.
For the workshop, she was a great professor. She grades kind of difficult (you have to go above and beyond to get an A), but it's all useful life skills. Really nice person though!

Probably my least favorite teacher I've had at IU because she's such a hardass. She stepped in for my class after Professor Robbins dropped out so I didn't have a choice. The class was really easy but would have rather avoided Votolato if possible.

Super easy class. Grade distribution is incredible (80% min A's if you earn it). Really learn excel with this class. Do the projects, learn the material and don't cheat: easiest A of your life. Did minimal work, aside from projects every 2 weeks, easy A. Show up to class ready to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very good professor that is passionate about what he is teaching. Lectures are copy and paste from a slideshow that will help you with the very little assignments given. Assignments were very easy and each test was posted with a study guide that helped you get no lower than a B on. Overall very easy class and would highly recommend.

Mr. Vogt is an amazing professor that I had the pleasure to take class from. His lectures are very engaging and move at a quick, but not too fast pace. Along with his amazing lectures the work load is very minimal with a discussion post and some readings for a deeper understanding of the course. I would def recommend!!!

Best professor ever. Kind, funny, charismatic, great lectures, extremely knowledgeable. Never thought I'd be this interested in war and violence in East Asia, but thanks to him it's the class I most look forward too. I wish I could keep taking Prof. Vogt's class for another semester and I fully intend on taking other classes he teaches.
He's super chill. He's passionate about the topic but the work isn't hard at all. Only assignments are quizzes every Monday and a discussion post every Friday (250 words).

Reading heavy, but no assignments outside of reading. If you read & participate in discussions the exams (always essays) are pretty easy. I loved her class because you can tell she loves to teach and wants people to learn and do well. Genuinely cares for her students. Gave me a 4-day extension on final paper because she wanted me to do well on it!

Olga makes her class stress-free and enjoyable. It is not an easy-A but if you put in a good effort you will do well. She is very funny in her own way. Class is more enjoyable if you read and try to participate. If nobody participates class drags on relentlessly. More meaningful than a lot of of my major related classes.

She seems to grade only on the basis of whether you agree with her opinion and quite frankly on whether or not she likes you. She straight up told my class that the only reason we got the grades we did is because we are nice and that we didn't actually earn them. She is very unclear in what she wants and grades ridiculously harshly. Good luck...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great class, very illuminating. Olga was always ready and engaging.
She is hard and not fair. Do not take this class. she does not give rubrics for papers and rips the papers apart and does not appreciate the time you put in papers. DO NOT TAKE any classes with her
She is an incredibly hard grader, and if you do not agree with her opinion she does not grade fairly. Do not take this class if you are wanting an easy A&H class.

She asks a lot of complicated and loaded classes but goes out of her way to make concepts understood.  She is very understanding and does her best to be fair.  This class involves a lot of reading and a few film screenings

Olga is incredible. We always knew what was expected of us and she is very patient and fair. She made first semester Russian run as smoothly as I think anyone could. I don't know what the other reviewer is talking about.

This is the worst professor I've ever had. First of all she is russian, so sometimes she is hard to understand. She does the same boring class routine everyday, never switches things up. Doesn't keep your attention for long. Hard grader, and won't really explain your grade. She grades based on if she liked it or not. STAY AWAY FROM THIS PROF!

She is the nicest prof I've ever had. Very sweet and helpful, and is easy to make an appointment with if you can't go to office hours. She is more than willing to help you understand the readings if you are having trouble. She always has a good attitude and is more than willing to help you succeed in her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A complete gem. She is incredibly kind and just wants her students to do well.

Amanda Vredenburgh is an incredibly kind and personable professor. If you show up, participate in class, and do the homework, you will have no trouble getting an A. I've thoroughly enjoyed her class this year and would recommend it to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Amanda is awesome! She gives excellent lectures so I learned a lot. The class was accelerated, but it never seemed rushed. The exams and in-class writing were challenging, but her feedback was specific and thorough. The online homework was sometimes a pain, but that's not her fault; it's department wide. Highly recommended.

I struggled in this foreign language class because Vredenburgh wasn't there to give much help when I needed it, and didn't show much sympathy for the students who struggled. There's a lot of work in this class, and if you miss one or two assignments you'll be behind. The french lab is tedious, but not doing it will drastically lower your grade.
The best teacher to teach K201. Truly one of a kind. He gives good advice, really approachable, and chill guy overall with amazing humor. Loads of love, Vahin!

Vahin is great! Very chill guy who cares about students understanding the content and is also helpful when it comes to the stress of being pre-Kelley because he provides great feedback and study suggestions. Very strongly suggest him!

Super chill guy def the best k201 prof. Very to the point and doesnt waste any time which sometimes led to ending class early. If you pay attention and show up to every class no zero you should do bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Vuppalanchi is a great professor. He makes time to speak to you about your grade, and helps make a plan for you on how to raise your grade by setting goals for next exams. He is understanding when it comes to major homework assignments. His class is fast paced but he makes it easy to keep up and meet with him.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Straight and too the point every class, sometimes we get out early, lighthearted humor, take this guy for k201 trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Vahin's lectures are always lighthearted while conveying all the information necessary. He does not require unnecessary busy work and provides students with what they need to do well in K201
Vahin is chill take him
Great teacher

Vahin is the best K201 professor. He truly cares about your growth as a student and will be willing to help you with anything, even assisting in teaching a class. His sense of humor keeps the class light and enjoyable. 100% would take again!

Professor Vahin was great all year! He is clear with what will be on the exams and graded projects. He explains everything in a manner that is understandable and manageable. Made taking K201 a cake walk!
Great computer skills, and gets straight to the points in lectures.  Always looks out for students learning and grades, made it a class to look forward to.
Super great teacher to have for K201. Explains concepts thoroughly and isn't strict with participation. Made classes fairly enjoyable.
He explains the course material exceptionally well and truly cares about his students' success.

He understands exactly what it is like to be in K-201 so he structures his lectures accordingly. Lectures are very to the point but effective. K-201 in general requires a lot of studying but that is not specific to Vahin's class.

Excellent at clearing up confusion at what can at first be a disorienting subject. Perfect dry humor to keep us awake at an 8am class. Understands the student mindset well and communicates exactly what we need to succeed.

Professor Vupplanchi strived to see success in all of his students by asking questions during the lab lectures to make sure to make sure that we were keeping up with the difficult concepts. He was also accessible outside of class which was helpful as K201 is not an easy course for everyone and for the revision of difficult concepts for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor. Make sure to show up to class as he explains the material very well. He stays after class to answer questions and help with problems. He is also accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor for K201. He was very clear about expectations and you always knew what you needed to do to get a good grade. He is super easy to talk to and I recommend him for any class.
love this professor, very good teacher and great at explaining

Professor Vuppalanchi is one of my favorite professors at IU. He is so nice, always available for extra help. He explains everything well in class, and always answers questions. He gives so many attempts on the quizzes, and he wants everyone to have a good grade in the class. Also, he is so funny, it was a fun morning experience.

Probably the worst professor I have had so far. She will bombard you with so much information and it is impossible to memorize it all in the 4 weeks you have. She flies through slides and doesn't care whether you got the information or not. I would recommend having a lot of background knowledge in Biology and Genetics before taking her class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Flies through powerpoint slides and makes you miss LOTS of critical information - extremely difficult to take notes during her lectures. The only way I could get down any information was to take pictures of each slide and copy them down as quickly as I could. Very rude and doesn't offer any sort of help or clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Did not use lecture notes in the slightest. Rude when you ask for clarification on topics. Rushes through notes and topics, gets flustered when asked to slow down. Asks rhetorical questions when students ask questions instead of giving actual help.

im not a big fan of this prof. surprised everyone actually likes him. his class isn't hard. just do the readings and study the chapter questions before tests. but he is so boring and just does too much sometimes. he's just an alright prof if u have him.

I enjoyed my time in Professor Wayne's class for sure. He was kind, generous, and caring. He was also quite engaging as a lecturer in my opinion. I will say that you must study hard for the 5 tests because they make up a majority of the course grade. But I think Professor Wayne sets everyone up to succeed, and is a great person. Highly recommend.

His class is overall fairly easy. The main drawback is that exams make up 70% of your final grade, with each exam being worth 14%, so they carry a lot of weight. It's important to stay on top of the chapter readings and take good notes. As long as you attend class and pay attention, you should do well.

Very awesome teacher, he doesn't want any students to fail. He gives extra credit to students who has attends his class. Really if you attend class and read the executive summary of the chapter you really can get an easy a in his class. He really wants students to pass his class.

Tests make up 95% of your grade, and that is not an exaggeration. The other 5% is attendance. Class is spent reading off lecture slides. Prof Wayne is cool, but the class is just honestly not the best. He's knowledgeable in his field which is great, but the course format just ruins it. If you're a bad test-taker, do not take H124 with Prof Wayne.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Wayne is the best! Very motivating and understanding. He always starts class by asking about us rather than jumping straight into material and it makes the environment feel more personal and like he actually cares that we are there. No surprises just straightforward material and good communication. Most of the grades are tests and attendance.
Loved this professor. We were only graded off tests, but if you pay attention and take good notes you'll learn a lot.

I loved Professor Wayne. He is very knowledgeable about the field, and he gives great advice. The class is very test heavy, but the tests were super easy. He pretty much tells you exactly what you need to know for each test during lectures and review classes. He is very kind and understanding as well. 100% recommend taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very kind professor! He cares about the students in his class and makes time to hear ideas from everyone in the class. It is heavy on participation. When I took the class online we met only once a week for 45 minutes with a small group so that everyone has a chance to talk. This was very effective.

Vogel is one of the best profs at IU. English majors should wait to take L371 so they can have him. Marx, Nietzsche, and Freud is the most interesting topic. Readings also include Adorno, Lacan, and Foucault. Best reading list available at IU. Vogel grades generously and gives a ton of feedback. He wants you to become a better writer and person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor! He was really passionate about the material and did a great job making lectures interesting and facilitating discussion. Assignments are open-ended but clear in requirements and grading is very fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory/harsh attend. policy but he leaves that to the TA who will probably be lenient. Lots of reading but mostly interesting. Decent lectures but refuses to post lecture slides online. Makes you trek across campus to turn in papers when no class. Gives good feedback when he grades but most papers graded by TA. Definitely an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took L260 with professor Vogel this semester and it has been an absolute treat. If anyone is getting a English BA or minor than I would highly recommend you take his nightlife L260 course.

I took L260 with Prof Vogel and he is an excellent teacher! He is super organized, gives great lectures, and is mindful and progressive in his choices for content. I loved the variety of works we studied. He gives thorough and constructive feedback and was available to meet. I'd like to take a class with him at a higher level with fewer students!
Fairly dull, the class was one I wanted to skip fairly often. That said, he never felt harsh and he is definitely smart. Expect to be graded harshly.

Shane was overall a very good professor. I would definitely take his class again, but be really on top of your own grade. He doesn't update online gradebooks, and unless you keep up on it or frequent his office, you won't know what's up. Lots of reading, and his lectures often go off on a tangent, but he's a great, passionate professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lectures are extremely boring and writing prompts can sometimes be unclear. Otherwise, an easy grader and an easy intensive writing class!

I loved his L260 course. Not only did Professor Vogel choose an interesting topic for the semester, but he obviously enjoyed talking about it. There's a fair amount of reading (with periodic breaks), but his choices were so fantastic that I didn't even mind. Make sure you participate in his discussion sections!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Overall, it was pretty easy class that Prof Vogel made interesting. Sometimes his lectures could drag on but it was mostly helpful information. You can tell he's very passionate about literature and helping students come to a better, more intellectual understanding of readings. As long as you read and put effort into your papers, you'll be fine.
Shane is petty about cell phones but he is SOOO great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I highly recommend taking this course with Prof. Vogel. It's an English major requirement, so obviously there is quite a bit of reading, but easily accomplished.  There are very few grades/assignments/tests, so just read with the syllabus and study for the two tests in total, and it's almost impossible to not pass. Interesting lectures, great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Vogel's lectures are very interesting and usually have different viewpoints that you probably have heard before, even if you've studied that material in depth before. He tries to have a variety of reading material so there's really something for everyone. Attendance is super important and so is taking notes. There are 2 papers and 2 tests
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Vogel is a great instructor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: For a 200 level english class, shane really helps bring students understanding of texts to a great level. Sometimes his lectures can be nuanced and it takes awhile for him to get to the point of things, but no strings are left untied. Obviously cares a lot about what he teaches, but has high expectations for students.

This class was horrible, and I feel in part it was due to the way Shane lectured. Lectures were often long, drawn out, confusing and came to no substancial conclusion. Shane doesn't grade anything, and heavily relies on AI's to teach the class in discussion sections.
He's an outstanding professor! He explains complex topics in a clear understandable way.  He seems to take a real interest in the students. Class is both fun and interesting
seems like a cool guy.
class can be boring but he knows what he's talking about!
A great professor!! I will definitely select him as many times as possible in the next three years!! His grading is very fair and his comments helpful. Great professor!
By far my favorite professor I had at IU. He is funny, explains the very hard material with perfect clarity ,using great analogies (real housewives!). Take him for L371!

Dr. Vogel is a great professor.  He makes clear connections between complex texts and everydsy life.  Advice: really read everything because class is heavily based in discussion.  If you don't read it, you will be lost.

I love shane. We read extremely difficult texts but he explains them perfectly. Very very sweet and responds to effort and engagement. Pretty easy grader, just wants you to get the main points. BEST teacher of L371.
So nice. Very very smart. Not condescending and pushes you to do your best.
shane is great!!
Great Teacher!!
Made the class fun and easy! (ps: he throws great end of the semester class parties :)
The class changed my life.
Shane is magical.  I don't know how he managed to make such complicated material understandible to his students.  He's also cute and fun, too.
The Coolest Prof. (who had to clarify he's a prof! b/c he's so freaking trendy) I've had yet at IU!
