reviews.comment: Genuinely horrid. I took her bc of good grade distribution which she has changed as of Fall 25. Grades all exemplary assignments at 8/10. Says to get an A you "need to be Lebron James of the class". Endlesss busy work that she grades 7 weeks later with AI and gives bad grades. No cushion grades. Assigns all her own terrible work for your reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
This teacher is legitimately the worst I have ever taken. She refuses to give constructive feedback, grades ridiculously hard for completion assignments, and releases said grading two months into the semester. By that point, it's too late to improve, and she is very very difficult to get any help from. 

Completely unreasonable, DO NOT TAKE
Don't take
Haha what a joke of a class. Everything was common sense, with wayyyyyyy too much useless busywork and assignments. Total joke, just take C204 instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Do yourself a favor and don't ever take business writing classes with Rodak. Out of all the C204 teachers her class distribution was one of the worse. She assigns way too much completion work and grades extremely harshly on major assignments while using chatgpt to give feedback. Really terrible and I regret taking her class.
She assigns way too many readings and assignments, most of which are busy work. At the end of the year she makes you comb through every single assignment she gave you to do a reflection
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Gives good feedback which is crucial, but another thing was that she gives out a lot of busy work which just feels useless at times but other than that I benefited from having Prof. Rodak as a professor at Kelley
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
Professor Rodak cares deeply about her students' success. Class is very work heavy and a lot of the assignments felt like they didn't teach me much... but I will say I feel like a better writer after this class, which I know many of my friends' can't say about their C204/5 classes.

If you don't have a packed schedule, Rodak's worth it imo.

Dr. Rodak will certainly challenge you, both in content and patience. While you will learn how to write for a business setting, you will also learn how to wait months for feedback for papers that were assigned to you on limited deadline. Easy to get an A, but overall frustrating class.

Rodak is one of the worst professors I've had. She assigns excessive work (6-page essays/100+ pages of reading) with unrealistic deadlines but takes weeks to grade assignments. Her feedback feels automated because it's from ChatGPT. She seems more interested in using the class for her research than in teaching. Avoid taking her for C205 if you can!

She assigns 100+ pages of reading, with a corresponding 9-page assignment with less than 48 hours of notice, on top of another 6-page paper due, and it still isn't a completion grade. She has violated FERPA, blasting our grades on the board. She singles out students. She gives ChatGPT feedback that is the same across groups. NEVER. TAKE. HER.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Rodak's lack of professionalism was heinous. She frequently assigned us large group presentations, papers, or 100+ pages of reading and reflections with less than 48 hours of notice. It also took her 2 months to provide feedback on our work, and she would not clarify assignment expectations when repeatedly asked to do so in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class was the catalyst to my first academic burn out. There is so much homework and reading that it is insanely overwhelming on top of other classes. It is a 200 level class that acts like you should be in grad school for writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: if you don't like reading or aren't a strong writer, I would not recommend her L204 course. But Rodak is one of the best professors I have ever had. There's a lot of reading and homework, but Rodak makes up for it by leading the class through deep analysis of fantastical content. She always encourages her students to work to their full potential :)
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The work load for this class is a lot for a 200 level class. Do not recommend if you don't like reading. Overall very hard.

I loved Miranda, but this was my heaviest course i had, topping calc by far. there were like 150pg readings due before almost every class and assignments were always due before class and never accepted late. she graded tough on essays, without giving much context on what she actually wanted us to write about. great person, but tough class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very participation heavy, but she truly cares for students and their progress. Required to read 4 large books in ~2 weeks each, so make sure to take with an easy course load. Grades essays harshly but always gives valid reasons. Overall, if you read and participate in this class and take it seriously, you will reap major benefits.
Cares about the subject and wants to motivate students. Grades harshly on essays for assignments. No late assignments accepted, participation graded heavily so get ready to talk.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Professor Rodak is so enthusiastic about her subject, and it makes students want to engage in learning. You are going to WORK in this class, but you will be glad you did because what you gain from this professor is SO important. Be ready to read, and write A LOT.
She also grades essays for completion at first, to help gauge where your skills are!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Rodak is super nice, but wasn't as accommodating as she says she is, especially during a pandemic. The class was fun and interesting, but the workload was over the top which made it hard to truly enjoy the class. If you have lots of time to read 400 page kids books, then this is the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm not gonna lie, I initially did not like her at all. Compared to other C204 classes, we 100% had the most work and I was extremely frustrated at the beginning. Somehow a switch flipped midway through and I realized that the extra work we put it allowed me to REALLY learn business writing. shes an expert at it, and she helps you grow so much!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Yaggi is a tough teacher, but rewards those willing to work. The class is difficult and seems overwhelming at times but she will help you through it and is extremely fair with grades. Yaggi taught me a ton and changed my view on how to be a professional for the better.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Yaggi is the absolute best, hands down. Sign up for her class if you want a dedicated professor who cares about you and your success.

This class is tough, but you'll come out of it with so many valuable lessons about strategic writing. I learned much more from Dr. Yaggi than my pees did from their C204 professors. One of the best, most caring professors at IU hands down.

Dr. Yaggi is hands down the best professor I've had at IU to date. I'm not someone who usually gets inspired by professors like this, but it was honestly a very special experience to have Dr. Yaggi. She cares about her students' success more than anyone, and while she will push you to do your best throughout the semester, her class is so valuable.

Professor Yaggi is absolutely awesome! She truly cares so much about their students and their success outside of school. She always goes the extra measure to make sure classes are fun and engaging and you actually work to get better at many soft business skills. She makes you work for your grade, but if you show an effort you'll have no problem
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: So far, she is the BEEEEEEEST professor I've ever met in collage. She is very helpful and hot.

Among all the pre-business classes, C204 could be one of the most tough one, but Prof. Yaggi will help you anything as long as you ask for help. Feedback was very thorough and you will know EXACTLY how you do to improve next time. Highly recommend her.
She treated everyone equally which most profs could barely do. Always make the class interesting, presentation could be tough but she made the process lot easier to accept. LOVE HER!

I had a great experience in Dr. Yaggi's course. Class started at 7 pm but it was engaging and informative. A friendly presence, feedback is easy to understand and is professional. Has high expectations but cares about the growth of her students. Class isn't longer than it needs to be so if you contribute, you'll learn a lot and get B+ or higher.

Miranda gives optional books that have mandatory reading. She gives terrible feedback and often contradicts herself. If you correct something she told you to correct, she tells you "fix it" and go back to your original content. Honestly, a terrible professor. Might note that she was a Compass 1 prof. before-- they just gave her c204 to fill spots.

Dr. Yaggi is very energetic and prepared to lecture each class, but makes C204 much more difficult and time consuming than other C204 professors. I still don't understand a lot of the feedback that I was given for most of my projects and papers. The class was much more work than any other person I've talked to taking this class at Kelley.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Easy A if you just go to class and do your homework. Take her for C204.

Overall she is great. However, sometimes u were not presenting very well but still get fairly good grade, and sometimes u did present pretty good but you might get low grade. She is unclear about what u did bad because all feedback is about how good are you. However, for students, we want to know that why she deducts grades when she said we r good.

She teaches a class about professionalism and is BY FAR the least professional teacher I've ever had. It's middle school level work. She sends about 5 emails per day that are all about a 10 minute read and are in color font. She has absolutely no idea how to be a professional and the fact that she's a Kelley professor is actually quite embarrassing
Professor Yaggi is enthusiastic, funny and she cares about her students. She truly gets you ready for a job interview or a career fair. She is definitely the best option for any Compass class!
Actually makes Compass worthwhile and useful. Her sarcasm makes class interesting.

Class is a joke, easy A if you turn in all assignments completed. No tests, no book which is nice. HUGE on participation and being her favorite pays off big time. Crazy about attendance policy and tardiness. Super nice lady who does care about you even though the amount of busy work is crazy. Super bubbly
Literally one of the best classes you will ever take. Take her you won't regret it.
Take her if you can. Her class will actually help you in life

My favorite class of the week. Yaggi makes this class amazing. Really helps you in your future business endeavors as well. Awesome class, awesome teacher, and REALLY easy. Also, everything you do in the class will help you later on in life. Take her. If you can't take her, take compass next semester. Really, she's the best.
Class is too much work for a 1.5 credit hour class. I don't think she realizes students are taking 15 credit hours. Very strict on attendance and deadlines.

Professor Yaggi is an excellent teacher. If you are looking for an easy teacher she is not the one for you, however if you are genuinely interested in bettering yourself in life and in business I highly recommend her. Very strict about deadlines and doesn't appreciate tardiness or rudeness. Holds her students accountable. Energetic, easy to follow

Not rational at all. Lost 7% on final grade over an assignment that was submitted with a wrong format (Mac format). Sent a message & gave 24 hours to change the format. Would not reconsider even though she physically saw my assignment was complete (in a 1 on 1 meeting)the day before. Also wouldn't accept a doctor's note for an ER visit 2 days prior
Pretty easy class by nature. Only got easier with Prof Yaggi. Great teacher that cares about her students. Very energetic. Highly recommend.

All in all a very good professor. Definitely a goo fit for the Kelley School of Business. She lays down her guidelines at the start of the semester and as long as you follow them, it is a very fair and smooth. She is very friendly and is there for the sole intention of teaching. I would definitely recommend her for C-104.
Do not need to attend every class, but do every assignment and youll get an A

This teacher is amazing! The best I've had at IU. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. She is tough, but it is just because she expects a lot out of you. If you participate she will give you a lot of help and like you more. Take a course with her, you will love it!

Miranda is probably one of the best teachers I've had at IU. She gets really excited about the material (I had her for  ENG E303) which makes class interesting. She is a skilled discussion leader, and I learned a ton in her class. I'd definitely suggest taking a class with her if you can.
Pretty cool teacher

she expects a lot out of her students, but she is very helpful.  she even cancelled class a few times in order to meet individually with each student to discuss our papers. she is a hard grader, but if you actually put a decent amount of work in your papers you can come out with an A in the course.  there are a lot of interesting class discussions.
Fair Warning: A lot of hard work, definitely NOT a blow-off class, I learned a lot of hard work but I tried really hard and still got a C - which is considered a good grade.

she is great!  really teaches for students to learn not just to get through the material so we can get tested over it! its been a few months since i was in her class but i found myself putting to use what she taught when revising  a paper for my sister in medical school.
Really hard - but very helpful! Improved my writing tons!
She really makes you work hard for you grade, but its definately worth it in the end. She made me a much better writer.

I really like her, she doesn't put ur papers on the overhead unless you say her can.  She is one the better eng. teachers and tells you exactly what to put into your papers.  She also canceled class due to the weather a few times, which was a real plus.
She is mean and cheap.
No Comments
A fabulous teacher who really cares about what she does.  If you want to really learn how to write, take her course.  She's also really funny, witty, and hip.

Hard grader but it is still possible to get an OK grade even if you dont do that well on all of the papers. Just as a warning, if youre shy.. dont take the class. She puts all of the papers on the overhead.
Nice guy, bad at explaining.

While Ye tries to teach in a good way he comes off as lacking as he reads directly from slides and often mixes several topics up with one another. When asked questions on how to solve something he often would confuse the class more as he was unable to answer clearly. He does care about his class and attempts to help but is just not quite up to par.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Ye is so caring, although this course is difficult in general and especially difficult online, he tries hard for his students. I understand it is a very difficult course but he really puts in the hours for review sessions before exams and is always willing to help to see his students succeed. He is very funny and wants to connect with us.

Prof Ye is one of the most passionate educators I have encountered. He is 100% ready to help his students any way that he can, like spending hours on review sessions. He isn't judgmental about questions and answers all of them eagerly. A great teacher, he just teaches a tough subject where you have to put in your own work outside of lectures!

Professor Ye would do anything to help his students understand more. He held multiple review sessions prior to exams and welcomed students asking questions mid-lecture. It's a tough course no matter who teaches it and I suspect negative reviews are from people who didn't put in the work.
Praise Ye  Amazing professor, just a tough course
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: While the course is very test heavy, Professor Ye will do anything he can to help you understand the material to his fullest extent. He held several review meetings that went over materials from lectures that would be very present on the test. He was the best Chemistry professor I have ever had.

Professor Ye is great. The professor manages to both effectively teach his students the necessary material to succeed and inspire his students to be the best chemists they can be. Professor Ye is open to feedback about exams, and treats his students with respect, working to sympathize with them in the trying times of the pandemic.

His teaching style is lacking (he reads off slides and expects you to teach yourself everything) and his class is extremely difficult. The tests are almost impossible and have trick questions, wrong answers, and you can not review a question once youve answered it. Top hat/discussion are only 8% of your grade, remaining 92% is tests.

Exams were nearly impossible to get done in allotted time, lectures made no sense and examples used never actually translated. Lots of homework assignments. Group project structure made no sense. Nice guy but I don't think he knows how to teach a high-level course
Poorly organized with an unrealistic workload. The lack of clear communication and helpful resources makes a difficult subject unnecessarily frustrating.

Little to no communication on deadlines, several of which were incorrect on the class calendar. Tests are rough, with questions being much more difficult than those done in class. Homework is time-consuming, and questions are vague. TAs will just put your question to ChatGPT during office hours, no real help. Avoid at all costs if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Bad comms on due dates + materials; Exam1 moved a week and 2 days b4 the syllabus date which was announced in class a week beforehand. Material is HARD and taught poorly. Slides and example problems are confusing, and quizzes on material are way harder than any examples you were shown/given. TA I went to for help read the FREE pdf textbook to me.
The workload is very high and good communication is lacking in the class and course materials.
Difficult to understand and difficult grading as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
Two words: heavy workload. Lots of quizzes and difficult homework with lenient grading. Not so lenient on Exams. Attendance is not mandatory but there are pop quizzes in class. His slides make no sense. He also knows he is difficult to understand and will elaborate or rephrase if asked.
Best advice, is to try to learn outside of class on your own.

The coding assignments were not too difficult, but the comprehension homework was rarely covered enough in lecture, and when it was, the professor's accent makes it very hard to understand the material. Everything I learned in this class was from the TA's in office hours. Difficult quizzes twice a week, sometimes concepts that were barely covered.

Justina was an amazing professor! She cares about her students, wrote me a recommendation that got me into a prestigious summer abroad program, last minute! Really engaging and dedicated. Best course and professor I've ever had at IU.

I didn't think this course would be interesting at all and it ended up being the best class I've ever taken at IU. Prof is awesome, very laid back, caring, passionate, and fair. She listens to what you have to say, even if you know nothing about art. Loved her teaching style.

Justina is a great teacher who definitely knows her stuff! She was so nice and tried to keep it interesting by taking us to the museum all the time. I had no prior interest in this class and only took it because  I had a certain requirement to fulfill but after I have an appreciation for some of the stuff we learned. Fully recommend this teacher!

Justina was a pretty awesome teacher. She was cool, enthusiastic and knew her stuff. She really cared what we thought about the art and was willing to take our points of views. Strict atendance policy but she took us to the museum all the time, this was the best part! Take notes, do some of the readings and you will do well.

Despite the fairly dull lectures, taking one of prof Lay's classes is NOT a bad idea. She is very mellow/easygoing, yet knowledgeable. Be sure to check the class notes (topic specifically) because I had no idea my whole semester would be about being a vegan. Not a bad thing!! I just recommend checking the details because that's what matters most.

This was not a difficult course, the readings were short and easy to understand and the assignments were super quick. Yi-Chen Lay however was not an engaging professor and her lectures were mandatory and really boring. She isn't too harsh of a grader but she can nitpick here and there.
He is very friendly with students. He guides you through the assignments. You need to post comments on an online discussion board.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is very helpful professor. He knows his stuff. He is interested in his every single students. Also, he knows how to run his classes.

Interesting prof. He had to lower his standards due to small class size. His attendance policy (after 1, each absence is 10% off final grade) was also ridiculous. We did Duolingo, but didn't use it. So much article reading. If you like L2 acquisition, he is good. If not, it might be dry. He is helpful though. Textbook is online.

I love Bao Laoshi! She always made lectures interesting by bringing in fun things related to the topics in class. Her Chinese is quite fast, but she helped me a lot understand Chinese and process it faster because of it.

Bao Laoshi is incredibly friendly and knowledgeable. She communicates concepts clearly and was very encouraging to someone like me, who started as a total beginner. If I felt lost, I knew I could ask her for help and get it figured out. I genuinely enjoyed my experience in this class and I credit my becoming a major in this subject to her as well.

Bao Laoshi is a great teacher-- she is great at explaining grammar and is very accessible outside of class if you have questions. I was a beginner at Chinese and came away from this class excited to learn more Chinese. If you are a total beginner, the class can feel very face-paced with all the vocab you'll learn. You learn 400 characters in 16w!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Bao Laoshi has been really great and is always super helpful! The tests can be pretty hard, and you've really gotta study for the dictations, but she's always ready to answer any questions and is willing to help if you reach out.

Bao Laoshi is genuinely one of the best professors in the Chinese department. She is always willing to help and genuinely cares about her students. However, due to the way that the Chinese department is organized, you must study well for the course. Dictation will screw you over if you don't study properly!
Bao was great, as always. She made the tests a bit too challenging but was accessible and willing to work with us.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Her tests are killer, but she's a wonderful teacher and a great mentor. As long as you yuxi before tingxie and prepare for her tests, you'll have a great time.

Bao Laoshi is a really great teacher. She's friendly and keeps lectures interesting. The course has a lot of work but she's reasonable about it and take's students' feedback into account. She's always happy to answer any questions about material and will arrange to meet outside of her office hours if you can't make them.

Bao Laoshi is the best. She's incredibly friendly and open to helping students. I audited the class and while I think she may have looked down on me initially, she was amazingly friendly and helpful. Do your work, and you'll reap the benefits.

Bao laoshi is the greatest Chinese teacher I've ever had. She's really helpful and always willing to work with you if something is going on. If you email her with ay type of question she gets back to you right away.

Bao Laoshi is a good teacher. She teaches the lecture portion of the Chinese classes. I audited the course, and she treated me the same as any other student who was taking it for a grade. The material is difficult, being a native English speaker learning Chinese, but she is very helpful and is enthusiastic to help and learn more. Recommend!!!

Bao Laoshi is a good teacher. I didn't receive a fantastic grade, but I received the grade I deserved. The material is difficult for me, but the class is structured such that if you make an HONEST effort you will learn enough to at least pass the class. That said, this is Chinese - not an easy A. She is very helpful and friendly. Recommended.
the best chinese teacher ive ever had. love her. she so engaged with the material and prepared for class

She is one of the best Chinese teachers I've ever had. I would definitely recommend taking this class because of her. She actually knows how to teach Chinese, unlike some teachers who only know how to speak it.

Professor Shen is a very caring professor and cares a lot about his students. Although the lectures can be boring, he does try his best to keep you listening. All tests I took were open note and the homework is easy. Just pay attention in class and you should find this class easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Shen really cares about the subject and knows what he's talking about. The material is very dry and his voice is soft, so it can be difficult to feel engaged and stay awake. He is super nice and funny in his own way. He wants you to do well and doesn't require a text book. A difficult class with a great teacher for sure.

Although this class definitely covered some tough material, Dr. Shen made it so almost all students did well. He is very knowledgable and passionate about the subject matter and genuinely wants to see students succeed. Also, he is pretty accessible outside of class if you want to talk about the class or literally anything.

The course was simply- 50% group work (easiest thing ever. submitted questions from chapter once a week), 20% midterm, 30% final.  He is very passionate and knowledgeable about the subjects, and extremely interested in helping you individually to get the grade you want.

Very caring professor. Genuinely wants us to succeed and did everything in her power for pre-kelley students to get a b+. Her lectures were helpful for me but you definitely need office hours if you have never taken econ before. If you talk to her she will do everything she can to help.
Everything's been good overall, just always gotta deal with some shady people trying to cheat on exams. they do bad and start blaming the professor for not curving.

I'd rather walk through glass shards barefoot then take her class again. 0/10 the tests are abnormally hard and she makes no effort to actually teach the material. Drop her class and don't look back, you'll thank yourself in the future
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Merry Christmas Ms. Young! Thank you !!!

I don't think there is a worse professor you can get for econ. She has trouble speaking english so her lecturers are pointless since its hard to understand her. Her tests are overly difficult and the questions don't make sense half the time. She made it 20x harder than it needs to be and I honestly wouldn't wish a professor like her on anyone.

Such a kind person and very generous when grading and helping out, but English is not her first language, which makes lectures confusing. You can tell she is very intelligent and knows what she is talking about but the teaching of it is so-so. I don't recommend her if you've never taken econ prior.
She's a nice person. I screwed up the second midterm but she's willing to help.

I really like Ms. Young as a person; she's kind and well-meaning. But her lectures are hard to follow, and many students use AI to interpret her slides during class. took time outside of class to help with presentation skills and bring the best out of students

Professor Yoder is so kind. She really cares about you and just wants to see you grow. She gives great feedback and does some great activities. I would highly recommend taking this class with her if you could!
Really an incredible teacher with so much to share. She really cares about what she teaches and although she is tough, she is very helpful with everything.

This professor is passionate about presenting and wants each student to perform well. very available to give extra help. Very kind and made class enjoyable.

Professor Yoder is hands down the best C104 professor. She cares for her students like her own children and is always willing to go the extra mile to help them succeed. AWESOME

Weekly assignment due on Saturday night with 2 exams through the year. Assignments are easy if you took notes on the lecture.

Best Professor I have ever had in my life, amazing professor. I never seen anyone this passionate about what they teach, I think she is the best of the best. I can tell everyone that from COGS100 which is the course that I am taking now I learned more than any course that I have taken through my entire 3 years in university. I am Economics major.

No attendance taken and an hour of work outside of class per week.

Maas is a great guy too and very willing to help during OHs

Annoying class

I would strongly recommend her course!

reviews.comment: One of the kindest teachers I have ever had. Very approachable. No matter what, she will ALWAYS find something positive to say about each and everyone of your projects. If you put at least a small amount of effort into the projects and show up to class, you're pretty much guaranteed to pass.

She is the sweetest professor you will ever have. Nothing but encouraging. So understanding and willing to listen if you have a problem with an assignment. Basically the course is you're given a topic space once a week - you create a rough draft and present it to a small group. People are then chosen to present to the whole class. Take it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: She really is a great professor, really cares about her students and making the class accessible. Wish more profs were like her!

Joanna is by far my favorite professor this semester. She is one of the nicest teachers I have met and genuinely cares about her students. The class has no tests or papers. Just one project every week that is pretty simple and enjoyable. Would give her and this class a 10/10.
She is caring and really enjoys the material she teaches. The weekly project routine does get a bit dry by the end of the semester, but she is very enjoyable and always willing to help.

reviews.comment: She really cares about the material she is trying to teach, but the level of difficulty is not on par with the course. Way too easy.

reviews.comment: Probably the most incompetent professor I have ever had. We had a project every week, and did not receive one grade throughout the entire semester. She always had an excuse for why she hadn't done her grading or she "wanted to give us good feedback". The problem is we never got any feedback at all. The grades are due in an hour and still not done.

Best Professor I've ever had. You will learn so much if you're fully committed. He lectures well, but writes very challenging exams and problem sets. Students who say negative about Dr. Zelhof are obviously weren't up to the work required. Some people might not be ready to take the class, but those who are will have a truly amazing experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Exams aren't like the lectures and problem sets so get ready to do a lot on your own. If you put in the work it is a great class and you'll learn great things.
Tough exams, but an excellent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know how better to express why you should avoid Zelhof than the fact that I did NOT do well in intro to chem, but I currently have a grade 15% higher in Organic chem than in this class with this prof. He's nice and all, but you do not get what you need to know for the exams from his lectures/problem sets. Never taken a less rewarding class

The absolute worst professor I've ever had. Purposely saved genetics for my last year at IU because I thought I would enjoy it. I would have too if I had taken it with literally any other professor. Seriously, do NOT take this course with Zelhof. This semester has been such a miserable experience.

I will preface this comment by saying DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR. His power points are put together like a kindergarten collage, and you can immediately tell the lack of effort he gives in class by avoiding questions and moving through material like we have already learned it. Chicken scratch handwriting + useless office hours.

This was the worst biology class I have taken so far at IU. Zelhof WILL NOT actually answer any questions you may have, nor will he teach the material. He will read a slideshow that will stimulate his memory as he goes along. The exams have nothing to do with the lectures which have nothing to do with the book. Take this with another professor.

One of the worst professors I have ever had.The tests include problems that you have never even seen before in class or material that he said he'd never ask.  With no assigned chapters  or extra problems we felt helpless .Learned more from my AI than I did from him. If you go to office hours he's rude & still doesn't prepare you for his tests.

Dr. Zelhof is an incredible teacher and a true geneticist.  If you take this class with him, you will learn more than you could ever hope to about genetics. And if you show an initiative, it won't go unnoticed, but don't kid yourself - this is a 300 level course and is challenging.  If you were expecting an easy course, change your major.

You will learn a lot in Dr. Zelhof's class. He lectures well and writes very challenging exams and problem sets. Students who enjoy science and problem solving shouldn't have trouble with this class. Students who are interested in collecting an A without working very hard, look elsewhere (OR: change your major. 300 level bio courses should be hard)

Take this class with another teacher and save yourself the trouble!  Rude teacher that does not explain questions even when you go to office hours.  You get a "the whole point of homework is for you to figure it out yourself" response.  One of the worst teachers in the biology department in my opinion.

Text is "optional" but may be necessary for understanding the material.  Do problem sets and problems in the book, review sessions are very helpful.  Tests are much more difficult than expected based on lectures and problem sets.

The problems he does in class are way easier than the ones on the exams. The problem sets will help your grade in the end so try to get 100% on all of them and also try and get all the extra credit you can. Before the exams make sure you know how to do every problem on the problem sets and if not go to the reveiw sessions!

If you could take this class with a different teacher I would recommend it. He is not good at explaining the material and does not understand when the class is not grasping the material(even if the class average on a test is below a D!)

This professor actually makes the material more difficult to understand than the text he claims is optional.  All of his lectures come directly from the text or other teachers exams but he lacks the understanding to explain well enough the extracted images/problems.  A very poor teacher whose inarticulate style is detrimental to learning.
tests are way more difficult than you think they are going to be, based on lectures and problem sets.

Gabe was one of the best professors I've had so far! I took his classes online so they were just recorded lectures, but he always kept them fun with lots of jokes. His exam questions come straight from the PowerPoints and the study guides, but it is a lot of information so you really have to study. Overall, I really enjoyed the class!

Prof. Zentner was a great professor. He knows the material really well and it's obvious that he cares a lot about what he's teaching. He makes dad jokes throughout the lectures which makes them more enjoyable. The class is memorization-heavy, so you have to put in the work and learn the material well, but he offers many extra-credit opportunities.

He's a good professor but molecular is just a hard course. Everything on the tests are on the slides. But the tests are pretty detailed so you have to memorize quite a lot. Beware that the tests are worth most of the grade with only some homework to supplement it.

Lectures were boring, but interesting. Passionate about his work. makes funny dad jokes randomly during lecture which are hilarious. Only went to lecture to voice record, and to go to his office hours, only one that went to his office hours after lecture, and he helped me on everything , clarified things that I didn't understand. 11/10 recommend.

The exams in Zentner's class are horrible! He puts SO much detail into them. Seriously little things on very small graphics on his slides, he will write a question about. ALSO!! He says you don't need to know things, and has questions about them. His exam questions make me mad. The amount of memorization you have to do for his class is crazy.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good luck with this course. I would highly suggest taking this course with a different professor. Sure, Zentner was funny, or at least he thought he was funny. In my opinion, he spent more time thinking of puns than he spent making sure he was properly conveying the material. I will be retaking this course with another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class does take a lot of work but it's all memorization. Professor Zenter provides all of his notes as powerpoint slides and everything on the exams comes from these slides. His lecture can be hard to pay attention to and the tests can be detail-oriented but it is a very fair class! He's a great guy so go to office hours for extra help!

The class overall was interesting, However it was a big timesuck, The professor is very well versed however a lot of the lectures are very detail specific and do require a lot of time for memorization.

Honestly I know that a few of these are written by his UTAs, Yea he is a nice guy, though I believe that throughout my time in the course it is to detail heavy. I wish I took it with another teacher, because I have stayed up more nights trying to memorize the material than I ever have for any other class at IU.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Very young, fun guy. I had him his first semester teaching, and there was a bit of a learning curve - he's very detail oriented, and the class is mostly memorization, so don't hesitate to break out the flash cards! If it's on a slide, it's fair game for a test. No textbook though, and he's a really nice guy who genuinely loves what he does.

Gabe is an outstanding professor. He's a closed shell when you first go to his office hours but if you keep going, which you definitely should, he really opens up. His very deep interest in the material can make it difficult for students, but overall he is phenomenal!

Gabe is honestly one of the most approachable professors I have ever had. He is extremely knowledgable and can relate the information presented in class extremely well. I would most definitely take his class again.

So far Gabe Zentner has easily been the most fair professor to teach molecular biology in years. In the class you are only tested over material covered in the lecture slides ( and they are all posted online). The tests and quizzes may be slightly info heavy, but he always makes them far and only asks questions over info he covered. And he gives BQs

Zeynep is one of the most caring professors you will have. She is very passionate about what she does and wants her students to be as well! This is not a difficult class, she gives you every necessary tool to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great professor. So nice and helps you a lot.

Zeynep Elbasan-Bozdogan is the most engaged, discerning, and effective instructor I have had the pleasure of studying under at IU. Her lessons are well-prepared and student-centered. She approaches each lesson with enthusiasm,  patience, and high expectations. You will not find a more caring teacher. Supportive, sharp, fun, demanding, fair.

Zeynep is great! I learned a lot for a required class and despite the BS taught in the lectures, she made it all make sense in the discussion. She also had good insight on the speeches/outlines and all her comments seemed to be truly helpful. Clearly a bright person and caring teacher anyone could have a conversation with. For final, go to quizlet.

Zeynep is an absolutely great person, but very unclear on the course material. Do not take the online lecture in this course, because none of the lecture material is ever covered in class. The midterm and final are really difficult, but sit down with Zeynep before hand and she will help.

Public Speaking is a manageable class. However, I really liked having Zeynep as my section leader -she's really sweet, funny, and nicer than some of the other lecture leader options (based off conversations with friends in other classes). Beware of the final- it is challenging so be sure to know all of the terms well enough to explain them.

Needed this class to fill a requirement. Zeynep knew what she was talking about but there were a lot of times of confusion and no one in class cared enough to ask for clarification. Go to class, participate, impossible to not get a good grade.

HATED THIS CLASS. She really knows her stuff but the class itself is WAY too difficult for what most people were expecting. She knows her subject, but not good at conveying it to her students. She also expects EVERYONE to participate plenty when it's obvious most are only taking it because it's and A&H.

Zeynep really knows her material and teaches it in a way that is easy to understand. If you go to class, take notes, and turn in papers, you should pass. Only have 2 exams, which were fair in content and length. She's really willing to help her students and is easy to talk to. Fell behind a few times, but always caught up even with 50 min. class.

In C190 her material are horrid.  For a 40min discussion there was a 75page section that was needed to be read.  Her organization is good but what she expects in undefined.  Basically if you don't know everything in the course already then there is no method to pass this class.
Definitely made a good move taking CMCL-121 over the BUS X104. Pretty easy grader and wants to see you do well. Very down to earth and easy to talk to.
Never clear. Always throw a flowing topic to you and jump to another without any logic.

One of the worst professors I've had. Goes on tangents all the time that are of no use, and seems out of touch with the technology he is supposed to be teaching. Quizzes are over material that is mostly not taught in class or posted online anywhere, & assignments are vague and not similar to the real world, as he claims they are.
Mr. Zeller is nice, flexible, a little tangential, but a good teacher. Very blackboard oriented. Laid back. Informative
Rambles on about nothing! Isn't clear on projects and the quizzes are kind of hard to understand.

Took him for B430, and have no complaints. Lectures were compact yet informative, and they often ended early. Labs were stressful at first because a failed lab is a failed class, but the lab objectives were achievable, and deadlines were often extended. Tests were all open answer and I felt prepared for them with how much review time he gave us.

Rating for INFO-I430. This professor does not speak english fluently. He reads directly off the slides, and asking him questions in class is nearly pointless. He does not understand your question 90% of the time, and attending class is pointless. If you have or are studying for your CompTIA Sec+, you do not need to care about this course or prof.

Honestly a great professor however he makes it so if you fail more than 1 lab you receive an immediate f for the whole course. This paired with the labs not functioning due to the required system makes for a high stress environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures last about 30 minutes (sometimes even less) and then instead of doing attendance in any normal way, he makes you connect to some local IP and fiddle around with some URL parameters. Not very good at explaining stuff but you do get notes posted for every lecture.

Dr. Zhu got much better as the semester went on. He restates quite a bit of what is on the slides in lecture. The three tests (including a final) were all take-home and open note. There is quite a bit of what feels like busy work in the weekly modules, but nothing is too hard. He definitely cares about the topic and hopes you learn a thing or two.

For an honors level class, it wasn't an easy A but very close. If you take notes during class and study a little the night before, you shouldn't have any problem acing the tests. Chen is a darling and will do everything he can to make you succeed in the class. Since he is a doctor in this field, he is teaching you from experience over a textbook.

He's really nice and cares a lot about his students. He doesn't want you to just pass the class, but the actually learn about what he's teaching. He knows his field well and is very passionate about it. Really good guy,  brought us all chocolate one day. Tests are hard, but he's super willing to help you if you ask a few questions.

When he wasn't talking about himself, I was able to learn subject matter from the iffy slide shows. Labs did not correspond with class lectures at all. Not a very exciting 100 level course. I'd say choose a different one if you're looking for a fun class.
Hard to understand sometimes but a great guy. He bought everyone in the class a bagel because he said he was so excited to teach us about peak oil. Highly recommended.
He's very organized and cares about his students. His tests are hard, but the labs in the class are easy.

Jingjing is so so nice, sometimes she moves a bit fast, but she usually posts SQL scripts to Canvas so you can use it later if needed. She graded pretty lax on the group project/presentation it felt like, and she brought food on group workdays. Not a walk-in-the-park class, but definitely recommend Jingjing for it.
Jingjing runs a very good class although the content gets a little boring at times. She definitely cares about her students and brings snacks on group work days.
She is one of the best at Kelley! Always clearify materials and respect students. Take her!

She is such a nice person and she gives you snacks on group days!! She is very understanding and has a good sense of humor. She doesn't take things too seriously. She really cares about her students and their grades. I would 100% take her again!!!

My final grade was close to an A- (89%). She is the best professor, and I would call her the Michael Jordan of the Kelley—the  GOAT. Her teaching style made me willing to learn. The course was well structured, and the exams were not difficult as long as you were willing to put in the effort. Overall, I highly, highly recommend taking her class.
shes so cute

This class meets once a week then you have 1-2hrs of Playposit videos as the "asynchronous" class. Class is pretty easy but would HIGHLY recommend going to class as she gives answers to HW/projects in class every week. Also takes Tophat attendance. Exams not hard but still need to study. Overall really nice and caring prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She knows a lot about stuff. Care about the students. Very nice. One of my favorite teacher.
This is a hybrid course, and I believe professor Zhu did a great job. She has lots of real-world case studies for working capital management.
I learned a lot from F101. Professor Zhu is a wonderful professor.

Professor Zhu is one of the best teachers I have had at IU. She was extremely caring and she did a great job explaining the course material. She was one of the nicest teachers I have ever had. She was understanding and put her students first. Take her course if having a teacher who will fight for you matters to you, because she will.
Professor Zhu is very good. She gives examples to make connections between theory and practice. The topics for working capital are dry but she made them very interesting.

Professor Zhu is awesome. The lectures are engaging and she gives examples of how to do everything in excel. Tests are open note open book and are relatively easy. She's super nice and funny. A little hard to understand sometimes but overall a great professor. She brought pizza and lemonade for the class multiple times. Would recommend her forsure!

I found her examples n class discussion very helpful in connecting concepts such as abstract financial ratios. Really approachable in office hours n gave me great insight into careers in finance n real estate. 
I don't know why someone is tr@lling her on here. Probably jealous of her. S. needs to reign in the toxicity.

Prof Zhu is extremely caring and engaging - take FDP even if the lecture timing seems daunting. You will learn so much from the course in all aspects of professional development and the assignments are there to help you grow (with lots of resources and 2nd chances to improve upon your work). Don't skip class, because otherwise what's the point?

I can't say she's bad. However, you need to know 2 things before taking her class.

1. Quizzes for participation and attendance every single class.

2. Exams are not difficult based on content, but on time. Some don't care about this, but it drove me really crazy knowing that I knew the content, but struggled with speed.
Very clear grading criteria
Amazing lecture and case studies
I really like the class discussions.

reviews.comment: She is really good.
The Professor really care about students.
Professor Zhu is great!
Professor Zhu is great! She uses lots of examples and gives practice questions for exams. I would highly recommend her courses.

reviews.comment: Lectures are so incredibly dry and boring it is impossible to pay attention. She continuously asks questions to which the answers are on the slide being presented on so no one answers it and class drags on. Exams are easy but these lectures are brutally hard to sit through
She is accessible outside class. Her lectures look great.
Professor Zhu is the best teacher I have had in Kelley.
She is very nice and well prepared for the lectures. The final is tough but she curved the grades.

Professor Zhu is nice, but this class was terrible. The expectations are unclear, for example, Tophat questions are graded for correction which we found out at the end of the semester. Her lectures are confusing and extremely boring (just reads from slides). My advise, find another finance elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Jia is young and handsome, his classes are clear and easy to follow, and no homework is a big plus.

First time teaching the course. Was not organized and lied about exam difficulty. Midterm and final are a total of 40% of your grade, but they are the only "difficult" parts of the course. Everything else is manageable and not a big-time commitment outside of class.

If you have the option, don't take him for D271. We had multiple group projects including a debate, report, and presentation, which isn't the case for all D271 professors. You are graded for your participation in class but get laughed at if you get the answer wrong. No homework though, just in class assignments and 2 challenging exams.

Dr. Z is a very rigorous but great professor. The bad reviews are from undergrads - E183 is a core class that varies by instructor. If you are a freshman and you want it to be easy, take it with someone else!! I have taken all of his grad-level classes by choice - you will learn so much in every one. You will read, write, talk, and learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Terrible in every way, do not recommend for sanity purposes.

His ego is huge; he has had about 3-4 power trips in front of our class in one semester giving kids assigned seats in college. He'll never let you explain yourself or quite frankly anything as he just tries to talk louder than you like a child. He's not lenient with grades, if you need help don't expect it from him.

Dr. Z is a must-take professor at O'Neill. He has extensive experience in energy policy, water, and the global environment. It's a tough course because we need to read and write each week/class. However, it's a rewarding class. I can see he puts his 200% self-energy into the teaching. He addresses each question we have seriously. Learned so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Z sets high expectations, and that's why some people don't enjoy or do well in his class. Relaxed attendance policy and good with curving/weighting. As long as you actually pay attention during lectures and do the readings and assignments, you'll do well in the course. He's a great professor who is very passionate about the topics discussed.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You can't even simply have a discourse with another student without disrupting his "train of thought." I had a conversation with a classmate asking about the course, and he stopped the whole lecture to call me out and told me to meet him after class. reviews.comment: Very strict and loves to call people out when they talk or are on their phones. If he catches you not on Canvas or a Word document in class, he takes away your computer privileges. reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice and knowledgeable professor. He helps you understand difficult topics and can talk for days about the course. By far one of the best professors I've ever had

Very strict and loves to call people out when they talk or on thier phones. if he catches you not on canvas or a word document in class he takes your computer privileges. Homeworks are very long and time consuming. Exams are a lot of the final grade and are harder than they should be.

reviews.comment: Dr. Z's course was extremely fast-paced.  We were given lengthy readings and papers each week on various subjects. The material is pushed at you so quickly and you are required to participate a lot. But Dr.Z reacts poorly if you answer his questions incorrectly. Overall, a very bad experience. Turned something I loved to learn about into a chore.

reviews.comment: Incredibly knowledgeable professor. I have learned more in his class than most of the classes I have taken throughout college and I would recommend Dr. Z every time. He takes respect very seriously though, as he should, so keep that in mind if you are often late to class or can't keep your cell phone away.

reviews.comment: I have taken many classes at IU and I can say that you shouldn't take this class. His lectures were boring and he wasn't a considerate person (rude sometimes).

reviews.comment: Dr. Z teaches this class like it way higher than an 100-level course. There are weekly assignments that require about 40 pages of reading and 600+ word response papers. Dr. Z spends all class lecturing about the readings, even though it's required to read them before class. However, most of the grade is based on only 2 (half MC/half written) exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is extremely knowledgeable in his expertise, and he ensures you leave his classes with greater understanding of every topic. He knows how to cater his teaching to student learning styles, making the complexity of the topics much more understandable. His classes are not easy but you will come out of them a better student and professional.

This is by far the most relevant course I have taken as a dual student. There's so many courses in the program that feel either too niche or too broad and this perfectly intertwines the importance of science, policy, and economics. The structure is consistent and demanding but worth it. Dr. Z is caring, understanding, engaging and knowledgeable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I learned a lot in this class, the class is set up in a way that really helps you learn the material so long as you keep up with the material. There is definitely a lot of reading and writing however, the readings and paper are never that long. Dr. Z is really good at making himself available for questions, lectures are discussion based. I
